Namo tassa bhagavato arahato sammāsambuddhassa

Homage to the Blessed One, the Arahant, the Perfectly Self-Enlightened One.

Vinayapiṭake

In the Vinaya Piṭaka.

Pācityādiyojanā

The Exposition of the Pācittiya and Similar Rules.

Pācittiyayojanā

The Exposition of the Pācittiya.

Mahākāruṇikaṃ [M 0.0001] nāthaṃ, abhinatvā samāsato;

Pācityādivaṇṇanāya, karissāmatthayojanaṃ.

Having bowed to the Great Compassionate Lord, we shall briefly make an exposition of the meaning of the commentary on the Pācittiya and so on.

5. Pācittiyakaṇḍaṃ

5. The Pācittiya Section.

1. Musāvādasikkhāpada-atthayojanā

1. The Exposition of the Meaning of the Training Rule on False Speech.

Khuddakānanti [V 1.0001] sukhumāpattipakāsakattā appakānaṃ, gaṇanato vā pacurattā bahukānaṃ. Yesaṃ sikkhāpadānanti sambandho. “Yesa”nti padaṃ “saṅgaho”ti pade sāmyatthachaṭṭhī. Saṅgahīyate saṅgaho[V 1.0002]. “Navahi vaggehī”tipadaṃ “saṅgaho, suppatiṭṭhito”ti padadvaye karaṇaṃ. Dānīti kālavācako sattamyantanipāto idāni-pariyāyo, imasmiṃ kāleti attho. Tesanti khuddakānaṃ, ayaṃ vaṇṇanāti sambandho. Bhavatīti ettha ti-saddo ekaṃsatthe anāgatakāliko hoti “nirayaṃ nūna gacchāmi, ettha me natthi saṃsayo”tiādīsu (jā. 2.22.331) viya. Kiñcāpettha hi yathā ekaṃsavācako nūnasaddo atthi, na evaṃ “bhavatī”ti pade, atthato pana ayaṃ vaṇṇanā nūna bhavissatīti attho gahetabbo. Atha vā avassambhāviyatthe anāgatakālavācako hoti “dhuvaṃ buddho bhavāmaha”ntiādīsu (bu. vaṃ. 2.109-114) viya. Kāmañhettha yathā avassambhāviyatthavācako dhuvasaddo atthi, na evaṃ “bhavatī”ti pade, atthato pana dhuvaṃ bhavissati ayaṃ vaṇṇanāti attho gahetabboti daṭṭhabbaṃ.

`Khuddakāni` (the minor rules) are so called because they reveal subtle offenses, or because they are few, or, by way of counting, because they are numerous. The connection is: 'of which training rules.' The word `yesaṃ` is in the genitive case expressing relation with the word `saṅgaho`. `Saṅgaho` is that which is collected. The phrase `navahi vaggehi` is the instrument for the two words `saṅgaho` and `suppatiṭṭhito`. `Dāni` is a temporal indeclinable in the locative case, a synonym for `idāni`, meaning 'at this time.' The connection is: 'of those minor ones, this is the commentary.' In `bhavati` here, the particle `ti` is in the sense of certainty and in the future tense, as in the example: 'Surely I will go to hell, there is no doubt for me here' (Jā. 2.22.331). Although in this case the word `nūna`, which expresses certainty, is present, it is not so in the word `bhavati`; however, the meaning should be understood as 'this commentary will surely be.' Alternatively, it is a future tense indicating inevitability, as in the example: 'Surely we will become Buddhas' (Bu.vaṃ. 2.109-114). Although here the word `dhuvaṃ`, which expresses inevitability, is present, it is not so in the word `bhavati`; however, the meaning should be understood as 'this commentary will certainly be.' This should be noted.

1. “Tatthā”ti [M 0.0002] padaṃ “musāvādavaggassā”ti pade niddhāraṇasamudāyo, tesu navasu vaggesūti attho. Paṭhamasikkhāpadeti vā, tesu khuddakesu sikkhāpadesūti attho. Sakyānaṃ puttoti bhaginīhi saṃvāsakaraṇato lokamariyādaṃ chindituṃ, jātisambhedato vā rakkhituṃ sakkuṇantīti sakyā. Sākavanasaṇḍe nagaraṃ māpentīti vā sakyā, pubbarājāno. Tesaṃ vaṃse bhūtattā etarahipi rājāno sakyā nāma, tesaṃ puttoti attho. “Buddhakāle”ti padaṃ “pabbajiṃsū”ti pade ādhāro. Sakyakulato nikkhamitvāti sambandho. “Vādakkhitto”tyādinā vādena khitto, vādamhi vāti atthaṃ dasseti. Yatra yatrāti yassaṃ yassaṃ diṭṭhiyaṃ pavattatīti sambandho. Avajānitvāti paṭissavena viyogaṃ katvā. Avasaddo hi viyogatthavācako. “Apajānitvā”tipi pāṭho, paṭiññātaṃ apanītaṃ katvāti attho. Dosanti ayuttidosaṃ, sallakkhento hutvāti sambandho. Kathento kathentoti antasaddo mānasaddakāriyo. Kathiyamāno kathiyamānoti hi attho. Paṭijānitvāti paṭiññātaṃ katvā. Ānisaṃsanti niddosaṃ guṇaṃ. Paṭipubbo carasaddo paṭicchādanatthoti āha “paṭicarati paṭicchādetī”ti. “Kiṃ pana rūpaṃ niccaṃ vā aniccaṃ vā”ti vutte “anicca”nti vadati. Kasmāti vutte “jānitabbato”ti vadati. Yadi evaṃ nibbānampi jānitabbattā aniccaṃ nāma siyāti vutte attano hetumhi dosaṃ disvā ahaṃ “jānitabbato”ti hetuṃ na vadāmi, “jātidhammato”ti pana vadāmi. Tayā pana dussutattā evaṃ vuttanti vatvā aññenaññaṃ paṭicarati. “Kurundiya”nti padaṃ “vutta”nti pade ādhāro. Etassāti “rūpaṃ aniccaṃ jānitabbato”ti vacanassa. Tatrāti kurundiyaṃ. Tassāti paṭijānanāvajānanassa. “Paṭicchādanattha”nti padaṃ “bhāsatī”tipade sampadānaṃ. “Mahāaṭṭhakathāya”ntipadaṃ “vutta”nti pade ādhāro. “Divāṭṭhānādīsū”ti padaṃ upanetabbaṃ. Idaṃ “asukasmiṃ nāmapadese”ti pade niddhāraṇasamudāyo.

1. The word `Tatthā` is a specification of the group in the phrase `musāvādavaggassā`, meaning 'among those nine sections.' Or, 'in the first training rule,' meaning 'among those minor training rules.' `Sakyānaṃ putto` means 'a son of the Sakyas.' The Sakyas are so called because they are able (`sakkuṇanti`) to break worldly convention by cohabiting with their sisters, or to protect their lineage from being mixed. Alternatively, the Sakyas were the ancient kings who had a city built in a grove of Sāka trees. Because they were born in their lineage, even now kings are called Sakyas; 'their son' has this meaning. The word `Buddhakāle` is the locative basis for the word `pabbajiṃsū`. The connection is 'having gone forth from the Sakyan clan.' `Vādakkhitto`, etc., shows the meaning 'assailed by debate' or 'in debate.' `Yatra yatra` connects with 'in whichever view it occurs.' `Avajānitvā` means 'having made a separation from what was promised'; for the word `ava-` expresses the meaning of separation. `Apajānitvā` is also a reading, meaning 'having removed what was acknowledged.' `Dosaṃ` means an improper fault; the connection is with 'being one who discerns.' In `kathento kathento`, the `-anta` suffix has the function of the `-māna` suffix; indeed, the meaning is 'being spoken of, being spoken of.' `Paṭijānitvā` means 'having acknowledged.' `Ānisaṃsaṃ` means a faultless quality. He says that the root `car` with the prefix `paṭi-` has the meaning of concealing, thus: `paṭicarati paṭicchādeti` (he conceals, he covers). When asked, 'Is form permanent or impermanent?' he replies, 'Impermanent.' When asked why, he says, 'Because it is knowable.' When it is said, 'If so, then Nibbāna too would be impermanent because it is knowable,' seeing the fault in his own reason, he says, 'I do not give the reason 'because it is knowable,' but rather 'because it is subject to birth.'' Then, saying, 'You have misheard,' he conceals one thing with another. The word `Kurundiyaṃ` is the locative basis for the word `vuttaṃ`. `Etassa` refers to the statement 'form is impermanent because it is knowable.' `Tatrā` means 'in the Kurundī.' `Tassa` refers to that acknowledging and denying. The phrase `Paṭicchādanatthaṃ` is the dative of purpose for the verb `bhāsati`. The phrase `Mahāaṭṭhakathāyaṃ` is the locative basis for `vuttaṃ`. The phrase `Divāṭṭhānādīsū` should be supplied. This is a specification of the group for the phrase 'in such and such a place.'

3. Sammā [V 1.0003] vadati anenāti saṃvādanaṃ, ujujātikacittaṃ, na saṃvādanaṃ visaṃvādanaṃ, vañcanādhippāyavasappavattaṃ cittanti dassento āha “visaṃvādanacitta”nti. “Vācā”tyādinā vacati etāyāti vācāti atthaṃ dasseti[M 0.0003]. Hīti daḷhīkaraṇajotakaṃ, tadaminā saccanti attho. “Vācāyevā”ti padaṃ “byappatho”ti pade tulyatthaṃ, “vuccatī”ti pade kammaṃ. Pathasaddaparattā vācāsaddassa byādeso kato. Suddhacetanā kathitāti sambandho. Taṃsamuṭṭhitasaddasahitāti tāya cetanāya samuṭṭhitena saddena saha pavattā cetanā kathitāti yojanā.

3. `Saṃvādana` (agreement) is so called because one speaks rightly by means of it; it is a mind of an upright nature. That which is not agreement is disagreement. Showing that it is a mind proceeding under the influence of deceitful intent, he said 'a mind of disagreement.' By `vācā`, etc., he shows the meaning: 'that by which one speaks is speech.' `Hi` is an indicator of strengthening; its meaning is 'indeed, this is true.' The word `vācāyeva` is equivalent in meaning to the word `byappatho` and is the object of the word `vuccati`. Because the word `patha` follows, a modification of the word `vācā` is made. The connection is that pure volition is spoken of. The explanation is that volition proceeding together with sound arisen from that volition is spoken of.

“Eva”nti padaṃ “dassetvā”ti pade nidassanaṃ, karaṇaṃ vā. “Dassetvā”ti padaṃ “dassento āhā”ti padadvaye pubbakālakiriyā. Anteti “vācā”tiādīnaṃ pañcannaṃ padānaṃ avasāne. “Āhā”ti ettha vattamāna-tivacanassa akāro paccuppannakālavācakena “idānī”ti padena yojitattā. “Tatthā”ti padaṃ “attho veditabbo”ti pade ādhāro. Etthāti “adiṭṭhaṃ diṭṭhaṃ me”tiādīsu. “Pāḷiya”nti padaṃ “desanā katā”ti pade ādhāro. Nissitaviññāṇavasena avatvā nissayapasādavasena “cakkhunā diṭṭha”nti vuttanti āha “oḷārikenevā”ti.

The word `evaṃ` is an illustration in the word `dassetvā`, or it may be an instrument. The word `dassetvā` is a prior-action in relation to the two words `dassento āha`. `Ante` refers to the end of the five words beginning with `vācā` and so on. Here in `āha`, the `a` which replaces the present tense ending `ti` is connected with the word `idāni`, which denotes the present time. The word `tattha` is the locative basis for the phrase 'the meaning should be understood.' `Ettha` refers to phrases like 'the unseen is seen by me,' etc. The word `Pāḷiyaṃ` is the locative basis for the phrase 'the teaching was given.' Not speaking in terms of dependent consciousness, but in terms of the physical sense-basis, it was said 'seen with the eye'—hence, he says, 'only by the coarse (sense faculty).'

4. Tassāti “tīhākārehī”tiādivacanassa. “Attho”ti padaṃ “veditabbo”ti pade kammaṃ. Hīti visesajotakaṃ, visesaṃ kathayissāmīti attho. Tatthāti catutthapārājike. Idhāti imasmiṃ sikkhāpade.

4. `Tassa` refers to the statement beginning with `tīhākārehi` ('by three modes'). The word `attho` is the object of the word `veditabbo`. The particle `hi` indicates a special point; the meaning is 'I will explain the special point.' `Tattha` refers to the fourth Pārājika. `Idha` refers to this training rule.

9. Ādīnampīti pisaddo sampiṇḍanattho.

9. In `ādīnampi`, the particle `pi` has the meaning of inclusion.

11. Mandasaddo jaḷatthavācakoti āha “mandattā jaḷattā”ti. Yo pana aññaṃ bhaṇatīti sambandho. “Sāmaṇerenā”ti padaṃ “vutto”ti pade kattā. Apisaddo pucchāvācako, “passitthā”ti padena yojetabbo, api passitthāti attho. “Adiṭṭhaṃ diṭṭhaṃ me”tiādivacanato aññā pūraṇakathāpi tāva atthīti dassento āha “aññā pūraṇakathā nāma hotī”ti. Appatāya ūnassa atthassa pūraṇavasena pavattā kathā pūraṇakathā. Esā pūraṇakathā [M 0.0004] nāma kāti āha “eko”tiādi. Esā hi gāme appakampi telaṃ vā pūvakhaṇḍaṃ vā passitvā vā labhitvā vā bahukaṃ katvā pūraṇavasena kathitattā pūraṇakathā nāma. Bahukāni telāni vā pūve vā passantopi labhantopi appakaṃ katvā ūnavasena kathitattā [V 1.0004] ūnakathāpi atthīti sakkā vattuṃ. Aṭṭhakathāsu pana avuttattā vīmaṃsitvā gahetabbaṃ. Bahukāya pūraṇassa atthassa ūnavasena pavattā kathā ūnakathāti viggaho kātabboti. Paṭhamaṃ.

11. He says that the word `manda` conveys the meaning of dullness, as in 'due to dullness, due to sluggishness.' The connection is 'whoever speaks otherwise.' The word `sāmaṇerena` is the agent in the word `vutto`. The word `api` is an interrogative particle and should be connected with the word `passitthā`, meaning 'have you seen?' Showing that, apart from statements like 'the unseen is seen by me,' there is also another kind of supplementary talk, he says 'there is indeed another kind of supplementary talk.' Talk that proceeds by way of supplementing an incomplete meaning is `pūraṇakathā`. What is this `pūraṇakathā`? He says 'one,' and so on. Indeed, this is called `pūraṇakathā` because, having seen or obtained even a small amount of oil or a piece of cake in a village, one speaks of it by way of supplementing it, making it much. It is also possible to say that there is `ūnakathā` (understated talk) because, even if one sees or obtains a large amount of oil or cakes, one speaks of it by way of understating it, making it little. However, since this is not mentioned in the commentaries, it should be understood after reflection. The analysis should be made that `ūnakathā` is talk that proceeds by way of understating an abundant meaning. First.

2. Omasavāda sikkhāpadaṃ

2. The Training Rule on Offensive Speech.

12. Dutiye masadhātu vijjhanatthe pavattati “omaṭṭhaṃ ummaṭṭha”ntiādīsu (saṃ. ni. aṭṭha. 1.1.21) viyāti dassento āha “omasantīti ovijjhantī”ti.

12. In the second instance, showing that the root 'mas' functions in the sense of piercing, as in passages like 'omaṭṭhaṃ ummaṭṭhaṃ' (Saṃ. Ni. Aṭṭha. 1.1.21), he said: 'omasanti' means 'ovijjhanti,' that is, 'they pierce.'

13. “Idaṃ vatthu”nti padaṃ “āharī”ti pade kammaṃ. Nanditabboti nando vaṇṇabalādi, so etassatthīti nandī. Visālāni mahantāni visāṇāni etassatthīti visālo, nandī ca so visālo ceti nandivisāloti vacanatthaṃ dasseti “nandivisālo nāmā”tiādinā. Soti nandivisālo, “āhā”ti pade kattā. Tatthevāti yuñjitaṭṭhāneyeva. Ahetukapaṭisandhikālepīti pi-saddo anuggahatthavācako, pageva dvihetuka tihetuka paṭisandhikāleti attho. “Tena cā”ti cakārassa avuttasampiṇḍanatthattā “attano kammena cā”ti atthaṃ sampiṇḍetīti āha “attano kammena cā”ti. Attanoti nandivisālassa.

13. The phrase 'idaṃ vatthu' is the object of the word 'āharī.' That which is to be enjoyed is 'nando' (joy), such as beauty, strength, etc.; one who possesses this is 'Nandī.' One who has large, great horns is 'Visālo.' He explains the meaning of the word 'Nandivisāla' as 'he is Nandī and he is Visālo,' by saying 'Nandivisālo nāma,' etc. 'So' refers to Nandivisāla; it is the subject of the word 'āhā.' 'Tattheva' means 'in the very place where it was yoked.' The particle 'pi' in 'ahetukapaṭisandhikālepi' conveys the sense of inclusion, meaning 'even at the time of a causeless rebirth-linking,' and it implies 'how much more so at the time of a two-rooted or three-rooted rebirth-linking.' Because the particle 'ca' in 'tena cā' serves to gather what has not been stated, it gathers the meaning 'and by his own kamma,' as he says, 'and by his own kamma.' 'Attano' refers to Nandivisāla.

15. Etthāti etissaṃ padabhājaniyaṃ, “āhā”ti pade ādhāro. “Yasmā”ti padaṃ vibhajitukāmo”ti pade hetu. Aṭṭhuppattiyaṃyeva “hīnenāpī”ti vatvā padabhājaniyaṃ avuttattā idaṃ vuttanti daṭṭhabbaṃ. Veṇukārajātīti vilīvakārajāti. Nesādajātīti ettha kevaṭṭajātipi saṅgahitā.

15. 'Ettha' refers to this analysis of the phrase; it is the locus of the word 'āhā.' The word 'yasmā' is the reason in the phrase 'desiring to analyze.' Although 'hīnenāpi' is stated in the origin story itself, since its analysis is not given there, this should be understood as stated here. 'Veṇukārajāti' means the bamboo-worker caste. 'Nesādajāti' here also includes the fisherman caste.

Pu vuccati karīsaṃ, taṃ kusati apanetīti pukkuso. Pupphaṃ vuccati karīsaṃ, kusumaṃ vā, taṃ chaḍḍetīti pupphachaḍḍako.

'Pu' is called excrement; one who cleanses it away is a 'pukkuso.' 'Puppha' is called excrement, or a flower; one who discards it is a 'pupphachaḍḍako.'

Kuṭati [M 0.0005] chindatīti koṭṭho, soyeva koṭṭhako. Yakārabhakāre ekato yojetvā “yabhā”ti yo akkoso atthi, eso hīno nāma akkosoti yojanā.

One who cuts and splits is called 'koṭṭho,' and that very same is 'koṭṭhako.' Combining the letters 'ya' and 'bha' into 'yabhā,' whatever insult there is, that is a base insult—this is the construction.

16. Sabbapadesūti nāmādīsu sabbapadesu. Etthāti imasmiṃ sikkhāpade. Alikanti asaccaṃ, micchāvācanti sambandho. Yopi vadatīti yojanā.

16. 'Sabbapadesu' means in all instances, such as names, etc. 'Ettha' refers to this training rule. 'Alika' means untrue; it is connected with 'micchāvācā' (wrong speech). 'Yopi vadati' is the construction.

26. Pariharitvāti [V 1.0005] parimukhaṃ kathanaṃ apanetvā. Davaṃ parihāsaṃ kāmetīti davakāmo, tassa bhāvo davakamyaṃ, taṃyeva davakamyatā. Anupasampannanti ettha akārassa sadisatthamaggahetvā aññatthova gahetabboti āha “ṭhapetvā bhikkhu”ntiādi. Yadi hi sadisattho bhaveyya, sāmaṇerova anupasampanno nāma siyā saṇṭhānena ca purisabhāvena ca sadisattā, tasmā aññatthova gahetabboti daṭṭhabbaṃ. Sabbasattāti ettha sabbasaddo anavasesattho manusse upādāya vacanatthajānanājānanapakatikānaṃ sabbasattānampi gahitattā.

26. 'Pariharitvā' means 'having removed face-to-face conversation.' One who desires 'dava' (frivolity, jest) is 'davakāmo'; the state of that is 'davakamya,' and that itself is 'davakamyatā.' Regarding 'anupasampanna,' here the prefix 'a-' should not be taken as having a similar meaning, but should be understood otherwise, as he says, 'except for a monk,' etc. For if it had a similar meaning, only a novice would be called 'anupasampanna' because of similarity in form and male nature. Therefore, it should be understood that it must be taken otherwise. Regarding 'sabbasatta,' here the word 'sabba' has the meaning of 'without remainder,' because it includes humans and all beings, whether they are naturally capable of understanding the meaning of speech or not.

35. Atthapurekkhāro nāmāti veditabboti sambandho. Sikkhāpadamapekkhiya napuṃsakaliṅgavasena “kiriya”ntiādi vuttaṃ. Āpattimapekkhiya itthiliṅgavasena “kiriyā”tiādi vuttaṃ. Vajjakammasaddā sikkhāpadamapekkhantāpi āpatti, mapekkhantāpi niyatanapuṃsakaliṅgattā napuṃsakāyeva, tasmā te dve āpattiṭṭhāne na vuttāti daṭṭhabbanti. Dutiyaṃ.

35. The connection is that 'atthapurekkhāro nāma' is to be understood. With reference to the training rule, terms like 'kiriya' are stated in the neuter gender. With reference to the offense, terms like 'kiriyā' are stated in the feminine gender. The words for blameworthy actions, whether with reference to the training rule or with reference to the offense, are only neuter due to their fixed neuter gender; therefore, it should be understood that those two are not stated in the sections on offenses. The second.

3. Pesuññasikkhāpadaṃ

3. The Training Rule on Slander

36. Tatiye “jātabhaṇḍanāna”nti vattabbe agyāhitotiādīsu viya visesanaparanipātavasena “bhaṇḍanajātāna”nti vuttanti āha “sañjātabhaṇḍanāna”nti. “Pubbabhāgo”ti vatvā tassa sarūpaṃ dasseti “iminā ca iminā cā”tiādinā. Viruddhaṃ vadati etenāti vivādo, viggāhikakathā[M 0.0006], taṃ āpannāti vivādāpannā, tesaṃ. Pisati sañcuṇṇetīti pisuṇo, puggalo, tassa idanti pesuññaṃ, vacananti atthaṃ dassento āha “pesuññanti pisuṇavāca”nti.

36. In the third, where 'jātabhaṇḍanānaṃ' should be said, it is stated as 'bhaṇḍanajātānaṃ' due to the post-positioning of the qualifier, as in 'agyāhitoti,' etc.; hence he says 'sañjātabhaṇḍanānaṃ.' Having stated 'pubbabhāgo,' he shows its form with 'iminā ca iminā ca,' etc. 'One speaks contrary by this' (`viruddhaṃ vadati etena`) is 'vivādo' (dispute), which is contentious talk; 'fallen into that' (`taṃ āpannā`) means 'vivādāpannā' (those fallen into dispute). 'One who crushes and grinds' (`pisati sañcuṇṇeti`) is 'pisuṇo,' a person; 'this of his' (`tassa idaṃ`) is 'pesuññaṃ,' meaning speech—thus, showing the meaning, he says, 'pesuññaṃ means slanderous speech' (`pisuṇavācā`).

37. Bhikkhupesuññeti bhikkhūnaṃ santikaṃ upasaṃhaṭe pesuññavacaneti chaṭṭhīsamāso.

37. 'Bhikkhupesuñña' is a sixth-case compound meaning 'in slanderous speech brought to the presence of monks.'

38. “Disvā”ti padaṃ “bhaṇantassā”ti pade pubbakālakiriyā, dassanaṃ hutvāti attho. Tatiyaṃ.

38. The word 'disvā' is an action of prior time in relation to the word 'bhaṇantassa'; the meaning is 'having seen.' The third.

4. Padasodhammasikkhāpadaṃ

4. The Training Rule on Reciting the Dhamma Word by Word

44. Catutthe paṭimukhaṃ ādarena suṇantīti patissā, na patissā appatissāti dassento āha “appatissavā”ti.

44. In the fourth, showing that 'patissā' means 'they listen respectfully face-to-face,' and that 'appatissā' is 'not patissā,' he said 'appatissavā' (non-compliant).

45. “Padaso”ti [V 1.0006] ettha so-paccayo vicchatthavācakoti āha “padaṃ pada”nti. Tatthāti tesu catubbidhesu. Padaṃ nāma idha atthajotakaṃ vā vibhatyantaṃ vā na hoti, atha kho lokiyehi lakkhito gāthāya catutthaṃso pādova adhippetoti āha “padanti eko gāthāpādo”ti. Anu pacchā vuttapadattā dutiyapādo anupadaṃ nāma. Anu sadisaṃ byañjanaṃ anubyañjananti atthaṃ dasseti “anubyañjana”ntiādinā. Byañjanasaddo pada-pariyāyo. Yaṃkiñci padaṃ anubyañjanaṃ nāma na hoti, purimapadena pana sadisaṃ pacchimapadameva anubyañjanaṃ nāma.

45. Here, regarding 'padaso,' he says that the suffix '-so' expresses distribution, meaning 'padaṃ padaṃ' (word by word). 'Tattha' refers to those four kinds. Here, 'pada' does not mean a meaning-illuminating term or an inflected ending; rather, what is intended is a 'pāda,' the fourth part of a verse as understood by worldly people; hence he says, 'a pada is one quarter of a verse.' Because it is a 'pada' stated after (`anu pacchā`), the second quarter is called 'anupada.' He explains the meaning of 'anubyañjana' as 'a similar (`anu sadisaṃ`) letter (`byañjana`),' by 'anubyañjana,' etc. The word 'byañjana' is a synonym for 'pada.' Not just any 'pada' is called 'anubyañjana'; rather, only a subsequent 'pada' that resembles the preceding 'pada' is called 'anubyañjana.'

Vācento hutvā niṭṭhāpetīti yojanā. “Ekamekaṃ pada”nti padaṃ “niṭṭhāpetī”ti pade kāritakammaṃ. “Therenā”ti padaṃ “vutte”ti pade kattā, “ekato”ti pade sahattho. Sāmaṇero apāpuṇitvā bhaṇatīti sambandho. Mattamevāti ettha evasaddo mattasaddassa avadhāraṇatthaṃ dasseti, tena pakāraṃ paṭikkhipati. “Anicca”nti ca “aniccā”ti ca dvinnaṃ padānaṃ satipi liṅgavisesatte anubyañjanattā āpattimokkho natthīti āha “anubyañjanagaṇanāya pācittiyā”ti.

'Having caused to recite, he finishes'—this is the construction. The phrase 'ekamekaṃ padaṃ' is the object of the causative action of the word 'niṭṭhāpeti.' The word 'therena' is the agent of the word 'vutte,' and 'ekato' has the meaning of 'together with.' The connection is that the novice recites without having attained mastery. Here, in 'mattameva,' the word 'eva' shows the specifying meaning of the word 'matta,' thereby rejecting the manner. Regarding 'anicca' and 'aniccā,' although there is a difference in gender between the two words, because they are 'anubyañjana' (similar words), there is no release from offense; hence he says, 'there is a pācittiya by counting the anubyañjana.'

Brahmajālādīnīti [M 0.0007] ettha ādisaddena sāmaññaphalasuttādīni dīghasuttāni (dī. ni. 1.150 ādayo) saṅgahitāni. Casaddena oghataraṇasuttādīni saṃyuttasuttāni (saṃ. ni. 1.1) ca cittapariyādānasuttādīni aṅguttarasuttāni (a. ni. 1.2 ādayo) ca saṅgahitāni. Soti devatābhāsito veditabboti yojanā.

Here, in 'Brahmajālādīni,' the word 'ādi' includes the long discourses such as the Sāmaññaphala Sutta (Dī. Ni. 1.150, etc.). And by the particle 'ca,' the connected discourses like the Oghataraṇa Sutta (Saṃ. Ni. 1.1) and the numerical discourses like the Cittapariyādāna Sutta (A. Ni. 1.2, etc.) are included. 'So' should be understood as spoken by a deity—this is the construction.

Kiñcāpi vadatīti sambandho. Ettha ca kiñcāpisaddo garahatthavācako, panasaddo anuggahatthavācako. Meṇḍakamilindapañhesūti meṇḍakapañhe ca milindapañhe ca. Yanti suttaṃ vuttanti sambandho. Ārammaṇakathā buddhikakathā daṇḍakakathā ñāṇavatthukathāti yojetabbaṃ peyyālavasena vuttattā. Imāyo pakaraṇāni nāmāti vadanti. Mahāpaccariyādīsu vatvā pariggahitoti yojanā. Yanti suttaṃ.

'Kiñcāpi vadati' is the connection. Here, the word 'kiñcāpi' conveys the sense of censure, while the word 'pana' conveys the sense of favor. 'Meṇḍakamilindapañhesu' means 'in the Meṇḍaka Question and the Milinda Question.' The connection is 'which sutta is stated.' The topics of discussion—'ārammaṇakathā,' 'buddhikakathā,' 'daṇḍakakathā,' and 'ñāṇavatthukathā'—should be connected, as they are stated by way of a repetitive passage. They say these are called 'pakaraṇas' (treatises). The construction is that having been stated in the Mahāpaccarī, etc., they are included. 'Yaṃ' refers to the sutta.

48. Tatrāti “ekato uddisāpento”ti vacane. Uddisāpentīti ācariyaṃ desāpenti bahukattāramapekkhiya bahuvacanavasena vuttaṃ. Tehīti upasampannānupasampannehi. Dvepīti upasampanno ca anupasampanno ca.

48. 'Tatra' refers to the expression 'causing to recite together.' 'Uddisāpenti' means they cause the teacher to teach; it is stated in the plural with reference to multiple agents. 'Tehi' refers to the ordained and the unordained. 'Dvepi' means both an ordained person and an unordained person.

Upacāranti [V 1.0007] dvādasahatthūpacāraṃ. Yesanti bhikkhūnaṃ. Palāyanakaganthanti parivajjetvā gacchantaṃ pakaraṇaṃ. Sāmaṇero gaṇhātīti yojanā.

'Upacāra' means an approach of twelve cubits. 'Yesaṃ' refers to the monks. 'Palāyanakagantha' refers to a treatise that proceeds by avoiding. The construction is 'the novice takes it'.

Opātetīti avapāteti, gaḷitāpetīti attho. Suttepīti veyyākaraṇasuttepi. Tanti yebhuyyena paguṇaganthaṃ. Parisaṅkamānanti sārajjamānaṃ. Yaṃ pana vacanaṃ vuttanti sambandho. Kiriyasamuṭṭhānattāti imassa sikkhāpadassa kiriyasamuṭṭhānattāti. Catutthaṃ.

'Opāteti' means 'avapāteti'; the meaning is 'to cause to fall.' 'Suttepi' means 'even in the grammar suttas.' 'Tanti' mostly refers to a well-mastered text. 'Parisaṅkamāna' means 'being embarrassed.' The connection is 'whatever statement was made.' 'Kiriyasamuṭṭhānattā' means 'because this training rule arises from an action.' The fourth section.

5. Sahaseyyasikkhāpadaṃ

5. The Training Rule on Sharing a Sleeping Place

49. Pañcame muṭṭhā sati etesanti muṭṭhassatī. Natthi sampajānaṃ etesanti asampajānā. Bhavaṅgotiṇṇakāleti niddokkamanakāle.

49. In the fifth, 'muṭṭhassatī' means those whose mindfulness is confused. 'Asampajānā' means those who lack clear comprehension. 'The time of descending into the life-continuum' refers to the time of falling asleep.

50. “Pakatiyā”ti padaṃ “dentī”ti pade visesanaṃ. Te bhikkhū dentīti sambandho. “Gāravenā”ti padañca “sikkhākāmatāyā”ti padañca “dentī”ti pade hetu. Sīsassa upadhānaṃ ussīsaṃ, tassa karīyate ussīsakaraṇaṃ[M 0.0008], taṃyeva attho payojanaṃ ussīsakaraṇattho, tadatthāya. Tatrāti purimavacanāpekkhaṃ, “sikkhākāmatāyā”ti vacaneti attho. Nidassananti seso. Atha vā sikkhākāmatāyāti paccatte bhummavacanaṃ. “Idampissa hoti sīlasmi”ntiādīsu (dī. ni. 1.195 ādayo) viya. Idampi sikkhākāmatāya ayaṃ sikkhākāmatā sikkhākāmabhāvo hotīti yojanā. Esa nayo “tatridaṃ samantapāsādikāya samantapāsādikattasmi”ntiādīsupi. Bhikkhū khipantīti yojanā. Tanti āyasmantaṃ rāhulaṃ. Athāti khipanato pacchā. Idanti vatthu. Sammuñcanikacavarachaḍḍanakāni sandhāya vuttaṃ. Tenāyasmatā rāhulena pātitaṃ nu khoti yojanā. So panāyasmā gacchatīti sambandho. Aparibhogā aññesanti aññehi na paribhuñjitabbā.

50. The word 'pakatiyā' qualifies the word 'dentī.' The connection is 'those monks give.' The words 'gāravena' and 'sikkhākāmatāya' are the reasons for the word 'dentī.' 'Ussīsaṃ' is a support for the head, and 'ussīsakaraṇaṃ' is the making of it; 'ussīsakaraṇattho' means its purpose is just that, for that aim. 'Tatra' refers to the previous statement, meaning the statement 'sikkhākāmatāya.' 'As an illustration' is to be supplied. Alternatively, 'sikkhākāmatāya' is a locative in an individual sense, as in 'this is for him in terms of virtue,' etc. (Dī. Ni. 1.195 ff.). Here too, the connection is: 'sikkhākāmatāya' means this desire for training is the state of wanting to train. This same method applies to 'therein, this is in the Samantapāsādikā in the sense of its being the Samantapāsādikā,' etc. The connection is 'the monks throw.' 'Taṃ' refers to the venerable Rāhula. 'Atha' means after throwing. 'Idaṃ' refers to the object. It is said with reference to sweeping-brooms, rubbish, and things to be discarded. Therefore, the connection is 'was it dropped by the venerable Rāhula or not?' The connection is 'but that venerable one goes.' 'Aparibhogā aññesaṃ' means they should not be used by others.

51. Hīti saccaṃ, yasmā vā. Sayanaṃ seyyā, kāyapasāraṇakiriyā, sayanti etthāti seyyā, mañcapīṭhādi. Tadubhayampi ekasesena vā sāmaññaniddesena vā ekato katvā “sahaseyya”nti vuttanti dassento āha “seyyā”tiādi. Tatthāti dvīsu seyyāsu. Tasmāti yasmā dve seyyā dassitā, tasmā. “Sabbacchannā”tiādinā lakkhaṇaṃ vuttanti yojanā. Pākaṭavohāranti loke viditaṃ vacanaṃ. Dussakuṭiyanti dussena chāditakuṭiyaṃ. Aṭṭhakathāsu yathāvutte pañcavidhacchadaneyeva gayhamāne ko dosoti āha “pañcavidhacchadaneyevā”tiādi. Yaṃ pana [V 1.0008] senāsanaṃ parikkhittanti sambandho. Pākārena vāti iṭṭhakasilādārunā vā. Aññena vāti kilañjādinā vā. Vatthenapīti pisaddo pageva iṭṭhakādināti dasseti. Yassāti senāsanasaṅkhātāya seyyāya. Uparīti vā samantatoti vā yojanā. Ekena dvārena pavisitvā sabbapāsādassa vaḷañjitabbataṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ “ekūpacāro”ti. Satagabbhaṃ vā catussālaṃ ekūpacāraṃ hotīti sambandho. Tanti senāsanasaṅkhātaṃ seyyaṃ.

51. 'Hī' means 'indeed,' or 'because.' 'Sayanaṃ' is 'seyyā,' the act of stretching out the body; 'seyyā' is also that wherein one lies down, such as a couch or chair. Showing that both are combined, either by ellipsis or by a general designation, and called 'sahaseyya,' he says 'seyyā,' and so on. 'Tatra' refers to the two types of sleeping places. 'Tasmā' means 'because two sleeping places are shown, therefore.' The connection is that the characteristic is stated by 'sabbacchannā,' and so on. 'Pākaṭavohāra' means a term known in the world. 'Dussakuṭi' means a hut covered with cloth. In the commentaries, if only the fivefold covering as stated is taken, what fault is there? Therefore, he says, 'only the fivefold covering,' etc. The connection is 'however, the dwelling that is enclosed.' 'By a wall' means with bricks, stones, or wood. 'Or by another' means with mats, etc. The particle 'pi' in 'even with cloth' indicates 'let alone bricks and so on.' 'Yassa' refers to the sleeping place designated as a dwelling. The connection is 'above' or 'all around.' 'Ekūpacāro' is said with reference to the entire palace being traversable after entering through a single door. The connection is that a hundred-roomed building or a four-gabled hall has a single approach. 'Taṃ' refers to the sleeping place designated as a dwelling.

Tatthāti senāsanasaṅkhātāyaṃ seyyāyaṃ. Sambahulā sāmaṇerā sace honti, eko bhikkhu sace hotīti yojanā. “Sāmaṇerā”ti [M 0.0009] idaṃ paccāsannavasena vuttaṃ, upalakkhaṇavasena vā aññehipi sahaseyyānaṃ āpattisambhavato. Teti sāmaṇerā. Sabbesanti bhikkhūnaṃ. Tassāti sāmaṇerassa. Eseva nayoti eso eva nayo, na añño nayoti attho. Atha vā eseva nayoti eso iva nayo, eso etādiso nayo iva ayaṃ nayo daṭṭhabboti attho.

'Tatra' means in the sleeping place designated as a dwelling. The connection is: if there are many novice monks, and if there is one monk. 'Sāmaṇerā'—this is said with reference to the immediate case, or by way of illustration, since an offense of sharing a sleeping place can arise even with others. 'Te' refers to the novice monks. 'Sabbesaṃ' refers to the monks. 'Tassa' refers to the novice monk. 'Eseva nayo' means this is the only method; there is no other method. Or alternatively, 'eseva nayo' means this is like the method; this method should be seen as being of this kind.

Api cāti ekaṃsena. Etthāti imasmiṃ sikkhāpade. Catukkanti ekāvāsaekānupasampannaṃ, ekāvāsanānupasampannaṃ, nānāvāsaekānupasampannaṃ, nānāvāsanānupasampannanti catusamūhaṃ, catuparimāṇaṃ vā. Yoti bhikkhu. Hisaddo vitthārajotako, taṃ vacanaṃ vitthārayissāmīti attho, vitthāro mayā vuccateti vā. Devasikanti divase divase. Ṇikapaccayo hi vicchatthavācako. Yopi sahaseyyaṃ kappeti, tassāpi āpattīti yojetabbo. Tatrāti “tiracchānagatenāpī”ti vacane.

'Api ca' means definitively. 'Ettha' means in this training rule. 'Catukkaṃ' refers to a fourfold set: one residence and one unordained person, one residence and many unordained persons, many residences and one unordained person, many residences and many unordained persons—this group of four, or measure of four. 'Yo' means a monk. The word 'hi' is an indicator of elaboration, meaning 'I will elaborate on that statement,' or 'the elaboration is spoken by me.' 'Devasikaṃ' means day by day. The suffix 'ṇika' indeed indicates distribution. It should be connected that 'even for one who arranges a shared sleeping place, there is an offense.' 'Tatra' refers to the phrase 'even with an animal.'

“Apadānaṃ ahimacchā, dvipadānañca kukkuṭī;

Catuppadānaṃ majjārī, vatthu pārājikassimā”ti. (pārā. aṭṭha. 1.55);

Of the footless, the snake and fish; of the two-footed, the hen; of the four-footed, the female cat—these are the bases for a pārājika offense.

Imaṃ gāthaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ “vuttanayenevā”ti. Tasmāti yasmā veditabbo, tasmā. Godhāti kuṇḍo. Biḷāloti ākhubhujo. Maṅgusoti nakulo.

With reference to this verse, it was said 'just as stated in the method.' 'Tasmā' means 'because it should be understood, therefore.' 'Godhā' means a monitor lizard. 'Biḷāla' means a cat (mouse-eater). 'Maṅgusa' means a mongoose.

Asambaddhabhittikassa katapāsādassāti yojanā. Tulāti ettha tulā nāma thambhāna, mupari dakkhiṇuttaravitthāravasena ṭhapito dāruviseso thalati thambhesu patiṭṭhātīti katvā. Tā pana heṭṭhimaparicchedato tisso, ukkaṭṭhaparicchedena pana pañcasattanavādayo. Nānūpacāre pāsādeti sambandho.

The connection is 'for a palace built with unconnected walls.' Here, 'tulā' refers to a specific type of wood placed horizontally over the pillars, extending from south to north, because it rests (thalati) or is established (patiṭṭhāti) on the pillars. At the lower section, there are three of them, but at the higher section, there may be five, seven, nine, etc. The connection is 'in a palace with various approaches.'

Vāḷasaṅghāṭādīsūti [V 1.0009] vāḷarūpaṃ dassetvā katesu saṅghāṭādīsu. Ādisaddena tulaṃ saṅgaṇhāti. Ettha ca saṅghāṭo nāma tulāna, mupari pubbapacchimāyāmavasena ṭhapito kaṭṭhaviseso sammā ghaṭenti ettha gopānasyādayoti [M 0.0010] katvā. Te pana tayo honti. Nibbakosabbhantareti chadanakoṭiabbhantare. Parimaṇḍalaṃ vā caturassaṃ vā senāsanaṃ hotīti sambandho. Tatrāti tasmiṃ senāsane. Aparicchinno gabbhassa upacāro etesanti aparicchinnagabbhūpacārā sabbagabbhā, te pavisantīti attho. Nipannānaṃ bhikkhūnanti yojanā. Tatrāti tasmiṃ pamukhe. Pamukhassa sabbacchannattā, sabbaparicchannattā ca āpattiṃ karotīti yojanā. Nanu pamukhe channameva atthi, no paricchannanti āha “gabbhaparikkhepo”tiādi. Hīti saccaṃ.

'In beast-shaped rafters, etc.' refers to rafters, etc., made showing the shape of a beast of prey. The word 'ādi' includes the crossbeams. Here, 'saṅghāṭa' is a particular piece of wood placed horizontally over the crossbeams, extending from east to west, because roof-rafters, etc., are properly joined there. There are three of these. 'Nibbakosabbhantare' means inside the edge of the roof. The connection is that the dwelling may be round or square. 'Tatra' means in that dwelling. 'Aparicchinnagabbhūpacārā' means those for whom the approach to the inner chamber is not delimited; the meaning is that they enter all inner chambers. The connection is 'for the monks lying down.' 'Tatra' means in that porch. The connection is that because the porch is entirely roofed and entirely enclosed, one commits an offense. One might object: 'But is the porch not only roofed, and not enclosed?' To this, he says: 'the enclosure of the interior,' etc. 'Hī' means 'indeed'.

Yaṃ pana andhakaṭṭhakathāyaṃ vuttanti sambandho. Jagatīti pathaviyā ca mandirālindavatthussa ca nāmametaṃ. Idha pana mandirālindavatthusaṅkhātā bhūbhedā gahitā. Tatthāti andhakaṭṭhakathāyaṃ. Kasmā pāḷiyā na sametīti āha “dasahatthubbedhāpī”tiādi. Hīti yasmā. Tatthāti andhakaṭṭhakathāyaṃ. Yepi mahāpāsādā hontīti yojanā. Tesupīti mahāpāsādesupi.

The connection is 'what is stated in the Andhakaṭṭhakathā.' 'Jagatī' is a name for both the earth and the ground of a building's terrace. Here, however, it refers to a type of ground designated as the ground of a building's terrace. 'Tatra' means in the Andhakaṭṭhakathā. 'Why does it not agree with the Pāḷi?' He says: 'even if it is ten cubits high,' etc. 'Hī' means 'because.' 'Tatra' means in the Andhakaṭṭhakathā. The connection is 'even those great palaces that exist.' 'Tesupi' means 'even in great palaces.'

Sudhāchadanamaṇḍapassāti ettha “sudhā”ti idaṃ upalakkhaṇavasena vuttaṃ yena kenaci chadanamaṇḍapassāpi adhippetattā. Maṇḍaṃ vuccati sūriyarasmi, taṃ pāti rakkhati, tato vā jananti maṇḍapaṃ. Nanu ekūpacāraṃ hoti pākārassa chiddattāti āha “na hī”tiādi. Hīti saccaṃ, yasmā vā. Vaḷañjanatthāya evāti evakāro yojetabbo. Tenāha “na vaḷañjanūpacchedanatthāyā”ti. Atha vā “saddantaratthāpohanena saddo atthaṃ vadatī”ti (udā. aṭṭha. 1; dī. ni. ṭi. 1.1; ma. ni. ṭī. 1.mūlapariyāyasuttavaṇṇanā; saṃ. ni. ṭī. 1.1.oghataraṇasuttavaṇṇanā; a. ni. ṭī. 1.1.rupādivaggavaṇṇanā) vuttattā “na vaḷañjanūpacchedanatthāyā”ti vuttaṃ. Kavāṭanti ettha dvārameva adhippetaṃ pariyāyena vuttattā, asati ca dvāre kavāṭassābhāvato. Saṃvaraṇavivaraṇakāle kavati saddaṃ karotīti kavāṭaṃ.

In "sudhāchadanamaṇḍapassa" (of a pavilion covered with plaster), the word "sudhā" (plaster) is used by way of indication, because any kind of roofed pavilion is intended. "Maṇḍa" is said to be the sun's rays; it protects (pāti) from them, or from that (tato) they call it a "maṇḍapa" (pavilion). "But is it not a single enclosure (ekūpacāraṃ) because of the gap in the wall?" To this, he says, "No, indeed," etc. "Hī" means indeed, or because. The particle "eva" should be connected to mean "only for traversing." Hence he says, "not for the purpose of cutting off traversing." Alternatively, because it is said, "a word conveys its meaning by the exclusion of another word's meaning" (Udāna Aṭṭhakathā 1; Dīgha Nikāya Ṭīkā 1.1; Majjhima Nikāya Ṭīkā 1, Mūlapariyāyasuttavaṇṇanā; Saṃyutta Nikāya Ṭīkā 1.1, Oghataraṇasuttavaṇṇanā; Aṅguttara Nikāya Ṭīkā 1.1, Rūpādivaggavaṇṇanā), it is said, "not for the purpose of cutting off traversing." Here, by "kavāṭa" (door-panel), a door itself is intended, being mentioned synonymously; moreover, without a door, there is no door-panel. At the time of closing or opening, it makes a sound (kavati), hence it is called "kavāṭa."

Tatrāti “ekūpacārattā”ti vacane. Yassāti paravādino. Anuyogo siyāti yojanā. Idhāti imasmiṃ sahaseyyasikkhāpade, vuttanti sambandho. Tatthāti pihitadvāre gabbhe. Soti paravādī. Sabbacchannattā āpatti iti vutteti yojanā. Eseva nayo [M 0.0011] “sabbaparicchannatā na hotī”ti etthāpi. Paccāgamissatīti pati āgamissati, puna āgamissatīti attho.

"Tatra" (there) refers to the phrase "because of a single enclosure." "Yassa" (whose) refers to the opponent. The construction is "an inquiry may arise." "Idha" (here) means in this training rule on sharing a sleeping place; the connection is with "vuttaṃ" (it is stated). "Tatra" (there) means in a chamber with a closed door. "So" (he) refers to the opponent. The construction is: "it is stated that there is an offense because of being entirely covered." This same method also applies here to "it is not entirely enclosed." "Paccāgamissati" (he will return) means "pati āgamissati" (he will come back), that is, "he will come again."

Byañjanamattenevāti “sabbacchannā”tiādiakkharapadamatteneva, na atthavasena. “Evañca satī”ti [V 1.0010] iminā abyāpitadosaṃ dasseti. Tatoti anāpattito, parihāyeyyāti sambandho. Tasmāti yasmā aniyatesu vuttaṃ, tasmā. Tatthāti aniyatesu. Idhāpīti imasmiṃ sikkhāpadepi. Yaṃ yanti senāsanaṃ. Sabbatthāti sabbesu senāsanesu, sahaseyyāpatti hotīti sambandho.

"Byañjanamatteneva" (by merely the phrasing) means just by the letters and words such as "completely covered," not by way of the meaning. By "evaṃ ca sati" (and this being so), he points out the fault of non-inclusiveness. "Tato" means "from non-offense"; the connection is with "parihāyeyya" (it would be lost). "Tasmā" (therefore) means: because it was stated regarding the indefinite cases, therefore. "Tatra" (there) refers to the indefinite cases. "Idhāpi" (here too) means in this training rule as well. "Yaṃ yaṃ" (whatever) refers to the lodging. "Sabbattha" (everywhere) means in all lodgings; the connection is "there is an offense of sharing a sleeping place."

53. Dvīsu aṭṭhakathāvādesu mahāaṭṭhakathāvādova yuttoti so pacchā vutto.

53. Among the two commentary traditions, the Great Commentary tradition is the appropriate one, and so it was stated later.

Imināpīti senambamaṇḍapenāpi. Etanti jagatiyā aparikkhittataṃ. Yathāti yaṃsaddattho tatiyantanipāto, yena senambamaṇḍapenāti atthoti. Pañcamaṃ.

"Imināpi" (by this too) means even by a pavilion of white cloth. "Etaṃ" (this) refers to its unenclosed nature on the ground. "Yathā" (as) is a particle in the instrumental case with the meaning of the word "yaṃ" (which); the meaning is "by which pavilion of white cloth." The fifth.

6. Dutiyasahaseyyasikkhāpadaṃ

6. The Second Training Rule on Sharing a Sleeping Place.

55. Chaṭṭhe āgantukā vasanti etthāti āvasatho, āvasatho ca so agārañceti āvasathāgāranti dassento āha “āgantukānaṃ vasanāgāra”nti. Manussānaṃ santikā vacanaṃ sutvāti vacanaseso yojetabbo. Sāṭakanti uttarasāṭakaṃ, nivatthavatthantipi vadanti. Accāgammāti tvāpaccayantapadassa sambandhaṃ dassetumāha “pavatto”ti. Yathā omasavādasikkhāpade akkosetukāmatāya khattiyaṃ “caṇḍālo”ti vadato alikaṃ bhaṇatopi musāvādasikkhāpadena anāpatti, omasavādasikkhāpadeneva āpatti, evamidhāpi mātugāmena saha sayato paṭhamasahaseyyasikkhāpadena anāpatti, imināva āpattīti daṭṭhabbanti. Chaṭṭhaṃ.

55. In the sixth [rule]: 'Here guests stay,' thus it is an āvasatha (lodging); and since that lodging is a house (agāra), it is an āvasathāgāra (guest-house). Explaining this, he says, 'a house for guests to stay.' The remainder of the phrase, 'having heard the speech from people,' should be supplied. By "sāṭaka" is meant an upper robe; some also say 'a lower garment.' To show the connection of the word ending in the gerund suffix, "accāgamma" (having transgressed), he says, "pavatto" (having proceeded). Just as in the training rule on abusive speech, when one intending to insult a khattiya calls him a 'caṇḍāla,' even though speaking falsely, there is no offense under the training rule on false speech but only under the training rule on abusive speech; so too here, if one sleeps together with a woman, there is no offense under the first training rule on sharing a sleeping place, but only under this rule. This should be understood. The sixth.

7. Dhammadesanāsikkhāpadaṃ

7. The Training Rule on Teaching the Dhamma.

60. Sattame [M 0.0012] mahādvāreti bahi ṭhite mahādvāre. Āgamma, pavisitvā vā vasanaṭṭhānattā ovarako āvasatho nāmāti āha “ovarakadvāre”ti. Suniggatenāti suṭṭhu bahi nikkhamitvā gatena saddena. “Aññātu”nti padassa “na ñātu”nti atthaṃ paṭikkhipanto āha “ājānitu”nti. Iminā nakāravikāro aiti nipāto na hoti, āiti upasaggoti pana dasseti. “Viññunā purisenā”ti ettakameva avatvā “purisaviggahenā”ti vadanto manussapurisaviggahaṃ gahetvā ṭhitena yakkhena petena tiracchānagatena saddhiṃ ṭhitāya mātugāmassa desetuṃ na vaṭṭatīti dasseti. Na yakkhenāti yakkhena saddhiṃ ṭhitāya mātugāmassa desetuṃ na vaṭṭatīti yojanā. Esa nayo “na petena, na tiracchānagatenā”ti etthāpi.

60. In the seventh [rule], "mahādvāre" (at the great gate) means at the great gate standing outside. "Āgamma" means having approached, or having entered. Because it is a place for staying, an inner chamber (ovarako) is called a lodging (āvasatho); thus he says, "ovarakadvāre" (at the door of the inner chamber). By "suniggatena" is meant 'with a sound that has gone out well from outside.' Rejecting the meaning 'not to know' for the word "aññātuṃ," he says "ājānituṃ" (to know fully). By this, he shows that the 'a' is not the negative particle, but is the prefix 'ā'. Without saying only 'by a wise man,' by saying 'by a male form,' he shows that it is not proper to teach a woman who is standing together with a yakkha, a peta, or an animal that has taken the form of a human male. The construction 'not with a yakkha' means that it is not proper to teach a woman who is standing together with a yakkha. The same method applies to 'not with a peta' and 'not with an animal'.

66. Chappañcavācāhīti [V 1.0011] ettha “pañcā”ti vācāsiliṭṭhavasena vuttaṃ kassaci payojanassābhāvā. Tatthāti “chappañcavācāhī”ti pade. Eko gāthāpādo ekā vācāti vadanto cuṇṇiye vibhatyantaṃ ekaṃ padaṃ ekā vācā nāmāti dasseti, atthajotakapadaṃ vā vākyapadaṃ vā na gahetabbaṃ. “Ekaṃ padaṃ pāḷito, pañca aṭṭhakathāto”ti iminā “dve padāni pāḷito, cattāri aṭṭhakathāto”tiādinayopi gahetabbo. Chapadānatikkamoyeva hi pamāṇaṃ. Tasminti ettha sati vibhattivipallāse liṅgassāpi vipallāso hoti “tasmi”nti pulliṅgena vuttattā. Sati ca vibhattivipallāse “tassā”ti itthiliṅgabhāvena pavattā. “Mātugāmassā”ti niyatapulliṅgāpekkhanassa asambhavato atthavasena “ekissā”ti itthiliṅgabhāvena vuttaṃ. Iminā bhedaliṅganissito visesanavisesyopi atthīti dasseti. Tumhākanti niddhāraṇasamudāyo. “Suṇāthā”ti avatvā ābhogopi vaṭṭatīti āha “paṭhama”ntiādi. Paṭhamanti ca paṭhamameva. Tena vuttaṃ “na pacchā”ti. Puṭṭho hutvā bhikkhu kathetīti yojanāti. Sattamaṃ.

66. Here, in 'by six or five words' (chappañcavācāhi), 'five' is stated for the sake of euphony, as there is no particular purpose for it. There, in the phrase 'by six or five words'. Saying that one line of a verse is one utterance, he shows that in prose, a single inflected word is called one utterance; a word that illuminates meaning or a phrase should not be taken. By 'one word from the Pāli, five from the commentary,' the method of 'two words from the Pāli, four from the commentary,' etc., should also be understood. For indeed, exceeding six words is the measure. Here, in "tasmiṃ," when there is an inversion of case ending, there is also an inversion of gender, because it is stated in the masculine. And when there is an inversion of case ending, it proceeds as "tassā" in the feminine gender. Since the expectation of a fixed masculine gender for "mātugāmassa" is impossible, it is stated as "ekissā" in the feminine gender according to the meaning. By this, he shows that there is also a qualifier-qualified relationship dependent on a difference of gender. "Tumhākaṃ" is a determinative aggregate. Without saying 'Listen!' (suṇātha), an intimation is also proper; thus he says 'first,' etc. And 'first' means indeed first. Therefore, it is said, 'not later.' The construction is that a bhikkhu speaks after being asked. The seventh.

8. Bhūtārocanasikkhāpadaṃ

8. The Training Rule on Declaring What is Actual.

67. Aṭṭhame [M 0.0013] tatthāti catutthapārājikasikkhāpade. Idhāti bhūtārocanasikkhāpade. Hīti saccaṃ, yasmā vā. Payuttavācāti paccayehi yuttā vācā. Tathāti tato guṇārocanakāraṇā, ariyā sādiyiṃsūti yojanā.

67. In the eighth [rule], 'there' refers to the fourth Pārājika training rule. 'Here' refers to the training rule on declaring what is actual. "Hi" means 'truly' or 'because'. By "payuttavācā" is meant 'speech connected with conditions'. By "tathā" is meant 'for that reason of declaring a quality'; the construction is 'the noble ones approved'.

Yatasaddānaṃ niccasambandhattā vuttaṃ “ye”tiādi. Sabbepīti puthujjanāriyāpi. Bhūtanti vijjamānaṃ. Kasmā sabbepi paṭijāniṃsu, nanu ariyehi attano guṇānaṃ anārocitattā na paṭijānitabbanti āha “ariyānampī”tiādi. Hīti saccaṃ, yasmā vā. Ariyānampi abbhantare uttarimanussadhammo yasmā bhūto hoti, tasmā sabbepi “bhūtaṃ bhagavā”ti paṭijāniṃsūti yojanā. Yasmā bhāsito viya hoti, tasmāti yojanā. Ariyā paṭijāniṃsūti sambandho. Anādīnavadassinoti dosassa adassanadhammā. Tehīti ariyehi, bhāsitoti sambandho. Yaṃ piṇḍapātaṃ uppādesunti yojanā. Aññeti puthujjanā. Sabbasaṅgāhikenevāti sabbesaṃ puthujjanāriyānaṃ saṅgahaṇe pavatteneva. Sikkhāpadavibhaṅgepīti sikkhāpadassa padabhājaniyepi. Tatthāti catutthapārājike. Idhāti imasmiṃ sikkhāpade.

Because relative pronouns have a constant connection, 'ye' (who) etc., is stated. By 'all' are meant both worldlings and noble ones. By "bhūtaṃ" is meant 'existing'. Why did all acknowledge it? Surely, since their own qualities are not declared by the noble ones, should they not acknowledge it? To this, he says, 'even of the noble ones,' etc. By "hi" is meant 'truly' or 'because'. Because a supramundane quality exists even within the noble ones, therefore all acknowledged, 'The Blessed One is actual'—this is the construction. The construction is: 'because it is as if spoken, therefore'. The connection is 'the noble ones acknowledged'. By "anādīnavadassino" is meant 'those whose nature is not to see fault'. By "tehi" is meant 'by the noble ones'; the connection is with 'spoken'. The construction is 'whatever almsfood they produced'. By "aññe" are meant 'worldlings'. By "sabbasaṅgāhikeneva" is meant 'precisely because it proceeds by way of including all, both worldlings and noble ones'. By "sikkhāpadavibhaṅgepi" is meant 'even in the word-by-word analysis of the training rule'. 'There' refers to the fourth Pārājika [rule]. 'Here' refers to this training rule.

77. Uttarimanussadhammameva sandhāya vuttaṃ, na sutādiguṇanti attho. Antarā vāti parinibbānakālato aññasmiṃ kāle vā. Atikaḍḍhiyamānenāti atinippīḷiyamānena. Ummattakassāti [V 1.0012] idaṃ panāti ettha iti-saddo ādyattho. Tena “khittacittassā”tiādiṃ saṅgaṇhāti. Diṭṭhisampannānanti maggapaññāya, phalapaññāya ca sampannānaṃ. Anāpattīti pācittiyāpattiyā anāpatti na vattabbā, āpattiyeva hoti, tasmā “ummattakassa anāpattī”ti na vattabbanti adhippāyoti. Aṭṭhamaṃ.

77. It is stated with reference only to supramundane qualities, not to virtues such as learning, etc.—this is the meaning. By antarā vā is meant 'or at another time than the time of final Nibbāna'. By atikaḍḍhiyamānena is meant 'by one being excessively pressed'. Here, in 'of one who is insane' (ummattakassa), the word iti has the meaning of 'and so forth', and thus it includes 'of one whose mind is deranged' (khittacittassa), etc. By diṭṭhisampannānaṃ is meant 'those accomplished in path-wisdom and fruition-wisdom'. By 'no offense' (anāpatti) is meant that it should not be said there is no pācittiya offense; an offense does indeed occur. Therefore, the intention is that one should not say, 'There is no offense for one who is insane.' The eighth.

9. Duṭṭhullārocanasikkhāpadaṃ

9. The Training Rule on Disclosing a Grave Offense

78. Navame tatrāti tassaṃ “duṭṭhullā nāmā”tiādipāḷiyaṃ, tāsu vā pāḷiaṭṭhakathāsu. Vicāraṇāti vīmaṃsanā. Upasampannasaddeti upasampannasaddatthabhāve[M 0.0014]. Ettha hi sadde vuccamāne avinābhāvato saddena atthopi vutto, vināpi bhāvapaccayena bhāvatthassa ñātabbattā bhāvopi gahetabbo, tasmā vuttaṃ “upasampannasaddatthabhāve”ti. Eseva nayo “duṭṭhullasadde”ti etthāpi. Etaṃ parimāṇaṃ yassāti etaṃ, “terasa saṅghādisesā”ti vacanaṃ. Etaṃ eva vattabbaṃ, na “cattāri ca pārājikānī”ti idanti attho. Tatthāti pāḷiyaṃ. Kassaci vimati bhaveyya, kiṃ bhaveyyāti yojanā. Āpattiṃ ārocentena akkosantassa samānattā vuttaṃ “evaṃ satī”tiādi. Pācittiyameva cāti casaddo byatirekattho, na dukkaṭaṃ āpajjatīti attho. Hīti saccaṃ. Etanti pācittiyāpajjanataṃ, “asuddho hoti…pe… omasavādassā”ti vacanaṃ vā, vuttanti sambandho. Etthāti pāḷiyaṃ. Aṭṭhakathācariyāveti ettha evakāro aṭṭhānayogo, pamāṇanti ettha yojetabbo, kāraṇamevāti attho. Tena vuttaṃ “na aññā vicāraṇā”ti. Atha vā aññāti sāmyatthe paccattavacanametaṃ, na aññesaṃ vicāraṇā pamāṇanti attho. Evañhi sati evakāro ṭhānayogova. Pubbepi cāti ganthārambhakālepi ca.

78. In the ninth, 'therein' refers to that passage beginning 'what is called grave' in the Pāli text or in those Pāli commentaries. 'Investigation' means examination. The term 'upasampanna' refers to the state of being 'upasampanna' in meaning. Here, when the word is spoken, due to its inseparability, the meaning is also stated by the word; and even without the bhāva suffix, the meaning of 'state' is to be understood, so the state must also be included. Therefore, it is said, 'in the state of being upasampanna in meaning.' The same method applies here to the term 'duṭṭhulla.' 'This is its measure' refers to the statement 'thirteen saṅghādisesa offenses.' This is what should be said, not 'the four pārājika offenses'—this is the meaning. 'Therein' refers to the Pāli text. Should someone have a doubt, what would be the case?—this is the connection. Since one who discloses an offense is equal to one who insults, it is said, 'this being so,' and so forth. 'Only a pācittiya'—the word ca here indicates exclusion, meaning one does not incur a dukkaṭa offense. 'Indeed' means truly. 'This' refers to the incurring of a pācittiya offense, or the statement 'he is impure... a reviler,' etc.; 'is stated' is the connection. 'Here' refers to the Pāli text. In the phrase Aṭṭhakathācariyāva, the word eva is misplaced; it should be connected with pamāṇaṃ, the meaning being 'only the reason'. Therefore it is said, 'no other investigation.' Alternatively, aññā here is a reflexive word in the sense of 'own', meaning 'the investigation of others is not the authority.' In this case, the word eva is appropriately placed. 'Even before' means also at the time of composing the text.

Etanti aṭṭhakathācariyānaṃ pamāṇataṃ. Saṃvaratthāya eva, anāpajjanatthāya eva ca anuññātanti yojanā. Tenāha “na tassa”tyādi. Tasmāti yasmā bhikkhubhāvo nāma na atthi, tasmā suvuttamevāti sambandho.

‘This’ refers to the authority of the commentary teachers. The connection is: ‘It is permitted only for the sake of restraint and for the sake of not incurring an offense.’ Therefore, he said, ‘not for him,’ and so forth. ‘Therefore’ means: because there is no such thing as the state of a monk, therefore ‘it is well said’—this is the connection.

80. Sāti bhikkhusammuti, saṅghena kātabbāti yojanā. Katthacīti kismiñci ṭhāne. Idhāti imasmiṃ sikkhāpade. “Vuttattā”ti padaṃ “kātabbā”ti pade hetu. Esāti eso bhikkhu. Hitesitāyāti hitassa esitāya, atthassa icchatāyāti attho.

80. 'That designation of a monk is to be made by the Saṅgha'—this is the connection. 'In any place' means in some place. 'Here' means in this training rule. The word 'because it was stated' is the reason for the word 'should be done.' 'This' refers to this monk. 'For the sake of welfare' means for the seeking of benefit, for the desire for good—this is the meaning.

82. Sesānīti [V 1.0013] ādimhi pañcasikkhāpadato sesāni upari pañca sikkhāpadāni. Assāti anupasampannassa. Ghaṭetvāti sambandhaṃ katvāti. Navamaṃ.

82. 'The rest' refers to the remaining five training rules, after the first five training rules. 'For him' means for one who is not fully ordained. 'Having connected' means having made a connection. The ninth.

10. Pathavīkhaṇanasikkhāpadaṃ

10. The Training Rule on Digging the Ground

86. Dasame [M 0.0015] bhagavā dassetīti yojanā. Etthāti pathaviyaṃ. Tatthāti tesu pāsāṇādīsu. Muṭṭhippamāṇatoti khaṭakapamāṇato. Sāti adaḍḍhapathavī. Hatthikucchiyanti evaṃnāmake ṭhāne. Ekapacchipūraṃ pathavinti sambandho. Tesaṃyevāti appapaṃsuappamattikāpadānaṃ eva. Hīti saccaṃ, yasmā vā. Etanti yebhuyyenapāsāṇādipañcakaṃ. Tanti kusītaṃ. Āṇāpetvāti ettha “āṇa pesane”ti dhātupāṭhesu vuttattā āṇadhātuyeva pesanasaṅkhātaṃ hetvatthaṃ vadati, na ṇāpepaccayo, so pana dhātvattheyeva vattati. Na hi tassa visuṃ vutto abhidheyyo atthi dhātvatthato aññassa abhidheyyassābhāvā. Tāvāti paṭhamaṃ pāḷimuttakavinicchayassa, tato vā.

86. In the tenth, the Blessed One shows—this is the connection. 'Here' means on the earth. 'There' means among those stones, etc. 'A fist-sized amount' means the size of a potsherd. 'That' refers to uncompacted earth. 'Elephant's belly' refers to a place of that name. The connection is 'a single basketful of earth.' 'Of those very things' refers to the terms 'little dust' and 'little clay' specifically. 'Indeed' means truly, or because. 'This' generally refers to the group of five, such as stones, etc. 'That' means sloth. Here, regarding 'having ordered' (āṇāpetvā), because in the Dhātupāṭhas it is stated that the root āṇa means 'sending,' therefore the root āṇa itself expresses the causal meaning of sending, not the suffix ṇāpe. The latter operates only within the meaning of the root, for it has no separate expressed meaning apart from the root's meaning, there being no expressed meaning other than that of the root. 'So long' refers first to the analysis independent of the Pāli text, or thereafter.

Pokkharaṃ padumaṃ netīti pokkharaṇī. “Sodhentehī”ti padaṃ “ussiñcituṃ apanetu”nti padesu bhāvakattā. Yoti “tanukaddamo”ti padena yojetabbo. Yo tanukaddamoti hi attho. Kuṭehīti ghaṭehi. Ussiñcitunti ukkhipitvā, uddharitvā vā siñcituṃ. Tatrāti sukkhakaddame, “yo”ti pade avayavīādhāro. Yoti sukkhakaddamo.

'Pokkharaṇī' means that which leads to lotuses (pokkharaṃ padumaṃ). The word 'by those who clean' (sodhentehi) is the agent for the words 'to draw out' (ussiñcituṃ) and 'to remove' (apanetuṃ). 'Yo' should be connected with the word 'thin mud' (tanukaddamo), for the meaning is 'which is thin mud.' 'Kuṭehi' means with pots. 'Ussiñcituṃ' means to lift up and sprinkle, or to draw out and sprinkle. 'There' refers to dry mud (sukkhakaddame), with 'yo' as the partitive locative in the phrase. 'Yo' means dry mud.

Taṭanti kūlaṃ. Udakasāmantāti udakassa samīpe. Omakacatumāsanti catumāsato ūnakaṃ. Ovaṭṭhanti devena ovassitaṃ hoti saceti yojanā. Patatīti taṭaṃ patati. Udakeyevāti pakatiudakeyeva. Udakassāti vassodakassa. Tatthāti pāsāṇapiṭṭhiyaṃ. Paṭhamamevāti soṇḍikhaṇanato paṭhamaṃ eva. Udake pariyādiṇṇeti udake sukkhe. Pacchāti udakapūrato pacchā. Tatthāti soṇḍiyaṃ. Udakeyevāti mūlaudakeyeva. Udakanti āgantukaudakaṃ. Allīyatīti piṭṭhipāsāṇe laggati. Tampīti sukhumarajampi. Akatapabbhāreti vaḷañjena akate pabbhāre. Upacikāhi vamīyati, gharagoḷikādayo vā satte vamatīti vammiko.

'Bank' means the shore. 'Near the water' means in the vicinity of the water. 'Less than four months' means fewer than four months. 'Drenched' means it is rained upon by the sky, if it is so—this is the connection. 'Falls' means the bank falls. 'In the water itself' means in the natural water itself. 'Of the water' refers to rainwater. 'There' means on the rock surface. 'First only' means first, even before digging the channel. 'When the water has been used up' means when the water has dried up. 'Afterward' means after the water has filled. 'There' refers to the channel. 'In the water itself' means in the original water itself. 'Water' refers to incoming water. 'Sticks' means it clings to the rock surface. 'Even that' includes fine dust. 'In an unmade crevice' means in a crevice not made by use. It is vomited up by termites, or it vomits up beings like house lizards—thus, it is an anthill (vammiko).

Gāvīnaṃ [M 0.0016] khuro kaṇṭakasadisattā gokaṇṭako nāma, tena chinno kaddamo “gokaṇṭako”ti vuccati. Acchadanaṃ vā vinaṭṭhacchadanaṃ vā purāṇasenāsanaṃ hotīti yojanā. Tatoti [V 1.0014] purāṇasenāsanato, gaṇhituṃ vaṭṭatīti sambandho. Avasesanti vinaṭṭhacchadanato. Avasesaṃ iṭṭhakaṃ gaṇhāmi iti saññāyāti yojetabbo. Tenāti iṭṭhakādinā. Yā yāti mattikā. Atintāti anallā, akilinnāti attho.

A cow's hoof, being like a thorn, is called 'gokaṇṭaka'; the mud cut by it is called 'gokaṇṭaka.' The connection is that it is an old dwelling either without a covering or with a decayed covering. From that, from the old dwelling, it is permissible to take—this is the connection. 'The remainder' is from the decayed covering. It should be connected with the thought, 'I will take the remaining brick.' 'By that' means by means of bricks and the like. 'That which' refers to clay. 'Not wet' means not moist, not saturated—this is the meaning.

Tasminti mattikāpuñje. Sabboti sakalo mattikāpuñjo. Assāti mattikāpuñjassa. “Kappiyakārakehī”ti padaṃ “apanāmetvā”ti pade kāritakammaṃ. Kasmā vaṭṭatīti āha “udakenā”tiādi. Hīti saccaṃ, yasmā vā.

'In that' means in that pile of clay. 'All' means the entire pile of clay. 'Of it' refers to the pile of clay. The word 'by those who make it allowable' (kappiyakārakehi) is the causative object in the word 'having removed' (apanāmetvā). Why is it allowable? He said, 'with water,' etc. 'Indeed' means truly, or because.

Tatthāti mattikāpākāre. Aññampīti maṇḍapathambhato aññampi. Tena apadesenāti tena pāsāṇādipavaṭṭanalesena.

'There' means at the clay wall. 'Also another' means another from the pillar of the pavilion. 'By that pretext' means by that excuse of rolling stones and the like.

Passāvadhārāyāti muttasotāya. Kattarayaṭṭhiyāti kattaradaṇḍena. Ettha hi kattarayati aṅgapaccaṅgānaṃ sithilabhāvena sithilo hutvā bhavatīti katvā kattaro vuccati jiṇṇamanusso, tena ekantato gahetabbattā kattarena gahitā yaṭṭhi, kattarassa yaṭṭhīti vā katvā kattarayaṭṭhi vuccati kattaradaṇḍo. Dantajapaṭhamakkharena sajjhāyitabbo. Vīriyasampaggahaṇatthanti vīriyassa suṭṭhu paggaṇhanatthaṃ, vīriyassa ukkhipanatthanti attho. Keci bhikkhūti yojanā.

'Stream of urine' means the flow of urine. 'With an old man's staff' means with an old man's stick. Here, indeed, because one becomes loose due to the looseness of one's limbs, having become so, a 'kattara' is called an old man (jiṇṇamanusso). Therefore, because it is to be taken by him entirely, the stick taken by a kattara, or the stick of a kattara—thus, it is called the 'kattara-staff' (kattarayaṭṭhi), meaning an old man's stick. It should be recited with the first letter of 'dantaja.' 'For the purpose of properly taking up energy' means for the purpose of well taking up energy, for the purpose of lifting up energy—this is the meaning. The connection is 'some monks'.

87. Tatrāpīti iṭṭhakakapālādīsupi. Hīti saccaṃ. Tesaṃ anupādānattāti tesaṃ iṭṭhakādīnaṃ aggissa anindhanattā. Hīti saccaṃ, yasmāvā. Tānīti iṭṭhakādīni. Avisayattāti āpattiyā anokāsattā. Tiṇukkanti tiṇamayaṃ ukkaṃ. Tatthevāti mahāpaccariyaṃ eva. Arīyati agginipphādanatthaṃ ghaṃsīyati etthāti araṇī, heṭṭhā nimanthanīyadāru. Saha dhanunā eti pavattatīti sahito, upari nimanthanadāru. Araṇī ca sahito ca araṇīsahito, tena aggiṃ nibbattetvāti yojanā. Yathā kariyamāne na ḍayhati, tathā karohīti sambandho.

87. 'There too' means even in the case of bricks, potsherds, and the like. 'Indeed' means truly. 'Because they are not fuel' means because those bricks and the like are not fuel for fire. 'Indeed' means truly, or because. 'Those' refers to the bricks and the like. 'Because it is not a domain' means because there is no opportunity for an offense. 'A grass torch' means a torch made of grass. 'Right there' means in the great fire-pit itself. 'Araṇī' means that which is rubbed there for the purpose of producing fire; the lower piece of wood to be twirled. 'Sahito' means that which proceeds together with the bow; the upper piece of wood for twirling. 'Araṇīsahito' is araṇī and sahito; the construal is 'having produced fire by that.' The connection is, 'Do it in such a way that it does not burn when being done'.

88. Āvāṭaṃ [M 0.0017] jānāti āvāṭaṃ kātuṃ, khaṇituṃ vā jānāhīti attho. “Evaṃ mahāmattikaṃ jāna, thusamattikaṃ jānā”ti etthāpi yathālābhaṃ sampadānavācakapadaṃ ajjhāharitvā yojanā kātabbā. Sāti pathavī. Tenāti pavaṭṭanādināti. Dasamaṃ.

88. 'Knows a pit' means knows how to make a pit, or knows how to dig; this is the meaning. Here too, in 'know this much clay, know a measure of chaff,' the interpretation should be made by supplying a word indicating the dative case according to what is obtained. 'Sā' refers to the earth. 'Tena' means by rolling and the like. The tenth.

Musāvādavaggo paṭhamo.

The Chapter on False Speech, the First.

2. Bhūtagāmavaggo

2. The Chapter on Living Plants

1. Bhūtagāmasikkhāpada-atthayojanā

1. The Construal of the Meaning of the Training Rule Concerning Living Plants

89. Dutiyavaggassa [V 1.0015] paṭhame tassāti devatāya. Ukkhittaṃ pharasunti uddhaṃ khittaṃ kuṭhāriṃ. Niggahetunti saṇṭhātuṃ, nivattetuṃ vā. Cakkhuvisayātīteti pasādacakkhussa gocarātikkante. Mahārājasantikāti vessavaṇamahārājassa santikā. Thanamūleyevāti thanasamīpeyeva. Himavanteti himauggiraṇe vane, himayutte vā. Tatthāti himavante, devatāsannipāte vā. Rukkhadhammoti rukkhasabhāvo. Rukkhadhammo ca nāma chedanabhedanādīsu rukkhānaṃ acetanattā kopassa akaraṇaṃ, tasmiṃ rukkhadhamme ṭhitā devatā rukkhadhamme ṭhitā nāma, chedanabhedanādīsu rukkhassa viya rukkhaṭṭhakadevatāya akopanaṃ rukkhadhamme ṭhitā nāmāti adhippāyo. Tatthāti tāsu sannipātadevatāsu. Itīti imassa alabhanassa, imasmiṃ alabhane vā, ādīnavanti sambandho. Bhagavato cāti ca-saddo “pubbacarita”nti ettha yojetabbo. Imañca ādīnavaṃ addasa, bhagavato pubbacaritañca anussarīti vākyasampiṇḍanavasena yojanā kātabbā. Tenāti dassanānussaraṇakāraṇena. Assāti devatāya. Saṃvijjati pitā assāti sapitiko, putto. (Tāvāti ativiya, paṭisañcikkhantiyāti sambandho) “mariyādaṃ bandhissatī”ti vatvā tassa atthaṃ dassento āha “sikkhāpadaṃ paññapessatī”ti. Iti paṭisañcikkhantiyā assā devatāya etadahosīti yojanā.

89. In the first section of the second chapter, 'tassā' refers to the deity. 'Ukkhittaṃ pharasuṃ' means an axe thrown upward. 'Niggahetuṃ' means to make it stand still or to turn it back. 'Cakkhuvisayātīte' means beyond the range of the sensitive eye. 'Mahārājasantikā' means from the presence of King Vessavaṇa. 'Thanamūleyeva' means right at the base of the trunk. 'Himavante' refers to the Himavanta forest, which emits snow, or is snow-covered. 'Tattha' means in Himavanta or in the assembly of deities. 'Rukkhadhammo' means the nature of a tree. The nature of a tree is this: due to the trees' insentience, there is no arising of anger towards cutting, breaking, and so on. A deity abiding in the nature of a tree is called 'one established in the nature of a tree'—the intention is that, like a tree, the deity dwelling in the tree does not become angry when it is cut, broken, and so on. 'Tattha' refers to those assembled deities. 'Iti' is connected with 'ādīnavaṃ' (disadvantage), in the sense of 'the disadvantage of this non-obtainment' or 'in this non-obtainment'. The word 'ca' in 'Bhagavato ca' should be connected here with 'pubbacaritaṃ' (previous conduct). The sentences should be combined thus: 'She saw this disadvantage and recollected the Blessed One’s past conduct.' 'Tena' means due to the reason of seeing and recollecting. 'Assā' refers to the deity. 'Sapitiko' means one for whom a father exists (saṃvijjati pitā assā); a son. (The word 'tāva' means 'very much,' and is connected to 'paṭisañcikkhantiyā' (reflecting)). Having said, 'He will establish a boundary,' it explains its meaning by saying, 'He will lay down a training rule.' Thus, reflecting in this way, this occurred to that deity—this is the construal.

Yoti [M 0.0018] yo koci jano. Veti ekantena. Uppatitanti uppajjanavasena attano upari patitaṃ. Bhantanti bhamantaṃ dhāvantaṃ, vārayeti nivāreyya niggaṇheyyāti attho. Tanti janaṃ. Ayaṃ panettha yojanā – sārathi bhantaṃ rathaṃ vāraye iva, tathā yo ve uppatitaṃ kodhaṃ vāraye, taṃ ahaṃ sārathiṃ iti brūmi. Itaro kodhanivārakato añño rājauparājādīnaṃ sārathibhūto jano rasmiggāho rajjuggāho nāmāti.

'Yo' means any person whatsoever. 'Ve' means entirely. 'Uppatitaṃ' means fallen upon oneself in the sense of arising. 'Bhantaṃ' means wandering or running. 'Vāraye' means he should restrain or control; that is the meaning. 'Taṃ' means that person. Here, the construal is this: just as a charioteer restrains a wandering chariot, so too, one who restrains arisen anger—him I call a charioteer. The other person, different from the restrainer of anger, who becomes a charioteer for kings, viceroys, and so on, is called a reins-holder or a rope-holder.

Dutiyagāthāya vejjo visaṭaṃ vitthataṃ sappavisaṃ sappassa āsīvisassa visaṃ garaḷaṃ osadhehi bhesajjena, mantena ca vineti iva, tathā yo bhikkhave uppatitaṃ kodhaṃ mettāya vineti, so bhikkhu urago bhujago purāṇaṃ pure bhavaṃ jiṇṇaṃ purāṇattā jiṇṇaṃ tacaṃ jahāti iva, tathā orapāraṃ apārasaṅkhātaṃ pañcorambhāgiyasaṃyojanaṃ jahātīti yojanā kātabbā.

In the second verse, just as a physician dispels the spread-out, extensive snake venom—the poison, the venom of a venomous serpent—with herbs, medicine, and mantras, so too, bhikkhus, whoever dispels arisen anger with loving-kindness—that bhikkhu, like a snake, a serpent, shedding its old, worn-out skin, a skin from a former time, so too does he abandon this shore and the far shore, that is, the five lower fetters which are designated as this shore. Thus should the construal be made.

Tatrāti [V 1.0016] dvīsu gāthāsu. Vatthu pana vinaye ārūḷhanti yojanā. Athāti pacchā. Yassa devaputtassāti yena devaputtena. Pariggahoti paricchinditvā gahito. Soti devaputto. Tatoti upagamanato. Yadā hoti, tadāti yojanā. Mahesakkhadevatāsūti mahāparivārāsu devatāsu, mahātejāsu vā. Paṭikkamantīti apenti. Devatā yampi pañhaṃ pucchantīti yojanā. Tatthevāti attano vasanaṭṭhāneyeva. Upaṭṭhānanti upaṭṭhānatthāya, sampadānatthe cetaṃ upayogavacanaṃ. Atha vā upagantvā tiṭṭhati etthāti upaṭṭhānaṃ, bhagavato samīpaṭṭhānaṃ, taṃ āgantvāti attho. Nanti taṃ, ayameva vā pāṭho.

'Tattha' refers to the two verses. The subject matter, however, is established in the Vinaya; this is the construal. 'Atha' means afterwards. 'Yassa devaputtassa' means 'by which devaputta'. 'Pariggaho' means taken after having been demarcated. 'So' refers to that devaputta. 'Tato' means from approaching. 'Yadā hoti, tadā' is the connection. 'Mahesakkhadevatāsu' refers to deities with great retinues or great power. 'Paṭikkamanti' means they depart. 'The deities also ask a question' is the construal. 'Tattheva' means in their own dwelling place. 'Upaṭṭhānaṃ' means for the purpose of attendance; this is a word indicating use in the dative sense. Alternatively, 'upaṭṭhānaṃ' is where one approaches and stands, that is, standing near the Blessed One; the meaning is 'having come there'. 'Naṃ' means 'that,' or this is the reading itself.

90. “Bhavantī”ti iminā virūḷhe mūle nīlabhāvaṃ āpajjitvā vaḍḍhamānake taruṇarukkhagacchādike dasseti. “Ahuvatthu”nti iminā pana vaḍḍhitvā ṭhite mahantarukkhagacchādike dasseti. “Ahuvatthu”nti ca hiyyattanisaṅkhātāya tthuṃ-vibhattiyā hū-dhātussa ūkārassa uvādeso hoti. Potthakesu pana “ahuvatī”ti pāṭho dissati, so apāṭhoti daṭṭhabbo. “Jāyantī”ti iminā bhū-dhātussa sattatthabhāvaṃ dasseti[M 0.0019], “vaḍḍhantī”ti iminā vaḍḍhanatthabhāvaṃ. Etanti “bhūtagāmo”ti nāmaṃ. Pīyate yathākāmaṃ paribhuñjīyate, pātabbaṃ paribhuñjitabbanti vā pātabyaṃ, pāsaddo yathākāmaparibhuñjanattho. Tenāha – “chedanabhedanādīhi yathāruci paribhuñjitabbatāti attho”ti.

90. By 'bhavanti,' it indicates young trees, plants, and so on, that are growing, having developed roots and attained a green state. By 'ahuvatthu,' on the other hand, it indicates large trees, plants, and so on, that are fully grown and established. And in 'ahuvatthu,' there is the substitution of 'uva' for the 'ū' vowel of the root 'hū' with the 'tthuṃ' ending, which is designated as the past tense. In manuscripts, however, the reading 'ahuvati' is found, but it should be regarded as an incorrect reading. By 'jāyanti,' it indicates the state of being of the root 'bhū,' and by 'vaḍḍhanti,' the state of growing. 'Etaṃ' is the name 'bhūtagāma'. 'Pātabyaṃ' means that which is used or enjoyed at will (pīyate yathākāmaṃ paribhuñjīyate), or that which is to be used or enjoyed; the word 'pā' has the meaning of enjoying as desired. Therefore it is said: 'The meaning is that it is to be enjoyed as desired, by cutting, breaking, and so on.'

91. “Idānī”ti padaṃ “āhā”ti pade kālasattamī. Yasminti bīje. Tanti bījaṃ. Pañca bījajātānīti ettha jātasaddassa tabbhāvatthataṃ sandhāya aṭṭhakathāsu evaṃ vuttaṃ. Tabbhāvatthassa “mūle jāyantī”ti imāya pāḷiyā asaṃsandanataṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ saṅgahakārena “na samentī”ti. Aṭṭhakathācariyānaṃ matena sati jātasaddassa tabbhāvatthabhāve “mūle jāyantī”tiādīsu mūle mūlāni jāyantīti doso bhaveyyāti manasi katvā āha “na hī”tiādi. Hīti saccaṃ, yasmā vā. Tānīti rukkhādīni. Tassāti “bhūtagāmo nāma pañca bījajātānī”ti padassa. Etanti “bījajātānī”ti nāmaṃ. Bījesu jātāni bījajātānīti vutte “mūle jāyantī”tiādinā sameti. Etenāti “bījato”tiādinā saṅgahoti sambandho.

91. The word 'idāni' is a locative of time in relation to the word 'āha'. 'Yasmiṃ' refers to the seed. 'Taṃ' means seed. In 'pañca bījajātāni,' regarding the word 'jāta,' it is said thus in the commentaries, intending its meaning as 'having the nature of'. Regarding the lack of agreement of that meaning with the Pāli passage 'mūle jāyanti,' it was said by the compiler, 'they do not agree'. Considering that, in the opinion of the commentary teachers, if the word 'jāta' has the meaning of 'having the nature of,' a fault would occur in passages like 'mūle jāyanti' by saying 'mūle mūlāni jāyanti' ('in the root, roots are born'), he says 'na hi' and so on. 'Hi' means 'truly,' or 'because'. 'Tāni' refers to trees, etc. 'Tassa' refers to the phrase 'bhūtagāmo nāma pañca bījajātāni'. 'Etaṃ' is the name 'bījajātāni'. When 'bījajātāni' is said to mean 'bījesu jātāni' (born from seeds), it agrees with 'mūle jāyanti' and so on. By this, the inclusion of things beginning with 'from the seed' is accomplished; this is the connection.

“Yehī”ti padaṃ “jātattā”ti pade apādānaṃ, hetu vā “vuttānī”ti pade karaṇaṃ, kattā vā. Tesanti bījānaṃ. Rukkhādīnaṃ viruhanaṃ janetīti bījaṃ. “Bījato”tiādinā kāriyopacārena kāraṇassa dassitattā kāraṇūpacāraṃ padīpeti. Aññānipi yāni vā pana gacchavallirukkhādīni atthi saṃvijjanti, tāni gacchavallirukkhādīni jāyanti sañjāyantīti yojanā. Tānīti gacchavallirukkhādīni[V 1.0017]. Tañca mūlaṃ, pāḷiyaṃ vuttahaliddādi ca atthi, sabbampi etaṃ mūlabījaṃ nāmāti sambandho. Etthāti bījesu, khandhabījesu vā.

The word 'yehi' is an ablative in relation to the word 'jātattā,' or a cause; or an instrument in relation to the word 'vuttāni,' or an agent. 'Tesaṃ' refers to seeds. A seed is that which produces the sprouting of trees and so forth. By 'bījato' and so on, the cause is shown by the metaphorical transference of effect, thus illustrating the causal metaphor. Whatever other shrubs, creepers, trees, and so forth exist and are found, those shrubs, creepers, and trees arise and come into being—this is the interpretation. 'Tāni' refers to shrubs, creepers, and trees. And that root, and also turmeric and other things mentioned in the Pāli text, all of this is called 'root-seed'—this is the connection. 'Ettha' means in the seeds, or in the trunk-seeds.

92. Saññāvasenāti “bīja”nti saññāvasena. “Tatthā”ti padaṃ “veditabbo”ti pade ādhāro. “Yathā”tiādinā kāraṇopacārena kāriyassa vuttattā phalūpacāraṃ dasseti. Yaṃ bījaṃ vuttaṃ, taṃ dukkaṭavatthūti yojanā. Yadetaṃ ādipadanti yojetabbaṃ. Tenāti ādipadena. Ravīyati bhagavatā kathīyatīti rutaṃ, pāḷi, tassa anurūpaṃ yathārutaṃ, pāḷianatikkantanti attho.

92. 'Saññāvasena' means 'by means of perception,' that is, by the perception of 'seed'. The word 'tattha' is the basis in relation to the word 'veditabbo'. By 'yathā' and so on, since the effect is stated by the metaphorical attribution of the cause, it illustrates the metaphorical attribution of the fruit. The seed that is mentioned is the basis for a wrong-doing—this is the interpretation. This 'ādipada' (initial word) should be connected. 'Tena' means by that initial word. 'Rutaṃ' is that which is spoken, declared by the Blessed One, meaning the Pāli; 'yathārutaṃ' is in accordance with that, not transgressing the Pāli—this is the meaning.

Etthāti [M 0.0020] “bīje bījasaññī”tiādipade, imasmiṃ sikkhāpade vā. Udake ṭhāti pavattatīti udakaṭṭho, evaṃ thalaṭṭhopi. Tatthāti udakaṭṭhathalaṭṭhesu. Sāsapassa mattaṃ pamāṇaṃ assa sevālassāti sāsapamattiko. Tilassa bījapamāṇaṃ assa sevālassāti tilabījako. Pamāṇatthe ko. Ādisaddena saṅkhapaṇakādayo sevāle saṅgaṇhāti. Tattha tilabījapamāṇo jalasaṇṭhito nīlādivaṇṇayutto sevālo tilabījaṃ nāma, sapatto appakaṇḍo ukkhalipidhānādipamāṇo samūlo eko sevālaviseso saṅkho nāma, bhamarasaṇṭhāno nīlavaṇṇo eko sevālaviseso paṇako nāma. Udakaṃ sevatīti sevālo. Tatthāti sevālesu. Yoti sevālo. Patiṭṭhitaṃ sevālanti sambandho. Yattha katthacīti mūle vā naḷe vā patte vā. Uddharitvāti uppāṭetvā. “Hatthehī”ti padaṃ “viyūhitvā”ti pade karaṇaṃ. Hīti saccaṃ, yasmā vā. Tassāti sevālassa. Ettāvatāti ito cito ca viyūhanamattena. Yo sevālo nikkhamati, taṃ sevālanti yojanā. Parissāvanantarenāti parissāvanachiddena. Uppalāni asmiṃ gaccheti uppalinī. Padumāni asmiṃ gaccheti paduminī, ino, itthiliṅgajotako ī. Tatthevāti udakeyeva. Tānīti vallītiṇāni. Hīti saccaṃ, yasmā vā. Anantakoti sāsapamattiko sevālo. So hi natthi attato anto lāmako sevālo etassāti katvā “anantako”ti vuccati. Attanāyeva hi sukhumo, tato sukhumo sevālo natthīti adhippāyo. Tatthāti dukkaṭavatthubhāve. Tampīti “sampuṇṇabhūtagāmaṃ na hotī”ti vacanampi. Pisaddo mahāpaccariādiaṭṭhakathācariyānaṃ vacanāpekkho. Hīti saccaṃ, yasmā vā. Na āgato, tasmā na sametīti yojanā. Athāti tasmiṃ anāgate. Etanti anantakasevālādiṃ. Gacchissatīti vadeyyāti sambandho. Tampīti “gacchissatī”ti vacanampi. Pisaddo purimaṭṭhakathācariyānaṃ vacanāpekkho.

Here, in the phrase 'perceiving a seed in a seed' and similar terms, or in this training rule. 'Stands in water' means it grows in water; similarly, 'stands on land' means it grows on land. 'There' refers to those that stand in water and those that stand on land. 'Mustard-seed measure' means the algae whose measure is that of a mustard seed. 'Sesame-seed measure' means the algae whose measure is that of a sesame seed. The suffix '-ka' is in the sense of measure. By the term 'etc.,' it includes saṅkha algae, paṇaka algae, and others among algae. Among these, algae the size of a sesame seed, submerged in water, and having blue or other colors, is called 'sesame-seed algae.' A single type of algae, with leaves, small stems, about the size of a pot lid, and with roots, is called 'saṅkha.' Another type of algae, resembling a bee and blue in color, is called 'paṇaka.' 'Algae' means that which frequents water. 'There' refers to among the algae. 'Which' refers to the algae. The connection is 'algae established.' 'Wherever' means at the root, or at the stem, or at the leaf. 'Having taken up' means having uprooted. The word 'with the hands' is an instrumental term for the word 'having scattered.' 'Hī' means 'indeed,' or 'because.' 'Of that' refers to the algae. 'By this much' means merely by scattering it here and there. The interpretation is 'that algae' refers to the algae that comes out. 'Through the strainer' means through the hole of the strainer. 'Lotuses are in this group' is called 'uppalinī.' 'Water lilies are in this group' is called 'paduminī.' The suffix '-inī' indicates the feminine gender. 'Right there' means in the water itself. 'Those' refers to vines and grasses. 'Hī' means 'indeed,' or 'because.' 'Boundless' refers to algae the size of a mustard seed. Indeed, it is called 'boundless' because there is no other inferior algae beyond itself. The meaning is that it is inherently very fine, and there is no algae finer than it. 'There' refers to the state of being a ground for wrongdoing. 'That too' refers to the statement, 'it is not a complete sprouting-group.' The word 'pi' refers to the opinion of the commentary teachers like Mahāpaccarī and others. 'Hī' means 'indeed,' or 'because.' 'Not arrived,' therefore it does not come together—this is the interpretation. 'Then' refers to when it has not yet arrived. 'This' refers to boundless algae and the like. The connection is 'one may say it will go.' 'That too' refers to the statement, 'it will go.' The word 'pi' refers to the opinion of the earlier commentary teachers.

Abhūtagāmamūlattā [V 1.0018] tādisassa bījagāmassāti ettha bījagāmo tividho hoti – yo sayaṃ bhūtagāmato hutvā aññampi bhūtagāmaṃ [M 0.0021] janeti, ambaṭṭhiādiko. Yo pana sayaṃ bhūtagāmato hutvā aññaṃ pana bhūtagāmaṃ na janeti, tālanāḷikerādikhāṇu. Yo pana sayampi bhūtagāmato ahutvā aññampi bhūtagāmaṃ na janeti. Pānīyaghaṭādīnaṃ bahi sevāloti. Bhūtagāmo pana catubbidho hoti – yo sayaṃ bījagāmato hutvā aññampi bījagāmaṃ janeti, etarahi ambarukkhādiko. Yo pana sayaṃ bījagāmato ahutvāva aññaṃ bījagāmaṃ janeti, ādikappakāle ambarukkhādiko.
