Yo pana sayaṃ bījagāmato hutvā aññaṃ pana bījagāmaṃ na janeti, nīlavaṇṇo phalitakadalīrukkhādiko. Yo pana sayampi bījagāmato ahutvā aññampi bījagāmaṃ na janeti, idha vutto anantakasevālādikoti. Tattha catutthaṃ bhūtagāmaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ “abhūtagāmamūlakattā tādisassa bījassā”ti. Ayaṃ pana tatiyabījagāmassa ca catutthabhūtagāmassa ca viseso – tatiyabījagāme mūlapaṇṇāni na paññāyanti, catutthabhūtagāme tāni paññāyantīti. Mūlapaṇṇānaṃ apaññāyanattā bījagāmoti vutto, tesaṃ paññāyanattā bhūtagāmoti vutto. Itarathā hi virodho bhaveyyāti. Attano vāde pācittiyabhāvato garukaṃ, mahāpaccariādīnaṃ vāde dukkaṭamattabhāvato lahukaṃ. Etanti ṭhānaṃ.

Here, regarding 'because of such a seed-group having its root in a non-sprouting-group,' the seed-group is of three kinds: 1. That which, being itself from the sprouting-group, produces another sprouting-group, such as a mango stone and so forth. 2. That which, though itself from the sprouting-group, does not produce another sprouting-group, such as the trunk of a palm or coconut tree and so forth. 3. That which is neither itself from the sprouting-group nor produces another sprouting-group, such as the algae on the outside of water pots and so forth. The sprouting-group, however, is of four kinds: 1. That which, being itself from the seed-group, produces another seed-group, such as a mango tree at present and so forth. 2. That which, though not itself from the seed-group, produces another seed-group, such as a mango tree at the beginning of the eon and so forth. 3. That which, though itself from the seed-group, does not produce another seed-group, such as a blue-colored fruiting banana tree and so forth. 4. That which is neither itself from the seed-group nor produces another seed-group, such as the boundless algae mentioned here and so forth. In this context, referring to the fourth sprouting-group, it is said: 'because of such a seed having its root in a non-sprouting-group.' Now, the distinction between the third seed-group and the fourth sprouting-group is this: in the third seed-group, roots and leaves are not discernible; in the fourth sprouting-group, they are discernible. Because roots and leaves are not discernible, it is called the seed-group; because they are discernible, it is called the sprouting-group. Otherwise, there would indeed be a contradiction. According to one's own view, it is grave due to being a pācittiya offense; according to the view of Mahāpaccarī and others, it is light due to being merely a dukkaṭa offense. This is the position.

Evaṃ udakaṭṭhaṃ dassetvā thalaṭṭhaṃ dassento āha “thalaṭṭhe”tiādi. Thalaṭṭhe vinicchayo evaṃ veditabboti yojanā. Tatthāti haritakhāṇūsu. Uddhaṃ vaḍḍhatīti navasākhāniggamanena chinnato upari vaḍḍhati. Soti khāṇu. Phalitāya kadaliyā khāṇu bījagāmena saṅgahitoti yojanā. Phalaṃ sañjātaṃ etissāti phalitā. Tathāti “bhūtagāmeneva saṅgahitā”ti padāni ākaḍḍhati. Yadāti yasmiṃ kāle. Ratanappamāṇāpīti hatthappamāṇāpi. Athāti apādānattho, tato rāsikaraṇato aññanti attho. Bhūmiyaṃ nikhaṇantīti sambandho. “Mūlesu ceva paṇṇesu cā”ti ettha casaddo samuccayatthova, na vikappatthoti āha “mūlamattesu panā”tiādi.

Having thus shown the water-standing plant, then showing the land-standing plant, he says 'on land,' and so forth. The interpretation is that the explanation regarding the land-standing plant should be understood thus. 'There' refers to among the green stumps. 'It grows upward' means it grows above where it was cut, by the emergence of new branches. 'That' refers to the stump. The interpretation is that the trunk of a fruiting banana plant is included in the seed-group. 'Fruit has arisen from it'—thus it is called 'fruiting.' 'Similarly,' he draws in the words 'included with the sprouting-group itself.' 'When' means at which time. 'Even the size of a gem' means even the size of a hand. 'Then' is in the sense of the ablative case, meaning 'other than that,' from the act of piling up. The connection is 'they plant in the ground.' In 'both in the roots and in the leaves,' the word 'ca' is indeed in the sense of accumulation, not of option, thus he says 'but only in the roots,' and so forth.

Bījānīti mūlādibījāni. Ṭhapitāni hontīti sambandho. “Uparī”ti padena heṭṭhā mūlāni cāti atthaṃ nayena ñāpeti. Na aṅkure niggatamatteyeva[M 0.0022], atha kho harite nīlapaṇṇavaṇṇe jāteyeva bhūtagāmasaṅgaho kātabboti āha “harite”tiādi. Tālaṭṭhīnaṃ mūlanti sambandho. Dantasūci viyāti hatthidantasūci viya. Yathā asampuṇṇabhūtagāmo tatiyo koṭṭhāso na āgato, na evaṃ amūlakabhūtagāmo. So pana āgatoyevāti āha “amūlakabhūtagāme”ti. Amūlikalatā viya amūlakabhūtagāme saṅgahaṃ gacchatīti attho.

'Seeds' means root-seeds and other seeds. The connection is 'they are established.' By the word 'above,' it implies the meaning that there are roots below as well. He says 'when green,' and so forth, to show that the inclusion in the sprouting-group should be made not merely when sprouts have emerged, but only when they have turned green and taken on the color of blue leaves. The connection is 'the roots of palm stones.' 'Like an ivory needle' means like an elephant's ivory needle. Just as the third division, the incomplete sprouting-group, has not arrived, so it is not with the rootless sprouting-group. But that has indeed arrived, hence he says 'in the rootless sprouting-group.' The meaning is that like a rootless creeper, it comes to be included in the rootless sprouting-group.

Vandākāti [V 1.0019] rukkhādanī. Sā hi sayaṃ rukkhaṃ nissāya jāyantīpi attano nissayānaṃ rukkhānaṃ adanattā bhakkhanattā vadīyati thutīyatīti “vandākā”ti vuccati. Aññā vāti vandākāya aññā vā. Tanti vandākādiṃ. Tatoti rukkhato. Vananti khuddako gaccho. Pagumboti mahāgaccho. Daṇḍakoti rukkho daṇḍayogato. Tassāpīti amūlikalatāyapi. Ayameva vinicchayoti vandākādikassa vinicchayo viya ayaṃ vinicchayo daṭṭhabboti yojanā. “Dve tīṇi pattānī”ti vuttattā ekapatto sañjāyantopi aggabījasaṅgahaṃ gacchatīti attho. “Anupasampannenā”ti padaṃ “littassā”ti pade kattā. Nidāghasamayeti gimhakāle. Abbohārikoti āpattiyā aṅganti na voharitabbo. Voharituṃ na arahatīti attho. Etanti abbohārikataṃ, “sace…pe… pamajjitabbā”ti vacanaṃ vā.

'Vandākā' means a tree-eater. Indeed, though it grows depending on a tree, because it eats and consumes the trees on which it depends, it is spoken of and praised, and thus it is called 'vandākā'. 'Aññā vā' means 'or another' than the vandākā. 'That' refers to the vandākā and so forth. 'From that' means from the tree. 'Vana' means a small thicket. 'Pagumba' means a large thicket. 'Daṇḍaka' refers to a tree because it is like a staff. 'Even for that' refers to even for a rootless creeper. The construction is that this explanation should be seen just like the explanation for the vandākā and so forth. Since 'two or three leaves' are mentioned, the meaning is that even if only one leaf has appeared, it is included under shoot-seeds. The word 'by one not fully ordained' is the agent in the word 'of one smeared.' 'In the hot season' means in the summer time. 'Not actionable' means it should not be treated as a factor of an offense. The meaning is that it is not fit to be legally considered. 'This' refers to the state of being not actionable, or the statement 'if... should be overlooked.'

Ahiṃ sappaṃ chādetīti ahicchattaṃ, taṃyeva ahicchattakaṃ. Yathākathañci hi byuppatti, ruḷhiyā atthavinicchayo. Tasmāti tato vikopanato. Tatthāti ahicchattake. Heṭṭhā “udakapappaṭako”ti vatvā idha “rukkhapappaṭikāyapī”ti vuttattā pappaṭakasaddo dviliṅgoti daṭṭhabbo. Tanti pappaṭikaṃ. Ṭhitaṃ niyyāsanti sambandho. Evaṃ “lagga”nti etthāpi. Hatthakukkuccenāti hatthalolena. “Chindantassāpī”ti pade hetu.

'That which covers a snake' is ahicchatta; that same is ahicchattaka. However the derivation may be, the meaning is determined by common usage. 'Therefore' means from that act of disturbing. 'There' refers to in the ahicchattaka. Since 'water-scum' (udakapappaṭako) was said below, and here 'even on tree-scum' (rukkhapappaṭikāya) is said, the word 'pappaṭaka' should be understood as having two genders. 'That' refers to the pappaṭika. The connection is 'standing sap.' Similarly, here too, with 'attached.' 'By restlessness of hand' means by a greedy hand. The word 'even of one cutting' is in the sense of cause.

Vāsatthikenāti vāsaṃ icchantena. “Ocināpetabbā”ti pade kattā. Uppāṭentehīti uddharantehi. Tesanti sāmaṇerānaṃ. Sākhaṃ gahitanti sambandho. Ṭhapitassa siṅgīverassāti yojanā.

'By one desiring residence' means by one who wishes for residence. It is the agent in the word 'should be caused to be gathered.' 'By those uprooting' means by those pulling out. 'Of them' refers to of the novices. The connection is 'having taken a branch.' The construction is 'of the planted ginger.'

Chijjanakanti [M 0.0023] chijjanayuttaṃ, chijjanārahanti attho. “Caṅkamitaṭṭhānaṃ dassessāmī”ti iminā vattasīsena caṅkamanaṃ vaṭṭatīti dasseti. “Bhijjatī”ti iminā abhijjamāne gaṇṭhipi kātabboti dasseti. Dārumakkaṭakanti makkaṭassa hattho makkaṭo upacārena, makkaṭo viyāti makkaṭako, sadisatthe ko. Dārusaṅkhāto makkaṭako dārumakkaṭako. Taṃ ākoṭentīti sambandho. Aniyāmitattāti imanti aniyāmitattā vacanassa. Idaṃ mahāsāmaññaṃ, visesasāmaññampi vaṭṭatīti āha “nāmaṃ gahetvāpī”tiādi. Sabbanti sabbaṃ vacanaṃ.

'Chijjanaka' means 'fit for breaking,' 'worthy of breaking'—this is the meaning. By the statement 'I will show the place for walking,' with this as a guiding principle, it shows that walking is proper. By the statement 'it breaks,' it shows that even when something does not break, a knot should be made. 'Wooden monkey' (dārumakkaṭaka): a monkey's hand is a 'monkey' by metaphor; 'monkey-like' (makkaṭako) means 'like a monkey' (makkaṭo viya), the suffix '-ka' being in the sense of similarity. A monkey-like thing made of wood is a 'wooden monkey.' The connection is 'striking it.' 'Because of being unspecified' means because the statement is unspecified. This is a great generality; to show that a specific generality also applies, he says 'even having taken the name,' and so forth. 'All' refers to the entire statement.

“Imaṃ jānātiādīsū”ti padaṃ “evamattho daṭṭhabbo”ti pade ādhāro. Imaṃ mūlabhesajjaṃ jānāti imaṃ mūlabhesajjaṃ yojituṃ jānāti yojanā. Ettāvatāti “imaṃ jānā”tiādivacanamattena. Kappiyanti samaṇavohārena, vohārassa vā yuttaṃ anurūpaṃ. Etthāti “kappiyaṃ [V 1.0020] kātabba”nti vacane. Nibbaṭṭabījamevāti phalato nibbaṭṭetvā visuṃ kataṃ bījaṃ eva. Tatthāti sutte. Karontena bhikkhunā kātabbanti yojanā. “Kappiyanti vatvāvā”ti iminā paṭhamaṃ katvā aggisatthanakhāni uddharitvā pacchā vattuṃ na vaṭṭatīti dasseti. Lohamayasatthassāti ayatambādilohamayassa satthassa. Tehīti manussādīnaṃ nakhehi. Tehīti assādīnaṃ khurehi. Tehīti hatthinakhehi. Yehīti nakhehi. Tatthajātakehipīti tasmiṃ satthe jātakehipi, nakhehīti sambandho.

The phrase 'in "He knows this," and so on' is the location for the phrase 'the meaning should be seen thus.' The construction is: 'He knows this root medicine; he knows how to prepare this root medicine.' 'By this much' means just by the statement 'he knows this,' and so on. 'Permissible' means according to monastic convention, or what is suitable and appropriate to the convention. 'Here' means in the statement 'it should be made permissible.' 'Only a seed that has been produced' means a seed that has been produced from the fruit and separated. 'There' means in the Sutta. The construction is: 'it should be done by the monk who is doing it.' By the phrase 'or having said "permissible"', it shows that it is not proper to speak afterwards, having first removed the seeds by means of fire, a knife, or a fingernail. 'Of a metal knife' means of a knife made of iron, copper, or similar metal. 'With these' means with the nails of humans and others. 'With these' means with the hooves of horses and others. 'With these' means with the nails of elephants. 'With which' means with the nails. 'Even with those grown there' means even with those grown on that knife; the connection is with 'nails'.

Tatthāti purimavacanāpekkhaṃ. “Kappiyaṃ karontenā”tiādivacanamapekkhati. “Ucchuṃ kappiyaṃ karissāmī”ti ucchumeva vijjhati, pageva. “Dāruṃ kappiyaṃ karissāmī”ti ucchuṃ vijjhati, “dāruṃ kappiyaṃ karissāmī”ti dārumeva vā vijjhati, vaṭṭati ekābaddhattāti vadanti. Tanti rajjuṃ vā valliṃ vā. Sabbaṃ khaṇḍanti sambandho. Tatthāti maricapakkesu. Kaṭāhanti ekāya bhājanavikatiyā nāmametaṃ. Idha pana bījānaṃ bhājanabhāvena taṃsadisattā phalapheggupi “kaṭāha”nti vuccati. Ekābaddhanti kaṭāhena ekato ābaddhaṃ.

'There' is with reference to the preceding statement. It refers to the statement beginning 'by one making it permissible.' 'Saying, "I will make the sugarcane permissible," one pierces only the sugarcane, and nothing else.' 'Saying, "I will make the wood permissible," one pierces the sugarcane, or saying, "I will make the wood permissible," one pierces only the wood; it is valid because it is bound together as one,' they say. 'That' refers to a rope or a vine. The connection is 'the whole piece.' 'There' refers to in ripe peppercorns. 'Pot' (kaṭāha) is the name for a certain type of vessel. Here, however, because it serves as a container for seeds and is similar to that, even the pulp of a fruit is called a 'pot.' 'Bound together as one' means bound together as one with the pot.

Tānīti tiṇāni. Tenāti rukkhapavaṭṭanādinā. Tatrāti tasmiṃ ṭhapanapātanaṭṭhāne. “Manussaviggahapārājikavaṇṇanāya”nti padaṃ “vutta”nti pade [M 0.0024] sāmaññādhāro. Bhikkhu ajjhotthaṭo hotīti sambandho. Opāteti āvāṭe. So hi avapatanaṭṭhānattā “opāto”ti vuccati. Rukkhanti ajjhotthaṭarukkhaṃ. Bhūminti opātathirabhūmiṃ. Jīvitahetūti nimittatthe paccattavacanaṃ, jīvitakāraṇāti attho. “Bhikkhunā”ti padaṃ “nikkhāmetu”nti pade bhāvakattā, kāritakattā vā. “Ajjhotthaṭabhikkhu”nti vā “opātabhikkhu”nti vā kāritakammaṃ ajjhāharitabbaṃ. Tatthāti anāpattibhāve, anāpattibhāvassa vā. Etassāti suttassa. Paro pana kāruññena karotīti sambandho. Etampīti kāruññampi. Hīti saccaṃ, yasmā vāti. Paṭhamaṃ.

'Those' means grasses. 'By that' means by felling a tree, and so on. 'There' means in that place of placing or felling. The phrase 'in the explanation of the defeat offense concerning a human being' is a general location for the word 'said.' The connection is 'a monk is crushed.' 'Causes to fall into' (opāteti) means into a pit (āvāṭe). For it is called a 'pit' (opāto) because it is a place for falling down. 'The tree' means the crushing tree. 'The ground' means the firm ground of the pit. 'For the sake of life' is an expression in the singular in the sense of cause; the meaning is 'for the reason of life.' The word 'by a monk' is the agent of the state or the causative agent in the word 'should remove.' The causative object should be supplied as either 'the crushed monk' or 'the monk in the pit.' 'There' means in the state of there being no offense, or of the state of there being no offense. 'Of this' means of this rule. But the connection is 'another acts out of compassion.' 'This too' means compassion also. 'Hi' means truly, or because. The first.

2. Aññavādakasikkhāpadaṃ

2. The Training Rule on Speaking Evasively.

94. Dutiye anācāranti acaritabbaṃ kāyavacīdvāravītikkamaṃ. Sabbanāmassa aniyamatthattā idha vacananti āha “aññena vacanena aññaṃ vacana”nti. Soti bhikkhu, vadatīti sambandho. Koti ko puggalo. Kinti kiṃ āpattiṃ. Kisminti kismiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Kinti kiṃ kammaṃ. Kanti kaṃ puggalaṃ. Kinti kiṃ vacanaṃ.

94. In the second, 'improper conduct' means a transgression through the doors of body and speech that should not be practiced. Because a pronoun has an unfixed meaning, here he says 'utterance': 'with one utterance, another utterance.' 'He' means a monk; the connection is 'speaks.' 'Who' means what person. 'What' means what offense. 'In what' means in what matter. 'What' means what action. 'Whom' means what person. 'What' means what utterance.

Etthāti [V 1.0021] “ko āpanno”tiādipāḷiyaṃ. “Bhikkhūhī”ti padaṃ “vutto”ti pade kattā. Asāruppanti bhikkhūnaṃ asāruppaṃ. Esoti eso attho, vibhavoti attho. Etanti vatthu. Bhaṇanto vā hutvā aññenaññaṃ paṭicaratīti sambandho. Etthāti paṭicchannāsane. Sotanti sotadvāraṃ. Cakkhunti cakkhudvāraṃ.

'Here' means in the Pāli text beginning 'who has committed an offense.' The word 'by the monks' is the agent in the word 'spoken.' 'Unsuitable' means unsuitable for monks. 'This' means this meaning; 'exposition' means meaning. 'This' means the matter. The connection is 'or having spoken, he evades one thing with another.' 'Here' means in a concealed seat. 'Ear' means the ear-door. 'Eye' means the eye-door.

98. Aññanti pucchitatthato aññaṃ apucchitamatthaṃ. Bhāvappadhānoyaṃ kattuniddesoti āha “aññenaññaṃ paṭicaraṇassetaṃ nāma”nti. Tuṇhībhāvassāti abhāsanassa. Ātyūpasaggo luttaniddiṭṭhoti āha “āropetū”ti. Evaṃ “aropite”ti etthapi. Tenāha “anāropite”ti.

98. 'Another' means another matter, one not asked about, other than the matter that was asked. This designation of the agent emphasizes the state, hence he says: 'this is the name for the act of evading one thing with another.' 'Of silence' means of not speaking. The prefix 'ati' is indicated as elided, hence he says 'having imputed.' Similarly here too with 'imputed.' Therefore he says 'not imputed.'

101. Tanti aññavādakavihesakaropanakammaṃ. Assāti bhaveyya, hoti vā.

101. 'That' means the act of imputing vexation by speaking evasively. 'Would be' means it might be, or it is.

102. Kinti [M 0.0025] kiṃ vacanaṃ. Yenāti yena byādhinā kathetuṃ na sakkoti, tādiso byādhi mukhe hotīti yojanā. Tappaccayāti tato kathitakāraṇāti. Dutiyaṃ.

102. 'What' means what speech. 'By which' means by which illness he is unable to speak; the construction is that such an illness is in his mouth. 'Because of that' means because of that stated reason. The second.

3. Ujjhāpanakasikkhāpadaṃ

3. The Training Rule on Fault-Finding.

103. Tatiye bhikkhū ujjhāpentīti ettha “bhikkhū”ti kāritakammattā karaṇatthe upayogavacananti āha “tehi bhikkhūhī”ti. Okāraviparīto ukāroti ca jhesaddo ñāṇatthoti ca dassento āha “avajānāpentī”ti. “Taṃ āyasmanta”nti padaṃ “avajānāpentī”ti pade dhātukammaṃ. Anekatthattā dhātūnaṃ jhesaddo olokanattho ca cintanattho ca hoti, tenāha “olokāpentī”tiādi. Etthāti “bhikkhū ujjhāpentī”ti pade. Chandāyāti chandatthaṃ. Yesaṃ senāsanāni ca paññapeti, bhattāni ca uddisati, tesaṃ attani pematthanti attho. Aṭṭhakathāyaṃ pana “chandāyāti chandenā”ti vuttaṃ. Iminā liṅgavipallāsanayo vutto. Paresaṃ attano pemenāti attho. Pakkhapātenāti attano pakkhe pātāpanena.

103. In the third case, 'the monks complain.' Here, the term 'monks', being the causative object, is a statement of application in the instrumental sense; thus he says, 'by those monks.' Showing that the 'u' sound is the reverse of the 'o' sound and that the word 'jhe' signifies knowledge, he says, 'they cause to despise.' The phrase 'that venerable one' is the object of the root of the verb 'they cause to despise.' Due to the multiple meanings of roots, the word 'jhe' also has the meanings of looking at and thinking about; therefore he says, 'they cause to look down upon,' etc. Here means in the phrase 'the monks complain.' 'Chandāya' means for the sake of desire. For those for whom he arranges lodgings and designates meals, it means affection for oneself. However, in the commentary, it is said, 'chandāya means with desire,' and by this, the method of gender transposition is stated. It means by one's own affection for others. 'By partiality' means by causing to fall into one's own faction.

105. Ujjhāpenti anenāti ujjhāpanakaṃ. Khiyyanti anenāti khiyyanakanti dassento āha “yena vacanenā”tiādi.

105. 'That by which they complain' is 'complaining.' 'That by which they are vexed' is 'vexing'; showing this, he says, 'by which speech,' and so on.

106. Upasampannaṃ saṅghena sammataṃ maṅkukattukāmoti sambandhaṃ dassento āha “upasampannaṃ saṅghena [V 1.0022] sammata”ntiādi. Sambajjhanaṃ sambandho, kātabboti yojanā. Upasampannassa saṅghena sammatassa avaṇṇaṃ kattukāmo ayasaṃ kattukāmoti vibhattivipariṇāmena sambandhaṃ dassento āha “vibhattivipariṇāmo kātabbo”ti. “Vasenā”ti padaṃ vibhattivipariṇāmo kātabbo”ti pade visesanaṃ. Yasmā viseso natthi, tasmā katanti yojanā. Tanti “khiyyanaka”nti padaṃ. So ca bhikkhūti ujjhāpanako ca khiyyanako ca so ca bhikkhu. Athāti tasmā ujjhāpanakakhiyyanakakarattā. Assāti bhikkhuno. Assāti bhaveyya.

106. Showing the connection in 'wishing to make one who is fully ordained and approved by the Sangha dispirited,' he says, 'one who is fully ordained and approved by the Sangha,' and so on. Connecting is the connection; 'should be made' is the construction. Showing the connection by means of a change of case—as 'wishing to speak ill of, wishing to defame, one who is fully ordained and approved by the Sangha'—he says, 'a change of case should be made.' The word 'vasenā' is a qualifier for the phrase 'a change of case should be made.' Because there is no difference, the construction is 'it is made.' 'That' refers to the word 'khiyyanaka.' 'And that monk' means both the one who causes complaining and the one who causes vexation, that very monk. 'Atha' means therefore, because of being one who causes complaining and vexation. 'Assa' means 'of the monk.' 'Assa' also means 'it would be'.

“Upasampanna”nti [M 0.0026] padaṃ “ujjhāpetī”ti pade dhātukammaṃ “anupasampanna”nti padaṃ kāritakammaṃ, “anupasampanna”nti padaṃ “ujjhāpetī”ti kāritakiriyaṃ apekkhitvā kammaṃ hoti. “Khiyyatī”ti suddhakiriyāya apekkhāya vibhattivipallāso hotīti āha “tassa vā”tiādi. Tassāti anupasampannassa santiketi sambandho. Tanti saṅghena sammataṃ upasampannaṃ. “Saṅghena asammata”nti ettha na apalokanakammena asammataṃ, kammavācāya pana asammatanti āha “kammavācāyā”tiādi. Dve tayo hutvā kammavācāya sammanitumasakkuṇeyyattā asammatanti ca dassento āha “yatrā”tiādi. Yatrāti yasmiṃ vihāre. “Anupasampannaṃ saṅghena sammata”nti ettha anupasampannassa sammutiyo dātumasakkuṇeyyattā pubbavohāravasena sammatanti vuttanti dassento āha “kiñcāpī”tiādi. Tanti anupasampannabhāve ṭhitaṃ. Byattassāti viyattassa. Saṅghena vā katoti yojanāti. Tatiyaṃ.

The word 'upasampanna' is the object of the root in the word 'ujjhāpeti'; the word 'anupasampanna' is the causative object. The word 'anupasampanna' becomes the object with respect to the causative action 'ujjhāpeti.' Because there is a transposition of case with respect to the simple action 'khiyyati,' he says, 'tassa vā,' and so on. 'Tassa' means 'in the presence of the unordained one'; this is the connection. 'That' means the fully ordained one approved by the Sangha. Here, 'not approved by the Sangha' means not unapproved by an act of information, but unapproved by a formal act; thus he says, 'by a formal act,' and so on. And showing that they are unapproved because of the inability to approve by a formal act when there are only two or three, he says, 'yatrā,' and so on. 'Yatrā' means in which monastery. In 'an unordained one approved by the Sangha,' showing that it is said to be 'approved' based on previous convention, since it is impossible to give approvals to an unordained one, he says, 'kiñcāpi,' and so on. 'That' refers to one standing in the state of being unordained. 'Byattassa' means 'of one who is competent.' Or 'done by the Sangha' is the construction. The third.

4. Paṭhamasenāsanasikkhāpadaṃ

4. The First Training Rule Concerning Lodgings.

108. Catutthe himameva himanto, himante niyutto hemantiko, kāloti āha “hemantakāle”ti. Otāpentā pakkamiṃsūti sambandho. Kālasaddassa sambandhisaddattā sambandhāpekkhoti āha “yassa kassacī”ti. Himavassenāti himena ca vassena ca.

108. In the fourth explanation, cold itself is 'himanto.' One appointed to the cold season is 'hemantiko.' 'Kālo' means time; thus he says 'hemantakāle' (in the winter season). 'Having warmed themselves, they departed' is the connection. Because the word 'kāla' is a relative word, it expects a relation; thus he says 'yassa kassaci' (of whosoever). 'Himavassena' means by cold and by rain.

110. “Vassiko”ti na saṅketāti avassikasaṅketā. “Aṭṭha māse”ti sāmaññato vuttepi “avassikasaṅkete”ti visesitattā hemantikagimhikamāsāyeva gahetabbāti āha “cattāro hemantike”tiādi. Yatthāti yasmiṃ rukkhe. Na ūhadantīti sambandho. “Kākā vā”ti ettha vāsaddo sampiṇḍanattho. Tenāha “aññe vā sakuntā”ti. Tasmāti yasmā anujānāti, tasmā. Yatthāti yasmiṃ rukkhe, vissamitvā gacchantīti yojanā. Yasminti rukkhe, katvā vasantīti yojanā. Aṭṭha māse evāti sambhavato āha “yesu janapadesū”tiādi[V 1.0023]. Tesupīti janapadesupi. Avassikasaṅkete evāti sambhavato āha “yatthā”tiādi. Yatthāti yesu [M 0.0027] janapadesu. “Vigatavalāhakaṃ visuddhaṃ nabhaṃ hotī”ti iminā sace avigatavalāhakaṃ avisuddhaṃ nabhaṃ hoti, nikkhipituṃ na vaṭṭatīti dīpeti. “Evarūpe kāle”ti padaṃ “nikkhipituṃ vaṭṭatī”ti pade ādhāro.

110. 'Vassiko' means not by agreement, thus 'avassikasaṅketā' (not by agreement for the rainy season). Although 'eight months' is stated generally, because it is specified as 'not by agreement for the rainy season,' only the months of the cold and hot seasons should be taken; thus he says, 'four in the cold season,' etc. 'Yattha' means in which tree. 'They do not defecate' is the connection. In 'or crows,' the word 'vā' has the meaning of inclusion. Therefore, he says, 'or other birds.' 'Tasmā' means because he permits, therefore. 'Yattha' means in which tree; 'having rested, they depart' is the construction. 'Yasmin' means in which tree; 'having made nests, they dwell' is the construction. Because 'only eight months' is possible, he says, 'in which regions,' etc. 'Tesupi' means even in those regions. Because 'only not by agreement for the rainy season' is possible, he says, 'where,' etc. 'Yattha' means in which regions. By 'the sky is free of clouds and clear,' it is indicated that if the sky is not free of clouds and not clear, it is not allowable to deposit it. The phrase 'at such a time' is the locative support for the phrase 'it is allowable to deposit'.

Abbhokāsikenāpīti abbhokāsadhutaṅgayuttenāpi. Pisaddo rukkhamūlikassa apekkhako. Vattaṃ vitthārento āha “tassa hī”tiādi. Tassāti abbhokāsikassa. Hisaddo vitthārajotako. Tatthevāti puggalikamañcakeyeva. Saṅghikaṃ mañcanti sambandho. Vītamañcakoti vāyitamañcako. Tasminti vītamañcake. Purāṇamañcako nassantopi anagghoti āha “purāṇamañcako gahetabbo”ti. Cammena avanahitabboti onaddho, so eva onaddhako. Gahetvā ca pana paññapetvā nipajjituṃ na vaṭṭatīti yojanā. Asamayeti vassikasaṅkhāte akāle. Catugguṇenāpīti catupaṭalenapi. Vaṭṭanti valāhakā āvaṭṭanti asmiṃ samayeti vaṭṭulo, so eva vaṭṭaliko, sattāhaṃ vaṭṭaliko, sattāho vā vaṭṭaliko sattāhavaṭṭaliko, so ādi yesaṃ tānīti sattāhavaṭṭalikādīni. Ādisaddena sattāhato ūnādhikāni gahetabbāni. Kāyānugatikattāti kāyaṃ anugamakattā kāyasadisattāti attho.

'Abbhokāsikenāpi' means even by one endowed with the ascetic practice of dwelling in the open air. The word 'pi' is in relation to the tree-root dweller. Expanding on the duty, he says, 'tassa hi,' etc. 'Tassa' refers to the open-air dweller. The word 'hi' indicates elaboration. 'Tattheva' means on the individual bed itself. The connection is 'a communal bed.' 'Vītamañcako' means a woven bed. 'Tasmin' refers to that woven bed. Even if an old bed is perishing, it is not without value; thus he says, 'an old bed should be taken.' 'To be covered with hide' is 'onaddho,' which is 'onaddhako.' 'However, having taken and prepared it, it is not proper to lie down' is the construction. 'Asamaye' means at an improper time, reckoned as the rainy season. 'Catugguṇenāpi' means even with four layers. 'Clouds gather and swirl at this time' is 'vaṭṭulo,' which is 'vaṭṭaliko.' 'Sattāhaṃ vaṭṭaliko' or 'sattāho vā vaṭṭaliko' is 'sattāhavaṭṭaliko.' Those things which have that as their beginning are 'sattāhavaṭṭalikādīni.' By the word 'ādi,' periods less or more than seven days should be understood. 'Kāyānugatikattā' means because of following the body, that is, because of being similar to the body.

Paṇṇakuṭīsūti paṇṇena chāditakuṭīsu. Sabhāgabhikkhūnanti attanā sabhāgabhikkhūnaṃ, santikanti sambandho. Anovassake ṭhāneti yojanā. Laggetvāti lambetvā, ayameva vā pāṭho. “Sammajjani”nti padaṃ “gahetvā”ti pade avuttakammaṃ, “ṭhapetabbā”ti pade vuttakammaṃ. Dhovitvāti sammajjaniṃ suddhaṃ katvā. Uposathāgārādīsūtiādisaddena pariveṇādīni gahetabbāni.

'Paṇṇakuṭīsu' means in huts covered with leaves. 'Sabhāgabhikkhūnaṃ' means 'of fellow monks like oneself'; the connection is 'to the presence of.' 'In a place sheltered from rain' is the construction. 'Laggetvā' means having hung up; or this itself is the reading. The word 'sammajjani' (broom) is the unstated object in the word 'gahetvā,' and the stated object in the word 'ṭhapetabbā.' 'Dhovitvā' means having made the broom clean. In 'in the Uposatha hall, etc.,' by the word 'ādi,' monastic cells and so on should be understood.

Yo pana bhikkhu gantukāmo hoti, tenāti yojanā. Tatthāti sālāyaṃ. Yattha katthacīti yasmiṃ kismiñci ṭhāne. Pākatikaṭṭhāneti pakatiyā gahitaṭṭhāne. Tatra tatrevāti tesu tesu cetiyaṅgaṇādīsuyeva[M 0.0028]. Asanasālanti asanti bhakkhanti assaṃ sālāyanti asanā, asanā ca sā sālā ceti asanasālā, bhojanasālāti attho. Tatrāti tassa sammajjantassa, tasmiṃ “vattaṃ jānitabba”nti pāṭhe vā. Majjhatoti pavittato, suddhaṭṭhānatoti attho. Pādaṭṭhānābhimukhāti sammajjantassa pādaṭṭhānaṃ abhimukhā. Vālikā haritabbāti paṃsu ca vālikā ca apanetabbā. Sammuñcanīsalākāya paraṃ pelletabbāti adhippāyo. Bahīti sammajjitabbatalato bahi.

'But if a monk wishes to go, by him' is the construction. 'Tattha' means in the hall. 'Yattha katthaci' means in any place whatsoever. 'Pākatikaṭṭhāne' means in the place usually taken. 'Tatra tatreva' means in those very places, such as the shrine courtyard, etc. 'Asanasālā': they eat, they consume in this hall, thus 'asanā'; it is 'asanā' and it is a 'sālā,' thus 'asanasālā'; the meaning is a dining hall. 'Tatra' means 'of that one sweeping'; or, in the reading 'the duty should be known,' it means 'in that.' 'Majjhato' means from the swept part, that is, from the clean place. 'Pādaṭṭhānābhimukhā' means facing the place for the feet of the one sweeping. 'Sand should be carried away' means dust and sand should be removed. The intention is that it should be pushed beyond with the broomstick. 'Bahī' means outside the surface to be swept.

111. Masārakotīti [V 1.0024] ettha itisaddo nāmapariyāyo, masārako nāmāti attho. Evaṃ bundikābaddhotītiādīsupi. Pāde masitvā vijjhitvā tattha aṭaniyo pavesetabbā etthāti masārako. Bundo eva bundiko, pādo, tasmiṃ ābaddhā bandhitā aṭanī yassāti bundikābaddho. Kuḷīrassa pādo viya pādo yassāti kuḷīrapādako, yathā kuḷīro vaṅkapādo hoti, evaṃ vaṅkapādoti vuttaṃ hoti. Āhacca aṅge vijjhitvā tattha pavesito pādo yassāti āhaccapādako. Āṇinti aggakhilaṃ. Mañcati puggalaṃ dhāretīti mañco. Pīṭhati visamadukkhaṃ hiṃsatīti pīṭhaṃ. Paṇavoti eko tūriyaviseso, tassa saṇṭhānaṃ katvāti attho. Tañhi etarahi buddhapaṭimassa pallaṅkasaṇṭhānaṃ hoti. Tanti kocchaṃ. Karonti kirāti sambandho. Etthāti senāsanaparibhoge. Hīti saccaṃ. Tanti kocchaṃ mahagghaṃ hoti, mahagghattā bhaddapīṭhantipi vuccati. Yenāti yena bhikkhunā. “Thāmamajjhimassā”ti padena pamāṇamajjhimaṃ nivatteti.

111. In 'Masārakoti', the word 'iti' is a synonym for 'name', meaning 'it is called Masāraka'. It is similar in 'bundikābaddhoti' and other such terms. 'Masārako' is so called because pivots are to be inserted therein after handling and piercing its legs. 'Bundikābaddho' means one whose pivot is bound to its leg, where 'bundo' itself is 'bundiko', a leg. 'Kuḷīrapādako' describes one whose leg is like a crab's leg; just as a crab has crooked legs, so this is said to be 'crooked-legged'. 'Āhaccapādako' refers to one whose leg is inserted after striking and piercing a limb. 'Āṇi' means the top peg. 'Mañco' is so called because it supports a person. 'Pīṭhaṃ' is so called because it afflicts or harms with uneven suffering. 'Paṇavo' is a type of musical instrument, and the meaning is 'made in its shape'. For nowadays, it has the shape of the cross-legged posture of a Buddha image. 'Tanti' means a couch. The connection is 'karonti kira' (they indeed make). 'Ettha' refers to the use of a lodging. 'Hi' means 'truly'. That couch is very valuable, and because of its high value, it is also called 'bhaddapīṭhaṃ', an auspicious seat. 'Yena' means 'by which monk'. By the phrase 'Thāmamajjhimassā', it excludes 'moderate in measure'.

Etthāti “anāpucchaṃ vā gaccheyyā”ti pade. Thero āṇāpetīti yojanā. Āṇāpetīti ca āṇa-dhātuyā eva pesanasaṅkhātassa hetvatthassa vācakattā ṇāpesaddo svatthova. Soti daharo. Tathāti yathā therena vutto, tathā katvāti attho. Tatthāti divāṭṭhāne, mañcapīṭhe vā. Tatoti ṭhapanakālato. Paribundheti hiṃ setīti palibodho, parisaddo upasaggo, so vikāravasena aññathā jāto. So palibodho aññattha āvāsādiko, idha pana [M 0.0029] santharāpitamañcādiko. Sāyanti sāyanhe, bhummatthe cetaṃ upayogavacanaṃ. Thero bhaṇatīti sambandho. Tatthāti mañcapīṭhe. “Bālo hotī”ti vatvā tassa atthaṃ dassento āha “anuggahitavatto”ti. Anuggahitaṃ vattaṃ yenāti anuggahitavatto, thero. Tajjetīti ubbejeti. Tasminti dahare. Assāti therassa.

'Ettha' refers to the phrase 'anāpucchaṃ vā gaccheyyā' (or one might go without asking permission). The interpretation is 'thero āṇāpeti' (the elder commands). And as for 'Āṇāpeti', because the root 'āṇā' expresses the causative sense known as 'sending', the word 'ṇāpe' is in its own meaning. 'So' refers to the young monk. 'Tathā' means 'having acted as instructed by the elder'. 'Tattha' refers to the daytime resting place, or the bed and bench. 'Tato' means 'from the time of placement'. 'Palibodho' is so called because it obstructs or hinders. The word 'pari' is a prefix; it has been altered through modification. That obstruction elsewhere refers to lodging and so on, but here it refers to a spread-out bed and so on. 'Sāyaṃ' means 'in the evening'; this is a usage in the sense of the locative. The connection is 'thero bhaṇati' (the elder speaks). 'Tattha' refers to the bed and bench. Having stated 'bālo hoti' (he is a fool), showing its meaning, he says, 'anuggahitavatto'. 'Anuggahitavatto' means 'one by whom the duty has not been undertaken'; the elder. 'Tajjeti' means 'to vex'. 'Tasmin' refers to the young monk. 'Assa' refers to the elder.

Āṇattikkhaṇeyevāti therassa pesanakkhaṇeyeva. Daharo vadatīti yojanā. “Thero”ti padaṃ “vatvā gacchatī”ti padadvaye kattā, “kāretabbo”ti pade kammaṃ. Nanti mañcapīṭhaṃ, “paññapetvā”tipadamapekkhiya evaṃ vuttaṃ. Nanti daharaṃ vā. “Vatvā”ti padamapekkhiya evaṃ vuttaṃ. Tatthevāti mañcapīṭheyeva. Assāti therassa. Tatthāti divāṭṭhāne. Bhojanasālato aññattha gacchantoti bhojanasālato nikkhamitvā mañcapīṭhapaññāpanaṭṭhānato aññaṃ ṭhānaṃ gacchanto, theroti yojanā. Tatthevāti divāṭṭhāneyeva. Yatricchatīti yaṃ ṭhānaṃ gantumicchatīti attho. Antarasannipāteti sakalaṃ ahorattaṃ asannipātetvā antare sannipāte satīti yojanā.

'Āṇattikkhaṇeyeva' means at the very moment of the elder's command. The interpretation is 'daharo vadati' (the young monk speaks). The word 'thero' (elder) is the subject in the two phrases 'vatvā gacchati' (having spoken, he goes), and the object in the phrase 'kāretabbo' (should be made to do). 'Naṃ' (it) refers to the bed or seat, and this is stated considering the word 'paññapetvā' (having prepared). 'Naṃ' can also refer to the young monk, and this is stated considering the word 'vatvā' (having spoken). 'Tattheva' means right there on the bed or seat. 'Assa' refers to the elder. 'Tattha' means at the daytime place. 'Bhojanasālato aññattha gacchanto' means going elsewhere from the dining hall, having departed from the dining hall and going to a place other than where the bed or seat was prepared; the interpretation is 'thero' (the elder). 'Tattheva' means right there at the daytime place. 'Yatricchati' means whichever place he wishes to go—that is the meaning. 'Antarasannipāteti' means not gathering for the entire day and night, but gathering in between—this is the interpretation.

Tatthāti tasmiṃ ṭhāne. Āgantukā gaṇhantīti sambandho. Tatoti gaṇhanato. Tesanti āgantukānaṃ[V 1.0025]. Yehīti āvāsiko vā hotu, āgantuko vā, yehi bhikkhūhi. Teti nisinnakabhikkhū. Uddhaṃ pāḷipāṭhaṃ sāreti pavattetīti ussārako. Dhammakathāyaṃ sādhūti dhammakathiko. Tasminti ussārake vā dhammakathike vā. Ahorattanti aho ca ratti ca ahorattaṃ, accantasaṃyogapadaṃ. Itarasminti paṭhamaṃ nisinnabhikkhuto aññasmiṃ bhikkhumhīti yojanā. Antoupacāraṭṭheyevāti leḍḍupātasaṅkhātassa upacārassa anto ṭhiteyeva, anādare cetaṃ bhummaṃ. Sabbatthāti āpattivāraanāpattivāresu.

'Tattha' means 'in that place'. The connection is 'āgantukā gaṇhanti' (the incoming monks take). 'Tato' means 'from that taking'. 'Tesaṃ' refers to the newcomers. 'Yehi' means 'by whichever monks', whether resident or newcomer. 'Te' refers to the seated monks. 'Ussārako' is one who causes the recitation of the Pāḷi text to proceed further. 'Dhammakathiko' is one who is skilled in giving a Dhamma talk. 'Tasmin' refers to either the reciter or the Dhamma speaker. 'Ahorattaṃ' means 'day and night'; it is a term indicating continuous connection. 'Itarasmin' means 'in the other', that is, 'in another monk other than the first-seated monk'—this is the interpretation. 'Antoupacāraṭṭheyeva' means 'while remaining right inside the precincts reckoned as a clod's throw'; and this is a locative of disregard. 'Sabbattha' means 'in all cases', that is, in the sections on offenses and non-offenses.

112. Cimilikaṃ vātiādīsu vinicchayo evaṃ veditabboti yojanā. Tanti cimilikattharaṇaṃ. Uttari attharitabbanti uttarattharaṇanti dassento [M 0.0030] āha “uttarattharaṇaṃ nāmā”tiādi. Bhūmiyanti sudhādiparikammena akatāyaṃ pakatibhūmiyaṃ. Cammakhaṇḍoti ettha cammaṃyeva ante khaṇḍattā chinnattā cammakhaṇḍoti vuccati. Nanu sīhacammādīni na kappantīti āha “aṭṭhakathāsu hī”tiādi. Hīti saccaṃ. Tasmāti yasmā na dissati, tasmā. Pariharaṇeyevāti attano santakanti paricchinditvā, puggalikanti vā pariggahetvā taṃ taṃ ṭhānaṃ haraṇeyeva. Pādo puñchīyati sodhīyati etāyāti pādapuñchanīti katvā rajjupilotikāyo pādapuñchanīti vuccatīti āha “pādapuñchanī nāmā”tiādi. Mayasaddalopaṃ katvā phalakapīṭhanti vuttanti āha “phalakapīṭhaṃ nāma phalakamayaṃ pīṭha”nti. Phalakañca pīṭhañca phalakapīṭhanti vā dassetuṃ vuttaṃ “atha vā”ti. Etenāti “phalakapīṭha”nti padena. “Saṅgahita”nti pade karaṇaṃ, kattā vā. Bījanipattakanti caturassabījanīyeva sakuṇapattasadisattā bījanipattakaṃ, sadisatthe ko. “Ajjhokāse”ti padaṃ “pacitvā”ti pade ādhāro. Aggisālāyanti agginā pacanasālāyaṃ. Pabbhāreti leṇasadise pabbhāre. Yatthāti yasmiṃ ṭhāne.

112. In 'cimilikaṃ vā' and other such phrases, the decision should be understood thus—this is the interpretation. 'Tanti' means a 'cimilika' covering. Showing that 'uttarattharaṇaṃ' means 'that which is to be spread over', he says: 'uttarattharaṇaṃ nāma...' and so on. 'Bhūmiyaṃ' refers to the natural ground, not prepared with plaster or other finishes. In 'cammakhaṇḍo', it is leather itself which, being a fragment or cut-off piece at the end, is called 'cammakhaṇḍa'. Raising the objection, 'Surely lion skins and so on are not allowable?', he says: 'aṭṭhakathāsu hi...' and so on. 'Hi' means 'truly'. 'Tasmā' means 'since it is not seen, therefore'. 'Pariharaṇeyyeva' means one should carry it to this or that place only after determining it is one's own, or after taking it as personal property. Because 'the foot is wiped or cleaned with it' (pādo puñchīyati sodhīyati etāya), it is a 'pādapuñchanī' (foot-wiper); stating that ropes and rags are called 'pādapuñchanī', he says: 'pādapuñchanī nāma...' and so on. Stating that it is called 'phalakapīṭha' after eliding the word 'maya', he says: 'phalakapīṭhaṃ nāma is a pīṭha made of planks (phalakamayaṃ)'. Or, to show that 'phalakapīṭha' is 'a plank and a seat' (phalakañca pīṭhañca), it is said: 'atha vā'. 'Etena' means by the word 'phalakapīṭha'. In the word 'saṅgahitaṃ', it is either the instrument or the agent. 'Bījanipattakaṃ' is a square fan, so called because of its similarity to a bird's wing; the suffix 'ka' is in the sense of similarity. The word 'ajjhokāse' is the location for the word 'pacitvā'. 'Aggisālāyanti' means 'in a hall for cooking with fire'. 'Pabbhāre' means in a mountain slope similar to a cave. 'Yattha' means 'in which place'.

Yasminti puggale. “Attano puggalikamiva hotī”ti iminā anāpattīti dasseti.

'Yasmiṃ' refers to 'in that person.' By this, 'it is as if it were one's own personal possession,' he shows that there is no offense.

113. Yo bhikkhu vā lajjī hoti, tathārūpaṃ bhikkhuṃ vā ti yojanā. “Lajjī hotī”ti vatvā tassa atthaṃ dassento āha “attano palibodhaṃ viya maññatī”ti. Yoti āpucchako bhikkhu. “Kenaci upaddutaṃ hotī”ti saṅkhepena vuttamatthaṃ vitthārento āha “sacepi hī”tiādi. Hisaddo vitthārajotako. Vuḍḍhataro bhikkhu gaṇhātīti sambandho. Taṃ padesanti senāsanaṭṭhapitaṭṭhānaṃ. Āpadāsūti vipattīsūti. Catutthaṃ.

113. The interpretation is: 'a monk who is modest, or such a monk.' Having said 'he is modest,' explaining its meaning, he says: 'he regards it as an impediment to himself.' 'Yo' refers to the monk who asks. Expanding on the meaning briefly stated as 'he is harassed by anyone,' he says: 'even if indeed...' and so on. The word 'hi' indicates expansion. The connection is that an elder monk takes it. 'Taṃ padesaṃ' refers to the place where the lodging is established. 'Āpadāsu' means 'in times of adversity.' The fourth.

5. Dutiyasenāsanasikkhāpadaṃ

5. The Second Training Rule on Lodgings.

116. Pañcame [V 1.0026] mañcakabhisīti mañce attharitabbo mañcako, soyeva bhisīti mañcakabhisi. Evaṃ pīṭhakabhisipi. Pāvāro kojavoti dveyeva paccattharaṇanti vuttāti āha “pāvāro”tiādi. Vuttanti aṭṭhakathāsu [M 0.0031] vuttaṃ. Dutiyātikkameti dutiyapādātikkame. Senāsanatoti sace ekaṃ senāsanaṃ hoti, tato. Atha bahūni senāsanāni honti, sabbapacchimasenāsanato. Eko leḍḍupāto senāsanassa upacāro hoti, eko parikkhepārahoti āha “dve leḍḍupātā”ti.

116. In the fifth, regarding 'mañcakabhisi': a 'mañcaka' is what is to be spread on a 'mañca' (bedstead); that itself is a 'bhisi' (mattress), thus 'mañcakabhisi'. Similarly for 'pīṭhakabhisi' (bench mattress). Because it is said that 'pāvāra' and 'kojava' are the only two coverlets, he says: 'pāvāro...' and so on. 'Vuttaṃ' means 'it is stated in the commentaries'. 'Dutiyātikkame' means 'in exceeding the second footstep'. 'Senāsanato' means: if there is one lodging, then from that; if there are many lodgings, then from the very last lodging. He says 'dve leḍḍupātā' (two clod-throws) because one clod-throw is the precinct of the lodging, and one is the extent of the boundary.

Sace bhikkhu, sāmaṇero, ārāmiko cāti tayo honti, bhikkhuṃ anāpucchitvā sāmaṇero vā ārāmiko vā na āpucchitabbo. Atha sāmaṇero, ārāmiko cāti dve honti, sāmaṇeraṃ anāpucchitvā ārāmikova na āpucchitabboti dassento āha “bhikkhumhi satī”tiādi. Tīsupi asantesu āpucchitabbavidhiṃ dassetuṃ vuttaṃ “tasmimpi asatī”tiādi. Yenāti upāsakena, “kārito”ti pade kattā. Tassāti vihārasāmikassa. Tasmimpi asati gantabbanti yojanā. Pāsāṇesūti pāsāṇaphalakesu. Sace ussahatīti sace sakkoti. Ussahantena bhikkhunā ṭhapetabbanti yojanā. Tepīti upāsakāpi, na sampaṭicchantīti sambandho. Tatthāti dārubhaṇḍādīsu.

If there are three—a monk, a novice, and a monastery attendant—then without asking the monk, neither the novice nor the monastery attendant should be asked. But if there are two—a novice and a monastery attendant—then without asking the novice, the monastery attendant should not be asked; this he shows by saying, 'when a monk is present,' and so on. To show the method of asking when none of the three are present, it is said, 'when even he is absent,' and so on. By 'by whom' is meant by the lay supporter, the agent in the word 'caused to be made.' 'Of him' means of the owner of the monastery. The construction is: 'when even he is absent, one should go.' 'On stones' means on stone slabs. 'If one is able' means if one is capable. The construction is: 'it should be placed by a monk who is able.' 'They also' means the lay supporters also; the connection is 'they do not accept.' 'Therein' means in wooden goods and so on.

Paricchedākārena veṇīyati dissatīti pariveṇaṃ. “Atha kho”ti padaṃ “veditabba”nti pade arucilakkhaṇaṃ. “Āsanne”ti iminā upacārasaddassa upaṭṭhānatthaaññaropanatthe nivatteti. Yasmā vammikarāsiyeva hoti, tasmāti yojanā. Upacinantīti upacikā, tāhi nimittabhūtāhi palujjati nassatīti attho. Senāsananti vihāraṃ. Khāyitunti khādituṃ, ayameva vā pāṭho. Tanti mañcapīṭhaṃ. Mañcapīṭhaṃ vihāre apaññapetvā vihārūpacāre paññāpanassa visesaphalaṃ dassetuṃ āha “vihārūpacāre panā”tiādi. Vihārūpacāre paññapitanti sambandho.

Because it is seen as delimited, it is called a precinct. The phrase 'but then' indicates a lack of interest in the word 'should be understood.' By the word 'nearby,' he prevents the word 'environs' from having the meaning of attendance or substitution. The construction is: 'because it is just an anthill, therefore…' Those that build up are termites; the meaning is that by them, which are a sign, it is broken and destroyed. 'Lodging' means a monastery. 'To be eaten' means to eat; or this may be the reading. 'That' refers to a bed or bench. To show the special benefit of designating a bed or bench in the monastery's environs, rather than designating it within the monastery, he says, 'but in the monastery's environs,' and so on. The connection is: 'designated in the monastery's environs.'

118. “Gacchantenā”ti padaṃ “gantabba”nti pade kattā. Tathevāti yathā purimabhikkhu karoti, tatheva. Vasantena bhikkhunā paṭisāmetabbanti yojanā. Rattiṭṭhānanti rattiṃ vasanaṭṭhānaṃ.

118. The word 'by one who is going' is the agent in the word 'one should go.' 'Just so' means just as the previous monk does, exactly so. The construction is: 'it should be put away by a monk who is dwelling there.' 'A place for the night' means a place for dwelling at night.

Yā dīghasālā vā yā paṇṇasālā vā upacikānaṃ uṭṭhānaṭṭhānaṃ hoti, tatoti yojanā. Tasminti [V 1.0027] dīghasālādike. Hīti saccaṃ[M 0.0032], yasmā vā, santiṭṭhantīti sambandho. Siluccayoti pabbato, tasmiṃ leṇaṃ siluccayaleṇaṃ, pabbataguhāti attho. Upacikāsaṅkāti upacikānaṃ uṭṭhānaṭṭhānanti āsaṅkā. Tatoti pāsāṇapiṭṭhiyaṃ vā pāsāṇathambhesu vā katasenāsanādito. Āgantuko yo bhikkhu anuvattanto vasatīti sambandho. Soti āgantuko bhikkhu. Puna soti āgantuko bhikkhuyeva. Tatoti gahetvā issariyena vasanato. Ubhopīti āvāsikopi āgantukopi dve bhikkhū. Tesūti dvīsu tīsu. Pacchimassāti sabbapacchimassa. Ābhogenāti ābhogamattena mutti natthi, āpucchitabbamevāti adhippāyo. Aññatoti aññāvāsato. Aññatrāti aññasmiṃ āvāse. Tatthevāti ānītāvāseyeva. Tenāti vuḍḍhatarena, “sampaṭicchite”ti pade kattā. Sampaṭicchiteti vuḍḍhatarena sampaṭicchitepi itarassa gantuṃ vaṭṭati āpucchitattāti vadanti. Naṭṭhaṃ vāti naṭṭhe vā senāsane sati gīvā na hotīti yojanā. Aññassāti avissāsikapuggalassa. Naṭṭhānīti naṭṭhesu mañcapīṭhesu santesu.

The construction is: 'from wherever a long hall or a leaf hall is a place where termites arise.' 'In that' refers to in that long hall and the like. 'Indeed' means truly, or because; the connection is 'they remain.' 'A rock formation' means a mountain; a cave in it is a 'rock-formation cave,' meaning a mountain cave. 'Suspicion of termites' means the suspicion that it is a place where termites arise. 'From that' means from a lodging made on a stone slab or on stone pillars, and so on. The connection is: 'whatever visiting monk dwells in compliance.' 'He' refers to the visiting monk. Again, 'he' refers to the very same visiting monk. 'From that' means from dwelling with authority after having taken it. 'Both' means both the resident monk and the visiting monk, the two monks. 'Among them' means among two or three. 'Of the last' means of the very last. 'By consideration' means there is no release by mere consideration; the intention is that one must ask permission. 'From another' means from another residence. 'Elsewhere' means in another residence. 'Right there' means in the very residence to which it was brought. 'By him' means by the elder, the agent in the word 'when it was accepted.' They say that even when it is accepted by the elder, it is proper for the other to go because permission has been asked. The construction is: 'or when the lodging is lost, there is no obligation.' 'Of another' means of an untrustworthy person. 'When they are lost' means when the beds and benches are lost.

Vuḍḍhataro bhikkhu ca issariyo ca yakkho ca sīho ca vāḷamigo ca kaṇhasappo ca vuḍḍha…pe… kaṇhasappā, te ādayo yesaṃ teti vuḍḍha…pe… kaṇhasappādayo, tesu. Ādisaddena petādayo saṅgaṇhāti. Yatthāti yasmiṃ ṭhāne. Assāti bhikkhuno. “Palibuddho”ti padassa atthaṃ dassetuṃ vuttaṃ “upadduto”ti. Pañcamaṃ.

Among these: an elder monk, a ruler, a yakkha, a lion, a beast of prey, and a black snake; those that have 'elder… (and so on)… black snakes' as their beginning are 'those beginning with an elder… (and so on)… black snake.' By the word 'and so on,' ghosts and the like are included. 'Where' means in which place. 'Of him' means of the monk. To show the meaning of the word 'obstructed,' it is said 'afflicted.' The fifth.

6. Anupakhajjasikkhāpadaṃ

6. The Training Rule on Encroaching

119. Chaṭṭhe rūmbhitvāti nivāretvā, āvaraṇaṃ katvāti attho. Vassaggenāti vassagaṇanāya. Anupakhajjāti ettha khada hiṃsāyanti dhātupāṭhesu (saddanītidhātumālāyaṃ 15 dakārantadhātu) vuttattā khadasaddo hiṃsattho hoti. Anusamīpaṃ upagantvā khadanaṃ hiṃ sanaṃ nāma anusamīpaṃ pavisanamevāti dassento āha “anupavisitvā”ti.

119. In the sixth: 'having obstructed' means having prevented, the meaning is having made a barrier. 'By seniority in the rains' means by the count of rains. In 'encroaching,' because it is said in the lists of roots that the root 'khad' is in the sense of injuring, the word 'khada' has the meaning of injury. To show that injuring by approaching very near is precisely entering very near, he says, 'having entered into.'

120. “Jāna”nti [M 0.0033] ettha jānanākāraṃ dassetuṃ vuttaṃ “anuṭṭhāpanīyo aya”nti. Tenevāti jānanahetunā eva. Assāti “jāna”ntipadassa. Hīti vitthārajotako. Saṅgho pana detīti sambandho. Yassāti vuḍḍhādīsu aññatarassa. Etthāti vuḍḍhagilānādīsu. Gilānassapi detīti yojanā. “Gilāno”ti padaṃ “na pīḷetabbo, anukampitabbo”tipadadvaye vuttakammaṃ. “Kāmañcā”ti padassa anuggahatthajotakattā panasaddo garahatthajotako.

120. Herein, in 'knowing,' to show the manner of knowing, it is said: 'this one is not to be displaced.' 'For that very reason' means solely for the reason of knowing. 'Of this' refers to the word 'knowing.' 'Indeed' is an expletive indicating detail. The connection is: 'the Saṅgha, however, gives.' 'To whom' refers to any one among the elders and so on. 'Herein' refers to among the elders, the sick, and so on. The construction is: 'it is given even to the sick.' The word 'a sick person' is the object stated in the two phrases 'should not be oppressed' and 'should be shown compassion.' Because the word 'and if one wishes' indicates support, the word 'but' indicates censure.

121. Mañcapīṭhānaṃ [V 1.0028] upacāro nāmāti sambandho. Yatoti yato kutoci ṭhānato. Yāva mañcapīṭhaṃ atthi, tāva upacāro nāmāti yojanā. Tasmiṃ upacāre ṭhitassa bhikkhuno upacāreti sambandho.

121. The connection is: it is called the environs of beds and benches. 'From which' means from whichever place. The construction is: as far as the bed or bench extends, so far is it called the environs. The connection is: for a monk standing within those environs, it is the environs.

“Abhinisīdati vā abhinipajjati vā”ti ettha vāsaddassa aniyamavikappatthaṃ dassetuṃ vuttaṃ “abhinisīdanamattenā”tiādi.

Herein, in 'sits down close by or lies down close by,' it is said 'merely by sitting down close by,' and so on, to show that the word 'or' has the meaning of an indefinite alternative.

122. Itoti vārato. Idhāti imasmiṃ pācittiyavāre. Yathā vutto, evanti sambandho. Sabbatthevāti sabbesu eva vihārapariveṇesu. Assāti visabhāgapuggalassa. Idhāpīti imasmimpi sikkhāpade. Tatthāti vissāsikapuggale.

122. 'From this' means from this section. 'Here' means in this section on offenses entailing expiation. The connection is: 'as it was said, so.' 'Everywhere' means in all monasteries and their precincts. 'Of this one' means of a person of a different kind. 'Here also' means in this training rule as well. 'Therein' refers to a trusted person.

123. Pāḷiyaṃ “āpadāsū”tipadaṃ “pavisatī”ti ajjhāhārapadena sambandhitabbanti āha “āpadāsūtiādī”ti. Chaṭṭhaṃ.

123. He says, 'in times of misfortune, and so on,' because in the canonical text the word 'in times of misfortune' should be connected with the supplied word 'he enters.' The sixth.

7. Nikkaḍḍhanasikkhāpadaṃ

7. The Training Rule on Expulsion

126. Sattame ye pāsādā vā yāni vā catussālānīti yojanā. Catasso bhūmiyo etesanti catubhūmakā. Evaṃ pañcabhūmakā. Koṭṭhakānīti dvārakoṭṭhakāni. “Pāsādā”tipadamapekkhiya vuttaṃ “ye”tipadaṃ, “catussālānī”tipade apekkhite “yānī”ti liṅgavipallāso hoti. Senāsanesu ekena payogena bahuke dvāre bhikkhuṃ atikkāmetīti sambandho. Nānāpayogehi nānādvāre bhikkhuṃ atikkāmentassāti yojanā. “Dvāragaṇanāyā”tiiminā payogagaṇanāyātipi atthaṃ ñāpeti atthato pākaṭattā. Anāmasitvāti achupitvā.

126. In the seventh, the construction is: 'whatever palaces or whatever four-halled buildings.' 'Four-storied' means those that have four stories. Likewise for 'five-storied.' 'Chambers' means door-chambers. The word 'whatever' is said with reference to the word 'palaces'; when referring to the word 'four-halled buildings,' there is a change of gender to 'whatever.' The connection is: in a lodging, with a single effort, one makes a monk pass through many doors. The construction is: of one who, with various efforts, makes a monk pass through various doors. By 'by the count of doors,' it also makes known the meaning 'by the count of efforts,' because this is clear from the sense. 'Without handling' means without touching.

Ettakānīti [M 0.0034] etapamāṇāni. Tassāti nikkaḍḍhiyamānassa bhikkhussa. Gāḷhanti daḷhaṃ.

'This many' means of this measure. 'Of him' means of the monk who is being expelled. 'Strongly' means firmly.

127. Idhāpīti imasmimpi sikkhāpade. Pisaddo purimasikkhāpadāpekkho. Sabbatthāti sabbesu sikkhāpadesu. Yatrāti yasmiṃ sikkhāpade.

127. 'Here also' means in this training rule as well. The word 'also' refers to the previous training rule. 'Everywhere' means in all training rules. 'Where' means in whichever training rule.

128. Soti bhaṇḍanakārakakalahakārako bhikkhu. Hīti saccaṃ, yasmā vā. Pakkhanti attano [V 1.0029] pakkhaṃ. Nikkaḍḍhiyamānapuggalapakkhe ummattakassa nikkaḍḍhati vā nikkaḍḍhāpeti vāti sambandhitabbaṃ. Nikkaḍḍhakapuggalapakkhe ummattakassa anāpattīti sambandhitabbanti. Sattamaṃ.

128. 'He' is the monk who makes quarrels and creates strife. 'Indeed' means truly, or because. 'Faction' means one's own faction. On the side of the person being expelled, it should be connected as: 'a mad person expels or causes to be expelled.' On the side of the person expelling, it should be connected as: 'there is no offense for a mad person.' The seventh.

8. Vehāsakuṭisikkhāpadaṃ

8. The Training Rule on a Dwelling in Mid-air

129. Aṭṭhame acchannatalattā upari vehāso etissāti uparivehāsā, sā ca sā kuṭi ceti uparivehāsakuṭīti dassento āha “upariacchannatalāyā”ti. Tassā kuṭiyā sarūpaṃ dassetuṃ vuttaṃ “dvibhūmikakuṭiyā vā”tiādi. “Mañca”nti padaṃ “abhī”tiupasaggena sambandhitabbanti āha “abhibhavitvā”ti. “Nisīdatī”ti kiriyāpadena vā yojetabboti āha “bhummatthe vā”tiādi. Etanti “mañca”ntipade etaṃ vacanaṃ upayogavacanaṃ. Atha vā etanti “mañca”ntipadaṃ upayogavacanavantaṃ. Ettha ca pacchimasambandhe abhītyūpasaggo padālaṅkāramatto padavibhūsanamattoti āha “abhīti idaṃ panā”tiādi. Padasobhaṇatthanti padassa alaṅkāratthaṃ vibhūsanatthaṃ padassa phullitatthanti adhippāyo. Nipatitvāti ettha nītyūpasaggo dhātvatthānuvattakoti āha “patitvā”ti. Atha vā nikkhantatthavācakoti āha “nikkhamitvā vā”ti. Iminā nītyūpasaggassa dhātvatthavisesakataṃ dīpeti, nikkhanto hutvā patitvāti attho. Hīti yasmā. Āṇīti aggakhīlā.

129. In the eighth, to show that 'uparivehāsā' means 'because its upper part is open to the sky (vehāso)', and that 'uparivehāsakuṭī' means 'that dwelling which is an uparivehāsā', it is said: 'with an uncovered upper surface'. To describe the form of that dwelling, it is said: 'a two-storied dwelling', etc. The word 'mañca' should be connected with the prefix 'abhi'—thus it is said: 'having overcome'. Or, it should be connected with the verb 'nisīdati' (sits)—thus it is said: 'in the locative sense', etc. In the word 'mañca', 'etaṃ' is a word of usage. Or, 'etaṃ' means the word 'mañca' has a word of usage. And here, in the latter connection, the prefix 'abhi' is merely an adornment of the word, merely an embellishment of the word—thus it is said: 'but this 'abhi'', etc. 'Padasobhaṇatthaṃ' means 'for the adornment of the word, for the embellishment, for the flourishing of the word'—this is the intention. In 'nipatitvā', the prefix 'nī' follows the meaning of the root—thus it is said: 'having fallen'. Or, it expresses the meaning of 'having gone out'—thus it is said: 'or having gone out'. With this, he clarifies that the prefix 'nī' specifies the meaning of the root: the meaning is 'having gone out and fallen'. 'Hī' means 'because'. 'Āṇī' means 'main pegs'.

131. Yā kuṭi sīsaṃ na ghaṭṭeti, sā asīsaghaṭṭā nāmāti yojanā. “Pamāṇamajjhimassā”tiiminā thāmamajjhimaṃ nivatteti. Sabbaheṭṭhimāhīti [M 0.0035] sabbesaṃ dabbasambhārānaṃ heṭṭhā ṭhitāhi. Tulāhīti gehathambhānamupari vitthāravasena ṭhitehi kaṭṭhavisesehi. Iminā aṭṭhakathāvacanena ca tulāya sarūpaṃ pākaṭaṃ. Keci pana tulāya sarūpaṃ aññathā vadanti. Etenāti “majjhimassa purisassa asīsaghaṭṭā”tivacanena dassitā hotīti sambandho. Hīti saccaṃ. Yā kāci kuṭi vuccatīti yojanā. Uparīti dvibhūmikakuṭiyaṃ bhūmito upari bhūmiyaṃ. Acchannatalāti anullocatalā, avitānatalāti attho. Idha panāti imasmiṃ pana sikkhāpade.

131. 'A dwelling that does not touch the head is called asīsaghaṭṭā'—this is the construction. By 'pamāṇamajjhimassa' (of medium size), one of medium strength is excluded. 'Sabbaheṭṭhimāhi' means 'by those placed below all the materials'. 'Tulāhi' refers to particular pieces of wood placed widthwise above the house posts. By this statement of the commentary, the characteristic of the beam is made clear. Some, however, describe the characteristic of the beam differently. By this—the statement 'asīsaghaṭṭā for a man of medium height'—it is shown—this is the connection. 'Hī' means 'truly'. 'Whatever dwelling is mentioned'—this is the construction. 'Upari' means 'the upper story in a two-storied dwelling, above the ground level'. 'Acchannatalā' means 'an un-overspread surface, a surface without a canopy'—this is the meaning. 'Idha pana' means 'but in this training rule'.

133. Hīti saccaṃ, yasmā vā. Yāyanti yā ayaṃ kuṭi. Tatthāti tassaṃ sīsaghaṭṭakuṭiyaṃ. Anoṇatena bhikkhunāti yojanā. Yassāti kuṭiyā. Aparibhoganti na paribhuñjitabbaṃ, na paribhuñjanārahanti attho. Patāṇīti patanassa nivāraṇā āṇi aggakhīlā. Sā hi ābandhaṃ nayati pavattetīti āṇīti vuccati. Yatthāti yasmiṃ mañcapīṭhe[V 1.0030]. Na nippatantīti nikkhanto hutvā na patanti. Āhaccapādaketi aṅge āhanitvā vijjhitvā tattha pavesitapādake. Nāgadantakādīsūti nāgassa danto viyāti nāgadantako, sadisatthe ko, so ādi yesaṃ teti nāgadantakādayo, tesu. Ādisaddena bhittikhīlādayo saṅgaṇhātīti. Aṭṭhamaṃ.

133. 'Hī' means 'truly', or 'because'. 'Yāyaṃ' means 'which is this hut'. 'Tattha' means 'in that head-bumping hut'. 'By a bhikkhu not bending down'—this is the construction. 'Yassa' refers to the hut. 'Aparibhogaṃ' means 'not to be used, not fit for use'—this is the meaning. 'Patāṇī' means 'pegs preventing falling', i.e., main pegs. Because it leads to and maintains the bond, it is called 'āṇī'. 'Yattha' means 'on whichever bed or bench'. 'Na nippatanti' means 'they do not fall having come out'. 'Āhaccapādake' means 'on that with legs fixed by hammering or piercing into the frame and placed there'. 'Nāgadantakādīsū'ti means 'in those like an elephant's tusk, etc.': 'nāgadantako' means 'like an elephant's tusk', 'ka' is in the sense of similarity; 'nāgadantakādayo' means 'those of which that is the beginning'. By the word 'ādi' (etc.), wall pegs and the like are included. The eighth.

9. Mahallakavihārasikkhāpadaṃ

9. The Training Rule Concerning a Large Dwelling

135. Navame piṭṭhasaṅghāṭassāti dvārabāhāya. Sā hi piṭṭhe dvinnaṃ kavāṭānaṃ saṃ ekato ghāṭo ghaṭanaṃ samāgamo etassatthīti piṭṭhasaṅghāṭoti vuccati. Kurundiyaṃ vuttanti sambandho. Mahāaṭṭhakathāyaṃ vuttanti yojanā. Tanti mahāaṭṭhakathāya vuttavacanaṃ. Evaṃ “tadevā”ti etthāpi. Hīti saccaṃ, yasmā vā. Bhagavatāpīti na mahāaṭṭhakathācariyehi eva vuttaṃ, atha kho bhagavatāpi katoti yojanā. Dvārabandhena aggaḷassa avinābhāvato “aggaḷaṭṭhapanāyā”ti vuttepi aggaḷena saha dvārabandhaṭṭhapanāyāti atthova gahetabboti āha “sakavāṭakadvārabandhaṭṭhapanāyā”ti. Aggaḷoti kavāṭaphalako. Imamevatthanti [M 0.0036] mayā vuttaṃ imaṃ eva atthaṃ sandhāyāti sambandho. Etthāti “aggaḷaṭṭhapanāyā”tivacane. Adhippāyoti bhagavato abhisandhi. Hi-saddo vitthārajotako. Kampatīti bhusaṃ kampati. Calatīti īsaṃ calati. Tenāti tena sithilapatanahetunā. Mātikāyaṃ, padabhājanīyañca “aggaḷaṭṭhapanāyā”tipadassa sambandhābhāvato tassa sambandhaṃ dassetuṃ vuttaṃ “tatthā”tiādi. Tattha tatthāti “aggaḷaṭṭhapanāyā”tivacane na vuttanti sambandho. Atthassa kāraṇassa uppatti atthuppatti, sāyeva aṭṭhuppattīti vuccati tthakārassa ṭṭhakāraṃ katvā. Adhikārato daṭṭhabboti yojanā.

135. In the ninth, 'piṭṭhasaṅghāṭassā'ti refers to the door frame. For it is the joining (saṅghāṭo) of two door panels at the back, hence it is called 'piṭṭhasaṅghāṭo'. The connection is 'as stated in the Kurundi'. The explanation is 'as mentioned in the Great Commentary'. 'Taṃ' refers to the statement in the Great Commentary. Similarly, the same applies to 'tadevā'ti here. 'Hī'ti means 'truly', or 'because'. The explanation for 'bhagavatāpī'ti is that it was not only stated by the teachers of the Great Commentary but also done by the Blessed One. Since a door-frame is inseparable from a bolt, even when 'for placing a bolt' is mentioned, the meaning to be understood is 'for placing the door-frame along with the bolt'. Hence, it is said, 'for placing the door-frame with its panels'. 'Aggaḷo'ti means the door plank. 'Imamevatthanti' is connected as 'having in mind this very meaning that I have stated'. 'Etthā'ti refers to the phrase 'for placing a bolt'. 'Adhippāyo'ti means the Blessed One's intention. The particle 'hi' serves to elaborate. 'Kampatī'ti means it shakes violently. 'Calatī'ti means it moves slightly. 'Tenā'ti refers to that reason of its loosening and falling. In the Mātikā and the Padabhājanīya, since the phrase 'for placing a bolt' lacks a connection, the phrase 'tatthā'tiādi is stated to show its connection. The connection is that 'there' is not stated in the phrase 'for placing a bolt'. The arising of a reason is 'atthuppatti', and this is also called 'aṭṭhuppatti' by changing the 'tth' to 'ṭṭh'. It should be understood from the context.

Yaṃ pana vacanaṃ vuttanti sambandho. Yassāti mahāvihārassa. Uparīti dvārato upari. Tīsu disāsūti ubhosu passesu, uparīti tīsu disāsu. Tatrāpīti khuddake vihārepi. Sāti bhitti. Aparipūraupacārāpīti samantā kavāṭapamāṇena aparipūraupacārāpi. Ukkaṭṭhaparicchedenāti ukkaṃsapamāṇena. Hatthapāsato atirekaṃ na limpitabboti adhippāyo. Tīsu disāsu eva limpitabbo na hoti, lepokāse sati adhobhāgepi limpitabboti āha “sace panassā”tiādi. Assāti vihārassa. Ālokaṃ sandhenti pidahantīti “ālokasandhī”ti vutte vātapānakavāṭakāyevāti dassento āha “vātapānakavāṭakā vuccantī”ti. Vātaṃ pivatīti vātapānaṃ, dvāraṃ, tasmiṃ ṭhitā kavāṭakā vātapānakavāṭakā. Teti vātapānakavāṭakā paharantīti sambandho. Etthāti ālokasandhimhi. Sabbadisāsūti ubhosu passesu, heṭṭhā, uparīti [V 1.0031] catūsu disāsu. “Tasmā”tipadaṃ “limpitabbo vā lepāpetabbo vā”tipadadvaye hetu. Etthāti “ālokasandhiparikammāyā”tipade.

The connection is with the statement 'yaṃ pana vacanaṃ vuttaṃ'. 'Yassā'ti refers to the large dwelling. 'Uparī'ti means above the door. 'Tīsu disāsū'ti means 'in three directions,' which are on both sides and above. 'Tatrāpī'ti includes even the small dwelling. 'Sā'ti means the wall. 'Aparipūraupacārāpī'ti means not fully plastered around, even up to the size of the door. 'Ukkaṭṭhaparicchedenā'ti means by the highest standard. The meaning is that it should not be plastered beyond what is within reach of the hand. It should not be plastered only in the three directions; if there is space for plastering, the lower part should also be plastered, as stated in 'sace panassā'tiādi. 'Assā'ti refers to the dwelling. To show that when 'ālokasandhī'ti is said, meaning 'they close the light openings', it refers specifically to the window shutters, he says 'vātapānakavāṭakā vuccantī'ti. 'Vātapānaṃ' means that which drinks the wind, i.e., a window or a door; the shutters placed on it are 'vātapānakavāṭakā'. The connection is with 'te vātapānakavāṭakā paharantī'ti. 'Etthā'ti refers to the light opening. 'Sabbadisāsū'ti means on both sides, below, and above—in the four directions. The word 'tasmā' is the reason for the two phrases 'limpitabbo vā lepāpetabbo vā'. 'Etthā'ti refers to the phrase 'ālokasandhiparikammāyā'.

Imināti setavaṇṇādinā. Sabbametanti etaṃ sabbaṃ setavaṇṇādikaṃ.

'Iminā'ti means by this, such as white color and so on. 'Sabbametan'ti means all of this, that is, all such as white color and so on.

Yanti kiccaṃ. Kattabbaṃ kiccanti sambandho. Saddantarabyavahitopi dvattisaddo pariyāyasaddena samāso hotīti āha “chadanassa dvattipariyāya”nti. Dve vā tayo vā pariyāyā samāhaṭāti dvattipariyāyaṃ[M 0.0037], samāhāre digu, tisadde pare dvissa akāro hoti. Parikkhepoti anukkamena parikkhepo. Apatyūpasaggassa paṭisedhavācakattā “aharite”ti vuttaṃ. Etthāti “apaharite”ti pade. “Harita”nti iminā adhippetanti sambandho. Ādikappakāle aparaṇṇato pubbe pavattaṃ annaṃ pubbaṇṇaṃ, aparasmiṃ pubbaṇṇato pacchā pavattaṃ annaṃ aparaṇṇaṃ, nakāradvayassa ṇakāradvayaṃ katvā. Tenevāti adhippetattā eva.

'Yaṃ'ti means duty (kiccaṃ). The connection is with 'kattabbaṃ kiccanti'. Even if separated by other words, the word 'dvatti' can be compounded with 'pariyāya', as stated in 'chadanassa dvattipariyāyaṃ'. 'Dve vā tayo vā pariyāyā samāhaṭā'ti means two or three layers combined; it is a 'digu' (numerical) compound in the collective sense. When the word 'ti' follows, the 'i' of 'dvi' becomes 'a'. 'Parikkhepo'ti means encompassing sequentially. Because the prefix 'apa' has the sense of negation, 'aharite'ti is stated. 'Etthā'ti refers to the word 'apaharite'. The connection is with what is intended by 'haritaṃ'. In the primordial age, 'pubbaṇṇaṃ' is the grain that arose before other grains, and 'aparaṇṇaṃ' is the grain that arose after 'pubbaṇṇaṃ', with the two 'n' sounds changed to two 'ṇ' sounds. 'Tenevā'ti means precisely because of being intended.

Vuttanti vapitaṃ, yathā “sumedhabhūto bhagavā”tiettha bodhiṃ asampattopi bodhisatto sumedhabhūto “bhagavā”ti vuccati avassambhāviyattā, evaṃ haritaṃ asampattampi khettaṃ “harita”nti vuccati avassambhāviyattāti atthaṃ dasseti “yasmimpi khette”tiādinā.

'Vutta' means sown. Just as in the phrase 'the Blessed One Sumedha,' the Bodhisatta Sumedha, though he had not yet attained enlightenment, is called 'Blessed One' because of the inevitability of his attainment; so too a field, though it has not yet become green, is called 'green' because of the inevitability of its becoming so. This meaning is shown by the phrase beginning 'yasmimpi khette.'

Ahariteyevāti haritavirahe eva khetteti yojanā. Tatrāpīti aharitakhettepi. “Piṭṭhivaṃsassā”tipadaṃ “passe”tipade sāmyatthachaṭṭhī, iminā pakatigehaṃ dasseti. “Kūṭāgārakaṇṇikāyā”tipadaṃ “upari, thūpikāyā”tipade sāmyatthachaṭṭhī, iminā ekakūṭayutte māḷādike dasseti. Ṭhitaṃ bhikkhunti sambandho. Nisinnakaṃ yaṃkañci jananti yojanā. Tassāti ṭhitaṭṭhānassa. Antoti abbhantare, hi yasmā ayaṃ okāso patanokāsoti yojanā.

'Ahariteyeva' means: in the very absence of green in a field; this is the construction. 'Tatrāpi' means: even in a field without green. The word 'piṭṭhivaṃsassa' is a genitive in the sense of proximity to the word 'passe'; by this, it indicates an ordinary house. The word 'kūṭāgārakaṇṇikāya' is a genitive in the sense of proximity to the words 'upari, thūpikāya'; by this, it indicates a single-peaked pavilion and so on. 'Ṭhitaṃ bhikkhuṃ' is the connection. The construction is: 'any person who is sitting.' 'Tassa' means: of the standing place. 'Anto' means: inside; for this space is a place for falling; this is the construction.

136. Chāditaṃ nāmāti ettha chāditasaddo bhāvattho hoti, tenāha “chādana”nti. Ujukamevāti chadanuṭṭhāpanato uddhaṃ ujukaṃ eva. Tanti chādanaṃ. Apanetvāpīti nāsetvāpi. Tasmāti yasmā labbhati, tasmā, pakkamitabbanti sambandho. Parikkhepenāti parivārena chādentassāti yojanā. Idhāpīti pariyāyachādanepi adhiṭṭhahitvāti sambandho. Tuṇhībhūtenāti tuṇhībhūto hutvā. Chadanuparīti chadanassa upari. Hīti saccaṃ. “Tato ce uttari”nti ettha tato dvattipariyāyato uparīti dassento āha “tiṇṇaṃ maggānaṃ vā”tiādi.

136. Here, in 'chāditaṃ nāma,' the word 'chādita' has the sense of an abstract noun, therefore he said, 'chādanaṃ.' 'Ujukameva' means: straight up from the raising of the covering. 'Taṃ' means that covering. 'Apanetvāpi' means: even after destroying. 'Tasmā' means: because it is obtainable, therefore, 'one should depart'; this is the connection. 'Parikkhepena' means: by surrounding, for one who is covering; this is the construction. 'Idhāpi' means: also here, in the case of a temporary covering, the connection is with 'adhiṭṭhahitvā.' 'Tuṇhībhūtena' means: having become silent. 'Chadanupari' means: above the covering. 'Hi' means: truly. In the phrase 'tato ce uttariṃ,' showing that 'tato' means beyond those two or three layers, he said, 'tiṇṇaṃ maggānaṃ vā,' and so on.

137. Karena [V 1.0032][M 0.0038] hatthena lunitabbo, chinditabbo, lātabbo gahetabboti vā karaḷoti kate atthapakaraṇādito tiṇamuṭṭhi evāti āha “tiṇamuṭṭhiya”nti. Navamaṃ.

137. 'Karena' means with the hand; it should be reaped, cut, or taken, that is, grasped. Therefore, when 'karaḷo' is said, from the context of the meaning and so on, it is precisely a handful of grass; thus he said 'tiṇamuṭṭhiyā.' The ninth.

10. Sappāṇakasikkhāpadaṃ

10. The Training Rule on [That Which] Contains Animate Beings

140. Dasame “jāna”nti gacchantādigaṇoti āha “jānanto”ti. Saṃ vijjati pāṇo etthāti sapāṇakaṃ. Etanti udakaṃ. Sayaṃ jānantopi parena jānāpentopi jānātiyeva nāmāti āha “yathā tathā vā”ti. Sapāṇakaṃ udakanti karaṇatthe cetaṃ upayogavacanaṃ, tenāha “tena udakenā”ti. Pubbeti pathavikhaṇanasikkhāpadādike.

140. In the tenth, 'jānaṃ' belongs to the class of participles beginning with 'gacchanta'; hence he said, 'jānanto.' 'Sapāṇakaṃ' is: a living being exists herein. 'Etaṃ' means this water. Whether knowing by oneself or causing another to know, it is indeed called knowing; hence he said, 'yathā tathā vā.' 'Sapāṇakaṃ udakaṃ' is an expression of use in the instrumental sense; hence he said, 'tena udakena.' 'Pubbe' refers to the previous training rules, such as that on digging the earth.

Tatthāti “siñceyya vā siñcāpeyya vā”tipade. Dhāranti sotaṃ. Mātikaṃ pamukhanti mātikaṃ abhimukhaṃ. Tattha tatthāti tasmiṃ tasmiṃ ṭhāne. Aññato ṭhānato aññaṃ ṭhānaṃ netīti yojanā. “Sapāṇakaṃ udaka”nti sāmaññavacanassapi visese avaṭṭhānato, visesatthinā ca visesassa anupayojitabbato idha visesaudakanti sandhāyabhāsitatthaṃ dassento āha “idaṃ panā”tiādi. Idaṃ pana na vuttanti sambandho. Yanti udakaṃ “gacchatī”tipade kattā. Yatthāti yasmiṃ udaketi. Dasamaṃ.

'Tattha' refers to the phrase 'siñceyya vā siñcāpeyya vā.' 'Dhāraṃ' means a stream. 'Mātikaṃ pamukhaṃ' means towards the water-course. 'Tattha tattha' means in this and that place. The construction is: one leads it from one place to another. Showing that here the intended meaning is a specific kind of water, he said, 'idaṃ pana,' and so on. This is because, although 'sapāṇakaṃ udakaṃ' is a general expression, it is established in a specific sense, and because a specific term was not employed by the one intending a specific meaning. 'Idaṃ pana na vuttaṃ' is the connection. 'Yaṃ' refers to the water; it is the agent in the word 'gacchati.' 'Yattha' means: in which water. The tenth.

Bhūtagāmavaggo dutiyo.

The Second Division on Plant Life.

3. Ovādavaggo

3. The Division on Instruction

1. Ovādasikkhāpada-atthayojanā

1. Exposition of the Training Rule on Instruction

144. Bhikkhunivaggassa paṭhame tesanti therānaṃ. Mahākulehi nikkhamitvā pabbajitāti yojanā. Kuladhītaro vijjamānaguṇaṃ kathayantīti [M 0.0039] sambandho. “Ñātimanussāna”ntipadaṃ “kathayantī”tipade sampadānaṃ. Kutoti kassa therassa santikāti attho. Tesanti therānaṃ guṇanti sambandho. “Kathetu”ntipadamapekkhitvā “vijjamānaguṇe”ti vattabbe avatvā “vaṭṭantī”tipadamapekkhiya [V 1.0033] “vijjamānaguṇā”ti vuttaṃ. Hīti saccaṃ, yasmā vā. Tatoti kathanakāraṇā abhihariṃsūti sambandho. Tenāti abhiharaṇahetunā.

144. In the first of the Bhikkhunī Chapter, 'tesaṃ' means: of the elders. The construction is: 'having gone forth from great families, they were ordained.' The connection is: 'the daughters of good family speak of their existing qualities.' The word 'ñātimanussānaṃ' is the dative in relation to the word 'kathayanti.' 'Kuto' means: from the presence of which elder? 'Tesaṃ' is connected with the qualities of the elders. Although 'vijjamānaguṇe' should have been said in reference to the word 'kathetuṃ', it was not; instead, 'vijjamānaguṇā' was said in reference to the word 'vaṭṭanti.' 'Hi' means truly, or because. 'Tato' means for the reason of speaking; the connection is with 'abhihariṃsu.' 'Tena' means: for the reason of the bringing of offerings.

Tesanti chabbaggiyānaṃ. Tāsūti bhikkhunīsu. “Bhikkhuniyo”tipadaṃ “upasaṅkamitvā”tipade kammaṃ. Chabbaggiyānaṃ bhikkhunīsu upasaṅkamanaṃ lābhataṇhāya hoti, bhikkhunīnaṃ chabbaggīsu upasaṅkamanaṃ calacittatāya hotīti aññamaññūpasaṅkamantānaṃ viseso. Tiracchānabhūtā kathā tiracchānakathā niratthakakathāti dassento āha “tiracchānakathantī”ti. Saggamaggagamanepīti pisaddo mokkhagamane pana kā nāma kathāti dasseti. Rājāno ārabbha pavattā kathā rājakathā. Ādisaddena corakathādayo saṅgaṇhāti.

‘Tesaṃ’ refers to the group of six monks. ‘Tāsu’ refers to the nuns. The word ‘bhikkhuniyo’ is the object of the word ‘upasaṅkamitvā’. The approach of the group of six monks to the nuns is due to craving for gain, while the approach of the nuns to the group of six monks is due to fickleness of mind—this is the distinction between their mutual approaches. ‘Tiracchānabhūtā kathā’ is ‘tiracchānakathā’, meaning animal-like talk, that is, useless talk, as shown by ‘tiracchānakathaṃ’. In ‘saggamaggagamane’pi,’ the particle ‘pi’ indicates that if this is so even for the path to heaven, what then could be said of the path to liberation? Talk concerning kings is ‘rājakathā’. The word ‘ādi’ includes talks about thieves and so on.

147. Te bhikkhūti chabbaggiyā bhikkhū bhaveyyunti sambandho. Adiṭṭhaṃ saccaṃ yehīti adiṭṭhasaccā, tesaṃ bhāvo adiṭṭhasaccattaṃ, tasmā adiṭṭhasaccattā bandhitvāti yojanā. Nesanti chabbaggiyānaṃ. Aññeneva upāyenāti aladdhasammutito aññeneva laddhasammutisaṅkhātena kāraṇena kattukāmoti sambandho. Paratoti parasmiṃ pacchā, uparīti attho. Karonto vāti paribāhire karonto eva hutvā āhāti yojanā. Hīti saccaṃ, yasmā vā. Yasmā na bhūtapubbāni, iti tasmā paribāhiraṃ karonto vāti attho.

147. 'Te bhikkhū' is connected with 'chabbaggiyā bhikkhū bhaveyyuṃ.' 'Adiṭṭhasaccā' are those by whom the truth has not been seen; their state is 'adiṭṭhasaccattaṃ'; therefore, the construction is 'adiṭṭhasaccattā bandhitvā.' 'Nesaṃ' means: of the group of six. 'Aññeneva upāyena' is connected with 'kattukāmo': by another means, that is, by a reason designated as 'having obtained consent,' different from that which has not obtained consent. 'Parato' means: afterwards in another, or above. 'Karonto vā' means: having become one who acts externally, he spoke; this is the construction. 'Hi' means truly, or because. Because they have not existed previously, therefore 'acting externally' is the meaning.

Tatthāti “anujānāmī”tiādivacane. Sīlavāti ettha vantusaddo pasaṃsatthe ca atisayatthe ca niccayogatthe ca hoti. Tassāti laddhasammutikassa. Tanti sīlaṃ. Pātimokkhasaṃvarasaddānaṃ kammadhārayabhāvaṃ, tehi ca saṃvutasaddassa tappurisabhāvaṃ dassetuṃ vuttaṃ “pātimokkhovā”tiādi. Tattha evasaddena kammadhārayabhāvaṃ, enasaddena ca tappurisabhāvaṃ dassetīti daṭṭhabbaṃ.

'Tattha' refers to the statement beginning 'anujānāmi.' In 'sīlavā,' the suffix '-vantu' is used in the sense of praise, excellence, and constant association. 'Tassa' refers to one who has obtained consent. 'Taṃ' refers to virtue. To show that the words 'pātimokkhasaṃvara' form a kammadhāraya compound, and that the word 'saṃvuta' forms a tappurisa compound with them, it was said 'pātimokkho vā,' and so on. Here, it should be understood that the particle 'eva' indicates the kammadhāraya nature, and the particle 'ena' indicates the tappurisa nature.

Vattatīti [M 0.0040] attabhāvaṃ pavatteti. Kāritapaccayo hi adassanaṃ gato. Iminā iriyāpathavihāra dibbavihāra brahmavihāra ariyavihāresu catūsu vihāresu attabhāvavattanaṃ iriyāpathavihāraṃ dasseti. Hīti saccaṃ. Etanti “pātimokkhasaṃvarasaṃvuto viharatī”tivacanaṃ. Vibhaṅgeti jhānavibhaṅge.

'Vattati' means it causes one’s individual existence to proceed. For the causative suffix has become invisible. By this, among the four abodes—the posture abode, the divine abode, the brahma abode, and the noble abode—it shows that the maintenance of individual existence is the posture abode. 'Hi' means truly. 'Etaṃ' refers to the statement, 'He dwells restrained with the restraint of the Pātimokkha.' 'Vibhaṅge' refers to the analysis in the Jhāna Vibhaṅga.

“Sīla”ntiādīni aṭṭha padāni tulyādhikaraṇāni. Ayaṃ panettha sambandho – sīlaṃ kusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ samāpattiyā patiṭṭhā ādi caraṇaṃ saṃyamo saṃvaro mokkhaṃ pamokkhanti. Samāpattiyāti [V 1.0034] samāpattatthāya. “Upeto”tiādīni satta padāni aññamaññavevacanāni. Tattha upapannoti yutto anuyutto. Samannāgatoti samantato anu punappunaṃ āgatoti samannāgato, samaṅgībhūtoti attho. Ettha hi saṃsaddo samantatthavācako, anusaddo naupacchinnatthavācako. Tenāti tena kāraṇena. Pāletīti attabhāvaṃ bādhanato rakkhati. Yapetīti attabhāvo pavattati. Yāpetīti attabhāvaṃ pavattāpeti. Yapa yāpane. Yāpanaṃ pavattananti hi dhātupāṭhesu vuttaṃ (saddanītidhātumālāyaṃ 18 pakārantadhātu). Viharatīti ettha eko ākāratthavācako itisaddo luttaniddiṭṭho, iti vuccati, iti vuttanti vā yojanā.

‘Sīla’ and the following seven terms are in apposition. Here, the connection is this: virtue is the foundation, the beginning, the conduct, restraint, control, liberation, and release for the attainment of wholesome qualities. ‘Samāpattiyā’ means for the purpose of attainment. ‘Upeta’ and the following six terms are synonyms. Among them, ‘upapanna’ means joined, associated. ‘Samannāgata’ means completely and repeatedly arrived at; the meaning is fully equipped. Here, the prefix ‘saṃ-’ conveys the meaning of completeness, and ‘anu-’ conveys the meaning of non-interruption. ‘Tena’ means for that reason. ‘Pāleti’ means it protects one’s own existence from harm. ‘Yapeti’ means one’s own existence proceeds. ‘Yāpeti’ means it causes one’s own existence to proceed. Yapa means to sustain. Sustaining means continuation, as stated in the Dhātupāṭha (Saddanīti Dhātumālā, 18 Pakārantadhātu). In ‘viharati’, the word ‘iti’ which indicates manner is omitted, and the meaning should be construed as ‘thus it is called’, or ‘thus it is said’.

Ācāragocarasaddānaṃ dvandabhāvaṃ, tehi ca sampannasaddassa tappurisabhāvaṃ dassento āha “ācāragocarasampanno”tiādi. Tattha casaddena dvandabhāvaṃ, enasaddena ca tappurisabhāvaṃ dasseti.
