Aṇusaddo appattho, mattasaddo pamāṇatthoti āha “appamattakesū”ti. “Dassanasīlo”tiiminā “dassāvī”tiettha āvīsaddassa tassīlatthabhāvaṃ dasseti. “Samādāyā”ti ettha saṃpubbaāpubbassa dāsaddassa kammāpekkhattā tassa kammaṃ dassetuṃ vuttaṃ “taṃ taṃ sikkhāpada”nti. Iminā “sikkhāpadesū”ti upayogatthe bhummavacananti dasseti. Atha vā sikkhāpadesūti niddhāraṇatthe bhummavacanametaṃ. “Taṃ taṃ sikkhāpada”nti kammaṃ pana ajjhāharitabbanti dasseti. “Samādāyā”ti ettha saṃsaddassa ca āpubbassa dāsaddassa ca yakārassa ca atthaṃ dassetuṃ [M 0.0041] “sādhukaṃ gahetvā”ti vuttaṃ. Etthāti imissaṃ aṭṭhakathāyaṃ. Vitthāro pana gahetabboti yojanā. Yoti kulaputto.

To show the dvandva nature of the words ‘ācāra’ and ‘gocara’, and the tappurisa nature of the word ‘sampanna’ in relation to them, it is said ‘ācāragocarasampanno’ and so on. Here, the particle ‘ca’ shows the dvandva nature, and the particle ‘ena’ indicates the tappurisa nature. The word ‘aṇu’ means insignificant, and the word ‘matta’ means measure, as stated in ‘appamattakesu’. By ‘dassanasīlo’, it shows that the suffix ‘āvī’ in ‘dassāvī’ has the meaning of 'being of that nature'. In ‘samādāya’, because the verb ‘dā’ with the prefixes ‘saṃ’ and ‘ā’ requires an object, the phrase ‘taṃ taṃ sikkhāpada’ is used to show that object. By this, it shows that ‘sikkhāpadesu’ is in the locative case in the sense of use. Alternatively, ‘sikkhāpadesu’ is the locative case in the sense of determination. The phrase ‘taṃ taṃ sikkhāpada’ shows that the object should be supplied. In ‘samādāya’, the meaning of the prefix ‘saṃ’, the prefix ‘ā’, the verb ‘dā’, and the suffix ‘ya’ is shown by the phrase ‘sādhukaṃ gahetvā’. ‘Ettha’ means in this commentary. The construction is that a detailed explanation should be understood. ‘Yo’ refers to a clansman.

Assāti laddhasammutikassa. Yaṃ taṃ bahu sutaṃ nāma atthi, taṃ na sutamattamevāti yojanā. Mañjūsāyanti peḷāyaṃ. Sā hi sāmikassa sadhanattaṃ maññate imāyāti “mañjūsā”ti vuccati. Mañjūsāyaṃ ratanaṃ sannicitaṃ viya sutaṃ sannicitaṃ asmiṃ puggaleti yojanā, etenāti “sannicita”ntipadena, dassetīti sambandho. Soti laddhasammutiko bhikkhu. Sannicitaratanassevāti sannicitaratanassa iva. Tanti “ye te dhammā”tiādivacanaṃ. Etthāti imasmiṃ sikkhāpade. Assāti laddhasammutikassa bhikkhuno. Tatthāti “vacasā paricitā”tiādivacane. Evamattho veditabboti yojanā. Paguṇāti ujukā. Ujuko hi ajimhattā pakaṭṭho uttamo guṇoti atthena “paguṇo”ti vuccati. Anupekkhitāti punappunaṃ upagantvā ikkhitā, passitā dassitāti attho. Atthatoti abhidheyyatthato, aṭṭhakathātoti attho. Kāraṇatoti dhammato, pāḷitoti attho. Diṭṭhisaddassa paññāsaddavevacanattā “paññāyā”ti vuttaṃ. Supaccakkhakatāti suṭṭhu akkhānaṃ indriyānaṃ paṭimukhaṃ katā.

‘Assa’ refers to one who has received the designation. The construction is that what is called ‘much learning’ is not merely heard. ‘Mañjūsāyaṃ’ means in a box. Indeed, because the owner considers it as having wealth by means of this, it is called ‘mañjūsā’. The construction is that just as jewels are accumulated in a treasure box, so too is learning accumulated in this person; by this, that is, by the word ‘sannicita’, it shows this connection. ‘So’ refers to the monk who has received the designation. ‘Sannicitaratanasseva’ means like one who has accumulated jewels. ‘Taṃ’ refers to the statement beginning with ‘ye te dhammā’. ‘Ettha’ means in this training rule. ‘Assa’ refers to the monk who has received the designation. ‘Tattha’ refers to the statement beginning with ‘vacasā paricitā’. The construction is that the meaning should be understood thus. ‘Paguṇa’ means straight. Indeed, one who is straight, being without crookedness, is called ‘paguṇa’ because it is an excellent and superior quality. ‘Anupekkhitā’ means having repeatedly approached and examined, seen, and shown—this is the meaning. ‘Atthato’ means with respect to the expressed meaning, that is, with respect to the commentary. ‘Kāraṇato’ means with respect to the Dhamma, that is, with respect to the Pāḷi. Because the word ‘diṭṭhi’ is a synonym of the word ‘paññā’, it is said ‘paññāya’. ‘Supaccakkhakatā’ means well made manifest to the faculties.

“Bahussuto”ti [V 1.0035] ettha bahussutassa tividhabhāvaṃ dassento āha “ayaṃ panā”tiādi. Nissayato muccatīti nissayamuccanako. Parisaṃ upaṭṭhāpetīti parisupaṭṭhāko. Bhikkhuniyo ovadatīti bhikkhunovādako. Tatthāti tividhesu bahussutesu. Nissayamuccanakena ettakaṃ uggahetabbanti sambandho. Upasampadāyāti upasampādetvā. Pañca vassāni etassāti pañcavasso. Tena uggahetabbanti yojanā. Sabbantimenāti sabbesaṃ paricchedānaṃ ante lāmake pavattena. Paguṇāti ajimhā ujukā. Vācuggatāti tasseva vevacanaṃ. Yassa hi pāḷipāṭhā sajjhāyanakāle paguṇā honti, tassa vācuggatā. Yassa vā pana vācuggatā honti, tassa paguṇā. Tasmā tāni padāni aññamaññakāraṇavevacanāni. Pakkhadivasesūti juṇhapakkhakāḷapakkhapariyāpannesu [M 0.0042] divasesu. Dhammasāvanatthāyāti sampattānaṃ parisānaṃ dhammassa sāvanatthāya suṇāpanatthāyāti adhippāyo. Sāvanatthāyāti ettha yupaccayaparattā kāritapaccayo lopo hotīti daṭṭhabbaṃ. Tasmā sāvīyate suṇāpīyate sāvananti vacanattho kātabbo. Bhāṇavārā uggahetabbāti sambandho. Sampattānanti attano santikaṃ sampattānaṃ. Parikathanatthāyāti parissaṅgena āliṅganena kathanatthaṃ, appasaddasaṅkhātāya vācāya kathanatthanti attho. “Kathāmaggo”ti vuttattā vatthukathāyeva adhippetā, na suttasaṅkhāto pāḷipāṭho. Anu pacchā, punappunaṃ vā dāyakā modanti etāyāti anumodanā. Jhānaṃ vā maggo vā phalaṃ vā samaṇadhammo nāma. Tassa karaṇatthaṃ uggahetabbanti yojanā. Hīti saccaṃ, yasmā vā. Catūsu disāsu apaṭihatoti cātuddiso, apaṭihatatthe ṇapaccayo.

In explaining the term "learned," the threefold nature of being learned is shown by the phrase "ayaṃ panā" and so on. One who is freed from dependence is called 'nissayamuccanaka'. One who attends to the assembly is called 'parisupaṭṭhāka'. One who advises the nuns is called 'bhikkhunovādaka'. Here, among the three types of learned persons. The connection is that 'so much should be learned by one who is freed from dependence'. By `upasampadāya` is meant 'after having given ordination'. By 'five years for this' (pañcavasso) is meant 'one who has completed five years' (since ordination). The construction is 'it should be learned by him'. By 'by the very end' (sabbantimena) is meant 'by the most inferior behavior at the end of all the sections'. By 'fluent' (paguṇā) is meant 'straight, not crooked'. By 'verbalized' (vācuggatā) is meant a synonym for that. For one whose Pāḷi texts are fluent at the time of recitation, they are said to be 'verbalized'. Or, for one whose words are 'verbalized', they are 'fluent'. Therefore, these terms are mutually causal synonyms. By 'on the days of the fortnights' (pakkhadivasesu) is meant 'on the days included in the waxing and waning fortnights'. By 'for the purpose of hearing the Dhamma' (dhammasāvanatthāya) is meant 'for the purpose of making the Dhamma heard to the assembled gatherings', that is, 'for the purpose of making them listen'. Here, in 'sāvanatthāya', it should be understood that the causative suffix is elided due to the following `yu` suffix. Therefore, the meaning of the word should be taken as 'causing to be heard' or 'causing to listen'. The connection is that 'sections should be learned'. By 'arrived' (sampattānaṃ) is meant 'arrived in one's presence'. By 'for the purpose of conversation' (parikathanatthāya) is meant 'for the purpose of talking with embrace or attachment', or 'for the purpose of talking with speech known as a soft sound'. Since 'the way of talk' (kathāmaggo) is mentioned, a narrative is intended, not the recitation of the Pāḷi text known as a sutta. Anumodanā means 'afterwards', or 'again and again, the donors rejoice by this', thus it is 'rejoicing'. Meditation, or the path, or the fruit is called 'ascetic practice' (samaṇadhammo). The construction is 'it should be learned for the purpose of doing that'. By 'hī' is meant 'truly', or 'because'. By 'unobstructed in the four directions' (cātuddiso) is meant 'in all directions'; the suffix ṇa is for the meaning of 'unobstructed'.

Parisupaṭṭhāpakena kātabbāti yojanā. Abhivinayeti aññamaññaparicchinne vinayapiṭake. Dve vibhaṅgāti bhikkhuvibhaṅgo ca bhikkhunivibhaṅgo ca. Asakkontena parisupaṭṭhāpakena bhikkhunāti sambandho. Evaṃ attano atthāya uggahetabbaṃ dassetvā idāni parisāya atthāya uggahetabbaṃ dassento āha “parisāya panā”tiādi. Abhidhammeti aññamaññaparicchinne suttantapiṭake eva, na abhidhammapiṭake. Tayo vaggāti sagāthāvaggo nidānavaggo khandhavaggoti tayo vaggā. Vāsaddo aniyamavikappattho. Ekanti ekaṃ nipātaṃ. Tato tatoti nikāyato. Samuccayaṃ katvāti rāsiṃ katvā. Na vuttanti aṭṭhakathāsu na kathitaṃ. Yassa pana natthi, so na labhatīti yojanā. Suttante cāti suttantapiṭake pana. Uggahitoti sarūpakathanena gahito, uccāritoti attho. Disāpāmokkhoti disāsu ṭhitānaṃ bhikkhuādīnaṃ pāmokkho. Yena kāmaṃ gamoti yathākāmaṃ gamo.

The construction is 'it should be done by one who attends to the assembly'. By 'abhivinaye' is meant 'in the Vinaya Piṭaka, which is distinct and mutually delimited'. The two Vibhaṅgas are the Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga and the Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga. The connection is 'by a monk, an attender of the assembly, who is unable'. Having thus shown what should be learned for one's own benefit, he now indicates what should be learned for the benefit of the assembly, saying: 'But for the assembly...' and so on. By 'abhidhamme' is meant 'in the Suttanta Piṭaka, which is distinct and mutually delimited', and not in the Abhidhamma Piṭaka. The three Vaggas are the Sagāthā Vagga, the Nidāna Vagga, and the Khandha Vagga. The word 'vā' (or) indicates optionality. By 'ekaṃ' is meant 'one Nipāta'. By 'tato tato' is meant 'from the Nikāyas'. By 'samuccayaṃ katvā' is meant 'having made a collection'. By 'na vuttaṃ' is meant 'not stated in the commentaries'. The construction is 'one who does not have it does not obtain it'. By 'suttante ca' is meant 'and in the Suttanta Piṭaka'. By 'uggahito' is meant 'grasped by reciting in the same form', that is, 'uttered'. By 'disāpāmokkho' is meant 'the foremost among the bhikkhus and others stationed in the directions'. By 'yena kāmaṃ gamo' is meant 'going wherever one wishes'.

Catūsu nikāyesūti khuddakanikāyato aññesu dīghanikāyādīsu. Ekassāti aññatarassa ekassa[V 1.0036]. Ekanikāyenāti ekasmiṃ [M 0.0043] nikāye laddhanayena. Hīti saccaṃ, yasmā vā. Tatthāti catuppakaraṇassa aṭṭhakathāyaṃ. Nānatthanti nānāpayojanaṃ. Tanti vinayapiṭakaṃ. Ettāvatāti ettakapamāṇena paguṇena. Hotīti itisaddo parisamāpanattho. Iti parisamāpanaṃ veditabbanti yojanā.

By 'catūsu nikāyesu' (in the four Nikāyas) is meant 'in the Dīgha Nikāya and others, other than the Khuddaka Nikāya'. By 'ekassa' (of one) is meant 'of any single one'. By 'ekanikāyena' (by one Nikāya) is meant 'by the method obtained in one Nikāya'. By 'hī' is meant 'truly', or 'because'. By 'tattha' (there) is meant 'in the commentary on the four treatises'. By 'nānatthaṃ' (of different meanings) is meant 'having different purposes'. By 'tanti' (the text) is meant 'the Vinaya Piṭaka'. By 'ettāvatā' (this much) is meant 'to this extent, by being proficient'. The word 'hoti' (is) and the particle 'iti' serve to conclude. The construction is 'thus, the conclusion should be understood'.

Ubhayāni kho panassāti ādi pana vuttanti sambandho. Aññasminti vinayapiṭakato itarasmiṃ. Tatthāti “ubhayāni kho panassā”tiādivacane. Yathā yenākārena āgatāni, taṃ ākāraṃ dassetunti yojanā. Padapaccābhaṭṭhasaṅkaradosavirahitānīti padānaṃ paccābhaṭṭhasaṅkarabhūtehi dosehi virahitāni. Ettha ca padapaccābhaṭṭhanti padānaṃ paṭinivattitvā ābhassanaṃ gaḷanaṃ, cutanti attho. Padasaṅkaranti padānaṃ vipatti, vināsoti attho. “Suttaso”ti sāmaññato vuttepi khandhakaparivārasuttaṃ eva gahetabbanti āha “khandhakaparivārato”ti. Anubyañjanasoti ettha byañjanasaddo akkharassa ca padassa ca vācakoti āha “akkharapadapāripūriyā cā”ti. Hīti saccaṃ, yasmā vā.

The connection is that 'and both of his' (ubhayāni kho panassa) and so on, was stated. By 'aññasmiṃ' (in the other) is meant 'in that which is other than the Vinaya Piṭaka'. The construction is that 'therein' (tattha), in the statement beginning 'and both of his' (ubhayāni kho panassa), the way in which they came is shown. By 'free from faults of word reversion and word mixture' (padapaccābhaṭṭhasaṅkaradosavirahitāni) is meant 'free from faults that are word reversion and word mixture'. Here, 'word reversion' (padapaccābhaṭṭhaṃ) means 'the turning back and spilling out of words', that is, 'their loss'. 'Word mixture' (padasaṅkaraṃ) means 'the corruption of words', that is, 'their ruin'. Although 'according to the Sutta' (suttaso) is stated generally, it should be understood as referring specifically to the Khandhaka and Parivāra; thus he says 'from the Khandhaka and Parivāra'. Here, in 'anubyañjanaso' (according to minor characteristics), the word 'byañjana' (characteristic) refers to both letters and words; thus he says 'and with the completeness of letters and words'. By 'hī' is meant 'truly', or 'because'.

“Sithiladhanitādīna”ntipadaṃ “vacanenā”tipade kammaṃ, “vacanenā”tipadaṃ “sampannāgato”tipade hetu, “vissaṭṭhāya anelagaḷāya atthassa viññāpaniyā”tipadāni “vācāyā”tipade visesanāni. Sithiladhanitādīnanti ādisaddena niggahitavimuttasambandhavavatthitadīgha rassa garu lahu saṅkhātā aṭṭha byañjanabuddhiyo saṅgaṇhāti. Yathāvidhānavacanenāti akkharacintakānaṃ yathā saṃvidahanavacanena. Vācāyeva karīyati kathīyati uccārīyati vākkaraṇaṃ cakārassa kakāraṃ katvā. Hīti tadeva yuttaṃ. Mātugāmo yasmā sarasampattirato, tasmā hīḷetīti yojanā. “Sarasampattirahita”ntipadaṃ “vacana”ntipade visesanabhāvena visesaṃ katvā “hīḷetī”tipade hetubhāvena sampajjanato hetuantogadhavisesananti daṭṭhabbaṃ. Sabbāsanti bhikkhunīnaṃ. “Sīlācārasampattiyā”tiiminā jāti gotta rūpa bhogādinātiatthaṃ nivatteti. Kāraṇañcāti aṭṭhakathañca. Tajjetvāti ubbejetvā. Tāsanti bhikkhunīnaṃ. Gihikāleti bhikkhunovādakassa gihikāle anajjhāpannapubbo [M 0.0044] hotīti sambandho. Hi tadeva yuttaṃ. “Mātugāmo”tipadaṃ “na karotī”tipade suddhakattā, “uppādetī”tipade hetukattā. Ṭhitassa bhikkhuno dhammadesanāyāpīti yojanā. Apisaddo garahattho. Visabhāgehīti viruddhehi vatthārammaṇehi. Ayuttaṭṭhāneti pabbajitānaṃ ananurūpaṭṭhāne. Chandarāganti balavataṇhaṃ. Tenāti tena hetunā.

The word 'sithiladhanitādīnaṃ' is the object of the word 'vacanenā'; the word 'vacanenā' is the cause in the word 'sampannāgato'; and the words 'vissaṭṭhāya anelagaḷāya atthassa viññāpaniyā' are qualifiers of the word 'vācāya'. By the word 'ādi' in 'sithiladhanitādīnaṃ' are included the eight types of consonant understanding, namely, niggaṇhīta, vimutta, sambandha, vavatthita, dīgha, rassa, garu, and lahu. By 'yathāvidhānavacanena' is meant 'by speech that conforms to the arrangement of those who analyze letters'. Speech itself is performed, spoken, or uttered; 'vākkaraṇaṃ' (vocalization) is formed by changing the 'ca' sound to 'ka'. By 'hī' is meant 'that is indeed appropriate'. The construction is 'because a woman delights in the excellence of speech, therefore she scorns'. The word 'sarasampattirahitaṃ' (devoid of excellence of speech), by qualifying the word 'vacanaṃ', becomes the reason in the word 'hīḷetī' (scorns); therefore, it should be understood as a qualification included within the reason. By 'sabbāsaṃ' (of all) is meant 'of all bhikkhunīs'. By 'sīlācārasampattiyā' (by the accomplishment of virtue and conduct), it dismisses the meaning of birth, clan, beauty, wealth, and so on. By 'kāraṇañca' (and the reason) is meant 'and the commentary'. By 'tajjetvā' is meant 'having frightened' or 'having agitated'. By 'tāsaṃ' (of them) is meant 'of the bhikkhunīs'. The connection is that 'in the time of being a householder' (gihikāle), the bhikkhu advisor was not previously one who had fallen into an offense. By 'hī' is meant 'that is indeed appropriate'. The word 'mātugāmo' (woman) is the object in the phrase 'na karoti' (does not do) and the object in the phrase 'uppādeti' (produces). The construction is 'even for the Dhamma teaching of a standing bhikkhu'. The particle 'api' has the meaning of censure. By 'visabhāgehi' is meant 'with incompatible objects or sense-objects'. By 'ayuttaṭṭhāne' is meant 'in a place unsuitable for renunciants'. By 'chandarāgaṃ' is meant 'strong craving'. By 'tena' is meant 'by that cause'.

“Ettha [V 1.0037] cā”tiādimhi ayaṃ pana saṅgaho –

In the statement beginning 'and herein' (ettha ca), this is the summary:

“Sīlavā bahussuto ca, svāgato ca suvācako;

Piyo paṭibalo cāpi, najjhāpanno ca vīsatī”ti.

"Virtuous, greatly learned, welcoming, and eloquent; beloved, capable, and not having transgressed—these are the twenty."

148. Vatthusminti aṭṭhuppattiyaṃ. Kakāralopaṃ katvā garudhammāti vuccantīti āha “garukehi dhammehī”ti. Teti garudhammā. Hīti yasmā. “Ekato”ti sāmaññena vuttavacanassa visesena gahetabbataṃ dassetuṃ vuttaṃ “bhikkhunīnaṃ santike”ti. Yathāvatthukamevāti pācittiyameva. Tañhi vatthussa āpattikāraṇassa anurūpaṃ pavattattā “yathāvatthuka”nti vuccati.

148. By 'vatthusmiṃ' (in the matter) is meant 'in the origin story of the offense'. By omitting the syllable 'ka', they are called 'garudhamma' (weighty principles); thus he says 'by weighty principles'. Those are the weighty principles. By 'hī' is meant 'because'. To show that the word 'ekato' (as one), though stated generally, should be taken specifically, it is said 'in the presence of the bhikkhunīs'. By 'yathāvatthukameva' (just according to the case) is meant 'just a pācittiya offense'. For it is called 'yathāvatthuka' because it proceeds in accordance with the matter, the cause of the offense.

149. Pātoti pageva, paṭhamanti attho. Asammaṭṭhaṃ sammajjītabbanti sambandho. Asammajjane dosaṃ pākaṭaṃ karonto āha “asammaṭṭhaṃ hī”tiādi. Hīti tappākaṭīkaraṇajotako. Tanti pariveṇaṃ. Disvā bhaveyyunti sambandho. Tenāti asotukāmānaṃ viya bhavanahetunā. Pariveṇasammajjanassa ānisaṃsaṃ dassetvā pānīyaparibhojanīyaupaṭṭhānassa tameva dassento āha “anto gāmato panā”ti ādi. Tasminti pānīyaparibhojanīye.

149. By 'pāto' (early) is meant 'early in the morning', that is, 'first'. The connection is 'what is not swept should be swept'. Making clear the fault in not sweeping, he says: 'For what is not swept...' and so on. By 'hī' is meant 'a particle indicating clarification'. By 'taṃ' (that) is meant 'the monastery enclosure'. The connection is 'having seen, they would be'. By 'tena' (by that) is meant 'by reason of being like those who do not wish to hear'. Having shown the benefit of sweeping the monastery enclosure, and indicating the same for the provision of drinking water and water for use, he says: 'But from within the village...' and so on. By 'tasmiṃ' (in that) is meant 'in the drinking water and water for use'.

Sākhābhaṅgampīti bhañjitabbasākhampi. Dutiyoti viññū puriso dutiyo. Nisīditabbaṭṭhānaṃ dassento āha “nisīditabba”ntiādi. “Vihāramajjhe”ti sāmaññato vatvā visesato dassetuṃ vuttaṃ “dvāre”ti. Osaranti avasaranti etthāti osaraṇaṃ, tañca taṃ ṭhānañceti osaraṇaṭṭhānaṃ, tasmiṃ. Samaggatthāti ettha saṃpubbo ca āpubbo ca gamusaddo [M 0.0045] hoti, tato hiyyattanīsaṅkhātaṃ tthavacanaṃ vā hoti, pañcamīsaṅkhātassa thavacanassa tthattaṃ vā hoti, saṃyogaparattā ā upasaggo rasso ca hoti, iti atthaṃ dassento āha “sammā āgatatthā”ti. Tattha “sammā”tipadena saṃsaddassa atthaṃ dasseti, “ā”itipadena ātyūpasaggaṃ, “gata”itipadena gamudhātuṃ, “ttha”itipadena hiyyattanīsaṅkhātaṃ tthavacanaṃ vā, pañcamīsaṅkhātassa thavacanassa tthattaṃ vā dasseti. Ayaṃ panetthattho – samaṃ tumhe āgatatthāti. Pañcamīsaṅkhātassa thavacanassa tthattakāle samaṃ tumhe āgā attha bhavathāti. “Āgacchantī”tipadena “vattantī”ti ettha vatudhātuyā atthaṃ dasseti, “paguṇā vācuggatā”tipadehi adhippāyaṃ dasseti. Pāḷīti garudhammapāḷi.

"Sākhābhaṅgampi" means even a branch that should be broken. "Dutiyo" means a wise man is the second. Showing the place to sit, he says: "nisīditabba" etc. "Vihāramajjhe" is said generally, and to show specifically, it is said: "dvāre" (at the door). "Osaranti" means "avasaranti" (they approach); hence "osaraṇa" (approach), and that place is "osaraṇaṭṭhānaṃ" (the place of approach), in that. Regarding "Samaggatthā", here the root 'gam' is preceded by 'saṃ' and 'ā'; then 'ttha' is either the suffix known as the aorist, or it is the form of the suffix 'tha' known as the imperative; because it is followed by a conjunct consonant, the prefix 'ā' becomes short; thus, showing the meaning, he says: "sammā āgatatthā". There, the word "sammā" indicates the meaning of the element 'saṃ', the word "ā" indicates the prefix 'ā', the word "gata" indicates the root 'gam', and the word "ttha" indicates either the suffix known as the aorist or the form of the suffix 'tha' known as the imperative. But this is the meaning here: "samaṃ tumhe āgatatthā" (you have come together). When 'ttha' is the form of the suffix 'tha' known as the imperative, it means: "samaṃ tumhe āgacchatha" (may you come together). The word "āgacchantī" indicates the meaning of the root "vat" (to proceed) in "vattantī" here, while the words "paguṇā vācuggatā" (fluent and committed to memory) indicate the intention. "Pāḷī" means the Garudhamma Pāḷi.

Tatthāti [V 1.0038] tassaṃ pāḷiyaṃ, tesu vā abhivādanādīsu catūsu. Maggasampadānanti maggaṃ pariharitvā bhikkhussa okāsadānaṃ. Bījananti bījaniyā vidhūpanaṃ. Pānīyāpucchananti pānīyassa āpucchanaṃ. Ādisaddena paribhojanīyāpucchanādikaṃ saṅgaṇhāti. Ettha cāti etesu catūsu abhivādanādīsu. “Anto gāme vā”tiādīni cha padāni “kātabbamevā”tipade ādhāro. Rājussāraṇāyāti rañño ānubhāvena janānaṃ ussāraṇāya. Mahābhikkhusaṅgho sannipatati etthāti mahāsannipātaṃ, tasmiṃ mahāsannipāte ṭhāne nisinne satīti yojanā. Paccuṭṭhānanti paṭikacceva uṭṭhānaṃ. Taṃ tanti sāmīcikammaṃ.

"Tattha" means in that Pāḷi text, or in those four acts beginning with paying respects. "Maggasampadāna" means giving a bhikkhu space by clearing the path. "Bījana" means fanning with a fan. "Pānīyāpucchana" means asking about drinking water. The word "ādi" includes asking about water for use, and so on. And here, in these four acts beginning with paying respects. The six words beginning with "anto gāme vā" are the basis for the word "kātabbamevā" (must be done). "Rājussāraṇāya" means for the clearing away of people by the king's power. "Mahābhikkhusaṅgho sannipatati etthāti mahāsannipātaṃ" (the great Saṅgha of bhikkhus assembles here, hence a great assembly); the connection is 'when sitting in that place of great assembly'. "Paccuṭṭhāna" means rising in anticipation. "Taṃ taṃ" means that particular proper act.

Sakkatvāti cittiṃ katvā, saṃ ādaraṃ katvāti attho. Tenāha “yathā kato”tiādi. Tiṇṇaṃ kiccānanti “sakkatvā garuṃkatvā mānetvā”tisaṅkhātānaṃ tiṇṇaṃ kiccānaṃ. Anīyasaddo kammatthoti āha “na atikkamitabbo”ti.

"Sakkatvā" means having shown respect, that is, having shown thorough reverence. Hence he said, "as done" and so on. "Of the three duties" refers to the three duties designated as "respecting, honoring, and esteeming." The word ending in '-anīya' has a passive meaning; thus he said 'not to be transgressed'.

Natthi bhikkhu etthāti abhikkhuko āvāso, so kittake ṭhāne abhikkhuko, yo āvāso abhikkhuko nāma hotīti āha “sace”ti ādi. “Upassayato”tipadaṃ “abbhantare”tipade apādānaṃ. Etthāti abhikkhuke āvāse. Hīti saccaṃ. Tatoti aḍḍhayojanabbhantare [M 0.0046] ṭhitaāvāsato. Paranti aññasmiṃ āvāse, bhummatthe cetaṃ upayogavacanaṃ. Pacchābhattanti bhattato pacchā. Tatthāti abhikkhuke āvāse. “Bhikkhuniyo”tipadaṃ “vadantī”tipade kammaṃ. Vuttappamāṇeti aḍḍhayojanabbhantarasaṅkhāte vuttappamāṇe. Sākhāmaṇḍapepīti sākhāya chāditamaṇḍapepi. Pisaddena āvāse pana kā nāma kathāti dasseti. Vuttāti vasitā. Ettāvatāti ekarattaṃ vasitamattena. Etthāti sabhikkhuke āvāse. Upagacchantīhi bhikkhunīhi yācitabbāti yojanā. Pakkhassāti āsaḷhīmāsassa juṇhapakkhassa. “Terasiya”ntipadena avayaviavayavabhāvena yojetabbaṃ. Mayanti amhe. Yatoti yena ujunā maggenāti sambandho. Tenāha “tena maggenā”ti. Aññena maggenāti ujumaggato aññena jimhamaggena. Ayanti ayaṃ āvāso. Tatoti bhikkhūnaṃ āvāsato, bhikkhuniupassayato vā, idameva yuttataraṃ. Vakkhati hi “amhākaṃ upassayato gāvutamatte”ti. Khemaṭṭhāneti abhayaṭṭhāne. Tañhi khīyanti bhayā etthāti khemaṃ, khemañca taṃ ṭhānañceti khemaṭṭhānanti katvā “khemaṭṭhāna”nti vuccati. Tāhi bhikkhunīhīti aḍḍhayojanamatte ṭhāne vasantīhi. Tā bhikkhuniyoti gāvutamatte ṭhāne vasantiyo. Antarāti tumhākaṃ, amhākañca nivāsanaṭṭhānassa, nivāsanaṭṭhānato vā antare vemajjhe. Bhummatthe cetaṃ nissakkavacanaṃ. Ṭhite maggeti sambandho “santikā”tipadaṃ [V 1.0039] “āgata”itipade apādānaṃ. Tatthāti aññāsaṃ bhikkhunīnaṃ upassaye. Iti yācitabbāti yojanā. Tatoti bhikkhūnaṃ yācitabbato, paranti sambandho.

'There is no bhikkhu here,' thus the dwelling is without bhikkhus. Within what distance is it without bhikkhus? A dwelling is called 'without bhikkhus,' he says, 'if,' and so on. The word 'upassayato' is in the ablative case in relation to the word 'abbhantare'. 'Here' means in a dwelling without bhikkhus. 'Hi' means truly. 'From there' means from a dwelling situated within half a yojana. 'Paraṃ' means in another dwelling; this is a locative case in meaning. 'Pacchābhatta' means after the meal. 'There' means in a dwelling without bhikkhus. The word 'bhikkhuniyo' is the object of the word 'vadantī'. 'Vuttappamāṇe' means in the stated measure, reckoned as within half a yojana. 'Even in a branch-pavilion' means even in a pavilion covered with branches. By the word 'pi', he shows: what more needs to be said about a dwelling? 'Vuttā' means resided. 'Ettāvatā' means merely by having resided for one night. 'Here' means in a dwelling with bhikkhus. The connection is: it should be requested by the bhikkhunīs who are approaching. 'Pakkhassa' means of the bright fortnight of the month of Āsaḷhī. The word 'terasiyaṃ' should be connected by the relation of part and whole. 'Mayaṃ' means we. 'Yato' is connected with 'by which straight path'. Therefore, he said, 'by that path'. 'By another path' means by a crooked path other than the straight path. 'Ayaṃ' means this dwelling. 'From there' means from the bhikkhus' dwelling, or from the bhikkhunīs' residence; the latter is more suitable. For it will be said, 'about a gāvuta from our residence'. 'Khemaṭṭhāne' means in a safe place. For fears are exhausted there, thus it is 'khema' (safe); and that place is safe, thus it is called 'khemaṭṭhāna' (a safe place). 'By those bhikkhunīs' means by those dwelling in a place within the measure of half a yojana. 'Those bhikkhunīs' means those dwelling in a place within the measure of a gāvuta. 'Antarā' means between your dwelling place and ours, or in the middle between the dwelling places. This is an ablative case in the sense of the locative. The connection is 'on the path situated'. The word 'santikā' is in the ablative case in relation to the word 'āgata'. 'There' means in the residence of other bhikkhunīs. The connection is: 'thus it should be requested'. 'From there' is connected with 'beyond,' meaning beyond where the bhikkhus should be requested.

Cātuddaseti āsaḷhīmāsassa juṇhapakkhassa catuddasannaṃ divasānaṃ pūraṇe divase. Idhāti imasmiṃ vihāre. “Ovāda”ntipadaṃ “anu”itipade kammaṃ. Anujīvantiyoti anugantvā jīvanaṃ vuttiṃ karontiyo. Vuttā bhikkhūti sambandho. Dutiyadivaseti āsaḷhīpuṇṇamiyaṃ. Athāti pakkamanānantaraṃ. Etthāti bhikkhūnaṃ pakkantattā apassane. “Ābhogaṃ katvā”tiiminā ābhogaṃ akatvā vasituṃ [M 0.0047] na vaṭṭatīti dīpeti. Sabhikkhukāvāsaṃ gantabbamevāti adhippāyo. Sāti vassacchedāpatti. Hīti saccaṃ, yasmā vā. Kenaci kāraṇenāti bhikkhācārassa asampadādinā kenaci nimittena. Hīti saccaṃ. Bhikkhūnaṃ pakkantādikāraṇā abhikkhukāvāse vasantiyā kiṃ abhikkhukāvāseva pavāretabbanti āha “pavārentiyā panā”tiādi.

'On the fourteenth day' means on the day that completes the fourteen days of the bright fortnight of the month of Āsaḷhī. 'Here' means in this monastery. The word 'ovāda' is the object of the word 'anu'. 'Anujīvantiyo' means those who make their living by following. The connection is 'the bhikkhus who were mentioned'. 'On the second day' means on the full moon day of Āsaḷhī. 'Then' means immediately after departure. 'Here' means in the absence of seeing, because the bhikkhus have departed. By 'having made an effort', he shows that it is not proper to dwell without making an effort; the intention is that one must go to a dwelling with bhikkhus. 'Sā' refers to the offense of interrupting the rains-residence. 'Hi' means truly, or because. 'For some reason' means due to some cause, such as the non-availability of alms. 'Hi' means truly. For one dwelling in a residence without bhikkhus because the bhikkhus have departed and so on, should the Pavāraṇā be performed in that very residence without bhikkhus? He says, 'But for one performing Pavāraṇā,' and so on.

Anvaddhamāsanti ettha anusaddo vicchatthavācako kammappavacanīyo, tena payogattā bhummatthe upayogavacananti āha “addhamāse addhamāse”ti. Paccāsīsitabbāti ettha patipubbo ca āpubbo ca sidhātu icchattheti āha “icchitabbā”ti. Sidhātuyā dvebhāvo hoti. Āpubbo sisi icchāyantipi dhātupāṭhesu vuttaṃ. Tatthāti “uposathapucchaka”ntivacane. Pakkhassāti yassa kassaci pakkhassa. Mahāpaccariyaṃ pana vuttanti sambandho. Ovādassa yācanaṃ ovādo uttarapadalopena, soyeva attho payojanaṃ ovādattho, tadatthāya. Pāṭipadadivasatoti dutiyadivasato. So hi cando vuddhiñca hāniñca paṭimukhaṃ pajjati ettha, etenāti vā pāṭipadoti vuccati. Itīti evaṃ vuttanayena. Bhagavā paññapetīti yojanā. Aññassāti dhammassavanakammato aññassa. Nirantaranti abhikkhaṇaṃ, “paññapetī”tipade bhāvanapuṃsakaṃ. Hīti vitthāro. Evañca satīti evaṃ bahūpakāre sati ca. Yanti yaṃ dhammaṃ. Sātthikanti sapayojanaṃ. Yathānusiṭṭhanti anusiṭṭhiyā anurūpaṃ. Sabbāyeva bhikkhuniyopīti yojanā. Hīti saccaṃ.

Regarding 'anvaddhamāsaṃ': here the word 'anu' is a prepositional particle (kammappavacanīya) expressing distribution. Due to its usage, it is a locative case in meaning; therefore he says, 'addhamāse addhamāse' (every half-month). Regarding 'paccāsīsitabbā': here the root 'sidh' with the prefixes 'pati' and 'ā' is in the sense of desiring; therefore he says, 'icchitabbā' (should be desired). The root 'sidh' is doubled. It is also said in the lists of roots (Dhātupāṭha) that 'sis' with the prefix 'ā' is in the sense of desire. 'There' means in the phrase 'uposathapucchaka'. 'Pakkhassa' means of any fortnight. The connection is: 'but it is stated in the Mahāpaccarī'. The requesting of instruction is 'ovāda', by elision of the latter part of the compound; that very meaning or purpose is 'ovādattho' (the purpose of instruction), for the sake of that. 'Pāṭipadadivasato' means from the second day. For here, or by this, the moon enters face to face with its waxing and waning, thus it is called 'pāṭipada'. 'Iti' means in the manner thus stated. The connection is: 'the Blessed One prescribes'. 'Aññassa' means other than the act of hearing the Dhamma. 'Nirantaraṃ' means repeatedly. The word 'paññapetī' is a neuter noun of action. 'Hi' is for elaboration. 'Evañca sati' means and when there is such great benefit. 'Yaṃ' means which Dhamma. 'Sātthikaṃ' means with purpose. 'Yathānusiṭṭhaṃ' means in accordance with the instruction. The connection is: 'all bhikkhunīs also'. 'Hi' means truly.

Ovādaṃ gacchatīti ovādaṃ yācituṃ bhikkhusaṅghassa ārāmaṃ gacchati. Na ovādo gantabboti ovādaṃ yācituṃ bhikkhusaṅghassa ārāmo na gantabbo. Ovādoti ca upayogatthe paccattavacananti daṭṭhabbaṃ. Itarathā hi saddapayogo virujjheyya. Ovādaṃ gantunti ovādaṃ yācanatthāya bhikkhusaṅghassa ārāmaṃ gantuṃ.

'Ovādaṃ gacchati' means she goes to the monastery of the Bhikkhu Saṅgha to request instruction. 'Na ovādo gantabbo' means the monastery of the Bhikkhu Saṅgha should not be gone to in order to request instruction. And 'ovādo' should be understood as a nominative singular in the sense of the accusative. Otherwise, the use of the word would be contradictory. 'Ovādaṃ gantuṃ' means to go to the monastery of the Bhikkhu Saṅgha for the purpose of requesting instruction.

“Dve [M 0.0048][V 1.0040] tisso bhikkhuniyo”tipadaṃ “yācitvā”tipade dutiyākammaṃ. “Pesetabbā”tipade paṭhamākammaṃ. Ovādūpasaṅkamananti ovādassa gahaṇatthāya upasaṅkamanaṃ. Ārāmanti bhikkhusaṅghassa ārāmaṃ. Tatoti gamanato paranti sambandho. Tena bhikkhunāti ovādapaṭiggāhakena bhikkhunā. Tanti sammataṃ bhikkhuṃ.

The phrase 'dve tisso bhikkhuniyo' (two or three bhikkhunīs) is the secondary object of the word 'yācitvā' (having requested). It is the primary object of the word 'pesetabbā' (should be sent). 'Ovādūpasaṅkamana' means approaching for the purpose of receiving instruction. 'Ārāmaṃ' means the monastery of the Bhikkhu Saṅgha. 'Tato' is connected with 'paraṃ' (beyond), meaning after going. 'By that bhikkhu' means by the bhikkhu who is the recipient of the instruction. 'Taṃ' means the appointed bhikkhu.

Ussahatīti sakkoti. Pāsādikenāti pasādaṃ āvahena pasādajanakena kāyavacīmanokammenāti attho. Sampādetūti tividhaṃ sikkhaṃ sampādetu. Ettāvatāti ettakena “pāsādikena sampādetū”ti vacanamattena. Hīti phalajotako. Etanti “tāhī”tivacanaṃ.

'Ussahati' means is able. 'Pāsādikena' means by bodily, verbal, and mental action that brings about and generates confidence; such is the meaning. 'Sampādetu' means to fulfill the threefold training. 'Ettāvatā' means merely by this much, by the statement 'should fulfill with inspiring confidence'. 'Hi' is an indicator of the result. 'Etaṃ' refers to the word 'tāhi'.

Ettha ca bhikkhūnaṃ saṅghagaṇapuggalavasena vacanavāro tividho hoti, taṃ tividhaṃ vacanavāraṃ bhikkhunīnaṃ saṅghagaṇapuggalavasena tīhi vacanavārehi guṇitaṃ katvā nava vacanavārā honti, taṃ ākāraṃ dassento āha “tatrāyaṃ vacanakkamo”ti. Tatrāti purimavacanāpekkhaṃ. Vacanākāro pākaṭova.

And here, the bhikkhus' turn for speaking is threefold, according to whether it is the Saṅgha, a group, or an individual. That threefold turn for speaking, when multiplied by the three turns for speaking of the bhikkhunīs—according to whether it is the Saṅgha, a group, or an individual—becomes nine turns for speaking. Showing this method, he says, 'Herein is the sequence of speaking'. 'Herein' is with reference to the preceding statement. The manner of speaking is evident.

Ekā bhikkhunī vā bahūhi bhikkhunīupassayehi ovādatthāya pesite vacanākāraṃ dassento āha “bhikkhunisaṅgho ca ayyā”tiādi.

Showing the manner of speaking when one bhikkhunī is sent from many bhikkhunī residences for the purpose of instruction, he says, 'The Bhikkhunī Saṅgha and the venerable ladies,' and so on.

Tenāpīti ovādapaṭiggāhakenāpi “ovāda”ntipadaṃ “paṭiggāhakenā”ti pade kammaṃ. Puna “ovāda”ntipadaṃ “apaṭiggahetu”ntipade kammaṃ. Balati assāsapassāsamattena jīvati, na paññājīvitenāti bālo. Gilāyati rujatīti gilāno. Gamissati gantuṃ bhabboti gamiko. Ayaṃ panettha yojanā – gantuṃ bhabbo yo bhikkhu gamissati gamanaṃ karissati, iti tasmā so bhikkhu gamiko nāma. Atha vā yo bhikkhu gantuṃ bhabbattā gamissati gamanaṃ karissati, iti tasmā so bhikkhu gamiko nāmāti. “Bhabbo”ti ca hetuantogadhavisesanaṃ.

'By him too' means by the recipient of the instruction too. The word 'ovādaṃ' is the object of the word 'paṭiggāhakena'. Again, the word 'ovādaṃ' is the object of the word 'apaṭiggahetuṃ'. One who lives (balati) merely by breath, by inhalation and exhalation, not by the life of wisdom, is a 'bālo' (fool). One who is ailing (gilāyati), who is afflicted, is 'gilāno' (sick). One who will go (gamissati), who is fit to go, is a 'gamiko' (traveler). Herein is the application: a bhikkhu who is fit to go, who will go, who will undertake the journey, therefore that bhikkhu is called a traveler. Or: a bhikkhu who, because of his fitness to go, will go, will undertake the journey, therefore that bhikkhu is called a traveler. And 'bhabbo' (fit) is an adjective implying a cause.

Tatthāti [M 0.0049][V 1.0041] bālādīsu tīsu puggalesu. Dutiyapakkhadivaseti pāṭipadato dutiyapakkhadivase. Uposathaggeti uposathagehe. Tañhi uposathaṃ gaṇhanti, uposatho vā gayhati asminti “uposathagga”nti vuccati. Tasmiṃ uposathagge. “Anārocetu”nti vacanassa ñāpakaṃ dassetvā “apaccāharitu”nti vacanassa tameva dassento āha “aparampi vutta”ntiādi.

'Therein' (tatthā) means among the three individuals, beginning with the fool. 'On the day of the second fortnight' (dutiyapakkhadivase) means on the second day of the fortnight, starting from the first day. 'In the Uposatha hall' (uposathagge) means in the Uposatha house. For therein they undertake the Uposatha, or the Uposatha is undertaken therein; thus it is called the 'Uposatha hall.' In that Uposatha hall. Having shown the indicator for the word 'without informing' (anārocetuṃ), and while showing the same for the word 'without taking back' (apaccāharituṃ), he says, 'Furthermore, it is said,' and so forth.

Tatthāti ovādapaṭiggāhakesu bhikkhūsu. No cassāti no ce assa. Sabhaṃ vāti samajjaṃ vā. Sā hi saha bhāsanti ettha, santehi vā bhāti dibbatīti “sabhā”ti vuccati, taṃ sabhaṃ vā upasaṅkamissāmīti yojanā. Tatrāti tasmiṃ sabhādike. Evaṃ “tatthā”tipadepi.

'Therein' (tatthā) refers to the bhikkhus who accept the instruction. 'No cassāti' means 'if it were not so.' 'Or an assembly' (sabhāṃ vā) means 'or a gathering.' For it is called 'sabhā' because they speak together there, or because it shines or is radiant with the virtuous. The application is: 'I will approach that assembly.' 'Therein' (tatrā) means 'in that assembly or the like.' Likewise for the word 'tatthā'.

Catuddasannaṃ pūraṇo cātuddaso, tasmiṃ pavāretvāti sambandho. Bhikkhusaṅgheti bhikkhusaṅghassa santike, samīpatthe cetaṃ bhummavacanaṃ. Ajjatanāti ettha asmiṃ ahani ajja, imasaddato ahanīti atthe jjapaccayo, imasaddassa ca akāro, ajja eva ajjatanā, svattho hi tanapaccayo. Aparasmiṃ ahani aparajja, aparasaddato ahanīti atthe jjapaccayo sattamyantoyeva. Etthāti pavāraṇe, “anujānāmī”tiādivacane vā. Hīti saccaṃ.

'Cātuddaso' is that which completes the fourteen. The connection is 'having performed the Pavāraṇā on that (fourteenth day).' 'In the Bhikkhu Saṅgha' (bhikkhusaṅghe) means 'in the presence of the Bhikkhu Saṅgha,' and this locative case denotes proximity. Regarding 'ajjatanā': here, 'ajja' means 'on this day'; it is from the word 'ima' with the suffix '-jja' in the sense of 'day,' and 'ima' becomes 'a'. 'Ajjatanā' is 'ajja eva' (on this very day); for the suffix '-tanā' is pleonastic. 'Aparajja' means 'on the following day' (aparasmiṃ ahani); it is from the word 'apara' with the suffix '-jja' in the sense of 'day,' and is only in the locative case. 'Herein' (etthā) refers to the Pavāraṇā, or to the statement 'I allow,' and so forth. 'Hi' means 'truly'.

Kolāhalanti kotūhalaṃ. Paṭhamaṃ bhikkhunī yācitabbāti saṅghena paṭhamaṃ bhikkhunī yācitabbā.

'Commotion' (kolāhala) means 'excitement' (kotūhala). 'The bhikkhunī should be asked first' (paṭhamaṃ bhikkhunī yācitabbā) means the Saṅgha should first ask the bhikkhunī.

Tāya bhikkhuniyā vacanīyo assāti yojanā. Passanto paṭikarissatīti vajjāvajjaṃ passanto hutvā paṭikarissati.

The application is: 'He should be addressed by that bhikkhunī.' 'Seeing, he will make amends' (passanto paṭikarissati) means, having seen what is faulty and what is not faulty, he will make amends.

Ubhinnanti bhikkhubhikkhunīnaṃ. Yathāṭhāneyevāti yaṃ yaṃ ṭhānaṃ yathāṭhānaṃ, tasmiṃ yathāṭhāneyeva. Kenaci pariyāyenāti kenaci kāraṇena. Avapubbo varasaddo pihitatthoti āha “pihito”ti. Vacanaṃyevāti ovādavacanaṃyeva. Pathoti jeṭṭhakaṭṭhāne ṭhānassa kāraṇattā patho. Dosaṃ panāti abhikkamanādīsu [M 0.0050] ādīnavaṃ pana. Añjentīti makkhenti. Bhikkhūhi pana ovadituṃ anusāsituṃ vaṭṭatīti yojanā.

'Of both' (ubhinnaṃ) refers to bhikkhus and bhikkhunīs. 'In the very proper place' (yathāṭhāneyeva) means: whatever place is the proper place, in that very proper place. 'By any means' (kenaci pariyāyena) means for any reason. The word 'vara' preceded by 'ava' has the meaning of 'covered,' hence he says 'covered' (pihito). 'Only the word' (vacanaṃyeva) means solely the word of advice. 'Patha' means the foremost position, because it is the cause of standing in the foremost position. 'But the fault' (dosaṃ pana) refers to the danger in going forward, and so forth. 'They anoint' (añjenti) means 'they smear.' The application is: 'But it is proper for bhikkhus to advise and instruct'.

Aññanti ovādato aññaṃ. Esoti garudhammo.

'Other' (aññaṃ) means other than the instruction. 'This' (eso) refers to the weighty rule.

150. “Adhammakamme”ti ettha katamaṃ kammaṃ nāmāti āha “adhammakammetiādīsū”tiādi. Tatthāti adhammakammadhammakammesu.

150. Here, regarding 'in an unlawful act' (adhammakamme), as to 'what is an act?', he says, 'in "unlawful act," and so forth.' 'Therein' (tatthā) means among unlawful and lawful acts.

152. Uddesaṃ dento bhaṇati, anāpattīti yojanā. Osāretīti katheti. Catuparisatīti catuparisasmiṃ. Tatrāpīti tena bhikkhunīnaṃ suṇanakāraṇenāti. Paṭhamaṃ.

152. 'Giving a recitation, he speaks' (uddesaṃ dento bhaṇati); the application is 'no offense.' 'He announces' (osāreti) means 'he declares.' 'In the fourfold assembly' (catuparisati) means 'in the four assemblies.' 'Even there' (tatrāpi) means because of the bhikkhunīs' listening. First.

2. Atthaṅgatasikkhāpadaṃ

2. The training rule that has lapsed.

153. Dutiye [V 1.0042] pariyāyasaddo vāratthoti āha “vārenā”ti. Vāroti ca anukkamoyevāti āha “paṭipāṭiyāti attho”ti. Adhikaṃ cittaṃ imassāti adhicetoti dassento āha “adhicittavato”tiādi. Adhicittaṃ nāma idha arahattaphalacittameva, na vipassanāpādakabhūtaṃ aṭṭhasamāpatticittanti āha “arahattaphalacittenā”ti. “Adhicittasikkhā”tiādīsu (pārā. 45; dī. ni. 3.305; ma. ni. 1.497; a. ni. 6.105; mahāni. 10) hi vipassanāpādakabhūtaṃ aṭṭhasamāpatticittaṃ “adhicitta”nti vuccati. Na pamajjatoti na pamajjantassa. Sātaccakiriyāyāti satatakaraṇena. Ubho loke munati jānātīti munīti ca, monaṃ vuccati ñāṇaṃ munanaṭṭhena jānanatthena, tamassatthīti munīti ca dassento āha “muninotī”tiādi. Tattha “yo munati…pe… munanena vā”tiiminā paṭhamatthaṃ dasseti, “monaṃ vuccati…pe… vuccatī”tiiminā dutiyatthaṃ dasseti. Muna gatiyanti dhātupāṭhesu (saddanītidhātumālāyaṃ 15 pakārantadhātu) vuttattā “yo munatī”ti ettha bhūvādigaṇiko munadhātuyeva, na kīyādigaṇiko mudhātūti daṭṭhabbaṃ. Atha vā muna ñāṇeti dhātupāṭhesu (saddanītidhātumālāyaṃ 17 kiyādigaṇika) vuttattā “munātī”ti kīyādigaṇikova. Dhātvantanakāralopoti daṭṭhabbaṃ. “Monaṃ vuccati ñāṇa”nti cettha ñāṇaṃ nāma [M 0.0051] arahattañāṇameva. Monassa patho monapathoti vutte sattatiṃsa bodhipakkhiyadhammāva adhippetāti āha “sattatiṃsabodhipakkhiyadhammesū”ti. Atha vā adhisīlasikkhādayo adhippetāti āha “tīsu vā sikkhāsū”ti. Pubbabhāgapaṭipadanti arahattañāṇassa pubbabhāge pavattaṃ sīlasamathavipassanāsaṅkhātaṃ paṭipadaṃ. Pubbabhāgeti arahattañāṇassa pubbabhāge. Etthāti “adhicetaso…pe… sikkhato”ti vacane. “Tādino”tipadaṃ “munino”tipadena yojetabbanti āha “tādisassa khīṇāsavamunino”ti. Etthāti “sokā na bhavanti tādino”ti vacane. Rāgādayo upasametīti upasantoti dassetuṃ vuttaṃ “rāgādīna”nti. Sati assatthīti satimāti katvā mantusaddo niccayogatthoti āha “satiyā avirahitassā”ti.

153. In the second instance, the word 'pariyāya' has the meaning of 'turn' (vāra), hence he says 'by turns' (vārena). And 'turn' (vāra) is simply succession, hence he says, 'the meaning is in due order' (paṭipāṭiyāti attho). Showing that 'adhiceto' means 'one whose mind is heightened' (adhikaṃ cittaṃ imassa), he says, 'of one possessing higher mind' (adhicittavato), and so forth. Here, 'higher mind' (adhicittaṃ) means only the mind of arahant-fruition, not the mind of the eight attainments that serves as a basis for insight, hence he says, 'by the mind of arahant-fruition' (arahattaphalacittena). For in contexts like 'the training in higher mind' (adhicittasikkhā), and so forth (Pārā. 45; Dī. Ni. 3.305; Ma. Ni. 1.497; A. Ni. 6.105; Mahāni. 10), the mind of the eight attainments that serves as a basis for insight is called 'higher mind'. 'Of one who does not neglect' (na pamajjato) means 'of one who is not negligent' (na pamajjantassa). 'By constant practice' (sātaccakiriyāya) means 'by constant doing' (satatakaraṇena). Showing that 'muni' means 'he knows both worlds' (ubho loke munati jānāti), and that 'mona' is called knowledge—in the sense of knowing, in the sense of discerning—and that he possesses this, he says, 'of the muni' (munino), and so forth. Here, with 'one who knows... or by knowing,' he shows the first meaning; with 'mona is called... is called,' he shows the second meaning. Since 'muna' is stated in the Dhātupāṭha (Saddanītidhātumālā, 15th pakāranta-dhātu) in the sense of motion, it should be understood that in 'one who knows' (yo munati), it is the root 'mun' belonging to the bhūvādi group, not the root 'mu' of the kiyādi group. Alternatively, since 'muna' is stated in the Dhātupāṭha (Saddanītidhātumālā, 17th kiyādigaṇika) in the sense of knowing, then in 'he knows' (munāti), it is indeed of the kiyādi group. The elision of the final 'n' of the root should be understood. In 'mona is called knowledge,' 'knowledge' here means only the knowledge of arahantship. When it is said, 'the path of wisdom is monapatha,' the thirty-seven factors of enlightenment are intended, hence he says, 'in the thirty-seven factors of enlightenment.' Alternatively, the higher trainings and so forth are intended, hence he says, 'or in the three trainings.' 'The preliminary practice' (pubbabhāgapaṭipadā) means the practice designated as virtue, serenity, and insight, which occurs in the preliminary stage of the knowledge of arahantship. 'In the preliminary stage' (pubbabhāge) means in the preliminary stage of the knowledge of arahantship. Here, in the statement 'of one with higher mind... training' (adhicetaso... sikkhato), the word 'tādino' should be connected with the word 'munino,' hence he says, 'of such a taintless muni.' Here, in the statement 'sorrows do not exist for such a one' (sokā na bhavanti tādino), 'of lust, etc.' (rāgādīnaṃ) is stated to show that one is 'pacified' (upasanto) because one pacifies (upasameti) lust and so forth. Having formed 'satimā' (mindful) from 'sati assa atthi' (he has mindfulness), and since the suffix '-mantu' is in the sense of constant connection, he says 'of one not separated from mindfulness' (satiyā avirahitassa).

Na kasīyati na vilekhīyatīti akāso, soyeva ākāso. Antarena chiddena ikkhitabboti antalikkho. Ākāso hi catubbidho ajaṭākāso, kasiṇugghāṭimākāso, paricchinnākāso, rūpaparicchedākāsoti. Tattha ajaṭākāsova idhādhippeto “antalikkhe”ti visesitattā. Tenāha “na kasiṇugghāṭime, na pana rūpaparicchede”ti. Paricchinnākāsopi rūpaparicchedākāsena saṅgahito. “Ma”nti padaṃ “avamaññantī”ti pade kammaṃ. Ettakamevāti etappamāṇaṃ [V 1.0043] “adhicetaso”tiādisaṅkhātaṃ vacanameva, na aññaṃ buddhavacananti attho. Ayanti cūḷapanthako thero. Handāti vassaggatthe nipāto. Mama ānubhāvaṃ dassemi, tumhe passatha gaṇhathāti adhippāyo. Vuṭṭhāyāti tato catutthajjhānato vuṭṭhahitvā. Antarāpi dhāyatīti ettha pisaddassa aṭṭhānatthaṃ dassento āha “antaradhāyatipī”ti. Eseva nayo “seyyampi kappetī”ti etthapi. Theroti cūḷapanthako thero. Idaṃ padaṃ antarantarā yuttaṭṭhānesu sambandhitvā “tañceva bhaṇatī”tiiminā sambandhitabbaṃ. Bhātutherassāti jeṭṭhakabhātubhūtassa mahāpanthakatherassa.

Because it is not plowed (na kasīyati) nor scratched (na vilekhīyati), it is 'unplowed' (akāso); that very thing is 'space' (ākāso). Because it is to be seen (ikkhitabbo) through an intermediate (antarena) gap (chiddena), it is 'the atmosphere' (antalikkho). Space is of four kinds: unconfined space, space revealed by a kasiṇa, bounded space, and space defined by form. Here, unconfined space is intended, because it is specified as 'in the atmosphere' (antalikkhe). Hence he says, 'not in the space revealed by a kasiṇa, nor in the space defined by form.' Bounded space is also included in space defined by form. The word 'me' (maṃ) is the object of the word 'they disdain' (avamaññanti). 'Only this much' (ettakameva) means just this amount, namely the statement designated as 'of one with higher mind,' and so forth; the meaning is, no other word of the Buddha. 'This one' (ayaṃ) refers to the Elder Cūḷapanthaka. 'Handa' is a particle in the sense of 'come now.' The intention is: 'I will show my power; you all watch and take note.' 'Having emerged' (vuṭṭhāya) means having risen from that fourth jhāna. Regarding 'antarāpi dhāyati', he says 'antaradhāyatipi', showing that the meaning here is 'disappears.' The same method applies also to 'seyyampi kappeti' (he even prepares a lodging). 'The Elder' (thero) refers to the Elder Cūḷapanthaka. This word should be connected intermittently in appropriate places and linked with 'he recites that very thing' (tañceva bhaṇati). 'Of his elder brother' (bhātutherassa) refers to the Elder Mahāpanthaka, who was his elder brother.

Padmanti [M 0.0052] gāthāyaṃ tayo pādā indavajirā, catutthapādo upendavajiro. Tasmā padmanti ettha makāre pare dukārukārassa lopaṃ katvā parakkharaṃ netvā “padma”nti dvibhāvena likhitabbaṃ. Avītagandhanti ettha vīti dīghuccāraṇameva yuttaṃ. Paṅke davati gacchatīti padumaṃ. Kokaṃ duggandhassa ādānaṃ nudati apanetīti kokanudaṃ. Sundaro gandho imassāti sugandhaṃ. Ayaṃ panettha yojanā – yathā kokanudasaṅkhātaṃ sugandhaṃ pāto pageva bālātapena phullaṃ vikasitaṃ avītagandhaṃ hutvā virocamānaṃ padumaṃ siyā, tathā aṅgīrasaṃ aṅgito sarīrato niccharaṇapabhassararasaṃ hutvā virocamānabhūtaṃ antalikkhe tapantaṃ ādiccaṃ iva tedhātuke tapantaṃ sammāsambuddhaṃ passāti.

In the verse beginning 'Padmaṃ', three lines are in the Indavajirā meter, and the fourth line is in the Upendavajirā meter. Therefore, here in 'padmanti', when the letter 'm' follows, having elided the u-vowel of the syllable 'du' and carrying over the following consonant, it should be written as 'padma' in two parts. In 'Avītagandhanti', the long pronunciation of 'vī' is indeed appropriate. 'It moves in the mud, it goes'—thus, it is a paduma (lotus). 'It dispels, removes the taking up of foul odors'—thus, it is a kokanuda. 'Beautiful is its fragrance'—thus, it is sugandha. Herein, this is the application: just as a fragrant lotus, known as a kokanuda, blooming early in the morning with the heat of the young sun, fully opened and not devoid of fragrance, shines brilliantly, so too one sees the Aṅgīrasa, who shines forth with the radiant essence emanating from his limbs and body, the Perfectly Enlightened One, blazing in the three realms like the sun blazing in the sky.

Paguṇanti vācuggataṃ. Tatoti asakkuṇeyyato. Nanti cūḷapanthakaṃ. Theroti mahāpanthako thero nikkaḍḍhāpesīti sambandho. Soti cūḷapanthako. Athāti tasmiṃ kāle. Bhagavā āhāti yojanā. Buddhacakkhunāti āsayānusayaindriyaparopariyattañāṇasaṅkhātena sabbaññubuddhānaṃ cakkhunā. Tanti cūḷapanthakaṃ. Tassāti cūḷapanthakassa. Athāti tasmiṃ ārocanakāle. Assāti cūḷapanthakassa, datvāti sambandho. Rajaṃ malaṃ harati apanetīti rajoharaṇaṃ, pilotikakhaṇḍaṃ. Soti cūḷapanthako. Tassāti pilotikakhaṇḍassa, “anta”ntipade avayavisambandho. Parisuddhampīti pisaddo aparisuddhe pilotikakhaṇḍe kā nāma kathāti dasseti. Saṃveganti santāsaṃ bhayanti attho. Athāti tasmiṃ ārambhakāle. Assāti cūḷapanthakassa. “Ta”ntipadaṃ “mamāyanabhāva”ntipadena sambandhaṃ katvā yojanā kātabbāti. Dutiyaṃ.

'Paguṇaṃ' means mastery of recitation. 'Tato' means because of inability. 'Naṃ' refers to Cūḷapanthaka. 'Thero' refers to the elder Mahāpanthaka; the connection is that the elder Mahāpanthaka had him expelled. 'So' refers to Cūḷapanthaka. 'Atha' means at that time. 'Bhagavā āha' is the construction. 'Buddhacakkhunā' means with the Buddha-eye, which is the knowledge of all-knowing Buddhas, designated as the knowledge of inclinations, latent tendencies, faculties, and the higher and lower states of others. 'Taṃ' refers to Cūḷapanthaka. 'Tassa' means of Cūḷapanthaka. 'Atha' means at the time of the announcement. 'Assa' refers to Cūḷapanthaka; the connection is with 'datvā'. 'It carries away (harati), removes (apaneti) dust (rajaṃ) and dirt (malaṃ)'—thus, it is a rajoharaṇaṃ, a piece of cloth. 'So' refers to Cūḷapanthaka. 'Tassa' refers to the piece of cloth; in the word 'anta', there is a part-whole relationship. Regarding 'Parisuddhampi', the particle 'pi' indicates: what then is to be said of an impure piece of cloth? 'Saṃvegaṃ' means agitation, fear. 'Atha' means at the time of beginning. 'Assa' refers to Cūḷapanthaka. The word 'taṃ' should be construed by connecting it with the word 'mamāyanabhāva' (the state of 'this is mine'). Second.

3. Bhikkhunupassayasikkhāpadaṃ

3. The Training Rule on the Bhikkhunī Residence

162. Tatiye “ovadati pācittiyassā”ti sāmaññato vuttepi visesato attho gahetabboti [V 1.0044] āha “aṭṭhahi garudhammehi ovadantasseva pācittiya”nti. Itoti imasmā sikkhāpadamhā. Yattha [M 0.0053] yatthāti yasmiṃ yasmiṃ sikkhāpade. Sabbattha tattha tatthāti yojanāti. Tatiyaṃ.

162. In the third, although 'ovadati pācittiyassa' ('advising incurs a pācittiya offense') is stated generally, the specific meaning should be understood, as it is said, 'a pācittiya applies only to one advising with the eight grave rules.' 'Ito' means from this training rule. 'Yattha yattha' means in whichever training rule. 'Sabbattha tattha tattha' is the construction. Third.

Pakiṇṇakakathā

Miscellaneous Discourse

Etthāti imasmiṃ sikkhāpade. Idaṃ pakiṇṇakaṃ vuttanti sambandho. Tīṇi pācittiyānīti bhikkhuno asammatattā ekaṃ pācittiyaṃ, sūriyassa atthaṅgatattā ekaṃ, bhikkhunupassayaṃ upasaṅkamitattā ekanti tīṇi pācittiyāni. Kathanti kena kāraṇena hotīti yojanā. Tatthāti bhikkhunupassayaṃ. Tassevāti sammatasseva bhikkhuno. Aññena dhammenāti garudhammehi aññena dhammena. Divā panāti sūriyuggamanato tassa anatthaṅgateyevāti.

'Ettha' means in this training rule. 'Idaṃ pakiṇṇakaṃ vuttaṃ' is the connection. 'Tīṇi pācittiyāni' means three pācittiya offenses: one because the bhikkhu is unappointed, one because the sun has set, and one because he approached the bhikkhunī residence. 'Kathaṃ' means for what reason it occurs; this is the construction. 'Tattha' means in the bhikkhunī residence. 'Tasseva' means of only the appointed bhikkhu. 'Aññena dhammena' means with another teaching, other than the grave rules. 'Divā pana' means from sunrise until it has not yet set.

4. Āmisasikkhāpadaṃ

4. The Training Rule on Material Gain

164. Catutthe bahuṃ mānaṃ kataṃ yehīti bahukatā. Bahukatā hutvā na ovadantīti atthaṃ dassento āha “na bahukatā”tiādi. Dhammeti sīlādidhamme. Adhippāyoti “na bahukatā”tipadassa, chabbaggiyānaṃ vā adhippāyoti yojanā. “Kattukāmoti ādīna”ntipadaṃ “attho”tipade vācakasambandho.

164. In the fourth, 'bahukatā' means 'those by whom much esteem has been shown.' Explaining the meaning that 'having been esteemed, they do not advise,' he said: 'na bahukatā,' etc. 'Dhamme' means in the Dhamma, such as virtue, etc. 'Adhippāyo' is the intention of the phrase 'na bahukatā,' or the intention of the group of six bhikkhus; this is the construction. The phrase 'kattukāmo ti ādīnaṃ' has a denotative relationship with the word 'attho' (meaning).

Asammato nāma ṭhapito veditabboti yojanā. Sammutinti bhikkhunovādakasammutiṃ. Pacchā sāmaṇerabhūmiyaṃ ṭhitoti yojanāti. Catutthaṃ.

'An unappointed one' should be understood as one who is set aside; this is the construction. 'Sammutiṃ' means the appointment as an advisor to bhikkhunīs. 'Pacchā sāmaṇerabhūmiyaṃ ṭhito' is the construction. Fourth.

5. Cīvaradānasikkhāpadaṃ

5. The Training Rule on Giving a Robe

169. Pañcame rathikāyāti racchāya. Sā hi rathassa hitattā rathikāti vuccati. Sandiṭṭhāti samodhānavasena dassīyitthāti sandiṭṭhā. Diṭṭhamattakā mittāti āha “mittā”ti. Sesanti vuttavacanato sesaṃ vacanaṃ. Tatrāti cīvarapaṭiggahaṇasikkhāpade. Hīti visesajotakaṃ. Idhāti imasmiṃ cīvaradānasikkhāpadeti. Pañcamaṃ.

169. In the fifth, 'rathikāya' means on a street. It is called 'rathikā' because it is suitable for chariots. 'Sandiṭṭhā' means one who is seen by way of coming together. 'Friends merely by sight' is what is meant by 'mittā'. 'Sesaṃ' means the remaining statement from what has been said. 'Tatra' refers to the training rule on accepting a robe. 'Hi' is a particle indicating emphasis. 'Idha' means in this training rule on giving a robe. Fifth.

6. Cīvarasibbanasikkhāpadaṃ

6. The Training Rule on Sewing a Robe

175. Chaṭṭhe [M 0.0054][V 1.0045] udāyīti ettha mahāudāyī, kāḷudāyī, lāḷudāyīti tayo udāyī honti. Tesu tatiyovādhippetoti āha “lāḷudāyī”ti. Pabhāvena ṭhāti pavattatīti paṭṭhoti kate paṭibalova labbhati. Tenāha “paṭibalo”ti. Nipuṇoti kusalo. “Paṭibhānena katacitta”ntiiminā “paṭibhānacitta”nti padassa majjhe padalopaṃ dasseti. Soti lāḷudāyī akāsīti sambandho. Tassāti cīvarassa. “Yathāsaṃhaṭa”nti ettha evasaddo ajjhāharitabboti āha “yathāsaṃhaṭamevā”ti.

175. In the sixth, 'Udāyī' here refers to three individuals: Mahāudāyī, Kāḷudāyī, and Lāḷudāyī. Among them, the third is intended, hence it is said, 'Lāḷudāyī.' 'One who stands (ṭhāti) or prevails (pavattati) by influence (pabhāvena)'—thus, he is paṭṭho; when this is said, 'one who is capable' (paṭibalo) is meant. Therefore, it is said, 'paṭibalo.' 'Nipuṇo' means skilled. By 'paṭibhānena katacittaṃ' he shows the elision of a word in the middle of the term 'paṭibhānacittaṃ.' 'So' has the connection: 'Lāḷudāyī did.' 'Tassa' refers to the robe. Regarding 'yathāsaṃhaṭaṃ', it is said that the word 'eva' should be supplied, hence 'yathāsaṃhaṭameva'.

176. Yaṃ cīvaraṃ nivāsituṃ vā pārupituṃ vā sakkā hoti, taṃ cīvaraṃ nāmāti yojanā. Evaṃ hīti evameva. “Dukkaṭa”ntiiminā “sayaṃ sibbati, āpatti pācittiyassā”ti ettha antarāpattiṃ dasseti. Ārāti sūci. Sā hi arati nissaṅgavasena gacchati pavisatīti “ārā”ti vuccati, tassā patho gamanaṃ ārāpatho, tasmiṃ, ārāpathassa nīharaṇāvasānattā “nīharaṇe”ti vuttaṃ. Satakkhattumpīti anekakkhattumpi. Āṇattoti āṇāpīyatīti āṇatto. “Āṇāpito”ti vattabbe ṇāpesaddassa lopaṃ, ikārassa ca akāraṃ katvā, “ādatte”ti ākhyātapade tevibhattiyā viya tapaccayassa ca dvibhāvaṃ katvā evaṃ vuttaṃ. Tenāha “sakiṃ cīvaraṃ sibbāti vutto”ti. Atha panāti tato aññathā pana. Āṇattassāti āṇāpitassa. Sambahulānipi pācittiyāni hontīti sambandho.

176. 'Whatever robe can be worn as a lower garment or an upper garment, that is called a robe'—this is the construction. 'Evaṃ hi' means just so. By 'dukkaṭa', he indicates an intermediate offense in the passage 'if he sews it himself, it is an offense of pācittiya.' 'Ārā' means a needle. It is called 'ārā' because it moves (arati), goes (gacchati), and enters (pavisati) without getting stuck. Its path or movement is the 'ārāpatha'; in that context, because the path of the needle ends in withdrawal, the word 'nīharaṇe' (on withdrawal) is used. 'Satakkhattumpi' means many times. 'Āṇatto' means one who is ordered. When 'āṇāpito' should be said, it is stated thus by eliding the syllable 'ṇāpe', changing the 'i' to an 'a', and doubling the 'ta' suffix, similar to the 'te' ending of the verb 'ādatte'. Therefore, he says, 'told once to sew the robe.' 'Atha pana' means but otherwise. 'Āṇattassa' means of the one who was ordered. 'Sambahulānipi pācittiyāni honti' is the connection.

Yepi nissitakā sibbantīti yojanā, ācariyupajjhāyesu sibbantesūti sambandho. Tesanti ācariyupajjhāyānaṃ. Tesampīti nissitakānampi. Ñātikānaṃ bhikkhunīnaṃ cīvaranti sambandho. “Antevāsikehī”tipadaṃ “sibbāpentī”tipade kāritakammaṃ. Tatrāpīti ācariyupajjhāyehi sibbāpanepi. “Antevāsike”tipadaṃ “vañcetvā”tipade [M 0.0055] suddhakammaṃ, “sibbāpentī”tipade kāritakammaṃ. Itaresanti ācariyupajjhāyānanti. Chaṭṭhaṃ.

'Yepi nissitakā sibbanti' is the construction, with the connection 'when the teachers and preceptors are sewing.' 'Tesaṃ' refers to the teachers and preceptors. 'Tesampi' refers also to the dependents. 'Ñātikānaṃ bhikkhunīnaṃ cīvaraṃ' is the connection. The word 'antevāsikehi' is the agent of the causative verb with 'sibbāpenti.' 'Tatrāpi' refers to even having it sewn by teachers and preceptors. The word 'antevāsike' is the direct object of 'vañcetvā' and the agent of the causative verb with 'sibbāpenti.' 'Itaresaṃ' refers to the other teachers and preceptors. Sixth.

7. Saṃvidhānasikkhāpadaṃ

7. The Training Rule on Arrangement

181. Sattame “tāsaṃ bhikkhunīnaṃ pacchā gacchantīna”nti padāni “pattacīvara”nti pāṭhasesena yojetabbānīti āha “pacchā gacchantīnaṃ pattacīvara”nti. Tā bhikkhuniyo pacchā gacchantiyoti vibhattivipallāsaṃ katvā “dūsesu”ntipadena yojetabbānīti āha “tā bhikkhuniyo [V 1.0046] corā dūsayiṃsū”ti. Atha vā vibhattivipallāsamakatvā “acchindiṃsū”ti pade “pattacīvara”ntipadaṃ ajjhāharitvā “dūsesu”ntipade “sīla”nti pāṭhaṃ ajjhāharitvā yojetabbanti daṭṭhabbaṃ.

181. In the seventh, the words “tāsaṃ bhikkhunīnaṃ pacchā gacchantīnaṃ” should be connected with the remainder of the reading, “pattacīvaraṃ,” hence it is said, “pacchā gacchantīnaṃ pattacīvaraṃ.” Having changed the grammatical case of “Tā bhikkhuniyo pacchā gacchantiyo,” they should be connected with the word “dūsesuṃ,” hence it is said, “thieves violated those bhikkhunīs.” Alternatively, without making a change of grammatical case, the word “pattacīvaraṃ” should be supplied to the word “acchindiṃsu,” and the reading “sīlaṃ” should be supplied to the word “dūsesuṃ”; this is how it should be understood.

182-3. Saṃpubbo, vipubbo ca dhādhātu tvāpaccayo hotīti āha “saṃvidahitvā”ti. Kukkuṭoti tambacūḷo. So hi kukati āhāratthaṃ pāṇakādayo ādadātīti kukkuṭo. Ayanti gāmo. Adhikaraṇe ṇoti āha “sampadanti etthā”ti. Etthāti ca etasmiṃ gāme. Uttarapadassa adhikaraṇatthattā pubbapadena chaṭṭhīsamāsoti āha “kukkuṭāna”ntiādi. Evaṃ ṇasaddassa adhikaraṇatthaṃ, pubbapadena chaṭṭhīsamāsañca dassetvā idāni ṇasaddassa bhāvatthaṃ, pubbapadena bāhiratthasamāsañca dassetuṃ vuttaṃ “atha vā”ti. Tatthāti pacchimapāṭhe. Uppatitvāti uḍḍitvā uddhaṃ ākāsaṃ laṅgitvāti attho. Etthāti pacchimapāṭhe. Dvidhāti padagamanapakkhagamanavasena dvipakārena. “Upacāro na labbhatī”tiiminā gāmantaro na hoti, ekagāmoyeva pana hoti, tasmā āpattipi ekāyeva hotīti dasseti. Paccūseti pabhāte. So hi paṭiviruddhaṃ timiraṃ useti nāsetīti paccūsoti vuccati. Vassantassāti ravantassa. “Vacanato”tipadaṃ “āpattiyevā”tipade ñāpakahetu. Ratanamattantaroti kukkupamāṇena byavadhāno.

182-183. The root ‘dhā’ with the prefixes ‘saṃ’ and ‘vi’ takes the suffix ‘tvā’; hence, it is said, “having arranged (saṃvidahitvā).” “Kukkuṭa” means a red-crested fowl. For it calls “kuka” and gathers food such as insects, it is called “kukkuṭa.” “Aya” means this village. Regarding the suffix ‘ṇa’ in the sense of location, it is said, “they meet here (sampadanti etthā).” And “ettha” means “in this village.” Because the latter word has the sense of location, the former word forms a genitive compound; hence, it is said, “of the roosters (kukkuṭāna),” etc. Thus, having shown that the suffix ‘ṇa’ has the sense of location and forms a genitive compound with the former word, now, to show that the suffix ‘ṇa’ has the sense of state and forms a compound with an external meaning with the former word, it is said, “or else (atha vā).” “Tattha” refers to the latter reading. “Uppatitvā” means having flown up, having soared into the sky—this is the meaning. “Ettha” refers to the latter reading. “Dvidhā” means in two ways: by going on foot and by going on wings. By “no approach is possible (upacāro na labbhatī),” it is indicated that there is no interval between villages, but it is the same village; hence, there is only one offense. “Paccūsa” means dawn. For it dispels and destroys the opposing darkness, it is called “paccūsa.” “Vassantassa” means of the one who is roaring. The word “from the statement (vacanato)” is the reason for “there is an offense (āpattiyevā).” “Ratanamattantara” means an interval the size of a kukkupa.

Tatrāti [M 0.0056] “gāmantare gāmantare”ti vacane. Hīti vitthāro. Ubhopīti bhikkhubhikkhuniyopi saṃvidahantīti sambandho. Na vadantīti aṭṭhakathācariyā na kathayanti. Catunnaṃ maggānaṃ samāgamaṭṭhānaṃ catukkaṃ, dvinnaṃ, tiṇṇaṃ, catukkato atirekānaṃ vā maggānaṃ sambaddhaṭṭhānaṃ siṅghāṭakaṃ. Tatrāpīti upacārokkamanepi. Gāmatoti attano gāmato. Yāva na okkamanti, tāvāti yojanā. Sandhāyāti ārabbha. Athāti tasmiṃ nikkhamanakāle. Dvepīti bhikkhubhikkhuniyopi gacchantīti sambandho. Tanti vacanaṃ.

“Tattha” refers to the statement, “between village and village.” “Hi” is an elaboration. “Both” means both bhikkhus and bhikkhunīs make arrangements—this is the connection. “They do not say” means the commentary teachers do not explain. A “catukka” is a place where four paths meet; a place where two, three, or more than four paths meet is a “siṅghāṭaka.” “Even there” means even when approaching the vicinity. “From the village” means from one’s own village. The connection is, “as long as they do not enter.” “Sandhāya” means concerning. “Atha” means at that time of departure. “Both” means both bhikkhus and bhikkhunīs are going—this is the connection. “Taṃ” means the statement.

Hīti viseso. “Gāmantare gāmantare”ti purimasmiṃ naye atikkame anāpatti, okkamane āpattīti ayaṃ viseso.

“Hi” is the distinction. In the former method, regarding “from village to village,” there is no offense for passing through, but there is an offense for entering—this is the distinction.

184. Gatapubbatthāti gatapubbā attha bhavathāti attho. Ehi gacchāmāti vā āgaccheyyāsīti vā vadatīti yojanā. Cetiyavandanatthanti thūpassa vandituṃ.

184. “Gatapubbattha” means “you have gone before.” The connection is: he says, “Come, let us go,” or “You should come.” “Cetiyavandanattha” means for paying homage to the stupa.

185. Visaṅketenāti [V 1.0047] ettha kālavisaṅketo, dvāravisaṅketo, maggavisaṅketoti tividho. Tattha kālavisaṅketeneva anāpattiṃ sandhāya “visaṅketena gacchanti, anāpattī”ti āha. Dvāravisaṅketena vā maggavisaṅketena vā āpattimokkho natthi. Tamatthaṃ dassento āha “purebhatta”ntiādi. Cakkasamāruḷhāti iriyāpathacakkaṃ vā sakaṭacakkaṃ vā sammā āruḷhā. Janapadāti janakoṭṭhāsā. Pariyāyantīti pari punappunaṃ yanti ca āyanti cāti. Sattamaṃ.

185. “Visaṅketena” (by a different arrangement) here refers to three types: a different arrangement by time, a different arrangement by door, and a different arrangement by path. Among these, referring to no offense only by a different arrangement by time, it is said, “They go by a different arrangement, no offense.” There is no release from an offense by a different arrangement by door or by a different arrangement by path. Showing this meaning, he said, “before the meal,” etc. “Cakkasamāruḷha” means properly mounted on the cycle of movement or a cartwheel. “Janapada” means inhabited regions. “Pariyāyanti” means they go and come repeatedly. The seventh.

8. Nāvābhiruhanasikkhāpadaṃ

8. The Training Rule on Boarding a Boat

188. Aṭṭhame saha aññamaññaṃ thavanaṃ abhitthavanaṃ santhavo, saṅgamoti vuttaṃ hoti. Mittabhāvena santhavo mittasanthavo, lokehi assādetabbo ca so mittasanthavo ceti lokassādamittasanthavo, tassa vaso pabhū, tena vā āyattoti lokassādamittasanthavavaso, tena. Uddhaṃ gacchatīti uddhaṃgāminīti dassento āha “uddha”ntiādi. Uddhanti ca idha paṭisoto. Tenāha [M 0.0057] “nadiyā paṭisota”nti. “Uddhaṃgāmini”ntimātikāpadaṃ “ujjavanikāyā”tipadabhājaniyā saṃsandento āha “yasmā panā”tiādi. Yoti bhikkhu. Uddhaṃ javanatoti paṭisotaṃ gamanato. Tenāti tena hetunā. Assāti “uddhaṃgāmini”ntipadassa. Anusotaṃ idha adho nāmāti āha “anusota”nti. Assapīti pisaddo purimāpekkho. Tatthāti “uddhaṃgāminiṃ vā adhogāminiṃ vā”tivacane. Yanti nāvaṃ harantīti sambandho. Sampaṭipādanatthanti sammā paṭimukhaṃ pādanatthaṃ, ujupajjāpanatthanti attho. Etthāti nāvāyaṃ. “Ṭhapetvā”tipadabhājanimapekkhitvā “upayogatthe nissakkavacana”nti āha. “Aññatrā”ti mātikāpade apekkhite nissakkatthe nissakkavacanampi yujjateva.

188. In the eighth, it is said, “saha aññamaññaṃ thavanaṃ abhitthavanaṃ santhavo, saṅgamo,” meaning mutual praise, glorification, intimacy, and association. Friendly association is “mittasanthavo”; and that friendly association is to be enjoyed by the world, hence “lokassādamittasanthavo”; its power is abundant, or it is dependent on it, hence “lokassādamittasanthavavaso,” by that. Showing that “uddhaṃ gacchati” means “going upstream,” he says “uddha,” etc. And “uddhaṃ” here means against the current. Hence, it is said, “against the river’s current.” Connecting the matrix term “uddhaṃgāminī” with the phrase “ujjavanikāyā” (going upstream) in the analysis of the word, he says, “yasmā panā,” etc. “Yo” refers to the bhikkhu. “Uddhaṃ javanato” means from going against the current. “Tena” means by that reason. “Assa” refers to the term “uddhaṃgāminī.” He says “anusotaṃ” (downstream), meaning “adho” (down) here. “Assapi”—the particle “pi” refers back to the preceding. “Tattha” refers to the phrase “uddhaṃgāminiṃ vā adhogāminiṃ vā” (either going upstream or going downstream). The connection is: “yanti” means they carry the boat. “Sampaṭipādanattha” means for the purpose of properly setting forth, that is, for straightening it out. “Ettha” refers to the boat. Referring to the analysis of the word “ṭhapetvā” (except), he says, “it is an exclusionary expression in the sense of use.” When “aññatra” (except) is considered in the matrix term, an exclusionary expression in the sense of exclusion is also appropriate.

189. Ekaṃ tīraṃ agāmakaṃ araññaṃ hotīti yojanā. Addhayojanagaṇanāya pācittiyāni hontīti sambandho. Majjhena gamanepīti pisaddo agāmakaaraññatīrapassena gamane kā nāma kathāti dasseti. Na kevalaṃ nadiyāti kevalaṃ nadiyā eva anāpatti nāti yojanā, aññesupi samuddādīsu anāpattīti adhippāyo. Yopi bhikkhu gacchatīti sambandho. Hīti saccaṃ, yasmā vā.

189. The connection is: one bank is an uninhabited wilderness. The connection is: the pācittiya offenses occur by counting half-yojanas. The particle “pi” in “even by going through the middle” shows that if one travels along the side of the uninhabited wilderness bank, what need is there to say? The connection is: “not only in a river” means it is not that there is no offense only in a river; the intention is that there is also no offense in other bodies of water, such as the ocean. The connection is: “yopi bhikkhu” means the bhikkhu who goes. “Hi” means truly, or because.

191. Kālavisaṅketo, titthavisaṅketo, nāvāvisaṅketoti tividho visaṅketo. Tattha kālavisaṅketena [V 1.0048] anāpattiṃ sandhāya “visaṅketena abhiruhantī”ti vuttaṃ. Aññena visaṅketena āpattiyeva, tamatthaṃ dassento āha “idhāpī”tiādīti. Aṭṭhamaṃ.

191. There are three types of different arrangements: a different arrangement by time, a different arrangement by landing-place, and a different arrangement by boat. Among these, referring to no offense by a different arrangement by time, it is said, “they board by a different arrangement.” With another kind of different arrangement, there is indeed an offense—showing this meaning, he says, “here too,” etc. The eighth.

9. Paripācitasikkhāpadaṃ

9. The Training Rule on What Has Been Thoroughly Prepared

192. Navame mahānāgesūti mahāarahantesu tiṭṭhamānesu santesu, cetake pessabhūte navake bhikkhū nimantetīti adhippāyo. Itarathāti vibhattivipallāsato vā pāṭhasesato vā aññena pakārena. Antaraṃ majjhaṃ pattā kathā antarakathāti dassento āha “avasāna”ntiādi. Pakirīyitthāti pakatā, na [M 0.0058] pakatā vippakatāti vutte kariyamānakathāvāti āha “kariyamānā hotī”ti. Addhacchikenāti upaḍḍhacakkhunā. Tehīti therehi.

192. In the ninth, 'among great nāgas' means in the presence of great arahants; the intention is that one invites junior monks, who are like servants and messengers. Otherwise—due to a change of case ending, an omission in the reading, or in some other way. Showing that a talk that has reached the middle is an 'intervening talk,' he said, 'not yet concluded,' etc. 'Pakirīyittha' means 'was done'; if it is said 'done, not done, undone,' then to indicate that it is a talk being done, he said, 'is being done.' 'With half an eye' means with half an eye. 'By them' means by the elders.

194. Laddhabbanti laddhārahaṃ. Assāti “bhikkhuniparipācita”ntipadassa. Sammā ārabhitabboti samārambhoti dassento āha “samāraddhaṃ vuccatī”ti. Paṭiyāditassāti paripācitassa bhattassa. Gihīnaṃ samārambhoti gihisamārambho, katvatthe cetaṃ sāmivacanaṃ. Tatoti tato bhattato. Aññatrāti vinā. Tamatthaṃ vivaranto āha “taṃ piṇḍapātaṃ ṭhapetvā”ti. Padabhājane pana vuttanti sambandho. “Ñātakapavāritehī”tipadaṃ “asamāraddho”tipade kattā. Atthatoti bhikkhuniaparipācitaatthato. Tasmāti yasmā atthato samāraddhova hoti, tasmā.

194. “Should be obtained” means worthy of obtaining. “Its” refers to the word “thoroughly prepared by a bhikkhunī.” Showing that “properly initiated” means “undertaking,” he said, “it is called 'undertaken.'” “Of that prepared” refers to the thoroughly prepared meal. “Undertaking by householders” means a householder's undertaking; and this is a genitive word in the sense of the agent. “From that” means from that meal. “Except” means without. Clarifying that meaning, he said, “having set aside that almsfood.” “But in the analysis of words, it is stated”—this is the connection. The word “by relatives who have invited” is the agent of the word “not undertaken.” “In meaning” means in the meaning of that not thoroughly prepared by a bhikkhunī. “Therefore” means “because in meaning it is actually undertaken, therefore.”

195. Paṭiyāditanti paṭiyattaṃ. Pakatiyā paṭiyattaṃ pakatipaṭiyattanti dassento āha “pakatiyā”tiādi. Mahāpaccariyaṃ pana vuttanti sambandho. Tassāti tasseva bhikkhuno. Aññassāti tato aññassa bhikkhuno.

195. “Prepared” means “arranged.” Showing that “naturally arranged” means “arranged by nature,” he said, “naturally,” etc. “But in the Mahāpaccarī, it is stated”—this is the connection. “For him” means for that very monk. “For another” means for a monk other than him.

197. Bhikkhuniparipācitepīti pisaddo bhikkhuniaparipācite kā nāma kathāti dassetīti. Navamaṃ.

197. The particle ‘pi’ in “even if thoroughly prepared by a bhikkhunī” shows that there is no need to mention what happens if it is not thoroughly prepared by a bhikkhunī. The ninth.

10. Rahonisajjasikkhāpadaṃ

10. The Training Rule on Sitting in Private

198. Dasame pāḷiattho cāti ettha pāḷisaddo vinicchiyasadde ca yojetabbo “pāḷivinicchayo”ti. Hīti saccaṃ, yasmā vā. “Idaṃ sikkhāpada”ntipadaṃ “ekapariccheda”ntipade [V 1.0049] tulyatthakattā, “paññatta”ntipade kammaṃ. Uparīti acelakavaggeti. Dasamaṃ.

198. In the tenth, regarding the phrase 'pāḷiattho ca', here the word 'pāḷi' should be combined with the word 'vinicchiya' to form 'pāḷivinicchayo'. 'Hī' means 'truly', or 'because'. The word 'this training rule' is the agent in relation to the word 'a single section' because they are equivalent in meaning, and it is the object of the word 'established'. 'Upari' means in the Acelaka section. Tenth.

Ovādavaggo tatiyo.

The Ovāda Section, the third.

4. Bhojanavaggo

4. The Food Section.

1. Āvasathapiṇḍasikkhāpada-atthayojanā

1. Explanation of the Meaning of the Training Rule on Alms-food at a Lodging.

203. Bhojanavaggassa [M 0.0059] paṭhame āvasathe paññatto piṇḍo āvasathapiṇḍoti dassento āha “samantā”tiādi. Parikkhittanti parivutaṃ āvasathanti sambandho. Addhaṃ pathaṃ gacchantīti addhikā. Gilāyanti rujantīti gilānā. Gabbho kucchiṭṭhasatto etāsanti gabbhiniyo. Malaṃ pabbājentīti pabbajitā, tesaṃ yathānurūpanti sambandho. Paññattāni mañcapīṭhāni etthāti paññattamañcapīṭho, taṃ. Anekagabbhaparicchedaṃ anekapamukhaparicchedaṃ āvasathaṃ katvāti yojanā. Tatthāti āvasathe. Tesaṃ tesanti addhikādīnaṃ. Hiyyosaddassa atītānantarāhassa ca anāgatānantarāhassa ca vācakattā idha anāgatānantarāhavācakoti āha “svepī”ti. Kuhiṃ gatā iti vutteti yojanā. “Kukkuccāyanto”tipadassa nāmadhātuṃ dassento āha “kukkuccaṃ karonto”ti.

203. In the first of the Food Section, showing that alms-food established at a lodging is 'lodging alms-food', he said, 'from all around', etc. 'Enclosed' means 'surrounded', and this relates to 'lodging'. 'Those who go on a long road' are travelers. 'Those who are ill' are the sick. 'A fetus, a being in the womb, is in them'—these are pregnant women. 'Those who drive out defilements' are those who have gone forth; and this relates to 'as is appropriate for them'. 'Beds and benches are established here' is the meaning of 'paññattamañcapīṭho', which is in the accusative case. 'Having made a lodging with multiple rooms and multiple frontages' is the explanation. 'There' means in the lodging. 'For each of them' refers to the travelers, etc. Since the word 'hiyyo' can refer to the immediately preceding day or the immediately following day, here it refers to the immediately following day, as stated with 'sve'pi' (also tomorrow). 'Where have they gone? it is said'—this is the explanation. To indicate the denominative verb of the word 'kukkuccāyanto', he said, 'kukkuccaṃ karonto' (doing scrupulousness).

206. “Addhayojanaṃ vā yojanaṃ vā”tiiminā “pakkamitu”ntipadassa kammaṃ dasseti. “Gantu”ntiiminā kamusaddassa padavikkhepatthaṃ dasseti. “Anodissā”tipadassa tvāpaccayantabhāvaṃ dassetuṃ “anuddisitvā”ti vuttaṃ. Pāsaṃ ḍetīti pāsaṇḍo, sattānaṃ cittesu diṭṭhipāsaṃ khipatīti attho. Atha vā taṇhāpāsaṃ, diṭṭhipāsañca ḍeti uḍḍetīti pāsaṇḍo, taṃ pāsaṇḍaṃ. Yāvatattho paññatto hotīti yāvatā attho hoti, tāvatā paññatto hotīti yojanā. “Yāvadattho”tipi pāṭho, ayamevattho. Dakāro padasandhikaro. Sakiṃ bhuñjitabbanti ekadivasaṃ sakiṃ bhuñjitabbanti attho. Tenāha “ekadivasaṃ bhuñjitabba”nti.

206. By 'half a yojana or a yojana', he indicates the object of the word 'to depart'. By 'to go', he indicates the meaning of 'stepping' for the root 'kamu'. To show that the word 'anodissā' is a form ending in the gerund suffix '-tvā', 'anuddisitvā' (having not specified) is stated. 'He throws a snare'—this is a heretic; the meaning is that he throws the snare of views into the minds of beings. Alternatively, he throws (ḍeti) or tears apart (uḍḍeti) the snare of craving and the snare of views—this is a heretic; that heretic. 'As much as is needed is established'—this is the explanation: as much meaning as there is, that much is established. The reading 'yāvadattho' also occurs; this is the same meaning. The letter 'd' serves as a word connector. 'To be eaten once' means to be eaten once in a day. Therefore he said, 'to be eaten once a day'.

Etthāti [V 1.0050] imasmiṃ sikkhāpade. Ekakulena vā paññattanti sambandho. Bhuñjituṃ na vaṭṭati ekato hutvā paññattattāti adhippāyo. Nānākulehi paññattaṃ piṇḍanti yojanā. Bhuñjituṃ vaṭṭati nānākulāni ekato ahutvā visuṃ visuṃ paññattattāti adhippāyo. Yopi piṇḍo [M 0.0060] chijjatīti sambandho. Upacchinditvāti asaddhiyādipāpacittattā upacchinditvā.

'Here' means in this training rule. 'Or established by a single family'—this is the connection. The intention is that it is not proper to eat because it was established as a single entity. 'Alms-food established by multiple families'—this is the explanation. The intention is that it is proper to eat because it was established by multiple families not as a single entity but separately. 'Whatever alms-food is cut off'—this is the connection. 'Having cut it off' means having cut it off due to unwholesome thoughts such as lack of faith, etc.

208. Anuvasitvāti punappunaṃ vasitvā. Antarāmagge gacchantattā “gacchanto bhuñjatī”ti idaṃ tāva yuttaṃ hotu, gataṭṭhāne pana gamitattā kathaṃ? Paccuppannasamīpopi atīto tena saṅgahitattā yuttaṃ. “Kuto nu tvaṃ bhikkhu āgacchasī”tiādīsu (saṃ. ni. 1.130) viya. Taṃsamīpopi hi tādiso. Nānāṭṭhānesu nānākulānaṃ santake pakatiyā anāpattibhāvato nānāṭṭhānesu ekakulasseva santakaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ “anāpattī”ti. Āraddhassa vicchedattā “puna ekadivasaṃ bhuñjituṃ labhatī”ti vuttaṃ. “Odissā”ti sāmaññato vuttepi bhikkhūyeva gahetabbāti āha “bhikkhūnaṃyevā”ti. Paṭhamaṃ.

208. 'Anuvasitvā' means having stayed repeatedly. Since he is traveling along the way, let the phrase 'he eats while going' be appropriate; but how can this apply when he has arrived at his destination, since the journey is over? It is fitting because the recent past is included by that present tense usage, just as in phrases such as, 'From where, bhikkhu, do you come?' (Saṃ. Ni. 1.130).
