'Byūho' is that which is arrayed (`viyūhīyate`) and gathered (`sampiṇḍīyate`); 'senāya byūho' (the army's array) is `senābyūho`. This shows the meaning of 'senāya viyūha,' and so forth. 'Aṇīkaṃ' is so called because it makes a terrifying sound (`aṇati`); with a retroflex 'ṇa'. An elephant itself is an `aṇīka`, hence `hatthāṇīkaṃ`. The same method applies to the rest. The connection is: 'with that elephant which was mentioned before.' The Tenth.

Acelakavaggo pañcamo.

The Fifth Chapter: The Acelaka Chapter.

6. Surāpānavaggo

6. The Chapter on Drinking Intoxicants

1. Surāpānasikkhāpada-atthayojanā

1. The Exposition of the Meaning of the Training Rule on Drinking Intoxicants

326. Surāpānavaggassa paṭhame bhaddā vati etthāti bhaddavatikāti ca, bhaddā vati bhaddavati, sā ettha atthīti bhaddavatikāti ca atthaṃ dassento āha “so”tiādi. Soti gāmo labhīti sambandho. Pathaṃ gacchantīti pathāvinoti kate addhikāyevāti āha “addhikā”ti. Addhaṃ gacchantīti addhikā. “Pathikā”tipi pāṭho, ayamevattho. “Tejasā teja”ntipadāni sambandhāpekkhāni ca honti[M 0.0101], padānaṃ samānattā sambandho ca samānoti maññituṃ sakkuṇeyyā ca honti, tasmā tesaṃ sambandhañca tassa asamānatañca dassetuṃ vuttaṃ “attano tejasā nāgassa teja”nti. “Ānubhāvenā”tiiminā pana tejasaddassa atthaṃ dasseti. Kapotassa pādo kapoto upacārena, tassa eso kāpoto, vaṇṇo. Kāpoto viya vaṇṇo assāti kāpotikāti dassento āha “kapotapādasamavaṇṇarattobhāsā”ti. Pasannasaddassa pasādasaddhādayo nivattetuṃ “surāmaṇḍassetaṃ adhivacana”nti vuttaṃ. Pañcābhiññassa satoti pañcābhiññassa samānassa sāgatassāti yojanā.

326. In the first section of the Surāpānavagga, to show the meaning of `Bhaddavatikā` as both 'bhaddā vati ettha' and 'bhaddā vati bhaddavati, sā ettha atthi,' he says 'so,' and so forth. The connection is: 'so gāmo labhī.' Regarding `pathāvino`, meaning 'those who go on a path,' he says `addhikā`, as it simply means travelers. `Addhikā` are those who go on a journey. `Pathikā` is also a reading with the same meaning. The words 'tejasā tejaṃ' are dependent on a connection, and because the words are similar, one might think the connection is also similar. Therefore, to show their connection and its dissimilarity, it is said: 'the nāga's splendor by his own splendor.' By 'ānubhāvena,' he then shows the meaning of the word 'tejasā.' The foot of a pigeon is metaphorically 'kapoto'; its color is 'kāpoto.' To show that `kāpotikā` means 'having a color like a pigeon's foot,' he says 'kapotapādasamavaṇṇarattobhāsā.' To exclude meanings such as 'clarity' or 'faith' for the word 'pasanna,' it is said: 'this is a designation for the scum of liquor.' 'Pañcābhiññassa sato' is to be construed as 'pañcābhiññassa samānassa sāgatassa'.

328. “Madhukapupphādīnaṃ rasena kato”tiiminā pupphānaṃ rasena kato āsavo pupphāsavoti vacanatthaṃ dasseti. Esa nayo “phalāsavo”tiādīsupi. Surāmerayānaṃ visesaṃ dassetuṃ vuttaṃ “surā nāmā”tiādi. Piṭṭhakiṇṇapakkhittāti piṭṭhena ca kiṇṇena ca pakkhittā katā vāruṇīti sambandho. Kiṇṇāti ca surāya bījaṃ. Tañhi kiranti nānāsambhārāni missībhavanti etthāti kiṇṇāti vuccati. Tassāyeva maṇḍeti yojanā. Suranāmakena ekena vanacarakena katāti surā. Madaṃ janetīti merayaṃ.

328. By 'made from the juice of madhuka flowers, etc.,' he shows the etymology of `pupphāsavo` as 'an intoxicant (`āsavo`) made from the juice of flowers.' The same method applies to `phalāsavo`, and so forth. To show the distinction between `surā` and `meraya`, it is said '`surā` is,' and so forth. The connection for `piṭṭhakiṇṇapakkhittā` is that `vāruṇī` is made by adding flour and yeast. `Kiṇṇa` is the 'seed' of liquor. It is called `kiṇṇa` because various ingredients are scattered (`kiranti`) and mixed in it. The construction is 'tassā yeva maṇḍo.' `Surā` is so called because it was made by a forest dweller named Sura. `Meraya` is so called because it produces intoxication (`mada`).

329. Loṇasovīrakanti [V 1.0085] evaṃnāmakaṃ pānaṃ. Suttantipi evameva. Tasminti sūpasaṃpāke. Telaṃ pana pacantīti sambandho. Natthi tikhiṇaṃ majjaṃ etthāti atikhiṇamajjaṃ, atikhiṇamajje tasmiṃyeva teleti attho. Yaṃ panāti telaṃ pana. Tikhiṇaṃ majjaṃ imassa telassāti tikhiṇamajjaṃ. Yatthāti tele. Ariṭṭhoti evaṃnāmakaṃ bhesajjaṃ. Tanti ariṭṭhaṃ, “sandhāyā”tipade avuttakammaṃ. Etanti “amajjaṃ ariṭṭha”ntivacanaṃ, “vutta”ntipade vuttakammanti. Paṭhamaṃ.

329. 'Loṇasovīraka' is a drink of that name. In the Suttanta too, it is likewise. 'Tasmiṃ' refers to the preparation of soup. The connection is 'telaṃ pana pacanti' (they cook oil). 'Natthi tikhiṇaṃ majjaṃ ettha' (there is no sharp intoxicant in this) means 'atikhiṇamajjaṃ' (non-sharp intoxicant); the meaning is that it is oil in that very non-sharp intoxicant. 'Yaṃ pana' refers to the oil. 'Tikhiṇaṃ majjaṃ imassa telassa' (sharp intoxicant for this oil) means 'tikhiṇaṃ majjaṃ' (sharp intoxicant). 'Yattha' refers to the oil. 'Ariṭṭha' is a medicine of that name. 'Taṃ' refers to 'ariṭṭha'; in the word 'sandhāyā', this is the unstated object. 'Etaṃ' refers to the statement 'amajjaṃ ariṭṭha' (non-intoxicating ariṭṭha); in the word 'vutta', this is the stated object. The first.

2. Aṅgulipatodakasikkhāpadaṃ

2. The Training Rule on Prodding with a Finger

330. Dutiye aṅgulīhi patujjanaṃ aṅgulipatodo, soyeva aṅgulipatodakoti dassento āha “aṅgulīhī”tiādi. Uttantoti [M 0.0102] avatapanto. Avatapantoti ca atthato kilamantoyevāti āha “kilamanto”ti. Kilamanto hutvāti yojanā. Assāsagahaṇena passāsopi gahetabboti āha “assāsapassāsasañcāro”ti. Tampīti bhikkhunimpīti. Dutiyaṃ.

330. In the second section, showing that 'aṅgulipatoda' is 'prodding with the fingers' and that this very thing is 'aṅgulipatodaka', he says 'aṅgulīhi' (with the fingers), and so on. The term 'uttanto' means 'avatapanto'. And since 'avatapanto' in essence means 'wearying', he says 'kilamanto' (wearying). The construction is 'having become weary'. By the taking of 'assāsa' (in-breath), the out-breath should also be understood, therefore he says 'assāsapassāsasañcāro' (the passage of in-breaths and out-breaths). 'Taṃpi' means 'even a bhikkhunī'. The second.

3. Hasadhammasikkhāpadaṃ

3. The Training Rule on Jocularity

335. Tatiye pakārena karīyati ṭhapīyatīti pakataṃ paññattanti dassento āha “yaṃ bhagavatā”tiādi. Yanti sikkhāpadaṃ.

335. In the third section, showing that 'pakataṃ paññattaṃ' means 'it is done and established in a certain manner', he says 'yaṃ bhagavatā' (what by the Blessed One), and so on. 'Yaṃ' means the training rule.

336. Hasasaṅkhāto dhammo sabhāvo hasadhammoti vutte atthato kīḷikāyevāti āha “kīḷikā vuccatī”ti.

336. When 'hasadhamma' is said to be the phenomenon or nature known as laughter, he says 'kīḷikā vuccati' (it is called play), meaning it is, in essence, just play.

337. Gopphakānanti caraṇagaṇṭhikānaṃ. Te hi pāde pādaṃ ṭhapanakāle aññamaññūpari ṭhapanato gopīyantīti gopphā, te eva gopphakāti vuccanti. Pādassa hi upari pādaṃ ṭhapanakāle ekassa upari eko na ṭhapetabbo. Tenāha bhagavā “pāde pādaṃ accādhāyā”ti (dī. ni. 2.196; ma. ni. 1.423; a. ni. 3.16). Oṭṭhajo dutiyo. Orohantassa bhikkhunoti sambandho.

337. 'Gopphakānaṃ' means 'of the ankle bones'. Indeed, they are called 'gopphā' because when placing one foot upon the other, they are protected; these very things are called 'gopphakā'. Indeed, when placing one foot upon the other, one should not be placed over the other. Therefore the Blessed One said: 'placing foot upon foot' (Dī. Ni. 2.196; Ma. Ni. 1.423; A. Ni. 3.16). 'Oṭṭhaja' is the second. The connection is 'to the descending bhikkhunī'.

338. Phiyārittādīhīti ādisaddena laṅkārādayo saṅgaṇhāti. Keci vadantīti sambandho. Patanuppatanavāresūti patanavāra uppatanavāresu. Tatthāti tassaṃ khittakathalāyaṃ. Hīti saccaṃ[V 1.0086], yasmā vā. Ṭhapetvā kīḷantassāti sambandho. Likhituṃ vaṭṭati kīḷādhippāyassa virahitattāti adhippāyo. Kīḷādhippāyena atthajotakaṃ akkharaṃ likhantassāpi āpattiyevāti vadanti. Etthāti imasmiṃ sikkhāpadeti. Tatiyaṃ.

338. By 'phiyārittādīhi' (with the game of oars, etc.), the word 'etc.' includes `laṅkāra` and so on. The connection is 'keci vadanti' (some say). 'Patanuppatanavāresu' means 'in the turns of falling and rising'. 'Tattha' means 'in that laid-out playing area'. 'Hī' means 'truly' or 'because'. The connection is 'to one playing, having set it up'. The intention is that it is allowable to write, because it is devoid of the intention of play. They say that even for one writing a letter that reveals meaning with the intention of play, there is an offense. 'Ettha' means 'in this training rule'. The third.

4. Anādariyasikkhāpadaṃ

4. The Training Rule on Disrespect

342. Catutthe dhammo nāma tantiyevāti āha “tantī”ti. Paveṇīti tasseva vevacanaṃ. “Taṃ vā na sikkhitukāmo”ti ettha taṃsaddassa atthamāvikātuṃ vuttaṃ “yena paññattenā”ti. Vinaye apaññattaṃ [M 0.0103] sandhāya vuttaṃ “apaññattenā”ti āha “sutte vā abhidhamme vā āgatenā”ti.

342. In the fourth section, the word 'dhamma' means the textual tradition, hence it is said 'the text' (`tantī`). 'Paveṇī' is a synonym for that. To reveal the meaning of the word 'taṃ' in 'or not wishing to learn that,' it is said 'by what is prescribed.' Referring to what is not prescribed in the Vinaya, it is said 'by what is not prescribed,' hence it is said 'by what comes in the Sutta or the Abhidhamma.'

344. Paveṇiyāti upāliādikāya ācariyaparamparasaṅkhātāya tantiyā. Kurundiyaṃ vuttanti sambandho. Mahāpaccariyaṃ vuttanti sambandho. Taṃ sabbanti kurundivādamahāpaccarivādasaṅkhātaṃ sabbaṃ taṃ vacanaṃ. Paveṇiyā āgateti paveṇiyā āgatasaṅkhāte mahāaṭṭhakathāvādeti. Catutthaṃ.

344. 'Paveṇiyā' means by the textual tradition known as the lineage of teachers beginning with Upāli. The connection is with what is stated in the Kurundi. The connection is with what is stated in the Mahāpaccarī. 'All that' means all that teaching known as the doctrines of the Kurundi and the Mahāpaccarī. 'Paveṇiyā āgate' refers to the doctrine of the Great Commentary, which is known as that which has 'come down by tradition.' The fourth.

345. Pañcame manussaviggaheti manussaviggahapārājiketi. Pañcamaṃ.

345. In the fifth, 'manussaviggaha' means the pārājika offense concerning a human being. The fifth.

6. Jotisikkhāpadaṃ

6. The Training Rule on Fire

350. Chaṭṭhe janapadassa nāmattā bahuvacanavasena “bhaggesū”ti pāḷiyaṃ vuttaṃ. Susumārasaṇṭhāno pabbatasaṅkhāto giri etthāti susumāragiri, etassa vā māpitakāle susumāro girati saddaṃ niggirati etthāti susumāragirīti atthamanapekkhitvā vuttaṃ “nagarassa nāma”nti. Taṃ panāti vanaṃ pana. “Migāna”ntiādinā migānaṃ abhayo dīyati etthāti migadāyoti atthaṃ dasseti.

350. In the sixth, because it is the name of a country, it is stated in the Pāli text as 'Bhaggesu' in the plural. A mountain (`giri`) shaped like a crocodile (`susumāra`) is there, hence Susumāragiri. Or, at the time of its construction, a crocodile makes a swallowing sound (`girati`) there, hence Susumāragiri; without considering this etymological meaning, it is said to be 'the name of the city'. 'Taṃ pana' means that forest, however. By 'Migānaṃ', and so on, he shows the meaning of Migadāya as: 'a refuge is given to deer there'.

352. “Jotike”tipadassa jotissa aggissa karaṇaṃ jotikanti dassetuṃ vuttaṃ “jotikaraṇe”ti.

352. To show that the word 'jotike' means 'jotika'—the making of light or fire—it is stated as 'jotikaraṇe' (in the making of a fire).

354. “Samādahitukāmatāyā”tipadaṃ [V 1.0087] “araṇisaṇṭhāpanato”tipade hetu. Jālāti sikhā. Sā hi jalati dibbatīti jālāti vuccati.

354. The word 'samādahitukāmatāya' is the reason for the word 'araṇisaṇṭhāpanato.' 'Jālā' means flame. It is called 'jālā' because it burns (`jalati`) and shines (`dibbati`).

Patilātaṃ ukkhipatīti ettha “patitālāta”nti vattabbe takāralopaṃ katvā sandhivasena patilātanti vuttanti āha “alātaṃ patitaṃ ukkhipatī”ti. Alātanti ummukkaṃ. Tañhi ādittaṃ hutvā atiuṇhattā na lātabbaṃ na gaṇhitabbanti alātanti vuccati. Avijjhātanti jhāyanato ḍayhanato avigataṃ alātanti sambandho. Jhāyanaṃ ḍayhanaṃ jhātaṃ, vigataṃ jhātaṃ imassālātassāti vijjhātaṃ.

Regarding 'patilātaṃ ukkhipati', here, when 'patitālātaṃ' should have been said, the letter 'ta' was elided, and by means of sandhi it is stated as 'patilātaṃ'; thus he says 'alātaṃ patitaṃ ukkhipati' (he lifts a fallen firebrand). 'Alāta' means a firebrand. It is called 'alāta' because, having been lit, it is too hot to be taken or held. 'Avijjhātaṃ' means a firebrand from which burning or blazing has not ceased; this is the connection. 'Jhātaṃ' is burning or blazing. 'Vijjātaṃ' means that for this firebrand, the burning has ceased.

356. Padīpādīnīti [M 0.0104] padīpajotikādīni. Tatthāti tāsu duṭṭhavāḷamigaamanussasaṅkhātāsu āpadāsu nimittabhūtāsu. Nimittatthe cetaṃ bhummavacananti. Chaṭṭhaṃ.

356. 'Padīpādīni' means lamps, lights, and so on. 'Tattha' refers to those dangers which have become signs, namely fierce wild animals and non-humans. And this is the locative case in the sense of a sign. The sixth.

7. Nahānasikkhāpadaṃ

7. The Training Rule on Bathing

366. Sattame pāraṃ gacchanto na kevalaṃ saudakāya nadiyā eva nhāyituṃ vaṭṭati, sukkhāya nadiyāpi vaṭṭatīti dassento āha “sukkhāyā”tiādi. Ukkiritvāti viyūhitvā. Āvāṭāyeva khuddakaṭṭhena āvāṭakā, tesūti. Sattamaṃ.

366. In the seventh, to show that one who is going to the other shore is permitted to bathe not only in a river with water but also in a dry river, it is stated: 'in a dry one,' and so on. 'Ukkiritvā' means having cleared away. `Āvāṭakā` are pits (`āvāṭā`) made with small sticks; 'tesu' means 'in them'. The seventh.

8. Dubbaṇṇakaraṇasikkhāpadaṃ

8. The Training Rule on Causing Discoloration

368. Aṭṭhame alabhīti labhoti vacanatthe apaccayaṃ katvā ṇapaccayassa svatthabhāvaṃ dassetuṃ vuttaṃ “labhoyeva lābho”ti. Apaccayamakatvā pakatiyā ṇapaccayopi yuttoyevāti daṭṭhabbaṃ. Saddantaropi atthantarābhāvā samāso hotīti āha “navacīvaralābhenāti vattabbe”ti. Anunāsikalopanti “nava”nti ettha niggahītassa vināsaṃ. Niggahītañhi nāsaṃ anugatattā “anunāsika”nti vuccati, tassa adassana, makatvāti attho. Majjhe ṭhitapadadvayeti “nava”nti ca “cīvaralābhenā”ti ca dvinnaṃ padānamantare “ṭhite panā”ti ca “bhikkhunā”ti ca padadvaye. Niddhāraṇe cetaṃ bhummavacanaṃ. Nipātoti nipātamattaṃ. Alabhīti labhoti vacanatthassa abhidheyyatthaṃ dassetuṃ “bhikkhunā”ti vuttanti āha “bhikkhunā”tiādi. Padabhājane pana vuttanti sambandho. Yanti yaṃ cīvaraṃ. “Cīvara”nti ettha cīvarasarūpaṃ dassento āha “yaṃ nivāsetuṃ vā”tiādi. Cammakāranīlanti cammakārānaṃ tiphale pakkhittassa ayagūthassa nīlaṃ. Mahāpaccariyaṃ [V 1.0088] vuttanti sambandho. Dubbaṇṇo karīyati anenāti dubbaṇṇakaraṇaṃ, kappabindunti āha “kappabinduṃ sandhāyā”ti. Ādiyantena bhikkhunā ādātabbanti sambandho. Koṇesūti antesu. Vāsaddo aniyamavikappattho. Akkhimaṇḍalamattaṃ vāti akkhimaṇḍalassa pamāṇaṃ vā kappabindūti sambandho. Paṭṭe vāti anuvātapaṭṭe [M 0.0105] vā. Gaṇṭhiyaṃ vāti gaṇṭhikapaṭṭe vā. Pāḷikappoti dve vā tisso vā tato adhikā vā binduāvalī katvā kato kappo. Kaṇṇikakappoti kaṇṇikaṃ viya bindugocchakaṃ katvā kato kappo. Ādisaddena agghiyakappādayo saṅgaṇhāti. Sabbatthāti sabbāsu aṭṭhakathāsu. Ekopi bindu vaṭṭoyeva vaṭṭatīti āha “ekaṃ vaṭṭabindu”nti.

368. In the eighth, `alābhi` has the meaning of `labhati`. To show the inherent meaning of the ṇa-affix, without treating it as a suffix, it is said, 'labhoyeva lābho.' It should be understood that even without treating it as a suffix, the ṇa-affix is naturally appropriate. Because there is no difference in meaning despite the different words, a compound is formed. Thus, it is said, 'when `navacīvaralābhena` should be said.' `Anunāsikalopa` means the elision of the nasal sound in `navaṃ`. The niggahīta is called `anunāsika` because it follows the nose; its disappearance means not making it into 'm'. `Majjhe ṭhitapadadvaye` refers to the two words `ṭhite pana` and `bhikkhunā` placed between the two words `navaṃ` and `cīvaralābhena`. This is a locative case in the sense of specification. `Nipāto` means merely a particle. To show the denotative meaning of the phrase `alābhi` which means `labhati`, it is said `bhikkhunā`, and so on. The connection is stated in the analysis of the words. `Yanti` refers to `yaṃ cīvaraṃ`. To indicate the nature of the robe, it is said, `yaṃ nivāsetuṃ vā`, and so on. `Cammakāranīlaṃ` refers to the blue dye from iron-scum that has been put in the three myrobalans by leatherworkers. This is connected to what is stated in the Mahāpaccarī. `Dubbaṇṇakaraṇa` is that by which disfigurement is made; it is said `kappabinduṃ sandhāya`, referring to the `kappabindu`. The connection is that it should be taken by the bhikkhu who is receiving it. `Koṇesūti` means `antesu` (at the edges). The word `vā` has the meaning of an unrestricted option. `Akkhimaṇḍalamattaṃ vā` means 'or the size of the pupil of an eye,' and the connection is that the `kappabindu` is the size of the pupil of an eye. `Paṭṭe vā` means on a border-strip. `Gaṇṭhiyaṃ vā` means on a knotted cloth band. `Pāḷikappo` is a marking made by making two, three, or more lines of dots. `Kaṇṇikakappo` is a marking made by making a cluster of dots like a pericarp. The word `ādi` includes markings like the `agghiyakappa` and others. `Sabbatthā` means in all the commentaries. Even one dot is permissible if it is round, hence it is said 'one round dot.'

371. Aggaḷādīnīti ādisaddena anuvātaparibhaṇḍe saṅgaṇhātīti. Aṭṭhamaṃ.

371. Regarding `aggaḷādīni`, by the word `ādi` it includes the border-strip and waistband. The eighth.

9. Vikappanasikkhāpadaṃ

9. The Training Rule on Designation

374. Navame tassāti ettha tasaddassa visayo cīvarasāmikoyevāti āha “cīvarasāmikassā”ti. Dutiyassa tasaddassa visayo vinayadharoyevāti āha “yenā”tiādi. “Avissāsanto”tipadassa kiriyāvisesanabhāvaṃ dassetuṃ vuttaṃ “avissāsenā”ti. Tenāti vinayadharenāti. Navamaṃ.

374. In the ninth, regarding `tassa`, here the referent of the word `tassa` is only the owner of the robe, hence it is said `cīvarasāmikassa`. The referent of the second word `tassa` is only the Vinaya expert, hence it is said `yena`, and so on. To show the adverbial nature of the word `avissāsanto`, it is said `avissāsena`. `Tena` means `vinayadharena` (by the Vinaya expert). The ninth.

10. Cīvarāpanidhānasikkhāpadaṃ

10. The Training Rule on Concealing Robes

377. Dasame “apanetvā”tiiminā apaityūpasaggassa atthaṃ dasseti. Nidhentīti nigūhitvā ṭhapenti. Hasādhippāyoti hasaṃ, hasanatthāya vā adhippāyo. Parikkhārassa sarūpaṃ dassetuṃ vuttaṃ “pattatthavikādi”nti. Pattassa pāḷiyamāgatattā pattassa thavikāti atthoyeva gahetabbo, na patto ca thavikā cāti. “Samaṇena nāmā”tipadaṃ “bhavitu”ntipade bhāvakattāti. Dasamaṃ.

377. In the tenth, by `apanetvā`, it shows the meaning of the prefix `apa`. `Nidhenti` means they conceal and put it aside. `Hasādhippāyo` means laughter, or an intention for laughter. To show the nature of requisites, it is said `pattatthavikādi` (bowl-bag, etc.). Since `patta` (bowl) is mentioned in the Pāli text, the meaning should be taken only as 'a bag for the bowl', not 'a bowl and a bag'. The phrase `samaṇena nāma` is the agent of the action in the word `bhavituṃ`. The tenth.

Surāpānavaggo chaṭṭho.

The Sixth Chapter: On Drinking Liquor.

7. Sappāṇakavaggo

7. The Chapter on Water Containing Living Beings

1. Sañciccapāṇasikkhāpada-atthayojanā

1. Exposition of the Meaning of the Training Rule on Intentionally Depriving a Living Being of Life

382. Sappāṇakavaggassa [V 1.0089] paṭhame usuṃ asati khipati anenāti issāsoti kate dhanuyeva mukhyato issāso nāma, dhanuggahā- cariyo [M 0.0106] pana upacārena. Usuṃ asati khipatīti issāsoti kate dhanuggahācariyo issāso nāma, idha pana upacārattho vā kattuttho vā gahetabboti āha “dhanuggahācariyo hotī”ti. Pabbajitakāle issāsassa ayuttattā vuttaṃ “gihikāle”ti. Voropitāti ettha vi ava pubbassa ruhadhātussa adhippāyatthaṃ dassetuṃ vuttaṃ “viyojitā”ti.

382. In the first rule of the Sappāṇaka Chapter, when it is stated, `usuṃ asati khipati anenāti issāso` (that by which one shoots an arrow is an `issāsa`), `issāsa` primarily means the bow itself, but by extension, the archery teacher. When it is stated, `usuṃ asati khipatīti issāso` (one who shoots an arrow is an `issāsa`), `issāsa` means the archery teacher; but here it should be taken either in its extended sense or in the sense of the agent, hence it is said, `dhanuggahācariyo hoti` (he is an archery teacher). Because being an archer is unsuitable at the time of going forth, it is stated `gihikāle` (in the time of a householder). Regarding `voropitā`, here it is said `viyojitā` (separated) to show the intended meaning of the root `ruh` preceded by the prefixes `vi` and `ava`.

Yasmā gacchatīti sambandho. Etanti “jīvitā voropitā”tivacanaṃ. Kasmā vohāramattameva hoti, nanu yato kutoci yasmiṃ kismiṃci viyojite dve vatthūni viya visuṃ tiṭṭhanti pāṇato jīvite viyojite pāṇajīvitāpīti āha “na hetthā”tiādi. Hīti saccaṃ. Etthāti “jīvitā voropitā”tivacane dassetunti sambandho. Kiñci jīvitaṃ nāmāti yojanā. Ayaṃ panettha atthasambandho – sīsālaṅkāre sīsato viyojite sīsaṃ alaṅkārato visuṃ tiṭṭhati yathā, evaṃ jīvite pāṇato viyojite jīvitaṃ pāṇato visuṃ na tiṭṭhati nāmāti. Aññadatthūti ekaṃsena. “Pāṇa”nti sāmaññato vuttopi manussapāṇassa pārājikaṭṭhāne gahitattā idha pārisesañāyena tiracchānapāṇova gahetabboti āha “tiracchānagatoyeva pāṇo”ti. Tanti pāṇaṃ. Mahante pana pāṇeti sambandho.

The connection is `yasmā gacchati`. `Etanti` refers to the statement `jīvitā voropitā` (deprived of life). Why is it merely a conventional expression? Surely, when one thing is separated from another, the two things stand apart. When life is separated from a living being, do the living being and life also stand apart? To this, it is said `na hettha`, and so on. `Hīti` means truly. `Etthāti` is connected with `dasseti` in the statement `jīvitā voropitā`. The construction is `kiñci jīvitaṃ nāma`. Here, the connection of meaning is this: just as when an ornament is removed from the head, the head and the ornament remain separate, so too, when life is separated from a living being, life does not remain separate from the living being. `Aññadatthūti` means `ekaṃsena` (certainly). Although `pāṇa` is stated generally, since a human being is taken as the subject in the case of a pārājika offense, here, by the principle of remainder, only an animal being is to be taken, hence it is said `tiracchānagatoyeva pāṇo` (only an animal being). `Tanti` means that living being. The connection is `mahante pana pāṇe`.

385. Sodhento apanetīti yojanā. Maṅguloti manussarattapo eko kimiviseso. So hi rattapivanatthāya maṅgati ito cito ca imaṃ cimañca ṭhānaṃ gacchatīti “maṅgulo”ti vuccati. Padakkharānañhi aviparitatthaṃ, sotūnañca sajjhāyopadesalabhanatthaṃ katthaci ṭhāne vacanattho vuttoti daṭṭhabbaṃ. Tassa bījameva khuddakaṭṭhena maṅgulabījakaṃ, tasmiṃ. Tanti maṅgulabījakaṃ. Bhindanto hutvāti yojanāti. Paṭhamaṃ.

385. The construction is `sodhento apaneti` (cleaning, he removes). A `maṅgula` is a type of worm that drinks human blood. Because it moves (`maṅgati`) from here to there, going to this place and that for the purpose of drinking blood, it is called `maṅgula`. It should be understood that the meaning of a word is stated in some places for the sake of the non-contrary meaning of the syllables and words, and for the sake of the listeners' receiving instruction for recitation. Its seed is the `maṅgulabījaka` (maṅgula-seed); in that. `Tanti` refers to the `maṅgulabījaka`. The construction is `bhindanto hutvā` (having been one who breaks). The first.

2. Sappāṇakasikkhāpadaṃ

2. The Training Rule on Water Containing Living Beings

387. Dutiye [V 1.0090] saha pāṇehīti sappāṇakaṃ udakanti dassento āha “ye pāṇakā”tiādi. Hīti saccaṃ. Pattapūrampi udakanti sambandho[M 0.0107]. Tādisenāti sappāṇakena. Dhovatopi pācittiyanti yojanā. Udakasoṇḍinti silāmayaṃ udakasoṇḍiṃ. Pokkharaṇinti silāmayaṃ pokkharaṇiṃ. Uṭṭhāpayatopi pācittiyanti sambandho. Tatoti soṇḍipokkharaṇīhi. Udakassāti udakena, pūre ghaṭe āsiñcitvāti sambandho. Tatthāti udake. Udaketi udakasaṇṭhānakapadese āsiñcitaudake. Patissatīti soṇḍipokkharaṇīhi gahitaudakaṃ patissatīti. Dutiyaṃ.

387. In the second, showing that `sappāṇakaṃ udakaṃ` means `saha pāṇehi udakaṃ` (water with living beings), he said, `ye pāṇakā`, and so on. `Hīti` means truly. The connection is `pattapūrampi udakaṃ` (even a bowlful of water). `Tādisena` means `sappāṇakena` (with that containing living beings). The construction is `dhovatopi pācittiyaṃ` (even from washing, there is a pācittiya). `Udakasoṇḍi` means a stone water trough. `Pokkharaṇi` means a stone pond. The connection is `uṭṭhāpayatopi pācittiyaṃ` (even from raising it, there is a pācittiya). `Tato` means from the trough and pond. `Udakassa` means `udakena` (by water); the connection is 'having poured it into a full pot'. `Tattha` means `udake` (in the water). `Udake` means in the water that has been poured in a place that has the appearance of a body of water. `Patissati` means the water taken from the trough or pond will flow back. The second.

3. Ukkoṭanasikkhāpadaṃ

3. The Training Rule on Re-opening an Issue

392. Tatiye “uccālentī”tiiminā ukkoṭentīti ettha upubbassa kuṭadhātussa uccālanatthaṃ dasseti dhātūna, manekatthattā. Yaṃ yaṃ patiṭṭhitaṃ yathāpatiṭṭhitaṃ, tassa bhāvo yathāpatiṭṭhitabhāvo, tena.

392. In the third, by `uccālentī` (stirring up), it shows that in `ukkoṭentī`, the root `kuṭ` with the prefix `u` has the meaning of 'raising', because roots have many meanings. `Yathāpatiṭṭhitaṃ` means 'as it was established'. The state of that is `yathāpatiṭṭhitabhāvo`. `Tena` refers to this.

393. Yo dhammoti yo samathadhammo. Dhammenāti ettha enasaddena “yathādhamma”nti ettha aṃitikāriyassa kāriṃ dasseti. Iminā “yathādhamma”nti padassa “nihatādhikaraṇa”nti ettha nihatasaddena sambandhitabbabhāvaṃ dasseti. “Satthārā”tipadaṃ “vuttaṃ” itipade kattā. Natthi hataṃ hananaṃ imassāti nihatanti vutte atthato vūpasamanamevāti āha “vūpasamita”nti.

393. `Yo dhammo` means the Dhamma of tranquility. Regarding `dhammena`, here the instrumental ending `ena` indicates the agent of the action implied by the adverbial ending in `yathādhammaṃ`. By this, it shows that the word `yathādhammaṃ` should be connected with the word `nihata` in `nihatādhikaraṇa` (a settled legal issue). The word `Satthārā` is the agent of the word `vuttaṃ`. When `nihata` is said, which means 'for this, there is no striking', in meaning it is simply pacification, hence it is said `vūpasamita` (pacified).

395. Yaṃ vā taṃ vā kammaṃ dhammakammaṃ nāma na hoti, atha kho adhikaraṇavūpasamakammameva dhammakammaṃ nāmāti dassento āha “yena kammenā”tiādi. Ayampīti ayampi bhikkhu. Sesapadānipīti “dhammakamme vematiko”tiādīni sesapadānipi. Etthāti imasmiṃ sikkhāpade. Vitthāro pana vuttoti sambandho. Tatthevāti parivāre eva. Idhāti imasmiṃ sikkhāpade, vibhaṅge vāti. Tatiyaṃ.

395. To show that just any action is not called a formal act, but that only a formal act for settling a legal issue is called a formal act, it is said, 'by which act,' and so on. 'This one also' means this bhikkhu also. 'The remaining phrases also' means the remaining phrases such as 'doubtful about the formal act.' 'Here' means in this training rule. The connection is 'the details, however, are stated.' 'There itself' means in the Parivāra itself. 'Here' means in this training rule, or in the Vibhaṅga. The third.

4. Duṭṭhullasikkhāpadaṃ

4. The Training Rule on Coarse Language.

399. Catutthe atthuddhāravasena dassitāni duṭṭhullasaddatthabhāvena sadisattāti adhippāyo. “Dhura”nti [V 1.0091] ettha lakkhaṇavantattā bhummatthe upayogavacananti āha “dhure”ti. Dhure nikkhittamatte satīti yojanā.

399. In the fourth, the intention is that they are shown by way of extracting the meaning to be similar in having the sense of a coarse word. Here, regarding 'dhura,' because it possesses a characteristic, it is a usage in the locative sense; thus he says 'dhure.' The construction is: 'when it has just been placed on the burden.'

Evaṃ [M 0.0108] dhuraṃ nikkhipitvāti “aññassa nārocessāmī”ti evaṃ dhuraṃ nikkhipitvā. Aññassāti vatthu, puggalato aññassa dutiyassa. Sopīti dutiyopi. Aññassāti tatiyassa. Yāva koṭi na chijjati, tāva āpajjatiyevāti yojanā. Tassevāti āpattiṃ āpannapuggalassa. Vatthupuggaloyevāti āpattiṃ āpannapuggaloyeva. Ayanti paṭhamabhikkhu. Aññassāti dutiyassa. Soti dutiyo ārocetīti sambandho. Yenāti paṭhamabhikkhunā. Assāti dutiyassa. Tassevāti paṭhamabhikkhusseva. Vatthupuggalaṃ upanidhāya “tatiyena puggalena dutiyassā”ti vuttaṃ.

'Having thus laid down the burden' means having laid down the burden in this way, thinking, 'I will not inform another.' 'To another' means to another matter, or to a second person other than the first. 'He also' means the second one also. 'To another' means to a third. The construction is: 'As long as the limit is not broken, one certainly incurs the offense.' 'Of that very one' means of the person who has incurred the offense. 'Only the person who is the basis' means only the person who has incurred the offense. 'This one' means the first bhikkhu. 'To another' means to the second. The connection is: 'He' means the second one informs. 'By whom' means by the first bhikkhu. 'Of him' means of the second. 'Of that very one' means of the first bhikkhu only. With reference to the person who is the basis, it is said: 'by a third person to the second.'

400. Pañcāpattikkhandheti thullaccayādike pañca āpattikkhandhe. Ajjhācāro nāmāti adhibhavitvā vītikkamitvā ācaritabbattā ajjhācāro nāmāti. Catutthaṃ.

400. 'In the five aggregates of offenses' means in the five aggregates of offenses, beginning with the grave offense. 'Transgression' is so called because it is conduct engaged in by overpowering and transgressing. The fourth.

5. Ūnavīsativassasikkhāpadaṃ

5. The Training Rule Concerning One Less Than Twenty Years Old.

402. Pañcame aṅguliyoti karasākhāyo. Tā hi aṅganti hatthato pañcadhā bhijjitvā uggacchantīti aṅguliyoti vuccanti. Likhantassa upālissāti sambandho. Tenāti bahucintetabbakāraṇena. Assāti upālissa. Uroti hadayaṃ. Tañhi usati cittatāpo dahati etthāti uroti vuccati. Rūpasuttanti heraññikānaṃ rūpasuttaṃ, yathā hatthācariyānaṃ hatthisuttanti. Akkhīnīti cakkhūni. Tāni hi akkhanti visayesu byāpībhavanti, rūpaṃ vā passati imehīti akkhīnīti vuccanti. Makasena sūcimukhānaṃ gahitattā ḍaṃsena piṅgalamakkhikāyova gahetabbāti āha “ḍaṃsāti piṅgalamakkhikāyo”ti. Piṅgalamakkhikāyo hi ḍaṃsanaṭṭhena khādanaṭṭhena ḍaṃsāti vuccanti. Dukkaro khamo etāsanti dukkhāti dassento āha “dukkhamāna”nti. Vedanānanti sambandho. Asātassa kāraṇaṃ dassetuṃ vuttaṃ “amadhurāna”nti. Iminā amadhurattā na sāditabbāti asātāti atthaṃ dasseti. Pāṇasaddajīvitasaddānaṃ pariyāyabhāvaṃ dassetuṃ vuttaṃ “jīvitaharāna”nti. Pāṇaṃ haranti apanentīti pāṇaharā, tāsaṃ vedanānanti sambandho.

402. In the fifth, 'fingers' means the branches of the hand. They are called 'fingers' because, like limbs, they branch out in five from the hand and extend. The connection is 'of Upāli, who is writing.' 'By that' means by the reason that should be much considered. 'Of him' means of Upāli. 'Chest' means the heart. It is called 'uro' because the mental fever burns there. 'Formula for forms' means the goldsmiths' formula for forms, just as elephant trainers have an elephant formula. 'Eyes' means the eyes. They are called 'akkhīni' because they pervade objects, or one sees forms with them. Since 'mosquito' is understood as those with needle-like mouths, by 'ḍaṃsa' only the yellow fly should be understood; thus it is said, 'ḍaṃsā means yellow flies.' For yellow flies are called 'ḍaṃsā' in the sense of biting and eating. To show that they are 'dukkha' because endurance of them is difficult, it is said, 'dukkhamānaṃ.' The connection is 'of feelings.' To show the cause of the unpleasant, it is said, 'of the unpleasing.' By this, it shows the meaning of 'unpleasant' as 'not to be enjoyed' because of being unpleasing. To show that the words 'pāṇa' and 'jīvita' are synonyms, it is said, 'of those that take away life.' They take away, they remove, life, thus they are 'life-takers'; the connection is 'of their feelings.'

404. Vijāyanakālato [M 0.0109] paṭṭhāya paripuṇṇavīsativasso na gahetabbo, gabbhagahaṇakālato [V 1.0092] pana paṭṭhāyāti dassento āha “paṭisandhiggahaṇato paṭṭhāyā”ti. Gabbhe sayitakālena saddhiṃ vīsatimaṃ vassaṃ paripuṇṇamassāti gabbhavīso puggalo. Hīti saccaṃ. Yathāhāti yenākārena saṅkhyaṃ gacchati, tenākārena bhagavā āhāti yojanā. Atha vā yathā kiṃ vacanaṃ bhagavā āhāti yojanā.

404. To show that one should not be considered fully twenty years old starting from the time of birth, but rather starting from the time of conception, it is said, 'starting from the taking of rebirth-linking.' A person whose twentieth year is complete, including the time spent lying in the womb, is a 'womb-twenty' person. 'Hi' means 'truly.' The construction is: 'As he said' means in whatever way the calculation proceeds, in that way the Blessed One spoke. Or else, the construction is: 'according to what statement did the Blessed One speak?'

Gabbhavīso hutvā upasampannoti sambandho. Amhīti asmi. Nusaddo parivitakkatthe nipāto. Yanti yādisaṃ paṭhamaṃ cittanti sambandho. Iminā paṭisandhicittaṃ dasseti. “Paṭhamaṃ viññāṇa”nti tasseva vevacanaṃ. Tanti paṭhamaṃ cittaṃ paṭhamaṃ viññāṇaṃ. Assāti sattassa. Sāva jātīti sā eva paṭisandhi, gabbho nāma hotīti sambandho.

The connection is: 'Having been womb-twenty, he is ordained.' 'Amhi' means 'asmi.' The word 'nu' is a particle in the sense of reflection. The connection is: 'Yaṃ' means 'whatever kind of first consciousness.' By this, it indicates the rebirth-linking consciousness. 'The first consciousness' is a synonym for that. 'That' means the first consciousness, the first consciousness. 'Of him' means of the being. The connection is: 'That very birth' means that very rebirth-linking, which is called the womb.

Tatthāti pāḷiyaṃ, vinicchayo evaṃ veditabboti yojanā. Yoti puggalo. Mahāpavāraṇāyāti assayujapuṇṇamiyaṃ. Sā hi pūjitapavāraṇattā mahāpavāraṇāti vuccati. Tatoti pavāraṇāya jātakālato. Tanti mahāpavāraṇaṃ. Pāṭipade cāti ettha casaddo aniyamavikappattho, pavāraṇadivasapāṭipadadivasesu aññatarasmiṃ divase upasampādetabboti attho. Hāyanavaḍḍhananti kucchimhi vasitamāsesu adhikesu hāyanañca ūnesu vaḍḍhunañca veditabbaṃ.

The construction is: 'There' means in the Pāli text, the decision should be understood thus. 'Who' means a person. 'On the Great Pavāraṇā' means on the full moon day of Assayuja. It is called the Great Pavāraṇā because it is an honored Pavāraṇā. 'From that' means from the time the Pavāraṇā occurred. 'That' means the Great Pavāraṇā. In 'and on the day following,' the word 'ca' has the sense of an unspecified alternative; the meaning is that the ordination should be conferred on either the day of Pavāraṇā or the day following it. 'Decrease and increase' should be understood as a decrease when there are extra months spent in the womb, and an increase when there are fewer.

Porāṇakattherā pana upasampādentīti sambandho. Ekūnavīsativassanti anantare vuttaṃ ekūnavīsativassaṃ. Nikkhamanīyoti sāvaṇamāso. So hi antovīthito bāhiravīthiṃ nikkhamati sūriyo asminti “nikkhamanīyo”ti vuccati. Pāṭipadadivaseti pacchimikāya vassūpagamanadivase. Taṃ upasampādanaṃ. Kasmāti pucchā. Ettha ṭhatvā parihāro vuccate mayāti yojanā. Vīsatiyā vassesūti upasampannapuggalassa vīsatiyā vassesu. Tiṃsarattidivassa ekamāsattā “cattāro [M 0.0110] māsā parihāyantī”ti vuttaṃ. Ukkaḍḍhantīti ekassa adhikamāsassa nāsanatthāya vassaṃ upari kaḍḍhanti. Tatoti chamāsato apanetvāti sambandho. Etthāti “ekūnavīsativassa”ntiādivacane. Pana-saddo hisaddattho, saccanti attho. Yoti puggalo. Tasmāti yasmā gabbhamāsānampi gaṇanūpagattā gahetvā upasampādenti, tasmā cha māse vasitvāti sambandho. Aṭṭha māse vasitvā jātopi na jīvatīti suttantaaṭṭhakathāsu (dī. ni. aṭṭha. 2.24-25; ma. ni. aṭṭha. 3.205) vuttaṃ.

The connection is: 'But the ancient elders ordain.' 'Nineteen years' means the nineteen years mentioned immediately before. 'The month of departure' means the month of Sāvaṇa. It is called 'the month of departure' because in it the sun departs from the inner path to the outer path. 'On the first day of the fortnight' means on the day of the later entering of the rains retreat. That is the ordination. 'Why?' is the question. The construction is: 'Standing here, the solution is stated by me.' 'In the twenty years' means in the twenty years of the ordained person. Because thirty nights and days are one month, it is said, 'four months are lost.' 'They draw up' means they draw the year up to eliminate one intercalary month. The connection is: 'From that' means after removing from the six months. 'Here' means in the statement beginning 'nineteen years.' The word 'pana' has the meaning of the word 'hi,' that is, 'truly.' 'Who' means a person. The connection is: 'Therefore' means because they ordain taking into account even the months in the womb as they are included in the calculation, therefore, 'having resided for six months.' 'Even one born after residing for eight months does not live'—this is stated in the Suttanta commentaries (Dī. Ni. Aṭṭha. 2.24-25; Ma. Ni. Aṭṭha. 3.205).

406. Dasavassaccayenāti upasampadato dasavassātikkamena. Upasampādetīti upajjhāyo vā [V 1.0093] kammavācācariyo vā hutvā upasampādeti. Tanti upajjhācariyabhūtaṃ anupasampannapuggalaṃ. Kammavācācariyo hutvā upasampādento taṃ muñcitvā sace aññopi kammavācācariyo atthi, sūpasampanno. Sova sace kammavācaṃ sāveti, nupasampanno. Ñatvā pana puna anupasampādente saggantarāyopi maggantarāyopi hotiyevāti daṭṭhabbanti. Pañcamaṃ.

406. 'After the passing of ten years' means after the lapse of ten years from ordination. 'He ordains' means he ordains having become either a preceptor or a teacher reciting the formal act. 'That' refers to an unordained person who has become a preceptor or teacher. If, while one is being ordained by such a person acting as the teacher reciting the formal act, that teacher is dismissed and there is another teacher reciting the formal act, then the candidate is properly ordained. But if that same person recites the formal act, the candidate is not ordained. However, it should be understood that for one who, having known this, is not ordained again, there is indeed an obstruction to heaven and an obstruction to the path. The fifth.

6. Theyyasatthasikkhāpadaṃ

6. The Training Rule on a Caravan of Thieves.

407. Chaṭṭhe “paṭiyāloka”nti ettha ālokasaddena sūriyo vutto upacārena. Sūriyo hi puratthimadisato uggantvā pacchimadisaṃ gato, tasmā sūriyasaṅkhātassa ālokassa paṭimukhaṃ “paṭiyāloka”nti vutte pacchimadisāyeva gahetabbāti āha “pacchimaṃ disanti attho”ti. Kammikāti kamme yuttā payuttā.

407. In the sixth, regarding 'paṭiyāloka,' here by the word 'light,' the sun is meant figuratively. The sun, indeed, having risen from the eastern direction, goes to the western direction; therefore, when 'facing the light,' which is designated as the sun, is said, only the western direction should be taken—thus it is said, 'the meaning is the western direction.' 'Kammika' means those engaged in or applied to work.

409. Rājānanti ettha rañño santakaṃ “rājā”ti vuccati upacārena, atha vā rañño eso “rājā”ti katvā rañño santakaṃ “rājā”ti vuccati. Theyyanti thenetvā “sakkacca”ntiādīsu (pāci. 606) viya niggahītāgamo hoti. Rājānaṃ, rañño santakaṃ vā theyyaṃ thenetvā [M 0.0111] gacchantīti attho. Iti imamatthaṃ dassento āha “rājānaṃ vā thenetvā”tiādi.

409. Regarding 'Rājānaṃ,' here that which belongs to the king is called 'the king' figuratively; or else, having considered it 'the king's,' that which belongs to the king is called 'the king.' Regarding 'theyyaṃ,' it means 'having stolen'; it has an inserted niggahīta like in 'sakkaccaṃ' and so on (Pāc. 606). The meaning is: 'they go away having stolen the king's property, or a stolen thing.' Thus, showing this meaning, he said, 'having stolen the king's,' etc.

411. Catūsu visaṅketesu dvīhi anāpatti, dvīhi āpattiyevāti. Chaṭṭhaṃ.

411. In four cases of uncertainty, there is no offense in two, and an offense in two. The Sixth.

7. Saṃvidhānasikkhāpadaṃ

7. The Training Rule on Agreement

412. Sattame “padhūpento”ti ettha papubba dhūpadhātu paribhāsanatthe vattatīti āha “paribhāsanto”ti. Tvaṃ samaṇopi mātugāmena saddhiṃ gacchasi, tuyheveso doso, netassa purisassāti attānaṃyeva paribhāsantoti attho. “Nikkhāmesī”tiiminā “nippātesī”tiettha nipubba patadhātu gatyatthoti dassetīti. Sattamaṃ.

412. In the seventh, regarding 'padhūpento,' here the root 'dhūpa' preceded by 'pa' is used in the sense of scorning, hence it is said 'paribhāsanto.' 'You, a monk, go about with women—this fault is yours, not that man's'—meaning you are the one reviling yourself. By 'Nikkhāmesī,' it is shown that the root 'pat' preceded by 'ni' in 'nippātesī' is in the sense of motion. The Seventh.

8. Ariṭṭhasikkhāpadaṃ

8. The Training Rule concerning Ariṭṭha

417. Aṭṭhame gandheti gijjhe. Te hi gidhanti kuṇapaṃ abhikaṅkhantīti “gandhā”ti vuccanti[V 1.0094]. Gaddhetipi pāṭho, sopi yujjati yathā “yuganandho, yuganaddho”ti ca “paṭibandho paṭibaddho”ti ca. Bādhayiṃsūti haniṃsu. Assāti ariṭṭhassa.

417. In the eighth, 'gandhe' means vultures. They are called 'gandhā' because they are greedy for corpses, that is, they desire them. There is also the reading 'gaddhe,' and it fits, just like 'yuganandho, yuganaddho' and 'paṭibandho, paṭibaddho.' 'Bādhayiṃsu' means they killed. 'Assā' means of Ariṭṭha.

Taddhitena vuttassa atthassa dassetumāha “te”tiādi. Teti antarāyikā. Tatthāti pañcavidhesu antarāyikesu. “Tathā”tipadena “kammantarāyikaṃ nāmā”ti padaṃ atidisati. Taṃ panāti bhikkhunidūsakakammaṃ pana. Mokkhassevāti magganibbānasseva. Maggo hi kilesehi muccatīti atthena mokkho nāma. Jhānampettha saṅgahitaṃ nīvaraṇehi vimuccanattā. Nibbānaṃ vimuccīti atthena mokkho nāma. Phalampettha saṅgahitaṃ vimuccitattā. Niyatamicchādiṭṭhidhammāti niyatabhāvaṃ pattā, niyatavasena vā pavattā micchādiṭṭhisaṅkhātā dhammā. Te pana natthikaahetuka akiriyavasena tividhā. Paṇḍakādigahaṇassa nidassanamattattā ‘paṭisandhidhammā”tipadena ahetukadvihetukapaṭisandhidhammā gahetabbā sabbesampi vipākantarāyikabhāvato. Tepi mokkhasseva antarāyaṃ karonti, na saggassa. Te panāti ariyūpavādā pana. Tāvadeva upavādantarāyikā [M 0.0112] nāmāti yojanā. Tāpīti sañcicca āpannā āpattiyopi. Pārājikāpattiṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ “bhikkhubhāvaṃ vā paṭijānātī”ti. Saṅghādisesāpattiṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ “na vuṭṭhāti vā”ti. Lahukāpattiṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ “na deseti vā”ti.

To explain the meaning expressed by the suffix, he said: 'te' and so on. 'Te' refers to obstructions. 'Tattha' means among the five kinds of obstructions. By the word 'tathā,' the term 'kammantarāyikaṃ nāma' is extended. That, however, is the act of corrupting a bhikkhunī. 'Mokkhasseva' means only of liberation, namely the path and Nibbāna. For the path is called liberation in the sense that one is freed from defilements by it. Here, jhāna is also included because it is freed from hindrances. Nibbāna is called liberation in the sense that it is freed. Here, fruition is also included because it is liberated. 'Niyatamicchādiṭṭhidhammā' refers to states that have attained a fixed condition, or states designated as wrong views that operate in a fixed manner. These, however, are threefold: nihilistic, causeless, and non-action. Since the inclusion of eunuchs and others is merely illustrative, by the term 'paṭisandhidhammā,' one should understand rebirth-linking states that are rootless or with two roots, because all of them constitute obstructions due to their resultant nature. They too obstruct only liberation, not heaven. 'Te pana' refers to slander of noble ones. The connection is: 'they are called obstructions by slander for just that long.' 'Tāpi' means even offenses that are intentionally committed. Regarding the Pārājika offense, it is said: 'or claims the state of a bhikkhu.' Regarding the Saṅghādisesa offense, it is said: 'or does not emerge.' Regarding the minor offense, it is said: 'or does not declare it.'

Tatrāti pañcavidhesu antarāyikesu. Ayaṃ bhikkhūti ariṭṭho gandhabādhipubbo bhikkhu. Sesantarāyiketi āṇāvītikkamantarāyikato sese catubbidhe antarāyike. Ime āgārikāti agāre vasanasīlā ime manussā. Bhikkhūpi passanti phusanti paribhuñjantīti sambandho. Kasmā na vaṭṭanti, vaṭṭantiyevāti adhippāyo. Rasena rasaṃ saṃsanditvāti upādiṇṇakarasena anupādiṇṇakarasaṃ, anupādiṇṇakarasena vā upādiṇṇakarasaṃ samānetvā. Yoniso paccavekkhaṇassa abhāvato saṃvijjati chandarāgo etthāti sacchandarāgo, soyeva paribhogo sacchandarāgaparibhogo, taṃ. Ekaṃ katvāti samānaṃ katvā. Ghaṭento viya pāpakaṃ diṭṭhigataṃ uppādetvāti yojanā. Kiṃsaddo garahattho, kasmā bhagavatā paṭhamapārājikaṃ paññattaṃ, na paññāpetabbanti attho. Mahāsamuddaṃ bandhanto yathā akattabbaṃ karoti, tathā paṭhamapārājikaṃ paññapento bhagavā apaññattaṃ paññapetīti adhippāyo. Etthāti paṭhamapārājike. Āsanti bhabbāsaṃ. Āṇācakketi āṇāsaṅkhāte cakke.

'Tattha' means among the five kinds of obstacles. 'This monk' refers to the monk Ariṭṭha, formerly a vulture-trapper. 'The remaining obstacles' means the other four kinds of obstacles besides the obstacle of transgressing a command. 'These householders' means these people who are in the habit of living in households. The connection is that monks also see, touch, and partake. Why are they not permissible? The meaning is that they are certainly permissible. By 'comparing taste with taste' means equating appropriated taste with unappropriated taste, or unappropriated taste with appropriated taste. Because of the absence of proper reflection, attachment exists here, hence it is 'sacchandarāgo' (with attachment). That very partaking is partaking with attachment—that. 'Making one' means making them equal. The explanation is: 'like one who, striving, produces a bad view.' The word 'kiṃ' is used to express disapproval. The meaning is: 'Why did the Blessed One prescribe the first pārājika? Should it not have been prescribed?' Just as someone binding the great ocean does what cannot be done, so the Blessed One, prescribing the first pārājika, prescribes what is unprescribed—this is the meaning. 'Here' means in the first pārājika. 'Āsaṃ' means a suitable hope. 'In the wheel of command' means in the wheel designated as command.

Aṭṭhiyeva aṭṭhikaṃ kucchitatthena, kucchitatthe hi ko. Aṭṭhikameva khalo nīcaṭṭhena lāmakaṭṭhenāti aṭṭhikaṅkhalo niggahītāgamaṃ katvā. Tena upamā sadisāti aṭṭhikaṅkhalūpamā. “Aṭṭhī”ti [V 1.0095] ca “kaṅkhala”nti ca padaṃ gahetvā vaṇṇenti ācariyā (sārattha. ṭī. pācittiya 3.417; vi. vi. ṭī. pācittiya 2.417; ma. ni. aṭṭha. 2.42; ma. ni. ṭī. 3.42). Aṅgārakāsūpamāti aṅgārarāsisadisā, aṅgārehi vā paripuṇṇā āvāṭasadisā. Asisūnūpamāti ettha asīti khaggo. So hi asate khipate anenāti “asī”ti vuccati. Sūnāti adhikoṭṭanaṃ. Tañhi sunati sañcuṇṇabhāvaṃ gacchati etthāti “sūnā”ti vuccati. Asinā sūnāti asisūnā, tāya upamā sadisāti asisūnūpamā. Sattisūlūpamāti sattiyā ca sūlena [M 0.0113] ca sadisā. Etthāti imissaṃ aṭṭhakathāyaṃ. Majjhimaṭṭhakathāyaṃ alagaddūpamasutte (ma. ni. aṭṭha. 1.234 ādayo) gahetabbo. Evaṃsaddakhosaddānamantare viyasaddassa byādesabhāvaṃ dassetuṃ vuttaṃ “evaṃ viya kho”ti. Aṭṭhamaṃ.

A bone indeed is 'aṭṭhika' in the sense of repulsive, for 'ka' is used in the sense of repulsion. 'Aṭṭhika' indeed is wretched in the sense of low and base—thus 'aṭṭhikaṅkhalo' is formed by the insertion of the niggahīta. The simile similar to that is 'aṭṭhikaṅkhalūpamā,' the simile of the skeleton. The teachers explain by taking the words 'aṭṭhi' and 'kaṅkhala' (Sārattha. ṭī. pācittiya 3.417; Vi. vi. ṭī. pācittiya 2.417; Ma. ni. aṭṭha. 2.42; Ma. ni. ṭī. 3.42). The simile of the pit of coals means similar to a heap of coals or similar to a pit filled with coals. The simile of the sword and the slaughterhouse—here 'asi' means a sword. For by it one casts away what is not, thus it is called 'asi.' 'Sūnā' means a slaughter-block. For in it things are pounded, they are ground into powder, thus it is called 'sūnā.' 'Asisūnā' means 'sword-slaughterhouse'; the simile similar to that is 'asisūnūpamā.' The simile of the spear and the stake means similar to a spear and a stake. 'Here' means in this commentary. In the Majjhima Nikāya Aṭṭhakathā, it should be taken from the Alagaddūpama Sutta (Ma. ni. aṭṭha. 1.234 ff.). To show the indicative nature of the word 'viya' between the words 'evaṃ' and 'kho,' it is said 'evaṃ viya kho.' The Eighth.

9. Ukkhittasambhogasikkhāpadaṃ

9. The Training Rule on Communion with a Suspended Monk

424. Navame anudhammassa sarūpaṃ dassetuṃ vuttaṃ “anulomavattaṃ disvā katā osāraṇā”ti. Iminā anulomavattaṃ disvā kato osāraṇasaṅkhāto dhammo anudhammoti dasseti. Osāraṇāti pavesanā. Tenevāti ukkhittakassa akaṭānudhammattā eva. Assāti “akaṭānudhammenā”ti padassa.

424. In the ninth, to show the nature of the 'subsequent Dhamma' (anudhammassa), it is said: “Having seen the conforming practice, the reinstatement was made.” By this, it is shown that the Dhamma, which is called 'reinstatement' (osāraṇā) made after seeing the conforming practice, is the 'subsequent Dhamma'. 'Osāraṇā' means 're-entry'. 'Tenevāti' means precisely because the suspended person has not performed the 'subsequent Dhamma'. 'Assāti' refers to the phrase “by the unperformed subsequent Dhamma.”

Dadato vā gaṇhato vāti vāsaddo aniyamavikappatthoti. Navamaṃ.

In “of one giving or of one receiving,” the word ‘vā’ indicates an indefinite alternative. The Ninth.

10. Kaṇṭakasikkhāpadaṃ

10. The Training Rule on Kaṇṭaka

428. Dasame ariṭṭhassa uppannaṃ viya etassāpi uppannanti yojanā. Ummajjantassāti manasikarontassa. Saṃvāsassa nāsanā saṃvāsanāsanā. Liṅgassa nāsanā liṅganāsanā. Daṇḍakammena nāsanā daṇḍakammanāsanā. Tatthāti tividhāsu nāsanāsu. Dūsako…pe… nāsethāti ettha ayaṃ nāsanā liṅganāsanā nāmāti yojanā. Ayanti daṇḍakammanāsanā. Idhāti imasmiṃ sikkhāpade, “nāsetū”ti pade vā. Tatthāti purimavacanāpekkhaṃ, “evañca pana bhikkhave”ti ādivacaneti attho. Pireti āmantanapadaṃ parasaddena samānatthanti āha “parā”ti. “Amhākaṃ anajjhattikabhūta”iti vā “amhākaṃ paccanīkabhūta” iti vā attho daṭṭhabbo. “Amāmaka”itipadena “para”itipadassa adhippāyatthaṃ dasseti. Amhe namamāyaka, amhehi vā namamāyitabba iti attho. “Amhāmaka”itipi hakārayutto pāṭho. Amhehi āmakaiti [V 1.0096] attho. Yatthāti yasmiṃ ṭhāne. Teti upayogatthe sāmivacanaṃ, tanti [M 0.0114] attho. Tava rūpasadde vāti sambandho. Na passāmāti na passāma, na suṇāma.

428. In the tenth, the explanation is that it arose for this one just as it arose for Ariṭṭha. 'Ummajjantassāti' means 'one who is reflecting'. 'Saṃvāsassa nāsanā' is 'expulsion from communal living'. 'Liṅgassa nāsanā' is 'removal of the distinguishing marks'. 'Daṇḍakammena nāsanā' is 'expulsion by way of a disciplinary act'. 'Tatthāti' refers to these three kinds of expulsion. In 'the defiler…pe… should expel', this expulsion is called 'removal of the distinguishing marks'—this is the explanation. 'Ayanti' refers to 'expulsion by way of a disciplinary act'. 'Idhāti' means in this training rule, or in the word 'should expel'. 'Tatthāti' refers to the preceding statement, meaning the statement beginning with “And thus, monks.” 'Pireti' is a vocative term, meaning the same as the word 'parā' (others)—he says “others.” The meaning should be understood as “not being internal to us” or “being hostile to us.” By the word 'amāmaka', he shows the intended meaning of the word 'para'. It means “not making us 'mine',” or “not to be made 'mine' by us.” The reading 'amhāmaka' is also a text with the letter 'ha'. It means “made 'mine' by us.” 'Yatthāti' means 'in which place'. 'Teti' is the genitive case used in the sense of relation, meaning 'that'. The connection is 'or in your form and sound'. 'Na passāmāti' means 'we do not see, we do not hear'.

429. Tenāti sāmaṇerena. “Kārāpeyyā”ti pade kāritakammanti. Dasamaṃ.

429. 'Tenāti' means 'by that novice'. In the word 'should cause to be done', it is a causative action. Tenth.

Sappāṇakavaggo sattamo.

The Seventh Chapter on Living Beings.

8. Sahadhammikavaggo

8. The Chapter on Those Who Share the Dhamma.

1. Sahadhammikasikkhāpada-atthayojanā

1. Explanation of the Training Rule on Those Who Share the Dhamma.

434. Sahadhammikavaggassa paṭhame yanti yaṃ paññattaṃ. “Sikkhamānenā”ti ettha mānapaccayassa anāgatatthabhāvaṃ dassetuṃ vuttaṃ “sikkhitukāmenā”ti. “Sikkhamānenā”tipadaṃ “bhikkhunā”tipade eva na kevalaṃ kārakavisesanaṃ hoti, atha kho “aññātabba”ntiādipadesupi kiriyāvisesanaṃ hotīti dassento āha “hutvā”ti. Padatthatoti padato ca atthato ca, padānaṃ atthato vāti. Paṭhamaṃ.

434. In the first of the Chapter on Those Who Share the Dhamma, 'yanti' refers to 'what has been laid down'. Here, to show that the suffix '-māna' in 'by one who is training' (sikkhamānenā) has a future meaning, it is said 'by one wishing to train'. Showing that the word 'sikkhamānenā' is not only an agent qualifier in the word 'by a monk' but also an action qualifier in words like 'should be known', etc., he says 'having been'. 'Padatthatoti' means both from the word and from the meaning, or from the meaning of the words. First.

2. Vilekhanasikkhāpadaṃ

2. The Training Rule on Scratching.

438. Dutiye vinaye paṭisaṃyuttā kathā vinayakathāti dassento āha “vinayakathā nāmā”tiādi. Tanti vinayakathaṃ. Padabhājanena vaṇṇanā vinayassa vaṇṇo nāmāti yojanā. Tanti vinayassa vaṇṇaṃ. Pariyāpuṇanaṃ pariyatti, vinayassa pariyatti vinayapariyatti, vinayapariyattisaṅkhātaṃ mūlamassa vaṇṇassāti vinayapariyattimūlako, taṃ. Vinayadharo labhatīti sambandho. Hīti vitthāro. Te sabbe bhagavā bhāsatīti sambandho. Hīti saccaṃ.

438. In the second, showing that the discussion connected with the Vinaya is called 'Vinaya-discourse', he said, “'Vinaya-discourse' means,” and so on. That is the Vinaya-discourse. The explanation by way of word analysis is called 'the exposition of the Vinaya'—this is the explanation. That is the exposition of the Vinaya. Learning is 'pariyatti'; the learning of the Vinaya is 'Vinaya-pariyatti'; that whose root is Vinaya-pariyatti, designated as Vinaya-pariyatti, is 'rooted in Vinaya-pariyatti'—that. The connection is “the Vinaya-holder obtains.” 'Hi' means 'elaboration'. The connection is “all these the Blessed One speaks.” 'Hi' means 'truly'.

Assāti vinayadharassa. Idhāti imasmiṃ sāsane. Alajjitātiādīsu karaṇatthe paccattavacanaṃ. Alajjitāyāti hi attho. Tena vuttaṃ “kathaṃ alajjitāyā”tiādi. Cāti saccaṃ[V 1.0097]. “Sañciccā”ti padaṃ tīsu vākyesu [M 0.0115] yojetabbaṃ. Sañcicca āpattiṃ āpajjati, sañcicca āpattiṃ parigūhati, sañcicca agatigamanañca gacchatīti attho. Mandoti bālo. Momūhoti atisammūḷho. Virādhetīti virajjhāpeti. Kukkucce uppanneti “kappati nu kho, no”ti vinayakukkucce uppanne. Ayaṃ panāti ayaṃ puggalo pana vītikkamatiyevāti sambandho. Acchamaṃsena sūkaramaṃsassa vaṇṇasaṇṭhānena sadisattā, dīpimaṃsena ca migamaṃsassa sadisattā vuttaṃ “acchamaṃsaṃ sūkaramaṃsa”ntiādi.

'Assāti' refers to 'of the Vinaya-holder'. 'Idhāti' means 'in this Dispensation'. In 'shamelessness', etc., the singular form is used in the instrumental sense. It means 'by shamelessness'. Therefore, it is said, “How by shamelessness?” etc. 'Cāti' means 'truly'. The word 'intentionally' should be connected to the three sentences. It means: 'he commits an offense intentionally, he conceals an offense intentionally, and he goes to a wrong destination intentionally'. 'Mandoti' means 'foolish'. 'Momūhoti' means 'extremely deluded'. 'Virādhetīti' means 'he causes to transgress'. 'Kukkucce uppanneti' means 'when a disciplinary doubt arises, whether it is allowable or not'. The connection is: 'But this person, however, transgresses'. Because bear meat is similar to pork in color and appearance, and leopard meat is similar to deer meat, it is said, “bear meat is like pork,” etc.

Āpattiṃca satisammosāyāti ettha casaddo avuttavākyasampiṇḍanattho, kattabbañca na hi karotīti attho. Evantiādi nigamanaṃ.

Here, in `Āpattiṃ ca satisammosāya`, the word 'ca' serves to gather together unstated sentences, meaning 'and he does not do what should be done'. 'Thus', and so on, is the conclusion.

Evaṃ avinayadharassa dosaṃ dassetvā vinayadharassa guṇaṃ dassento āha “vinayadharo panā”tiādi. Soti vinayadharo. Hīti vitthāro. Parūpavādanti paresaṃ upavādaṃ. Suddhanteti suddhassa koṭṭhāse. Tatoti patiṭṭhānato paranti sambandho. Assāti vinayadharassa. Evantiādi nigamanaṃ. Assāti vinayadharassa. Kukkuccapakatānanti kukkuccena abhibhūtānaṃ. Soti vinayadharo. Tehīti kukkuccapakatehi. Saṅghamajjhe kathentassa avinayadharassāti yojanā. Tanti bhayaṃ sārajjaṃ.

Having thus shown the fault of one who does not uphold the Vinaya, he then reveals the virtue of one who does uphold it, saying, “But one who upholds the Vinaya,” and so on. 'So' means 'that Vinaya-holder'. 'Hi' means 'elaboration'. 'Parūpavādaṃ' means 'the reproach of others'. 'Suddhante' means 'in the pure part'. The connection is 'beyond the foundation from that'. 'Assāti' refers to 'of the Vinaya-holder'. 'Thus', and so on, is the conclusion. 'Assāti' refers to 'of the Vinaya-holder'. 'Kukkuccapakatānaṃ' means 'of those overcome by scruples'. 'So' means 'that Vinaya-holder'. 'Tehi' refers to 'by those overcome by scruples'. The explanation is: 'of one who does not uphold the Vinaya speaking in the midst of the Sangha'. 'That' refers to 'fear and hesitation'.

Paṭipakkhaṃ, paṭiviruddhaṃ vā atthayanti icchantīti paccatthīkā, ṇyasaddo bahulaṃ kattābhidhāyako, attano paccatthikā attapaccatthikā. Tatthāti duvidhesu paccatthikesu. Imeti mettiyabhummajakavaḍḍhalicchavino. Aññepi ye vā pana bhikkhūti sambandho. Ariṭṭhabhikkhu ca kaṇṭakasāmaṇero ca vesālikavajjiputtakā ca ariṭṭha…pe… vajjīputtakā. Te ca sāsanapaccatthikā nāmāti sambandho. Parūpahāro ca aññāṇo ca kaṅkhāparavitaraṇo ca parū…pe… vitaraṇā. Te ādayo yesaṃ vādānanti parū…pe… vitaraṇādayo. Te eva vādā etesanti parū…pe… vitaraṇādivādā. Te ca sāsanapaccatthikā nāmāti sambandho. Abuddhasāsanaṃ buddhasāsananti vatvā katapaggahā mahāsaṅghikādayo ca sāsanapaccatthikā nāmāti yojanā. Kaṅkhāparavitaraṇādīti ettha [M 0.0116] ādisaddena kathāvatthupakaraṇe āgatā vādā saṅgayhanti. Mahāsaṅghikādayoti ettha ādisaddena dīpavaṃse āgatā gaṇā saṅgayhanti. Ādimhi “viparītadassanā”ti padaṃ sabbapadehi yojetabbaṃ. “Sahadhammenā”ti padassatthaṃ dassetuṃ vuttaṃ “saha kāraṇenā”ti. Yathāti yenākārena niggayhamāneti sambandho.

Those who desire to oppose or to be contrary are called 'opponents' (paccatthikā); the suffix '-ṇya' often denotes the agent. One's own opponents are called 'attapaccatthikā'. 'Tatthāti' refers to 'among these two kinds of opponents'. 'Imeti' refers to 'Mettiya, Bhummajaka, Vaḍḍha, and the Licchavis'. The connection is 'and also any other monks'. The monk Ariṭṭha, the novice Kaṇṭaka, and the Vajjiputtakas of Vesālī—Ariṭṭha…the Vajjiputtakas. The connection is 'and these are called opponents of the Dispensation'. 'Parūpahāro ca aññāṇo ca kaṅkhāparavitaraṇo ca' means 'misrepresentation, ignorance, and the resolving of doubt through others'—misrepresentation…resolving. Those whose doctrines begin with these are 'proponents of misrepresentation…resolving and the like'. These very doctrines are theirs—'doctrines beginning with misrepresentation…resolving and similar doctrines'. The connection is 'and these too are called opponents of the Dispensation'. The explanation is that the Mahāsaṅghikas and others, who, saying that what is not the Buddha’s Dispensation is the Buddha’s Dispensation, have taken a firm stance, are also called opponents of the Dispensation. Here, in 'the resolving of doubt, etc.', the word 'etc.' includes the views mentioned in the Kathāvatthupakaraṇa. In 'the Mahāsaṅghikas and others', the word 'etc.' includes the groups mentioned in the Dīpavaṃsa. At the beginning, the word 'with distorted views' should be connected with all the words. To explain the meaning of the word 'with the Dhamma', it is said 'with the reason'. The connection is 'as'—'in the manner in which one is refuted'.

Tatthāti [V 1.0098] tividhesu saddhammesu. Mahāvattāni santi, ayaṃ sabboti yojanā. Cattāri phalāni cāti liṅgavipallāsena yojetabbaṃ. Ettha cakārena abhiññāpaṭisambhidā saṅgahitā tāsampi adhigamasāsanabhāvato.

'Tatthāti' refers to 'among the three kinds of true Dhamma'. The explanation is: 'Great practices exist; this is all'. The four fruits too—this should be connected by the inversion of gender. Here, by the word 'ca', the higher knowledges and analytical knowledges are included, since they too are a mode of realization and teaching.

Tatthāti tividhesu saddhammesu. Keci therāti dhammakathikā keci therā. “Yo kho”ti kaṇṭhajadutiyakkharena paṭhitabbo. Potthakesu pana “yo vo”ti vakārena pāṭho atthi, so ayutto. Kasmā? “So vo”ti parato vuttattā, ekasmiṃ vākye dvinnaṃ samānasutisaddānaṃ ayuttattā ca. Keci therāti paṃsukūlikā keci therā āhaṃsūti sambandho. Itare pana therāti dhammakathikatherehi ca paṃsukūlikatherehi ca aññe therā. Teti pañca bhikkhū karissantīti sambandho. Jambudīpassa paccante tiṭṭhatīti paccantimo, tasmiṃ. Jambudīpassa majjhe vemajjhe tiṭṭhatīti majjhimo. Atha vā majjhānaṃ suddhānaṃ buddhādīnaṃ nivāso majjhimo, tasmiṃ. Vīsati vaggā imassāti vīsativaggo, soyeva gaṇo vīsativaggagaṇo, taṃ. Evantiādi nigamanaṃ.

'Tatthāti' refers to 'among the three kinds of true Dhamma'. 'Keci therā' means 'some elders, namely Dhamma-preaching elders'. 'Yo kho' should be read with the second letter as 'kho'. In the texts, however, there is a reading 'yo vo' with the letter 'va', but that is incorrect. Why? Because 'so vo' is stated later, and in one sentence, two identical-sounding words are inappropriate. The connection is: 'Keci therā' means 'some elders, namely rag-robe wearers, spoke'. 'Itare pana therā' means 'other elders, namely those other than the Dhamma-preaching elders and the rag-robe-wearing elders'. The connection is: 'They' refers to 'the five monks who will act'. 'Paccantimo' means 'stands at the border of Jambudīpa'; in that place. 'Majjhimo' means 'stands in the middle, the very center of Jambudīpa'. Or alternatively, 'majjhimo' is the dwelling place of the pure ones, such as the Buddhas, etc.; in that place. 'Vīsativaggo' means 'twenty groups of this'; that very group is the 'twenty-group assembly'—that. 'Thus', and so on, is the conclusion.

Tassādheyyoti tassāyatto, tassa santakoti vuttaṃ hoti. Pavāraṇā ādheyyā, saṅghakammaṃ ādheyyaṃ, pabbajjā ādheyyā, upasampadā ādheyyāti yojanā.

'Tassādheyya' means 'dependent on that'; it is said to mean 'belonging to that'. The connection is: 'the Pavāraṇā is dependent, the Sangha act is dependent, the going forth is dependent, the full ordination is dependent'.

Yepi ime nava uposathāti sambandho. Yāpi ca imā nava pavāraṇāyoti yojanā. Tassāti vinayadharassa. Tāsanti navapavāraṇānaṃ.

The connection is: 'And these are the nine Uposathas'. The explanation is: 'And these are the nine Pavāraṇās'. 'Tassa' means 'of the Vinaya-holder'. 'Tāsaṃ' means 'of the nine Pavāraṇās'.

Yānipi [M 0.0117] imāni cattāri saṅghakammānīti yojetabbaṃ. Ettha ca tāni vinayadharāyattānevāti pāṭhaseso ajjhāharitabbo.

'And these are the four Sangha acts' should be connected. And here, the remainder of the text, 'these are dependent solely on the Vinaya-holder', should be supplied.

Yāpi ca ayaṃ pabbajjā ca upasampadā ca kātabbāti yojanā. Hīti saccaṃ. Aññoti vinayadharato paro. So evāti vinayadharo eva. “Upajjha”nti dhātukammaṃ, “sāmaṇerenā”ti kāritakammaṃ upanetabbaṃ. Ettha cāti uposathādīsu ca. Nissayadānañca sāmaṇerūpaṭṭhānañca visuṃ katvā dvādasānisaṃse labhatītipi sakkā vattuṃ.

'And this going forth and full ordination should be performed'—this is the connection. 'Indeed' means truly. 'Another' means someone other than the Vinaya-holder. 'He himself' means the Vinaya-holder himself. 'Preceptor' is the root action; 'by the novice' is the causative action—this should be supplied. 'And here' means in the Uposatha and so on. And the giving of dependence and the attending upon novices, having performed them separately, one obtains twelve benefits—this also can be said.

Visuṃ visuṃ katvāti “pañcāti ca…pe… ekādasā”ti ca koṭṭhāsaṃ koṭṭhāsaṃ katvā, satta koṭṭhāse katvā bhāsatīti adhippāyo. Thometīti sammukhā thometi. Pasaṃsatīti parammukhā pasaṃsati. “Uggahetabba”ntipadassatthaṃ dassetuṃ vuttaṃ “pariyāpuṇitabba”nti. Addhani dīghe [V 1.0099] sādhūti addhaniyaṃ addhakkhamaṃ addhayogyanti attho sādhuatthe niyapaccayo (moggallāne 4.33.73).

'Having done separately, separately' means: having made it section by section, from 'five... up to... eleven', having made seven sections, he speaks—this is the intention. 'He commends' means he commends to the face. 'He praises' means he praises behind the back. To show the meaning of the term 'should be learned', it is said 'should be mastered'. 'Good in the long term' means suitable for the long term, enduring on the path, fit for the path—this is the meaning; the suffix 'niya' is in the sense of 'good' (Moggallāna 4.33.73).

Therā ca navā ca majjhimā ca bahū te bhikkhū pariyāpuṇantīti yojanā.

The elders, the newly ordained, and those of middle standing—many of those monks master it—this is the connection.

439. “Uddissamāne”ti padassa kammarūpattaṃ dassetuṃ vuttaṃ “uddisiyamāne”ti. So panāti pātimokkho pana. Yasmā uddissamāno nāma hoti, tasmāti yojanā. Uddisante vāti uddisiyamāne vā. Uddisāpente vāti uddisāpiyamāne vā. Antasaddo hi mānasaddakāriyo. Yoti bhikkhu. Nanti taṃ pātimokkhaṃ. Casaddo khuddānukhuddakapadassa dvannavākyaṃ dasseti, pubbapade kakāralopo daṭṭhabbo. Tesanti khuddānukhuddākānaṃ. Hīti saccaṃ. Etānīti khuddānukhuddakāni. Yeti bhikkhū. “Yāva uppajjatiyeva, tāva saṃvattanti iti vuttaṃ hotīti yojanā imassa nayassa pāṭhasesehi yojetabbattā. Garukabhāvaṃ sallakkhento lahukabhāvaṃ dassento āha “atha vā”tiādi. Ativiyāti ati i eva. Ikāro hi sandhivasena adassanaṃ gato. Viyasaddo evakāratthavācako “varamhākaṃ bhusāmivā”ti ettha [M 0.0118] (jā. 1.3.108) ivasaddo viya, ati hutvā evāti attho daṭṭhabbo. “Upasampannassā”ti ettha samīpe sāmivacananti (rupasiddhiyaṃ 316 sutte) āha “upasampannassa santike”ti. Tassāti upasampannassa. Tasminti vinaye. Vivaṇṇetīti na kevalaṃ tasseva vivaṇṇamattameva, atha kho nindatiyevāti āha “nindatī”ti. Garahatīti tasseva vevacanaṃ. Atha vā nindatīti upasampannassa sammukhā nindati. Garahatīti parammukhā garahatīti. Dutiyaṃ.

439. To show the passive form of the word 'uddissamāne', it is said 'uddisiyamāne'. 'So pana' means 'that Pātimokkha'. Because it is called 'being recited', therefore—this is the connection. 'When reciting' means 'when it is being recited'. 'When causing to recite' means 'when it is being caused to recite'. For the suffix '-anta' has the function of the suffix '-māna'. 'Yo' refers to a monk. 'Naṃ' refers to that Pātimokkha. The word 'ca' indicates the two parts of the term 'khuddānukhuddaka', and the elision of the letter 'ka' in the first part should be noted. 'Tesaṃ' refers to the minor and secondary rules. 'Hī' means truly. 'Etāni' refers to the minor and secondary rules. 'Ye' refers to the monks. 'As long as it arises, so long it continues'—it is said; this is the connection, because this method should be connected with the remainder of the text. Noting the gravity and showing the lightness, he said 'or alternatively', and so on. 'Ativiya' means 'ati i eva'. For the letter 'i' has become invisible due to sandhi. The word 'viya' expresses the meaning of 'eva', just like the word 'iva' in the phrase 'varamhākaṃ bhusāmivā' (Jā. 1.3.108); the meaning should be understood as 'exceedingly indeed'. Regarding 'upasampannassa', he says 'in the presence of one fully ordained', because (according to Rūpasiddhi, sutta 316) the genitive case is used for proximity. 'Tassa' refers to the fully ordained one. 'Tasmiṃ' refers to the Vinaya. 'He disparages' means it is not merely disparagement of him alone, but he indeed criticizes; therefore he says 'he criticizes'. 'He blames' is a synonym for that. Alternatively, 'he criticizes' means he criticizes in the presence of the fully ordained one, while 'he blames' means he blames behind his back. The second.

3. Mohanasikkhāpadaṃ

3. The Training Rule on Causing Confusion.

444. Tatiye anusaddo paṭipāṭiatthaṃ antokatvā vicchatthavācakoti āha “anupaṭipāṭiyā addhamāse addhamāse”ti. Soti pātimokkho. Uposathe uposathe uddisitabbanti anuposathikaṃ. Etthāpi hi anusaddo vicchatthavācako. Soti pātimokkho. Uddisiyamāno nāma hotīti yojanā. “Tasmiṃ anācāre”ti padena “tatthā”ti padassatthaṃ dasseti. “Yaṃ āpatti”nti padena yaṃsaddassa visayaṃ dasseti. Yathādhammoti ettha dhammasaddena dhammo ca vinayo ca adhippetoti āha “dhammo ca vinayo cā”ti. Yathāti yenākārena. Sādhusaddo sundarattho, kasaddo padapūraṇoti āha “suṭṭhū”ti. Aṭṭhinti ca “katvā”ti ca dve padāni daṭṭhabbāni. “Aṭṭhikatvā”ti vā ekaṃ padaṃ. Tattha pubbanaye attho yassatthīti aṭṭhi tthakārassa [V 1.0100] ṭṭhakāraṃ katvā, taṃ aṭṭhiṃ. Katvāti tvāpaccayantauttarapadena samāso na hoti. Aṭṭhikabhāvanti ettha ikasaddena “aṭṭhī”ti ettha īpaccayaṃ dasseti. “Bhāva”ntipadena bhāvapaccayena vinā bhāvatthassa ñāpetabbataṃ dasseti. Attho panevaṃ daṭṭhabbo – aṭṭhibhāvaṃ katvāti. Pacchimanaye attho yassatthīti aṭṭhiko purimanayeneva tthakārassa ṭṭhakāraṃ katvā. Atthayitabbo icchitabboti vā aṭṭhiko, aṭṭhikaiti nāmasaddato tvāpaccayo kātabbo. “Aṭṭhikatvā”ti idaṃ padaṃ kiriyāvisesanaṃ. Kiriyāvisesane vattamāne karadhātu vā bhūdhātu vā yojetabbāti dassebhuṃ [M 0.0119] vuttaṃ “katvā hutvā”ti. Taṃ sabbaṃ dassento āha “aṭṭhikatvāti aṭṭhikabhāvaṃ katvā, aṭṭhiko hutvā”ti. Tatiyaṃ.

444. In the third, the prefix 'anu' includes the meaning of 'sequence' and is a distributive word; therefore he says 'in sequence, every half-month'. 'So' refers to the Pātimokkha. To be recited on each Uposatha day is 'anuposathikaṃ'. Here too, the prefix 'anu' functions as a distributive word. 'So' refers to the Pātimokkha. It is called 'being recited'—this is the connection. With the phrase 'in that misconduct', he shows the meaning of the word 'there'. With the phrase 'whatever offense', he shows the scope of the word 'whatever'. In 'according to the Dhamma', by the word 'Dhamma', both the Dhamma and the Vinaya are intended; therefore he says 'the Dhamma and the Vinaya'. 'According to' means 'in what manner'. The word 'sādhu' means 'excellent', and 'ka' is a particle filler; therefore he says 'well'. 'Aṭṭhiṃ' and 'katvā' should be seen as two words, or 'aṭṭhikatvā' as a single word. In the first interpretation, 'aṭṭhi' means 'that which has purpose' (attho yassa atthi), by changing 'tth' to 'ṭṭh'; that is 'aṭṭhiṃ'. 'Katvā' does not form a compound with a following word ending in the 'tvā' suffix. In 'aṭṭhikabhāvaṃ', the suffix 'ika' indicates the 'ī' suffix in 'aṭṭhī'. With the word 'bhāva', he shows that the meaning of 'state' should be understood without a 'bhāva' suffix. The meaning, however, should be seen thus: 'having made it into the state of purpose'. In the latter interpretation, 'aṭṭhiko' means 'one who has purpose', by changing 'tth' to 'ṭṭh' as in the former interpretation. Or 'aṭṭhiko' means 'that which should be sought' or 'that which is desired'; from the noun 'aṭṭhika', the 'tvā' suffix should be formed. The word 'aṭṭhikatvā' is an adverb. To show that when an adverb is present, the roots 'kar' or 'bhū' should be employed, it is said 'katvā' or 'hutvā'. Explaining all that, he says: ''aṭṭhikatvā' means having made it into the state of purpose, or having become purposeful.' The third.

4. Pahārasikkhāpadaṃ

4. The Training Rule on Striking.

449. Catutthe kasmā chabbaggiyā sattarasavaggiyānaṃ pahāraṃ denti, nanu akāraṇena pahāraṃ dentīti āha “āvuso”tiādi. Iminā yathā vadanti, tathā akatattā pahāraṃ dentīti dasseti.

449. In the fourth, why do the group-of-six monks give blows to the group-of-seventeen monks? Do they not give blows without cause? He says 'Friends', and so on. By this, he shows that they give blows because the others did not do as they said.

451. Sacepīti ettha pisaddena sace amarati, kā nāma kathā, pācittiyamevāti dasseti. Pahārenāti pahārahetunā. Yathāti yenākārena. Ayanti bhikkhu. Na virocatīti na sobhati.

451. 'Even if': Here, the particle 'pi' shows that if he does not die, what is there to say? It is simply a Pācittiya offense. 'By a blow' means by reason of a blow. 'As' means in what manner. 'This' refers to the monk. 'Does not shine' means is not becoming.

452. “Anupasampannassā”ti ettha akārassa aññatthaṃ dassetuṃ vuttaṃ “gahaṭṭhassa vā”tiādi. Pabbajitassa vāti paribbājakassa vā sāmaṇerassa vā.

452. 'To one not fully ordained': Here, to show another meaning of the particle 'a', it is said: 'or to a householder', and so on. 'Or to one gone forth' means to a wandering ascetic or a novice.

453. “Kenacī”ti padassa atthaṃ dassetuṃ vuttaṃ “manussena vā”tiādi. Tatoti viheṭhanato, iminā mokkhassa apādānaṃ dasseti, “attano”ti iminā sambandhaṃ dasseti. “Patthayamāno”ti iminā “adhippāyo”ti padassatthaṃ dasseti. Muggarena vāti catuhatthadaṇḍassa addhena daṇḍena vā. Soti corādikoti. Catutthaṃ.

453. To explain the meaning of the word 'by someone', it is said: 'or by a human being', and so on. 'From that' means from harassment; by this, the ablative case of 'liberation' is shown. By 'of oneself', the connection is shown. By 'aspiring', the meaning of the word 'intention' is shown. 'Or with a club' means with a stick half the length of a four-cubit stick. 'He' refers to a thief, and so on. The fourth.

5. Talasattikasikkhāpadaṃ

5. The Training Rule on a Threatening Gesture.

454. Pañcame talanti hatthatalaṃ. Tañhi talati yaṃkiñci gahitavatthu patiṭṭhāti etthāti [V 1.0101] “tala”nti vuccati. Sattīti kunto. So hi sakati vijjhituṃ samatthetīti “sattī”ti vuccati. Talameva sattisadisattā talasattikaṃ, sadisatthe ko, taṃ talasattikaṃ upacārena gahetvā “kāyampī”ti vuttaṃ. Kāyato aññaṃ vatthumpi talasattikasaṅkhātena kāyena gahetvā uggirattā vuttaṃ “kāyapaṭibaddhampī”ti. “Pahārasamuccitā”ti ettha saṃpubbo ca upubbo ca cisaddo paguṇanasaṅkhāte paricite vattatīti āha “pahāraparicitā”ti. Pahārena saṃ punappunaṃ uccitā paricitāti attho. Imamevatthaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ [M 0.0120] “pubbepi…pe… attho”ti. Aññampi sajjhāyananayaṃ dassetuṃ vuttaṃ “pahārassa ubbigā”ti. Tassāti tassa pāṭhassa. Pahārassāti pahārato. Nissakkatthe cetaṃ sāmivacanaṃ. “Bhītā”ti iminā “ubbigā”ti ettha upubba vijadhātussatthaṃ dasseti.

454. In the fifth, `tala` means the palm of the hand. For it bears (talati), and whatever object is grasped is established there—hence it is called `tala`. `Satti` means a spear. For it is able (sakati) to pierce—hence it is called `satti`. The palm itself, being similar to a spear, is called `talasattika`, with the suffix ‘ka’ denoting similarity. Taking `talasattika` metaphorically, it is said: “even the body.” Another object too, apart from the body, is referred to by the phrase “even what is bound to the body” because it is grasped by the body—which is designated as `talasattika`—and then expelled. In `pahārasamuccitā`, the root `ci` with the prefixes `saṃ` and `u` refers to being thoroughly acquainted, that is, habituated. Thus it is said: `pahāraparicitā` (accustomed to blows), meaning that one is repeatedly struck and thus accustomed. Referring to this very meaning, it is said: “previously… the meaning.” To show another method of recitation, it is said: `pahārassa ubbigā` (terrified by blows). `Of that` refers to that passage. `Of a blow` means from a blow. This is a genitive case in the sense of the ablative. By `afraid`, the meaning of the root `vij` with the prefix `u` in `ubbigā` is shown.

457-8. Viraddhoti paṇṇako hutvā. Pubbeti purimasikkhāpade. Vuttesu vatthūsūti “coraṃ vā paccatthīkaṃ vā”tiādinā vuttesu vatthūsūti. Pañcamaṃ.

457-8. `Viraddho` means having become a leaf-eater. `Previously` refers to the earlier training rule. `In the cases stated` means in the cases stated, such as “a thief or an adversary,” and so on. The fifth.

6. Amūlakasikkhāpadaṃ

6. The Training Rule on a Baseless Charge.

459. Chaṭṭhe teti chabbaggiyā. Codenti kirāti sambandho. Ākiṇṇadosattāti tesaṃ ākulaādīnavattā. Evanti codiyamāne. Attaparittāṇanti attano parisamantato tāṇaṃ rakkhanaṃ karontā codentīti yojanāti. Chaṭṭhaṃ.

459. In the sixth, `te` refers to the group of six. The connection is: ‘they accuse.’ `Because of being beset by faults` means because of their being beset by troubles and faults. `Thus` refers to being accused. `Self-protection` means the construction is: they accuse while making protection and guarding themselves all around. The sixth.

7. Sañciccasikkhāpadaṃ

7. The Training Rule on Deliberate Action.

464. Sattame upapubbadahadhātussa sakammikattā kāritantogadhabhāvaṃ dassetuṃ vuttaṃ “uppādentī”ti. “Anupasampannassā”ti ettha akārassa sadisatthaṃ dassetuṃ vuttaṃ “sāmaṇerassā”ti. Sāmaṇeropi hi upasampannena sadiso hoti saṇṭhānena ca purisabhāvena ca. Sāmaṇerassa kukkuccaṃ upadahatīti sambandho. Nisinnaṃ maññe, nipannaṃ maññe, bhuttaṃ maññe, pītaṃ maññe, kataṃ maññeti yojanā. Nisinnanti nisīditaṃ. Nipannanti nipajjitanti. Sattamaṃ.

464. In the seventh, to show that the root `dah` with the prefix `upa` has a causative sense because it is transitive, it is said: “they cause to arise.” In the phrase `for one not fully ordained`, to show that the negative particle `a` has the meaning of similarity, it is said: “for a novice.” For a novice is indeed similar to one fully ordained in form and in being a man. The connection is: it causes remorse in the novice. The construction is: “I think he is seated, I think he is lying down, I think he has eaten, I think he has drunk, I think he has done.” `Seated` means having sat. `Lying down` means having lain down. The seventh.

8. Upassutisikkhāpadaṃ

8. The Training Rule on Eavesdropping.

471. Aṭṭhame [V 1.0102] “adhikaraṇajātāna”nti ettha adhikaraṇassa pakaraṇato vivādādhikaraṇabhāvañca visesanaparapadabhāvañca dassento āha “uppannavivādādhikaraṇāna”nti. Tattha uppannasaddena jātasaddassatthaṃ dasseti[M 0.0121]. Vivādasaddena adhikaraṇassa sarūpaṃ dasseti. Suyyatīti suti vacanaṃ, sutiyā samīpaṃ upassuti ṭhānanti atthaṃ dassetuṃ vuttaṃ “sutisamīpa”nti. “Samīpa”nti iminā upasaddassatthaṃ dasseti. “Yatthā”tiādinā “upassutī”ti ettha upasaddassa padhānattā tassa sarūpaṃ dasseti. Yatthāti yasmiṃ ṭhāne. Mantentanti ettha upayogavacanassa bhummatthe adhippetattā vuttaṃ “mantayamāne”ti.

471. In the eighth, regarding `adhikaraṇajātāna`, showing that from the context the `adhikaraṇa` is a dispute-adhikaraṇa and that `jāta` is a qualifying subsequent word, he says: “for those with an arisen dispute-adhikaraṇa.” There, the word `arisen` shows the meaning of the word `jāta`. The word `dispute` shows the nature of the `adhikaraṇa`. `Suti` is what is heard, speech; to show that the meaning of `upassuti` is a place near hearing, it is said: “near hearing.” By `near`, the meaning of the prefix `upa` is shown. By “where,” and so on, because the prefix `upa` is primary in `upassuti`, its nature is shown. `Where` means in which place. Regarding `mantenti`, because the present participle is intended in the locative absolute sense, it is said: `mantayamāne` (while deliberating).

473. “Vūpasamissāmī”ti ettha idhātuyā gatyatthaṃ dassetuṃ vuttaṃ “vūpasamaṃ gamissāmī”ti. Akārakabhāvanti niddosabhāvaṃ. Sotukāmatāya gamanavasena siyā kiriyanti yojanā. Paratopi eseva nayoti. Aṭṭhamaṃ.

473. `I will be calmed`—here, to show that the root `i` has the meaning of going, it is said: “I will go to calm.” `The state of being without an agent` means the state of being faultless. The construction is: “Because of the desire to hear, there might be an action in the manner of going.” The same method applies to the subsequent one as well. The eighth.

9. Kammapaṭibāhanasikkhāpadaṃ

9. The Training Rule on Obstructing Acts of the Sangha.

474. Navame mayanti chabbaggiyanāmakā amhe. Katattāti kammānaṃ katattā. Dhammoti bhūto sabhāvo. Etesūti catūsu saṅghakammesūti. Navamaṃ.
