854. Pañcame tesanti gharasāmikānaṃ. Gharampīti na kevalaṃ āsanameva, gharampi sodhemāti attho. Tatoti parivitakkanato, paranti sambandho.

854. In the fifth, ‘of them’ means of the householders. ‘Even the house’ means the meaning is ‘we should clean the house too, not only the seat.’ ‘From that’ means from reflecting upon it; the connection is with ‘further.’

858. Corā vā uṭṭhitā hontīti yojanāti. Pañcamaṃ.

858. The construction is: ‘or thieves have arisen.’ The fifth.

6. Chaṭṭhasikkhāpadaṃ

6. The Sixth Training Rule.

860. Chaṭṭhe abhinisīdeyyāti ettha abhisaddo upasaggamattovāti dassento āha “nisīdeyyā”ti. Eseva nayo abhinipajjeyyāti etthāpi. Dve āpattiyoti sambandhoti. Chaṭṭhaṃ.

860. In the sixth, in ‘should sit down’ (abhinisīdeyya), showing that the prefix ‘abhi’ is merely a particle, he says, ‘should sit’ (nisīdeyya). This same method applies also in ‘should lie down’ (abhinipajjeyya). ‘Two offenses’—this is the connection. The sixth.

7. Sattamasikkhāpadaṃ

7. The Seventh Training Rule.

864. Sattame [V 1.0144] sabbanti sakalaṃ vattabbavacananti. Sattamaṃ.

864. In the seventh, ‘all’ means the entire statement. The seventh.

8. Aṭṭhamasikkhāpadaṃ

8. The Eighth Training Rule.

869. Aṭṭhame anuttānavacanaṃ natthīti. Aṭṭhamaṃ.

869. In the eighth, there is no difficult word. The eighth.

9. Navamasikkhāpadaṃ

9. The Ninth Training Rule.

875. Navame [M 0.0166] abhisapeyyāti ettha sapadhātussa akkosanatthaṃ antokatvā karadhātuyā atthaṃ dassento āha “sapathaṃ kareyyā”ti. Niraye nibbattāmhīti ahaṃ niraye nibbattā amhīti yojanā. Niraye nibbattatūti esā bhikkhunī niraye nibbattatūti yojanā. Īdisā hotūti mama sadisā hotūti attho. Kāṇāti ekakkhikāṇā, dvakkhikāṇā vā. Kuṇīti hatthapādādivaṅkā.

875. In the ninth, regarding ‘should curse’: here, taking the root ‘sap’ in the sense of abuse and showing the meaning of the root ‘kar,’ he says ‘should make an oath.’ ‘May I be reborn in hell’—the construction is, ‘May I be reborn in hell.’ ‘May she be reborn in hell’—the construction is, ‘May this nun be reborn in hell.’ ‘May she be like this’—the meaning is, ‘may she be like me.’ ‘Blind’ means blind in one eye or in both eyes. ‘Crippled’ means with crooked hands, feet, and so on.

878. Edisāti virūpādijātikā. Viramassūti viramāhi. Addhāti dhuvanti. Navamaṃ.

878. ‘Like this’ means of deformed birth and so on. ‘Desist’ means desist. ‘Indeed’ means certainly. The ninth.

10. Dasamasikkhāpadaṃ

10. The Tenth Training Rule.

879. Dasame anuttānaṭṭhānaṃ natthīti. Dasamaṃ.

879. In the tenth, there is no difficult point. The tenth.

Andhakāravaggo dutiyo.

The Chapter on Darkness, the Second.

3. Naggavaggo

3. The Chapter on the Naked.

1. Paṭhamasikkhāpada-atthayojanā

1. Analysis of the First Training Rule.

883. Naggavaggassa [V 1.0145] paṭhame brahmacariyena ciṇṇenāti ciṇṇena brahmacariyena kiṃ nu kho nāmāti attho. “Brahmacariyassa caraṇenā”ti iminā ciṇṇasaddassa caraṇaṃ ciṇṇanti vacanatthaṃ dasseti. “Na aññaṃ cīvara”nti iminā evatthaṃ dasseti, aññatthāpohanaṃ vāti. Paṭhamaṃ.

883. In the first of the Chapter on the Naked, regarding ‘by the holy life that has been practiced’: the meaning is, ‘what indeed is this practiced holy life?’ By ‘by the practice of the holy life,’ he shows that the verbal meaning of ‘practiced’ is ‘practice.’ By ‘not another robe,’ he shows the meaning of emphasis or the exclusion of something else. The first.

2. Dutiyasikkhāpadaṃ

2. The Second Training Rule

887. Dutiye anuttānaṭṭhānaṃ natthīti. Dutiyaṃ.

887. In the second, there is no difficult point. Second.

3. Tatiyasikkhāpadaṃ

3. The Third Training Rule

893. Tatiye [M 0.0167] anantarāyikinīti ettha natthi antarāyo etissāti anantarāyā, sā eva anantarāyikinīti vacanatthaṃ dassento āha “anantarāyā”ti. Tatiyaṃ.

893. In the third, regarding 'anantarāyikinī': 'there is no obstruction for her,' thus she is 'anantarāyā' (unobstructed); showing the verbal meaning that she herself is 'anantarāyikinī' (one who is unobstructed), he says 'anantarāyā.' Third.

4. Catutthasikkhāpadaṃ

4. The Fourth Training Rule

898. Catutthe pañcāhanti samāhāradigu, ṇikapaccayo svattho. Saṅghāṭicārotiettha kenaṭṭhena saṅghāṭi nāma, cārasaddo kimatthoti āha “paribhogavasena vā”tiādi. Tattha saṅghaṭitaṭṭhenāti saṃharitaṭṭhena. Iminā “kenaṭṭhena saṅghāṭi nāmā”ti pucchaṃ visajjeti. “Parivattana”nti iminā “cārasaddo kimattho”ti codanaṃ pariharati. Pañcasūti ticīvaraṃ udakasāṭikā saṃkaccikāti pañcasūti. Catutthaṃ.

898. In the fourth, 'pañcāhaṃ' is a collective dvigu compound; the suffix '-ika' is pleonastic. Regarding 'saṅghāṭicāro,' it is asked: 'In what sense is it called saṅghāṭi? What does the word cāra mean?' He answers: 'By way of use,' and so on. There, 'by the meaning of being joined' means by the meaning of being collected. With this he answers the question: 'In what sense is it called saṅghāṭi?' With 'changing,' he resolves the objection: 'What does the word cāra mean?' 'In the five' means: the three robes, the bathing cloth, and the bodice—thus five. Fourth.

5. Pañcamasikkhāpadaṃ

5. The Fifth Training Rule

903. Pañcame “cīvarasaṅkamanīya”ntiettha saṅkametabbaṃ paṭidātabbanti saṅkamanīyanti kamudhātussa paṭidānatthañca anīyasaddassa kammatthañca, ‘cīvarañca taṃ saṅkamanīyañce’ti cīvarasaṅkamanīyanti [V 1.0146] visesanaparapadabhāvañca dassento āha “saṅkametabbaṃ cīvara”nti. Tattha “saṅkametabbaṃ cīvara”nti iminā kammatthañca visesanaparapadabhāvañca dasseti. “Paṭidātabbacīvara”nti iminā kamudhātuyā atthaṃ dasseti adhippāyavasenāti. Pañcamaṃ.

903. In the fifth, regarding 'cīvarasaṅkamanīya': 'saṅkamanīya' means 'to be exchanged' or 'to be given back.' This shows the meaning of 'giving back' for the root 'kamu' and the objective sense for the suffix '-anīya.' And showing that 'cīvarasaṅkamanīya' is a karmadhāraya compound meaning 'a robe that is to be exchanged,' he says 'a robe to be exchanged.' Therein, by 'a robe to be exchanged,' he indicates the objective sense and the karmadhāraya relationship. By 'a robe to be given back,' he shows the meaning of the root 'kamu' according to the intention. Fifth.

6. Chaṭṭhasikkhāpadaṃ

6. The Sixth Training Rule

909. Chaṭṭhe “aññaṃ parikkhāra”ntiettha parikkhārassa sarūpaṃ dassento āha “yaṃkiñcī”tiādi. Yaṃkiñci aññataranti sambandho. Kittakaṃagghanakanti kiṃ pamāṇena agghena arahaṃ cīvaraṃ. Dātukāmatthāti tumhe dātukāmā bhavathāti attho. Katipāhenāti katipayāni ahāni katipāhaṃ, yakāralopo. Katipayasaddohi dvitivācako rūḷhīsaddo[M 0.0168], tena katipāhena. Samagghanti appagghaṃ. Saṃsaddo hi appatthavācakoti. Chaṭṭhaṃ.

909. In the sixth, regarding 'another requisite,' showing the nature of a requisite, he says, 'whatever,' and so on. The connection is 'whatever other.' 'Of what value?' means: 'A robe worthy of what value?' 'For one who wishes to give' means: 'You wish to give.' 'In a few days' comes from 'katipayāni ahāni' (a few days), becoming 'katipāhaṃ' with the elision of 'ya.' The word 'katipaya' is a conventional term denoting a small number, hence 'katipāhena.' 'Samagghaṃ' means 'of little value,' for the prefix 'saṃ' indicates smallness. Sixth.

7. Sattamasikkhāpadaṃ

7. The Seventh Training Rule

911. Sattame “vipakkamiṃsū”ti ettha vividhaṃ ṭhānaṃ pakkamiṃsūti dassento āha “tattha tattha agamaṃsū”ti. Amhākampi āgamananti sambandho.

911. In the seventh, regarding 'they departed,' showing that this means they departed to various places, he says, 'they went here and there.' The connection is 'our arrival also.'

915. Katipāhena uppajjissatīti katipāhena cīvaraṃ uppajjissati. Tatoti tasmiṃ cīvaruppajjanakāleti. Sattamaṃ.

915. 'In a few days it will arise' means: 'in a few days the robe will arise.' 'Then' means: 'at that time of the robe's arising.' Seventh.

8. Aṭṭhamasikkhāpadaṃ

8. The Eighth Training Rule

916. Aṭṭhame ye nāṭakaṃ nāṭenti, te naṭā nāmāti yojanā. Iminā naṭakaṃ nāṭentīti naṭāti vacanatthaṃ dasseti. Ye naccanti, te nāṭakā nāmāti yojanā. Iminā sayaṃ naṭantīti nāṭakāti vacanatthaṃ dīpeti. Vaṃsavarattādīsūti ettha vaṃso nāma veṇu. Varattā nāma naddhikā. Ādisaddena rajjuādayo saṅgaṇhāti. Ye laṅghanakammaṃ karonti, te laṅghakā nāmāti yojanā. Māyākārāti ettha māyā nāma mayanāmakena asurena sure calayituṃ katattā mayassa esāti māyā, taṃ karotīti māyākāro, mayanāmako asuroyeva. Aññe pana rūḷhīvasena “māyākārā”ti vuccanti. Sokena jhāyanaṃ ḍayhanaṃ sokajjhāyaṃ, surānaṃ sokajjhāyaṃ karotīti sokajjhāyiko, mayanāmako asuroyeva. Aññe pana rūḷhīvasena “sokajjhāyikā”ti [V 1.0147] vuccanti. Iti imamatthaṃ dassetuṃ vuttaṃ “sokajjhāyikā nāma māyākārā”ti. Kumbhathuṇikā nāmāti ettha vissaṭṭhattā thavīyatīti thuṇo, saddo. Kumbhassa thuṇo kumbhathuṇo. Tena kīḷantīti kumbhathuṇikā, iti imamatthaṃ dasseti “ghaṭakena kīḷanakā”ti iminā. Bimbisakanti caturassaambaṇatāḷanaṃ, taṃ vādentīti bimbisakavādakāti. Aṭṭhamaṃ.

916. In the eighth, the construction for 'actors' (naṭā) is: those who perform a play (nāṭakaṃ) are called actors. By this he shows the verbal meaning of 'naṭā' is 'those who perform a play.' The construction for 'dancers' (nāṭakā) is: those who dance are called dancers. By this he clarifies the verbal meaning of 'nāṭakā' is 'those who dance themselves.' In 'on bamboo poles, straps, and so on,' 'bamboo pole' (vaṃso) means a bamboo. 'Strap' (varattā) means a leather strap. With the word 'and so on' (ādi), he includes ropes and the like. The construction for 'acrobats' (laṅghakā) is: those who perform acrobatic feats are called acrobats. Regarding 'magicians' (māyākārā): 'māyā' is so called because it was created by the asura named Maya to delude the gods—'this is Maya's'—and one who does that is a 'māyākāro,' that is, the asura Maya himself. Others, however, are conventionally called 'magicians.' 'Sokajjhāya' is burning (ḍayhanaṃ) or meditation (jhāyanaṃ) with sorrow; one who causes the gods sorrowful meditation is a 'sokajjhāyiko,' that is, the asura Maya himself. Others, however, are conventionally called 'sokajjhāyikā.' To show this meaning it is said: 'sokajjhāyikā are called māyākārā.' Regarding 'kumbhathuṇikā': 'thuṇa' is a sound (saddo), so called because it is emitted (vissaṭṭhattā) and praised (thavīyati). The sound of a pot (kumbha) is 'kumbhathuṇa.' Those who play with it are 'kumbhathuṇikā.' He shows this meaning with the phrase 'those who play with a small pot.' 'Bimbisaka' is the striking of a four-sided instrument; those who play it are 'bimbisakavādakā.' Eighth.

9. Navamasikkhāpadaṃ

9. The Ninth Training Rule

921. Navame [M 0.0169] tesanti ye “na mayaṃ ayye sakkomā”ti vadanti, tesaṃ. Dassatīti acchādessatīti. Navamaṃ.

921. In the ninth, 'to them' refers to those who say, 'Venerable lady, we are not able.' 'He will give' means 'he will clothe.' Ninth.

10. Dasamasikkhāpadaṃ

10. The Tenth Training Rule

927. Dasame yassāti kathinassa. Ubbhāramūlakoti uddhāramūlako. Saddhāparipālanatthanti kathinuddhāraṃ yācantassa saddhāya paripālanatthanti. Dasamaṃ.

927. In the tenth, 'of which' means of the kathina. 'Ubbhāramūlako' means 'uddhāramūlako' (rooted in withdrawal). 'For the purpose of protecting faith' means for the purpose of protecting the faith of one who is requesting the withdrawal of the kathina. Tenth.

Naggavaggo tatiyo.

The Chapter on the Naked, the Third.

4. Tuvaṭṭavaggo

4. The Tuvaṭṭa Chapter.

1. Paṭhamasikkhāpada-atthayojanā

1. Explanation of the Meaning of the First Training Rule.

933. Tuvaṭṭavaggassa paṭhame “tuvaṭṭa nipajjāya”nti dhātupāṭhesu (saddanītidhātumālāyaṃ 18 ṭakārantadhātu) vuttattā “tuvaṭṭeyyunti nipajjeyyu”nti vuttanti. Paṭhamaṃ.

933. In the first of the Tuvaṭṭa Chapter, since it is stated in the lists of roots, 'tuvaṭṭa, in lying down' (in the Saddanīti Dhātumālā, the 18th ṭ-final root), it is therefore said: 'tuvaṭṭeyyuṃ' means 'they should lie down.' First.

2. Dutiyasikkhāpadaṃ

2. The Second Training Rule

937. Dutiye [V 1.0148] ekattharaṇapāvuraṇantiettha uttarapadānaṃ dvandabhāvaṃ, pubbapadena ca bāhiratthasamāsabhāvaṃ dassetuṃ vuttaṃ “eka”ntiādi. Tattha ceva, casaddehi dvandabhāvaṃ dīpeti, “etāsa”ntiiminā bāhiratthasamāsabhāvaṃ. Etanti “ekattharaṇapāvuraṇā”ti etaṃ nāmanti. Dutiyaṃ.

937. In the second, regarding 'ekattharaṇapāvuraṇā', the explanation beginning 'eka...' is given to show that the latter words form a dvandva compound and that with the first word they form a bahiratthasamāsa. Therein, the dvandva nature is indicated by the words 'ca' and 'eva', and the bahiratthasamāsa nature by the word 'etāsaṃ'. 'Etaṃ' means this name, 'ekattharaṇapāvuraṇā'. Second.

3. Tatiyasikkhāpadaṃ

3. The Third Training Rule

941. Tatiye uḷārakulāti jātiseṭṭhakulā, issariyabhogādīhi vā vipulakulā. Guṇehīti sīlādiguṇehi. “Uḷārāti sambhāvitā”ti iminā itilopatulyādhikaraṇasamāsaṃ dasseti.

941. In the third, 'families of high standing' means families excellent in birth, or families abundant in sovereignty, wealth, and so on. 'By qualities' means by qualities such as virtuous behavior. By the phrase 'Uḷārā means respected,' it indicates an appositional compound with an elided 'iti'.

“Abhibhūtā”ti [M 0.0170] iminā “apakatā”ti ettha karadhātu sabbadhātvatthavācīpi idha apapubbattā visesato abhibhavanatthe vattatīti dasseti. Etāsanti bhikkhunīnaṃ. “Saññāpayamānā”ti iminā saññāpanaṃ saññattīti vacanatthaṃ dasseti. Hetūdāharaṇādīhīti ettha ādisaddena upamādayo saṅgaṇhāti. “Vividhehi nayehi ñāpanā”ti iminā vividhehi ñāpanaṃ viññattīti vacanatthaṃ dasseti.

By the word 'abhibhūtā,' it shows that in the word 'apakatā,' although the root 'kar' can express the meaning of any root, here, because it is preceded by the prefix 'apa,' it is used specifically in the sense of overpowering. 'Etāsaṃ' means 'of the bhikkhunīs.' By the word 'saññāpayamānā,' it shows the etymological meaning that 'saññāpana' is 'saññatti.' In the phrase 'by means of reasons, examples, etc.,' the word 'etc.' includes similes and so on. By the phrase 'making known by various methods,' it shows the etymological meaning that 'vividhehi ñāpanaṃ' is 'viññatti'.

943. Caṅkamane padavāragaṇanāya āpattiyā na kāretabboti āha “nivattanagaṇanāyā”ti. Padādigaṇanāyāti padaanupadādigaṇanāyāti. Tatiyaṃ.

943. He said 'by counting the returns' to show that an offense should not be incurred for counting the rounds of steps during walking meditation. 'By counting steps, etc.' means by counting step after step, etc. Third.

4. Catutthasikkhāpadaṃ

4. The Fourth Training Rule

949. Catutthe anuttānaṭṭhānaṃ natthīti. Catutthaṃ.

949. In the fourth, there is no obscure point. The fourth.

5. Pañcamasikkhāpadaṃ

5. The Fifth Training Rule.

952. Pañcame āṇattā bhikkhunīti yojanā. Idañca paccāsannavasena vuttaṃ yaṃkiñcipi āṇāpetuṃ sakkuṇeyyattāti. Pañcamaṃ.

952. In the fifth, the construction is: 'a bhikkhunī who has been instructed.' And this is said with reference to what is near, because she would be able to command anything whatsoever. The fifth.

6-9. Chaṭṭhādisikkhāpadaṃ

6-9. The Training Rules Beginning with the Sixth.

955. Chaṭṭha-sattama-aṭṭhama-navamesu [V 1.0149] anuttānavacanaṃ natthīti. Chaṭṭha sattama aṭṭhama navamāni.

955. In the sixth, seventh, eighth, and ninth, there is no obscure word. The sixth, seventh, eighth, and ninth.

10. Dasamasikkhāpadaṃ

10. The Tenth Training Rule.

973. Dasame ahundarikāti tasmiṃ kāle, dese vā sambādhassa nāmametanti āha “ahundarikāti sambādhā”ti.

973. In the tenth, he said, 'Ahundarikā means congested,' to show that this is a name for 'congested' at that time or in that place.

975. Yathā “uttarichappañcavācāhī”ti (pāci. 62-65) ettha pañcasaddo na koci attho, vācāsiliṭṭhatthaṃ lokavohāravasena vutto, na evamidha, idha pana attho atthi, pañca yojanāni gacchantiyāpi anāpattiyevāti āha [M 0.0171] “pavāretvā…pe… anāpattī”ti. Paccāgacchatīti paṭinivattetvā āgacchatīti. Dasamaṃ.

975. Just as in the phrase 'uttarichappañcavācāhi' (Pāc. 62–65), the word 'pañca' (five) has no particular meaning but is spoken according to worldly usage for the sake of euphony, it is not so here. Here, however, there is a meaning. He said, 'Having been invited… no offense,' to show that there is no offense even for one going five yojanas. 'She returns' means 'having turned back, she comes.' The tenth.

Tuvaṭṭavaggo catuttho.

The Tuvaṭṭa Chapter, the Fourth.

5. Cittāgāravaggo

5. The Cittāgāra Chapter.

1. Paṭhamasikkhāpada-atthayojanā

1. Explanation of the Meaning of the First Training Rule.

978. Cittāgāravaggassa paṭhame rañño kīḷanaṭṭhānaṃ agāraṃ rājāgāranti vacanatthaṃ dassento āha “rañño kīḷanaghara”nti. Cittaṃ agāraṃ cittāgāraṃ. Ārāmanti nagarato nātidūraārāmoti āha “upavana”nti. Uyyānanti sampannapupphaphalatāya uddhaṃ ulloketvā manussā yanti gacchanti etthāti uyyānaṃ. Pokkharaṇinti pokkharaṃ padumaṃ netīti pokkharaṇī. Pañcapīti rājāgārādīni pañcapi. Sabbatthāti dassanatthāya gamane ca gantvā passane cāti sabbesu.

978. In the first of the Cittāgāra Chapter, showing the etymological meaning of rājāgāra as 'a house that is the king's place of amusement,' he says, 'the king's pleasure-house.' A decorated house is a cittāgāra. Regarding ārāma, he says 'upavana' (park) because it is a park not far from the city. Uyyāna (garden) is so called because people go (yanti) there looking up (uddhaṃ) on account of the abundance of flowers and fruits. Pokkharaṇī (lotus pond) is so called because it leads to lotuses. 'All five' means the five beginning with the royal residence. 'Everywhere' means in all cases, that is, in going for the purpose of seeing and in going and seeing.

981. “Ajjhārāme”tiādinā [V 1.0150] ārāme ṭhitāya ārāmato bahi kate rājāgārādike passantiyāpi anāpattīti dasseti. Tānīti rājāgārādīnīti. Paṭhamaṃ.

981. By the phrase beginning 'ajjhārāme,' it is shown that there is no offense even for one standing in the park who sees a royal residence and so on situated outside the park. 'Those' means the royal residence and so on. The first.

2. Dutiyasikkhāpadaṃ

2. The Second Training Rule.

982. Dutiye anuttānaṭṭhānaṃ natthīti. Dutiyaṃ.

982. In the second, there is no obscure point. The second.

3. Tatiyasikkhāpadaṃ

3. The Third Training Rule.

988. Tatiye yattakanti yattakaṃ suttanti sambandho. Añchitanti kaḍḍhitaṃ. Tasminti tattake sutteti sambandho. Takkamhīti ettha takkoti eko ayomayo suttakantanassa upakaraṇaviseso. So hi takīyati suttaṃ bandhīyati ettha, etenāti vā takkoti vuccati, tasmiṃ. Kantanatoti kantīyate kappāsādibhāvassa chindīyate kantanaṃ, tato.

988. In the third, 'as much as' is connected with 'as much thread.' 'Drawn out' means pulled. 'In that' is connected with 'in that much thread.' Regarding 'on a spindle': here a takka (spindle) is a special implement made of iron for spinning thread. It is called a takka because thread is spun (takīyati) or bound on it or by it; the word in the text is tasmiṃ (on it). 'From spinning': kantana (spinning) is when the state of being cotton and so on is cut; tato means 'from that.'

989. Dasikasuttādinti [M 0.0172] ettha dasāti vatthassāvayavo. So hi diyyati avakhaṇḍīyatīti dasāti vuccati, tassaṃ dasāyaṃ pavattaṃ dasikaṃ, tameva suttaṃ dasikasuttaṃ. Ādisaddena vakkhamānaṃ dukkantitasuttādiṃ saṅgaṇhātīti. Tatiyaṃ.

989. Regarding 'dasikasutta, etc.': here dasā is a part of the cloth. It is called dasā because it is given (diyyati) or cut off (avakhaṇḍīyati). What comes from that dasā is dasikaṃ; that very thread is dasikasuttaṃ. By the word 'etc.' it includes the poorly spun thread and so on, which will be mentioned. The third.

992. In the fourth, 'having begun with' means having begun with washing and so on. 'In edibles, etc.' refers to cakes, edibles, and the like. 'By counting forms' means by counting the forms of cakes and so on.

8. The Eighth Training Rule.

1008. Aṭṭhame anissajjitvāti ettha brahmadeyyena na anissajjanaṃ, atha kho tāvakālikamevāti dassento āha “rakkhanatthāyā”tiādi.

1008. In the eighth, regarding 'not having relinquished': here it is not a non-relinquishing in the sense of a brahminical gift, but is only temporary. To show this, it is said, 'for the purpose of guarding,' and so on.

1012. Paṭijaggikanti [M 0.0173] rakkhaṇakaṃ. Vacībhedanti “paṭijaggāhī”ti vacībhedaṃ. Raṭṭheti vijite. Tañhi raṭhanti gāmanigamādayo tiṭṭhanti etthāti raṭṭhanti vuccatīti. Aṭṭhamaṃ.

1012. 'A guardian' means a protector. 'A verbal utterance' means the utterance, 'Protect it!' 'In a kingdom' means in a conquered territory. For villages, towns, and so on stand and delight in it; therefore it is called a 'kingdom.' The eighth.

9. Navamasikkhāpadaṃ

9. The Ninth Training Rule

1015. Navame sippasaddo paccekaṃ yojetabbo “hatthisippañca assasippañca rathasippañca dhanusippañca tharusippañcā”ti. Tattha tharusippanti asikīḷanasippaṃ. Mantasaddopi paccekaṃ yojetabbo “āthabbaṇamanto ca khīlanamanto ca vasīkaraṇamanto ca sosāpanamanto cā”ti. Tattha āthabbaṇamantoti āthabbaṇavedena vihito parūpaghātakaro manto. Khīlanamantoti sāradārukhīlaṃ mantena jappitvā pathaviyaṃ nikhaṇitvā dhāraṇamanto. Vasīkaraṇamantoti mantena jappitvā parassa ummattabhāvamāpannakaraṇo manto. Sosāpanamantoti parassa maṃsalohitādisosāpanamanto. Agadapayogoti bhusavisassa payojanaṃ. Ādisaddena aññepi parūpaghātakaraṇe sippe saṅgaṇhāti. Yakkhaparittanti yakkhehi samantato tāṇaṃ. Nāgamaṇḍalanti sappānaṃ pavesananivāraṇatthaṃ maṇḍalabandhamanto. Ādisaddena visapaṭihananamantādayo saṅgaṇhātīti. Navamaṃ.

1015. In the ninth, the word 'craft' should be applied to each term individually: 'the craft of the elephant, the craft of the horse, the craft of the chariot, the craft of the bow, and the craft of the sword.' Therein, 'the craft of the sword' means the skill of swordplay. The word 'spell' should also be applied to each term individually: 'the Āthabbaṇa spell, the peg spell, the subjugation spell, and the wasting spell.' Therein, 'the Āthabbaṇa spell' is a spell harmful to others prescribed in the Atharva Veda. 'The peg spell' is a spell for protection, recited over a peg of heartwood which is then driven into the ground. 'The subjugation spell' is a spell recited to make another person go mad. 'The wasting spell' is a spell for withering another's flesh and blood, etc. 'The use of remedies' means the application of a strong poison. By the word 'etcetera,' other crafts that cause harm to others are included. 'Yakkha-protection' is protection on all sides from yakkhas. 'Nāga-circle' is a spell for binding a circle to prevent the entry of snakes. By the word 'etcetera,' spells that counteract poison and so on are included. The ninth.

1043. Pañcame [V 1.0153] “kule maccharo”ti ettha maccharanaṃ maccharoti vacanattho kātabbo. “Taṃ kulaṃ assaddhaṃ appasanna”nti kulassa avaṇṇaṃ bhāsatīti yojanā. “Bhikkhuniyo dussīlā pāpadhammā”ti bhikkhunīnaṃ avaṇṇaṃ bhāsatīti yojanā.

1043. In the fifth, regarding 'stingy towards the family,' the meaning of the word 'maccharo' should be understood as 'stinginess.' 'That family is faithless and displeased' is to be construed as speaking ill of the family. 'The nuns are immoral and of evil character' is to be construed as speaking ill of the nuns.

1045. “Santaṃyeva ādīnava”nti sambandhiyā sambandhaṃ dassetuṃ vuttaṃ “kulassa vā bhikkhunīnaṃ vā”ti iminā dvīsu aññatarameva na sambandho hoti, atha kho dvayampīti dassetīti. Pañcamaṃ.

1045. The phrase 'a real drawback' is stated to show the connection. By the phrase 'of the family or of the nuns,' it shows that the connection is not with just one of the two, but with both. The fifth.

6. The Sixth Training Rule

1048. Chaṭṭhe ovādāyāti ettha na yo vā so vā ovādo hoti, atha kho garudhammoyevāti āha “garudhammatthāyā”ti. Saha vasati ettha, etenāti vā saṃvāsoti vacanatthena uposathapavāraṇā saṃvāso nāmāti āha “uposathapavāraṇāpucchanatthāyā”ti. “Pucchanatthāyā”ti iminā “saṃvāsāyā”ti ettha uttarapadalopabhāvaṃ dasseti. Etthāti bhikkhunivibhaṅge, sikkhāpade vā pāḷiyaṃ vāti. Chaṭṭhaṃ.

1048. In the sixth, regarding 'for exhortation': here it is not just any exhortation, but specifically the weighty rules; thus it says, 'for the purpose of the weighty rules.' Based on the verbal meaning 'one lives together here' or 'one lives together with this,' 'communion' refers to the Uposatha and Pavāraṇā; thus it says, 'for the purpose of asking about the Uposatha and Pavāraṇā.' By the phrase 'for the purpose of asking,' it indicates the elision of the final part of the word in 'saṃvāsāya.' 'Here' means in the Bhikkhunīvibhaṅga, or in the training rule, or in the Pāḷi text. The sixth.

10. Dasamasikkhāpadaṃ

10. The Tenth Training Rule

1062. Dasame dve kāyā uparimakāyo heṭṭhimakāyoti. Tattha kaṭito uddhaṃ uparimakāyo, heṭṭhā heṭṭhimakāyo. Tattha “pasākhe”ti idaṃ heṭṭhimakāyassa nāmanti āha “adhokāye”ti. Hīti saccaṃ. Tatoti adhokāyato. Iminā pañcamībāhiratthasamāsaṃ dasseti. Rukkhassa sākhā pabhijjitvā gatā viya ubho ūrū pabhijjitvā gatāti yojanā.

1062. In the tenth, there are two bodies: the upper body and the lower body. Therein, from the waist upwards is the upper body; below is the lower body. Therein, it says that 'pasākhe' is a name for the lower body, thus 'adhokāye' ('in the lower body'). 'Hi' means 'truly.' 'Tato' means 'from that,' that is, from the lower body. By this, it indicates a compound with an external meaning in the ablative case. The construction is: just as a branch of a tree, having broken off, is gone, so both thighs, having broken off, are gone.

1065. Phālehīti [V 1.0154] ettha itisaddo ādyattho. Tena “dhovā”tiādīni cattāri padāni saṅgaṇhāti. Āṇattidukkaṭānīti heṭṭhā vuttesu aṭṭhasu dukkaṭesu vinayadukkaṭameva. Sesesūti bhindanato sesesu phālanādīsūti. Dasamaṃ.

1065. In 'Phālehi,' the word 'iti' has the sense of 'and so on.' It thus includes the four words beginning with 'dhovā.' 'Āṇattidukkaṭāni' means that among the eight dukkaṭas mentioned below, it is only the Vinaya dukkaṭa. 'Sesesūti' means in the remaining cases apart from breaking, such as splitting and so on. The tenth.

1069. Gabbhinivaggassa paṭhame kucchiṃ paviṭṭho satto etissā atthīti kucchipaviṭṭhasattā. “Kucchi”ntipi pāṭho. Iminā gabbhinīti ettha gabbhasaddo kucchiṭṭhasattavācakoti dasseti. Gabbhasaddo (abhidhānappadīpikāyaṃ 944 gāthāyaṃ) hi kucchiṭṭhasatte ca kucchimhi ca ovarake ca vattatīti. Paṭhamaṃ.

For the word 'gabbha' (in the Abhidhānappadīpikā, verse 944) is said to refer to a being in the womb, to the womb itself, and to an inner chamber. The first.

8. Kumāribhūtavaggo

8. The Section on Former Maidens

1-2-3. Paṭhama-dutiya-tatiyasikkhāpada-atthayojanā

1-3. The Application of the Meaning of the First, Second, and Third Training Rules

1119. Kumāribhūtavaggassa [M 0.0177] paṭhamadutiyatatiyesu yā pana tā mahāsikkhamānāti sambandho. Sabbapaṭhamā dve mahāsikkhamānāti gabbhinivagge sabbāsaṃ sikkhamānānaṃ paṭhamaṃ vuttā dve mahāsikkhamānā. Tā panāti mahāsikkhamānā pana. Sikkhamānāicceva vattabbāti sammutikammesu [V 1.0156] sāmaññato vattabbā. “Gihigatā”ti vā “kumāribhūtā”ti vā na vattabbā, vadanti ce, sammutikammaṃ kuppatīti adhippāyo. Gihigatāyāti ettha gihigatā nāma purisantaragatā vuccati. Sā hi yasmā purisasaṅkhātena gihinā gamiyittha, ajjhācāravasena, gihiṃ vā gamittha, tasmā gihigatāti vuccati. Ayaṃ sikkhamānāti sambandho. Kumāribhūtā nāma sāmaṇerā vuccati. Sā hi yasmā agihigatattā kumārī hutvā bhūtā, kumāribhāvaṃ vā bhūtā gatā, tasmā kumāribhūtāti vuccati. Tissopīti gihigatā kumāribhūtā mahāsikkhamānāti tissopi. Sikkhamānāti sikkhaṃ mānetīti sikkhamānāti. Paṭhama dutiya tatiyāni.

1119. In the first, second, and third of the Section on Former Maidens, the connection is with 'yā pana tā mahāsikkhamānā.' 'Sabbapaṭhamā dve mahāsikkhamānā' means the two great probationers mentioned first among all the probationers in the Section on Pregnant Women. 'Tā pana' means 'but those great probationers.' 'Sikkhamānāicceva vattabbā' means that in formal acts, they should be referred to in general terms. The intention is that they should not be called 'gihigatā' or 'kumāribhūtā'; if they are so called, the formal act becomes invalid. Here, 'gihigatā' is said to be one who has gone to another man. For she is called 'gihigatā' because she was approached by a man, a householder, by way of transgression, or she went to a householder. The connection is with 'this probationer.' A 'kumāribhūtā' is said to be a female novice. For she is called 'kumāribhūtā' because, not having cohabited, she has been a maiden, or she has attained the state of maidenhood. 'Tissopi' refers to the gihigatā, the kumāribhūtā, and the great probationer. 'Sikkhamānā' is so called because she honors the training. The first, second, and third.

9. Navamasikkhāpadaṃ

9. The Ninth Training Rule

1158. Navame antoti abbhantare. Iminā ātyūpasaggassatthaṃ dasseti. “Soka”ntiādinā anto vāseti pavesetīti āvāsā[M 0.0178]. Sokaṃ āvāsā sokāvāsāti vacanatthaṃ dasseti. Gharaṃ gharasāmikā āvisanti viya, evaṃ ayampi sokaṃ āvisatīti yojanā. Itīti evaṃ. Yanti sokaṃ. Svāssāti so assā. Soti soko. Assāti sikkhamānāya. Āvāsoti āvāsokāso. “Edisā aya”nti iminā “ajānantī”ti ettha ajānanākāraṃ dassetīti. Navamaṃ.

1158. In the ninth, 'anto' means 'inside.' By this, he shows the meaning of the prefix 'ā.' By the words beginning with 'soka,' he shows that 'āvāsā' means 'one dwells within' or 'one enters.' He shows the meaning of the expression 'sokāvāsā' as 'sokaṃ āvāsā.' The construing is: just as householders enter a house, so too this one enters sorrow. 'Iti' means 'thus.' 'Yanti sokaṃ.' 'Svāssā' is 'so assā.' 'So' is sorrow. 'Assā' refers to the probationer. 'Āvāso' means a dwelling, an opportunity. By 'edisā aya,' he shows the manner of not knowing here in 'ajānantī.' The ninth.

10. Dasamasikkhāpadaṃ

10. The Tenth Training Rule

1162. Dasame [V 1.0157] anāpucchāti ettha tvāpaccayo lopoti āha “anāpucchitvā”ti. Dvikkhattunti dve vāre. Sakinti ekavāraṃ.

1162. In the tenth, regarding 'anāpucchā,' he says 'anāpucchitvā' because the suffix '-tvā' has been elided. 'Dvikkhattuṃ' means twice. 'Sakiṃ' means once.

1163. Apubbaṃ samuṭṭhānasīsaṃ imassāti apubbasamuṭṭhānasīsaṃ. Dvīsupi ṭhānesūti vācāto ca kāyavācāto cāti dvīsu ṭhānesupi. Ananujānāpetvāti mātāpitūhi ca sāmikena ca na anujānāpetvāti. Dasamaṃ.

1163. 'Apubbasamuṭṭhānasīsaṃ' is a compound explained as 'that which has an unprecedented chief origination.' 'Dvīsupi ṭhānesu' means in two cases: from speech and from body and speech. 'Ananujānāpetvā' means not having been given permission by her mother and father and by her husband. The tenth.

11. Ekādasamasikkhāpadaṃ

11. The Eleventh Training Rule

1167. Ekādasame tatthāti “pārivāsiyachandadānenā”ti vacane. Aññatrāti aññaṃ ṭhānaṃ.

1167. In the eleventh, 'tattha' refers to the phrase 'pārivāsiyachandadānena.' 'Aññatra' means another place.

Ekaṃ ajjhesantīti ekaṃ bhikkhuṃ dhammakathanatthāya niyyojenti. Aññaṃ panāti uposathikato aññaṃ pana.

'Ekaṃ ajjhesanti' means they appoint one bhikkhu for the purpose of teaching the Dhamma. 'Aññaṃ pana' means another apart from the one on Uposatha duty.

Tatrāti tesu bhikkhūsu. Subhāsubhaṃ nakkhattaṃ paṭhatīti nakkhattapāṭhako. Dāruṇanti kakkhaḷaṃ. Teti bhikkhū. Tassāti nakkhattapāṭhakassa bhikkhussa. “Nakkhattaṃ paṭimānentaṃ, attho bālaṃ upaccagā”tijātakapāḷi (jā. 1.1.49). Ayaṃ panettha yojanā – nakkhattaṃ paṭimānentaṃ bālaṃ attho hitaṃ upaccagā upasamīpe atikkamitvā agāti. Ekādasamaṃ.

'Tatra' means among those bhikkhus. One who recites the auspicious and inauspicious constellations is an astrologer. 'Dāruṇaṃ' means harsh. 'Te' means the bhikkhus. 'Tassa' refers to the astrologer bhikkhu. The Jātaka text states: 'While he was waiting for the constellation, the goal passed the fool by.' This is the construing here: the goal, the benefit, passed by the fool who was waiting for the constellation; that is, having approached near, it went away, having passed by. The eleventh.

12. Dvādasamasikkhāpadaṃ

12. The Twelfth Training Rule

1170. Dvādasame [M 0.0179] nappahotīti bhikkhuniyo nivāsāpetuṃ na sakkotīti. Dvādasamaṃ.

1170. In the twelfth, 'nappahoti' means he is unable to make the bhikkhunīs dwell. The twelfth.

13. Terasamasikkhāpadaṃ

13. The Thirteenth Training Rule

1175. Terasame ekaṃ vassanti ettha vassasaddo saṃvaccharapariyāyo, upayogavacanañca bhummatthe hotīti āha “ekasmiṃ saṃvacchare”ti. Terasamaṃ.

1175. In the thirteenth, in the phrase ekaṃ vassaṃ, the word vassa is a synonym for saṃvacchara. And the case ending is used in the sense of the locative; thus he says 'ekasmiṃ saṃvacchare.' The thirteenth.

Kumāribhūtavaggo aṭṭhamo.

The Kumāribhūta Chapter, the Eighth.

9. Chattupāhanavaggo

9. The Chapter on the Umbrella and Footwear.

1. Paṭhamasikkhāpada-atthayojanā

1. Construing the Meaning of the First Training Rule.

1181. Chattavaggassa [V 1.0158] paṭhame kaddamādīnīti cikkhallādīni. Ādisaddena udakādīni saṅgaṇhāti. Gacchādīnīti khuddapādapādīni. Ādisaddena aññānipi chattaṃ dhāretuṃ asakkuṇeyyāni sambādhaṭṭhānāni saṅgaṇhātīti. Paṭhamaṃ.

1181. In the first of the Chapter on the Umbrella, kaddamādīni means muddy places and the like. By the word ādi, he includes water and so on. Gacchādīni means small trees and the like. By the word ādi, he also includes other constricted places where one would be unable to hold up an umbrella. The first.

2. Dutiyasikkhāpadaṃ

2. The Second Training Rule.

1184. Dutiye yānenāti yanti icchitaṭṭhānaṃ sukhena gacchanti anenāti yānanti. Dutiyaṃ.

1184. In the second, regarding yānena: yāna (vehicle) is so called because they go (yanti), they travel with ease to a desired place, by means of it. The second.

3. Tatiyasikkhāpadaṃ

3. The Third Training Rule.

1191. Tatiye “vippakiriyiṃsū”ti kiriyāpadassa kattunā avinābhāvato kattāraṃ dassetuṃ vuttaṃ “maṇayo”ti. Maṇayoti ca ratanānīti. Tatiyaṃ.

1191. In the third, because the verb vippakiriyiṃsū ('they were scattered') is inseparable from its agent, the word maṇayo ('jewels') is stated in order to show that agent. And maṇayo means gems. The third.

4. Catutthasikkhāpadaṃ

4. The Fourth Training Rule.

1194. Catutthe sīsūpagādīsūti ādisaddena gīvūpagādayo saṅgaṇhāti. Yaṃ yanti alaṅkāranti. Catutthaṃ.

1194. In the fourth, regarding sīsūpagādīsu ('on head-ornaments, etc.'), by the word ādi ('etc.'), he includes neck-ornaments and so on. Yaṃ yaṃ means any kind of ornament. The fourth.

5. Pañcamasikkhāpadaṃ

5. The Fifth Training Rule.

1199. Pañcame [M 0.0180] gandhena cāti gandheti attano vatthuṃ sūceti pakāsetīti gandho. Vaṇṇakena cāti vilepanena ca. Tañhi vaṇṇayati chavisobhaṃ pakāsetīti vaṇṇakanti vuccati. Casaddena samāhāradvandavākyaṃ dīpetīti. Pañcamaṃ.

1199. In the fifth, regarding gandhena ca ('and with perfume'): gandho (perfume) is so called because it indicates, makes known, or reveals its own substance. Vaṇṇakena ca means 'and with unguent.' For that describes or reveals the beauty of the complexion, therefore it is called vaṇṇaka (cosmetic). By the word ca ('and'), he indicates a copulative compound. The fifth.

6. Chaṭṭhasikkhāpadaṃ

6. The Sixth Training Rule.

1202. Chaṭṭhe [V 1.0159] anuttānavacanaṃ natthīti. Chaṭṭhaṃ.

1202. In the sixth, there is no word that is not plain. The sixth.

7. Sattamasikkhāpadaṃ

7. The Seventh Training Rule.

1208. Sattame ummaddaneti uppīḷitvā maddane. Saṃbāhanepīti punappunaṃ bāhanepīti. Sattamaṃ.

1208. In the seventh, ummaddane means pressing down and rubbing. Saṃbāhanepi means repeatedly stroking. The seventh.

8-10. Aṭṭhamādisikkhāpadaṃ

8-10. The Training Rules Beginning with the Eighth.

1210. Aṭṭhamādīsu tīsu anuttānavacanaṃ natthīti. Aṭṭhamanavamadasamāni.

1210. In the three beginning with the eighth, there is no word that is not plain. The eighth, ninth, and tenth.

11. Ekādasamasikkhāpadaṃ

11. The Eleventh Training Rule.

1214. Ekādasame abhimukhamevāti abhimukhe eva. Mukhassa hi abhi abhimukhanti vacanattho kātabbo, sattamiyā aṃkāro. Iminā puratoti ettha topaccayo bhummatthe hotīti dasseti. Upacāranti dvādasahatthūpacāranti. Ekādasamaṃ.

1214. In the eleventh, abhimukhameva means 'right in front.' The meaning of the word abhimukhaṃ should be understood as 'towards (abhi) the face (mukhassa)'; the ending -aṃ is in the locative sense. By this he shows that here in purato, the suffix -to is in the sense of the locative. Upacāraṃ means the range of twelve cubits. The eleventh.

12. Dvādasamasikkhāpadaṃ

12. The Twelfth Training Rule.

1219. Dvādasame “anokāsakata”ntipadassa ayuttasamāsabhāvañca visesanaparapadabāhirasamāsabhāvañca dassetuṃ vuttaṃ “akataokāsa”nti. Okāso na kato yenāti anokāsakato, bhikkhu, taṃ. “Aniyametvā”ti iminā “anodissā”ti padassa tvāpaccayantabhāvaṃ dassetīti. Dvādasamaṃ.

1219. In the twelfth, to show that the word anokāsakata is an irregular compound and an exocentric compound in which the latter member is qualified, the word akataokāsa is stated. He by whom permission has not been given (okāso na kato yena) is anokāsakato; this refers to the bhikkhu. By the word aniyametvā ('without designating'), he shows that the word anodissā is a gerund ending in the suffix -tvā. The twelfth.

13. Terasamasikkhāpadaṃ

13. The Thirteenth Training Rule.

1226. Terasame [M 0.0181] upacārepīti aparikkhittassa gāmassa parikkhepārahaṭṭhānasaṅkhāte upacārepi.

1226. In the thirteenth: upacārepi ('in the environs') means in the environs of an unenclosed village, reckoned as a place suitable for an enclosure.

1227. “Acchinnacīvarikāyā”ti [V 1.0160] sāmaññato vuttepi visesoyevādhippetoti āha “saṅkaccikacīvaramevā”ti. Samantato purisānaṃ dassanaṃ kantīyati chindīyati etthāti saṅkacci, adhakkhakaubbhanābhiṭṭhānaṃ, saṅkacce nivasitabbanti saṃkaccikaṃ, tameva cīvaranti saṅkaccikacīvaranti. Terasamaṃ.

1227. Acchinnacīvarikāya ('for one with an unseparated robe'): although this is stated generally, a specific meaning is intended, thus he says, 'specifically, the saṅkaccika-robe.' A saṅkacci is that by which the sight of men from all around is cut off or severed; it is the area of the lower belly, hips, and navel. What is to be worn over the saṅkacci is a saṅkaccika. That very robe is the saṅkaccika-robe. The thirteenth.

Chattupāhanavaggo navamo.

The Chapter on the Umbrella and Footwear, the Ninth.

Sabbāneva sikkhāpadānīti sambandho. Tatoti tehi aṭṭhāsītisatasikkhāpadehi, apanetvāti sambandho.

Sabbāneva sikkhāpadāni ('all the training rules') is the connection. Tato ('from that') means 'from those one hundred and eighty-eight training rules'; apanetvā ('having excluded') is the connection.

Tatrāti tesu khuddakesu. Etthāti dasasu sikkhāpadesūti.

Tatra ('there') means 'among those minor ones.' Ettha ('here') means 'in these ten training rules.'

Bhikkhunivibhaṅge khuddakavaṇṇanāya

In the Bhikkhunīvibhaṅga, in the Explanation of the Minor Rules.

Yojanā samattā.

The Yojanā is completed.

5. Pāṭidesanīyasikkhāpada-atthayojanā

5. The Construing of the Meaning of the Pāṭidesanīya Training Rules.

Khuddakānaṃ anantarā pāṭidesanīyā nāma aṭṭha ye dhammā saṅkhepeneva saṅgahaṃ ārūḷhā saṅgītikārehi, tesaṃ aṭṭhannaṃ pāṭidesanīyanāmakānaṃ dhammānaṃ saṅkhepeneva esā vaṇṇanā pavattateti yojanā.

After the minor rules are the eight rules named Pāṭidesanīya, which were included in the collection only briefly by the Reciters of the Council. This explanation of those eight rules named Pāṭidesanīya proceeds only concisely. This is the construing.

1228. Yāni sabbitelādīnīti sambandho. Hīti vitthāro. Etthāti aṭṭhasu pāṭidesanīyesu. Pāḷivinimuttakesūti pāḷito vinimuttakesu. Sabbesūti akhilesu sabbitelādīsūti.

1228. 'Whatever things such as ghee and oil' is the connection. 'Hi' means an elaboration. 'Here' means in the eight Pāṭidesanīya rules. 'Those freed from the Pāḷi' means those released from the Pāḷi. 'In all' means in all without exception, that is, in all such as ghee and oil.

Bhikkhunivibhaṅge pāṭidesanīyavaṇṇanāya yojanā samattā.

In the Bhikkhunīvibhaṅga, the Yojanā on the Explanation of the Pāṭidesanīya Rules is completed.

Panāti pakkhantarajotako. Ye dhammā uddiṭṭhāti sambandho. Tesanti pāṭidesanīyānaṃ. Puna tesanti sekhiyaadhikaraṇasamathadhammānaṃ.

'Pana' illuminates an alternative. 'Which rules were set forth' is the connection. 'Of those' refers to the Pāṭidesanīya rules. 'Again, of those' refers to the Sekhiya and Adhikaraṇasamatha rules.

Tanti [V 1.0161][M 0.0182] atthavinicchayaṃ, vidū vadantīti sambandho. Yakāro padasandhikaro. Ayaṃ panettha yojanā – tesaṃ pāṭidesanīyānaṃ anantarā ye ca sekhiyā pañcasattati ye ca dhammā, casaddo luttaniddiṭṭho, adhikaraṇavhayā adhikaraṇasamathanāmakā satta ye ca dhammā bhagavatā uddiṭṭhā, tesaṃ sekhiyaadhikaraṇasamathadhammānaṃ yo atthavinicchayo vibhaṅge mayā vutto, tādisameva taṃ atthavinicchayaṃ bhikkhunīnaṃ vibhaṅgepi vidū vadanti yasmā, tasmā tesaṃ dhammānaṃ sekhiyaadhikaraṇasamathadhammānaṃ yā atthavaṇṇanā tattha mahāvibhaṅge visuṃ mayā na vuttā. Imā atthavaṇṇanā idhāpi bhikkhunīnaṃ vibhaṅgepi, pisaddo luttaniddiṭṭho, mayā na vuttāyevāti. Nakāro dvīsu kiriyāsu yojetabbo.

'That' means the determination of the meaning; 'the wise say' is the connection. The letter 'y' is for euphonic conjunction. This is the construing here: After those Pāṭidesanīya rules are the seventy-five Sekhiya rules and the seven rules for the settlement of issues set forth by the Blessed One—the word 'ca' is elided. Since the wise state that the determination of the meaning of these Sekhiya and Adhikaraṇasamatha rules, which was stated by me in the Vibhaṅga, is exactly the same also in the Bhikkhunīvibhaṅga, therefore the explanation of those Sekhiya and Adhikaraṇasamatha rules was not stated separately by me in the Mahāvibhaṅga. This explanation was also not stated by me here in the Bhikkhunīvibhaṅga—the word 'pi' is elided. The negative particle 'na' should be connected with both verbs.

“Sabbāsavapahaṃ maggaṃ, puññakammena ciminā;

Uppādetvā sasantāne, sattā passantu nibbuti”nti.

"By this meritorious action, having generated in their own continuities of being the path that abandons all taints, may beings see Nibbāna!"

Ayaṃ gāthā etarahi potthakesu natthi, ṭīkāsu pana atthi. Tasmā evamettha yojanā veditabbā – iminā puññakammena ca vibhaṅgavaṇṇanāya katena iminā puññakammena ca aññena puññakammena ca. Casaddo hi avuttasampiṇḍanattho. Sattā sabbe sattā sabbāsavapahaṃ sabbesaṃ āsavānaṃ vighātakaṃ maggaṃ arahattamaggaṃ sasantāne attano niyakajjhatte uppādetvā janetvā nibbutiṃ khandhaparinibbānaṃ ñāṇālocanena passantūti.

This verse is not found in the books nowadays, but it is in the subcommentaries. Therefore, the construing here should be understood thus: 'By this meritorious action' means by this meritorious action done in composing the explanation of the Vibhaṅga and by other meritorious action. For the word 'ca' serves to include what has not been stated. 'Beings' means all beings. 'The path that abandons all taints' means the path that destroys all taints, the path of arahantship. 'Having generated in their own continuities of being' means having produced in their own personal existence. 'May they see Nibbāna' means may they see with the light of knowledge the final Nibbāna of the aggregates.

Iti samantapāsādikāya vinayasaṃvaṇṇanāya

Thus in the Samantapāsādikā, the Vinaya Commentary,

Bhikkhunivibhaṅgavaṇṇanāya

in the Explanation of the Bhikkhunīvibhaṅga,

Yojanā samattā.

the Yojanā is completed.

Jādilañchitanāmena, nekānaṃ vācito mayā;

Bhikkhunīnaṃ vibhaṅgassa, samatto yojanānayoti.

"By me, named Jādilañchita, this has been recited for many; the methodical Yojanā on the Bhikkhunīvibhaṅga is completed."

Namo tassa bhagavato arahato sammāsambuddhassa

Homage to the Blessed One, the Arahant, the Perfectly Self-Enlightened One.

Mahāvaggayojanā

The Yojanā on the Mahāvagga

1. Mahākhandhakaṃ

1. The Great Chapter

1. Bodhikathā

1. The Discourse on Enlightenment

Evūbhatovibhaṅgassa[V 1.0162][M 0.0183], katvāna yojanānayaṃ;

Mahāvaggakhandhakassa, karissaṃ yojanānayaṃ.

Having thus composed the methodical Yojanā for the two Vibhaṅgas, I will now compose the methodical Yojanā for the Mahāvagga Khandhaka.

Ubhinnanti ubhayesaṃ. Pātimokkhānanti pātimokkhavibhaṅgānaṃ. Pātimokkhagahaṇena hettha tesaṃ vibhaṅgopi gahito abhedena vā uttarapadalopavasena vā. Khandhakanti paññattisamūhaṃ. Khandhasaddo hettha paññattivācako. Vinayapaññattiyo vuccanti “khandho”ti. Tesaṃ samūho khandhako. Athavā khandhoti rāsi. Khandhasaddo hi rāsatthavācako. Vinayapaññattirāsi vuccati “khandho”ti. Kakāro pakāsakavācako. Khandhānaṃ vinayapaññattirāsīnaṃ ko pakāsakoti khandhako, [V 1.0163] taṃ khandhakaṃ. Ayaṃ panettha yojanā – ubhinnaṃ pātimokkhānaṃ saṅgītisamanantaraṃ khandhakovidā khandhakesu kusalā mahātherā yaṃ khandhakaṃ saṅgāyiṃsu, tassa khandhakassa dāni saṃvaṇṇanākkamo yasmā sampatto, tasmā tassa khandhakassa ayaṃ anuttānatthavaṇṇanā hotīti.

'Of both' means of the two. 'Of the Pātimokkhas' means of the Pātimokkha Vibhaṅgas. By the inclusion of 'Pātimokkha' here, its Vibhaṅga is also included, either because they are inseparable or by way of eliding the latter term. 'Khandhaka' means a collection of rules. Here the word 'khandha' denotes a rule. The Vinaya rules are called 'khandha.' Their collection is a 'khandhaka.' Alternatively, 'khandha' means a heap. For the word 'khandha' denotes the meaning 'heap.' The heap of Vinaya rules is called 'khandha.' The suffix 'ka' is an indicator. What indicates the heaps of Vinaya rules? The Khandhaka. That is the Khandhaka. This is the construing here: Immediately after the communal recitation of both Pātimokkhas, the great elders skilled in the Khandhakas recited a certain Khandhaka. Since the turn for its commentary has now come, therefore this is the explanation of the non-obvious meaning of that Khandhaka.

Ye atthāti sambandho. Hisaddo padālaṅkāro. Yesanti padānaṃ. Teti te atthe. Bhaveti bhaveyya, bhavituṃ sakkuṇeyyāti attho. Tesanti atthānaṃ. Kinti kiṃ payojanaṃ. Teti atthe, ñātunti sambandho. Athavā teti atthā, avaṇṇitāti sambandho. Tesaṃyevāti atthānameva. Ayaṃ panettha yojanā – padabhājanīye yesaṃ padānaṃ ye atthā bhagavatā pakāsitā, tesaṃ padānanti pāṭhaseso, te atthe puna vadeyyāma ce, kadā pariyosānaṃ saṃvaṇṇanāya pariniṭṭhānaṃ bhave, na bhaveyyāti adhippāyo. Ye ceva atthā uttānā, tesaṃ saṃvaṇṇanāya kiṃ payojanaṃ, na payojananti adhippāyo. Adhippāyānusandhīhi ca adhippāyena ca anusandhinā ca byañjanena ca ye pana atthā anuttānā, te atthe, atthā vā avaṇṇitā [M 0.0184] yasmā ñātuṃ na sakkā, tasmā tesaṃyeva atthānaṃ ayaṃ saṃvaṇṇanānayo hotīti. Itisaddo parisamāpanattho.

'Which meanings' is the connection. The word 'hi' is a particle of embellishment. 'Of which' refers to the words. 'Those' refers to those meanings. 'Would be' means it could be, it could come to be. 'Of those' refers to the meanings. 'What' means for what purpose. 'Those' refers to the meanings; 'to be known' is the connection. Alternatively, 'those' refers to the meanings; 'unexplained' is the connection. 'Of those very' refers to the meanings themselves. This is the construing here: In the Padabhājanīya, for whichever words the meanings were declared by the Blessed One—the phrase 'of those words' is the remainder of the text—if we were to state those meanings again, when would the commentary reach its conclusion? It would not reach it, is the intention. And for those meanings that are plain, what is the use of a commentary? There is no use, is the intention. But as for those meanings that are not plain by way of intention, connection, and phrasing, since those meanings, being unexplained, cannot be known, therefore this is the method of commentary for just those meanings. The word 'iti' is for the purpose of conclusion.

1. “Tena…pe… verañjāya”ntiādīsu (pārā. 1) karaṇavacane visesakāraṇamatthi viya, “tena…pe… paṭhamābhisambuddho”ti ettha kiñcāpi natthīti yojanā. Asadisopamāyaṃ. Kiñcāpisaddo garahatthajotako, pana-saddo sambhāvanatthajotako. “Karaṇavacanenevā”ti ettha evakārena upayogavacanaṃ vā bhummavacanaṃ vā nivāreti. Abhilāpoti abhimukhaṃ atthaṃ lapatīti abhilāpo, saddo. Āditoti verañjakaṇḍato. Etanti “tena samayena buddho bhagavā uruvelāya”ntiādivacanaṃ. “Aññesupī”ti vatvā tamevatthaṃ dassetuṃ vuttaṃ “ito paresū”ti.

1. In such passages as 'By that ... in Verañjā' (Pārā. 1), there seems to be a special reason for the instrumental case, but here in 'by that ... first perfectly enlightened,' although there is none—this is the construing. This is a simile of the incomparable. The word 'kiñcāpi' (although) indicates censure, while the word 'pana' (but) indicates possibility. Here in 'by the instrumental case alone,' the word 'alone' excludes the instrumental of means and the locative. 'Expression' means it speaks the meaning directly, thus it is an expression; it is sound. 'From the beginning' means from the Verañjā section. 'This' refers to the statement beginning 'At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was at Uruvelā…' Having said 'in others as well,' in order to show that very meaning, it is said 'in those that follow this.'

Yadi visesakāraṇaṃ natthi, kiṃ panetassa vacane payojananti codento āha “kiṃ panetassā”tiādi. Etassāti “tena samayena buddho bhagavā uruvelāya”ntiādivacanassa. Nidānadassanaṃ payojanaṃ nāmāti yojanā. Tamevatthaṃ vibhāvetumāha “yā hī”tiādi. Yā pabbajjā ceva yā upasampadā ca bhagavato anuññātāti yojanā. Yāni ca anuññātānīti sambandho. Tānīti pabbajjādīni. Abhisambodhinti arahattamaggañāṇapadaṭṭhānaṃ sabbaññutaññāṇañca sabbaññutaññāṇapadaṭṭhānaṃ arahattamaggañāṇañca. Bodhimahāmaṇḍeti mahantānaṃ maggañāṇasabbaññutaññāṇānaṃ pasannaṭṭhāne bodhirukkhamūleti attho. Evantiādi nigamanaṃ.

Raising an objection, one says, 'If there is no special reason, then what is the purpose of this statement?' beginning with 'What then is the purpose of this?' 'Of this' refers to the statement beginning 'At that time the Buddha, the Blessed One, was at Uruvelā…' 'Showing the occasion is the purpose'; this is the construing. To clarify that very meaning, he says, beginning, 'For whatever...' 'The going forth and the higher ordination that were permitted by the Blessed One'; this is the construing. 'And whatever things were permitted' is the connection. 'Those' means the going forth and so on. 'Full enlightenment' means the knowledge of the path of arahantship as the basis for the knowledge of omniscience, and the knowledge of omniscience as the basis for the knowledge of the path of arahantship. 'At the great Bodhi-terrace' means at the place where the great path-knowledge and knowledge of omniscience became clear, that is, at the foot of the Bodhi tree. 'Thus, etc.,' is the conclusion.

Tatthāti [V 1.0164] yaṃ “tena samayena uruvelāya”ntiādivacanaṃ vuttaṃ, tattha. Uruvelāyanti ettha urusaddo mahantapariyāyoti āha “mahāvelāya”nti. “Vālikarāsimhī”ti iminā velāsaddassa rāsatthaṃ dasseti, kālasīmādayo nivatteti. Yadi pana “urū”ti vālikāya nāmaṃ, “velā”ti mariyādāya, evañhi sati nanu uruyā velāti attho daṭṭhabboti āha “velātikkamanahetu āhaṭā uru uruvelā”ti. Iminā [M 0.0185] velāya atikkamo velā uttarapadalopavasena, velāya āhaṭā uru uruvelā padavipariyāyavasenāti dasseti. Etthāti “uruvelāya”ntipade. Tamevatthaṃ vibhāvento āha “atīte kirā”tiādi. Anuppanne buddhe pabbajitvāti sambandho. Tāpasapabbajjanti isipabbajjaṃ, na samaṇapabbajjaṃ. Katikavattanti karaṇaṃ kataṃ, katena pavattaṃ katikaṃ, tameva vattaṃ katikavattaṃ. Akaṃsu kirāti sambandho. Yoti yo koci. Aññoti attanā aparo. So ākiratūti sambandho. Pattapuṭenāti paṇṇena katena puṭena. Tatoti katikavattakaraṇato. Tatthāti tasmiṃ padese. Tatoti mahāvālikarāsijananato, paranti sambandho. Nanti taṃ padesaṃ. Tanti mahāvālikarāsiṃ.

'Therein' refers to the passage that was stated beginning, 'At that time in Uruvelā.' In 'Uruvelā,' the word 'uru' is a synonym for 'great,' thus he says 'in the great expanse.' By 'in a heap of sand,' he shows that the meaning of the word 'velā' is 'heap,' thereby excluding time-limit and so on. But if 'uru' is the name for sand and 'velā' for boundary, should not the meaning be understood as 'the boundary of the sand'? Thus he says: 'Uruvelā is so called because sand (uru) was brought on account of surpassing the boundary.' By this he shows that 'surpassing the boundary' (velāya atikkamo) becomes 'velā' through elision of the final member of the compound, and 'sand brought to the boundary' (velāya āhaṭā uru) becomes 'Uruvelā' through reversal of the words. 'Here' means in the word 'Uruvelā.' Explaining this same meaning, he says, 'in the past, it seems,' and so on. The connection is: 'having gone forth when a Buddha had not arisen.' 'The ascetic going-forth' means the going-forth of seers, not that of recluses. 'The agreed practice': 'kataṃ' is what is done; 'katikaṃ' is what proceeds from what is done; that very practice is 'katikavattaṃ.' The connection is: 'they made, it seems.' 'Who' means whoever. 'Another' means someone other than oneself. The connection is: 'let him scatter.' 'With a leaf-container' means with a container made of a leaf. 'From that' means from making the agreed practice. 'Therein' means in that region. 'From that' means from the creating of the great heap of sand. The connection is 'afterwards.' 'It' refers to that region. 'That' refers to the great heap of sand.

“Bodhirukkhamūle”ti ettha assattharukkhassa upacāravasena bodhīti nāmalabhanaṃ dassento āha “bodhi vuccati catūsu maggesu ñāṇa”ntiādi. Iminā cattāri saccāni bujjhatīti bodhīti vacanatthena catūsu maggesu ñāṇaṃ bodhi nāmāti dasseti. Etthāti bodhimhi, bodhiyaṃ vā. Samīpatthe cetaṃ bhummavacanaṃ. Rukkhopīti pisaddena na maggañāṇamevāti dasseti. Mūleti āsanne. Paṭhamābhisambuddhoti anunāsikalopavasena sandhīti āha “paṭhamaṃ abhisambuddho”ti. “Hutvā”ti iminā “paṭhama”ntipadassa bhāvanapuṃsakaṃ dasseti. Sabbapaṭhamaṃyevāti sabbesaṃ janānaṃ paṭhamameva abhisambuddho hutvāti sambandho. Eko eva pallaṅko ekapallaṅkoti avadhāraṇasamāsaṃ dassento āha “ekeneva pallaṅkenā”ti. “Sakiṃ…pe… ābhujitenā”ti iminā avadhāraṇaphalaṃ dasseti. Pallaṅkoti ca ūrubaddhāsanaṃ. Vimuttisukhaṃ paṭisaṃvedīti ettha tadaṅgādīsu (paṭi. ma. aṭṭha. 1.1.104) pañcasu vimuttīsu paṭippassaddhisaṅkhātā phalasamāpatti evādhippetāti āha “phalasamāpattisukha”nti. Phalasamāpattīti arahattaphalasamāpatti. Sā hi viruddhehi upakkilesehi muccitaṭṭhena vimuttīti vuccati, tāya sampayuttaṃ sukhaṃ vimuttisukhaṃ, catutthajjhānikaṃ arahattaphalasamāpattisukhaṃ. Athavā tāya jātaṃ sukhaṃ vimuttisukhaṃ, sakalakilesadukkhūpasamasukhaṃ[M 0.0186]. “Paṭisaṃvedayamāno”tiiminā “paṭisaṃvedī”ti ettha ṇīpaccayassa kattutthaṃ dasseti. Punappunaṃ suṭṭhu vadati anubhavatīti paṭisaṃvedī. Paṭisaṃvedī hutvā nisīdīti sambandho.

“At the foot of the Bodhi tree”: Here, to show how the Assattha tree acquired the name “Bodhi” by way of figurative speech, he says: “’Bodhi’ is said to be knowledge in the four paths,” and so on. By this, he shows that because one awakens to (bujjhati) the four truths, knowledge in the four paths is named “Bodhi” by verbal definition. “Here”: in Bodhi, or at Bodhi. This locative is in the sense of proximity. “And the tree”: by the word “also,” he shows that it is not merely the knowledge of the path. “At the foot”: near. “First fully enlightened”: saying “first fully enlightened” (paṭhamaṃ abhisambuddho), he indicates that the sandhi is by way of elision of the nasal. By “having been,” he shows the adverbial sense of the word “first.” “Indeed the very first”: the connection is: having been fully enlightened as the very first among all people. “One and the same seat”: to show the determinative compound “one seat,” he says: “with one and the same seat.” By “once... having bent,” he shows the result of the determination. And “seat” is the cross-legged posture. “Experiencing the bliss of liberation”: here, among the five kinds of liberation, it is fruition attainment, designated as “tranquility,” that is intended; hence he says: “the bliss of fruition attainment.” “Fruition attainment”: the fruition attainment of Arahantship. This is called “liberation” because it is freed from opposing defilements. The bliss associated with it is the bliss of liberation, the bliss of the fruition attainment of Arahantship belonging to the fourth jhāna. Alternatively, the bliss born of it is the bliss of liberation, a bliss which is the pacification of all suffering from the defilements. By “experiencing” (paṭisaṃvedayamāno), he shows the agentive meaning of the suffix -ī in “experienced” (paṭisaṃvedī). One who repeatedly and well speaks of or enjoys is one who “experiences.” The connection is: “having experienced, he sat.”

Paccayākāranti [V 1.0165] avijjādipaccayānaṃ uppādākāraṃ. Kasmā paccayākāro paṭiccasamuppādo nāmāti āha “paccayākāro hī”tiādi. Hīti saccaṃ, yasmā vā. “Aññamañña”ntiiminā “paṭiccā”tipadassa kammaṃ dasseti, “sahite”tiiminā saṃsaddassatthaṃ. “Dhamme”tiiminā tassa sarūpaṃ. Etthāti imissaṃ vinayaṭṭhakathāyaṃ. Tatthāti “anulomapaṭiloma”ntipade, anulomapaṭilomesu vā. Sveva paccayākāro vuccatīti yojanā. “Attanā kattabbakiccakaraṇato”tiiminā anulomasaddassa sabhāvatthaṃ dasseti. Svevāti paccayākāro eva. Taṃ kiccanti attanā kattabbaṃ taṃ kiccaṃ. Tassa akaraṇatoti attanā kattabbakiccassa akaraṇato. Iminā paṭilomasaddassa sabhāvatthaṃ dasseti. Purimanayenevāti “avijjāpaccayā saṅkhārā”tiādinā purimanayeneva. Vāti athavā. Pavattiyāti saṃsārapavattiyā. Anulomoti anukūlo, anurūpo vā. Itaroti “avijjāyatvevā”tiādinā vutto paccayākāro. Tassāti pavattiyā. Paṭilomoti paṭiviruddho, etthāti “anulomapaṭiloma”ntipade. Attho daṭṭhabboti ettha attho evāti sambhavato tassa phalaṃ vā “saddantaratthāpohanena saddo atthaṃ vadatī”ti vacanato (udā. aṭṭha. 1; dī. ni. ṭī. 1.1; ma. ni. ṭī. 1.mulapariyāyasuttavaṇṇanā; saṃ. ni. ṭī. 1.1.oghatarayasuttavaṇṇanā; a. ni. ṭī. 1.1.rupādivaggavaṇṇanā) saddantaratthāpohanaṃ vā dassento āha “ādito panā”tiādi. Yāvasaddo avadhivacano. Yāva antaṃ pāpetvāti sambandho. Itoti imehi vuttehi dvīhi atthehi. “Manasākāsī”ti ettha ikāralopavasena sandhīti āha “manasi akāsī”ti. Tatthāti “manasākāsī”tipade. Yathāti yenākārena. Idanti imaṃ ākāraṃ. Tatthāti “avijjāpaccayā saṅkhārā”tiādipāṭhe avayavattho evaṃ veditabboti yojanā. Samāsamajjhe tasaddena pubbapadasseva liṅgavacanāni gahetabbānīti āha “avijjā ca sā paccayo cā”ti[M 0.0187]. Vākye pana tasaddena parapadasseva liṅgavacanāni gahetabbāni. “Avijjāpaccayā”tipadaṃ “sambhavantī”tipadena sambandhitabbanti āha “tasmā avijjāpaccayā saṅkhārā sambhavantī”ti. Sabbapadesūti “saṅkhārapaccayā viññāṇa”ntiādīsu sabbesu padesu.

“The mode of conditions” means the mode of arising of the conditions beginning with ignorance. Why is the mode of conditions called dependent origination? He says: “Because it is the mode of conditions,” and so on. “Because” (hi) means truly, or since. By “mutually” he shows the object of the word “dependent.” By “together” he shows the meaning of the prefix saṃ-. By “phenomena” he shows its nature. “Here” means in this Vinaya commentary. “There” means in the term “forward and reverse,” or in the forward and reverse orders. The connection is: that same mode of conditions is so called. By “because of performing the task to be done by oneself,” he shows the intrinsic meaning of the word “forward.” “That same” means the mode of conditions itself. “That task” means that task to be performed by oneself. “Because of not performing it” means because of not performing the task to be done by oneself. By this he shows the intrinsic meaning of the word “reverse.” “By the previous method” means by the earlier method, as in “with ignorance as condition, formations,” and so on. “Or” means alternatively. “In the process” means in the process of saṃsāra. “Forward” means favorable or conforming. “The other” means the mode of conditions stated as “from ignorance indeed,” and so on. “Of that” means of the process. “Reverse” means opposed. “Here” means in the term “forward and reverse.” “The meaning should be understood”: here, the meaning itself is possible, or its result, or, in accordance with the saying, “a word conveys meaning by excluding the meaning of other words,” showing the exclusion of the meaning of other words, he says: “from the beginning,” and so on. The word “up to” (yāva) denotes a limit. The connection is: “having brought it up to the end.” “Thus” means by these two stated meanings. “He attended” (manasākāsī): saying “he attended in mind” (manasi akāsi), he indicates that the sandhi is by way of elision of the vowel i. “There” means in the term “he attended.” “As” means in what manner. “This” means this manner. “There”: in the text beginning “with ignorance as condition, formations,” the meaning of the parts should be understood thus—this is the connection. In the middle of a compound, by the word 'ta', the gender and number of the preceding word itself should be taken; thus he says: 'ignorance and that is a condition.' In a sentence, however, by the word 'ta', the gender and number of the following word itself should be taken. The phrase “with ignorance as condition” should be connected with the word “arise”; thus he says: “therefore, with ignorance as condition, formations arise.” “In all instances” means in all passages, such as “with formations as condition, consciousness,” and so on.

Yathā panāti yenākārena pana. Idanti imaṃ ākāraṃ. Tatthāti “avijjāya…pe… nirodho”tiādivākye. Avijjāyatvevāti ettha “bhaddiyotvevā”tiādīsu viya “bhaddiyo iti evā”ti padacchedo kattabbo, na evaṃ “avijjāya iti evā”ti, atha kho “avijjāya tu evā”ti kātabboti āha “avijjāya tu evā”ti. “Pa atimokkhaṃ atipamokkha”ntiādīsu (kaṅkhā. aṭṭha. nidānavaṇṇanā) viya upasaggabyattayena vuttaṃ, evamidha [V 1.0166] nipātabyattayena vuttanti daṭṭhabbaṃ. Tattha evasaddena sattajīvādayo nivatteti. Tusaddo pakkhantaratthajotako. Anulomapakkhato paṭilomasaṅkhātaṃ pakkhantaraṃ manasākāsīti attho. Asesavirāganirodhasaddo ayuttasamāso, uttarapadena ca tatiyāsamāsoti āha “virāgasaṅkhātena maggena asesanirodhā”ti. Tattha asesasaddaṃ virāgasaddena sambandhamakatvā nirodhasaddena sambandhaṃ katvā atthassa gahaṇaṃ ayuttasamāso nāma. “Maggenā”tiiminā virāgasaddassatthaṃ dasseti. Maggo hi virajjanaṭṭhena virāgoti vuccati. Saṅkhāranirodhoti ettha maggena nirodhattā anuppādanirodho hotīti āha “saṅkhārānaṃ anuppādanirodho hotī”ti. Anuppādanirodhoti ca anuppādena nirodho samucchedavasena niruddhattā. Evanti yathā avijjāyatveva asesavirāganirodhā saṅkhāranirodho, evaṃ tathāti attho. Tatthāti “evametassā”tiādivacane. Kevalasaddo sakalapariyāyoti āha “sakalassā”ti, anavasesassāti attho. Athavā sattajīvādīhi amissitattā amissatthoti āha “suddhassa vā”ti. “Sattavirahitassā”ti iminā suddhabhāvaṃ dasseti. Dukkhakkhandhassāti ettha khandhasaddo rāsatthavācakoti āha “dukkharāsissā”ti.

“Now, as follows” means in what manner now. “This” means this manner. “Therein” means in the statement beginning “from ignorance... cessation.” Regarding “from ignorance indeed” (avijjāyatveva): here, as in such cases as “indeed Bhaddiya” (bhaddiyotveva), the word division should not be made as avijjāya iti eva, but rather as avijjāya tu eva; thus he says “from ignorance but indeed” (avijjāya tu evā). Just as in cases like pa atimokkhaṃ atipamokkha, it is stated by interchange of prepositions, so here it should be understood that it is stated by interchange of particles. Here, with the word eva (indeed), he refutes views of a being, a soul, etc. The word tu (but) illuminates the meaning of an alternative. The meaning is: he attended to the alternative, designated the reverse order, as distinct from the forward order. The word asesavirāganirodha (cessation through the remainderless fading away) is an improperly constructed compound, and with the latter word it is an instrumental compound; thus he says: “through the remainderless cessation by the path designated as ‘fading away.’” Here, taking the meaning by connecting the word asesa (remainderless) with the word nirodha (cessation) instead of with the word virāga (fading away) is what is called an improperly constructed compound. By “through the path,” he shows the meaning of the word virāga, for the path is called virāga in the sense of fading away. “Cessation of formations”: here, because there is cessation by the path, it is a cessation of non-arising; thus he says: “there is a cessation of the non-arising of formations.” And “cessation of non-arising” is cessation by non-arising, because they have ceased by way of eradication. “Thus” means: just as “from ignorance indeed, through the remainderless fading away, there is the cessation of formations,” so it is. “Therein,” that is, in the statement “thus of this”: The word “entire” (kevala) is a synonym for “whole”; thus he says “of the whole,” meaning “of what is without remainder.” Alternatively, because it is unmixed with views of a being, a soul, etc., it has the meaning of “unmixed”; thus he says “or of the pure.” By “devoid of a being,” he shows the state of purity. “Of the mass of suffering”: here the word “mass” (khandha) is a term for “heap”; thus he says “of the heap of suffering.”

Etamatthaṃ [M 0.0188] viditvāti ettha etasaddassa visayaṃ dassetuṃ vuttaṃ “yvāya”ntiādi. Tattha “avijjādivasena…pe… nirodho hotī”ti yvāyaṃ attho vuttoti yojanā. Samudayo ca hotīti sambandho. Viditavelāyanti pākaṭavelāyaṃ pasiddhakāleti attho. Imaṃ udānanti ettha imasaddo vuccamānāpekkho. Tasmiṃ atthe vidite satīti yojanā. Pajānanatāyāti pakārena jānanabhāvassa. Somanassayuttañāṇasamuṭṭhānanti somanassena ekuppādādivasena yuttena ñāṇena samuṭṭhānaṃ, yuttaṃ vā ñāṇasaṅkhātaṃ samuṭṭhānaṃ udānanti sambandho. Tattha udānanti kenaṭṭhena udānaṃ? Udānaṭṭhena, modanaṭṭhena, kīḷanaṭṭhena cāti attho. Kimidaṃ udānaṃ nāma? Pītivegasamuṭṭhāpito udāhāro. Yathā (udā. aṭṭha. ganthārambhakathā) hi yaṃ telādiminitabbavatthu mānaṃ gahetuṃ na sakkoti visanditvā gacchati, taṃ “avaseko”ti vuccati. Yañca jalaṃ taḷākaṃ gahetuṃ na sakkoti, ajjhottharitvā gacchati, taṃ “ogho”ti vuccati. Evamevaṃ yaṃ pītivegasamuṭṭhāpitaṃ vitakkavipphāraṃ hadayaṃ sandhāretuṃ na sakkoti, so adhiko hutvā anto asaṇṭhahitvā vacīdvārena nikkhamanto paṭiggāhakanirapekkho udāhāraviseso “udāna”nti vuccati. “Attamanavācaṃ nicchāresī”ti iminā udadhātussa udāhāratthaṃ dasseti.

In 'Having understood this meaning'—here, to show the referent of the word 'this,' it is said, 'that which,' and so on. Therein, the connection is with the meaning stated: 'by dependence on ignorance, etc. … cessation occurs.' The relation is: 'And arising occurs.' 'At the time of knowing' means at the time it becomes manifest, the established time. 'This inspired utterance'—here, the word 'this' refers to what is being spoken of. The connection is: 'when that meaning is understood.' 'By way of discerning' refers to the state of knowing in a special way. 'Arisen from knowledge conjoined with gladness' means the inspired utterance is an arising from knowledge conjoined with gladness by way of co-arising, etc., or it is an arising designated as knowledge that is conjoined. Here, 'inspired utterance'—by what meaning is it an 'inspired utterance'? By the meaning of uttering forth, rejoicing, and sporting—this is the meaning. What is this so-called 'inspired utterance'? An utterance produced by the force of rapture. For just as (Ud-a, Ganthārambhakathā) oil or the like that cannot be contained by a measure and spills over is called 'overflow'; and water that cannot be held in a lake and inundates it is called a 'flood'; similarly, when the heart cannot contain the expansion of thought produced by the force of rapture, this, having become excessive and not staying inside, issues forth through the speech door as a special kind of utterance independent of a recipient—this is called an 'inspired utterance.' 'He uttered a gladdened utterance'—this shows that the root ud has the meaning of uttering forth.

Tassāti udānassa attho evaṃ veditabboti yojanā. Yadāti ettha dāpaccayassa atthavākyaṃ [V 1.0167] dassento āha “yasmiṃ kāle”ti. Haveti “byatta”nti imasmiṃ atthe nipāto. Byattaṃ pākaṭanti hi attho. Pātubhavantīti ettha pātunipātassa atthassa “have”ti nipātena vuttattā bhūdhātusseva atthaṃ dassento āha “uppajjantī”ti. Anuloma paṭiloma paccayākāra paṭivedhasādhakāti anulomato ca paṭilomato ca paccayākārassa paṭivijjhanassa sādhakā. Bodhipakkhiyadhammāti bodhiyā maggañāṇassa pakkhe bhavā sattatiṃsa dhammā. Athavā pātunipātena saha “bhavantī”tipadassa atthaṃ dassento āha “pakāsantī”ti. Imasmiṃ naye havesaddo ekaṃsatthavācako. Have ekaṃsenāti hi attho. Abhisamayavasenāti maggañāṇavasena[M 0.0189]. Maggañāṇañhi yasmā abhimukhaṃ cattāri saccāni samecca ayati jānāti, tasmā abhisamayoti vuccati.

The meaning of that inspired utterance is to be understood thus—this is the connection. Regarding 'yadā' (when), showing the explanatory phrase for the suffix '-dā,' he says 'at which time.' 'Have' is a particle in the sense of 'manifest.' For the meaning is 'manifest,' 'clear.' In 'pātubhavanti' (they become manifest), since the meaning of the particle 'pātu' is expressed by the particle 'have,' showing the meaning of just the root 'bhū,' he says 'they arise.' 'Conducive to the penetration of the structure of conditions in direct and reverse order' means they are aids for the penetration of the structure of conditions directly and in reverse. 'The factors of enlightenment' are the thirty-seven dhammas that are on the side of the path-knowledge of enlightenment. Alternatively, showing the meaning of the word 'bhavanti' together with the particle 'pātu,' he says 'they shine forth.' In this interpretation, the word 'have' means 'definitely.' For 'have' means 'definitely.' 'By way of breakthrough' means by way of the path-knowledge. For since the path-knowledge directly confronts, comes together with, and proceeds to know the four truths, it is called 'breakthrough' (abhisamaya).

“Kilesasantāpanaṭṭhenā”ti iminā ābhuso kilese tāpetīti ātāpoti vacanatthaṃ dasseti. Na vīriyasāmaññaṃ hoti, atha kho sammappadhānavīriyamevāti āha “sammappadhānavīriyavato”ti. Iminā ātāpīti ettha īpaccayassa vantuatthaṃ dasseti. Ārammaṇūpanijjhānalakkhaṇena cāti kasiṇādiārammaṇaṃ upagantvā nijjhānasabhāvena aṭṭhasamāpattisaṅkhātena jhānena ca. Lakkhaṇūpanijjhānalakkhaṇena cāti aniccādilakkhaṇaṃ upagantvā nijjhānasabhāvena vipassanāmaggaphalasaṅkhātena jhānena ca. “Bāhitapāpassā”ti iminā bāhito aṇo pāpo anenāti brāhmaṇoti vacanatthaṃ dasseti. Aṇasaddo hi pāpapariyāyo. “Khīṇāsavassā”ti iminā tassa sarūpaṃ dasseti. Athassāti atha assa, tasmiṃ kāle brāhmaṇassāti attho. Yā etā kaṅkhā vuttāti sambandho. “Ko nu kho…pe… avocā”tiādinā (saṃ. ni. 2.12) nayena ca tathā “katamaṃ nu kho…pe… avocā”tiādinā (saṃ. ni. 2.35) nayena ca paccayākāre vuttāti yojanā. No kallo pañhoti ayutto pañho, duppañho esoti attho. Tathāti evaṃ, tato aññathā vā. Yā ca soḷasa kaṅkhā (ma. ni. 1.18; saṃ. ni. 2.20) āgatāti sambandho. Apaṭividdhattā kaṅkhāti yojanā. Soḷasa kaṅkhāti atītavisayā pañca, anāgatavisayā pañca, paccuppannavisayā chāti soḷasavidhā kaṅkhā. Vapayantīti vi apayanti, ikāralopenāyaṃ sandhi. Vityūpasaggo dhātvatthānuvattako, apayanti – saddo apagamanatthoti āha “apagacchantī”ti. “Nirujjhantī”tiiminā apagamanatthameva pariyāyantarena dīpeti. “Kasmā”ti iminā “yato pajānāti sahetudhamma”nti vākyassa pubbavākyakāraṇabhāvaṃ dasseti. Sahetudhammanti ettha saha avijjādihetunāti sahetu, saṅkhārādiko paccayuppannadhammo. Sahetu ca so dhammo cāti sahetudhammoti vacanatthaṃ dassento āha “avijjādikenā”tiādi[V 1.0168]. “Paṭivijjhatī”ti iminā pajānā tīti [M 0.0190] ettha ñādhātuyā avabodhanatthaṃ dasseti, māraṇatosanādike atthe nivatteti. Itīti tasmā, vapayantīti yojanā.

By 'because it intensely burns the defilements,' this shows the etymology of 'ardent' (ātāpī) as one who intensely burns (tāpeti) the defilements (kilese). It is not mere energy in general, but specifically the energy of right exertion; thus it says, 'of one possessing the energy of right exertion.' This shows that the suffix '-ī' in 'ātāpī' has the meaning of 'possessing' (-vant). 'And by the characteristic of absorption upon an object' means by the absorption, designated as the eight attainments, which has the nature of absorption upon an object such as a kasiṇa. 'And by the characteristic of absorption upon characteristics' means by the absorption, designated as insight, path, and fruition, which has the nature of absorption upon characteristics such as impermanence. For 'one who has cast out evil,' this shows the etymology of 'brahmin' as 'one by whom a subtle evil has been cast out.' For the word 'aṇu' is a synonym for 'pāpa.' By 'of one whose taints are destroyed,' it shows his true nature. 'Then for him' means then, at that time, for the brahmin. The connection is: 'those doubts that have been mentioned.' The connection is: 'stated in the structure of conditions' by the method beginning 'Who, now… he said' (SN 12.12) and similarly by the method beginning 'What, now… he said' (SN 12.35). 'Not a proper question' means an unsuitable question, this is a bad question. 'Thus' means in this way, or otherwise than that. The connection is: 'And the sixteen doubts that have come about' (MN 2; SN 12.20). The connection is: 'they are doubts because they have not been penetrated.' 'The sixteen doubts' are the sixteen kinds of doubt: five concerning the past, five concerning the future, and six concerning the present. 'They vanish' (vapayanti): this is a sandhi for 'vi apayanti,' with the elision of the vowel 'i.' The prefix 'vi-' follows the meaning of the root; the word 'apayanti' has the meaning of going away, thus it says 'they depart.' By 'they cease,' it illuminates the meaning of 'going away' with a synonym. 'Why?'—this shows that the phrase 'because one understands the phenomenon with its cause' is the reason for the preceding phrase. In 'the phenomenon with its cause,' 'with its cause' (sahetu) means together with its cause, ignorance, etc.; this is the conditioned phenomenon (paccayuppannadhammo), formations, etc. Showing the etymology of 'sahetudhammo' as 'it is with a cause and it is a phenomenon,' it says 'with its cause, ignorance, etc.' By 'one penetrates,' this shows that the root 'ñā' in 'pajānāti' has the meaning of comprehension, thereby excluding meanings such as killing or pleasing. 'Therefore' (iti), the connection is 'they vanish.'

2. Paccayakkhayassāti paccayānaṃ khayaṭṭhānassa asaṅkhatassāti yojanā. Tatrāti dutiyaudāne. Khīyanti paccayā etthāti khayaṃ, nibbānanti āha “paccayānaṃ khayasaṅkhātaṃ nibbāna”nti. “Aññāsī”ti iminā avedīti ettha vidadhātuyā ñāṇatthaṃ dasseti, anubhavanalābhādike nivatteti. Tasmā vapayantīti sambandho. Vuttappakārāti paṭhamaudāne vuttasadisā. Dhammāti bodhipakkhiyadhammā, catuariyasaccadhammā vā.

2. 'Of the destruction of conditions' means of the unconditioned, the state of the destruction of conditions—this is the connection. Therein, in the second inspired utterance, 'destruction' (khaya) is so called because 'conditions are destroyed here'; this is Nibbāna. It says: 'Nibbāna, which is designated as the destruction of conditions.' By 'one has understood,' it shows that the root 'vid' in 'avedi' has the meaning of knowledge, excluding meanings such as experiencing and attainment. Therefore, the connection is 'they vanish.' 'Of the kind stated' means similar to what was stated in the first inspired utterance. 'Dhammas' means the factors of enlightenment or the dhammas of the Four Noble Truths.

3. Imaṃ udānaṃ udānesīti sambandho. Yena maggena viditoti yojanā. Tatrāti tatiyaudāne. So brāhmaṇo tiṭṭhatīti sambandho. Tehi uppannehi bodhipakkhiyadhammehi vā yassa ariyamaggassa catusaccadhammā pātubhūtā, tena ariyamaggena vā vidhūpayanti yojanā. Vuttappakāranti suttanipāte vuttappakāraṃ. Mārasenanti kāmādikaṃ dasavidhaṃ mārasenaṃ. “Vidhamento”tiiminā vidhūpayanti ettha dhūpadhātuyā vidhamanatthaṃ dasseti, limpanatthādayo nivatteti. “Viddhaṃ sento”tiiminā vidhamentoti ettha dhamudhātuyā dhaṃsanatthaṃ dasseti, saddatthādayo nivatteti. “Sūriyova obhāsaya”ntipadassa “sūriyo ivā”ti atthaṃ dassento āha “yathā”tiādi. Sūriyoti ādicco. So hi yasmā paṭhamakappikānaṃ sūraṃ janeti, tasmā sūriyoti vuccati. Abbhuggatoti abhimukhaṃ uddhaṃ ākāsaṃ gato, abbhaṃ vā ākāsaṃ uggato. Abbhasaddo hi ākāsapariyāyo. Ākāso hi yasmā ābhuso bhāti dippati, tasmā “abbha”nti vuccati. Ayaṃ panettha opammasaṃsandanaṃ – yathā sūriyo obhāsayanto tiṭṭhati, evaṃ brāhmaṇo saccāni paṭivijjhanto. Yathā sūriyo andhakāraṃ vidhamento tiṭṭhati, evaṃ brāhmaṇo mārasenampi vidhūpayantoti.

3. The connection is: 'He uttered this inspired utterance.' The connection is: 'known by which path.' Therein, in the third inspired utterance, the connection is: 'that brahmin stands.' The connection is: 'they dispel' either by those arisen factors of enlightenment, or by that noble path for which the dhammas of the Four Truths have become manifest. 'Of the kind stated' means of the kind stated in the Suttanipāta. 'Māra's army' refers to the tenfold army of Māra, beginning with sensual desire. By 'dispelling' (vidhumento), this shows that the root 'dhū' in 'vidhūpayanti' has the meaning of shaking off, excluding meanings such as smearing. By 'destroying' (viddhaṃsento), this shows that the root 'dham' in 'vidhamenti' has the meaning of destroying, excluding meanings such as sound. Showing that the word 'sūriyova obhāsayaṃ' means 'like the sun illuminating,' it says 'just as,' etc. 'Sūriya' means the sun (ādicca). Because it generates courage (sūraṃ) in the first-aeon beings, it is called 'sūriya.' 'Abbhuggato' means gone up towards the sky, or risen into the sky (abbha). The word 'abbha' is a synonym for sky. The sky is called 'abbha' because it shines (bhāti) and glows (dippati) intensely (ābhuso). Herein, this is the connection of the simile: just as the sun stands illuminating, so the brahmin stands penetrating the truths. Just as the sun stands dispelling the darkness, so the brahmin stands dispelling Māra's army.

Etthāti etesu tīsu udānesu. Paṭhamaṃ udānaṃ uppannanti sambandho. Imissā khandhakapāḷiyā udānapāḷiṃ saṃsandanto āha “udāne panā”tiādi[M 0.0191]. Udāne pana vuttanti sambandho. Tanti udāne vuttavacanaṃ, vuttanti sambandho. Accayenāti atikkamena, tamevatthaṃ vibhāvento āha “tadā hī”tiādi. Tadāti “sve āsanā vuṭṭhahissāmī”ti rattiṃ uppāditamanasikārakāle. Bhagavā manasākāsīti sambandho. Purimā dve udānagāthā ānubhāvadīpikā hontīti yojanā. Tassāti paccayākārapajānanapaccayakkhayādhigamassa. Ekekamevāti [V 1.0169] anulomapaṭilomesu ekekameva. Paṭhamayāmañcāti accantasaṃyoge upayogavacanaṃ, nirantaraṃ paṭhamayāmakālanti attho. Idha panāti imasmiṃ khandhake pana. Tamevatthaṃ vitthārento āha “bhagavā hī”tiādi. Tattha bhagavā udānesīti sambandho. Visākhapuṇṇamāyāti visākhāya yuttāya puṇṇamāya. “Aruṇo uggamissatī”ti vattabbasamayeti sambandho. Sabbaññutanti sabbaññubhāvaṃ, anāvaraṇañāṇanti attho. Tatoti aruṇuggamanato. Taṃ divasanti bhummatthe upayogavacanaṃ, tasmiṃ divaseti hi attho. Accantasaṃyoge vā, taṃ divasaṃ kālanti hi attho. Evaṃ manasi katvāti yathā taṃ divasaṃ anulomapaṭilomaṃ manasākāsi, evaṃ manasi katvāti attho. Itīti evaṃ. “Bodhirukkhamūle…pe… nisīdī”ti evaṃ vuttaṃ taṃ sattāhanti yojanā. Tatthevāti bodhirukkhamūleyeva.

Herein means in these three inspired utterances. The first inspired utterance is connected with 'arisen.' Connecting the Udāna passage with the text of this chapter, it says, 'But in the Udāna,' etc. 'But in the Udāna' is connected with 'was spoken.' 'That' refers to the words spoken in the Udāna; it is connected with 'was spoken.' 'By the passing' means by the transcending. Explaining that very meaning, it says, 'For then,' etc. 'Then' means at the time during the night when he formed the intention, 'Tomorrow I will rise from my seat.' 'The Blessed One attended' is the connection. The first two stanzas of the inspired utterance are to be construed as illuminating his power. 'Of that' means of the attainment of the destruction of conditions through the knowledge of the structure of conditions. 'One by one' means one by one in the direct and reverse orders. 'During the first watch' is the accusative case used in the sense of continuous duration; the meaning is the uninterrupted time of the first watch. 'But here' means but in this chapter. Elaborating on that very meaning, it says, 'For the Blessed One,' etc. There, 'the Blessed One uttered an inspired utterance' is the connection.
