'On the Visākha full moon' means on the full moon associated with the constellation Visākha. It is connected with the time when it should be said, 'The dawn will rise.' 'Omniscience' means the state of omniscience; the meaning is unobstructed knowledge. 'From then' means from the rising of the dawn. 'That day' is the accusative case used in the locative sense, for the meaning is 'on that day.' Or it is used in the sense of continuous duration, for the meaning is 'for the time of that day.' 'Having thus attended' means having attended in direct and reverse order on that day, thus 'having attended.' 'Thus' means in this way. The statement 'at the foot of the Bodhi tree… he sat' is to be construed as 'for those seven days.' 'Right there' means right at the foot of the Bodhi tree.

2. Ajapālakathā

2. The Story of the Goatherd's Banyan

4. Na bhagavāti ettha nakāro “upasaṅkamī”ti padena yojetabbo, na upasaṅkhamīti hi attho. Tamhā samādhimhāti tato arahattaphalasamāpattisamādhito. Anantarameva anupasaṅkamanaṃ upamāya āvikaronto āha “yathā panā”tiādi. Iccevaṃ vuttaṃ na hotīti yojanā. Idanti idaṃ atthajātaṃ. Etthāti “bhutvā sayatī”ti vākye. Evanti upameyyajotako. Idhāpīti imissaṃ “atha kho bhagavā”tiādipāḷiyampi. Idanti ayamattho dīpito hotīti yojanā. Etthāti “atha kho bhagavā”tiādipāṭhe.

4. In 'The Blessed One did not,' the negative particle na is to be connected with the word upasaṅkami (approached); for the meaning is 'he did not approach.' 'From that concentration' means from that concentration which is the attainment of the fruit of arahantship. Immediately revealing the non-approaching by way of a simile, he says, 'Just as,' etc. 'It is not said thus' is the construction. 'This' means this collection of meanings. 'Herein' means in the sentence 'having eaten, he sleeps.' 'Thus' is an indicator of the object of comparison. 'Here too' means also in this passage beginning 'Then the Blessed One…' 'This' means this meaning is illuminated; this is the construction. 'Herein' means in the text beginning 'Then the Blessed One…'

Aparānipīti pallaṅkasattāhato aññānipi. Tatrāti “aparānipī”tiādivacane. Bhagavati nisinne satīti yojanā. Kirasaddo vitthārajotako[M 0.0192]. Kiṃ nu khoti parivitakkanatthe nipāto. Ekaccānanti appesakkhānaṃ ekaccānaṃ. Tāsanti devatānaṃ. Balādhigamaṭṭhānanti balena tejasā adhigamaṭṭhānaṃ. Animisehīti ummisehi. Sattāhanti kammatthe cetaṃ upayogavacanaṃ, accantasaṃyoge vā. Evañhi sati “kāla”nti kammaṃ veditabbaṃ. Taṃ ṭhānanti animisehi akkhīhi olokiyamānaṭṭhānaṃ. Athāti animisasattāhassa anantare. Ratanacaṅkameti ratanamaye caṅkame. Taṃ ṭhānanti caṅkamaṭṭhānaṃ. Tatoti caṅkamasattāhato. Ratanagharanti ratanamayaṃ gehaṃ. Tatthāti ratanaghare abhidhammapiṭakaṃ vicinantoti sambandho. Etthāti ratanaghare, abhidhammapiṭake vā, niddhāraṇe cetaṃ bhummavacanaṃ. Taṃ ṭhānanti abhidhammapiṭakavicinanaṭṭhānaṃ.

'And other [weeks]' means other than the seven days of sitting cross-legged. 'There' means in the phrase 'and other,' etc. It is to be construed as 'when the Blessed One was seated.' The word kira is an illuminator of detail. Kiṃ nu kho is a particle used in the sense of deliberation. 'Of some' means of some of the less influential ones. 'Of them' means of the devas. 'The place of attainment by power' means the place of attainment by power and majesty. 'With unblinking [eyes]' means without blinking. 'For seven days': this is an accusative expression in the sense of the object, or in the sense of continuous duration. For if so, 'time' should be understood as the object. 'That place' means the place that was gazed upon with unblinking eyes. 'Then' means after the seven days of unblinking gaze. 'On the Jeweled Promenade' means on the promenade made of jewels. 'That place' means the place of the promenade. 'From there' means from the seven days of promenading. 'The Jeweled House' means the house made of jewels. 'There' is connected with 'while he was scrutinizing the Abhidhamma Piṭaka in the Jeweled House.' 'Herein' means in the Jeweled House, or in the Abhidhamma Piṭaka; this is a locative expression used for specification. 'That place' means the place where he scrutinized the Abhidhamma Piṭaka.

Evantiādi pubbavacanassa nigamavasena pacchimavacanassa anusandhinidassanaṃ. Tenāti ajapālānaṃ [V 1.0170] nisīdanakāraṇena. Assāti nigrodhassa. “Ajapālanigrodhotveva nāma”nti iminā upacāravasena nāmalabhanaṃ dasseti. Ajapā brāhmaṇā lanti nivāsaṃ gaṇhanti etthāti ajapālo, uṇhakāle vā antopaviṭṭhe aje attano chāyāya pāletīti ajapālo, ajapālo ca so nigrodho ceti ajapālanigrodhoti vacanatthānipi pakaraṇantaresu (udā. aṭṭha. 4) dassitāni. Tatrāpīti ajapālanigrodhepi. Bodhitoti bodhirukkhato. Etthāti ajapālanigrodhe. Bhagavati nisinneti yojanā. Tatthāti “atha kho aññataro”tiādivacane. Soti brāhmaṇo. Diṭṭhamaṅgaliko nāmāti diṭṭhasutamutasaṅkhātesu tīsu maṅgalikesu diṭṭhamaṅgaliko nāma kirāti attho. “Mānavasena…pe… vuccatī”ti iminā “huṃhu”nti karotīti huṃhuṅko, huṃhuṅko jāti sabhāvo imassāti huṃhuṅkajātikoti vacanatthaṃ dasseti.

'Thus,' etc., shows the connection of the latter statement by way of concluding the former. 'By that' means for the reason that goatherds sat there. 'Of it' means of the banyan tree. By 'named the Goatherd's Banyan,' it shows the acquisition of the name by figurative usage. Goatherds (ajapālā) take up residence (nivāsaṃ gaṇhanti) there (ettha), hence ajapālo; or, in the hot season, it protects (pāleti) the goats (aje) that have entered within by its shade, hence ajapālo. That which is both a goatherd's [tree] and a banyan tree is the Goatherd's Banyan (ajapālanigrodho). The meanings of the word have also been shown in other sections (Ud-a. 4). 'There too' means at the Goatherd's Banyan too. 'From the Bodhi' means from the Bodhi tree. 'Here' means at the Goatherd's Banyan. It is to be construed as 'when the Blessed One was seated.' 'There' means in the phrase 'Then a certain...' 'He' means the brahmin. 'Named one who relies on auspicious signs by sight': the meaning is that among the three kinds of those who rely on auspicious signs—by sight, by hearing, and by thought—he, it seems, was one who relies on auspicious signs by sight. By 'because of conceit… he is called,' it shows the word-meaning: he makes the sound 'humph, humph,' thus he is a 'humph-humpher' (huṃhuṅko); one whose nature is to be a 'humph-humpher' is 'of the humph-humphing kind' (huṃhuṅkajātiko).

Tenāti brāhmaṇena. Sikhāppattanti aggappattaṃ. Tassāti udānassa. Yoti puggalo, paṭijānātīti sambandho. “Na diṭṭhamaṅgalikatāyā”ti iminā avadhāraṇaphalaṃ dasseti. “Bāhitapāpadhammattā”ti iminā bāhito [M 0.0193] pāpo dhammo anenāti bāhitapāpadhammoti vacanatthaṃ dasseti. “Huṃhuṅkārapahānenā”ti iminā natthi huṃhuṅkāro imassāti nihuṃhuṅkoti vacanatthaṃ dasseti. Rāgādikasāvābhāvenāti iminā natthi rāgādikasāvo imassāti nikkasāvoti vacanatthaṃ dasseti. “Bhāvanānuyogayuttacittatāyā”ti iminā yataṃ anuyuttaṃ attaṃ cittaṃ imassāti yatattoti vacanatthaṃ dasseti. Ettha hi yatasaddo vīriyavācako, yatadhātuyā nipphanno, attasaddo cittapariyāyo. Yatasaddassa yamudhātuyā ca nipphannabhāvaṃ dassetuṃ vuttaṃ “sīlasaṃvarena vā”tiādi. “Saññatacittatāyā”ti iminā yamati saṃyamatīti yataṃ, yataṃ attaṃ cittaṃ imassāti yatattoti vacanatthaṃ dasseti. Saccāni vidanti jānantīti vedānīti vacanatthena maggañāṇāni vedāni nāmāti dassento āha “catumaggañāṇasaṅkhātehi vedehī”ti. “Catumaggañāṇasaṅkhātāna”nti vibhattipariṇāmaṃ katvā “vedāna”ntipadena yojetabbo. Antanti nibbānaṃ. Tañhi yasmā saṅkhārānaṃ avasāne jātaṃ, tasmā antanti vuccati. Puna antanti arahattaphalaṃ. Tañhi yasmā maggassa pariyosāne pavattaṃ, tasmā antanti vuccati. “Maggabrahmacariyassa vusitattā”ti iminā vusitaṃ maggasaṅkhātaṃ brahmacariyaṃ anenāti vusitabrahmacariyoti vacanatthaṃ dasseti. Dhammena brahmavādaṃ vadeyyāti vuttavacanassa atthaṃ dassento āha “brāhmaṇo ahanti etaṃ vādaṃ dhammena vadeyyā”ti. Dhammenāti bhūtena sabhāvena. Loketi ettha sattalokovādhippetoti āha “sakale lokasannivāse”ti.

'By him' means by the brahmin. 'Having reached the peak' means having reached the summit. 'Of that' means of the inspired utterance. 'Whoever' means the person; it is connected with 'claims.' By 'not because of relying on auspicious signs by sight,' it shows the result of the specification. By 'because he has dispelled evil states,' it shows the word-meaning: evil states have been dispelled by him, thus he is one who has 'dispelled evil states' (bāhitapāpadhammo). By 'through the abandoning of humph-humphing,' it shows the word-meaning: he has no humph-humphing, thus he is 'free from humph-humphing' (nihuṃhuṅko). By 'because of the absence of taints such as lust,' it shows the word-meaning: he has no taints such as lust, thus he is 'taintless' (nikkasāvo). By 'because his mind is yoked to the practice of development,' it shows the word-meaning: his self (atta), his mind (citta), is restrained (yata) and dedicated (anuyutta), thus he is 'of restrained self' (yatatto). Here the word yata signifies energy, being derived from the root yat; the word atta is a synonym for mind. To show that the word yata is also derived from the root yam, it is said, 'or by restraint in virtue,' etc. By 'because his mind is restrained,' it shows the word-meaning: he restrains, he controls, thus 'restrained' (yata); his self (atta), his mind (citta), is restrained, thus he is 'of restrained self' (yatatto). Showing that by the word-meaning 'they know (vidanti) the truths (saccāni), thus they are knowledges (vedāni),' the path-knowledges are called 'knowledges' (vedāni), he says, 'by the knowledges comprised in the four path-knowledges.' 'Of those comprised in the four path-knowledges' is to be connected with the word 'of the knowledges' by changing the case ending. 'The end' means Nibbāna. For since it arises at the cessation of formations, it is called 'the end.' Again, 'the end' means the fruit of arahantship. For since it occurs at the culmination of the path, it is called 'the end.' By 'because the holy life of the path has been lived,' it shows the word-meaning: the holy life comprised in the path has been lived by him, thus he is one who has 'lived the holy life' (vusitabrahmacariyo). Showing the meaning of the statement 'he might rightly make the claim of a brahmin,' he says, 'he might rightly make this claim: "I am a brahmin."' 'Rightly' means truthfully, in accordance with reality. In 'in the world,' here the world of beings is intended, thus he says, 'in the entire world-system.'

3. Mucalindakathā

3. The Story of Mucalinda

5. Akālameghoti [V 1.0171] ettha vappādikālassa abhāvā na akālo hoti, atha kho vassakāle asampattattā akāloti āha “asampatte vassakāle”ti. “Uppannamegho”ti iminā akāle uppanno megho akālameghoti vacanatthaṃ dasseti. Gimhānaṃ pacchime māseti jeṭṭhamūlamāse. Tasminti meghe. Sītavātaduddinīti ettha sītena vātena dūsitaṃ dinaṃ imissā vaṭṭalikāyāti sītavātaduddinīti vacanatthaṃ [M 0.0194] dassento āha “sā ca panā”tiādi. Sā ca pana sattāhavaṭṭalikā sītavātaduddinī nāma ahosīti sambandho. “Samīpe pokkharaṇiyā nibbatto”ti iminā mucalindassa samīpe nibbatto mucalindoti vacanatthaṃ dasseti. Mucalindoti ca niculo. So nīpoti ca piyakoti ca vuccati. Nāgassa bhogo ekopi sattābhujattā “bhogehī”ti bahuvacanavasena vuttaṃ. Tasminti nāgarāje ṭhite satīti yojanā. Tassāti nāgarājassa. Tasmāti yasmā bhaṇḍāgāragabbhapamāṇaṃ ahosi, tasmā. Ṭhānassa kāraṇaṃ paridīpeti anenāti ṭhānakāraṇaparidīpanaṃ “mā bhagavantaṃ sīta”ntiādivacanaṃ. Soti nāgarājā. Hīti saccaṃ. Pāḷiyaṃ “bādhayitthā”ti kiriyāpadaṃ ajjhāharitabbanti āha “mā sītaṃ bhagavantaṃ bādhayitthā”ti. Tatthāti “mā bhagavantaṃ sīta”ntiādivacane. Sattāhavaṭṭalikāya satīti sambandho. Tampīti uṇhampi. Nanti bhagavantaṃ. Tassāti nāgarājassa. Ubbiddhanti uddhaṃ chiddaṃ. Viddhachiddasaddā hi pariyāyā. Ākāsaṃ meghapaṭalapaṭicchannaṃ āsannaṃ viya hoti, meghapaṭalavigame dūraṃ viya upaṭṭhāti, tasmā vuttaṃ “meghavigamena dūrībhūta”nti. Vigatavalāhakanti ettha vigatasaddo apagatatthavācako, valāhakasaddo meghapariyāyoti āha “apagatamegha”nti. Indanīlamaṇi viya dibbatīti devoti vacanatthena ākāso devo nāmāti āha “devanti ākāsa”nti. Attano rūpanti attano nāgasaṇṭhānaṃ. Iminā sakavaṇṇanti ettha sakasaddo attavācako, vaṇṇasaddo saṇṭhānavevacanoti dasseti.

5. Herein, an unseasonal cloud (akālamegho): it is not called 'unseasonal' (akālo) due to the absence of the sowing season, but because the proper rainy season had not yet arrived, it is called 'unseasonal,' as stated in the phrase 'when the rainy season had not arrived.' By this, it shows the word-meaning of akālamegho as 'a cloud that has arisen out of season' (akāle uppanno megho). 'In the last month of the hot season' means the month of Jeṭṭhamūla. 'In that' means in that cloud. Herein, a cold, windy, cloudy day (sītavātaduddinī): showing the word-meaning of sītavātaduddinī as 'a day spoiled by a cold wind for this rain-cloud,' he says: 'And that...,' etc. The connection is: and that seven-day rain-cloud was called a 'cold, windy, cloudy day.' By 'born near the pond' (samīpe pokkharaṇiyā nibbatto), he shows the meaning of Mucalinda as 'born near the Mucalinda.' And Mucalinda is the Nicula tree; it is also called Nīpa or Piyaka. Though the nāga's coil is single, because it has seven bends, it is spoken of in the plural as 'with his coils' (bhogehī). The construction is: 'when that nāga king was standing there.' 'Of that' means of that nāga king. 'Therefore' means because it was the size of a treasure chamber, therefore. The clarification of the reason for his standing is the statement: 'Let not the Blessed One be cold,' etc. 'He' means that nāga king. 'Indeed' means truly. In the Pāḷi, the verb 'should afflict' (bādhayitthā) should be supplied, thus: 'Let not cold afflict the Blessed One.' Therein: in the statement 'Let not the Blessed One be cold,' etc. The connection is: 'when there was a seven-day rain-cloud.' 'That too' means the heat too. 'Him' means the Blessed One. 'Of that' means of that nāga king. 'Opened up' (ubbiddhaṃ) means an opening above. The words viddha and chidda are synonyms. The sky, covered by a layer of clouds, seems near; when the layer of clouds disperses, it appears far away. Therefore it is said: 'become distant with the departure of the clouds.' Herein, 'with the clouds dispersed' (vigatavalāhakaṃ): the word vigata means 'departed,' and the word valāhaka is a synonym for 'cloud'; thus he says: 'with clouds departed.' Because it shines like a sapphire (indanīlamaṇi viya dibbati), the sky is called 'deva' by the word-meaning; thus he says: 'deva means the sky.' 'His own form' means his own nāga-form. By this, he shows that in the word sakavaṇṇaṃ ('his own form'), the word saka means 'own' and the word vaṇṇa is a synonym for 'form'.

Sukho vivekoti ettha tadaṅga vikkhambhana samuccheda paṭippassaddhinissaraṇavivekasaṅkhātesu pañcasu vivekesu nibbānasaṅkhāto nissaraṇaviveko ca kāyacittaupadhivivekasaṅkhātesu tīsu vivekesu nibbānasaṅkhāto upadhiviveko ca gahetabboti āha “nibbānasaṅkhāto upadhiviveko”ti. “Catumaggañāṇasantosenā”ti iminā tuṭṭhassāti ettha piṇḍapātasantosādike nivatteti. Sutadhammassāti ettha sutasaddo vissutapariyāyoti āha “pakāsitadhammassā”ti, pākaṭasaccadhammassāti attho. Passatoti ettha maṃsacakkhussa karaṇabhāvena [M 0.0195][V 1.0172] āsaṅkā bhaveyyāti āha “ñāṇacakkhunā”ti. “Akuppanabhāvo”ti iminā abyāpajjanti ettha byāpādasaddassa dosavācakabhāvo ca ṇyapaccayassa bhāvattho ca dassito. Etenāti “abyāpajja”ntipadena. Mettāpubbabhāgoti abyāpajjassa pubbabhāge mettāya uppannabhāvo. Pāṇabhūtesu saṃyamoti ettha pāṇabhūtasaddā vevacanabhāvena sattesu eva vattantīti āha “sattesu cā”ti. Karuṇāpubbabhāgoti saṃyamassa pubbabhāge karuṇāya uppannabhāvo. Yāti yā virāgatā. Anāgāmimaggassa kāmarāgassa anavasesapahānattā vuttaṃ “etena anāgāmimaggo kathito”ti. Yāthāvamānassa arahattamaggena niruddhattā vuttaṃ “asmi…pe… kathita”nti. Itoti arahattato.

Seclusion is happiness: Herein, among the five kinds of seclusion—seclusion by substitution, by suppression, by cutting off, by tranquillization, and by escape—it is seclusion by escape, designated as Nibbāna, that should be taken. And among the three kinds of seclusion—seclusion of body, of mind, and from the substrates—it is seclusion from the substrates, designated as Nibbāna, that should be taken. Thus he says: 'seclusion from the substrates, which is designated as Nibbāna.' By 'content with the knowledge of the four paths,' he excludes contentment with almsfood and the like for one who is content. Of one who has heard the Dhamma: here the word 'heard' is a synonym for 'renowned'; thus he says: 'of one to whom the Dhamma has been made manifest,' that is, one to whom the true Dhamma is evident. Of one who sees: here, lest one should assume the physical eye is the instrument, he says: 'with the eye of wisdom.' By 'the state of being imperturbable,' he shows that in the word non-malevolence (abyāpajjaṃ), the word 'malevolence' (byāpāda) signifies aversion, and the suffix -jja has the sense of 'state.' By this: by the word 'non-malevolence.' Having loving-kindness as its prior part: the state of non-malevolence arises having been preceded by loving-kindness. Restraint towards living beings: here the words 'living beings' (pāṇabhūta) are synonyms for 'beings' (satta); thus he says: 'and towards beings.' Having compassion as its prior part: the state of restraint arises having been preceded by compassion. That: that which is dispassion. Because the path of the non-returner completely abandons sensual lust, it is said: 'by this the path of the non-returner is stated.' Because the conceit 'I am' is eradicated by the path of arahantship, it is said: 'conceit ... is stated.' From this: from arahantship.

4. Rājāyatanakathā

4. The Discourse on the Rājāyatana Tree

6. Pācīnakoṇeti puratthimaasse, pubbadakkhiṇadisābhāgeti attho. Rājāyatanarukkhanti khīrikārukkhaṃ. Tena kho pana samayenāti ettha tasaddassa visayaṃ pucchitvā dassento āha “katarena samayenā”ti. Nisinnassa bhagavatoti yojanā. Devarājasaddassa aññe pajāpatiādayo devarājāno nivattetuṃ “sakko”ti vuttaṃ. Tanti harītakaṃ. Paribhuttamattasseva bhagavatoti sambandho. Nisinne bhagavati.

6. In the eastern corner: in its eastern part, meaning in the southeastern quarter. The Rājāyatana tree: the Khīrikā tree. Now at that time: here, showing the scope of the word 'that' by asking, 'At what time?' The construction is: 'of the Blessed One who was seated.' In order to exclude other kings of the devas such as Pajāpati, 'Sakka' is said in connection with the word 'king of the devas.' That: the myrobalan fruit. The connection is: 'as soon as the Blessed One had consumed it.' When the Blessed One was seated.

“Tena kho pana samayenā”ti iminā yena samayena bhagavā rājāyatanamūle nisīdi, tena kho pana samayenāti atthaṃ dasseti. Ukkalajanapadatoti ukkalanāmakā janapadamhā. Yasmiṃ dese bhagavā viharati, taṃ desanti yojanā. Etthāti “taṃ desaṃ addhānamaggappaṭipannā”tipade. Tesanti vāṇijānaṃ. Ñātisālohitasaddānaṃ aññamaññavevacanattā “ñātī”ti vutte sālohitasaddassa attho siddhoti dassetuṃ vuttaṃ “ñātibhūtapubbā devatā”ti. Sāti devatā. Nesanti vāṇijānaṃ. Tatoti apavattanakāraṇā. Teti vāṇijā[M 0.0196]. Idanti apavattanaṃ. Balinti upahāraṃ. Tesanti vāṇijānaṃ. “Sabbimadhuphāṇitādīhi yojetvā”ti padaṃ pubbāparāpekkhaṃ, tasmā majjhe vuttaṃ. Patimānethāti ettha māna pūjāyaṃ pemaneti dhātupāṭhesu (saddanītidhātumālāyaṃ 18 nakārantadhātu) vuttattā pūjanapemanaṃ nāma atthato upaṭṭhahananti āha “upaṭṭhahathā”ti. Taṃ voti ettha taṃsaddo patimānanavisayo, vosaddo tīsu vosaddesu tumhasaddassa kāriyo vosaddo, so ca catutthyatthoti āha “taṃ patimānaṃ tumhāka”nti. Vokāro hi tividho tumhasaddassa kāriyo, yovacanassa kāriyo, padapūraṇoti. Tattha tumhasaddassa kāriyo pañcavidho paccattaupayogakaraṇasampadānasāmivacanavasenāti. Tattha tumhasaddakāriyo sampadānavacano [V 1.0173] idhādhippeto. Tenāha “tumhāka”nti. “Ya”ntisaddassa visayo paṭiggahaṇatthoti āha “yaṃ paṭiggahaṇa”nti. Assāti bhaveyya. Yo patto ahosīti yojanā. Assāti bhagavato. Soti patto. Sujātāya āgacchantiyā evāti sambandho. Anādare cetaṃ sāmivacanaṃ. Tenāti antaradhāyahetunā. Assāti bhagavato. Hatthesūti karaṇatthe cetaṃ bhummavacanaṃ. Hatthehīti hi attho. Kimhīti kena.

By 'Now at that time,' he shows the meaning: 'at the time when the Blessed One sat at the foot of the Rājāyatana tree, at that time.' From the country of Ukkala: from the country named Ukkala. The construction is: 'to that country where the Blessed One was dwelling.' Herein: in the phrase 'traveling along the long road to that country.' Of them: of the merchants. Because the words 'relative' and 'kinsman' are synonyms, he says 'a devatā who had formerly been a relative' to show that when 'relative' is said, the meaning of 'kinsman' is established. She: the devatā. To them: to the merchants. From that: from the cause of the turning back. They: the merchants. This: the turning back. An offering: a gift. Of them: of the merchants. The phrase 'having mixed it with all kinds of honey, molasses, etc.' is dependent on what precedes and follows, therefore it is stated in the middle. You should honor: here, since it is said in the Dhātupāṭha that the root māna is in the sense of 'to worship' and 'to love,' worship and love in meaning are 'to attend upon'; thus he says: 'you should attend upon.' That for you: here the word 'taṃ' refers to the honoring; the word 'vo' is a substitute for the pronoun 'tumha,' and it is in the dative sense; thus he says: 'that honoring for you.' For the particle 'vo' is of three kinds: a substitute for the pronoun 'tumha,' a substitute for the pronoun 'yo,' or a word-filler. Among these, the substitute for 'tumha' is of five kinds, in the sense of agent, object, instrument, dative, and genitive. Here, the substitute for 'tumha' in the dative sense is intended. Therefore he says: 'for you.' The word 'what' has the meaning 'receiving' as its scope; thus he says: 'what is the receiving.' It would be: it might be. The construction is: 'which was the bowl.' His: the Blessed One's. It: the bowl. The connection is: 'just as it came from Sujātā.' And this is a genitive of disregard. By that: by the cause of its disappearance. His: the Blessed One's. In the hands: this is a locative in the sense of the instrumental, for the meaning is 'with the hands.' In what?: by what?

Itoti āsaḷhīmāsajuṇhapakkhapañcamito. Ettakaṃ kālanti etaṃ pamāṇaṃ ekūnapaññāsadivasakālaṃ. Jighacchāti ghasitumicchā. Pipāsāti pātumicchā. Assāti bhagavato. Cetasā-cetosaddānaṃ sambandhāpekkhattā tesaṃ sambandhaṃ dassetuṃ vuttaṃ “attano”ti ca “bhagavato”ti ca. Imehi sambandhisaddānamasadisattā sambandhopi asadisoti dasseti. Attanoti catunnaṃ mahārājānaṃ. Samāsoyeva avayavīpadhāno hoti, vākyaṃ pana avayavapadhānoyevāti dassento āha “catūhi disāhī”ti. Pāḷiyaṃ “āgantvā”ti pāṭhaseso yojetabbo. “Silāmaye”ti iminā silāmayameva selāmayanti atthaṃ dasseti. Idanti “selāmaye patte”ti vacanaṃ. Yeti muggavaṇṇasilāmaye patte. Tatoti indanīlamaṇimayapattaupanāmanato, paranti sambandho. Tesanti catunnaṃ mahārājānaṃ. Cattāropi adhiṭṭhahīti sambandho[M 0.0197]. Yathāti yenākārena, adhiṭṭhiyamāneti yojanā. Ekasadisoti ekaṃsena sadiso. Adhiṭṭhite patteti sambandho. Patteti ca karaṇatthe bhummavacanaṃ. Pattena paṭiggahesīti hi attho. Paccaggheti ettha ekāro smiṃvacanassa kāriyoti āha “paccagghasmi”nti. Paṭi agghanti padavibhāgaṃ katvā paṭisaddo pāṭekkattho, “aggha”nti sāmaññato vuttepi mahagghatthoti dassento āha “pāṭekkaṃ mahagghasmi”nti. Iminā cattāro ekato hutvā na mahagghā honti, pāṭekkaṃ pana mahagghā hontīti dasseti. Atha vā saupasaggo paccagghasaddo abhinavapariyāyoti āha “abhinave”ti. Abhinavoti ca aciratanavatthussa nāmaṃ. Aciratanavatthu aciratanattā abbhuṇhaṃ viya hoti, tasmā vuttaṃ “abbhuṇhe”ti. “Taṅkhaṇe nibbattasmi”nti iminā tamevatthaṃ vibhāveti. Dvevācikātipadassa samāsavasena ca taddhitavasena ca nipphannabhāvaṃ dassento āha “dve vācā”tiādi. Pattāti ettha eko itisaddo luttaniddiṭṭho. Iti tasmā dvevācikāiti atthoti yojanā. Teti vāṇijā. Athāti tasmiṃ kāle. Teti kese. Tesanti vāṇijānaṃ. Pariharathāti attano abhivādanapaccuṭṭhānaṭṭhānanti paṭiggahetvā, paricchinditvā vā harathāti attho. Teti vāṇijā. Amatenevāti amatena iva, abhisittā ivāti yojanā.

From this point (ito) means from the fifth day of the bright fortnight of the month of Āsāḷhī. This much time (ettakaṃ kālaṃ) means a period of forty-nine days. Hunger (jighacchā) means the desire to eat. Thirst (pipāsā) means the desire to drink. His (assā) means the Blessed One's. Because a connection between the words 'cetasā' and 'ceto' is expected, 'his own' (attano) and 'the Blessed One's' (bhagavato) are stated to show their connection. This shows that because these connecting words are dissimilar, the connection too is dissimilar. 'His own' (attano) means of the four great kings. Showing that a compound has the whole as its principal element, while a sentence has the parts as its principal element, he says 'from the four directions' (catūhi disāhi). In the Pāli text, 'having come' (āgantvā) should be supplied as the rest of the reading. By 'made of stone' (silāmaye), he shows that 'silāmaya' is the same as 'selāmaya.' 'This' (idaṃ) means the phrase 'the stone bowls' (selāmaye patte). 'Which' (ye) means the bowls made of stone the color of mung beans. 'From that' (tato) means after the offering of the bowl made of sapphire; 'after' (paraṃ) is the connection. 'Their' (tesaṃ) means of the four great kings. 'He resolved the four' (cattāropi adhiṭṭhahi) is the connection. 'As' (yathā) means in which manner; the connection is with 'being resolved' (adhiṭṭhiyamāne). 'Completely similar' (ekasadiso) means similar in every respect. The connection is with 'the resolved bowl' (adhiṭṭhite patte). And 'in the bowl' (patte) is the locative case in the sense of the instrumental, for the meaning is 'he received with the bowl' (pattena paṭiggahesi). Here in 'new' (paccagghe), the 'e' is a modification of the locative ending 'smiṃ'; thus he says 'in the new' (paccagghasmiṃ). Having divided the word into 'paṭi' and 'aggha,' the word 'paṭi' has the sense of 'each,' and although 'aggha' is stated generally, to show that it has the meaning 'of great value,' he says 'each of great value' (pāṭekkaṃ mahagghasmiṃ). By this he shows that the four together are not of great value, but each one separately is of great value. Alternatively, the word 'paccaggha' with its prefix is a synonym for 'new'; thus he says 'in the new' (abhinave). 'New' (abhinava) is a term for a thing not old. Because a thing not old is not old, it is as if fresh; therefore it is said 'in the fresh' (abbhuṇhe). By 'produced at that moment' (taṅkhaṇe nibbattasmiṃ), he clarifies this same meaning. Showing that the word 'dvevācikā' is formed both by way of a compound and by way of a derivative, he says 'two words' (dve vācā), etc. Here in 'attained' (pattā), one 'iti' is elided. The construction is: thus (iti), therefore (tasmā), they are called 'of two words' (dvevācikā); this is the meaning. 'They' (te) means the merchants. 'Then' (atha) means at that time. 'Those' (te) means the hairs. 'Their' (tesaṃ) means of the merchants. 'Keep them' (pariharatha) means: having accepted them as a place for your own veneration and attendance, or having defined it as such, carry them. This is the meaning. 'They' (te) means the merchants. 'As if with the deathless' (amateneva) is construed as 'as if with the deathless, as if sprinkled'.

5. Brahmayācanakathā

5. The Discourse on Brahmā's Request

7. Bhagavā [V 1.0174] upasaṅkamīti sambandho. Tasminti ajapālanigrodhe. Āciṇṇasamāciṇṇoti ācarito sammācarito, na ekassa buddhassa āciṇṇo, atha kho sabbabuddhānaṃ āciṇṇasamāciṇṇo, atiāciṇṇo niccāciṇṇoti attho. Saṅkhepena vuttamatthaṃ vitthārento āha “jānanti hī”tiādi. Dhammadesananti bhagavato dhammadesanaṃ, dhammadesanatthāya vā bhagavantaṃ, bhagavantaṃ vā dhammadesanaṃ. Tatoti yācanakāraṇā. Hīti saccaṃ, yasmā vā. Lokasannivāso brahmagaruko yasmā, iti tasmā uppādessantīti yojanā. Itītiādi nigamanaṃ.

7. 'The Blessed One approached' is the connection. 'Therein' (tasmiṃ) means at the Goatherd's Banyan Tree. 'Frequented and well-frequented' (āciṇṇasamāciṇṇo) means visited, well-visited; not frequented by one Buddha alone, but frequented and well-frequented by all Buddhas, meaning exceedingly frequented, constantly frequented. Elaborating on the meaning stated in brief, he says 'for they know' (jānanti hi), etc. 'The teaching of the Dhamma' (dhammadesanaṃ) means the Blessed One's teaching of the Dhamma; or approaching the Blessed One for the sake of the teaching of the Dhamma; or hearing from the Blessed One the teaching of the Dhamma. 'From that' (tato) means because of the request. 'Indeed' (hi) means truly, or because. The construction is: because (yasmā) the world-assembly holds Brahmā in high esteem, therefore (tasmā) 'they will generate' (uppādessanti). 'Thus,' etc., is the conclusion.

Tatthāti [M 0.0198] parivitakkanākārapāṭhe. “Pañcakāmaguṇesu allīya”ntīti iminā allīyanti abhiramitabbaṭṭhena lagganti etthāti ālayā pañca kāmaguṇāti vacanatthaṃ dasseti. Allīyantīti lagganti. “Pañca kāmaguṇe allīyantī”tipi pāṭho, evaṃ sati allīyanti abhiramitabbaṭṭhena seviyantīti ālayā pañca kāmaguṇāti vacanattho kātabbo. Allīyantīti sevanti. Teti pañca kāmaguṇā. “Yadida”ntipadassa yaṃ idanti padavibhāgaṃ katvā “ya”nti ca “ida”nti ca sabbanāmapadanti āsaṅkā bhaveyyāti āha “yadidanti nipāto”ti. Iminā tīsu liṅgesu dvīsu ca vacanesu vināsaṃ, vikāraṃ vā visadisaṃ vā naayanattā nagamanattā abyayaṃ nāmāti dasseti, attho pana sabbanāmatthoyevāti daṭṭhabbaṃ. Tassāti “yadida”ntinipātassa, atthoti sambandho. Ṭhānanti “ṭhānaṃ”itipadaṃ. Paṭiccasamuppādanti “paṭiccasamuppādo”itipadaṃ. Atthopi yuttoyevāti daṭṭhabbaṃ. Imesanti saṅkhārādīnaṃ paccayuppannānaṃ. Paccayāti avijjādikāraṇā. “Idappaccayā evā”ti iminā idappaccayatāti ettha tāpaccayassa svatthaṃ dīpeti “devatā”tiādīsu (khu. pā. aṭṭha. evamiccādipāṭhavaṇṇanā) viya.

'Therein' (tattha) means in the passage on the mode of reflection. By 'indulging in the five strands of sensual pleasure' (pañcakāmaguṇesu allīya), he shows the etymological meaning that the five strands of sensual pleasure are 'abodes' (ālayā) because one clings (allīyanti) to them, that is, one gets stuck (lagganti) in them in the sense of taking delight. 'Indulging' (allīyanti) means getting stuck. There is also the reading 'they indulge in the five strands of sensual pleasure' (pañca kāmaguṇe allīyanti). In this case, the etymological meaning should be made that the five strands of sensual pleasure are 'abodes' (ālayā) because they are indulged in (allīyanti), that is, they are frequented (seviyanti) in the sense of taking delight. 'Indulging' (allīyanti) means frequenting. 'They' (te) means the five strands of sensual pleasure. Since the doubt might arise that, by dividing the word 'yadidaṃ' into 'yaṃ' and 'idaṃ,' both 'yaṃ' and 'idaṃ' are pronouns, he says: ''Yadidaṃ' is a particle.' By this he shows that because it does not undergo destruction, alteration, or dissimilarity in the three genders and two numbers—because it does not change—it is called an indeclinable (abyayaṃ). However, its meaning should be understood as simply that of a pronoun. 'Its' (tassa) means of the particle 'yadidaṃ'; 'meaning' is the connection. 'State' means the word 'state' (ṭhānaṃ). 'Dependent origination' means the word 'dependent origination' (paṭiccasamuppādo). The meaning too should be seen as fitting. 'Of these' (imesaṃ) means of the conditionally arisen things beginning with formations. 'As a condition' (paccayā) means because of causes such as ignorance. By 'because of this condition' (idappaccayā evā), he indicates that here in 'specific conditionality' (idappaccayatā), the suffix '-tā' has the sense of the word itself, as in 'deity' (devatā), etc.

So mamassa kilamathoti ettha taṃsaddassa visayaṃ dassento āha “yā ajānantānaṃ desanā nāmā”ti, iminā “deseyyaṃ, na ājāneyyu”nti dvinnameva kiriyāpadānaṃ tasaddassa visayabhāvaṃ dasseti, na ekassa kiriyāpadassa. Soti desanāsaṅkhāto kāyavacīpayogo, iminā vākyavisaye tasaddo uttarapadasseva liṅgavacanāni gaṇhātīti dasseti, samāsamajjhe pana tasaddo pubbapadasseva liṅgavacanāni gaṇhāti. Tena vuttaṃ “avijjā ca sā paccayo cā”ti (udā. aṭṭha. paṭhamabodhisuttavaṇṇanā) ca “abhidhammo ca so piṭakañcā”ti ca (pārā. aṭṭha. 1.paṭhamamahāsaṅgītikathā; dha. sa. aṭṭha. nidānakathā) ādi[V 1.0175]. Kilamathoti kāyakilamanahetu. Kilamati anenāti kilamatho. Assāti bhaveyya. Sāti kāyavacīpayogasaṅkhātā desanā. Vihesāti kāyavihiṃsāhetu. Vihiṃsati imāyāti vihesā. Cittena pana buddhānaṃ kilamatho vā vihesā vā natthi arahattamaggena samucchinnattā[M 0.0199]. “Paṭibhaṃsū”ti ettha paṭīti kammappavacanīyayogattā “bhagavanta”nti ettha sāmyatthe upayogavacananti āha “bhagavato”ti. “Anu acchariyā”ti iminā “na acchariyā”ti padavibhāgaṃ nivatteti, punappunaṃ acchariyāti attho. Paṭibhaṃsūti ettha paṭisaddo paṭibhānattho, bhādhātu khāyanatthoti āha “paṭibhānasaṅkhātassa ñāṇassa gocarā ahesu”nti. “Gocarā ahesu”nti iminā khāyanaṃ nāma atthato gocarabhāvena bhavananti dasseti.

Here in 'that would be weariness for me' (so mamassa kilamatho), showing the scope of the pronoun 'taṃ', he says 'that which is called the teaching for those who do not know.' By this he shows that the pronoun 'taṃ' refers to the two verbal actions 'I might teach, and they might not understand,' not to a single verbal action. 'That' (so) means the bodily and verbal effort designated as teaching. By this he shows that in the context of a sentence, the pronoun 'taṃ' takes the gender and number of the following word, but in the middle of a compound, it takes the gender and number of the preceding word. Thus it is said: 'that ignorance which is a condition' (avijjā ca sā paccayo cā) and 'that Abhidhamma which is a Piṭaka' (abhidhammo ca so piṭakañcā), etc. 'Weariness' (kilamatho) means a cause of bodily fatigue. That by which one becomes fatigued is weariness. 'Would be' (assa) means 'would be' (bhaveyya). 'That' (sā) means the teaching designated as bodily and verbal effort. 'Vexation' (vihesā) means a cause of bodily harm. That by which one is harmed is vexation. But for the Buddhas there is no mental weariness or vexation, as it has been cut off by the path of arahantship. Here in 'occurred to' (paṭibhaṃsū), since 'paṭi' is used as a prepositional adverb, here in 'the Blessed One' (bhagavantaṃ), he says 'of the Blessed One' (bhagavato) using the genitive of relationship. By 'repeatedly wonderful' (anu acchariyā), he rejects the word-division 'not wonderful' (na acchariyā); the meaning is 'wonderful again and again.' Here in 'occurred to' (paṭibhaṃsū), the word 'paṭi' has the sense of inspiration, and the root 'bhā' has the sense of appearing; thus he says 'they became the domain of the knowledge designated as inspiration.' By 'they became the domain' (gocarā ahesuṃ), he shows that 'appearing' (khāyanaṃ) in essence means becoming a domain.

Meti mama, mayā vā, adhigataṃ dhammaṃ pakāsitunti sambandho. Ariyamaggasotassa paṭi paṭisotanti vutte nibbānamevāti āha “paṭisotaṃ vuccati nibbāna”nti. Nibbānagāminti ariyamaggaṃ. Ariyamaggo hi yasmā nibbānaṃ gamayati, tasmā nibbānagāmīti vuccati. Tamokhandhenāti ettha tamasaddo avijjāpariyāyo, khandhasaddo rāsatthoti āha “avijjārāsinā”ti. “Ajjhotthaṭā”ti iminā āvuṭāti ettha vudhātu āvaraṇatthoti dasseti. Appossukkatāyāti ettha apatyūpasaggo abhāvattho, tāpaccayo bhāvatthoti āha “nirussukkabhāvenā”ti.

'Me' (me) means 'my' (mama) or 'by me' (mayā); the connection is 'to proclaim the Dhamma attained by me.' When it is said 'against the stream' (paṭisotaṃ), that is, contrary (paṭi) to the stream of the noble path, it means Nibbāna itself; thus he says ''against the stream' is a term for Nibbāna.' 'Leading to Nibbāna' (nibbānagāmiṃ) means the noble path. For since the noble path leads to Nibbāna, it is called 'leading to Nibbāna.' Here in 'by the mass of darkness' (tamokhandhena), the word 'darkness' (tamo) is a synonym for ignorance, and the word 'mass' (khandha) has the sense of a heap; thus he says 'by the heap of ignorance' (avijjārāsinā). By 'overwhelmed' (ajjhotthaṭā), he shows that here in 'covered' (āvuṭā), the root 'vudh' has the sense of covering. Here in 'to lack of eagerness' (appossukkatāya), the prefix 'appa-' has the sense of absence, and the suffix '-tā' has the sense of state; thus he says 'through the state of being without eagerness' (nirussukkabhāvena).

8. Loketi sattaloke. Mahābrahmeti mahābrahmāno. Apparajakkhajātikāti ettha appaṃ rajaṃ akkhimhi etesanti apparajakkhā, apparajakkhā jāti sabhāvo etesanti apparajakkhajātikāti vacanatthaṃ dassento āha “paññāmaye”tiādi. “Paññāmaye”ti iminā maṃsamayeti atthaṃ nivatteti. Etesanti sattānaṃ. Dhammassāti tupaccayayoge chaṭṭhīkammaṃ. Āpubbo ñādhātu paṭivijjhanatthoti āha “paṭivijjhitāro”ti.

8. 'In the world' (loke) means in the world of beings. 'Mahābrahmā' means the Great Brahmās. Here, as to 'of a nature with little dust in their eyes' (apparajakkhajātikā), he shows the etymological meaning: 'those with little dust in their eyes' (apparajakkhā) are those for whom there is little dust in the eye; 'of a nature with little dust in their eyes' (apparajakkhajātikā) are those whose nature (jāti) or disposition (sabhāvo) is to have little dust in their eyes. To show this, he says 'in the wisdom eye' (paññāmaye), etc. By 'in the wisdom eye' (paññāmaye), he rejects the meaning 'in the physical eye' (maṃsamaye). 'Of those' (etesaṃ) means of beings. 'Of the Dhamma' (dhammassa) is the objective genitive in connection with the suffix '-tu'. The root 'ñā' with the prefix 'ā' has the sense of penetration; thus he says 'those who will penetrate' (paṭivijjhitāro).

Saṃvijjati malaṃ etesanti samalā, pūraṇakassapādikā cha satthāro, tehi. “Rāgādīhī”ti iminā malasarūpaṃ dasseti. Avāpuretanti ettha avapubbo ca āpubbo ca puradhātu vivaraṇatthoti āha “vivara eta”nti. Vakārassa pakāraṃ katvā “apāpureta”ntipi pāṭho[M 0.0200]. Amatasaddassa salilādayo nivattetuṃ vuttaṃ “nibbānassā”ti. Ime sattā suṇantūti sambandho. Vimalenāti ettha visaddo abhāvatthoti āha “abhāvato”ti. Iminā natthi malaṃ etassāti vimaloti vacanatthaṃ dasseti[V 1.0176]. “Sammāsambuddhenā”ti iminā aññapadatthasarūpaṃ dasseti. Anukkamena maggena bujjhitabbanti anubuddhanti vutte catusaccadhammo gahetabboti āha “catusaccadhamma”nti.

'Defilement exists in them,' thus they are samalā, 'the defiled ones': the six teachers beginning with Pūraṇa Kassapa; by them. By 'lust, etc.,' he shows the nature of defilement. Concerning 'avāpureta', here the prefix 'ava' and the prefix 'ā' with the root 'pur' have the meaning of opening; thus he says, 'open this' (vivara eta). By changing the letter 'v' to 'p', there is also the reading 'apāpureta'. To preclude 'the deathless' (amatassa) from referring to water and so on, it is said 'of Nibbāna' (nibbānassa). The connection is: 'May these beings listen.' Concerning 'vimalena', here the word 'vi' has the meaning of absence; thus he says, 'due to the absence' (abhāvato). By this he shows the etymological meaning: 'There is no defilement in him, thus he is vimala, stainless.' By 'by the Perfectly Self-Enlightened One' (sammāsambuddhena), he shows the nature of the meaning pertaining to the other word. When it is said 'anubuddhaṃ', meaning 'to be awakened by the gradual path,' the Dhamma of the Four Truths is to be understood; thus he says, 'the Dhamma of the Four Truths' (catusaccadhamma).

“Selamaye”ti iminā silāya nibbatto seloti vacanatthaṃ dasseti. “Sabbaññutaññāṇenā”ti iminā samantacakkhusarūpaṃ dasseti. Bhagavā tvampīti yojanā. Dhammasaddo paññāpariyāyoti āha “dhammamayaṃ paññāmaya”nti. Apeto soko imassāti apetasoko, bhagavā. Sokaṃ avataratīti sokāvatiṇṇā, janatā. Sokāvatiṇṇañca jātijarābhibhūtañcāti casaddo yojetabbo. Iminā casaddo luttaniddiṭṭhoti dasseti.

By 'selamaye', he shows the etymological meaning: 'sela' (made of rock) is what is produced from 'silā' (rock). By 'with the knowledge of omniscience' (sabbaññutaññāṇena), he shows the nature of the universal eye. The connection is: 'You too, Blessed One' (Bhagavā tvampi). The word 'dhamma' is a synonym for wisdom; thus he says, 'consisting of Dhamma, consisting of wisdom' (dhammamayaṃ paññāmayaṃ). 'Sorrow has departed from him,' thus he is apetasoko, 'one free from sorrow': the Blessed One. 'They descend into sorrow,' thus they are sokāvatiṇṇā, 'immersed in sorrow': the populace. The word 'ca' should be connected thus: 'and immersed in sorrow and overcome by birth and aging.' By this he shows that the word 'ca' is indicated as elided.

“Bhagavā”tipadaṃ “vīro”tiādīsu yojetabbaṃ. “Vīriyavantatāyā”ti iminā vīraṃ yassatthīti vīroti vacanatthaṃ dasseti. Saddasatthesu ālapanapadesu viggaho na kātabboti idaṃ ālapanāvatthaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ, idha pana tesamatthadassanatthāya viggaho vuttoti daṭṭhabbaṃ. “Devaputta…pe… vijitattā”ti iminā vijito mārehi saṃgāmo anenāti vijitasaṅgāmoti vacanatthaṃ dasseti. Ettha ca khandhamāro maccumārena saṅgahito dvinnaṃ mārānaṃ ekato vijitattā. “Sattavāho”ti paṭhamakkharena ca “satthavāho”ti dutiyakkharena ca yutto. Tattha satthavāho viyāti “satthavāho”ti upacārena vutte dutiyakkharena yutto, satte vahahīti sattavāhoti mukhyato vutte paṭhamakkharena yutto. Idha pana paṭhamakkharena yuttoti āha “satte vahatīti sattavāho”ti. Natthi iṇaṃ imassāti aṇaṇo bhagavā.

The term ‘Bhagavā’ should be connected with ‘vīro,’ etc. By ‘because of possessing energy,’ he shows the etymological meaning of vīro: ‘one who has energy (vīraṃ) is a hero (vīro).’ ‘In the treatises on words, analysis should not be done on vocative terms.’ This is said with reference to the vocative case, but it should be seen that here the analysis is stated in order to show the meaning of those terms. By ‘Devaputta… because of having conquered,’ he shows the etymological meaning of vijitasaṅgāmo: ‘one by whom the battle with the Māras has been won.’ And here, the Māra of the aggregates is included under the Māra of death, because the two Māras were conquered together. Sattavāho is connected with the first letter, and satthavāho with the second letter. There, when satthavāho is said metaphorically, as in ‘like a caravan leader,’ it is connected with the second letter. When sattavāho is said in a primary sense, as in ‘he leads beings,’ it is connected with the first letter. Here, however, it is connected with the first letter; thus he says: ‘he leads beings, therefore he is a sattavāho.’ ‘He has no debt,’ thus the Blessed One is aṇaṇo, ‘debtless.’

9. Buddhacakkhunāti [M 0.0201] ettha cakkhu duvidhaṃ maṃsacakkhuñāṇacakkhuvasena. Tatthāpi maṃsacakkhu duvidhaṃ pasādacakkhusasambhāracakkhuvasena. Tattha pasādarūpaṃ pasādacakkhu nāma, bhamukaṭṭhiparicchinno maṃsapiṇḍo sasambhāracakkhu nāma. Ñāṇacakkhu pana pañcavidhaṃ (paṭi. ma. aṭṭha. 1.1.3) dibbadhammapaññābuddhasamantacakkhuvasena. Tattha dibbacakkhuabhiññāñāṇaṃ dibbacakkhu nāma, heṭṭhimamaggattayaṃ dhammacakkhu nāma, arahattamaggañāṇaṃ paññācakkhu nāma, indriyaparopariyattañāṇañca āsayānusayañāṇañca buddhacakkhu nāma, sabbaññutaññāṇaṃ samantacakkhu nāma. Idha pana “buddhacakkhunā”ti vuttattā yathāvuttadveñāṇāniyevāti āha “indriya…pe… ñāṇena cā”ti. Hīti saccaṃ. Yesanti sattānaṃ. Saddhādīnīti ādisaddena vīriyasatisamādhipaññindriyāni saṅgaṇhāti. Tikkhānīti tikhiṇāni. Mudūnīti sukhumatarāni. Ākārāti kāraṇā. Imāni tīṇi dukāni bāhiratthasamāsavasena vuttāni. Sukhena viññāpetabbāti suviññāpayā, tathā duviññāpayāti vacanatthaṃ dassento āha “ye kathitakāraṇa”ntiādi[V 1.0177]. Paraloko ca vajjañca paralokavajjāni, tāni bhayato passantīti paralokavajjabhayadassāvinoti vacanatthaṃ dassento āha “ye”tiādi. Imāni dve dukāni kitavasena vuttāni, idha pacchimaduke “na appekacce paralokavajjabhayadassāvino”ti dutiyapadaṃ na vuttaṃ, paṭisambhidāmaggapāḷiyaṃ (paṭi. ma. 1.111) pana yugaḷavasena vuttaṃ. Uppalāni ettha santīti uppalinīti vacanatthena gaccho vā latā vā pokkharaṇī vā vanaṃ vā “uppalinī”ti vuccati, idha pana “vana”nti āha “uppalavane”ti. Nimuggāneva hutvāti sambandho. Posayantīti vaḍḍhanti, iminā antonimuggāneva hutvā posayantīti antonimuggaposīnīti vacanatthaṃ dasseti. “Udakena sama”nti iminā udakena samaṃ samodakaṃ, samodakaṃ hutvā ṭhitānīti atthaṃ dasseti. “Atikkamitvā”ti iminā accuggammātipadassa atiuggantvāti atthaṃ dasseti.

9. Concerning buddhacakkhunā: here, ‘eye’ is twofold: the fleshly eye and the knowledge eye. Therein, the fleshly eye is also twofold: the sensitive eye and the composite eye. Therein, the sensitive matter is called the sensitive eye; the ball of flesh bounded by the brow-bone is called the composite eye. The knowledge eye, however, is fivefold: the divine eye, the Dhamma eye, the wisdom eye, the Buddha eye, and the universal eye. Therein, the supernormal knowledge of the divine eye is called the divine eye; the three lower paths are called the Dhamma eye; the knowledge of the path of arahantship is called the wisdom eye; the knowledge of the disposition of others’ faculties and the knowledge of their inclinations and underlying tendencies are called the Buddha eye; the knowledge of omniscience is called the universal eye. Here, however, since it is said ‘with the Buddha eye,’ it refers only to the two aforesaid knowledges; thus he says, ‘of the faculties… and with the knowledge.’ Hi means truly. Yesaṃ means ‘of beings.’ Concerning saddhādīni: by the word ‘etc.’ he includes the faculties of energy, mindfulness, concentration, and wisdom. Tikkhāni means sharp. Mudūni means more subtle. Ākārā means reasons. These three pairs are stated by way of externally referential compounds. Showing the etymological meaning of suviññāpayā as ‘to be instructed with ease’ and likewise duviññāpayā, he says, ‘those for whom the reason has been stated,’ etc. Showing the etymological meaning of paralokavajjabhayadassāvino as ‘they see the next world and blame as fearful,’ he says, ‘those who,’ etc. These two pairs are stated by way of verbal derivatives. Here, in the last pair, the second phrase, ‘some are not those who see fear in blame regarding the next world,’ is not stated, but in the Pāḷi of the Paṭisambhidāmagga it is stated as a pair. By the etymological meaning ‘lotuses are here,’ a bush, a creeper, a pond, or a forest is called an uppalinī, ‘a place of lotuses.’ Here, however, it means ‘forest’; thus he says, ‘in a lotus forest.’ The connection is: ‘being just submerged.’ Posayanti means they grow. By this he shows the etymological meaning of antonimuggaposīni: ‘they nourish while being just submerged within.’ By ‘level with the water,’ he shows the meaning: samodakaṃ is ‘level with the water’; ‘standing level with the water.’ By ‘having surpassed,’ he shows the meaning of the word accuggamma as ‘having risen beyond.’

Paṭicchannena āropitāti pārutā, na pārutā apārutā. Apārutā nāma atthato vivaraṇāti āha “vivaṭā”ti soti ariyamaggo[M 0.0202]. Hīti saccaṃ. Pacchimapadadvayeti gāthāya uttamapadadvaye. Ayamevatthoti ayaṃ vakkhamāno evaṃ attho daṭṭhabboti yojanā. Hīti vitthāro. Na bhāsinti ettha uttamapurisattā “aha”nti vuttaṃ. “Devamanujesu”ti vattabbe ekasesavasena “manujesū”ti vuttanti āha “devamanussesū”ti.

‘Covered’ (pārutā) means veiled by what is concealed; not covered is ‘uncovered’ (apārutā). ‘Uncovered’ by name means opened in meaning; thus he says, ‘opened’ (vivaṭā). That is the noble path. Hi means truly. Pacchimapadadvaye means ‘in the last two lines of the verse.’ The connection for ayamevattho is: ‘This meaning which will be stated should be understood thus.’ Hi means in detail. Concerning na bhāsiṃ, here, because it is the first person, ‘I’ is stated. When ‘among gods and humans’ should be said, ‘among humans’ is said by way of elliptical compound; thus he says, ‘among gods and humans.’

6. Pañcavaggiyakathā

6. The Story of the Group of Five

10. Ṭhānuppattiyāti kāraṇena uppattiyā. Nikkileso jāti sabhāvo imassāti nikkilesajātiko. “Ñāṇa”nti avisesena vuttepi atthato anāvaraṇañāṇamevāti āha “sabbaññutaññāṇa”nti. Itoti “dhammaṃ desessāmī”ti parivitakkadivasato, heṭṭhāti sambandho. Devatā pana āḷārassa kālaṅkaraṇameva jānāti, na ākiñcaññāyatane nibbattabhāvaṃ. Bhagavā pana sabbaṃ jānāti, tena vuttaṃ “ākiñcaññāyatane nibbatto”ti. “Parihīnattā”ti iminā mahājāniyoti ettha hādhātuyā atthaṃ dasseti. Assāti āḷārassa. Mahatī jāniassāti “mahājāniko”ti vattabbe kakārassa yakāraṃ katvā “mahājāniyo”ti vuttaṃ. Akkhaṇeti brahmacariyavāsāya anokāse, ākiñcaññāyataneti attho. Hiyyoti anantarātītāhe. Sopīti udako rāmaputtopi. Pisaddo āḷārāpekkho. Tattha āḷāro kālāmo yāvaākiñcaññāyatanajhānalābhī hoti, tasmā ākiñcaññāyatane nibbatto. Udako rāmaputto yāvanevasaññānāsaññāyatanajhānalābhī hoti, tasmā nevasaññānāsaññāyatane nibbattoti [V 1.0178] daṭṭhabbaṃ. “Bahukārā”ti ca “bahūpakārā”ti ca pāṭhassa dvidhā yuttabhāvaṃ dassetuṃ vuttaṃ “bahukārāti bahūpakārā”ti. Pesitattabhāvaṃ manti yojanā. Iminā pahitattanti ettha attasaddo kāyavācakoti dasseti.

10. Ṭhānuppattiyā means arising due to a cause. Nikkilesajātiko means one whose innate nature is to be free from defilements. Although 'knowledge' is spoken of without qualification, in meaning it is specifically unobstructed knowledge; thus it is said, 'the knowledge of omniscience.' Itoti (from this): from the day of the reflection, 'I will teach the Dhamma,' the connection is with what follows. The deities, however, know only of Āḷāra's death, not of his rebirth in the sphere of nothingness. The Blessed One, however, knows everything; hence it is said, 'he was reborn in the sphere of nothingness.' By 'because of loss' (parihīnattā), he indicates the meaning of the root hā in mahājāniyo. Assa refers to Āḷāra. Although one should say mahājāniko, meaning 'one who has a great loss,' mahājāniyo is said, having changed the 'k' to a 'y'. Akkhaṇe means at an unpropitious time, an occasion unsuitable for the holy life; the meaning is in the sphere of nothingness. Hiyyo means on the immediately preceding day. Sopi means 'he too,' referring to Udaka Rāmaputta. The particle pi is used in comparison with Āḷāra. Here, Āḷāra Kālāma was an attainer of the jhānas up to the sphere of nothingness, thus he was reborn in the sphere of nothingness. Udaka Rāmaputta was an attainer of the jhānas up to the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception, thus he was reborn in the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception; this should be understood. To show the twofold suitability of the readings bahukārā and bahūpakārā, it is said, 'bahukārā means bahūpakārā.' The construction is with pesitattabhāvaṃ ('the state of being one whose self is dispatched'). By this, he shows that here in pahitatta, the word atta is a designation for the body.

11. Antarāsaddena yuttattā “gayaṃ, bodhi”nti ettha sāmyatthe upayogavacananti āha “gayāya ca bodhimaṇḍassa cā”ti.

11. Because of its connection with the word antarā (between), he says that here, in the phrase concerning Gayā and the Bodhi tree, the genitive case is used to express relation; hence the reading 'gayāya ca bodhimaṇḍassa ca'.

Gāthāya [M 0.0203] catūsu sabbasaddesu dutiyo sabbasaddo anavasesattho, sesā sāvasesatthāti dassento āha “sabbaṃ tebhūmakadhamma”ntiādi. Vacanattho suviññeyyova. Arahattaphalassāpi taṇhākkhayattā vuttaṃ “taṇhākkhaye nibbāne”ti. Sayaṃsaddo attapariyāyo, abhiññāyasaddo tu tvāpaccayantoti āha “attanāva jānitvā”ti. “Sabbaṃ catubhūmakadhamma”nti iminā ñādhātuyā kammaṃ dasseti. “Ayaṃ me ācariyo”ti uddisanākāradassanaṃ.

Showing that among the four instances of the word 'all' in the verse, the second has the meaning 'without remainder' while the others have a qualified meaning, he says, 'all phenomena of the three planes,' etc. The meaning of the statement is easy to understand. Since the fruit of arahantship is also the destruction of craving, it is said, 'in the destruction of craving, Nibbāna.' The word sayaṃ is a synonym for 'self,' while the word abhiññāya is a gerund ending in -tvā; thus he says, 'having known by oneself.' By 'all phenomena of the four planes,' he indicates the object of the root ñā. 'This is my teacher': this shows the mode of designation.

“Lokuttaradhamme”ti iminā lokiyadhamme pana ācariyo (mi. pa. 4.5.11) atthīti dasseti. Paṭipuggaloti ettha paṭisaddo paṭibhāgatthoti āha “paṭibhāgapuggalo”ti. Sadisapuggalo nāma natthīti attho. Sītibhūtoti sīti hutvā bhūto, sītibhāvaṃ vā patto.

By 'in the supramundane Dhamma,' he shows that in regard to the mundane Dhamma, however, there is a teacher (cf. Mil 4.5.11). Paṭipuggalo: here the prefix paṭi has the meaning of 'counterpart'; thus it is said, 'a counterpart-person.' The meaning is that there is no person who is his equal. Sītibhūto: one who has become cool, or one who has attained the state of coolness.

Kāsīnanti bahuvacanavasena vuttattā janapadānaṃ nāmaṃ. Janapadasamūhassa raṭṭhanāmattā vuttaṃ “kāsiraṭṭhe”ti. “Nagara”nti iminā purasaddo nagarapariyāyoti dasseti. Paṭilābhāyāti paṭilābhāpanatthāya. “Bheri”nti iminā dundubhisaddo bherivācakoti dasseti. Bheri hi “duṃdu”ntisaddena ubhi pūraṇametthāti dundubhīti vuccati. Dakārarakārānaṃ saṃyogaṃ katvā dundrubhītipi pāṭho atthi, so apāṭhoyeva. “Paharissāmī”ti ettha pahārasaddena āhaññinti ettha āpubbahanadhātuyā atthaṃ dasseti, ssāmisaddena ajjataniiṃvibhattiyā anāgatakāle pavattabhāvaṃ, itisaddena gamanākāravācakassa itisaddassa lopabhāvaṃ dasseti.

`Kāsīnaṃ`: since this is in the plural, it is the name of the districts. Because a collection of districts is named a country, it is said, 'in the Kāsī country.' By 'city' (`nagara`), he shows that the word `pura` is a synonym for `nagara`. `Paṭilābhāya` means for the purpose of causing to obtain. By 'drum' (`bheri`), he shows that the word `dundubhi` designates a `bheri`. For a `bheri` is called a `dundubhī` because 'it is filled here on both sides with the sound "duṃdu".' There is also a reading `dundrubhī`, making a conjunct of the letters `d` and `r`; that is indeed an incorrect reading. Regarding '`paharissāmi`' (I will strike): here, with the word `pahāra` (striking), he indicates the meaning of the root `han` with the prefix `ā`. With the ending `ssāmi`, he shows that the aorist (`ajjatanī`) verb form has a future sense. With the word `iti`, he shows the elision of the word `iti` that indicates the mode of going.

Anantajinoti anantasaṅkhātassa sabbaññutaññāṇassa padaṭṭhānabhūtena arahattamaggañāṇena sabbakilesārīnaṃ jitavā, etena phalūpacārena anantajinabhāvaṃ dasseti. Huveyya pāvusoti ettha “huveyya api āvuso”ti padavibhāgaṃ katvā hudhātu sattatthavācako, apisaddo evaṃnāmavācakoti dassento āha āvuso “evaṃ nāma bhaveyyā”ti. Vakārassa pakāraṃ katvā “hupeyyā”ti pāṭhopi yujjatiyeva.

`Anantajino` (Infinite Conqueror): he has conquered all the enemies, the defilements, by means of the knowledge of the path of arahantship, which is the basis for the knowledge of omniscience that is reckoned as infinite. By this, he shows the state of being the Infinite Conqueror through a figurative usage based on the fruit. In `huveyya pāvuso`: here, dividing the words as `huveyya api āvuso`, he shows that the root `hu` designates existence and the particle `api` designates 'such a name,' and thus he says: 'Friend, may it be so by name.' By changing the `v` to a `p`, the reading `hupeyyā` is also suitable.

12. “Atthāya [V 1.0179][M 0.0204] paṭipanno”ti iminā bāhullassa atthāya paṭipanno bāhullikoti vacanatthaṃ dasseti. Padhānatoti dukkaracariyāya padahanato. “Bhaṭṭho”ti iminā vibbhantoti ettha vipubbabhamudhātuyā anavaṭṭhānattho nāma atthato bhaṭṭhoti dasseti. Sotanti ettha sotasaddassa sotaviññāṇādivācakattā “sotindriya”nti vuttaṃ. Iriyāyāti ettha iriyanaṃ caraṇaṃ iriyāti vacanatthaṃ dassento āha “dukkaracariyāyā”ti. Abhijānātha noti ettha nosaddo nusaddatthoti āha “abhijānātha nū”ti. Vākyanti vācakaṃ. Saññāpetuntipadassa saññāpanākāraṃ dassetuṃ vuttaṃ “ahaṃ buddho”ti.

12. By 'entered upon for the sake of,' he shows the etymological meaning of `bāhulliko` as 'one who has entered upon for the sake of abundance.' `Padhānato`: because of striving in difficult practices. By `bhaṭṭho` (lost), he shows that here in `vibbhanto`, the meaning of the root `bhamu` with the prefix `vi-` is 'instability,' which in meaning is `bhaṭṭho`. `Sotaṃ`: here, because the word `sota` can designate ear-consciousness, etc., it is said 'ear-faculty.' `Iriyāya`: here, showing the etymological meaning of `iriyā` as 'moving, conduct,' he says 'by difficult practice.' `Abhijānātha no`: here, the word `no` has the meaning of the word `nu`; thus he says `abhijānātha nū`. `Vākyaṃ` means a statement. To show the mode of convincing for the word `saññāpetuṃ`, it is said, 'I am the Buddha'.

13. Itoti “cakkhukaraṇī”tiādito. Padatthatoti padato ca atthato ca, padānaṃ atthato vā. Itoti yathāvuttato. Hīti saccaṃ. Suttantakathanti suttantavasena vuttavacanaṃ.

13. `Ito` (from this): from 'vision-producing,' etc. `Padatthato`: from the word and from the meaning, or from the meaning of the words. `Ito`: from what has been said. `Hi`: truly. `Suttantakathā`: speech spoken in the manner of a discourse.

18. Devatākoṭīhīti brahmasaṅkhātāhi devatākoṭīhi. Patiṭṭhitassa tassa āyasmatoti sambandho. Sāva ehibhikkhuupasampadāti yojanā.

18. By 'crores of deities' (`devatākoṭīhi`): by crores of deities reckoned as brahmās. The connection is: 'of that venerable one who was established' (`patiṭṭhitassa tassa āyasmato`). The construction (`yojanā`) is: 'that very "come, bhikkhu" ordination' (`sā eva ehibhikkhu-upasampadā`).

19. Dutiyadivase dhammacakkhuṃ udapādīti sambandho. “Dutiyadivase”tiādi pāṭipadadivasaṃ upanidhāya vuttaṃ. Pakkhassāti āsaḷhīmāsakāḷapakkhassa. Sabbeva te bhikkhūti yojanā. Anattasuttenāti anattalakkhaṇasuttantena (mahāva. 20; saṃ. ni. 3.59).

19. `Dutiyadivase dhammacakkhuṃ udapādi` (on the second day the Dhamma eye arose): this is the connection. 'On the second day,' etc., is said with reference to the first day of the fortnight. `Pakkhassa` (of the fortnight): of the dark fortnight of the month of Āsāḷhī. `Sabbe eva te bhikkhū` (all those bhikkhus): this is the construction. `Anattasuttena` (by the Anatta Sutta): by the Anattalakkhaṇa Sutta (Mv I 20; SN 22:59).

Pañcamiyā pakkhassāti pakkhassa pañcamiyā. Lokasminti sattaloke. “Manussaarahantoti iminā devaarahanto bahūti dasseti.

`Pañcamiyā pakkhassa` (on the fifth of the fortnight): this means `pakkhassa pañcamiyā`. `Lokasmiṃ` (in the world): in the world of beings. By 'human arahants,' he shows that there are many deva arahants.

7. Pabbajjākathā

7. Discourse on the Going Forth

31. Porāṇānuporāṇānanti purāṇe ca anupurāṇe ca bhavānaṃ. Ekasaṭṭhīti eko ca saṭṭhi ca, ekena vā adhikā saṭṭhi ekasaṭṭhi.

31. 'Of ancient and subsequent ones' means of ancient and subsequent existences. 'Sixty-one' means one and sixty, or sixty with one added is sixty-one.

Tatrāti [M 0.0205] tesu ekasaṭṭhimanussaarahantesu. Pubbayogoti pubbe kato upāyo, pubbūpanissayoti attho. Vaggabandhenāti samūhaṃ katvā bandhena. Teti pañcapaññāsa janā. Jhāpessāmāti ḍayhissāma. Nīhariṃsūti gāmato nīhariṃsu. Tesūti pañcapaññāsajanesu. Pañca jane [V 1.0180] ṭhapetvāti sambandho. Sesāti pañcahi janehi avasesā. Soti yaso dārako. Tepīti cattāropi janā. Tatthāti sarīre. Te sabbepīti yasassa mātāpitubhariyāhi saddhiṃ sabbepi te sahāyakā. Tenāti pubbayogena.

'Among them' means among those sixty-one human arahants. 'Past connection' means a means undertaken in the past; the meaning is a past supporting condition. 'By a group-bond' means by making a group and binding it together. 'They' means fifty-five people. 'We will have them burned' means we will be burned. 'They removed' means they removed them from the village. 'Among them' means among the fifty-five people. 'Having excluded five people': this is the connection. 'The rest' means those remaining apart from the five people. 'He' means the boy Yasa. 'They too' means the four people too. 'There' means in the body. 'All of them' means all those companions, together with Yasa’s mother, father, and wife. 'By that' means by that past connection.

Āmantesīti kathesi.

'He addressed' means he spoke.

32. Dibbesu visayesu bhavā dibbā lobhapāsāti dassento āha “dibbā nāmā”tiādi. Lobhapāsāti lobhasaṅkhātā bandhanā. Asavanatāti ettha karaṇatthe paccattavacananti āha “asavanatāyā”ti. Parihāyantīti ettha kena parihāyantīti āha “visesādhigamato”ti. Visesādhigamatoti maggaphalasaṅkhātassa visesassa adhigamato.

32. Showing that 'divine snares of greed' are so called because they exist in divine sense objects, he said: 'divine indeed,' etc. 'Snares of greed' means bonds reckoned as greed. Regarding `Asavanatā`: here, this is a singular ablative used in the sense of cause; thus he said `asavanatāyā` (by non-flowing). Regarding 'they decline': here, explaining by what they decline, he said, 'from the attainment of distinction.' 'From the attainment of distinction' means from the attainment of the distinction reckoned as path and fruit.

33. Antaṃ lāmakaṃ karotīti antakoti vacanatthaṃ dassento āha “lāmakā”ti. “Hīnasattā”ti iminā antakassa sarūpaṃ dasseti. Āmantanapadametaṃ. Tanti rāgapāsaṃ. Hīti saccaṃ. Soti māro pāpimā. Antalikkhe carantānaṃ pañcābhiññānampi bandhanattā antalikkhe carati pavattatīti antalikkhacaroti vacanatthena rāgapāso “antalikkhacaro”ti mārena pāpimatā vutto.

33. Explaining the etymological meaning of `antaka` as 'he makes a base end,' he says, '`lāmakā`.' With 'beings of low estate,' he indicates the nature of Antaka. This is a vocative term. 'That' means the noose of passion. 'Hi' means truly. 'He' is Māra the Evil One. Because it is a bond even for those possessing the five superknowledges who wander in the sky, the noose of passion is called 'sky-wanderer' by Māra the Evil One, based on the meaning 'it wanders, it proceeds in the sky'.

34. Nānājanapadatoti ekissāpi disāya nānājanapadato. “Anujānāmi…pe… pabbājethā”tiādimhi vinicchayo evaṃ veditabboti yojanā. Pabbājentena bhikkhunā pabbājetabboti sambandho. Ye paṭikkhittā puggalāti yojanā. Paratoti parasmiṃ. “Na bhikkhave…pe… pabbājetabbo”ti pāḷiṃ (mahāva. 89) ādiṃ katvāti yojanā. Teti paṭikkhittapuggale. Sopi cāti sopi ca puggalo. Anuññātoyeva pabbājetabboti [M 0.0206] sambandho. Tassa cāti puggalassa ca, atha vā tesañca mātāpitūnaṃ. Vacanavipallāso hesa. Anujānanalakkhaṇaṃ vaṇṇayissāmāti sambandho.

34. 'From various districts' means from various districts even within a single direction. Regarding the passage beginning 'I allow... you should give the going-forth,' the connection is that the decision should be understood thus. The connection is that he should be given the going-forth by a monk who is giving the going-forth. 'Those persons who are prohibited': this is the connection. 'Elsewhere' means in another. 'Taking as the starting point the Pāli passage (Mahāvagga 89), "Monks, one should not... be given the going-forth"': this is the connection. 'Those' means the prohibited persons. 'And he too' means and that person too. 'He should be given the going-forth only with permission': this is the connection. 'And his' means of that person, or of their parents. This is indeed a change of expression. 'I will describe the characteristic of permission': this is the connection.

Evanti iminā vuttanayena. Casaddo vākyasampiṇḍanattho. Sace acchinnakeso hoti ca, sace ekasīmāya aññepi bhikkhū atthi cāti attho. Aññepīti attanā aparepi. Bhaṇḍūti muṇḍo, soyeva kammaṃ bhaṇḍukammaṃ. Tassāti bhaṇḍukammassa. Okāsoti pabbajjāya khaṇo. “Okāsaṃ na labhatī”ti vatvā tassa kāraṇaṃ dassetuṃ vuttaṃ “sace”tiādi.

'Thus' means in this stated manner. The word 'and' serves to connect the sentences. The meaning is: 'if he has unshorn hair, and if there are other monks too within the same boundary.' 'Others too' means others besides oneself. 'Shaven-headed' means shaven; that very action is the act of making shaven. 'Of that' means of that act of making shaven. 'Opportunity' means the moment for the going-forth. Having said, 'He does not get an opportunity,' to show the reason for this, it is said: 'if,' etc.

Avuttopīti [V 1.0181] ettha pisaddo vutto pana kā nāma kathāti dasseti. Upajjhāyaṃ uddissa pabbājetīti ettha pabbajjā catubbidhā tāpasapabbajjā paribbājakapabbajjā sāmaṇerapabbajjā upasampadapabbajjāti. Tattha kesamassuharaṇaṃ tāpasapabbajjā nāma vakkalādigahaṇato paṭhamameva vajitabbattā. Isipabbajjātipi tassāyeva nāmaṃ. Kesamassuharaṇameva paribbājakapabbajjā nāma kāsāyādigahaṇato paṭhamameva vajitabbattā. Kesamassuharaṇañca kāsāyacchādanañca sāmaṇerapabbajjā nāma saraṇagahaṇato paṭhamameva vajitabbattā. Upasampadapabbajjā tividhā ehibhikkhuupasampadapabbajjā saraṇagahaṇūpasampadapabbajjā ñatticatutthavācikūpasampadapabbajjāti. Tattha ehibhikkhūpasampadapabbajjāyaṃ kesamassuharaṇādi sabbaṃ ekatova sampajjati “ehi bhikkhū”ti bhagavato vacanena abhinipphannattā. Saraṇagahaṇūpasampadapabbajjā sāmaṇerapabbajjasadisāyeva. Kesamassuharaṇañca kāsāyacchādanañca saraṇagahaṇañca ñatticatutthavācikūpasampadapabbajjā nāma kammavācāgahaṇato paṭhamameva vajitabbattā. Tattha sāmaṇerapabbajjaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ “upajjhāyaṃ uddissa pabbājetī”ti. Upajjhāyaṃ uddissāti upajjhāyassa veyyāvaccakaraṭṭhānaniyamaṃ katvā. Pabbajjākamme attano issariyamakatvāti attho. Daharena bhikkhunā kesacchedanaṃ kāsāyacchādanaṃ saraṇadānanti tīṇi kiccāni kātabbāniyeva. Keci “saraṇāni pana sayaṃ dātabbānī”ti pāṭhaṃ idhānetvā daharena bhikkhunā saraṇāni na dātabbānīti [M 0.0207] vadanti, taṃ na gahetabbaṃ daharassa bhikkhuttā, bhikkhūnaṃ pabbājetuṃ labhanattā ca. Upajjhāyo ce kesacchedanañca kāsāyacchādanañca akatvā pabbajjatthaṃ saraṇāniyeva deti, na ruhati pabbajjā pabbajjāya akattabbattā. Kammavācaṃ sāvetvā upasampādeti, ruhati upasampadā apattacīvarānaṃ upasampadasiddhito, kammavipattiyā abhāvato ca. Khaṇḍasīmanti upacārasīmaṭṭhaṃ baddhasīmaṃ. Pabbājetvāti kesacchedanaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ “kāsāyāni acchādetvā”ti kāsāyacchādanassa visuṃ vuttattā. Sāmaṇerassa saraṇadānassa aruhattā “saraṇāni pana sayaṃ dātabbānī”ti vuttaṃ. Purisaṃ pabbājetunti sambandho. Hīti saccaṃ. Āṇattiyāti bhikkhūnaṃ āṇattiyā. Yena kenacīti gahaṭṭhapabbajitesu yena kenaci.

Here, in 'avuttopi,' the particle 'pi' indicates the sense of 'but what talk has been spoken?' Here, regarding 'he gives the going-forth with reference to a preceptor,' the going-forth is fourfold: the going-forth of an ascetic, the going-forth of a wanderer, the going-forth of a novice, and the going-forth of higher ordination. Among these, the removal of hair and beard is called the ascetic's going-forth, because it should be done first, before taking bark-cloth garments and so on; its name is also the seer's going-forth. The mere removal of hair and beard is called the wanderer's going-forth, because it should be done first, before taking the ochre robe and so on. The removal of hair and beard and the donning of the ochre robe is called the novice's going-forth, because it should be done first, before taking the refuges. The going-forth of higher ordination is threefold: the 'come, bhikkhu' higher ordination, the higher ordination by taking the refuges, and the higher ordination by a formal motion with a proclamation as the fourth part. Among these, in the 'come, bhikkhu' higher ordination, everything from the removal of hair and beard onwards is accomplished at once, being effected by the Blessed One's words, 'Come, bhikkhu.' The higher ordination by taking the refuges is just like the novice's going-forth. The removal of hair and beard, the donning of the ochre robe, and the taking of the refuges is called the higher ordination by a formal motion with a proclamation as the fourth part, because it should be done first, before undertaking the formal act. Here, 'he gives the going-forth with reference to a preceptor' is said concerning the novice's going-forth. 'With reference to a preceptor' means having established the position of doing service for the preceptor. The meaning is not exercising one's own authority in the act of going-forth. A junior monk must certainly perform three duties: cutting the hair, putting on the ochre robes, and giving the refuges. Some, citing the reading 'but the refuges should be given by oneself,' say that the refuges should not be given by a junior monk. That should not be accepted, because a junior is a monk, and because monks are allowed to give the going-forth. If a preceptor, without having done the cutting of hair and the putting on of ochre robes, gives only the refuges for the going-forth, the going-forth is not valid, because the going-forth has not been done. If he confers the higher ordination by reciting the formal motion, the higher ordination is valid, because the higher ordination of those without bowl and robes is established, and because there is no defect in the formal act. 'Incomplete boundary' means a consecrated boundary that stands as a perimeter boundary. 'Having given the going-forth' is said with reference to the cutting of hair, because 'having put on the ochre robes' is stated separately. Because a novice is not fit to give the refuges, it is said, 'but the refuges should be given by oneself.' The connection is 'to give the going-forth to a man.' 'Hi' means truly. 'By command' means by the command of the monks. 'By anyone' means by anyone among householders and the gone-forth.

“Bhabbarūpo”ti vatvā tassa atthaṃ dassetuṃ vuttaṃ “sahetuko”ti. Sahetukoti maggaphalānaṃ upanissayehi saha pavatto. Yasassīti parivārayasena ca kittiyasena ca samannāgato. Okāsaṃ katvāpīti okāsaṃ katvā eva. Sayamevāti na añño āṇāpetabbo. Ettoyevāti dassanaṭṭhānatoyeva. Assāti pabbajjāpekkhassa. Khajju vāti kaṇḍuvanaṃ vā. “Kacchu vā”tipi pāṭho, pāmaṃ vāti attho. Piḷakā vāti phoṭā vā. Ettakenāti etapamāṇena [V 1.0182] ghaṃsitvā nhāpanamattena. Anivattidhammāti gihibhāvaṃ anivattanasabhāvā. Kataññūti katassūpakārassa jānanasīlā. Katavedinoti kataññūpakārassa vedaṃ pākaṭaṃ karonto.

Having said 'of suitable form,' to explain its meaning, it is said, 'with a cause.' 'With a cause' means proceeding together with the supporting conditions for the path and fruits. 'Famous' means endowed with a retinue and with fame. 'Even having made an opportunity' means having made an opportunity indeed. 'By oneself' means another should not be commanded. 'From just this' means from just the place of seeing. 'His' means of one who desires the going-forth. 'Or scabies' means or itching. 'Or kacchu' is also a reading; the meaning is 'or skin-disease.' 'Or boils' means or blisters. 'With this much' means with just this amount of rubbing and bathing. 'Of irreversible nature' means having a nature of not returning to the household life. 'Grateful' means having the habit of knowing a service that has been done. 'Acknowledging what was done' means making known the service that was done.

Aniyyānikakathāti yāvadatthaṃ supitvā yāvadatthaṃ bhuñjītvā cittakeḷiṃ karonto anukkaṇṭhito viharāhītiādikā kathā. Nakathetabbaṃ dassetvā kathetabbaṃ dassento āha “athakhvassā”ti. Assāti pabbajjāpekkhassa. Ācikkhanākāraṃ dassento āha “ācikkhantena cā”tiādi. Vaṇṇa…pe… vasenāti vaṇṇo ca saṇṭhānañca gandho ca āsayo ca okāso ca, tesaṃ vasena, ācikkhitabbanti sambandho. Hīti phalajotako, ācikkhanassa phalaṃ vakkhāmīti attho. Soti pabbajjāpekkho. Pubbeti pubbabhave, pabbajanato [M 0.0208] pubbe vā. Kaṇṭakavedhāpekkho paripakkagaṇḍo viya ñāṇaṃ pavattatīti yojanā. Assāti pabbajjāpekkhassa. Indāsanīti sakkassa vajirāvudho. So hi indena asīyati khipīyatīti indāsanīti vuccati. Indāsani pabbate cuṇṇayamānā viya sabbe kilese cuṇṇayamānaṃyevāti yojanā. Khuraggeyevāti khurassa koṭiyameva. Khurakammapariyosāneyevāti attho. Hīti saccaṃ. Tasmāti yasmā pattā, tasmā. Assāti pabbajjāpekkhassa.

'Talk that is not a guide to release' is talk such as: 'Live without striving, having slept as you please, having eaten as you please, and amusing your mind.' Having shown what should not be said, showing what should be said, he said 'but now to him.' 'His' means of one who desires the going-forth. Showing the mode of instruction, he said 'and by one instructing,' etc. The connection is: 'by means of color... etc.' means it should be explained by means of their color, shape, smell, support, and location. 'Hi' is an illuminator of the result; the meaning is 'I will state the fruit of the instruction.' 'He' means one who desires the going-forth. 'Formerly' means in a former existence, or before going forth. The connection is: knowledge proceeds like a ripe boil for one who is expecting the piercing of a thorn. 'His' means of one who desires the going-forth. 'Indra's missile' is Sakka's diamond-weapon. For it is thrown by Indra, therefore it is called 'Indra's missile.' The connection is: just as Indra's missile pulverizes a mountain, so it pulverizes all the defilements. 'On the very razor's edge' means on the very tip of the razor. The meaning is 'at the very conclusion of the razor-work.' 'Hi' means truly. 'Therefore' means because it is attained, therefore. 'His' means of one who desires the going-forth.

Gihigandhanti gehe ṭhitassa janassa gandhaṃ. Athāpīti yadipi acchādetīti sambandho. Assāti pabbajjāpekkhassa. Ācariyo vāti saraṇadānācariyo vā kammavācācariyo vā ovādācariyo vā. Taṃyeva vāti pabbajjāpekkhameva vā. Tena bhikkhunāvāti ācariyupajjhāyabhikkhunā eva.

'The householder's scent' means the scent of a person staying in a house. 'Athāpi' means 'even if'; the connection is with 'he covers.' 'His' means of one who desires the going-forth. 'Or a teacher' means either the teacher who gives the refuges, or the teacher of the formal act, or the teacher who gives the exhortation. 'Or that very one' means or just the one who desires the going-forth. 'By that monk' means precisely by the monk who is the teacher or preceptor.

Anāṇattiyāti ācariyupajjhāyehi anāṇattiyā. Iminā ācariyupajjhāyehi anāṇattena yena kenaci nivāsanādīni na kātabbānīti dasseti. Bhikkhunāti ācariyupajjhāyabhikkhunā. Tassevāti pabbajjāpekkhasseva. Upajjhāyamūlaketi upajjhāyamūlake nivāsanapārupane. Ayanti vinicchayo.

'Not by command' means not by the command of the teachers and preceptors. By this—not being commanded by the teachers and preceptors—it is shown that the lower robe and so forth should not be put on by anyone. 'By a bhikkhu' means by a bhikkhu who is a teacher or preceptor. 'For him alone' means for the one seeking to go forth alone. 'Based on the preceptor' means the lower and upper robes are based on the preceptor. This is the judgment.

Tatthāti pabbajjūpasampadaṭṭhāne. Tesanti bhikkhūnaṃ. Athāti vandāpanato pacchā, vandāpanassa anantarā vā. “Evaṃ vadehī”ti pāḷinayanidassanamukhena “yamahaṃ vadāmi, taṃ vadehī”ti aṭṭhakathānayaṃ nidasseti. Athāti tadanantaraṃ. Assāti pabbajjāpekkhassa, dātabbānīti sambandho. Ekapadampīti tīsu vākyapadesu ekaṃ vākyapadampi, navasu vā vibhatyantapadesu ekapadampi. Ekakkharampīti catuvīsatakkharesu ekakkharampi.

'Therein' means at the place of the going forth and the higher ordination. 'Of them' means of the bhikkhus. 'Then' means after the paying of homage, or immediately after the paying of homage. By way of illustrating the method of the Pāli, 'Speak thus,' it illustrates the method of the commentary: 'What I say, that you should say.' 'Then' means immediately after that. 'To him' means to the one seeking to go forth; 'should be given' is the connection. 'Even one phrase' means even one phrase among the three sentence-phrases, or even one word among the nine inflected words. 'Even one letter' means even one letter among the twenty-four letters.

Ekato [V 1.0183] suddhiyāti ekasseva kammavācācariyassa ṭhānakaraṇasampattiyā sujjhanena. Ubhato suddhiyāvāti ubhayesaṃ saraṇadānācariyasāmaṇerānaṃ sujjhanena eva. Ṭhānakaraṇasampadanti uraādiṭṭhānānañca saṃvutādikaraṇānañca sampadaṃ. Vattunti ṭhānakaraṇasampadaṃ vattuṃ. Na sakkotīti vattuṃ na sakkotīti yojanā.

'Purity on one side' means by the purification of just one—the teacher of the formal act—through the accomplishment of the place and manner of articulation. 'Purity on both sides' means by the purification of both the teacher who gives the refuges and the novice. 'Accomplishment of the place and manner of articulation' means the accomplishment of both the places of articulation, such as the chest, and the manners of articulation, such as being constricted. 'To state' means to state the accomplishment of the place and manner of articulation. 'He is unable' means he is unable to state—this is the construction.

Imānīti [M 0.0209] saraṇāni. Casaddo upanyāso, panasaddo padālaṅkāro. Ekasambandhānīti ekato sambandhāni. Anunāsikantaṃ katvā dānakāle “buddhaṃ”iti “saraṇaṃ”iti padānañca “saraṇaṃ”iti “gacchāmi”iti padānañca antarā vicchedamakatvā ekasambandhameva katvā dātabbānīti vuttaṃ hoti. Kasmā tiṇṇaṃ padānamantarā byavadhānassa kassaci akkharassa abhāvato. Vicchinditvāti vicchedaṃ katvā. Makārantaṃ katvā dānakāle tiṇṇaṃ padānamantarā ekasambandhamakatvā vicchinditvā eva katvā dātabbānīti vuttaṃ hoti. Kasmā? Tiṇṇaṃ padānamantarā byavadhānassa nissarassa makārassa atthibhāvato. Andhakaṭṭhakathāyaṃ vuttanti sambandho. Tanti vacanaṃ, “natthī”tipade kattā, “na vutta”ntipade kammaṃ. Tathāti “ahaṃ bhante buddharakkhito”tiādinā ākārena, avadantassa saraṇaṃ na kuppati, bukāradakārādīnaṃ byañjanānaṃ ṭhānakaraṇasampadaṃ hāpentasseva saraṇaṃ kuppatīti adhippāyo.

"These" means the refuges. The particle 'ca' is an introduction; the particle 'pana' is a phrase-filler. "Connected as one" means connected together as one. This means it is said that when giving them, one should make it end in a nasal and, without making a break between the words "Buddhaṃ" and "saraṇaṃ," or between "saraṇaṃ" and "gacchāmi," one should give them as a single connected utterance. Why? Because there is no intervening letter between the three words. "Breaking apart" means making a break. This means it is said that when giving them, one should make it end in 'm' and, not making a single connection between the three words, one should give them having broken them apart. Why? Because there is an intervening silent 'm' between the three words. "It is stated in the Andhaka Commentary" is the connection. "That" is the statement; in the word "there is not," it is the agent; in the word "was not stated," it is the object. Similarly, for one who does not speak in the manner of "Venerable sir, I am Buddharakkhita," and so on, the refuge is not invalidated. But for one who abandons the accomplishment of the place and means of articulation of consonants such as b, k, r, and d, the refuge is invalidated—this is the intention.

“Tikkhattu”nti iminā sakiṃ vā dvikkhattuṃ vā na vaṭṭatīti dīpeti. Tikkhattuto adhikaṃ pana sahassakkhattumpi vaṭṭatiyeva. Tatthāti tāsu pabbajjāupasampadāsu. Paratoti parasmiṃ. Sāti upasampadā. Pabbajjā pana anuññātā evāti sambandho. Paratopīti pisaddo pubbāpekkho. Sāti pabbajjā. Ettāvatāti ettakena kesacchedanakāsāyacchādanasaraṇadānena. Hīti phalajotako.

"Three times": by this it shows that once or twice is not allowable. But more than three times, even a thousand times, is indeed allowable. "Therein" means in those goings forth and higher ordinations. "From another" means in another. "That" means the higher ordination; but the going forth is indeed permitted—this is the connection. "From another too": the particle 'pi' refers back. "That" means the going forth. "To this extent" means by this much: the cutting of the hair, the donning of the ochre robe, and the giving of the refuges. "Hi" is a particle that illuminates the result.

Esāti eso sāmaṇeroti attho. “Gatimā”ti vatvā tassatthaṃ dassento āha “paṇḍitajātiko”ti. Athāti evaṃ sati. Assāti sāmaṇerassa. Tasmiṃyeva ṭhāneti sāmaṇerabhūmiyaṃ ṭhitaṭṭhāneyeva. Yathā bhagavatā uddiṭṭhāni, tathā uddisitabbānīti yojanā. Etanti “anujānāmi…pe… jātarūpa rajatapaṭiggahaṇā veramaṇī”ti vacanaṃ.

"This one" means this novice. Having said "intelligent," he shows its meaning by saying "of wise birth." "Then" means this being so. "Of him" means of the novice. "In that very place" means in the very place where he stands on the level of a novice. As they were set forth by the Blessed One, so they should be set forth—this is the construction.
