"This" refers to the statement, "I allow…pe… abstinence from accepting gold and silver."

Tanti andhakaṭṭhakathāyaṃ vuttavacanaṃ. Yathāpāḷiyāvāti evasaddo sanniṭṭhānattho, tena yathāpāḷiyāva uddisitabbāni. Yathāpāḷiṃ visajjetvā aññathā eva uddisitabbānīti vādaṃ nivāreti. Yathāpāḷiṃ visajjetvā [M 0.0210] aññathā “pāṇātipātā veramaṇiṃ sikkhāpadaṃ samādiyāmī”ti [V 1.0184] uddisantopi niddosoyeva. Hīti saccaṃ, yasmā vā. Tānīti sikkhāpadāni. Yāvāti yattakaṃ kālaṃ na jānāti, na kusalo hotīti sambandho. Santikāvacaroyevāti ācariyupajjhāyānaṃ samīpe avacārova. Assāti sāmaṇerassa. Kappiyākappiyanti dasasikkhāpadavinimuttaṃ kappiyaṃ parāmāsādiñca akappiyaṃ aparāmāsādiñca. Tenāpīti sāmaṇerenāpi. Nāsanaṅgānīti liṅganāsanaaṅgāni. Sādhukaṃ sikkhitabbanti sādhukaṃ asikkhantassa liṅganāsanañca daṇḍakammanāsanañca hotīti adhippāyo.

"That" refers to the statement found in the Andhaka Commentary. "Exactly as in the Pāli": the particle 'eva' has the sense of determination; therefore, they should be set forth exactly as in the Pāli. This refutes the view that, having set aside the Pāli wording, they should be set forth otherwise. Even one who, having set aside the Pāli wording, sets them forth otherwise, saying, "I undertake the training rule of abstaining from taking life," is still without fault. "Hi" means "truly," or "because." "Those" refers to the training rules. "As long as" means for as long a time as one does not know and is not skilled—this is the connection. "One who stays nearby" means one who stays only in the vicinity of the teachers and preceptors. "Of him" refers to the novice. "Allowable and unallowable" means that which is allowable, apart from the ten training rules, such as touching, and that which is unallowable, such as not touching. "Even by him" means even by the novice. "Grounds for expulsion" means the grounds for expulsion from the status of a novice. "Should be well learned": for one who does not learn well, there is expulsion from the status of a novice and expulsion by disciplinary action—this is the intention.

10. Dutiyamārakathā

10. The Second Account of Māra

35. Mayhantipadassa “anuppattā sacchikatā”tipadesu chaṭṭhīkattubhāvaṃ dassento āha “mayā khoti attho”ti. “Atha vā”tiādinā “mayha”ntipadassa “yoniso manasikārā, yoniso sammappadhānā”tipadesu sambandhabhāvaṃ dasseti. “Yoniso manasikārā, yoniso sammappadhānā”ti ettha kāraṇatthe nissakkavacananti āha “tena hetunā”ti. “Punā”tiādinā “mayha”ntipadaṃ “yoniso manasikārā, yoniso sammappadhānā”tipadesu sāmyatthe sāmibhāvena yojetvā puna “anuppattā, sacchikatā”ti padesu kattutthe sāmibhāvena vibhattivipallāso kātabboti dasseti.

35. Explaining the agentive sense of the genitive for the word 'mayhaṃ' in the phrases 'anuppattā sacchikatā,' he says: 'The meaning is “by me.”' By means of 'Atha vā,' and so on, he shows the connection of the word 'mayhaṃ' with the phrases 'yoniso manasikārā, yoniso sammappadhānā.' Concerning 'yoniso manasikārā, yoniso sammappadhānā,' he says that the ablative here is in the sense of cause, hence 'for that reason.' By means of 'Punā,' and so on, he shows that the word 'mayhaṃ' should be connected with the phrases 'yoniso manasikārā, yoniso sammappadhānā' in the sense of ownership, and then that for the words 'anuppattā, sacchikatā', a change of case to the agentive sense should be made.

11. Bhaddavaggiyakathā

11. The Account of the Fortunate Group

36. Bhaddaṃ rūpañca cittañca etesamatthīti bhaddakā. Vaggabandhanaṃ vaggo uttarapadalopena, vaggena carantīti vaggiyā. Bhaddakā ca te vaggiyā cāti bhaddavaggiyā kakāralopenāti atthaṃ dassento āha “bhaddavaggiyā”tiādi. “Vokāro nipātamatto”ti iminā tumhasaddassa ca yovacanassa ca kāriyabhāvaṃ nivatteti. Hīti saccaṃ. Teti bhaddavaggiyā. Idanti pañcasīlarakkhanaṃ. Pubbakammanti pubbe upacitaṃ kusalakammaṃ.

36. They have good form and mind, therefore they are 'bhaddakā.' 'Vagga' (group) is from 'vaggabandhanaṃ' (group-binding) by elision of the latter word. They move in a group, so they are 'vaggiyā.' 'They are bhaddakā and they are vaggiyā,' thus 'bhaddavaggiyā,' by elision of the syllable 'ka'—showing this meaning, he says 'bhaddavaggiyā,' and so on. By 'The syllable “vo” is a mere particle,' he dismisses the function of the word 'tumha' and of the vocative case. 'Hī' means 'truly.' 'Te' means the Bhaddavaggiyas. 'Idaṃ' means the keeping of the five precepts. 'Pubbakamma' means wholesome kamma accumulated in the past.

12. Uruvelapāṭihāriyakathā

12. The Account of the Uruvelā Miracle

38. Pariyādiyeyyanti [M 0.0211] ettha dādhātussa parīti ca āti ca upasaggavasena abhibhavanatthoti āha “abhibhaveyya”nti.

38. Here, in 'pariyādiyeyya,' because of the prefixes 'pari' and 'ā' with the root 'dā,' the meaning is 'to overpower'; therefore, he says 'abhibhaveyya.'

39. Pacchā [V 1.0185] pakkhittāti saṅgītito paraṃ potthakārūḷhehi ṭhapitāti attho.

39. "Inserted afterwards" means that they were included after the council by those who committed them to books; this is the meaning.

44. “Evaṃ vadanto viya oṇato”ti iminā “āharahattho”tipadassa taddhitabhāvaṃ dasseti. Vitthiṇṇamukhattā mandaṃ hīnaṃ atimukhametāsanti vacanatthena aggikapālā mandāmukhiyoti vuccantīti āha “aggibhājanāni vuccantī”ti.

44. By the phrase 'as if speaking thus, he bowed down,' he indicates the nature of the term 'āharahattho' as a secondary derivative. Because they have wide mouths, by the meaning of the expression 'their mouth is slow and inferior,' the fire-pots (aggikapālā) are called 'mandāmukhiyo'; hence he says, 'they are called fire-vessels.'

51. Yasmā yo nāgadamanakālo ciraṃ patati pavattati, tasmā so cirapatikoti vuccati, tasmā cirapatikā paṭṭhāya abhippasannāti yojanā. Iti imamatthaṃ dassento āha “cirakālato paṭṭhāyā”ti.

51. Because the time of the Nāga's taming occurred and continued for a long time, it is called 'cirapatiko.' Therefore, the construction is: 'they have been confident since that long time ago.' To show this meaning, he says: 'cirakālato paṭṭhāya' (since a long time ago).

52. Sabbatthāti sabbesu “jaṭāmissa”ntiādipadesu. Khārikājanti ettha kamaṇḍaluādikā tāpasaparikkhārā khārīti vuccanti, khārisaṅkhātena bhārena pūrito kājo khārikājoti atthaṃ ekadesena dassento āha “khāribhāro”ti.

52. "In all places" means in all phrases, such as 'jaṭāmissa,' and so on. Here, in 'khārikāja,' ascetic requisites such as the water pot are called 'khārī.' A shoulder-pole filled with a load called a 'khārī' is a 'khārikāja.' Showing the meaning partially, he says 'khāribhāro' (a khārī-load).

13. Bimbisārasamāgamakathā

13. The Account of the Meeting with Bimbisāra

55. Laṭṭhisaddo taruṇarukkhavācako “ambalaṭṭhikāya”ntiādīsu (dī. ni. 1.2), idhāpi taruṇatālarukkho laṭṭhi nāmāti dassento āha “tāluyyāne”ti. Vaṭarukkheti nigrodharukkhe. Ettha “vaṭa”iti iminā vaṭarukkho bahumūlattā suṭṭhuṃ patiṭṭhātīti atthena suppatiṭṭho nāmāti dasseti. “Rukkhe”iti iminā cetiyasaddo cetiyarukkhe vattatīti dasseti, devālayañca thūpañca nivatteti. Tassāti vaṭarukkhassa. Etanti “suppatiṭṭhe cetiye”ti etaṃ nāmaṃ. Lokavohāravasena dasasahassasaṅkhāte saṅkhyāvisese nīharitvā yujjitabbanti niyutanti vacanatthena [M 0.0212] dasasahassaṃ niyutaṃ nāmāti dassento āha “ekaniyutaṃ dasasahassānī”ti. “Nahuta”ntipi pāṭho, so ayutto nahutasaṅkhātena saṅkhyāvisesena missībhāvena pasaṅgattā. Tesanti dvādasaniyutānaṃ brāhmaṇagahapatikānaṃ.

55. The word 'laṭṭhi' denotes a young tree, as in 'ambalaṭṭhikāya' (DN 1.2). Here too, showing that a young palm tree is called 'laṭṭhi,' he says 'in the palm grove.' 'On a banyan tree' means on a nigrodha tree. Here, by the word 'vaṭa,' he shows that because a banyan tree has many roots, it stands firm, and in that sense it is called 'suppatiṭṭha' (well-established). By the word 'rukkhe,' he shows that the word 'cetiya' refers to a shrine-tree, thereby excluding a temple or a stupa. 'Tassa' means of the banyan tree. 'Etaṃ' means this name, 'suppatiṭṭhe cetiye.' Showing that ten thousand is called a 'niyuta' by the meaning of the expression 'yujjitabban ti niyutan ti' ('it should be connected, therefore it is a niyuta'), having taken the specific number designated as ten thousand according to worldly usage, he says: 'One niyuta is ten thousand.' There is also the reading 'nahuta,' but it is incorrect as it would be confused with the specific number called 'nahuta.' 'Tesaṃ' means of the twelve niyutas of brahmins and householders.

“Kisasarīrattā”ti iminā kiso ko attā etesanti kisakāti vacanatthaṃ dasseti. Kakāro hettha attavācako. “Ovādako”ti iminā ovadānoti ettha yupaccayo kattutthoti dasseti. Gāthābandhattā akārassa dīgho. “Atha vā”tiādinā kisako hutvā aññe ovadāno [V 1.0186] kisakovadānoti vacanatthaṃ dasseti. Idanti idaṃ atthajātaṃ, ayamattho vā. Tvaṃ pahāsīti sambandho. Tanti tuvaṃ. Iti vuttaṃ hotīti yojanā.

By 'because of having an emaciated body,' he shows the meaning of the expression 'kisakā' as 'one whose self (ko = attā) is emaciated (kiso).' Here the syllable 'ka' denotes 'self.' By 'ovādako' (advisor), he shows that in 'ovadāno' the suffix 'yu' is in the agentive sense. The 'a' is long because of the verse meter. By 'Atha vā,' etc., he shows the meaning of the expression 'kisakovādano' as 'one who, being emaciated, advises others.' 'Idaṃ' means this collection of meanings, or this meaning. The connection is 'You have abandoned.' 'Taṃ' means 'you.' The construction is 'thus it is said.'

Kāmitthiyoti ekāralopavasena sandhīti āha “kāme itthiyo cā”ti. Upacīsūti ettha kāmakhandhakilesaabhisaṅkhārasaṅkhātesu catūsu upadhīsu khandhupadhi adhippetoti āha “khandhupadhīsū”ti.

'Kāmitthiyo' is a sandhi by elision of one vowel, he says, as in 'kāme itthiyo ca.' Here, in 'upacīsu,' among the four upadhis—sensual pleasures, the aggregates, the defilements, and volitional formations—the aggregate-upadhi is intended; hence he says, 'in the aggregate-upadhis.'

Kocarahīti ettha kosaddo “ko te balaṃ mahārājā”tiādīsu (jā. 2.22.1880) viya kvasaddatthoti āha “kvacarahī”ti. Nipātoyevesa.

Here, in 'kocarahi,' the word 'ko' is in the sense of the word 'kva' (where), as in 'ko te balaṃ mahārājā' (Jā 2.22.1880), meaning 'Where is your army, great king?'; thus he says 'kvacarahi.' This is just a particle.

Padasaddassa caraṇapadādayo nivattetuṃ vuttaṃ “nibbānapada”nti. “Santasabhāvatāyā”tiādinā santo sabhāvo imassa padassāti santaṃ. Natthi upadhayo etthāti anupadhikaṃ. Natthi kiñcanametthāti akiñcanaṃ. Tīsu bhavesu na sañjatīti asattaṃ. Aññathā na bhavatīti anaññathābhāvi. Aññena kenaci na netabbanti anaññaneyyanti vacanatthaṃ dasseti. Tenāti “santa”ntiādipadena. Meti mama, manoti sambandho. Ettha devamanussaloke me mano rato nāmāti kiṃ vakkhāmi. Iti imamatthaṃ dassetīti yojanā.

To exclude other meanings of the word 'pada,' such as 'footprint,' etc., the term 'nibbānapada' (the state of Nibbāna) is used. By 'because of its peaceful nature,' etc., he shows the meaning of the expressions: 'santaṃ' (peaceful) is so called because the nature of this state is peaceful. 'Anupadhikaṃ' (without acquisitions) is so called because there are no acquisitions here. 'Akiñcanaṃ' (possessing nothing) is so called because there is nothing here. 'Asattaṃ' (unattached) is so called because it is not attached in the three kinds of existence. 'Anaññathābhāvi' (unalterable) is so called because it does not become otherwise. 'Anaññaneyyaṃ' (not to be led by another) is so called because it cannot be led by any other. 'Tena' means by the words 'santa,' etc. 'Me' means 'my'; the connection is with 'mano' (mind). The construction is that it shows this meaning: 'What can I say of my mind being delighted here in the world of gods and humans?'

56. Tañcāti sāvakabhāvañca.

56. 'Tañca' means and the state of a disciple.

57. Assāsakāti ettha āpubbo sāsadhātu āpubba sisadhātunā sadiso, “me”ti chaṭṭhīyogattā ṇvupaccayo ca bhāvatthoti [M 0.0213] āha “āsisanā”ti. “Patthanā”ti iminā āpubbasisadhātuyā atthaṃ dasseti. Assāti bimbisārarañño. Tatthāti ratanattaye. Nicchayagamanamevāti “saraṇa”itinicchayena jānanameva gato. Attasanniyyātananti attano attānaṃ ratanattaye sanniyyātanaṃ. Iminā attasanniyyātana, paṇipāta, tapparāyana, sissabhāvūpagamanasaṅkhātesu catūsu saraṇagamanesu (dī. ni. aṭṭha. 1.250; ma. ni. aṭṭha. 1.56; khu. pā. aṭṭha. 1.saraṇagamanagamakavibhāvanā) attasanniyyātanasaraṇagamanaṃ dīpeti. Ayanti bimbisāro rājā. Tanti niyatasaraṇataṃ. Paṇipātagamanañcāti ettha paṇīti karo. Yathā hi pādapadasaddā dīgharassavasena hutvā caraṇaṃ vadanti, evaṃ pāṇipaṇisaddā karaṃ vadanti. Tasmā vuttaṃ “paṇīti karo”ti. Patanaṃ pāto, paṇino pāto paṇipāto. Atthato añjalipaṇamananti vuttaṃ hoti. Tassa gamanañca gacchantoti attho. Iminā paṇipātasaraṇagamanaṃ [V 1.0187] dīpeti. Casaddo “pākaṭa”nti etthāpi yojetabbo. Pākaṭañca karontoti hi attho.

57. Here, in 'assāsakā,' the root 'sās' with the prefix 'ā' is similar to the root 'sis' with the prefix 'ā'; and because of its connection with 'me' in the genitive case, the suffix 'ṇvu' is used in the sense of a state; thus he says 'āsisanā' (wishing). By 'patthanā' (aspiration), he indicates the meaning of the root 'sis' with the prefix 'ā.' 'Assa' refers to King Bimbisāra. 'Tattha' means in the Triple Gem. 'Nicchayagamanaṃ eva' means going just by knowing with the certainty 'it is a refuge.' 'Attasanniyyātanaṃ' means the entrusting of oneself to the Triple Gem. By this he explains the going for refuge by self-surrender, one of the four kinds of going for refuge: self-surrender, prostration, taking it as one's final destination, and approaching it as a disciple. 'Ayaṃ' refers to King Bimbisāra. 'Taṃ' means the state of having a definite refuge. In 'paṇipātagamanañca,' 'paṇi' means hand. Just as the words 'pāda' and 'pada,' being long and short, mean 'foot,' so the words 'pāṇi' and 'paṇi' mean 'hand.' Therefore it is said, 'paṇi means hand.' 'Pāto' is falling; 'paṇipāto' is the falling of the hands. In meaning, this is said to be bowing with joined palms. 'Tassa gamanañca gacchantoti' means 'and they go that going.' By this he explains the going for refuge by prostration. The word 'ca' should also be connected here with 'pākaṭaṃ,' for the meaning is 'and they make it manifest.'

58. Siṅgīnikkhasavaṇṇoti ettha siṅgīsaṅkhāto nikkho siṅgīnikkho, tena samāno vaṇṇo etassāti siṅgīnikkhasavaṇṇoti vacanatthaṃ dassento āha “siṅgīsuvaṇṇanikkhena samānavaṇṇo”ti. Tattha “suvaṇṇa”itipadena nikkhasaddassa suvaṇṇatthaṃ dasseti, pañcasuvaṇṇādayo atthe nivatteti. “Samāna”itipadena savaṇṇoti ettha sakāro samānasaddasseva kāriyoti dasseti. Sabbesūti akhilesu cakkhādiindriyesu. Dantoti damito. Indriyasaṃvaroti vuttaṃ hoti. Tamevatthaṃ pākaṭaṃ karonto āha “bhagavato hī”tiādi.

58. Here, in 'siṅgīnikkhasavaṇṇo,' a 'nikkha' called 'siṅgī' is a 'siṅgīnikkha.' Showing the meaning of the expression 'siṅgīnikkhasavaṇṇo' as 'one whose color is the same as that,' he says: 'of a color similar to a siṅgī-gold nikkha.' There, by the word 'suvaṇṇa,' he shows that the word 'nikkha' means gold, excluding other meanings. By the word 'samāna,' he shows that here in 'savaṇṇo,' the 'sa' is a function of the word 'samāna' itself. 'Sabbesu' means in all, that is, in the faculties such as the eye, etc. 'Danto' means tamed. This is said to be 'restraint of the faculties.' Making that same meaning clear, he says 'bhagavato hi,' etc.

59. Oṇīto pattato pāṇi yenāti oṇītapattapāṇīti vacanatthaṃ dassento āha “pattato cā”tiādi. “Apanītapāṇi”nti iminā oṇītasaddo apanītattho, pāṇisaddena ca sambandhitabboti dasseti. “Sallakkhetvā”ti iminā “bhagavanta”nti imaṃ kammaṃ “sallakkhetvā”ti pāṭhasesena yojetabbanti dasseti. Ekamantanti ettha antasaddo samīpadesattho, koṭidesattho vā hoti[M 0.0214], upayogavacanañca bhummatthe hotīti dassento āha “ekasmiṃ padese”ti. Atthikapayoge karaṇassa sambhavato āha “buddhābhivādanagamanena vā dhammassavanagamanena vā”ti. Appākiṇṇanti ettha appasaddo paṭisedhatthoti āha “anākiṇṇa”nti. “Abbokiṇṇa”ntipi pāṭho. Appanigghosanti ettha “appasadda”ntipadena vacanasaddassa gahitattā iminā pārisesanayena nagaranigghosasaddoyeva gahetabboti āha “nagaranigghosasaddena appanigghosa”nti. Tīsu pāṭhesu paṭhamena pāṭhena janassa vāto janavāto, tena virahitaṃ vijanavātanti vikappaṃ dasseti. Dutiyena janassa vādo janavādo, tena virahitaṃ vijanavādanti vikappaṃ dasseti. Tatiyena janassa pāto sañcaraṇaṃ janapāto, tena virahitaṃ vijanapātanti vikappaṃ dasseti. Rahassaṃ karīyati etthāti rāhasseyyakaṃ. Manussānaṃ rāhasseyyakaṃ manussarāhasseyyakanti vacanatthaṃ dasseti “manussāna”ntiādinā.

59. Showing the verbal meaning of oṇītapattapāṇī as 'one by whom the hand has been removed from the bowl,' he says: 'from the bowl and,' etc. By 'apanītapāṇi,' he shows that the word oṇīta has the meaning 'removed' and should be connected with the word pāṇi. By 'sallakkhetvā,' he shows that this object, 'bhagavantaṃ,' should be connected with the remainder of the reading, 'sallakkhetvā.' Here in ekamantaṃ, the word anta means a nearby place or an edge, and the instrumental case is used in the sense of the locative. Showing this, he says: 'in one place.' Since an instrumental is possible in a purposive sense, he says: 'either by going to pay homage to the Buddha or by going to listen to the Dhamma.' Here in appākiṇṇaṃ, the word appa has the sense of negation, so he says: 'uncrowded.' There is also the reading 'abbokiṇṇaṃ.' Here in appanigghosaṃ, since the word for 'sound' is taken by the term 'appasadda,' by the method of elimination only the sound of the city's noise should be taken here. Thus, he says: 'with little of the city's noise.' Among the three readings, with the first reading he shows the alternative that 'the wind of people' (janassa vāto) is janavāto, and being devoid of that is vijanavātaṃ. With the second, he shows the alternative that 'the talk of people' (janassa vādo) is janavādo, and being devoid of that is vijanavādaṃ. With the third, he shows the alternative that 'the coming and going of people' (janassa pāto sañcaraṇaṃ) is janapāto, and being devoid of that is vijanapātaṃ. A secret is made here, thus it is rāhasseyyakaṃ. He shows the verbal meaning of manussarāhasseyyakaṃ as 'a secret place for humans' with the words beginning 'of humans.'

14. Sāriputtamoggallāna pabbajjākathā

14. The Story of Sāriputta and Moggallāna's Going Forth

60. “Teti sāriputtamoggallānā. Agamaṃsu kirāti yojanā. Tatrāti giraggasamajje. Athāti parivitakkanānantaraṃ. Tassāti sañcayassa. Pāranti paratīraṃ. Etthāti tumhākaṃ vāde. Idanti ayaṃ vādo ettakoyevāti attho. Yoti yo koci. Tvañca ahañca [V 1.0188] amhe, tesu. Nāmatumhasaṅkhātesu hi tīsu saddesu ekasesena kattabbesu pacchimasseva ekaseso kātabbo. Tenāti katikakaraṇahetunā.

60. 'Te' means Sāriputta and Moggallāna. The connection is: 'agamaṃsu kira' (they went, it is said). 'Tatrā' means at the festival on the mountain-top. 'Athā' means after the reflection. 'Tassā' means of Sañcaya. 'Pāraṃ' means the further shore. 'Etthā' means in your doctrine. 'Idaṃ' means this doctrine is just this much; that is the meaning. 'Yo' means whoever. 'Tvañca ahañca' (you and I) becomes 'amhe' (we); 'tesu' (among them). For among the three words counted as pronouns, when a single-remainder compound is to be made, the single remainder should be of the last one only. 'Tenā' means for the reason of making the agreement.

Saṃkhepena vuttaṃ vitthārena dassento āha “idaṃ hī”tiādi. Atthīkehīti amatena atthikehi. Upaññātaṃ magganti amatassa maggo upagantvā ñāto. Ñāto ceva upagato cāti saha upasaggena padaṃ parivattitvā atthaṃ kathento upasaggattho ca dhātuttho ca visuṃyeva hotīti ñāpeti. Atthikehi amhehi upaññātaṃ [M 0.0215] nibbānaṃ maggaṃ magganto anubandheyyanti vā dassento āha “atha vā”tiādi. Maggaphalapaccavekkhaṇañāṇehi upagantvā ñātabbanti upaññātaṃ nibbānaṃ. Maggadhāthuyā anvesanatthaṃ dassento āha “pariyesanto”ti.

Showing in detail what was stated in brief, he says: 'idaṃ hī,' etc. 'Atthīkehī' means by those who have need of the deathless. 'Upaññātaṃ maggan' means the path to the deathless is known by having approached it. Saying the meaning as 'known and approached' by transposing the word together with its prefix, he makes it known that the meaning of the prefix and the meaning of the root are indeed separate. Or, showing that 'we who have need of it should follow the path to Nibbāna that has been made known,' he says: 'atha vā,' etc. Nibbāna is upaññātaṃ because it is to be known by approaching it with the knowledges of reviewing the path and fruit. Showing the meaning of the root 'magg' as 'searching,' he says: 'pariyesanto.'

Sāriputtopi pañhaṃ pucchīti sambandho. Kamaṇḍalutoti kuṇḍikato. Attano ca paresañca akathanena antare vivaraṃ paṭisandahatīti paṭisandhāro, taṃ. Etthāti “na tyāhaṃ sakkomī”tipade. Adhippāyo evaṃ veditabboti yojanā. Ettakanti ettakaṃ pañhaṃ. Imassāti paribbājakassa. Avisayabhāvanti attano avisayabhāvaṃ.

The connection is: Sāriputta too asked a question (Sāriputtopi pañhaṃ pucchi). Kamaṇḍaluto means from the water pot (kuṇḍikato). A friendly inquiry (paṭisandhāro) is so called because by not speaking of oneself and others it closes the gap in between; taṃ (that). Etthā means in the phrase 'na tyāhaṃ sakkomī.' The connection is: the intention should be understood thus. Ettakan means this much of a question. Imassā means of this wanderer. Avisayabhāvan means the state of its being beyond his own scope.

Hetuṃ paṭicca bhavantīti hetuppabhavāti vacanatthena pañcakkhandhā hetuppabhavā nāmāti dassento āha “hetuppabhavā nāma pañcakkhandhā”ti. Tenāti “ye dhammā hetuppabhavā”ti padena. Assāti sāriputtaparibbājakassa. “Tesaṃ hetu nāma samudayasacca”nti iminā hinoti etasmā phalanti hetūti vacanatthena samudayasaccaṃ hetu nāmāti dasseti. Tañcāti samudayasaccañca. Tesanti ettha tasaddassa visayaṃ dassetuṃ vuttaṃ “ubhinnampi saccāna”nti. Apavattivasena nirujjhati etthāti nirodho. Tañcāti nirodhañca. Tenāti “tesañca yo nirodho”tipadena. Assāti sāriputtaparibbājakassa. Etthāti imissaṃ gāthāyaṃ, catūsu saccesu vā. Nayatoti nānantarikanayato, avinābhāvanayato vā, nettidesanāhāranayato vā. Tamevatthaṃ pākaṭaṃ karonto āha “nirodhe hī”tiādi. Ekadesasarūpekasesanayena vā maggasaccaṃ gahetabbanti dassento āha “atha vā”tiādi. Nirodho ca nirodhūpāyo ca nirodhoti ekadesasarūpekaseso kātabbo. Tesañcāti ettha avuttasampiṇḍanatthena casaddena maggasaccaṃ gahetabbantipi vadanti. Ayaṃ nayo aṭṭhakathāyaṃ na vutto. Tamevatthanti catusaccasaṅkhātaṃ tamevatthaṃ. Paṭipādentoti nigamento.

Showing that by the verbal meaning 'they arise in dependence on a cause' (hetuṃ paṭicca bhavantīti), the five aggregates are called 'originated from a cause' (hetuppabhavā), he says: 'originated from a cause, namely, the five aggregates.' Tenā means by the phrase 'ye dhammā hetuppabhavā.' Assā means to the wanderer Sāriputta. By 'tesaṃ hetu nāma samudayasaccaṃ,' he shows that by the verbal meaning 'fruits proceed (hinoti) from this,' the truth of origin is called 'cause' (hetu). Tañcā means and the truth of origin. To show the referent of the word tesaṃ here, it is said: 'of both truths.' It ceases (nirujjhati) here by way of non-continuation (apavattivasena), thus it is cessation (nirodho). Tañcā means and cessation. Tenā means by the phrase 'tesañca yo nirodho.' Assā means to the wanderer Sāriputta. Etthā means in this verse, or in the four truths. Nayato means by the method of immediate succession, or by the method of invariable connection, or by the method of the guideline demonstration in the Nettippakaraṇa. Making that same meaning clear, he says: 'nirodhe hī,' etc. Or, showing that the truth of the path should be taken by the method of the single remainder of a partial form, he says: 'atha vā,' etc. A single remainder of a partial form should be made as: 'cessation and the way to cessation is cessation.' Here in tesañca, some say that the truth of the path should also be taken by the word ca with its meaning of including what has not been stated. This method is not stated in the commentary. Tamevatthan means that same meaning designated as the four truths. Paṭipādento means concluding.

“Sacepī”ti [M 0.0216] iminā yadīti padassatthaṃ vaṇṇeti. “Ettakamevā”ti iminā tāvadevāti padassatthaṃ [V 1.0189] vaṇṇeti. “Ito uttari natthī”ti iminā evakārassa phalaṃ dasseti. Itoti sotāpattiphalato. “Idaṃ…pe… pattabba”nti iminā “ettakamevā”ti padassa atthasarūpaṃ dasseti. “Eso eva dhammo”ti iminā “eseva dhammo”tipadassa atthaṃ vaṇṇeti. Paccabyatthāti patiavapubbo idhātu paṭividdhatthoti āha “paṭividdhatthā”ti. Tumhehīti assajittheraṃ sandhāyāha. Iminā “paccabyatthā”ti ettha hiyyattanīparassapadamajjhimapurisabahuvacanatthavibhattiṃ dīpeti. Kappanahutehīti kappānaṃ nahutehi, koṭipakoṭisatasahassānaṃ satehi nahutehīti attho. Abbhatītanti abhiatītaṃ. Amhehi adiṭṭhameva hutvā atikkamāpitanti attho.

With 'sacepi,' he explains the meaning of the word yadi. With 'ettakamevā,' he explains the meaning of the word tāvadeva. With 'ito uttari natthi,' he shows the effect of the particle eva. Ito means from the fruit of stream-entry. With 'idaṃ…pe… pattabba,' he shows the essential meaning of the phrase 'ettakamevā.' With 'eso eva dhammo,' he explains the meaning of the phrase 'eseva dhammo.' Paccabyatthā: the root i preceded by pati-ava has the meaning of 'penetrated', so he says 'paṭividdhatthā'. Tumhehī (by you): he says this referring to the Elder Assaji. With this, he indicates that here in 'paccabyatthā' there is the inflection of the aorist, active voice, second person plural. Kappanahutehī means by myriads of eons; the meaning is by hundreds of myriads of hundreds of thousands of crores of eons. Abbhatītan means gone beyond (abhi-atītaṃ). The meaning is: it was made to pass by, having been unseen by us.

62. Ārammaṇabhūtassa nibbānassa gambhīrattā ārammaṇikabhūtaṃ ñāṇampi gambhīramevādhippetanti āha “gambhīrassa ca ñāṇassā”ti. Yathā hi saṇhavatthassa sibbanatthāya saṇhasūci adhippetāti. Upadhīnaṃ sammā khayaṭṭhena nibbānaṃ upadhisaṅkhayaṃ nāmāti āha “upadhisaṅkhayeti nibbāne”ti. Tadārammaṇāyāti taṃnibbānārammaṇāya. Vimuttiyāti phalavimuttiyā. Sāvakapāramīñāṇeti aggasāvakapāramīñāṇe. Tesūti sāriputtamoggallānesu. Aḍḍhamāsena arahatte patiṭṭhitoti sambandho.

62. Due to the profundity of Nibbāna, which has become the object, the knowledge that has become the subject is also intended as profound. Thus he says: 'and of profound knowledge.' For it is like a fine needle being intended for sewing a fine cloth. Nibbāna is called the destruction of acquisitions (upadhisaṅkhayaṃ) because of its meaning as the complete destruction of the acquisitions (upadhīnaṃ). Thus he says: 'upadhisaṅkhaye, in Nibbāna.' Tadārammaṇāyā means for that which has Nibbāna as its object. Vimuttiyā means for the liberation of fruition. Sāvakapāramīñāṇe means in the knowledge of the perfections of the chief disciples. Tesū means in Sāriputta and Moggallāna. The connection is: established in arahantship in half a month (aḍḍhamāsena arahatte patiṭṭhito).

Atīteti kappasatasahassādhike asaṅkhyeyyamatthake. Tassāti buddhassa santike aggasāvakabhāvaṃ patthesīti yojanā. Assameti munīnaṃ ṭhāne. Tañhi ā kodhaṃ, ā bhuso vā rāgādayo samenti etthāti assamoti vuccati, tasmiṃ. Patthayitvā ca pesesīti sambandho. Tatthāti nīluppalamaṇḍape. Tesūti tāpasaseṭṭhīsu.

Atīte means at the head of an incalculable eon plus a hundred thousand eons. Tassā: the connection is, he aspired to the state of a chief disciple in the presence of that Buddha. Assame means in the place of the sages. For it is called a hermitage (assamo) because anger (kodhaṃ) or lust and other passions subside (samenti) completely (ā, bhuso vā) there; tasmiṃ (in that). The connection is: and having aspired, he sent (patthayitvā ca pesesi). Tatthā means in the blue water lily pavilion. Tesū means among the foremost ascetics.

63. Yesanti kulānaṃ. “Vidhavabhāvāyā”ti iminā vidhavāya bhāvo vedhabyanti vacanatthaṃ dasseti. Vidhavāti ca patisuññā. Sā hi dhavena vigatāti “vidhavā”ti ca, vigato dhavo imissāti “vidhavā”ti ca vuccati. Ubhayenāpīti puttapabbajjapatipabbajjasaṅkhātena duvidhenapi.

63. Yesan means of families. With 'vidhavabhāvāya,' he shows the verbal meaning of vedhabyaṃ as the state of a widow (vidhavāya bhāvo). And vidhavā means one bereft of a husband. For she is called 'vidhavā' because she is gone from a husband (dhavena vigatā), or because a husband is gone from her (vigato dhavo imissā). Ubhayenāpi means by both of the two kinds, designated as the going forth of a son and the going forth of a husband.

Sañcayānīti [M 0.0217] ettha nissayūpacārena nissaye nissitūpacāro hotīti āha “sañcayassa antevāsikānī”ti. Atha vā ṇapaccayo tassedamatthe hotīti āha “sañcayassa antevāsikānī”ti. “Magadhāna”nti bahuvacanavasena vuttattā janapadassa nāmanti āha “magadhānaṃ janapadassā”ti. Giribbajanti ettha vajo viyāti vajo, giri. Vajasadiso giri etthāti [V 1.0190] giribbajaṃ padaheṭṭhupariyavasena, nagaraṃ. “Mahāvīriyavanto”ti iminā mahanto vīro etesaṃ tathāgatānanti mahāvīrāti vacanatthaṃ dasseti. Dhammena nayamānānaṃ kā usūyā vijānatanti ettha kaccāyananayena (kaccāyane 277 sutte) usūyapayoge sampadānaṃ hotīti āsaṅkā bhaveyyāti āha “bhummatthe sāmivacanaṃ, upayogatthe vā”ti. Vijānantānanti vijānantesu tathāgatesu, vijānante vā.

Here in Sañcayānī, by the metaphor of the support, there is a metaphor of the supported for the support. Thus he says: 'the disciples of Sañcaya.' Alternatively, the suffix -ṇa is in the sense of 'this is his,' so he says: 'the disciples of Sañcaya.' Since 'Magadhānaṃ' is stated in the plural, it is the name of a country. Thus he says: 'of the country of the Magadhans.' Giribbajaṃ: here, a pen (vajo) is like a mountain (giri). A mountain like a pen is here, thus it is Giribbajaṃ, a city, by way of the area below and above the base. With 'mahāvīriyavanto,' he shows the verbal meaning of mahāvīrā as 'great is the hero of these, the Tathāgatas.' Here in 'dhammena nayamānānaṃ kā usūyā vijānatanti,' there might be a doubt that, according to the method of Kaccāyana (in Kaccāyana's Sutta 277), the dative is used with usūyā. Thus he says: 'the genitive is in the sense of the locative, or in the sense of the instrumental.' Vijānatanti means among the knowing Tathāgatas, or toward the knowing one.

15. Upajjhāyavattakathā

15. The Discourse on the Duties toward a Preceptor

64. Anupajjhāyakāti ettha vajjāvajjaṃ upagantvā jhāyatīti upajjhāyo, so natthi etesanti anupajjhāyakāti atthaṃ dassento āha “vajjāvajja”ntiādi. “Piṇḍāya caraṇakapatta”nti iminā piṇḍāya uddissa, uṭṭhahitvā vā tiṭṭhati anenāti uttiṭṭho, soyeva patto uttiṭṭhapattoti atthaṃ dasseti. “Uttiṭṭhe na pamajjeyyā”tiādīsu (dha. pa. 168) pana piṇḍāya caraṇaṃ “uttiṭṭha”nti vuccati. Tasmā tattha piṇḍāya uddissa, uṭṭhahitvā vā tiṭṭhanaṃ uttiṭṭhanti vacanattho kātabbo. “Piṇḍāya caraṇapatta”nti idaṃ vacanaṃ “tasmiñhi manussā ucchiṭṭhasaññino”tipadaṃ laṅghitvā “tasmā uttiṭṭhapattanti vutta”ntipadena yojetabbaṃ, tasmā piṇḍāya caraṇakapattattā uttiṭṭhapattanti vuttanti vuttaṃ hoti. Tasmiṃ manussā kiṃsaññinoti āha “tasmiñhi manussā ucchiṭṭhasaññino”ti. Tasmiñhi tasmiṃ eva uttiṭṭhapatte pabbajitānaṃ paribhogabhāvena manussehi avasajjitabbattā, avachaḍḍetabbattā vā manussā ucchiṭṭhasaññino hontīti yojanā. Pabbajitānaṃ piṇḍāya caraṇakapattattā uttiṭṭhapattanti vuttaṃ, manussānaṃ pana avasajjitapattattā ucchiṭṭhapattanti vuttanti adhippāyo. Uttiṭṭha pattantipadaṃ vākyameva, na samāsotipi dassento āha “atha [M 0.0218] vā”tiādi. “Uṭṭhahitvā”ti iminā uttiṭṭhāti ettha tvālopoti dasseti. “Gahetu”nti iminā pāṭhasesaṃ dasseti. Gehasitapemavasenāti gehe nissitapemavasena, mettāpubbaṅgamapemavasenāti attho. Sagāravā hutvā sappatissā hutvā viharantāti atthaṃ dassento āha “upaṭṭhapetvā”ti. “Sabhāgajīvikā”ti iminā sabhāgavuttikāti ettha vuttisaddo jīvikatthoyeva, na vivaraṇādyatthoti dasseti. Upajjhāyabhāvaṃ sampaṭicchati etehīti upajjhāyabhāvasampaṭicchanāni, tāniyeva vevacanāni upajjhāyabhāvasampaṭicchanavevacanāni. Tikkhattunti ukkaṭṭhavasena vuttaṃ, sakimpi vaṭṭatiyeva. Padassa vasena viññāpetīti sambandho. Hīti saccaṃ. Etthāti upajjhāyagahaṇaṭṭhāne. Yadidaṃ vācāya vā sāvanaṃ, yadidaṃ kāyena vā atthaviññāpanaṃ atthi, idameva sāvanaatthaviññāpanameva upajjhāyagahaṇanti yojanā. Sādhūti sampaṭicchananti upajjhāyena [V 1.0191] pañcasu padesu yasmiṃ kismiṃci vutte saddhivihārikassa “sādhū”ti sampaṭicchanaṃ. Tanti kesañci vacanaṃ. Hīti saccaṃ, yasmā vā. Etthāti upajjhāyagahaṇe. “Na sampaṭicchanaṃ aṅga”nti iminā āyācanadānāniyeva aṅgāni nāmāti dasseti. Saddhivihārikenāpi ñātunti sambandho. Iminā padenāti “sādhū”ti iminā padena.

64. Herein, regarding the words 'without a preceptor' (anupajjhāyakā): A preceptor (upajjhāya) is one who, having approached what is blameworthy and blameless, reflects upon it. Since they do not have one, they are 'without a preceptor.' To show this meaning, he says: 'blameworthy and blameless,' etc. By the words 'a bowl for going on almsround,' he shows the meaning of uttiṭṭhapatta (risen-bowl) thus: it is for the sake of alms; one rises up or stands by means of it, thus it is an uttiṭṭha. That very bowl is an uttiṭṭhapatta. However, in such passages as 'One should rise up, one should not be heedless' (Dhp 168), going for alms is called uttiṭṭha. Therefore, in that context, the verbal meaning of uttiṭṭha should be understood as 'rising up' or 'standing' for the sake of alms. The phrase 'a bowl for going on almsround' should be connected with the words 'therefore it is called an uttiṭṭhapatta,' skipping over the phrase 'for in it people have the perception of leftovers.' Thus, it is said that because it is a bowl for going on almsround, it is called an uttiṭṭhapatta. What perception do people have in regard to it? He says: 'for in it people have the perception of leftovers.' The construction is: For in that very uttiṭṭhapatta, because it is to be used by the renunciants and thus to be given up or discarded by laypeople, people have the perception of it as leftovers (ucchiṭṭha). The intended meaning is: for the renunciants, because it is a bowl for going on almsround, it is called an uttiṭṭhapatta; but for laypeople, because it is a bowl to be given up, it is called an ucchiṭṭhapatta (leftover-bowl). To show that the words uttiṭṭha pattaṃ are a clause and not a compound, he says: 'Or alternatively,' etc. By 'having risen' (uṭṭhahitvā), he shows that in uttiṭṭha there is an elision of the suffix -tvā. By 'to take' (gahetuṃ), he indicates the rest of the reading. Gehasitapemavasena means: through affection connected with the home, that is, through affection preceded by loving-kindness. To show the meaning of 'they dwell respectfully and with deference,' he says: 'having attended upon.' By 'of similar livelihood,' he shows that in sabhāgavuttikā, the word vutti has only the meaning of livelihood, not of explanation and so on. Upajjhāyabhāvasampaṭicchanāni means the acts of accepting the state of a preceptor. These very terms are synonyms for the acceptance of the state of a preceptor. 'Three times' is said as the maximum; even once is permissible. The connection is: 'he makes it known by means of the word.' Hi means truly. Ettha means in the context of taking a preceptor. The construction is: Whatever verbal announcement there is, or whatever intimation of the meaning by the body there is, this very announcement and intimation of meaning is the taking of a preceptor. 'Good' is acceptance: this is the co-resident's acceptance by saying 'Good' when the preceptor has spoken on any of the five points. That is the view of some. Hi means truly, or because. Ettha means in the taking of a preceptor. By 'acceptance is not a factor,' he shows that only the request and the granting are factors. The connection is: 'it should also be known by the co-resident.' 'By this word' means by the word 'Good.'

Tatrāyaṃ sammāvattanāti ettha tasaddassa visayaṃ dassetuṃ vuttaṃ “yaṃ vuttaṃ sammā vattitabba”nti. Iminā kiriyāvisayabhāvameva dīpeti, na dabbavisayabhāvaṃ. Ayanti vuccamānā. Assāti saddhivihārikassa. Dhotapādapariharaṇatthāyāti dhotassa pādassa paṃsumakkhanādīnaṃ pariharaṇatthāya. Tāti upāhanāyo. Kālassevāti paccūsakālatoyeva, nissakkatthe cetaṃ sāmivacanaṃ. Tatoti tehi tīhi dantakaṭṭhehi, vibhattaapādānametaṃ. Tesu vā tīsu dantakaṭṭhesu. Yanti yaṃ dantakaṭṭhaṃ. Athāti tasmiṃ gahaṇe.

Herein, regarding 'this is the proper conduct': to show the domain of the word ta (that), it is said: 'that which was stated should be properly practiced.' By this he clarifies that it is the object of an action, not the object as a substance. Ayaṃ (this) means: that which is being spoken of. Assa (his) means: of the co-resident. 'For the purpose of protecting the washed feet' means: for the purpose of protecting the washed feet from being smeared with dust and so on. Tā (those) means: the sandals. Kālasseva means: just at the time of dawn. And this genitive is in the sense of separation. Tato means: from those three tooth-sticks; this is an ablative of separation. Or: among those three tooth-sticks. Yaṃ means: whichever tooth-stick. Atha means: at the time of taking it.

Tatoti sītuṇhodakehi, sītuṇhodakesu vā. Vaḷañjetīti paribhuñjati. Udakanti mukhadhovanodakaṃ. “Vaccakuṭito”ti iminā passāvakuṭīpi [M 0.0219] gahetabbā. Evanti sammajjiyamāne. Asuññanti janasaddato atucchaṃ. Āsananti therassa āsanaṃ. Tasminti āsane. Nisinnassa therassa vattaṃ kātabbanti sambandho. Uklāpo asmiṃ dese atthīti uklāpoti atthaṃ dassento āha “kenaci kacavarena saṃkiṇṇo”ti. Ettha ca saṅkāro ucchiṭṭho kalāpo samūho uklāpoti vacanatthena uklāpoti vuccati. Kacīyati bandhīyati asmiṃ deseti kaco, so varīyati icchīyati anenāti kacavaroti vacanatthena kacavaroti vuccati. Hatthenapīti ettha pisaddo pilotikenapītiādiṃ saṅgaṇhāti.

Tato means: with cool and warm water, or in cool and warm water. Vaḷañjeti means: he uses. Udakaṃ means: water for washing the mouth. By vaccakuṭito (from the toilet), the urinal should also be understood. Evaṃ means: while it is being swept. Asuññaṃ means: not devoid of the sound of people. Āsanaṃ means: the elder's seat. Tasmiṃ means: on that seat. The connection is: 'the duties for the elder who is seated should be done.' To show the meaning of uklāpo as 'there is rubbish in this place,' he says: 'strewn with some kind of sweepings.' And here, saṅkāra is refuse; a heap (kalāpa, samūha) of leftovers (ucchiṭṭha) is called uklāpo based on its verbal derivation. Kaco is so called because things are tied up or bound (kacīyati, bandhīyati) in this place; kacavara is so called from the verbal derivation because it is chosen (varīyati) or desired (icchīyati) by that. In hatthenāpi (even with the hand), the particle pi also includes 'even with a rag,' and so on.

Ekato katvāti ekato samānapaṭalaṃ katvā. Kasmā saṅghāṭīti āha “sabbaṃ hī”tiādi. “Saṅghaṭitattā”ti iminā saṃharitabbāti saṅghāṭīti vacanatthaṃ dasseti. Nivattitvā olokentaṃ upajjhāyaṃ saṃpāpuṇātīti yojanā. Ekena vā padavītihārenāti sambandho. Pattoyeva uṇhabhārikesu pariyāpannoti pattapariyāpanno, patte pariyāpanno yāguādiko pattapariyāpannotipi yujjatiyeva. Bhikkhācāreti bhikkhācāraṭṭhāne. Yāguyā vā laddhāyāti sambandho. Tassāti upajjhāyassa. So pattoti uṇhādīsu pariyāpanno so patto. Aññatra vāti ārāmādīsu vā. Tassāti upajjhāyassa. Vacane aniṭṭhiteti sambandho. Ito paṭṭhāyāti “na upajjhāyassa bhaṇamānassā”ti ettha vuttanakārato paṭṭhāya. Iminā heṭṭhā vuttesu “nātidūre gantabba”ntiādīsu nakārapaṭisiddhesu āpatti natthīti dasseti. Yattha katthacīti “na [V 1.0192] ca uṇhe cīvaraṃ nidahitabba”ntiādīsu yesu kesuci. Ayanti dukkaṭāpatti. Hīti saccaṃ. Āpattisāmantāti ettha āpattiyā sāmantā āpattisāmantāti atthaṃ dassento āha “āpattiyā āsanna”nti. “Āsanna”nti iminā sāmantāsaddassa āsannavevacanatañca upayogatthe nissakkavacanatañca dasseti. Īdisaṃ vacanaṃ bhante vattuṃ vaṭṭati nāmāti yojanā.

Ekato katvā (having made it one) means: having made it into a single, even layer. Why is it a saṅghāṭī? He says: 'Because all,' etc. By 'because it is joined together' (saṅghaṭitattā), he shows the verbal meaning of saṅghāṭī as 'it should be collected together' (saṃharitabbā). The construction is: it reaches the preceptor who turns around and looks. Or the connection is with 'by a single footstep.' The bowl itself is included among heavy, warm things, thus it is pattapariyāpanno (included in the bowl). Or, what is included in the bowl, such as gruel, etc., is pattapariyāpanno. This is also fitting. Bhikkhācāre means: in the place for the almsround. The connection is with 'or when gruel has been received.' Tassa means: of the preceptor. So patto means: that bowl which is included among warm things, etc. Aññatra vā means: or in the monastery, etc. Tassa means: of the preceptor. The connection is with 'when his speech is not finished.' 'From this point onwards' means: starting from the negative particle na stated here in 'not while the preceptor is speaking.' By this he shows that for the prohibitions stated earlier with the negative particle, such as 'one should not go too far,' there is no offense. Yattha katthaci means: in any of the cases such as 'and a robe should not be placed in the heat.' Ayaṃ means: this offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭāpatti). Hi means: truly. Herein, regarding āpattisāmantā: to show the meaning of āpattisāmantā as 'what is adjacent to an offense,' he says: 'proximate to an offense.' By 'proximate,' he shows that the word sāmanta is a synonym for āsanna (proximate) and that it is a statement of what is not allowable in usage. The construction is: 'Venerable sir, is it proper to say such a thing?'

Gāmato [M 0.0220] paṭhamataranti gāmato upajjhāyassa paṭhamataraṃ. Tenevāti upajjhāyeneva. Nivattantena saddhivihārikenāti sambandho. “Tinta”nti vatvā tamevatthaṃ dassetuṃ vuttaṃ “sedaggahita”nti. Iminā sedena sīdatīti sinnanti atthaṃ dasseti. “Atirekaṃ katvā”ti iminā ussāretvātipadassa adhippāyatthaṃ dasseti, uddhaṃ uddhaṃ sāretvāti vuttaṃ hoti. Pacchimavākyassa pubbavākyakāraṇabhāvaṃ dassetuṃ vuttaṃ “kiṃ kāraṇā”ti. Majjhe bhaṅgassa dosaṃ āvikaronto āha “samaṃ katvā”tiādi. Tatoti samaṃ katvā saṃharaṇato, niccaṃ bhijjamānanti sambandho. Majjhe bhaṅgato vā, dubbalanti sambandho. Etanti “caturaṅgulaṃ kaṇṇaṃ ussāretvā”ti etaṃ vacanaṃ. Yathāti yenākārena saṃhariyamāneti sambandho. Cīvarabhogassa oro anto obhogoti atthaṃ dassento āha “kāyabandhana”ntiādi.

Gāmato paṭhamataraṃ means: ahead of the preceptor from the village. Teneva means: by the preceptor himself. The connection is with 'by the co-resident who is returning.' Having said tintaṃ (wet), to show that very meaning it is said 'affected by sweat.' By this he shows the meaning of sinnaṃ as 'it sinks (sīdati) with sweat.' By 'having made it extra,' he shows the intended meaning of the word ussāretvā (having raised). It means 'having shifted it higher and higher.' To show that the preceding statement is the reason for the latter statement, it is said: 'For what reason?' Making clear the fault in its breaking in the middle, he says: 'having made it even,' etc. Tato means: from folding it after making it even; the connection is with 'it constantly breaks.' Or, because it breaks in the middle; the connection is with 'it is weak.' Etaṃ refers to this statement: 'having raised the corner four finger-breadths.' Yathā (as): the connection is with 'in whatever way it is being folded.' To show the meaning of obhogo as the lower limit of the wearing of the robe, he says: 'the waistband,' etc.

Yoti upajjhāyo. “Gāmeyevā”ti vatvā tamevatthaṃ dassetuṃ vuttaṃ “antaraghare vā paṭikkamane vā”ti. Paṭikkamane vāti bhojanasālāyaṃ vā. Tassāti upajjhāyassa. Laddhā bhikkhā yenāti laddhabhikkho, tassa vā. Piṇḍapāto hotīti yojanā. Tassāti upajjhāyassa. Piṇḍapāto na hotīti sambandho. Attanā laddhopīti pisaddo upajjhāyena laddhopīti atthaṃ sampiṇḍeti. Āhariyatūti ettha tuvibhatti pucchāyaṃ hoti, āhariyatu kinti attho. Kāloti bhojanakālo. Bhuñjitthāti bhutto, tasmiṃ satīti sambandho. Upakaṭṭhoti majjhanhikassa āsanno.

Yo means: the preceptor. Having said 'in the village itself,' to show that very meaning it is said: 'either inside a house or at the retreat.' 'At the retreat' means: or in the dining hall. Tassa means: of the preceptor. Laddhabhikkho means: one by whom alms have been received; or, of him. The construction is: 'there is almsfood.' Tassa means: of the preceptor. The connection is: 'there is no almsfood.' In 'even if obtained by oneself,' the particle pi (even) also combines the meaning 'even if obtained by the preceptor.' In āhariyatu (let him bring), the suffix -tu is in the sense of a question. The meaning is: 'Should he bring it?' Kālo means: the time for eating. Bhuñjittha means: he has eaten. The connection is: 'when this is so.' Upakaṭṭho means: near to midday.

Anantarahitāyāti ettha antaradhāyatīti antarahito, taṭṭikacammakhaṇḍādi, natthi antarahito etasmiṃ pattabhūmīnamantareti anantarahitoti atthaṃ dassento āha “anatthatāyā”ti. Kāḷavaṇṇakatā vā sudhābaddhā vā nirajamattikā hotīti yojanā. Tanti pattaṃ. Dhotavālikāyapīti suddhavālikāyapi. Tatthāti paṃsurajasakkharādīsu. Puna tatthāti paṇṇādhārakesu. Idaṃ vacanaṃ vuttanti sambandho. Abhimukhenāti attano abhimukhena. Saṇikanti sinnaṃ[M 0.0221]. Ante panāti cīvarassa koṭiyaṃ pana. Nikkhipantassa saddhivihārikassa cīvarassa bhogoti yojanā.

Herein, 'uninterrupted' (anantarahitāya): what is interposed is 'interrupted' (antarahito), such as a mat or a piece of leather. 'There is no interruption in this between the bowl and the ground, thus it is "uninterrupted"'—explaining the meaning thus, he said, 'for non-detriment' (anatthatāya). 'It is either blackened, or plastered with stucco, or is dust-free clay'—this is the construction. 'That' means the bowl. 'Even on washed sand' means on pure sand. 'There' means on dust, dirt, gravel, and so on. 'Again there' means on leaf-stands. 'This statement was said'—this is the connection. 'Facing' means facing oneself. 'Gently' means wet. 'But at the edge' means at the hem of the robe. 'The fold of the robe of the co-resident who is placing it down'—this is the construction.

Cuṇṇaṃ [V 1.0193] sannetabbanti ettha cuṇṇasamodhānena netabbanti atthaṃ dassento āha “piṇḍi kātabbā”ti. “Ekasmiṃ niddhūme ṭhāne”ti iminā ekamantanti ettha ekasmiṃ ante ṭhāneti atthaṃ dasseti. Jantāghareti aggisālāyaṃ. Sā hi jalati dibbati aggi etthāti jantā, janeti sarīrasedametthāti vā jantā, sā eva gharaṃ jantāgharanti vuccati, tasmiṃ. Paripūjāvasena karīyatīti parikammanti atthena aṅgāradānādikaṃ parikammaṃ nāmāti dassento āha “parikammaṃ nāmā”tiādi.

'Powder should be kneaded': here, explaining the meaning as 'it should be mixed by combining the powder,' he said, 'a ball should be made.' By 'in one smokeless place,' he shows the meaning of `ekamantaṃ` here as 'in a place to one side.' 'In the steam bath' means in the fire-hall. For 'fire burns and shines in it,' thus it is a `jantā`; or 'it generates bodily sweat in it,' thus it is a `jantā`. That very building is called a `jantāghara`, a steam bath; in that. Explaining that 'preliminary work' (`parikamma`) means 'what is done by way of thorough service,' he shows that giving embers and so on is called 'preliminary work,' saying, 'preliminary work is called…,' and so on.

“Na kenaci gelaññenā”tiādinā ussahanassa kāraṇaṃ dasseti. Hīti saccaṃ. Agilānena saṭṭhivassena saddhivihārikenāpi kātabbanti yojanā. Anādarenāti vattakaraṇassa anādarena. Nakārapaṭisaṃyuttesūti paṭisedhavācakena nakārena paṭisaṃyuttesu. Padesūti “na upajjhāyassa bhaṇamānassa antarantarā kathā opātetabbā”tiādīsu vākyesu. Bhūmiyanti upalakkhaṇavasena vuttaṃ bhittiyampi apaṭighaṃsitabbattā. “Piṭhasaṅghāṭañcā”ti iminā kavāṭapīḷanti ettha pīṭhasaddena piṭhasaṅghāṭaṃ vuccati uttarapadalopavasena vā ekadesavohāravasena vāti dasseti. “Acchupantenā”ti iminā appaṭighaṃsantenāti ettha ghaṃsadhātuyā atthaṃ dasseti. Sammā tāyati attānañca parañca anenāti santānaṃ, tameva santānakanti atthena kīṭakulāvakamakkaṭakasuttādi santānakaṃ nāmāti dassento āha “santānaka”ntiādi. Ullokatoti vitānato. Tañhi uddhaṃ lucīyate bandhīyateti ullokanti vuccati, cakārassa kakāramakatvā “ulloca”ntipi vuccati. Tosaddena ākārassa smāvacanassa kāriyabhāvaṃ dasseti. Apaharitabbanti apanetabbaṃ. “Avaharitabba”ntipi pāṭho, heṭṭhā haritabbaṃ pātetabbanti attho.

By 'Not because of any illness,' etc., he shows the reason for the exertion. 'Hi' means truly. 'It should be done even by a healthy sixty-year-old co-resident'—this is the construction. 'Through disrespect' means through disrespect for performing the duties. 'In those connected with the letter "na"' means in those connected with the negative particle 'na.' 'In the passages' means in sentences such as 'One should not interrupt the preceptor's speech with intervening talk.' 'On the ground' is said by way of synecdoche, since a wall too should not be rubbed against. By 'and a stool-frame,' he shows that in the word `kavāṭapīḷa` (door-bench), the word `pīṭha` (stool) refers to a `piṭhasaṅghāṭa` (stool-frame), either by elision of the latter part of the compound or by synecdoche. By 'without touching,' he shows the meaning of the root `ghaṃs` in the word `appaṭighaṃsantena` (without rubbing against). Explaining that 'it properly protects oneself and others,' thus it is a `santāna` (canopy), and that this very thing is a `santānaka`, he shows that cobwebs, spiders' threads, and so on, are called `santānaka`, saying, '`santānaka`…,' and so on. 'From the ceiling' means from the canopy. For it is pulled up and tied above, thus it is called an `ulloka`. By making the 'k' into a 'c', it is also called `ulloca`. By the suffix `-to`, he shows that it functions as the ablative ending `-smā`. 'It should be removed' means it should be taken away. There is also the reading `avaharitabbaṃ`; the meaning is 'it should be brought down and dropped'.

Ālokasandhibhāgāti [M 0.0222] ettha bhāgasaddassa dvandato parattā pubbapadesupi paccekaṃ yojetabboti āha “ālokasandhibhāgā ca kaṇṇabhāgā cā”ti. Tassa atthaṃ dassento āha “antarabāhirā”tiādi. “Vātapānakavāṭakānī”ti iminā ālokasandhisaddassa vātapānakavāṭakapariyāyabhāvaṃ dasseti. “Koṇā”ti iminā kaṇṇasaddassa koṇavevacanabhāvaṃ dasseti.

'The parts of the window-joints': Here, because the word 'part' comes after the dvandva compound, it should be applied individually to the preceding terms as well. Thus he says: 'the parts of the window-joints and the parts of the corners.' Explaining its meaning, he said, 'inner and outer,' and so on. By 'windows and shutters,' he shows that the term `ālokasandhi` is a synonym for windows and shutters. By 'corners,' he shows that the word `kaṇṇa` is a synonym for corner.

“Yathā paṭhama”ntiādinā paṭhamapaññattameva paññapetabbaṃ, na aññathāti dasseti. Idaṃ patirūpaṃ paṭhamapaññattaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ. Paṭhamapaññatte apatirūpe aññathāpi paññapetabbaṃ. Etadatthamevāti yathāpaññattaṃ paññapetabbassa atthāya eva. Sace paññattaṃ ahosi, evaṃ satīti yojanā. Idanti bhittiṃ mocetvā paññāpanaṃ. Kaṭesu kiḷañjesu sārattā uttamattā kaṭasārakoti [V 1.0194] vuccati. Nivattetvāti saṃharitvā. Puratthimāti ettha yakāralopena niddesoti āha “puratthimāyā”ti.

By 'Just as at first,' etc., he shows that it should be laid out exactly as it was first laid out, not otherwise. This is said with reference to a suitable first arrangement. If the first arrangement is unsuitable, it may be laid out otherwise. 'For this very purpose' means solely for the purpose of laying it out as it was arranged. 'If it was arranged, this being so'—this is the construction. 'This' means laying it out after removing it from the wall. Because it is the core and the best among mats and screens, it is called `kaṭasāraka`. 'Having rolled it up' means having gathered it up. '`Puratthimā`' (eastern): here, it is a directive with the elision of the letter 'y'; thus he says, '`puratthimāyā`'.

Vūpakāsetabboti ettha kasadhātu gatyatthoti āha “aññattha netabbo”ti. Upajjhāyaṃ gahetvā aññattha gantabboti attho. Aññatthāti aññaṃ ṭhānaṃ. Vivecetabbanti ettha diṭṭhigatato upajjhāyaṃ vivecetabbanti dassento āha “vissajjāpetabba”nti. “Añño vattabbo”ti vatvā tassa ākāraṃ dasseti “thera”ntiādinā. So so bhikkhu yācitabboti sambandho. Aññena dāpetabboti attanā aññena bhikkhunā upajjhāyassa parivāso dāpetabboti attho. Kinti nu khoti kena eva upāyena dadeyya nukhoti attho. Itisaddo hi avadhāraṇattho. Aṭṭhakathāyapi imameva nayaṃ dasseti “kena nu kho upāyenā”ti iminā. Sabbatthāti sabbesu “kinti nu kho paṭikasseyyā”tiādivākyesu. Sattasu kammesu tividhassa ukkhepanīyakammassa garukattā vuttaṃ “ukkhepanīyaṃ akatvā”ti. Tamevatthaṃ vitthārento āha “tena hī”tiādi.

'He should be removed': Here the root `kas` has the meaning of motion; thus he says, 'he should be led elsewhere.' The meaning is that one should take the preceptor and go elsewhere. 'Elsewhere' means to another place. 'He should be dissociated': here, showing that the preceptor should be dissociated from his wrong view, he says, 'he should be made to give it up.' Having said, 'Another should be addressed,' he shows the manner of doing so with 'An elder…,' etc. 'This or that bhikkhu should be requested'—this is the connection. 'It should be caused to be given by another': the meaning is that the probation (`parivāsa`) should be caused to be given to the preceptor by another bhikkhu, not by oneself. 'How then?': the meaning is, 'By what means indeed should he give it?.' The word `iti` is indeed for emphasis. The commentary too shows this same method with 'By what means, then?.' 'In all cases' means in all sentences such as 'How, then, should one remove him?.' Because the threefold act of suspension is the most serious among the seven formal acts, it is said, 'without having performed the act of suspension.' Elaborating on that very meaning, he says, 'Therefore…,' and so on.

Tena [M 0.0223] saddhivihārikena yācitabbāti sambandho. Sace karontiyevāti bhikkhū sace kammaṃ karontiyeva. Puna sace karontiyevāti bhikkhū sace ukkhepanīyakammaṃ karontiyeva. Athāti tasmiṃ kamme kate. Itīti evaṃ yācanena. Nanti taṃ upajjhāyaṃ.

'He should be requested by that co-resident'—this is the connection. 'If they indeed act' means if the bhikkhus indeed perform the formal act. 'Again, if they indeed act' means if the bhikkhus indeed perform the formal act of suspension. 'Then' means when that formal act has been done. 'Thus' means in this way, by requesting. 'Him' means that preceptor.

Samparivattakanti ettha “piṇḍukkhepaka”ntiādīsu (pāci. 620) viya samparivattakantipadaṃ kiriyāvisesanaṃ, kapaccayo ca vicchatthoti āha “samparivattetvā samparivattetvā”ti. Yadīti yāva. Yadisaddo hi yāvapariyāyo, tena vuttaṃ “na tāva pakkamitabba”nti. Yāva appamattakampi rajanaṃ galati, na tāva pakkamitabbanti yojanā. Visabhāgapuggalenāti visabhāgena puggalena karaṇabhūtena. Na upajjhāyaṃ anāpucchā gāmo pavisitabboti ettha na aññeneva karaṇīyena pavisitabbo. Piṇḍāya pana pavisitabboti āsaṅkā bhaveyyāti āha “piṇḍāya vā”tiādi. “Anāpucchitvā”ti iminā anāpucchāti ettha ākāro tvāpaccayassa kāriyoti dasseti. Bhikkhācāranti bhikkhāya caraṇaṭṭhānaṃ, upajjhāyena gantabbanti yojanā. Pariveṇanti upajjhāyassa pariveṇaṃ. Passatīti upajjhāyaṃ passati.

`Samparivattakaṃ`: Here, as in `piṇḍukkhepakaṃ` (Pāc. 620), etc., the word `samparivattakaṃ` is an adverb, and the suffix `-ka` has a distributive sense; thus he says, 'having turned it over and over.' 'If' (`yadi`) means 'as long as' (`yāva`). For the word `yadi` is a synonym for `yāva`; therefore it is said, 'one should not depart so long.' 'As long as even a little dye drips, one should not depart so long'—this is the construction. 'By a dissimilar person' means by a dissimilar person in the instrumental sense. 'A village should not be entered without asking the preceptor': here, it means it should not be entered for any other business. Lest there be the doubt, 'But may one enter for alms?,' he says, 'or for alms,' and so on. By 'without having asked' (`anāpucchitvā`), he shows that the final `ā` in `anāpucchā` has the function of the gerund suffix `-tvā`. 'The alms-round' means the place for wandering for alms; 'it should be gone to with the preceptor'—this is the construction. 'The monastic cell' means the preceptor's monastic cell. 'He sees' means he sees the preceptor.

Dassanatthāya vāti asubhadassanatthāya vā. Imināpi vāsatthāya eva na gantabbanti āsaṅkaṃ [V 1.0195] nivatteti. Kammanti pakkamanassa kāraṇaṃ kammaṃ. Ananujānanaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ “yāvatatiya”nti. Tanti upajjhāyaṃ. Assāti saddhivihārikassa. “Na sampajjatī”ti iminā sace sampajjati, na pakkamitabbāti dasseti. Kevalanti vinā uddesādisampajjanehi. Evarūpe upajjhāye nivārentepīti yojanā. “Gelaññato”ti iminā vuṭṭhānasaddassa avadhiapekkhataṃ dasseti. Assāti upajjhāyassa. Aññoti attanā añño. Tassāti aññassa bhikkhussa.

'Or for the purpose of seeing' means or for the purpose of seeing the foul. By this too he dispels the doubt that one should not go even just for the purpose of dwelling. 'Act' means the act that is the reason for departing. 'Up to the third time' is said with reference to his not giving permission. 'Him' means the preceptor. 'Of him' means of the co-resident. By 'it does not succeed,' he shows that if it does succeed, one should not depart. 'Merely' means without the accomplishment of recitation and so on. 'Even when such a preceptor is restraining him'—this is the construction. By 'from illness,' he shows that the word 'recovery' (`vuṭṭhāna`) requires a boundary. 'Of him' means of the preceptor. 'Another' means another than oneself. 'Of him' means of another bhikkhu.

16. Saddhivihārikavattakathā

16. The Explanation of the Duties of a Co-resident

67. Sammāvattanāyaṃ [M 0.0224] vinicchayo evaṃ veditabboti yojanā. Uddesādīhīti ādisaddena paripucchādayo saṅgaṇhāti. Saṅgahasaddassa saṅkhepagahaṇesupi vuttito “anuggaho”ti vuttaṃ. Atha vā sammukhā saṅgaho ca parammukhā anuggaho ca kātabbo. Āmisena vā saṅgaho, dhammena vā anuggaho. Diṭṭhadhammikatthāya vā saṅgaho, samparāyikatthāya vā anuggaho. Lokiyatthāya vā saṅgaho, lokuttaratthāya vā anuggaho kātabbo. Tatthāti yaṃ vuttaṃ “uddesena paripucchāya ovādena anusāsanīyā”ti. Tattha uddisanaṃ uddesoti vacanatthena pāḷivācanā uddeso nāmāti dassento āha “uddesoti pāḷivācanā”ti. “Pāḷiyā atthavaṇṇanā”ti iminā punappunaṃ, samantato vā pāḷiyā atthassa pucchanaṃ paripucchāti atthaṃ dasseti. Vatthusminti cārittavārittavatthusmiṃ. Idanti cārittaṃ. Puna idanti vārittaṃ. “Vacana”nti iminā ovadanaṃ ovādoti vacanatthaṃ dasseti. Otiṇṇe vatthusmiṃ “idaṃ karohi, idaṃ mā karitthā”ti vacanaṃ anusāsanī nāmāti yojanā. “Punappunaṃ vacana”nti iminā anusāsanīti ettha anusaddassa naupacchinnatthaṃ dasseti. “Sace upajjhāyassa patto hotī”ti sāmaññato vuttepi na pakatipatto hoti, atha kho atirittapatto hotīti āha “atirekapatto”ti. Sabbatthāti sabbesu “sace upajjhāyassa cīvaraṃ hotī”tiādīsu padesu. Aññopīti pattacīvarehi aññopi. Samaṇaparikkhāroti chattupāhanādi samaṇaparikkhāro. Idhāti saddhivihārikavatte. Nayenāti ñāyena. Uppajjamānaupāyapariyesananti uppajjamānassa, uppajjamānatthāya vā upāyassa pariyesanaṃ. Itoti “kinti nu kho saddhivihārikassa parikkhāro uppajjiyethā”ti pāḷito. Cīvaraṃ rajantenāti ettha rajantena upajjhāyenāti attho na daṭṭhabbo, saddhivihārikenāti attho evāti dassento āha “upajjhāyato upāyaṃ sutvā rajantenā”ti. Upajjhāyato upāyanti upajjhāyato laddhaṃ upāyaṃ.

67. The construction is: the decision on proper conduct should be understood thus. By ‘recitation, etc.’: by the word ‘etc.’ he includes questioning and so on. Since the word saṅgaha is also used in the sense of a concise inclusion, it is said to be ‘assistance’ (anuggaha). Or, support (saṅgaha) should be given face-to-face and assistance (anuggaha) should be given when one is not present. Or, support is with material things, assistance is with the Dhamma. Or, support is for benefit in this life, assistance is for benefit in the lives to come. Or, support is for a worldly purpose, assistance is for a supramundane purpose. Therein: concerning what was said, ‘by recitation, questioning, advice, and instruction.’ Therein, since the verbal sense of uddesa is ‘pointing out,’ he shows that uddesa means the recitation of the Pāli, saying: ‘Uddesa means the recitation of the Pāli.’ By ‘the explanation of the meaning of the Pāli,’ he shows that paripucchā means to repeatedly and thoroughly question the meaning of the Pāli. ‘In the matter’: in the matter of what should be practiced and what should be avoided. ‘This’: what should be practiced. ‘Again this’: what should be avoided. By ‘speaking,’ he shows the verbal sense that ovāda is advising. The construction is: when a matter has arisen, the statement, ‘Do this; do not do that,’ is called anusāsanī, instruction. By ‘repeated speaking,’ he shows that the prefix anu- here in anusāsanī indicates what is uninterrupted. ‘If the preceptor has a bowl’: although this is stated generally, it is not a regular bowl but an extra bowl; thus he says ‘an extra bowl.’ ‘In all cases’: in all passages such as, ‘If the preceptor has a robe.’ ‘Another’: another apart from the bowl and robe. ‘Requisites of a recluse’: the requisites of a recluse such as an umbrella, sandals, etc. ‘Here’: in the duties of a co-resident. ‘By the method’: by the right way. ‘The seeking of a means for what is arising’: the seeking of a means for what is arising or for the sake of what is arising. ‘From this’: from the Pāli text, ‘How, indeed, might requisites arise for the co-resident?’ ‘When a robe is being dyed’: here, the meaning should not be taken as ‘by the preceptor who is dyeing,’ but only as ‘by the co-resident’; showing this, he says: ‘by one who is dyeing after having heard the method from the preceptor.’ ‘The method from the preceptor’: the method obtained from the preceptor.

Nasammāvattanādikathā

The Explanation of Improper Conduct, etc.

68. Upajjhāyavattanti [V 1.0196][M 0.0225] upajjhāyamhi vattitabbaṃ vattaṃ. Soti saddhivihāriko. Dukkaṭaṃ āpajjatīti assa, so vā dukkaṭaṃ āpajjatīti yojanā. Paṇāmetabboti ettha papubba namudhātu atthapakaraṇādivasena idha apasādanatthoti āha “apasādetabbo”ti. Adhimattanti adhikappamāṇaṃ. Gehasitapemanti mettāsinehaṃ. Vuttapaṭipakkhanayenāti kaṇhapakkhe vuttena paṭipakkhena nayena. Alaṃ paṇāmetunti ettha alaṃsaddassa arahatthapaṭikkhittesu dvīsu atthesu arahatthoti āha “yutto paṇāmetu”nti.

68. ‘The duties toward the preceptor’: the duty to be observed in regard to the preceptor. ‘He’: the co-resident. ‘He incurs a dukkaṭa offense’: the construction is, ‘a dukkaṭa offense is incurred by him,’ or ‘he incurs a dukkaṭa offense.’ ‘Should be dismissed’: here, the root nam with the prefix pa- has the sense of ‘to send away’ (apasādana) on account of the context, etc.; thus he says ‘should be sent away.’ ‘Excessive’: beyond the proper measure. ‘Household-based affection’: affection and love. ‘By the method that is the opposite of what was stated’: by the method that is the opposite of what was stated for the dark side. ‘Sufficient to dismiss’: here, of the two meanings of the word alaṃ—fitness and rejection—it has the meaning of fitness; thus he says, ‘it is fit to dismiss.’

Sātisāro hotīti ettha pakatibhāvaṃ atikkamitvā saraṇaṃ pavattanaṃ atisāro, doso. Saṃvijjati so etassāti sātisāroti dassento āha “sadoso hotī”ti. Tassatthaṃ dassetuṃ vuttaṃ “āpattiṃ āpajjatī”ti. Āpattinti dukkaṭāpattiṃ. Tanti vattaṃ.

‘He is transgressive’: here, transgression (atisāra), a fault (doso), is the occurrence of going beyond one's natural state. Showing that he is sātisāra because that (transgression) is found in him, he says, ‘he is at fault (sadoso).’ To show the meaning of this, it is said, ‘he incurs an offense.’ ‘An offense’ means a dukkaṭa offense. ‘That’ means the duty.

Tesanti saddhivihārikānaṃ. Vattanti bahukānaṃ saddhivihārikānaṃ vattaṃ. Sādiyanaṃ vā…pe… bālo hotīti ettha bālassa kāraṇaṃ dassetuṃ vuttaṃ “sādiyanaṃ vā asādiyanaṃ vā na jānātī”ti. Sādiyanassa vā asādiyanassa vā ajānanattā bālo hotīti vuttaṃ hoti. Ajānanassa kāraṇaṃ dassetuṃ vuttaṃ “bālo hotī”ti. Bālattā sādiyanaṃ vā asādiyanaṃ vā na jānātīti vuttaṃ hoti. Tesūti bahukesu saddhivihārikesu. Tassāti vattasampannabhikkhussa. Tesanti itaresaṃ saddhivihārikānaṃ.

‘Of them’: of the co-residents. ‘Duty’: the duty toward many co-residents. ‘Whether accepting or not … he is a fool’: here, to show the reason for his being a fool, it is said, ‘he does not know what should be accepted or not accepted.’ It means that he is called a fool because he does not know what should be accepted or not accepted. To show the reason for his not knowing, it is said, ‘he is a fool.’ It means that because he is a fool, he does not know what should be accepted or not accepted. ‘Among them’: among the many co-residents. ‘Of him’: of the monk accomplished in the duties. ‘Of them’: of the other co-residents.

Rādhabrāhmaṇavatthukathā

The Story of Rādha the Brahmin

69. Kiñcāpi āyasmā sāriputto jānātīti yojanā. Iminā “kiṃ nu kho ajānanto pucchī”ti āsaṅkaṃ nivāreti. Bhagavā anuññātukāmo [M 0.0226] hotīti sambandho. Panasaddo garahattho, tathā jānantopīti attho. Lahukanti hetuantogadhavisesanaṃ. Lahukattā paṭikkhipitvāti vuttaṃ hoti. Assāti bhagavato, ajjhāsayanti sambandho. “Ajjhāsayaṃ viditvā”tivacanassa yuttiṃ dassento āha “buddhānaṃ hī”tiādi. Hīti saccaṃ. Ayañcāti sāriputtatthero ca. Aggoti koṭiukkaṃso. Seṭṭhoti pavaro uttamo.

69. The construction is: ‘Although the Venerable Sāriputta knows.’ By this he dispels the doubt, ‘Why indeed did he ask as if not knowing?’ The connection is: ‘The Blessed One wishes to grant permission.’ The word pana has the sense of censure; the meaning is ‘although he knew.’ ‘Lightly’ is an adjective included within the reason. It means ‘having rejected it because it is a light matter.’ ‘His’: of the Blessed One; the connection is with ‘intention.’ Showing the reason for the statement ‘having known his intention,’ he says, ‘For of the Buddhas…,’ etc. ‘Hi’ means truly. ‘And this one’: and the Elder Sāriputta. ‘Foremost’ (agga) means the highest peak. ‘Best’ (seṭṭha) means excellent, supreme.

“Byattena bhikkhunā paṭibalenā”ti ettha byattapaṭibalānaṃ visesaṃ dassetuṃ vuttaṃ “byatto nāmā”tiādi. Tattha yassa sāṭṭhakathaṃ vinayapiṭakavācuggataṃ pavattati, ayaṃ byatto nāmāti yojanā[V 1.0197]. Tasminti vinayapiṭakaṃ vācuggatabhikkhumhi. Yassāti bhikkhuno. Suggahitanti sāṭṭhakathāya suṭṭhu gahitaṃ. Ayampīti pisaddo purimabhikkhuṃ apekkhati. Imasmiṃ attheti imasmiṃ vatthumhi, imasmiṃ visayeti attho. Byatirekānvayavasena paṭibalaṃ dassento āha “yo panā”tiādi. Yo pana na sakkotīti sambandho. Kasmāti āha “kāsasosasemhādinā vā”tiādi. Tattha kāso ca soso ca semho ca, te ādayo yassa gelaññassāti kāsasosasemhādi, ādisaddena eḷamūgādayo saṅgaṇhāti. Oṭṭho ca danto ca jivhā ca, tā ādayo yesaṃ tāluādīnanti oṭṭhadantajivhādayo, tesaṃ. Padabyañjanehīti padaakkharehi. Byañjanasaddo hettha akkharavācako. Hāpetīti galattā hāpeti. Aññathā vā vattabbanti aññena sithilādinā ākārena vā vattabbaṃ. Aññathā vadatīti aññena dhanitādiākārena vadati. Tabbiparītoti tassa apaṭibalassa viparīto bhikkhūti sambandho. Tatoti jānāpetabbato. Yanti yaṃ ākāraṃ dhātukammametaṃ, saṅghoti kāritakammametaṃ. Idha kāritakammaṃ kito vadati.

‘By a competent, capable monk’: here, to show the distinction between competent and capable, it is said, ‘One who is competent is called…,’ etc. Therein, the construction is: one for whom the Vinaya Piṭaka together with its commentary is fluent on his tongue is called competent. ‘In that case’: in the case of a monk for whom the Vinaya Piṭaka is fluent. ‘Of one’: of a monk. ‘Well-grasped’: well-grasped along with the commentary. ‘This one too’: the particle pi refers to the preceding monk. ‘In this sense’: in this case, in this subject matter. Showing capability by way of negative and positive concomitance, he says, ‘But one who…,’ etc. The connection is: ‘But one who is not able.’ Why? He says, ‘because of cough, consumption, phlegm, etc.’ Therein, ‘cough, consumption, phlegm, etc.’ means an illness of which these are the beginning; by the word ‘etc.’ he includes being deaf-mute, and so on. ‘Of the lips, teeth, tongue, etc.’: of those things, such as the palate, of which these are the beginning. ‘By phrases and syllables’: by words and letters. Here the word byañjana means a letter. ‘He omits’: he omits because it slips away. ‘Or must be spoken otherwise’: must be spoken in another manner, such as a lax one. ‘He speaks otherwise’: he speaks in another manner, such as a tense one. ‘The opposite of that’: the connection is ‘a monk who is the opposite of that incapable one.’ ‘From that’: from what is to be made known. ‘Which’ (yaṃ): which manner. This is the object of the verb root. ‘The Sangha’ (saṅgho): this is the object of the causative verb. Here he speaks of the object of the causative verb as ‘done’ (kito).

71. Upasampannasamanantarāti ettha upasampannassa samanantarāti atthaṃ nivārento āha “upasampanno hutvāva samanantarā”ti. Evasaddena cirakālaṃ [M 0.0227] nivatteti. Ullumpatūti ettha upubbalupadhātuyā upasaggavasena vā atthātisayavasena vā dhātūnamanekatthattā idha upubbadharadhātuyā atthe vattatīti dassento āha “uddharatū”ti. Uṭṭhāpetvā, ukkhipitvā vā dharatūti attho. Tamevatthaṃ dassento āha “akusalā”tiādi. Tattha “akusalā vuṭṭhāpetvā”ti iminā sahāvadhinā utyūpasaggassa atthaṃ dasseti. “Kusale patiṭṭhāpetū”ti iminā sahādhārena dharadhātussa atthaṃ dasseti. Utyūpasaggassa ukkhipanatthaṃ dassento āha “sāmaṇerabhāvā vā uddharitvā”ti. “Paṭiccā”ti iminā upādāyāti ettha samīpe ādiyitvāti saddatthamagahetvā saṅketatthavasena pākaṭattā tassa saṅketatthaṃ dasseti, adhippāyatthaṃ dassetīti attho.

71. ‘Immediately after ordination’: here, preventing the meaning ‘immediately after the ordained one,’ he says, ‘immediately just after having become ordained.’ By the word eva he excludes a long time. ‘Let him pull up’ (ullumpatu): here, regarding ullumpatu, showing that because of the prefix, or because of an intensification of meaning, or because roots have many meanings, the root lup with the prefix u- is used here in the sense of the root dhar with the prefix u-, he says, ‘Let him lift up’ (uddharatu). The meaning is: let him uphold him after having made him rise up or having lifted him up. To show this very meaning, he says, ‘from the unwholesome,’ etc. Therein, by ‘having made him rise up from the unwholesome,’ he shows the meaning of the prefix u- along with the ablative limit. By ‘let him establish him in the wholesome,’ he shows the meaning of the root dhar along with the locative base. Showing the meaning of the prefix u- as ‘lifting up,’ he says, ‘or having lifted him up from the state of a novice.’ ‘Because of’: by this, with regard to upādāya, without taking the literal meaning ‘having taken up near,’ he shows its conventional meaning, since that is evident by way of convention; the meaning is that he shows the intended meaning.

73. Adhiṭṭhitāti ettha adhi niccavasena ṭhāti pavattatīti adhiṭṭhitāti vacanatthaṃ dassento āha “niccappavattinī”ti. Kasmā cattāro paccayā nissayāti vuttāti āha “yasmā”tiādi. “Cattāro”tiādinā cattāro paccaye nissāya attabhāvo seti pavattatīti nissāyāti avuttakammatthaṃ dasseti.

73. ‘Established’: here, showing the verbal sense of adhiṭṭhitā as ‘it stands (ṭhā) and proceeds (pavattati) upon (adhi) in a constant way,’ he says, ‘perpetually proceeding.’ Why are the four requisites called ‘supports’ (nissayā)? He says, ‘Because…,’ etc. By ‘the four,’ etc., he shows the sense of the unstated object in nissāyā: because the individual existence lies (seti) and proceeds (pavattati) in dependence on (nissāya) the four requisites.

18. Ācariyavattakathā

18. Discourse on the Duties of a Teacher

75. Kintāyanti [V 1.0198] ettha ekāralopavasena sandhi hotīti āha “kiṃte aya”nti. “Ovaditabboti”iminā ovadiyoti ettha ṇyapaccayassa kammatthaṃ dasseti. “Tadatthāyā”ti iminā “yadidaṃ gaṇabandhika”nti uttaravākye yaṃsaddaṃ disvā pubbavākye taṃsaddaṃ ñāpeti, tassa bāhullassa atthāyāti attho.

75. In 'Kintāyanti,' there is a sandhi here by way of the elision of the vowel 'a'; thus he says, 'kiṃ te ayaṃ.' By 'Ovaditabbo,' he shows the passive meaning of the suffix '-ṇya' in 'ovadiyo.' By 'Tadatthāya,' having seen the word 'yaṃ' in the subsequent sentence, 'yadidaṃ gaṇabandhika,' he makes known the word 'taṃ' in the preceding sentence; the meaning is 'for the sake of that abundance'.

76. Soti pasūro paribbājako. Tenāti udāyittherena. Sahadhammikanti saha dhammena kāraṇena. Byatto tāva pubbe vuttalakkhaṇo hotu, paṭibalo pana kathaṃ ñātabboti āha “yo panā”tiādi[M 0.0228]. Yo pana sakkotīti sambandho. Cāti saccaṃ. Etanti paṭibalattaṃ, “pañcahi…pe… vinetu”ntivacanaṃ vā.

76. 'So' is the wanderer Pasūra. 'Tena' means by the Elder Udāyi. 'Sahadhammikaṃ' means 'together with the Dhamma, by reason.' A competent person should first have the previously stated characteristics, but how is capability to be known? He says: 'But whoever...,' etc. The phrase 'yo pana sakkoti' is the connection. 'Ca' means 'truly.' 'Etaṃ' refers to capability, or the statement '...with five... and so on... to train'.

77. Titthiyapakkhasaṅkantesūti titthiyasaṅkhātaṃ sāsanassa paṭipakkhaṃ saṅkamantesu. Ācārasamācārasikkhāpanakanti ativiya caritabbaṃ ābhisamācārikasīlaṃ sikkhāpanakaṃ. Iminā ācāraṃ sikkhāpetīti ācariyoti vacanatthaṃ dasseti. Nāmamattamevāti “ācariyo”ti vā “antevāsiko”ti vā nāmamattameva. Nānanti upajjhāyato vā saddhivihārikato vā nānaṃ.

77. 'Titthiyapakkhasaṅkantesu' means 'among those inclining toward the faction of sectarians,' those considered opponents of the Dispensation. 'Ācārasamācārasikkhāpanakaṃ' refers to the training in the code of conduct and good behavior, which should be practiced very strictly. This shows the meaning of the term 'ācariyo' (teacher) as 'one who trains in conduct.' 'Nāmamattameva' means 'merely the name,' whether 'teacher' or 'pupil.' 'Nānaṃ' means 'different' from the preceptor or from the co-resident.

20. Paṇāmanākhamāpanākathā

20. Discourse on Assigning and Asking for Pardon

80. Yaṃ lakkhaṇaṃ vuttanti sambandho. Nissayantevāsikena kātabbanti yojanā. Pabbajjāupasampadādhammantevāsikehīti pabbajjantevāsikena ca upasampadantevāsikena ca dhammantevāsikena ca. Etesanti pabbajjāupasampadādhammantevāsikānaṃ. Etesūti etesu tīsu antevāsikesu. Ācariyassāti pabbajjantevāsiko pabbajjācariyassa, upasampadantevāsiko upasampadācariyassāti attho. Samīpeti nissayācariyassa ca dhammācariyassa ca āsanne. Tasmāti yasmā antevāsikena ācariyamhi sammā vattitabbaṃ, tasmā. Ācariyenāpīti nissayapabbajjā upasampadā dhammācariyenāpi. Ovādācariyo tesu saṅgahaṃ gacchati. Tesūti catūsu antevāsikesu.

80. The connection is 'yaṃ lakkhaṇaṃ vuttaṃ.' The application is 'nissayantevāsikena kātabbaṃ.' 'Pabbajjāupasampadādhammantevāsikehi' means by the pupil of the going forth, by the pupil of the higher ordination, and by the pupil of the Dhamma. 'Etesaṃ' refers to these pupils of the going forth, higher ordination, and Dhamma. 'Etesu' refers to these three kinds of pupils. 'Ācariyassa' means: the pupil of the going forth belongs to the teacher of the going forth, and the pupil of the higher ordination belongs to the teacher of the higher ordination. 'Samīpe' means near the dependence-teacher and the Dhamma-teacher. 'Tasmā' means: because a pupil must behave rightly toward a teacher, therefore. 'Ācariyenāpi' means also by the dependence-teacher, the going-forth-teacher, the higher-ordination-teacher, and the Dhamma-teacher. The advising teacher is included among them. 'Tesu' refers to the four kinds of pupils.

22. Nissayapaṭippassaddhikathā

22. Discourse on the Cessation of Dependence

Āṇattivinicchayo

Decision on Commands

83. “Nissayapaṭipassaddhīsū”ti [V 1.0199] samūhādhāro. “Upajjhāyo pakkanto vātiādīsū”ti avayavādhāro. “Vippavasitukāmo”ti iminā nirālayabhāvaṃ dasseti. Evaṃ gateti evaṃ upajjhāye gateti yojanā. Aññadāpīti aññasmimpi kāle. Upajjhāyena pavāsitakāleti attho. Ekasambhogaparibhogoti attanā vā upajjhāyena vā eko paccayasambhogo ca dhammaparibhogo ca. Ekadivasampīti pisaddo [M 0.0229] garahattho, dvihādikaṃ pana pagevāti attho. Parihāro natthīti āpattiparihāro natthi, āpattiyā pariharaṇaṃ apanayanaṃ natthīti adhippāyo. Lajjī pesaloti lajjī hutvā piyasīlo bhikkhūti sambandho. Tadahevāti tasmiṃ upajjhāyassa pakkantaahani eva. Tathāti yathā “upajjhāyo lahuṃ āgamissatī”ti pucchati, tathā “ahaṃ lahuṃ āgamissāmī”ti vuttanti attho. Sace vadatīti sace ācariyo vadatīti yojanā. Assāti bhikkhussa. Sabhāgatanti lajjipesalabhāvaṃ.

83. 'Nissayapaṭipassaddhīsū' is a locative of scope. 'Upajjhāyo pakkanto vā, etc.' is a locative of part. By 'vippavasitukāmo,' he shows the state of being without attachment. The application for 'evaṃ gate' is 'evaṃ upajjhāye gate.' 'Aññadāpi' means 'at another time too'; the meaning is 'at a time when the preceptor is dwelling abroad.' 'Ekasambhogaparibhogo' means having the same communion in material things and the same enjoyment of the teaching. In 'ekadivasampi,' the particle 'pi' is used in the sense of censure; the meaning is that two or more days is all the more so. 'Parihāro natthi' means there is no getting around the offense; the intention is that there is no avoidance or removal of the offense. The connection for 'lajjī pesalo' is 'a monk who, being conscientious, is amiable.' 'Tadaheva' means on the very day that the preceptor departed. 'Tathā' means: just as one asks, 'Will the preceptor return soon?,' so it is said, 'I will return soon.' The application for 'sace vadati' is 'if the teacher says.' 'Assa' means 'of the monk.' 'Sabhāgataṃ' is the state of being conscientious and amiable.

Yāva āgamanāti upajjhāyassa yāva āgamanā. Nanti upajjhāyaṃ. “Vāsentiyevā”tipade kāritakammaṃ. Tatthāti upajjhāyassa gataṭṭhāne. Tenāti upajjhāyena. Pavattīti pavattanaṃ. Nadīpūrena vā upaddutoti sambandho. Nadīpūrattā udakosakkanaṃ āgameti, corādīnaṃ upaddutattā sahāye pariyesati. Soti upajjhāyo.

'Yāva āgamanā' means 'until the preceptor's return.' 'Naṃ' refers to the preceptor. In the word 'vāsentiyeva,' it is a causative object. 'Tattha' means in the place where the preceptor has gone. 'Tena' means by the preceptor. 'Pavatti' means news. The connection is 'or oppressed by a river flood.' Because of the river flood, he waits for the water to recede; because of oppression by thieves and others, he seeks companions. 'So' refers to the preceptor.

“Nissayapaṇāmanā”ti iminā āṇāpanaṃ āṇattīti vacanatthena nissayapaṇāmanā āṇattīti vuccatīti dasseti. Nissayapaṇāmanāti nissayassa upajjhācariyassa paṇāmanā. Tasmā paṇāmito hotīti sambandho. “Āpucchītiādinā”ti ettha ādisaddena “mā maṃ susānagamanaṃ āpucchī”tiādayo saṅgaṇhāti. Tenāti saddhivihārikena. Khamāpetabboti titikkhāpetabbo.

By 'Nissayapaṇāmanā,' he shows that because the word 'āṇatti' has the meaning of 'a command,' 'nissayapaṇāmanā' is called 'āṇatti.' 'Nissayapaṇāmanā' is the directing of one's dependence, that is, of the preceptor or teacher. Therefore, the connection is 'he is directed.' In 'āpucchīti, etc.,' the word 'etc.' includes such things as 'do not take leave of me for going to the charnel ground.' 'Tena' means by the co-resident. 'Khamāpetabbo' means he should be asked for forgiveness.

Tāvāti mahātherehi, mahātherānaṃ vā paṭhamaṃ. Aññatthāti upajjhāyassa vihārato aññaṃ vihāraṃ. Appevāti api eva nāma khameyyāti yojanā. Tatrevāti aññattheva. Dubbhikkhādidosenāti ettha ādisaddena ñātiviyogādidoso gahetabbo. Taṃyevāti attanā vasitaṃ tameva ṭhānaṃ. Aññassāti upajjhāyato aññassa bhikkhussāti sambandho. Iminā upajjhāyena pariccattattā upajjhāyasamodhāne nissayapaṭippassaddhi natthīti dīpeti.

'Tāva' means 'first, by the senior monks,' or 'first, of the senior monks.' 'Aññattha' means to another monastery apart from the preceptor's monastery. The application for 'appeva' is 'api eva nāma khameyya' (perhaps it might be suitable). 'Tatreva' means 'in that other place itself.' In 'dubbhikkhādidosena,' the word 'etc.' should be taken to include the fault of separation from relatives and so on. 'Taṃyeva' means that very place where one has dwelt. The connection for 'aññassa' is 'of another monk' apart from the preceptor.
