By this he shows that because one has been abandoned by the preceptor, the rule for cessation of dependence upon meeting with that preceptor does not apply.

Samodhānavinicchayo

The Decision on Combination

Āpucchitvāti =00 [M 0.0230] antevāsikaṃ āpucchitvā. Tatrāpīti ācariyantevāsikesupi. Kadāti kasmiṃ kāle. Sāyanhe vā rattiṃvāti ajja sāyanhe vā rattiṃ vā. Taṃkhaṇeyevāti tasmiṃ sampaṭicchanakkhaṇeyeva.

Having taken leave = having taken leave of the resident pupil. There too = also in the case of teachers and resident pupils. When = at what time. In the evening or at night = this evening or tonight. At that very moment = at the very moment of acceptance.

So cāti antevāsiko ca. Tatoti gāmato. Sugatoti suṭṭhu gato, nissayo paṭippassambhatīti adhippāyo. Athāpīti puna ca paraṃ. Āpucchitvā pakkamane vinicchayaṃ dassetvā āpucchitvā pakkamane taṃ dassento āha “ācariyaṃ anāpucchā”tiādi. Upacārasīmātikkameti upacārasīmāya atikkame sati, atikkamanahetu vāti yojanā. Ettha ca upacārasīmā nāma parikkhittassa vihārassa parikkhepoyeva, aparikkhittassa parikkhepārahaṭṭhānaṃ.

And he = and the resident pupil. From there = from the village. Well-gone = well gone; the intention is that dependence is relinquished. And then = and furthermore. Having explained the ruling on departing after taking leave, now, to explain the ruling on departing without taking leave, he says: 'Without asking the teacher,' etc. Crossing the boundary of the environs = when the boundary of the environs is crossed, or because of crossing it; this is the construction. And here, the boundary of the environs means the very enclosure of an enclosed monastery, or for an unenclosed one, the place suitable for an enclosure.

Sāyanhe vā rattibhāge vāti ajja sāyanhe vā rattibhāge vā. Sveti suve.

In the evening or during the night part = this evening or during the night part. Tomorrow = tomorrow.

Bahisīmanti upacārasīmato bahi. Tatoti bahisīmato. Dvinnaṃ leḍḍupātānanti antevāsikato dvinnaṃ leḍḍupātānaṃ. Atikkamitvāti upacārasīmato bahi antevāsikasaddhivihārikānaṃ vasanaṭṭhānato atikkamitvā.

Outside the boundary = outside the boundary of the environs. From there = from outside the boundary. Of two stone-throws = two stone-throws from the resident pupil. Having crossed = having crossed beyond the dwelling place of the resident pupil and co-resident, outside the boundary of the environs.

Muccitukāmoti antevāsikamhā muccitukāmo eva. Paṇāmetīti kāyavācāhi paṇāmeti. Sālayoti ācariye sāpekkho. “Nirālayo”ti vatvā tassa atthaṃ dassetuṃ vuttaṃ “na dānī”tiādi. Evampīti dhure nikkhittepi. Ubhinnaṃ dhuranikkhepe sati, dhuranikkhepahetu vā paṭippassambhatīti yojanā. Paṇāmitena paṭipajjitabbanti sambandho.

Wishing to be released = just wishing to be released from the resident pupil. Dismisses = dismisses by body and speech. Attached = dependent on the teacher. Having said 'unattached,' to show its meaning it is said: 'not now,' etc. Even so = even when the burden is laid down. When the burden is laid down by both, or because the burden is laid down, it is relinquished; this is the construction. It should be practiced by the one who has been dismissed; this is the connection.

Vuttamevatthaṃ vitthārento āha “sace hī”tiādi. Ācariyanti nissayācariyaṃ. Cetiyaṃ vā vandantaṃ upajjhāyanti sambandho, maggappaṭipannaṃ vā upajjhāyanti yojanā. Dūrattāti dūrabhāvato. Uparipāsādeti pāsādassa upari. Tanti upajjhāyaṃ. Nisinnaṃ upajjhāyanti sambandho.

Elaborating on the meaning just stated, he said: 'If indeed,' etc. The teacher means the dependence-teacher. 'Or venerating a shrine' connects with 'the preceptor'; or 'entered on the path' is construed with 'the preceptor.' From a distance means because of being far. On the upper storey means on top of the mansion. Him means the preceptor. 'Seated' connects with 'the preceptor'.

Savanavasena [M 0.0231] samodhāne vinicchayo evaṃ veditabboti yojanā. Upajjhāyassa saddanti sambandho.

The decision in the case of combination by means of hearing should be understood thus; this is the construction. 'The preceptor's voice'; this is the connection.

23. Upasampādetabbapañcakakathā

23. The Talk on the Pentad concerning Giving Higher Ordination

84. Idāni =01 yaṃ lakkhaṇaṃ vuttanti sambandho. Saṅkhepatoti aṅgāni anuddharitvā samāsato. Tatthāti yaṃ “pañcahi bhikkhave aṅgehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā”tiādimāha, tattha. Aguṇaṅgehīti guṇavirahitehi aṅgehi. Soti bhikkhu. Na upasampādetabbanti ettha kammavācācariyena hutvā na upasampādetabbanti āsaṅkā bhaveyyāti āha “upajjhāyena hutvā na upasampādetabba”nti. Etthāti etesu pañcakesu. Ādīsūti ettha pubbo nidassanattho itisaddo lopo hoti. Itiādīsūti hi attho. Ayuttavasenāti ananurūpavasena. Yoti bhikkhu. Hīti saccaṃ, yasmā vā. Pare ca samādapetunti sambandho. Tatthāti sīlakkhandhādike. Pariharatīti parisaṃ parissayato harati apaneti. Tassāti bhikkhuno. “Sīlādīhī”tipadaṃ “parihāyatiyevā”tipade apādānaṃ, “na vaḍḍhatī”tipade karaṇaṃ. Tasmātiādi laddhaguṇaṃ. Tenāti bhikkhunā. Kasmā āpattiaṅgavasena na vuttanti āha “na hī”tiādi. Hīti yasmā. Tassevāti khīṇāsavasseva. Na vadeyyāti khīṇāsavānaṃ anabhiratiyā anuppannattā na vadeyya. Yadi na khīṇāsavasseva upajjhāyācariyabhāvo anuññāto, atha kasmā khīṇāsavapañcako vuttoti āha “yasmā panā”tiādi. Yasmā na parihāyatīti sambandho.

84. Now, the connection is with what was said as the characteristic. 'In brief' means summarily, without enumerating the factors. 'There' refers to what was said beginning with: 'Bhikkhus, a monk endowed with five factors....' 'With unvirtuous factors' means with factors devoid of virtue. 'He' means the monk. Regarding 'should not give higher ordination,' here, lest the doubt should arise that one should not give it only as the announcer of the formal act, it is said: 'One should not give higher ordination as a preceptor.' 'Here' means in these pentads. In 'etc.': here the preceding illustrative word 'iti' is elided, for the meaning is 'thus, etc.' 'By way of what is improper' means by way of what is unsuitable. 'Who' means the monk. 'Indeed' means truly, or because. 'And he encourages others'; this is the connection. 'There' means in the aggregates of virtue, etc. 'He protects' means he removes the assembly from danger. 'His' means of the monk. The word 'sīlādīhi' is in the ablative case in relation to 'parihāyatiyeva,' and in the instrumental case in relation to 'na vaḍḍhati.' The phrase beginning with 'Therefore' refers to an acquired quality. 'By him' means by the monk. Why was it not stated by way of factors of an offense? It is said: 'Indeed not,' etc. 'Indeed' means because. 'Of him alone' refers solely to one whose taints are destroyed. 'He would not speak': because discontent does not arise for those whose taints are destroyed, he would not speak. If the state of being a preceptor or teacher is permitted for others besides one whose taints are destroyed, then why is the pentad of one whose taints are destroyed mentioned? It is said: 'But because,' etc. 'Because he does not decline'; this is the connection.

Antaggāhikāyāti sassatucchedasaṅkhātaṃ antaṃ lāmakaṃ gaṇhāti, gaṇhāpetīti vā antaggāhikā, tāya. Diṭṭhiyāti micchādiṭṭhiyā. Yattakaṃ sutanti bhikkhunovādakasikkhāpade (pāci. aṭṭha. 145-147) vuttaṃ yattakaṃ sutaṃ. Tenāti sutena ऋ. Yaṃ āpattādi tena jānitabbanti yojanā.

'Grasping at an extreme': one grasps the base extreme designated as eternalism and annihilationism, or causes others to grasp it; hence it is called 'grasping at an extreme'; by that view. 'With a view' means with a wrong view. 'As much as has been heard' is as much as has been heard stated in the Training Rule on the Exhortation to Bhikkhunīs (Pācittiya Aṭṭha. 145-147). 'By that' means by what has been heard. 'Whatever offense, etc., should be known by that'; this is the construction.

Āpattiṃ [M 0.0232] na jānātīti ettha āpattiṃ āpannoti na jānātīti atthaṃ dassento āha “idaṃ nāmā”tiādi. Tattha “āpanno”ti iminā “āpatti”ntipadaṃ “āpanno”tipāṭhasesena yojetabbanti dasseti.

Regarding 'He does not know an offense': here, to show the meaning is 'he does not know that he has incurred an offense,' he says: 'This is called,' etc. There, by 'incurred,' he shows that the word 'offense' should be construed with the remainder of the reading, 'incurred'.

Ābhisamācārikāyāti ettha ubhatovibhaṅgapariyāpannasīlato abhivisesena sammā caritabbanti ābhisamācāraṃ, khandhakapariyāpannaṃ vattapaṭipattisīlaṃ, taṃ ārabbha paññattā ābhisamācārikā, khandhakapariyāpannā sikkhā, tāya. Ādibrahmacāriyakāyāti ettha maggasaṅkhātassa brahmacariyassa ādi mariyādo ādibrahmacariyo, tasmiṃ pavattā ādibrahmacariyakā =02, ubhatovibhaṅgapariyāpannā sikkhā, tāya. Sekkhapaṇṇattiyanti sikkhitabbaṭṭhena sikkhā, sā eva bhagavatā paññattattā sekkhapaṇṇatti. Atha vā sikkhanaṃ sikkhā, tāya sikkhanatthāya bhagavatā paññapīyatīti sekkhapaṇṇatti ubhatovibhaṅgapariyāpannasikkhāyeva, tassaṃ. Abhidhammeti ettha suttantapāḷito abhi atireko, abhivisiṭṭho vā dhammo abhidhammoti vutte nāmarūpaparicchedakaṃ abhidhammapiṭakanti āha “nāmarūpaparicchede”ti. Abhivinayeti ettha abhibhavitvā kāyavācaṃ vinetīti abhivinayo, abhibhavitvā kāyavācaṃ vineti ettha, etenāti vā abhivinayoti vutte vinayapiṭakanti āha “sakale vinayapiṭake”ti. Sabbatthāti sabbesu padesu, sabbesaṃ vā padānaṃ. Attho daṭṭhabboti yojanā. “Kāraṇenā”ti ettha kāraṇasaddena “dhammato”ti ettha dhammasaddassa sabhāvatthādayo nivāretvā kāraṇatthataṃ dīpeti, enasaddena topaccayassa visesanatthaṃ. Itīti evaṃ yathāvuttanayenāti attho. Catuttheti catutthapañcake. Catutthapañcakato tīṇi padāni, pañcamapañcakato dve padāni gahetvā pañcakaṃ katvā vuttaṃ “cattāro pañcakā”ti. Aṭṭhasu pañcakesūti sambandho.

Regarding the training rule of proper conduct: Here, proper conduct (ābhisamācāra) is to conduct oneself rightly with special distinction from the virtue comprised in the two Vibhaṅgas; it is the virtue of observances and duties comprised in the Khandhakas. The training rule concerning proper conduct (ābhisamācārikā) is the training rule laid down in reference to that, the one comprised in the Khandhakas; by that. Regarding the fundamentals of the holy life: Here, the beginning and boundary of the holy life (brahmacariya), which is designated as the path, is the fundamental of the holy life (ādibrahmacariya). The training rule pertaining to this (ādibrahmacariyakā) is the one comprised in the two Vibhaṅgas; by that. Regarding the training rule for trainees: A training rule (sikkhā) is so called because it should be trained in (sikkhitabba); it is a training rule for trainees (sekkhapaṇṇatti) because it was laid down by the Blessed One. Or, training (sikkhanā) is sikkhā; because it is laid down by the Blessed One for the purpose of that training, it is a sekkhapaṇṇatti. It is just the training rule comprised in the two Vibhaṅgas; in that. Regarding the Abhidhamma: Here, Abhidhamma is the Dhamma that is additional to or more distinguished than the Suttanta Piṭaka. When it is said thus, it means the Abhidhamma Piṭaka, which is the analysis of name-and-form; hence he says 'in the analysis of name-and-form.' Regarding the Abhivinaya: Here, Abhivinaya is so called because it disciplines body and speech by overpowering them; or, one disciplines body and speech by overpowering them herein, or by means of this. When it is said thus, it means the Vinaya Piṭaka; hence he says 'in the entire Vinaya Piṭaka.' 'Everywhere' means in all sections, or of all words. The meaning should be seen; this is the construction. Regarding 'by reason': Here, the word 'reason' (kāraṇa) clarifies that the word 'dhamma' in 'from the Dhamma' (dhammato) has the meaning of cause, precluding the meanings of intrinsic nature, etc. The word 'ena' is for the purpose of specifying the '-to' suffix. 'Thus' means in this way, according to the method stated. 'In the fourth' means in the fourth pentad. Having taken three items from the fourth pentad and two items from the fifth pentad, a pentad was made. Thus it was said 'four pentads.' 'In the eight pentads'; this is the connection.

Iti soḷasapañcakavinicchaye yojanā samattā.

Thus ends the construction in the Analysis of the Sixteen Pentads.

24. Upasampādetabbachakkakathā

24. The Discourse on the Hexad of Those to be Ordained

85. Tanti [M 0.0233] ūnadasavassapadaṃ. Sabbatthāti sabbesu chakkesu. Tatthāti chakkesu. “Pātimokkhāni vitthārenā”ti vuttattā vibhaṅgavasena gahetabbānīti āha “ubhatovibhaṅgavasena vuttānī”ti. Mātikāvibhaṅgavasena suṭṭhu vibhajitabbānīti suvibhattāni, vācuggatavasena sundarā pavatti etesanti suppavattīni, suttato anubyañjanato suṭṭhu vinicchitabbānīti suvinicchitabbānīti atthaṃ dassento āha “mātikāvibhaṅgavasenā”tiādi.

85. The thread is the passage on 'less than ten years.' 'Everywhere' means in all the hexads. 'There' means in the hexads. Because it is said, 'The Pātimokkhas in detail,' they should be understood by way of the analysis; hence he says, 'stated by way of the twofold analysis.' They should be well divided by way of the matrix and the analysis, thus they are 'well-divided.' Their progression is beautiful by way of recitation, thus they are 'well-progressed.' They should be thoroughly discerned from the rule and its details, thus they are 'well-discerned.' Showing this meaning, he says: 'By way of the matrix and analysis,' and so on.

25. Aññatitthiyapubbavatthukathā

25. The Discourse on the Case of the Former Sectarian

86. Yo panāti yo pana aññatitthiyapubbo. Aññopīti pasūrato aparopi. Idhāti imasmiṃ sāsane. Tasminti aññatitthiyapubbe. Tatthāti “yo so bhikkhave aññopī”tiādivacane. Ayanti parivāso. Naggaparibbājakassevāti vatvā tassa bhedaṃ dassetuṃ vuttaṃ “ājīvakassa vā acelakassa vā”ti. Tattha ājīvako upari ekameva vatthaṃ upakacchake pavesetvā paridahati, heṭṭhā naggo. Acelako pana sabbena sabbaṃ naggoyeva. Sopīti =03 naggaparibbājakopi. Vālakambalādīnanti vālena kataṃ kambalaṃ, ādisaddena kesakambalādayo saṅgaṇhāti. Assāti paribbājakassa. Aññassāti naggaparibbājakato aparassa. Paṇḍaraṅgādikassāti paṇḍaraṃ setavatthaṃ aṅge sarīre etassatthīti paṇḍaraṅgo, ādisaddena nīlaṅgādayo saṅgaṇhāti.

86. 'But whoever' means: whoever was formerly an adherent of another sect. 'Another also' is explained as `pasūrato aparopi`. 'Here' means in this Dispensation. 'In that one' means in that former adherent of another sect. 'Therein' means in the statement beginning, 'Bhikkhus, whoever else....' 'This' means this probation. Having said 'of a naked wanderer,' it is then said 'of an Ājīvaka or an Acelaka' in order to show a distinction concerning him. Here, an Ājīvaka wears only one cloth above, tucking it into his armpit, and is naked below. An Acelaka, however, is completely naked. 'He also' means: a naked wanderer also. 'Of a hair blanket, etc.' means: a blanket made of animal hair; by the word 'etc.,' he includes blankets made of human hair and so on. 'His' means: of the wanderer. 'Of another' means: of one other than a naked wanderer. 'Of one clad in white, etc.' means: he has a white cloth on his body, thus he is 'one clad in white'; by the word 'etc.,' he includes those clad in blue and so on.

Evanti iminā kesamassuoropanādinā. Pabbājentehi bhikkhūhīti sambandho. Tasminti aññatitthiyapubbe, nisinneyevāti yojanā. Anādare cetaṃ bhummavacanaṃ. Tassāti aññatitthiyapubbassa. Nayimeti na ime, bhikkhūti sambandho. Tanti aññatitthiyapubbaṃ.

'Thus' means: by this, that is, by the shaving of hair and beard, etc. 'By the bhikkhus who are giving the going forth' is the connection. 'In that one' refers to a former adherent of another sect; 'he should be seated' is the construction. And this is a locative of disregard. 'His' means: of the former adherent of another sect. 'Not these' means `na ime`; the connection is with 'bhikkhus.' 'That one' refers to the former adherent of another sect.

87. “Evaṃ kho…pe… anārādhako”ti ayaṃ kathā mātikāti yojanā. Assāti aññatitthiyapubbassa. Tassevāti tassāyeva mātikāya. Tatthāti vibhaṅge. Atikālenāti ettha bhattakiccaṃ katvā vattakaraṇavelāyeva atikālo nāmāti dassento āha [M 0.0234] “vattakaraṇavelāyamevā”ti. Iminā bhummatthe karaṇavacanantipi dasseti. Tatthevāti kulagharesuyeva. Aññadatthūti ekaṃsena, “karonto”ti iminā pāṭhasesaṃ dasseti. Evampi karonto aññatitthiyapubboti yojanā. “Sampādako”ti iminā anārādhakoti ettha ārādhasaddassa sādhanatthaṃ dasseti, tosanatthādayo nivatteti.

87. The construction is: this discourse, 'Thus indeed ... pe ... displeasing,' is the matrix. 'His' means: of the former adherent of another sect. 'Of that very one' means: of that very matrix. 'Therein' means: in the analysis. Regarding 'at the wrong time': showing that here 'wrong time' means the time for performing one's duties after having finished the meal-duties, he says, 'at the very time for performing one's duties.' By this he also shows that the instrumental is used in the sense of the locative. 'Right there' means: right in the houses of families. 'Certainly' means: definitely; by 'doing' he indicates the remainder of the text. The construction is: 'Even doing thus, he is a former adherent of another sect.' By 'accomplishing,' he shows that here in 'displeasing,' the word `ārādha` has the meaning of 'achieving,' and he excludes the meanings of 'satisfying,' etc.

Ajjhācāratthikā visanti pavisanti etthāti vesiyā, sobhaṇarūpasaṅkhātaṃ vesaṃ dhāretīti vā vesiyā. Tena vuttaṃ “sulabhajjhācārā”tiādi. Āmisoyeva kiñjakkho appamattakaṭṭhenāti āmisakiñjakkho, visesanaparapado. Atha vā āmiso ca tato añño kiñjakkho ca āmisakiñjakkhaṃ, tassa sampadānaṃ āmisakiñjakkhasampadānaṃ. Kiñjakkhasaddo kesarasseva mukhyato vācako, appamattakassa pana rūḷhīvasena. Vidhavāti ettha dhavasaddo patinoyeva vācako, na rukkhavisesassāti dassento āha “matapatikā vā”tiādi. Imehi padehi matavasena vā pavutthavasena vā vigato dhavo etāsaṃ, dhavena vā vigatāti vidhavāti vacanatthaṃ dasseti. Tāti vidhavā. Yobbanapattattā vā yobbanātītattā vā thullā mahantā kumārikāti thullakumārikāti dassento āha “yobbanapattā”tiādi. Paṇḍakāti ettha āsittapaṇḍakādīsu pañcasu paṇḍakesu napuṃsakapaṇḍakovādhippetoti āha “napuṃsakā”ti. Samānapabbajjāti bhikkhūhi samānapabbajjā. Tatoti vissāsato.

A courtesan (`vesiyā`) is so called because those desirous of misconduct enter her; or she is a courtesan because she wears an attire considered beautiful. For that reason it is said, 'of easily accessible misconduct,' etc. `Āmisakiñjakkho` means: a mere material thing that is a trifle in the sense of being insignificant; this is a compound with the adjective placed second. Or else, a material thing and apart from that a trifle is `āmisakiñjakkhaṃ`; the giving of that is `āmisakiñjakkhasampadānaṃ`. The word `kiñjakkha` primarily denotes a filament, but by convention it denotes something insignificant. Regarding 'widow' (`vidhavā`): here the word `dhava` denotes only a husband, not a particular kind of tree; showing this, he says, 'one whose husband is dead,' etc. By these words he shows the meaning of `vidhavā` as 'one whose husband is gone either through death or through absence,' or 'one who is gone from her husband.' 'She' means: the widow. Showing that a 'mature maiden' (`thullakumārikā`) is a 'large' or 'big' girl either because she has reached youth or has passed beyond youth, he says, 'one who has attained youth,' etc. Regarding 'paṇḍaka': here, among the five kinds of paṇḍakas such as the `āsittapaṇḍaka`, the `napuṃsakapaṇḍaka` is intended; hence he says, 'impotent ones.' 'The same going forth' means: the same going forth as the bhikkhus. 'From that' means: from trust.

Tatthāti vesiyādīsu. Tāsanti vesiyānaṃ. Soti aññatitthiyapubbo. Sabbatthāti sabbesu =04 vidhavādīsu. Gantabbataṃ dassento āha “sace panā”tiādi. Tathāti yathā gantabbattaṃ vuttaṃ, tathā.

'Therein' means: in regard to courtesans, etc. 'Their' means: of the courtesans. 'He' means: the former adherent of another sect. 'Everywhere' means: in all cases, such as with widows, etc. Showing the approachability, he says, 'But if...,' etc. 'So' means: just as the approachability was stated, so.

Uccāvacānīti ettha uddhaṃ cayati vaḍḍhatīti uccaṃ, cayato avagato viyogoti avacaṃ. Uccañca avacañca uccāvacānīti vacanatthena mahantakhuddakatthoti āha “mahantakhuddakānī”ti. “Kammānī”ti iminā “karaṇīyānī”tipadassa sarūpaṃ dasseti. Taṃdassanena ca kattabbānīti karaṇīyānīti vacanattho kātabbo. Tatthāti mahantakhuddakesu kammesu[M 0.0235]. Tattha na dakkhoti ettha tasaddassa visayaṃ dassetuṃ vuttaṃ “tesu tesu navakammesū”ti. “Uṭṭhānavīriyasampanno”ti iminā natthi alaso kosajjaṃ etassāti analasoti vacanatthaṃ dasseti. Tatrāti ettha trapaccayo sattamyatthe vicchājotakoti āha “tesu tesū”ti. “Ṭhānuppattikāya vīmaṃsāyā”ti vuttavacanassatthaṃ dassento āha “idameva”ntiādi. “Tasmiṃyeva khaṇe uppannapaññāyā”ti iminā “ṭhānuppattikāyā”ti ettha ṭhānasaddo taṅkhaṇatthoti dasseti. Alaṃ kātunti ettha alaṃsaddo bhūsanavāraṇapariyattasaṅkhātesu tīsu atthesu pariyattatthoti āha “kātuṃ samattho”ti.

Regarding 'high and low' (`uccāvacāni`): here, 'high' (`uccaṃ`) is what accumulates (`cayati`) upwards, what grows; 'low' (`avacaṃ`) is what has gone down from accumulation, what is separated. 'High and low' (`uccāvacāni`), by the meaning of the word, means 'great and small'; hence he says, 'great and small.' By 'deeds' (`kammāni`), he shows the word `karaṇīyāni` itself. And by showing that, the meaning of the word `karaṇīyāni` is to be understood as 'what ought to be done.' 'Therein' (`tattha`) means: in those great and small deeds. Regarding 'there he is not skilled' (`tattha na dakkho`): here, to show the scope of the word 'that' (`ta`), it is said, 'in those various new works.' By 'endowed with energy and effort,' he shows the meaning of the word 'not lazy' (`analaso`) as 'one who has no idleness or indolence.' Regarding `tatrā`: here the suffix `-tra` indicates distribution in the locative sense; hence he says, 'in those various' (`tesu tesu`). Explaining the meaning of the statement 'with investigation arisen for the occasion' (`ṭhānuppattikāya vīmaṃsāyā`), he says, 'this very,' etc. By 'with wisdom arisen at that very moment,' he shows that here in `ṭhānuppattikāya`, the word `ṭhāna` has the meaning of 'that moment.' Regarding 'able to do' (`alaṃ kātuṃ`): here, among the three meanings of the word `alaṃ`—namely, ornament, prohibition, and sufficiency—it has the meaning of sufficiency; hence he says, 'is able to do' (`kātuṃ samattho`).

Tibbacchandoti tikhiṇachando. “Balavacchando”ti iminā adhippāyatthaṃ dasseti. Lokiyasamādhibhāvanāyāti lokiyāya aṭṭhasamāpattisaṅkhātāya samādhibhāvanāya.

`Tibbacchando` means: one with keen desire. By 'one with strong desire,' he shows the intended meaning. 'By the development of worldly concentration' means: by the development of concentration designated as the eight worldly attainments.

Idhāgatoti imasmiṃ sāsane āgato. Titthāyatanasāmikassāti taranti uplavanti sattā ummujjanimujjaṃ karonti etthāti titthaṃ, dvāsaṭṭhi diṭṭhiyo. Tameva āyatanaṃ diṭṭhigatikānanti titthāyatanaṃ. Atha vā titthametesamatthīti titthino, tesamāyatanaṃ titthāyatanaṃ, tassa sāmiko titthāyatanasāmiko, tassa. Tassa diṭṭhiyāti ettha diṭṭhisaddo laddhipariyāyoti āha “tassa santakāya laddhiyā”ti. Kasmā sā laddhi “khantī”ti ca “rucī”ti ca “ādāyo”ti ca vuccatīti āha “idānī”tiādi. Sāyeva laddhi khamati ceva ruccati ca gahitā cāti yojanā. Tassa titthakarassāti katvatthe sāmivacanaṃ. Tassāti titthāyatanasāmikassa. Bhaññamānāyāti bhaṇiyamānāya. Anabhiraddhoti ettha anabhirādhito aparitositacittoti atthaṃ dassento āha “aparipuṇṇasaṅkappo, no paggahitacitto”ti. Yadidanti yaṃ idaṃ “anattamanatta”nti vā “attamanatta”nti vā sambandho. Iminā “ida”ntipadassa aniyamaṃ dasseti. Imeti bhikkhū. Yañca anattamanattanti yojanā. Tassevāti aññatitthiyapubbassa [M 0.0236] eva anattamanattanti sambandho. Idanti dve attamanattāni, dve anattamanattānīti catubbidhaṃ idaṃ dhammajātaṃ. Saṅghāṭanīyanti saṅghaṭitabbaṃ, sannicayaṃ kātabbanti attho. “Anārādhake”tiādinā anārādhanīyasminti =05 ettha na ārādheti vattaṃ anena kammenāti anārādhanīyanti vacanatthaṃ dasseti. Idanti catubbidhaṃ. Liṅganti kāraṇaṃ. Lakkhaṇanti cihanaṃ. Itoti aṭṭhaṅgato nīhaṭenāti sambandho. Vuttavipallāsenāti kaṇhapakkhe vuttaviparītena.

'Come here' (`idhāgato`) means: come into this Dispensation. 'Of the master of the sectarian haunt' (`titthāyatanasāmikassa`): a 'ford' (`titthaṃ`) is where beings cross over, float, and do sinking and emerging; these are the sixty-two views. That very 'haunt' (`āyatanaṃ`) is the destination of those with speculative views, hence `titthāyatanaṃ`. Or else, those who have fords are 'sectarians' (`titthino`); their haunt is `titthāyatanaṃ`; the master of that is `titthāyatanasāmiko`; 'of him' (`tassa`). Regarding 'by his view' (`tassa diṭṭhiyā`): here the word 'view' (`diṭṭhi`) is a synonym for 'tenet' (`laddhi`); hence he says, 'by the tenet that is his own.' Why is that tenet called 'forbearance' (`khanti`), 'inclination' (`ruci`), and 'acceptance' (`ādāyo`)? He says, 'now,' etc. The construction is: that very tenet is approved of (`khamati`), is liked (`ruccati`), and is adopted (`gahitā`). 'Of that ford-maker' (`tassa titthakarassa`) is a genitive in the sense of the agent. 'His' (`tassa`) means: of the master of the sectarian haunt. 'Being spoken' (`bhaññamānāya`) means `bhaṇiyamānāya`. Regarding 'not delighted' (`anabhiraddho`): here, showing that the meaning is 'not gratified, with mind not pleased,' he says, 'with resolve unfulfilled, with mind not uplifted.' 'Whatever this' (`yadidaṃ`) is connected with either 'dissatisfaction' (`anattamanattā`) or 'satisfaction' (`attamanattā`). By this he shows the indefiniteness of the word 'this' (`idaṃ`). 'These' (`ime`) means: the bhikkhus. The construction is: 'and which is dissatisfaction.' The connection is: 'of that very one' (`tasseva`) means the dissatisfaction of that very former adherent of another sect. 'This' (`idaṃ`) means: this fourfold set of things, namely, two kinds of satisfaction and two kinds of dissatisfaction. 'To be combined' (`saṅghāṭanīyaṃ`) means: to be brought together; the meaning is that an accumulation should be made. By 'displeasing' (`anārādhake`), etc., he shows the meaning of `anārādhanīyasmiṃ` as 'that by which one does not please,' explaining: 'one does not accomplish the duty by this deed.' 'This' (`idaṃ`) is fourfold. 'Sign' (`liṅgaṃ`) means: cause. 'Characteristic' (`lakkhaṇaṃ`) means: mark. The connection is: 'from this' (`ito`) means 'extracted from the eightfold.' 'By the opposite of what was said' (`vuttavipallāsena`) means: by the reverse of what was said in the dark side (`kaṇhapakkhe`).

Sukkapakkhe aṭṭhaṅgāni samodhānetvā dassento āha “nātikālena gāmapavesanaṃ nātidivā paṭikkamana”ntiādi. Kaṇhapakkhepi iminā nayena aṭṭhaṅgāni samodhānetabbāni. “Paritosako”ti iminā ārādhakasaddassa tosanatthaṃ dasseti. Heṭṭhā pana “sampādako”ti vuttattā sādhanatthaṃ dassetīti daṭṭhabbaṃ.

In the bright side (`sukkapakkhe`), combining and showing the eight factors, he says: 'not entering the village at the wrong time, not returning too late in the day,' etc. In the dark side (`kaṇhapakkhe`), too, the eight factors should be combined in this way. By 'gratifying' (`paritosako`), he shows that the word `ārādhaka` has the meaning of 'gratification.' But since 'accomplishing' was stated below, it should be understood that it shows the meaning of 'achievement.'

Upasampadamāḷakepīti upasampādaṭṭhāne ekakūṭayutte anekakoṇe patissayavisesepi. So hi ekakūṭaṃ katvā anekehi koṇehi malīyati vibhūsīyatīti māḷoti vuccati. “Cattāro māse parivasitabba”ntivacanaṃ asadisūpamāya pākaṭaṃ karonto “yathā panā”tiādimāha. Hīti saccaṃ. Assāti aññatitthiyapubbassa. Parivasanto aññatitthiyapubboti sambandho. Antarāti catumāsassa abbhantare. Kuppanasabhāvoti nassanasabhāvo. Pariggaṇhātīti paricchinditvā gaṇhāti. Nāmarūpaṃ vavatthapetīti “idaṃ nāmaṃ, idaṃ rūpa”nti vavatthapeti. Lakkhaṇanti namanaruppanalakkhaṇaṃ, aniccādilakkhaṇaṃ vā. Sotāpattimaggassa diṭṭhivicikicchāpahānaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ “samūhatāni…pe… salla”nti. Abbuḷhanti āvahiyitthāti abbuḷhaṃ, uddhaṃ vahiyitthāti attho. Ātyūpasaggo hi uddhaṅgamattho. Taṃdivasamevāti tasmiṃ sotāpattimaggassa paṭilabhanadivaseyeva. Bhummatthe cetaṃ upayogavacanaṃ. Tadahevāti tasmiṃ sotāpannabhavanaahani eva.

`Upasampadamāḷakepi` means: even in a special dwelling with a single peak and many corners at the place of higher ordination. For since it is made with a single peak and is adorned and decorated with many corners, it is called a `māḷa`. Making the statement ‘Probation is to be undertaken for four months’ clear by means of an incomparable simile, he said, ‘But just as…,’ etc. `Hi` means truly. `Assa` means: of one formerly of another sect. The connection is: ‘one formerly of another sect undergoing probation.’ `Antarā` means within the four months. `Kuppanasabhāvo` means having a perishable nature. `Pariggaṇhāti` means he delimits and grasps. `Nāmarūpaṃ vavatthapeti` means he defines, ‘This is name, this is form.’ `Lakkhaṇaṃ` means the characteristic of bending and breaking up, or the characteristics of impermanence, etc. With reference to the abandoning of view and doubt by the path of stream-entry, it is said, ‘uprooted… the dart.’ `Abbuḷhaṃ` means ‘it has been drawn out’; the meaning is ‘it has been pulled up.’ For the prefix `ā` has the meaning of upward movement. `Taṃdivasameva` means on the very day of attaining the path of stream-entry. And this is a locative of reference. `Tadaheva` means on the very day of becoming a stream-enterer.

Tassāti aññatitthiyapubbassa. Pāḷiyaṃ pattassa anāgatattā vuttaṃ “pattampi tathevā”ti. Yathā upajjhāyamūlakaṃ cīvaraṃ pariyesitabbaṃ, pattampi tathevāti [M 0.0237] attho. Idanti pattacīvaraṃ. Imassāti aññatitthiyapubbassa. Aññeti upajjhāyato apare. Tehipīti aññehipi. Vilomāti paṭilomā. Āyattanti adhīnaṃ. Āyattajīvikattāti aññatitthiyapubbassa upajjhāyena āyattajīvikattā. Tassāti upajjhāyassa. Vacanakaroti vacanaṃ karo. Vākyepi samāsepi vacanasaddassa “tassā”ti padameva apekkhattā “vacanakaro”ti samāso hoti. Eseva nayo “upajjhāyena āyattajīvakattā”ti etthāpi. Tenāti vacanakarahetunā.

`Tassa` means: of one formerly of another sect. Because the bowl is not mentioned in the Pāḷi, it is said, ‘the bowl also in the same way.’ The meaning is: just as the robe should be sought with the preceptor as the basis, so too the bowl. `Idaṃ` means the bowl and robe. `Imassa` means: of this one formerly of another sect. `Aññe` means others apart from the preceptor. `Tehipi` means by others too. `Vilomā` means contrary. `Āyattaṃ` means dependent. `Āyattajīvikattā` means: because the one formerly of another sect has a livelihood dependent on the preceptor. `Tassa` means: of the preceptor. `Vacanakaroti` means he is an obeyer of his word. Whether in a sentence or in a compound, since the word `vacana` requires the word `tassa`, the compound `vacanakaro` is formed. This same principle applies also to `upajjhāyena āyattajīvikattā`. `Tena` means: for the reason of being an obeyer of his word.

Aggiparicaraṇakāti =06 aggipūjakā. Iminā aggiṃ paricarantīti aggikāti vacanatthaṃ dasseti. Tāpasāti jaṭādharā. Te hi yasmā jaṭā ca tapo ca etesamatthi, tasmā “jaṭilā”ti ca “tāpasā”ti ca vuccanti. Eteti jaṭilakā. “Kiriyaṃ na paṭibāhantī”ti vuttavacanassa atthaṃ dassento āha “atthi kammaṃ, atthi kammavipāko”ti. Etadeva pabbajjanti etaṃ eva tāpasapabbajjaṃ. Etesanti jaṭilānaṃ. Sāsaneti buddhassa sāsane. Tesanti ñātīnaṃ, imaṃ parihāranti sambandho. Teti ñātayo. Hīti saccaṃ, yasmā vā. Ñātiseṭṭhassāti ñātiyeva seṭṭho, ñātīnaṃ vāti ñātiseṭṭho, tassa, buddhassāti sambandho.

`Aggiparicaraṇakā` means fire-worshippers (`aggipūjakā`). By this he shows the etymological meaning of `aggikā`: ‘they tend the fire.’ `Tāpasā` means wearers of matted hair (`jaṭādharā`). For since they have both matted hair and asceticism, they are called both `jaṭilā` (matted-hair ascetics) and `tāpasā` (ascetics). `Ete` means these matted-hair ascetics. Showing the meaning of the statement ‘They do not reject action,’ he says, ‘There is kamma, there is the result of kamma.’ `Etadeva pabbajjanti` means this very going forth of ascetics (`tāpasapabbajjaṃ`). `Etesaṃ` means: of the matted-hair ascetics. `Sāsane` means: in the Buddha’s teaching. `Tesaṃ` means: of the relatives; the connection is with 'this privilege' (`imaṃ parihāraṃ`). `Te` means those relatives. `Hi` means truly, or because. `Ñātiseṭṭhassa` means: he is the best kinsman, or the best of kinsmen; the connection is: of him, of the Buddha.

26. Pañcābādhavatthukathā

26. The Story concerning the Five Afflictions

88. Magadhesūti ettha bahuvacanapadena vuttattā janapadassa nāmanti āha “magadhanāmake janapade”ti. Amanussānañcāti manussehi aññasattānañca. Ussannasaddo ca ussadasaddo ca vuḍḍhippattapariyāyoti āha “ussannā vuḍḍhippattā”ti. “Phātippattā”ti iminā tamevatthaṃ dasseti. Tehīti kuṭṭhādīhi pañcahi ābādhehi.

88. Regarding 'in Magadha': here, because it is stated with a plural term, he says it is the name of a country: 'in the country named Magadha.' Regarding 'and of non-humans': and of beings other than humans. The word 'ussanna' and the word 'ussada' are synonyms for having attained growth, thus he says: 'ussannā means having attained growth.' With 'having become widespread' he indicates that same meaning. Regarding 'by them': by the five diseases beginning with leprosy.

Tatthāti kuṭṭhādīsu pañcasu ābādhesu. Ābādhikaṃ ābhuso bādhati pīḷetīti ābādho, aṅgapaccaṅgaṃ kuṭati chindatīti kuṭṭhaṃ. “Rattakuṭṭhaṃ vā”tiādīsu vāsaddena setakuṭṭhādīnipi saṅgaṇhāti. Kīṭibha daddu khajju ādippabhedampīti kīṭibho ca daddu ca khajju ca kīṭibhadaddukhajjuyo[M 0.0238], tā ādayo yesaṃ kuṭṭhānanti kīṭibhadaddukhajjuādayo, tesaṃ pabhedo kīṭibhadaddu khajjuādippabhedo, tampi. Tattha kīṭibhoti kīṭa ibhoti padavibhāgo kātabbo. Tattha kīṭoti kimi. Iminā kīṭakulāvakaṃ “kīṭo”ti gahetabbaṃ, kīṭo viyāti kīṭo, kuṭṭhaviseso. Ibhoti gajo. Iminā gajassa sabalaṃ “ibho”ti gahetabbaṃ. Ibho viyāti ibho, kuṭṭhaviseso. Kīṭoyeva ibho kīṭibho, kuṭṭhābādhaviseso, yaṃ loke “kuṭṭābādha viseso”iti voharanti. Daddūti kacchu. Sā hi sarīraṃ daṃsati vidaṃsati, hiṃsatīti vā dadduti vuccati. Ekassa dakārassa rakāraṃ katvā “daddu”tipi pāṭho. Yaṃ loke “pve:”iti voharanti. Khajjūti kaṇḍuvanaṃ. Tañhi sarīraṃ khajjati byathati khadati, hiṃsatīti vā khajjūti vuccati. Yaṃ loke “khajja”iti voharanti. “Kacchū”tipi pāṭho, so apāṭho daddusaddena tassa gahitattā. Tanti kuṭṭhaṃ. Pakatipaṭicchannaṭṭhāneti pakatiyā paṭicchannaṭṭhāne, yathānivatthapārutaṭṭhāneti attho. Iminā visesato paṭicchannaṃ nivatteti. Avaḍḍhanakapakkhe ṭhitaṃ sace hotīti yojanā. Pakativaṇṇeti =07 pakatichaviyaṃ. Yathā avaṇā chavi hoti, tathāti attho. Idaṃ vaṇavatthuṃ sandhāya na vuttaṃ.

Regarding 'therein': among the five diseases beginning with leprosy. An affliction (ābādho) is so called because it repeatedly harms and oppresses. Leprosy (kuṭṭhaṃ) is so called because it crushes and cuts off the limbs and members. In such phrases as 'or red leprosy,' by the word 'or' he also includes white leprosy and others. Also included are the varieties beginning with kīṭibha, daddu, and khajju: kīṭibha, daddu, and khajju are kīṭibhadaddukhajjuyo; those which have these as their beginning are kīṭibhadaddukhajjuādayo; the variety of these is kīṭibhadaddukhajjuādippabhedo, that also. Therein, 'kīṭibho' should be analyzed as the words 'kīṭa' and 'ibha'. 'Kīṭa' is a worm; by this, a nest of worms should be understood as 'kīṭo'. 'Like a worm' is kīṭa, a type of leprosy. 'Ibha' is an elephant; by this, the mottled skin of an elephant should be understood as 'ibho'. 'Like an elephant' is ibho, a type of leprosy. Kīṭa itself is ibha, thus kīṭibho, a specific type of the disease of leprosy, which is known in the world as 'a specific leprosy disease.' 'Daddū' is scabies; it is so called because it bites, gnaws, or harms the body. By changing one 'd' to an 'r', there is also the reading 'dadru.' This is what is known in the world as 'pve.' 'Khajjū' is itching; it is so called because it scrapes, afflicts, eats, or harms the body. This is what is known in the world as 'khajja.' There is also the reading 'kacchū', but that is an incorrect reading because it is already included by the word 'daddū.' That is leprosy. Regarding 'in a naturally concealed place': in a place naturally concealed; the meaning is, in a place covered by what is worn and draped. By this he excludes what is specifically concealed. The construction is: 'if it is in a state of not increasing.' Regarding 'of natural color': in its natural skin color. The meaning is: just as the skin is without a sore. This was not said in reference to the matter of a sore.

Medagaṇḍoti medo asmiṃ atthīti medo, gaṇḍati phoṭo bhavatīti gaṇḍo, medoyeva gaṇḍo medagaṇḍo. Yaṃ loke “medagaṇḍoiti voharanti. Kolaṭṭhīti kolaṃ vuccati badaraphalaṃ, tassa aṭṭhi kolaṭṭhi. Avaḍḍhanakapakkhe ṭhite satīti yojanā. Sañchavinti saṃvijjamānachaviṃ, sañjātachaviṃ vā. Uṇṇigaṇḍāti uddhaṃ namantīti uṇṇiyo, tāyeva gaṇḍā uṇṇigaṇḍā. Ye loke “uṇṇigaṇḍā” iti voharanti. Tattha tatthāti tasmiṃ tasmiṃ sarīrapadese. Khīrapīḷakāti khīraṃ ettha atthīti khīrā, tā eva pīḷakā khīrapīḷakā. Yā loke “khīrapīḷakā” iti ca iti ca voharanti. Tāsūti pīḷakāsu. Khīrapīḷakā nāma gaṇḍā hontīti sambandho. Kharapīḷakāti kharasabhāvā pīḷakā. Kharasabhāvattā tena sattā maraṇampi gacchanti, maraṇamattampi dukkhaṃ. Yā [M 0.0239] loke iti “khīrapīḷakā” voharanti. Padumakaṇṇikā nāma gaṇḍā hontīti sambandho. Padumassa kaṇṇikā viya padumakaṇṇikā. Yā loke “padumakaṇṇikā”iti voharanti. Sāsapabījakā nāma gaṇḍāti sambandho. Sāsapassa bījaṃ pamāṇametāsanti sāsapabījakā. Yā loke “sāsapabījakā” iti voharanti. Tā sabbāti sabbā tā pīḷakā, gaṇḍajātiyo vā. Tāsūti pīḷakāsu, gaṇḍajātīsu vā.

Regarding 'a fatty tumor' (medagaṇḍo): 'medo' (fat) is so called because 'there is fat in it'; 'gaṇḍo' (tumor) is so called because it becomes a boil; a fatty tumor is a tumor of fat. This is what is known in the world as a 'fatty tumor.' Regarding 'the size of a jujube stone': a 'kola' is the jujube fruit; its stone is a 'kolaṭṭhi'. The construction is: 'when it is in a state of not increasing.' Regarding 'with intact skin': having existing skin, or having skin that has formed. Regarding 'raised tumors' (uṇṇigaṇḍā): 'uṇṇiyo' are so called because they bend upwards; these same are the tumors, 'raised tumors.' These are what are known in the world as 'raised tumors.' Regarding 'here and there': in this or that region of the body. Regarding 'milk boils' (khīrapīḷakā): 'khīrā' is so called because 'there is milk here'; these same are the boils, 'milk boils.' These are what are known in the world as 'milk boils.' Regarding 'in them': in those boils. The connection is: 'milk boils are a type of tumor.' Regarding 'harsh boils' (kharapīḷakā): boils of a harsh nature. Because of their harsh nature, beings can even die from them, or suffer pain equivalent to death. These are what are known in the world as 'harsh boils.' The connection is: 'lotus-pericarp tumors are a type of tumor.' 'Lotus-pericarp tumors' (padumakaṇṇikā) are like the pericarp of a lotus. These are what are known in the world as 'lotus-pericarp tumors.' The connection is: 'mustard-seed tumors are a type of tumor.' 'Mustard-seed tumors' (sāsapabījakā) are so called because they are the size of a mustard seed. These are what are known in the world as 'mustard-seed tumors.' Regarding 'all of them': all those boils, or types of tumors. Regarding 'in them': in those boils, or in those types of tumors.

Padumapuṇḍarīkapattavaṇṇanti padumaṃ nāma rattaṃ, puṇḍarīkaṃ nāma setaṃ, tesaṃ pupphapattassa vaṇṇaṃ viya vaṇṇametassāti padumapuṇḍarīkapattavaṇṇaṃ, saṅkhakuṭṭhaṃ. Yaṃ loke “padumapuṇḍarīkapattavaṇṇaṃ, saṅkhakuṭṭhaṃ” iti voharanti. Yenāti kuṭṭhena. Gunnaṃ sarīraṃ sabalaṃ viya manussānaṃ sarīraṃ sabalaṃ hotīti yojanā. Tasminti kilāse. Sosabyādhīti khayarogo. So hi yasmā maṃsalohitādīni sosāpeti, tasmā sosoti vuccati. Yaṃ loke “sāṃsa” iti ca “sosabyādhi” iti ca voharanti. Tasminti sosabyādhimhi. Apamāroti apasmāro. So hi sārato apagatattā “apamāro”ti vuccati sakārassa makāraṃ katvā. Yaṃ loke “apamāra” iti ca “arū?”Iti ca voharanti. Tatthāti dvīsu ummādesu. Ādhāre cetaṃ bhummavacanaṃ. Duttikiccho hotīti sambandho.

Regarding 'the color of a red and white lotus petal': a 'paduma' is a red lotus, a 'puṇḍarīka' is a white lotus; it is so called because its color is like the color of their flower petals; this is shell-leprosy (saṅkhakuṭṭhaṃ). This is what is known in the world as 'the color of a red and white lotus petal, shell-leprosy.' Regarding 'by which': by that leprosy. The construction is: 'the bodies of humans become mottled like the bodies of cattle.' Regarding 'in that': in that vitiligo. Regarding 'consumption': a wasting disease. It is called 'consumption' (soso) because it causes flesh, blood, and so on, to dry up. This is what is known in the world as 'sāṃsa' and 'consumption disease.' Regarding 'in that': in that consumption disease. Regarding 'apamāra': epilepsy (apasmāro). It is called 'apamāra'—changing the 's' to an 'm'—because it is a departure from memory. This is what is known in the world as 'apamāra' and 'arū.' Regarding 'therein': in the two kinds of insanity. And this is a locative expression indicating the basis. The connection is: 'it is difficult to cure.'

27. Rājabhaṭavatthukathā

27. The Story Concerning the King's Soldier

90. Uccinathāti ettha cidhātuyā vaḍḍhanatthaṃ dassento āha “vaḍḍhethā”ti. Sotāpannattāti bimbisārarañño =08 sotāpannabhāvato. Ghātethāti jīvitā voropetha. Hanathāti paharatha. Tatoti upajjhāyato. Ācariyo seṭṭhoti sambandho. Tatoti ācariyato. Idanti vacanaṃ, āgatanti sambandho. Āhaṃsu vohārikā mahāmattā musāvādenāti yojanā. Amaccoti sabbarājakiccesu amā saha raññā bhavatīti amacco. Amāsaddo sahatthe nipāto. “Amā”ti nipātato bhavatthe accapaccayo [M 0.0240] (moggallāne 4.23 sutte). Mahāmattoti mahanto mattā issariyā etassāti mahāmatto. Mattāsaddo hettha issariyavācako. Sevakoti rājānaṃ sevati bhajatīti sevako. Bhattavetanabhaṭoti bhattavetanānamatthāya bhaṭo. Tassāti rājabhaṭassa. Puttanattabhātukādayotiādisaddena bhāgineyyādayo saṅgaṇhāti. Yo panāti rājabhaṭo pana. Niyyātetīti appeti. Taṃ ṭhānanti taṃ rājabhaṭaṭṭhānaṃ. Yena vāti kammakārena vā. Yaṃkammakāraṇāti yassa kammassa kāraṇā. Yo vāti rājabhaṭo vā. Pabbajassūti pabbājehi.

90. Herein, regarding 'Uccinatha', showing the meaning 'to increase' from the root 'ci', he says 'vaḍḍhethā' (you should increase). 'Sotāpannattā' means because of King Bimbisāra's state of being a stream-enterer. 'Ghātethā' means deprive of life. 'Hanathā' means strike. 'Tato' means from the preceptor. The connection is 'Ācariyo seṭṭho' (the teacher is best). 'Tato' means from the teacher. Regarding 'idaṃ': it means 'the statement'; the connection is with 'āgataṃ'. The construction is: the judicial ministers spoke with a false statement. 'Amacco' means one who is with (amā saha) the king in all royal duties, hence a minister (amacco). The word 'amā' is a particle in the sense of 'together.' From the particle 'amā', the suffix 'acca' is added in the sense of 'being' (as in Moggallāna 4.23). 'Mahāmatto' means one for whom authority (mattā issariyā) is great (mahanto), hence a high official (mahāmatto). Here the word 'mattā' is a term for authority. 'Sevako' means one who serves (sevati) or attends upon (bhajati) the king, hence a servant (sevako). 'Bhattavetanabhaṭo' means a soldier (bhaṭo) for the sake of food and wages. 'Tassa' means of the king's soldier. Regarding 'puttanattabhātukādayo', by the word 'ādi' (and so on) it includes nephews and others. 'Yo pana' means that royal soldier. 'Niyyāteti' means hands over. 'Taṃ ṭhānaṃ' means that position of a king's soldier. 'Yena vā' means by whatever workman. 'Yaṃkammakāraṇā' means because of which work. 'Yo vā' means that royal soldier. 'Pabbajassu' means ordain him.

28. Coravatthukathā

28. The Story Concerning a Thief

91. Diṭṭhapubboti aṅgulimālo pubbe diṭṭho. Ayanti coro. Soti aṅgulimālo. Aññesaṃ santikā vacanaṃ suṇantīti yojanā. Teti manussā. Ubbijjantipīti kāyena ubbijjantipi. Uttasantipīti cittena uttasantipi. Aṅgulimālo bhikkhūhi na pabbājito, nanu bhagavatā pana sayaṃ pabbājito, atha kasmā “na bhikkhave”ti vuttanti āha “bhagavā sayaṃ dhammassāmī”ti. Dhammassāmīti ca dhammassa issaro, dhammena vā devamanussānaṃ issaro, adhipatīti attho. Bhikkhūnaṃ akaraṇatthāya bhikkhūnaṃ sikkhāpadanti yojanā. Tatthāti “na bhikkhave”tiādivacane. “Dhajaṃ bandhitvā”tiādinā dhajassa bandhanaṃ dhajabandho, dhajabandho viyāti dhajabandho, dhajabandho hutvā caratīti dhajabandhoti vacanatthaṃ dasseti. Tasmāti yasmā dhajabandho, tasmā. Yoti coro. Panthaduhanaṃ vāti panthe duhanaṃ vā. Paññāyati cāti ettha casaddo vākyasampiṇḍanattho. Na kevalañhi vicaratiyeva, atha kho paññāyati cāti attho. Idanti corakammaṃ. Rajjanti rājabhāvaṃ. Soti rājaputto. Hīti saccaṃ, yasmā vā. Tasminti rājaputte. Pubbeti pubbakāle. Tanti coraṃ. Evanti iminākārena, jānanti ceti yojanā. Adissamānāti attānaṃ apaññāyamānā. Idaṃ sandhicchedādicore [M 0.0241] sandhāya vuttaṃ, na ambalabujādicore. Pacchāpīti theyyakaraṇato pacchāpi. Tepīti corepi.

91. Diṭṭhapubbo means Aṅgulimāla was seen before. Ayaṃ means this thief. So means Aṅgulimāla. The construction is: they hear the word from others. Te means those people. Ubbijjantipi means they are agitated in body. Uttasantipi means they are terrified in mind. Aṅgulimāla was not ordained by the bhikkhus, but was he not ordained by the Blessed One himself? So why was it said, 'Not, O bhikkhus'? To this, it is said: 'The Blessed One is himself the master of the Dhamma.' Master of the Dhamma means he is the lord of the Dhamma, or through the Dhamma he is the lord and sovereign of gods and humans; this is the meaning. The construction is: for the purpose of it not being done by the bhikkhus, it is a training rule for the bhikkhus. Therein, in the statement beginning 'Not, O bhikkhus,' by the phrase beginning 'having tied a flag,' he shows the meaning of the word dhajabandho: the tying of a flag is dhajabandho; like a tied flag is dhajabandho; one who roams about having become a tied flag is a dhajabandho. Tasmā means because he is a dhajabandho, therefore. Yo means the thief. Panthaduhanaṃ vā means harassing on the road. Herein, regarding paññāyati ca, the particle ca is for the purpose of connecting the sentence. The meaning is: not only does he roam, but he is also recognized. Idaṃ means the act of thievery. Rajjaṃ means the state of kingship. So means the king's son. Hi means truly, or because. Tasmiṃ means in that king's son. Pubbe means in a former time. Taṃ means that thief. The construction is: evaṃ, in this way, they know. Adissamānā means not being perceived. This is said with reference to a house-breaking thief, not to thieves such as Ambalabujā. Pacchāpi means even after the act of stealing. Tepi means even those thieves.

92. Bhayenāti bhayato. Ete panāti bhikkhū pana. Laddhābhayattāti rājato laddho abhayo imehīti laddhābhayā, tesaṃ bhāvo laddhābhayattaṃ, tasmā. Kārabhedakoti ettha kārasaddo rukkhavisese =09 ca sakkāre ca bandhanālaye ca pavattati, idha pana bandhanālayeti dassento āha “kāraṃ vuccati bandhanāgāra”nti. Bandhanāgārañhi karonti taṃ pavesite jane hiṃsanti etthāti “kārā”ti vuccati. Idhāti “kārabhedako”tipade. Dīpabandhanaṃ vā hotūti yojanā. Imehi padehi na kevalaṃ bandhanāgāraṃyeva kārā nāma hoti, atha kho andubandhanādīnipi kārāyeva nāmāti dasseti. Yoti coro. Etesūti bandhanesu. Muñcitvā vāti rajjubandhanaṃ nibbeṭhetvā vā. Imehi padehi na kevalaṃ kārāya bhindanato eva kārabhedako nāma hoti, atha kho chindanamuñcanavivaraṇehipi kārabhedakoyeva nāmāti dasseti. Dīpantaranti bandhanadīpato antaraṃ aññaṃ dīpanti attho. Cakkavāḷabandhanaṃ bhinditvā cakkavāḷantaraṃ gato aṭṭhakathāyaṃ na vutto. Soti nacorako. Gāmanigamapaṭṭanādīnīti ettha paṭṭananti nāvāpaṭṭanaṃ, sakaṭapaṭṭanañca. Keṇiyāti rañño dātabbaāyena. Tanti keṇiṃ. Nidhānanti nikkhaṇitvā ṭhapitaṃ dhanaṃ. Upasaṃharitvāti rājādīnaṃ santikaṃ haritvā. Tanti kasikammādīhi sampādetvā jīvantaṃ. Tatthevāti bandhāpitaṭṭhāneyeva.

92. Bhayena means from fear. Ete pana means these bhikkhus. Laddhābhayattā means: safety from the king has been obtained by them, thus they are laddhābhayā; their state is laddhābhayattaṃ; therefore. Regarding kārabhedako, herein the word kāra pertains to a type of tree, to honor, and to a place of confinement. But here, showing it means a place of confinement, he says: 'A prison is called kāra.' For a prison is made, and since they harm people led into it, it is called kārā. Idha means in the term kārabhedako. The connection is: or it may be confinement on an island. By these terms it is shown that not only a prison is called kārā, but also confinement in stocks and so on are also called kārā. Yo means the thief. Etesu means in these confinements. Muñcitvā vā means having untied the rope bonds. By these terms it is shown that one is called a kārabhedako not only from breaking out of a prison, but also from cutting, releasing, or opening bonds. Dīpantaraṃ means another island different from the island of confinement; this is the meaning. Breaking the confinement of a world-sphere and going to another world-sphere is not stated in the commentary. So means one who is not a thief. Herein, regarding gāmanigamapaṭṭanādīni, paṭṭana means a seaport or a caravan town. Keṇiyā means by the revenue to be given to the king. Taṃ means that revenue. Nidhānaṃ means treasure that has been dug up and stored. Upasaṃharitvā means having brought it to the king and others. Taṃ means one who lives by providing for himself through agriculture and other work. Tattheva means right in the place where one was confined.

93. Yatthāti yasmiṃ ṭhāne. Yo koci palātoti sambandho. Nanti yaṃ kiñci janaṃ, likhāpetīti yojanā. Paṇṇe vāti kuse vā. Assāti janassa. Daṇḍanti dhanadaṇḍaṃ. Likhitakoti likhitabboti likhito, soyeva likhitako.

93. Yattha means in whatever place. The connection is yo koci palāto (whoever has fled). Naṃ means any person; the construction is likhāpeti (he has it written). Paṇṇe vā means on a leaf or on kusa grass. Assa means of a person. Daṇḍaṃ means a monetary fine. Likhitako means what is to be written is written; that itself is likhitako.

94. Yo pana kasāhi haññatīti sambandho. Iminā aññehi kasāhi haññatīti kasāhatoti vacanatthaṃ dasseti. “Ayameva te daṇḍo hotū”ti iminā kataṃ daṇḍakammaṃ imassāti katadaṇḍakammoti vacanatthaṃ dasseti. Allavaṇoti tintavaṇo. Ghātetvāti hanitvā [M 0.0242] paharitvāti attho. Gaṇḍigaṇḍiyoti phoṭaphoṭā. Sannisinnāsūti gaṇḍīsu pakatisarīrena samaṃ nisinnāsu.

94. The connection is yo pana kasāhi haññati (but whoever is beaten with whips). By this he shows the meaning of the word kasāhato as 'one who is beaten with whips or other such things.' By the phrase 'Let this itself be your punishment,' he shows the meaning of the word katadaṇḍakammo as 'one for whom a punishment has been inflicted.' Allavaṇo means of a moist color. Ghātetvā means having struck or beaten; this is the meaning. Gaṇḍigaṇḍiyo means blister upon blister. Sannisinnāsu means when the blisters have subsided to the level of the natural body.

95. Katadaṇḍakammabhāvo tāva purimanayeneva veditabbo hotu, kathaṃ pana lakkhaṇāhatabhāvo veditabboti āha “yassa panā”tiādi. Tattha tattenāti tāpena. Lakkhaṇanti saññāṇaṃ. Soti jano. Bhujissoti bhujo etassatthīti bhujisso (ma. ni. ṭī. 2.426). Parehi apālito ca anajjhoharāpito ca hutvā sayameva attānaṃ pālanena ca bhojanaṃ ajjhoharaṇena ca samannāgatoti vuttaṃ hoti. Assāti lakkhaṇāhatassa. Vaṇāti arūni. Tāni hi yasmā vaṇanti gattāni vicuṇṇāni karonti, tasmā vaṇāti vuccanti. Rūḷhāti taruṇamaṃsena ruhā. Timaṇḍalavatthassa lakkhaṇāhatassa janassāti sambandho.

95. Let the state of one for whom a punishment has been inflicted be understood in the preceding way. But how is the state of one who has been struck with a mark to be understood? To this, he says the passage beginning 'But for whom...' Therein, tattena means by heat. Lakkhaṇaṃ means a sign. So means a person. Bhujisso means one who has freedom. It is said that he is endowed with self-sustenance and with obtaining food by himself, being neither protected nor fed by others. Assa means of one who has been struck with a mark. Vaṇā means sores. For since they wound—that is, they break up—the limbs, they are called wounds. Rūḷhā means healed with new flesh. The connection is: of a person who has been struck with a mark on the area of the three circles.

33. Iṇāyikavatthukathā

33. The Story of the Debtor

96. Iṇāyiko [V 1.0210] nāmāti ettha iṇanti uddhāro. So hi yasmā eti vuddhiṃ gacchati, tasmā iṇanti vuccati. Taṃ gaṇhāti, dhāretīti vā iṇāyiko. Yaṃ vāti janaṃ vā āṭhapetvāti sambandho. Āṭhapetvāti ca pesanatthāya dhanasāmikassa santike ṭhapetvāti attho. Ākāro hi pesanatthavācako. Sopīti pisaddo purimajane apekkhati. “Dhāretī”ti iminā āyikapaccayo dhāraṇatthe hotīti dasseti. Aññeti mātāpitūhi aññe. Hīti saccaṃ, yasmā vā. Teti aññe ñātakā, taṃ āṭhapetuṃ yasmā na issarā, tasmā na iṇāyikoti yojanā. Itaranti naiṇāyikato aññaṃ. Assāti janassa. Nanti taṃ janaṃ. Tesūti ñātisālohitādīsu. Tathārūpassāti attano ñātisālohitassāti attho. Ārocetabbākāraṃ dassento āha “sahetuko”tiādi. Tattha sahetukoti bhabbo. Soti upaṭṭhāko[M 0.0243]. Paṭipajjatīti paṭidadāti. Etanti kappiyabhaṇḍaṃ. Ajānitvāti iṇāyikabhāvamajānitvā. Passantenāti iṇāyikaṃ passantena. “Apassantassa gīvā na hotī”ti iminā passitvā adassentassa gīvā hotīti dasseti.

96. Herein, regarding 'a debtor' (iṇāyiko): 'debt' (iṇa) means a loan (uddhāro). Because it goes (eti) to growth (vuddhiṃ gacchati), it is called 'debt.' One who takes (gaṇhāti) or holds (dhāreti) it is a 'debtor' (iṇāyiko). The connection is with 'or having placed a person' (janaṃ vā āṭhapetvā). 'Having placed' (āṭhapetvā) means placing someone in the presence of the owner of the wealth for the purpose of sending. For the prefix 'ā' expresses the meaning of sending. In 'he too' (so pi), the word pi refers to the previous person. By 'holds' (dhāreti), it shows that the suffix -āyika is in the sense of holding. 'Others' (aññe) means others than mother and father. Hi means 'indeed' or 'because.' The construction is: 'they' (te) refers to other relatives; because they are not able to place him, they are therefore not debtors. 'The other' (itaraṃ) means other than a non-debtor. Assa means 'of the person.' Naṃ means 'that person.' Tesu means 'among relatives, kinsmen, and so on.' 'Of such a one' (tathārūpassa) means of one's own relatives and kinsmen. Showing the way it should be announced, he said, 'with a reason' (sahetuko), and so on. Therein, 'with a reason' means capable (bhabbo). 'He' (so) is the attendant. 'Undertakes' (paṭipajjati) means 'repays' (paṭidadāti). 'This' (etaṃ) means a suitable requisite. 'Not knowing' (ajānitvā) means not knowing his status as a debtor. 'By one who sees' (passantena) means by one who sees the debtor. By the phrase 'for one who does not see, there is no liability,' it shows that for one who sees but does not point him out, there is liability.

Pucchiyamānopīti “kiṃ tvaṃ iṇāyikosī”ti pucchiyamānopi. Tanti iṇāyikaṃ. Tatthāti aññasmiṃ dese. Tanti iṇasāmikaṃ. Soti iṇasāmiko. Ayanti iṇāyiko. Ayanti vacanā. Tatthāti iṇāyikassa pabbājane. Sāmīcīti anudhammatā.

'Even when asked' means being questioned, 'Are you a debtor?'. 'That' refers to the debtor. 'There' means in another country. 'That' refers to the creditor. 'He' is the creditor. 'This' refers to the debtor. 'This' is the expression. 'There' refers to the ordination of the debtor. 'Proper' means conformity with the Dhamma.

Nanti iṇāyikaṃ. Soti iṇasāmiko. Assāti therassa. Gīvā na hotīti sambandho. Acchatūti āsatu upavesatūti attho. Soti iṇāyiko. Īdisoti sahetuko vattasampannoti attho. Atiārādhakoti vattācārena therassa atitosako.

'Naṃ' refers to the debtor. 'He' is the creditor. 'Assa' refers to the elder. The connection is 'there is no liability.' 'Acchatu' means let him stay or let him be seated. 'He' is the debtor. 'Such' means one with a reason, accomplished in his duties. 'Highly pleasing' means one who greatly satisfies the elder through his conduct and duties.

34. Dāsavatthukathā

34. The Story of the Slave

97. Dāsāti ceṭakā. Te hi sāmikehi dukkhe vā duṭṭhakamme vā asīyanti khipīyantīti dāsāti vuccanti. Tatthāti catūsu dāsesu. “Gharadāsiyā putto”ti iminā antogehe gharadāsiyā kucchimhi jāto antojātoti vacanatthaṃ dasseti. Dhanaṃ datvā kīto dhanakkītoti vacanatthaṃ dassento āha “dhanakkīto nāmā”tiādi. Dhanena kīto dhanakkītoti [V 1.0211] vacanatthopi yuttoyeva. Dāsacārittanti desakālavasena dāsānaṃ cārittaṃ. Tattha tatthāti tasmiṃ tasmiṃ dese, kāle vā.

97. 'Slaves' (`dāsa`) means servants (`ceṭaka`). They are called slaves because they are thrown or cast by their masters into suffering or evil deeds. 'Therein' refers to the four kinds of slaves. By 'the son of a female household slave,' it shows the etymological meaning of 'born inside' (`antojāta`) as one born in the womb of a female household slave inside the house. Showing the etymological meaning of 'bought with wealth' (`dhanakkīta`), he says, 'one bought with wealth is called…,' and so on. The etymological meaning 'one bought with wealth is `dhanakkīta`' is also suitable. 'The conduct of slaves' means the conduct of slaves according to country and time. 'In this or that' means in this or that country, or time.

Karamarānīto nāmāti ettha karamaroti vandi. So hi sattūnaṃ karena hatthena maritabbattā karamaroti vuccati. Karamarabhāvena ānīto karamarānīto. Tiroraṭṭhā āharantīti sambandho. Upalāpetvā [M 0.0244] vāti palobhetvā vā. Tatoti kasmāci gāmato. Manussā eva mānussakāni. Itthipurisānaṃ sādhāraṇabhāvena sāmaññabhāvato napuṃsakaliṅgavasena vuttaṃ. Pisaddena na kevalaṃ dhanāniyeva āharanti, atha kho mānussakānipīti sampiṇḍeti. Tatthāti mānussakesu. Evarūpo karamarānīto dāso na pabbājetabboti yojanā. Sabbasādhāraṇenāti bandhanāgārasodhanakāle sabbesaṃ sādhāraṇena.

Herein, regarding 'one brought as a captive of war' (`karamarānīta`): a 'captive of war' (`karamara`) means a prisoner (`vandi`). He is called a `karamara` because he is to be killed by the hand (`karena`, that is, `hatthena`) of his enemies. One brought in the state of a captive of war is a `karamarānīta`. The connection is with 'they bring from a foreign country.' 'Or having persuaded' (`upalāpetvā`) means 'or having enticed' (`palobhetvā`). 'From there' means from some village. 'Human beings' (`mānussakāni`) means people themselves. Because it is common to men and women, due to its generic nature, it is stated in the neuter gender. By the word `pi` (also), he combines them, meaning: 'they bring not only wealth, but also human beings.' 'Therein' means among the human beings. The construction is: a slave of this kind, one brought as a captive of war, should not be ordained. 'By what is common to all' means what is common to all at the time of a prison amnesty.

Dāsabyanti dāsassa bhāvo dāsabyaṃ, taṃ. Tena vuttaṃ “dāsabhāva”nti. “Sayamevā”ti iminā sāmaṃsaddo sayamatthe nipātoti dasseti. Bhujissitthiyoti rañño bhujissitthiyo. Vaṇṇadāsīhīti nagarasobhinīhi. Tā hi vaṇṇasampannadāsibhāvato vaṇṇadāsīti vuccanti. Tāsanti bhujissitthīnaṃ. Paṇṇanti dāsipaṇṇaṃ. Bhaṭiputtakagaṇādīnanti ādisaddena mallaputtagaṇādayo saṅgaṇhāti. Iminā bahusāmikadāsaṃ dasseti. Tehīti bhaṭiputtakagaṇādīhi. Adinnā na pabbājetabbāti bahūsu sāmikesu ekenapi adinnā na pabbājetabbā. Tepīti ārāmikadāsepi. Imasmiṃ ārāmikadāsapabbājane aṭṭhakathāvādaṃ dassento āha “mahāpaccariya”ntiādi. “Takka”nti padaṃ “āsittaka”iti pade kammaṃ. “Sīse”ti padaṃ “āsittaka”iti pade ādhāro. Kesuci janapadesu desacārittavasena sīse takkassa āsiñcanaṃ dāsānaṃ bhujissakaraṇanti adhippāyo. “Ārāmikaṃ demā”ti vacanaṃ dāsānaṃ bhujissavacananti vuttaṃ hoti. Yena kenaci vohārenāti “ārāmikaṃ demā”ti vā “ārāmikadāsaṃ demā”ti vā “kappiyakārakaṃ demā”ti vā yena kenaci vohārena. Dvīsu aṭṭhakathāvādesu kurundivādassa pacchā vuttattā soyeva pamāṇanti daṭṭhabbaṃ. Duggatamanussāti dukkhaṃ gatamanussā. Eteti duggatamanusse. Taṃ pabbājetuṃ na vaṭṭatīti mātāpitūnaṃ dāsabhāvaṃ upagatakāle jātaṃ puttaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ. Atha pana mātāpitaro dāsabhāvaṃ upagatā, na putto, taṃ pabbājetuṃ vaṭṭati. “Bhikkhussā”tipadaṃ “ñātakā vā upaṭṭhākā vā”tipadesu sāmisambandho, “dentī”ti pade sampadānaṃ. Assāti [M 0.0245] bhikkhussa. Imanti dāsaṃ. Abhiramissatīti bhikkhubhāve abhiramissati. Vibbhamissatīti vinivattetvā gihibhāvaṃ bhamissati. Iti vatvā dentīti sambandho. Nissāmikadāsoti pariggāhakasāmikavirahito dāso[V 1.0212]. Nissāmikassa dāsassa rājā sāmī, tasmā raññā apariggahite attanāva attānaṃ bhujissaṃ kātuṃ vaṭṭati. Pariggahite rājānaṃ kārāpetuṃ vaṭṭati. Ajānantoti attano dāsabhāvamajānanto.

'Slavery' (`dāsabya`) is the state of being a slave. Therefore it is said, 'the state of slavery' (`dāsabhāva`). By 'by oneself' (`sayamevā`), it shows that the word `sāmaṃ` is a particle in the sense of 'oneself.' 'Freedwomen' (`bhujissitthiyo`) means the king's freedwomen. 'By courtesans' (`vaṇṇadāsīhi`) means by city-beautifying women. They are called `vaṇṇadāsī` because they are slaves endowed with beauty. 'Of them' (`tāsaṃ`) means of the freedwomen. 'Price' (`paṇṇaṃ`) means the price of a female slave. Regarding 'guilds of soldiers' sons, etc.,' by the word 'etc.' (`ādi`), he includes guilds of wrestlers' sons and so on. By this, he indicates a slave with many masters. 'By them' (`tehi`) means by the guilds of soldiers' sons, etc. 'Not given, they should not be ordained' means that if not given permission by even one among many masters, they should not be ordained. 'They too' (`tepi`) refers also to monastery slaves. Showing the commentarial opinion on this matter of ordaining monastery slaves, he says, 'In the Mahāpaccarī,' etc. The word 'buttermilk' (`takka`) is the object of the word 'sprinkled' (`āsittaka`). The word 'on the head' (`sīse`) is the location for the word 'sprinkled.' The intention is that in some districts, according to local custom, the sprinkling of buttermilk on the head is the act of freeing slaves. The statement 'We give a monastery attendant' is said to be the statement of freeing for slaves. 'By whatever expression' means by whatever expression, such as 'We give a monastery attendant,' or 'We give a monastery slave,' or 'We give an allowable attendant.' It should be understood that of the two commentarial views, since the view of the Kurundī is stated last, that alone is the authority. 'Wretched people' (`duggatamanussā`) means people who have gone to suffering. 'These' (`ete`) means these wretched people. 'It is not allowable to ordain him' is said with reference to a son born at the time his parents had entered a state of slavery. But if the parents have entered a state of slavery, but not the son, it is allowable to ordain him. The word 'of the bhikkhu' has a possessive relation with the words 'relatives or supporters,' and a dative relation with the word 'they give.' 'Of him' (`assa`) means of the bhikkhu. 'This' (`imaṃ`) means this slave. 'He will delight' means he will delight in the state of a bhikkhu. 'He will become disaffected' means he will turn back and revert to the lay life. The connection is: 'having said this, they give.' 'A masterless slave' is a slave devoid of an owner who has taken possession of him. For a masterless slave, the king is the owner. Therefore, if he has not been taken possession of by the king, it is allowable for him to free himself. If he has been taken possession of, it is allowable to have the king perform the freeing. 'Not knowing' means not knowing his own state of slavery.

Anurādhapurāti anurādhanagarato nikkhamitvāti sambandho. Soti putto. Idhāti rohaṇe. Mātaraṃ pucchitvāti sambandho. Āgammāti āgantvā. Aticchathāti atikkamitvā icchatha, idha kiñci deyyadhammaṃ natthi, idaṃ atikkamitvā aññattha ṭhātumicchathāti vuttaṃ hoti. Teti gharasāmikā. Catūhi paccayehi paṭijaggantā vasāpesunti yojanā.

'From Anurādhapura' is connected with 'having departed from the city of Anurādha.' 'He' (`so`) means the son. 'Here' (`idha`) means in Rohaṇa. The connection is with 'having asked his mother.' 'Āgamma' means 'having come.' 'Aticchatha' means 'having passed by, you desire.' This means it is said: 'Here there is nothing to be given; having passed this by, you desire to stay elsewhere.' 'They' (`te`) refers to the householders. The construction is: 'they had them stay, looking after them with the four requisites.'

35. Kammārabhaṇḍuvatthuādikathā

35. The Story of the Bald Smith

98. Tulādhāramuṇḍakoti mānabhaṇḍadhāro muṇḍako. Iminā kammārabhaṇḍūti ettha kammārasaddo tulādhārapariyāyo, bhaṇḍusaddo muṇḍakapariyāyoti dasseti. Tulādhāro hi alaṅkāravikatikaraṇatthāya kammaṃ arati jānātīti kammāroti vuccati. Muṇḍako bhaṇḍīyati “muṇḍo”ti paribhāsīyatīti bhaṇḍūti vuccati. “Suvaṇṇakāraputto”ti iminā tassa sarūpaṃ dasseti. Apaloketunti ettha apapubbo lokasaddo āpucchanatthoti āha “āpucchitu”nti. “Bhaṇḍukammatthāyā”ti iminā bhaṇḍukammāyāti ettha tadatthe catutthīti dasseti. Tatrāti “saṅghaṃ apaloketu”ntiādivacane. Sīmāpariyāpanneti vihārasīmāya vā upacārasīmāya vā pariyāpanne. Tatthāti bhikkhūnaṃ sannipātaṭṭhānaṃ. Ettha cāti āpucchane ca. Vattuṃ vaṭṭatiyevāti pañcasu vākyesu yaṃkiñci vākyaṃ kathetuṃ vaṭṭatiyeva. Pisaddena “imassa muṇḍakammaṃ āpucchāmī”ti vākyampi saṅgaṇhāti.

98. `Tulādhāramuṇḍako` means a bald man carrying a balance. By this it is shown that in the term `kammārabhaṇḍu`, the word `kammāra` is a synonym for a balance-holder, and the word `bhaṇḍu` is a synonym for a bald man. A balance-holder is called a `kammāra` because he undertakes or knows the work of making and selling ornaments. A bald man is called a `bhaṇḍu` because he is reviled or addressed as 'bald-head.' 'Son of a goldsmith' indicates his identity. Regarding `apaloketun`, the word `loka` preceded by `apa` has the sense of asking permission; thus he says, 'to ask permission.' By '`bhaṇḍukammatthāyā`,' it is shown that here in `bhaṇḍukammāya` the dative case is used in the sense of 'for that purpose.' `Tatrā` refers to the statement such as 'to ask permission of the Saṅgha.' `Sīmāpariyāpanne` means included within the monastery boundary or its surrounding area. `Tatthā` is the monks' assembly place. `Ettha ca` means 'and also in asking permission.' `Vattuṃ vaṭṭatiyeva` means it is indeed permissible to say any one of the five sentences. The word `pi` also includes the sentence, 'I ask permission for this man's tonsure.'

Tesanti [M 0.0246] vīsatiādīnaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ. “Daharabhikkhū vā sāmaṇere vā”ti idaṃ āsannavasena vuttaṃ. Gihimpi pesetvā āpucchāpetuṃ vaṭṭati. Kasmā? “Pabbajjāpekkhaṃ vinā vā”ti vuttattā.

`Tesaṃ` refers to the twenty or so monks. 'Young monks or novices' is said with reference to what is at hand. It is permissible to send even a layperson to have permission asked. Why? Because it is said, 'or without one who is seeking to go forth'.

Pabbājentassa anāpattiyeva, supabbajitoti āha “pabbājentassāpi anāpattī”ti.

For one who gives the going forth, there is no offense—he is well gone forth; hence it is said, 'for one who gives the going forth also, there is no offense.'

Āpucchitaṃ pagevāti yojanā. Khaṇḍasīmāyanti vihārasīmāya vā upacārasīmāya vā abbhantare ṭhitāyaṃ khaṇḍasīmāyaṃ. Yo panāti pabbajjāpekkho pana. Vibbhantako vāti navavibbhantako [V 1.0213] vā. Pabbajitānaṃ dvaṅgulakeso vaṭṭatīti āha “dvaṅgulakeso vā”ti. Dvīhi aṅgulīhi atiritto keso imassāti dvaṅgulātirittakeso. Ekasikhāmattadharopi hotīti yojanā.

The construction is: `Āpucchitaṃ pageva`. `Khaṇḍasīmāyaṃ` means in a separate boundary located within the monastery boundary or its surrounding area. `Yo pana` means 'but one who is seeking to go forth.' `Vibbhantako vā` means 'or one who has recently returned to lay life.' He says 'or hair two finger-breadths long' because for those who have gone forth, hair two finger-breadths long is allowable. `Dvaṅgulātirittakeso` means 'one whose hair is longer than two finger-breadths.' The construction is: 'or one who wears just a single topknot.'

100. Mārabyādhināti māraṇābādho. So hi sattānaṃ māraṇaṭṭhena, vividhassa ca dukkhassa ādahaṭṭhena mārabyādhīti vuccati. Iminā ahivātakarogenāti ettha ahivisasadisena vātena pavatto rogo ahivātakarogoti vuccatīti dasseti. Tamatthaṃ vitthārento āha “yatra hī”tiādi. Tattha yatrāti yasmiṃ kule. So rogo tasmiṃ kule dvipade catuppade paṭhamaṃ gaṇhāti, pacchā gehasāmike gaṇhātīti dhammapadaaṭṭhakathāyaṃ (dha. pa. aṭṭha. 1.sāmāvatīvatthu) vuttaṃ. Tathāti yathā añño bhittiṃ vā chadanaṃ vā bhinditvā palāyitvā tirogāmādigato vā hutvā muccati, tathā. Ettha ca kule pitāputtā mucciṃsūti attho.

100. Mārabyādhinā means a deadly illness. For it is called a deadly illness (mārabyādhi) because it means death for beings and because it inflicts various kinds of suffering. Herein, regarding 'by this disease of snake-wind,' it is shown that a disease that arises from a wind similar to snake venom is called the 'disease of snake-wind.' Expanding on that meaning, he says, 'For where,' etc. There, yatra means 'in which family.' That disease first seizes the bipeds and quadrupeds in that family, and afterwards it seizes the masters of the house; so it is said in the Dhammapada Commentary (Dhp-a I, Sāmāvatīvatthu). Tathā means: just as another is freed by breaking through a wall or a roof and escaping, having gone to another village, etc., so too. And here the meaning is that in the family the father and son were freed.

Kākuḍḍepakanti ettha kāke uḍḍāpetīti kākuḍḍepako, kāke vā uḍḍāpetvā bhattaṃ bhuñjituṃ sakkotīti kākuḍḍepakoti vacanatthaṃ dassento āha “yo vāmahatthenā”tiādi. Tattha uḍḍāpetvāti uddhaṃ ākāsaṃ gamanāpetvā. Tanti kākuḍḍepakaṃ.

Herein, regarding kākuḍḍepaka: one who makes crows fly up is a kākuḍḍepaka, or one who is able to eat his meal after having made the crows fly up is a kākuḍḍepaka. Showing the meaning of the word, he says, 'He who with his left hand,' etc. There, uḍḍāpetvā means having made them go up into the sky. Tan refers to the kākuḍḍepaka.

102. Ittarasaddo [M 0.0247] appamattakavācako anipphannapāṭipadikoti āha “appamattako”ti. “Katipāhamevā”ti iminā tassa atthaṃ dasseti.

102. The word ittara is an underived nominal stem that signifies something slight; hence he says, 'slight.' By 'for just a few days,' it shows its meaning.

40. Nissayamuccanakakathā

40. The Discourse on Release from Dependence

103. Ogaṇenāti ettha otyūpasaggo lāmakatthavācakoti āha “parihīnagaṇenā”ti. Attano vuḍḍhatarasseva bhikkhussa santike nissayo gahetabboti āha “sacāyaṃ vuḍḍhatara”ntiādi. Tattha ayanti abyatto bhikkhu. Upasampadāyāti upasampādetvā. Āyasmatoti āyasmantaṃ, upayogatthe cetaṃ sāmivacanaṃ. Āyasmato vā ovādanti yojanā. Sabbatthāti sabbesu. Āpucchanesūti disāpakkamanādiatthāya āpucchanesu. Etthāti imasmiṃ nissayavasanaṭṭhāne. Tanti tattakaṃ sutaṃ. Tassāti sutassa.

103. Regarding ogaṇena, here the prefix o- signifies something base; hence he says, 'with an inferior group.' He says, 'If this one is senior,' etc., because dependence should be taken from a monk who is senior to oneself. There, ayaṃ means the incompetent monk. Upasampadāya means having given the higher ordination. Āyasmato means āyasmantaṃ (accusative); this genitive is used in the sense of the objective case. Or the construction is: 'the advice of the venerable one.' Sabbattha means in all cases. Āpucchanesu means in cases of asking permission for such purposes as departing for another region. Ettha means in this place of living in dependence. Tan means that much has been heard. Tassa means of what has been heard.

41. Rāhulavatthukathā

41. The Story of Rāhula

105. Kapilavatthūti [V 1.0214] ettha kapiloti kaḷāravaṇṇo isi vuccati, so vasati etthāti kapilavatthu, assamo. Tasmiṃ ṭhāne māpitattā nagarampi kapilavatthūti (dī. ni. aṭṭha. 1.267; su. ni. aṭṭha. 2.362) vuccati. Ayanti vakkhamānakathā. Suddhodanamahārājāti ettha suddhodanoti tassa rañño nāmaṃ. Atha vā suddhaṃ odanaṃ imassāti suddhodano, soyeva mahārājā suddhodanamahārājā. Viharati kirāti sambandho. Soti suddhodanamahārājā. Rājagahanti rājagahanagaraṃ. Sādhūti āyācanatthe nipāto. Āyācāmīti hi attho. Meti mama, puttanti sambandho, anādare vā sāmivacanaṃ. Soti amacco. Sādhūti sampaṭicchanatthe nipāto. Evanti hi attho. Athāti tasmiṃ nisīdanakāle. Assāti purisasahassaparivārassa amaccassa. Tatoti yācanakāraṇā[M 0.0248]. Nanti purisasahassaparivāraṃ amaccaṃ. Tatthevāti rājagaheyeva. Tepīti aṭṭha dūtāpi. Teti nava dūtā.

105. Regarding Kapilavatthu: here, kapila refers to a tawny-colored sage. 'He dwells here'—thus it is Kapilavatthu, a hermitage. Because a city was built in that place, it too is called Kapilavatthu (Dī. Ni. Aṭṭha. 1.267; Su. Ni. Aṭṭha. 2.362). Ayaṃ means the following account. Regarding King Suddhodana: here, Suddhodana is that king's name. Or, 'he has pure rice,' thus Suddhodana; he, the great king, is King Suddhodana. The connection is with 'was dwelling, it is said.' So means King Suddhodana. Rājagahaṃ means the city of Rājagaha. Sādhu is a particle in the sense of a request, for the meaning is 'I request.' Me means 'my'; the connection is with 'son.' Or it is a genitive used with disrespect. So means the minister. Sādhu is a particle in the sense of acceptance, for the meaning is 'So be it.' Athā means at the time of his sitting down. Assa means of the minister who had a retinue of a thousand men. Tato means because of the request. Naṃ means the minister with his retinue of a thousand men. Tattheva means right there in Rājagaha. Tepi means the eight messengers too. Te means the nine messengers.

Athāti tato pacchā. Ekadivasajātakanti ekasmiṃ divase jātakaṃ. Soti kāḷudāyīamacco. Pabbajitvāpīti pisaddena “apabbajitvāpī”ti atthaṃ sampiṇḍeti. Tathevāti yathā nava dūtā saparivārā arahattaṃ pāpuṇiṃsu, tathevāti attho. Soti kāḷudāyī. Sambhatesūti sambharitesu gahetvā niṭṭhāpitesūti attho. Vissaṭṭhakammesūti vissaṭṭhā kammantā etesanti vissaṭṭhakammantā, tesu. Supupphitesūti sundarapupphasañjātesu. Paṭipajjanakkhameti paṭipajjanatthāya khame yogye. Gamanavaṇṇaṃ saṃvaṇṇesīti sambandho. Saṭṭhimattāhīti (bu. vaṃ. aṭṭha. nidānakathā 2) saṭṭhipamāṇāhi. Etanti etaṃ saṃvaṇṇassa kāraṇaṃ kinti pucchi. Cārikaṃ pakkamituṃ kāloti yojanā. Tena hīti uyyojanatthe nipāto. Bhagavā pakkāmīti sambandho. Parivutoti parisamantato vuto āvuto nivuto hutvāti sambandho. Aturitacārikanti ajavanacārikaṃ.

Athā means 'then, after that.' Ekadivasajātakaṃ means born on the same day. So means the minister Kāḷudāyī. By the particle pi, it condenses the meaning to 'even after having gone forth.' Tatheva means: just as the nine messengers with their retinues attained arahantship, so too. So means Kāḷudāyī. Sambhatesu means on what has been collected, gathered, and completed. Vissaṭṭhakammesu means on those whose work has been dispatched. Supupphitesu means on those that have produced beautiful flowers. Paṭipajjanakkhame means fit and suitable for undertaking the journey. The connection is: 'he praised the journey.' Saṭṭhimattāhi means by about sixty (verses). Etan means he asked, 'What is the reason for this praise?' The construction is: 'It is time to set out on the journey.' Tena hi is a particle in the sense of urging. The connection is: 'The Blessed One set out.' Parivuto means being surrounded, enclosed, and enveloped on all sides. Aturitacārikaṃ means a journey without haste.

Evanti iminā nayena. Bhagavati pakkante ca satīti yojanā. Nikkhantadivasatoti phagguṇapuṇṇamiyā pāṭipadadivasato. Uttamabhojanarasassāti uttamabhojanarasena. Dassathāti dadeyyātha. Tenevāti saddhāya uppādanakāraṇeneva. Nanti kāḷudāyiṃ. Bhagavā ṭhapesīti sambandho. Etadagganti eso aggo. Yadidanti yo ayaṃ. Etadaggeti etadaggaṭṭhāne.

Evaṃ means in this way. The construction is: 'and when the Blessed One had departed.' From the day of departure, that is, from the day after the full moon of Phagguṇa. Uttamabhojanarasassa means with the flavor of the finest food. Dassatha means 'you should give.' Teneva means for the very reason of inspiring faith. Naṃ means Kāḷudāyī. The connection is: 'The Blessed One appointed.' Etadaggaṃ means 'this is the foremost.' Yadidaṃ means 'that is.' Etadagge means in the foremost position.

Sākiyāpi kho pahiṇiṃsūti sambandho. Ñātiseṭṭhanti ñātīnaṃ seṭṭhaṃ, ñātiyeva vā seṭṭhaṃ, bhagavantanti [V 1.0215] yojanā. Nigrodhasakkassāti nigrodhanāmakassa sakkassa. Tatthāti nigrodhasakkassa ārāme. Paccuggamananti paṭimukhaṃ uṭṭhahitvā gamanaṃ. Tatoti pahiṇato, paranti sambandho[M 0.0249]. Rājakumāre ca rājakumārikāyo ca pahiṇiṃsūti yojanā. Tesanti rājakumārarājakumārikānaṃ. Tatrāti nigrodhārāme. Māno jāti sabhāvo etesanti mānajātikā, mānena, māno vā thaddho etesanti mānathaddhā. Teti sākiyā, āhaṃsūti sambandho.

The connection is: 'The Sākyans, indeed, also sent.' Ñātiseṭṭhaṃ means 'the best of relatives,' or 'the relative who is best'; the construction is with 'the Blessed One.' Nigrodhasakkassa means of the Sākyan named Nigrodha. Tattha means in the park of Nigrodha the Sākyan. Paccuggamanaṃ means rising and going to meet face to face. Tato means 'after sending'; the connection is with paraṃ. The construction is: 'They sent princes and princesses.' Tesaṃ means of the princes and princesses. Tatra means in the Nigrodhārāma. Mānajātikā means those for whom pride is their birth and nature; mānathaddhā means stubborn with pride, or pride is their stubbornness. The connection is: Te, the Sākyans, said.

Tesūti sākiyesu. Neti ñātayo. Vuṭṭhāyāti catutthajjhānato vuṭṭhahitvā. Tesanti ñātīnaṃ. Kaṇḍambarukkhamūleti kaṇḍanāmakena uyyānapālena ropimassa ambarukkhassa āsanne. Rājāti suddhodanamahārājā. Voti tumhākaṃ, pādeti sambandho. Ayanti vandanā. Jambucchāyāyāti jamburukkhassa chāyāya. Iti āhāti yojanā.

Tesu means among the Sākyans. Ne means the relatives. Vuṭṭhāya means having emerged from the fourth jhāna. Tesaṃ means of the relatives. Kaṇḍambarukkhamūle means near the mango tree planted by the park keeper named Kaṇḍa. Rājā means King Suddhodana. Vo means 'your'; the connection is with pāde. Ayaṃ means this veneration. Jambucchāyāya means in the shade of the rose-apple tree. The construction is: 'Thus he spoke'.

Sikhāppattoti aggappatto, koṭippattoti attho. Tatoti nisīdanato, paranti sambandho. Pokkharavassanti padumavane vuṭṭhavassasadisaṃ. Tambavaṇṇanti lohitavaṇṇaṃ. Tanti apatanaṃ bhagavā kathesīti sambandho.

Sikhāppatto means having reached the summit, that is, having reached the peak. Tato means 'after sitting down'; the connection is with paraṃ. Pokkharavassaṃ means like a rain that has fallen on a lotus pond. Tambavaṇṇaṃ means copper-colored. The connection is: 'The Blessed One described that falling'.

Dutiyadivaseti kapilavatthuṃ pattadivasato dutiye divase. Indakhīleti nagarassa ummāre. Kathanti kenākārena cariṃsu nu khoti yojanā. Agamaṃsu kiṃ cariṃsu kinti yojanā. Sapadānacāranti gharapaṭipāṭikhaṇḍanavirahitena saha pavattaṃ cāraṃ. Tatoti āvajjanato, paranti sambandho. Ayameva vaṃsoti pubbabuddhānaṃ ayameva vaṃso. Ayaṃ paveṇīti tasseva vevacanaṃ. Anusikkhantāti anu paṭibhāgaṃ sikkhantā. Niviṭṭhagehatoti nivāsanatthāya visitagehato. Ayyoti adhipo sāmīti attho. Siddhatthakumāroti sabbalokassa siddho attho asmiṃ atthīti siddhattho, soyeva kumāro siddhatthakumāro. Sīhapañjaranti vātapānaṃ. Tañhi sīharūpaṃ dassetvā katapañjarattā sīhapañjaranti vuccati. Dassanabyāvaṭoti dassane, dassanatthāya vā byāvaṭo. Rāhulamātāpi devī ārocesīti sambandho. Kapālahatthoti kapālo hatthesu assa bhagavatoti kapālahattho, hutvāti sambandho. Nānāvirāgasamujjalāyāti nānāṭhānesu virāgāya samujjalāya. Virocamānaṃ bhagavantanti sambandho.

“On the second day”: on the second day from the day of arriving in Kapilavatthu. “At the city-post”: at the city’s threshold post. “How”: the construction is, “In what manner did they behave?” The construction is, “Did they come?
