How did they behave?” “Unbroken alms round”: a round that proceeds without breaking the sequence of houses. “From that”: from adverting. “Further”: this is the connection. “This is the very lineage”: this is the very lineage of the past Buddhas. “This is the tradition”: a synonym for that very word. “Training accordingly”: training in accordance with a portion. “From the house he had entered”: from the excellent house suitable for dwelling. “Lord”: the meaning is ruler, master. “Prince Siddhattha”: one for whom the purpose of the whole world is accomplished is Siddhattha; he is that prince, Prince Siddhattha. “Lion-window”: a window. For it is called a “lion-window” because it is a window made showing the form of a lion. “Engaged in seeing”: engaged in seeing, or for the purpose of seeing. The connection is: “Rāhula’s mother, the queen, also informed.” “With bowl in hand”: the Blessed One has a bowl in his hands, thus “with bowl in hand”; the connection is with “having become.” “Radiant with various hues”: radiant in various places with various colors. The connection is: “the resplendent Blessed One.”

Uṇhīsatoti [M 0.0250] siroveṭhanato. Tañhi uparisīse nahati bandhati, nahīyati bandhīyatīti vā uṇhīsoti vuccati. Narasīhagāthāhi nāmāti narasīhagāthānāmakāhi. Tā hi yasmā naroyeva sabbasattānaṃ sīho seṭṭho, narānaṃ, naresu vā sīho seṭṭhoti narasīho, tassa pakāsakā [V 1.0216] gāthā honti, tasmā narasīhagāthāti vuccanti. Raññoti sassurarañño, mātularañño vā. Saṃviggahadayoti calanacitto. Saṇṭhāpayamānoti suṭṭhu ṭhāpayamāno. Turitaturitanti turitato turitaṃ, atisīghanti attho. Kiṃ bhanteti kiṃ kāraṇā bhante. Ahuvatthāti hiyyattanīmajjhimapurisasaṅkhātāya tthavibhattiyā hūdhātussa ūkārassa uvādeso hoti, tasmā tumhe evaṃsaññino ahuvatthāti yojanā. Vaṃsacārittametanti etaṃ piṇḍāya caraṇaṃ vaṃsato paveṇito cārittaṃ. Tattha cāti mahāsammatakhattiyavaṃse ca. Ayanti mahāsammatakhattiyavaṃso. Antaravīthiyanti vīthiyā majjhe. Ṭhitova āhāti sambandho.

‘Uṇhīsa’ is so called because it is a head-covering. For it is bound on top of the head; or because it is bound, it is called uṇhīsa. ‘The verses are named narasīhagāthā’ means they are called narasīhagāthā. For since a man is the lion, the best, among all beings—the lion of men, or the lion among men, is called narasīha—and these verses proclaim him, therefore they are called narasīhagāthā. ‘Of the king’ refers to either the father-in-law king or the maternal uncle king. ‘With an agitated heart’ means with a shaking mind. ‘Establishing well’ means establishing well. ‘Very quickly’ means from quick to quick, that is, with excessive speed. ‘What, venerable sir?’ means ‘For what reason, venerable sir?’ ‘You were’ is formed by the substitution of ‘uva’ for ‘ū’ in the verb-root hū with the past tense, second person plural ending; therefore, the construction is ‘you were of such a perception.’ ‘This is a custom of the lineage’ means this practice of going for alms is a custom, a tradition, from the lineage. There, ‘and’ refers to also in the lineage of the Great Elected Khattiyas. ‘This’ means this lineage of the Great Elected Khattiyas. ‘In the middle of the street’ means in the middle of the street. The connection is: ‘Standing, he spoke.’”

Uttiṭṭheti uddissa, uṭṭhahitvā vā piṇḍāya tiṭṭhane. Dhammaṃ sucaritanti suṭṭhu caritabbaṃ bhikkhācariyasaṅkhātaṃ dhammaṃ. Careti careyya. Dhammacārīti bhikkhācariyasaṅkhātaṃ dhammaṃ caraṇasīlo samaṇo. Sukhaṃ setīti upalakkhaṇavasena vuttaṃ. Sesairiyāpathāpi lakkhaṇahāravasena gahetabbā samānakiccattā. Asmiñca loke paramhi ca loketi yojanā.

‘One should stand up’: intending to go for alms, or having risen up, standing for alms. ‘The Dhamma well-practiced’: the Dhamma, known as the practice of the alms-round, which should be practiced well. ‘One should practice’: one should practice. ‘A practitioner of the Dhamma’: a renunciate whose nature is to practice the Dhamma known as the alms-round. ‘Dwells happily’: this is said by way of example. The other postures should also be understood in the same way, as they have the same function. The construction is: ‘both in this world and in the next world.’”

Na taṃ duccaritaṃ careti vesiyādigocarasaṅkhātaṃ duṭṭhu caritabbaṃ taṃ dhammaṃ na careyya.

‘One should not practice that misconduct’: one should not practice that wrong way of living, known as frequenting prostitutes and the like.”

Ettha ca paṭhamagāthaṃ antaravīthiyaṃ kathetvā rājānaṃ sotāpattiphale patiṭṭhāpesi, dutiyagāthaṃ pitunivesane kathetvā mahāpajāpatiṃ sotāpattiphale, rājānaṃ sakadāgāmiphale patiṭṭhāpesīti daṭṭhabbaṃ. Dhammapālajātakaṃ sutvāti puna aparasmiṃ divase (jā. aṭṭha. 4.98 ādayo; dha. pa. aṭṭha. 1.nandattheravatthu) dhammapālajātakaṃ (jā. aṭṭha. 4.mahādhammapālajātakavaṇṇanā) [M 0.0251] sutvā. Maraṇasamayeti maraṇāsannakāle, maraṇasamayasamīpe vā, samīpatthe cetaṃ bhummavacanaṃ.

Here it should be understood that, having spoken the first verse in the middle of the street, he established the king in the fruit of stream-entry. Having spoken the second verse in his father’s residence, he established Mahāpajāpatī in the fruit of stream-entry and the king in the fruit of once-returning. ‘Having heard the Dhammapāla Jātaka’ means then on another day, having heard the Dhammapāla Jātaka (Ja. Aṭṭha. 4.98 ff.; Dhp. Aṭṭha. 1. Nandattheravatthu) (Ja. Aṭṭha. 4. Mahādhammapālajātakavaṇṇanā). ‘At the time of death’ means at the time nearing death, or near the time of death; this is a locative case expressing proximity.”

Sotāpattiphalaṃ sacchikatvā parivisīti sambandho. Sabbaṃ itthāgāranti sabbo orodho. So hi itthīnaṃ agāranti itthāgāranti vuccati. Iminā vacanatthena agārameva mukhyato labbhati, rājitthiyo pana upacārenāti daṭṭhabbaṃ. Sā panāti rāhulamātā pana. Parijanenāti parivārena. Nanti ayyaputtaṃ. “Rājāna”ntipadaṃ “gāhāpetvā”tipade kāritakammaṃ, “patta”ntipadaṃ tattheva dhātukammaṃ. Rājadhītāyāti suppabuddharañño dhītāya. Sāti rājadhītā. Gopphakesūti caraṇagaṇṭhīsu bhagavantaṃ gahetvāti yojanā. Atha vā bhagavato gopphake gahetvāti yojanā. Evañhi sati upayogatthe bhummavacananti daṭṭhabbaṃ.

The connection is: ‘Having realized the fruit of stream-entry, he served.’ ‘All the women’s quarters’ means the entire inner palace. For it is called the women’s quarters because it is the abode of women. By this expression, the abode itself is primarily meant, but the royal women should be understood by extension. ‘And she’ refers to Rāhula’s mother. ‘By her attendants’ means by her retinue. ‘Him’ refers to the noble son. The word ‘king’ is the causative object in the word gāhāpetvā, and the word ‘bowl’ is the direct object of the verb there. ‘Of the king’s daughter’ means of the daughter of King Suppabuddha. ‘She’ refers to the king’s daughter. ‘At the ankles’: the construction is, “having taken hold of the Blessed One at the ankles.” Alternatively, the construction is, “having taken hold of the Blessed One’s ankles.” In this case, the locative case should be understood as having the sense of instrumentality.”

Rājā [V 1.0217] kathesīti sambandho. Anacchariyanti na acchariyaṃ, accharaṃ paharituṃ na yogyanti attho. Rājadhītā yaṃ attānaṃ rakkhi, idaṃ anacchariyanti yojanā.

The connection is: ‘The king spoke.’ ‘Not strange’ means it is not strange, not fit to be struck with wonder—this is the meaning. The construction is: ‘That the king’s daughter protected herself, this is not strange.’”

Taṃdivasamevāti tasmiṃ dutiyadivaseyeva. Kesavisajjananti rājacūḷāmaṇibandhanatthaṃ kumārakāle bandhitasikhāveṇisaṅkhātassa kesassa visajjanaṃ, mocananti attho. Paṭṭabandhoti asuko nāma rājāti nalāṭe suvaṇṇamayassa paṭṭassa bandhanaṃ. Gharamaṅgalanti abhinavagharaṃ pavesanamaṅgalaṃ. Āvāhamaṅgalanti āvāhe pavattaṃ maṅgalaṃ. Chattamaṅgalanti rājachattussāpanakāle pavattaṃ maṅgalaṃ. Maṅgalaṃ vatvāti maṅgalasaṃyuttaṃ dhammakathaṃ kathetvā. Janapadakalyāṇīti janapadamhi kalyāṇasamannāgatā. Tuvaṭṭaṃ khoti khippameva. Sopīti nandarājakumāropi. Itītiādi nigamanaṃ. Dutiyadivaseti kapilavatthupattadivasato dutiye divase. Dhammapadaaṭṭhakathāyaṃ (dha. pa. aṭṭha. 1.nandattheravatthu; theragā. aṭṭha. 1.nandattheragāthāvaṇṇanā) pana “tatiyadivase nandaṃ pabbājesī”ti vuttaṃ.

“On that very day” means on that second day itself. “Letting loose the hair” means the release, the loosening, of the hair which was tied in his youth as a braided topknot for the purpose of binding the royal crest-jewel. “The forehead band” means the fastening of a golden band on the forehead, with the declaration, “He is King so-and-so.” “House blessing” means the auspicious ceremony for entering a new house. “Marriage blessing” means the auspicious ceremony performed at a wedding. “Umbrella blessing” means the auspicious ceremony performed at the raising of the royal umbrella. “Having spoken the blessing” means having given a Dhamma talk connected with auspiciousness. “The beauty of the land” means one endowed with beauty in the country. “Very quickly” means swiftly. “He too” means Prince Nanda as well. “Thus” and so on is the conclusion. “On the second day” means the second day from the day of arrival at Kapilavatthu. In the Dhammapada Commentary (DhpA 1, Nanda Thera’s Story; ThagA 1, Nanda Theragāthā Commentary), however, it is said, “On the third day, he ordained Nanda.”

Sattame divaseti kapilavatthupattadivasatoyeva sattame divase. Etaṃ samaṇaṃ passāti yojanā. Brahmarūpavaṇṇanti brahmuno rūpasaṅkhāto [M 0.0252] vaṇṇo viya vaṇṇo imassāti brahmarūpavaṇṇo, taṃ. Ayanti ayaṃ samaṇo. Tyassāti te assa. Teti nidhayo. Assāti samaṇassa. Nanti samaṇaṃ. Yācāti yācāhi. Ayaṃ dvikammikadhātu. Hīti saccaṃ, yasmā vā. Putto pitusantakassa sāmiko, iti tasmā me dehīti yojanā. Anurūpaṃ vacananti sambandho. Bhagavantaṃ anubandhīti bhagavato piṭṭhito piṭṭhito anubandhi.

“On the seventh day” means on the seventh day from the day of arrival at Kapilavatthu. The connection is: “See this ascetic.” “With the appearance of Brahmā” means: his appearance is like the appearance designated as the form of Brahmā; thus, it refers to him. “This” means this ascetic. “Tyassā” means “te assa” (those of him). “Te” means treasures. “Assa” means of the ascetic. “Naṃ” means the ascetic. “Yācā” means beg. This is a verb with two objects. “Hī” means truly, or because. The construction is: “A son is the owner of what belongs to his father,” therefore, “give it to me.” The connection is: “Suitable words.” “Following the Blessed One” means following right behind the Blessed One.

Na visahatīti na samattheti. Ayaṃ kumāro pitusantakaṃ yaṃ dhanaṃ icchati, tanti yojanā. Vaṭṭānugatanti vaṭṭadukkhaṃ anugataṃ. Savighātakanti vighātakehi pañcahi verehi sahitaṃ. Assāti kumārassa. Nanti kumāraṃ. Ayanti kumāro. Dāyajjanti dāyasaṅkhātaṃ mātāpitūnaṃ dhanaṃ ādadātīti dāyādo, putto, tassa idanti dāyajjaṃ, mātāpitūnaṃ dhanaṃ.

‘He cannot endure’: he is not capable. The construction is: ‘This prince desires that wealth which belongs to his father.’ ‘Following the round’: following the suffering of the round. ‘With destruction’: together with the five destructive enmities. ‘Assa’: of the prince. ‘Naṃ’: the prince. ‘Ayaṃ’: the prince. ‘Inheritance’: because he takes the wealth of his parents, which is designated as the inheritance (dāya), he is an heir (dāyāda), a son; that which is his is the inheritance (dāyajja), the wealth of his parents.

“Kathāhaṃ bhante rāhulakumāraṃ pabbājemī”ti kasmā āha, nanu āyasmā sāriputto bārāṇasiyaṃ tīhi saraṇagamanehi anuññātaṃ pabbajjaṃ na jānātīti āha “idānī”tiādi. Yā sā pabbajjā ca upasampadā ca anuññātāti yojanā. Tatoti pabbajjāupasampadato. Upasampadaṃ paṭikkhipitvāti sambandho. Vimatīti vividhā icchā. Imañca [V 1.0218] panatthanti imameva vimatisaṅkhātamatthaṃ. Dhammasenāpati āhāti sambandho. Bhagavato taṃ ajjhāsayanti yojanā.

Why did he say, “Venerable sir, how should I ordain Prince Rāhula?” Didn’t the Venerable Sāriputta know about the going forth that was permitted with the three refuges in Bārāṇasī? He said, “Now,” etc. The connection is that the going forth and the higher ordination were permitted. “From that” means from the going forth and higher ordination. “Having rejected higher ordination” is the connection. “Doubt” means various wishes. “And this meaning” refers specifically to this meaning which is called doubt. “The General of the Dhamma said”—this is the connection. “The Blessed One’s inclination”—this is the connection.

“Atha kho…pe… pabbājesī”ti ettha kiṃ kumārassa kesacchedanādīni sabbakiccāni āyasmā sāriputtoyeva karotīti āha “mahāmoggallānatthero”tiādi. Ovādācariyoti nivāsanapārupanādīsu sekhiyavattesu, ābhisamācārikesu ca ovādako ācariyo. Atha kasmā “āyasmā sāriputto rāhulakumāraṃ pabbājesī”ti vuttanti āha “yasmā panā”tiādi. Tatthāti tassaṃ pabbajjāupasampadāyaṃ. Na ācariyoti pabbajjācariyo ca ovādācariyo ca na issaro.

Regarding “Then… he ordained him,” does it mean the Venerable Sāriputta himself performed all the duties such as cutting the prince’s hair? He says, “The Elder Mahāmoggallāna,” etc. “Instructor” means the teacher who gives advice on the training rules concerning matters such as the lower and upper robes, and on the rules of proper conduct. But why is it said, “The Venerable Sāriputta ordained Prince Rāhula”? He says, “Because,” etc. “There” means in that going forth and higher ordination. “Not the teacher” means neither the preceptor nor the instructor is the master.

Uppannasaṃvegena hadayenāti ettha itthambhūtalakkhaṇe karaṇavacanaṃ. Uppannasaṃvego hadayo hutvāti hi yojanā. Sabbanti sabbaṃ vacanaṃ.

Regarding “with a heart experiencing urgency,” here the instrumental case indicates the characteristic of being in that state. The connection is, “the heart being one that has experienced urgency.” “All” means the entire utterance.

Tatthāti [M 0.0253] purimavacanāpekkhaṃ. Avisesenāti “dhana”nti vā “añña”nti vā “sāvajja”nti vā “anavajja”nti vā visesamakatvā sāmaññena. Na ca buddhānanti ettha casaddena na kevalaṃ apaṭirūpameva, atha kho buddhānañca na āciṇṇanti atthaṃ dasseti. Yanti yaṃ varaṃ. Tathā nandeti ettha tathāsaddassa upameyyatthajotakabhāvaṃ dassento āha “yatheva kirā”tiādi. Yatheva bodhisattaṃ byākariṃsu, evaṃ nandampi rāhulampi byākariṃsu kirāti yojanā. Pāḷiyaṃ pana yathā bhagavati me bhante pabbajite anappakaṃ dukkhaṃ ahosi, tathā nande pabbajite anappakaṃ dukkhaṃ ahosi, tathā rāhule pabbajite adhimattaṃ dukkhaṃ ahosīti yojanā. Nemittakāti subhāsubhanimittaṃ kathentīti nemittakā. Puttassāti jeṭṭhaputtassa siddhatthakumārassa. Pabbajjāyāti pabbajjāhetu pabbajjākāraṇā, pabbajjānimittaṃ vā. Tatoti bhagavato pabbajjato. Tampīti nandampi. Itīti īdisaṃ. Bhagavato pabbajjāya mahantaṃ icchāvighātasadisanti attho. Tampīti rāhulampi. Tenāti pabbajjāhetunā. Assāti rañño. Uppajjīti sambandho. Itoti sokuppattito varayācanato vā.

“Tattha” refers to the preceding statement. “Avisesena” means generally, without making a distinction—whether ‘wealth’ or ‘something else,’ ‘blameworthy’ or ‘blameless.’ In “Na ca buddhānaṃ,” the word “ca” indicates not only that it is unsuitable but also that it is not the practice of the Buddhas. “Yaṃ” means ‘whatever boon.’ In “Tathā nande,” showing that the word “tathā” indicates the meaning of comparison, he says, “yatheva kirā,” and so on. The connection is: just as they made a prediction about the Bodhisatta, so too, it is said, they made a prediction about Nanda and Rāhula. But in the Pāli text, the connection is: ‘Venerable sir, just as when the Blessed One went forth no little suffering arose for me, so too when Nanda went forth no little suffering arose, and when Rāhula went forth excessive suffering arose.’ “Nemittakā” are those who tell of auspicious and inauspicious signs. “Puttassa” means of the eldest son, Prince Siddhattha. “Pabbajjāya” means on account of the going forth, for the reason of the going forth, or as a sign of the going forth. “Tato” means from the Blessed One’s going forth. “Tampi” means Nanda as well. “Iti” means ‘such.’ The meaning is: on account of the Blessed One’s going forth, there was something like a great frustration of his wish. “Tampi” means Rāhula as well. “Tena” means on account of that, i.e., the going forth. “Assa” means of the king. “Uppajji” is the connection. “Ito” means from the arising of sorrow or from the request for a boon.

Soti rājā. Yatra hi nāmāti yo nāma. Ahampi nāma yo yādiso buddhamāmako dhammamāmako saṅghamāmako samāno, so tādiso ahampi na sakkomīti yojanā. Aññeti mayā apare. Dukkhanti ñātiviyogadukkhaṃ. Niyyānikakāraṇanti manussānaṃ garahaupavādaakkosato niyyānikaṃ kāraṇaṃ.

“So” means the king. “Yatra hi nāma” means ‘who indeed.’ The connection for “Ahampi nāma...na sakkomi” is: I, who am such a one—a devotee of the Buddha, a devotee of the Dhamma, and a devotee of the Saṅgha—even I, being such, am not able. “Aññe” means others besides me. “Dukkhaṃ” means the suffering of separation from relatives. “Niyyānikakāraṇaṃ” means the reason that leads to deliverance from the censure, blame, and abuse of people.

Tatthāti [V 1.0219] “ananuññāto”tiādivacane. Janetīti jananī, mātā. Janetīti janako, pitā. Iminā posāvanikamātāpitaro nivatteti. Mātā vā matā hotīti yojanā. So eva vāti putto eva vā. Anuññātomhīti vadatīti saccena vā alikena vā “anuññātomhī”ti vadati. Mātā vā sayaṃ pabbajitāti yojanā. Pitassāti pitā assa. Assāti puttassa. Vippavutthoti mātuyā kenaci kāraṇena pavāso.

“Tattha” refers to the statement beginning with “ananuññāto.” “Janetī” means she who gives birth, the mother. “Janako” means he who begets, the father. By this, it excludes foster parents. The connection for “Mātā vā matā hoti” is: ‘or the mother is dead.’ “So eva vā” means ‘or the son himself.’ “Anuññātomhīti vadati” means he says, ‘I have been given permission,’ either truthfully or falsely. The connection for “Mātā vā sayaṃ pabbajitā” is: ‘or the mother herself has gone forth.’ “Pitassa” means ‘his father.’ “Assa” means ‘of the son.’ “Vippavuttho” means being away from the mother for some reason.

Cūḷamātādīnantiādisaddena [M 0.0254] mahāmātādīni saṅgaṇhāti. Posanakāti vaḍḍhanakā. Tesupīti posanakamātāpitaresupi.

In “Cūḷamātādīnaṃ,” the word “ādi” (etc.) includes the great mothers and so on. “Posanakā” means those who raise. “Tesupi” means even in the case of nurturing mothers and fathers.

Yaṃ pana puttaṃ nānujānantīti sambandho. Jīvassevāti tassa jīvassa eva, pabbājentassa vā bhikkhussa, na desantaragamanādīnamatthāyāti attho. Tesanti mātāpitūnaṃ.

The connection is with “Yaṃ pana puttaṃ nānujānanti.” “Jīvassa” means for the sake of that very person, or of the bhikkhu who is giving the going forth, and not for the purpose of travelling to another country and so on; this is the meaning. “Tesaṃ” means of the parents.

Mahākantāroti kena udakena taritabboti kantāro, nirudakakantārova mukhyato labbhati, vāḷakantāro corakantāro amanussakantāro dubbhikkhakantāro marukantāroti ime pañca kantārā rūḷhīvasena. Mahanto kantāro mahākantāro.

Mahākantāra: A wilderness (kantāra) is so called because one wonders, ‘By what water (kena udakena) is it to be crossed?’ A waterless wilderness is primarily meant. By conventional usage, there are these five wildernesses: a wilderness of wild beasts, a wilderness of thieves, a wilderness of nonhuman beings, a wilderness of famine, and a desert wilderness. A large wilderness is a great wilderness (mahākantāra).

Yāvataketi ettha yāvasaddo pamāṇatthoti āha “yattake”ti.

In “yāvatake,” the word “yāva” here has the meaning of measure; thus he says, “yattake” (as much as).

42. Sikkhāpadadaṇḍakammavatthukathā

42. The Exposition on the Grounds for the Training Rules and Disciplinary Actions

106. Nāsanavatthūti liṅganāsanāya adhiṭṭhānaṃ, kāraṇanti vuttaṃ hoti. Pacchimānaṃ pañcannanti yojanā. Daṇḍakammavatthūti daṇḍakammassa kāraṇaṃ.

106. “Nāsanavatthu” (ground for expulsion) means the determination for the destruction of the characteristic mark; this is said to be the cause. The connection is with ‘for the last five.’ “Daṇḍakammavatthu” (ground for disciplinary action) means the reason for the disciplinary action.

107. Appatissāti ettha bhikkhūnaṃ vacanassa paṭimukhaṃ ādarena asavanaṃ bhikkhū jeṭṭhakaṭṭhāne na ṭhapenti nāmāti dassento āha “bhikkhū jeṭṭhakaṭṭhāne”tiādi. “Samānajīvikā”ti iminā asabhāgavuttikāti ettha sabhāgasaddo samānasaddapariyāyo, vuttisaddo jīvikapariyāyoti dasseti. Parisakkatīti ettha sakka gatiyantidhātupāṭhesu (saddanītidhātumālāyaṃ 16 ḷakārantadhātu) vuttattā paripubbo sakkasaddo gatyatthoti āha “parakkamatī”ti. Kintīti kimeva. Itisaddo hettha evasaddattho, kena eva upāyenāti hi attho. Akkosati cevāti jātiādīhi akkosati ceva. Bhedetīti bhedāpeti. Āvaraṇaṃ kātunti [V 1.0220] ettha āvaraṇasaddo nivāraṇasaddavevacanoti āha “nivāraṇaṃ [M 0.0255] kātu”nti. Yatthāti yasmiṃ pariveṇe, senāsane vā. Vassaggenāti vassagaṇanāya. (Tassāti pariveṇasenāsanassa. Upacāreti āsanne). Mukhadvārikanti mukhasaṅkhātena dvārena ajjhoharitabbaṃ. “Vadatopī”ti iminā vacīpayogena dukkaṭāpattiṃ dasseti, “nikkhipatopī”ti iminā kāyapayogena. Anācārassāti daṇḍakamme anācārassa. Ettake nāma daṇḍakammeti ettake nāma udakāharāpanādisaṅkhāte daṇḍakamme. Idanti yāgubhattādiṃ. Lacchasīti labhissasi. “Ettake nāma daṇḍakamme”ti vuttavacanassa yuttiṃ dassento āha “bhagavatā hī”tiādi. Daṇḍakammanti daṇḍenti damenti etenāti daṇḍo, soyeva kattabbattā kammanti daṇḍakammaṃ āvaraṇādi. Aparādhānurūpanti vītikkamassa aparādhassa anurūpaṃ. Tampīti udakadāruvālikādiāharāpaṇampi. Tañca khoti tañca karaṇaṃ. Oramissatīti kāyena oramissati. Viramissatīti vācāya viramissati. Uṇhapāsāṇe vātiādīsu vāsaddena aññānipi attatāpanaparitāpanādīni kammāni saṅgaṇhāti.

107. “Appatissā” (disrespectful): here, showing that not listening respectfully to the speech of bhikkhus face-to-face means ‘they do not place bhikkhus in the position of seniors,’ he says, ‘bhikkhus in the position of seniors,’ etc. By “samānajīvikā” (of the same livelihood), it shows that in “asabhāgavuttikā,” the word “sabhāga” is a synonym for the word “samāna” (same), and the word “vutti” is a synonym for “jīvikā” (livelihood). “Parisakkati” (strives): here, because the root “sak” is mentioned in the Dhātupāṭha in the sense of ‘to go,’ he says “parakkamati” (exerts), since the word “sak” preceded by “pari” has the meaning of movement. “Kinti” means ‘what indeed?’ (kim eva). Here the word “iti” has the meaning of the word “eva,” for the meaning is ‘by what means indeed?’ “Akkosati ceva” (and he abuses) means he abuses with reference to birth, etc. “Bhedeti” (he divides) means he causes to be divided. In “āvaraṇaṃ kātuṃ” (to make an obstruction), he says “nivāraṇaṃ kātuṃ” because the word “āvaraṇa” is a synonym for the word “nivāraṇa.” “Yattha” means in which monastic compound or lodging. “Vassaggena” means by the count of rains-residences. (“Tassa” means of that monastic compound or lodging. “Upacāre” means in the vicinity.) “Mukhadvārikaṃ” means what is to be consumed through the door called the mouth. By ‘even when speaking,’ he shows an offense of wrong conduct through verbal action; by ‘even when placing,’ through bodily action. “Anācārassa” means of misconduct in a disciplinary action. “Ettake nāma daṇḍakamme” means in so many disciplinary actions designated as fetching water, etc. “Idaṃ” means gruel, rice, etc. “Lacchasi” means ‘you will get.’ Showing the reason for the statement “Ettake nāma daṇḍakamme,” he says, ‘For by the Blessed One,’ etc. “Daṇḍakammaṃ”: that by which they punish (daṇḍenti) or tame (damenti) is a punishment (daṇḍo); since that itself is to be done (kattabba), it is an action (kamma), thus “daṇḍakammaṃ,” such as obstruction, etc. “Aparādhānurūpaṃ” means in accordance with the transgression, the offense. “Tampi” means even the fetching of water, firewood, sand, etc. “Tañca kho” means and that action. “Oramissati” means he will desist with the body. “Viramissati” means he will desist with speech. In “uṇhapāsāṇe vā” (or on a hot stone), etc., by the word “vā” (or) he includes other actions such as tormenting oneself and tormenting others.

43. Anāpucchāvaraṇavatthuādikathā

43. The Discourse Beginning with the Case of Prohibition Without Asking Permission

108. Upajjhāyaṃ anāpucchāti ettha upajjhāyaṃ anāpucchitvā. Sabbathā kiṃ na kātabbanti āha “tumhāka”ntiādi. Daṇḍakammamassāti daṇḍakammaṃ assa. Assāti sāmaṇerassa. Saddhiṃ upajjhāyena viharantīti saddhivihārikā. Nissayācariyādīnaṃ ante samīpe vasantīti antevāsikā, upasampannāyeva.

108. “Without asking the preceptor”: here this means without having asked the preceptor. “What should not be done at all?” He says, “yours,” etc. “Disciplinary action for him”: this means disciplinary action for him. “For him”: this refers to the novice. “Co-residents” (saddhivihārikā) are so called because they live together with their preceptor. “Pupils” (antevāsikā) are so called because they live near their teachers of dependence and so on; they are only the fully ordained.

Apalāḷentīti ettha laḷa upasevāyanti dhātupāṭhesu vuttattā (saddanītidhātumālāyaṃ 18 ḷakārantadhātu) there laḷato upasevato apagamentīti attho daṭṭhabbo. Idha pana adhippāyatthaṃ dassento āha “tumhāka”ntiādi. Apalāḷetabbāti aññaṃ laḷato upasevato apagametabbā. Parisabhūte sāmaṇerūpasampanneti yojanā. Ādīnavanti dussīlaṃ nissāya vasanassa [M 0.0256] dosaṃ. Nhāyituṃ āgatena tayā gūthamakkhanaṃ kataṃ viya dussīlaṃ nissāya viharantena dussīlaṃ katanti yojanā. “Dussīla”nti padaṃ purimapacchimapadāpekkhaṃ, tasmā dvinnaṃ padānaṃ majjhe vuttaṃ. Tattha purimapadāpekkhakāle vuttakammaṃ, pacchimapadāpekkhakāle avuttakammaṃ. Soti sāmaṇerūpasampanno. Upajjhāyaṃ vāti sāmaṇeraṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ. Nissayaṃ vāti upasampannaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ.

“They make desist”: here, since it is stated in the root manuals (Dhātupāṭha; Saddanītidhātumālā, 18th root ending in ḷa) that the root laḷa means “to attend upon,” the meaning should be understood as “they cause one to desist from attending upon.” Here, however, explaining the intended meaning, he says, “yours,” etc. “Should be made to desist”: another should be made to desist from attending upon. The construction is: “a novice or a fully ordained one in the assembly.” “Disadvantage”: this refers to the fault of living in dependence on an immoral person. The construction is: “Just as one who comes to bathe smears oneself with excrement, so too one who lives in dependence on an immoral person commits an immoral act.” The word “immoral” relates to both the preceding and the following words; therefore, it is stated between the two words. There, in relation to the preceding word, it is an expressed object; in relation to the following word, it is an unexpressed object. “He”: the novice or the fully ordained one. “Or the preceptor” is said with reference to the novice. “Or the dependence” is said with reference to the fully ordained one.

Tīsu [V 1.0221] nāsanāsūti saṃvāsaliṅgadaṇḍakammanāsanasaṅkhātāsu tīsu nāsanāsu. Yoti sāmaṇero. Nānāāpattiyoti pārājikathullaccaya pācittiyāpattiyo. Hīti saccaṃ, yasmā vā. Kunthakipillikampīti ettha pāṇakhādakehi sattehi kuthiyati hiṃsiyatīti kuntho, kuṃ pathaviṃ vā dhāretīti kundho.

“Among the three expulsions”: this refers to the three expulsions designated as expulsion from communion, expulsion by removing the characteristic sign, and expulsion by disciplinary action. “He”: the novice. “Various offenses”: offenses of the pārājika, thullaccaya, and pācittiya classes. “Hi”: this means truly, or because. “Kunthakipillikam”: here, a kuntha is so called because it is tormented or harmed by creatures that devour living beings; or it is a kundha because it supports the earth.

Kimiyeva pillikaṃ potakaṃ kipillikaṃ mikārassa lopaṃ katvā. Pillikasaddo hi potakapariyāyo. Kimīnaṃ, kimīsu vā pillikaṃ kipillikaṃ. Nāsetabbataṃyevāti liṅgena nāsetabbabhāvameva. Tāvadevāti tasmiṃ māraṇabhindanakkhaṇeyeva. Assāti sāmaṇerassa. Senāsanaggāho ca paṭippassambhatīti vassacchedo hotīti adhippāyo. Ākiṇṇadosovāti liṅganāsanadosena ca daṇḍakammanāsanadosena ca ākuladosova. Virajjhitvāti virādhetvā. Yathānivatthapārutasseva sāmaṇerassāti sambandho. Tasmāti saraṇagamanaupasampadakammavācānaṃ sadisattā. Bhikkhunā samādinnaṃ viya imināpi samādinnāneva hontīti yojanā. Evanti evamijjhane, samādinne vā. Daḷhīkaraṇatthanti sikkhāpadānaṃ daḷhīkaraṇatthaṃ. Patiṭṭhāpanatthanti sāmaṇerassa patiṭṭhāpanatthaṃ. Lacchatīti labhissati. Saṅghena dātabboti sambandho. Apaloketvāti saṅghaṃ āpucchitvā. Iminā chinnavassakaṃ dasseti.

Kipillikaṃ: a young one (pillikaṃ = potakaṃ) of an insect (kimi), with the elision of the syllable “mi.” For the word pillika is a synonym for potaka (a young one). Kipillikaṃ: a young one (pillikaṃ) of insects or among insects. “The very state of having to be expelled”: the state of having to be expelled by means of removing the characteristic sign. “Just then”: at that very moment of killing or breaking. “For him”: for the novice. “And the taking up of a lodging is allayed”: the intention is that his rains-residence is interrupted. “A fault of being beset”: a fault of being troubled by the fault of expulsion by removing the sign and the fault of expulsion by disciplinary action. “Having failed”: having transgressed. The connection is with “of the novice just as he was dressed and robed.” “Therefore”: because of the similarity of the formal declarations for the going for refuge and for the higher ordination. The construction is: “They are undertaken by this one just as they are undertaken by a bhikkhu.” “Thus”: when it succeeds thus, or when it is undertaken. “For the purpose of strengthening”: for the purpose of strengthening the training rules. “For the purpose of establishing”: for the purpose of establishing the novice. “He gets”: he will get. The connection is: “it should be given by the Saṅgha.” “Having obtained consent”: having asked the Saṅgha. By this he shows one whose rains-residence is broken.

Adinnādāne tiṇasalākamattenāpi vatthunā asamaṇo hotīti yojanā. Vippaṭipattiyāti vikārena paṭipajjanato. Bhaṇiteti [M 0.0257] bhaṇane. Jānitvāti jānitvā eva. Evakāro hettha ajjhāharitabbo, tena vuttaṃ “na ajānitvā”ti. Yāni pañca sikkhāpadānīti yojanā. Assāti sāmaṇerassa. Ṭhapanatthāyāti sikkhāpadānaṃ ṭhapanatthāya. Ayanti pārājiko. Visesoti bhikkhūnaṃ pācittiyato viseso.

The construction is: “In taking what is not given, one is not a recluse even for an object worth a blade of grass or a ticket-stick.” “Through wrong practice”: because of practicing improperly. “When it is said”: in the saying. “Having known”: having known indeed. Here the particle eva should be supplied; hence it is said, “not without knowing.” The construction is: “Those five training rules.” “For him”: for the novice. “For the purpose of establishing”: for the purpose of establishing the training rules. “This one”: a person who has committed a pārājika offense. “A difference”: a difference from the pācittiya offense for bhikkhus.

Paṭipakkhavasenāti “anarahaṃ asammāsambuddho”tiādinā ca “dvākkhāto”tiādinā ca “duppaṭippanno”tiādinā ca paṭiviruddhavasena garahanto sāmaṇero nivāretabboti sambandho. Kaṇḍakanāsanāyāti kaṇḍakanāmakassa sāmaṇerassa daṇḍakammanāsanāya. Taṃ laddhinti avaṇṇabhāsanadiṭṭhiṃ. Accayanti atikkamaṃ, dosaṃ vā. Desāpetabboti “accayo maṃ bhante accagamā”tiādinā desāpetabbā. Taṃ yuttanti “liṅganāsanāya nāsetabbo”ti taṃ vacanaṃ patirūpaṃ. Hīti saccaṃ, yasmā vā. Idhāti khandhake, “sāmaṇeraṃ nāsetu”ntivacane vā.

“By way of opposition”: the connection is that a novice who finds fault in an opposing way, with such statements as “He is not an Arahant, not a Perfectly Self-Enlightened One,” and “badly proclaimed,” and “badly practiced,” should be restrained. “For the expulsion of Kaṇḍaka”: for the expulsion by disciplinary action of the novice named Kaṇḍaka. “That view”: the view of speaking dispraise. “Transgression”: a transgression, or a fault. “He should be made to confess”: he should be made to confess with the words, “Venerable sir, a transgression overcame me,” etc. “That is proper”: that statement, “He should be expelled by expulsion of the characteristic sign,” is suitable. “Hi”: truly, or because. “Here”: in this Khandhaka, or in the statement, “Let them expel the novice.”

“Eseva nayo”ti vuttavacanaṃ pākaṭaṃ karonto āha “sassatucchedānañhī”tiādi. Aññataradiṭṭhiko [V 1.0222] sāmaṇeroti yojanā. Etthāti dasasu nāsanaṅgesu. “Kāma”ntipadena punaruttiniratthakadosāropanena garahaṃ dasseti. “Panā”tipadena tesaṃ dosānaṃ pahānena sambhāvanaṃ dasseti. Abrahmacāriṃ sāmaṇeranti sambandho. Upasampādetuṃ vaṭṭatīti upasampādanaṃ vaṭṭati. Bhikkhunidūsako sāmaṇeroti sambandho. Pabbajjampīti ettha pisaddassa garahatthabhāvaṃ dassetuṃ vuttaṃ “pageva upasampada”nti. Etamatthanti etādisamatthaṃ.

Making clear the statement “This is the method,” he says, “For of eternalism and annihilationism,” etc. The construction is: “a novice holding some other view.” “Here”: among the ten grounds for expulsion. By the word “kāma” (if you wish), he indicates censure by imputing the fault of pointless repetition. By the word “pana” (but), he indicates the possibility of their abandoning those faults. The connection is with “a novice who is unchaste.” “It is allowable to give higher ordination”: the higher ordination is allowable. The connection is: “a novice who corrupts bhikkhunīs.” “Even the going forth”: here, to show that the particle pi has the sense of censure, it is said, “still less the higher ordination.” “This matter”: a matter such as this.

47. Paṇḍakavatthukathā

47. Account of the Paṇḍaka

109. Daharataruṇasaddānaṃ vevacanattā vuttaṃ “dahare…pe… taruṇe”ti. Moḷigallasaddo thūlasarīravācako anipphannapāṭipadikoti āha “moḷigalleti thūlasarīre”ti. Hatthibhaṇḍeti ettha hatthisaṅkhātaṃ bhaṇḍaṃ etesanti hatthibhaṇḍāti vutte hatthigopakāti āha “hatthigopake”ti. Abhidhāne (abhidhānappadīpikāyaṃ 367 gāthāyaṃ) pana “hatthimeṇḍo”ti pāṭho atthi.

109. Because the terms “dahara” and “taruṇa” are synonyms, it is said, “dahare…pe… taruṇe.” The term “moḷigalla” refers to a large body; it is an underived nominal stem, thus he says, “moḷigalla means a large body.” Regarding “hatthibhaṇḍā,” when it is said that these are “hatthibhaṇḍā” (those whose goods are elephants), he says “elephant keepers.” In the lexicon (Abhidhānappadīpikā, verse 367), however, there is the reading “elephant chief.”

Paṇḍakoti [M 0.0258] paḍati vikalabhāvaṃ gacchatīti paṇḍako. Saṃkhepena vuttamatthaṃ vitthārena dassento āha “tatthā”tiādi. Tattha yassāti paṇḍakassa. Asucināti sambhavena. Āsittassāti āsiñcitabbassa. Iminā asucinā mukhe āsiñcitabboti āsittoti vacanatthaṃ dasseti. Ayanti paṇḍako. Ajjhācāranti methunajjhācāraṃ. “Usūyāya uppannāyā”tiiminā usūyatīti usūyoti vacanatthaṃ dasseti. Upakkamenāti vāyāmena. Bījānīti aṇḍāni. Iminā upakkamena etasmā bījāni apanītānīti opakkamikoti vacanatthaṃ dasseti. Pakkhe pavatto paṇḍako pakkhapaṇḍako, pakkhe pariḷāhavūpasamo paṇḍako pakkhapaṇḍakoti vacanatthaṃ dassento āha “ekacco panā”tiādi. Tattha pubbavacanatthe pakkheti kālapakkheti attho daṭṭhabbo. Pacchimavacanatthe pakkheti juṇhapakkheti attho daṭṭhabbo. “Akusalavipākānubhāvenā”ti padaṃ “paṇḍako hotī”tipadeyeva sambandhitabbaṃ. Assāti paṇḍakassa. Napuṃsakapaṇḍakoti puriso viya sātisayaṃ paccāmitte na puṃsaketi abhimaddanaṃ kātuṃ na sakkotīti napuṃsako. Na pumā na itthīti napuṃsakoti katvā napumanaitthisaddassa niruttinayena napuṃsakakaraṇampi vadanti. Napuṃsakoyeva paṇḍako napuṃsakapaṇḍako. Tesūti pañcasu paṇḍakesu. Tesupīti opakkamikādīsu tīsupi. “Yasmiṃ pakkhe”ti iminā pakkhe pakkhe paṇḍakabhāvaṃ nivatteti. Assāti paṇḍakassa. Etthāti pañcasu paṇḍakesu. Sopīti paṇḍakopi. Itoti paṇḍakavārato. “Eseva nayo”ti iminā liṅganāsanameva atidisati.

A paṇḍaka is so called because he is deficient and attains a defective state. Explaining the briefly stated meaning in detail, he says, “Herein,” etc. Herein, “of whom” means of the paṇḍaka. “With impurity” means due to origin. “To be poured” means what should be poured. This shows the meaning of the word “āsitta” as “to be poured in the mouth with this impurity.” “This” means this paṇḍaka. “Misconduct” means sexual misconduct. By “when envy arises,” he shows the meaning of the word “usūya” as “being envious.” “By effort” means by exertion. “Seeds” refers to the testicles. This shows the meaning of the word “opakkamiko” as “the seeds being removed from this by effort.” Explaining the meaning of “pakkhapaṇḍaka” as “a paṇḍaka who occurs in a period” and “a paṇḍaka whose fever subsides in a period,” he says, “But some,” etc. Herein, in the former statement, “period” should be understood as a time period. In the latter statement, “period” should be understood as the bright fortnight. The phrase “due to the influence of unwholesome karmic results” should be connected with the phrase “becomes a paṇḍaka.” “Assa” means of the paṇḍaka. A napuṃsaka-paṇḍaka is so called because, unlike a man, he cannot excessively subdue opponents; thus, he is a napuṃsaka. Considering that he is neither male nor female, some also explain the derivation of the word “napuṃsaka” according to the rules of etymology for the words “na pumā na itthi.” The paṇḍaka who is simply a napuṃsaka is a napuṃsaka-paṇḍaka. “Among them” refers to the five types of paṇḍakas. “Among them too” refers to the three types, including the one made by effort. By “in which period,” he indicates that the state of being a paṇḍaka reverts in each period. “Assa” means of the paṇḍaka. “Here” refers to the five types of paṇḍakas. “He too” refers to the paṇḍaka as well. “Thus” is the conclusion from the section on paṇḍakas. By “this is the method,” he applies by analogy the destruction of the sexual sign.

48. Theyyasaṃvāsakavatthukathā

48. Explanation of the Case of the Thief-in-Communion.

110. Pārijaññapattassāti [V 1.0223] parihāyatīti parijāni, issariyabhogādi, tassa bhāvo pārijaññaṃ, issariyabhogādikkhayo, taṃ pattoti pārijaññapatto, tassa. “Pārijuññapattassā”tipi ukārena saha pāṭho atthi. Khīṇakolaññoti ettha kule jātā kolaññā, ṇyapaccayo, nakārāgamo. Khīṇā kolaññā assāti khīṇakolaññoti [M 0.0259] vacanatthaṃ dassento āha “mātipakkhapitipakkhato”tiādi. Tattha mātipakkhapitipakkhatoti mātuyā pakkho mātipakkho, pituno pakkho pitipakkho, mātipakkho ca pitipakkho ca mātipakkhapitipakkhā. Phātiṃ kātunti ettha phā-dhātu vaḍḍhanatthoti āha “vaḍḍhetu”nti. “Pucchiyamāno”ti iminā anuyuñjiyamānoti ettha anutyūpasaggavasena yujasaddo pucchanatthoti dasseti.

110. Pārijaññapattassa (of one who has attained decline): 'parijāni' means 'it declines,' referring to sovereignty, wealth, and so on. The state of that is 'pārijañña,' the decline of sovereignty, wealth, and so on. One who has attained that is 'pārijaññapatto,' of him. There is also a reading with the 'u' vowel, 'Pārijuññapattassā.' 'Khīṇakolaññoti': Here, 'kolaññā' are those born in a clan, with the suffix 'ṇya' and the insertion of 'n.' Explaining the meaning of 'Khīṇakolañña' as 'whose clan-qualities are exhausted,' he says, 'from the mother's side and the father's side,' and so on. There, 'mātipakkhapitipakkhato' means 'mātipakkho' is the mother's side, 'pitipakkho' is the father's side, and 'mātipakkhapitipakkhā' are both the mother's and father's sides. 'Phātiṃ kātunti': Here, the root 'phā' means to increase, as stated by 'vaḍḍhetu' (to increase). 'Pucchiyamāno': By this, he shows that in 'anuyuñjiyamāno' (being questioned), the word 'yuj' with the prefix 'anu' conveys the meaning of asking.

Theyyasaṃvāsakoti thenanaṃ theyyaṃ nakārassa yakāraṃ katvā, theyyāya saṃvāsako imassāti theyyasaṃvāsako. Ettha ca na kevalaṃ vassagaṇanādikoyeva saṃvāso nāma hoti, atha kho theyyāya liṅgagahaṇampi saṃvāsoyeva nāma. Tasmā tassa tividhabhāvaṃ dassento āha “tayo”tiādi. Tattha liṅgaṃ thenetīti liṅgathenako, eseva nayo itaresupi. Tamatthaṃ vitthārento āha “tatthā”tiādi. Tattha yoti theyyasaṃvāsako. Liṅgamattassevāti ettha mattasaddena saṃvāsādayo nivatteti.

Theyyasaṃvāsako: 'Theyya' is formed by changing the 'n' to 'y' in 'thena' (thief). Thus, 'theyyāya saṃvāsako imassāti' means 'one who lives in communion for the purpose of theft,' hence 'theyyasaṃvāsako.' And here, 'saṃvāsa' (communion) is not merely counting years and so on; rather, even the assumption of the outward mark for the purpose of theft is also 'saṃvāsa.' Therefore, showing its threefold nature, he said, 'three,' and so on. There, 'liṅgaṃ thenetīti' (one who steals the outward mark) is 'liṅgathenako' (a stealer of the outward mark); the same method applies to the others. Elaborating on that meaning, he said, 'therein,' and so on. There, 'yo' refers to the thief-in-communion. 'Liṅgamattassevāti': Here, by the word 'matta' (mere), he excludes communion and so on.

Videsanti attano desato viyogaṃ desaṃ. Visaddo hettha viyogatthavācako. Atha vā vi dūraṃ desaṃ. Visaddo hettha dūratthavācako. Musāti abhūtatthe dutiyantanipāto, abhūtaṃ vacananti attho. Paṭibāhatīti aññe nivāreti. Saṃvāsathenako nāmāti ettha ko saṃvāso nāma, nanu ekakammādikoti āha “bhikkhuvassagaṇanādiko”tiādi. Bhikkhuvassagaṇanādikoti ādisaddena yathāvuḍḍhaṃ vandanasādiyanaṃ āsanapaṭibāhanaṃ uposathapavāraṇādīsu sandissananti imāni saṅgaṇhāti. “Kiriyabhedo”ti iminā saṃ ekato vasiyati anenāti saṃvāsoti vacanatthena kiriyabhedo saṃvāso nāmāti dasseti. Imasmiṃ attheti imasmiṃ vatthumhi, imasmiṃ ṭhāneti attho. Iminā pārājikādiṭṭhāne pana ekakammādiko saṃvāso nāmāti dasseti.

Videsanti: 'Videsa' means a country that is a separation from one's own country. Here, the word 'vi' conveys the meaning of separation. Or alternatively, 'vi' means far, and 'desaṃ' means country. Here, the word 'vi' conveys the meaning of distance. 'Musāti': 'Musā' is an indeclinable word in the accusative case in the sense of 'untrue'; the meaning is 'an untrue statement.' 'Paṭibāhatīti': 'Paṭibāhati' means 'prevents others.' 'Saṃvāsathenako nāmāti': Here, what is 'saṃvāsa'? Is it not 'ekakammādiko' (one or more shared acts)? He answers, 'counting the years of a monk's seniority,' and so on. 'Bhikkhuvassagaṇanādikoti': By the word 'ādi' (and so on), it includes practices such as paying respects according to seniority, accepting seats, preventing seats, and those visible in matters of Uposatha and Pavāraṇā. 'Kiriyabhedo': By this, it is shown that 'saṃvāsa' (communion) is the division of actions, meaning 'one lives together by this.' 'Imasmiṃ attheti': In this matter, in this subject, this is the meaning. By this, it is shown that in cases like Pārājika offenses, 'saṃvāsa' refers to shared duties like 'ekakammādiko.'

“Liṅgassa [M 0.0260] ceva saṃvāsassa cā”ti iminā ubhayathenakoti ettha ubhayasarūpaṃ dasseti.

By 'both the outward mark and communion,' he shows the twofold nature in 'ubhayathenako' (a thief of both).

Etthāti [V 1.0224] theyyasaṃvāsakaṭṭhāne. Rāja…pe… bhayehi vāti ettha bhayasaddo paccekaṃ yojetabbo. Rājabhayena ca dubbhikkhabhayena ca kantārabhayena ca rogabhayena ca veribhayena cāti hi attho. Cīvaragahaṇatthanti cīvarāharaṇatthaṃ, ayameva vā pāṭho. Vāsaddo hetvatthaṃ vā sampadānatthaṃ vā sampiṇḍeti. Ayaṃ gāthā vibhattiyā uppaṭipāṭittā bhaggarītisaṅkhātā alaṅkāradosā na muttā. Liṅganti samaṇaliṅgaṃ. Idhāti imasmiṃ sāsane.

Etthāti: Here, that is, in the context of the thief-in-communion. Rāja…pe… bhayehi vāti: Here, the word 'bhaya' (fear) should be connected individually. For the meaning is: by fear from a king, by fear from famine, by fear from a wilderness, by fear from disease, and by fear from enemies. Cīvaragahaṇatthaṃ: For the purpose of taking robes, that is, for the purpose of fetching robes; or this is just a variant reading. Vāsaddo hetvatthaṃ vā sampadānatthaṃ vā sampiṇḍeti: The word 'vā' (or) combines either in the sense of cause or in the sense of purpose. Ayaṃ gāthā vibhattiyā uppaṭipāṭittā bhaggarītisaṅkhātā alaṅkāradosā na muttā: This verse, due to the disordered arrangement of its inflections, is not free from the rhetorical fault called 'bhaggarīti' (broken style). Liṅganti: The outward mark, that is, the outward mark of a recluse. Idhāti: Here, that is, in this Dispensation.

Nādhivāsetīti na sampaṭicchati. Yāvāti yattakaṃ kālaṃ, ayaṃ panettha yojanā – idha yo rāja…pe… bhayena vā cīvaragahaṇatthaṃ vā liṅgaṃ ādiyati, so suddhamānaso hutvā yāva saṃvāsaṃ nādhivāseti, tāva eso “theyyasaṃvāsako nāmā”ti na vuccatīti.

Nādhivāsetīti: 'Does not consent,' that is, 'na sampaṭicchati' (does not accept). Yāvāti: 'As long as,' that is, 'yattakaṃ kālaṃ' (for whatever period of time). Ayaṃ panettha yojanā: This is the connection here. Here, whoever assumes the outward mark due to fear of kings... or for the purpose of taking robes, if he, with a pure mind, does not consent to the communion for that long, then he is not called a 'thief-in-communion.'

Tatrāti tāsu gāthāsu. Idhāti imasmiṃ sāsane. Evanti liṅge gahiyamāne. Tasminti jane. Anosaritvāvāti anokkamitvāva. Liṅgaṃ apanetvāti sayaṃ gahitaṃ samaṇaliṅgaṃ vināsetvā. Pabbajitālayanti pabbajitachāyaṃ. Pubbeti saṃvāsathenake.

Tatrāti: There, that is, in those verses. Idhāti: Here, that is, in this Dispensation. Evanti: Thus, that is, when the outward mark is assumed. Tasminti jane: In that person. Anosaritvāvāti: Without stepping back, that is, without retreating. Liṅgaṃ apanetvāti: Having removed the outward mark, that is, having destroyed the outward mark of a recluse taken by oneself. Pabbajitālayanti: The appearance of one gone forth, that is, the shadow of one gone forth. Pubbeti: Formerly, that is, in the case of the thief-in-communion.

Sabbapāsaṇḍiyabhattānīti sabbāni pāsaṇḍaṃ uddissa dinnāni bhattāni.

Sabbapāsaṇḍiyabhattānīti: All meals given to sectarians, that is, all meals given dedicated to a sect.

Satte vahatīti sattavāho. Viramitabbanti veraṃ, taṃ pavattetīti veriko. Kāyena pariharitabbānīti kāyaparihāriyāni. Tanti tuvaṃ. Hīnāyāvattabhāvanti hīnāya gihibhāvāya āvattabhāvaṃ.

Satte vahatīti sattavāho: 'Sattavāho' (a carrier of beings) means 'satte vahati' (he carries beings). Viramitabbanti veraṃ, taṃ pavattetīti veriko: 'Veraṃ' (hostility) is that from which one should refrain; 'veriko' (hostile) is one who promotes that. Kāyena pariharitabbānīti kāyaparihāriyāni: 'Kāyaparihāriyāni' (things to be maintained by the body) means 'kāyena pariharitabbāni' (things to be maintained by the body). Tanti tuvaṃ: 'Taṃ' (you) means 'tuvaṃ' (you). Hīnāyāvattabhāvanti hīnāya gihibhāvāya āvattabhāvaṃ: 'Hīnāyāvattabhāvaṃ' (the state of reverting to the low) means 'hīnāya gihibhāvāya āvattabhāvaṃ' (the state of reverting to the inferior state of a householder).

Uppabbajitvāti pabbajaviyogaṃ katvā. Tamatthanti uppabbajitasaṅkhātamatthaṃ. Assāti mahāsāmaṇerassa.

Uppabbajitvāti: Having disrobed, that is, having made an abandonment of the going forth. Tamatthanti: That meaning, that is, the meaning consisting of having disrobed. Assāti: Of him, that is, of the great novice.

Mahanto vāti ettha vāsaddo garahattho. Pageva daharoti dasseti. Abyatto hotīti yojanā. Soti sāmaṇero.

Mahanto vāti: Here, the word 'vā' is in the sense of dispraise. This shows 'how much more so a young one.' Abyatto hotīti yojanā: The construction is 'he is unskilled.' So: He, that is, the novice.

Vacchagorakkhādīnīti [M 0.0261] ettha vacchoti taruṇagoṇo. So hi mātusantike vasatīti vaccho. Mātuyā viyogakāle vā vassatīti vacchoti vuccati. Iminā dammagavajaraggavāpi sāmaññato gahitā. Go vuccati khettabhūmi. Vaccho ca go ca vacchagavā, tesaṃ rakkhanaṃ vacchagorakkho, so ādi yesaṃ kasikammādīnanti vacchagorakkhādīni. “Sūpasampanno”ti iminā [V 1.0225] gahaṭṭhampi sace upasampādeti, sūpasampannoti dasseti. Anupasampannakāleyevāti sāmaṇerakāleyeva. Vinayavinicchayeti vinaye vuttassa theyyasaṃvāsakassa vinicchaye. Theyyasaṃvāsako hoti liṅgassa apanītattā.

Vacchagorakkhādīnīti: Here, 'vaccho' means a young bull. It is called 'vaccho' because it stays near its mother. Or it is called 'vaccho' because it cries when separated from its mother. By this, tame cattle and old bullocks are also generally included. 'Go' is said to be a field. A calf and a field are 'vacchagavā'; their tending is 'vacchagorakkho.' 'Vacchagorakkhādīni' means those activities, such as farming, of which the tending of calves and fields is the foremost. 'Sūpasampanno'ti: By this, it is shown that even if he ordains a householder, he is 'sūpasampanno' (well-ordained). Anupasampannakāleyeva: Even during the time of not being fully ordained, that is, even during the novice period. Vinayavinicchaye: In the adjudication of the Vinaya, that is, in the adjudication regarding the thief-in-communion stated in the Vinaya. Theyyasaṃvāsako hoti liṅgassa apanītattā: He is a thief-in-communion because the outward mark has been removed.

Theyyasaṃvāsako na hoti saliṅge ṭhitattā. Ayampi theyyasaṃvāsako na hoti kāsāye saussāhattā. Theyyasaṃvāsako hoti kāsāye dhurassa nikkhittattā.

He is not a thief-in-communion because he remains in his own outward mark. This one is also not a thief-in-communion because he has zeal for the ochre robe. He is a thief-in-communion because the burden of the ochre robe has been discarded.

Theyyasaṃvāsako na hoti saliṅge ṭhitattā. Neva theyyasaṃvāsako hoti kāsāye saussāhattā. Methunasevanādīhītiādisaddena pāṇātipātādayo saṅgaṇhāti. Theyyasaṃvāsako hoti kāsāye dhurassa nikkhittattā. Ovaṭṭikanti adhovaṭṭena karaṇaṃ. Rakkhati tāvāti tāva rakkhati vīmaṃsanena nivāsitattā. Liṅganti samaṇaliṅgaṃ. Theyyasaṃvāsako hoti gihiliṅgassa sampaṭicchitattā.

He is not a thief-in-communion because he remains in his own outward mark. Nor is he a thief-in-communion because he has zeal for the ochre robe. Methunasevanādīhīti: By the word 'ādi' in 'methunasevanādīhi' (by engaging in sexual intercourse and so on), it includes killing living beings and so on. He is a thief-in-communion because the burden of the ochre robe has been discarded. Ovaṭṭikanti: 'Ovaṭṭikaṃ' means acting with concealment. Rakkhati tāvāti: 'He protects for a while' means he protects for a while, because it was put on with consideration. Liṅganti: The outward mark, that is, the outward mark of a recluse. Theyyasaṃvāsako hoti gihiliṅgassa sampaṭicchitattā: He is a thief-in-communion because he has accepted the outward mark of a householder.

Vīmaṃsati vā sampaṭicchati vā rakkhatiyeva odātavatthassa antokāsāyabhāvato. “Bhikkhuniyāpi eseva nayo”ti vuttamevatthaṃ vibhāvento āha “sāpī”tiādi.

He investigates or accepts, but still protects, because the white cloth is inside the ochre robe. Explaining the meaning already stated, 'The same principle applies to a bhikkhunī,' he says, 'she also,' and so on.

Vuḍḍhapabbajito sāmaṇeroti sambandho. Pāḷiyampīti pantiyampi. Seno maṃsapesiṃ gahetvā gacchati viya bhattapiṇḍe pattaṃ upanāmetvā gahetvā gacchati. Theyyasaṃvāsako na hoti vassānaṃ agaṇanattā.

Vuḍḍhapabbajito sāmaṇeroti sambandho: The connection is 'an elder monk and a novice.' Pāḷiyampīti pantiyampi: Even in the Pāḷi, that is, even in the line of text. Seno maṃsapesiṃ gahetvā gacchati viya bhattapiṇḍe pattaṃ upanāmetvā gahetvā gacchati: Like a hawk taking a piece of meat and going, so too, he goes, having presented the bowl for a lump of food and taken it. Theyyasaṃvāsako na hoti vassānaṃ agaṇanattā: He is not a thief-in-communion because the rains-residences are not counted.

48. Titthiyapakkantakakathā

48. The Account of One Who Departed to the Sectarians

110. Pakkamatīti [M 0.0262] pakkanto, “paviṭṭho”ti iminā kamudhātuyā padavikkhepatthaṃ dasseti, icchākantiatthe nivatteti. Soti titthiyapakkantako. Tatrāti titthiyapakkantake. Upasampanno bhikkhu gacchatīti sambandho. Tesanti titthiyānaṃ. “Titthiyo bhavissāmī”ti pubbeva laddhigahitattā vuttaṃ “liṅge ādinnamatte”ti. Kusacīrādīnīti ettha kuso vuccati salākā. Cīroti panti, āvalīti attho. Kuse rajjunā āvunitvā kato cīro kusacīro, so ādi yesaṃ tānīti kusacīrādīni. Ādisaddena phalakacīrādayo saṅgaṇhāti. Kusatiṇehi kato cīro kusacīrotipi vadanti. Naggoti acelako. Ājīvakoti acelakavatamādāya [V 1.0226] jīvatīti ājīvako. Tesanti ājīvakānaṃ. Ovadito hutvāti sambandho.

110. 'Pakkamati' means 'pakkanto'. By 'paviṭṭho' (entered), it shows the meaning of 'placing the feet' for the root 'kamu', and it turns it away from the meaning of 'desire' or 'wishing'. So, he is a 'titthiyapakkantako' (one who has gone over to the sectarians). 'Tatra' means 'in the case of one who has gone over to the sectarians'. The connection is 'an ordained monk goes'. 'Tesaṃ' means 'of the sectarians'. Because the view was grasped beforehand, 'I will become a sectarian,' it is said 'just upon the mark being taken'. 'Kusacīrādīnīti': here, 'kusa' is called 'salākā' (a thin strip). 'Cīra' means a row, a line; that is the meaning. A 'cīra' made by binding 'kusa' with a string is a 'kusacīra'; those things of which this is the foremost are 'kusacīrādīni'. By the word 'ādi', it includes bark garments and the like. Some also say that a 'cīra' made from kusa grass is a 'kusacīra'. 'Naggo' means 'acelako' (one without clothes). 'Ājīvako' means one who lives by adopting the vow of being without clothes. 'Tesaṃ' means 'of the Ājīvakas'. The connection is 'having been advised'.

Kinti kiṃ vataṃ. Luñcāpetīti apanayāpeti. Morapiñchādīnīti ettha piñchaṃ vuccati pakkho. So hi piñchati ākāse gacchati anenāti piñchanti vuccati. Pichi gatiyanti dhātupāṭho. Morassa piñchaṃ morapiñchaṃ, taṃ ādi yesaṃ tānīti morapiñchādīni. Ādisaddena ulūkapiñchādayo saṅgaṇhāti. Yāva na sampaṭicchatīti yāva laddhiṃ na sampaṭicchati. Nanti vīmaṃsamānaṃ bhikkhuṃ. Laddhīti titthiyaladdhi. Rakkhatīti titthiyapakkantakato rakkhati. Laddhiyā abhāvena titthiyapakkantako na hotīti adhippāyo. Acchiddacīvaroti ettha ākāro kodhattho, aḍḍattho vā hoti, chiddasaddo dūsanattho hoti. Tasmā ākodhena aḍḍena vā chiddo dūsitoti acchiddoti attho daṭṭhabbo. “Acchinno”tipi pāṭho. Acchiddaṃ cīvarametassāti acchiddacīvaro. Titthāyatananti titthīnaṃ nivāsaṭṭhānaṃ, titthiyānaṃ upassayanti attho.

'Kiṃ' means 'kiṃ vataṃ' (what vow)? 'Luñcāpeti' means 'causes to remove'. 'Morapiñchādīnīti': here, 'piñcha' is called 'pakkha' (feather). For it is called 'piñcha' because it spreads and one goes in the sky by means of it. The Dhātupāṭha states 'pichi' is in the sense of 'movement'. A peacock's feather is 'morapiñcha'; those things of which that is the foremost are 'morapiñchādīni'. By the word 'ādi', it includes owl feathers and the like. 'Yāva na sampaṭicchati' means 'as long as he does not accept the view'. 'Naṃ' means 'the monk who is investigating'. 'Laddhi' means 'the view of the sectarians'. 'Rakkhati' means 'protects from becoming one who has gone over to the sectarians'. The intention is that due to the absence of the view, he does not become one who has gone over to the sectarians. 'Acchiddacīvaro': here, the prefix 'ā' has the meaning of 'slight' or 'half', and the word 'chidda' has the meaning of 'blemish'. Therefore, the meaning 'acchidda' should be understood as 'blemished slightly or by half'. There is also a reading 'acchinno' (unbroken). One whose robe is without defect is 'acchiddacīvaro'. 'Titthāyatana' means 'the dwelling place of the sectarians', that is, 'the residence of the sectarians'.

49. Tiracchānagatavatthu

49. The Account of the Animal

111. Devasampattisadisaṃ issariyasampattiṃ anubhavantopi so nāgo kasmā nāgayoniyā aṭṭīyatīti āha “kiñcāpī”tiādi.

111. Even though that nāga experiences a fortune of power similar to divine attainment, why is he afflicted by the nāga existence? He said, 'Kiñcāpi...' (though indeed...).

Tattha [M 0.0263] kiñcāpi anubhotīti sambandho. Kiñcāpisaddo hettha sambhāvanājotako, panasaddo garahatthajotako. Kusalavipākenāti ahetukakusalavipākena. Tassāti nāgassa. Sajātiyāti samānajātiyā nāgiyā. Udakasañcārimaṇḍūkabhakkhanti udake sañcaraṇasīlaṃ maṇḍūkasaṅkhātaṃ bhakkhaṃ pātubhavatīti yojanā. Soti nāgo. Aṭṭīyatīti aramaṇaṃ pīḷiyati. Harāyatīti ettha haredhātu lajjanatthoti āha “lajjatī”ti. Ekāranto dhātu bhūvādigaṇiko (saddanītidhātumālāyaṃ 16 rakārantadhātu). Jigucchatīti ettha gupadhātuyā kammaṃ dassento āha “attabhāva”nti. “Tassa bhikkhuno”tipadassa “nikkhante”tipadena yojitabbattā bhummatthe sāmivacananti āha “tasmiṃ bhikkhusmi”nti. Atha vā tassa bhikkhunoti sāmiyogattā “nikkhante”ti ettha bhāvatthe mānapaccayoti āha “nikkhamane”ti. Iminā nikkhanteti ettha na antapaccayo, mānapaccayasseva antabhāvaṃ katvā vuttoti dasseti. Vissaṭṭhoti sativissajjito. Tasminti bhikkhumhi. Kapimiddhavasenevāti kapino middhavasena eva. Atha vā kapimiddhavasena niddāyanto iva niddāyantoti yojanā. Paṭinipajjīti puna nipajji. Vissaramakāsīti [V 1.0227] ettha visaddo virūpatthajotako, sarasaddo saddavācakoti dassento āha “virūpaṃ mahāsaddamakāsī”ti.

There, the connection is 'kiñcāpi anubhoti' (though he experiences). Here, the word 'kiñcāpi' indicates possibility, and the word 'pana' indicates reproach. 'Kusalavipākena' means 'by rootless wholesome result'. 'Tassa' means 'of the nāga'. 'Sajātiyā' means 'of a female nāga of the same kind'. 'Udakasañcārimaṇḍūkabhakkhaṃ': the construction is 'food, known as frogs, which are accustomed to moving in the water, appears'. 'So' means 'the nāga'. 'Aṭṭīyati' means he is afflicted with discontent. 'Harāyati': here, the root 'hare' has the meaning of 'shame', thus he says 'lajjatī' (he is ashamed). The root ending in 'e' belongs to the bhū-group (in the Saddanīti Dhātumālā, the 16th root ending in 'ra'). 'Jigucchati': here, showing the object of the root 'gup', he says 'attabhāvaṃ' (his own body). Because the word 'tassa bhikkhuno' should be connected with the word 'nikkhante', it is a genitive in the sense of the locative, thus he says 'tasmiṃ bhikkhusmiṃ'. Alternatively, because 'tassa bhikkhuno' implies a relationship, 'nikkhante' here is the māna-suffix in the sense of 'state of being', thus he says 'nikkhamane' (upon the departure). By this, it is shown that in 'nikkhante', it is not the anta-suffix, but the māna-suffix which has been made into the form of 'anta'. 'Vissaṭṭho' means 'one whose mindfulness is released'. 'Tasmiṃ' means 'in that monk'. 'Kapimiddhavaseneva' means 'just by the power of a monkey's torpor'. Alternatively, the construction is 'sleeping as if sleeping by the power of a monkey's torpor'. 'Paṭinipajji' means 'he lay down again'. 'Vissaramakāsi': here, the word 'vi' indicates the meaning of 'deformed', and the word 'sara' denotes 'sound', thus he says 'virūpaṃ mahāsaddamakāsi' (he made a deformed, loud sound).

“Akārassa lopaṃ katvā”ti iminā tumhe khotthāti ettha “tumhe kho atthā”ti padavibhāgaṃ katvā okārato parassa akārassa lopaṃ dasseti. “Akārassālopa”ntipi pāṭho. Evañhi sati akārassa alopaṃ katvāti attho daṭṭhabbo. Iminā “tumhe kho atthā”ti padacchedaṃ katvā akāre pare okārassa vakāraṃ katvā tumhe khvatthā”ti pāṭho dassito. Kasmā imasmiṃ dhammavinaye avirūḷhidhammāti āha “jhāna…pe… abhabbattā”ti. “Bhavathā”ti iminā atthāti ettha asadhātu sattatthavācako thavibhattīti dasseti. Sajātiyāti ettha samānā jāti etissāti sajātīti [M 0.0264] vutte nāgī evāti āha “nāgiyā evā”ti. Manussitthiādīti ettha ādisaddena tiracchānagatitthīpetitthīdevitthiyo saṅgaṇhāti. “Dveme bhikkhave paccayā”ti desanā sāvasesadesanāti dassento āha “ettha cā”ti. Etthāti tiracchānagatavatthumhi. Abhiṇhanti abhikkhaṇaṃ punappunanti attho.

By 'having made the elision of the 'a' sound', it shows the elision of the 'a' sound after the 'o' sound, having divided the words as 'tumhe kho atthā' in 'tumhe khotthā'. There is also the reading 'akārassālopaṃ'. If so, the meaning should be understood as 'having made the non-elision of the 'a' sound'. By this, having divided the words as 'tumhe kho atthā', it is shown that when an 'a' sound follows, the 'o' sound is changed to a 'v' sound, giving the reading 'tumhe khvatthā'. Why are they said to be of a nature not to grow in this Dhamma-Vinaya? He said, 'because of... inability regarding jhāna... etc.'. By 'bhavathā', it shows that in 'atthā', the root 'asa' denotes the meaning of 'being', and 'tha' is the personal ending. 'Sajātiyā': here, when 'sajāti' is said, meaning 'she for whom the birth is the same', he says 'nāgiyā eva' (of a female nāga only). 'Manussitthiādi': here, by the word 'ādi', it includes female animals, female petas, and female devas. Showing that the teaching 'These two conditions, O monks...' is a teaching with something remaining, he says 'and here'. 'Ettha' means 'in the account of the animal'. 'Abhiṇhaṃ' means 'repeatedly, again and again'; that is the meaning.

Tiracchānagatoti ettha kiṃ apāyapariyāpanno duggatiahetukapaṭisandhikovādhippetoti āha “nāgo vā hotū”tiādi.

“Tiracchānagata” (animal): here, is one who is included in the states of deprivation meant, or one with a rootless rebirth-linking in a woeful state? He says, ‘whether one becomes a nāga,’ and so on.

50. Mātughātakādivatthukathā

50. The Discourse on the Case of the Matricide and Others

112. Nikkhantinti ettha “imassa pāpakammassā”ti chaṭṭhīyogattā bhāvatthe tipaccayoti āha “nikkhamana”nti. Apavāhananti apāyapaṭisandhivahanato apagamanaṃ. Yenāti manussabhūtena yena jīvitā voropitāti sambandho. Manussitthibhūtāti manussitthī hutvā bhūtā, manussitthībhāvaṃ vā bhūtā pattā. Iminā tiracchānagatitthiādayo nivatteti. “Janikā”ti iminā posāvanikamātādayo nivatteti. Sayampīti ettha pisaddo na kevalaṃ mātāyeva, atha kho puttenāpīti dasseti. Satāti santena. Manussajātikeneva satā manussajātiko eva hutvā voropitāti yojanā. Anantare bhave phalaṃ nibbattetīti ānantariyaṃ, mātughātakakammaṃ, tena jātisāmaññampi ajanikaṃ ghātento ca janikampi jātibhedaṃ ghātento ca na anantariko hoti, tassa pabbajjā ca upasampadā ca na vāritāti dassento āha “yena panā”tiādi. Tattha poseti vaddhetīti posāpaniyā, sā eva posāvanikā pakārassa vakāraṃ, yakārassa ca kakāraṃ katvā, posāvanikā ca sā mātā ceti posāvanikamātā. Assāti [V 1.0228] puttassa. Idaṃ padaṃ pubbāparāpekkhaṃ. Tattha pubbapade bhāvasambandho, pacchimapade sāmisambandho. Sabbathā eseva nayo hotīti āha “sacepī”tiādi. Vesiyāti upalakkhaṇavasena vuttaṃ[M 0.0265]. Yāya kāyaci itthiyā puttassāpi gahetabbattā. “Ayaṃ me pitā”ti ajānanameva hi pamāṇaṃ. Anenāti iminā puttena. “Pitughātakotveva saṅkhyaṃ gacchatī”ti iminā mātughātakepi “ayaṃ me mātā”ti ajānitvā ghātentopi mātughātakotveva saṅkhyaṃ gacchatīti dasseti.

112. Here, in the word `nikkhanti`, because of its connection with `imassa pāpakammassa` (of this evil kamma) in the genitive case, the suffix `-ti` is in the sense of an abstract noun; thus he says it means `nikkhamana` (departure). `Apavāhana` means removal, as it is the departing from what leads to rebirth in the plane of misery. `Yena` (by whom): the connection is 'by whom, being a human, life was deprived.' `Manussitthibhūtā` means 'having become a human female,' or 'having attained the state of a human female.' By this he excludes female animals and so on. `Janikā` (birth-mother): by this he excludes a foster-mother and so on. Here in `sayampi`, the particle `pi` shows that it is not only by the mother but also by the son. `Satā` means 'by one who is.' The construction is: 'by one who is of human birth, being a human himself, he deprived of life.' That which produces its result in the immediately following existence is an `ānantariya` (immediately effective) deed; matricide is such a kamma. Therefore, one who kills someone of the same species who is not his mother, or who kills his mother who is of a different species, does not commit an immediately effective deed. To show that for such a person, going forth and higher ordination are not barred, he says: `yena pana`, etc. Therein, `posāpaniyā` means one who rears and raises. She is a `posāvanikā` (foster-mother), by changing `pa` to `va` and `ya` to `ka`. `Posāvanikā ca sā mātā ceti` becomes `posāvanikamātā` (foster-mother). `Assa` means 'of the son.' This word has reference to what precedes and what follows. In the preceding part, there is a connection of state; in the following part, a connection of ownership. To show that this is the method in all cases, he says: `sacepi`, etc. `Vesiyā` (a courtesan) is stated by way of illustration, because it should be understood of the son of any woman whatsoever. For not knowing 'This is my father' is indeed the standard. `Anena` means 'by this son.' By the phrase 'he is reckoned as a patricide,' he shows that in the case of matricide too, one who kills her without knowing 'This is my mother' is still reckoned as a matricide.

114. Saṅkhepena vuttamatthaṃ vitthārena dassento āha “manussajātiyaṃ hī”tiādi. Apabbajitanti gihibhūtaṃ. Pabbajjā cassāti ettha casaddena upasampadāpi vāritāti dasseti. Assāti arahantaghātakassa. Avasesanti arahantato avasesaṃ. Assāti ariyaghātakassa. Ānantariyo na hoti tiracchānagatattā panassa pabbajjā vāritāti attho netabbo. Etthāti mātughātakādikammesu. Vadhāyāti tadatthe catutthīti āha “vadhatthāyā”ti. “Māretu”nti iminā “vadhatthāyā”ti ettha hanadhātu hiṃsanatthoti dasseti. “Nīyantī”ti iminā onīyantīti ettha otyūpasaggo dhātvatthānuvattakoti dasseti. Yaṃ pana vacanaṃ vuttanti sambandho. Tassa vacanassa atthoti yojanā. “Sacā ca iti ayaṃ nipāto vutto”ti iminā bhayapīḷitattā ca niruttīsu akusalattā ca davābhaṇanena ravābhaṇanena ayaṃ nipāto corehi vuttoti dasseti. “Sace ca icceva vā pāṭho”ti iminā tehi tathā vuttepi saṅgītikāle vā potthakārūḷhakāle vā yathābhūtaṃ saṅgītattā, potthakārūḷhattā ca yathābhūto pāṭho atthīti dasseti. Tatthāti tesu padesu. Niddhāraṇe bhummaṃ. Tassāti “sacajja maya”nti pāṭhassa. “Sace ajja maya”nti iminā ekāralopasandhiṃ dasseti. “Sacejja maya”nti akāralopasandhināpi pāṭho atthi.

114. To show in detail the meaning stated in brief, he says: `manussajātiyaṃ hī`, etc. `Apabbajitaṃ` means one who is a layperson. Here in `pabbajjā c'assa` (and his going forth), by the particle `ca` he shows that higher ordination is also barred. `Assa` means 'of one who kills an arahant.' `Avasesaṃ` means what is remaining from an arahant. `Assa` means 'of one who kills a noble one.' He is not one who commits an immediately effective deed, but because he is an animal, his going forth is barred—this is the meaning to be inferred. `Ettha` means in these kammas of matricide and so on. `Vadhāya`: the dative is in the sense of purpose; thus he says `vadhatthāya` (for the purpose of killing). By `māretuṃ` (to kill), he shows that here in `vadhatthāya`, the root `han` has the sense of injuring. By `nīyanti` (they are led), he shows that here in `onīyanti`, the prefix `o-` follows the meaning of the root. The connection is: 'But what statement was said.' The construction is: 'the meaning of that statement.' By '`sacā ca`, this particle was spoken,' he shows that this particle was spoken by the thieves because they were afflicted by fear and unskilled in grammar, with confused and clamorous speech. Or by 'the reading is `sace ca`,' he shows that although it was spoken thus by them, at the time of the council or when it was committed to books, the authentic reading exists because it was recited and committed to books as it actually was. `Tattha` means in those passages. The locative is in the sense of specification. `Tassa` means of the reading `sacajja mayaṃ`. By `sace ajja mayaṃ` (if today we), he shows the sandhi with elision of one `a`. There is also a reading `sacejja mayaṃ` with the sandhi of eliding the vowel `a`.

115. Pakatattanti pakatiyā sīlasaṅkhāto attā sabhāvo etissāti pakatattā, taṃ. Kāyasaṃsaggena bhikkhunīnaṃ pārājikattā vuttaṃ “sīlavināsaṃ pāpetī”ti. Anicchamānaṃyeva bhikkhuninti sambandho.

115. `Pakatattaṃ`: She is `pakatattā` because her own nature is reckoned as virtue by nature; `taṃ` refers to her. Because physical contact with bhikkhunīs is a pārājika offense, it is said, 'he causes the destruction of her virtue.' The connection is with 'a bhikkhunī who is unwilling.'

Icchamānanti [M 0.0266] odātavatthavasanaṃ icchamānaṃ. Yasmā abhikkhunī hoti, tasmā bhikkhunīdūsako na hotīti yojanā. Sīlavipannaṃ bhikkhuninti sambandho.

`Icchamānaṃ` means desiring to wear white clothes. The construction is: because she is not a bhikkhunī, therefore he is not one who corrupts a bhikkhunī. The connection is with 'a bhikkhunī who is corrupt in virtue.'

Yo [V 1.0229] devadatto saṅghaṃ bhindati viya, bhindatīti yojanā. Uddhammanti dhammato virahitaṃ. Ubbinayanti vinayato virahitaṃ. Catunnaṃ kammānanti apalokanādīnaṃ catunnaṃ kammānaṃ.

The construction is: 'He who, like Devadatta, splits the Sangha, splits it.' `Uddhammaṃ` means devoid of the Dhamma. `Ubbinayaṃ` means devoid of the Vinaya. `Catunnaṃ kammānaṃ` means of the four kammas beginning with announcement.

Yo devadatto lohitaṃ uppādeti viya, uppādetīti yojanā. Duṭṭhacittenāti ettha na yaṃkiñci duṭṭhacittaṃ duṭṭhacittaṃ nāma, atha kho vadhakacittanti āha “vadhakacittenā”ti. Sarīreti sarīrabbhantare. Tathāgatassa hi abhejjakāyattā parūpakkamena cammacchedaṃ katvā lohitassa uppādanaṃ nāma natthi. Yo pana jīvako phāsuṃ karoti viya, phāsuṃ karotīti yojanā. Lohitañcāti pūtilohitañca.

The construction is: 'He who, like Devadatta, draws blood, draws it.' Here, by `duṭṭhacittena` (with a corrupt mind), it is not just any corrupt mind that is meant by 'corrupt mind,' but rather, he says, 'with a mind intent on killing.' `Sarīre` means inside the body. For in the case of the Tathāgata, because his body is inviolable, there is no such thing as drawing blood by cutting the skin through another's effort. The construction is: 'But he who, like Jīvaka, makes an incision, makes an incision.' `Lohitañca` means and putrid blood.

54. Ubhatobyañjanakavatthukathā

54. The Story Concerning the Hermaphrodite

116. Ubhatobyañjanakoti ettha bāhiratthasamāsaṃ dassento āha “itthinimittuppādanakammato cā”tiādi. Tattha “itthi…pe… kammato cā”ti iminā ubhayasarūpaṃ dasseti. Ubhato kammato pavattanti pāṭhaseso yojetabbo. Byañjananti nimittaṃ. Assāti janassa. Karotipi kāretipīti ettha karadhātuyā suddhakammakāritakammāni dassento āha “purisanimittenā”tiādi. Tattha “vītikkama”nti iminā suddhakammaṃ dasseti, “para”nti iminā kāritakammaṃ dasseti. Samādapetvāti uyyojetvā. Tassa duvidhabhāvaṃ dassento āha “duvidho”tiādi. Tattha itthibhāvena lakkhito ubhatobyañjanako itthiubhatobyañjanako. Esa nayo itaratthāpi.

116. As to 'hermaphrodite': here, to show the meaning of the external compound, he says: 'from the kamma that produces the female characteristic, etc.' Therein, by this 'female... (etc.)... from the kamma, and,' he shows the nature of both. The rest of the text, 'they proceed from the kamma of both,' should be supplied. `Byañjana` means a characteristic. `Assa` means 'of a person.' As to 'he does and causes to be done': here, to show the simple action and the causative action of the root `kar`, he says: 'with the male characteristic, etc.' Therein, by 'transgression,' he shows the simple action; by 'another,' he shows the causative action. `Samādapetvā` means having instigated. To show its twofold nature, he says: 'twofold, etc.' Therein, the hermaphrodite characterized by the female state is a female-hermaphrodite. This same method applies in the other case too.

Tatthāti duvidhesu ubhatobyañjanakesu. Itthinimittanti itthiyā aṅgajātaṃ. Eseva nayo “purisanimitta”nti etthāpi. Pākaṭaṃ paṭicchannanti sabhāvato pākaṭaṃ paṭicchannaṃ. Puna paṭicchannaṃ pākaṭanti rāgavasena paṭicchannaṃ [M 0.0267] pākaṭaṃ. Paraṃ gaṇhāpetīti parameva gaṇhāpetīti attho. Idanti kāraṇaṃ. Etesanti dvinnaṃ ubhatobyañjanakānaṃ. Kurundiyaṃ pana vuttaṃ, kiṃ vuttanti yojanā. Tatthāti ubhatobyañjanake. Vicāraṇakkamoti vīmaṃsanānukkamo. “Tattha vicārakkamo”tipi pāṭho. Vicāraṇakkamo dhammasaṅgahaṭṭhakathāya veditabbo, idha pana kiṃ veditabbanti āha “idamidha veditabba”nti. Tattha idanti napabbajjūpasampadakāraṇaṃ. Idhāti imissaṃ vinayaṭṭhakathāyaṃ.

`Tattha` means: among the two kinds of hermaphrodites. `Itthinimitta` means: the female sexual organ. This same method applies also to 'male characteristic.' `Pākaṭaṃ paṭicchannaṃ` means: obvious or concealed by nature. `Puna paṭicchannaṃ pākaṭaṃ` means: concealed and then obvious on account of lust. `Paraṃ gaṇhāpeti` means: he causes only another to take. `Idaṃ` means: this reason. `Etesaṃ` means: of the two hermaphrodites. But in the Kurundī it is said. The connection is: what is said? `Tattha` means: regarding the hermaphrodite. `Vicāraṇakkamo` means: the order of investigation. There is also the reading `tattha vicārakkamo`. The order of investigation is to be understood from the commentary to the Dhammasaṅgaṇī, but as to what should be understood here, he says: 'This should be understood here.' Therein, `idaṃ` means: the reason for not giving the going forth and the higher ordination. `Idha` means: in this Vinaya commentary.

55. Anupajjhāyakādivatthukathā

55. The Story Concerning One Without a Preceptor, etc.

117. Tena kho pana samayenāti ettha tasaddassa aniyamaniddesabhāvaṃ dassento āha “yena samayenā”ti. Sikkhāpadaṃ apaññattaṃ hotīti “na bhikkhave anupajjhāyako upasampādetabbo”ti [V 1.0230] sikkhāpadaṃ apaññattaṃ hoti. “Upajjhāyavirahita”nti iminā anupajjhāyakanti ettha akārassa virahatthaṃ dasseti. Upajjhāyavirahitaṃ upasampadāpekkhanti sambandho. “Eva”ntiādinā dosaṃ dasseti. Upajjhaṃ agāhāpetvāti “upajjhāyo me bhante hohī”ti (mahāva. 65; mahāva. aṭṭha. 64) upajjhaṃ agāhāpetvā. Upasampādentassa kārakasaṅghassāti yojanā. Kammaṃ panāti upasampadakammaṃ pana. “Eseva nayo”ti iminā upasampādentassa āpatti, kammaṃ pana na kuppatīti vacanaṃ atidisati.

117. As to `Tena kho pana samayena`: here, showing that the word `ta` is an indefinite indicator, he says: `yena samayena`. As to `Sikkhāpadaṃ apaññattaṃ hoti`: the training rule, 'Bhikkhus, one without a preceptor should not be given the higher ordination,' had not been laid down. By `Upajjhāyavirahitaṃ`, he shows that the `a` in `anupajjhāyaka` has the meaning of 'without.' The connection is: 'one seeking higher ordination who is devoid of a preceptor.' By 'Thus,' etc., he shows the fault. As to `Upajjhaṃ agāhāpetvā`: without having had a preceptor accepted by saying, 'Venerable sir, be my preceptor' (Mv 1:65). The connection is: of the Sangha that performs the act of giving the higher ordination. `Kammaṃ pana` means: but the act of higher ordination. By 'This is the same method,' he applies the statement that for the one giving the higher ordination there is an offense, but the act is not invalid.

56. Apattakādivatthukathā

56. The Explanation of the Cases Beginning with One Without a Bowl

118. Yo piṇḍo hatthesu labbhatīti yojanā. Tadatthāyāti tassa piṇḍassa atthāya. Seyyathāpi titthiyāti ettha seyyathāpisaddo upamattho, titthiyasaddo ājīvakanāmake titthiye hotīti dassento āha “yathāpi ājīvakanāmakā titthiyā”ti. Tasmā ājīvakasaṅkhāte titthiye upamaṃ katvā ujjhāyantīti āha “sūpabyañjanehī”tiādi. Hīti saccaṃ, yasmā vā. Teti ājīvakā. Kammaṃ pana na kuppatīti pattacīvaresu asantesupi kammavācāya [M 0.0268] “paripuṇṇassa pattacīvara”nti parikittitattā kammaṃ na kuppatīti adhippāyo.

118. The connection is: 'Whatever almsfood is received in the hands.' `Tadatthāya` means: for the sake of that almsfood. As to `Seyyathāpi titthiyā`: here the word `seyyathāpi` has the meaning of a comparison; showing that the word `titthiyā` refers to the sectarians called Ājīvakas, he says: 'just as the sectarians called Ājīvakas.' Therefore, having made a comparison to the sectarians known as Ājīvakas, they complain, he says: 'with curries and condiments,' etc. `Hi` means: truly, or because. `Te` means: those Ājīvakas. As to `Kammaṃ pana na kuppati`: the meaning is that the act is not invalid because, even though the bowl and robes are not present, it has been announced in the formal act with the words 'whose bowl and robes are complete'.

Yācitakenāti ettha yācito hutvā gahito yācitakoti dassento āha “yācitvā gahitenā”ti. “Īdisena hī”tiādinā dosaṃ dasseti. Tasmāti yasmā āpatti hoti, tasmā. Tassāti upasampadāpekkhassa. Nirapekkhehi ācariyupajjhāyādīhīti yojanā. Nissajjitvāti brahmadeyyena nissajjitvā. Anadhiṭṭhānupagānaṃ pattacīvarānaṃ apattacīvarattā vuttaṃ “adhiṭṭhānupagaṃ pattacīvara”nti. Paṇḍupalāsanti samaṇuddesabhāvāpekkhaṃ. So hi rūḷhivasena paṇḍupalāsoti vuccati. Atha vā yathā paṇḍupalāso na harito, nāpi sukkho hoti, evaṃ sopi pabbajāpekkho na gihī hoti, nāpi sāmaṇero, tasmā samaṇuddesabhāvāpekkho “paṇḍupalāso”ti vuccati.

As to `Yācitakena`: here, to show that `yācitaka` means what is taken after having been requested, he says: `yācitvā gahitena`. By 'With such,' etc., he shows the fault. `Tasmā` means: because there is an offense, therefore. `Tassa` means: of one seeking higher ordination. The connection is: by teachers, preceptors, etc., who are unconcerned. `Nissajjitvā` means: having relinquished as a gift of devotion. Because bowls and robes that have not been determined are not (proper) bowls and robes, it is said: 'a bowl and robes that have not been determined.' `Paṇḍupalāsa` means: one aspiring to the state of a postulant. For he is called a 'yellow leaf' by convention. Or, just as a yellow leaf is neither green nor dry, so too one aspiring to the going forth is neither a householder nor a novice; therefore one aspiring to the state of a postulant is called a 'yellow leaf'.

Vasantassa paṇḍupalāsassāti sambandho. Anāmaṭṭhapiṇḍapātanti bhikkhūhi anāmasitabbaggaṃ piṇḍapātaṃ. Sāmaṇerabhāgasamakoti sāmaṇerehi laddhena bhāgena samaṃ pavatto. Assāti paṇḍupalāsassa. Sāmaṇerassa sabbaṃ paṭijagganakammaṃ kātuṃ vaṭṭati viya, assa kātuṃ vaṭṭatīti yojanā.

The connection is with `vasantassa paṇḍupalāsassa` (of the 'yellow leaf' who is dwelling). `Anāmaṭṭhapiṇḍapāta` means: almsfood from a portion that should not be touched by bhikkhus. `Sāmaṇerabhāgasamako` means: proceeding equally with the share obtained by the novices. `Assa` means: of the 'yellow leaf.' The connection is: just as it is allowable for a novice to perform all the duties of looking after, so it is allowable for him to do so.

57. Hatthacchinnādivatthukathā

57. The Explanation of the Cases Beginning with the One with a Severed Hand

119. Hatthacchinnādivatthūsu [V 1.0231] hatthā chinnā yassāti hatthacchinnotiādivacanatthaṃ dassento āha “yassā”tiādi. Maṇibandheti pakoṭṭhante. So hi yasmā ettha maṇisaṅkhātaṃ alaṅkāravikatiṃ bandhati, tasmā maṇibandhoti vuccati. Kappareti kapoṇiyaṃ. Sā hi paresaṃ piṭṭhīsu kapati hiṃsati anenāti “kapparo”ti vuccati. Yassa hatthā chinnā honti, ayaṃ hatthacchinno nāmāti yojanā. Eseva nayo sesesupi. Eko vā pādoti yojanā. Heṭṭhā “eko vā dve vā hatthā”ti etthāpi eseva nayo. Catūsu hatthapādesu dve vāti eko hattho, eko pādoti dve [M 0.0269] vā. Kaṇṇāti saddaggahā. Te hi kaṇṇati savati etehīti kaṇṇāti vuccanti. Kaṇṇābaddheti kaṇṇacchiddassa ābaddhe. Saṅghāṭetunti saṅghaṭanaṃ kātuṃ, ābandhanaṃ kātunti attho. Ajapadaketi ajapadasaṇṭhāne ṭhāne. Nāsāti ghānāni. Tāni hi nāsati abyattasaddaṃ karoti etāhīti nāsāti vuccanti. Nāsikāti nāsāyeva. Saṇṭhāpetunti suṭṭhu ṭhapetuṃ, pakatiyā ṭhapetunti attho. Nakhasesanti nakhoyeva seso chinnaṅgulitoti nakhaseso, taṃ. Agge pure uṭṭhahatīti aṅguṭṭho. “Vuttanayenevā”ti iminā “nakhasesaṃ adassetvā”ti vacanaṃ atidisati. Kaṇḍaranāmakāti mahāsiranāmakā. Te hi kaṃ sarīraṃ dhārentīti kaṇḍarāti vuccanti dhakārassa ḍakāraṃ katvā. Yesūti kaṇḍaresu, niddhāraṇe bhummaṃ.

119. In the cases beginning with 'one with a severed hand,' showing the meaning of words such as 'hatthacchinno,' the commentator says 'yassa,' and so on. 'Maṇibandha' means the wrist. For since one binds on it an ornament known as a gem, it is called 'maṇibandha.' 'Kappara' means the elbow. For since one strikes or harms others on their backs with it, it is called 'kappara.' The construction is: 'One whose hands are cut off is called a "hatthacchinno."' This same method applies to the remaining cases. The construction of 'one foot' is similar. Below, for 'one or two hands,' this same method also applies. Among the four limbs—hands and feet—'or two' means one hand and one foot. 'Kaṇṇā' means the ears. For since one hears sounds with them, they are called 'kaṇṇā.' 'Kaṇṇābaddha' means tied to the ear-hole. 'Saṅghāṭetuṃ' means to join together; the meaning is to bind. 'Ajapadaka' means in a place shaped like a goat's foot. 'Nāsā' means the nostrils. For since one makes an indistinct sound with them, they are called 'nāsā.' 'Nāsikā' is just the nose.
