Uparimassa (of the one above) means of the one situated above the inner cave. Pārato (from the far side) means from the outside. Assa (of this): the connection is 'outside of this mountain.' Orato (from the near side) means from the inside. The connection is: 'there is a cave.' How large? He said: 'Standing having exceeded the boundary's delimitation.' How small? He said: 'Of the measure of the smallest possible boundary.' Taṃ (that) means the small cave. Atikhuddakaṃ (too small) means excessively small because it lacks the measure of the smallest possible boundary. Tato (from that) means from the boundary above. Bahi (outside) means outside the boundary. By 'If it is of boundary-measure, it is indeed a boundary,' he shows that if it is not of boundary-measure, it is indeed not a boundary.

Tanti khaṇḍasīmaṃ. Pūretvāti iṭṭhakamattikādīhi pūretvā. Aṭṭaṃ bandhitvāti aṭṭālakaṃ bandhitvā. Umaṅganadīti ettha ukāro okāraviparīto, tasmā pathaviyaṃ otaritvā pavisitvā maṅgati gacchatīti umaṅgāti attho daṭṭhabbo. Umaṅgāca sā nadī ceti umaṅganadī. Tatthāti umaṅganadiyaṃ. Heṭṭhāpathavitale ṭhitoti sīmāya heṭṭhāpathavitale iddhiyā ṭhito.

Taṃ (that) means the chapter boundary. Pūretvā (having filled) means having filled with bricks, clay, and so on. Aṭṭaṃ bandhitvā (having constructed a platform) means having constructed a watchtower. Regarding Umaṅganadī (Tunnel River): here the 'u' is the reverse of 'o,' therefore the meaning of umaṅga should be understood as 'it goes, having descended and entered into the earth.' That which is a tunnel (umaṅga) and a river is a Tunnel River. Tatra (therein) means in the Tunnel River. Heṭṭhāpathavitale ṭhito (standing on the ground-surface below) means standing by psychic power on the ground-surface below the boundary.

Sīmāmāḷaketi khaṇḍasīmāya māḷake. Vaṭarukkhoti nigrodharukkho. Tatoti vaṭarukkhato. Niggatapārohoti pavaddhaṃva hutvā rukkho ārohati anenāti pāroho, eko mūlaviseso. Niggato pāroho niggatapāroho. Mahāsīmaṃ sodhetvāti ettha sodhanaṃ nāma mahāsīmagatānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ hatthapāsānayanaṃ, sīmato vā bahikaraṇaṃ. Bahiddhāti dvīhi sīmāhi bahiddhā. “Bahiṭṭhā”tipi pāṭho. Bahi ṭhitā kātabbāti attho. Anāhaccāti mahāsīmāya pathavītalaṃ vā tatthajātarukkhādīni vā na āhanitvā. Evanti yathā khaṇḍasīmāya, evaṃ tathāti attho. Sīmāmāḷaketi khaṇḍasīmāmāḷake.

Sīmāmāḷake (on the boundary terrace) means on the terrace of the chapter boundary. Vaṭarukkho (banyan tree) means a nigrodha tree. Tato (from that) means from the banyan tree. Niggatapāroho (having a descended aerial root): an aerial root (pāroha) is so called because a tree ascends by means of it after it has grown; it is a particular kind of root. A descended aerial root is a niggatapāroho. Mahāsīmaṃ sodhetvā (having cleared the great boundary): here, 'clearing' means bringing the bhikkhus who are in the great boundary to within arm's reach, or making them go outside the boundary. Bahiddhā (outside) means outside the two boundaries. There is also the reading bahiṭṭhā; the meaning is 'they should be made to stand outside.' Anāhacca (without touching) means without striking the ground-surface of the great boundary or the trees and so on growing there. Evaṃ (thus) means: as with the chapter boundary, so there. Sīmāmāḷake (on the boundary terrace) means on the terrace of the chapter boundary.

Sīmāmāḷaketi dvinnaṃ sīmānaṃ aṅgaṇe. Sīmāmāḷakassāti kammassa kataṭṭhānassa sīmāmāḷakassa. Vehāsaṭṭhitasākhāyāti kammassa akataṭṭhāne sīmāmāḷake uṭṭhitāya vehāse ṭhitāya sākhāya. Tassāti bhikkhuno pādā vā nivāsanapārupanaṃ vāti sambandho. Purimanayepīti “sīmāmāḷake vaṭarukkho hotī”tiādinā vutte purimanayepi. Tatrāti purimanaye. Ukkhipāpetvā kātuṃ na vaṭṭatīti dvīhi sīmāhi uṭṭhitarukkhassa sākhā vā tato niggatapāroho vā dvīsu sīmāsu pathavītalaṃ vā tattha jātarukkhādīni vā āhacca ṭhitattā ukkhipāpetvā kātuṃ na vaṭṭati. Ānetabboti ettha dvikammikāya nīdhātuyā apadhānakammasseva vuttattā [V 1.0248] “bhikkhū”ti padhānakammaṃ ajjhāharitabbaṃ[M 0.0290]. Abbhuggacchatīti abbhaṃ ākāsaṃ uggacchati. Tatrāti pabbate. Kasmā ānetabboti āha “bajjhamānāyeva hī”tiādi. Tattha bajjhamānāyevāti kammavācāya bajjhamānāyeva. Iminā abaddhasīmā pamāṇarahitaṃ desaṃ otaratīti dasseti. Yaṃkiñcīti yaṃkiñci pabbatādi. Yattha katthacīti yasmiṃ kasmiṃci ṭhāne. Ekasambandhenāti baddhasīmāya ekasambandhena. Itīti tasmā ānetabboti yojanā.

Sīmāmāḷaketi (in the boundary enclosure) means in the courtyard of two boundaries. Sīmāmāḷakassā (of the boundary enclosure) means of the boundary enclosure, the place where the formal act was performed. Vehāsaṭṭhitasākhāyā (for a branch standing in the air) means for a branch standing in the air, which has arisen in a boundary enclosure where a formal act has not been performed. Tassā (of that) means of that monk; the connection is with 'feet' or 'lower and upper robes.' Purimanayepī (also in the previous method) means also in the previous method, stated with the words, 'there is a banyan tree in the boundary enclosure,' etc. Tatrā (therein) means in the previous method. 'It is not permissible to perform it after having it lifted up' means: because a branch of a tree that has arisen from two boundaries, or an aerial root that has emerged from it, touches the ground in both boundaries, or because of trees, etc., that have grown there, it is not permissible to perform the act after having them lifted up. Ānetabbo (it should be brought in): here, since with the verb nī, which takes two objects, only the secondary object is stated, the primary object 'monks' should be supplied. Abbhuggacchati (it goes up) means it goes up into the sky. Tatrā (therein) means on the mountain. Why should it be brought in? He says: 'Because it is being bound,' etc. Therein, 'being bound' means being bound by the formal proclamation of the act. This shows that an unbound boundary extends into an area without measure. Yaṃkiñci (whatever) means any mountain, etc. Yattha katthaci (wherever) means in any place whatsoever. Ekasambandhenā (by one connection) means through a single connection with the bound boundary. Iti (thus) means therefore; the connection is with 'it should be brought in'.

140. Tīṇi yojanāni tiyojanaṃ. “Pamāṇa”nti iminā paramasaddassa atirekauttamatthe nivatteti. Etissāti sīmāya. Sammanantena bhikkhunāti sambandho. Koṇato minitaṃ koṇanti yojanā. Hīti saccaṃ, yasmā vā. Āpattiñcāti dukkaṭāpattiñca.

140. Three yojanas are a tiyojana. By this word 'measure' (pamāṇa), he prevents the meaning of excess and superiority for the word 'parama'. Etissā (of this) means of this boundary. The connection is with 'by the monk who is establishing (the boundary).' The connection is: a yojana measured from corner to corner. Hī (indeed) means truly, or because. Āpattiñca (and an offense) means and an offense of wrong-doing.

Pārayatīti ajjhottharati. “Kitakābhidheyyaliṅgā”ti (kaccāyanasāre 45 gāthāyaṃ) vacanato abhidheyyabhūtaṃ sīmaṃ sandhāya itthiliṅgavasena pārāti vuttaṃ. Nadiyāti upayogatthe sāmivacanaṃ. Nadinti hi attho. Nadiṃ ajjhottharamānaṃ sīmanti sambandho. Etthāti nadipārasīmāyaṃ. Yatthassāti ettha yattha assāti padavibhāgaṃ dassento āha “yattha nadiyā”tiādi. “Nadiyā”ti iminā yaṃsaddassa visayaṃ dasseti. Dhuvanāvāti ettha dhuvasaddo niccatthoti āha “niccasañcaraṇanāvā”ti. Iminā dhuvena niccena sañcaraṇanāvā dhuvanāvāti vacanatthaṃ dasseti. Assāti hoti, bhaveyya vā. Nāvāya pamāṇaṃ dassento āha “yā”tiādi. Tattha yāti nāvā. Pājanapurisenāti ettha pājanaṃ nāma eko nāvāya gamanūpakaraṇaviseso. So hi pajati nāvā gacchati anenāti pājananti vuccati. Jakārassa cakāraṃ katvā pācanantipi yujjateva. Tassa gāhakena purisena saddhinti attho. Sā nāvā nītāti sambandho. Uddhaṃ vā adho vāti nadiyā paṭisotaṃ vā heṭṭhāsotaṃ vā. Thenehi vāti corehi vā. Kiñcāpi haṭā, pana tathāpi avassaṃ labbhaneyyā, dhuvanāvāva hotīti yojanā. Vātena vāti mālutena vā “chinna”iti sambandho. Vīcīhīti taraṅgehi. Taraṅgo hi [M 0.0291] vicittākārena cinoti vaḍḍhatīti vīcīti vuccati. Kiñcāpi nadīmajjhaṃ nītā, pana tathāpi avassaṃ āharitabbā, dhuvanāvāva hotīti yojanā. Ogateti otaritvā gate. Thalaṃ ussāritāti thalaṃ ukkhipitvā sāritā pāpitā nāvāpīti sambandho. Visaṅkhatapadarāti saṅkhatavirahitaphalakā vā. Dhuvanāvāva hotīti nimittakittanakāle niccasañcaraṇanāvattā dhuvanāvāva hotīti adhippāyo. Tatrāti “dhuvanāvā”tivacane. Nimittaṃ vā sīmā vā kammavācāya gacchatīti ettha kiñcāpi na nimittaṃ kammavācāya gacchati, sīmāya pana avinābhāvato [V 1.0249] vuttaṃ “kammavācāya gacchatī”ti. Tasmāti yasmāva nāvāya āgacchantāpi bhagavatā anuññātā, tasmā.

`Pārayati` means it pervades. In accordance with the rule, 'The gender is that of the thing designated by the derivative term,' with reference to the boundary, which is the thing to be designated, the word `pārā` is used in the feminine gender. `Nadiyā` is a genitive in the sense of an object, for the meaning is 'the river' (accusative). The connection is: the boundary that pervades the river. `Ettha` means in the boundary on the other side of the river. Explaining the word-division of `yatthassā` as `yattha assā`, he says, 'where, of the river,' and so on. By 'of the river,' he indicates the referent of the word `yaṃ`. `Dhuvanāvā`: here the word `dhuva` means 'permanent'; thus he says, 'a permanently traversing boat.' By this he shows the etymological meaning: a permanently traversing boat is a `dhuvanāvā`. `Assā` means there is, or there might be. Indicating the size of the boat, he says, 'that which,' and so on. Therein, `yā` is the boat. `Pājanapurisenāti`: here, `pājana` is a particular kind of implement for the boat's movement. For it is called `pājana` because one drives with it, the boat goes. Changing `ja` to `ca`, `pācana` is also correct. The meaning is: with the man who handles it. The connection is: that boat is taken. `Uddhaṃ vā adho vā` means upstream or downstream. `Thenehi vā` means or by thieves. The construction is: although it is seized, it is nevertheless certainly recoverable; it is a permanent boat indeed. `Vātena vā` means or by the wind; the connection is with 'broken loose.' `Vīcīhi` means by waves. A wave is called `vīci` because it gathers and grows in various forms. The construction is: although it is taken to the middle of the river, it is nevertheless certainly to be brought back; it is a permanent boat indeed. `Ogate` means having gone down and departed. `Thalaṃ ussāritā` means a boat lifted up and moved onto dry land. `Visaṅkhatapadarā` means or with its planks disassembled. The intention of `dhuvanāvāva hoti` is: at the time of announcing the marker, because it is a permanently traversing boat, it is a `dhuvanāvā` indeed. `Tatrā` means in the expression 'a permanent boat.' Regarding 'the marker or the boundary goes with the formal proclamation': here, although the marker does not go with the formal proclamation, it is said 'it goes with the formal proclamation' because of its inseparability from the boundary. `Tasmā` means: because those coming by boat were permitted by the Blessed One, therefore.

Yatthāti nadipārasīmasammananaṭṭhāne. Rukkhasaṅghāṭamayoti rukkhasamūhena kato. Padarabaddhoti phalakehi baddho. Sañcaraṇayoggoti sañcaraṇakkhamo. Pāḷiyaṃ “assā”ti ṭhāne aṭṭhakathāyaṃ “atthī”ti vuttattā “assā”tipadassa hotīti atthoyeva daṭṭhabbo. Taṃkhaṇaññevāti tasmiṃ nimittakittakkhaṇeyeva. Rukkhaṃ chinditvā katoti sambandho. Ekapadikasetūti ekena padena gamanayoggo ekapadiko, soyeva setūti ekapadikasetu. Akappiyasetuṃ dassento āha “sace panā”tiādi. Tenāti setunā. Sañcarituṃ na sakkā hotīti yojanā.

`Yatthā` means: at the place for establishing the boundary on the other side of the river. `Rukkhasaṅghāṭamayo` means: made from a group of trees. `Padarabaddho` means: bound with planks. `Sañcaraṇayoggo` means: fit for crossing. Because in the Pāli, in place of `assā`, the commentary says `atthi`, the meaning of the word `assā` should be seen as 'there is.' `Taṃkhaṇaññeva` means: at that very moment of announcing the marker. The connection is with 'having cut a tree and made it.' `Ekapadikasetu` means: a single-path bridge, suitable for passage by a single foot; that itself is the bridge. Showing an unsuitable bridge, he says: 'But if,' etc. `Tena` means: by that bridge. The connection is: 'it is not possible to cross'.

Yatthāti yasmiṃ nadipārasīmasammananaṭṭhāne. Abhimukhatittheyevāti sīmāya abhimukhatitthe eva. Dhuvanāvā vā dhuvasetu vā abhimukhatitthato īsakaṃ uddhaṃ ārohantopi adho orohantopi kappatīti dassento āha “sace”tiādi. Īsakanti ekausabha dviusabhādivasena manaṃ appamattaṃ. Uddhaṃ vāti abhimukhatitthato upari vā. Adho vāti tato heṭṭhā vā. Gāvutamattabbhantareti gāvutapamāṇassa ṭhānassa abbhantare.

`Yatthā` means: in whatever place for establishing the boundary on the other side of the river. `Abhimukhatittheyeva` means: right at the landing place opposite the boundary. Showing that a permanent boat or a permanent bridge is allowable even if it goes up a little or goes down a little from the opposite landing place, he says: 'If,' etc. `Īsakaṃ` means: a small measure, such as one or two `usabhas`. `Uddhaṃ vā` means: or above the opposite landing place. `Adho vā` means: or below it. `Gāvutamattabbhantare` means: within a space measuring a `gāvuta`.

Sahanimittakittanavidhinā sammanitabbavidhiṃ dassento āha “imañca panā”tiādi. Dvīsu tīresu ṭhātumasakkuṇeyyattā vuttaṃ “ekasmiṃ tīre [M 0.0292] ṭhatvā”ti. Tatoti nimittato. Attānanti nimittakittanaṃ vinayadharaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ. Parikkhipantenāti pariyāyantena. Tassāti tattakassa paricchedassa. Sammukhaṭṭhāneti adhosote naditīre ṭhitassa nimittassa sammukhaṭṭhāne. Tatoti nimittato. Tassāti tattakassa paricchedassa. Sammukhā naditīre nimittaṃ atthīti sambandho. Saṅghaṭetabbanti sambandhitabbaṃ. Athāti nimittakittanato pacchā. “Sabbanimittānaṃ anto ṭhite bhikkhū hatthapāsagate katvā”ti idaṃ sabbaṃ ekaṃ gāmakhettaṃ byāpetvā sammanitabhāvaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ. Sace sakalaṃ gāmakhettaṃ abyāpetvā ekadese sammanitaṃ hoti, nimittato bahi ṭhite bhikkhūpi hatthapāsagate katvā sammanitabbā. Kammanti sīmasammutikammaṃ. “Ṭhapetvā nadi”ntivacanassa kāraṇaṃ dassento āha “nadī pana baddhasīmasaṅkhyaṃ na gacchatī”ti.

Showing the procedure for establishing the boundary along with the procedure for announcing the markers, he says: 'And this, however,' etc. Because it would be impossible to stand on both banks, it is said: 'having stood on one bank.' `Tato` means: from the marker. `Attānaṃ` is said with reference to the Vinaya expert who is announcing the markers. `Parikkhipantena` means: by one who is going around. `Tassā` means: of that much of a defined area. `Sammukhaṭṭhāne` means: in the place opposite the marker standing on the riverbank downstream. `Tato` means: from the marker. `Tassā` means: of that much of a defined area. The connection is: 'there is a marker on the riverbank opposite.' `Saṅghaṭetabbaṃ` means: it should be connected. `Athā` means: after the announcing of the markers. The entire statement, 'having brought the monks standing inside all the markers to be within hand's reach,' is said with reference to the fact of having established the boundary so as to encompass an entire village-field. If it is established in one part without encompassing the entire village-field, it should be established after having brought even the monks standing outside the markers to be within hand's reach. `Kammaṃ` means: the formal act of establishing a boundary. Showing the reason for the statement 'excluding the river,' he says: 'But the river is not included in the reckoning of a bound boundary'.

Dīpako hotīti ettha dīpoti antaradīpo. So hi yasmā jalamajjhe dippati, yasmā ca dvidhā āpo ettha sandati, tasmā dīpoti vuccati, soyeva khuddakaṭṭhena dīpako. Kakāro hi [V 1.0250] khuddakatthavācako. Tanti dīpakaṃ. Attanāti vinayadharena. Orimante ca pārimante cāti adhosote naditīre ṭhitassa nimittassa sammukhe orimante ca pārimante ca. Paratīre nimittaṃ kittetvāti sambandho. Kissa sammukhaṭṭhāne nimittanti āha “nadiyā orimatīre nimittassa sammukhaṭṭhāne”ti. Tatoti nimittato. Sammukhā nimittaṃ atthīti sambandho. Pārimante ca orimante cāti paratīre uparisote ṭhitassa nimittassa sammukhe pārimante ca orimante ca. Paṭhamakittitanimittenāti orimatīre uparisote paṭhamaṃ kittitena nimittena. Ekā sīmā imassāti ekasīmo, dīpako. “Tīradvayañcā”ti padamapekkhitvā “ekasīma”nti sambandhitabbaṃ. Vaccamanapekkhitvā “ekasīmā”tipi niccaitthiliṅgavasena pāṭho atthi.

Here, in `dīpako hoti`, `dīpo` means an island in between. For because it shines in the middle of the water, and because water flows in two ways here, it is therefore called a `dīpa`. That very thing, in the sense of being small, is a `dīpako`. For the suffix `-ka` indicates the meaning of smallness. `Taṃ` means: that `dīpaka`. `Attanā` means: by the Vinaya expert. `Orimante ca pārimante ca` means: on the near bank and on the far bank opposite the marker standing on the riverbank downstream. The connection is with 'having announced the marker on the far bank.' Opposite what is the marker? He says: 'at the place opposite the marker on the near bank of the river.' `Tato` means: from the marker. The connection is: 'there is a marker opposite.' `Pārimante ca orimante ca` means: on the far bank and on the near bank opposite the marker standing on the far bank upstream. `Paṭhamakittitanimittena` means: with the marker first announced on the near bank upstream. `Ekasīmo` means: this has one boundary; this refers to the `dīpaka`. The word `ekasīma` should be connected in dependence on the word `tīradvayañca`. Without regard to the gender of the referent, there is also the reading `ekasīmā` as a constant feminine.

Uddhaṃ vā adho vāti ettha vāsaddo aniyamavikappattho. Athāti tasmiṃ adhikatare satīti yojanā. Vihārasīmaparicchedanimittassa ujukamevāti sace dīpako adho adhikataro hoti, orimatīre adhosote ṭhitassa vihārasīmaparicchedanimittassa ujukameva[M 0.0293]. Sikharanti siṅgaṃ. Tañhi sikhaṃ matthakaṃ rāti gaṇhātīti sikharanti vuccati. Tatoti dīpakassa pārimantanimittato. Paratīranimittāni kittetvāti sambandho. Ayaṃ dīpakassa vihārasīmaparicchedato adho adhikatare vinicchayo. Uddhaṃ adhikatarepi iminānusārena veditabboti so na dassito. Pabbatasaṇṭhānāti pabbatena samaṃ ṭhānaṃ etissāti pabbatasaṇṭhānā.

'Upwards or downwards'—here the word `vā` has the sense of an indefinite alternative. `Athā`—the construction is: when there is an excess in that direction. Regarding 'directly in line with the boundary marker of the monastery's area': if the island is further below, then for one standing on the near bank by the downstream current, it is directly in line with the boundary marker of the monastery's area. 'Peak' means a summit. For it is called 'peak' (sikhara) because it takes (rāti = gaṇhāti) the crest (sikhaṃ), the top (matthakaṃ). 'From that' means from the boundary marker on the far bank of the island. The connection is with 'having declared the markers of the far bank.' This is the determination when the island is further below than the monastery's boundary marker. When it is further above, it should be understood in accordance with this method, so that is not shown. 'Having the shape of a mountain' means: that for which the form is the same as a mountain's.

Uddhampi adhopīti pisaddo samuccayattho. Ubhopi sikharānīti uddhaṃ sikharaṃ, adho sikharanti ubhopi sikharāni. Mudiṅgasaṇṭhānāti mūle ca agge ca tanukassa majjhe thūlassa mudiṅgassa saṇṭhānā.

'Above and also below'—the word 'pi' has a conjunctive sense. 'Both peaks' means the upper peak and the lower peak; both are peaks. 'Having the shape of a mudiṅga drum' means having the shape of a mudiṅga drum that is slender at the base and the tip and thick in the middle.

Sabbapaṭhamena nayenāti uddhaṃ adhikanayassa, adho adhikanayassa, uddhaṃadhoadhikanayassa cāti sabbesaṃ nayānaṃ paṭhamena vihārasīmadīpakānaṃ samena nayena. Paṇavasaṇṭhānāti mūle ca agge ca thūlassa majjhetanukassa paṇavassa saṇṭhānā.

'By the very first method' means by the first of all the methods—that of the method when the island is further above, the method when it is further below, and the method when it is further above and below—that is, by the method where the monastery boundary and the island are equal. 'Having the shape of a paṇava drum' means having the shape of a paṇava drum that is thick at the base and the tip and slender in the middle.

72. Uposathāgārādikathā

72. The Discourse on the Uposatha Hall and Other Matters

141. Anupariveṇiyanti ettha anusaddassa vicchatthaṃ, pariveṇasaddassa ca liṅgavipallāsabhāvaṃ dassetuṃ vuttaṃ “tasmiṃ tasmiṃ pariveṇe”ti. Pariveṇasaddo hi napuṃsakaliṅgo, idha pana liṅgavipallāsaṃ katvā itthiliṅgavasena vuttaṃ. “Saṅketaṃ akatvā”ti iminā asaṅketenāti [V 1.0251] padassa kiriyāvisesanattaṃ dīpeti. “Kammavācāyā”ti iminā samūhanitvāti padassa karaṇaṃ dasseti.

141. Regarding 'anupariveṇiyaṃ': to show the distributive sense of the word 'anu' and the change of gender of the word 'pariveṇa,' it is said, 'in each and every monastic cell (pariveṇe).' The word 'pariveṇa' is indeed neuter, but here, a change of gender having been made, it is stated in the feminine. By 'without having made an agreement,' it indicates that the word 'asaṅketena' is an adverbial modifier. By 'by a formal act of the Saṅgha,' it shows the instrument for the word 'samūhanitvā' (having invalidated).

142. Yatoti ettha topaccayassa kāraṇatthe pavattabhāvaṃ dassento āha “yasmā”ti. “Hatthapāse”ti iminā hatthapāsato bahi nisinne akatovassa uposatho hotīti dasseti. Assāti bhikkhuno. Vatthuvasenāti aṭṭhuppattivasena. Uposathassa pamukhassa abbhokāse vā māḷakādīsu vāti sambandho. Nimittupagā vā animittupagā vāti heṭṭhā aṭṭhasu nimittesu vuttā nimittupagā vā animittupagā vā pabbatādayo vā aññe vā kittetabbā.

142. Regarding 'yato': showing that the suffix '-to' occurs in the sense of reason, he says 'yasmā' (because). By 'within arm's reach,' it shows that for one sitting outside arm's reach, the Uposatha is not performed for him. 'Assa' means 'of a bhikkhu.' 'According to the story' means according to the origin of the matter. The connection is: in front of the Uposatha, in the open air, or on a terrace, etc. 'Connected with a boundary marker or not connected with a boundary marker'—the markers connected with a boundary marker mentioned below among the eight markers, or those not connected with a boundary marker, or mountains and so on, or others, should be declared.

Paṭhamataraṃ [M 0.0294] na āgacchati, dukkaṭanti uposathe ghosiyamāne paṭhamataraṃ na āgacchati, dukkaṭaṃ. Vihārassa majjhe hotīti yojanā. Etthāti porāṇake āvāse. Tatthāti porāṇake āvāse. Asambādhoti saṅghassa nisajjaṭṭhānapahonako. Tatthāti pacchā uṭṭhite āvāse.

'He does not come first; it is a dukkaṭa': when the Uposatha is being announced, if he does not come first, it is a dukkaṭa offense. 'It is in the middle of the monastery'—this is the connection. 'Here' means in the old residence. 'There' means in the old residence. 'Uncrowded' means sufficient as a sitting place for the Saṅgha. 'There' means in a residence established later.

Sabbesaṃ nisajjaṭṭhānanti yojanā. Tatthāti therassa vihāre. Soti therassa vihāro. Etthāti tumhākaṃ vihāre. Sabbesaṃ okāso natthīti sambandho. Tatthāti taṃ asukaṃ nāma āvāsaṃ. “Vaṭṭatī”ti vattabbanti yojanā. Tassāti therassa.

'A sitting place for all'—this is the connection. 'There' means in the elder's monastery. 'That' is the elder's monastery. 'Here' means in your monastery. 'There is no space for all'—this is the connection. 'There' means to that residence named so-and-so. 'It is allowable' means they say—this is the connection. 'Of that one' means of the elder.

74. Avippavāsasīmānujānanakathā

74. The Discourse on the Allowance of the Boundary of Non-separation

143. Andhakavindaṃ nāmāti tassa gāmassa nāmaṃ. Tanti andhakavindaṃ. Theroti mahākassapatthero. Tatoti andhakavindato. Iminā “andhakavindā”ti ettha nissakkatthe nissakkavacananti dasseti. Uposathanti tadatthe upayogavacanaṃ. Uposathatthāyāti hi attho. Andhakavindā rājagahaṃ āgamanassa kāraṇaṃ dassento āha “rājagahaṃ hī”tiādi. Tattha hīti yasmā. Andhakavindā vihāraṃ anto katvā “aṭṭhārasa mahāvihārā”ti vuttaṃ. Nesanti aṭṭhārasannaṃ mahāvihārānaṃ. Saṅghassa sāmaggidānatthanti ettha saṅghassa sāmaggidānaṃ attano uposathakiccaṃ siddhaṃ. Tasmā pāḷiyaṃ “uposathaṃ āgacchanto”ti vuttaṃ. “Sippiniyaṃ nāmā”ti iminā nadiṃ tarantoti ettha nadiyā nāmaṃ dasseti. Manaṃ vūḷhoti ettha mananti nipāto īsakatthoti dassento āha “īsaka”nti. “Appamatta”nti iminā “īsaka”ntipadassa atthaṃ dasseti. “Vūḷhabhāvo”ti iminā bhāvapaccayena vinā bhāvattho [M 0.0295] ñātabboti dasseti. Caṇḍenāti kharena. Tatthāti nadiyaṃ. Amanasikarontoti “caṇḍasota”nti ābhogaṃ [V 1.0252] akaronto. Na pana vūḷhoti na pana mahāvūḷho. Udakabbhāhatānīti udakena abhiāhatāni. Assāti therassa. Allānīti tintāni.

143. 'Andhakavinda by name' means the name of that village. 'That' means Andhakavinda. 'The elder' means the Elder Mahākassapa. 'From there' means from Andhakavinda. By this, it shows that here in 'andhakavindā,' it is an ablative expression in the ablative sense. 'Uposatha' is a term of application for that purpose. For the meaning is indeed 'for the sake of the Uposatha.' Showing the reason for coming to Rājagaha from Andhakavinda, he says, 'For Rājagaha…,' etc. There 'hi' means 'because.' Including the monastery at Andhakavinda, it is said, 'eighteen great monasteries.' 'Of them' means of the eighteen great monasteries. 'For the purpose of giving unity to the Saṅgha'—here, giving unity to the Saṅgha is the accomplishment of one's own Uposatha duty. Therefore in the Pāli it is said, 'coming for the Uposatha.' By 'Sippinī by name,' it shows the name of the river in the phrase 'crossing the river.' 'Slightly swollen'—here, showing that 'manaṃ' is a particle in the sense of 'a little,' he says 'īsakaṃ' (a little). By 'a small amount,' it shows the meaning of the word 'īsakaṃ.' By 'the state of being swollen,' it shows that the abstract sense should be understood without an abstract suffix. 'Fierce' means harsh. 'There' means in the river. 'Not attending' means not paying attention to the 'fierce current.' 'But not swollen' means not greatly swollen. 'Struck by water' means struck all over by water. 'His' means of the elder. 'Wet' means soaked.

144. Purimakammavācāti “sammatā sā sīmā saṅghena ticīvarena avippavāsā”ti pure vuttā kammavācā. Ayamevāti “ṭhapetvā gāmañca gāmūpacārañcā”tipadaṃ pakkhipitvā anupaññattā ayameva kammavācā. Ayanti pacchimakammavācā. Hi yasmā bhikkhunisaṅgho antogāme vasati, tasmā purimāyeva vaṭṭatīti yojanā. Yadi evanti yadi bhikkhunisaṅghassa ayaṃ pacchimakammavācā vaṭṭanaṃ siyā bhaveyya, evaṃ satīti yojanā. Soti bhikkhunisaṅgho. Etāya kammavācāyāti pacchimakammavācāya. Na labheyyāti antogāme vasanattā ticīvaraparihāraṃ na labheyya. Kiṃ na labhatiyevāti āha “atthi cassa parihāro”ti. Assāti bhikkhunisaṅghassa. Dvepi sīmāyoti samānasaṃvāsakasīmā ca avippavāsasīmā cāti dvepi sīmāyo. Tatthāti bhikkhubhikkhunīsu. Tassāti bhikkhūnaṃ sīmāya. Eseva nayoti bhikkhunīnaṃ sīmaṃ ajjhottharitvāpi antopavisitvāpi bhikkhūnaṃ sīmāya sammane eseva nayo. Eteti bhikkhubhikkhuniyo. Sāmaññattā hi pulliṅgena vuttaṃ. Ettha cāti “ṭhapetvā gāmañca gāmūpacārañcā”tipade ca. Saṅgaho veditabbo, kasmā? Gāmena nigamanagarānaṃ ekalakkhaṇattā.

144. 'The former formal act' is the formal act stated previously: 'That boundary has been agreed upon by the Saṅgha for non-separation from the three robes.' 'This very one'—this very formal act is the one subsequently allowed with the insertion of the phrase 'excluding a village and a village precinct.' 'This' is the latter formal act. The connection is: since the Saṅgha of bhikkhunīs dwells inside a village, therefore only the former one is allowable. 'If so'—the connection is: if this latter formal act were to be allowable for the Saṅgha of bhikkhunīs, this being so... 'That' is the Saṅgha of bhikkhunīs. 'By this formal act' means by the latter formal act. 'She would not obtain'—because of dwelling inside a village, she would not obtain the exemption concerning the three robes. Why would she not obtain it? He says: 'But there is an exemption for her.' 'For her' means for the Saṅgha of bhikkhunīs. 'Both boundaries' means the two boundaries: the boundary for common residence and the boundary for non-separation. 'There' means among the bhikkhus and bhikkhunīs. 'Of that' means of the bhikkhus' boundary. 'This is the same method'—even if the bhikkhunīs' boundary is established overlapping or entering within it, this is the same method for agreeing upon the bhikkhus' boundary. 'These' means the bhikkhus and bhikkhunīs. For because of commonality, it is stated in the masculine gender. 'And here' means in the phrase 'excluding a village and a village precinct.' An inclusion should be understood. Why? Because a village, a market town, and a city have a single characteristic.

Parikkhepokāsoti parikkhepārahokāso. Tesūti gāmagāmūpacāresu. Parihāranti cīvaravippavāsaāpattiapanayanaṃ. “Itī”tiādi nigamanaṃ. Etthāti samānasaṃvāsakaavippavāsasīmāsu. Attano dhammatāyāti attano sabhāvena. Yatthāti yasmiṃ ṭhāne. Hīti saccaṃ, yasmā vā. Tassāti avippavāsasīmāya. Visunti samānasaṃvāsakasīmato pāṭekkaṃ. Tatthāti dvīsu sīmāsu. Avippavāsāyāti avippavāsasīmāya. Tanti gāmaṃ. Sāti avippavāsasīmā. Sammatāya sīmāyāti [M 0.0296] avippavāsasīmāya sammatāya satiyāti sambandho. Sammatato pacchāti vā yojanā. Nivisatīti nivāsatthāya visati pavisati. Sopīti gāmopi. Sīmasaṅkhyaṃyevāti avippāsasīmavohārameva. Adhiṭṭhitatecīvarikā bhikkhū parihāraṃ labhantīti adhippāyo. Yathā pacchā niviṭṭho gāmo sīmasaṅkhyaṃyeva gacchati, evanti yojanā. “Pavisissāmā”ti gehāni katāni, “pavisissāmā”ti ālayopi atthīti yojanā. Ālayopīti apekkhopi. Apaviṭṭhāti gehāni apaviṭṭhā. Gehameva chaḍḍetvāti gehaṃ chaḍḍetvā eva. Iminā gehe chaḍḍite sabbaṃ chaḍḍitamevāti dasseti. Paviṭṭhaṃ vā agataṃ vā ekampi kulaṃ atthi [V 1.0253] saceti yojanā. Ettha ca “ekampi kulaṃ paviṭṭhaṃ vā”ti idaṃ navagāmaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ. “Ekampi kulaṃ agataṃ vā”ti idaṃ porāṇakagāmaṃ sandhāyāti daṭṭhabbaṃ.

'An area for enclosure' means an area suitable for enclosure. 'In those' means in a village and a village precinct. 'Exemption' means the removal of the offense of separation from the robes. 'Thus,' etc., is the conclusion. 'Here' means in the boundaries for common residence and for non-separation. 'By its own nature' means by its own intrinsic nature. 'Where' means in which place. 'Hi' means indeed, or because. 'Of that' means of the boundary of non-separation. 'Separately' means apart from the boundary of common residence. 'There' means in the two boundaries. 'For non-separation' means for the boundary of non-separation. 'That' means the village. 'That' is the boundary of non-separation. 'When the boundary has been agreed upon'—the connection is: when the boundary of non-separation has been agreed upon. Or the connection is: 'after it has been agreed upon.' 'Settles' means enters for the purpose of dwelling. 'It too' means the village too. 'The reckoning of a boundary' means the designation of a boundary of non-separation. The intention is that bhikkhus with the three robes determined obtain the exemption. The connection is: just as a village settled later comes to be reckoned as a boundary, so... 'We will enter'—houses have been made; 'we will enter'—the connection is: there is also an attachment. 'Attachment too' means expectation too. 'Not entered' means the houses have not been entered. 'Having abandoned only the house' means having abandoned the house itself. By this it shows that when the house is abandoned, everything is abandoned. The connection is: if there is even one family that has entered or has not gone away. And here, 'even one family has entered' is said in reference to a new village. It should be seen that 'or even one family has not gone away' is said in reference to an old village.

Tatrāti “vattaṃ jānitabba”ntivacane. Avippavāsasīmāyanti mahāsīmāya. Sā eva hi yasmā avippavāsakammavācāya bahulapayojanā hoti, tasmā avippavāsasīmāti vuccati. Itarāyāti avippavāsasīmāya. Tatthāti tāsu dvīsu sīmāsu. Nirāsaṅkaṭṭhānesu ṭhatvāti cetiyaṅgaṇādīnaṃ khaṇḍasīmāya anokāsattā vuttaṃ. Khaṇḍasīmañhi sammanantā cetiyaṅgaṇādiṭṭhānaṃ pahāya aññasmiṃ vivittokāse vihārapaccantaṃ khaṇḍitvā sammananti. Samūhanitunti avippavāsasīmaṃ samūhanituṃ. Paṭibandhituṃ na sakkhissantevāti avippavāsaṃyeva jānitvā khaṇḍasīmāya aññātattā paṭibandhituṃ na sakkhissanteva. Sīmasambhedanti khaṇḍasīmaavippavāsasīmānaṃ sambhedaṃ. Sāsanantaradhānena vāti satthu āṇāya antaradhānena vā. Sādhukaṃ panāti nikkaṅkhaṃ pana.

'Here' means in the statement 'the boundary should be known.' 'The boundary for non-separation' means the great boundary. Since that itself is frequently useful for the formal act concerning non-separation, it is therefore called 'the boundary for non-separation.' By 'the other' is meant the boundary for non-separation. 'There' means in those two boundaries. 'Having stood in places free from danger' is said because the grounds of cetiyas, etc., provide no space for a partial boundary. For when designating a partial boundary, having abandoned the site of a cetiya ground, etc., they designate it in another secluded place, having marked off a section at the edge of the monastery. 'To abolish' means to abolish the boundary for non-separation. 'They will not be able to obstruct' means that since they know only the non-separation boundary and are unaware of the partial boundary, they will indeed be unable to obstruct. 'The intermingling of boundaries' means the intermingling of the partial boundary and the boundary for non-separation. 'Or by the disappearance of the Dispensation' means or by the disappearance of the Teacher's command. 'But properly' means without doubt.

76. Gāmasīmādikathā

76. The Discussion on Village Boundaries and So On

147. Uposathakammassa visuṃ gahitattā sesakammavasena samānasaṃvāsakatā gahetabbā gobalibaddanayena vā pārisesanayena vā. Tanti samānasaṃvāsaekūposathabhāvaṃ. “Aparicchinnāyā”ti iminā [M 0.0297] aṭṭhapitāyāti ettha ṭhapadhātuyā adhippāyatthaṃ dasseti. Gāmaṃ vā nigamaṃ vāti ettha nagaraṃ kena saṅgahitanti āha “gāmaggahaṇena cetthā”tiādi. Tattha etthāti “gāmaṃ vā nigamaṃ vā”ti pāṭhe, gāmaggahaṇenāti sambandho. Atha vā etthāti gāmanigamanagaresu, nagarampīti sambandho. Gāmādīnaṃ paricchedaṃ vitthārena dassento āha “tatthā”tiādi. Tattha tatthāti gāmanigamanagaresu. Gāmabhojakāti gāmaṃ bhuñjantīti gāmabhojakā. Balinti karaṃ. So hi taṃ nissāya gāmabhojakā balanti jīvanti anenāti balīti vuccati. Yampi ekaṃ padesaṃ paricchinditvā detīti yojanā. Gāmakhetteti rañño āṇā khipiyati etthāti khettaṃ, gāmoyeva khettaṃ gāmakhettaṃ, tasmiṃ. Ayampīti ayaṃ padesopi. Sopīti padesopi. Visuṃgāmo nāmāti yojanā. Sopi visuṃgāmo gāmasīmā hotiyevāti yojanā. Visuṃ paricchinditvā dinno gāmo visuṃgāmo. Tasmāti yasmā visuṃ gāmo hoti, tasmā. Sā cāti visuṃgāmasīmā ca. Itarāti visuṃgāmasīmato aññā pakatigāmanagaranigamasīmā cāti yojanā.

147. Since the Uposatha act is taken separately, communion should be understood by way of the remaining acts, either by the maxim of the ox and the bullock or by the maxim of elimination. 'That' means the state of being in communion and having a single Uposatha. By 'undemarcated,' he shows the intended meaning of the root ṭhā in the word 'unestablished.' Concerning 'a village or a market town,' he asks by what a city is included and says: 'Here, by the inclusion of "village,"' and so on. Therein, 'here' is in the text 'a village or a market town'; the connection is with 'by the inclusion of "village."' Or else, 'here' refers to villages, market towns, and cities; the connection is with 'the city also.' Explaining the delimitation of villages, etc., in detail, he says: 'Therein,' and so on. Therein, 'therein' refers to villages, market towns, and cities. 'Village-enjoyers' are those who enjoy a village. 'Tribute' means tax. For, relying on that, the village-enjoyers are strong or live; that by which they live is called 'tribute.' The construction is also: 'in that one demarcates and gives a region.' 'In the village-field': a 'field' is where the king's command is cast; the village itself is the field, 'village-field'; in that. 'This also' means this region also. 'That also' means that region also. The construction is: 'it is called a separate village.' The construction is: 'That separate village, too, is indeed a village boundary.' A 'separate village' is a village that has been separately demarcated and given. 'Therefore' means: because it is a separate village, therefore. 'And that' means: and that separate village boundary. The construction is: 'The other' means the other, apart from the separate village boundary, that is, the ordinary village, city, and market town boundaries.

Evanti [V 1.0254] “asammatāya bhikkhave”tiādinā pāṭhena. Tanti sīmaparicchedaṃ. Aparicchinneti rājūhi aparicchinne. “Aṭavipadese”ti iminā natthi gāmo etthāti agāmakoti vacanatthassa sarūpaṃ dasseti. Vijjhāṭavisadiseti vigataṃ aggino jhāyanametthāti vijjhā, corādayo manusse ābhuso ṭavanti pīḷayanti etthāti āṭavi. Vijjhā ca sā āṭavi ceti vijjhāṭavi, tāya sadise vijjhāṭavisadise. Ettha purimanaye gāmādīhi āsanno vā hotu, anāsanno vā tehi aparicchinno aṭavipadeso gahetabbo. Pacchimanaye dūro manussānaṃ anāgamanapatho āṭavipadeso gahetabboti ayametesaṃ viseso. Assāti bhikkhuno. Samantāti samantato. Ayaṃ sīmāti ayaṃ sattabbhantarasīmā. Tatthāti sattasu abbhantaresu. Samantā ṭhitassa vā nisinnassa vā abbhantare antokoṭṭhāse jātaṃ abbhantaraṃ aṭṭhavīsahatthapamāṇaṃ.

'Thus' means by the text beginning, 'On an unconsecrated boundary, bhikkhus….' 'That' means the demarcation of the boundary. 'Undemarcated' means undemarcated by kings. By 'in a forest region,' he shows the form of the verbal meaning of 'villageless,' that is, 'there is no village here.' 'Like the Vijjhāṭavi wilderness': 'vijjhā' is a place where the burning of fire is gone; 'āṭavi' is where robbers and others repeatedly harass people. 'Vijjhā' and 'āṭavi' together make 'vijjhāṭavi'; 'like that' means like the Vijjhāṭavi wilderness. Here, according to the first method, a forest region undemarcated by them—whether it is near to or not near to villages, etc.—should be taken. According to the later method, a remote forest region, a path not frequented by people, should be taken. This is the difference between them. 'His' means of the bhikkhu. 'Around' means all around. 'This boundary' means this boundary of seven abbhantaras. 'Therein' means in the seven abbhantaras. An 'abbhantara' is the interior, the inner part, that arises for one standing or sitting all around, measuring twenty-eight cubits.

Yā [M 0.0298] kāci nadī asīmāva hotīti sambandho. Nadīsīmalakkhaṇapattāti nadīsīmalakkhaṇaṃ pattā. Iminā sīmalakkhaṇaṃ apattā nadī bandhiyamānā sīmāva hotīti dasseti. Sāvadhāraṇena “attano sabhāvenevā”ti iminā bhikkhūnaṃ bandhanabhāvenāti atthaṃ nivatteti. Etthāti nadiyaṃ. Etthāti jātassarasamuddesu. Yena kenacīti antamaso tiracchānagatenapi yena kenaci. Khaṇitvā akato sayaṃjātoti sambandho. Idaṃ hetuantogadhavisesanaṃ. Khaṇitvā akatattāti hi attho. Sayaṃjātoti sayameva jātoti evakāro yojetabbo. Tena vuttaṃ “yena kenaci khaṇitvā akato”ti. Sobbhoti saṃ ubhoti padavibhāgo kātabbo. Tattha saṃsaddo samantatthavācako, ubhasaddo pūraṇatthavācako. Tasmā samantato āgatena udakena ubhati pūrati etthāti sobbhoti vacanattho kātabbo. Tena vuttaṃ “samantato āgatena udakena pūrito tiṭṭhatī”ti.

The connection is: 'Whatever river is without a boundary.' 'Having attained the characteristic of a river boundary' means it has attained the characteristic of a river boundary. By this he shows that a river that has not attained the boundary characteristic, when it is bounded, is indeed a boundary. With the emphatic particle in 'by its own very nature,' he excludes the meaning 'by the act of binding on the part of the bhikkhus.' 'Here' means in a river. 'Here' means in natural lakes and oceans. 'By anyone whomsoever' means by anyone at all, even by an animal. The connection is: 'not made by digging, self-arisen.' This is a qualification included within the reason, for the meaning is 'because it was not made by digging.' 'Self-arisen': the emphatic particle 'eva' should be construed as 'arisen by itself.' Therefore it is said: 'not made by digging by anyone whomsoever.' 'Sobbha': the word should be divided as 'saṃ' and 'ubha.' Therein, the word 'saṃ' has the meaning 'all around,' and the word 'ubha' has the meaning 'filling.' Therefore, the verbal meaning of 'sobbha' should be understood as: 'a place that fills up with water coming from all around.' Therefore it is said: 'it remains filled with water that has come from all around.'

Tatthāti nadīsamuddajātassaresu, ādhāre bhummaṃ. Yaṃsaddo ṭhānavisayoti āha “yaṃ ṭhāna”nti. Majjhimassāti thāmamajjhimassa. Vakkhati hi “thāmamajjhimenā”ti. “Samantato”ti iminā samantāti ettha nissakkatthe nissakkavacananti dasseti. “Udakukkhepenā”ti iminā udakukkhepāti ettha karaṇatthe nissakkavacananti dasseti. Udakaṃ ukkhipitvā khipiyati etthāti udakukkhepo. “Paricchinna”nti iminā pāṭhasesaṃ dasseti. Akkhadhuttāti ettha akkhoti pāsako. So hi akati kuṭilaṃ gacchati anenāti akkhoti vuccati, dhavanti mariyādamatikkamma kīḷādipasutaṃ gacchantīti dhuttā, akkhesu dhuttā akkhadhuttā[V 1.0255]. Dāruguḷanti sāradārumayaṃ guḷaṃ. “Vālukaṃ vā”ti iminā “udakukkhepā”ti ettha upalakkhaṇaṃ dasseti. Yatthāti yasmiṃ padese. Ayanti padeso. Tassāti udakukkhepassa.

'Therein' refers to rivers, oceans, and natural lakes; it is the locative case in the sense of location. The word 'which' pertains to a place, thus he says 'which place.' 'Of a man of medium build' means of medium strength. For it will be said: 'by a man of medium strength.' By 'all around,' he shows that 'around' here is a word used in the locative sense without the case inflection. By 'by a throw of water,' he shows that 'a throw of water' here is a word used in the instrumental sense without the case inflection. A 'throw of water' is where water, having been scooped up, is thrown. By 'demarcated,' he indicates the rest of the text. 'Gamblers': here, 'akkha' means a die. It is called 'akkha' because one moves crookedly with it. 'Rogues' (dhuttā) are so called because they run (dhavanti), transgressing the limit, engrossed in play and so on. Rogues at dice are 'gamblers.' 'A wooden ball' means a ball made of heartwood. By 'or sand,' he shows that 'a throw of water' here is an illustrative example. 'Where' means in which region. 'This' means this region. 'Of that' means of the throw of water.

Etthāti nadīsamuddajātassaresu. Mukhadvāranti samuddādīnaṃ mukhasaṅkhātaṃ dvāraṃ. Sabbatthāti sabbāya nadiyaṃ. Theravādaṃ dassento āha “yaṃ panā”tiādi. “Yojanaṃ…pe… vaṭṭatī”ti yaṃ pana vacanaṃ mahāsumattherena vuttanti [M 0.0299] yojanā. Tatrāpīti yojananadiyampi. Paṭikkhittākāraṃ vitthārento āha “bhagavatā hī”tiādi. Nadiyā pamāṇanti nadiyā gambhīrapamāṇameva, na āyāmavitthārapamāṇanti attho. “Na yojanaṃ vā addhayojanaṃ vā”ti vacanampi idameva sandhāya vuttanti daṭṭhabbaṃ. Kiñcāpi āyāmavitthārapamāṇaṃ na vuttaṃ, pabhavato pana yāva mukhadvārā āyāmavitthāravasena kammaṃ kātuṃ pahonakanadīyeva gahetabbāti daṭṭhabbā. Yā nadīti sambandho. Imassa suttassāti “timaṇḍala”ntiādikassa imassa suttassa. Pabhavatoti samudāgamato. Etthāti nadiyaṃ. Sabbehi bhikkhūhi ṭhapetabboti sambandho. Tatoti ekaudakukkhepato.

'Here' means in rivers, oceans, and natural lakes. 'Mouth-entrance' means the entrance, designated as the mouth, of an ocean and so on. 'Everywhere' means in the entire river. Showing the Theravāda position, he says: 'But whatever,' and so on. The construction is: the statement 'A yojana ... is allowable,' was spoken by the Great Elder Suma. 'There too' means even in a river a yojana wide. Elaborating on the reason for the rejection, he says: 'For by the Blessed One,' and so on. 'The measure of a river' means only the measure of the river's depth, not the measure of its length and breadth; this is the meaning. It should be seen that the statement 'not a yojana or half a yojana' was also said in reference to this. Although the measure of length and breadth was not stated, it should be seen that only a river that is sufficient for performing the act in terms of length and breadth from its source up to its mouth-entrance should be taken. The connection is: 'Whatever river….' 'Of this rule' means of this rule beginning 'three circles….' 'From its source' means from its origin. 'Here' means in the river. The connection is: 'should be established by all the bhikkhus.' 'From that' means from a single throw of water.

Kittakā paripuṇṇā hotīti āha “samatitthikā”ti. Titthena samaṃ paripūratīti samatitthikā. Udakasāṭikaṃ nivāsetvāpīti pisaddo “anivāsetvāpī”ti dasseti. Udakasāṭikaṃ anivāsentopi vatthena avinābhāvato aññaṃ nivāsetvāti attho gahetabbo. Nāvāya ṭhatvā kariyamāne kiṃ gacchantiyāpi nāvāya kātuṃ vaṭṭatīti āha “gacchantiyā panā”tiādi. “Kasmā”tiādinā kāraṇaṃ dasseti. Hīti yasmā. Tanti udakukkhepamattaṃ. Evaṃ sati…pe… anusāvanā hoti, tasmā gacchantiyā nāvāya kātuṃ na vaṭṭatīti yojanā. “Tasmā”tiādinā laddhaguṇaṃ dasseti. Na kevalaṃ nāvāyamevāti dassento āha “antonadiya”ntiādi.

'To what extent is it full?' He says: 'Level with the ford.' 'Level with the ford' means it is full, level with the ford. 'Even having put on a bathing-cloth': the particle 'pi' (even) indicates 'even without putting it on.' Even when not putting on a bathing-cloth, since one is not without a cloth, the meaning should be taken as 'having put on another one.' When it is being done standing on a boat, is it allowable to do it even on a moving boat? He says: 'But on a moving one,' and so on. With 'Why?' and so on, he shows the reason. 'Hi' means because. 'That' means just a throw of water. The construction is: 'This being so ... there is an announcement; therefore it is not allowable to do it on a moving boat.' With 'Therefore,' and so on, he shows the benefit obtained. Showing that it is not only on a boat, he says: 'within the river,' and so on.

Rukkhassāti antonadiyaṃ jātassa rukkhassa. Sākhā vā patiṭṭhitāti sambandho. Sīmaṃ vā sodhetvāti vihārasīmagāmasīmāsu ṭhitānaṃ hatthapāsānayanabahikaraṇavasena sīmaṃ vā sodhetvā. Jātarukkhassa paviṭṭhasākhāya vā pārohe vāti sambandho. Assāti bahinaditīre jātarukkhassa. Tatthāti khāṇuke.

'Of a tree' means of a tree that has grown within the river. The connection is: 'or established on a branch.' 'Or having purified the boundary' means having purified the boundary by excluding those standing within the monastery or village boundaries from hand's reach. The connection is: 'or on a branch of a grown tree that has entered the water, or on a shoot.' 'Its' means of a tree that has grown on the outer bank of the river. 'Thereon' means on the stump.

Tassāti pāsāṇadīpakassa. Pubbe vuttappakāreti pubbe nadīnimittaṭṭhāne “anvaddhamāsa”ntiādinā [V 1.0256] (mahāva. aṭṭha. 138) vuttappakāre. Soti pāsāṇadīpako. Puna soti pāsāṇadīpakoyeva. Hīti saccaṃ, yasmā vā.

`Tassa` means of the stone beacon. `Pubbe vuttappakāre` means in the manner stated previously in the section on the river-sign with the words `anvaddhamāsaṃ` (every half-month), etc. (Mahāva. Aṭṭha. 138). `So` means the stone beacon. `Puna so` means the stone beacon itself. `Hi` means truly, or because.

Āvaraṇanti [M 0.0300] pāḷiṃ. Tanti āvaraṇaṃ. Āvaraṇena vā koṭṭhakabandhena vā hetubhūtena, pacchijjatīti sambandho. Koci āvaraṇappadeso ajjhotthariyatīti sambandho. Tatthāti āvaraṇappadese. Hīti saccaṃ, yasmā vā. “Heṭṭhāpāḷi baddhā”ti idaṃ nadiṃ vināsetvā taḷākakaraṇākāradassanaṃ. Etthāti nadiyaṃ, taḷāke vā. Chaḍḍitamodakanti taḷākarakkhanatthaṃ ekena vārimaggena chaḍḍitaṃ udakaṃ. Deve avassanteti dubbuṭṭhikālattā vassantakālepi deve avassante. Sāti nadito nīhaṭamātikā. Kālantarenāti aññena kālena. Uppatitvāti gāmanigamānaṃ upari patitvā. Pavattatīti pubbe vuttapakāre vassakāle cattāro māse abbhocchinnā sandati. Vihārasīmanti vihārasambandhaṃ baddhasīmaṃ.

`Āvaraṇaṃ` means an embankment. `Taṃ` means the embankment. The connection is: 'it is cut off' because of the embankment or the enclosing wall, which is the cause. The connection is: 'some part of the embankment is submerged.' `Tattha` means in the area of the embankment. `Hi` means truly, or because. `Heṭṭhāpāḷi baddhā` (the lower embankment is built): this shows the appearance of having destroyed the river and made a tank. `Ettha` means in the river or in the tank. `Chaḍḍita-udakaṃ`: water discarded through one water-channel for the protection of the tank. `Deve avassante` means when the devas do not rain, even during the rainy season, because it is a time of drought. `Sā` means the channel led from the river. `Kālantarena` means at another time. `Uppatitvā` means having overflowed onto villages and towns. `Pavattati` means it flows uninterruptedly for the four months of the rainy season in the manner stated previously. `Vihārasīmaṃ` means the fixed boundary connected to the monastery.

Samuddepīti pisaddo nadimapekkhati. Tatthāti padese. Otaritvāti heṭṭhā taritvā. “Osaritvā”tipi pāṭho, ayamevattho. Saṇṭhahantīti udakena samaṃ tiṭṭhanti. Soti padeso. Udakantatoti udakakoṭito. Tatthāti samudde. Bādhatīti pīḷayati. Tesūti nāvāaṭṭakesu. Tanti piṭṭhipāsāṇaṃ. Ūmiyoti vīciyo. Tā hi paraṃparāvasena uggantvā saviññāṇakāviññāṇake miyanti hiṃsanti, anto pakkhipantīti vā ūmiyoti vuccanti. Tatthāti piṭṭhipāsāṇe. Hīti saccaṃ, yasmā vā. Udakeneva piṭṭhipāsāṇo ottharīyatīti yojanā. Soti dīpakapabbato. “Dūre”ti vatvā tassa pamāṇaṃ dassento āha “macchavadhānaṃ anāgamanapathe”ti. Macchavadhānanti kevaṭṭānaṃ. Te hi yasmā macche hananti, tasmā macchavadhāti vuccanti. “Macchabandhāna”ntipi pāṭho. Macche bandhantīti macchabandhāti vacanattho kātabbo. Anāgamanapatheti yattha gantvā tadaheva paccāgantvā na āgamanapathike dese. Natthi āgamanapatho etthāti anāgamanapatho, deso. Tasmiṃ “agamanapathe”tipi pāṭho, so ayutto. Kasmā? Agamanapathassa nādhippetattā. Gantvā hi puna anāgamanapathoyevādhippeto. Tesanti macchavadhānaṃ. Gamanapariyantassāti gamanakoṭiyā[M 0.0301]. Oratoti orabhāge ṭhito dīpako vā pabbato vāti yojetabbo. Tatthāti orabhāge ṭhitesu dīpakapabbatesu. Ottharitvāti pakatiudakena ottharitvā. Tatthāti ottharitvā ṭhite samudde.

`Samudde pi`: the particle `pi` has reference to the river. `Tattha` means in the place. `Otaritvā` means having crossed below. `Osaritvā` (having entered) is also a reading; the meaning is the same. `Saṇṭhahanti` means they stand level with the water. `So` means the place. `Udakantato` means from the edge of the water. `Tattha` means in the ocean. `Bādhati` means it afflicts. `Tesu` means in the boat-shelters. `Taṃ` means the ridge-rock. `Ūmiyo` means waves. For they, rising up in succession, kill or harm sentient and insentient beings, or they are called `ūmiyo` because they enclose them within. `Tattha` means on the ridge-rock. `Hi` means truly, or because. The construction is: the ridge-rock is submerged by the water itself. `So` means the island-mountain. Having said `dūre` (far), to show its measure he says: `macchavadhānaṃ anāgamanapathe` (on the path of no return for fishermen). `Macchavadhānaṃ` means of fishermen. Because they kill fish, they are called `macchavadhā` (fish-killers). `Macchabandhānaṃ` (of fish-binders) is also a reading; the meaning 'they bind fish, thus they are `macchabandhā`' should be made. `Anāgamanapathe` means in a region where, having gone, one does not return on the same day. `Anāgamanapatho` means a place where there is no path of return. `Agamanapathe` (on the path of going) is also a reading on this, but it is incorrect. Why? Because a path of going is not intended, for what is intended is a path of no return after having gone. `Tesaṃ` means of the fishermen. `Gamanapariyantassa` means of the limit of their journey. The construction should be: `orato` means the island or mountain standing on the near side. `Tattha` means on the islands and mountains standing on the near side. `Ottharitvā` means having been submerged by the normal water. `Tattha` means in the ocean that stands submerged.

Karontehipi kātabbanti sambandho. Yatthāti yasmiṃ sare. Ayanti ayaṃ saro, na jātassaro hoti. Ayaṃ saro gāmakhettasaṅkhyameva gacchatīti yojanā. Tatthāti sare. Yattha panāti [V 1.0257] yasmiṃ sare pana. Tassāti jātassarassa. Tatthāti padese. Sace gambhīraṃ udakaṃ hotīti yojanā. Tatthāti aṭṭake. Etthāti jātassare, ṭhitesu piṭṭhipāsāṇadīpakesūti yojanā. Pahonakajātassaroti saṅghakammaṃ kātuṃ pahonako jātassaro. “Sukkhatī”ti vatvā tadeva samatthetuṃ vuttaṃ “nirudako”ti. Tatthāti jātassare. Sace nirudakamattena gāmakhettaṃ gacchati. Kadā gacchatīti āha “sace panetthā”tiādi. Tattha etthāti jātassare. Pokkharaṇīādīnīti ettha ādisaddena udakamātikādayo saṅgaṇhāti. Yadā khaṇanti, tadāti pāṭhaseso yojetabbo. “Taṃ ṭhāna”nti vuttepi na khaṇanaṭṭhānameva gahetabbaṃ, “etthā”ti sāmaññato vuttattā sabboyeva jātassaro gahetabbo. Na kevalaṃ ajātassaramattaṃ hoti, atha kho gāmakhettanti āha “gāmasīmāsaṅkhyameva gacchatī”ti.

The connection is 'it should be done even by those who are doing'. 'Yattha' (where) means 'in which pond'. 'Ayaṃ' (this) means 'this pond', it is not a natural pond. The interpretation is: 'this pond just goes by the designation of a village field'. 'Tattha' (there) means 'in the pond'. 'Yattha pana' (but where) means 'but in which pond'. 'Tassa' (of that) means 'of the natural pond'. 'Tattha' (there) means 'in the place'. The interpretation is: 'if the water is deep'. 'Tattha' (there) means 'in the platform'. 'Ettha' (here) means 'in the natural pond', the interpretation applying to 'on the situated backrest stones and beacons'. 'Pahonakajātassaro' (a natural pond sufficient) means 'a natural pond sufficient for performing a Sangha act'. Having said 'sukkhati' (it dries up), to confirm that, it is said 'nirudako' (waterless). 'Tattha' (there) means 'in the natural pond'. If it goes to the village field merely by being waterless. When does it go? He says, 'sace panettha...' (but if here...). There, 'ettha' (here) means 'in the natural pond'. 'Pokkharaṇīādīni' (ponds, etc.): here, the word 'ādi' (etc.) includes water channels and the like. When they dig, then—the remainder of the passage should be interpreted accordingly. Even if 'taṃ ṭhāna' (that place) is said, not only the place of digging should be taken, but since 'ettha' (here) is stated generally, the entire natural pond should be included. It is not merely a non-natural pond, but indeed a village field—he says, 'it goes just by the designation of the village boundary'.

Nanti jātassaraṃ. Pūretvāti mattikādīhi pūretvā. Pāḷinti āvaraṇaṃ. Sabbameva nanti sakalameva taṃ jātassaraṃ. Loṇīpīti pisaddena na kevalaṃ sobbhoyeva jātassarasaṅkhyaṃ gacchati, atha kho loṇīpīti dasseti. Udakaṭṭhānokāseti udakassa ṭhāne okāse.

'Naṃ' (it) means 'the natural pond'. 'Pūretvā' (having filled) means 'having filled with clay and so on'. 'Pāḷi' (embankment) means 'an enclosure'. 'Sabbameva naṃ' (all of it) means 'that entire natural pond'. 'Loṇīpi' (even a salt-marsh) shows that by the particle 'pi', not only does a cesspool go by the designation of a natural pond, but also a salt-marsh. 'Udakaṭṭhānokāse' (in a place for water) means 'in a place, a space for water'.

148. Sīmāya sīmaṃ sambhindantīti ettha “sīmāya sīma”nti padānaṃ sambandhāpekkhattā tesaṃ sambandhaṃ dassetuṃ vuttaṃ “attano paresa”nti. “Baddhasīma”nti iminā “sīma”nti sāmaññato vuttepi visesato baddhasīmāyeva gahetabbāti dasseti. Tamevatthaṃ vitthārento āha “sace [M 0.0302] hī”tiādi. Saṃsaṭṭhaviṭapāti aññamaññaṃ āsannattā saṃsaṭṭho viṭapo etesanti saṃsaṭṭhaviṭapā. “Saṃsaṭṭhaviṭapā”ti idaṃ upalakkhaṇamattaṃ, mūlānipi saṃsaṭṭhāniyevāti daṭṭhabbaṃ. Tesūti dvīsu rukkhesu. Vihārasīmā cāti porāṇakavihārasīmā ca. Anto katvāti sīmāya anto katvā. Atha pacchāti ettha “pacchā”ti iminā athasaddassatthaṃ dasseti. Evaṃ ke akaṃsūti āha “evaṃ chabbaggiyā akaṃsū”ti. Tenāti karaṇena.

148. Regarding 'breaking a boundary with a boundary': here, because the words 'sīmāya sīmaṃ' (boundary with boundary) require a connection, to show their connection, it is said 'attano paresaṃ' (one's own and others'). By 'baddhasīma' (established boundary), it is shown that even though 'sīma' (boundary) is stated generally, specifically only an established boundary should be taken. Elaborating on that very meaning, he says, 'sace hi...' (if indeed...). 'Saṃsaṭṭhaviṭapā' (intertwined branches) means 'those whose branches are intertwined due to being close to each other'. The phrase 'saṃsaṭṭhaviṭapā' is merely illustrative; it should be understood that the roots are also intertwined. 'Tesu' (in them) means 'in the two trees'. 'Vihārasīmā ca' (and the monastery boundary) means 'and the ancient monastery boundary'. 'Anto katvā' (having made it inside) means 'having made it inside the boundary'. 'Atha pacchā' (then afterwards): here, by 'pacchā' (afterwards), it shows the meaning of the word 'atha' (then). Thus, who acted? He says, 'Thus the group of six acted'. 'Tena' (by that) means 'by that reason'.

Ajjhottharaṇākāraṃ dassento āha “paresa”ntiādi. Tassāti baddhasīmāya. Padesanti bhikkhūhi kammaṃ kātuṃ pahonakaṃ ekadesaṃ. Antamaso ekassapi bhikkhuno ṭhatvā adhiṭṭhānuposathaṃ kātuṃ pahonakaṃ padesaṃ. Kammaṃ kātuṃ appahonakapadesaṃ anto karitvā bandhantā sīmāya sīmaṃ sambhindanti nāma. Sīmāya upacāroti pacchā bandhitabbāya sīmāya upacāro. “Vaḍḍhanto sīmāsaṅkaraṃ karotī”ti iminā sace avaḍḍhanako pāsāṇo hoti, dvinnampi sīmānaṃ nimittaṃ kātuṃ vaṭṭatīti dasseti.

Showing the manner of encompassing, he said, 'paresaṃ...' (of others...). 'Tassa' (of that) means 'of the established boundary'. 'Padesaṃ' (a portion) means 'a single portion sufficient for monks to perform a legal act'. Even a portion sufficient for a single monk to stand and perform the Uposatha by determination. If they establish a boundary by including an area insufficient for performing a legal act, they are said to confound the boundary with a boundary. 'Sīmāya upacāro' (the vicinity of the boundary) means 'the vicinity of the boundary to be established later'. By 'expanding, he creates a confusion of boundaries', it is shown that if there is a non-growing stone, it is permissible to make it a marker for both boundaries.

77. Uposathabhedādikathā

77. Discourse on the Division of the Uposatha, and So Forth

149. Pannarasikassa [V 1.0258] pubbakiccassa pāḷiyaṃ āgatattā cātuddasikasseva pubbakiccaṃ dassento āha “ajjuposatho cātuddaso”ti.

149. Since the preliminary duties for the fifteenth are mentioned in the Pāḷi, showing only the preliminary duties for the fourteenth, he said, "Today is the fourteenth Uposatha."

“Adhammena vagga”ntiādīsu vinicchayo evaṃ veditabboti yojanā. Adhammena vagganti ettha adhammaṃ nāma ekasmiṃ vihāre catunnaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ suttuddesauposathamakatvā pārisuddhiuposathakaraṇañca tiṇṇaṃ pārisuddhiuposathamakatvā suttuddesakaraṇañca. Vaggaṃ nāma sabbeva asannipatitvā ekassa chandapārisuddhiharaṇaṃ. Chandapārisuddhi nāma saṅghamajjhaṃyeva āgacchati, na gaṇamajjhaṃ, na puggalassa santikaṃ. Adhammena samagganti ettha adhammaṃ vuttanayameva. Samaggaṃ nāma sabbesaṃ sannipatanaṃ. Dhammena vagganti ettha dhammaṃ nāma catunnaṃ suttuddesauposathakaraṇañca tiṇṇaṃ pārisuddhiuposathakaraṇañca. Vaggaṃ vuttanayameva.

The judgment regarding such phrases as 'a faction by unrighteousness' should be understood as follows. Here, in 'a faction by unrighteousness', 'unrighteousness' means, in one monastery, four monks performing the Pārisuddhi-uposatha without having performed the Suttuddesa-uposatha, and three monks performing the Suttuddesa-uposatha without having performed the Pārisuddhi-uposatha. 'A faction' means that they do not all assemble, and one brings the consent and purity. 'Consent and purity' comes only to the midst of the Saṅgha, not to the midst of a group, nor to an individual. Here, in 'in harmony by unrighteousness', 'unrighteousness' is as stated above. 'In harmony' means the assembling of all. Here, in 'a faction by righteousness', 'righteousness' means four monks performing the Suttuddesa-uposatha and three monks performing the Pārisuddhi-uposatha. 'A faction' is as stated above.

78. Pātimokkhuddesakathā

78. Discourse on the Recitation of the Pātimokkha

150. Imaṃ [M 0.0303] nidānanti pātimokkhassa imaṃ nidānaṃ. Sutā kho panāti ettha suyyitthāti sutā, suyyassantīti vā sutā, pārājikuddesādayo. Sutā ca sutā ca sutāti sarūpekaseso kātabbo. Avasesanti nidānuddesādito avasesaṃ pārājikuddesādi. Sutenāti sutasaddena. “Atthe asambhavato sadde vuttavidhānaṃ hotī”ti hi paribhāsato “sutenā”ti ettha saddova gahetabbo. Tena nayenāti tena nidānuddesanayena.

150. ‘This introduction’ (imaṃ nidānaṃ) means this introduction to the Pātimokkha. Here, in ‘have been heard’ (sutā kho pana), ‘heard’ (sutā) means ‘were heard’ (suyyittha) or ‘will be heard’ (suyyassanti), referring to the recitations beginning with the Pārājika. ‘Heard and heard and heard’ (sutā ca sutā ca sutā) should be treated as an ellipsis of a similar form (sarūpekasesa). ‘The rest’ (avasesaṃ) refers to the remainder after the introductory recitation, namely, the Pārājika recitation and so on. ‘By what was heard’ (sutena) means by the word ‘heard’ (suta). For according to the maxim, ‘When the meaning is impossible, the stated procedure applies to the word,’ here in ‘by what was heard’ (sutena), only the word (sadda) should be taken. ‘By that method’ (tena nayena) means by that method of the introductory recitation.

Aṭavimanussabhayanti aṭaviyaṃ nivasantassa manussassa bhayaṃ, vanacarakabhayanti attho. Rājantarāyotiādīsu evaṃ viseso veditabboti yojanā. Davadāhoti dāyaṃ dahatīti davadāho ākārassa rassaṃ, yakārassa ca vakāraṃ katvā. Nanti bhikkhuṃ. Ekaṃ vā bhikkhunti yojanā. Paṭhamo vā uddesoti nidānuddeso. Etthāti pañcasu uddesesu. Yasminti uddese. Sopīti uddesopi. Suteneva sāvetabboti sutapadeneva saṅghassa sāvetabboti evasaddo “na vitthārenā”ti dasseti.

‘The fear of forest humans’ (aṭavimanussabhayaṃ) means the fear of humans living in the forest; the meaning is the fear of forest-wanderers. In cases like ‘the danger from kings’ (rājantarāyo), the distinction should be understood in this way—this is the connection. ‘Forest fire’ (davadāho) is from ‘it burns the forest’ (dāyaṃ dahati), by shortening the ā and changing the y to a v. ‘Him’ (naṃ) refers to a bhikkhu. ‘One or more bhikkhus’ (ekaṃ vā bhikkhuṃ)—this is the connection. ‘The first recitation’ (paṭhamo vā uddeso) means the introductory recitation. ‘Here’ (ettha) means in the five recitations. ‘In which’ (yasmiṃ) means in the recitation. ‘That too’ (so pi) means the recitation as well. ‘It should be announced by the text alone’ (suteneva sāvetabbaṃ) means it should be announced to the Saṅgha using only the words of the text; the word ‘eva’ indicates ‘not in detail.’

Anajjhiṭṭhāti ettha upasaggavasena isudhātussa icchākantito aññamatthaṃ dassento āha “anāṇattā, ayācitā vā”ti. Ettha “anāṇattā”ti idaṃ therena anāṇattabhāvaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ[V 1.0259]. “Ayācitā”ti idaṃ sammutiladdhena navakena ayācitabhāvaṃ sandhāya vuttanti daṭṭhabbaṃ. Etthāti “anajjhiṭṭhā dhammaṃ bhāsantī”ti vacane. Dhammajjhesaketi dhammakathanatthāya ajjhesatīti dhammajjhesako, tasmiṃ. Āpucchitvā vā tena saṅghattherena yācito hutvā vāti yojanā. Vārapaṭipāṭiyāti vārānukkamena. Dehīti vāti ettha iti-vā-saddo “bhaṇa” itipadena ca “kathehi” itipadena ca yojetabbo. “Bhaṇa” iti vā “kathehi”iti vā “dehi”iti vā vattabbāti yojanā[M 0.0304]. Tīhipi vidhīhīti osāraṇakathanasarabhaññasaṅkhātehi tīhi sajjanehi. Ettha ca suttassa osāriyate uccāriyate osāraṇaṃ, atthassa kathiyate kathanaṃ, suttassa ca tadatthassa ca sarena bhaṇiyate sarabhaññaṃ. Osārehīti suttaṃ uccārehi. Kathehīti atthaṃ kathehi. Sarabhaññanti suttassa ca tadatthassa ca sarena bhaṇanaṃ. Nanti saddhivihārikaṃ. Sajjhāyaṃ adhiṭṭhahitvāti “sajjhāyaṃ karomī”ti adhiṭṭhahitvā. Etthāti ajjhesanaṭṭhāne.

Regarding ‘unrequested’ (anajjhiṭṭhā): here, showing a meaning of the root ‘is’ (to wish) different from ‘desire’ by way of the prefix, he said: ‘uncommanded’ (anāṇattā) or ‘unsolicited’ (ayācitā). Here, ‘uncommanded’ is said in reference to not being commanded by an elder. ‘Unsolicited’ should be understood as said in reference to not being requested by a junior monk who has received authorization. ‘Here’ (ettha) means in the statement ‘they speak the Dhamma unrequested’. Regarding ‘one who requests the Dhamma’ (dhammajjhesake): one who requests for the purpose of a Dhamma talk is a ‘dhammajjhesako’; in that case. The connection is: ‘having asked permission, or having been requested by that senior bhikkhu of the Saṅgha’. ‘In order of turns’ (vārapaṭipāṭiyā) means in sequence of turns (vārānukkamena). Regarding ‘give’ (dehi): here, the particle ‘or’ (iti-vā) should be connected with the word ‘speak’ (bhaṇa) and the word ‘explain’ (kathehi). The connection is that one should say ‘speak’, or ‘explain’, or ‘give’. ‘By three methods’ (tīhi vidhīhi) means by the three kinds of recitation (sajjhāya) reckoned as presentation (osāraṇa), explanation (kathana), and chanting (sarabhañña). And here, the presenting or uttering aloud of the sutta is presentation; the telling of the meaning is explanation; the speaking with a melodious voice of both the sutta and its meaning is chanting. ‘Present’ (osārehi) means utter the sutta. ‘Explain’ (kathehi) means explain the meaning. ‘Chanting’ (sarabhaññaṃ) means the chanting of both the sutta and its meaning. ‘Him’ (naṃ) refers to a co-resident. ‘Having resolved to study’ (sajjhāyaṃ adhiṭṭhahitvā) means having resolved, ‘I will study’. ‘Here’ (ettha) means in the context of requesting.

Nissitaketi saddhivihārikādayo. Soti saṅghatthero, “vattabbo”tipade kammaṃ, “vadatī”tiādīsu padesu kattā. Āraddhanti saṅghena āraddhaṃ. Ṭhapetvāti dhammasavanaṃ ṭhapetvā. Osāretvāti paṭhamaṃ suttaṃ osāretvā. Puna kathentenāti pacchā atthaṃ kathentena. Aṭṭhapetvāyeva vāti suttassa ca atthassa ca antarā aṭṭhatvā eva vā. Kathetabbanti atthajātaṃ kathetabbaṃ. Kathentassa…pe… nayoti paṭhamaṃ atthaṃ kathetvā puna suttañca atthañca sarena bhaṇantassa puna āgatepi eseva nayoti attho.

‘Dependents’ (nissitake) refers to co-residents and others. ‘He’ (so) refers to the senior bhikkhu of the Saṅgha; in the word ‘should be spoken to’ (vattabbo) it is the object, while in words like ‘speaks’ (vadati) it is the subject. ‘Initiated’ (āraddhaṃ) means initiated by the Saṅgha. ‘Having set aside’ (ṭhapetvā) means having set aside listening to the Dhamma. ‘Having presented’ (osāretvā) means having first presented the sutta. ‘By one explaining again’ (puna kathentena) means by one explaining the meaning afterwards. ‘Or without having paused’ (aṭṭhapetvāyeva vā) means or without having paused between the sutta and its meaning. ‘Should be explained’ (kathetabbaṃ) means the body of meaning should be explained. The meaning of ‘for one who explains… and so on… the method’ (kathentassa…pe… nayo) is that for one who first explains the meaning and then chants the sutta and the meaning with a melodious voice, this is the same method even when it comes up again.

Upanisinnakathāyapīti samīpe nisinnena kathāyapi. Tenāti saṅghattherena. Vattuṃ vaṭṭatīti visesetvā vattuṃ vaṭṭati. Tenāti manussehi jānanabhikkhunā. Saṅghatthero bhaṇati, tuṇhī vā hotīti sambandho. “Pucchantī”ti vutteti yojanā. Anumodanādīsupītiādisaddena dhammakathādayo saṅgaṇhāti. Saṅghatthero anujānātīti sambandho. Sabbatthāti sabbesu vihāraantaragharesu.

‘Even by a conversation with one sitting nearby’ (upanisinnakathāyapi) means even by a conversation with one sitting nearby. ‘By him’ (tena) refers to the senior bhikkhu of the Saṅgha. ‘It is appropriate to speak’ (vattuṃ vaṭṭati) means it is appropriate to speak specifically. ‘By him’ (tena) refers to a bhikkhu who knows the people. The connection is: the senior bhikkhu of the Saṅgha speaks or remains silent. The connection is: when it is said ‘they ask’ (pucchantīti vutte). In ‘in cases of approval etc.’ (anumodanādīsupi), by the word ‘etc.’ (ādi), Dhamma talks and the like are included. The connection is: the senior bhikkhu of the Saṅgha permits. ‘Everywhere’ (sabbattha) means in all monasteries and inside houses.

Sajjhāyanti sayaṃ issarena ayanaṃ uccāraṇaṃ, kenaci anajjhiṭṭho sayaṃ adhiissarena ayanaṃ uccāraṇanti attho. Theroti saddhivihāro thero. Vissamissāmīti khedavirahitaṃ gamissāmi. Āpucchitabbanti paṭhamatherampi puna āgatattherampi āpucchitabbaṃ. Ekena saṅghattherena anuññātenāti sambandho. Aññasmīnti anuññātattherato aññasmiṃ thereti sambandho. Tanti puna āgataṃ theraṃ. Attānaṃ [M 0.0305] sammanitabbanti ettha paccatte upayogavacananti āha “attā sammanitabbo”ti[V 1.0260]. Kiṃ sammatena parisaṃ anoloketvā pucchitabboti āha “pucchantena panā”tiādi.

‘Recitation’ (sajjhāyaṃ) means one’s own authoritative utterance; the meaning is that, unrequested by anyone, it is one’s own utterance with supreme authority. ‘Elder’ (thero) means the co-resident is an elder. ‘I will rest’ (vissamissāmi) means I will go without weariness. ‘Should be asked for leave’ (āpucchitabbaṃ) means leave should be asked from both the first elder and the elder who has returned. The connection is: ‘having been permitted by one senior bhikkhu of the Saṅgha’. ‘To another’ (aññasmiṃ) is connected as: to an elder other than the elder who gave permission. ‘Him’ (taṃ) refers to the elder who has returned. Regarding ‘one should authorize oneself’ (attānaṃ sammanitabbaṃ), here, saying it is a reflexive expression, he said ‘oneself should be authorized’ (attā sammanitabbo). To the question, ‘Should one who is authorized ask without looking at the assembly?’, he said, ‘However, by one who asks…’ and so on.

153. Meti mayhaṃ. Itoti puggalato, uppannoti sambandho. Puramhākanti padassa pure amhākanti padacchedaṃ katvā puresaddo paṭhamatthoti āha “paṭhamaṃ amhāka”nti. Paṭikaccevasaddo pagevapariyāyo, “paṭhamataramevā”ti iminā tassa atthaṃ dasseti. Bhūtamevāti vijjamānameva, tathameva vā.

153. ‘My’ (me) means mine (mayhaṃ). ‘From this’ (ito) means from the individual; the connection is ‘arisen’ (uppanno). Regarding the word ‘before us’ (puramhākaṃ), having made the word division as ‘before, ours’ (pure amhākaṃ), he said that the word ‘before’ (pure) means first: ‘first, ours’ (paṭhamaṃ amhākaṃ). The word ‘in advance’ (paṭikacceva) is a synonym of ‘beforehand’ (pageva); he shows its meaning with ‘even earlier’ (paṭhamatarameva). ‘As it truly is’ (bhūtameva) means as it actually exists, or similarly.

82. Adhammakammapaṭikkosanādikathā

82. Discourse on Objecting to Unrighteous Acts, and so on

154. Adhammakammanti abhūtakammaṃ. Paṭikkositunti ettha kusadhātu apanayanatthoti āha “vāretu”nti. Diṭṭhinti laddhiṃ. Tesanti catunnaṃ pañcannaṃ. Yathāti yenākārena bhaṇiyamāneti yojanā. Na suṇantīti aññe bhikkhū na suṇanti. Therādhīnanti therena adhīnaṃ ābandhanti attho. Therāyattanti therena āyattaṃ, therassa santakanti attho. Etthāti pātimokkhuddese.

154. "Unrighteous action" means "untrue action." Regarding "to object": here, the root 'kus' has the meaning of removal, thus it is said "to ward off." "View" means "doctrine." "Of them" refers to four or five. "As" means the connection is 'in the manner in which it is spoken'. "They do not listen" means 'other monks do not listen'. "Dependent on the elder" means 'bound by the elder'; this is the meaning. "Subject to the elder" means 'reliant on the elder', 'belonging to the elder'; this is the meaning. "Here" means in the recitation of the Pātimokkha.

83. Pātimokkhuddesakaajjhesanādikathā

83. Discourse on Requesting the Recitation of the Pātimokkha, and so on.

155. Navavidhañcāti divasavasena tividhaṃ, kārakavasena tividhaṃ, kattabbākāravasena tividhañcāti navakoṭṭhāsañca, navapakārañca vā. Catubbidhanti “adhammena vagga”ntiādikaṃ catubbidhaṃ. Duvidhanti bhikkhubhikkhunīvasena duvidhaṃ. Navavidhanti bhikkhupātimokkhe pañcavidhaṃ, bhikkhunipātimokkhe catubbidhanti navavidhaṃ. Etthāti “yo tattha bhikkhu byatto paṭibalo”ti pāṭhe. Suvisadāti suṭṭhu byattā, suddhā vā. Ettakampīti pisaddo garahāyaṃ, adhike kā nāma kathāti dasseti.

155. "Ninefold" means threefold according to days, threefold according to agents, and threefold according to the manner of acting, thus nine categories or nine kinds. "Fourfold" refers to the four kinds beginning with "by what is not Dhamma, a faction," and so on. "Twofold" means twofold with respect to monks and nuns. "Ninefold" means five kinds in the monks' Pātimokkha and four kinds in the nuns' Pātimokkha, thus nine kinds. "Here" is in the passage, "Whatever monk there is, skilled and competent." "Very clear" means "very skilled" or "very pure." "Even this much": here the particle 'pi' expresses censure, showing, "What is there to say about more?"

Sāmantā āvāsāti ettha upayogatthe nissakkavacananti āha “sāmantaṃ āvāsa”nti. Yo sakkotīti bahūsu navesu yo sakkoti.

"From the adjacent residences": here, the ablative is used in the sense of proximity; thus he said "to the adjacent residence." "Whoever is able" refers to whoever is capable among many new monks.

84. Pakkhagaṇanādiuggahaṇānujānanakathā

84. Discourse on the Permission to Learn the Counting of Fortnights, and so on.

156. Katinaṃ [V 1.0261][M 0.0306] pūraṇīti katinaṃ tithīnaṃ pūraṇī. Ko divasoti kittako divaso. Ayyāyattanti ayyehi bhikkhūhi āyattaṃ ābaddhaṃ. Saṃharitvāti puna salākaṃ saṃharitvā. Ayaṃ pāṭho kesuci aṭṭhakathāpotthakesu natthi. Kālavatoti ettha vantupaccayo svatthoti āha “kālassevā”ti. Evasaddo pana sambhavato yujjiyati. Pagevāti pātova.

156. "The completion of how many" means the completion of how many lunar days. "What day" means "what number day." "Subject to the venerables" means "dependent on the venerable monks," "bound by them." "Having gathered" means "collecting the voting sticks again." This reading is not found in some commentary manuscripts. Regarding "timely": here the suffix 'vantu' is in the sense of 'sva' (its own), thus it is said "of the time itself." The word 'eva', however, is suitable in the sense of possibility. "Early" means "at dawn."

158. Sāyampīti sāyanhepi. Pisaddena aññampi saraṇakālaṃ sampiṇḍeti.

158. "Even in the evening" means "also in the late afternoon." The particle 'pi' also includes other times for remembering.

159. Āṇāpetunti ettha anāṇāpetabbabhikkhū apanetvā āṇāpetabbabhikkhū dassetuṃ vuttaṃ “kiñci kamma”ntiādi. Sadākālameva kiñci kammaṃ karontoti yojanā. Dhammakathikādīsūtiādisaddena gaṇavācakādayo saṅgaṇhāti. Vārenāti pariyāyena. Sammuñcaninti yaṭṭhisammuñcaniṃ vā muṭṭhisammuñcaniṃ vā. Samaṃ, suṭṭhu vā muñcati sodheti imāyāti sammuñcanī, tālujo paṭhamo. Tampīti sākhābhaṅgampi.

159. Regarding "to order": here, to show which monks should be ordered, after excluding those who should not be ordered, it is stated "whatever action," and so on. The construction is: 'they are always performing some action'. Regarding "among Dhamma preachers, and so on": the word 'and so on' includes group reciters and others. "In turn" means "alternately." "A broom" means a broom made of sticks or a broom made from a handful of grass. By this one sweeps evenly or cleans well, hence 'sammuñcanī'; the first type is made of palm leaves. "That too" means even a broken branch.

160. Vuttanayenevāti sammajjane vuttanayeneva. Puna āharitabbānīti saṅghikāvāsaṃ āsanāni puna āharitabbāni. Taṭṭikāyopīti veṇuādimayā taṭṭikāyopi.

160. "In the stated manner" means "in the manner stated for sweeping." "Should be brought again" means "the seats should be brought again to the Saṅgha's dwelling." "Even mats" means "even mats made of bamboo or similar material."

161. Kapallikā vāti kapālesu pariyāpannā padīpakapālā vā. Tanti telādiṃ. Pariyesitabbānīti anavajjapariyesanena pariyesitabbāni.

161. "Or a small bowl" means either that which is included under the term 'bowls,' or lamp bowls. "That" means oil, and so on. "Should be sought" means they should be sought with a blameless search.

86. Disaṃgamikādivatthukathā

86. Discourse on the Matter of the Monk Going to Another Region, and so on.

163. Saṃgahetabbotiādīnaṃ catunnaṃ kiriyāpadānaṃ visesaṃ dassento āha “saṃgahetabbo”tiādi. Saṃgahasaddassa saṅkhepagahaṇesupi vattanato idha “anuggahatthe”ti dassetuṃ pāḷiyaṃ vuttaṃ “anuggahetabbo”ti. Tena vuttaṃ “tathākaraṇavasenā”ti. Upalāpetabboti [M 0.0307] saṅghena bahussuto bhikkhu bhikkhūhi upagantvā lāpetabbo kathāpetabbo. Upaṭṭhāpetabboti saṅghena bahussuto bhikkhu bhikkhūhi upa accanena pūjanena ṭhāpetabbo. “Sabbesaṃ dukkaṭa”nti vatvā tadeva samatthetuṃ vuttaṃ “idha neva therā, na daharā muccantī”ti. Tenāti bahussutena bhikkhunā. Evampi satīti evaṃ asādiyanepi sati. Sāyaṃ pātanti sāyañca pāto ca sāyaṃpātaṃ. Upaṭṭhānanti [V 1.0262] upaṭṭhānaṭṭhānaṃ, upaṭṭhānatthāya vā. Tenāti bahussutena bhikkhunā. Tesanti mahātherānaṃ. Assāti bahussutassa bhikkhuno. Saddhiṃcarāti attanā saddhiṃ carantīti saddhiṃcarā. Athāpīti yadipi. Eko vā vattasampanno vadatīti yojanā. Eso ca ahañcāti mayaṃ. Nāmatumhaamhasaddesu hi ekasesena kattabbesu parova gahetabbo. Viharantūti vadantīti yojanā.

163. To show the distinctions among the four verbs beginning with "should be supported," it is said "should be supported," and so on. Since the word "saṅgaha" can also mean "concise inclusion," here, to show that it is in the sense of "support," it is stated in the Pāli as "should be supported." Therefore, it is said: "by way of acting thus." "Should be made to speak" means that a learned monk should be approached by the Saṅgha and by the monks, and should be made to speak or to talk. "Should be attended upon" means that a learned monk should be attended upon by the Saṅgha and the monks with reverence and honor. Having said, "For all, it is a dukkaṭa offense," to confirm that very point, it is stated: "Here, neither the elders nor the juniors are exempt." "By him" refers to the learned monk. "Even when this is so" means "even when not consenting thus." "Evening and morning" means "in the evening and in the morning." "Attendance" means "the place of attendance" or "for the purpose of attendance." "By him" refers to the learned monk. "Of them" refers to the great elders. "His" refers to the learned monk. "Companions" means "those who travel together with oneself." "Even if" means "although." The construction is: "or one who is accomplished in duties speaks." "He and I" means "we." Indeed, in the words 'nāma', 'tumha', and 'amha', when a single remainder is to be made, the latter should be taken. The construction is: "they say, 'May they dwell'."

So āvāso gantabboti ettha kimatthāya gantabbo, kiṃ anudivasaṃ gantabboti āha “uposathakaraṇatthāya anvaddhamāsaṃ gantabbo”ti. So ca khoti āvāso. Utuvasseyevāti hemantagimheyeva. Utuvasseyeva gantabboti atthassa ñātabbabhāvaṃ dassento āha “vassāne panā”tiādi. Yanti kammaṃ. Tatthāti “vassaṃ vasantī”tiādivacane. Soti pātimokkhuddesako bhikkhu. Aññasminti aparasmiṃ pātimokkhuddesake. Māsadvayanti sāvaṇamāsapuṇṇamito yāva assayujapuṇṇamī, tāva māsadvayaṃ vasitabbaṃ. Idaṃ purimavassaṃ upagantvā pacchimikāya pakkamanādiṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ. Sace pacchimikaṃ upagantvā anantarameva pakkamanādiṃ karoti, māsattayampi vasitabbaṃ.

Regarding "that monastery should be gone to": here, for what purpose should it be gone to? Should it be gone to daily? It is said: "For the purpose of performing the Uposatha, it should be gone to every half-month." "And that monastery" is the meaning. "Only according to the season" means "only in winter and summer." Regarding "it should be gone to only according to the season": showing that the meaning should be understood, it is said: "But in the rainy season," and so on. "Which" refers to the action. "There" refers to the statement "spending the rains," and so on. "He" refers to the monk who recites the Pātimokkha. "In another" refers to another reciter of the Pātimokkha. "Two months" means "from the full moon of Sāvaṇa up to the full moon of Assayuja, for that long, two months should be spent." This is said with reference to undertaking the earlier rains retreat and departing during the later one.
