If one undertakes the later rains retreat and immediately departs, and so on, one must stay for three months.

87. Pārisuddhidānakathā

87. Discourse on the Giving of Pārisuddhi (Declaration of Purity).

164. Yena kenaci aṅgapaccaṅgena viññāpetīti paṭivacanaṃ nicchāretumasakkonto yena kenaci aṅgapaccaṅgena viññāpeti. Ubhayathāti ubhayehi kāyavācāsaṅkhātehi ākārehi. Kāyavācāhi viññāpetīti sambandho. Sabbeti akhilā gilānā. Hatthapāseti [M 0.0308] saṅghassa hatthapāsamhi. Sace dūre hontīti sace bahū gilānā aññamaññaṃ dūre honti. Taṃ divasanti tasmiṃ saṅghaappahonakadivase.

164. "One may make it known by any limb or minor limb": being unable to utter a response, one may make it known by any limb or minor limb. "In both ways" refers to both modes, namely those designated as bodily and verbal action. The connection is "one makes it known by body and speech." "All" means all the sick without exception. "Within arm's reach" refers to being within the arm's reach of the Saṅgha. "If they are far apart" means if many sick individuals are far from each other. "That day" refers to that day when the Saṅgha is insufficient.

Tattheva pakkamatīti ettha nissakkatthe thapaccayoti āha “tatovā”ti, pārisuddhihāraṭṭhānato evāti attho. “Gacchatī”ti iminā kamudhātuyā padavikkhepatthaṃ dasseti, “katthacī”ti iminā tassa kammaṃ. Sāmaṇero paṭijānātītiādīsu paṭijānanākāratthassa itisaddassa lopabhāvaṃ dassento āha “sāmaṇero aha”nti evaṃ paṭijānātī”tiādi. Bhūtaṃyevāti vijjamānaṃyeva. Sabbatthāti sabbesu “sikkhaṃ paccakkhātako paṭijānātī”tiādīsu.

Here, regarding 'he departs right there', the suffix 'tha' is used in the ablative sense, as stated by 'or from there', meaning 'from the very place of bringing the declaration of purity'. By 'he goes', he indicates the meaning of 'stepping' from the root 'kam'; by 'somewhere', its object is indicated. In phrases such as 'the novice declares', showing the elision of the word 'iti' (which indicates the manner of declaration), he says, 'he declares thus: "I am a novice,"' and so forth. 'What is real' means precisely 'what exists'. 'In all cases' means in all instances, such as 'one who has renounced the training declares,' and so forth.

Sabbantimena [V 1.0263] paricchedena catunnaṃ bhikkhūnanti sambandho. Sabbatthāti sabbesu “saṅghappatto vibbhamatī”tiādīsu. Etthāti pārisuddhiharaṇe. Bahūnampīti ettha pisaddena ekena ekassāpi, bahūhi ekassāpi, bahūhi bahūnampi āhaṭā pārisuddhi āhaṭāva hotīti dasseti. Soti pārisuddhihārako bhikkhu. Yesanti bhikkhūnaṃ. Tassevāti pārisuddhihārakasseva. Itarā panāti itaresaṃ pārisuddhi pana. Biḷālasaṅkhalikāti ettha biḷāloti ākhubhujo. So hi biḷāsayaṃ ākhuṃ gaṇhituṃ alati samatthetīti biḷāloti vuccati. Saṅkhalikāti etaṃ sattānaṃ bandhanūpakaraṇavisesassa nāmaṃ. Biḷālassa saṅkhalikā tena sambandhasambandhibhāvena sambandhattāti biḷālasaṅkhalikā. Idaṃ upalakkhaṇamattaṃ yesaṃ kesañci saṅkhalikāya gahetabbattā. Tāya sadisā biḷālasaṅkhalikā pārisuddhīti attho. Idaṃ panettha opammasaṃsandanaṃ – yathā saṅkhalikāya paṭhamaṃ valayaṃ dutiyaṃyeva valayaṃ pāpuṇāti, na tatiyaṃ, evameva paṭhamaṃ dinnā pārisuddhi dutiyameva pāpuṇāti, na tatiyanti.

The connection is to the four monks by the very last division. 'Everywhere' (sabbatthā) means in all cases, such as 'one who has reached the Saṅgha is going astray,' and so forth. 'Here' (ettha) means in the bringing of purity. By the particle 'pi' in 'even for many' (bahūnampi), it is shown that purity brought by one for one, by many for one, or by many for many, is indeed brought. 'He' (so) refers to the monk who brings the purity. 'Of whom' (yesaṃ) refers to the monks. 'Of him alone' (tasseva) means only of the one bringing the purity. 'But of others' (itarā pana) refers to the purity of the others. In 'a cat's chain' (biḷālasaṅkhalikā), 'cat' (biḷālo) means one who eats mice. For it is called 'cat' because it is able to catch a mouse in a hole. 'Chain' (saṅkhalikā) is the name of a particular binding instrument for beings. It is a cat's chain because it is connected to the cat by a possessive relationship. This is merely an illustration, as it can be taken with any chain whatsoever. The meaning is that purity is like that chain. Here, the comparison of the simile is as follows: just as with a chain, the first link reaches only the second link, not the third, so too the purity first given reaches only the second, not the third.

Āgantvāti saṅghassa hatthapāsaṃ āgantvā. Pāḷiyaṃ sutto na ārocetītiādīsu hetvatthe paccattavacanaṃ. Suttena nārocetīti hi [M 0.0309] attho. Pārisuddhihārakassa anāpattīti ettha āpattīti anvayatthaṃ atthāpattito dassento āha “sace…pe… āpajjatī”ti. Assāti bhikkhussa. Ubhinnampīti pārisuddhidāyakassa, taṃhārakassa cāti ubhinnampi.

'Having come' (āgantvā) means having come within arm's reach of the Saṅgha. In the Pāli, in phrases such as 'he does not announce by the Sutta' (sutto na āroceti), the singular is used in the sense of cause. The meaning is 'because he does not announce by the Sutta.' Regarding 'non-offense for the purity carrier' (pārisuddhihārakassa anāpatti), here, showing the connected meaning of 'offense' by way of implication, he says, 'if... commits an offense.' 'Of him' (assā) refers to the bhikkhu. 'Of both' (ubhinnampi) means both the giver of purity and its carrier—thus of both.

88. Chandadānakathā

88. Discussion on Giving Chanda

165. Chandadānepi vinicchayo veditabboti yojanā. Uposatho kato hotīti pārisuddhidāyakassa ca saṅghassa ca uposatho kato hoti. Aññanti uposathakammato aññaṃ. Yaṃ pana kammanti sambandho. Kammampīti uposathakammato aññaṃ kammampi. Ettha ca tadahuposathe attano ca saṅghassa ca sace uposathakammaṃ hoti, pārisuddhiyeva dātabbā. Atha aññaṃ kammaṃ hoti, chandoyeva dātabbo. Yadi uposathakammañca aññakammañca hoti, pārisuddhi ca chando ca dātabbo. Taṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ “tadahuposathe pārisuddhiṃ dentena chandampi dātu”nti. Sīmāya vāti baddhasīmāya vā. Acchitunti upavesituṃ. “Āsa upavesane”ti hi dhātupāṭhesu (saddanītidhātumālāyaṃ 16 sakārantadhātu) vuttaṃ. Sāmaggī vāti kāyasāmaggī vā.

165. This is the connection: the decision should also be understood in the giving of chanda. 'The Uposatha has been performed' (uposatho kato hoti) means the Uposatha has been performed for both the one giving purity and the Saṅgha. 'Other' (aññaṃ) means other than the Uposatha kamma. 'But whatever act' (yaṃ pana kammaṃ) is the connection. 'An act also' (kammampi) means another kamma besides the Uposatha kamma. Here, on that Uposatha day, if the Uposatha kamma is performed for oneself and the Saṅgha, only purity should be given. But if another kamma is performed, only chanda should be given. If both the Uposatha kamma and another kamma are performed, both purity and chanda should be given. Referring to this, it is said, 'On that Uposatha day, when giving purity, chanda should also be given.' 'Or in a boundary' (sīmāya vā) means or in a consecrated boundary. 'To sit' (acchituṃ) means to sit down. For it is stated in the Dhātupāṭha (Saddanītidhātumālā, 16 Sakārantadhātu): 'Āsa: to sit down.' 'Or harmony' (sāmaggī vā) means or bodily harmony.

167. Saratipi uposathaṃ, napi saratīti ettha pisaddassa aniyamavikappatthaṃ dassetuṃ vuttaṃ “ekadā sarati, ekadā na saratī”ti. “Ekanta”nti iminā neva saratīti ettha evasaddassa [V 1.0264] sanniṭṭhānatthaṃ dasseti. Kammaṃ na kopetīti sammutiladdhopi aladdhopi ummattako kammaṃ na kopeti.

167. Here, regarding 'remembers the Uposatha, and does not remember' (saratipi uposathaṃ, napi sarati), to show the indefinite optional meaning of the particle 'pi', it is said, 'sometimes remembers, sometimes does not remember.' By 'absolutely' (ekantaṃ), the conclusive meaning of the word 'eva' in 'does not remember at all' (neva sarati) is shown. 'Does not invalidate the act' (kammaṃ na kopeti) means that an insane person, whether having obtained formal recognition or not, does not invalidate the act.

91. Saṅghuposathādikathā

91. Discussion of the Saṅgha Uposatha and so forth

168. “Sammajjitvā”ti padamapekkhitvā so desoti ettha “upayogatthe paccattavacana”nti vuttaṃ. Etanti “so deso sammajjitabbo”tiādivacanaṃ. Tenāti tena hetunā. Aṭṭhakathācariyā “sammajjanī…pe… vuccati” iti āhūti yojanā.

168. With reference to the word 'sammajjitvā' (having swept) and the phrase 'so deso' (that place), it is said here that this is 'the singular in the sense of instrumentality.' 'This' (etaṃ) refers to a statement such as 'that place should be swept.' 'By that' (tena) means by that reason. The connection is: the commentary teachers said, 'a broom... is called.'

Sammajjanīti [M 0.0310] sammajjanakaraṇaṃ. Padīpoti padīpujjalanaṃ. Udakanti udakaṭṭhapanaṃ. Āsanenāti āsanapaññāpanena. “Itī”ti ajjhāharitabbaṃ. Uposathassāti navavidhassa uposathassa pubbakaraṇanti sambandho. Etānīti cattāri kammāni. Vuccatīti kathiyati. Idaṃ “etānī”ti kammassa ca “pubbakaraṇa”nti ākārassa ca abhedattā āsannaṃ ākāramapekkhitvā ekavacanavasena vuttaṃ. “Akkhātānī”ti idaṃ pana “imāni cattārī”ti kammamapekkhitvā bahuvacanavasena vuttanti daṭṭhabbaṃ.

'Sweeping' (sammajjanī) means the act of sweeping. 'Lamp' (padīpo) means the lighting of a lamp. 'Water' (udakaṃ) means the placing of water. 'By a seat' (āsanena) means by the providing of a seat. The word 'iti' (thus) should be supplied. 'Of the Uposatha' (uposathassa) is connected as a preliminary duty for the ninefold Uposatha. 'These' (etāni) refers to the four acts. 'It is said' (vuccati) means it is told. Here, because there is no distinction between 'these' (etāni) as the act and 'preliminary duty' (pubbakaraṇa) as the state, it is stated in the singular form, considering the closely related state. However, 'declared' (akkhātāni) should be understood as being stated in the plural form, considering 'these four' (imāni cattāri) as the acts.

Chandapārisuddhiutukkhānanti chandakkhānañca pārisuddhikkhānañca utukkhānañca. Bhikkhugaṇanāti bhikkhū gaṇetvā akkhānaṃ. Ovādoti bhikkhunīhi yācitassa ovādassa akkhānaṃ. Etānīti etāni pañca. Pubbakaraṇato pacchāti pubbakaraṇassa karaṇato pacchā. Ettha ca “pubbakaraṇato pacchā kattabbānī”ti idaṃ kattabbākārasseva visesanaṃ, na atthassa. Ayaṃ pana viseso – saṅghasannipātato pubbabhāge kattabbattā pubbakaraṇaṃ nāma, uposathakaraṇato pubbabhāge kattabbattā pubbakiccaṃ nāmāti.

'Chandapārisuddhiutukkhāna' means the declaration of consent, the declaration of purity, and the declaration of the season. 'Bhikkhugaṇanā' means the announcement after counting the monks. 'Ovāda' means the announcement of the instruction requested by the bhikkhunīs. 'These' (etāni) refers to these five. 'After the preliminary act' (pubbakaraṇato pacchā) means after the performance of the preliminary act. Here, 'to be done after the preliminary act' (pubbakaraṇato pacchā kattabbāni) qualifies only the manner of action, not its meaning. This, however, is the distinction: because it is to be done in the preliminary stage before the assembly of the Saṅgha, it is called a 'preliminary act' (pubbakaraṇa); because it is to be done in the preliminary stage before performing the Uposatha, it is called a 'preliminary duty' (pubbakicca).

Uposathoti uposathadivaso. Yāvatikā ca bhikkhūti yattakā bhikkhū. Kammapattāti uposathakammassa pattā yuttā anurūpā. Tāvatikā bhikkhū hatthapāsaṃ avijahitvā ekasīmāyaṃ ṭhitā ca hontīti yojanā. Sabhāgāpattiyoti vatthusabhāgā āpattiyo. Vajjanīyāti vajjetabbā. Puggalāti gahaṭṭhādipuggalā. Tasminti tasmiṃ uposathasīmamāḷake. Etāni cattārīti pāṭhaseso.

'Uposatha' means the Uposatha day. 'And however many monks' (yāvatikā ca bhikkhū) means 'as many monks.' 'Qualified for the act' (kammapattā) means suited, fit, and appropriate for the Uposatha act. The connection is: 'that many monks should be standing within a single boundary, without leaving arm's reach.' 'Offenses of the same kind' (sabhāgāpattiyo) means offenses of the same basis. 'To be avoided' (vajjanīyā) means 'must be avoided.' 'Persons' (puggalā) means laypersons and similar individuals. 'In that' (tasmiṃ) means 'in that Uposatha boundary enclosure.' 'These four' (etāni cattāri) is the remainder of the text.

Āgatehi [V 1.0265] tehi bhikkhūhīti yojanā. Pannarasopīti pisaddena na kevalaṃ pāḷiyaṃ āgatanayeneva adhiṭṭhātuṃ vaṭṭati, atha kho “ajja me uposatho pannaraso”tipīti dasseti.

The connection is: 'with those monks having arrived.' 'On the fifteenth too' (pannarasopi) means that with the particle 'pi', it is not only permissible to determine it according to the way it has come down in the Pāli, but it also shows that one can say, 'Today is my Uposatha, the fifteenth.'

92. Āpattipaṭikammavidhikathā

92. Discussion of the Procedure for Rectifying Offenses

169. Bhagavatā…pe… kātabboti idaṃ veditabbanti sambandho. “Yassa siyā āpattītiādivacaneneva cā”tiādihetuttayena “na sāpattikena uposatho kātabbo”ti yathārutaṃ apaññattampi [M 0.0311] atthato siddhamevāti dasseti. Hetuttayaṃ “veditabba”nti padena yojetabbaṃ. Thullaccayādīsūti ādisaddena pācittiyapāṭidesanīyadukkaṭadubbhāsitāpattiyo saṅgaṇhāti. “Taṃ paṭidesemī”ti idaṃ suvuttameva hotīti sambandho. Tanti āpattiṃ. Tumhamūleti tumhaṃ santike. Niggahitalopañhi vākyameva, na samāso. “Tumha” iti ca “tuyha” iti ca navakattherānaṃ vattabbākāradassanamattameva, na icchitatthavipattidassanaṃ. Vuttampīti pisaddena na kevalaṃ pāḷinayeneva suvuttaṃ, iminā nayenapi suvuttanti dasseti. “Passasī”ti idañca vattabbanti sambandho. Vattabbākāraṃ pana suviññeyyaṃ. “Āma passāmī”ti idaṃ pana suvuttameva hotīti sambandho. Vuttampīti pisaddo pāḷinayaṃ sampiṇḍeti. Āyatiṃ saṃvareyyāsīti ettha pana vattabboti sambandho. Garūsu bahuvacanassa kattabbattā vuttaṃ “saṃvareyyāthā”ti. Evaṃ vuttena āpattidesakenāti sambandho.

169. The connection is that 'this should be understood' (idaṃ veditabbaṃ) refers to 'it should be done by the Blessed One... and so forth' (Bhagavatā...pe... kātabbaṃ). It shows that even though 'the Uposatha should not be performed by one with an offense' (na sāpattikena uposatho kātabbo) is not explicitly laid down in its literal sense, its meaning is established by the threefold reason beginning with the statement 'if one has an offense' (yassa siyā āpatti), and so forth. The threefold reason should be connected with the word 'should be understood' (veditabbaṃ). In 'Thullaccayādīsū' (in grave offenses, etc.), the word 'etc.' includes offenses entailing expiation (pācittiya), offenses to be acknowledged (pāṭidesanīya), offenses of wrong conduct (dukkaṭa), and offenses of wrong speech (dubbhāsita). The connection is that 'I confess that' (taṃ paṭidesemi) is indeed well-stated. 'That' (taṃ) refers to the offense. 'In your presence' (tumhamūle) means 'near you.' Indeed, it is merely a phrase with an elided final consonant, not a compound. The forms 'tumha' and 'tuyha' are merely a demonstration of how new elders might be addressed, not an indication of a deviation from the intended meaning. 'It is also said' (vuttampi) shows that with the particle 'pi', it is not only well-stated according to the Pāli method but also well-stated in this way. The connection is that 'Do you see?' (passasi) should also be spoken. The manner of speaking, however, is easily understood. The connection is that 'Yes, I see' (āma passāmi) is indeed well-stated. The particle 'pi' in 'it is also said' (vuttampi) here consolidates the Pāli method. The connection is that 'You should restrain yourself in the future' (āyatiṃ saṃvareyyāsi) should be spoken here. Because the plural form is appropriate when addressing elders, 'you should restrain yourselves' (saṃvareyyāthā) is said. The connection is: 'when this is said by the one confessing the offense'.

Tatrāti “yadā nibbematiko”ti pāṭhe. Sūriye meghacchanne satīti yojanā. Tena bhikkhunā vattabbanti sambandho, vatthuṃ kittetvāti bhojanasaṅkhātaṃ vatthuṃ kittetvā. Tāti āpattiyo.

'Tatra' refers to the reading 'yadā nibbematiko' (when without doubt). The construction is: 'when the sun is covered by clouds.' The connection is: 'it should be said by that monk.' 'Vatthuṃ kittetvā' (having declared the thing) means having declared the thing reckoned as food. 'Tā' (those) refers to the offenses.

Sabhāgā āpattīti ettha dvīsu vatthusabhāgaāpattisabhāgāsu vatthusabhāgāva adhippetāti dassento āha “yaṃ dvepi janā”tiādi. Yaṃ āpattinti sambandho. Samāno bhāgo etāsanti sabhāgā. Desetuṃ vaṭṭatīti āpattisabhāgāpi vatthuvisabhāgattā desetuṃ vaṭṭati. Sudesitāvāti āpattito bhikkhu vuṭṭhātiyevāti adhippāyo. Aññaṃ dukkaṭanti sambandho. Panasaddo garahatthajotako sudesitāya garahākārena pavattattā. Kiñcāpi sudesitāva, pana tathāpīti yojanā. Tanti dukkaṭaṃ. Nānāvatthukanti desanāpaṭiggahaṇavasena nānāvatthukaṃ.

Here, in 'sabhāgā āpatti' (an offense of the same kind), showing that among the two—offenses sharing the same basis (vatthusabhāga) and offenses of the same kind (āpattisabhāgā)—it is offenses sharing the same basis that are intended, he says, 'when two people...' and so forth. The connection is to 'which offense' (yaṃ āpattiṃ). 'Sabhāgā' means 'having the same part.' 'It is proper to confess' means that even an offense of the same kind is proper to confess on account of its basis being different. 'Sudesitāva' (well confessed) means the intention is that the monk is indeed absolved from the offense. The connection is to 'another offense of wrong conduct' (aññaṃ dukkaṭaṃ). The particle 'pana' indicates censure, as it proceeds in a manner of censure toward that which is well confessed. The construction is: 'Although it is well confessed, nevertheless...' 'Taṃ' refers to the offense of wrong conduct. 'Nānāvatthukaṃ' (with different bases) means having different bases with respect to the confession and the acceptance.

170. Sabhāgoyeva [V 1.0266] vattabbo, na visabhāgo. Hīti saccaṃ, yasmā vā. Tassāti visabhāgassa. Itoti saṅghasannipātato.

170. Only what is of the same kind should be spoken, not what is of a different kind. 'Hi' means 'indeed,' or 'because.' 'Tassa' (of that) refers to that which is of a different kind. 'Ito' (from here) refers to 'from the assembly of the Saṅgha'.

95. Anāpattipannarasakādikathā

95. The Discussion on the Fifteen Cases of No Offense, etc.

172. Te [M 0.0312] na jāniṃsūti ettha jānanākāradassanatthaṃ “sīmaṃ okkantāti vā okkamantīti vā”ti vuttaṃ. Okkantāti vāti pavisittha iti vā. Tesanti catunnaṃ vā atirekānaṃ vā bhikkhūnaṃ. Vaggā samaggasaññinoti ettha kasmā vaggā, kasmā samaggasaññinoti āha “tesa”ntiādi. Tattha tesanti aññesaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ. Sīmaṃ okkantattāti sīmaṃ pavisitattā, vaggā hutvāti sambandho. Samaggo iti saññā samaggasaññā, sā etesamatthīti samaggasaññino.

172. In 'Te na jāniṃsu' (They did not know), to show the manner of knowing, it is said, 'they had crossed the boundary' or 'they are crossing the boundary.' 'Okkantā' means 'they had entered.' 'Tesaṃ' (of those) refers to four or more monks. In 'Vaggā samaggasaññino' (divided, yet perceiving themselves as united), as to why 'divided' and why 'perceiving themselves as united,' he says 'tesaṃ,' etc. There, 'tesaṃ' refers to the other monks. 'Sīmaṃ okkantattā' (because they had crossed the boundary) means 'because they had entered the boundary'; the connection is with 'having become divided.' The perception 'united' is 'samaggasaññā'; 'samaggasaññino' means they possess that perception.

175. Kukkuccapakatāti padassa “icchāpakato”ti padena samānabhāvaṃ dassetuṃ vuttaṃ “yathā”tiādi. Pubbabhāgeti uposathakammato pubbabhāge. Sanniṭṭhānaṃ katvāpīti kappatevāti sanniṭṭhānaṃ katvāpi. “Abhibhūtā”ti iminā pakatāti ettha papubbakaradhātuyā upasaggavasena abhibhavanatthaṃ dasseti.

175. To show the similarity of the word 'kukkuccapakatā' (done with scruples) with the word 'icchāpakato' (done with desire), it is said, 'just as,' etc. 'Pubbabhāge' (in the preliminary part) means in the part before the Uposatha ceremony. 'Sanniṭṭhānaṃ katvāpi' (even after having resolved) means even after having resolved, 'it is indeed allowable.' By the word 'abhibhūtā' (overcome), he shows that here in 'pakatā,' the prefix 'pa' before the root 'kar' has the meaning of 'overcoming'.

176. Yathā heṭṭhā vaggāvaggasaññīpannarasakādīsu dukkaṭaṃ vuttaṃ, evamakatvā kasmā “thullaccaya”nti āha “akusalabalavatāyā”ti.

176. Just as below, in the fifteenth case and so on concerning perceptions of being divided and undivided, a dukkaṭa offense was stated; why, instead of that, does he say it is a 'grave offense' (thullaccaya)? He says, 'due to the strength of the unwholesome.'

100. Sīmokkantikapeyyālakathā

100. The Discussion on the Abbreviated Passages Concerning Boundary-Crossing

177. Āvāsikenaāgantukapeyyāle sabbaṃ veditabbanti sambandho. Veditabbākāraṃ saha upamāya dassento āha “yathā”tiādi. Āgantukenaāvāsikapeyyāle pana ānetabbanti sambandho. Purimapeyyāleti āvāsikenaāgantukapeyyāle. Āgantukenaāgantukapeyyāle pana yojetabboti sambandho. Ettha ca peyyālanti sadisanayassa ca taṃjānanañāṇassa ca pātabbaṃ rakkhanaṃ peyyaṃ, peyyaṃ, peyye vā, peyyāya vā alati samatthetīti peyyālanti vacanattho kātabbo.

177. The connection is: 'by the resident, in the abbreviated passage concerning the visitor, everything should be understood.' Showing the manner in which it should be understood, along with an analogy, he says, 'just as,' etc. The connection is: 'by the visitor, in the abbreviated passage concerning the resident, however, it should be supplied.' 'The former abbreviated passage' refers to the abbreviated passage concerning the resident and the visitor. The connection is: 'by the visitor, in the abbreviated passage concerning the visitor, however, it should be connected.' And here, the word-meaning of 'peyyāla' should be understood as follows: 'peyya' means that which is to be drunk in (i.e., absorbed) and the protection of a similar method and of the knowledge that recognizes it. 'Peyyāla' is so called because it suffices for (alati) or is capable of (samattheti) that 'peyya' (in its various grammatical forms: peyyaṃ, peyye, or peyyāya).

178. Āvāsikānaṃ cātuddaso hutvā kasmā āgantukānaṃ pannarasoti āha “yesa”ntiādi[V 1.0267]. Tattha yesanti āgantukānaṃ. Tiroraṭṭhatoti āvāsikānaṃ raṭṭhassa aññaraṭṭhato. Tirojanapadatoti [M 0.0313] ekaraṭṭhepi aññajanapadato. Cātuddasikaṃ akaṃsūti saññānānattavasena cātuddasikaṃ akaṃsu. Anuvattitabbanti anumatiṃ vattitabbaṃ. Na paṭikkositabbanti “na cātuddaso”ti vatvā na vāritabbaṃ. Na akāmāti ettha kamudhātu icchattho, karaṇatthe ca nissakkavacananti āha “na anicchāya dātabbā”ti.

178. It being the fourteenth for the residents, why is it the fifteenth for the visitors? He says, 'yesaṃ,' etc. There, 'yesaṃ' refers to the visitors. 'Tiroraṭṭhato' (from beyond the country) means from a country other than the residents' country. 'Tirojanapadato' (from beyond the district) means from another district, even within the same country. 'They performed the fourteenth' means they performed the fourteenth due to a difference in perception. 'Anuvattitabbaṃ' (should be followed) means consent should be given. 'Na paṭikkositabbaṃ' (should not be rejected) means it should not be prevented by saying, 'It is not the fourteenth.' In 'na akāmā' (not unwillingly), the root 'kam' has the meaning of wishing, and in the sense of doing, it is an emphatic statement; he says, 'it should not be given against their will.'

101. Liṅgādidassanakathā

101. The Discussion on the Showing of Marks, etc.

179. “Āvāsikānaṃ ākāra”nti iminā āvāsikākāranti padassa chaṭṭhīsamāsaṃ dasseti. Sabbatthāti sabbesu “āvāsikaliṅga”ntiādīsu. Yenāti supaññattamañcapīṭhādinā, gaṇhatīti sambandho. Tesanti āvāsikānaṃ. Ācārasaṇṭhānanti ācārasaṇṭhitiṃ. So supaññattamañcapīṭhādiko ākāro nāmāti yojanā. Yanti supaññattamañcapīṭhādiṃ, gamayatīti sambandho. Tattha tatthāti tasmiṃ tasmiṃ ṭhāne. Līne āvāsiketi sambandho. Taṃ supaññattamañcapīṭhādi liṅgaṃ nāmāti yojanā. “Adissamāne”ti iminā līneti padassa atthaṃ dasseti. “Jānāpetī”ti iminā gamayatīti padassa ñāṇatthaṃ dasseti. Yanti supaññattamañcapīṭhādiṃ. Teti āvāsikā. Taṃ supaññattamañcapīṭhādi nimittaṃ nāmāti yojanā. Yenāti supaññattamañcapīṭhādinā. Teti āvāsikā uddisiyanti, so supaññattamañcapīṭhādiko uddeso nāmāti yojanā. Imehi padehi ākiriyanti pakāsiyanti etenāti ākāro, līne gamayati bodhetīti liṅgaṃ. Nimiyanti paricchijja ñāyanti etenāti nimittaṃ, uddisiyanti apadisiyanti etenāti uddesoti vacanatthaṃ dasseti. Sabbametanti “āvāsikākāra”ntiādi etaṃ sabbaṃ. Yathāyoganti pāḷiyaṃ yogānurūpaṃ. Tatthāti āgantukākārādīsu. “Amhākaṃ ida”nti na ñātabbanti aññātaṃ, tadeva aññātakaṃ, nisīdanādi. “Amhākaṃ ida”nti ajānanaṃ nāma attano asantakattā, aññesameva santakattā hotīti āha “aññesaṃ santaka”nti. Udakanissekanti siñcanavirahitaṃ udakaṃ. Bahuvacanassāti “dhotāna”nti ettha chaṭṭhībahuvacanassa. Ekavacananti “dhotassā”ti ekavacanaṃ[M 0.0314]. Pacchimapāṭhe malaṃ dhunāti anenāti dhotaṃ, dhotañca taṃ udakañceti dhotaudakaṃ, tameva nissekaṃ dhotaudakanissekaṃ.

179. By 'āvāsikānaṃ ākāra' (the characteristic of the residents), he indicates the genitive compound of the word 'āvāsikākāra.' 'Sabbattha' (everywhere) means in all instances, such as 'āvāsikaliṅga,' etc. 'Yena' (by which) refers to a well-arranged bed, bench, etc.; it is connected with 'gaṇhati' (takes hold). 'Tesaṃ' (theirs) refers to the residents. 'Ācārasaṇṭhānaṃ' (the manner of conduct) means the established practice. The construction is: that well-arranged bed, bench, etc., is called a 'characteristic' (ākāra). 'Yaṃ' (which) refers to the well-arranged bed, bench, etc.; it is connected with 'gamayati' (makes known). 'Tattha tattha' (here and there) means in each respective place. It is connected with 'the resident being concealed' (līne āvāsike). The construction is: that well-arranged bed, bench, etc., is called a 'mark' (liṅga). By 'adissamāne' (when not seen), he indicates the meaning of the word 'līne.' By 'jānāpetī' (makes known), he indicates that the word 'gamayati' has the meaning of knowledge. 'Yaṃ' refers to the well-arranged bed, bench, etc. 'Te' (they) refers to the residents. The construction is: that well-arranged bed, bench, etc., is called a 'sign' (nimitta). 'Yena' refers to the well-arranged bed, bench, etc. 'Te' refers to the residents being designated; the construction is: that well-arranged bed, bench, etc., is called a 'designation' (uddesa). He shows the word-meanings thus: 'ākāra' is that by which things are made known (ākiriyanti pakāsiyanti); 'liṅga' is that which makes known or informs (gamayati bodheti) what is concealed (līne); 'nimitta' is that by which things are measured, distinguished, and known (nimiyanti paricchijja ñāyanti); 'uddesa' is that by which things are designated or pointed out (uddisiyanti apadisiyanti). 'Sabbametaṃ' (all this) refers to everything from 'āvāsikākāra' onwards. 'Yathāyogaṃ' (according to context) means in accordance with the usage in the Pāli. 'Tattha' (there) refers to the characteristics of the visitor, etc. 'Aññātakaṃ' (unknown item) is so called because it is not to be known as 'this is ours' (amhākaṃ idaṃ); that very thing is the unknown, such as a seat, etc. Not knowing 'this is ours' is because it is not one's own property, but is the property of others; thus he says, 'belonging to others' (aññesaṃ santakaṃ). 'Udakanissekaṃ' means water devoid of sprinkling. 'Bahuvacanassa' (of the plural) refers to the genitive plural in 'dhotānaṃ.' 'Ekavacanaṃ' (the singular) refers to the singular 'dhotassa.' In the latter reading, 'dhota' is that by which dirt is shaken off; and that water is 'dhotaudaka' (washed-water); that very sprinkling is 'dhotaudakanissekaṃ' (sprinkling with washed-water).

180. Samānasaṃvāsakadiṭṭhinti padassa itilopasamāsaṃ dassento āha “samānasaṃvāsakā eteti diṭṭhi”nti. Eteti āvāsikā bhikkhū. “Laddhi”nti iminā na pucchantīti padassa kammaṃ [V 1.0268] dasseti. Nānāsaṃvāsakabhāvanti tesaṃ laddhinānāsaṃvāsakabhāvaṃ. “Madditu”nti iminā nābhivitarantīti ettha abhisaddassatthaṃ dasseti. “Abhibhavitu”nti iminā ca tadevatthaṃ dasseti. Nānāsaṃvāsakabhāvassa maddanaṃ nāma laddhinissajjāpananti āha “taṃ diṭṭhiṃ na nissajjāpentī”ti.

180. To show the compound with elision of 'iti' in the word 'samānasaṃvāsakadiṭṭhiṃ' (the view of having a common communion), he says, 'samānasaṃvāsakā ete, iti diṭṭhi' (they have a common communion, this is the view). 'Ete' (they) refers to the resident monks. By 'laddhiṃ' (belief), he indicates the object of the word 'na pucchanti' (they do not ask). 'Nānāsaṃvāsakabhāvaṃ' (the state of having a different communion) refers to their belief in the state of having a different communion. By 'maddituṃ' (to crush), he shows the meaning of the prefix 'abhi' in 'nābhivitaranti' (they do not overcome). And by 'abhibhavituṃ' (to overpower), he shows the very same meaning. The crushing of the state of having a different communion is the causing to abandon that belief; thus he says, 'they do not cause them to abandon that view' (taṃ diṭṭhiṃ na nissajjāpenti).

103. Nagantabbagantabbavārakathā

103. The Discussion on the Section Concerning Where One Should and Should Not Go

181. Sabhikkhukāti padassa saṃvijjanti bhikkhū etasmimāvāseti sabhikkhukoti vacanatthaṃ dassento āha “yasmiṃ āvāse”tiādi. Yanti āvāsaṃ. Tadahevāti tadahuposathe eva. Iminā sace sakkoti, tadaheva gantuṃ, so gantabboti dasseti. “Akatvā”ti iminā katvā pana gantabboti dasseti. “Aññatrā”ti nipāto “vinā”ti nipātassa pariyāyoti āha “vinā”ti. Attacatutthena vā attapañcamena vā saṅghena gantuṃ vaṭṭatīti yojanā. Ettha ca “attacatutthena vā”ti idaṃ uposathakammaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ. “Attapañcamena vā”ti idaṃ pavāraṇākammaṃ sandhāya vuttanti daṭṭhabbaṃ. Vihāreti vihārasīmāya mahāsīmāyanti attho. Idañhi vihārasīmānaṃ abhedena vuttaṃ. Sīmāpīti khaṇḍasīmāpi. Na gantabbāti saṅghassa garukattā na gantabbā. Etthāti khaṇḍasīmādīsu. Tassāti bhikkhussa. Gantuṃ vaṭṭatīti gaṇuposathaṭṭhānato gantuṃ vaṭṭati, saṅghuposathaṭṭhānato pana na vaṭṭatiyevāti daṭṭhabbaṃ. Vissaṭṭhauposathā āvāsāpi aññaṃ gantuṃ vaṭṭatīti yojanā. Āraññakenāpīti araññe ekakena nivāsenapi. Tatthāti aññavihāre. Uposathanti saṅghuposathañca gaṇuposathañca.

181. Regarding the term 'sabhikkhuka,' showing the meaning of the word 'sabhikkhuka' as 'bhikkhus exist in this monastery,' he says, 'in which monastery,' and so on. They go to a monastery. 'Tadaheva' (on that very day) means on that very Uposatha day. By this, it is shown that if one is able to go on that very day, one should go. By 'akatvā' (without having done), it is shown that one should go after having done it. The particle 'aññatrā' (except) is a synonym for the particle 'vinā' (without), he says, 'vinā.' The connection is that it is permissible to go with a Sangha of four including oneself or a Sangha of five including oneself. And here, 'with a Sangha of four including oneself' is said with reference to the Uposatha ceremony. 'With a Sangha of five including oneself' should be understood as said with reference to the Pavāraṇā ceremony. 'Vihāre' (in a monastery) means within the boundary of the monastery, that is, the great boundary. This is indeed stated without distinguishing the boundaries of monasteries. 'Sīmāpi' (even a boundary) means even a partial boundary. 'Na gantabbā' (should not be gone to) means it should not be gone to because of the importance of the Sangha. 'Ettha' (here) refers to partial boundaries, etc. 'Tassa' (for him) refers to the bhikkhu. 'Gantuṃ vaṭṭati' (it is permissible to go) should be understood to mean it is permissible to go from the place of a group Uposatha, but it is indeed not permissible to go from the place of a Sangha Uposatha. The connection is that it is permissible to go to another monastery even from a monastery where the Uposatha has been abandoned. 'Āraññakenāpi' (even by a forest-dweller) means even by one dwelling alone in the forest. 'Tattha' (there) means in another monastery. 'Uposatha' refers to both the Sangha Uposatha and the group Uposatha.

182. Yanti āvāsaṃ. Tatthāti taṃ āvāsaṃ. Gantuṃ sakkomi iti jāneyyāti yojanā. Tatthāti tasmiṃ āvāse. Iminā neva katoti [M 0.0315] sambandho. Neva kato bhavissati iti jāneyyāti yojanā.

182. They go to a monastery. 'Tattha' (there) means to that monastery. The connection is that one should know, 'I am able to go.' 'Tattha' (there) means in that monastery. By this, the connection is 'not done.' The connection is that one should know, 'It will not be done.'

105. Vajjanīyapuggalasandassanakathā

105. Discussion on Pointing Out Blameworthy Individuals

183. Hatthapāsūpagamanamevāti uposathasaṅghādīnaṃ hatthapāsassa upagamanameva. Idaṃ pārivāsiyapārisuddhidānaṃ nāma na vaṭṭatīti yojanā. Tassāti pārivāsiyapārisuddhidānassa. Anuposatheti ettha akārassa aññatthaṃ dassento āha “aññasmiṃ divase”ti. Tattha aññasminti dvīhi uposathehi aññasmiṃ. Yā saṅghasāmaggī kariyati, tathārūpinti yojanā. Kosambakabhikkhūnanti [V 1.0269] kosambiyaṃ nivāsīnaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ. Sāmaggī viya yā sāmaggīti yojanā. “Ṭhapetvā”ti iminā aññatrāti nipātassa atthaṃ dasseti. Ye panāti bhikkhū pana samaggā hontīti sambandho. Uposatheyevāti uposathadivaseyeva.

183. 'Hatthapāsūpagamanameva' (only approaching within arm’s reach) means only approaching within arm’s reach of the Uposatha Sangha, etc. The connection is that this granting of purity to one on probation is not permissible. 'Tassa' (of that) refers to the granting of purity to one on probation. Regarding 'anuposathe' (not on the Uposatha day), here, showing another meaning for the 'a' prefix, he says, 'on another day.' There, 'aññasmiṃ' (on another) means on a day other than the two Uposatha days. The connection is: such as the unity of the Sangha that is created. 'Kosambakabhikkhūnaṃ' (of the Kosambaka bhikkhus) means of the bhikkhus residing in Kosambi. The connection is: a unity like that unity. By 'ṭhapetvā' (except), he shows the meaning of the particle 'aññatrā' (other than). The connection is: 'But those bhikkhus are in harmony.' 'Uposatheyeva' (only on the Uposatha day) means only on the Uposatha day.

Iti uposathakkhandhakavaṇṇanāya yojanā samattā.

Thus ends the explanation of connections in the commentary on the Uposatha Chapter.

3. Vassūpanāyikakkhandhakaṃ

3. The Chapter on Entering the Rains Residence

107. Vassūpanāyikānujānanakathā

107. Discussion on the Allowance for Entering the Rains Residence

184. Vassūpanāyikakkhandhake “ananuññāto”ti iminā apaññattoti ettha ñādhātuyā anujānanatthaṃ dasseti, “asaṃvihito”ti iminā ñādhātuyā ṭhapanatthaṃ. Tedhāti te idha. Idhasaddo sāsanañca lokañca desañca padapūraṇañca upādāya vattati, idha pana padapūraṇeti dassento āha “idhasaddo nipātamatto”ti. Saṃhananaṃ saṅghāto, vināsoti attho. Iti imamatthaṃ dasseti “vināsa”nti iminā. Sakuntakasaddo sakuṇapariyāyoti āha “sakuṇā”ti. Sakuṇāti ca vihaṅgamā. Te hi ākāse gantuṃ sakkontīti sakuṇāti vuccanti. Saṃkasāyissantīti ettha “saṃ kase acchane”ti dhātupāṭhesu (saddanītidhātumālāyaṃ 16 sakārantadhātu) vuttattā saṃpubbo kasedhātu acchanatthoti āha [M 0.0316] “vasissantī”ti. Ekārantoyaṃ dhātu. Nibaddhavāsanti niccavāsaṃ. Vassānanāmaketi vassānautunāmake. Vassānassa catumāsattā “temāse”ti vuttaṃ. Vassūpanāyikāti ettha nīdhātu gamanatthoti āha “vassūpagamanānī”ti. Aparajjūti puṇṇamito aparaṃ ahanti aparajju, ahatthe jjupaccayo, atthato pāṭipadadivaso. Ayaṃ aparajjusaddo paṭhamantanipāto. Assāti āsaḷhīpuṇṇamiyā. Asamānādhikaraṇavisayo bāhiratthasamāsoyaṃ, atikkantāya satiyāti yojanā. Aparasmiṃ divaseti pāṭipadadivase. Assāti sāvaṇamāsapuṇṇamiyā. Tasmāti yasmā ca aparajjugatā, yasmā ca māsagatā, tasmā. “Anantare pāṭipadadivase”ti iminā pāḷiyaṃ aparajjugatāya āsaḷhiyā anantare pāṭipadadivase purimikā upagantabbāti atthaṃ dasseti. Āsaḷhiyāti āsaḷhīpuṇṇamiyā. Pacchimanayepi māsagatāya āsaḷhiyā anantare pāṭipadadivase pacchimikā upagantabbāti attho [V 1.0270] daṭṭhabbo. Āsaḷhiyāti āsaḷhīpuṇṇamiyā samīpe pavattattā āsaḷhīsaṅkhātāya sāvaṇapuṇṇamiyāti attho. Pāṭipadadivaseyeva vassaṃ upagantabbanti sambandho. Sakiṃ vātiādīsu vāsaddo aniyamavikappattho. Nicchāretvāti niccāretvā, uccāretvāti attho. Aphuṭṭhakkharasaññogehi paro kvaci phuṭṭhattamāpajjati “nikkhamatī”tiādīsu viya. Tasmā parassa cakārassa chakāraṃ katvā “nicchāretvā”ti vuttaṃ.

184. In the Chapter on Entering the Rains Residence, by 'ananuññāto' (unpermitted), he shows the meaning of permission for the root ñā in 'apaññatto' (unprescribed); by 'asaṃvihito' (unarranged), the meaning of establishment for the root ñā. 'Tedha' means 'te idha' (they here). The word 'idha' (here) is used with reference to the Dispensation, the world, the region, and as a word-filler; here, however, showing that it is a word-filler, he says, 'the word “idha” is merely a particle.' 'Saṃhananaṃ' is 'saṅghāto' (a mass), meaning destruction. By 'vināsa,' he shows this meaning. The word 'sakuntaka' is a synonym for 'sakuṇa' (bird), he says, 'sakuṇā.' And 'sakuṇā' means birds. For they are able to go in the sky, therefore they are called 'sakuṇā.' Regarding 'saṃkasāyissanti' (they will dwell), here, because it is stated in the Dhātupāṭhas that the root 'kas' with the prefix 'saṃ' has the meaning of 'dwelling,' he says, 'vasissanti' (they will dwell). This root ends in 'e.' 'Nibaddhavāsa' (fixed dwelling) means permanent dwelling. 'Vassānanāmake' (named after the rains) refers to the season named 'vassāna' (rains). Although the rains season lasts four months, it is referred to as 'the three months.' Regarding 'vassūpanāyikā' (entering the rains), here, because the root 'nī' has the meaning of 'to go,' he says, 'vassūpagamanāni' (the goings to the rains). 'Aparajju' (the next day) means 'the day after the full moon,' thus 'aparajju'; the suffix 'jju' is in the sense of 'aha' (day); in meaning, it is the first day of the lunar fortnight. This word 'aparajju' is a particle in the nominative case. 'Assā' (of that) refers to the full moon of Āsaḷhī. This is a compound with an external referent in the sphere of different case relations; the connection is 'when it has passed.' 'Aparasmiṃ divase' (on the next day) means on the first day of the lunar fortnight. 'Assā' (of that) refers to the full moon of the month of Sāvaṇa. 'Tasmā' (therefore) means 'because it relates to the day after, and because it relates to the month, therefore.' By 'on the immediately following first day of the lunar fortnight' in the Pāli, he shows the meaning that the earlier rains retreat should be entered on the first day of the lunar fortnight immediately following the Āsaḷhī full moon. Similarly, in the latter method, it should be understood that the meaning is that the later rains retreat should be entered on the first day of the lunar fortnight immediately following the Āsaḷhī of the month. 'Āsaḷhiyā' means the full moon of Sāvaṇa, which is designated Āsaḷhī because it occurs near the Āsaḷhī full moon. The connection is that the rains retreat should be entered only on the first day of the lunar fortnight. In 'sakiṃ vā' (once or), etc., the word 'vā' has the meaning of an indefinite option. 'Nicchāretvā' means 'niccāretvā', that is, 'uccāretvā' (having uttered). Sometimes, a letter following an unarticulated consonant cluster becomes articulated, as in 'nikkhamati' (goes out), etc. Therefore, having changed the following 'c' to 'ch', it is said 'nicchāretvā'.

108. Vassānecārikāpaṭikkhepādikathā

108. The discussion beginning with the prohibition of wandering during the rains.

185. Āpatti veditabbāti anapekkhagamanena upacārātikkame sāpekkhagamanena aññattha aruṇuṭṭhāpane āpatti veditabbā. Vihāragaṇanāya āpattiyo veditabbāti ettha vassūpanāyikadivase vassaṃ anupagantukāmatācittena vihāraṃ atikkameyya, vihāragaṇanāya āpattiyo veditabbā. Tamevatthaṃ vitthārento āha “sace hī”tiādi. Taṃ divasanti tasmiṃ vassūpagamanadivase. Sataṃ āpattiyoti ettha satanti saṅkhyāpadhānattā ekavacananti saddasatthesu vuttaṃ[M 0.0317]. Ekā eva āpattīti attano vihārassa atikkamaneyeva ekā eva āpatti. Kenaci antarāyena anupagatenāti sambandho.

185. An offense should be understood thus: an offense is incurred by transgressing the precincts through heedless departure, or by the dawn rising elsewhere through a deliberate departure. Regarding 'offenses should be understood by the count of monasteries,' here, if one should transgress a monastery on the day of entering the rains with the thought of desiring not to enter the rains, offenses should be understood by the count of monasteries. Expounding on that very meaning, he said, 'If indeed...' and so forth. 'That day' means on that very day of entering the rains. Regarding 'a hundred offenses,' here, 'hundred' is singular because the number is primary, as stated in grammatical treatises. There is only one offense: a single offense is incurred by the very transgression of one's own monastery. The connection is: 'not having entered due to some impediment.'

Vassanāmo imassatthīti vassoti vacanatthaṃ dassento āha “vassanāmaka”nti. “Paṭhamaṃ māsa”nti iminā aññapadassa sarūpaṃ dasseti. Paṭhamaṃ māsanti catūsu vassamāsesu paṭhamaṃ māsaṃ. Ukkaḍḍhitukāmoti upari kaḍḍhitukāmo. Āsaḷhīmāsameva, na sāvaṇamāsanti attho. Juṇhasaddo candapabhāyutto māsoti āha “māse”ti. Candapabhāyutto māsoti āha “māse”ti. Candapabhāyutto hi māso jotati dippatīti juṇhoti vuccati. Tasmā “māse”ti sāmaññato vuttepi puṇṇamiyutto māsova gahetabbo. Kāci parihāni nāmāti kiñci sīlādīnaṃ hāyanaṃ nāma. Aññasmimpīti vassūpagamanato aññasmimpi. Dhammiketi dhammena yutte.

Explaining the meaning of the word 'vassa' as 'this has the name "vassa" (rain),' he says, 'vassanāmaka' (named after the rains). By 'the first month,' he shows the form of the other word. 'The first month' means the first month among the four rains-months. 'Ukkaḍḍhitukāmo' means desiring to draw upwards. The meaning is the month of Āsaḷhī alone, not the month of Sāvaṇa. The word 'juṇha' signifies a month endowed with moonlight, he says, 'in the month.' For a month endowed with moonlight shines and gleams, it is called 'juṇha.' Therefore, even when 'month' is stated generally, only a month connected with the full moon should be taken. 'Any decline' means some deterioration in virtue, and so forth. 'In another also' means in another case besides entering the rains. 'Dhammike' means endowed with the Dhamma.

109. Sattāhakaraṇīyānujānanakathā

109. Discussion on the Allowance for Seven-Day Duties

187. Sattāhakaraṇīyesu evaṃ vinicchayo veditabboti yojanā. “Sattāhakaraṇīyenā”ti padassa sattamīsamāsañca anīyasaddassa kammatthañca dassento āha “sattāhabbhantare yaṃ kattabba”nti[V 1.0271]. Tattha “sattāhabbhantare”ti iminā sattamīsamāsaṃ dasseti, “kattabba”nti iminā kammatthaṃ. “Sattāhabbhantare”ti iminā sattāhassa abbhantaraṃ sattāhanti uttarapadalopaṃ dasseti. Pahite gantunti ettha pahitesaddassa kattukammāni dassetuṃ vuttaṃ “bhikkhuādīhi dūte”ti. Tattha “bhikkhuādīhī”ti iminā kattāraṃ dasseti, “dūte”ti iminā kammaṃ. Sattāhanti ettha uttarapadalopañca bhummatthe upayogavacanañca dassento āha “antosattāheyevā”ti. Tatthevāti tasmiṃ pahitaṭṭhāneyeva. “Na uṭṭhāpetabbo”ti iminā “sattāheyevā”ti ettha evasaddassa phalaṃ dasseti.

187. Regarding seven-day duties, the decision should be understood thus; this is the connection. Regarding the phrase 'by a seven-day duty,' showing the locative compound and the objective sense of the suffix '-anīya,' he says, 'what is to be done within seven days.' Herein, 'within seven days' shows the locative compound, and 'to be done' shows the objective sense. By 'within seven days,' he shows the elision of the latter member of the compound, meaning 'the interior of seven days' is 'seven days.' In 'sent to go,' to show the agent and object of the word 'sent,' it is said, 'by monks and others as messengers.' Herein, 'by monks and others' shows the agent, and 'as messengers' shows the object. In 'seven days,' showing the elision of the latter member and the use of the locative case, he says, 'only within seven days.' 'There only' means in that very place to which one was sent. By 'should not be raised,' he shows the effect of the word 'only' in 'only within seven days.'

189. Raso etasmiṃ atthīti rasavatīti vutte bhattagehaṃ gahetabbanti āha “bhattagehaṃ vuccatī”ti. Bhattagehanti bhattapacanagehaṃ. Purāyaṃ suttantoti ettha purā ayanti padacchedaṃ katvā purāsaddo [M 0.0318] yāvapariyāyoti āha “yāva ayaṃ suttanto”ti. Na palujjatīti ettha lujadhātu vināsatthoti āha “na vinassatī”ti. Parisaṅkhatanti parisaṅkharitabbaṃ. Sabbatthāti sabbesu pahitesu. Imināva kappiyavacanenāti iminā eva kappiyena tivākyasaṅkhātena vacanena. Etesanti etesaṃ tiṇṇaṃ vākyānaṃ. Vevacanenāti “yaññañca yajituṃ, suttañca uggaṇhituṃ, samaṇe ca dassitu”nti pariyāyena. Sattasūti upāsaka upāsika bhikkhubhikkhunī sikkhamāna sāmaṇera sāmaṇerī saṅkhātāsu sattasu.

189. When it is said, 'It has taste,' meaning it is flavorful, it should be understood as the refectory; he says, 'the refectory is meant.' 'Refectory' means the house for cooking food. In 'this ancient discourse,' having separated the words as 'purā ayaṃ,' the word 'purā' is a synonym for 'yāva'; he says, 'as long as this discourse.' In 'it does not perish,' the root 'luj' has the meaning of destruction; he says, 'it does not get destroyed.' 'Parisaṅkhata' means 'should be prepared.' 'In all cases' means 'in all things sent.' 'By this very allowable statement' means by this very allowable statement consisting of three phrases. 'Of these' means of these three phrases. 'By alternative expression' means by the alternatives: 'to perform a sacrifice, to learn a discourse, and to see ascetics.' 'In the seven' means in the seven enumerated as: male lay follower, female lay follower, monk, nun, female probationer, male novice, and female novice.

110. Pañcannaṃ appahitepi anujānanakathā

110. A discussion on permission regarding the five, even when not sent.

193. Pageva pahiteti iminā “apahitepi gantabba”nti ettha pisaddassa sambhāvanatthaṃ dasseti. Pañcannaṃ sahadhammikānaṃ santikaṃ gantabbabhāvassa kāraṇaṃ vibhajitvā dassento āha “bhikkhu gilāno hotī”tiādi. Dasahīti “saṅgho kammaṃ kattukāmo hoti, kataṃ vā saṅghena kammaṃ hotī”ti idaṃ aṅgaṃ ekaṃ katvā dasahi. Navahīti parivāsārahaṃ apanetvā navahi. Catūhīti gilānaanabhiratikukkuccadiṭṭhigatauppannasaṅkhātehi catūhi. Iti imehi chahīti yojanā. Sāmaṇerassapi chahīti ettha channaṃ sarūpaṃ vitthāretvā dassento āha “ādito”tiādi. Taṃ suviññeyyameva. Sāmaṇeriyā santikaṃ pañcahi gantabbanti yojanā. Paratoti parasmā, parasmiṃ vā. Andhakaṭṭhakathāyaṃ vuttanti sambandho. Ye ñātakā vā ye aññātakā vā atthi, tesampīti yojanā. Tanti vacanaṃ.

193. By 'previously sent,' he shows that in the phrase 'one should go even if not sent,' the word 'pi' has the sense of possibility. Dividing and showing the reason for the state of having to go to the presence of the five co-religionists, he says, 'a monk is sick,' and so on. 'By ten' means by ten, having made this factor—'the Saṅgha wishes to perform a formal act, or a formal act has been performed by the Saṅgha'—one. 'By nine' means by nine, after removing the one deserving probation. 'By four' means by the four enumerated as: illness, discontent, scruples, and the arising of a wrong view. 'Thus, by these six' is the connection. In 'for a male novice also, by six,' explaining the nature of the six in detail, he says, 'from the beginning,' and so on. That is easily understood. 'One should go to a female novice for five reasons' is the connection. 'From another' means from another, or in another. 'It is said in the Andhaka Commentary' is the connection. 'Whoever are relatives or non-relatives, for them also' is the connection. That is the text.

112. Pahiteyevaanujānanakathā

112. A discussion on permission only in the case of one who is sent.

199. Bhikkhugatikoti [V 1.0272] bhikkhu eva gati patiṭṭhā etassāti bhikkhugatikoti vutte bhikkhunissitako purisoti āha “bhikkhūhi saddhiṃ vasanakapuriso”ti. Palujjatīti vinassati. Bhaṇḍaṃ chedāpitanti ettha bhaṇḍasaddo parikkhārattho eva, na mūladhanatthoti āha [M 0.0319] “dabbasambhārabhaṇḍa”nti. Chedāpitanti curādigaṇikadhātuṃ “chindāpita”nti rudhādigaṇikadhātuyā vaṇṇeti. Dajjāhanti ekāralopasandhīti āha “dajje aha”nti. “Dajjeha”ntipi pāṭho. Evañhi sati akāralopasandhi. Dajjeti dadeyyaṃ, dadāmi vā. Saṅghakaraṇīyenāti saṅghassa kātabbena kiccena. Tamatthaṃ dassento āha “yaṃkiñcī”tiādi. Tattha yaṃkiñci kātabbanti yojanā. Cetiyachattavedikādīsūti cetiyassa chatte ca vedikāya ca. Ādisaddena sudhālimpādayo saṅgaṇhāti. Tassāti saṅghakaraṇīyassa. Nipphādanatthaṃ gantabbanti sambandho.

199. 'One whose resort is the bhikkhu' means one for whom a bhikkhu is his resort and support; when 'bhikkhugatika' is said, it means a man dependent on a bhikkhu. He says, 'a man who lives with bhikkhus.' 'Palujjati' means it is destroyed. In 'having goods destroyed,' the word 'bhaṇḍa' has the meaning of requisites only, not the meaning of capital; thus he says, 'goods consisting of material supplies.' He explains 'chedāpita' by 'chindāpita.' 'Dajjāhaṃ' is a sandhi with the elision of one 'a'; thus he says, 'dajje ahaṃ.' There is also the reading 'dajjehaṃ'; in that case, it is a sandhi with the elision of the vowel 'a'. 'Dajje' means 'I would give' or 'I give.' 'By a duty for the Saṅgha' means by a task to be done for the Saṅgha. Showing its meaning, he says, 'whatever,' and so on. Herein, 'whatever is to be done' is the connection. 'In a cetiya's umbrella, railing, etc.' means on the umbrella of a cetiya and on its railing. By the word 'etc.,' he includes applying plaster and so on. 'Of that' means of the duty for the Saṅgha. 'One should go for the purpose of accomplishing' is the connection.

Etthāti vassūpanāyikakkhandhake. “Animantitenā”ti padaṃ “gantu”nti pade bhāvakattā. Gantunti gamituṃ, gamanaṃ vā “na vaṭṭatī”ti pade kattā. Paṭhamaṃyevāti dhammassavanato paṭhamameva. Sannipatitabbaṃ iti katikā katā hotīti yojanā. Bhaṇḍakanti cīvarādibhaṇḍakaṃ. Gantuṃ na vaṭṭatīti sayameva gantuṃ na vaṭṭatīti attho daṭṭhabbo. Tena vuttaṃ “sace panā”tiādi. Tatthāti taṃ vihāraṃ. “Vaṭṭatī”ti iminā vassacchedo ca āpatti ca na hotīti dasseti. Atthāyapīti pisaddena “bhaṇḍakaṃ dhovissāmī”ti atthaṃ apekkhati. Nanti antevāsikaṃ. Vaṭṭatīti ācariyassa āṇāya sattāhe anatikkante vaṭṭati, vassacchedo ca āpatti ca na hoti. Sattāhe atikkante vassacchedova hoti, na āpattīti adhippāyo.

'Here' means in the section on entering the rains-residence. The word 'by one who is uninvited' is the agent with respect to the word 'to go.' 'To go' means for going, or the going; it is the agent with respect to the phrase 'it is not allowable.' 'At the very first' means at the very first, before hearing the Dhamma. 'An agreement has been made that "one should assemble"' is the connection. 'Goods' means goods such as robes. The meaning 'it is not allowable for oneself to go' should be understood from 'it is not allowable to go.' For that reason it is said, 'but if,' and so on. 'There' means to that monastery. By 'it is allowable,' he shows that there is neither an interruption of the rains-residence nor an offense. 'For the purpose also': by the particle 'pi,' it refers to the purpose, 'I will wash the goods.' 'Him' means the resident pupil. 'It is allowable' means it is allowable by the teacher's command when seven days have not passed; there is neither an interruption of the rains-residence nor an offense. When seven days have passed, there is only an interruption of the rains-residence, not an offense; this is the intention.

113. Antarāye anāpattivassacchedakathā

113. A discussion on no offense and the interruption of the rains-residence in case of an obstacle.

201. Avidūreti āsanne. Tatthāti gāme. Sattāhavārenāti sattāhe ekavārena. Aruṇo uṭṭhāpetabboti vihāre aruṇo uṭṭhāpetabbo. Tatrevāti gāmeyeva. Mayanti bhikkhū sandhāya vuttaṃ. Puna mayanti manusse sandhāya vuttaṃ. Tesaṃyevāti vassacchedabhikkhūnaṃ eva. Tanti salākabhattādiṃ. Vassaggenāti vassagaṇanāya.

201. 'Not far' means nearby. 'There' means in the village. 'By a seven-day turn' means once in seven days. 'The dawn should be made to arise' means the dawn should be made to arise in the monastery. 'In that very place' means in that very village. 'We' is said with reference to the bhikkhus. 'Again, we' is said with reference to human beings. 'Of those very ones' means of those very bhikkhus whose rains-residence was interrupted. 'That' refers to ticket-food and so on. 'By the total of rains' means by the counting of rains.

Vassāvāsikanti [M 0.0320] vassāvāsānaṃ dātabbaṃ cīvaraṃ. Tatthāti tasmiṃ vihāre. Yesaṃ pāpitanti [V 1.0273] sambandho. Vihāreti vuṭṭhitagāmavihāre. Upanikkhittakaṃ bhaṇḍanti sambandho. Idhāti bhikkhuno nivāsaṭṭhāne. Yaṃ cīvarādivebhaṅgiyabhaṇḍaṃ atthi, tanti yojanā. Tatthevāti vuṭṭhitagāmavihāre eva. Itoti khettavatthuādito. Kappiyakārakānaṃ hattheti sambandho. Tatruppādepīti tassa vihārassa dinnakhettavatthuādito uppāde paccayepi. “Tattheva gantvā apaloketvā bhājetabba”nti vacanassa yuttiṃ dassento āha “saṅghikañhī”tiādi. Antovihāre vāti antosīmāya vā. Ubhayatthāti antosīmabahisīma saṅkhātesu dvīsu ṭhānesu ṭhitaṃ vebhaṅgiyabhaṇḍanti sambandho.

'Rains-residence-robe' means the robe to be given to those observing the rains-residence. 'Therein' means in that monastery. 'To whom it was brought' is the connection. 'In the monastery' means in the village-monastery from which one has departed. 'Deposited goods' is the connection. 'Here' means in the monk's dwelling place. 'Whatever goods, such as robes, are divisible, that' is the connection. 'In that very place' means in that very village-monastery from which one has departed. 'From this' means from fields, land, and so on. 'In the hands of the stewards' is the connection. 'Even in what is produced there' means even in the requisites produced from the fields, land, and so on, that were given to that monastery. Showing the reason for the statement, 'Having gone to that very place and obtained consent, it should be divided,' he says, 'for it belongs to the Saṅgha,' and so on. 'Within the monastery, or' means within the boundary, or. 'In both places' is connected with 'the divisible goods situated in the two places designated as inside the boundary and outside the boundary.'

114. Saṅghabhede anāpattivassacchedakathā

114. A discussion on no offense and the interruption of the rains-residence in case of a schism in the Saṅgha.

202. Bhinnoti ettha tapaccayassa atītatthe ayuttabhāvaṃ dassento āha “bhinne saṅghe karaṇīyaṃ natthī”ti. Yo panāti saṅgho pana. Idaṃ “bhijjissatī”tipade kattā, “āsaṅkito”tipade kammaṃ. “Bhijjissatī”ti iminā bhinnoti ettha tapaccayassa anāgatatthe pavattabhāvaṃ dasseti. Bhikkhunīhi saṅgho bhinnoti ettha kiṃ bhikkhunīhi saṅgho bhinnoti daṭṭhabboti āha “na bhikkhunīhi saṅgho bhinnoti daṭṭhabbo”ti. Etanti bhikkhunīhi abhinnabhāvaṃ. Etā panāti bhikkhuniyo pana. Tanti saṅghaṃ. Etanti “sambahulāhi bhikkhunīhi saṅgho bhinno”ti vacanaṃ.

202. Here, showing the unsuitability of the past tense meaning of the 'ta' suffix in 'bhinno', he said: 'When the Saṅgha is split, there is nothing to be done.' 'Yo pana' means 'the Saṅgha.' This is the agent in the word 'bhijjissati' and the object in the word 'āsaṅkito.' By 'bhijjissati,' he indicates that the 'ta' suffix in 'bhinno' here has the sense of the future tense. Regarding 'the Saṅgha is split by the bhikkhunīs,' he asks whether it should be understood that the Saṅgha is split by the bhikkhunīs, and states: 'The Saṅgha should not be understood as split by the bhikkhunīs.' 'This' refers to the state of not being split by the bhikkhunīs. 'Etā pana' means 'the bhikkhunīs.' 'That' refers to the Saṅgha. 'This' refers to the statement: 'The Saṅgha is split by numerous bhikkhunīs.'

115. Vajādīsu vassūpagamanakathā

115. The Account of Undertaking the Rains Residence in Vajji and So Forth

203. “Gopālakānaṃ nivāsaṭṭhāna”nti iminā gopālakā gāvo viya vaje nivasantīti dasseti.

203. ‘The dwelling place of cowherds’—by this it is shown that cowherds dwell in enclosures like cattle.

Upakaṭṭhasaddo āsannapariyāyoti āha “āsannāyā”ti. Tatthāti kuṭikāyaṃ. Idhāti imissaṃ kuṭikāyaṃ. Avihārattā “idhāti”sāmaññavasena vuttaṃ. Tikkhattunti idaṃ ukkaṭṭhavasena vuttaṃ. Heṭṭhā hi “sakiṃ vā dvikkhattuṃ vā tikkhattuṃ vā”ti (mahāva. aṭṭha. 184) vuttattā sakimpi vaṭṭatīti daṭṭhabbaṃ. Tampīti [M 0.0321] sālāsaṅkhepena ṭhitasakaṭampi. “Ālayo”ti iminā “idha vassaṃ upemī”ti vacībhedo na kātabboti dasseti. Ālayoti ca satthe “idha vassaṃ vasissāmī”ti cittassa allīyanaṃ. Maggapaṭipanneyeva sattheti anādare bhummavacanaṃ. Tatthevāti sattheyeva. Sattho atikkamatīti sambandho. Tatthāti patthitaṭṭhāne. Vippakiratīti visuṃ visuṃ gacchati[V 1.0274]. Sace agāmake ṭhāne vippakirati, purimaṃ gāmaṃ sannivattitabbaṃ. Na aññagāmaṃ gantabbaṃ. Tatoti gāmato.

The word ‘upakaṭṭha’ is a synonym for ‘nearby,’ thus it is said ‘āsannāya.’ ‘Tattha’ means ‘in the hut.’ ‘Idha’ means ‘in this hut.’ Since it is not a dwelling, ‘idha’ is stated in a general sense. ‘Tikkhattuṃ’ (thrice) is stated in the sense of the maximum. For since it is stated below, ‘once, or twice, or thrice’ (Mahāva. Aṭṭha. 184), it should be understood that even once is permissible. ‘Tampi’ (that too) refers even to a cart standing for a short time in a hall. By ‘ālayo’ (attachment), it is shown that a verbal declaration, ‘I will undertake the Rains residence here,’ should not be made. And ‘ālayo’ in the context of a caravan is the mind’s clinging, ‘I will dwell here for the Rains.’ ‘Maggapaṭipanneyeva satthe’ is a locative of disregard. ‘Tattheva’ (right there) means ‘in the caravan itself.’ The connection is ‘the caravan moves on.’ ‘Tattha’ (there) means ‘in the desired place.’ ‘Vippakirati’ means ‘goes separately.’ If the caravan disperses in a place without a village, one should return to the previous village. One should not go to another village. ‘Tato’ (from that) means ‘from the village.’

Upagantabbanti “idha vassaṃ upemī”ti tikkhattuṃ vatvā upagantabbaṃ. Tatthevāti samuddeyeva. Kūlanti tīraṃ. Tañhi kulati udakaṃ āvaratīti kūlanti vuccati. Ayañcāti nāvāyaṃ vassūpagamanabhikkhu. Anutīramevāti anukkamena, anusārena vā tīrameva. Aññatthāti paṭhamaladdhagāmato aññasmiṃ ṭhāne. Tatthevāti paṭhamaladdhagāmeyeva.

‘One should undertake’ means one should undertake after saying thrice, ‘I will undertake the Rains residence here.’ ‘Tattheva’ (right there) means ‘in the sea itself.’ ‘Kūla’ means ‘bank.’ For it is called ‘kūla’ because it obstructs (kulati) or holds back (āvarati) the water. ‘Ayañca’ (and this) refers to the monk undertaking the Rains residence in a boat. ‘Anutīrameva’ (along the shore only) means ‘successively’ or ‘following the shore itself.’ ‘Aññattha’ (elsewhere) means ‘in a place other than the village first obtained.’ ‘Tattheva’ (right there) means ‘in the very village first obtained.’

Itītiādi nigamanaṃ. Pavāretuñca labhatīti ettha casaddo vākyasampiṇḍanattho. Purimesu ca panāti ettha casaddo byatirekattho, panasaddo visesatthajotako. Anāpatti hotīti anāpattimattameva hoti.

‘Iti’ and so forth is the conclusion. In ‘and one is allowed to invite,’ the word ‘ca’ has the meaning of connecting sentences. In ‘but in the earlier cases,’ the word ‘ca’ has the meaning of contrast, and the word ‘pana’ indicates a special meaning. ‘There is no offense’ means there is merely no offense.

116. Vassaṃ anupagantabbaṭṭhānakathā

116. The Account of Places Where the Rains Residence Should Not Be Undertaken

204. Rukkhasusīreyevāti rukkhassa vivare eva. Vivarañhi su saṃ irati gacchatīti susīroti vuccati. Padaracchadananti phalakehi chāditaṃ. Pavisanadvāranti pavisananikkhamanadvāraṃ. Pavisanañca nikkhamanañca pavisananti virūpekasesena kātabbaṃ. Khāṇumatthaketi khāṇuno upari. Viṭabhīti viṭaṃ aññamaññavedhanaṃ apati gacchatīti viṭapo, pakārassa bhakāraṃ, itthiliṅgajotakaīpaccayañca katvā viṭabhīti vuccati. Tatthāti aṭṭake. Yassāti bhikkhuno, natthīti sambandho. Pañcannaṃ chadanānanti tiṇapaṇṇaiṭṭhakāsilāsudhāsaṅkhātānaṃ (cūḷava. 303) pañcannaṃ chadanānaṃ. Idañca yebhuyyavasena vuttaṃ padaracchadanādīnampi gahitattā. Dvārabandhananti dvārena bandhitabbaṃ. Chavakuṭikāti chavānaṃ sayanaṭṭhāne susāne katā kuṭikā chavakuṭikāti vuccati. Ṭaṅkitamañcādītiādisaddena [M 0.0322] ṭaṅkitapīṭhaṃ saṅgaṇhāti. Tatthāti chavakuṭiyaṃ. Aññaṃ kuṭikanti chavakuṭito aññaṃ kuṭikaṃ. Āvaraṇanti bhittiṃ. Dvāranti pavisananikkhamanadvāraṃ. Chattakuṭikā nāmesāti esā chattena katā kuṭikā nāma. Mahantena kapallena kuṭikaṃ katvāti sambandho.

204. ‘In the hollow of a tree’ means ‘in the cavity of a tree itself.’ For a cavity is called ‘susīra’ because it moves (`irati`) well (`su`) together (`saṃ`). ‘Plank-covered’ means ‘covered with planks.’ ‘A door for entry’ means ‘a door for entering and exiting.’ ‘Pavisana’ (entry) should be understood by way of virūpekasesa (retention of one form for two dissimilar ones) to include both entering and exiting. ‘At the top of a post’ means ‘above a post.’ A branch, `viṭapo`, is so called because it goes forth (`apati gacchati`) piercing one another (`aññamaññavedhanaṃ`); by changing the ‘p’ to ‘bh’ and adding the feminine suffix ‘ī’, it is called `viṭabhī`. ‘Tattha’ (there) means ‘on the platform.’ ‘Yassa’ (for whom) refers to a monk, and the connection is ‘there is not.’ ‘Of the five kinds of roofing’ refers to the five types of roofing, namely, thatch, leaves, tiles, stone, and plaster (Cūḷavagga 303). And this is stated by way of generalization, as plank roofing and others are also included. ‘Door-fastening’ means ‘that which is to be fastened by a door.’ ‘A charnel hut’ is so called because it is a hut made in a cemetery, a resting place for corpses. ‘A hanging bed, etc.’—the word ‘etc.’ includes a hanging bench. ‘Tattha’ (there) means ‘in the charnel hut.’ ‘Another hut’ means ‘a hut other than the charnel hut.’ ‘A screen’ means ‘a wall.’ ‘A door’ means ‘a door for entering and exiting.’ ‘This is called a parasol-hut’—this is a hut made with a parasol. The connection is ‘having made a hut with a large potsherd.’

117. Adhammikakatikākathā

117. The Account of Unlawful Agreements

205. Aññāpīti “antarāvassaṃ na pabbājetabba”nti katikāya aññāpi. Katikā hotīti [V 1.0275] sambandho. Tassāti adhammikakatikāya. Vuttanti catutthapārājikavaṇṇanāyaṃ (pārā. aṭṭha. 2.226) vuttaṃ.

205. ‘Also another’ refers to another agreement, such as ‘one should not give the going forth during the Rains residence.’ The connection is ‘there is an agreement.’ ‘Tassa’ (of that) means ‘of the unlawful agreement.’ ‘Stated’ refers to what was stated in the commentary on the fourth Pārājika (Pārājika Aṭṭhakathā 2.226).

118. Paṭissavadukkaṭāpattikathā

118. The Account of the Offense of Wrongdoing Through Assent

207. Paṭissave āpatti dukkaṭassāti ettha kiṃ vassāvāsapaṭissuteyeva dukkaṭāpatti hotīti āha “na kevala”ntiādi. Etassevāti vassāvāsasseva. Evamādināpīti pisaddo “paṭissave”ti ettha yojetabbo. “Paṭissavepī”ti hi attho. Tassa tassāti kammassa. Tañca khoti tañca dukkaṭaṃ visaṃvādanapaccayā hotīti yojanā. Paṭhamampīti pisaddo “pacchāpī”ti padaṃ sampiṇḍeti. Paṭhamampi hi pācittiyaṃ, pacchāpi dukkaṭanti attho.

207. Regarding ‘an offense of wrongdoing for assent,’ the question is asked whether the offense of wrongdoing occurs only in the case of assent regarding the Rains residence. It is said, ‘Not only,’ and so forth. ‘Of that very’ means ‘of the Rains residence itself.’ Regarding ‘and so on also,’ the word ‘pi’ should be connected here with ‘for assent.’ For the meaning is ‘also in the case of assent.’ ‘Of that, of that’ refers to the respective action. And ‘that indeed’—the connection is that that wrongdoing arises on account of deceit. Regarding ‘even the first also,’ the word ‘pi’ combines with the word ‘later also.’ For the meaning is that the first is a Pācittiya offense, and later is also a wrongdoing.

So tadaheva akaraṇīyotiādīsu evaṃ vinicchayo veditabboti yojanā. Purimikā ca na paññāyatīti ettha pure bhavā purimā, sā eva purimikā, pāṭipadatithī. Nānāsīmāya dvīsu āvāsesu vassaṃ upagacchantassa dutiye “vasissāmī”ti paṭhamāvāsassa upacārato nikkhantamatte paṭhamasenāsanaggāhassa passambhanaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ “purimikā ca na paññāyatī”ti. Aruṇaṃ anuṭṭhāpetvāti vassaṃ upagamanavihāre aruṇaṃ anuṭṭhāpetvā. Tadahevāti tasmiṃ vassūpagamanaahani eva, pakkantassāpīti sambandho. Pisaddassa garahatthaṃ dassento āha “ko pana vādo”tiādi. Ālayoti cittassa allīyanaṃ. Asatiyāti satipamuṭṭhena. Vassaṃ na upetīti “imasmiṃ vihāre imaṃ temāsaṃ vassaṃ upemī”ti (mahāva. aṭṭha. 184) vacībhedaṃ katvā vassaṃ na upeti.

In ‘that is not to be done on that very day,’ and so forth, the connection is that the decision should be understood thus. In ‘and the previous one is not apparent,’ `purimā` is what was before, and that very one is `purimikā`, the first day of the lunar fortnight. In the case of one undertaking the Rains residence in two monasteries with different boundaries, upon merely leaving the precincts of the first monastery and declaring in the second, ‘I will dwell here,’ the phrase ‘and the previous one is not apparent’ is stated with reference to the cessation of the taking of the first lodging. ‘Not having let the dawn arise’ means not having let the dawn arise in the monastery where one undertakes the Rains residence. ‘On that very day’ means on the very day of undertaking the Rains residence; the connection is ‘even for one who has departed.’ Showing the meaning of censure of the word ‘pi,’ he says, ‘what more to say,’ and so forth. ‘Ālayo’ (attachment) means the mind’s clinging. ‘Due to lack of mindfulness’ means ‘due to loss of mindfulness.’ ‘One does not undertake the Rains residence’ means one does not undertake the Rains residence after having made the verbal declaration, ‘In this monastery, I will undertake the Rains residence for these three months’ (Mahāva. Aṭṭha. 184).

Sattāhanti [M 0.0323] sattāhena, anāgatāyāti sambandho. Navamitoti pubbakattikamāsassa juṇhapakkhanavamito, pacchimakattikamāsassa juṇhapakkhanavamito vā. Mā vā āgacchatu, anāpattīti vassaṃvutthattā mā vā āgacchatu, anāpattīti attho.

‘Seven days’ means ‘within seven days’; the connection is with ‘not yet come.’ ‘From the ninth’ means from the ninth day of the bright fortnight of the earlier Kattika month, or from the ninth day of the bright fortnight of the later Kattika month. ‘Or let him not come, there is no offense’—because he has completed the Rains residence, the meaning is, ‘Even if he does not come, there is no offense.’

Iti vassūpanāyikakkhandhakavaṇṇanāya yojanā samattā.

Thus, the exposition of the commentary on the Chapter on Undertaking the Rains Residence is completed.

4. Pavāraṇākkhandhakaṃ

4. The Chapter on the Invitation

120. Aphāsukavihārakathā

120. The Discourse on Uncomfortable Dwelling

209. Pavāraṇākkhandhake [V 1.0276] allāpoti ettha ātyūpasaggassa ādikammatthaṃ, lapadhātuyā ca kathanatthaṃ dassento āha “paṭhamavacana”nti. Ādito, ādimhi vā lapanaṃ kathanaṃ, lapati anenāti vā allāpo saṃyoge pare rasso. Saṃ puna lapanaṃ, lapati vā anenāti sallāpo. Hatthavilaṅghakenāti ettha vipubbo laghidhātu ukkhipanatthoti āha “hatthukkhepakenā”ti. Pasusaṃvāsanti ettha pasūti sabbacatuppadā. Te hi aññamaññaṃ pasanti bādhanti, manussādīhi vā pasīyanti bādhīyantīti pasavoti vuccanti. Pasūnaṃ viya saṃvāsanti pasūnaṃ saṃvāso viya saṃvāsoti pasusaṃvāso, taṃ pasusaṃvāsaṃ. Tamatthaṃ vitthārento āha “pasavopi hī”tiādi. Tathāti yathā na karonti, tathāti attho. Etepīti bhikkhavopi. Tasmāti yasmā akaṃsu, tasmā. Nesanti bhikkhūnaṃ. Sabbatthāti sabbesu eḷakasaṃvāsasapattasaṃvāsesu. Mūgabbatanti mūgassa vataṃ viya vatanti mūgabbataṃ, suññavacanavatanti attho. Titthiyasamādānanti titthiyehi samādātabbaṃ. Vatasamādānanti samādātabbaṃ vataṃ. Aññamaññānulomatāti ettha tāsaddassa bhāvatthaṃ dassento āha “anulomabhāvo”ti. Iminā “devatā”tiādīsu (saṃ. ni. aṭṭha. 1.1.1; khu. pā. aṭṭha. 5.evamiccādipāṭhavaṇṇanā; su. ni. aṭṭha. 2.aṅgalasuttavaṇṇanā) viya tāpaccayassa svatthaṃ “janatā”tiādīsu (pe. va. aṭṭha. 460) viya samūhatthañca nivatteti. “Aññamaññaṃ vattu”nti vacanassa yuttiṃ [M 0.0324] dassento āha “vadantu ma”ntiādi. Vadantaṃ bhikkhuṃ vattunti yojanā. “Āpattīhi vuṭṭhānabhāvo”ti iminā āpattivuṭṭhānatāti padassa pañcamīsamāsañca tāpaccayassa bhāvatthañca dasseti. “Vinaya”ntiādinā purato katvā karaṇaṃ purekkhāro, tassa bhāvo purekkhāratā, vinayaṃ purekkhāratā vinayapurekkhāratāti vacanatthaṃ dasseti. Ettha purasaddassa ekārattaṃ saddasatthesu (moggallānabyākaraṇe 5.134 sutte) vadanti. Tassa yuttiṃ dassento āha “vadantuma”ntiādi (moggallānabyākaraṇe 5.134 sutte).

209. In the Pavāraṇā Chapter, regarding 'allāpo', here, showing the meaning of the prefix 'ā' as 'initial action' and the root 'lap' as 'speaking', he says 'first utterance.' From the beginning, or at the start, speaking is 'lapanaṃ'; or, 'allāpo' is that by which one speaks, with the vowel shortened when a conjunct consonant follows. Again, 'sallāpo' is conversation, or that by which one speaks together. Regarding 'hatthavilaṅghakena', here, explaining that the root 'laghi' with the prefix 'vi' means 'lifting up', he says 'with the lifting up of the hand.' Regarding 'pasusaṃvāsa', here 'pasu' means all quadrupeds. For they harm one another, or are harmed by humans and others, therefore they are called 'pasavo'. Living together like animals, or an association like that of animals, is 'pasusaṃvāso'; that 'pasusaṃvāsaṃ'. Expanding on that meaning, he says, 'for 'pasavo' also...' etc. 'Tathā' means 'as they do not do.' 'Etepi' means 'these monks also.' 'Tasmā' means 'because they did, therefore.' 'Nesaṃ' means 'of the monks.' 'Sabbattha' means 'in all,' in all associations with goats and associations with rivals. 'Mūgabbataṃ' means a vow like the vow of a mute person; the meaning is a vow of refraining from speech. 'Titthiyasamādānaṃ' means that which is to be undertaken by sectarians. 'Vatasamādānaṃ' means a vow to be undertaken. Regarding 'aññamaññānulomatā', here, showing the meaning of the suffix '-tā' as 'state', he says 'the state of being compliant.' By this, he excludes the reflexive meaning of the suffix '-tā', as in instances like 'devatā' (Saṃyutta Nikāya Aṭṭhakathā 1.1.1; Khuddakapāṭha Aṭṭhakathā 5, explanation of such readings as 'evamiccādi'; Sutta Nipāta Aṭṭhakathā 2, explanation of the Aṅgalasutta), and also its collective meaning, as in 'janatā' (Peṭakopadesa Aṭṭhakathā 460). To show the rationale of the phrase 'aññamaññaṃ vattuṃ', he says, 'vadantu maṃ', etc. The construction is: one should speak to the monk who is speaking. By 'āpattīhi vuṭṭhānabhāvo', he shows both that the word 'āpattivuṭṭhānatā' is a fifth-case compound and that the suffix '-tā' has the meaning of 'state'. By 'vinaya', etc., he explains the meaning of the expression: 'purekkhāro' is the act of placing something foremost; the state of that is 'purekkhāratā'; therefore, 'vinayapurekkhāratā' is placing the Vinaya foremost. Here, in the grammatical treatises, they say that the word 'pura' has a single 'ra' (as in Moggallāna’s Grammar 5.134). To show the rationale for this, he says, 'vadantu maṃ', etc. (Moggallāna’s Grammar 5.134).

210. Sabbasaṅgāhikāti “saṅgho pavāreyyā”ti sāmaññato vuttattā sabbesaṃ tevācikādīnaṃ saṅgāhakā. Ñattīti ñāpeti saṅghaṃ etāya vacanāyāti ñatti. Sabbasaṅgāhikabhāvaṃ [V 1.0277] vitthārento āha “evañhi vutte”tiādi. Tevācikanti tisso vācā etassāti tevācikaṃ, tīhi vācāhi kattabbanti vā tevācikaṃ. Eseva nayo sesesupi. Samānavassikanti samānaṃ vassaṃ etesanti samānavassā, tehi kattabbanti samānavassikaṃ. Aññanti dvevācikaekavācikaṃ.

210. 'Sabbasaṅgāhikā' means that because 'the Saṅgha should invite' is stated generally, it is inclusive of all, such as those requiring three utterances, etc. 'Ñatti' is so called because by this statement one informs the Saṅgha. Expanding on the state of being all-inclusive, he says, 'for when it is said thus,' etc. 'Tevācikaṃ' means that which has three utterances, or that which is to be done with three utterances. This same method applies to the rest. 'Samānavassikaṃ' means: those who have the same rains-residence are 'samānavassā'; that which is to be done by them is 'samānavassikaṃ'. 'Aññaṃ' refers to that which requires two utterances or one utterance.

211. Acchantīti ettha āsadhātuyā upavesanatthaṃ dassento āha “nisinnāva hontī”ti. “Na uṭṭhahantī”ti iminā evaphalaṃ dasseti. Tadamantarāti ettha “tadantarā”ti vattabbe vācāsiliṭṭhavasena makārāgamaṃ katvā vuttanti āha “tadantarā”ti. Tassa attano pavāritakālassa antarā. “Yāva pavārentī”ti padassa niyamatthaṃ dassetuṃ vuttaṃ “tāvatakaṃ kāla”nti. Yāvāti nipātassa payogattā “tadamantarā”ti ettha abhividhiavadhyatthe pañcamīvibhatti hotīti daṭṭhabbaṃ.

211. Regarding 'acchanti', here, showing the meaning of the root 'ās' as 'sitting down', he says, 'they remain seated.' By 'they do not rise', he shows the result of that. Regarding 'tadamantarā', here—where 'tadantarā' should be said—it is stated with the insertion of the letter 'm' for the sake of euphony; thus he says 'tadantarā'. This means in the interval before one's own time of invitation. To show the limiting sense of the phrase 'yāva pavārenti', it is said, 'for that duration.' Because of the use of the particle 'yāva', it should be understood that here in 'tadamantarā', the fifth case ending has the meaning of an inclusive limit.

121. Pavāraṇābhedakathā

121. Discussion on the Division of Pavāraṇā

212. Cātuddasikāyāti bhaṇḍanakārakehi upaddutattā paccukkaḍḍhitāya pubbakattikamāsassa kāḷapakkhacātuddasikāya. “Ajja pavāraṇā pannarasī”ti pubbakiccaṃ kātabbanti yojanā.

212. 'Cātuddasikāya' means on the fourteenth day of the dark fortnight of the first Kattika month, which was postponed because of troubles caused by quarrelsome monks. The construction is: 'Today is the Pavāraṇā, the fifteenth,' implying that preliminary duties should be done.

Pavāraṇākammesūti [M 0.0325] niddhāraṇe bhummaṃ, “adhammena vaggaṃ pavāraṇākamma”ntiādīsu sambandhitabbaṃ. Adhammena vagganti ettha adhammaṃ nāma saṅgho hutvāpi saṅghapavāraṇamakatvā gaṇapavāraṇāya karaṇaṃ, gaṇo hutvāpi gaṇapavāraṇamakatvā saṅghapavāraṇāya karaṇañca. Vaggaṃ nāma ekasīmāyaṃ vasantānampi sabbesaṃ ekato asannipatanaṃ.

Regarding 'pavāraṇākammesu', the locative case is used for specification; it should be connected with phrases like 'an unlawful group invitation procedure', etc. Here, 'adhammena vaggaṃ' refers to what is unlawful: for a Saṅgha to perform a group invitation instead of a Saṅgha invitation, or for a group to perform a Saṅgha invitation instead of a group invitation. 'Vaggaṃ' means the failure of all to assemble together, even though residing within the same boundary.

Adhammena samagganti ettha adhammaṃ vuttanayameva. Samaggaṃ nāma sabbesaṃ ekato sannipatanaṃ.

Regarding 'adhammena samaggaṃ', here 'adhammaṃ' is as explained above. 'Samaggaṃ' means the assembling together of all in one place.

Dhammena vagganti ettha dhammaṃ nāma saṅgho hutvā saṅghapavāraṇāya karaṇaṃ, gaṇo hutvā gaṇapavāraṇāya karaṇañca. Vaggaṃ vuttanayameva. Dhammena samaggaṃ suviññeyyameva. Itisaddo parisamāpanattho.

Regarding 'dhammena vaggaṃ', here 'dhammaṃ' means for a Saṅgha to perform a Saṅgha invitation, and for a group to perform a group invitation. 'Vaggaṃ' is as explained before. 'Dhammena samaggaṃ' is easily understood. The word 'iti' serves to conclude the passage.

213. Evaṃ dinnāyāti evaṃ pāḷiyaṃ vuttanayeneva dinnāya. Pavāretabbanti vassaṃvutthapavāraṇāya [V 1.0278] pavāretabbaṃ. Tissoti tissanāmako. Diṭṭhena vā vadatūti sambandho. Tanti tissanāmakaṃ bhikkhuṃ. Saṅgho anukampaṃ upādāya vadatūti yojanā. Vuḍḍhataroti pavāraṇādāyako taṃhārakato vuḍḍhataro. Hīti laddhaguṇo. Tenāti pavāraṇāhārakena. Tassāti pavāraṇādāyakassa.

213. 'Thus given' means given according to the manner stated in the Pāḷi. 'Should be invited' means one should be invited with the pavāraṇā after having dwelt for the rains. 'Tissa' means one named Tissa. The connection is: 'let him speak by what is seen.' 'Him' refers to the monk named Tissa. The construction is: 'The Saṅgha, out of compassion, should speak.' 'The elder' means the one who gives the pavāraṇā is elder than the one who conveys it. 'Hī' means one who has obtained qualities. 'By him' refers to the one who conveys the pavāraṇā. 'For him' refers to the one who gives the pavāraṇā.

Idhāpi cāti imasmiṃ pavāraṇākkhandhakepi ca. Apisaddo uposathakkhandhakaṃ apekkhati. Avasesakammatthāyāti pavāraṇākammato avasesānaṃ kammānamatthāya hotīti sambandho. Pavāraṇāya āhaṭāya satiyāti yojanā. Tassa cāti pavāraṇādāyakassa ca. Sabbesanti pavāraṇādāyakassa ca saṅghassa cāti sabbesaṃ. Aññaṃ pana kammanti pavāraṇākammato aññaṃ kammaṃ pana. Tena pana bhikkhunāti pavāraṇādāyakena bhikkhunā pana. Ettha ca tadahupavāraṇāya attano ca saṅghassa ca sace pavāraṇākammameva hoti, pavāraṇāyeva dātabbā. Atha aññameva kammaṃ hoti, chandoyeva dātabbo. Yadi pavāraṇākammañca aññakammañca hoti, pavāraṇā ca chando ca dātabbo[M 0.0326]. Taṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ “tadahu pavāraṇāya pavāraṇaṃ dentena chandampi dātu”nti (mahāva. 213). Tenāti dānahetunā.

'Here too' means in this Pavāraṇā Chapter as well. The word 'api' (also) refers back to the Uposatha Chapter. 'For the remaining formal acts'—the connection is that it is for the sake of formal acts remaining apart from the pavāraṇā act. 'When the pavāraṇā has been brought' is the construction. 'For him too' refers to the one who gives the pavāraṇā as well. 'For all' means for all, that is, for both the one who gives the pavāraṇā and the Saṅgha. 'But another formal act' refers to another formal act other than the pavāraṇā act. 'But by that monk' refers to the monk who gives the pavāraṇā. Here, on the day of the pavāraṇā, concerning oneself and the Saṅgha, if it is only the pavāraṇā act to be done, only the pavāraṇā should be given. If there is another formal act, only consent should be given. If there is both the pavāraṇā act and another formal act, both the pavāraṇā and consent should be given. With reference to this, it is said: 'On the day of the pavāraṇā, one giving the pavāraṇā should also give consent' (Mahāva. 213). 'Tena' means for that reason of giving.

218. Ajja me pavāraṇāti ettha pāḷinayato aññaṃ aṭṭhakathānayaṃ dassento āha “sace”tiādi.

218. Regarding 'Today is my pavāraṇā', here, showing a commentarial method different from that of the Pāḷi, he says, 'if,' etc.

219. Vuttanayamevāti uposathakkhandhake (mahāva. aṭṭha. 169) vuttanayameva.

219. 'Just as stated' means just as stated in the Uposatha Chapter (Mahāva. Aṭṭha. 169).

222. Puna pavāretabbanti ettha na kevalaṃ pavāraṇāyeva puna kātabbā, pubbakiccādīnipi puna kātabbānīti dassento āha “puna pubbakicca”ntiādi.

222. Regarding 'Should invite again', here, showing that not only the pavāraṇā but also the preliminary duties, etc., should be repeated, he says, 'again the preliminary duties,' etc.

228. Eseva nayoti “ajja pavāraṇā pannarasī”ti pubbakiccaṃ atidisati. Assāti vacanassa. Ñattinti “suṇātu me bhante saṅgho ajja pavāraṇā”ti ñattiṃ. Pacchimehīti pacchimavassaṃ upagatehi bhikkhūhi. Uposathaggeti uposathassa gaṇhanaṭṭhāne gehe. Dve ñattiyoti pavāraṇāñatti ca uposathañatti cāti dve ñattiyo. Idañcāti idaṃ vakkhamānaṃ pana. Etthāti purimikapacchimikabhikkhūnaṃ saṃsaggaṭṭhāne. Purimikāya upagatehīti vibhattaapādānaṃ anumeyyavisayaapādānaṃ, thokatarāti sambandho, sahādiyogo vā, samasamāti sambandho. Samasamāti samena, samato vā samā samasamā, atirekasamāti attho. Kiñci ūnaṃ vā adhikaṃ vā natthīti adhippāyo. Itīti idaṃ lakkhaṇaṃ.

228.
