'Pākatikacuṇṇaṃpi' means also powder from sweepings. 'Etaṃpi' means also ordinary powder.

Tanti āmakamaṃsaṃ, na khādīti sambandho. Tanti āmakalohitaṃ vā, na pivīti sambandho. Amanussoti manussasadiso bhūto. Tanti āmakamaṃsalohitaṃ.

'Taṃ' means raw meat; the connection is with 'na khādi' (he did not eat). Or, 'taṃ' means raw blood; the connection is with 'na pivi' (he did not drink). 'Amanusso' means a being similar to a human. 'Taṃ' means raw meat and blood.

265. “Añjana”nti nāmaṃ sāmaññanti āha “añjananti sabbasaṅgāhakavacanameta”nti. Sabbasaṅgāhakavacananti sabbesaṃ añjanānaṃ saṅgāhakavacanaṃ. Etanti “añjana”nti etaṃ vacanaṃ. Añjati cakkhuṃ makkheti anenāti añjanaṃ, añjati cakkhuṃ byattaṃ karotīti vā añjanaṃ, tālujo tatiyakkharo. Kapallanti kapalle pavattaṃ. Kapālañhi dīpasikhāya upari nikujjitvā tattha pavattaṃ masi “kapalla”nti vuccati. Tamatthaṃ dassento āha “dīpasikhato gahitamasī”ti. Añjanūpapisanehīti ettha añjanehi saddhiṃ upanetuṃ pisitabbanti añjanūpapisananti vacanatthaṃ dassento āha “añjanena saddhiṃ ekato pisitehī”ti. “Ekato”ti iminā “saddhi”nti padasseva atthaṃ dasseti. Hīti saccaṃ. Yaṃkiñci añjanūpapisanaṃ cuṇṇaṃ na na vaṭṭatīti yojanā. Atha vā na vaṭṭati na hoti, vaṭṭatiyevāti yojanā. Imasmiṃ naye “na vaṭṭatī”ti ākhyātapadaṃ kiriyāntarāpekkhattā kattā hoti. Ākhyātesupi hi kattuttañca kammattañca labbhati. Candanantiādīni suviññeyyāneva.

265. 'Añjana' is a general name; therefore he said, 'añjanaṃ is this comprehensive term.' 'Sabbasaṅgāhakavacanaṃ' means a term comprehensive of all añjanas. 'Etaṃ' means this word 'añjana.' 'Añjana' is that by which one anoints, that is, smears, the eye; or, it makes the eye clear, hence 'añjana.' The third letter is a palatal. 'Kapallaṃ' means that which is produced on a potsherd. For, when a potsherd is inverted over a lamp flame, the soot produced there is called 'kapallaṃ.' Showing that meaning, he said 'soot taken from a lamp flame.' Here, regarding 'añjanūpapisanehi,' to show the etymological meaning of 'añjanūpapisanaṃ' as 'that which is ground to be brought near with collyrium,' he said 'ground together with collyrium.' By 'ekato,' he shows the meaning of the word 'saddhiṃ.' 'Hi' means truly. The connection is: whatever powder for grinding with collyrium is not unsuitable. Alternatively, the connection is: 'na vaṭṭati' means it is not that it is unsuitable; it is indeed suitable. In this method, the finite verb 'na vaṭṭati,' because of its dependence on another action, becomes the agent. For in finite verbs, both agent-hood and object-hood are found. 'Candana' and so on are easily understood.

Aṭṭhimayanti [M 0.0346] padassa atibyāpitadosaṃ paṭikkhipanto āha “manussaṭṭhiṃ ṭhapetvā”ti. Salākaṭṭhāniyanti ettha salākā tiṭṭhanti etthāti salākaṭṭhāniyanti vacanatthaṃ dassento āha “yatthā”tiādi. Tattha yatthāti yasmiṃ susiradaṇḍakādike. Salākanti añjanisalākaṃ. Odahantīti ṭhapenti. Aṃsabaddhakoti aṃse baddhati anenāti aṃsabaddhako. Yamakanatthukaraṇinti natthu karīyati imāyāti natthukaraṇī, yamakā natthukaraṇī yamakanatthukaraṇī.

Rejecting the fault of over-application of the word 'aṭṭhimayaṃ,' he said 'excepting human bone.' Here, regarding 'salākaṭṭhāniyaṃ,' showing the etymological meaning 'probes stand here,' he said 'yattha' and so on. Therein, 'yattha' means in which hollow stick or the like. 'Salākaṃ' means a collyrium-applicator. 'Odahanti' means they place. 'Aṃsabaddhako' means that by which one binds it on the shoulder. 'Yamakanatthukaraṇī' means: 'natthukaraṇī' is that by which snuffing is done; a pair of snuff-inhalers is a 'yamakanatthukaraṇī'.

267. Taṃ sabbaṃ telapākanti sambandho. “Ati viya khittamajjānī”ti iminā ati viya khipīyanti pakkhipīyantīti atikhittāni, tāniyeva majjāni atikhittamajjānīti vacanatthaṃ dasseti.

267. The connection is: all that is 'telapākaṃ.' By 'ati viya khittamajjāni,' he shows the etymological meaning: 'they are thrown in, cast in excessively,' hence 'atikhittāni'; those very kernels are 'atikhittamajjāni'.

Paṇṇasedanti [V 2.0014] paṇṇehi sedaṃ. Aṅgārānanti aṅgārehi. Tatthāti tesu paṃsuvālikādīsu. Vātaharaṇapaṇṇānīti vātassa apanayanāni uddālādīni paṇṇāni. Tatthāti tesu paṇṇesu. Nānāpaṇṇabhaṅgakuthitanti nānāpaṇṇāniyeva bhañjitabbaṭṭhena nānāpaṇṇabhaṅgaṃ, tena kuthitaṃ nānāpaṇṇabhaṅgakuthitaṃ. Uṇhodakassāti uṇhodakena. Tatthāti udakakoṭṭhake.

'Paṇṇasedaṃ' means sweating by means of leaves. 'Aṅgārānaṃ' means by means of coals. 'Tattha' means among those, such as dust and sand. 'Vātaharaṇapaṇṇāni' are leaves, such as uddāla, that dispel wind. 'Tattha' means among those leaves. 'Nānāpaṇṇabhaṅgakuthitaṃ' means: 'nānāpaṇṇabhaṅgaṃ' is various leaves, in the sense that they are to be broken; boiled with that is 'nānāpaṇṇabhaṅgakuthitaṃ.' 'Uṇhodakassa' means with hot water. 'Tattha' means in the water-chamber.

Pabbe pabbeti phaḷumhi phaḷumhi. Yenāti pajjena. Taṃ pajjaṃ abhisaṅkharitunti yojanā. “Pādānaṃ sappāyabhesajja”nti iminā pādassa hitaṃ pajjanti vacanatthaṃ dasseti. Tilakakkenāti ettha kakkasaddassa cuṇṇavācakattā “piṭṭhehī”ti vuttaṃ. Kabaḷena pakkhipanaṃ kabaḷikaṃ. Sattupiṇḍassa bhattakabaḷasadisattā sattupiṇḍanti vuttaṃ. Āṇi viyāti khīlā viya. Khārenāti loṇasakkharikamayena khārena. Vikāsaṃ rundhatīti vikāsikaṃ, telarundhanapilotikaṃ. Vaṇakammanti vaṇassa, vaṇe vā kammaṃ.

'Pabbe pabbe' means at each joint, at each segment. 'Yena' means by what is suitable (pajjena). The connection is 'to prepare that suitable remedy.' By 'a suitable medicine for the feet,' he shows the etymological meaning of 'pajjaṃ' as that which is beneficial for the foot. Here, in 'tilakakkena,' because the word 'kakka' denotes powder, 'piṭṭhehi' is said. Putting it in with a morsel is 'kabaḷikaṃ.' Because a ball of roasted grain meal is similar to a morsel of food, it is called 'sattupiṇḍa.' 'Āṇi viya' means like a peg, like a stake. 'Khārena' means with an alkali made of salt and gravel-sugar. 'Vikāsikaṃ' is that which obstructs spreading; a cloth for containing oil. 'Vaṇakammaṃ' means work of the wound, or work on the wound.

268. Sappadaṭṭhakāleyeva kiṃ sāmaṃ gahetvā paribhuñjitabbanti āha “na kevala”ntiādi. Idanti mahāvikaṭaṃ, paribhuñjīkabbanti sambandho[M 0.0347]. Aññesu panāti sappadaṭṭhato aññesu pana. Sace bhūmipatto gūtho hoti, paṭiggahetabboti yojanā.

268. The question is: 'At the very time one is bitten by a snake, should one take it oneself and consume it?' He said 'na kevalaṃ' and so on. 'Idaṃ' means the great offal; the connection is 'it should be consumed.' 'Aññesu pana' means in the case of others than one bitten by a snake. The connection is: if it is excrement that has reached the ground, it should be accepted.

269. Vasīkaraṇapānakasamuṭṭhitarogoti kantibhāvasaṅkhātaṃ vasaṃ karoti anenāti vasīkaraṇaṃ, bhesajjaṃ, pivate pānaṃ, taṃyeva pānakaṃ, vasīkaraṇassa pānakaṃ vasīkaraṇapānakaṃ, tena samuṭṭhito rogo vasīkaraṇapānakasamuṭṭhitarogo. Iminā gharadinnakābādhoti ettha gharaṇiyā dinnena vasīkaraṇapānakena samuṭṭhito ābādho gharadinnakābādhoti vacanatthaṃ dasseti. Sītāya āloḷetabbanti sītāloḷaṃ, udakaṃ. Sītāsaddo naṅgalalekhāsaṅkhātaṃ phālapaddhatiṃ mukhyato vadati, phālapaddhatikare phāle laggamattikaṃ upacārato vadati. Tena vuttaṃ “sītāya āloḷetabba”nti. Aṭṭhakathāyampi tamatthaṃ dassento āha “naṅgalenā”tiādi.

269. A disease arisen from a subduing-potion is 'vasīkaraṇapānakasamuṭṭhitarogo.' 'Vasīkaraṇaṃ' is that by which one brings another under one's control, which is called 'kantibhāva'; it is a medicine. A drink is 'pānaṃ'; that itself is 'pānakaṃ.' A potion for subduing is 'vasīkaraṇapānakaṃ.' A disease arisen from that is 'vasīkaraṇapānakasamuṭṭhitarogo.' By this, he shows the etymological meaning of 'gharadinnakābādho' as an illness arisen from a subduing-potion given by the wife of the house. 'Sītāloḷaṃ' means to be stirred with a 'sītā'; it refers to water. The word 'sītā' primarily means the track of the plowshare, known as the plow-line; by extension, it refers to the mud clinging to the plowshare that makes the track. Therefore it is said, 'it should be stirred with a sītā.' In the commentary also, showing that meaning, he said 'with a plow' and so on.

Vipakkagahaṇikoti visesena pācāpanagahaṇiko. Muttaharītakanti ettha “mutta”nti sāmaññato vuttepi gomuttameva gahetabbanti dassento āha “gomuttaparibhāvitaṃ harītaka”nti. Iminā muttena paribhāvitaṃ harītakaṃ muttaharītakanti vacanatthaṃ dasseti. Taṇḍulakasaṭoti taṇḍuladhovanodakakasaṭo dhotasiniddho, sova muggapacitapānīyoti yojanā. “Maṃsarasenā”ti iminā maṃsaraso maṃsena paṭicchādetabbanti paṭicchādanīyanti vuccatīti dasseti.

'Vipakkagahaṇiko' means one who takes what is ripened, specifically one who takes what has been caused to ripen. Regarding 'muttaharītaka,' here, although 'mutta' is spoken of in a general sense, to show that it is specifically cow's urine that should be taken, it is said: 'harītaka treated with cow's urine.' By this, it shows the meaning of 'muttaharītaka' as harītaka treated with urine. 'Taṇḍulakasaṭo' means the sediment of rice-washing water, which is washed and smooth; the interpretation is that this is the water in which mung beans have been cooked. By 'maṃsarasena,' it shows that meat broth is to be covered with meat, hence it is called 'paṭicchādanīya' (that which is to be covered).

163. Guḷādianujānanakathā

163. The Account of Allowing Jaggery, etc.

272. Hīti [V 2.0015] saccaṃ. Pakkattāti muggānaṃ pakkabhāvato. Teti muggā.

272. 'Hī' means 'truly.' 'Pakkattā' means 'because of the ripened state of the mung beans.' 'Te' refers to the mung beans.

274. Akappiyakuṭiyanti akappiyakuṭiyā anto. Assāti bhikkhuno na vaṭṭatīti sambandho. Tampīti uṇhayāgumpi. Pisaddena pageva āmisaṃ pacitunti dasseti. Uttaṇḍulabhattanti pakkataṇḍulato viyogoti uttaṇḍulo, ukāro hi viyogatthavācako, apakkataṇḍuloti attho. Uttaṇḍulamayaṃ bhattanti uttaṇḍulabhattaṃ. Sakiṃ kuthitesu khīratakkādīsu aggiṃ dātuṃ vaṭṭatīti yojanā. Biḷālādīnaṃ [M 0.0348] sattānaṃ samūho rūḷhīvasena ukkapiṇḍakoti vuccatīti āha “biḷālamūsikagodhāmaṅgusā”ti. Vighāsādabhāvena nihatamānattā kāyavācaṃ dametīti damako vighāsādoti āha “vighāsādā”ti.

274. 'Akappiyakuṭiyaṃ' means inside an unsuitable hut. 'Assa' means 'for a monk it is not allowable'—this is the connection. 'Taṃ pi' means 'even hot gruel.' By the word 'pi,' it shows that choice food is cooked beforehand. 'Uttaṇḍulabhatta' means 'uttaṇḍula,' which is separation from cooked rice—for the letter 'u' signifies separation—meaning uncooked rice. 'Uttaṇḍulabhatta' means rice made of uncooked rice. The interpretation is that it is allowable to apply fire once to things like milk, buttermilk, etc., that have been boiled. A group of creatures such as cats is conventionally called an 'ukkapiṇḍaka,' hence it is said: 'cats, rats, lizards, and mongooses.' Because of being an eater of leftovers and thus having subdued pride, one restrains body and speech and is thus a 'damaka' (one who is restrained); he is a 'vighāsāda' (eater of leftovers), hence it is said: 'vighāsādā'.

276. Tato nīhaṭanti ettha tasaddassa visayaṃ dassento āha “yatthā”tiādi. Yatthāti yasmiṃ ṭhāne. Nīhaṭanti nīharitvā haritaṃ.

276. Regarding 'tato nīhaṭaṃ,' here, showing the referent of the word 'ta,' it is said: 'yatthā,' etc. 'Yatthā' means 'in which place.' 'Nīhaṭaṃ' means 'having taken out and carried.'

278. Vanaṭṭhaṃ pokkharaṭṭhanti ettha vane tiṭṭhatīti vanaṭṭho, pokkhare tiṭṭhatīti pokkharaṭṭhoti vacanatthaṃ dassento āha “vane cevā”tiādi. “Paduminigacche”ti iminā pokkharasaddo padumavācakoti dasseti. Yassa bījaṃ aṅkuraṃ na janeti, taṃ phalaṃ abījaṃ nāmāti yojanā.

278. Regarding 'vanaṭṭhaṃ pokkharaṭṭhaṃ,' here, showing the meaning of the words, it is said, beginning with 'in the forest and,' etc.: 'one who stands in the forest is a vanaṭṭha,' and 'one who stands in a lotus pond is a pokkharaṭṭha.' By 'paduminigacche,' it shows that the word 'pokkhara' is a designator of the lotus. The interpretation is: that fruit whose seed does not generate a sprout is called 'abījaṃ'.

167. Satthakammapaṭikkhepakathā

167. The Account of the Rejection of Surgical Operations

279. Dukkhena rupatīti duropayoti dassento āha “dukkhena ruhatī”ti. Satthakammaṃ vā vatthikammaṃ vāti ettha satthena kātabbaṃ kammaṃ satthakammaṃ, vatthipīḷanaṃ kātabbaṃ kammaṃ vatthikammanti vacanatthaṃ dassento āha “yathā paṭicchanne”tiādi. “Sūciyā vā”tiādinā satthakammanti ettha “sattha”nti padaṃ upalakkhaṇamattanti dasseti. “Satthena vā”ti padaṃ “chindanaṃ vā phālanaṃ vā”tipadehi yojetabbaṃ. “Sūciyā vā kaṇṭakena vā sattikāya vā”tipadāni “vijjhanaṃ vā”ti padena yojetabbāni. “Pāsāṇasakkhalikāya vā nakhena vā”ti padāni “lekhanaṃ vā”ti padena yojetabbāni. Etanti satthena chindanādikammaṃ. Ettha cāti satthakammavatthikammesu. Tattha panāti sambādhe pana. Tenāti khārādinā. Vaccamagge yāya bhesajjamakkhitādānavaṭṭiyā [V 2.0016] khārakammaṃ vā karonti, yāya veḷunāḷikāya telaṃ vā pavesenti, sā bhesajjamakkhitādānavaṭṭi vā sā veḷunāḷikā vā vaṭṭatiyevāti yojanā.

279. Showing that 'duropaya' means 'it heals with difficulty,' it is said: 'dukkhena ruhati.' 'Satthakamma or vatthikamma'—here, explaining the meaning of the words, it is said, beginning with 'as when covered,' etc.: 'work to be done with an instrument is satthakamma,' and 'work involving pressing with a suppository is vatthikamma.' By 'sūciyā vā,' etc., in reference to 'satthakamma,' it shows that the word 'sattha' here is merely illustrative. The phrase 'satthena vā' should be connected with the phrases 'cutting or splitting.' The phrases 'sūciyā vā kaṇṭakena vā sattikāya vā' should be connected with the phrase 'piercing.' The phrases 'pāsāṇasakkhalikāya vā nakhena vā' should be connected with the phrase 'scratching.' 'Etaṃ' refers to actions like cutting with an instrument. 'Ettha ca' means 'in surgical and suppository procedures.' 'Tattha pana' means 'but in the obstruction.' 'Tena' refers to things like alkali. The interpretation is that a medicine-smeared tube with which they perform alkali treatment in the anal passage, or a bamboo tube with which they insert oil, is permissible.

280. Taṃ [M 0.0349] divasanti tasmiṃ divase. Kiñci satthanti yojanā. Imāyāti suppiyāya aññaṃ kiñci adeyyaṃ kimpi bhavissatīti yojanā. Yatra nāmāti ettha trapaccayo kāraṇatthe hotīti āha “yasmā nāmā”ti. “Vīmaṃsī”ti iminā paṭivekkhīti ettha paṭiavapubbo ikkhadhātu vīmaṃsanatthoti dasseti. Asukamaṃsanti asukaṃ maṃsaṃ, asukassa vā sattassa maṃsaṃ.

280. 'Taṃ divasaṃ' means 'on that day.' The connection is: 'any instrument.' The interpretation is: 'Will there be anything else not to be given by Suppiyā?' 'Yatra nāmā'—here, it is said that the suffix 'tra' is in the sense of reason, hence it is said: 'yasmā nāmā.' By 'vīmaṃsī,' it shows that in 'paṭivekkhī,' the root 'ikkh' preceded by 'paṭi-ava' is in the sense of investigation. 'Asukamaṃsaṃ' means 'a certain piece of meat,' or 'the flesh of a certain being'.

169. Hatthimaṃsādipaṭikkhepakathā

169. The Account of the Rejection of Elephant Meat, etc.

281. Araññakokā nāmāti sasabiḷālādayo satte khādanatthāya kukati ādadātīti koko araññe jāto koko araññakoko, sunakhasadisāti gāmasunakhena sadisā. Tesanti araññakokānaṃ. Yo panāti sunakho pana, uppannoti sambandho. Gāmasunakhiyāti sāmyatthe sāmivacanaṃ. Kokenāti sahādiyoge karaṇavacanaṃ. Tāni padāni “saṃyogenā”ti padena yojetabbāni. Tassāti sunakhassa.

281. ‘Araññakokā’ are so named because they are creatures like hares and cats that act badly for the sake of eating beings and take them; thus, a ‘koka’ born in the forest is called ‘araññakoko’. ‘Sunakhasadisā’ means similar to a village dog. ‘Tesaṃ’ refers to the araññakokas. ‘Yo pana’ means ‘the dog, however’; ‘uppanno’ is the connection. ‘Gāmasunakhiyā’ is the genitive case in the sense of similarity. ‘Kokena’ is the instrumental case indicating association. Those words should be connected with the word ‘saṃyogena’. ‘Tassa’ refers to the dog.

Etthāti manussamaṃsādīsu. Sajātikatāyāti samānajātikabhāvato. Anupaddavatthāyāti anupaddavatthaṃ, paṭikkhittānīti sambandho. Āpattīti manussamaṃse thullaccayena, sese dukkaṭena āpatti. Uddissa kataṃ panāti bhikkhuṃ uddissa katamaṃsaṃ pana.

‘Ettha’ refers to human flesh, etc. ‘Sajātikatāya’ means due to being of the same species. ‘Anupaddavatthāya’ means ‘without an injured basis’; ‘paṭikkhittāni’ is the connection. ‘Āpatti’ means an offense by way of a grave offense for human flesh, and a wrong-doing for the rest. ‘Uddissa kataṃ pana’ refers to meat prepared specifically for a bhikkhu.

170. Yāgumadhugoḷakādikathā

170. The Discussion on Gruel, Honey Balls, etc.

282. Ekakoti ettha ekato asahāyatthe kapaccayoti āha “natthi me dutiyo”ti. Soti brāhmaṇo. Vayaṃ katvāti paribbayaṃ katvā, paṭiyādāpesi kirāti yojanā. Anumodanagāthāyāti anumodanapakāsakāya gāthāya. “Patthayataṃ icchata”nti padānaṃ alamatthapayoge sampadānattā vuttaṃ “alameva dātunti iminā sambandho”ti. Soyeva gahetabboti “dātu”ntibhāvassa kattubhāvena so eva pāṭho gahetabboti attho.

282. ‘Ekako’ here means ‘alone’, in the sense of ‘without a companion’, with the suffix ‘ka’; thus it is said, ‘I have no second’. ‘So’ refers to the brahmin. ‘Vayaṃ katvā’ means ‘having made an expenditure’; ‘paṭiyādāpesi kira’ is the construction. ‘Anumodanagāthāya’ refers to the verse expressing appreciation. The words ‘patthayataṃ icchataṃ’ are said because the dative case is used when ‘alaṃ’ has the sense of capability; the connection is with ‘alameva dātuṃ’. ‘So yeva gahetabbo’ means that that very reading, ‘dātuṃ,’ should be taken as having the sense of the agent.

283. Yā [M 0.0350] yāgu pavāraṇaṃ janeti, sā yāgu bhojjayāgu nāmāti yojanā. Yanti kālaṃ. “Ādiṃ katvā”ti iminā yadaggenāti ettha aggasaddo ādyattho kiriyāvisesanatthe karaṇavacananti [V 2.0017] dasseti. “Sagganibbattakapuñña”nti iminā saggāti ettha phalūpacāraṃ dasseti. Soti guḷo.

283. The interpretation is: that gruel which produces satisfaction, that gruel is called 'bhojjayāgu.' ‘Yanti’ means ‘they pass the time’. By ‘ādiṃ katvā’, it shows that in ‘yadaggena’, the word ‘agga’ means ‘beginning’, and the instrumental case is in the sense of an adverb of action. By ‘sagganibbattakapuñña’, it shows that in ‘sagga’, there is a metaphorical usage of the result. ‘So’ refers to molasses.

284. Tathārūpenāti tathāsabhāvena. Guḷassa anurūpasabhāvenāti attho.

284. ‘Tathārūpena’ means ‘of such a nature’. The meaning is ‘having a nature similar to molasses’.

173. Pāṭaligāmavatthukathā

173. The Pāṭaligāma Account

285. Yathā sabbaṃ santhataṃ hoti, evaṃ tathā sabbasantharisanthatanti yojanā.

285. The interpretation is: 'Just as everything is spread out, so too is it completely spread out.'

286. Sunidho ca vassakāro cāti ettha cakārehi dvandavākyaṃ dasseti. Āyamukhapacchindanatthanti suṅkamukhassa pacchedanatthaṃ. “Gharavatthūnī”ti iminā vatthusaddassa kāraṇadabbatthe paṭikkhipitvā bhūbhedatthaṃ dīpeti. Tā devatā nāmenti kirāti yojanā. Yathānurūpanti yaṃ yaṃ bhogabalānurūpaṃ. Loketi sattaloke. Saddoti kittighoso. Tenevāti tena saddassa abbhuggatahetunā eva. “Osaraṇaṭṭhānaṃ nāmā”ti iminā ariyaṃ āyatananti ettha āyatanasaddo samosaraṇaṭṭhānatthoti dasseti. Yattakaṃ kayavikkayaṭṭhānaṃ nāmāti sambandho. “Vāṇijānaṃ…pe… kayavikkayaṭṭhānaṃ nāmā”ti iminā vaṇijā patanti sannipatanti etthāti vaṇippatoti vacanatthaṃ dasseti. “Vaṇijapato”ti vattabbe jakāralopoti daṭṭhabbo. Pāḷiyaṃ “tesa”nti pāṭhasesassa ajjhāharitabbabhāvaṃ dassetuṃ vuttaṃ “tesaṃ ariyāyatanavāṇijapatāna”nti. Tesanti ca sāmyatthe sāmivacanaṃ, niddhāraṇatthe vā vibhattaapādānatthe vā. Idanti puraṃ[M 0.0351]. Puṭabhedananti ettha puṭaṃ bhindanti etthāti puṭabhedananti vacanatthaṃ dassento āha “bhaṇḍikabhedanaṭṭhāna”nti. “Samuccayattho vāsaddo”ti vuttavacanaṃ vitthārento āha “tatra hī”tiādi. Tattha tatrāti pāṭaliputte, tīsu vā aggiudakamithubhedesu. “Aññamaññabhedā”ti iminā mithubhedāti ettha mithusaddassa aññamaññavevacanabhāvaṃ dasseti. Uḷumpakullasaddānaṃ atthe samānepi karaṇavisesaṃ dassento āha “uḷumpa”ntiādi. Uḷu vuccati udakaṃ, tato pāti rakkhatīti uḷumpo. Kaṃ vuccati udakaṃ, tasmiṃ ulati gacchatīti kullo.

286. Here, by the conjunctions ‘ca’ in ‘Sunidho ca Vassakāro ca’, it shows a conjunctive phrase. ‘Āyamukhapacchindanatthaṃ’ means ‘for the purpose of cutting off the source of revenue’. By ‘gharavatthūni’, it rejects the word ‘vatthu’ in the sense of ‘causal substance’ and clarifies its meaning as ‘a plot of ground’. ‘Tā devatā nāmenti kira’ is the construction. ‘Yathānurūpaṃ’ means ‘whatever is appropriate to their enjoyment and power’. ‘Loke’ refers to the sentient world. ‘Saddo’ means ‘fame’. ‘Teneva’ means ‘for that very reason of the fame’s arising’. By ‘osaraṇaṭṭhānaṃ nāma’, it shows that in ‘ariyaṃ āyatanaṃ’, the word ‘āyatana’ means ‘place of resort’. ‘Whatever the place of trade is’ is the connection. By ‘vāṇijānaṃ…pe… kayavikkayaṭṭhānaṃ nāma’, it explains the etymology of ‘vaṇippato’ as ‘the place where merchants resort to or gather’. It should be understood that the ‘j’ is elided where it should be ‘vaṇijapato’. In the Pāli, ‘tesaṃ’ is stated to show that the remaining part of the reading, ‘tesaṃ ariyāyatanavāṇijapatānaṃ’, should be supplied. And ‘tesaṃ’ is the genitive case in the sense of possession, or in the sense of determination, or in the sense of the ablative case. ‘Idaṃ’ means ‘the city’. Explaining the etymology of ‘puṭabhedana’ as ‘they break bundles there’, he says ‘bhaṇḍikabhedanaṭṭhāna’ (place of breaking bundles). Expanding on the statement ‘the word ‘vā’ has the sense of collection’, he says ‘tatra hi’ etc. ‘Tattha’ or ‘tatra’ refers to Pāṭaliputta, or to the three divisions of fire, water, and mutual discord. By ‘aññamaññabhedā’, it shows that in ‘mithubhedā’, the word ‘mithu’ means ‘mutual’. Though the meanings of the words ‘uḷumpa’ and ‘kulla’ are similar, he shows the specific instrument: he says ‘uḷumpa’ etc. ‘Uḷu’ is called water; because it protects (pāti) from that, therefore it is ‘uḷumpa’. ‘Kaṃ’ is called water; because it goes (ulati) in that, therefore it is ‘kulla’.

Aṇṇavanti ettha aṇṇavo nāma kiṃ samuddassa nāmanti āha “aṇṇava”ntiādi. “Aṇṇava”nti etaṃ nāmaṃ udakaṭṭhānassa adhivacananti yojanā. Aṇṇo vuccati udakaṃ, taṃ etasmiṃ [V 2.0018] atthīti aṇṇavo. Sarasaddassa akārādimhi ca kaṇḍe ca pavattanato vuttaṃ “saranti idha nadī adhippetā”ti. Idhāti imissaṃ gāthāyaṃ. Idanti atthajātaṃ.

Here, regarding ‘aṇṇava’, asking ‘Is ‘aṇṇava’ the name of the ocean?’, he says ‘aṇṇava’ etc. ‘Aṇṇava’—this name is a designation for a place of water; this is the construction. ‘Aṇṇa’ is called water; because that exists in this, therefore it is ‘aṇṇava’. Since the word ‘sara’ occurs in the section beginning with ‘a’ and also in the section on ‘kaṇḍa’, it is said, ‘here, a river is intended by ‘sara’’. ‘Idha’ refers to ‘in this verse’. ‘Idaṃ’ refers to ‘this collection of meanings’.

Yeti ariyā. Teti ariyā, tarantīti sambandho. Visajjapallalānīti ettha visajjasaddo tvāpaccayanto, pallalasaddo ninnaṭṭhānavācakoti āha “visajja…pe… ninnaṭṭhānānī”ti. Ayaṃ pana jano kullaṃ bandhatīti yojanā. Tiṇṇā medhāvino janā iti vuttaṃ hotīti yojanā.

‘Ye’ refers to the noble ones. ‘Te’ refers to the noble ones; ‘they cross over’ is the connection. In ‘visajjapallalāni’, the word ‘visajja’ is a gerund (ending in -tvā), and the word ‘pallala’ denotes a low-lying place; thus he says, ‘having abandoned… the low-lying places’. ‘This person, however, builds a raft’ is the construction. ‘Wise people have crossed over’—this is the meaning conveyed.

287. Ananubodhāti ettha kāraṇatthe nissakkavacananti āha “abujjhanenā”ti. Sandhāvitaṃ saṃsaritanti ettha tapaccayassa kammatthaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ “mayā ca tumhehi cā”ti. Iminā kattutthe sāmivacananti dasseti. “Atha vā”tiādinā tapaccayassa bhāvatthaṃ dasseti. Saṃsitanti ettha saradhātuyā rakāro lopoti āha “saṃsarita”nti. “Taṇhārajjū”ti iminā bhavato bhavaṃ netīti bhavanettīti vacanatthena taṇhārajju bhavanetti nāmāti dasseti.

287. Here, regarding ‘ananubodhā’, it is the ablative case in the sense of cause; thus he says, ‘due to non-comprehension’. In ‘sandhāvitaṃ saṃsaritaṃ’, referring to the passive sense of the suffix ‘-ta’, it is said, ‘by me and by you’. By this, it shows the genitive case in the sense of the agent. By ‘atha vā’ etc., it shows the suffix ‘-ta’ in the sense of an abstract noun. In ‘saṃsitaṃ’, the letter ‘r’ of the root ‘sara’ is elided; thus he says, ‘saṃsaritaṃ’. By ‘taṇhārajjū’, it shows that the rope of craving is called ‘bhavanetti’ based on the meaning of the word: ‘it leads from one existence to another’.

289. Vaṇṇavatthālaṅkārāni [M 0.0352] sāmaññavasena “nīlā”ti vuttānīti āha “nīlāti idaṃ sabbasaṅgāhaka”nti. Tatthāti “nīlā”tiādipāṭhe. Tesanti licchavīnaṃ. Pakativaṇṇā nīlā na hontīti yojanā. Etanti “nīlā”tiādivacanaṃ. Paṭivattesīti ettha vatudhātu upasaggavasena vā atthātisayavasena vā paharaṇatthoti āha “pahāresī”ti. “Sajanapada”nti iminā sāhāranti ettha āhārasaddo janapadatthoti dasseti. Janapado hi yasmā nagarassa parivārabhāvena āharitabbo, imasmā ca rājapurisā baliṃ āharanti, tasmā āhāroti vutto. Sajanapadaṃ vesāliṃ dajjeyyāthāti yojanā. Aṅguliṃ phoṭesunti ettha phuṭadhātu sañcalanatthoti āha “aṅguliṃ cālesu”nti. Itthikāyāti itthīyeva purisato khuddakaṭṭhena itthikā, tāya.

289. He says that colors, objects, and ornaments are generally referred to as ‘nīlā’ (blue); thus he says, ‘this ‘nīlā’ is all-inclusive’. ‘Tattha’ refers to the reading ‘nīlā’ etc. ‘Tesaṃ’ refers to the Licchavis. ‘Their natural color is not blue’ is the construction. ‘Etaṃ’ refers to the statement ‘nīlā’ etc. In ‘paṭivattesi’, the root ‘vatt’, either by way of a prefix or by way of an intensified meaning, has the sense of striking; thus he says, ‘pahāresi’ (struck). By ‘sajanapadaṃ’, it shows that in ‘sāhāraṃ’, the word ‘āhāra’ means ‘territory’. For since the territory is to be brought as an accessory to the city, and from it the king’s men bring tribute, therefore it is called ‘āhāra’. ‘You should give Vesāli with its territory’ is the construction. In ‘aṅguliṃ phoṭesuṃ’, the root ‘phuṭa’ has the sense of movement; thus he says, ‘aṅguliṃ cālesuṃ’ (moved the finger). ‘Itthikāya’ means ‘by the female’, because a female is ‘itthikā’ by being smaller than a male.

178. Sīhasenāpativatthukathā

178. The Story of General Sīha

290. Dhammassa ca anudhammanti ettha dhammasaddo kāraṇatthoti āha “kāraṇassa anukāraṇa”nti. “Parehī”ti padaṃ “vutta”iti pade kattā. “Vuttakāraṇenā”tipadaṃ “sakāraṇo”tipade karaṇaṃ. Koci appamattakopi tumhākaṃ vādoti yojanā. “Viññūhī”ti padaṃ “garahitabba”iti pade kattā. “Garahitabbakāraṇa”nti padaṃ “na āgacchatī”ti pade kammaṃ[V 2.0019]. Anabbhakkhātukāmāti ettha abhityūpasaggo abhibhavanattho āpubbo khādhātu pakathanatthoti āha “abhibhavitvā na ācikkhitukāmā”ti.

290. Here, in 'Dhammassa ca anudhammanti', the word 'dhamma' has the meaning of 'reason'; thus, it is said 'in accordance with the reason'. The word 'by others' is the agent of the word 'said'. The word ‘vuttakāraṇena’ (with the reason stated) is the instrumental case within the word ‘sakāraṇo’ (with reason). The construction is: 'even a slight view of yours'. The word 'by the wise' is the agent of the word 'should be criticized'. The phrase 'a reason for criticism' is the object in the phrase 'does not come'. Here, in 'anabbhakkhātukāmā', the prefix 'abhi' has the meaning of 'overcoming', and the root 'khyā' preceded by 'ā' has the meaning of 'declaring'; thus, it is said 'not wishing to declare after overcoming'.

293. Anuviccakāranti ettha anuviccasaddo vicadhātu tvāpaccayantoti āha “anuvicitvā”ti. “Cintetvā”ti iminā vicadhātuyā ñāṇatthaṃ dasseti. “Kātabba”nti iminā kātabbanti kāranti vacanatthaṃ dasseti. Paṭākanti dhajapaṭākaṃ. “Āhiṇḍeyyu”nti iminā pariyāyeyyunti ettha paripubbaāpubba yādhātuyā gatyatthaṃ dasseti. Pāḷiyaṃ “parihareyyu”ntipi pāṭho. Āhiṇḍeyyunti āhiṇḍanti. Muddhajo tatiyakkharo[M 0.0353]. Opānabhūtanti ettha opāno viya bhūto opānabhūtoti atthaṃ dassento āha “paṭiyattaudapāno viya ṭhita”nti. “Udapāno”ti iminā opānasaddo udapānatthoti dasseti. Udapāno hi sabbe janā osaritvā pivanti etthāti opānoti vuccati. Imesanti nigaṇṭhānaṃ. Hīti saccaṃ, yasmā vā. Sampattānaṃ dānaṃ dātabbameva, tasmā mā upacchinditthāti yojanā. Uddissāti tvāpaccayantasaddo “kata”nti uttarapadena samāsoti āha “uddisitvā kata”nti. Eseva nayo “paṭiccakamma”nti etthāpi.

293. Here, in 'anuviccakāraṃ', the word 'anuvicca' is a gerund from the root 'vic'; thus, it is said 'having considered'. By 'cintetvā' (having thought), it shows the meaning of 'knowledge' for the root 'vic'. By 'kātabbaṃ' (what should be done), it shows the meaning of the word 'kāra'. 'Paṭāka' means a flag or banner. By 'āhiṇḍeyyuṃ', it shows the meaning of 'movement' for the root 'yā' with the prefixes 'pari' and 'ā', as in 'pariyāyeyyuṃ'. In the Pali text, 'parihareyyuṃ' is also a variant reading. 'Āhiṇḍeyyuṃ' means 'they wander'. The third letter is a cerebral. Here, in 'opānabhūtaṃ', showing the meaning 'being like a well', he says 'standing like a prepared well'. By 'udapāno', it shows that the word 'opāna' has the meaning of 'well'. A well is called 'opāna' because all people resort to and drink from it. 'Imesaṃ' refers to the Nigaṇṭhas. 'Hī' means 'truly' or 'because'. The construction is: 'gifts should indeed be given to those who have arrived, therefore do not withhold them'. 'Uddissa' is a gerund, and it is a compound with the latter word 'kata'; thus, it is said 'having dedicated and done'. The same method applies to 'paṭiccakamma' here.

294. Paṭiccakammanti etaṃ nāmaṃ nimittakammassa adhivacananti yojanā. Yoti yo koci jano. Vadhakassa pāṇaghātakammaṃ hoti viya, tassāpi hotīti yojanā. Na jīrantīti ettha jaradhātu gatyatthoti āha “na gacchantī”ti.

294. The connection is: 'Paṭiccakamma' is a name synonymous with 'nimittakamma'. 'Yo' means any person. The construction is: 'just as a killer has the act of killing, so does this one'. Here, in 'na jīranti', the root 'jara' has the meaning of 'movement'; thus, he says 'they do not go'.

179. Kappiyabhūmianujānanakathā

179. Discourse on the Allowance of a Suitable Site

295. Bahārāmakoṭṭhaketi ettha samīpatthe bhummavacananti āha “bahārāmakoṭṭhakasamīpeti ārāmakoṭṭhakassa bahi samīpeti attho”ti. Acchantīti vasanti. Etanti “paccantima”nti etaṃ vacanaṃ. Dhuravihāropīti padhānavihāropi. Tattha tatthāti tasmiṃ tasmiṃ ṭhāne. Anupageyevāti pātoyeva. Oravasaddanti uccaravasaṅkhātaṃ saddaṃ. Kapilasuttapariyosāneti suttanipāte (su. ni. aṭṭha. 2.kapilasuttavaṇṇanā) saṅgahitassa kapilasuttassa pariyosāne. Pañcasatānaṃ kevaṭṭapurisānanti sambandho.

295. Here, in 'bahārāmakoṭṭhake', the locative case has the meaning of proximity; thus, it is said 'near the outer monastery gate', meaning 'near the outside of the monastery gate'. 'Acchanti' means 'they dwell'. 'This' refers to the word 'paccantima'. 'Dhuravihāra' also means a principal monastery. 'Here and there' means 'in that particular place'. 'Anupageyeva' means 'early in the morning'. 'Oravasadda' means a loud noise. 'At the end of the Kapila Sutta' refers to the conclusion of the Kapila Sutta included in the Sutta Nipāta (Su. Ni. Aṭṭha. 2, Kapila Sutta Commentary). 'Of five hundred fishermen' is the connection.

Ussāvanantikādīsu evaṃ vinicchayo veditabboti yojanā. Yo vihāro kariyatīti sambandho. Bhūmiyā gati viya gati etesanti bhūmigatikā. Patiṭṭhāpentehi bahūhi bhikkhūhi patiṭṭhāpetabboti [V 2.0020] sambandho. Nicchārentehi bhikkhūhīti yojanā. Sayanti bhikkhu. Taṃ panāti “saṅghassa kappiyakuṭiṃ adhiṭṭhāmī”ti vacanaṃ pana. Avatvāpīti pisaddo tathā “vatvāpī”ti atthaṃ sampiṇḍeti. Aṭṭhakathāsūti [M 0.0354] mahāaṭṭhakathādīsu tīsu aṭṭhakathāsu. Etthāti ussāvanantikakuṭiyaṃ. “Samakālaṃ vaṭṭatī”ti vacanaṃ daḷhīkaronto āha “sace hī”tiādi. Vacaneti “kappiyakuṭiṃ karomā”ti vacane. Tasminti thambhe. Tenevāti akatabhāveneva. Hīti saccaṃ. Etthāti bahūsu.

The construction is: 'In cases such as the ussāvanantikā hut, the decision should be understood thus'. The connection is: 'The dwelling is being built'. Their movement is like movement on the ground; thus, they are called 'ground-movers'. The connection is: 'It should be established by many monks who are establishing it'. The construction is: 'by monks who are removing obstacles'. The word 'sayanti' (they lie down) refers to a bhikkhu. That, however, refers to the statement 'I dedicate a suitable hut to the Sangha'. In 'avatvāpi', the particle 'pi' also includes the meaning 'even if said'. 'Aṭṭhakathāsu' refers to the three commentaries, such as the Great Commentary. 'Here' refers to the ussāvanantikā hut. Strengthening the statement 'It is valid at the same time', he says: 'For if...' etc. In 'vacane' (statement), it refers to the statement 'Let us make a suitable hut'. In 'tasmiṃ' (there), it refers to that pillar. By 'teneva' (by that very fact), it means 'by the very fact of not being done'. 'Hī' means 'truly'. 'Here' refers to many cases.

Yatoti iṭṭhakasilāmattikāpiṇḍato. Vuttanayenevāti “bahūhi samparivāretvā kappiyakuṭiṃ karomā”ti vuttanayeneva. Iṭṭhakādayoti “kappiyakuṭiṃ karomā”ti adhiṭṭhātabbaiṭṭhakādayo. Andhakaṭṭhakathāyaṃ vuttanti sambandho. Tathāti yathā andhakaṭṭhakathāyaṃ vuttaṃ, tathā. Thambhādīni ukkhipitvā patiṭṭhāpanañca “kappiyakuṭiṃ karomā”ti sāvanañca antaṃ pariyosānametissāti ussāvanantikā.

From a lump of bricks, stones, or clay. By 'vuttanayeneva' (in the manner stated), it means 'in the manner stated: "Let us make a suitable hut, surrounded by many"'. By 'iṭṭhakādayo' (bricks and so on), it means the bricks and other materials to be determined with the thought 'Let us make a suitable hut'. 'As stated in the Andhaka commentary' is the connection. By 'tathā' (thus), it means 'as it was stated in the Andhaka commentary, so too'. Raising and setting up posts and so on, and the proclamation 'Let us make a suitable hut'—this is its end and conclusion; thus, it is called 'ussāvanantikā'.

Tāsūti dvīsu gonisādikāsu. Yatthāti kuṭiyaṃ. Neva ārāmo parikkhitto hotīti sambandho. Puna yatthāti kuṭiyaṃ. Ayanti kuṭi. Ubhayatthāpīti ārāmavihāragonisādikāsu dvīsupi. Bahutaraṃ parikkhittopi parikkhittoyeva nāmāti yojanā. Etthāti upaḍḍhaparikkhittabahutaraparikkhittaārāme. Gāvo pavisitvā yathāsukhaṃ nisīdanti etthāti gonisādā gosālā. Gonisādā viyāti gonisādikā kuṭi.

By 'tāsu' (in those), it means 'in the two gonisādikā huts'. By 'yattha' (where), it means 'in the hut'. 'The monastery is not enclosed' is the connection. Again, by 'yattha' (where), it means 'in the hut'. 'This' means the hut. By 'ubhayatthāpi' (in both places), it means 'in both the monastery-dwelling and the two gonisādikā huts'. The construction is: 'even if more is enclosed, it is still called enclosed'. 'Here' means in a monastery that is half-enclosed or more than half-enclosed. 'The cows enter and lie down as they please here'—this is a gonisāda, a cowshed. By 'gonisādā viya' (like a cow-pen), it means a gonisādikā hut.

Manussā vadantīti sambandho. Esāti kuṭi. Vuttepīti pisadde, “kappiyakuṭiṃ demā”ti vākyaṃ apekkhati. Andhakaṭṭhakathāyaṃ vuttanti sambandho. Yasmā vaṭṭati, tasmāti yojanā. Tesanti sesasahadhammikadevamanussānaṃ. Tehīti sesasahadhammikadevamanussehi. Punapi vuttaṃ, kiṃ vuttanti āha “bhikkhussa…pe… hotī”ti. Apīti tadaññesaṃ. Tanti vacanaṃ. Hīti saccaṃ, yasmā vā. Saṅghassa santakameva vā bhikkhussa santakameva vāti yojanā. Iti tasmā suvuttanti sambandho. Gahapatīnaṃ santakaṃ gahapati kuṭi. “Kammavācaṃ sāvetvā”ti idaṃ upalakkhaṇamattaṃ kammavācamavatvā apalokanenapi kappiyattā. Kammavācāya [M 0.0355] vā apalokanena vā sammanitabbāti sammuti kuṭi. Itisaddo parisamāpanattho.

'People speak' is the connection. 'This' refers to the hut. In 'vuttepi', the particle 'pi' refers to the sentence 'Let us give a suitable hut'. 'Stated in the Andhaka commentary' is the connection. The construction is: 'because it is fitting, therefore'. By 'tesaṃ' (to them), it refers to the remaining co-religionists, devas, and humans. By 'tehi' (by them), it means by the remaining co-religionists, devas, and humans. Again, it is said, what is said? He says, 'For a bhikkhu…pe… it occurs'. By 'api' (even), it refers to others. 'That' refers to the statement. 'Hī' means 'truth', or 'because'. The construction is: 'belonging to the Sangha alone or belonging to a bhikkhu alone'. 'Thus, therefore, it is well-spoken' is the connection. A householder's hut is that which belongs to householders. The phrase 'having proclaimed the Kammavācā' is merely an indication, because it is suitable even without a Kammavācā, by means of an apalokana (proclamation). A hut should be designated either by a formal act (kammavācā) or by a proclamation (apalokana); thus, it is a designated hut. The word 'iti' serves to conclude the text.

Yaṃ āmisaṃ vutthaṃ, sabbaṃ taṃ āmisantiyojanā. Akappiyabhūmiyaṃ sahaseyyapahonake gehe vutthaṃ ṭhapitanti sambandho. Yaṃ pana saṅghikaṃ vā puggalikaṃ vā atthīti yojanā. Tesaṃyevāti bhikkhubhikkhunīnameva[V 2.0021]. Ekarattampi ṭhapitaṃ yaṃ santakaṃ atthīti yojanā. Tanti saṅghikādi. Tatthāti akappiyabhūmiyaṃ sahaseyyapahonakagehe. Etanti antovutthaantopakkasaṅkhātaṃ yāvayāmakālikaṃ, “na kappatī”ti byatirekassa anvayaṃ dassento āha “sattāhakālikaṃ panā”tiādi.

The construction is: 'whatever material has been used, all that is material'. The connection is: 'what has been used or placed in an impermissible area, in a house sufficient for shared sleeping'. The construction is: 'but whatever belongs to the Sangha or to an individual exists'. By 'tesaṃyeva' (for them only), it means 'only for monks and nuns'. The construction is: 'even if placed for a single night, whatever property exists'. 'That' refers to what belongs to the Sangha, etc. By 'tattha' (there), it means 'in an impermissible area, in a house suitable for shared sleeping'. By 'etaṃ' (this), it refers to what is designated as 'dwelling within' or 'storing within', which is yāvakālika (food to be consumed within the forenoon). Showing the application of the exclusion 'it is not permissible', he says 'but for seven days...' etc.

Tatrāti purimavacanāpekkhaṃ. Tatra vacaneti hi attho. Sāmaṇero detīti sambandho. Yaṃkiñci taṇḍulādikaṃ āmisanti yojanā. Mukhasannidhi nāmāti āpattiyā mukho upāyo sannidhi nāmāti attho. Tatthāti mahāpaccariyaṃ, mukhasannidhiantovutthesu vā. Bhikkhu pacitvā paribhuñjatīti sambandho. Āmisasaṃsaṭṭhanti āmisena saṃsaggaṃ.

By 'tatra' (there), it refers to the preceding statement. Indeed, the meaning is 'in that statement'. 'A novice gives' is the connection. The construction is: 'whatever rice etc. is material'. The meaning of 'mukhasannidhi' is: 'mukho' is the entrance or means to an offense; 'sannidhi' means storing. By 'tattha' (there), it means 'in the Mahāpaccarī, or in cases of mukhasannidhi (storing in the mouth) and antovuttha (dwelling within)'. 'A monk cooks and consumes' is the connection. 'Āmisasaṃsaṭṭha' means 'association with material'.

Jahitavatthukāti jahitaṃ vatthu etāsanti jahitavatthukā. Ussāvanantikā katāti sambandho. Sāti ussāvanantikā. Yo yoti thambho vā bhittipādo vā. Iṭṭhakādīhi katā ussāvanantikāti yojanā. Cayassāti adhiṭṭhānassa. Yehi pana iṭṭhakādīhītiādisaddena thambhasilāmattikāyo saṅgaṇhāti. Tadaññesūti tehi adhiṭṭhitaiṭṭhakādīhi aññesu.

'Jahitavatthukā' means 'those that have a base that has been abandoned'. 'It is made into an ussāvanantikā' is the connection. 'That' refers to the ussāvanantikā. By 'yo yo' (whatever), it means a pillar or a wall base. The construction is: 'an ussāvanantikā made of bricks etc.'. By 'cayassa' (of the pile), it means 'of the determination'. By the word 'etc.' in 'but by which bricks etc.', it includes pillars, stones, and clay. By 'tadaññesu' (in others than these), it means 'in things other than those determined bricks etc.'.

Pākārādiparikkhepeti upacārasīmāparicchinnassa ārāmassa pākārādinā parikkhepe kate. Pākārādīti ādisaddena vatiṃ saṅgaṇhāti. Kappiyakuṭiṃ laddhuṃ vaṭṭatīti gonisādikāya abhāvena sesāsu [M 0.0356] tīsu kappiyakuṭīsu yaṃkiñci kappiyakuṭiṃ laddhuṃ vaṭṭatīti attho. Tattha tatthāti tasmiṃ tasmiṃ ṭhāne. Itarā panāti ussāvanantikagonisādikāhi aññā. Dveti ubho gahapatisammutiyo, jahitavatthukāva hontīti sambandho. Pakkhapāsakamaṇḍalanti dve pakkhe apatanatthāya pasati bandhatīti pakkhapāsako, maṇḍalanti chadanakoṭigopānasīnaṃ upari ṭhapitakaṭṭhaviseso, pakkhapāsako ca maṇḍalañca pakkhapāsakamaṇḍalaṃ.

In 'pākārādiparikkhepe' (enclosure by walls etc.), it means when an enclosure by walls etc. has been made for a monastery whose boundary is defined by proximity. By 'pākārādi' (walls etc.), the word 'etc.' includes fences. The meaning is: 'it is permissible to obtain a suitable hut', because in the absence of a gonisādikā, it is permissible to obtain any suitable hut from the remaining three suitable huts. By 'tattha tattha' (here and there), it means 'in each respective place'. The other, however, refers to that which is other than the ussāvanantikā and gonisādikā. The connection is: 'the two, that is, the householder-hut and the designated-hut, are indeed of abandoned property'. 'Pakkhapāsakamaṇḍala' means: 'pakkhapāsaka' is that which ties and fastens the two wings in order not to fall; 'maṇḍala' is a special piece of wood placed above the ends of the roof and the rafters; and 'pakkhapāsaka' and 'maṇḍala' together form 'pakkhapāsakamaṇḍala'.

Yatrāti yasmiṃ ṭhāne. Anupasampannassa datvāti anapekkhavissajjanena anupasampannassa datvā. Cīvaravikappanaṃ viya sāpekkhavissajjanampi vaṭṭatīti vadanti. Tatrāti purimavacanāpekkhaṃ. Soti karavīkatissatthero, passitvā pucchīti sambandho. Theroti mahāsivatthero. Lūkhadivaseti asiniddhadivase. Tatoti bravanato, paranti sambandho. Nanti mahāsivattheraṃ. Pamukheti gabbhassa pamukhe. Tanti sabbikumbhiṃ. Bahīti vihārassa bahi. Soti mahāsivatthero.

'Where' means in which place. 'Given to one not fully ordained' means given to one not fully ordained by way of an unexpecting release. Some say that even a release with expectation, like the formal disposal of a robe, is permissible. 'There' refers to the previous statement. 'He' refers to the Elder Karavīka Tissa; the connection is that having seen, he asked. 'The Elder' refers to the Great Elder Sīva. 'On a rough day' means on a day without moisture (asiniddha). By 'tato' (then), it means 'from speaking'; 'paraṃ' (what follows) is the connection. 'Him' refers to the Great Elder Sīva. 'At the entrance' means at the front of the inner chamber. 'That' refers to the kettle (sabbikumbhiṃ). 'Outside' means outside the monastery. 'He' refers to the Great Elder Sīva.

180. Meṇḍakagahapativatthukathā

180. The Story of the Householder Meṇḍaka

296. “Bahidvāre”ti [V 2.0022] ettha kassa bahidvāreti āha “dhaññāgārassa bahidvāre”ti. Āḷakathālikanti ettha āḷakataṇḍulapacanakaṃ gaṇhakathāli āḷakathāli, tāya pacitaṃ bhattaṃ āḷakathālikanti vacanatthaṃ dassento āha “āḷakataṇḍulapacanakathālika”nti. Byañjanabhaṇḍikanti byañjanaparikkhārikaṃ, byañjanaparivārakanti attho. Iminā sūpabhiñjanakanti ettha sūpasaddo byañjanavācako, bhiñjanakasaddo bhaṇḍikapariyāyoti dasseti. Dāsakammakaraporisanti ettha dāsaporisā ca kammakaraporisā ca dāsakammakaraporisaṃ, samāhāradvando pubbapade uttaralopo, iti imamatthaṃ dassento āha “dāsapurise ca kammakarapurise cā”ti. Porisasaddopi purisasaddena samāno “puriso eva poriso”ti atthena. Dhuvabhattenāti ettha dhuvasaddo niccapariyāyoti āha “niccakāla”nti. Duyhena khīrenāti sambandho. “Meṇḍakavatthusmiṃ panā”ti pāṭhato paṭṭhāya yāva “khaṇaññeva duyhenā”ti [M 0.0357] pāṭhā kesuciyeva aṭṭhakathāpotthakesu atthi. Etthāti meṇḍakavatthumhi. Goraseti gavayehi nibbatte khīradadhitakkanavanītasabbisaṅkhāte rase. Pātheyyanti pathassa hitaṃ pātheyyaṃ. Ñatvāti pātheyyamicchatīti ñatvā. Bhikkhācāravattena vāti aññātakaapavāritaṭṭhānato bhikkhācāravattena vā. Yācitvāpīti pisaddo pageva bhikkhācāravattenāti dasseti. Yattakena pātheyyenāti sambandho.

296. 'Outside the gate'—here, when asked whose outer gate, it is said, 'outside the gate of the granary.' Regarding 'āḷakathālikaṃ,' a pot for cooking a measure of rice is an 'āḷakathāli.' To show that the meaning of the word is 'rice cooked in that pot,' he says, 'a pot for cooking a measure of rice.' 'Byañjanabhaṇḍikaṃ' means 'that which is an accessory to curry,' or 'curry accompaniments.' By this, regarding 'sūpabhiñjanakaṃ,' it is shown that the word 'sūpa' is a term for curry, and the word 'bhiñjanaka' is a synonym for 'bhaṇḍika.' Regarding 'dāsakammakaraporisaṃ,' here, male slaves and male laborers are 'dāsakammakaraporisaṃ,' a collective compound with elision of the latter part of the first word. To show this meaning, it is said, 'male slaves and male laborers.' Also, the word 'porisa' is synonymous with 'purisa,' with the meaning 'a man is indeed a porisa.' Regarding 'dhuvabhattena,' here, the word 'dhuva' is a synonym for 'constant,' so he says, 'at all times.' The connection is 'with freshly milked milk.' The passage from the reading 'But in the story of Meṇḍaka' up to the reading 'milked only for a moment' is found only in some commentary manuscripts. 'Here' means in the story of Meṇḍaka. 'Gorase' refers to the products derived from cattle, consisting of milk, curds, buttermilk, butter, and ghee. 'Pātheyyaṃ' is what is beneficial for the journey. 'Knowing' means knowing that he desires provisions for the journey. 'Or by the practice of the alms-round' means by the practice of the alms-round from a place of non-relatives or from an uninvited place. Regarding 'yācitvāpi,' the word 'pi' shows 'how much more so than by the practice of the alms-round.' The connection is 'with whatever provisions for the journey.'

182. Keṇiyajaṭilavatthukathā

182. The Story of Keṇiya the Jaṭila Ascetic

300. Kājehīti ettha kājassa gaṇanaṃ dassento āha “pañcahi kājasatehī”ti. Ekena kājena dvinnaṃ kuṭānaṃ gahitattā vuttaṃ “kuṭasahassa”nti. Voti tumhe. Suṭṭhu pasannoti sambandho.

300. Regarding 'kājehi,' here, indicating the number of kāja poles, he says, 'with five hundred kāja poles.' Because two huts are obtained from one kāja pole, it is said 'a thousand huts.' 'Vo' means 'you.' The connection is, 'very pleased.'

Tatthāti “aṭṭha pānānī”ti pāṭhe, aṭṭhasu pānesu vā. “Ambehi katapāna”nti iminā majjhelopasamāsaṃ dasseti. Tatthāti āmapakkesu. Karontena kātabbanti sambandho. Ādiccapākenāti ādiccahetunā pacanena. Purebhattameva kappatīti bhikkhunā sayaṃ katattā purebhattameva kappati. Tena vuttaṃ “anupasampannehī”tiādi. Kataṃ ambapānanti sambandho. Sabbapānesūti jambupānādīsu sabbesu pānesu.

'There' means in the reading 'eight drinks,' or among the eight drinks. By 'a drink made with mangoes,' he indicates a compound with a middle term elided. 'There' means among unripe and ripe fruits. The connection is 'what should be done by the one doing.' 'By sun-cooking' means by cooking due to the sun. 'It is suitable only before the meal'—since it is made by the monk himself, it is suitable only before the meal. Hence it is said, 'by those not fully ordained,' etc. The connection is 'made mango drink.' 'Among all drinks' means among all drinks, such as jambu drink, etc.

Tesūti [V 2.0023] jambupānādīsu sattasu pānesu. Panasaddo visesatthajotako. Jambuphalehīti āmehi vā pakkehi vā jambuphalehi. Aṭṭhikehīti aṭṭhi asmimatthīti aṭṭhikaṃ phalaṃ. Jātirasenāti yathājātena rasena. Iminā madhusakkharakappurādīhi na yojetabboti dasseti. Taṃ panāti madhukapānaṃ pana. Muddikāti muddikaphalāni. Sāluketi kande. Sattannaṃ dhaññānaṃ phalarasanti taṇḍuladhovanodakaṃ. “Pakkaḍākarasa”nti iminā apakkaḍākarasaṃ vaṭṭatīti dīpeti. Hīti saccaṃ, vitthāro vā. Rasoti pakkaraso. Paṭiggahetvā ṭhapitasabbiādīhi pakkānaṃ yāvajīvikānaṃ pattānaṃ rasoti yojanā. Pakkaṃ yāvajīvikapattarasanti sambandho. Yāvakālikapattānampīti pisaddo pageva [M 0.0358] yāvajīvikapattānanti dasseti. Yaṃ pānanti yaṃ madhukapuppharasapānaṃ. Soti madhukapuppharaso. Tenāti madhukapupphena. Yato kālato paṭṭhāya majjaṃ na karonti, tatoti yojanā. Ucchuraso nikasaṭo pacchābhattaṃ vaṭṭati sattāhakālikattā. Ime cattāro rasāti phalapattapupphaucchurasasaṅkhātā ime cattāro rasā. Aggihuttamukhāti yaññā aggihutamukhā, aggihutaseṭṭhāti attho.

'Among these' means among the seven kinds of drinks, such as jambu drink. The word 'pana' indicates a special meaning. 'With jambu fruits' means with either unripe or ripe jambu fruits. 'With stones'—a fruit that has a stone is 'aṭṭhikaṃ.' 'With natural juice' means with its inherent juice. This shows that it should not be mixed with honey, sugar, camphor, etc. 'But that' means but that madhuka-drink. 'Muddikā' means grapes. 'Sāluke' means in the edible root. 'The juice of the fruit of seven kinds of grains' means the water from washing rice. By 'the juice of cooked grains,' he indicates that the juice of uncooked grains is permissible. 'Hi' means indeed, or it is an elaboration. 'Juice' means cooked juice. The construction is: the juice of lifelong leaves cooked with ghee and so on, which have been received and set aside. The connection is ‘the juice of cooked lifelong leaves.’ Regarding 'even of leaves permissible for a limited time,' the word 'pi' shows 'how much more so of leaves permissible for life.' 'Whatever drink' means whatever drink made from madhuka-flower juice. 'That' means the madhuka-flower juice. 'By that' means by the madhuka-flower. The construction is: from whatever time they do not make it into an intoxicant, from then on. Sugarcane juice without dregs is permissible after the midday meal because it is allowed for seven days. 'These four juices' means these four juices enumerated as fruit juice, leaf juice, flower juice, and sugarcane juice. 'Having the fire-sacrifice as foremost' means sacrifices that have the fire-offering as foremost; the meaning is the best of sacrifices.

183. Rojamallādivatthukathā

183. The Story of Roja the Mallian and Others

301. Saṅkaramakaṃsūti ettha saṅkarasaddassa yuddhatthādīsu pavattanato idha paṭiññātattheti dassento āha “katikamakaṃsū”ti. Katikanti paṭiññātasaṅkhātaṃ katikaṃ. Uḷāraṃ khoti ettha uḷārasaddo seṭṭhavācako. Seṭṭhanti ca sundaramevāti āha “sundaraṃ kho te ida”nti. Teti tuyhaṃ. “Bahukato”ti padassa katabahumānoti atthaṃ dassento āha “pasādabahumānenā”ti. “Piṭṭhamayaṃkhādanīya”nti iminā piṭṭhakhādanīyanti ettha mayasaddalopaṃ dasseti.

301. Regarding 'saṅkaramakaṃsu,' here, since the word 'saṅkara' is used in meanings such as 'war,' to show that here it is in the sense of 'agreed upon,' he says 'katikamakaṃsu.' 'Katikaṃ' is an agreement, that which is known as an agreement. Regarding 'uḷāraṃ kho,' here, the word 'uḷāra' is a term for 'excellent.' And, saying that 'excellent' is indeed 'beautiful,' he says, 'This is indeed beautiful for you.' 'Te' means 'your.' To show that the meaning of the word 'bahukato' is 'much respect shown,' he says, 'with faith and much reverence.' By 'piṭṭhamayaṃkhādanīyaṃ,' he shows the elision of the word 'maya' in 'piṭṭhakhādanīyaṃ.'

303. Paṭibhāneyyakāti ettha paṭibhāne niyuttā paṭibhāneyyakāti dassento āha “paṭibhānasampannā”ti. “Niddosasippā”ti iminā pariyodātasippāti ettha parisamantato odātaṃ sippaṃ etesanti pariyodātasippāti atthaṃ dasseti. Sippatthikehi siyati seviyatīti sippaṃ, sippikānaṃ hitāya seti pavattatīti vā sippaṃ, oṭṭhajo paṭhamakkharo. Nāḷiyāvāpakenāti padassa dvandabhāvaṃ dassento āha “nāḷiyā ceva āvāpakena cā”ti. Iminā yakāro padasandhimattoti dasseti. “Nāḷiyā vā pasibbakenā”tipi pāṭho, so apāṭhoyeva. Ko āvāpako nāmāti āha “āvāpako nāma yatthā”tiādi. Tattha yatthāti yasmiṃ thavike. Iminā āharitvā yathāladdhaṃ vapanti pakkhipanti etthāti āvāpakoti vacanatthaṃ dasseti. Vapa bījanikkhepeti dhātupāṭhesu (saddanītidhātumālāyaṃ 15 pakārantadhātu) vuttaṃ. Idha pana [V 2.0024] pakkhipaneti daṭṭhabbo. Tena vuttaṃ “pakkhipantī”ti. Pariharitumevāti pariggahetvā [M 0.0359] haritumeva. Vetananti bhatiṃ. Yoti bhikkhu. Taṃ vāti pariharitakhurabhaṇḍaṃ vā. Aññaṃ vāti aññassa santakaṃ vā.

303. Regarding 'paṭibhāneyyakā,' here, to show that 'paṭibhāneyyakā' means 'those appointed to respond,' he says 'endowed with the ability to respond.' By 'niddosasippā,' he shows the meaning of 'pariyodātasippā' here as 'those whose craft is thoroughly pure.' A craft is called 'sippaṃ' because it is bound to or practiced by those desiring a skill, or it exists for the benefit of craftsmen; the first letter is labial. To show the compound nature of the word 'nāḷiyāvāpakena,' he says 'by the needle case and by the pouch.' By this, he shows that the letter 'y' is merely for word conjunction. The reading 'nāḷiyā vā pasibbakenā' is indeed an incorrect reading. What is called an 'āvāpaka'? He says, 'An āvāpaka is where...' etc. There, 'where' means 'in which bag.' By this, he shows the meaning of the word 'āvāpaka' as that into which they bring and deposit what they have gathered. In the Dhātupāṭhas, 'vapa' is said to mean 'to scatter seeds.' Here, however, it should be understood as 'depositing.' Hence, it is said, 'they deposit.' 'Pariharitumeva' means 'to take and carry around.' 'Vetanaṃ' means 'wages.' 'Yo' means 'the monk.' 'Taṃ vā' means 'or the razor equipment being carried.' 'Aññaṃ vā' means 'or belonging to another.'

304. Idanti dasamabhāgadānaṃ. Dasa koṭṭhāseti dasa paṭivīse.

304. 'This' means 'a tenth-part offering.' 'Ten portions' means 'ten shares.'

185. Catumahāpadesakathā

185. The Discourse on the Four Great Authorities

305. Idaṃ na kappatītiādīti “idaṃ na kappatī”tiādayo ime cattāro mahāpadeseti yojanā. Apassayaṃ katvā disiyanti etthāti apadesā okāsā, apassayaṃ katvā disiyanti etehīti vā apadesā kāraṇā, “mahantā apadesā mahāpadesā. Tañcāti mahāpadesasaṅkhātaṃ tañca suttaṃ, gahetvāti yojanā. Parimaddantāti punappunaṃ maddantā, upaparikkhantāti attho. Idanti kāraṇaṃ. Tanti navamahāphalaaparaṇṇaṃ. Tānīti khuddakaphalapānāni. Hīti saccaṃ.

305. The connection is: 'these four great authorities, beginning with “This is not allowable.”' 'Apadesā' are locations (okāsā), because they are pointed out by making a reliance in them; or, 'apadesā' are causes (kāraṇā), because they are pointed out by making a reliance by means of them. 'Great apadesā' are 'mahāpadesā.' 'And that' means that discourse known as the Mahāpadesa; the connection is 'having taken.' 'Parimaddantā' means 'repeatedly rubbing,' that is, 'scrutinizing.' 'This' means 'the cause.' 'That' means 'the new great fruits and other grains.' 'Those' means 'the small fruits and drinks.' 'Hi' means 'indeed.'

Tesanti channaṃ cīvarānaṃ. Tatthāti chasu anulomacīvaresu. “Pāṇakehi sañjātavattha”nti iminā koseyyavatthabhāvaṃ dasseti. Dve paṭāti cīnapaṭasomārapaṭā. Dukūlaṃ sāṇassa anulomanti yojanā.

'Of these' means 'of the six robes.' 'Therein' means 'among the six allowable robes.' By 'cloth produced by living creatures,' he shows the nature of silk cloth. 'Two cloths' means 'Chinese cloth and Somāra cloth.' The connection is that 'dukūla' is similar to hempen cloth.

Tesaṃyevāti dvinnaṃ pattānameva. Tesaṃyevāti tiṇṇaṃ tumbānameva. Tesaṃyevāti dvinnaṃ kāyabandhanānameva. Setacchattanti setehi vatthehi kataṃ chattaṃ. Tesaṃyevāti tiṇṇaṃ chattānameva.

'Tesaṃyeva' means 'of just two bowls'. 'Tesaṃyeva' means 'of just three water pots'. 'Tesaṃyeva' means 'of just two waistbands'. 'Setacchatta' means 'an umbrella made of white cloth'. 'Tesaṃyeva' means 'of just three umbrellas'.

Sambhinnarasanti saṃsaggarasaṃ. Ettha bhijjitthāti bhinnoti vacanatthena bhididhātu dvidhākaraṇasaṅkhāto bhedattho hoti, dhātvatthabādhakena saṃtyūpasaggena bhididhātuyā bhedatthaṃ bādhetvā saṃsaggatthavācako hotīti daṭṭhabbaṃ. Challimpīti tacampi. Sakalenevāti challiyā eva. Pāyāsena asaṃsaṭṭhaṃ yaṃ sabbīti yojanā. Tānīti takkolajātiphalādīni. Yaṭṭhimadhukādīsupīti madhulaṭṭhikādīsupi. “Laṭṭhimadhukādīsupī”ti vā pāṭho, so apāṭhoyeva. Yaṃ yanti vatthu. Yathāti yenākārena, dhoviyamāne tacchiyamāneti sambandho.

'Sambhinnarasa' means 'the taste of association'. Here, by the meaning of the word 'bhinnoti' (it breaks), the root 'bhid' has the meaning of 'division', which is 'making into two parts'. However, it should be understood that the prefix 'saṃ', by obstructing the meaning of division of the root 'bhid', becomes a term for the meaning of 'association'. 'Challimpī' means 'even the bark'. 'Sakalena eva' means 'only with the bark itself'. The connection is: 'that ghee which is unmixed with rice-gruel'. 'Tāni' means 'takkola, jāti fruit, and so on'. 'Yaṭṭhimadhukādīsupi' means 'even in madhulaṭṭhikā and the like'. Alternatively, the reading 'Laṭṭhimadhukādīsupi' is indeed an incorrect reading. 'Yaṃ yaṃ' means 'whatever substance'. 'Yathā' means 'in whatever manner'; the connection is 'while being washed and scraped'.

Sambhinnarasanti [M 0.0360] vatvā tamevatthaṃ dassetuṃ vuttaṃ “saṃsaṭṭha”nti. Sabhāvanti yāvakālaṃ kappiyasabhāvaṃ[V 2.0025]. Tasmāti yasmā upaneti, tasmā. Tenāti sattāhakālikena. Tadahupaṭiggahitanti tadaheva paṭiggahitaṃ. Dvīhapaṭiggahitena sattāhakālikenāti sambandho.

Having stated 'sambhinnarasa', 'saṃsaṭṭha' is said to illustrate the same meaning. 'Sabhāva' means 'its suitable nature as long as it lasts'. 'Tasmā' means 'because it brings near, therefore'. 'Tena' means 'with that which is for seven days'. 'Tadahupaṭiggahita' means 'received on that very day'. The connection is 'with that received two days ago and that which is for seven days'.

Etthāti kālikasaṃsagge. Āpattiyo veditabbāti yathākkamaṃ āpattiyo veditabbā. Sabbatthāti sabbasmiṃ bhesajjakkhandhake.

'Ettha' means 'in this temporary association'. 'Āpattiyo veditabbā' means 'the offenses should be understood in due order'. 'Sabbattha' means 'throughout the entire section on medicines'.

Iti bhesajjakkhandhakavaṇṇanāya yojanā samattā.

Thus ends the explanation in the commentary on the section concerning medicines.

7. Kathinakkhandhakaṃ

7. The Kathina Section

187. Kathinānujānanakathā

187. The Discussion on the Authorization of the Kathina

306. Kathinakkhandhake pāveyyakāti ettha pāvāraṭṭhe nivasantīti pāveyyakāti vacanatthaṃ dassento āha “pāvāraṭṭhavāsino”ti. Tatthāti pāvānāmake raṭṭhe. Eko pitā etesanti ekapitukā. Te ca te bhātaro ceti ekapitukabhātaro, tesaṃ. Etanti “pāveyyakā”ti etaṃ nāmaṃ. Tesūti pāveyyakesu. “Dhutaṅgasamādānavasenā”ti visesanassa byavacchedabhāvaṃ dassetuṃ vuttaṃ “na araññavāsamattenā”ti. Visesanañhi duvidhaṃ byavacchedaṃ, tappākaṭikaraṇañcāti. Tesanti pāveyyakānaṃ. Piṇḍapātikādibhāvepīti sambandho. Pisaddo āraññakaṃ apekkhati. Etanti “sabbe āraññakā”tiādi etaṃ vacanaṃ. Ime panāti pāveyyakā pana. Udakasaṃgaheti ettha udakena saṃgahetabbanti dassento āha “udakena saṃgahite”ti. “Thale ca ninne cā”ti iminā “udakasaṃgahe”ti padassa sarūpaṃ dasseti.

306. In the Kathina Section, regarding 'Pāveyyakā'—here, explaining the meaning of 'Pāveyyakā' as 'those dwelling in the Pāvā country', he says 'Pāvāraṭṭhavāsino'. 'Therein' means in the country named Pāvā. 'Having one father' means 'ekapitukā'. 'And they, those brothers' means 'ekapitukabhātaro' (brothers with one father); of them. 'This' refers to this name 'Pāveyyakā'. 'Among them' means among the Pāveyyakas. To show the restrictive nature of the specification 'by way of undertaking the ascetic practices', it is said 'not merely by dwelling in the forest'. For a specification is of two kinds: restrictive and explicative. 'Of them' means of the Pāveyyakas. The connection is with being alms-food eaters and so on. The particle 'pi' refers to the forest-dweller. 'This' refers to this statement 'all are forest-dwellers' and so on. 'But these' means these Pāveyyakas. Regarding 'udakasaṃgahe', here, showing that it is to be collected by water, he says 'udakena saṃgahite' (collected by water). By 'on high ground and in low ground', he shows the nature of the word 'udakasaṃgahe'.

Udakacikkhalloti udakena loḷito cikkhallo udakacikkhallo. Okapuṇṇehīti ettha okasaddo udakavevacanoti āha “udakapuṇṇehī”ti. Udakañhi ucayati samavāyabhāvena pavattatīti okanti [M 0.0361] vuccati. Tesanti pāveyyakānaṃ. Ghanānīti nirantarāni. Tesūti cīvaresu. Tenāti cīvarānaṃ ghanattā, udakassa ca na paggharaṇattā. Bhagavatā “avivadamānā phāsukaṃ vassaṃ vasitthā”ti pucchiyamānāpi te bhikkhū yathāpucchitaṃ avatvā kasmā phāsukapadaṃ apanetvā [V 2.0026] “avivadamānā vassaṃ vasimhā”ti avocunti āha “avivadamānā vassaṃ vasimhāti etthā”tiādi. Ukkaṇṭhitatāya cāti ettha casaddo “phāsutāya abhāvenā”ti etthāpi yojetabbo. Senāsanaphāsutāya abhāvena ca bhagavato dassanālābhena ukkaṇṭhitatāya cāti hi attho. Anamataggiyakathanti saṃyuttanikāye anamataggiyasuttantakathaṃ (saṃ. ni. 2.135). Sabbeva te pāveyyakā bhikkhūti yojanā. Tanti anamataggiyakathaṃ. Tatoti dhammakathanato, paranti sambandho. Bhagavā āmantesīti sambandho. Ekaṃ cīvaranti saṅghāṭiṃ. Santaruttarenāti saha antarenāti santaraṃ, santarañca taṃ uttarañceti santaruttaraṃ, tena. Assuti bhaveyyuṃ. Abhavissaṃsūti hi attho. Sattamīvibhattikālātipattivibhattīnaṃ samānatthabhāvo saddasatthesu vuttoyeva. Casaddo upanyāsattho. Esa kathinatthāro nāmāti yojanā. Anujānitukāmo hutvāti sambandho.

'Udakacikkhallo' means mud stirred up by water. Regarding 'okapuṇṇehi', here, saying that the word 'oka' is a synonym for water, he says 'udakapuṇṇehi' (filled with water). For water accumulates and flows in a continuous manner, hence it is called 'oka'. 'Of them' means of the Pāveyyakas. 'Dense' means without gaps. 'In them' means in the robes. 'By that' means due to the density of the robes and the water not dripping through. Though asked by the Blessed One, 'Did you dwell comfortably and harmoniously during the rains?', why did those bhikkhus, without answering as asked, omit the word 'comfortably' and say, 'We dwelled without dispute during the rains?' He says, 'Regarding “We dwelled without dispute during the rains,”' and so on. And regarding 'due to discontent', here the particle 'ca' should be connected also to 'due to the absence of comfort'. For the meaning is: due to discontent arising from the lack of comfort in lodging places and from not obtaining a sight of the Blessed One. 'Anamataggiyakathā' means the discourse on the beginningless, the Anamatagga Sutta in the Saṃyutta Nikāya (SN 15). The connection is: all those Pāveyyaka bhikkhus. 'That' refers to the Anamataggiyakathā. 'From that' means from the teaching of the Dhamma; 'after' is the connection. The connection is: the Blessed One addressed them. 'A single robe' means the saṅghāṭi. 'Santaruttarena' means 'santara' is 'saha antara' (together with the inner robe), and that which is 'santara' and 'uttara' (outer robe) is 'santaruttara'; by that. 'Assu' means 'bhaveyyuṃ' (they would be). For the meaning is 'abhavissaṃsu' (they would have been). The identical meaning of the seventh case (locative) and the conditional mood is indeed stated in the grammatical texts. The particle 'ca' has an introductory sense. The connection is: this is called the spreading of the Kathina. The connection is: wishing to allow it.

Tatthāti “anujānāmi bhikkhave”tiādipāṭhe. Vokārassa nipātamatte sati kathamattho bhavissatīti āha “atthatakathinānanti attho”ti. Atthatakathinānaṃ bhikkhūnanti sambandho. Laddhaguṇaṃ dassento āha “evañhī”tiādi. Hisaddo laddhaguṇajotako. Paratoti paramhi. “So tumhāka”nti vā “so vo”ti vā avatvā “so nesaṃ bhavissatī”ti vuttattā vo-kāro nipātamattoti adhippāyo. “Voti sāmivacanameveta”nti iminā vo tumhākanti atthaṃ dasseti. Evaṃ sati “parato so nesa”nti ettha kathamattho bhavissatīti āha “so nesanti ettha panā”tiādi. Ye tumhe atthatakathinā, tesaṃ tumhākanti yojanā. Kathinasaddo thiratthavācako anipphannapāṭipadiko[M 0.0362]. Anāmantacārādikānaṃ pañcānisaṃsānaṃ antokaraṇasamatthabhāve thiranti attho.

Therein, in the passage beginning 'I allow, bhikkhus,' and so on. If 'vo' were merely a particle, how would there be meaning? He says, 'the meaning is “of those who have spread the Kathina.”' The connection is to the bhikkhus who have spread the Kathina. Showing the quality that has been obtained, he says 'for indeed,' and so on. The word 'hi' indicates the quality that has been obtained. 'Parato' means 'from another'. Because it was not said 'that is yours' or 'that is for you', but rather 'that will be for them', the intention is that 'vo' is merely a particle. By 'vo is indeed a term of ownership', he shows the meaning of 'vo' as 'yours'. This being so, how would there be meaning in 'from another, that is for them'? He says, 'But regarding “that is for them,”' and so on. The connection is: 'of you who have spread the Kathina, it is yours'. The word 'kathina' conveys the meaning of 'steadfast' and is an underived nominal stem. The meaning is 'steadfast' in its capacity to encompass the five benefits beginning with unannounced wandering.

Tatthāti anāmantacārādīsu pañcānisaṃsesu. Anāmantacāroti ettha caraṇaṃ cāro, anāmantetvā cāro anāmantacāroti dassento āha “anāmantetvā caraṇa”nti. “Asamādāya caraṇa”nti iminā asamādānacāroti ettha pubbapade tvāpaccayassa anādesaṃ katvā asamādānacāroti vuttanti dasseti. Yāvatatthacīvaranti ettha ākāralopena sandhīti āha “yāvatā cīvarena attho”ti. “Yāvadatthacīvara”ntipi pāṭho, evaṃ sati dakāro padasandhimatto. Yāvasaddo paricchedatthavācako, na abhivijhatthavācako. Atthasaddena samāso hoti. Yo ca tattha cīvaruppādoti ettha tatthasaddassa visayaṃ dassento āha “kathinatthārasīmāya”nti. Tatruppādenāti tatra kathinatthārasīmāyaṃ uppādena mūlena. “Cīvaraṃ uppajjatī”ti [V 2.0027] iminā cīvaruppādoti ettha cīvarameva uppādo cīvaruppādoti visesanaparapadattaṃ dasseti.

Therein, among the five benefits beginning with unannounced wandering. Regarding 'anāmantacāro', here, showing that 'caraṇa' is 'cāro', and 'anāmantetvā cāro' is 'anāmantacāro', he says 'anāmantetvā caraṇa'. By 'asamādāya caraṇa', he shows that in 'asamādānacāro', the 'tvā' suffix in the prior term has been omitted, and thus it is stated as 'asamādānacāro'. Regarding 'yāvatatthacīvaraṃ', here, he says 'yāvatā cīvarena attho', explaining that the sandhi is due to the elision of the 'ā' vowel. 'Yāvadatthacīvaraṃ' is also a reading; in that case, the 'da' is merely for connecting words. The word 'yāva' expresses limitation, not pervasion. It is compounded with the word 'attha'. And regarding 'yo ca tattha cīvaruppādo', here, showing the scope of the word 'there', he says 'within the Kathina-spreading boundary'. 'Tatruppādena' means by the arising within that Kathina-spreading boundary, which is the root. By 'cīvaraṃ uppajjati', he shows that in 'cīvaruppādo', where 'the robe-material itself is the arising', it is a compound where the latter member is the qualifier.

Keti kittakā. Idaṃ “gaṇavasenā”ti vacanaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ. Atha vā keti kinnāma vutthavassā. Idaṃ “vutthavassavasenā”ti vacanaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ. Satasahassampi janā labhantīti yojanā. Pisaddena tato adhikampi labhantīti dasseti. Chinnavassā vāti purimikāya upagantvā chinnavassā vā. Aññasmiṃ vihāreti kathinatthāravihārato aparasmiṃ vihāre. Sabbe chinnavassādikā bhikkhū purimikāya vassūpagatānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ gaṇapūrakā hontīti yojanā. Itaresaṃyevāti purimikāya vassaṃ upagantvā paṭhamapavāraṇāya pavāritānameva. Paripuṇṇavassoti paripuṇṇo vīsativasso, acchinnavasso vā. Soti sāmaṇero. Iti etthāpīti evaṃ etesu tīsu vāresupi.

'Ke' means 'kittakā' (how many). This is said with reference to the phrase 'by way of the group'. Alternatively, 'ke' means 'kinnāma vutthavassā' (what kind of rains-dweller). This is said with reference to the phrase 'by way of those who have dwelt through the rains'. The construction is: even a hundred thousand people may obtain it. By the particle 'pi', he shows that they may obtain even more than that. 'Chinnavassā vā' (or those whose rains-residence has been broken) means those whose rains-residence has been broken, having joined the earlier group. 'Aññasmiṃ vihāre' (in another monastery) means in a monastery other than the one where the kathina is laid out. The construction is: all the bhikkhus, beginning with those whose rains-residence has been broken, are completers of the group for the bhikkhus who entered the rains-residence in the earlier group. 'Itaresaṃyeva' (only of the others) means only of those who, having entered the rains-residence in the earlier group, have performed the first Pavāraṇā. 'Paripuṇṇavasso' (one with rains-residence completed) means one who has fully completed twenty years of seniority, or one whose rains-residence was not broken. 'So' (he) means a novice. 'Iti etthāpi' (thus here also) means thus, even in these three instances.

Kena dinnaṃ kathinacīvaraṃ vaṭṭatīti yojanā. Yena kenaci dinnaṃ cīvaraṃ vaṭṭatīti sambandho. Tanti vattaṃ. Ajānantoti ajānanahetu. Hetvatthe [M 0.0363] hi antapaccayo. Tassāti kathinadāyakassa. Evanti iminā vakkhamānanayena. Aññatarapahonakaṃ vatthanti sambandho. Tassāti kathinacīvarassa. Ettakā nāma sūciyo vaṭṭatīti sambandho. Iti ācikkhitabbanti yojanā.

The construction is: a kathina robe given by whom is allowable? The connection is: a robe given by anyone whatsoever is allowable. 'Taṃ' (that) means the duty. 'Ajānanto' (not knowing) means because of not knowing. For the 'anta' suffix is used here in the sense of cause. 'Tassa' (his) means of the kathina giver. 'Evaṃ' (thus) means in this way that is to be explained. The connection is: a certain suitable cloth. 'Tassa' (its) means of the kathina robe. The connection is: so many needles are allowable. The construction is: thus it should be taught.

Kathinatthārakenāpi vattaṃ jānitabbanti sambandho. Pisaddo kathinadāyakaṃ apekkhati. Vattaṃ vitthārento āha “tantavāyagehato hī”tiādi. Ābhatasantānenevāti ābhatasantatiyā eva. Khalimakkhitasāṭakoti ahatasāṭako. So hi khalena takkena kañjikena makkhitasāṭakattā “khalimakkhitasāṭako”ti vuccati. Kathinatthārasāṭakanti kathinatthāratthāya dinnaṃ sāṭakaṃ. Tadahevāti tasmiṃ dinnaahani eva. Tasminti paṭhamaṃ dinne kathinatthārasāṭake. Aññāni cāti kathinasāṭakato aññāni ca. Casaddena na kathinasāṭakameva āharati, aññāni cāti dasseti. Yoti kathinadāyako. Itaroti paṭhamaṃ kathinadāyako. Yathā tathā ovaditvāti tava santakato etassa santakaṃ saṅghassa bahupakāraṃ, saṅghassa bahupakārattaṃ tayāpi icchitabbaṃ, evamicchantassa bahupuññanti yena tenākārena ovaditvā.

The connection is: even the one who lays out the Kathina should know the duties. The particle 'pi' has reference to the Kathina donor. Elaborating on the duties, he says 'for from the weaver's house,' and so forth. 'Ābhatasantānena eva' means 'ābhatasantatiyā eva' (by the very succession of what has been brought). 'Khalimakkhitasāṭako' means a new robe. For it is called 'khalimakkhitasāṭako' because it is a robe smeared with paste, buttermilk, and rice gruel. 'Kathinatthārasāṭakaṃ' means the robe given for the purpose of laying out the Kathina. 'Tadaheva' means on the very day it was given. 'Tasmiṃ' means in the first Kathina-laying robe that was given. 'Aññāni ca' means other things besides the Kathina robe. By the particle 'ca', he shows that not only the Kathina robe is brought, but also other things. 'Yo' means the Kathina donor. 'Itaro' means the first Kathina donor. 'Yathā tathā ovaditvā' means advising in whatever manner, for instance, by saying: 'Compared to your possession, this possession of his is of great benefit to the Saṅgha. Since it is of great benefit to the Saṅgha, this should also be desired by you. For one who desires thus, there is much merit.'

Kena bhikkhunāti sambandho. Yassa saṅgho kathinacīvaraṃ deti, tena bhikkhunā attharitabbanti yojanā. Kassa bhikkhussāti sambandho. Yo jiṇṇacīvaro hoti, tassa dātabbanti [V 2.0028] yojanā. Mahatī parisā etassāti mahāpariso thero. “Navakataro sakkoti, tassa dātabba”nti vacanassa anekantabhāvaṃ dassento āha “api cā”tiādi. Api cāti ekantena. Tadatthāyāti tassa jiṇṇacīvarassa atthāya. Assāti bhikkhussa. Pelavoti viraḷo. Tenāpīti kathinatthārakenāpi. Tanti vidhiṃ. Dānakammavācāti dānakāraṇakammavācā.

The connection is: 'by which bhikkhu'. The construction is: it should be spread by that bhikkhu to whom the Saṅgha gives the Kathina robe. The connection is: 'to which bhikkhu'. The construction is: it should be given to him who has worn-out robes. 'Mahatī parisā etassa' (he has a large assembly) is the analysis of 'mahāpariso thero' (an elder with a large following). To show the non-conclusive nature of the statement, 'A more junior one is capable, it should be given to him,' he says, 'api ca,' and so forth. 'Api ca' means certainly. 'Tadatthāya' means for the sake of that worn-out robe. 'Assa' means to the bhikkhu. 'Pelavo' means sparse. 'Tenāpi' means even by the one who spreads the Kathina. 'Taṃ' means the procedure. 'Dānakammavācā' means the formal act of donation.

Evaṃ dinne pana kathine niṭṭhāpetabbānīti yojanā. Ekenāpīti pisaddena pageva bahūhi panāti dasseti. Buddhappasatthanti buddhehi pasatthaṃ. Atīte kappasatasahassamatthaketi yojanā. Tassāti padumuttarassa[M 0.0364]. Kathinaṃ gaṇhi kirāti yojanā. Tanti kathinaṃ, satthā akāsīti sambandho.

The construction is: when the Kathina is thus given, the duties should be completed. The particle 'pi' in 'ekenāpi' indicates: if by one, how much more so by many. 'Buddhappasatthaṃ' means praised by the Buddhas. The construction is: 'in the past, at the culmination of a hundred thousand aeons.' 'Tassa' refers to the Buddha Padumuttara. The construction is: 'he took up the Kathina, it is said.' 'Taṃ' refers to the Kathina; the connection is: 'the Teacher did it.'

Katapariyositaṃ kathinaṃ kiṃ kātabbanti āha “katapariyositaṃ panā”tiādi. Kathinaṃ gahetvā attharitabbanti sambandho. “Tena kathinatthārakena bhikkhunā”ti padaṃ “vacanīyo”ti pade suddhakattā, “anumodāpetabba”nti pade kāritakattā. Kiṃ vacanīyoti āha “atthataṃ…pe… anumodathā”ti. “Tehi anumodakehi bhikkhuhī”ti padaṃ “vacanīyo”ti pade avuttakattā, “anumodāpetabba”nti pade kāritakammaṃ avuttakammaṃ, vā. “Kathina”nti dhātukammaṃ vā vuttakammaṃ vā upanetabbaṃ. Kiṃ vacanīyoti āha “atthataṃ…pe… anumodāmā”ti. Itarehi cāti anumodakehi ca. Sabbesanti atthārakaanumodakānaṃ. Hīti saccaṃ. Etanti sabbesaṃ atthatabhāvaṃ, “dvinnaṃ…pe… anumodakassa cā”ti vacanaṃ vā.

Regarding what should be done with the completed Kathina, he says, 'The completed Kathina, then...' and so forth. The connection is: 'Having taken the Kathina, it should be spread.' The phrase 'by that monk who spreads the Kathina' is the instigating agent in relation to the word 'should be addressed,' and the causative agent in relation to the word 'should be made to rejoice.' What should be said? He says, 'The Kathina has been spread... please rejoice.' The phrase 'by those rejoicing monks' is the unexpressed agent in relation to the word 'should be addressed,' and the causative object or unexpressed object in relation to the word 'should be made to rejoice.' The word 'Kathina' should be supplied either as the object of the verb root or as the expressed object. What should be said? He says, 'The Kathina has been spread... we rejoice.' 'And by the others' means by the rejoicing ones. 'Sabbesaṃ' refers to the spreader and the rejoicers. 'Hi' means truly. 'Etaṃ' refers to the state of its having been spread for all, or to the statement 'of two... and of the rejoicer.'

Evaṃ kathine atthate sati panāti yojanā. Yenāti bhikkhunā. Avicāretvāvāti “kathinatthārakassa demā”ti vā “saṅghassa demā”ti vā avicāretvā eva. Sesacīvarānipīti kathinatthāracīvarato sesacīvarānipi. Saṅghena dātabbānīti sambandho. “Apaloketvā”ti iminā kammavācāya kiccābhāvaṃ dasseti. Vassāvāsikaṭṭhitikāyāti vassāvāsakāle pavattāya ṭhitikāya. Garubhaṇḍanti mañcabibbohanādigarubhaṇḍaṃ. Ekasīmāyāti ekāya upacārasīmāya.

The construction is: when the Kathina has been thus spread... 'Yena' refers to the bhikkhu. 'Avicāretvā' means without deliberation, that is, without considering whether to say, 'We give to the one who spreads the Kathina,' or 'We give to the Saṅgha.' 'Sesacīvarānipi' refers to the remaining robes apart from the Kathina-spreading robe. The connection is: 'They should be given by the Saṅgha.' By 'apaloketvā' (having announced), he shows the absence of any need for a formal act. 'Vassāvāsikaṭṭhitikāya' refers to the established practice prevailing during the time of the rains-residence. 'Garubhaṇḍa' means heavy goods such as couches and bolsters. 'Ekasīmāya' refers to a single precinct boundary.

308. Yathā cāti ettha yathāsaddo yaṃsaddattho. Yena vidhināti hi attho. Mahābhūmikanti mahāvisayaṃ. Catuvīsatiākāravantatāya mahāvitthārikanti vuttaṃ hoti. Tatoti anatthatalakkhaṇato. Parivārepīti pisaddo na idha evāti dasseti.

308. Regarding 'yathā ca,' here the word 'yathā' has the meaning of the word 'yaṃ.' Indeed, the meaning is 'by which method.' 'Mahābhūmika' means having a vast domain. It is said to be 'mahāvitthārika' (greatly extensive) because it possesses twenty-four aspects. 'Tato' means from the characteristic of not being spread. The particle 'pi' in 'parivārepi' indicates that it is not only here.

Tatthāti catuvīsatiyā ākāresu. Ullikhitamattenāti ettha pamāṇassa uggahaṇatthaṃ nakhādīhi [V 2.0029] likhanaṃ ullikhitaṃ, ullikhitaṃ mattaṃ pamāṇaṃ ullikhitamattanti dassento āha “dīghato ca puthulato [M 0.0365] ca pamāṇagahaṇamattenā”ti. Tamevatthaṃ vitthārento āha “pamāṇaṃ hī”tiādi. Dassento hutvā ullikhatīti yojanā. Pañcakanti pañcapamāṇaṃ, pañcasamūhaṃ vā khaṇḍaṃ. Vāsaddena aññānipi terasakādīni saṅgaṇhāti. Moghasuttakāropanamattenāti moghasuttassa cīvarassūpari āropanamattena. Dīghasibbitamattenāti dīghato sibbitamattena. Muddiyapaṭṭabandhanamattenāti muddiyapaṭṭassa bandhanamattena. Dve cimilikāyoti dve pilotikāyo. Paṭhamacimilikāti kathinacimilikato aññā attano pakaticimilikā ghaṭetvā ṭhapitā hotīti yojanā. “Taṃ paṭhamacimilika”nti pāṭhasesaṃ ajjhāharitvā kathinasāṭakassa kucchicimilikaṃ katvāti iminā sambandhitabbaṃ. Pakaticīvarassāti attano pakaticīvarassa. Pakatipaṭṭabandhacīvaranti pakatipaṭṭena bandhacīvaraṃ. Piṭṭhianuvātāropanamattenāti dīghato anuvātassa cīvarassūpari āropanamattena. Dīghānuvātañhi pārupanakāle piṭṭhiyaṃ ṭhitattā piṭṭhianuvātanti vuccati. Kucchianuvātāropanamattenāti puthulato anuvātassa cīvarassūpari āropanamattena. Puthulānuvātañhi pārupanakāle kucchiyaṃ ṭhitattā kucchianuvātanti vuccati. Āgantukapaṭṭāropanamattenāti āgantukapaṭṭassa cīvarassūpari āropanamattena. Vāti athavā.

'Therein' refers to the twenty-four aspects. Regarding 'ullikhitamattena': here, 'ullikhitaṃ' means scratching with nails and so on for the purpose of grasping the measurement. Showing that 'ullikhitamattaṃ' means the mere measurement of what is scratched, it is said: 'merely by grasping the measurement in length and breadth.' Elaborating on that very meaning, it is said: 'The measurement, indeed,' and so forth. The explanation is that one scratches in order to show. 'Pañcakaṃ' means five measurements, or a group of five fragments. By the word 'vā', it also includes other sets like thirteen, etc. 'Merely placing a useless thread' means merely placing a useless thread over the robe. 'Merely a long seam' means merely sewn lengthwise. 'Merely fastening a muddiyapaṭṭa' means merely fastening a muddiyapaṭṭa. 'Two cimilikā' means two pieces of cloth. The explanation is that 'the first cimilikā' means another cimilikā, one's own usual cimilikā, is prepared and placed apart from the Kathina cimilikā. The remaining text 'that first cimilikā' should be supplied and connected thus: 'making the Kathina cloth into a belly cimilikā.' 'Pakaticīvarassa' means of one's own usual robe. 'Pakatipaṭṭabandhacīvaraṃ' means a robe fastened with one's usual band. 'Merely placing a back anuvāta' means merely placing a long anuvāta over the robe. Indeed, the long anuvāta is called 'back anuvāta' because it stays on the back when worn. 'Merely placing a belly anuvāta' means merely placing a broad anuvāta over the robe. Indeed, the broad anuvāta is called 'belly anuvāta' because it stays on the belly when worn. 'Merely placing a visiting band' means merely placing a visiting band over the robe. 'Vā' means alternatively.

Sāruppanti samaṇānucchavikaṃ. Parikathāyāti pariyāyena uppāditāya kathāya. Atiukkaṭṭhaṃ vaṭṭatīti atiukkaṭṭhaṃ eva vaṭṭati. Otiṇṇasadisamevāti otiṇṇena vatthena sadisameva kathinacīvaranti sambandho. Tatthāti duvidhesu sannidhīsu. Tadahevāti tasmiṃ dinnaahani eva.
