'Sāruppaṃ' means appropriate for ascetics. 'Parikathāya' means by a talk generated indirectly. 'Atiukkaṭṭhaṃ vaṭṭati' means it is indeed excessively excellent. The connection is that 'otiṇṇasadisameva' means the Kathina robe is just like a spread-out cloth. 'Therein' refers to the two kinds of presence. 'Tadaheva' means on that very day it was given.

Rattinissaggiyenāti rattiatikkantaṃ hutvā nissaggiyena. Aññenāti ticīvarato aññena. Samaṇḍalikatanti saha mahāmaṇḍalaaḍḍhamaṇḍalena kataṃ.

'Rattinissaggiyena' means by that which is to be forfeited after the night has passed. 'Aññena' means by another, apart from the three robes. 'Samaṇḍalikaṃ' means made together with the great circle and a half-circle.

309. Evaṃ catuvīsatiākāraṃ anatthatalakkhaṇaṃ dassetvā idāni sattarasākāraṃ atthatalakkhaṇaṃ dassento āha “ahatenā”tiādi[M 0.0366]. Tattha paribhogaṃ na hanittha na gacchitthāti ahataṃ, paribhogena na hanitabbaṃ na hiṃsitabbanti vā ahatanti dassento āha “aparibhuttenā”ti. “Ahatasadisenā”ti iminā ahatakappenāti ettha kappasaddo sadisatthoti dasseti. Pāpaṇikenāti ettha pasārito āpaṇo pāpaṇo, tasmiṃ patitaṃ pāpaṇikanti dassento āha “āpaṇadvāre patita”nti. “Pilotika”nti iminā ṇikapaccayassa sarūpaṃ dasseti. Vuttavipallāsenevāti vuttehi “nimittakatenā”tiādīhi vipallāsena eva. Tatthāti parivāre[V 2.0030]. Hīti saccaṃ, yasmā vā. Idhāti kathinakkhandhake. Avuccamānena tena vacanena parihāyatīti sambandho.

309. Having thus shown the twenty-four characteristics of the unspread Kathina, now, showing the seventeen characteristics of the spread Kathina, he says, 'by an unspoiled one,' and so forth. Here, showing that 'ahataṃ' means it was not damaged or lost by use, or it should not be damaged or harmed by use, he says, 'by an unused one.' By 'ahatasadisena', it shows that the word 'kappa' here in 'ahatakappena' means 'like'. Regarding 'pāpaṇikena', here, showing that 'pāpaṇika' means something fallen in a shop, pāpaṇa, which is a spread-out shop, he says, 'fallen at the shop door.' By 'pilotika,' it shows the form of the suffix '-ṇika.' 'By the very perversion of what was said' means by the perversion of what was said, such as 'by what was made a sign,' and so forth. 'Therein' refers to the vicinity. 'Hi' means indeed, or because. 'Here' means in the Kathina section. The connection is that it is lost by that word not being spoken.

310. Tatthāti “kathañca bhikkhave ubbhataṃ hoti kathina”ntiādipāṭhe. Janettiyo mātaroti yojanā. Iminā dhammena putte mānetīti mātā, dhammena puttehi māniyatīti vā mātā, sā viya hontīti mātikāti dasseti. Kathinubbhāranti ca kathinuddhāranti ca atthato sadisaṃ. Etāti etā padajātiyo. Tāsūti aṭṭhasu mātikāsu. Assāti kathinubbhārassa.

310. 'Therein' refers to the passage beginning, 'And how, bhikkhus, is the Kathina withdrawn?' and so forth. The explanation is that 'janettiyo' means mothers. It shows that 'mātikā' is so called because she honors her sons by this Dhamma, thus she is a mother; or she is honored by her sons through Dhamma, thus she is a mother; and being like her, they are mātikās. 'Kathinubbhāra' and 'kathinuddhāra' are similar in meaning. 'Etā' refers to these types of terms. 'Tāsu' refers to the eight mātikās. 'Assa' refers to the withdrawal of the Kathina.

188. Ādāyasattakakathā

188. The Discourse on the Heptad of Taking

311. Na paccessanti ettha patītyūpasaggassa punatthaṃ, idhātuyā ca gatyatthaṃ dassento āha “na puna āgamissa”nti. Evaṃ pakkamato chijjatīti sambandho.

311. Regarding 'na paccessanti': here, showing that the prefix 'paṭi' has the meaning of 'again' and the root 'i' has the meaning of 'going,' he says, 'they will not come again.' The connection is that it is thus severed upon departure.

Etañcāti pakkamanantikaṃ, kathinuddhārañca. Tāhanti te ahaṃ. Teti tuyhaṃ.

'And this' refers to the end of the departure and the withdrawal of the Kathina. 'Tāhaṃ' means 'te ahaṃ' (those I). 'Te' means 'tuyhaṃ' (your).

Aññanti attano vihārato aññaṃ. Evaṃ hotīti eso parivitakko hoti. Soti āvāsapalibodho. Ādiccabandhunā vuttoti yojanā.

'Aññaṃ' means other than one's own monastery. 'Evaṃ hoti' means this is a reflection. 'So' means the obstruction of lodging. The connection is 'spoken by the Kinsman of the Sun'.

Dve palibodhā ekato chijjantīti sambandho. Apubbaṃ acarimanti ekapahāreneva. So palibodhūpacchedo kasmā vitthārato na vuttoti āha “so panā”tiādi. So panāti palibodhūpacchedo [M 0.0367] pana. Na vuttoti sambandho. Etthāti imasmiṃ kathinubbhāre. Kasmā ayaṃ kathinuddhāro “nāsanantiko”ti vuttoti āha “yasmā”tiādi. Tassāti bhikkhuno.

The connection is 'two obstructions are cut off together.' 'Apubbaṃ acarimanti' means with a single strike. Why is this cutting off of obstructions not described in detail? He says, 'so panā,' etc. 'So pana' means 'but that cutting off of obstructions.' The connection is 'is not described.' 'Ettha' means in this withdrawal of the Kathina. Why is this withdrawal of the Kathina called 'nāsanantiko' (ending in destruction)? He says, 'yasmā,' etc. 'Tassa' means 'of the monk.'

Āsāvacchedike chijjatīti sambandho. Ayaṃ panāti āsāvacchediko kathinuddhāro pana. Anekapabhedo hotīti sambandho. Tassāti bhikkhussa. Vuttoti ayaṃ āsāvacchediko kathinuddhāro vuttoti yojanā. Ettha panāti imasmiṃ pana ṭhāne. Tatthāti sīmātikkantike.

The connection is 'it is cut off in the cutting off of hope.' 'Ayaṃ pana' means 'but this hope-severing withdrawal of the Kathina.' The connection is 'it has many distinctions.' 'Tassa' means 'of that monk.' The explanation is 'vutto' means 'this hope-severing withdrawal of the Kathina is spoken of.' 'Ettha pana' means 'but in this place.' 'Tattha' means 'in the crossing of the boundary.'

312-325. Evantiādi nigamanaṃ. Sattaketi aṭṭhasu mātikāsu āsāvacchedato sese sattapamāṇe, sattasamūhe vā. Teyevāti sattake eva. Tatoti vārato. Ye yeti kathinuddhārā. Itarehīti āsāvacchedato aññehi. Ye palibodhā vuttāti sambandho. Āvāso cajīyati anenāti [V 2.0031] cattanti vacanatthaṃ dassento āha “yena cittenā”tiādi. Tanti cittaṃ. “Eseva nayo”ti iminā āvāso vamīyati anenāti vantaṃ. Āvāsato muccati anenāti muttanti vacanatthaṃ atidisati. Sabbatthāti sabbasmiṃ kathinakkhandhake.

312-325. 'Evantiādi' is the conclusion. 'Sattake' means, in the eight matrices, the remainder of seven in measure from the cutting off of hope, or a group of seven. 'Teyeva' means 'just in the seven.' 'Tato' means 'in turn.' 'Ye ye' refers to the withdrawals of the Kathina. 'Itarehi' means 'by others than the cutting off of hope.' The connection is with 'which obstructions are spoken of.' Showing the meaning of the word 'cattaṃ' as 'a dwelling is abandoned by this,' he says, 'by which mind,' etc. 'Taṃ' means 'that mind.' By 'eseva nayo,' he extends the meaning of the word 'vantaṃ' as 'a dwelling is vomited by this,' and 'muttaṃ' as 'one is freed from the dwelling by this.' 'Sabbattha' means 'in the entire Kathina Chapter.'

Iti kathinakkhandhakavaṇṇanāya yojanā samattā.

Thus, the explanation of the connections in the commentary on the Kathina Chapter is complete.

8. Cīvarakkhandhakaṃ

8. The Chapter on Robes

202. Jīvakavatthukathā

202. The Story of Jīvaka

326. Cīvarakkhandhake padakkhiṇasaddassa apasabyatthaṃ paṭikkhipanto āha “chekā kusalā”ti. Abhisaṭāti ettha saradhātuyā gaticintāsu idha gatyattheti dassento āha “abhigatā”ti. Abhigatāti abhimukhaṃ gantabbā. Nanu pāḷiyaṃ “atthikānaṃ atthikānaṃ manussāna”nti vuttaṃ, kasmā pana “atthikehi atthikehi manussehī”ti vuttanti āha “karaṇatthe panā”tiādi. Iminā chaṭṭhīkattā nāma [M 0.0368] tatiyākattunā samānoyevāti dasseti. Nigame vasatīti negamoti vutte kuṭumbiyagaṇo negamo nāmāti āha “kuṭumbiyagaṇo”ti.

326. In the Chapter on Robes, rejecting the meaning of 'apasabya' for the word 'padakkhiṇa', he says, 'skilled, expert.' Regarding 'abhisaṭā': here, showing that the root 'sar', which has the meanings of 'movement' and 'thought', is here in the sense of 'movement', he says, 'abhigatā.' 'Abhigatā' means 'to be approached directly.' Although in the Pāḷi it is said 'atthikānaṃ atthikānaṃ manussānaṃ' (of desirous people), why is it said 'atthikehi atthikehi manussehi' (by desirous people)? He says, 'but in the sense of the instrument,' etc. By this, he shows that the agent in the sixth case is indeed the same as the agent in the third case. When 'negamo' is said, from 'one who dwells in a town,' he states that 'negamo' means 'a group of householders'.

327. Nagare nivasantīti nāgarā. Datvā, vuṭṭhāpesunti sambandho. Ārāmuyyānavāhanādīti ettha ādisaddena aññāni upabhogaparibhogāni saṅgaṇhāti. Gaṇikaṭṭhāneti gaṇikāya ṭhāne. Gaṇikāti ca nagarasobhinī. Sā hi atthikena janagaṇena abhigantabbāti gaṇikāti vuccati. Paṭisatena cāti ettha casaddo avadhāraṇattho. Rattiṃ gamanassa paṭinidhisaṅkhātena satena evāti hi attho. Gilānanti ettha bhāvapaccayena vināpi bhāvattho ñātabboti āha “gilānabhāva”nti. “Jānāpeyya”nti iminā paṭivedeyyanti ettha vidadhātuyā ñāṇatthaṃ dasseti. Kattarasuppeti ettha kattarasaddo jiṇṇapariyāyoti āha “jiṇṇasuppe”ti. Supanti sunakhādayo etthāti suppaṃ, kattaraṃ suppaṃ kattarasuppaṃ.

327. 'Nāgarā' means 'city-dwellers' because 'they dwell in the city.' 'Having given, they caused to rise' is the connection. In 'Ārāmuyyānavāhanādi,' by the word 'ādi' (etc.), other enjoyments and items for use are included. 'Gaṇikaṭṭhāne' means 'in the place of a courtesan.' 'Gaṇikā' means 'one who adorns the city.' For she is called 'gaṇikā' because she is to be approached by a group of people who desire her. In 'Paṭisatena ca,' the word 'ca' has the sense of emphasis. Indeed, the meaning is precisely 'by a hundred,' which is a substitute for going at night. Regarding 'gilāna,' he says 'the state of being ill' because the meaning of 'state' should be understood even without a suffix indicating state. By 'Jānāpeyya,' he shows that the root 'vid' in 'paṭivedeyya' has the meaning of 'knowing.' Regarding 'Kattarasuppa,' he says 'old winnowing basket' because the word 'kattara' is a synonym for 'old.' 'Suppaṃ' is so called because dogs and the like sleep in it; 'kattarasuppaṃ' is an old winnowing basket.

328. Tanti jīvakaṃ. Aññe rājadārakā vadanti kirāti sambandho. Natthi mātā etassāti [V 2.0032] nimmātiko. Yathā cātiādīsu yathā pesanti, tathāti yojanā. Casaddo sampiṇḍanattho. Na kevalaṃ vadantiyeva, atha kho na koci kiñci pesetīti hi attho. Aññesanti jīvakato aññesaṃ. Tassāti jīvakassa. Itīti evaṃ. Soti jīvako. Taṃ sabbanti “nimmātiko nippitiko”ti vadanañca paṇṇākārassa apesanañcāti taṃ sabbaṃ.

328. 'Taṃ' refers to Jīvaka. 'Other princes say' is the connection. 'Nimmātika' means 'motherless' because 'he has no mother.' In phrases like 'yathā ca,' the construction is: 'as they send, so...'. The word 'ca' has the meaning of combining. Indeed, the meaning is: not only do they say so, but also no one sends anything. 'Aññesaṃ' means 'to others than Jīvaka.' 'Tassa' means 'of Jīvaka.' 'Iti' means 'thus.' 'So' refers to Jīvaka. 'Taṃ sabbaṃ' means 'all that,' namely, being called 'motherless' and 'fatherless' and the non-sending of gifts.

Yaṃnūnāti sādhu vata. Ahaṃ vajjasippaṃ sikkheyyaṃ sādhu vatāti yojanā. Tassāti jīvakassa. Etadahosīti etaṃ ahosi, parivitakko ahūti attho. Parūpaghātapaṭisaṃyuttānīti paraṃ upagantvā, upa bhusena vā hananena paṭisaṃyuttāni. Mettāpubbabhāganti sippassa pubbabhāge pavattā mettā etassāti mettāpubbabhāgaṃ. Iti ahosīti yojanā. Purimacintāya anekantabhāvato ekantabhāvaṃ dassento āha “api cā”tiādi. Api cāti ekantena. Ayanti jīvako. Itoti bhaddakappato. Ayanti upāsako[M 0.0369]. Catuparisantareti catuparisamajjhe. Patthataguṇanti pattharitaguṇaṃ. Ṭhānantaranti ṭhānabhedaṃ, ahampīti na ayaṃ upāsakoyeva, ahampīti attho. Bhagavāti ālapanapadametaṃ. Patthananti icchitavaraṃ. Codiyamānopīti uyyojiyamānopi. Pisaddena purimacintanamapekkhati. Esāti eso jīvako.

'Yaṃ nūna' means 'how good!' The construction is: 'How good it would be if I were to learn the Vajja craft!' 'Tassa' means 'of Jīvaka.' 'Etadahosi' means 'this occurred,' that is, a reflective thought arose. 'Connected with harming others' means associated with harming others by approaching them, or by severe violence. 'Mettāpubbabhāga' means 'having compassion as a preliminary,' because compassion arose in the initial stage of the craft. 'Thus it was' is the construction. Showing the certainty from the uncertainty of the earlier thought, he says, 'but also,' etc. 'Api ca' means 'definitively.' 'Ayaṃ' refers to Jīvaka. 'Ito' means 'from this auspicious eon.' 'Ayaṃ' refers to the lay follower. 'Catuparisantara' means 'in the midst of the four assemblies.' 'Patthataguṇa' means 'widespread virtues.' 'Ṭhānantara' means 'a different status'; 'I too' means 'not only this lay follower, but I too'—this is the meaning. 'Bhagavā' is a term of address. 'Patthanā' means 'the wished-for boon.' 'Codiyamānopi' means 'even when urged.' The particle 'pi' refers to the earlier thought. 'Esa' refers to Jīvaka.

329. Disāpāmokkhoti padassa disāsu pāmokkho disāpāmokkhoti vacanatthaṃ dassento āha “sabbadisāsū”tiādi. Tasmiñca samayeti jīvakassa tasmiṃ cintanasamaye ca, āgamaṃsūti sambandho. Teti vāṇije, pucchīti sambandho. Kutoti nagarato. Takkasīlatoti takkasīlanagarato. Tatthāti takkasīle. Āmāti sampaṭicchanatthe nipāto, āma atthīti hi attho. Teti vāṇijā. Tathāti yathā jīvako āha, tathā akaṃsūti attho. Soti jīvako. Pitaranti abhayarājakumāraṃ. Tehīti vāṇijehi.

329. Explaining the meaning of the word 'disāpāmokkha' as 'foremost in the directions,' he says, 'in all directions,' etc. 'At that time' refers to Jīvaka's time of reflection, and 'they came' is the connection. 'Te' refers to the merchants, and 'he asked' is the connection. 'Kuto' means 'from which city.' 'Takkasīlato' means 'from the city of Takkasīlā.' 'Tattha' means 'in Takkasīlā.' 'Āma' is a particle in the sense of acceptance; indeed, the meaning is 'yes, there is.' 'Te' refers to the merchants. 'Tathā' means 'as Jīvaka said, so they did'—this is the meaning. 'So' refers to Jīvaka. 'Pitaraṃ' refers to Prince Abhaya. 'Tehi' refers to the merchants.

Tanti jīvakaṃ, pucchīti sambandho. Soti jīvako. Kasmā tāta tvaṃ idhāgato asi panāti pucchīti yojanā. Tatoti pucchato. Soti jīvako. Sikkhituṃ āgato amhīti yojanā. Bahuñca gaṇhātītiādīsu so kiñci kammaṃ akatvā sippasseva sikkhitattā bahuñca gaṇhātīti āha “yathā”tiādi. Tattha yathā sikkhantiyeva, evaṃ tathā so na sikkhatīti yojanā. So panāti jīvako pana, karoti sikkhatīti sambandho. Ekaṃ kālanti ekasmiṃ kāle. Evaṃ sante kasmā so bahuñca gaṇhātīti āha “evaṃ santepī”tiādi. Medhāvitāyāti khippaṃ gahaṇadhāraṇapaññatāya, bahuñca sippanti sambandho. Assa jīvakassa gahitañca sippaṃ na sammussatīti yojanā.

'Taṃ' refers to Jīvaka, and 'he asked' is the connection. 'So' refers to Jīvaka. The exposition is the question: 'Why, dear one, have you come here?' 'Tato' means 'when asked.' 'So' refers to Jīvaka. The exposition is: 'I have come to learn.' In phrases like 'and he learns much,' he says 'as,' etc., because he learned only the craft itself without doing any other work, and thus learns much. Here, the exposition is: just as they are learning, so he does not learn. 'So pana' means 'but Jīvaka,' and 'he does learn' is the connection. 'Ekaṃ kālaṃ' means 'at one time.' If it is so, why does he learn much? He says, 'Even so,' etc. 'Medhāvitāya' means 'by intelligence,' that is, by the wisdom of quick grasping and retention, and 'much of the craft' is the connection. The exposition is: the craft learned by him, Jīvaka, is not forgotten.

Yattakaṃ [V 2.0033] sippaṃ ācariyo jānāti, tattakaṃ ayaṃ jīvako jānātīti yojanā. Yanti sippaṃ. Ayanti jīvako, bhavissatīti sambandho. Nanti jīvakaṃ. Yathāti yenākārena. Kammavipākanti kammavipākajaṃ rogaṃ. “Na”nti padaṃ “sikkhāpesī”ti pade kāritakammaṃ, “bhesajjayojana”nti [M 0.0370] padaṃ dhātukammaṃ. Bhesajjayojananti bhesajjena rogassa yojanaṃ. So panāti jīvako pana. Imināti jīvakena na uggahitaṃ, uggahitanti sambandho. Ekena dvārenāti catūsu dvāresu ekena dvārena. Āhiṇḍantoti vicaranto. Parittaṃ pātheyyanti ettha parittasaddassa ārakkhanatthepi pavattanato idha appatthe pavattatīti dassento āha “appamattaka”nti. Kasmā appamattakaṃ pātheyyaṃ adāsīti yojanā. Tassāti disāpāmokkhassa. Ayanti jīvako, labhissatīti sambandho. Tatoti labhanato. Khīṇe pātheyyeti pātheyye khīṇe satīti yojanā.

The construction is: whatever skill the teacher knows, that much Jīvaka knows. 'Yaṃ' refers to the skill. 'Ayaṃ' refers to Jīvaka, and 'he will be' is the connection. 'Naṃ' refers to Jīvaka. 'Yathā' means 'in whatever manner.' 'Kammavipāka' means 'illness born from the result of karma.' The word 'naṃ' is the causative object with the verb 'sikkhāpesī', and the word 'bhesajjayojana' is the root object. 'Bhesajjayojana' means 'the application of medicine to the disease.' 'So pana' means 'but Jīvaka.' 'Iminā' means 'by this Jīvaka'; 'na uggahitaṃ' means 'not learned'; 'uggahitaṃ' is the connection. 'Ekena dvārena' means 'through one of the four doors.' 'Āhiṇḍanto' means 'wandering about.' Regarding 'parittaṃ pātheyya,' showing that the word 'paritta' is used here in the sense of 'little,' even though it also has the meaning of 'protection,' he says, 'a small amount.' The construction is: 'Why did he give only a small amount of provisions?' 'Tassa' refers to the one foremost in the directions. 'Ayaṃ' refers to Jīvaka, and 'he will obtain' is the connection. 'Tato' means 'from that obtaining.' The construction for 'khīṇe pātheyyeti' is 'pātheyye khīṇe sati' (when the provisions were exhausted).

203. Seṭṭhibhariyādivatthukathā

203. The Story of the Merchant's Wife and Others

330. Yā nāmāti yā nāma gharaṇī. Kimpi māyanti ettha ekāralopasandhīti āha “kimpi me aya”nti. Iminā yakārādesasandhiṃ nivatteti, “myāya”ntipi pāṭho, evaṃ sati ādesasandhiyeva, na lopasandhi. Ayaṃ gharaṇī me kiñci deyyadhammaṃ kimpi dassatīti yojanā. Tassa cāti sabbissa ca, katassātipi pāṭho. Rogūpasamassa cāti mama rogassa upasamassa ca, imehi padehi saṃyamassāti padassa atthaṃ dasseti. “Upakāra”nti iminā upajānāmīti ettha upasaddassa atthaṃ dasseti. Adhippāyoti gharaṇiyā āsayo.

330. 'Yā nāma' means 'whatever mistress of the house.' Regarding 'kimpi māyaṃ,' he says it is 'kimpi me ayaṃ' because there is an elision of the letter 'e'. By this, he rejects the sandhi involving the substitution of 'y'. There is also the reading 'myāyaṃ'; if so, it is indeed a substitution sandhi, not an elision sandhi. The construction is: 'This mistress of the house will give me some gift.' 'Tassa ca' means 'of all that'; there is also the reading 'katassa' (of what was done). 'Rogūpasamassa ca' means 'and for the subsiding of my disease'; by these words, he shows the meaning of the word 'saṃyamassa'. By 'upakāra' (help), he shows the meaning of the prefix 'upa' in 'upajānāmi'. 'Adhippāyo' means the intention of the mistress of the house.

331. “Sabbālaṅkāraṃ tuyhaṃ hotū”ti idaṃ vacanaṃ rājā sabhāvato āha, udāhu kiñci cintetvāti āha “rājā”tiādi. Tattha imanti alaṅkāraṃ. Pamāṇayutteti kāraṇānurūpe. Nanti jīvakaṃ. Nāṭakānampīti pañcasatikānaṃ nāṭakānampi. Sopīti jīvakopi. Tesanti abhayakumāranāṭakānaṃ. Meti mayhaṃ, na patirūpanti sambandho. Ayyikānanti mātāmahīnaṃ. Katassa me upakāranti yojanā. Iminā adhikāro ca upakāro ca atthato sadisanti dasseti. Rājā pasanno datvā āhāti sambandho.

331. Regarding the statement, ‘May all the adornments be yours,’ did the king utter this spontaneously, or did he say it after some deliberation? This is why it is said, ‘The king,’ etc. Here, ‘this’ refers to the adornments. ‘Pamāṇayutta’ means ‘appropriate to the reason.’ ‘Naṃ’ refers to Jīvaka. ‘Nāṭakānampi’ means ‘even of the five hundred female entertainers.’ ‘He too’ refers to Jīvaka as well. ‘Tesaṃ’ refers to the female entertainers of Prince Abhaya. ‘Me’ means ‘for me’; ‘not fitting’ is the connection. ‘Ayyikānaṃ’ means ‘of the maternal grandmothers.’ The construction is: ‘the help done to me.’ By this, it is shown that ‘authority’ and ‘help’ are similar in meaning. ‘The king, being pleased, gave and said’—this is the connection.

205. Rājagahaseṭṭhivatthukathā

205. The Story of the Chief Merchant of Rājagaha

332. Iriyāpathasamparivattanenāti [M 0.0371] iriyāpathassa punappunaṃ parivattanena. Tīhi sattāhehi niccalassa [V 2.0034] nipannassa assa seṭṭhissa matthaluṅganti yojanā. Appeva nipajjeyyāti yojanā. Nanti seṭṭhiṃ. Tenevāti teneva kāraṇena. Sīsaṃ chādetīti sīsacchavīti vutte sīsapaṭicchādanacammanti āha “sīsacamma”nti. Tassāti seṭṭhissa. Tīhi sattāhenāti ettha pubbapadena pacchimapadaṃ guṇitvā gahetabbanti āha “tīhi passehi ekenekena sattāhenā”ti.

332. ‘Iriyāpathasamparivattanenāti’ means by the repeated changing of posture. ‘The brain-matter of this merchant, who lay motionless for three weeks’—this is the connection. ‘Perhaps he might lie down’—this is the connection. ‘Naṃ’ refers to the merchant. ‘Teneva’ means for that very reason. Because it covers the head, when ‘sīsacchavi’ is said, it means the skin covering the head; therefore, he said ‘sīsacammaṃ’ (head-skin). ‘Tassa’ means of the merchant. Regarding ‘tīhi sattāhena’ (for three weeks), here, because the latter term should be taken as multiplied by the former, he said, ‘on three sides, for one week on each.’

333. Janaṃ nīharāpetvāti janaṃ apakkamāpetvā.

333. ‘Janaṃ nīharāpetvā’ means having made the people depart.

207. Pajjotarājavatthukathā

207. The Story of King Pajjota

334. Vicchikassa jātoti vicchikassa kāraṇā jāto, vicchikaṃ paṭicca jātoti attho. Sabbi ca bhesajjaṃ vicchikānaṃ paṭikūlaṃ hotīti yojanā. Paññāsayojanikāti ettha ṇikapaccayassa gantuṃ samatthatthe pavattabhāvaṃ dassento āha “gantuṃ samattho hotī”ti. Assa raññoti candapajjotanāmakassa assa rañño. Hatthinīyevāti bhaddavatikā nāma hatthinīyeva. Vīsayojanasatanti vīsādhikaṃ yojanasataṃ.

334. ‘Vicchikassa jāto’ (born of a scorpion) means born because of a scorpion; the meaning is born on account of a scorpion. ‘And all medicine is repulsive to scorpions’—this is the connection. Regarding ‘paññāsayojanikā’ (able to travel fifty yojanas), here, showing that the -ṇika suffix is used in the sense of ‘able to go,’ he said, ‘is able to go.’ ‘Assa rañño’ (of this king) means of this king named Candapajjota. ‘Hatthinīyeva’ (the she-elephant indeed) means the she-elephant named Bhaddavatikā indeed. ‘Vīsayojanasataṃ’ (one hundred and twenty yojanas) means one hundred yojanas plus twenty.

Bhuñjituṃ nisinnassa ekassa kulaputtassa dvāreti yojanā. Tassāti kulaputtassa, ārocesīti sambandho. Soti kulaputto, “āharā”ti āṇāpesīti sambandho. Itaroti puriso. Tanti pattaṃ. Yattha yatthāti yasmiṃ yasmiṃ bhave. Tattha tattha vāhanasampanno homīti yojanā. Soti puriso. Pajjoto nāma ayaṃ rājā jātoti yojanā.

‘At the door of a certain clansman seated to eat’—this is the connection. ‘Tassa’ means of the clansman; it is connected with ‘ārocesi’ (he announced). ‘So’ means the clansman; it is connected with ‘āṇāpesi’ (he ordered), ‘“Bring it!”’ ‘Itaro’ means the man. ‘Taṃ’ means the bowl. ‘Yattha yatthā’ means in whatever existence. ‘There, there may I be endowed with a vehicle’—this is the connection. ‘So’ means the man. ‘This king was born named Pajjota’—this is the connection.

Sabbiṃ pāyetvāti idaṃ upalakkhaṇamattanti dassento āha “sabbiñca pāyetvā”tiādi. Sabbiñca pāyetvā, paricārakānaṃ āhārācāre vidhiñca ācikkhitvāti attho. Olumpetvāti lupidhātu [M 0.0372] odahanatthoti āha “odahitvā”ti. Virecesīti uddhañca adho ca virecesi.

Regarding ‘sabbiṃ pāyetvā’ (having made him drink ghee), showing that this is merely an indication, he said, ‘sabbiñca pāyetvā’ (and having made him drink ghee), etc. The meaning is: and having made him drink ghee, and having explained the rules about food and conduct to the attendants. Regarding ‘olumpetvā,’ because the root ‘lup’ has the meaning of immersing, he said ‘odahitvā’ (having immersed). ‘Virecesi’ (he purged) means he purged both upwards and downwards.

208. Siveyyakadussayugakathā

208. The Story of the Pair of Siveyyaka Cloths

335. Sivathikanti sivā jambukā kuṇapakhādanatthāya āgantvā tiṭṭhanti etthāti sivaṭṭhaṃ, tadeva sivathikaṃ, iminā sivathikāyaṃ uppannaṃ siveyyakaṃ thikasaddassa lopaṃ katvāti dasseti. Tatthāti uttarakurūsu. Tanti mataṃ. Hatthisoṇḍakasakuṇāti hatthiliṅgavihaṅgamā. Te hi hatthino soṇḍo viya soṇḍo etesu atthīti hatthīsoṇḍakā, te ca te sakuṇā ceti hatthisoṇḍakasakuṇāti [V 2.0035] vuccanti. Rañño āharantīti rañño atthāya, santikaṃ vā āharanti. Idanti siveyyakaṃ dussayugaṃ. Siviraṭṭhe vāyitaṃ siveyyakanti ca dassento āha “athavā”tiādi. Tenāti kāraṇena. “Siveyyakanti…pe… vadantī”ti porāṇā āhūti yojanā.

335. ‘Sivathikaṃ’: jackals (sivā jambukā) come and stand here (ettha) to eat corpses, hence it is a sivaṭṭhaṃ (a place for jackals); that itself is a sivathikaṃ. By this, he shows that ‘siveyyakaṃ’ is what arises in a sivathikā (charnel ground), having elided the sound ‘thika.’ ‘Tattha’ means in Uttarakuru. ‘Taṃ’ means a dead body. ‘Hatthisoṇḍakasakuṇā’ means birds with the characteristic of an elephant. For they have a trunk (soṇḍo) like an elephant’s trunk, hence they are called hatthisoṇḍakā; and they are birds (sakuṇā), hence they are called hatthisoṇḍakasakuṇā. ‘They bring for the king’ means they bring for the king’s sake, or they bring it into his presence. ‘Idaṃ’ means this pair of siveyyaka cloths. And showing that ‘siveyyakaṃ’ is so-called because it was woven in the Sivi country, he said, ‘or alternatively,’ etc. ‘Tena’ means for that reason. ‘“They call it siveyyakaṃ…” etc.’—the ancients said this; this is the connection.

209. Samattiṃsavirecanakathā

209. The Story of the Thirty Laxatives

336. Kiṃpanāti ettha kiṃsaddo aniyamattho. Lūkho kiṃ, na lūkho kinti hi attho. “Sinehapānaṃ pana temetī”ti ca “karotī”ti ca sambandho. Sabbatthāti sakalakāye. Sirāti kaṇḍarā. Ayanti jīvako. Oḷārikadosaharaṇatthanti oḷārikassa dosassa apanayanatthaṃ. Pakatatteti pakatisaṅkhāte sabhāve satīti sambandho. Bhagavā bhanteti yojanā. Kutoti kassa santikā. Vaṭṭati nu khoti cintesīti yojanā. Tatoti cintanato. Soṇoti koḷivīsasoṇo, bhuñjatīti sambandho. Tatoti soṇassa santikā. Tassāti soṇassa. Soti soṇo. Therassāti moggallānattherassa. Idaṃ “patta”ntipade sāmī, “adāsī”ti pade sampadānaṃ. Aññaṃ piṇḍapātanti sambandho.

336. Regarding ‘kiṃpana,’ here the word ‘kiṃ’ has an indefinite meaning. The meaning is indeed: is it rough, or is it not rough? ‘The oil drink moistens’ is connected with ‘does.’ ‘Sabbattha’ means in the entire body. ‘Sirā’ means sinews. ‘Ayaṃ’ means Jīvaka. ‘Oḷārikadosaharaṇatthaṃ’ means for the purpose of removing a gross defect. ‘Pakatatte’ means when its nature, called its natural state, exists; this is the connection. ‘The Blessed One, Venerable Sir’—this is the connection. ‘Kuto’ means from whose presence. ‘“Is it suitable, I wonder?” he thought’—this is the connection. ‘Tato’ means from that thought. ‘Soṇo’ is Koḷivīsa Soṇa; it is connected with ‘bhuñjati’ (eats). ‘Tato’ means from Soṇa’s presence. ‘Tassa’ means of Soṇa. ‘So’ means Soṇa. ‘Therassa’ means of the Elder Moggallāna. Here, in the word ‘pattaṃ’ (bowl), it is the genitive case; in the word ‘adāsi’ (he gave), it is the dative case. ‘Another almsfood’—this is the connection.

Rājāpi kho bhuñjitukāmo ahosīti sambandho. Yañca sujātā adāsi, yañca parinibbānakāle cundo kammāraputto, bhājanagatesu [M 0.0373] dvīsuyeva tesu piṇḍapātesu devatā ojaṃ pakkhipantīti yojanā. Aññesūti dvīhi piṇḍapātehi aññesu. Icchanti ruciṃ. Soti bimbisāro rājā. Tavevāti tuyhameva. Tanti bhagavato vacanaṃ. Rājā akāsīti sambandho. Teti asītikulaputtasahassā. Etadatthamevāti soṇassa arahatte patiṭṭhāpanatthameva, na rañño anuggahatthanti adhippāyo.

‘The king also wished to eat’—this is the connection. ‘What Sujātā gave, and what Cunda the blacksmith's son gave at the time of the final extinguishment—the deities placed nutritive essence only in those two alms-foods contained in vessels’—this is the connection. ‘Aññesu’ means in others than those two alms-foods. ‘Icchanti’ means they like the taste. ‘So’ means King Bimbisāra. ‘Taveva’ means for you alone. ‘Taṃ’ means the Blessed One's word. ‘The king did’—this is the connection. ‘Te’ means the eighty thousand sons of good family. ‘Etadatthameva’ means only for the purpose of establishing Soṇa in arahantship; the intention is that it was not for the purpose of favouring the king.

210. Varayācanakathā

210. The Story of Requesting a Boon

337. Kataṃ bhattakiccaṃ yenāti katabhattakicco, tasmiṃ satīti sambandho. Vuttanayenevāti rāhulavatthumhi (mahāva. aṭṭha. 105) vuttanayeneva. Idaṃ vatthanti idaṃ siveyyakaṃ vatthaṃ, uppannanti sambandho. “Tāvā”ti ajjhāharitabbo. Etthantareti etasmiṃ vatthuppannakālamajjhe. Koci bhikkhūti sambandho. Tenāti paṃsukūlikahetunā. Ayanti jīvako. Gahapaticīvaranti ettha gahapatīnaṃ cīvaranti atthaṃ paṭikkhipanto āha “gahapatīhi dinnaṃ cīvara”nti[V 2.0036]. Vatthadānānisaṃsapaṭisaṃyuttāyāti “vatthado hoti vaṇṇado”tiādikāya (saṃ. ni. 1.42) vatthadānassa ānisaṃsena paṭisaṃyuttāya. Vicchāvasena vutto “itarītarenā”ti sabbanāmasaddo aniyamatthoti āha “appagghenapi mahagghenapi yena kenacī”ti. Pāvāroti uttarāsaṅgo. So hi pārupanatthāya variyati icchiyatīti pāvāroti vuccati. “Kappāsādibhedo”ti iminā tassa sarūpaṃ dasseti. Pakatikojavamevāti pakatiyā bhikkhūnaṃ sāruppaṃ kojavameva. Soḷasanāṭakitthīnaṃ ṭhatvā naccayogyattā mahatī piṭṭhi etassāti mahāpiṭṭhiyaṃ, tameva kojavaṃ mahāpiṭṭhiyakojavaṃ. Tassa kira lomāni caturaṅgulādhikāni honti.

337. ‘Katabhattakicco’ means one by whom the duty of the meal has been done; ‘tasmiṃ sati’ (when that is the case) is the connection. ‘Vuttanayeneva’ means in the way stated in the story of Rāhula (Mahāvagga Commentary 105). ‘Idaṃ vatthaṃ’ means this Siveyyaka cloth; it is connected with ‘uppannaṃ’ (arisen). The word ‘tāva’ should be supplied. ‘Etthantare’ means in the interim, in the middle of the time when this cloth arose. ‘Koci bhikkhu’—this is the connection. ‘Tena’ means for the reason of being a wearer of rag-robes. ‘Ayaṃ’ means Jīvaka. Regarding ‘gahapaticīvaraṃ’ (householder robe), here, rejecting the meaning ‘a robe belonging to householders,’ he said, ‘a robe given by householders.’ ‘Vatthadānānisaṃsapaṭisaṃyuttāya’ means connected with the benefits of giving a cloth, beginning with “a giver of cloth is a giver of beauty” (Saṃyutta Nikāya 1.42). Because it is spoken in the sense of an alternative, the pronoun ‘itarītarena’ (by one or the other) has an indefinite meaning; therefore, he said, ‘by any whatsoever, whether of little value or of great value.’ ‘Pāvāro’ means an upper robe. For it is desired (variyati, icchiyati) for the purpose of wearing, hence it is called a ‘pāvāro.’ By ‘of the kind of cotton, etc.,’ he shows its nature. ‘Pakatikojavameva’ means a rug that is naturally suitable for monks. Because it is suitable for sixteen dancing girls to stand and dance upon, it has a large surface (mahatī piṭṭhi), hence it is a ‘mahāpiṭṭhiyaṃ’; that very rug is a ‘mahāpiṭṭhiyakojavaṃ.’ Its pile, it is said, is more than four finger-breadths long.

211. Kambalānujānanādikathā

211. The Story of Allowing Blankets, etc.

338. Kāsīnanti kāsīnaṃ janapadānaṃ, kāsiraṭṭhe nivāsīnaṃ janānaṃ vā. Pasenadissāti paccuṭṭhaṃ, paṭipakkhaṃ vā senaṃ jinātīti pasenadi jakārassa dakāraṃ katvā. Esāti eso kāsirājā. “Sahassa”nti [M 0.0374] iminā kāsisaddassa saṅketasaṅkhyaṃ dasseti. Taṃagghanakoti tena kāsinā agghanako. Kasmā aḍḍhakāsīti (therīgā. aṭṭha. 25) vuttoti āha “ayaṃ panā”tiādi. Ayanti kambalo. Panāti kāraṇatthajotako. Yasmāti hi attho.

338. ‘Kāsīnaṃ’ means of the Kāsi country, or of the people dwelling in the Kāsi realm. ‘Pasenadi’: because he conquers (jināti) a hostile (paccuṭṭhaṃ) or opposing (paṭipakkhaṃ) army (senaṃ), he is Pasenadi, the letter ‘ja’ having been changed to ‘da.’ ‘Eso’ means this king of Kāsi. By ‘a thousand,’ he shows the conventional number for the word ‘kāsi.’ ‘Taṃagghanako’ means worth that much in Kāsi currency. As to why it is called ‘aḍḍhakāsi’ (half-kāsi) (Therīgāthā Commentary 25), he said, ‘ayaṃ pana’ (but this), etc. ‘Ayaṃ’ means the blanket. ‘Pana’ is a particle that indicates a reason. The meaning is indeed ‘yasmā’ (because).

339. Bhañjitabbaṃ khomādīni pañca suttāni missitvā avamadditabbanti bhaṅganti dassento āha “bhaṅgaṃ nāmā”tiādi. Vākamayamevāti bhaṅganāmakena vākena nibbattameva.

339. Showing that it is called ‘bhaṅga’ because the five kinds of thread, beginning with linen, are to be broken (bhañjitabbaṃ) by being mixed and crushed, he said, ‘bhaṅgaṃ nāma’ (called bhaṅga), etc. ‘Vākamayameva’ means produced only from the bark-fibre called bhaṅga.

340. Teti bhikkhū, sallakkhiṃsu kirāti sambandho. Etassāti padassa, atthanti sambandho. Na acchiṃsūti na āsiṃsu, na vasiṃsūti attho. Nākāmāti ettha kamudhātu icchattho yakāralopoti āha “na anicchāyā”ti. Dātabboti bhāgo dātabbo. Upacāreti susānassa samīpe. “Akāmā bhāgaṃ dātu”nti vacanassa anekantabhāvaṃ dassetuṃ vuttaṃ “yadi panā”tiādi. Idhāti imaṃ susānaṃ. “Sampattā gaṇhantū”ti dentīti yojanā. Yenāti bhikkhunā. Sadisā okkamiṃsūti ettha sadisasaddo samapariyāyoti āha “samaṃ okkamiṃsū”ti. Samanti bhāvanapuṃsako. Samānadisāyāti vā dassento āha “ekadisāya vā”ti. Ettha pana yakāralopo daṭṭhabbo. Bahimevāti susānato bahi eva. Katikanti katena pavattaṃ saṅgaraṃ.

340. The connection is: 'Those monks considered, it is said.' With the word `etassa`, the connection is 'meaning.' `Na acchiṃsu` means they were not; the meaning is 'they did not dwell.' Regarding `Nākāmā`, here the root `kam` has the meaning of desire, and there is an elision of `ya`; he says `na anicchāya` (not unwillingly). `Dātabbo` means a portion should be given. `Upacāre` means near the charnel ground. To show the inconclusive nature of the statement 'unwilling to give a share,' it is said, 'But if...' and so on. `Idha` means this charnel ground. The construction is: they give thinking, 'Let those who have arrived take it.' `Yena` means by the monk. Regarding `Sadisā okkamiṃsu`, here the word `sadisa` is a synonym for `sama` (equal); he says `samaṃ okkamiṃsu` (they approached equally). `Samaṃ` is a neuter adverb. Or, showing it means 'from the same direction,' he says 'or from one direction.' Here, however, the elision of `ya` should be understood. `Bahim eva` means just outside the charnel ground. `Katikaṃ` means an agreement established by what has been done.

213. Cīvarapaṭiggāhakasammutikathā

213. Discussion on the Designation of a Robe-Receiver

342. “Yo [V 2.0037] na chandāgatiṃ gacchatī”tiādīsu evaṃ vinicchayo veditabboti yojanā. Ñātakādīnaṃ cīvaranti sambandho. Ekaccasminti jane. Vāsaddo vikappattho. Etesu tīsu aññatarena kāraṇena chandāgatiṃ gacchati nāmāti hi attho. Āgatassāpi cīvaranti sambandho pisaddo garahattho. Pageva pacchā āgatassāti hi attho. Avamaññanti uññātaṃ. Voti tumhākaṃ. Natthi kinti yojanā. Muṭṭhā [M 0.0375] sati etassāti muṭṭhassati. Āgatānampi cīvaranti sambandho. Pisaddo sambhāvanattho. Pageva paṭhamaṃ āgatānanti hi attho. Etaṃ cīvarapaṭiggāhakaṭṭhānaṃ nāmāti yojanā. Santasanto vāti khedakhedo vā. Idañcidañcāti idañca idañca cīvaraṃ. Tasmāti yasmā ca gacchati, yasmā ca jānāti, tasmā. Yoti bhikkhu. Sakkotīti sambandho. Evarūpo bhikkhu sammanitabboti yojanā.

342. In such phrases as 'One who does not go the wrong way through desire,' the construction is: 'the analysis should be understood thus.' The connection is 'the robe of relatives and so on.' `Ekaccasmiṃ` means a certain person. The word `vā` has the meaning of an alternative. For the meaning is that for one or another of these three reasons, one is said to go the wrong way through desire. The connection is 'the robe even of one who has arrived'; the particle `pi` has the meaning of censure. For the meaning is 'especially for one who arrived later.' `Avamaññanti` means despised. `Vo` means 'of you.' The construction is `Natthi kiṃ`. `Muṭṭhassati` means one whose mindfulness is confused. The connection is 'the robe even of those who have arrived.' The particle `pi` has the meaning of possibility. For the meaning is 'especially for those who arrived first.' The construction is: 'This is called the position of robe-receiver.' `Santasanto vā` means being distressed or remorseful. `Idañcidañca` means this robe and that robe. `Tasmā` means: because he goes and because he knows, therefore. `Yo` means the monk. The connection is `sakkoti` (he is able). The construction is: 'A monk of such a kind should be appointed.'

Apalokanenapīti “itthannāmaṃ bhikkhuṃ cīvarapaṭiggāhakaṃ kātuṃ saṅghaṃ apalokemī”ti apalokanenapi, sammanitunti sambandho. Yattha panāti yasmiṃ pana dhuravihāre.

`Apalokanenapī` means: even by an announcement, such as, 'I announce to the Saṅgha the appointment of the monk named so-and-so as the robe-receiver.' The connection is `sammanituṃ` (to appoint). `Yattha pana` means 'but where,' that is, in which monastery with fixed duties.

“Gahitaṭṭhāneyevā”ti iminā tatthevāti ettha tasaddassa visayaṃ dasseti. “Chaḍḍetvā”ti iminā ujjhitvāti ettha udhadhātuyā vissajjanatthaṃ dasseti. Cīvarapaṭiggāhakanti padassa cīvaraṃ paṭiggaṇhātīti cīvarapaṭiggāhakoti vacanatthaṃ dassento āha “yo”tiādi. Tattha yo paṭiggaṇhāti, so cīvarapaṭiggāhako nāmāti yojanā. “Cīvarapaṭisāmaka”nti iminā cīvaraṃ gahitaṭṭhānato nīharitvā bhaṇḍāgāre dahati ṭhapetīti cīvaranidahakoti atthaṃ dasseti. Yo na chandātiṃ gacchatītiādīsu ettha etesu ca ito parañcāti yojanā.

By `Gahitaṭṭhāne yeva`, he shows the referent of the word `ta` in `tattheva`. By `Chaḍḍetvā`, he shows that in `ujjhitvā`, the root `udh` has the meaning of abandoning. Showing the etymological meaning of the word `cīvarapaṭiggāhaka` as 'one who receives a robe is a robe-receiver,' he says `yo`, and so on. Therein, the construction is: 'Whoever receives, he is called a robe-receiver.' By `cīvarapaṭisāmaka`, he shows the meaning of `cīvaranidahaka` as 'one who, having taken the robe from the place where it was received, places or stores it in the storeroom.' In such phrases as 'One who does not go the wrong way through desire,' here the construction is: 'in these and also in what follows.'

214. Bhaṇḍāgārasammutiādikathā

214. Discussion on the Designation of a Storehouse, and so on

343. Yo vihāro vā yo aḍḍhayogo vā hoti, so vihārādiko sammanitabboti yojanā. “Ārāmikasāmaṇerādīhī”ti padaṃ vivittatthe apādānaṃ, karaṇampi yujjati. Paccantasenāsanaṃ pana na sammanitabbaṃ corādiupaddavattā. Vihāramajjheyevāti bhaṇḍāgāravihāramajjheyeva.

343. The construction is: 'Whatever dwelling or half-gabled building there is, that dwelling and so on should be designated.' The word `Ārāmikasāmaṇerādīhi` is in the ablative case in the sense of being separate from; the instrumental is also fitting. However, a lodging in a frontier region should not be designated because of the danger from thieves and so on. `Vihāramajjhe yeva` means right in the middle of the storeroom-dwelling.

Yassāti bhaṇḍāgārassa. Idaṃ padaṃ “chadanādīsū”ti pade sāmī, “natthī”ti pade sampadānaṃ[V 2.0038]. Yassa panāti bhaṇḍāgārassa pana. Yattha katthacīti [M 0.0376] yasmiṃ kasmiṃci ṭhāne. Yenāti patitahetunā. Mūsitvā khādatīti mūsiko. Ādisaddena godhāmaṅgusādayo saṅgaṇhāti. Upa bhusaṃ, upaguhitvā vā cinantīti upacikā. Tanti ovassanādiṃ. Hīti saccaṃ, yasmā vā. Evantiādi nigamanaṃ.

`Yassa` means of the storehouse. This word is the possessor (genitive) in relation to the word `chadanādīsu`, and the recipient (dative) in relation to the word `natthi`. `Yassa pana` means but of the storehouse. `Yattha katthaci` means in any place whatsoever. `Yena` means by reason of falling. `Mūsiko` (mouse) is so called because it steals and eats. By the word `ādi` (and so on), he includes the iguana, the mongoose, and so on. `Upacikā` (termite) is so called because they build up excessively or while clinging together. `Tanti` means leaking and so on. `Hi` means truly, or because. `Evaṃ`, and so on, is the conclusion.

Cīvarapaṭiggāhakādīhīti ādisaddena cīvaranidahakabhaṇḍāgārike saṅgaṇhāti. Tatthāti tesu. Cīvarapaṭiggāhakena na gaṇhitabbanti sambandho. Tāvāti cīvaranidahakabhaṇḍāgārikānaṃ, tehi vā paṭhamaṃ. Yaṃ yanti cīvaraṃ. Tathevāti yathā visuṃ visuṃ katvā gaṇhati, tatheva. Cīvaranidahakenāpīti pisaddo na kevalaṃ paṭiggāhakeneva, atha kho nidahakenapīti sampiṇḍeti. Tathevāti yathā nidahako ācikkhati, tatheva. Tatoti tehi cīvarehi, vibhattaapādānaṃ, tesu cīvaresu vā niddhāraṇaṃ. Tadevāti saṅghena vuttacīvarameva.

In `Cīvarapaṭiggāhakādīhi`, by the word `ādi` (and so on), he includes the robe-storer and the storekeeper. `Tattha` means among them. The connection is: 'it should not be taken by the robe-receiver.' `Tāva` means first, of the robe-storer and the storekeeper, or by them. `Yaṃ yaṃ` means whichever robe. `Tathā eva` means just as one takes it after setting it apart individually, just so. Regarding `Cīvaranidahakenāpi`, the particle `pi` summarizes: 'not only by the receiver, but also by the storer.' `Tathā eva` means just as the storer indicates, just so. `Tato` means from those robes, an ablative of separation; or it is a selection from among those robes. `Tad eva` means the very robe spoken of by the Saṅgha.

Itītiādi nigamanaṃ. Bhagavatā anuññātoti sambandho. Bhaṇḍāgāranti bhaṇḍassa ṭhapanokāsaṃ agāraṃ. Bhaṇḍāgārikoti bhaṇḍāgāre niyutto. Bāhullikatāyāti paccayabāhullena niyuttabhāvatthaṃ. Evaṃ sante kimatthāya anuññātoti āha “api cā”tiādi. Anuggahāya anuññātoti sambandho. Hīti vitthāro. Neva jāneyyunti yojanā. Dve dve vā cīvareti sambandho. Saṅgahaṃ kātunti saṅghena saṅgahaṃ kātuṃ.

`Iti`, and so on, is the conclusion. The connection is: 'permitted by the Blessed One.' `Bhaṇḍāgāraṃ` means a building that is a place for storing goods. `Bhaṇḍāgāriko` means one appointed in the storehouse. `Bāhullikatāya` means for the purpose of being appointed due to an abundance of requisites. This being so, for what purpose was it permitted? He says, 'Moreover,' and so on. The connection is: 'permitted for the sake of assistance.' `Hi` is an elaboration. The construction is: 'they would not know.' The connection is: 'two robes each.' `Saṅgahaṃ kātuṃ` means to make a collection by the Saṅgha.

Na vuṭṭhāpetabboti ettha atthuddhāravasena aññepi avuṭṭhāpanīye dassento āha “aññepī”tiādi. Hīti vitthāro. Tatthāti catūsu. Saṅgho pana detīti sambandho. Upakāratāya cāti saṅghassa upakāratāya ca. Ettha ca purimesu tīsu ekoyeva hetu, pacchime pana dve hetavoti daṭṭhabbaṃ.

Here, regarding 'should not be removed,' by way of extracting the meaning, he shows others who should not be removed, saying 'others also,' and so on. `Hi` is an elaboration. `Tattha` means among the four. The connection is: 'but the Saṅgha gives.' `Upakāratāya ca` means and for the benefit of the Saṅgha. And here it should be understood that for the first three there is only one reason, but for the last there are two reasons.

Sammukhībhūtenāti aññamaññassa mukhe saṃvijjamāno, sannipatito vā sammukho, sammukho hutvā bhūto sammukhībhūto. Bhūsaddayogattā akārassīkāro hoti, antoupacārasīmāyaṃ ṭhito saṅgho[M 0.0377]. Tamatthaṃ dassento āha “antoupacārasīmāyaṃ ṭhitenā”ti. Kolāhalanti bahujanehi sannipatitvā ekato kataṃ abyattasaddaṃ. Tadākāraṃ dassento āha “amhāka”ntiādi. “Cīvarabhājakesū”tiādinā agatigamanākāraṃ dasseti, taṃ suviññeyyameva. Tulābhūtoti tulāya sadiso hutvā bhūto, tulāya sadisabhāvaṃ patto vā. Majjhattoti majjhe ṭhito attā sabhāvo etassāti majjhatto.

`Sammukhībhūtena` means: `sammukho` is being present in each other's presence, or having assembled; `sammukhībhūto` is one who has become present. Due to the connection with the word `bhū`, the `a` becomes `ī`; it means the Saṅgha standing within the boundary of the vicinity. Showing that meaning, he says, 'by one standing within the boundary of the vicinity.' `Kolāhalaṃ` means the loud, indistinct sound made by many people who have assembled together. Showing its form, he says, 'our,' and so on. By 'among the distributors of robes,' and so on, he shows the manner of not going the wrong way; this is easily understood. `Tulābhūto` means one who has become like a balance, or one who has attained a state similar to a balance. `Majjhatto` (impartial) is one whose self or nature stands in the middle.

Idanti [V 2.0039] cīvaraṃ. Ghananti nirantaraṃ. Tanukanti viraḷaṃ. Ettha “uccinitvā”ti iminā vatthassa pamāṇena uccinanaṃ dasseti. “Tulayitvā”ti iminā agghena tulanaṃ dasseti. Vaṇṇāvaṇṇaṃ katvāti vaṇṇañca avaṇṇañca khuddakañca pamāṇaṃ, mahantañca pamāṇaṃ katvāti attho. Ekaccāni cīvarāni appagghāni honti, ekaccāni mahagghānīti vuttaṃ hoti. Dasadasaagghanakanti dasahi dasahi kahāpaṇehi agghanakaṃ. Yanti cīvaraṃ, bandhitvāti navagghanakaṃ ekagghanakena, aṭṭhagghanakañca dviagghanakena bandhitvāti attho. Same paṭivīseti samapamāṇe paṭivīse ṭhapetvā, iminā “vaṇṇāvaṇṇa”nti ettha vaṇṇasaddo pamāṇatthoti dīpeti. Dasa dasa bhikkhūti idaṃ upalakkhaṇavasena vuttaṃ aññenākārenāpi gaṇetuṃ sakkuṇeyyattā. Bhaṇḍikanti cīvarabhaṇḍena niyuttaṃ puṭaṃ. Kusoti salākadaṇḍo.

"This is a robe." "Solid" means without gaps. "Thin" means sparse. Here, "having selected" indicates selection by the size of the cloth. "Having weighed" indicates weighing by price. "Having made distinctions of quality and non-quality" means having made distinctions of small and large size; this is the meaning. It is said that some robes are of little value, and some are of great value. "Priced at ten each" means priced at ten kahāpaṇas each. "Having bound" means binding a nine-priced one with a one-priced one, and an eight-priced one with a two-priced one; this is the meaning. "He divides into equal shares" means having established shares of equal measure. By this, it is shown that here in the phrase "vaṇṇāvaṇṇa", the word "vaṇṇa" has the meaning of measure. "Ten monks each" is said by way of example, as it is possible to count in other ways as well. "Bundle" means a pouch for the robe-goods. "Lot" means a tally stick.

Attissarāti attanāva attānaṃ issarā. Aññesaṃ vattapaṭipattinti sambandho. Upaḍḍhabhāgoti bhikkhūnaṃ laddhabhāgato upaḍḍho bhāgo. Ye panāti sāmaṇerā pana. Samabhāgoti bhikkhūnaṃ bhāgena samo bhāgo. Idañcāti “upaḍḍhapaṭivīsa”nti vacanañca, kathitanti sambandho. Samakamevāti bhikkhusāmaṇerānaṃ samapamāṇameva. Tatruppādavassāvāsikanti tasmiṃ vihāre uppādena mūlena uppāditaṃ vassāvāsikaṃ. Phātikammanti vaḍḍhanakammaṃ “yattakena vinayāgatena sammuñjanibandhanādinā hatthakammena vihārassa ūnatā na hoti, tattakaṃ katvāti attho. Etanti phātikammaṃ katvā gahaṇaṃ[M 0.0378]. Hīti saccaṃ. Etthāti tatruppādavassāvāsikagahaṇe. Sabbesanti akhilānaṃ bhikkhusāmaṇerānaṃ. Bhaṇḍāgārikacīvarepīti bhaṇḍāgāre ṭhapite akālacīvarepi. Pisaddena tatruppādavassāvāsikamapekkhati. Sāmaṇerā ukkuṭṭhiṃ karontīti sambandho. Apaharitakanti haritavirahitaṃ. Raṅgachallinti rajanacchaviṃ. Etanti ukkuṭṭhikaraṇato samabhāgadānaṃ, vuttanti sambandho. Ye cāti sāmaṇerā ca. Virajjhitvā karontīti kattabbakālesu akatvā yathicchitakkhaṇe karonti. Teti sāmaṇere. Samapaṭivīso dātabboti “karissāmā”ti paṭiññātamattena samo paṭivīso dātabbo.

"Attissarā" means they are masters of themselves. "Aññesaṃ vattapaṭipatti": this is the connection. "Upaḍḍhabhāgo" means half a share of the share received by the monks. "Ye pana" means the novices. "Samabhāgo" means a share equal to the monks' share. "Idaṃ ca" refers to the statement "upaḍḍhapaṭivīsa"; "kathitaṃ" is the connection. "Samakam eva" means of exactly equal measure for both monks and novices. "Tatruppādavassāvāsikaṃ" means the rains-residence robe produced from the income in that monastery. "Phātikamma" means an act of improvement—"by whatever means, according to the Vinaya, through manual labor such as sweeping and binding, the monastery is not left deficient, that much having been done"; this is the meaning. "Etaṃ" means the taking after having done the act of improvement. "Hi" means truly. "Ettha" means in the taking of the rains-residence robe produced there. "Sabbesaṃ" means of all, without exception, monks and novices. "Bhaṇḍāgārikacīvare pi" means also in the case of an out-of-season robe placed in the storeroom. By the word "pi", it also includes the rains-residence robe produced there. "Sāmaṇerā ukkuṭṭhiṃ karonti" is the connection. "Apaharitakaṃ" means undyed. "Raṅgachalli" means a dyed skin. "Etaṃ" means the giving of an equal share because of the commotion; "vuttaṃ" is the connection. "Ye ca" means and the novices. "Virajjhitvā karonti" means they do it at a moment of their own choosing, not doing it at the times it should be done. "Te" means those novices. "An equal share should be given" means an equal share should be given merely on the basis of their promise, 'We will do it.'

“Sakaṃ bhāgaṃ dātu”nti idaṃ vuttanti sambandho. Kiṃ sandhāya vuttanti āha “bhaṇḍāgārato…pe… sandhāyā”ti. Pahatāyāti paharitabbāya, pahanitabbāya vā. Tasmāti yasmā sandhāya vuttaṃ, tasmā. Anīhaṭesūti bhaṇḍāgārato anīharitesu. Imassa bhikkhunoti uttaritukāmassa imassa bhikkhuno. Tulāyāti mānena.

"To give one's own share": this was said, is the connection. With reference to what was this said? He says, "With reference to... from the storeroom..." "Pahatāya" means to be struck, or to be abandoned. "Tasmā" means: because it was said with reference to that, therefore. "Anīhaṭesu" means not taken out from the storeroom. "For this monk" means for this monk who desires to cross over. "By a balance" means by measure.

Tesūti sāṭakesu, eko sāṭakoti yojanā. Sabbesu pātitesūti sambandho. Ettakenāti [V 2.0040] dvādasagghanakena. Taṃ sutvāti bhikkhūnaṃ taṃ vacanaṃ sutvā. Sabbatthāti sabbasmiṃ saṅghagaṇasantake. Anuppadānena khipiyati pakkhipiyatīti anukkhepanti dassento āha “anukkhepaṃ nāmā”tiādi. Yattakaṃ agghanti sambandho. Tattakena agghena agghanaketi yojanā. Vikallakāti vikalassa bhāvo vikallaṃ, cīvarapuggalānaṃ apahonakabhāvo, tadeva vikallakā. “Tatthā”ti pāṭhaseso, tesu dvīsu vikallakesūti attho. Atthīti saṃvijjanti, nipātoyaṃ. Chindantehi ca dātabbānīti sambandho. Dātabbānīti ca chinditabbāni. Dāsaddo hi avakhaṇḍanattho. Dātunti avakhaṇḍituṃ. Evantiādi nigamanaṃ. Etthāti etesu vikallakesu. Tanti cīvaraṃ[M 0.0379]. Athāti tositato paraṃ. Tatthāti ekassa bhikkhuno koṭṭhāse. Sāmaṇakanti samaṇassa anurūpaṃ. Yoti bhikkhu. Tenāti parikkhārena. Idampīti aññaṃ sāmaṇakassa parikkhārassa ṭhapanampi. Pisaddena purimaṃ vatthachindanamapekkhati.

"Tesu" means in the cloths. "Eko sāṭako" is the construction. "Sabbesu pātitesu" is the connection. "Ettakena" means with a value of twelve. "Taṃ sutvā" means having heard that statement of the monks. "Sabbattha" means in everything belonging to the Sangha or a group. Showing that "anukkhepa" means it is cast out or put aside through non-giving, he says, "anukkhepaṃ nāma", and so on. "Yattakaṃ agghaṃ" is the connection. "Tattakena agghena agghanakaṃ" is the construction. "Vikallakā" means the state of being defective is "vikallaṃ", the state of insufficiency for the robe and the person; that itself is "vikallakā". "Tattha" is the remainder of the reading, meaning in those two cases of defectiveness. "Atthi" means they exist; this is a particle. "Chindantehi ca dātabbāni" is the connection. "Dātabbāni" also means they should be cut. For the word "dā" has the meaning of cutting off. "Dātuṃ" means to cut off. "Evaṃ", and so on, is the conclusion. "Ettha" means in these cases of defectiveness. "Taṃ" means the robe. "Atha" means after being satisfied. "Tattha" means in the share of one monk. "Sāmaṇakaṃ" means suitable for a recluse. "Yo" means the monk. "Tena" means with the requisite. "Idam pi" means also the setting aside of another requisite suitable for a recluse. By the word "pi", it refers to the previous cutting of the cloth.

Vagganti samūhaṃ. Aṭṭha vā nava vā bhikkhū hontīti yojanā. Tesanti aṭṭhannaṃ vā navannaṃ vā. Evantiādi nigamanaṃ. Ayaṃ apahonakabhāvoti yojanā. Puna cīvarasseva vikallakabhāvaṃ dassento āha “athavā”tiādi. Ettha purimanaye cīvarassa ca puggalassa ca vikallakaṃ hoti, pacchime cīvarassevāti ayametesaṃ viseso.

"Vaggaṃ" means a group. "There are eight or nine monks" is the construction. "Tesaṃ" means of the eight or nine. "Evaṃ", and so on, is the conclusion. "This is the state of insufficiency" is the construction. Again, showing the state of defectiveness of the robe alone, he says, "athavā", and so on. Here, in the former method, there is defectiveness of both the robe and the person, but in the latter, only of the robe—this is the difference between them.

215. Cīvararajanakathā

215. The Account of Dyeing Robes

344. Gihiparibhuttaṃ panāti gihinā paribhuttaṃ vatthaṃ pana, kiñci phalanti sambandho.

344. "Gihiparibhuttaṃ pana" means a cloth used by a householder; "kiñci phalaṃ" is the connection.

Sītudakāti sītaṃ udakaṃ. Liṅgavipallāso hi ayaṃ. Uttarāḷumpanti ettha uttara uḷumpanti padacchedaṃ katvā akārato ukārassa lopaṃ katvā, pubbasarassa ca dīghaṃ katvā “uttarāḷumpa”nti vuccati. Uttarāḷūti uttaraudakaṃ. Uḷusaddo hi udakavācako, taṃ pāti rakkhatīti uttarāḷumpaṃ. Tassa sarūpaṃ dassento āha “vaṭṭādhāraka”nti. Rajananti rajanachalliṃ. Hīti phalajotako. Rajananti rajanudakaṃ. Hīti vitthāro. Thevoti rajanabindu. Na visaratīti na paggharati. Rajanāḷuṅkanti etthāpi purimanayeneva padasiddhi veditabbā. Rajanauḷuṅkanti rajanasaṅkhātassa udakassa gahaṇatthāya kariyatīti rajanauḷuṅkaṃ. Daṇḍakena niyuttaṃ thālakaṃ daṇḍakathālakanti dassento āha “tameva sadaṇḍaka”nti. Rajanakuṇḍanti rajanapakkhipanaṃ mahāghaṭaṃ. Aññatrāti aññaṃ ṭhānaṃ. Patthinnasaddo thaddhapariyāyoti āha “thaddha”nti. Dantakāsāvānīti ettha dantasaddena tassa vaṇṇo gahetabbo, so etesamatthīti dantāni, dantāni ca [V 2.0041] tāni kāsāvāni ceti dantakāsāvāni, tamatthaṃ dassento āha “dantavaṇṇānī”ti. Dantavaṇṇāni kāsāvāni dhārentīti sambandho.

"Sītudakaṃ" means cold water. This is indeed a change of gender. Here, regarding "uttarāḷumpaṃ", having divided the words as "uttara uḷumpa", and having elided the "u" after the "a", and having lengthened the preceding vowel, it is called "uttarāḷumpa". "Uttarāḷū" means the water on top. For the word "uḷu" is a term for water; that which protects it is "uttarāḷumpaṃ". Showing its form, he says, "a circular support". "Rajanaṃ" means a dye-skin. "Hi" indicates the result. "Rajanaṃ" means dye-water. "Hi" is an elaboration. "Thevo" means a drop of dye. "Na visarati" means it does not drip. Here too, in "rajanāḷuṅkaṃ", the word formation should be understood in the same way as before. "Rajanauḷuṅkaṃ" is so called because it is made for the purpose of taking the water known as dye. Showing that "daṇḍakathālakaṃ" is a bowl fitted with a stick, he says, "that very one with a stick". "Rajanakuṇḍaṃ" means a large pot for putting dye in. "Aññatra" means another place. The word "patthinna" is a synonym for "thaddha", thus he says, "thaddha". Regarding "dantakāsāvāni": here, by the word "danta", its color should be understood; because they have this, they are "dantāni"; and they are "kāsāvāni", thus "dantakāsāvāni". Showing this meaning, he says, "of tooth color". The connection is: they wear robes of tooth color.

216. Chinnakacīvarānujānanakathā

216. The Account of the Allowance for Cut Robes

345. Dīghamariyādabaddhanti [M 0.0380] dīghena mariyādena baddhaṃ. Catukkasaṇṭhānanti catunnaṃ maggānaṃ samodhānasaṇṭhānaṃ. Ussahasi tvanti ettha upubbo sahadhātu samatthatthoti āha “sakkosi tva”nti. Papubbo pana abhibhavanattho hoti “pasahatī”tiādīsu. Yo nāmāti yo ānando ājānissati nāma, so ānando paṇḍitoti yojanā. “Kusī”ti etaṃ nāmaṃ adhivacananti yojanā. Anuvātādīnanti ādisaddena paribhaṇḍādīni saṅgaṇhāti. “Aḍḍhakusī”ti etanti yojanā.

345. "Dīghamariyādabaddhaṃ" means bound with a long border. "Catukkasaṇṭhānaṃ" means having the shape of the meeting of four roads. Here, in "ussahasi tvaṃ", the root "sah" preceded by "u-" has the meaning of being able, thus he says, "sakkosi tvaṃ". The prefix "pa-", however, has the meaning of overcoming, as in "pasahati", and so on. "Yo nāma" means: whatever Ānanda will indeed know, that Ānanda is wise; this is the construction. "Kusī" is a designation for this name; this is the construction. In "anuvātādīnaṃ", by the word "ādi", it includes things like utensils, and so on. "Aḍḍhakusī": this is the construction.

Gīveyyakanti ettha gīvāyaṃ suttasaṃsibbitaṃ gīveyyakanti vacanatthaṃ dassento āha “gīvāveṭhanaṭṭhāne”tiādi. “Āgantukapaṭṭa”nti iminā eyyakapaccayassa sarūpaṃ dasseti. Eseva nayo jaṅgheyyakanti etthāpi. Etaṃ nāmanti “gīveyyakaṃ, jaṅgheyyaka”nti etaṃ nāmaṃ. Itīti evaṃ. Etanti “anuvivaṭṭa”ntiādi etaṃ. “Anuvivaṭṭa”nti etaṃ nāmanti yojanā. Vivaṭṭassāti majjhimakhaṇḍakassa. Bāhantanti ettha bāhāya upari ṭhapitā antā bāhantāti vacanatthaṃ dassento āha “bāhāyā”tiādi. Tesanti ubhinnamantānaṃ. Etanti “bāhanta”nti etaṃ.

Regarding 'gīveyyaka,' showing the meaning of the word 'gīveyyaka' as 'that which is stitched with thread on the neck,' he says, 'in the place of a neck-wrapping,' and so on. By this, 'Āgantukapaṭṭa,' he indicates the nature of the suffix 'eyyaka.' This same method applies also to 'jaṅgheyyaka.' 'This name' means 'gīveyyaka, jaṅgheyyaka' is this name. 'Iti' means thus. 'This' refers to 'anuvivaṭṭa,' and so on. The construal is: 'Anuvivaṭṭa' is this name. 'Of vivaṭṭa' means of the middle section. Regarding 'bāhanta,' showing the meaning of the word 'bāhanta' as 'the ends placed upon the arm,' he says, 'of the arm,' and so on. 'Their' means of the two ends. 'This' refers to 'bāhanta.'

217. Ticīvarānujānanakathā

217. The Account of the Allowing of the Three Robes.

346. “Ukkhittabhaṇḍikabhāvaṃ āpādite”ti iminā ubbhaṇḍiteti ettha ukkhittaṃ bhaṇḍaṃ ubbhaṇḍaṃ, ubbhaṇḍabhāvaṃ itā āpāditāti ubbhaṇḍitāti vacanatthaṃ dasseti. Te ubbhaṇḍite bhikkhū addasāti yojanā. Bhisisaṅkhepenāti bhisiyaṃ pakkhepena, pavesenāti attho, bhisiākārenāti vuttaṃ hoti. Tatthāti dakkhiṇāgiriṃ. Gacchantā te bhikkhūti yojanā. “Aṭṭhapamāṇāsū”ti iminā antaraṭṭhakāsūti ettha kapaccayo pamāṇatthe hotīti dasseti, kesuci potthakesu pamāṇasaddo na dissati, gaḷitoti daṭṭhabbo. Rattīsūti sambandho. Bhagavantanti ettha sampadānatthe upayogavacananti āha “bhagavato”ti. Sītālukāti ettha sītaṃ pakati etesanti sītāluno[M 0.0381], teyeva sītālukāti vacanatthaṃ dassento āha “sītapakatikā”ti[V 2.0042]. Ye kulaputtā pakatiyāva sītena kilamanti, te sītālukā nāmāti yojanā. Ekacciyanti ettha ekaccasaddo ekapariyāyoti āha “ekaṃ paṭṭa”nti. Iminā ekoyeva ekaccoti katvā sakatthe accapaccayoti dasseti. “Paṭṭa”nti iminā ekaccena niyuttaṃ ekacciyanti vacanatthaṃ katvā niyuttatthe pavattassa iyapaccayassa sarūpaṃ dasseti. Itīti evaṃ. Bhagavā anujānātīti sambandho. Itareti saṅghāṭito itare uttarāsaṅgaantaravāsake.

346. By 'Ukkhittabhaṇḍikabhāvaṃ āpādite,' he explains 'ubbhaṇḍite.' Here, he shows the meaning of the word 'ubbhaṇḍitā' as: 'ukkhittaṃ bhaṇḍaṃ' is 'ubbhaṇḍaṃ,' and 'ubbhaṇḍabhāvaṃ itā āpāditā' means 'brought to a state of having their bundles removed.' The construal is: 'He saw those monks who had their bundles removed.' 'Bhisisaṅkhepenāti' means by putting into a cushion, that is, by inserting; it is said to be in the manner of a cushion. 'Tatthāti' means to Dakkhiṇāgiri. The construal is: 'those monks going.' By 'Aṭṭhapamāṇāsū,' he shows that in 'antaraṭṭhakāsu,' the suffix 'ka' is in the sense of measure. In some books, the word 'pamāṇa' is not seen; it should be understood as omitted. 'Rattīsūti' is the connection. Regarding 'Bhagavantaṃ,' here it is a case usage in the dative sense, thus he says 'Bhagavato.' Regarding 'sītālukā,' showing the meaning of the word as 'sītaṃ pakati etesanti sītāluno, teyeva sītālukā,' he says 'sītapakatikā' (of a cold nature). The construal is: those sons of good family who by nature are afflicted by cold are called 'sītālukā.' Regarding 'ekacciyaṃ,' here the word 'ekacca' is a synonym, thus he says 'one piece.' By this, taking 'ekacca' as just 'eka,' he shows that the suffix 'acca' is in its own sense. By this, 'piece,' having given the word-meaning of 'ekacciyaṃ' as 'assigned by one,' he shows the nature of the suffix 'iya' which occurs in the sense of 'assigned.' 'Itīti' means thus. 'Bhagavā anujānātīti' is the connection. 'Itareti' means the others apart from the saṅghāṭi, namely the upper robe and the inner robe.

218. Atirekacīvarādikathā

218. Discussion on Extra Robes and So Forth.

348. Acchupeyyanti ettha acchi vuccati nettamaṇḍalaṃ, taṃ viyāti acchi chiddo, tasmiṃ upagantabbaṃ upanetabbanti acchupeyyaṃ. “Laggāpeyya”nti iminā adhippāyatthaṃ dasseti. Etthāti paṃsukūle. Sabbamidanti “diguṇaṃ saṅghāṭi”ntiādikaṃ sabbaṃ idaṃ vacanaṃ. Uddharitvāti apanetvā. Saṃsibbitanti aññamaññaṃ sambandhitvā sibbitaṃ.

348. Regarding 'acchupeyyaṃ': 'acchi' is said to be the orb of the eye; like that, the eye is a hole; that which should be approached or brought near to it is 'acchupeyyaṃ.' By 'Laggāpeyya,' he shows the intended meaning. 'Etthāti' means in the rag-robe. 'Sabbamidanti' means all this utterance, namely, 'a double-layered outer robe,' and so forth. 'Uddharitvāti' means having removed. 'Saṃsibbitanti' means stitched, having connected them one to another.

351. Sovaggikanti ettha sundarāni aggāni rūpādīni etthāti saggo, pubbapade ukārassa lopo, ukārassa uvādese “suvaggo”ti sijjhati. Suvaggappattahetukaṃ sovaggikaṃ, dānaṃ, tamatthaṃ dassento āha “saggappattahetuka”nti. “Apanetī”ti iminā nudadhātuyā apanayanatthaṃ dasseti. Anāmayāti ettha āmayasaddo rogapariyāyoti āha “arogā”ti. Natthi āmayo etissāti anāmayā.

351. Regarding 'sovaggikaṃ': 'sagga' is where there are beautiful, foremost things such as form; in the first part, there is elision of the 'u,' and with the substitution of 'uva' for 'u,' 'suvaggo' is formed. 'Sovaggikaṃ' is that which is a cause for attaining 'suvagga,' that is, giving. Showing that meaning, he says, 'a cause for attaining sagga.' By 'Apanetī,' he shows the meaning of removal for the root 'nud.' Regarding 'anāmayā': the word 'āmaya' is a synonym for disease, thus he says 'arogā.' 'Natthi āmayo etissāti anāmayā' means: there is no disease for her, thus she is 'anāmayā.'

353. Jhānalābhinoti jhānalābhīnaṃ puthujjanānaṃ kāmacchandanīvaraṇassa vikkhambhanattā vuttaṃ.

353. 'Jhānalābhino' is said on account of the suppression of the hindrance of sensual desire for ordinary people who are attainers of jhāna.

356. Samodhānavasena dassiyitthāti sandiṭṭho. Samodhānavasena bhajiyitthāti sambhatto. Abhimukhaṃ lapitthāti ālapito. Imehīti imehi dvīhi.

356. 'Sandiṭṭho' means: he was shown by way of conjunction. 'Sambhatto' means: he was associated with by way of conjunction. 'Ālapito' means: he was spoken to face-to-face. 'Imehīti' means by these two.

221. Pacchimavikappanupagacīvarādikathā

221. Discussion on Robes and So Forth Connected with the Final Allocation.

359. Katapaṃsukūloti [M 0.0382] kato paṃsukūlo. Iminā “paṃsukūlato”ti padassa visesanaparapadattaṃ dasseti. Aggaḷāropanenāti aggaḷassa āropanena. “Suttenevā”ti ettha evasaddena [V 2.0043] pilotikaṃ nivatteti. Añchitvā añchitvāti ākaḍḍhitvā ākaḍḍhitvā. Abhidhātu hi ākaḍḍhanattho. “Saṅghāṭikoṇo dīgho”ti iminā vikaṇṇoti ettha visamo kaṇṇo vikaṇṇoti katvā kaṇṇasaddassa koṇatthaṃ dasseti. Tatoti gaḷanato. Lujjantīti valiṃ gaṇhanti. Aṭṭhapadakanti padassa aṭṭhapadena sibbitaṃ aṭṭhapadakanti vacanatthaṃ dassento āha “aṭṭhapadakacchinnena pattamukhaṃ sibbitu”nti. Tattha aṭṭhapadakacchinnena pattamukhaṃ sibbitunti aṭṭhapadalikhanena tattha tattha gabbhaṃ dassetvā pattamukhaṃ sibbituṃ. “Aṭṭhapadakacchannenā”tipi pāṭho, aṭṭhaphalakākārenāti attho.

359. 'Katapaṃsukūloti' means a made rag-robe. By this, he shows that the word 'paṃsukūlato' is the qualifying latter member of a compound. 'Aggaḷāropanenāti' means by the placing of a bolt. In 'Suttenevā,' the word 'eva' excludes a strip of cloth. 'Añchitvā añchitvāti' means pulling and pulling. For the root 'abhidhā' has the meaning of pulling. By 'Saṅghāṭikoṇo dīgho,' having taken 'vikaṇṇa' as 'uneven corner,' he shows the meaning of 'kaṇṇa' as 'corner.' 'Tatoti' means from decaying. 'Lujjantīti' means they form wrinkles. Regarding 'aṭṭhapadakaṃ,' showing the meaning of the word 'aṭṭhapadakaṃ' as 'stitched with an aṭṭhapada pattern,' he says, 'to stitch the mouth of the bowl with a cutting in the aṭṭhapada pattern.' Here, 'to stitch the mouth of the bowl with a cutting in the aṭṭhapada pattern' means to stitch the mouth of the bowl by showing indentations here and there with an aṭṭhapada marking. There is also the reading 'aṭṭhapadakacchannena,' meaning in the manner of an eight-paneled board.

360. “Āgantukapattampi dātu”nti iminā anvādikanti padassa anupacchā āgantukabhāvena dīyatīti anvādikanti vacanatthaṃ dasseti. Catutthakkharenapi pāṭho, anupacchā āgantukabhāvena dhīyati ṭhapīyatīti anvādhikanti kātabbo. Idaṃ panāti anvādhikaṃ pana.

360. By 'Āgantukapattampi dātu,' he shows the meaning of the word 'anvādikaṃ' as: it is given afterwards as a portion for a newcomer, thus it is 'anvādikaṃ.' There is also a reading with the fourth letter, which should be taken as 'anvādhikaṃ': it is placed or established afterwards as a portion for a newcomer. 'Idaṃ panāti' means this 'anvādhikaṃ,' however.

361. Sesañātīnanti mātāpitūhi sesañātīnaṃ. Vinipātetiyevāti vinassanto nipātetiyeva.

361. 'Sesañātīnanti' means of the remaining relatives apart from mother and father. 'Vinipātetiyevāti' means, being ruined, he indeed casts down.

362. “Vassiko”ti saṅketīyati gaṇhīyatīti vassikasaṅketanti vutte cattāro māsāti āha “cattāro māse”ti. Hīti saccaṃ, yasmā vā. Āraññakassa bhikkhunoti sambandho. Tenāti āraññakena bhikkhunā.

362. Regarding 'vassiko': it is agreed upon, it is undertaken, thus when 'vassikasaṅketaṃ' is said, meaning 'four months,' he says 'four months.' 'Hīti' means indeed, or because. 'Āraññakassa bhikkhunoti' is the connection. 'Tenāti' means by that forest-dwelling monk.

222. Saṅghikacīvaruppādakathā

222. The Account of the Arising of Robes Belonging to the Sangha.

363. Aññatthāti dinnaṭṭhānato aññattha. Haṭānipi cīvarāni tuyheva santakānīti yojanā. Tesanti cīvarānaṃ. Aññoti ekakavassāvāsikato [M 0.0383] añño. Pañcamāse taṃ sabbaṃ tasseva bhikkhuno hotīti sambandho. Yanti cīvaraṃ, taṃ sabbaṃ cīvaranti sambandho. Yampīti cīvarampi. Soti bhikkhu, gaṇhātīti sambandho. Vassāvāsatthāyāti vassaṃ āvāsassa bhikkhuno atthāya. Ṭhapitaupanikkhepatoti veyyāvaccakarehi vaḍḍhiṃ payojetvā ṭhapitaupanikkhepato. Tatruppādatoti tasmiṃ vihāre uppādato nāḷikeraārāmādito. Idanti vakkhamānaṃ. Etthāti “tasseva tāni cīvarāni yāva kathinassa ubbhārāyā”ti vacane. Yanti cīvaraṃ. Pana saddo visesatthajotako. Idanti padālaṅkāramattaṃ. Idhāti imasmiṃ vihāre. Abhilāpamattantipi vadanti. Anatthatakathinassāpīti pisaddo pageva atthatakathinassāti dasseti[V 2.0044]. Pañcamāseti accantasaṃyogatthe upayogavacanaṃ. Tatoti pañcamāsato. Atītavasse vassaṃvutthasaṅghassa idaṃ vassāvāsikaṃ deti kiṃ? Udāhu anāgatavasseti yojanā. Piṭṭhisamayeti gimhānaṃ paṭhamadivasato paṭṭhāya yāva assayujapuṇṇamī, tāva piṭṭhisamaye.

363. 'Aññatthāti' means elsewhere than the place it was given. The construal is: 'Even robes taken by force are your property.' 'Tesanti' means of the robes. 'Aññoti' means other than one who has resided for a single rains-residence. The connection is: in the fifth month, all of that belongs to that very monk. 'Yanti cīvaraṃ, taṃ sabbaṃ cīvaranti' is the connection. 'Yampīti' means even the robe. 'Soti' means that monk; 'gaṇhātīti' is the connection. 'Vassāvāsatthāyāti' means for the sake of the monk who is a resident for the rains. 'Ṭhapitaupanikkhepatoti' means from a deposit set aside by stewards after having applied interest. 'Tatruppādatoti' means from that which arises in that monastery, from a coconut grove and so on. 'Idanti' means that which will be said. 'Etthāti' means in the statement, 'those robes are his until the dismantling of the Kathina.' 'Yanti' means which robe. The word 'pana' illuminates a special meaning. 'Idanti' is merely a verbal embellishment. 'Idhāti' means in this monastery. They also say it is a mere utterance. 'Anatthatakathinassāpīti': the word 'pi' shows 'how much more so for one whose Kathina is spread.' 'Pañcamāseti' is a case usage in the sense of continuous connection. 'Tatoti' means from the fifth month. The construal is: Does one give this rains-residence benefit to the Sangha that has dwelt the rains in a past year? Or in a future year? 'Piṭṭhisamayeti' means in the 'back-season,' which is from the first day of the hot season up to the full moon of Assayuja.

Vassānatoti vassānamāsato. Etthāti etesu cīvaresu. Keci bhikkhūti sambandho. Tamatthanti tassa saṅghikacīvarassa kāraṇaṃ. Tatthevāti gataṭṭhāne eva. Esāti saṅghikacīvarahārako bhikkhu. Tatrāti vihārādīsu. Nanti cīvarahārakaṃ bhikkhuṃ.

'At the end of the rains' means concerning the months of the rains. 'Here' means in these robes. 'Some monks' is the connection. 'For that purpose' means the reason for that Saṅgha robe. 'Right there' means in the very place gone to. 'This' refers to the monk who carries the Saṅgha robe. 'There' means in a monastery and so on. 'Him' refers to the monk carrying the robe.

Vattaṃ vitthāretvā dassento āha “tena hī”tiādi. Tena bhikkhunā bhājetabbānīti sambandho. Tassevāti adhiṭṭhahantasseva.

Explaining the duty in detail, he said, 'Well then,' etc. The connection is: they are to be distributed by that monk. 'Of that very one' means of the one who has resolved upon it.

Ekekaṃ bhāganti sambandho. Ettha ṭhāne ahameva asmīti yojanā. Duggahitāni hontīti saṅghikāneva hontīti adhippāyo. Mayhamevimāni cīvarānīti issaravasena gahaṇe duggahitāni. Mayhetāni pāpuṇantīti anissaravasena gahaṇe suggahitānīti viseso.

'A share for each one' is the connection. Here, in this place, the construction is 'I alone am here.' 'They are wrongly taken' means they are indeed the Saṅgha's—this is the intention. In the case of grasping with a sense of ownership, as in 'These robes are mine,' they are wrongly taken. In the case of grasping without a sense of ownership, as in 'These accrue to me,' they are rightly taken—this is the distinction.

Pātite kuseti ettha tapaccayassa paccuppannakālikabhāvaṃ dassento āha “ekakoṭṭhāse”tiādi. Gahitamevāti ekakoṭṭhāse [M 0.0384] pātitassa kusadaṇḍassa vasena “imassida”nti ekakoṭṭhāse vidite sabbesaṃ viditattā gahitamevāti adhippāyo.

Regarding 'when the kusa-grass stalk has been cast,' here, showing that the past participle suffix has the sense of the present time, he says, 'in one portion,' etc. 'It is indeed taken' means: because the cast kusa-grass stalk is in one portion, and when it is known in that one portion 'this is for this one,' it is known to all, therefore it is indeed taken—this is the intention.

Itovāti sacīvarabhattatova. Visuṃ sajjiyamāneti cīvare ca bhatte ca visuṃ sajjiyamāne.

'From this' means from that which includes the robe and food. 'When being prepared separately' means when the robe and the food are being prepared separately.

Yathā purimesu dvīsu vatthūsu “adaṃsū”ti vuttaṃ, tathā avatvā kasmā idha “dentī”ti vuttanti āha “saṇikaṃ saṇikaṃ dentiyevā”ti. Saṇikaṃ saṇikaṃ dente dānakiriyāya anupacchinnattā “dentī”ti paccuppannavasena vuttanti adhippāyo. Pacchinnadānattāti pacchinnadānakiriyabhāvato. Idaṃ pana vatthu uppannanti sambandho. Ime ca therāti nilavāsiādayo vinayadharapāmokkhā ime ca therā.

Just as in the two previous stories it was said 'they gave,' why is it not said so here, but instead 'they give'? He said, 'Because they are giving slowly, slowly.' Because they are giving slowly, slowly, the act of giving is uninterrupted; therefore, it is said in the present tense as 'they give'—this is the intention. 'Because the giving was concluded' means because the act of giving was a concluded action. 'But this story has arisen' is the connection. And 'these elders' refers to these elders who are the foremost experts in the Vinaya, such as Nilavāsi and others.

223. Upanandasakyaputtavatthukathā

223. The Story of Upananda the Sakyan

364. Etthāti [V 2.0045] upanandavatthumhi. Tassāti upanandassa. Gāmakāvāsinoti gāmake āvāsino. Ayanti upanando. Mukharoti mukhaṃ kharaṃ etassāti mukharo khakāralopo, atha vā mukhaṃ etassatthīti mukharo mantutthe pavatto rapaccayo nindatthavācako. Lahukāpattīti dukkaṭāpatti. Tassevāti gahitabhikkhusseva. Dhuranikkhepe satīti yojanā.

364. 'Here' means in the story of Upananda. 'His' means of Upananda. 'A dweller in a small village' means one who dwells in a small village. 'This one' means Upananda. 'Harsh-mouthed' means one whose mouth is harsh; this is 'harsh-mouthed' with the elision of the 'kha' sound. Or alternatively, 'he has a mouth,' thus 'harsh-mouthed,' with the suffix 'ra' used in the sense of 'possessing' and indicating censure. 'A light offense' means an offense of wrong-doing. 'Of that very one' means of the very monk who took it. 'When the burden is laid down' is the construction.

Ekassa puggalassatthāya adhippiyate icchiyateti ekādhippāyo, ekapuggalapaṭivīso, tenāha “ekapuggalapaṭivīsamevā”ti. Yathā yathāti yena yenākārena. Yoti paṭivīso. “Tathā tathā”ti ajjhāharitabbo. Tatthāti “idha panā”tiādivacane. Ekekasmiṃ āvāseti sambandho. Vāsaddo aññepi dvīhadvīhādivāre saṅgaṇhāti. Yanti paṭivīsaṃ. Eko puggaloti eko niccāvāso puggalo. Evanti upaḍḍhe diyyamāne. Yattha vā panāti ettha yasaddassa visayaṃ dassetuṃ vuttaṃ “evaṃ purimasmi”nti. Purimasmiṃ āvāseti sambandho[M 0.0385]. Tatoti ettha tasaddassa visayaṃ dassento āha “bahutaraṃ vasitavihārato”ti. Idañcāti “amutra upaḍḍho cīvarapaṭivīso dātabbo”ti vacanañca. Ekasīmavihārehīti ekissaṃ upacārasīmāyaṃ ṭhitehi vihārehi. Nānāsīmavihāreti nānāupacārasīmāyaṃ ṭhite vihāre. Senāsanaggāhoti purimaupacārasīmāyaṃ senāsanaggāho. Tatthāti passambhanavihāre. Sesanti cīvarato sesaṃ. Sabbatthāti sabbesu vihāresu. Antosīmagatassāti antoupacārasīmāyaṃ gatassa, bhikkhunoti sambandho. Cīvaraṃ senāsanaggāhasseva pāpuṇāti, sesaṃ pana āmisabhesajjādisabbaṃ aññavihārato āgantvā antosīmagatassa pāpuṇātīti adhippāyo.

'Intended for one' means it is intended or desired for the sake of one person, a share for one person; therefore he said, 'a share for one person only.' 'In whatever way' means by whatever mode. 'Which' means the share. 'In that way' is to be supplied. 'There' means in the phrase 'but here,' etc. 'In each residence' is the connection. The word 'residence' also includes other occasions, such as for two days, etc. 'Which' means the share. 'One person' means one person who is a permanent resident. 'Thus' means when a half is being given. Regarding 'But where,' here, to show the scope of the word 'which,' it is said 'thus in the former.' 'In the former residence' is the connection. Regarding 'from that,' here, showing the scope of the word 'that,' he said 'from the monastery where one has resided longer.' 'And this' means the statement 'over there, half a share of the robes is to be given.' 'By monasteries with a single boundary' means by monasteries situated within one parish boundary. 'In monasteries with different boundaries' means in monasteries situated in different parish boundaries. 'The taking of lodging' means the taking of lodging in the former parish boundary. 'There' means in the Passambhana monastery. 'The remainder' means the remainder from the robes. 'Everywhere' means in all monasteries. 'To one who has gone inside the boundary' means to a monk who has gone inside the parish boundary—this is the connection. The robe accrues only to the one who took the lodging, but the remainder—all material things, medicine, etc.—coming from another monastery, accrues to one who has gone inside the boundary—this is the intention.

224. Gilānavatthukathā

224. The Story of the Sick Person

365. Mañcake nipātesunti ettha mañcake nipātanaṃ nāma mañcake nipajjāpananti āha “mañcake nipajjāpesu”nti. Muttakarīsakiliṭṭhanti muttakarīsehi kiliṭṭhaṃ. Yoti yo koci. Manti mama. Tamatthaṃ dassento āha “ovādānusāsanīkaraṇenā”ti. Mama ovādassa ca anusāsaniyā ca karaṇenāti attho. Etthāti “yo bhikkhave maṃ upaṭṭhaheyyā”tiādipāṭhe. Suttassa neyyatthattā agahetabbatthaṃ dassento āha “bhagavato cā”tiādi. Yassāti gilānassa. Upajjhāyādayoti ettha ādisaddena ācariyasaddhivihārikaantevāsikasamānupajjhāyakasamānācariyakasaṅkhāte [V 2.0046] pañca jane saṅgaṇhāti. Ekacāriko vā hotīti sambandho. Saṅghattheropīti pisaddo pageva aññesanti dasseti.

365. Regarding 'they laid him on a couch,' here 'laying on a couch' means causing to lie down on a couch, so he said 'they caused him to lie down on a couch.' 'Soiled with urine and feces' means soiled by urine and feces. 'Who' means whoever. 'Me' means my. Explaining that meaning, he says, 'by carrying out the advice and instruction.' The meaning is: 'by carrying out my advice and instruction.' Here, in the text beginning, 'Monks, whoever would attend to me,' because the discourse is of inferential meaning, showing the meaning that is not to be taken literally, he says 'of the Blessed One,' etc. 'Whose' means of the sick person. 'Preceptor and so on'—here the word 'so on' includes the five persons designated as: teacher, co-resident, pupil, one with the same preceptor, and one with the same teacher. 'Or he may be one who lives alone' is the connection. 'Even the elder of the Saṅgha'—the particle 'pi' shows that it applies all the more to others.

366. Abhikkamantaṃ vāti ettha abhimukhaṃ kamatīti abhikkamantoti vutte vaḍḍhanatthoti āha “vaḍḍhantaṃ vā”ti. Ābādhaṃ nāvikarotīti sambandho. Iminā antapaccayassa sarūpaṃ dasseti. Idaṃ nāma bhojananti sambandho. Saṃvidhātunti ettha saṃvipubbo dhādhātu karadhātvattho, karadhātu ca sabbadhātvattho, tasmā vuttaṃ “bhesajjaṃ yojetu”nti[M 0.0386]. Assāti gilānupaṭṭhākassa. Antarasaddassa majjhatthādayo paṭikkhipanto āha “kāraṇaṃ vuccatī”ti.

366. Regarding 'or advancing,' here, when 'advancing' is said, meaning 'he goes forward,' it has the sense of 'increasing,' so he said 'or increasing.' 'It does not make the illness manifest' is the connection. By this he shows the form of the suffix '-anta.' 'This is indeed food' is the connection. Regarding 'to arrange,' here the root 'dhā' with the prefix 'saṃvi' has the meaning of the root 'kar' (to do), and the root 'kar' has the meaning of all roots; therefore it is said 'to compound medicine.' 'His' means of the one attending the sick. Rejecting the meanings 'middle,' etc., for the word 'antara,' he says 'it is called the reason'.

225. Matasantakakathā

225. The Account of the Possessions of the Deceased

367. Kālaṅkateti ettha karaṇaṃ katanti dassento āha “kālakiriyāyā”ti. Apaloketvāti “itthannāmo bhante bhikkhu kālaṅkato, tassa ticīvarañca pattañca gilānupaṭṭhākānaṃ dātuṃ saṅghaṃ apalokemī”ti apaloketvā.

367. Regarding 'has died,' here, showing that `karaṇa` means `kata`, he says 'by the act of making time.' 'Having obtained consent' means having obtained consent thus: 'Venerable sirs, the monk named so-and-so has died. I ask for the Saṅgha's consent to give his three robes and bowl to those who attended him when he was sick'.

369. Gilānupaṭṭhākalābheti gilānupaṭṭhākānaṃ labhitabbe.

369. Regarding the gain for the attendants of the sick: this means in what is to be obtained by the attendants of the sick.

Sabbepi bhikkhūti sambandho. Tatthāti tasmiṃ kālaṅkate. Kiṃ vadanti? “Sabbepi…pe… sāmino”ti vadantīti yojanā. Dvīsu vādesu pacchimavādo aṭṭhakathācariyena ruccatīti vadanti. Yanti yaṃ vatthu. “Yaṃ atthi, taṃ dātabba”nti vuttamevatthaṃ āvikaronto āha “aññasmiṃ…pe… dātabba”nti. Tanti parikkhāraṃ.

'All the monks' is the connection. 'There' means regarding the one who has died. What do they say? The construction is: they say, 'All... are the owners.' They say that of the two opinions, the latter opinion is preferred by the commentator. 'Which' means which thing. Making clear this very meaning that was stated, 'Whatever there is, that is to be given,' he says 'in another... is to be given.' 'That' means the requisite.

Samakoti samaṃ pamāṇametassa bhāgassāti samako. Saṃvidahanamattamevāti idañcidañca karohīti sajjanamattameva. Jeṭṭhakabhāgoti diguṇabhāgo.

'Equal share' means: the measure of this share is equal, thus 'equal share.' 'Merely arranging' means merely preparing, as in 'do this and this.' 'The elder's share' means a double share.
