Yo panāti bhikkhu pana. Etthāti bahūsu bhikkhūsu. Yenāti yena kenaci, dinnaṃ paṭiyāditanti sambandho. Ekadivasampīti pisaddo pageva dvīhādiketi dasseti. Sopīti pisaddo na kevalaṃ bahudivasaṃ upaṭṭhākoyeva, atha kho sopīti dasseti. Samīpanti gilānassa santikaṃ. Āgacchatīti samīpamāgacchati.

'But whoever' means but a monk. 'Here' means among many monks. 'By which' means by whichever one; 'given' or 'prepared' is the connection. 'Even for one day'—the particle 'pi' shows that it applies all the more to two days, etc. 'He also'—the particle 'pi' shows that it is not only one who attends for many days, but indeed also he. 'Near' means in the presence of the sick person. 'He comes' means he comes near.

Paccāsīsāyāti [V 2.0047] bhāgassa paccāsīsāya. “Puna āgantvā jaggissāmī”ti iminā “puna āgantvā na jaggissāmī”ti gacchantassa na dātabbanti dasseti. Dhuraṃ nikkhipitvāti upaṭṭhahane dhuraṃ nikkhipitvā.

'With expectation' means with expectation of a share. By this, 'I will return and attend,' he shows that it is not to be given to one who goes away thinking, 'I will not return and attend.' 'Having laid down the burden' means having laid down the burden of attending.

Mātugāmopi hotūti yojanā. Tassa bhikkhunoti kālaṅkatassa tassa bhikkhuno. Sacepi sahassaṃ agghati, gilānupaṭṭhākānaṃyeva [M 0.0387] dātabbanti yojanā. Aññanti pattacīvarato aññaṃ. Teti gilānupaṭṭhākā. Avasesanti pattacīvarato avasesaṃ. Tatoti bahukamahagghato. Ticīvaraparikkhāroti tiṇṇaṃ cīvarānaṃ parivāro. Sabbañcetanti sabbameva etaṃ parikkhāraṃ. Labhatīti gilānupaṭṭhāko labhati.

The construction is: 'even a woman should be included.' 'Tassa bhikkhuno' means 'of that bhikkhu who has passed away.' The construction is: 'Even if it is worth a thousand, it should be given only to the attendants of the sick.' 'Aññaṃ' means 'other than the bowl and robes.' 'Te' refers to the attendants of the sick. 'Avasesaṃ' means 'the remainder from the bowl and robes.' 'Tato' means 'from much that is valuable.' 'Ticīvaraparikkhāro' means 'the accessories of the three robes.' 'Sabbañcetaṃ' means 'all of this equipment.' 'Labhati' means 'the attendant of the sick obtains'.

Soti kālaṅkato. Kassacīti gahaṭṭhassa vā pabbajitassa vā. Tassevāti dinnagāhakasseva. Ruciyā evāti kāmā eva. Tattha tattha saṅghassevāti tasmiṃ tasmiṃ vihāre ṭhitassa saṅghasseva. Idaṃ vihāre ṭhapitaparikkhāre sandhāya vuttaṃ. Sace gāme vā araññe vā ṭhapitā honti, sakalova saṅgho issaro. Kasmā? Saṅghasseva dāyajjabhāvato. Bahūnampīti tīhi paṭṭhāya bahūnampi. Īdisavacanaṃ upanidhāya sāsanepi eko dve bahūti tīṇi vacanāni atthe dissanti, sadde pana dvivacanabahuvacanānaṃ visesābhāvato dvivacanaṃ natthīti daṭṭhabbaṃ. Adinnamevāti attanoyeva asantakattā, aññesampi sādhāraṇattā ca adinnameva. Sace sabbe matā anumatiyā denti, sudinnameva. Tanti santakaṃ. Tesūti tesu sabbesu.

'So' refers to the one who has passed away. 'Kassaci' means 'of anyone, whether a householder or a renunciant.' 'Tasseva' means 'only of the recipient of the gift.' 'Ruciyā eva' means 'simply by desire.' 'Tattha tattha saṅghasseva' means 'only of the Saṅgha established in each respective monastery.' This is stated with reference to the requisites placed in the monastery. If they are placed in a village or in the wilderness, the entire Saṅgha is the owner. Why? Because it is solely the Saṅgha's inheritance. 'Bahūnaṃ pi' means 'even for many, starting from three.' By analogy with such expressions, in the Teaching too, the three terms 'one,' 'two,' and 'many' are seen in meaning, but in grammar, due to the absence of distinction between dual and plural, the dual is not to be seen. 'Adinnameva' means 'indeed ungiven,' because it is not one's own property and is common to others. If all, having agreed, give with consent, it is indeed well-given. 'Taṃ' means 'property.' 'Tesu' means 'among all of them'.

227. Kusacīrādipaṭikkhepakathā

227. Discussion on the Rejection of Grass-Cloth Robes and the Like

371. “Akkanāḷamaya”nti iminā akkanāḷena nibbattaṃ akkanāḷanti vacanatthaṃ dasseti. Makacimayoti ettha makacisaddena potthakasaddassa ganthādayo atthe nivatteti. Mayasaddena purimanayeneva nibbattataddhitaṃ dasseti. Sesānīti akkanāḷapotthakehi sesāni kusacīrādīni. Tesūti kusacīrādīsu.

371. By 'Akkanāḷamaya' (made of akkanāḷa), this shows the meaning of the word 'akkanāḷa' to be 'that which is made from akkanāḷa.' In 'made of bark,' the word 'makaci' excludes meanings of 'potthaka' such as 'texts' and the like. The word 'maya' indicates a taddhita derivative meaning 'made of,' in the same way as before. 'The rest' refers to things other than those made of akkanāḷa and bark, such as grass-cloth garments and the like. 'Among them' means among the grass-cloth garments and similar items.

372. Tipaṭṭacīvarassa vāti idaṃ dvipaṭṭacīvarassa majjhe dānaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ. Tesanti sabbanīlakādīnaṃ. Kañcukanti vāraṇaṃ. Tañhi kaciyati kāye bandhiyatīti kañcukoti vuccati. Veṭhanepīti uṇhīsepi. Tañhi yasmā yena sīse veṭhiyati, tasmā veṭhananti vuccati. Rukkhachallimayanti ettha rukkhachallisaddena tirīṭasaddassa vakkalatthaṃ dasseti. Vakkalañhi [V 2.0048][M 0.0388] nivasanānaṃ aṅgapaccaṅgaṃ tirobhāvaṃ paṭicchannabhāvaṃ eti gacchati anenāti vā rukkhaṃ tiropaṭicchannaṃ hutvā eti pavattatīti vā tirīṭanti vuccati. Abhidhāne (abhidhānappadīpikāyaṃ 442 gāthāyaṃ) pana tarīṭanti takāre ikāravirahito pāṭho atthi. Pādapuñjananti pādo pujiyati sodhiyati anenāti pādapuñjanaṃ, tālujo tatiyakkharo.

372. In 'or of a triple-layered robe,' this is stated with reference to a donation in the middle of a double-layered robe. 'Of them' means of all those like the completely blue ones. 'Kañcuka' means a covering. For it is called 'kañcuka' because it is tied and bound to the body. 'Veṭhane' also means a turban. For since it is wrapped around the head by means of it, therefore it is called 'veṭhana.' In 'made of tree bark,' the word 'tree bark' indicates the meaning of 'bark' for 'tirīṭa.' For 'vakkala' (bark) is called 'tirīṭa' because it covers and conceals the limbs and parts of the body when used as clothing, or because it comes into being having concealed and covered a tree. However, in the Abhidhāna (Abhidhānappadīpikā, verse 442) there is a reading 'tarīṭa,' without the 'i' vowel in the letter 'ta.' 'Pādapuñjana' means that by which the foot is honored or cleaned, hence 'pādapuñjana'; the third letter is palatal.

374. Sante patirūpake gāhaketi ettha patirūpako nāma pakkamantassa bhikkhuno sandiṭṭhasambhatto. Iminā patirūpake gāhake asati adatvā saṅghena bhājite subhājitamevāti dasseti. Satta janāti pakkamantaummattakakhittacittavedanaṭṭā cattāro, ukkhittakā tayoti satta janā.

374. In 'when there is a suitable recipient,' a suitable recipient is one who is an acquaintance or intimate friend of a departing monk. This indicates that if a suitable recipient is unavailable, when it is divided by the Saṅgha without having been given, it is indeed well-divided. The seven persons are: the four who are departing, insane, mentally deranged, and afflicted by pain; and the three types of expelled monks.

230. Saṅghe bhinne cīvaruppādakathā

230. Discussion on Robe Production When the Saṅgha is Divided

376. Saṅgho bhijjatīti ettha dvikoṭṭhāsavasena bhijjanamevādhippetaṃ, na aññanti āha “dve koṭṭhāsā”ti. Ekasmiṃ pakkhe cīvarāni dentīti yojanā. Dvipakkhaṃ sandhāya “sakalassa saṅghassā”ti vuttaṃ. Etanti cīvaraṃ. Tasseva cīvaranti tassa koṭṭhāsassa cīvarameva. Yatthāti yasmiṃ dese. Dakkhiṇodakaṃ pamāṇanti dakkhiṇodakameva pamāṇaṃ, na deyyadhammo. Tasmā dakkhiṇodakaṃ paṭiggaṇhantā, deyyadhammassa sāmino hontīti adhippāyo. Ubhohipi pakkhehīti yojanā. Parasamuddeti jambudīpe. So hi sīhaḷadīpato samuddassa pārattā parasamuddoti vuccati. Itaro pakkhoti dakkhiṇodakassa ca cīvarassa ca laddhapakkhato itaro aladdho pakkho.

376. Here, in 'the Saṅgha is divided,' division into two factions is intended, not any other kind, as stated by 'two factions.' The construction is: 'they give robes to one faction.' Referring to both factions, it is said 'of the entire Saṅgha.' 'This' means this robe. 'The robe of that very one' means the robe of that very faction. 'Where' means in whatever place. 'The libation water is the measure' means the libation water itself is the measure, not the donation. Therefore, the meaning is that those who accept the libation water become owners of the donation. The construction is 'by both factions.' 'Parasamudda' means in Jambudīpa. For it is called 'parasamudda' because it is beyond the ocean from the island of Sri Lanka. 'The other faction' means the faction that has not received either the libation water or the robe, as opposed to the faction that has.

232. Aṭṭhacīvaramātikākathā

232. Discussion on the Eight Robe Headings

379. Idāni āhāti sambandho. Puggalādhiṭṭhānanayenāti “sīmāya detī”ti kattuvācakena kiriyāpadena dāyakapuggalasaṅkhātakattuno adhiṭṭhānavasena vuttattā puggalādhiṭṭhānena nayena. Etthāti [M 0.0389] etāsu aṭṭhasu mātikāsu. Aṭṭhamā mātikāti yojanā. Tatthāti aṭṭhasu mātikāsu. Sabbatthāti sabbesu “katikāya detī”tiādīsu.

379. Now, 'he says' is the connection. 'By way of designation based on the individual' means by way of designation based on the individual, because 'he gives within a boundary' is expressed through the active verb, stating it based on the designation of the agent, which is the donor. 'Here' means in these eight headings. The construction is: 'the eighth heading.' 'There' means in the eight headings. 'Everywhere' means in all instances such as 'he gives according to agreement'.

Sīmāya…pe… bhājetabbantiādimhi mātikāniddese pana evaṃ vinicchayo veditabboti yojanā. Sīmāya detīti ettha pannarasa sīmā veditabbāti sambandho.

In the exposition of the headings beginning with 'by the boundary... to be divided,' the decision should be understood thus: this is the construction. Here, in 'he gives by the boundary,' the connection is that fifteen boundaries should be understood.

Tatthāti [V 2.0049] pannarasasu sīmāsu. Upacārasīmā paricchinnā hotīti sambandho. Ettakaṃ ṭhānanti parikkhepārahaṭṭhānassa ekantena avuttattā ekantena parikkhepārahaṭṭhānaṃ dassento āha “apicā”tiādi. Dhuvasannipātato vā khipitānanti sambandho. “Pariyante”ti padaṃ pubbāparāpekkhaṃ. Tasmā tīsu nissakkapadesu yojetabbaṃ. Sā panāti upacārasīmā pana. Bhikkhūsu vaḍḍhantesu āvāsopi vaḍḍhatīti manasikatvā vuttaṃ “bhikkhūsu vaḍḍhantesū”ti. Sabbesaṃ bhikkhūnanti sambandho. Vuttamevāti sīmakathāyaṃ (mahāva. aṭṭha. 138, 144) vuttameva.

'There' means in the fifteen boundaries. The connection is that the proximity boundary is defined. In 'this much space,' since the area to be enclosed is not absolutely specified, to indicate the exact area appropriate to be enclosed, it is said, 'moreover,' etc. Or, 'from the fixed assembly' or 'thrown' is the connection. The word 'at the boundary' considers both before and after. Therefore, it should be connected with the three places free from transgression. 'But that' means that proximity boundary, however. Considering that as the monks increase, the monastery also expands, it is said, 'as the monks increase.' 'Of all the monks' is the connection. 'It has already been stated' means it has already been stated in the discussion on boundaries (Mahāvagga Aṭṭhakathā 138, 144).

Apica khoti ettha apisaddo pucchatthavācako. Kehi ṭhapitāti hi attho. Rājarājamahāmattā ṭhapentīti sambandho. Lābhasīmāti lābhassa mariyādo. Yanti yo lābho. Etthantareti etasmiṃ gāvutādiantare. Lābhasīmā nāmāti lābhena paricchinnā sīmā nāma. Tatthāti bahūsu janapadesu. Antaradīpā cāti mahādīpato aññadīpā ca, khuddakadīpāti adhippāyo.

Here, in 'apica kho,' the word 'api' is used in the sense of asking a question. For the meaning is: 'By whom was it established?' The connection is: 'Kings and royal ministers establish it.' 'Lābhasīmā' means the boundary of gain. 'Which' means whatever gain. 'Within this interval' means within this interval of a league and so on. 'Lābhasīmā' means a boundary defined by gain. 'There' means in many countries. 'And intermediate islands' means other islands apart from the great island, implying small islands.

Ettheva sīmāyāti khaṇḍasīmāya eva. Tesaṃyevāti khaṇḍasīmagatānaṃyeva. Evatthaphalaṃ dassento āha “aññesa”ntiādi. Rukkhe vā pabbate vā ṭhitassa vā heṭṭhā pathavīmajjhagatassa vā bhikkhussāti yojanā. Imissā upacārasīmāya ṭhitassāti sambandho. Samānasaṃvāsasīmāyāti mahāsīmāya. Khaṇḍasīmasīmantarikāsūti khaṇḍasīmāyañca dvinnaṃ sīmānaṃ sīmantarikāyañca. Tattha dvinnaṃ gāmaṭṭhānampi pāpuṇāti. Avippavāsasīmāya dinnaṃ gāmaṭṭhānaṃ na pāpuṇāti “ṭhapetvā gāmañca gāmūpacārañcā”ti vuttattā.

'Here indeed in the boundary' means just in a sectional boundary. 'For them alone' means just for those included within the sectional boundary. Showing the effect of the emphatic particle, he said, 'for others,' etc. The construction is: for a bhikkhu standing on a tree or a mountain, or situated in the middle of the earth below. The connection is: 'for one standing within this proximity boundary.' 'The boundary of common dwelling' means the great boundary. In the sectional boundary and in the intervening space between two boundaries—there, even the site of a village is reached for both. The site of a village given within the non-separation boundary is not reached, because it is said, 'excepting the village and the vicinity of the village'.

Jambuyā [M 0.0390] lakkhito dīpo jambudīpo. Tambo lohito pāṇi hattho etesanti tambapāṇino. Vijayakumārādayo sattasatā janā. Tesaṃ nivāso tambapaṇṇi, soyeva dīpoti tambapaṇṇidīpo, tasmiṃ. Sabbesaṃ bhāganti sambandho. Tatrevāti jambudīpeyeva. Evantiādi nigamanaṃ.

The island marked by the rose-apple tree is Jambudīpa. Those whose hands are red (tambo lohito pāṇi hattho) are the Tambapaṇṇino. Seven hundred people, including Prince Vijaya and others. Their dwelling was Tambapaṇṇi, and that very island is Tambapaṇṇidīpa; in that island. The connection is: 'the share of all'. 'There itself' means in Jambudīpa itself. 'Thus' and so on is the conclusion.

Yo pana bhaṇatīti sambandho. Tatoti kathanato, paranti sambandho. Nanti mahāsivattheraṃ. Tiyojanāpīti pisaddo tato ūnāpi hotīti dasseti. Sabbaṃpetanti sabbaṃpi etaṃ lābhagaṇhanādiṃ. Iti āhaṃsūti yojanā.

The connection is: 'but he who speaks'. 'From that' means from the telling; 'other' is the connection. 'Na' refers to the great Elder Siva. 'Even three yojanas'—the particle 'pi' indicates that it may also be less than that. 'All this too' means all this, including the taking of gains and so on. The construction is: 'Thus they said'.

Katikānaṃ yathicchitakatena pavattattā bahu hoti, tasmā idha icchitakatikaṃ dassetuṃ vuttaṃ “samānalābhakatikāyā”ti[V 2.0050]. Tatrāti “katikāya detī”ti pāṭhe. Sannipatitehi bhikkhūhi bhājetabbanti sambandho. Tassāti vihārassa. Buddhādhivutthoti buddhena adhi issaravasena vasiyitthāti buddhādhivuttho. Ettāvatāti ettakena sāvanamattena. Nisinnovāti nisinno eva hoti, nisinno iva vā. Tasmiṃ vihārepīti tasmiṃ porāṇakādivihārepi. Evamevāti “ayaṃ porāṇako vihāro tena navavihārena saddhiṃ samānalābhaṃ kātuṃ saṅghassa ruccatī”tiādinā evameva. Idhāti porāṇakavihāre. Tasminti navavihāre. Evanti yathā ekena vihārena saddhiṃ eko vihāro kātabbo, evaṃ tathāti attho.

Since agreements are many because they proceed according to what is wished for, therefore here it is said, 'of the agreement for an equal share', to show the wished-for agreement. 'There' means in the reading 'he gives according to agreement'. The connection is: 'it should be distributed by the assembled monks'. 'Of that' means of the dwelling. 'Sanctioned by the Buddha' means dwelt in by the Buddha by his authority as master; thus, 'sanctioned by the Buddha'. 'To this extent' means by this mere announcement. 'Seated' means he is actually seated, or as if seated. 'In that dwelling too' means in that ancient dwelling and so on. 'Just so' means just so, by 'this ancient dwelling is agreeable to the Sangha to make an equal share with the new dwelling', and so on. 'Here' means in the ancient dwelling. 'In that' means in that new dwelling. 'Thus' means just as one dwelling should be made with another dwelling, so in that way; this is the meaning.

Bhikkhāpaññattiyāti ettha bhikkhā paññapiyati niccavasena ṭhapiyati etthāti bhikkhāpaññattīti dassento āha “attano pariccāgapaññāpanaṭṭhāne”ti. Tassāti “yattha saṅghassa dhuvakārā kariyantī”tipāṭhassa. Attho evaṃ veditabboti yojanā. Yattha vāti yasmiṃ vā ṭhāne. Anenāti cīvaradāyakena. Salākabhattādīni vā nibaddhāni kāritānīti sambandho. Yena panāti cīvaradāyakena pana. Sakalopi vihāroti sakalopi saārāmo vihāro. Tatthāti cīvaradāyake. Imeti pākavattassa vattanaṭṭhānādayo vihārā. Dhuvena [M 0.0391] kariyantīti dhuvakārā vihārā. Soti cīvaradāyako. Yatthāti yasmiṃ ṭhāne. Sabbatthāti sabbesu bahūsu vihāresu.

In 'on the establishment of alms', here, indicating that alms are established and permanently fixed in this, hence 'establishment of alms', it is said: 'in a place for demonstrating one's own relinquishment'. 'Of that' means of the reading 'where the Sangha's permanent duties are performed'. The construction is: the meaning should be understood thus. 'Or where' means in whatever place. 'By this' means by the robe-donor. The connection is: 'or salāka meals and the like are regularly provided'. 'But by whom' means but by the robe-donor. 'The entire monastery' means the entire monastery including its park. 'There' means regarding the robe-donor. 'These' are the monasteries that are places for the duties of the cook and so on. 'Permanently performed' means monasteries where permanent duties are carried out. 'He' means the robe-donor. 'Where' means in whatever place. 'Everywhere' means in all the many monasteries.

Tehīti bahutarehi bhikkhūhi. Dhuvakāresūti niddhāraṇe bhummaṃ. Ekatthāti ekasmiṃ dhuvakāre. “Sace bhikkhugaṇanāya gaṇhathāti vadatī”ti iminā sace na vadati, bhikkhugaṇanāya bhājetvā gaṇhituṃ na vaṭṭatīti dasseti, vihāragaṇanāya gaṇhituṃ vaṭṭatīti adhippāyo. Tathāti yathā “bhikkhugaṇanāya gaṇhathā”ti vadati, tathāti attho. Etthāti bhājetabbavatthūsu. Tanti mañcapīṭhakaṃ, pucchitvā dātabbanti sambandho. Pucchitvāti dāyakaṃ pucchitvā, vadatīti dāyako vadati. Saṅghassāpīti pisaddo na dāyakassevāti dasseti.

'By them' means by the majority of monks. 'In the permanent duties' is the locative of specification. 'In one place' means in one permanent duty. By 'if he says, "Take it by counting the number of monks"', it shows that if he does not say so, it is not proper to divide and take by counting the monks. The intention is that it is proper to take by counting the dwellings. 'Thus' means just as he says, 'Take it by counting the number of monks', so it is the meaning. 'Here' means among the things to be divided. 'That' means the bed and bench; the connection is: 'it should be given after asking'. 'After asking' means after asking the donor; 'he speaks' means the donor speaks. 'Even for the Sangha'—the word 'pi' shows it is not only for the donor.

Upacārasīmāyaṃ ṭhitena saṅghena bhājetabbanti sambandho[V 2.0051]. Sīmaṭṭhassāti upacārasīmāyaṃ ṭhitassa. Asampattassāpīti bhājanaṭṭhānaṃ asampattassāpi. Alasajātikāti kosajjajātikā. Ṭhitikāti pabandhavasena ṭhiyate ṭhiti, sāyeva ṭhitikā. Atha vā “ṭhitaṭṭhānato paṭṭhāya dātabba”nti aṭṭhakathāyaṃ (mahāva. aṭṭha. 379) vuttattā tiṭṭhati pabandhavasena etthāti ṭhiti, sāyeva ṭhitikāti vacanattho kātabbo. Ṭhitikaṃ ṭhapetvāti vīsativassasaṅkhātaṃ ṭhitikaṃ ṭhapetvā. Tesanti therānaṃ.

The connection is that it should be distributed by the Sangha standing within the precinct boundary. 'Of one standing within the boundary' means of one standing within the precinct boundary. 'Even of one who has not arrived' means even of one who has not arrived at the place of distribution. 'Of a lazy nature' means of a lazy disposition. 'Duration' means a persistence that is maintained continuously; that very persistence is called 'duration'. Alternatively, as it is stated in the commentary, 'It should be given starting from the place where one stands,' the meaning to be understood is that 'duration' is that which persists continuously in this way, and that very persistence is called 'duration'. 'Setting aside the duration' means setting aside the duration reckoned as twenty years. 'Of them' refers to the elders.

Sampattasampattānanti bhājanaṭṭhānaṃ sampattasampattānaṃ. Attano vihāradvāre vā attano antovihāreyeva vāti yojanā. Sīmāti upacārasīmā. Therāsanaṃ ārūḷhe satīti yojanā. Vassaggenāti vassagaṇanāya.

'Of those who have arrived and are suitable' means of those who have arrived at the place of distribution and are suitable. The construction is: 'either at the door of one's own monastery or within one's own monastery itself'. 'Boundary' refers to the precinct boundary. The construction is: 'when he has ascended the elder's seat'. 'By seniority in rains' means by the reckoning of years.

Pāṭekkanti paccekaṃ. Sabbāneva cīvarānīti sambandho. Dubbhāsitaduggahitānamatthaṃ dassento āha “gatagataṭṭhāne saṅghikāneva hontī”ti. Ekanti dasasu vatthesu ekaṃ.

'Separately' means individually. The connection is 'all the robes'. Explaining the meaning of what was badly spoken and wrongly grasped, he says: 'In each and every place, they are indeed for the Sangha'. 'One' means one out of the ten cloths.

Vatthasseva pupphaṃ vā vali vā atthīti yojanā. Tenāti pupphavalinā. Ekaṃ tantanti ekaṃ suttaṃ. Tatthāti tesu ṭhitikāya ṭhānāṭṭhānesu. Dvīhipi gahetabbaṃ ṭhitikāya abhāvato.

The construction is: 'A cloth has a flower or a wrinkle'. 'By that' means by that flower or wrinkle. 'One thread' means one yarn. 'Therein' means among those places, suitable and unsuitable, for the duration. It should be taken even by two, due to the absence of a fixed duration.

Bhikkhu [M 0.0392] attano santakaṃ yaṃ cīvaranti yojanā. Paṃsukūlikānampi vaṭṭatīti “saṅghassa demā”ti vā “tuyhaṃ demā”ti vā avatvā “bhikkhūnaṃ dema, therānaṃ demā”ti vuttattā paṃsukūlikānampi vaṭṭati. Bhikkhutherā nāma hi na attanāyeva honti, aññepi bahū, tasmā vaṭṭati. “Saṅghassā”ti vutte attanā ekantena saṅghoyeva, tasmā “saṅghassā”ti vuttepi na vaṭṭati, pageva “tuyha”nti vutte.

The construction is: 'whatever robe is one's own possession, a monk...'. It is valid even for rag-robe wearers because, without saying 'We give to the Sangha' or 'We give to you,' it is said 'We give to the monks, we give to the elders,' thus it is valid even for rag-robe wearers. For the terms 'monks' and 'elders' do not refer solely to oneself, but there are many others; therefore, it is valid. If 'to the Sangha' is said, it refers exclusively to the Sangha itself; therefore, even if 'to the Sangha' is said, it is not valid, much less if 'to you' is said.

Tatoti bahuvatthato. Gahetuṃ na vaṭṭatīti paṃsukūlikānaṃ gahetuṃ na vaṭṭati.

'From that' means from the many cloths. 'It is not proper to take' means it is not proper for the rag-robe wearers to take.

Yanti vatthaṃ. Tatthāti parikkhāresu. Suttanti tantaṃ.

'That which' refers to cloth. 'Therein' means among the requisites. 'Thread' means yarn.

Evaṃ antosīmaṃ pavisitvā “saṅghassa demā”ti dinne vinicchayaṃ dassetvā bahisīmāya dinne taṃ dassento āha “sace panā”tiādi. Ekabaddhā cāti dvādasahatthamanatikkamitvā ekatobaddhā ca. Ye panāti bhikkhū pana.

Having thus shown the decision when something is given by entering within the boundary, saying 'We give to the Sangha,' he then shows it when given outside the boundary, saying, 'But if,' and so on. 'And bound together' means bound together at one point, not exceeding twelve cubits. 'But those' refers to the monks.

Ubhatosaṅghassa detīti ettha catunnaṃ vākyānaṃ vasena vuttepi ubhatosaṅghassa detiyeva nāmāti dassento āha “ubhatosaṅghassa dammīti vuttepī”tiādi. Ubhatosaṅghaggahaṇena gahitattāti puggalassa ubhatosaṅghaggahaṇena gahitattā. “Eseva nayo”ti iminā ekavīsatipaṭivīse katvā eko cetiyassa dātabboti nayaṃ atidisati. Pāpuṇanakoṭṭhāso nāma natthi cetiyassa ubhatosaṅghaggahaṇena agahitattā.

To show that even when stated in terms of four phrases, it is indeed called 'given to both Sanghas,' he says, 'Even if it is said, "I give to both Sanghas,"' and so on. 'Because it is taken by the inclusion of both Sanghas' means because the individual is taken by the inclusion of both Sanghas. By 'This is the method', he extends the method that, after making twenty-one portions, one portion should be given to the cetiya. There is no portion that reaches the cetiya, because it is not included by the term 'both Sanghas'.

Tatthāti [V 2.0052] ubhatosaṅghapuggalacetiyesu. Sesaṃ suviññeyyameva.

'Therein' refers to both Sanghas, individuals, and cetiyas. The rest is easily understood.

Pubbeti buddhassa bhagavato dharamānakāle. Tadāti yadā buddho bhagavā dharati, tadā. Paṭimaṃ vāti paṭibimbaṃ vā. Tañhi bhagavatā paṭi sadisaṃ mānīyatīti paṭimāti vuccati. Cetiyaṃ vāti thūpaṃ vā. So hi devamanussehi cititabbaṃ, pūjetabbaṃ, iṭṭhakādīhi vā cinitabbanti cetiyanti vuccati. Tatthāti deyyadhammesu. Yanti kiriyāparāmasanaṃ. Yaṃ [M 0.0393] dentīti yojanā. Tatthāti tasmiṃ dāne. Aniyamavācakassa “yo”ti sabbanāmassa atthaṃ dassento āha “pabbajito vā gahaṭṭho vā”ti. Vattaṃ katvā paribhuñjitunti pubbakālaaparakālakiriyānaṃ vikāravasena aniyatattā vuttaṃ “bhuñjitvā pacchāpi vattaṃ kātu”nti.

'Formerly' means during the time when the Blessed Buddha was still living. 'Then' means when the Blessed Buddha was living, at that time. 'Or an image' means or a reflection. For that is considered similar to the Blessed One; hence, it is called an image. 'Or a cetiya' means or a stupa. For that is to be revered and honored by devas and humans, or built with bricks and so on; hence, it is called a cetiya. 'Therein' means among the things to be given. 'That which' is a reference to action. The construction is 'that which they give'. 'Therein' means in that act of giving. Explaining the meaning of the indefinite pronoun 'whoever', he says: 'whether a monastic or a layperson'. Regarding 'having performed the obligation, they may use it', because the sequence of prior and subsequent actions is uncertain due to variation, it is said, 'having used it, they may later perform the obligation'.

“Dūrampi haritvā pūjetabba”nti iminā jaṅghapesanikakammaṃ na hotīti dasseti. Harantassa bhikkhunoti sambandho. Gacchatoti anādare sāmivacanaṃ. Tanti saṅghassa āhaṭabhattaṃ.

By 'Dūrampi haritvā pūjetabbaṃ' (even if carried far, it should be honored), he shows that it does not become an act of sending by foot. The connection is 'of the monk who carries it'. 'Gacchato' (of one going) is a genitive case used in a sense of disregard. 'Taṃ' (that) refers to food brought for the Sangha.

Vassaṃvutthasaṅghassāti vassaṃ vasitthāti vassaṃvuttho. Aluttakitantasamāsoyaṃ, soyeva saṅgho vassaṃvutthasaṅgho, tassa. Yāvatikasaddo yattakapariyāyoti āha “yattakā”ti. Disāpakkantassāpīti aññaṃ disaṃ pakkantassapi, dātabbanti sambandho. Vadantīti aṭṭhakathācariyehi apare ācariyā vadanti. Etanti vacanaṃ.

'Vassaṃvutthasaṅghassa' (of the Sangha that has completed the rains residence) means 'vassaṃvuttho' (one who has completed the rains residence) is one who has dwelt during the rains. This is a compound where the case-ending is not elided. That very Sangha is the Sangha that has completed the rains residence; for that Sangha. He says that the word 'yāvatika' (as much as) is a synonym for 'yattaka' (however much). 'Disāpakkantassāpi' (even of one who has departed to another region) means even of one who has departed to another region; the connection is 'it should be given'. 'Vadanti' (they say) means other teachers, apart from the commentary teachers, say so. 'Etaṃ' (this) refers to the statement.

Sampattānanti dinnaṭṭhānaṃ sampattānaṃ. Sabbesanti yattha katthaci vutthavassānaṃ sabbesaṃ. Tatrāti vihāre. Tatrāti tasmiṃ vadane sati, tesu bhikkhūsu vā. Vassaṃ vasantīti vassaṃvasantā, tesaṃ. Cīvaramāseti cīvarena lakkhite pacchimakattikamāse.

'Sampattānaṃ' (of those who have arrived) means of those who have arrived at the place where it is given. 'Sabbesaṃ' (of all) means of all those who have completed the rains residence wherever they may have stayed. 'Tatra' (therein) means in the monastery. 'Tatra' (therein) means when that statement is made, or concerning those monks. 'Vassaṃ vasanti' (they dwell during the rains) refers to those dwelling during the rains; for them. 'Cīvaramāse' (in the month of robes) means in the last month of Kattika, designated by robes.

Hemantassa pacchimo divasoti phagguṇapuṇṇamīsaṅkhāto hemantassa pacchimo divaso. Vassāvāsikanti vassaṃ āvasantānaṃ dātabbaṃ cīvaraṃ. Āropetabbākāraṃ dassento āha “atītavassāvāsassā”tiādi. Tattha atītavassāvāsassāti atītavassaṃ, atītavasse vā āvāsassa saṅghassa. Tanti cīvaraṃ.

'Hemantassa pacchimo divaso' (the last day of winter) means the last day of winter, reckoned as the full moon day of Phagguna. 'Vassāvāsikaṃ' (the rains-residence robe) means the robe to be given to those who dwell during the rains. Showing the manner of its application, he says, 'of one who has completed the rains residence,' and so on. Here, 'atītavassāvāsassa' (of one who has completed the rains residence) means of the Sangha of the past rains, or of the Sangha of the residence in the past rains. 'Taṃ' (that) refers to the robe.

Ṭhapetvāti vihāre ṭhapetvā. Sampattānanti imaṃ ṭhānaṃ sampattānaṃ. Itoti cīvaradānakālato. Teti antovasse vutthabhikkhū.

'Ṭhapetvā' (having placed) means having placed it in the monastery. 'Sampattānaṃ' (of those who have arrived) means of those who have arrived at this place. 'Ito' (from this) means from the time of the robe-giving. 'Te' (those) refers to the monks who dwelt during the rains residence.

Ādissāti [V 2.0053] padassa tvāpaccayantabhāvaṃ dassento āha “ādisitvā”ti. Ayamattho veditabboti yojanā. Tatrāti “yāguyā vā”tiādipāṭhe. Ajjatanāya vāti ajja bhavānaṃ puññānaṃ atthāya [M 0.0394] vā. Tesanti nimantakānaṃ, paviṭṭhānaṃ bhikkhūnanti sambandho. Yehi nimantitehīti nimantitehi yehi bhikkhūhi. Yesaṃ vā pattanti sambandho. Tesaṃ na pāpuṇātīti sabbesaṃ tesaṃ na pāpuṇāti, kasmā? Animantitattā. Tesaṃ na pāpuṇanti, kasmā? Nimantitagehaṃ apaviṭṭhattā. Soti dāyako.

To show that the word 'ādissa' is an absolutive ending in the equivalent of the '-tvā' suffix, he says 'ādisitvā'. The construction is: 'This meaning should be understood'. 'Tatra' (therein) refers to the passage beginning with 'yāguyā vā' (or with gruel). 'Ajjatanāya vā' (or for today) means or for the sake of your merits today. 'Tesaṃ' (of them) refers to the inviters; the connection is 'of the monks who have entered'. 'Yehi nimantitehi' (by whom they were invited) means by which invited monks. The connection is 'or to whom it reaches'. 'Tesaṃ na pāpuṇāti' (it does not reach them) means it does not reach all of them. Why? Because they were not invited. It does not reach them. Why? Because they have not entered the house of those who invited them. 'So' (he) refers to the donor.

Pubbepīti ito pubbepi. Assāti dāyakassa. Vāsetvāti vāsāpetvā. Soti dāyako. Yoti bhikkhu, vasatīti sambandho. Tānīti bhesajjāni. Idanti cīvaraṃ.

'Pubbepi' (even before) means even before this. 'Assa' (of him) refers to the donor. 'Vāsetvā' (having caused to dwell) means having caused to reside. 'So' (he) refers to the donor. 'Yo' (whoever) refers to the monk; the connection is 'dwells'. 'Tāni' (those) refers to the medicines. 'Idaṃ' (this) refers to the robe.

“Antevāsikānañcā”ti padena saddhivihārikāpi gahetabbā uddesādivasena ante vasanasīlattā. Uddesaṃ gahetuṃ āgato ca gahetvā gacchanto cāti ime ante avasanasīlāpi rūḷhīvasena antevāsikā nāma. Iminā nissayaṃ gahetuṃ āgato ca therassa santike nissayaṃ gahitapubbo ca antevāsiko nāmāti dasseti. Vattaṃ katvā uddesaparipucchādīni gahetvā vicarantānaṃ sabbesaṃ uddesantevāsikānaṃ pāpuṇātīti yojanā. Iminā saddhivihārikanissayantevāsikaupasampadantevāsikapabbajjantevāsikāpi gahetabbā tesampi nibaddhacārikabhikkhubhāvato. Sabbatthāti sabbasmiṃ cīvarakkhandhake.

By the term 'Antevāsikānañca' (and of the pupils), co-residents (saddhivihārikā) should also be included, as they are accustomed to dwelling near (the teacher) by way of instruction, etc. Those who come to receive instruction and those who leave after receiving it—these, though not habitually dwelling near, are conventionally called 'pupils' (antevāsikā). By this, he shows that one who comes to take dependence (nissaya) and one who has previously taken dependence near a Thera is called a 'pupil'. The construction is that it reaches all pupils for instruction who wander about, having performed their duties and having received instruction, questioning, and so on. By this, co-residents (saddhivihārikā), those under dependence (nissayantevāsikā), those under full ordination (upasampadantevāsikā), and those under novice ordination (pabbajjantevāsikā) should also be included, because they too are monks who have a regular round. 'Sabbattha' (everywhere) means throughout the entire chapter on robes (cīvarakkhandhaka).

Iti cīvarakkhandhakavaṇṇanāya yojanā samattā.

Thus the explanation of the commentary on the Robes Chapter is concluded.

9. Campeyyakkhandhakaṃ

9. The Chapter on Campā

234. Kassapagottabhikkhuvatthukathā

234. The Story of the Monk Kassapagotta

380. Campeyyakkhandhake gaggarāya pokkharaṇiyāti ettha gaggarasaddassa nāmasaddabhāvaṃ dassento āha “gaggaranāmikāya itthiyā”ti. Iminā gaggarasaddo gaggaraiti nāmaṃ pavattinimittaṃ katvā itthidabbaṃ vadatīti dasseti. Tantipaṭibaddhoti tantiyā paṭibaddho. “Ussukkampi [V 2.0054] akāsi yāguyā”tiādīsu evaṃ vinicchayo veditabboti yojanā[M 0.0395]. Tassa bhikkhunoti kassapagottanāmakassa tassa bhikkhuno. Tatthevāti vāsabhagāmeyeva.

380. In the Campeyya chapter, regarding the phrase 'Gaggarāya pokkharaṇiyā,' to show that the word 'gaggarā' is a noun, he says: 'of the woman named Gaggarā.' By this, it is shown that the word 'gaggarā', taking the name 'Gaggarā' as the reason for its application, refers to a woman. 'Tantipaṭibaddho' means bound by threads. The interpretation should be understood accordingly in phrases like 'Ussukkampi akāsi yāguyā.' 'Tassa bhikkhuno' refers to that monk named Kassapagotta. 'Tattheva' means in that same Vāsabhagāma.

382. Adhammena vaggakammaṃ karontītiādīnaṃ nānākaraṇanti sambandho.

382. 'Adhammena vaggakammaṃ karontīti' and similar expressions are connected by their differing applications.

236. Ñattivipannakammādikathā

236. Discussion on Defective Formal Acts and Similar Matters

385. Aññatrāpi dhammāti ettha dhammāti upayogatthe nissakkavacanametanti āha “aññatra dhamma”nti. “Aññatrā”ti nipātapayoge dutiyātatiyāpañcamīsu aññatarassa sambhavato upayogavacanampi hoti. Tasmā vuttaṃ “ayameva vā pāṭho”ti. “Bhūtena vatthunā”ti iminā dhammasaddassa saccatthaṃ dasseti. “Eseva nayo”ti iminā saddasabhāvameva sandhāya atidisati, na atthaṃ. Tena vuttaṃ “ettha panā”tiādi. Satthusāsananti satthu āṇā. Satthuāṇā nāma ñattianusāvanānaṃ sampadāti āha “ñattisampadā anusāvanasampadā cā”ti. “Paṭikuṭṭhañceva katañcā”ti iminā paṭikuṭṭhakatanti padassa dvandavākyaṃ dasseti. Paṭikusitabbanti paṭikuṭṭhaṃ, kattabbanti kataṃ, kammaṃ. Tamevatthaṃ dassento āha “yaṃ aññesū”tiādi. Tattha yanti kammaṃ.

385. Regarding 'Aññatrāpi dhammā,' here 'dhammā' is a word in the ablative case expressing usage, hence it is explained as 'aññatra dhamma.' Since in the use of the particle 'aññatra,' one of the second, third, or fifth case endings is possible, it is also a word expressing usage. Therefore, it is said: 'this could also be the reading.' The phrase 'Bhūtena vatthunā' shows that the meaning of the word 'dhamma' is truth. 'Eseva nayo' here refers merely to the nature of the word, and extends it by similarity, not to the meaning. Hence, it is said: 'here, however,' etc. 'Satthusāsana' means the Teacher’s command. The Teacher’s command refers to the accomplishment of the ñatti and anusāvana, as stated: 'accomplishment of ñatti and accomplishment of anusāvana.' 'Paṭikuṭṭhañceva katañcā' here indicates that the term 'paṭikuṭṭhakata' is a dvandva phrase. ‘Paṭikuṭṭhaṃ’ means that which is to be censured; ‘kataṃ’ means that which is to be done; this refers to the formal act. To explain this meaning, it is said: 'which in others,' etc. Here, 'yaṃ' refers to the formal act.

387. Pāḷiyāti vinayapāḷiyā. Yanti kammaṃ, na kariyatīti sambandho. Etthāti aṭṭhakathāyaṃ. So ca khoti so ca vitthāro, āgatoti sambandho. Kasmā ñattidutiyañatticatutthakammānameva vasena āgato, nanu ñattiapalokanakammavasenapi āgatena bhavitabbanti āha “yasmā panā”tiādi. Ñattidutiyañatticatutthesu hāpanaṃ vā aññathā karaṇaṃ vā atthi viya ñattikamme natthīti yojanā. Ñattikamme ñattiṭṭhapanato aññakiccassa asambhavato hāpanaṃ vā aññathā karaṇaṃ vā natthīti adhippāyo. Tānīti ñattikammaapalokanakammāni. Sabbesampi kammānanti sabbesampi catunnaṃ kammānaṃ. Paratoti parasmiṃ parivārāvasāne (pari. aṭṭha. 482).

387. 'Pāḷiyā' means in the Vinaya Pāḷi. The connection is 'yaṃ kammaṃ na kariyati' (which formal act is not done). 'Ettha' means in the commentary. 'So ca kho' means that detailed explanation has come; this is the connection. Why has it come only in terms of formal acts by motion with one announcement and formal acts by motion with three announcements? Shouldn’t it have come in terms of formal acts by motion only and formal acts by inquiry as well? Hence, he says, 'Yasmā pana,' etc. The explanation is that in formal acts by motion with one announcement and formal acts by motion with three announcements, there is the possibility of reduction or alteration, but not so in a formal act by motion only. The meaning is that in a formal act by motion only, because no other function is possible after the motion is established, there is no reduction or alteration. 'Tāni' refers to the formal act by motion only and the formal act by inquiry. 'Sabbesampi kammānaṃ' means of all four kinds of formal acts. 'Parato' means in a later section, at the end of the Parivāra commentary.

237. Catuvaggakaraṇādikathā

237. Discussion on the Formation of a Four-Member Group and Similar Matters

388. Yadidaṃ [M 0.0396] kammanti yojanā. Tesanti saṅghānaṃ. Kammappattoti ettha kammena, kammassa vā pattoti atthaṃ paṭikkhipanto āha “kammaṃ patto”ti. “Sabbakammesu kammapatto”ti [V 2.0055] pāḷinayena “kammesu patto”ti atthopi yujjati. Lokavohāravasena “kammena kammassa vā patto”ti atthopi yujjateva.

388. The explanation is 'yadidaṃ kammaṃ' (that which is the formal act). 'Tesaṃ' means of the Sanghas. 'Kammappatto' here, rejecting the meaning of either 'attained by the formal act' or 'attained for the formal act,' he says 'attained the formal act.' According to the Pāli textual method, 'attained in all formal acts,' the meaning 'attained in formal acts' is also fitting. According to worldly usage, the meaning 'attained by the formal act or for the formal act' is also valid.

389. Parisatoti parisakāraṇā. Tatthāti “catuvaggakaraṇañce bhikkhave”tiādipāṭhe, catuvīsatipuggalesu vā. Kammanānāsaṃvāsakoti ukkhepanīyakammakato. Laddhinānāsaṃvāsakoti ukkhittānuvattako. “Hutvā”ti iminā “bhikkhunīcatuttho”tiādīsu catuvīsatiyā ṭhānesu kiriyāvisesanabhāvaṃ dasseti. Bhikkhunī catutthī etassāti bhikkhunīcatuttho, catuvaggo saṅghotiādinā vacanattho kātabbo.

389. 'Parisato' means because of the reason for the assembly. 'Tattha' refers to the passage beginning 'if, monks, concerning the formation of a fourfold group,' or among the twenty-four individuals. 'Kammanānāsaṃvāsako' means one who has been subjected to a formal act of suspension. 'Laddhinānāsaṃvāsako' means a follower of one who has been suspended. 'Hutvā' indicates its adverbial nature in the twenty-four instances such as 'with a nun as the fourth.' 'Bhikkhunī catutthī etassāti bhikkhunīcatuttho' means 'one who has a nun as the fourth,' and the meaning should be construed from the phrase 'the fourfold group is the Sangha,' etc.

393. Parivāsādītiādisaddena mūlāyakassanamānattaabbhānāni saṅgaṇhāti. Tesanti parivāsādikammānaṃ. Paratoti parasmiṃ cūḷavagge (cūḷava. aṭṭha. 75 ādayo).

393. By the word "etcetera" in "probation, etcetera," are included return to the beginning, penance, and rehabilitation. "Tesaṃ" refers to those acts beginning with probation. "Parato" means further on, in the Cūḷavagga (Cūḷavagga commentary, 75 and following).

394. Paṭikuṭṭhakatakammassāti paṭikuṭṭhassa hutvā katassa kammassa. Pakatattassāti ettha pakatisīlasaṅkhāto attā sabhāvo etassāti pakatattoti atthaṃ dassento āha “avipannasīlassā”ti. Saṅghādisesaṃ anāpajjantassāpi avipannasīlattā vuttaṃ “pārājikaṃ anajjhāpannassā”ti. Iminā saṅghādisesaṃ āpajjantopi pakatattoyevāti dasseti. Sopi hi idha avipannasīlo nāma, aññattha pana saṅghādisesassa sīlavipattibhāvato taṃ āpajjantopi vipannasīloyeva nāma. Ānantarikassāti ettha anantarasaddassa sambandhañca ṇikapaccayassa atthañca dassento āha “attano anantaraṃ nisinnassā”ti. Tattha “attano”ti iminā anantarasaddassa sambandhaṃ dasseti. “Nisinnassā”ti iminā ṇikapaccayassa atthaṃ dasseti.

394. "Paṭikuṭṭhakatakammassa" means of an action done after having become blameworthy. Regarding "pakatattassa," here, showing the meaning 'one whose nature is characterized by normal virtue,' he says 'of one whose virtue is unimpaired.' Although one who does not incur a Saṅghādisesa offense is of unimpaired virtue, it is stated 'of one who has not incurred a pārājika.' By this he shows that even one who incurs a Saṅghādisesa offense is still of normal state. For that person here is called "one whose virtue is unimpaired," but elsewhere, because incurring a Saṅghādisesa is a breach of virtue, one who incurs it is called "one whose virtue is impaired." Regarding "ānantarikassa," here, showing the connection of the term "anantara" and the meaning of the suffix "ṇika," he says, "of one who is seated immediately after oneself." Therein, by "attano," he shows the connection of the term "anantara," and by "nisinnassa" he indicates the meaning of the suffix "ṇika."

239. Dvenissāraṇādikathā

239. The Account of the Two Kinds of Expulsion, and so forth.

395. Vatthutoti [M 0.0397] vatthukāraṇā. Tatthāti “dvemā bhikkhave”tiādipāṭhe. “Sandhāya vutta”nti iminā “appatto”tiādisuttassa neyyatthabhāvaṃ dasseti. Hīti saccaṃ, yasmā vā. Tanti pabbājanīyakammaṃ. Puna tanti pabbājanīyakammameva. Esa bhikkhu appattoti sambandho. Kasmā appattoti āha “yasmā”tiādi. Āveṇikalakkhaṇenāti avinā hutvā pavattena lakkhaṇena. Attanā avinā hutvā attano santakena visuṃ bhūtena lakkhaṇenāti vuttaṃ hoti. Yadi appatto, kasmā sunissāritoti āha “yasmā panassā”tiādi. Assāti bhikkhussa, kareyyāti sambandho. Taṃ ce saṅgho tajjanīyakammādivasena nissāreti, sunissāritoti sambandho[V 2.0056]. Soti bhikkhu. Yasmā anuññātā, tasmā sunissāritoti yojanā. Kittakena aṅgena anuññātāti āha “ekenapi aṅgenā”ti.

395. "Vatthuto" means from the basis or reason. "Tattha" refers to the passage beginning with "These two, monks." By "spoken in reference to," it indicates that the sutta beginning with "appatto" is of indirect meaning (neyyattha). "Hi" means "indeed" or "because." "Taṃ" refers to the act of banishment (pabbājanīyakamma). "Puna taṃ" refers to the act of banishment itself. The connection is "This monk is not attained." To "Why not attained?" it is explained by "because," and so forth. "Āveṇikalakkhaṇena" means "by an exclusive characteristic," or "by a characteristic that is inseparable." It is said that it is a distinct characteristic that is inseparable from oneself, belonging to oneself. To "If he is not attained, why is he well-expelled?" it is explained by "But because for him," and so forth. "Assa" refers to the monk; the connection is with "kareyya." If the Sangha expels him by means of an act of censure (tajjanīyakamma) and so forth, the connection is that he is "well-expelled." "So" refers to the monk. The construction is: because it is permitted, therefore he is "well-expelled." To "By how many factors is it permitted?" it is explained by "even by one factor."

396. Osāraṇāti ettha otyūpasaggavasena saradhātu pavesanatthoti āha “pavesanā”ti. Tatthāti “osāraṇā”tiādipāṭhe. Osāretīti ettha abbhānādivasena pavesanaṃ paṭikkhipanto āha “upasampadakammavasenā”ti. Sahassakkhattumpīti pisaddo garahattho. Ekavārādike pana kā nāma kathāti dasseti. Sātisārāti sadosā. Tathāti yathā ācariyupajjhāyā sātisārā, tathā. Seso kārakasaṅgho sātisāroti sambandho. “Hatthacchinnādayo pana dvattiṃsa suosāritā”ti vuttattā andhamūgabadhirānaṃ apabbajitānampi upasampadā ruhatīti daṭṭhabbaṃ. Teti hatthacchinnādayo dvattiṃsa.

396. Regarding "osāraṇā," here, because the root "sar" with the prefix "o" has the meaning of entering, it says "pavesanā" (entry). "Tattha" refers to the passage beginning with "osāraṇā." Regarding "osāreti," here, rejecting entry by way of rehabilitation and so forth, it says "by way of the act of higher ordination (upasampadakamma)." Regarding "sahassakkhattumpi," the particle "pi" has the sense of censure. It shows that there is no need to speak of one time or more. "Sātisārā" means "with fault." "Tathā" means "just as the teachers and preceptors are with fault, so too." The connection is that the rest of the Sangha that performs the act is with fault. Since it is said, "But the thirty-two, such as those with severed hands, are well reinstated," it should be understood that the higher ordination of the blind, mute, and deaf, even of those who have not gone forth, is valid. "Te" refers to those thirty-two, such as those with severed hands.

397. Abhūtavatthuvasenāti asaccavatthuvasena, asaṃvijjamānavatthuvasena vā. Tatthāti “idha pana bhikkhave”tiādipāṭhe. Paṭinissajjitāti ettha tapaccayassa kammatthe pavattabhāvaṃ dassento āha “paṭinissajjitabbā”ti.

397. "Abhūtavatthuvasena" means by way of an untrue basis, or by way of a non-existent basis. "Tattha" refers to the passage beginning with "But here, monks." Regarding "paṭinissajjitā," here, showing that the suffix -ta occurs in the passive sense, it says, "paṭinissajjitabbā."

241. Upālipucchākathā

241. The Account of Upāli's Questions.

400. Tatthāti [M 0.0398] upālipañhesu. Tassapāpiyasikādīhi saddhiṃ ekā pucchā katāti yojanā. Bhikkhūnampi vāreti sambandho. Pisaddena “na kevalaṃ upālipañhesuyeva yojetabbāni, atha kho bhikkhūnaṃ vārepī”ti dasseti.

400. "Tattha" refers to Upāli's questions. The construction is that one question was asked together with the tassapāpiyasikā procedure and so forth. The connection is also with "bhikkhūnaṃ vāre." By the particle "pi," it indicates: "not only are they to be connected with Upāli's questions, but also with the turn of the monks."

242. Tajjanīyakammakathā

242. The Account of the Act of Censure.

407. “Idha pana bhikkhave bhikkhu bhaṇḍanakārako”tiādi vuttanti sambandho. Tatthāti “idha pana bhikkhave”tiādipāṭhe. Anapadānoti ettha apapubbo dāsaddo avakhaṇḍanatthoti āha “apadānaṃ vuccati paricchedo”ti. Natthi apadānaṃ avakhaṇḍanaṃ āpattipariyanto etassāti anapadānoti vacanattho kātabbo. Sāyeva pāḷi vuttāti sambandho. Tatthāti tassaṃ pāḷiyaṃ. Kiñci atthavinicchayaṃ pāḷianusārena vidituṃ na sakkā na hotīti yojanā.

407. The connection is with what is said, "Here, monks, a monk is quarrelsome," and so forth. "Tattha" refers to the passage beginning with "Here, monks." Regarding "anapadāno," here, he says that the word "dā" with the prefix "apa" has the meaning of cutting off; thus, "apadāna" is called a boundary. The meaning of the word "anapadāno" should be understood as: "one for whom there is no boundary, no cutting off, no limit to the offenses." The connection is that that same Pāli passage is stated. "Tattha" refers to that Pāli passage. The interpretation is that it is not possible to discern any determination of the meaning according to the Pāli itself.

Iti campeyyakkhandhakavaṇṇanāya yojanā samattā.

Thus ends the explanation of the commentary on the Campeyya Chapter.

10. Kosambakakkhandhakaṃ

10. The Kosambī Chapter.

271. Kosambakavivādakathā

271. The Account of the Kosambī Dispute.

451. Kosambakakkhandhake [V 2.0057] ayamanupubbikathā evaṃ veditabbāti yojanā. Vinayaṃ pāḷito ca, tadatthato ca dhāretīti vinayadharo, tathā suttantaṃ dhāretīti suttantiko. Tesūti dvīsu bhikkhūsu. Suttantiko bhikkhu nikkhamīti sambandho. Ācamanaudakāvasesanti ācameti dhovati anenāti ācamanaṃ, tameva udakaṃ ācamanaudakaṃ, tameva avasesaṃ ācamanaudakāvasesaṃ, avasesaācamanaudakanti attho. Taṃ bhikkhunti suttantikaṃ bhikkhuṃ. Etthāti ācamanaudakāvasesaṭṭhapane. “Sace hoti, desessāmī”ti iminā attano subbacabhāvañca sikkhākāmatañca dasseti. Teti tayā, kathanti sambandho. Atha vā teti tuyhaṃ, natthīti sambandho. Asañcicca asatiyā katattā anāpattipakkhopi [M 0.0399] bhaveyyāti āha “natthi āpattī”ti. Ettha pana āpattiyeva. Soti suttantiko.

451. The construction is: in the Kosambaka Chapter, this sequential account should be understood thus. One who retains the Vinaya, both in its text and in its meaning, is a Vinayadhara; likewise, one who retains the Suttanta is a Suttantika. "Tesu" refers to the two monks. The connection is that the Suttantika monk departed. "Ācamanaudakāvasesaṃ": "ācamana" is that by which one rinses or washes, thus "ācamanaudaka" is that rinsing water, and the remainder of it is "ācamanaudakāvasesaṃ," meaning the leftover rinsing water. "Taṃ bhikkhuṃ" refers to that Suttantika monk. "Ettha" refers to the placing of the leftover rinsing water. By "If there is, I will point it out," he shows his own quality of being easy to correct and his desire for training. "Te" means "by you"; the connection is with "kathaṃ." Or, "te" means "for you"; the connection is with "natthi." He says, "There is no offense," implying that because it was done unintentionally and without mindfulness, it might be a case of no offense. But here, there is indeed an offense. "So" refers to the Suttantika.

Vinayadharopīti vinayadharo pana, ārocesīti sambandho. Āpajjamānopīti pisaddo garahattho. Teti vinayadharassa nissitakā, āhaṃsūti sambandho. Tassāti suttantikassa. Teti suttantikassa nissitakā, ārocesunti sambandho. Soti suttantiko. Musāvādīti abhūtato, abhūtaṃ vā vacanaṃ vadanasīlo. Esoti vinayadharo. Teti suttantikassa nissitakā, āhaṃsūti sambandho. Tatoti kalahavaḍḍhanakāraṇā. Vinayadharo akāsīti sambandho.

"Vinayadharopi" means "the Vinayadhara, however"; the connection is with "ārocesi." Regarding "āpajjamānopi," the particle "pi" is in the sense of censure. "Te" refers to those dependent on the Vinayadhara; the connection is with "āhaṃsu." "Tassa" refers to the Suttantika. "Te" refers to those dependent on the Suttantika; the connection is with "ārocesum." "So" refers to the Suttantika. "Musāvādī" means one accustomed to speaking what is untrue, or from what is untrue. "Eso" refers to the Vinayadhara. "Te" refers to those dependent on the Suttantika; the connection is with "āhaṃsu." "Tato" means from the cause of increasing the quarrel. The connection is that the Vinayadhara did it.

453. “Na tāva bhinno”ti iminā bhinnoti ettha tapaccayassa avassambhāviyatthe anāgatakālikataṃ dasseti. Tamevatthaṃ saha upamāya dassento āha “apicā”tiādi. Tanti sassaṃ. “Bhijjissatī”ti iminā bhijjissatīti bhinnoti vacanatthaṃ dasseti. So ca khoti saṅgho. Kalahavasena bhijjissatīti sambandho. Sambhamaatthavasenāti saṃvegaatthavasena. Sambhamasaddo hi tīsu atthesu vattati gārave, bhītiyaṃ, saṃvege cāti. Idha pana saṃvege vattati. Bhikkhusaṅghassa bhinne saṃvegaatthavasenāti adhippāyo. Idaṃ heṭṭhā kathitāya “bhaye kodhe pasaṃsāya”nti gāthāya (pārā. aṭṭha. 1.15) casaddena sampiṇḍitaṃ sambhamaatthaṃ sandhāya vuttanti [V 2.0058] daṭṭhabbaṃ. Etthāti “bhinno bhikkhusaṅgho bhinno bhikkhusaṅgho”ti pāṭhe. Āmeḍitanti ā punappunaṃ bhayādipīḷitattā meḍena ummādena itaṃ kathitaṃ āmeḍitaṃ.

453. By "not yet split," it shows the future tense of the suffix -ta in "bhinno" in the sense of inevitability. Showing that same meaning with an analogy, he says, "moreover," and so forth. "Taṃ" refers to the crop. By "it will split," it shows that "it will split" is the meaning of the word "bhinno." "So ca kho" refers to the Sangha. The connection is that it will split because of quarrels. "Sambhamaatthavasena" means "by way of the sense of urgency." Indeed, the word "sambhama" is used in three senses: respect, fear, and urgency. Here, however, it is used in the sense of urgency. The intention is that the sense of urgency arises from the split in the Bhikkhu Sangha. This should be understood as referring to the meaning of "sambhama" that is encompassed by the particle "ca" in the verse mentioned below, "in fear, anger, or praise" (Pārā. Aṭṭha. 1.15). "Ettha" refers to the passage "the Bhikkhu Sangha is split, the Bhikkhu Sangha is split." "Āmeḍitaṃ" means "repeated," that is, spoken repeatedly due to being afflicted by fear and so forth, spoken with madness or derangement, thus it is called "repeated."

454. Hīti vitthāro. Bhagavā vadeyyāti sambandho. Ukkhipanti apanentīti ukkhepakā. Ukkhittamanuvattantīti ukkhittānuvattakā. Etesanti ukkhittānuvattakānaṃ. Puna etesanti ukkhepakānaṃ. Pakkhoti sakhā. Tantimevāti pāḷimeva, byāpārameva vā.

454. "Hīti" means "elaboration." The connection is, "The Blessed One would say." "Ukkhipanti apanentīti": those who raise up or remove are the expellers (ukkhepakā). "Ukkhittamanuvattantīti": those who follow the expelled are the followers of the expelled (ukkhittānuvattakā). "Etesanti" refers to these followers of the expelled. Again, "etesanti" refers to these expellers. "Pakkhoti" means "a faction" or "an ally." "Tantimevāti" means "just the text," or "just the affair."

455. Yoti bhikkhu. Cittaṃ uppādetīti sambandho. Tumheti dhammavādino sandhāya vuttaṃ. Kiṃ bhaṇathāti kiṃ vacanaṃ bhaṇatha. Iti pucchitvāti [M 0.0400] sambandho. Tesañcāti dhammavādīnañca. Itaresañcāti adhammavādīnañca. Imeti attano pakkhe ime bhikkhū. Tesanti adhammavādīnaṃ. “Kammaṃ kopetī”ti “nānāsaṃvāsakacatuttho ce bhikkhave kammaṃ kareyya, akammaṃ, na ca karaṇīya”nti vacanato (mahāva. 389) kammaṃ kopeti. Itaresampīti dhammavādīnampi. Dhammavādīnaṃ pakkhe nisīditvā adhammavādīnaṃ laddhiṃ gaṇhantopi dhammavādīnaṃ nānāsaṃvāsako hotiyeva, ayaṃ nayo vuttanayassa atthato siddhoti katvā idha na vutto. Evantiādi nigamanaṃ. Yoti bhikkhu, pavisati gaṇhātīti sambandho. Nisinno hutvāti yojanā. Imeti attano pakkhe ime bhikkhū. Itareti parapakkhe itare bhikkhū. Tesanti dhammavādīnaṃ. Yattha tattha vā pana pakkheti yasmiṃ kasmiṃci vā dhammavādīnaṃ pakkhe. Ime dhammavādinoti gaṇhātīti taṃtaṃpakkhagate bhikkhū yāthāvato vā ayāthāvato vā “ime dhammavādino”ti gaṇhāti.

455. "Yoti" refers to a bhikkhu. The connection is "he generates the thought." "Tumheti" is said in reference to those who advocate the Dhamma. "Kiṃ bhaṇathāti" means "what statement do you utter?" The connection is "having asked thus." "Tesañcāti" refers to those who advocate the Dhamma, and "itaresañcāti" refers to those who do not advocate the Dhamma. "Imeti": these bhikkhus are on his own side. "Tesanti" refers to those who do not advocate the Dhamma. "Kammaṃ kopetīti" (he invalidates the act): as stated in the text, "If, bhikkhus, a fourth among those of a different communion performs an act, it is not an act, and it should not be done" (Mahāva. 389), thus he invalidates the act. "Itaresampīti" refers to those who advocate the Dhamma as well. Even if one sits on the side of those who advocate the Dhamma but adopts the view of those who do not advocate the Dhamma, he is still one of a different communion from the advocates of the Dhamma; this principle, being established in meaning by the stated principle, is therefore not mentioned here. "Evantiādi" is the conclusion. "Yoti" refers to a bhikkhu; the connection is "he enters and takes up." The construction is "having sat down." "Imeti": these bhikkhus are on his own side. "Itareti": those others are on the opposing side. "Tesanti" refers to those who advocate the Dhamma. "Yattha tattha vā pana pakkheti" means "in whichever faction of those who advocate the Dhamma." "Ime dhammavādinoti gaṇhātīti": thus, he takes the bhikkhus belonging to that particular faction, whether rightly or wrongly, as "these are the advocates of the Dhamma."

456. Kāyena kataṃ kammaṃ kāyakammaṃ, vaciyā kataṃ kammaṃ vacīkammaṃ. Tattha kāyakammaṃ upadaṃsentā bhikkhū paharantā upadaṃsenti. Vacīkammaṃ upadaṃsentā bhikkhū pharusaṃ vadantā upadaṃsenti. Tena vuttaṃ “kāyena paharantā”tiādi. Upadaṃsentīti pavattenti. “Kodhavasenā”ti iminā pemavasenāti atthaṃ nivatteti. Adhammiyānīti adhammena kattabbāni. “Kiccānī”ti iminā iyapaccayassa sarūpaṃ dasseti. Asammodikāti ettha yakāralopoti āha “asammodikāyā”ti. “Kathāyā”ti iminā asammodaṃ janetīti asammodikāti katvā ṇikapaccayassa sarūpaṃ dasseti. Upacāraṃ muñcitvāti ettha upacāro nāma aññamaññaṃ paharantānaṃ hatthassa pāpuṇanaṭṭhānaṃ, taṃ muñcitvāti attho. Āsanantarikāyāti ettha ekaṃ āsanaṃ antaraṃ byavahitaṃ imissā nisinnakiriyāyāti āsanantarikāti dassento āha “ekekaṃ āsanaṃ antara”nti. “Katvā”ti iminā kiriyāvisesanabhāvaṃ dasseti.

456. Action done by the body is bodily action; action done by speech is verbal action. There, monks demonstrate bodily action by striking; they demonstrate verbal action by speaking harshly. Therefore, it is said, "by striking with the body," and so on. "Upadaṃsenti" means "they cause to proceed." By "out of anger," the meaning "out of affection" is negated. "Adhammiyāni" means "to be done unlawfully." By "kiccāni" (duties), he shows the form of the suffix 'iya'. Regarding "asammodikā" (disharmonious), he says "asammodikāyā" to indicate the elision of the 'ya' sound. By "kathāyā" (by speech), he shows that because it generates disharmony (asammodaṃ janeti), it is called "asammodikā," thus showing the form of the suffix 'ṇika'. Regarding "having abandoned the range," here "range" (upacāro) is the place within reach of the hand of those striking one another; "having abandoned that" is the meaning. Regarding "āsanantarikāya" (with a seat's interval), he shows that because one seat is interposed as an interval in this act of sitting, it is called "āsanantarikā," by saying "one seat apart." By "katvā" (having done), he shows its nature as a verbal modifier.

457-8. Ayaṃ [V 2.0059] assa bhikkhuno adhippāyo kirāti yojanā. Eteti kodhābhibhūte bhikkhū. Bhagavā pana kathesīti sambandho. “Anattho [M 0.0401] ato”ti iminā anatthatoti padassa okāralopasandhiṃ dasseti. Tesaṃ padānamatthaṃ dassento āha “etasmā”tiādi. “Atha vā”tiādinā “anatthado”ti vattabbe “sugato”tiādīsu viya da-kārassa ta-kāraṃ katvā anatthatoti vuttanti dasseti. Anatthadoti anatthaṃ dadātīti anatthado.

457-458. The construction is: This is said to be the intention of that monk. 'Ete' refers to the monks overwhelmed by anger. The connection is: But the Blessed One spoke. By "anattho ato," he shows the sandhi involving the elision of the 'o' sound in the word "anatthato." Explaining the meaning of those words, he says, "from this," and so on. Or else, by "atha vā" and so on, he shows that where "anatthado" should be said, the 'da' sound is changed to 'ta', as in "Sugato" and so on, and thus "anatthato" is said. "Anatthado" means one who gives what is harmful.

464. Puthusaddoti ettha puthusaddo mahantapariyāyoti āha “mahā”ti. Assāti bhaṇḍanakārakassa janassa. Samajanoti ettha samasaddo sadisapariyāyoti āha “ekasadiso”ti, tulyādhikaraṇasamāsoyaṃ. Bhaṇḍanakārako ayaṃ janoti yojanā. Tatthāti bhaṇḍanakārakesu janesu. Aññampi ekaṃ idaṃ kāraṇanti sambandho. Na maññitthāti koci ekopi na maññitthāti yojanā. Iminā amaññarunti ettha āvibhattiyā “ru”nti ādeso dassito.

464. Regarding 'puthusadda', here the word 'puthu' is a synonym for 'great', thus he says 'mahā' (great). 'Assa' refers to the quarrelsome person. Regarding 'samajano', here the word 'sama' is a synonym for 'similar', thus he says 'ekasadiso' (alike); this is an appositional compound. The construction is: this person is quarrelsome. 'Tattha' refers to among quarrelsome people. The connection is: this is another single cause. The construction is: 'na maññittha' means not even a single one thought. By this, in 'amaññaru', the substitution of 'ru' for the aorist ending is shown.

Parimuṭṭhāti parimuṭṭhā sati etesanti parimuṭṭhāti dassento āha “parimuṭṭhasatino”ti. Aṭṭhakkharagāthāyaṃ “pañcamaṃ laghu sabbatthā”ti vuttattā pañcamassa rākārassa rasso hoti. Tena vuttaṃ “rākārassa rassādeso kato”ti. Kathaṃ bhāṇinoti vācaṃ bhāṇino. Mukhāyāmanti ettha āyāmasaddo vitthārapariyāyo, vitthāro ca nāma pasāraṇanti āha “pasāretu”nti. Sampadānatthajotakena tuṃpaccayena sampadānatthe upayogavacananti dasseti. Nītāti kammavācakassa kitassa appadhānakammaṃ dassento āha “imaṃ nillajjabhāva”nti. Dvikammakadhātubhāvato “attano”ti padhānakammampi ajjhāharitabbaṃ. Tanti kalahaṃ. “Jāna”nti padena “vidū”ti padassa atthañca vākyañca dasseti. Vidanti jānantīti vidūti vacanattho kātabboti adhippāyo. Sādīnavotiādīnavena dosena saha pavatto. Ayanti kalaho.

Regarding 'parimuṭṭhā', showing that it means 'mindfulness is deluded in these' (parimuṭṭhā sati etesaṃ), he says 'parimuṭṭhasatino' (of deluded mindfulness). In the eight-syllable verse, because it is said "the fifth is light everywhere," the fifth 'rā' sound becomes short. Therefore, it is said, "the shortening of the 'rā' sound has been done." 'Kathaṃ bhāṇino' means one who speaks words. Regarding 'mukhāyāma', here, the word 'āyāma' is a synonym for 'extension', and extension is called 'spreading', thus he says 'pasāretuṃ' (to spread). By the suffix 'tuṃ', which indicates the dative sense, he shows the use of the word in the dative sense. Regarding 'nītā' (led), showing the secondary object of the passive participle, he says "this shameless state." Because it is a ditransitive root, the principal object "attano" (oneself) must also be supplied. 'Taṃ' refers to the quarrel. By the word "jāna," he indicates both the meaning and the sentence implied by the word "vidū." The intention is that the meaning of the word 'vidū' should be understood as 'they know' (vidanti), that is, 'they are knowing' (jānanti). 'Sādīnavo' means proceeding together with the fault of danger. 'Ayaṃ' refers to the quarrel.

Ye [M 0.0402] ca taṃ upanayhantīti ettha tasaddassa visayaṃ dassetuṃ vuttaṃ “āghāta”nti. Yeti janā. Upanayhanti upanahanti bandhanti. Sanantanoti ettha sanantanasaddo purāṇapariyāyoti āha “porāṇo”ti.

Regarding 'ye ca taṃ upanayhanti' (and those who harbor it), here, to show the object of the word 'taṃ' (that), 'āghāta' (grudge) is said. 'Ye' refers to people. 'Upanayhanti' means they harbor, they bind, they hold onto. Regarding 'sanantano', here, the word 'sanantana' is a synonym for 'ancient', thus he says 'porāṇo' (old).

“Aññe”ti iminā pareti ettha parasaddassa pacchābhāgatthādayo nivāreti. Mayamettha yamāmaseti ettha etasaddassa visayaṃ dassento āha “saṅghamajjhe”ti. Yamudhātu upayamanattho sekāro nipātamattoti āha “upayamāmā”ti. “Satataṃ samitaṃ maccusantikaṃ gacchāmā”ti iminā [V 2.0060] “na jānantī”ti padassa ākāraṃ dasseti. Tatthāti mahājanakāye ye paṇḍitāti yojanā. Evaṃ hīti evameva. Jānantā te paṇḍitā paṭipajjantīti yojanā. Medhantā hiṃsantā gacchanti pavattantīti medhagā kalahā. Keci medhadhātuto ṇvupaccayaṃ vadanti, tesaṃ matena medhakāti paṭhamakkharena pāṭho bhaveyya.

By "aññe" (others), he here excludes other meanings of the word "para," such as "later." Regarding 'mayamettha yamāmase', showing the scope of 'ettha', he says 'saṅghamajjhe' (in the midst of the Sangha). The root 'yamu' has the meaning of 'to restrain'; 'se' is merely a particle, thus he says 'upayamāma' (we restrain ourselves). By "constantly, continuously, we go toward the presence of death," he indicates the meaning of the phrase "they do not know." The construction is: 'Tattha' refers to those who are wise among that great multitude. 'Evaṃ hi' means "just so." The construction is: those wise ones, knowing, act accordingly. 'Medhagā' means quarrels, because they proceed (gacchanti) while disputing (medhantā) and harming (hiṃsantā). Some say the suffix 'ṇvu' comes from the root 'medh'; according to their view, the reading would be 'medhakā'.

Tesampīti brahmadattadīghāvukumārānampi. Saṅgatīti samāgamo. Voti tumhākaṃ. Yesaṃ tumhākaṃ neva mātāpitūnaṃ aṭṭhīni chinnāni, na pāṇā hatā, na gavassadhanāni haṭāni. Tesaṃ tumhākaṃ kasmā saṅgati na hotīti yojanā.

'Tesampi' refers to even Brahmadatta and Prince Dīghāvu. 'Saṅgati' means "coming together." 'Vo' refers to 'tumhākaṃ' (of you). The construction is: For you, whose parents' bones have not been severed, whose living beings have not been killed, and whose cattle, horses, and wealth have not been stolen—why is there no harmony for you?

Sabbāni parissayānīti ettha sabbānīti vuttakāraṇañca liṅgavipallāsañca dassento āha “pākaṭaparissaye ca paṭicchannaparissaye cā”ti. “Abhibhavitvā”ti iminā abhibhuyyāti padassa tvāpaccayantabhāvaṃ dasseti. Tenāti nipakena sahāyena.

Regarding 'sabbāni parissayāni' (all dangers), here, showing the reason for saying 'sabbāni' (all) and the alteration of gender, he says: "both obvious dangers and concealed dangers." By "abhibhavitvā" (having overcome), he shows that the word "abhibhuyya" is a form ending in the suffix '-tvā'. 'Tena' refers to "by that wise companion."

Rājāvāti ettha rājā ivāti padavibhāgaṃ katvā rājasaddassa upalakkhaṇavasena mahājanaka, arindamarājāno ca ivasaddassa opammatthajotakañca dassento āha “yathā”tiādi. Raṭṭhavijitasaddā aññamaññapariyāyā. Visesanavisesyānaṃ kāmācārato gamyamānattā vuttaṃ “vijitaṃ raṭṭha”nti. “Mātaṅgo araññe nāgo ivā”ti iminā [M 0.0403] padavibhāgaṃ dasseti. Tesaṃ padānaṃ atthaṃ dassento āha “mātaṅgoti hatthī vuccatī”tiādi. “Hatthī vuccatī”ti iminā mahanto aṅgo sarīrametassāti mātaṅgoti vacanatthena hatthī mātaṅgo nāmāti dasseti. Mahantasaddassa mātādeso. Nāgasaddo urage ca hatthimhi ca nāgarukkhe ca uttame ca nāmapaññattiyañcāti pañcasu atthesu vattati, idha uttamattheti dassento āha “nāgoti mahantādhivacanameta”nti. Mātaṅgaraññevāti ettha ivasaddassa opammatthajotakabhāvaṃ dassetvā atthayojanaṃ dassento āha “yathā hī”tiādi. “Yathā ca pālileyyako”ti iminā mātaṅganāgassa sarūpaṃ upalakkhaṇena dasseti.

Regarding 'rājāva', here, making the word division 'rājā iva' (like a king), and showing that the word 'rājā' is an illustration for Mahājanaka and the king Arindama, and that the word 'iva' indicates comparison, he says 'yathā' and so on. The words 'raṭṭha' and 'vijita' are synonyms. Because the relationship between adjective and noun is understood freely, it is stated as 'vijitaṃ raṭṭhaṃ'. By 'mātaṅgo araññe nāgo iva' (an elephant in the forest like a nāga), he demonstrates the word division. Explaining the meaning of these words, he says: 'mātaṅga means elephant,' and so on. By stating 'hatthī vuccati' (it is called an elephant), he shows that an elephant is called 'mātaṅga' by its verbal meaning, 'it has a large body' (mahanto aṅgo sarīram etassa). 'Māta' is a substitute for the word 'mahanta'. The word 'nāga' is used in five senses: serpent, elephant, Nāga tree, the supreme, and as a proper name. Here, he indicates that it conveys the sense of 'supreme,' stating: 'nāga is a designation for greatness.' Regarding 'mātaṅgaraññeva', here, after showing the function of the word 'iva' as indicating comparison, he shows the application of the meaning, saying: 'just as,' and so on. The phrase 'yathā ca pālileyyako' (and just as the Pālileyyaka elephant) shows the specific nature of the mātaṅga-nāga by way of illustration.

275. Pālileyyakagamanakathā

275. The Account of the Journey to Pālileyyaka

467. Pālileyyakanti palilavanasaṇḍe vasantahatthināgaṃ. “Hatthī”ti ca “nāgo”ti ca dvinnaṃ saddānaṃ pariyāyabhāvena vuttattā adhikatthoti āha “mahāhatthī”ti. Purato purato gacchantehi tehi hatthiādīhi chinnaggānīti yojanā. Obhaggobhagganti bhañjitvā adhopātitaṃ obhagganti [V 2.0061] dassento āha “bhañjitvā bhañjitvā pātita”nti. “Uccaṭṭhānato”ti iminā avatyūpasaggassa adhotthaṃ nayena dasseti. Etassāti hatthināgassa. Teti hatthiādayo. Tehīti hatthiādīhi. Pivantehi tehīti yojanā. Kaddamodakānīti kaddamena saṃsaṭṭhāni udakāni.

467. ‘Pālileyyaka’ means the elephant-noble dwelling in the Palila forest grove. Because the two words ‘hatthī’ (elephant) and ‘nāgo’ (noble one) are stated as synonyms, to indicate an additional meaning, he says ‘mahāhatthī’ (great elephant). The construction is: ‘chinnaggāni’ (with broken tops) by those elephants and others going further and further forward. Showing that ‘obhaggobhagga’ means ‘broken and cast down,’ he says ‘bhañjitvā bhañjitvā pātita’ (having broken and broken, cast down). By ‘uccaṭṭhānato’ (from a high place), he indicates the downward meaning of the prefix ‘ava’ by this method. ‘Etassa’ means ‘of this elephant-noble.’ ‘Te’ means ‘those elephants and others.’ ‘Tehi’ means ‘by those elephants and others.’ The construction is ‘by those drinking.’ ‘Kaddamodakāni’ means ‘waters mixed with mud.’

Īsādantassāti ettha īsāya sadiso danto imassāti īsādantoti dassento āha “rathaīsāsadisadantassā”ti. “Rathaīsā”ti iminā naṅgalaīsaṃ nivatteti. Yadekoti yaṃ eko. Yaṃsaddo kāraṇatthoti āha “yasmā”ti. Assa nāgassāti hatthināgassa. Nāgenāti buddhanāgena.

Here, showing that ‘īsādanta’ means ‘one who has a tusk similar to a pole,’ he says ‘rathaīsāsadisadantassa’ (of one having a tusk similar to a chariot’s pole). By ‘rathaīsā’ (chariot’s pole), he excludes the plow’s pole. ‘Yadeko’ means ‘yaṃ eko’ (because he is one). He says that the word ‘yaṃ’ is in the sense of cause, thus ‘yasmā’ (because). ‘Assa nāgassa’ means ‘of this elephant-noble.’ ‘Nāgena’ means ‘by the Buddha, the Nāga.’

Yathābhirantanti [M 0.0404] ettha kittakaṃ kālaṃ ramatīti āha “temāsa”nti. Ettāvatāti ettakena temāsaviharaṇena. Patthaṭā ahosīti sambandho. Sabbatthāti sabbasmiṃ jambudīpatale.

Here, concerning ‘yathābhirantaṃ’ (as long as he pleased), he says ‘temāsaṃ’ (for three months), answering the question, ‘For how long does he delight?’ ‘Ettāvatā’ means ‘by this much,’ that is, ‘by this three-month dwelling.’ The connection is ‘patthaṭā ahosi’ (was spread). ‘Sabbattha’ means ‘everywhere,’ that is, ‘throughout the entire surface of Jambudīpa.’

“Kosambinivāsino”ti iminā kosambiyaṃ nivasantīti kosambakāti vacanatthaṃ dasseti.

By ‘Kosambinivāsino’ (residents of Kosambi), he shows the verbal meaning of ‘Kosambakā’ as ‘they dwell in Kosambi.’

276. Aṭṭhārasavatthukathā

276. The Account of the Eighteen Grounds

471. “Laddhiggahaṇa”nti iminā ādīyate ādāyoti vacanatthaṃ dasseti.

471. By ‘laddhiggahaṇa’ (grasping of views), he shows the verbal meaning of ‘ādāya’ as ‘ādīyate’ (is taken).

475. Taṃ divasamevāti tasmiṃ saṅghasāmaggikaraṇadivaseyeva.

475. ‘Taṃ divasameva’ means on that very day, that is, on the very day of creating harmony in the Sangha.

476. Na mūlā mūlaṃ gantvāti mūlato mūlaṃ na gantvāva. “Atthato apagatā”ti iminā atthato apetā atthāpetāti vacanatthaṃ dasseti. “Byañjanamattaṃ upetā”ti iminā byañjanamattaṃ upetā upagatā byañjanūpetāti vacanatthaṃ dasseti.

476. ‘Na mūlā mūlaṃ gantvā’ means ‘not going from root to root,’ that is, ‘not having gone to a root from a root.’ By ‘atthato apagatā’ (departed from the meaning), he shows the verbal meaning of ‘atthāpetā’ as ‘departed from the meaning.’ By ‘byañjanamattaṃ upetā’ (endowed with the mere letter), he shows the verbal meaning of ‘byañjanūpetā’ as ‘endowed with the mere letter’ or ‘having approached the mere letter.’

477. Atthesu jātesūti ettha jātasaddo uppannapariyāyoti āha “vinayaatthesu uppannesū”ti. Tañca padaṃ “saṅghassa kiccesū”tiādīsu sabbapadesu yojetabbaṃ. Mahatthikoti mahanto upakārasaṅkhāto attho imassāti mahatthikoti dassanto āha “mahāupakāro”ti.

477. Here, concerning ‘atthesu jātesu’ (when matters have arisen), he says ‘vinayaatthesu uppannesu’ (when Vinaya matters have arisen), showing that the word ‘jāta’ is a synonym for ‘uppanna’ (arisen). And that phrase should be connected to all the terms, such as ‘saṅghassa kiccesu’ (in the Sangha’s affairs). Showing that ‘mahatthiko’ means ‘one whose benefit is great,’ being reckoned as a great help, he says ‘mahāupakāro’ (of great assistance).

Anānuvajjo paṭhamenāti ettha paṭhamasaddo tāvapariyāyoti dassento āha “tāvā”ti. Sīlatoti [V 2.0062] sīlena. Upekkhitācāroti upapattito ikkhitācāro. “Apekkhitācāro”tipi pāṭho. Upaparikkhitācāroti upaparikkhito ācāro etassāti upaparikkhitācāro.

Here, concerning ‘anānuvajjo paṭhamena’ (not to be reproached at first), showing that the word ‘paṭhama’ is a synonym for ‘tāva’ (for the time being), he says ‘tāvā.’ ‘Sīlato’ means ‘by morality.’ ‘Upekkhitācāro’ means ‘conduct observed from its basis.’ There is also the reading ‘apekkhitācāro.’ ‘Upaparikkhitācāro’ means ‘one whose conduct has been thoroughly investigated.’

Visayhāti ettha vipubbo sahadhātu abhibhavanattho, tvāpaccayo ca hotīti dassento āha “abhibhavitvā”ti. Anapagatanti kāraṇato [M 0.0405] anapetaṃ. Bhaṇanto bhikkhūti sambandho. Tamatthaṃ dassento āha “yasmā hī”tiādi. Soti bhikkhu, na hāpetīti sambandho. “Usūyāyā”ti iminā dosāgatigamanassa gahitattā “agatigamanavasenā”ti iminā pārisesanayena avasesaagatigamanamevādhippetaṃ. Soti bhikkhu. Chambhati cevāti thambhati ceva, thaddhaṃ karoti cevāti attho. Vedhati cāti kampati ca. Yo cāti bhikkhu pana. Īdisoti usūyāya vā agatigamanena vā bhaṇanasaṅkhāto ediso na hoti.

Here, concerning ‘visayhā’, showing that the root ‘sah’ with the prefix ‘vi’ has the meaning of overcoming, and that it is a gerund equivalent to the suffix ‘tvā’, he says ‘abhibhavitvā’ (having overcome). ‘Anapagataṃ’ means ‘not departed from the cause.’ The connection is ‘bhaṇanto bhikkhu’ (the monk speaking). To show that meaning, he says ‘yasmā hi’ (because indeed) and so on. The connection is ‘so bhikkhu na hāpeti’ (that monk does not abandon). By ‘usūyāya’ (out of envy), since going to a wrong course due to hatred is included, by ‘agatigamanavasena’ (by way of going to a wrong course), the remaining ways of going to a wrong course are intended by the principle of the remainder. ‘So’ refers to the monk. ‘Chambhati ceva’ means ‘he is stupefied and also becomes stiff,’ that is, ‘he makes himself rigid.’ ‘Vedhati ca’ means ‘and he trembles.’ ‘Yo ca’ means ‘but the monk who...’ ‘Īdiso’ means ‘such a one’; that is, he is not such a one reckoned as speaking out of envy or by way of going to a wrong course.

Kiñca bhiyyoti nipātasamudāyo, tato vuttato atirekaṃ kathetabbaṃ kiṃ panāti attho. Tassā gāthāya attho veditabboti yojanā. Yoti bhikkhu. Hīti saccaṃ. Kālāgatanti ettha gahetabbakālañca sattamītappurisasamāsañca dassento āha “kathetabbayuttakāle āgata”nti. Vacoti padaṃ na vacanapadhānaṃ, vacanavantapuggaloyeva padhānanti dassento āha “vadanto”ti.

‘Kiñca bhiyyo’ is a collection of particles, meaning ‘What more is to be said beyond what has been stated?’ The construction is ‘the meaning of that verse should be understood.’ ‘Yo’ refers to the monk. ‘Hī’ means ‘truly.’ Here, concerning ‘kālāgataṃ’ (arrived at the right time), showing both the appropriate time and that it is a locative tatpurisa compound, he says ‘kathetabbayuttakāle āgata’ (arrived at the appropriate time for speaking). Showing that the word ‘vaco’ (speech) is not primary, but the person possessing speech is primary, he says ‘vadanto’ (speaking).

Ācerakamhi ca saketi ettha ācariyassa eso ācerako, sassa attano eso sakoti vacanatthaṃ dassento āha “attano ācariyavāde”ti. Gāthābhāvato ācariyasaddassa ācerādeso kātabbo. “Vāde”ti iminā idamatthe pavattassa ṇikapaccayassa sarūpaṃ dasseti. Alaṃ pametunti ettha alaṃsaddo samatthattho, pamasaddotulanatthoti āha “tulayituṃ samattho”ti. Kathetaveti ettha tavesaddo aññattha yebhuyyena bhāvavācako, idha pana kammavācakoti āha “kathetabbe”ti. Viraddhaṭṭhānakusaloti viraddhaṭṭhāne kusalo.

Here, concerning ‘ācerakamhi ca sake’ (in his own teacher’s), showing the verbal meaning that ‘āceraka’ is ‘that which belongs to the teacher’ and ‘saka’ is ‘that which belongs to oneself,’ he says ‘attano ācariyavāde’ (in his own teacher’s doctrine). Because it is a verse, the substitution of ‘ācera’ for ‘ācariya’ should be made. By ‘vāde’ (in the doctrine), he shows the nature of the suffix ‘-ka’ which occurs in the sense of ‘belonging to this.’ Here, concerning ‘alaṃ pametuṃ’ (capable of comparing), showing that the word ‘alaṃ’ has the meaning of ‘capable’ and the word ‘pama’ has the meaning of ‘comparing,’ he says ‘tulayituṃ samattho’ (capable of comparing). Here, concerning ‘kathetave’ (to be spoken), he says ‘kathetabbe’ (what should be spoken), showing that the suffix ‘-tave’, which elsewhere generally expresses an abstract state, here expresses the object. ‘Viraddhaṭṭhānakusalo’ means ‘skilled in the point of error.’

Ayaṃ gāthā vuttāti sambandho. Tanti kathetabbaṃ. Ayaṃ hetthatthoti ayaṃ eva ettha gāthāyaṃ atthoti yojanā. “Gacchantī”ti iminā vajantīti ettha vajadhātuyā gatyatthaṃ dasseti. “Attano ācariyavāda”nti iminā “sakaṃ ādāya”nti padassa atthaṃ dasseti. Ācariyavādo [M 0.0406] hi ādātabbato gahetabbato ādāyanti vutto. Tadanurūpanti tassa vatthussa anurūpaṃ. Byākaramāno bhikkhūti sambandho. Aṭṭhahi dūtaṅgehīti “sotā ca hoti, sāvetā ca, uggahetā ca, dhāretā ca, viññātā ca, viññāpetā, ca kusalo ca sahitāsahitassa, no ca kalahakārako”ti (cūḷava. 347; a. ni. 8.16) evaṃ vuttehi aṭṭhahi dūtassa [V 2.0063] aṅgehi. Kassa dūteyyakammanti āha “saṅghassā”ti. Dūtassa etāni dūteyyāni, tāniyeva kammāni dūteyyakammāni, tesu. Idanti atthajākaṃ, vuttaṃ hotīti yojanā. Atha vā idanti ayamattho. Vuttaṃ hotīti vutto hoti. Pacchimanaye liṅgavipallāsoti daṭṭhabbo. Ānetvā havanti pūjentīti āhavo dāyakā, tesaṃ āhūnaṃ. Ānetvā hunitabbaṃ pūjetabbanti āhuti, taṃ āhutiṃ. Saṅghassa kiccesūti niddhāraṇe bhummaṃ. Tena vuttaṃ “tassa tassa kiccassā”ti. Karavacoti ettha “vacokaro”ti vattabbe gāthābhāvato padavipariyāyavasena “karavaco”ti vuttoti āha “vacanaṃ karonto”ti. “Vacanakaraṇenā”ti iminā “na tena maññatī”ti ettha tasaddassa visayaṃ dasseti.

The connection is ‘ayaṃ gāthā vuttā’ (this verse is spoken). ‘Taṃ’ means ‘it should be spoken.’ The construction is ‘ayaṃ hetthattho’ means ‘this very meaning is in this verse.’ By ‘gacchanti’ (going), he shows the meaning of movement in the root ‘vaj’ in ‘vajanti’ (going). By ‘attano ācariyavāda’ (one’s own teacher’s doctrine), he shows the meaning of the word ‘sakaṃ ādāya’ (taking up one’s own). For the teacher’s doctrine is called ‘ādāya’ (taking up) because it is to be taken up, to be grasped. ‘Tadanurūpaṃ’ means ‘suitable to that subject.’ The connection is ‘byākaramāno bhikkhu’ (the monk explaining). ‘Aṭṭhahi dūtaṅgehi’ means ‘with the eight qualities of a messenger’ as stated thus: ‘He is a listener, a reporter, a learner, a retainer, a knower, a communicator, skilled in what is fitting and unfitting, and not a quarrel-maker’ (Cūḷavagga 347; Aṅguttara Nikāya 8.16). He says ‘saṅghassa’ (for the Sangha), answering ‘whose messenger duty?’ These are the messenger duties of a messenger; those very tasks are messenger duties; in them. The construction is ‘idaṃ’ (this) is the collection of meanings; ‘vuttaṃ hoti’ (it is said). Alternatively, ‘idaṃ’ means ‘this meaning.’ ‘Vuttaṃ hoti’ means ‘it is spoken.’ In the latter method, an inversion of gender should be seen. ‘Āhavo’ means ‘givers,’ those who, having brought, offer and honor; ‘tesaṃ āhūnaṃ’ means of those givers. ‘Āhuti’ means ‘that which should be offered and honored after being brought,’ that offering. ‘Saṅghassa kiccesu’ (in the Sangha’s affairs) is a locative of determination. Therefore, it is said ‘tassa tassa kiccassa’ (for each respective duty). Here, concerning ‘karavaco’ (doer of speech), he says ‘vacanaṃ karonto’ (making speech), showing that it is stated as ‘karavaco’ by way of word inversion due to being a verse, where ‘vacokaro’ should have been said. By ‘vacanakaraṇena’ (by the act of speaking), he shows the scope of the word ‘tena’ (by that) in ‘na tena maññati’ (he does not think by that).

Āpajjamāno bhikkhu āpatti hotīti yojanā. Tassā cāti ettha smāvacanassa ssādeso kātabbo. Yathāti yenākārena, vinayakammākārenāti attho. Yesūti yattakesu vatthūsu. Ubhaye ete vibhaṅgāti sambandho. Assāti bhikkhussa.
