Āpattivuṭṭhānapadassāti padasaddo kāraṇattho, bhummatthe sāmivacano ca hotīti āha “āpattivuṭṭhānakāraṇe”ti. “Kusalo”ti iminā cheko paṇḍito, kucchitaṃ pāpaṃ vidati jānātīti kovidoti vacanatthena kovido nāmāti dasseti.

The construction is ‘āpajjamāno bhikkhu āpatti hoti’ (for a monk incurring an offense, it is an offense). And here, concerning ‘tassā,’ the substitution of ‘ssā’ for the ablative ending ‘smā’ should be made. ‘Yathā’ means ‘in what manner,’ that is, ‘in the manner of a Vinaya procedure.’ ‘Yesu’ means ‘in how many instances.’ The connection is ‘ubhaye ete vibhaṅgā’ (both these are classifications). ‘Assa’ means ‘of the monk.’ ‘Āpattivuṭṭhānapadassa’ (of the word for arising from an offense) — here, the word ‘pada’ has the sense of ‘reason,’ and the genitive case can also be in the sense of the locative; therefore, he says ‘āpattivuṭṭhānakāraṇe’ (in the reason for arising from an offense). By ‘kusalo’ (skilled), he shows that ‘cheka’ means ‘expert,’ ‘paṇḍita’ means ‘wise,’ and that the term ‘kovida’ means ‘one who knows and understands base evil’ by the meaning of the word.

Ācaranto [M 0.0407] bhikkhu gacchatīti yojanā. “Vatta”nti iminā osāraṇaṃ tanti ettha tasaddassa visayaṃ dasseti. “Yā”ti iminā etampīti ettha etasaddassa aniyamaniddesabhāvaṃ dasseti. Sabbatthāti sabbasmiṃ kosambakakkhandhake.

The construction is ‘ācaranto bhikkhu gacchati’ (the monk behaving appropriately goes). By ‘vattaṃ’ (duty), he shows the scope of the word ‘taṃ’ (that) in ‘osāraṇaṃ taṃ’ (that reinstatement). By ‘yā’ (which), he shows the unspecified nature of ‘etaṃ’ (this) in ‘etaṃ pi’ (this also). ‘Sabbattha’ means ‘everywhere,’ that is, ‘in the entire Kosambaka Khandhaka.’

Iti kosambakakkhandhakavaṇṇanāya yojanā samattā.

Thus ends the explanation of the commentary on the Kosambaka Khandhaka.

Iti samantapāsādikāya vinayasaṃvaṇṇanāya

Thus, in the Samantapāsādikā, the commentary on the Vinaya,

Mahāvaggavaṇṇanāya

in the commentary on the Mahāvagga,

Yojanā samattā.

the explanation is complete.

Jādilañchitanāmena, nekānaṃ vācito mayā;

Mahāvaggakhandhakassa, samatto yojanānayoti.

By me, named Jādilañchita, this has been recited for many; the method of explanation for the Mahāvagga Khandhaka is completed.

Namo tassa bhagavato arahato sammāsambuddhassa

Homage to the Blessed One, the Arahant, the Perfectly Self-Enlightened One.

Pācityādiyojanā

Explanation of the Pācittiya, etc.

Cūḷavaggayojanā

Explanation of the Cūḷavagga

Mahāvaggakhandhakassevaṃ[M 0.0409], katvāna yojanānayaṃ;

Adhunā cūḷavaggassa, karissaṃ yojanānayaṃ.

Having thus made the method of explanation for the Mahāvagga Khandhaka, I shall now make the method of explanation for the Cūḷavagga.

1. Kammakkhandhakaṃ

1. The Chapter on Formal Acts

1. Tajjanīyakammakathā

1. The Account of the Act of Censure

1. Cūḷavaggassa [V 2.0065] paṭhame kammakkhandhake evamattho veditabboti yojanā. “Cūḷavaggassā”ti padaṃ “kammakkhandhake”ti pade avayavisambandho. Tāvāti pārivāsikakkhandhakādito[V 2.0066], pārivāsikkhandhakādīnaṃ vā paṭhamaṃ. Cevasaddo ca casaddo ca “paṇḍukalohitakā”ti padassa asamāhāradvandavākyaṃ dīpenti. Nissayānaṃ nāmaṃ nissitesu upacāravasena tesaṃ saddhivihārikaantevāsikāpi paṇḍukalohitakanāmāyeva hontīti dassento āha “tesaṃ nissitakāpī”tiādi. Pisaddena upacāratthaṃ sampiṇḍeti. “Suṭṭhu balava”nti iminā balavābalavanti dvinnaṃ saddānaṃ pariyāyabhāvena vuttattā atisayatthoti dasseti. “Balavabalava”nti vattabbe vācāsiliṭṭhavasena dīghaṃ katvā evaṃ vuttaṃ. Paṭivadathāti paṭicchannaṭṭhāne kathetha. Iminā paṭimantethāti ettha mantadhātuyā guttabhāsanatthaṃ dasseti. Atthesu karaṇabhāsanakiccesu alaṃ samatthāti alamatthā, tesaṃ visesenāti alamatthatarāti dassento āha “samatthatarā”ti.

1. In the first chapter of the Cūḷavagga, the Kammakkhandhaka, the meaning should be understood thus—this is the explanation. The word ‘Cūḷavaggassa’ is connected to the word ‘Kammakkhandhake’ as a part-whole relationship. ‘Tāva’ means from the Pārivāsikakkhandhaka onwards, or the first of the Pārivāsikakkhandhaka, etc. The particles ‘ca’ and ‘eva’ indicate that ‘paṇḍukalohitakā’ is a non-collective dvandva compound. Showing that, by way of convention, the name of the preceptor (nissaya) is applied to those dependent on them, their co-residents and pupils are also called paṇḍukalohitaka, he says, ‘their dependents as well,’ etc. The particle ‘pi’ summarizes the conventional meaning. By ‘suṭṭhu balava’ he shows that because the two words ‘balava’ and ‘abalava’ are spoken of as synonyms, it has the sense of excess. Although ‘balavābalava’ should be said, it is spoken thus by lengthening it for the sake of euphony. ‘Paṭivadatha’ means ‘speak in a concealed place.’ With this he shows that in ‘paṭimantetha,’ the root ‘mant’ has the meaning of secret speech. Showing that ‘alamatthā’ means ‘capable enough’ in the matters of action and speech, and ‘alamatthatarā’ means ‘particularly superior to them,’ he says, ‘more capable.’

Adhammakammadvādasakakathā

The Account of the Twelve Unlawful Acts

4. Asammukhā [M 0.0410] katantiādīsu evaṃ vinicchayo veditabboti yojanā. Sammukhehi virahitā asammukhāti dassento āha “saṅghadhammavinayapuggalasammukhānaṃ vinā kata”nti. “Appaṭipucchitvā”ti iminā appaṭipucchāti ettha tvāpaccayassākārabhāvaṃ dasseti. Tassevāti cuditakasseva. Adesanāgāminiyāti ettha akārassa aññatthaṃ dassento āha “pārājikā…pe… vā”ti. Etthāti tajjanīyakamme. Nava padāti navasu padesu, niddhāraṇe cetaṃ paccattavacanaṃ. Purimakesu tīsu tikesu vuttesu navasu padesūti yojanā. “Ekeka”nti padena sambandhitabbaṃ. Imehīti imehi dvīhi padehi. Dvādasa tikāti purimehi tīhi tikehi nava tike missetvā dvādasa. Sukkapakkhesupīti paṭisedhavirahavasena sukkesu pakkhesupi.

4. Regarding ‘done without being present,’ etc., the determination should be understood thus—this is the explanation. Showing that ‘asammukhā’ means ‘lacking presence,’ he says: ‘done without the presence of the Sangha, the Dhamma, the Vinaya, or a person.’ By ‘appaṭipucchitvā’ he shows that in ‘appaṭipucchā,’ the tvā suffix has become ‘ā.’ ‘Tasseva’ means ‘of that very accused person.’ Concerning ‘adesanāgāminiyā,’ showing that the ‘a’ here refers to something else, he says: ‘pārājika…or…’ ‘Ettha’ means ‘in the act of censure.’ ‘Nava padā’ means ‘in nine instances’; this is a singular form used for specification. The explanation is: ‘in the nine instances spoken of in the first three triads.’ It should be connected with the word ‘ekeka.’ ‘Imehi’ means ‘by these two terms.’ ‘Dvādasa tikā’ means twelve triads, by mixing the nine triads with the first three triads. ‘Sukkapakkhesupi’ means ‘even in the favorable aspects,’ due to the absence of prohibition.

6. “Pabbajitāna”nti iminā gihīnaṃ ananulomikataṃ nivatteti. Sahasokitādīhīti ādisaddena sahanandiṃ saṅgaṇhāti. Imasmiṃ ṭhāne sabbaaṭṭhakathāpotthakesu “na upasampādetabbanti upajjhāyena hutvā na upasampādetabba”nti pāṭhato paṭṭhāya yāva “na sampayojetabbanti aññamaññaṃ yojetvā kalaho na kāretabbo”ti pāṭho atthi, tāva aṭṭhārasasammāvattanavattānaṃ saṃvaṇṇanāpāṭho likhito, so pāṭho imasmiṃ ṭhāne na likhitabbo. Kasmā? Pāḷikkamānuppattābhāvato, aṭṭhakathāyameva “aṭṭhārasa sammāvattanavattāni pārivāsikakkhandhake vaṇṇayissāmā”ti vakkhamānattā, yathāvacanañca pārivāsikakkhandhake (cūḷava. aṭṭha. 76) saṃvaṇṇitatthā ca. Tasmā so pāṭho na porāṇapāṭho hoti, pacchā pakkhittapāṭhoti daṭṭhabbo.

6. By ‘pabbajitāna’ he negates its suitability for laypeople. By ‘sahasokitādīhi’ (with sorrow, etc.), the term ‘etc.’ includes ‘sahanandiṃ’ (with joy). In this context, in all the commentary texts, from the passage ‘na upasampādetabbaṃ—meaning an upajjhāya should not confer higher ordination’ up to the passage ‘na sampayojetabbaṃ—meaning one should not cause quarrels by connecting one another,’ there is written a descriptive passage of the eighteen duties of right conduct and misconduct. That passage should not be written here. Why? Because it does not arise from the sequence of the Pāli text, and because the commentary itself will say, ‘We will describe the eighteen duties of right conduct and misconduct in the Pārivāsikakkhandhaka.’ Moreover, just as stated, it is described in the Pārivāsikakkhandhaka (Cūḷavagga, Aṭṭha. 76). Therefore, that passage is not an ancient reading; it should be seen as a passage inserted later.

Tiṇṇaṃ [V 2.0067] bhikkhave bhikkhūnantiādi vuttanti sambandho. Ekekenāpīti tīsu aṅgesu ekekenāpi. Iminā avayavavākyanibbattivasena kammārahabhāvaṃ dasseti. Hīti saccaṃ. Niyassassa visesena abhiṇhāpattikattaṃ aṅgaṃ iti vuttanti yojanā. Ettha ākāravācako [M 0.0411] itisaddo luttaniddiṭṭhoti daṭṭhabbaṃ. Eseva nayo anantarepi. Tajjīyati anena vinayakammenāti tajjanīyaṃ, tameva kammaṃ tajjanīyakammaṃ. “Nissāya te vatthabba”nti niyassīyati bālo bhajāpīyati anena vinayakammenāti niyassaṃ, divādigaṇikattā sakārassa dvebhāvo hoti “nassaṃ vassa”ntiādīsu viya, niyassameva kammaṃ niyassakammaṃ. Gāmādito pabbājiyati anena vinayakammenāti pabbājanīyaṃ, tameva kammaṃ pabbājanīyakammaṃ. Tīsūti bhaṇḍanakārakaabhiṇhāpattikakuladūsakavasena tividhesu aṅgesu. Yena kenaci aṅgenāti sambandho. Yadi sabbāni kammāni kātuṃ vaṭṭatīti yojanā. Evaṃ sati campeyyakkhandhake (mahāva. 400 ādayo) vuttaṃ idaṃ vacanaṃ virujjhatīti sambandho. Vacanatthanānattatoti vacanassa ca atthassa ca nānābhāvato. Tamevatthaṃ vitthārento āha “tajjanīyakammārahassāti imassa hī”tiādi. Tattha “tiṇṇaṃ bhikkhave”tiādivacanassa aṅgasambhavo atthoti yojanā. Tasmāti yasmā na virujjhati, tasmā. Saṅghena kataṃ hotīti sambandho. Iminā lakkhaṇena tajjanīyādikammārahassa tassa bhikkhussāti yojanā. Evaṃ kammasanniṭṭhānatthaṃ dassetvā aṅgasambhavatthaṃ dassento āha “yassa panā”tiādi. Tattha yassāti bhikkhussa, atthīti sambandho. Bhaṇḍanakārakādīsūtiādisaddena abhiṇhāpattikakuladūsakāni saṅgaṇhāti. Ākaṅkhamāno saṅgho kareyyāti sambandho. Kammārahanti kammassa, kamme vā arahaṃ. Etthāti kammakkhandhake. Pubbenāti pubbe vuttena campeyyakkhandhakena. Aparanti apare vuttaṃ kammakkhandhakaṃ. Sametīti samaṃ gacchati.

The connection is that ‘Tiṇṇaṃ bhikkhave bhikkhūnaṃ,’ etc., is stated. ‘Ekekenāpi’ means ‘even by one of the three factors.’ Through this, he shows the qualification for a disciplinary action by way of the formation of a subordinate clause. ‘Hī’ means ‘indeed.’ The explanation is that being a frequent offender, especially for one under dependence, is a factor, as stated. Here, the word ‘iti,’ which indicates manner, should be understood as elliptically stated. The same method applies to what immediately follows. ‘Tajjanīya’ means ‘he is censured by this disciplinary action’; that very action is the tajjanīyakamma. ‘Nissāya te vatthabba’ means ‘the fool is subjected to dependence or made to associate through this disciplinary action’; hence, ‘niyassa.’ Due to its belonging to the divādi class of roots, the ‘sa’ is doubled, as seen in ‘nassaṃ vassa’ and similar cases. The action itself is called ‘niyassakamma.’ ‘Pabbājanīya’ means ‘he is banished from the village, etc., by this disciplinary action’; that very action is the pabbājanīyakamma. ‘Tīsu’ refers to the threefold factors: being a quarrel-maker, a frequent offender, or a corrupter of families. The connection is: ‘by any one of these factors.’ The interpretation is: ‘If all actions are fit to be performed.’ Thus, the connection is that this statement mentioned in the Campeyya chapter (Mahāvagga 400, etc.) is contradicted. ‘Vacanatthanānattato’ means ‘due to the difference in the word and its meaning.’ Elaborating on that very meaning, he says: ‘tajjanīyakammārahassa’ (for one qualified for the act of censure), ‘this indeed,’ etc. There, the explanation is that the statement ‘tiṇṇaṃ bhikkhave,’ etc., has the meaning of the possibility of the factors. ‘Tasmā’ means ‘therefore,’ because it is not contradicted. The connection is: ‘it is done by the Sangha.’ The explanation is: ‘by this characteristic, that monk is qualified for the tajjanīya and similar actions.’ Having thus shown the purpose of establishing the disciplinary action, and showing the purpose of the possibility of the factors, he says: ‘yassa pana,’ etc. There, ‘yassa’ refers to the monk; ‘atthi’ is the connection. By ‘bhaṇḍanakārakādīsu,’ the term ‘etc.’ includes frequent offenders and corrupters of families. The connection is: ‘if the Sangha wishes, it may act.’ ‘Kammāraha’ means ‘deserving of the action’ or ‘worthy in the action.’ ‘Ettha’ means ‘in the Kammakkhandhaka.’ ‘Pubbena’ means ‘by the Campeyya chapter mentioned previously.’ ‘Apara’ means ‘the Kammakkhandhaka mentioned later.’ ‘Sameti’ means ‘it comes together.’

Tatthāti kammesu, tajjanīyakammeti sambandho, aṅgesu vā, bhaṇḍanakārakavasenāti sambandho. Atha khoti tathā vuttāpīti attho. Karontena kammavācāvācakenāti sambandho. Hīti phalajotako. Bhūtena vatthunāti tacchena vatthunā. Aññassa kammassāti tajjanīyakammato aññassa kammassa. Kasmā bālassa abyattassa āpattibahulassa [M 0.0412] tajjanīyakammaṃ kātabbanti yojanā. Idampīti tajjanīyakammampi. Sabbatthāti sabbesu kammesu.

‘Tattha’ means ‘in the actions,’ the connection is ‘in the act of censure’; or, regarding the factors, the connection is ‘by way of a quarrel-maker.’ ‘Atha kho’ means ‘even though it has been stated thus.’ The connection is: ‘by the one performing the act, who is uttering the kammavācā.’ ‘Hī’ is a particle indicating a result. ‘Bhūtena vatthunā’ means ‘with a factual basis.’ ‘Aññassa kammassa’ means ‘of an action other than the act of censure.’ The explanation is: ‘Why should an act of censure be imposed on a foolish, incompetent, and frequently offending person?’ ‘Idampi’ means ‘this too,’ referring to the act of censure. ‘Sabbattha’ means ‘in all cases,’ referring to all acts.

Nappaṭippassambhetabbaaṭṭhārasakādikathā

The Discussion on the Eighteen and Other Matters Not to Be Allayed

8. Pannalomāti patitamānalomā. Etanti vattaṃ. Netthāranti ettha aphuṭṭhakkharasaṃyoge parassa [V 2.0068] takārassa thakāro hoti, tasmā dutiyakkharena pāṭho yutto. Yenāti vattena. Nissāraṇāti nissāraṇato. Dasa vā divasāni, pañca vā divasāni pūretabbanti yojanā. Hīti saccaṃ. Ettakenāti etappamāṇena dasapañcadivasena.

8. ‘Pannaloma’ means ‘whose hair of pride has fallen.’ ‘Etaṃ’ refers to the observance. In ‘netthāranti’, here, in a consonant cluster, the ‘t’ of the following letter becomes ‘th’; therefore, the reading with the second letter is appropriate. ‘Yena’ refers to the observance. ‘Nissāraṇā’ means ‘from expulsion.’ The explanation is that ‘ten days or five days must be completed.’ ‘Hi’ means ‘truly.’ ‘Ettakena’ refers to that amount, ten or five days.

2. Niyassakammakathā

2. The Discussion on the Act of Requiring Dependence

11. Apissu bhikkhū pakatāti ettha nipātānamanekatthattā idha apissusaddo niccattho hoti. Pakatasaddo “kukkuccapakatā”tiādīsu (pārā. aṭṭha. 1.tatiyasaṅgītikathā; pāci. aṭṭha. 438) abhibhavanattho, idha pana byāvaṭatthoti dassento āha “niccaṃ byāvaṭā hontī”ti.

11. In the phrase ‘apissu bhikkhū pakatā’, here, because particles have multiple meanings, the word ‘apissu’ in this context has the meaning of 'constantly'. The word ‘pakata’ in phrases like ‘kukkuccapakatā’ (Pārājika Aṭṭhakathā, 1, Third Recitation; Pācittiya Aṭṭhakathā, 438) has the meaning of ‘overcome’, but here it has the meaning of ‘occupied’, as shown by the statement ‘they are constantly occupied’.

3. Pabbājanīyakammakathā

3. The Discussion on the Act of Banishment

27. Etthāti assajipunabbasukavatthumhi. Kāyikoti ettha kāyena kīḷatīti kāyikoti vacanatthaṃ dassento āha “kāyakīḷā vuccatī”ti. “Eseva nayo”ti iminā vācāya kīḷatīti vācasiko, kāyiko ca vācasiko ca kāyikavācasikoti vacanatthaṃ atidisati. Ettha ca pacchimavacanattho samāhāradvando, samāhāradvandepi katthaci pulliṅgamicchanti saddavidū “dhammavinayo”tiādīsu (vibha. aṭṭha. 509) viya. Kāyadvārapaññattasikkhāpadaṃ vītikkamatīti kāyikoti vacanatthaṃ dassento āha “kāyadvāre paññattasikkhāpadavītikkamo vuccatī”ti. Kāyena paññattasikkhāpadaṃ vītikkametīti kāyikoti vacanatthopi yujjateva. “Upahananaṃ vuccatī”ti iminā upahananaṃ upaghātaṃ, tameva upaghātikanti [M 0.0413] vacanatthaṃ dasseti. “Nāsana”nti iminā hanadhātuyā hiṃsanatthaṃ dasseti. Paṭikkhittavejjakammādivasena telapacanaariṭṭhapacanādīni kāyiko micchājīvo nāmāti yojanā. Iminā micchājīvassa sarūpaṃ dasseti.

27. ‘Here’ refers to the case of Assaji and Punabbasu. In ‘kāyiko’, here, explaining the meaning of ‘kāyiko’ as ‘one who plays with the body’, he says, ‘it is called bodily play.’ By ‘this is the same method’, he extends the meaning to ‘vācasiko’ as ‘one who plays with speech’, and to ‘kāyikavācasiko’ as ‘both bodily and verbal.’ Here, the meaning of the latter word is a collective compound, and even in a collective compound, grammarians sometimes prefer the masculine gender, as in ‘dhammavinayo’ (Vibhaṅga Aṭṭhakathā, 509). Explaining the meaning of ‘kāyiko’ as ‘one who transgresses a training rule prescribed through the body-door’, he says, ‘it is called a transgression of a training rule prescribed through the body-door.’ The meaning of ‘kāyiko’ as ‘one who transgresses a training rule prescribed by the body’ is also appropriate. By ‘it is called striking’, he shows the meaning of ‘upahanana’ as ‘injury’, and the same as ‘upaghātika’. By ‘nāsana’, he shows the meaning of ‘violence’ from the root ‘han’. The explanation is that bodily wrong livelihood is so named by way of prohibited medical practices and so forth, such as boiling oil and preparing medicinal decoctions. By this, he shows the nature of wrong livelihood.

4. Paṭisāraṇīyakammakathā

4. The Discussion on the Act of Reconciliation

33. Sudhammavatthusmiṃ evamattho veditabboti yojanā. Anapaloketvāti ettha apapubbo lokasaddo āpucchanatthoti āha “na āpucchitvā”ti.

33. The explanation is that the meaning should be understood thus in the Sudhamma story. In ‘anapaloketvā’, here, the word ‘loka’ with the prefix ‘apa’ has the meaning of ‘asking permission’, hence he says, ‘without asking’.

34. Kinti [V 2.0069] kiṃ nāma khādanīyabhojanīyaṃ. Voti tumhehi. Gahapatīti ālapanapadaṃ. Therānaṃ atthāyāti sambandho. Paṭiyattanti paṭiyāditaṃ. “Etaṃ avocā”ti iminā etadavocāti ettha niggahitādesasandhiṃ dasseti. Yadidanti saddo “tilasaṃguḷikā”ti padena yojitattā itthiliṅgoti āha “yā aya”nti. Tilasakkhalikāti tilena saṃsaṭṭhā sakkhalikā. “Sā natthī”ti iminā uttaravākye yaṃsaddassa pubbavākye taṃsaddāpekkhataṃ dasseti. Eko purisoti sambandho. Pūviyoti pūvaṃ, pūvena vā kayavikkayo. Tenāti kāraṇena. Nanti gahapatiṃ. Theroti sudhammatthero. Yadeva kiñcīti ettha kiñci eva yaṃ vacananti dassento āha “kiñcideva tilasaṃguḷikāvacana”nti. Idanti imaṃ atthaṃ. Soti kukkuṭapotako. Kākavassitanti kākassa vassitaṃ, neva akāsīti sambandho. Tayāpīti pisaddo kukkuṭapotakaṃ apekkhati. Neva bhikkhuvacanaṃ vuttaṃ, na gihivacanaṃ vuttaṃ, iti imamatthaṃ dassetīti yojanā.

34. ‘Kiṃ’ means ‘what kind of edible and chewable food.’ ‘Vo’ means ‘by you.’ ‘Gahapati’ is a vocative term. ‘For the sake of the elders’ is the connection. ‘Paṭiyattaṃ’ means ‘prepared.’ By ‘etaṃ avocā’, he shows the niggahīta-substitution sandhi in ‘etadavocā.’ Because the word ‘yadidaṃ’ is connected with the word ‘tilasaṃguḷikā,’ it is feminine in gender, hence he says, ‘yā ayaṃ.’ ‘Tilasakkhalikā’ means ‘a sweetmeat mixed with sesame.’ By ‘sā natthi’, he shows the dependence of the relative pronoun ‘yaṃ’ in the subsequent clause on the demonstrative pronoun ‘taṃ’ in the preceding clause. ‘Eko puriso’ is the connection. ‘Pūviyo’ means ‘a cake,’ or ‘buying and selling with a cake.’ ‘Tena’ means ‘for that reason.’ ‘Naṃ’ refers to the householder. ‘Thera’ refers to the Elder Sudhamma. In ‘yadeva kiñci’, showing that it is simply any word, he says, ‘just any word like “tilasaṃguḷikā.”’ ‘Idaṃ’ refers to this meaning. ‘So’ refers to the young cock. ‘Kākavassitaṃ’ means ‘the cry of a crow,’ and the connection is ‘he did not make.’ In ‘tayāpi’, the word ‘pi’ refers to the young cock. The explanation is that this shows the meaning that neither the monk’s words were spoken, nor the layperson’s words were spoken.

Adhammakammādidvādasakakathā

The Discussion on the Twelve Unrighteous Acts and So Forth

39. Purimehi kammehīti sambandho. Tatthāti aṅgesu. Yathā parisakkiyamāne gihino lābhaṃ na labhantīti yojanā. Paripubbo sakkadhātu parakkamatthoti āha “parakkamanto”ti. Tatthāti anatthādīsu[M 0.0414]. Atthabhaṅgoti gihīnaṃ atthassa bhaṅgo. Avasananti gihīnaṃ avasanaṃ. Gihīnanti ettha sāmyatthe sāmivacananti āha “gihīnaṃ santike”ti. Yathā kariyamāne sacco hoti, evaṃ na karotīti yojanā. Ekaṅgenāpīti pisaddo sambhāvanattho, tato adhikehi aṅgehi kā nāma kathāti dasseti. Etthāti paṭisāraṇīyakamme. Paṭimukhaṃ attano dosaṃ sarāpetabbaṃ anena vinayakammenāti paṭisāraṇīyaṃ, tameva kammaṃ paṭisāraṇīyakammaṃ.

39. ‘Purimehi kammehi’ is the connection. ‘Tattha’ refers to the constituents. The construction is: ‘just as laypeople do not gain profit when being served’. The root ‘sakk’ with the prefix ‘pari’ has the meaning of ‘effort’, hence he says, ‘striving’. ‘Tattha’ refers to disadvantages and so forth. ‘Atthabhaṅga’ means ‘the ruin of the laypeople’s welfare’. ‘Avasana’ means ‘the non-residence of laypeople’. In ‘gihīnaṃ’, here, it is a genitive case in the sense of proximity, hence he says, ‘in the vicinity of laypeople’. The construction is: he does not act in such a way that it would be true when done. In ‘ekaṅgenāpi’, the word ‘pi’ has the meaning of possibility, hence it shows, ‘what need be said of more constituents?’ ‘Herein’ refers to the act of reconciliation. ‘Paṭisāraṇīya’ is so called because by this disciplinary act one must be made to remember one's own fault face to face; that very act is the act of reconciliation.

5. Āpattiyā adassane ukkhepanīyakammakathā

5. An Account of the Act of Suspension for Non-acknowledgment of an Offense.

46. Saṃsathāti ettha saṃsadhātuyā kathanatthaṃ dassento āha “ārocethā”ti. Tumhe saṃsatha, kathethāti attho.

46. Here, in `saṃsatha`, showing that the root `saṃsa` has the meaning of 'to speak', he says, 'ārocetha'. The meaning is: 'You speak, you tell.'

50. Bhaṇḍanakārako hotītiādi kāraṇūpacāravasena vuttoti āha “bhaṇḍanādipaccayā”tiādi. Bhaṇḍanakārakādi kāraṇaṃ, tena āpannā āpatti phalaṃ, tassā adassane ukkhepanīyakammaṃ kātabbanti adhippāyo. Tassāti āpattiyā.

50. The phrase 'he is a quarrel-maker,' etc., is stated by way of causal imputation, hence it is said, 'due to quarrels, etc.' Being a quarrel-maker, etc., is the cause; the offense incurred thereby is the result. The intention is that the act of suspension should be performed for the non-acknowledgment of that offense. 'Of that' means of the offense.

51. Etthāti [V 2.0070] ukkhepanīyakamme. Tatthāti tecattālīsavattesu. Anuddhaṃsetabboti ettha dhaṃsadhātuyā gatyatthaṃ paṭikkhipanto āha “na codetabbo”ti. “Rajonuddhaṃsatī”tiādīsu (bu. vaṃ. 2.101) hi dhaṃsadhātu gatyatthe vattati. “Na bhikkhu bhikkhūhī”ti ettha soyeva bhikkhu teheva bhikkhūhīti atthaṃ nivārento āha “añño bhikkhu aññehi bhikkhūhī”ti. Na gihiddhajoti ettha gihīnaṃ dhajo gihiddhajoti vutte odātavatthādīnīti āha “odātavatthānī”tiādi. Na titthiyādipadattayanti “na titthiyā sevitabbā, bhikkhū sevitabbā, bhikkhusikkhāya sikkhitabba”nti padānaṃ tayaṃ. “Na apasādetabbo”ti iminā na āsādetabboti ettha āpubbasadadhātuyā apapubbasadadhātuyā samānabhāvaṃ dasseti. “Anto vā bahi vāti” ettha kassa anto vā bahi vāti āha “vihārassā”ti. Sesaṃ sabbaṃvattanti [M 0.0415] yojanā. Imināti āpattiyā adassane ukkhepanīyakammena.

51. ‘Ettha’ refers to the act of suspension. ‘Tattha’ refers to the forty-three duties. Regarding 'anuddhaṃsetabbo', here, rejecting the meaning of movement for the root 'dhaṃsa,' he says, 'should not be reproached.' Indeed, in phrases like 'Rajonuddhaṃsatī' (Bu Va 2.101), the root 'dhaṃsa' is used in the sense of movement. Regarding 'a monk by monks,' here, preventing the meaning that the same monk is reproached by the same monks, he says, 'another monk by other monks.' Regarding 'not the banner of householders,' here, when 'gihiddhaja' is said to be 'the banner of householders', he says 'white cloths, etc.', referring to white cloths and so on. 'Not the triad of statements concerning sectarians' means the three statements: 'Sectarians should not be associated with, monks should be associated with, and one should train in the training of monks.' By 'na apasādetabbo' (should not be disparaged), he shows the similarity between the root 'sad' with the prefix 'ā' (in āsādetabbo) and the root 'sad' with the prefix 'apa'. Regarding 'inside or outside,' here, asking 'inside or outside of what?' he says, 'of the monastery.' The construction is: the rest is all the duties. 'By this' means by the act of suspension for non-acknowledgment of an offense.

65. Tassāti āpattiyā. Idhāti pāpikāya diṭṭhiyā appaṭinissagge kate ukkhepanīyakamme. Āpattiadassanādīsu uddharitvā khipīyati apanīyati anena vinayakammenāti ukkhepanīyaṃ, tameva kammaṃ ukkhepanīyakammaṃ.

65. 'Of that' means of the offense. 'Here' means in the act of suspension performed when there is non-relinquishment of a wrong view. Because one is lifted up, thrown out, and removed by this disciplinary act in cases of non-acknowledgment of an offense, etc., it is called 'ukkhepanīya'; that very act is the act of suspension.

Iti kammakkhandhakavaṇṇanāya yojanā samattā.

Thus ends the exposition in the commentary on the Chapter on Formal Acts.

2. Pārivāsikakkhandhakaṃ

2. The Chapter on Probation

1. Pārivāsikavattakathā

1. An Account of the Duties of One on Probation.

75. Pārivāsikakkhandhake pārivāsikāti padassa parivāsaṃ parivasantīti pārivāsikāti dassento āha “parivāsaṃ parivasantā”ti. Tatthāti “parivāsaṃ parivasantā”ti taddhitavākye. Tesūti catubbidhesu parivāsesu. Titthiyaparivāsoti titthiyānaṃ parivāso, titthiyānaṃ vā dātabbo parivāso, titthiyehi vā parivasitabbo parivāso titthiyaparivāso. Appaṭicchannaparivāsoti appaṭicchanno parivāso appaṭicchannaparivāso. Tatthāti appaṭicchannaparivāse. Yanti vacanaṃ. Ayaṃ panāti ayaṃ paṭicchannaparivāso pana. Idhāti [V 2.0071] pārivāsikakkhandhake. Sesāti appaṭicchannaparivāsato sesā. Tayoti appaṭicchannaparivāsādayo tayo, dātabbāti sambandho. Kassa dātabbāti āha “yenā”tiādi. Āpannā cevāti āpajjitabbā ceva. Tesūti tividhesu parivāsesu. Ete panāti tayo pana. Idhāti pārivāsikakkhandhake. Tasmāti yasmā idha adhippetā, tasmā. Etesūti tividhesu parivāsesu.

75. In the Chapter on Probation, showing that the word 'pārivāsikā' means 'they undergo probation, therefore they are probationers,' he says, 'those who are undergoing probation.' 'There' means in the taddhita expression 'parivāsaṃ parivasantā.' 'Among these' means among the four kinds of probation. 'Probation for sectarians' means the probation of sectarians, or the probation to be given to sectarians, or the probation to be undergone by sectarians is 'probation for sectarians'. 'Unconcealed probation' means probation that is unconcealed is 'unconcealed probation'. 'There' means in unconcealed probation. 'Yanti' is the word. 'But this' means this concealed probation. 'Here' means in the Chapter on Probation. 'The rest' means those remaining from unconcealed probation. 'Three' means the three, beginning with unconcealed probation; 'are to be given' is the connection. To whom are they to be given? He explains, 'by whom,' etc. 'And having committed' also means 'and being liable to commit.' 'Among these' means among the three kinds of probation. 'But these' means these three. 'Here' means in the Chapter on Probation. 'Therefore' means: because they are intended here, therefore. 'Among these' means among the three kinds of probation.

Pakatattānaṃ bhikkhūnanti ettha adhippetapakatatte dassento āha “ṭhapetvā”tiādi. Mūlāyapaṭikassanārahādīnampīti ettha ādisaddena mānattārahamānattacārikaabbhānārahādayo saṅgaṇhāti. Pisaddena pakatipakatattaṃ apekkhati. Teti pakatattā. Yaṃ abhivādanādiṃ karontīti [M 0.0416] yojanā. Sādiyantīti ettha sādiyanaṃ nāma sampaṭicchananti āha “sampaṭicchantī”ti. Tatthāti abhivādanādīsu, niddhāraṇe cetaṃ bhummavacanaṃ. Sāmīcikammanti etaṃ ābhisamācārikassa adhivacananti yojanā. Abhivādanādīnīti abhivādanapaccuṭṭhānaañjalikammāni. Bījanavātadānādinoti bījaniyā paharitena pavattassa vātassa dānādino. Āsanābhihāranti ettha abhiharaṇaṃ abhihāro, āsanassa abhihāro āsanābhihāroti vacanatthaṃ dassento āha “āsanassa abhiharaṇa”nti. Paññāpanampi abhiharitvā paññāpitattā abhihāroyeva nāmāti āha “paññāpanameva vā”ti. “Pādadhovanaudaka”nti iminā pādassa dhovanaṃ udakaṃ pādodakanti vacanatthaṃ dasseti. “Pādaṭṭhapanaka”nti iminā pādassa ṭhapanakaṃ pīṭhaṃ pādapīṭhanti vacanatthaṃ dasseti. “Pādaghaṃsanaṃ vā”ti iminā pādassa ghaṃsanaṃ kathalikaṃ pādakathalikanti vacanatthaṃ dasseti. Saddhivihārikānampi abhivādanādinti sambandho. Pisaddena aññesaṃ sādiyantassa kā nāma kathāti dasseti. Teti saddhivihārikā. Saddhāpabbajitāti saddhāya pabbajitā. Kulaputtāti jātikulaputtā, ācārakulaputtā ca. Karonti, āpucchantiyevāti sambandho. Vāritampi asādiyanaṃ nāmāti āha “vāritakālato paṭṭhāya anāpattī”ti. Mithu yathāvuḍḍhanti ettha mithusaddo aññamaññapariyāyo, yathāsaddo yaṃsaddapariyāyo, vicchattho cāti āha “aññamaññaṃ yo yo vuḍḍho”ti. Aññamaññañhi mithati saṅgamaṃ karotīti mithūti vuccati. Tena tenāti bhikkhunā, “sāditu”nti pade bhāvakattā. Sādituṃ anujānāmīti sambandho.

Regarding 'monks of normal status,' here, showing what is meant by 'of normal status,' he says, 'excluding,' etc. Regarding 'of those deserving to be sent back to the beginning, etc.,' here, the word 'etc.' includes those deserving of penance, those undergoing penance, those deserving of rehabilitation, and so on. The particle 'pi' refers to the naturally normal status. They are the ones of normal status. The construction is 'who perform acts of homage, etc.' Regarding 'sādiyanti' (they consent), here, he says that 'sādiyana' (consenting) means 'sampaṭicchana' (accepting), thus 'they accept.' 'There' means in acts of homage, etc.; and this is a locative expression indicating specification. The construction is that 'sāmīcikamma' (proper conduct) is a designation for 'ābhisamācārika' (courtesy). 'Acts of homage, etc.' means paying homage, rising to greet, and making reverential gestures. 'Of giving wind from a fan, etc.' refers to giving wind produced by fanning with a fan, and so on. Regarding 'āsanābhihāra' (offering a seat), here, showing the meaning of the word, he says that 'abhiharaṇa' is 'abhihāra,' and the offering of a seat is 'āsanābhihāra,' thus 'the offering of a seat.' He says that 'preparing' is also called 'offering' because it is prepared after being brought, thus 'or simply preparing.' By 'pādadhovanaudaka' (water for washing the feet), he shows the meaning of 'pādodaka' as water for washing the feet. By 'pādaṭṭhapanaka' (a footrest), he shows the meaning of 'pādapīṭha' as a stool for placing the feet. By 'pādaghaṃsanaṃ vā' (or rubbing the feet), he shows the meaning of 'pādakathalika' as a foot-scraper. The connection is 'homage, etc., even of co-residents.' The particle 'pi' indicates, 'What need is there to speak of others who consent?' They are the co-residents. 'Those who have gone forth out of faith' means those who have gone forth through faith. 'Sons of good families' means those born into good families and those of virtuous conduct. The connection is 'they do,' 'they take leave.' He says that 'even what is forbidden is called not consenting,' thus 'from the time of being forbidden, there is no offense.' Regarding 'mithu yathāvuḍḍhaṃ' (mutually, according to seniority), here, he says that the word 'mithu' is synonymous with 'to one another,' the word 'yathā' is synonymous with 'whichever,' and it has a distributive meaning, thus 'whichever is senior to the other.' Indeed, 'mithu' is so called because it unites one with another. The connection is 'by that monk,' because the word 'sādituṃ' implies an agent. The connection is 'I allow them to consent.'

“Vuḍḍhapaṭipāṭiyā”ti iminā vuḍḍhānaṃ paṭipāṭi yathāvuḍḍhanti catutthīabyayībhāvaṃ dasseti. Purimapade pana paṭhamāabyayībhāvo. Pāḷiyāti pantiyā. Tatthevāti saṅghanavakaṭṭhāne eva. Pavāraṇāyapīti [V 2.0072] pisaddena na kevalaṃ uposatheyeva, atha kho pavāraṇāyapīti dasseti. Saṅghena bhājiyamānanti sambandho.

By 'vuḍḍhapaṭipāṭiyā,' he shows an avyayībhāva compound in the dative sense, meaning 'yathāvuḍḍhaṃ' (according to seniority), the order of the elders. In the preceding word, however, it is an avyayībhāva compound in the nominative sense. 'Pāḷiyā' means 'in the row.' 'Tattheva' means 'right there in the place of the junior-most monk of the Sangha.' By the particle 'pi' in 'pavāraṇāyapi,' he shows that it is not only for the Uposatha but also for the Pavāraṇā. The connection is 'being distributed by the Sangha.'

Oṇojananti avanudate oṇojanaṃ. Avapubbo nudadhātu nakārassa ṇakāraṃ, dakārassa ca jakāraṃ katvā oṇojananti vuccati. Nudadhātu [M 0.0417] apanayanattho, tena vuttaṃ “vissajjanaṃ vuccatī”ti. Uddesabhattādīnītiādisaddena salākabhattādīni saṅgaṇhāti. Assāti pārivāsikassa. Tānīti dve tīṇi uddesabhattādīni. Heṭṭhāti attano heṭṭhā. Gāhethāti navakatare bhikkhū gāhāpetha. Bhattapaccāsāti bhattameva paccāsā bhattapaccāsā, paccāsābhattanti attho. “Vissajjetabbānī”ti iminā avanuditabbanti oṇojananti atthaṃ dasseti. Evanti gahetvā vissajjamāneti yojanā. Tānīti uddesabhattādīni. Yadi pana na gaṇhātīti sace saṅghato vassaggena na gaṇhāti. Na vissajjetīti sace aññassa na vissajjeti. Odissāti uddisitvā. Tassāti pārivāsikassa. Hīti yasmā. Saṅghanavakaṭṭhāne nisinnassa tassāti yojanā. Bhattaggeti bhattassa gahaṇaṭṭhāne. Soti pārivāsiko, mā kilamitthāti sambandho. Idanti oṇojanaṃ. Assāti pārivāsikassa, anuññātanti sambandho.

'Oṇojana' means 'removing' or 'dismissing.' It is called 'oṇojana' by transforming the 'n' into 'ṇ' and the 'd' into 'j' from the root 'nud' with the prefix 'ava.' The root 'nud' means 'to remove,' hence it is said, 'it is called dismissal.' By the word 'etc.' in 'uddesabhattādīni' (assigned meals, etc.), he includes things like ticket meals, etc. 'Assa' means 'of the probationer.' 'Those' means those two or three assigned meals, etc. 'Heṭṭhā' means 'below oneself.' 'Gāhetha' means 'make the newer monks take/receive.' 'Bhattapaccāsā' means 'the expectation of a meal,' that is, the meal itself is the expectation, or the expectation is for the meal. By 'vissajjetabbāni' (should be dismissed), he shows the meaning of 'oṇojana' as 'should be removed.' The construction is: 'Thus, having taken, one dismisses it.' 'Those' refers to the assigned meals, etc. 'But if he does not accept' means if he does not accept it from the Sangha by seniority of rains. 'If he does not dismiss' means if he does not dismiss it to another. 'Odissa' means 'having assigned.' 'Tassa' means 'of the probationer.' 'Hi' means 'because.' The construction is 'of him sitting in the place of the Sangha's junior members.' 'Bhattagga' means 'at the place of meal acceptance.' The connection is 'that probationer, do not tire yourself.' 'This' refers to the oṇojana. The connection is 'of the probationer, it is allowed.'

Āgatāgatehi bhikkhūhīti sambandho. Catussālabhattanti catumukhā sālā catussālā bhojanasālā, tattha paṭipāṭiyā dinnaṃ bhattaṃ catussālabhattaṃ. Etanti catussālabhattaṃ. Pāḷiyāti bhikkhūnaṃ pāḷiyā. Osakkitvāti heṭṭhā sakkitvā. Hatthapāseti bhattadāyakassa hatthapāse. Senoti kulalo. “Ārāmikasamaṇuddesehī”ti padaṃ “āharāpetu”nti pade kāritakammaṃ. Sayamevāti pārivāsikena anāṇatto hutvā sayameva. Mahāpeḷabhattepīti mahatiyaṃ peḷāyaṃ pakkhipitvā dinne bhattepi. Yattha panāti parivisaṭṭhāne pana.

The connection is 'by the monks who have come.' 'Catussālabhatta' means a four-sided hall, which is a dining hall; the meal given there in turn is called 'catussālabhatta.' 'Etaṃ' means this 'catussālabhatta.' 'Pāḷiyā' means 'according to the row of monks.' 'Osakkitvā' means 'having moved down.' 'Hatthapāse' means 'within arm's reach of the one giving food.' 'Sena' means 'a hawk.' The word 'ārāmikasamaṇuddesehī' is the causative object in the word 'āharāpetu.' 'Sayameva' means 'by oneself,' having not been instructed by the probationer. 'Mahāpeḷabhattepi' means even with food given after being placed in a large basket. 'Yattha pana' means, however, in the place where it is served.

76. Tatrāyaṃ sammāvattanāti ettha tasaddassa aniyamaniddesabhāvaṃ dassento āha “idāni yā ayaṃ sammāvattanā vuttā”ti. Sammā vattitabbaṃ etāyāti sammāvattanā. Tatthāti sammāvattanāyaṃ. Na upasampādetabbanti ettha ācariyena hutvā kammavācāsāvanampi upasampādanamevāti āha “ācariyena hutvāpi kammavācā na sāvetabbā”ti. Aññasmiṃ asatīti attanā aññasmiṃ kammavācāvācake asati. Na nissayo dātabboti ettha āgantukānameva nissayo na dātabbo, na dinnanissayānampīti dassento āha “āgantukānaṃ nissayo [M 0.0418] na dātabbo”tiādi, yehipi bhikkhūhi gahitoti sambandho.

76. Here, regarding 'this is the proper procedure': showing the unspecified nature of the word 'tatra' in this context, he says, 'Now, this proper procedure has been stated.' Because one should properly conduct oneself by it, it is the proper procedure. 'There' means in this proper procedure. Regarding 'one should not confer the full ordination,' showing that even reciting the Kammavācā as a preceptor is considered ordination, he says, 'Even acting as the preceptor, the Kammavācā should not be recited.' 'When another is not present' means when there is no other reciter of the Kammavācā apart from oneself. Regarding 'reliance should not be given,' showing that reliance should not be given only to newcomers, and not to those to whom reliance has already been given, he says, 'Reliance should not be given to newcomers,' and so forth; the connection is with 'by whichever monks it has been taken.'

Añño [V 2.0073] sāmaṇeroti pakatattakāle upajjhaṃ datvā gahitasāmaṇerehi añño sāmaṇero. Ādhipaccaṭṭhānabhūtāti sabbasammutīnaṃ adhipatibhāvassa ṭhānabhūtā. Paṭibalassāti bhikkhuniyo ovadituṃ paṭibalassa. Iminā laddhasammutikena āṇatto aladdhasammutikopi garudhammehi vā aññehi vā bhikkhuniyo ovadituṃ labhatīti dasseti. Āgatā bhikkhuniyo vattabbāti sambandho. Voti tumhākaṃ. Soti bhikkhu. Voti tumhākaṃ, dassatīti sambandho.

'Another novice' means a novice other than those accepted by giving an upajjhāya while one is in a normal state. 'The basis of authority' means being the basis for the state of being the master of all agreements. 'Capable' means capable of advising the bhikkhunīs. By this, it is shown that even one who has not obtained the agreement, if commanded by one who has obtained the agreement, can advise the bhikkhunīs by means of the grave rules or other matters. The connection is: 'The bhikkhunīs who have come should be spoken to.' 'Vo' means 'of you.' 'So' means 'a bhikkhu.' 'Vo' means 'of you'; the connection is with 'dassati' (he will give).

Sukkavissaṭṭhiyāti sukkavissaṭṭhiāpattikāraṇā. Kāyasaṃsaggādigarukāpatti nāpajjitabbāti yojanā. Āpattikkhandhavasena āpattivatthūnaṃ pāpiṭṭhabhāvañca pāpiṭṭhatarabhāvañca vitthārento āha “sattasu hī”tiādi. Pāpiṭṭhatarāti dubbhāsitāpattito dukkaṭāpatti pāpiṭṭhatarā. Tāsanti sattannaṃ āpattīnaṃ. Purimanayenevāti purimānaṃ āpattīnaṃ nayeneva. Bhedoti vatthūnaṃ viseso. Evaṃ āpattikkhandhavasena āpattivatthūnaṃ pāpiṭṭhapāpiṭṭhatarabhāvaṃ dassetvā idāni sikkhāpadavasena tesaṃ taṃ dassento āha “paṇṇattivajjasikkhāpade panā”tiādi. Ubhayampīti vatthuāpattisaṅkhātaṃ ubhayampi.

'Sukkavissaṭṭhi' means because of the cause for the offense of emission of semen. The connection is: one should not incur grave offenses such as bodily contact, and so forth. Explaining the state of being most blameworthy and more blameworthy of the bases for offenses in terms of the categories of offenses, he says, 'Among the seven,' and so forth. 'More blameworthy' means the dukkaṭa offense is more blameworthy than the dubbhāsita offense. 'Tāsaṃ' means of those seven offenses. 'Purimanayeneva' means in the same way as the previous offenses. 'Bhedo' means the distinction of the bases. Having thus shown the state of being most blameworthy and more blameworthy of the bases for offenses in terms of the categories of offenses, now, showing this in terms of the training rules, he says, 'But in the case of a training rule that is an offense by prescription,' and so forth. 'Ubhayampi' means both, that is, both what is designated as the base and the offense.

Kammanti ettha kāraṇabhūtassa kammassa nāmaṃ kāriyabhūtāyaṃ kammavācāyaṃ upacāravasena kāriyabhūtā kammavācā kammanti vuccatīti āha “parivāsakammavācā vuccatī”ti. Kammasmiṃ sati, kammena vā vacitabbāti kammavācāti vacanattho kātabbo. Kasikammanti kasisaṅkhātaṃ kammaṃ. Gorakkhakammanti gorakkhasaṅkhātaṃ kammaṃ. “Kammaṃ kata”nti iminā kammaṃ karontīti kammikāti vacanatthaṃ dasseti. Teti kammikā bhikkhū, na garahitabbāti sambandho.

Regarding 'kamma': here, because the kammavācā, which is the effect, is figuratively called 'kamma'—the name of the act which is the cause—he says, 'it is called the parivāsakammavācā.' The meaning of the word 'kammavācā' should be understood as 'that which should be spoken when there is an act, or by means of an act.' 'Kasikamma' means the action known as plowing. 'Gorakkhakamma' means the action known as cattle-tending. By 'kammaṃ kataṃ' (an act was done), he shows the meaning of the word 'kammikā' as 'those who perform actions.' 'Te' means those bhikkhus who are kammikā; the connection is that they should not be criticized.

Vacitabbaṃ anena dosenāti vacanīyaṃ, saṃvijjati vacanīyaṃ assāti savacanīyaṃ, taṃ na kātabbanti attho. Tamevatthaṃ vitthārento āha “palibodhatthāya hī”tiādi. Yāva na taṃ [M 0.0419] adhikaraṇaṃ vūpasantaṃ hoti, tāva imamhā āvāsā ekapadampi mā pakkāmīti yojanā. Teti tuyhaṃ.

'Vacanīya' means blameworthy because of this fault. 'Savacanīya' means he has something blameworthy; the meaning is that this should not be done. Elaborating on this very point, he says, 'For the sake of obstruction,' and so forth. The construction is: 'Until that legal issue is settled, do not depart even a single step from this monastery.' 'Te' means 'to you.'

Anuvādoti ettha anusāsanavasena aññe vadatīti anuvādoti vutte jeṭṭhakaṭṭhānanti āha “vihāre jeṭṭhakaṭṭhānaṃ na kātabba”nti. Jeṭṭhakaṭṭhānaṃ sarūpena dassento āha “pātimokkhuddesakena vā”tiādi. Meti mayhaṃ. Tanti tavaṃ. Na codetabboti ettha kena na codetabboti āha “vatthunā vā āpattiyā vā”ti. Na sāretabboti na sarāpetabbo. Na bhikkhūhi [V 2.0074] sampayojetabbanti ettha bhikkhūhi attanā kalahavasena na sampayojetabbanti dassento āha “aññamaññaṃ yojetvā kalaho na kāretabbo”ti.

Here, regarding 'anuvāda': when it is said, 'one who speaks to others by way of instruction,' he says this means a 'jeṭṭhakaṭṭhāna' (position of seniority), and says, 'a position of seniority should not be taken in the monastery.' To show what constitutes a position of seniority, he says, 'by being the reciter of the Pātimokkha,' and so forth. 'Me' means 'of me.' 'Ta' means 'you.' Regarding 'should not be accused,' he says by what one should not be accused: 'by the matter or by the offense.' 'Should not be reminded' means one should not be made to remember. Regarding 'should not engage with the bhikkhus,' to show that one should not engage with bhikkhus by way of a quarrel, he says, 'having incited them against one another, a quarrel should not be caused.'

Saṅghattherena hutvāti saṅghattherena hontenapīti attho. Purato agantabbe samāne kiṃ pacchato gantabbanti āha “dvādasahattha”ntiādi. Āsanapariyantoti āsanameva pariyanto lāmakoti āsanapariyanto, tadatthaṃ dassento āha “saṅghanavakāsanaṃ vuccatī”ti. Svāssāti so assa. Soti āsanapariyanto. Assāti pārivāsikassa. Tatthāti āsanapariyante. Ayanti pārivāsiko, na labhatīti sambandho. Gahitāvasesāti gahitāhi seyyāhi avasesā. Maṅgulagūthabharitāti maṅgulānaṃ gūthehi pūritā. Assāti pārivāsikassa. Rajehi hatā nāsitā bhūmi etthāti rajohatabhūmi. Jatukamūsikabharitāti jatūhi ca mūsikāhi ca pūritā. Paṇṇasālāti paṇṇehi chāditā sālā. Assāti pārivāsikassa. Sabbepi āvāsāti yojanā. Etehīti pakatattehi. Tesūti āvāsesu. Yanti āvāsaṃ. Paccayanti vassāvāsikalābhaṃ. Ekapasseti bhikkhūnaṃ pāḷiyaṃ aṭṭhatvā ekasmiṃ passe.

'Having become a senior in the Saṅgha' means even if one has become a senior in the Saṅgha. When it is proper to go in front, why go behind? He says, 'twelve hands,' and so forth. 'The limit of the seat' means the seat itself is the limit, and it is inferior; to explain its meaning, he says, 'it is called the Saṅgha’s junior’s seat.' 'Svāssa' means 'so, his.' 'So' means the limit of the seat. 'Assa' means 'of the probationer.' 'Tattha' means at the limit of the seat. 'Ayaṃ' means the probationer; the connection is that he does not obtain. 'The remaining taken' means the remainder of the beds that have been taken. 'Filled with the dung of mongooses' means filled with the excrement of mongooses. 'Assa' means 'of the probationer.' 'Ground destroyed by dust' means ground covered with dust. 'Filled with bats and mice' means filled with bats and mice. 'A leaf hut' means a hut covered with leaves. 'Assa' means 'of the probationer.' The construction is: 'All the dwellings.' 'By these' means by those who are in their normal state. 'Tesū' means in those dwellings. 'Yanti' means 'they go to the dwelling.' 'Paccayanti' means 'they obtain the gains of the rains residence.' 'Ekapasse' means not standing in the bhikkhus’ line, but on one side.

Assāti pārivāsikassa, dentīti sambandho. So evāti āsanādipariyanto eva. Ñātipavāritaṭṭhāne nimantitenāti sambandho. Tatthāti [M 0.0420] taṃ kulaṃ. Saṃvidhāyāti saṃvidahitvā. Assāti kulassa, bhaveyya vā.

“Assa” means the probationer’s; the connection is with “they give.” “So eva” means just the limit of seats, and so forth. The connection is with “invited in a place warded off by relatives.” “Tattha” means that family. “Saṃvidhāya” means having arranged. “Assa” means of the family; “bhaveyya vā” means may be.

Harāyamānenāti lajjamānena. Yenāpīti pārivāsikenapi. Samādinnanti āraññikadhutaṅgasamādinnaṃ. Tathāti yathā āraññikaṅgaṃ na samādātabbaṃ, tathā. Piṇḍapātikadhutaṅgampīti pisaddo āraññikaṅgaṃ apekkhati. Yo panāti pārivāsiko pana.

“Harāyamānena” means feeling shame. “Yenāpi” means even by the probationer. “Samādinnaṃ” means undertaken the forest-dwelling ascetic practice. “Tathā” means just as the forest-dwelling practice should not be undertaken, so too. “Piṇḍapātikadhutaṅgampi” means the word ‘pi’ (also) refers back to the forest-dwelling practice. “Yo pana” means but the probationer.

Anārocentassa meti yojanā. Anārocente satīti vā yojanā. “Iminā kāraṇenā”ti iminā tappaccayāti ettha paccayasaddo kāraṇattho, nissakkavacanañca kāraṇatthe hotīti dasseti. So ratticchedo eva paccayo tappaccayoti vacanattho kātabbo. “Sāmaṇerehī”ti padaṃ “pacāpetvā”ti pade kāritakammaṃ. Etthāpi pakatiyā nīharāpetvāpi vihāre pacāpetvāpi bhuñjantassa paṭisedho natthi. Kasmā? “Tappaccayā”ti vuttattā. Gāmeti mahāgāme, sabbakālaṃ anekasatehi bhikkhūhi avivitte gāmeti attho. Gāmakāvāsanti gāmoyeva khuddakaṭṭhena gāmako, tasmiṃ kārito āvāso gāmakāvāso, taṃ.

The construction is “for me who does not announce.” Or, the construction is “when not announcing.” Regarding “iminā kāraṇenā” (by this reason) and “tappaccayā” (because of that), here the word “paccaya” has the meaning of “cause,” and it shows that the ablative case also occurs in the meaning of “cause.” The meaning of the word “tappaccayoti” should be understood as “that cutting off of the night is the very cause.” The word “sāmaṇerehi” (by the novices) is the causative object in the word “pacāpetvā” (having had cooked). Here too, there is no prohibition even if one has had food brought out from its natural state, or having had it cooked in the monastery and then eats it. Why? Because it is said, “because of that.” “Gāma” means a large village; the meaning is a village not secluded, always crowded with many hundreds of monks. “Gāmakāvāsa” means a village itself, by way of being small, is a “gāmaka”; the dwelling made in that is a “gāmakāvāsa.”

Gatena [V 2.0075] āgantukapārivāsikenāti sambandho. Tatthāti kismiñci vihāre, sabbe bhikkhūti sambandho. Tattha tatthāti tasmiṃ tasmiṃ ṭhitaṭṭhāne. Na ekacce passati, apassitattā nāroceti, ratticchedova hotīti adhippāyo.

The connection is with “by the incoming probationer who has gone.” “Tattha” means in a certain monastery; the connection is with “all the bhikkhus.” “Tattha tattha” means in that very place where they are standing. The intention is that some do not see, and because of not seeing, they do not inform, so there is a break in the night.

Ekassa vā bahūnaṃ vā āgantukānanti sambandho. Etthāti “āgantukassa ārocetabba”nti pade. Vuttanayenevāti “āgantukena ārocetabba”nti pade vuttanayeneva. Taṃ vuttanayamāvikaronto āha “sace”tiādi. Tesampīti āgantukānampi. Tassāti pārivāsikassa. Ajānantassevāti anādare cetaṃ sāmivacanaṃ. Ayañca panāti pārivāsiko ca. Gatakāleti āgantukānaṃ gatakāle. Yepīti āgantukāpi. Okkamitvāti osaritvā, pavisitvāti attho. Ayañcāti pārivāsiko ca, jānātīti sambandho. Nesanti āgantukānaṃ. Yopīti āgantukopi. Assāti [M 0.0421] pārivāsikassa. Aññātattāti āgatabhāvassa ajānitattā. “Abbhāna”nti padaṃ “karotī”ti pade kammaṃ, “hotī”ti pade kattā. Adhikā rattiyoti āpattipaṭicchannarattito adhikā rattiyo. Ayanti pārivāsikavattapaṭipadā. Apaṇṇakapaṭipadāti aviraddhapaṭipadā, ekaṃsapaṭipadāti attho.

The connection is with “whether for one or for many guests.” “Ettha” means in the phrase “the guest should be informed.” “Vuttanayeneva” means in the same way as stated in the phrase “should be informed by the guest.” Explaining that method, he says, “if,” and so forth. “Tesampi” means for the guests too. “Tassa” means for the probationer. “Ajānantasseva” means this is the genitive case indicating disregard. “Ayañca pana” means and this probationer. “Gatakāle” means at the time when the guests have left. “Yepī” means even the guests. “Okkamitvā” means having withdrawn, meaning having entered. “Ayañca” means and this probationer; the connection is that he knows. “Nesaṃ” means for the guests. “Yopi” means even the guest. “Assa” means for the probationer. “Aññātattā” means because of not knowing the fact of having arrived. The word “abbhāna” is the object in the phrase “does,” and the subject in the phrase “is.” “Adhikā rattiyo” means more nights than those required to conceal the offense. “Ayaṃ” means this is the practice of the pārivāsika vow. “Apaṇṇakapaṭipadā” means the uncorrupted practice, the meaning is the one-sided practice.

Gacchantampi bhikkhunti sambandho. Sāvetunti suṇāpetuṃ. Visayāvisayenāti ārocetuṃ desādesena. Karavīkatissatthero āhāti sambandho.

The connection is with “even the bhikkhu who is going.” “Sāvetuṃ” means to make heard. “Visayāvisayena” means to announce by specifying the territory or non-territory. The connection is: The Elder Karavīka Tissa said.

“Uposathadivase”ti iminā uposatheti ettha uposathasaddassa pātimokkhuddesādayo atthe nivatteti. Pavāraṇāyapīti pavāraṇadivasepi. Gantunti bhikkhussa ṭhitaṭṭhānaṃ gantuṃ. Dūtenāpīti ettha anadhippetadūtaṃ paṭikkhipitvā adhippetadūtaṃ dassetuṃ vuttaṃ “anupasampannaṃ…pe… ārocāpetabba”nti.

By “Uposathadivase,” the word “Uposatha” here excludes meanings such as the recitation of the Pātimokkha. “Pavāraṇāyapi” means also on the Pavāraṇā day. “Gantuṃ” means to go to the standing place of a bhikkhu. Regarding “Dūtenāpi” (even by a messenger), here, to reject an unauthorized messenger and show an authorized messenger, it is said, “An unordained person… should be informed.”

Suññavihāroti bhikkhūhi vivittavihāro. Yatthāti yasmiṃ āvāse. Hīti saccaṃ, yasmā vā. Tatthāti suññavihāre. Dasavidhantarāye sati pana gantabbamevāti yojanā. Nānāsaṃvāsakehīti kammanānāsaṃvāsakaladdhinānāsaṃvāsakehi.

A 'suññavihāra' is a dwelling secluded from bhikkhus. 'Yatthāti' means 'in which dwelling'. 'Hīti' means 'truly' or 'because'. 'Tatthāti' means 'in the solitary dwelling'. The construction is that when there are ten kinds of dangers, one must go. 'Nānāsaṃvāsakehīti' refers to those with whom there is non-communion due to differences in kamma or differences in views.

81. Āvāsādīnaṃ sarūpaṃ dassento āha “āvāso nāmā”tiādi. Tatiyapadenāti “āvāse vā anāvāse vā”ti tatiyapadena. Etesūti āvāsādīsu. Chadanatoti chadanakoṭito. Antoāvāseti bhittiparicchinne antoāvāse. Avisesenāti “ukkhittako”ti [V 2.0076] vā “pārivāsiko”ti vā visesaṃ akatvā sāmaññena. Udakapātenāti chadanato udakaṃ patati etthāti udakapāto, tena. Pañcavaṇṇacchadanabaddhaṭṭhānesūti pañcapamāṇena chadanena baddhaṭṭhānesu etesu āvāsesūti sambandho. Pārivāsikassa ca ukkhittakassa ca pakatattena saddhiṃ vāritanti yojanā. Nānūpacārepīti pisaddena ekūpacāre pana kā nāma kathāti dasseti[M 0.0422]. Etthāti ekacchanne āvāsādike, sace nipajjatīti sambandho. Tasminti saṭṭhivassepi pārivāsike.

81. To show the characteristics of dwellings and the like, it is said, 'A dwelling is called...' and so on. 'Tatiyapadenāti' refers to the third phrase, 'whether in a dwelling or in a non-dwelling'. 'Etesūti' means 'among these dwellings and the like'. 'Chadanatoti' means 'from the edge of the roof'. 'Antoāvāseti' means 'in an inner dwelling enclosed by walls'. 'Avisesenāti' means 'without making a distinction, such as 'one under suspension' or 'one undergoing penance,' but generally'. 'Udakapātenāti' means 'where water falls from the roof'—thus, 'by the water drip'. 'Pañcavaṇṇacchadanabaddhaṭṭhānesūti' means 'in places that are joined by a five-sectioned roof'—this is the connection regarding these dwellings. The construction is: it is forbidden for a probationer and one under suspension to be together with a monk in good standing. 'Nānūpacārepīti'—with the 'pi' particle, it is shown what need be said about a single approach. 'Etthāti'—here, in a dwelling having a single roof and the like, if one lies down—this is the connection. 'Tasminti'—even in the case of one who has been undergoing penance for sixty years.

Vuṭṭhātabbaṃ, nimantetabboti ettha kiṃ attano vuḍḍhataraṃ pakatattaṃ disvā vuṭṭhātabbaṃ, nimantetabboti āha “tadahupasampannampī”tiādi. Obuddhanti palibuddhaṃ. Ekāsaneti ettha ekasaddo samānapariyāyoti āha “samānavassikāsane”ti, samānavassikānaṃ āsaneti attho. Chamāyaṃ nisinneti ettha chamāsaddo bhūmipariyāyoti āha “bhūmiyaṃ nisinne”ti. Itarenāti pārivāsikena. Sahāyena saddhiṃ caṅkamati viyāti yojanā. “Ekasmiṃ caṅkame”ti iminā ekacaṅkamasaddassa tulyādhikaraṇasamāsavākyaṃ dasseti.

'Vuṭṭhātabbaṃ, nimantetabboti'—here, seeing one's own elder in good standing, should one rise or invite? This is explained by 'tadahupasampannampīti' and so on. 'Obuddhanti' means 'obstructed'. 'Ekāsaneti'—here, the word 'eka' has the same meaning as 'same'—thus, 'on a seat of the same seniority,' meaning a seat for those of the same seniority. 'Chamāyaṃ nisinneti'—here, the word 'chamā' means 'ground'—thus, 'sitting on the ground'. 'Itarenāti' means 'by the probationer'. The construction is: ‘as if one walks with a companion’. 'Ekasmiṃ caṅkame'—by this, a compound word in apposition is shown.

Chamāyaṃ caṅkamantanti ettha bhummatthe upayogavacananti āha “chamāyaṃ caṅkamante”ti. Ayaṃ panāti vakkhamāno pana. Etthāti “chamāyaṃ caṅkamante”ti pāṭhe. Caṅkamanteti pakatatte caṅkamante. Na caṅkamitabbanti pārivāsikena na caṅkamitabbaṃ. Ko pana vādo iṭṭhakācayasampanne vedikāparikkhitte iti atthoti yojanā. Pabbatantaravanantaragumbantaresūti pabbatamajjhavanamajjhagumbamajjhesu, pabbatavivaravanavivaragumbavivaresu vā. Upacāranti dvādasahatthaṃ upacāraṃ.

'Chamāyaṃ caṅkamantanti'—here, it is said that 'chamāyaṃ caṅkamante' is an instance of the locative case in the sense of location. 'Ayaṃ panāti'—but 'pana' refers to what is to be stated. 'Etthāti'—in the reading 'chamāyaṃ caṅkamante'. ‘Caṅkamanteti’ means when the one in good standing is walking. 'Na caṅkamitabbanti'—the one undergoing penance should not walk. What need is there to speak of someone on a brick platform complete with a railing? This is the meaning and the construction. 'Pabbatantaravanantaragumbantaresūti'—in the middle of a mountain, the middle of a forest, or the middle of a thicket; or in mountain crevices, forest clearings, or thicket openings. 'Upacāranti'—the vicinity is twelve cubits.

82. Itaroti navako. Assāti navakassa. Na vattabhede dukkaṭanti aññātattā na vattabhede dukkaṭaṃ. Eseva nayo sabbattha. Apacchāpurimanti apacchā apurimaṃ, ekapahārenāti attho. Samavassā dve pārivāsikāti yojanā. Dvinnaṃ pārivāsikānaṃ ekato vasanadosaṃ dassento āha “sace hi dve”tiādi. Nesanti dvinnaṃ pārivāsikānaṃ. Etthāti pārivāsikādīsu pañcasu bhikkhūsu. Mūlāyapaṭikassanārahādayo cattāroti yojanā.

82. 'Itaroti' refers to the new one. 'Assāti' means 'of the new one'. 'Na vattabhede dukkaṭanti' means 'because of not knowing, there is no dukkata in a difference of observance'. This is the method everywhere. 'Apacchāpurimanti' means 'not later, not before'; the meaning is: 'with one strike'. The construction is: ‘two probationers of the same seniority’. Showing the fault of two probationers dwelling together, it is said, 'If there are two,' etc. 'Nesanti' refers to the two probationers. 'Etthāti' refers to these five bhikkhus, beginning with the probationer. The construction is: ‘the four, beginning with the one worthy of being sent back to the beginning’.

Parivāsadānādīnīti ādisaddena mūlāyapaṭikassanamānattadānaabbhānāni saṅgaṇhāti. Etesvevāti parivāsadānādīsu eva. Ayanti pārivāsiko.

'Parivāsadānādīnīti' includes by the word 'ādi' the reinstatement at the root, the giving of penance, and the calling back. 'Etesvevāti' means 'specifically in the giving of probation, etc.'. 'Ayanti' refers to the one observing probation.

83. “Atha [M 0.0423] kho āyasmā upālī”tiādivacanassa anusandhiṃ dassento āha “imaṃ panā”tiādi[V 2.0077]. Rahogatassa upālittherassāti yojanā. Atha vā anādare sāmivacanaṃ katvā upālittherassa rahogatassāti yojanā kātabbā. Etthāti pārivāsikavatte. Soti upālitthero. Assāti upālittherassa. Tatthāti tīsu ratticchedesu. Yvāyanti yo ayaṃ, ekato vāsoti sambandho. So vāso sahavāso nāmāti yojanā. Vippavāsoti ettha pakatattena vippayutto hutvā vāsoti dassento āha “ekakasseva vāso”ti. Āgantukādīnanti ādisaddena āvāsikā gahetabbā.

83. Showing the connection to the statement, 'Then the Venerable Upāli,' etc., it is said, 'Now this,' etc. The construction is 'Rahogatassa upālittherassāti'. Alternatively, using the genitive case in the sense of disregard, the construction should be 'Upālittherassa rahogatassāti'. 'Etthāti' refers to the probationer’s observance. 'Soti' refers to the Venerable Upāli. 'Assāti' refers to the Venerable Upāli. 'Tatthāti' refers to the three interruptions of nights. 'Yvāyanti' means 'whoever this is,' the connection being 'living together'. The construction is 'So vāso sahavāso nāmāti'. 'Vippavāsoti' here, showing it means living separated from what is established, is explained as 'living alone'. By 'Āgantukādīnanti,' resident monks are included by the word 'ādi'.

84. Tattha tatthāti taṃ taṃ ṭhānaṃ. Dvīsu padesūti dvīsu vākyasaṅkhātesu padesu. Ekenekenapīti ekena ekena vākyapadenapi. Parivasiyitthāti parivuttho, parivuttho parivāso etassāti parivutthaparivāso, tassa. Hīti saccaṃ. Esāti eso bhikkhūti sambandho. Suddhanteti suddhakoṭṭhāse. Dukkhassāti vaṭṭadukkhassa. Antanti avasānaṃ, vināsaṃ vā.

84. 'Tattha tatthāti' means 'in each respective place'. 'Dvīsu padesūti' refers to 'in two parts designated as phrases'. 'Ekenekenapīti' means 'even by each single phrase-part'. 'Parivasiyitthāti' means 'he has lived out'; one for whom probation has been lived out is 'parivutthaparivāso,' of him. 'Hīti' means 'truly'. 'Esāti' connects with 'this monk'. 'Suddhanteti' means 'in the pure section'. 'Dukkhassāti' refers to 'the suffering of the cycle of rebirth'. 'Antanti' means 'an end, or destruction'.

2. Mūlāyapaṭikassanārahavattakathā

2. Account of the Observance of One Worthy of Relegation to the Beginning.

86. Navakataraṃ mūlāyapaṭikassanārahaṃ ṭhapetvāti yojanā. Imesaṃ pañcannaṃ pakatattā evāti sambandho. Nesanti mūlāyapaṭikassanārahamānattārahamānattacārikaabbhānārahānaṃ catunnaṃ, mūlāyapaṭikassanārahādilakkhaṇanti sambandho. Etthāti mūlāyapaṭikassanārahassa vatte. Itoti mūlāyapaṭikassanārahassa vattato.

86. The explanation is: "excluding the more recent one worthy of relegation to the beginning." The connection is: "because these five are in their ordinary state." "Nesanti" refers to the four—those worthy of relegation to the beginning, those worthy of mānatta, those undergoing mānatta, and those worthy of reinstatement—and the characteristics of those worthy of relegation to the beginning, etc.; this is the connection. "Etthāti" refers to the observance of one worthy of relegation to the beginning. "Itoti" means from the observance of one worthy of relegation to the beginning.

87. Yatheva pārivāsiko gaṇapūrako na hoti, evaṃ etepi na hontīti yojanā.

87. The explanation is: "Just as one undergoing probation is not a quorum-filler, so too these are not."

4. Mānattācārikavattakathā

4. Account of the Observance of One Undergoing Mānatta.

92. Ūne [M 0.0424] gaṇeti ettha gaṇo nāma gaṇabhojanasikkhāpade (pāci. 217 ādayo) viya hotīti āha “cattāro vā atirekā vā”ti. Sabbatthāti pārivāsikakkhandhake.

92. 'Ūne gaṇeti'—here, 'gaṇo' means a group, as in the training rule concerning group meals (Pācittiya 217 and so forth), hence it is said, 'four or more.' 'Sabbatthāti' refers to the Chapter on Probation.

Iti pārivāsikakkhandhakavaṇṇanāya yojanā samattā.

Thus the explanation in the commentary on the Chapter on Probation is concluded.

3. Samuccayakkhandhakaṃ

3. The Chapter on Combinations.

1. Sukkavissaṭṭhikathā

1. Account of the Emission of Semen.

Samuccayakkhandhake [V 2.0078] tatthāti catubbidhesu mānattesu. Yaṃ mānattaṃ diyyati, idaṃ appaṭicchannamānattaṃ nāmāti yojanā. Eseva nayo anantaravākyesupi. Paṭicchannāya āpattiyāti hetvatthe karaṇavacanaṃ, kāraṇatthe nissakkavacanaṃ vā. Addhamāsanti pannarasadivasakālaṃ. Odhāyāti samūhaṃ katvā. “Ekato katvā”ti iminā “odhāyā”ti padassa atthaṃ dasseti. Tesūti catubbidhesu mānattesu. Idanti mānattaṃ. Appaṭicchannāya…pe… vacanatoti ñāpakahetu. Etena appaṭicchannāya āpattiyā dātabbaṃ mānattaṃ appaṭicchannamānattanti vacanatthaṃ dasseti. Tanti appaṭicchannamānattaṃ. Idhāti imissaṃ pāḷiyaṃ. Tatuttarīti tato tīhipi uttari. Nānāvatthūni etāsanti nānāvatthukāyo. Tāsanti nānāvatthukānaṃ.

In the Chapter on Combinations, 'therein' refers to the four kinds of mānatta. The explanation is: 'The mānatta that is given is called unconcealed mānatta.' The same method applies to the subsequent statements as well. 'For a concealed offense'—here the instrumental case denotes cause, or the ablative case denotes reason. 'Half a month' means a period of fifteen days. 'Odhāya' means having made a group. By 'having made it one,' it shows the meaning of the word 'odhāya.' 'Among these' refers to the four kinds of mānatta. 'This' means mānatta. 'For an unconcealed [offense]... the statement'—is an indicative reason. By this, it shows that the mānatta to be given for an unconcealed offense is called unconcealed mānatta—this is the meaning of the statement. 'That' refers to unconcealed mānatta. 'Here' means in this Pāli passage. 'Thereafter' means beyond that in three ways. 'Nānāvatthūni etāsanti' means they are of various grounds. 'Tāsanti' means of those of various grounds.

Māḷakasīmāyamevāti sīmamāḷake eva, sīmaṅgaṇe evāti attho. Tatthevāti māḷakasīmāyameva.

'Māḷakasīmāyameva' means just in the boundary-pavilion, that is, just in the boundary-courtyard. 'Tattheva' means just in the boundary-pavilion itself.

Vedayāmahanti vedayāmi ahaṃ. Mama mānattacarabhāvaṃ saṅghaṃ jānāpemīti attho. Vedayatīti manti jānāpeti, iti maṃ saṅgho dhāretūti adhippāyo. Vuttanayenevāti pārivāsikakkhandhake vuttanayeneva. Nikkhipitabbanti “mānattaṃ nikkhipāmi, vattaṃ nikkhipāmī”ti nikkhipitabbaṃ. Māḷakatoti sīmaṅgaṇato. Sopīti saha gacchantopi. “Māḷake nārocita”nti [M 0.0425] iminā yassa māḷake ārocitaṃ, tassa anārocetvāpi nikkhipitabbanti dasseti. Ārocentena vattabbanti sambandho.

'Vedayāmahaṃ' means 'I make known.' The meaning is: 'I inform the Saṅgha of my state of undergoing mānatta.' 'Vedayati' means he informs, with the intention: 'May the Saṅgha thus remember me.' 'As previously stated' means in the manner stated in the Chapter on Probation. 'It should be relinquished' means one should relinquish by saying, 'I relinquish the mānatta, I relinquish the observance.' 'From the māḷaka' means from the boundary-courtyard. 'Even he' means even one going along with. By 'not announced in the māḷaka,' it is shown that it should be relinquished even without announcing it to the one to whom it had been announced in the māḷaka. The connection is: 'The observance should be undertaken by one who is announcing'.

Visabhāgehi saha vasantassa vattassa duppūritattā vuttaṃ”sabhāgā bhikkhū vasantī”ti. Catūhi, pañcahi vāti vāsaddena tato atirekampi saṅgaṇhāti. Parikkhepārahaṭṭhānatoti cīvarakkhandhake (mahāva. aṭṭha. 379) vuttaparikkhepārahaṭṭhānato. “Dve leḍḍupāte atikkamitvā”ti idaṃ vihāre bhikkhūnaṃ [V 2.0079] sajjhāyādisaddasavanūpacārapahānatthaṃ vuttaṃ. Sace savanūpacārato na muccati, tato atirekampi atikkamitabbaṃ. Okkammāti maggapaṭipannānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ vacanasaddasavanūpacārapahānatthaṃ okkamitvā. “Gumbena vā vatiyā vā”ti dassanūpacārapahānatthaṃ vuttaṃ. Idha upacāro nāma yattha ṭhatvā passati suṇāti, soyeva deso. Aññoti catūhi pañcahi vā bhikkhūhi añño. Esāti eso mānattacāriko.

Because the observance of one living with those of a dissimilar kind is difficult to fulfill, it is said: 'Monks of a similar kind live together.' 'By four or five'—the word 'or' includes even more than that. 'From a place worthy of enclosure' refers to the place worthy of enclosure mentioned in the Cīvarakkhandhaka (Mahāvagga Aṭṭhakathā 379). 'Having gone beyond two clod-throws'—this is said for the purpose of abandoning the range of hearing the sounds of recitation and so forth of the monks in the monastery. If one is not freed from the range of hearing, one should go even further. 'Having stepped aside' means stepping aside for the purpose of abandoning the range of hearing the sound of speech of monks who are on the path. 'By a thicket or a fence'—this is said for the purpose of abandoning the range of sight. Here, 'range' means that very place where, standing, one sees or hears. 'Another' means someone other than the four or five monks. 'This one' refers to this one undergoing mānatta.

“Dvādasahatthaṃ upacāraṃ okkamitvā”ti iminā anokkamitvā ajānantasseva gacchati, natthi ratticchedopīti dasseti. Ettha diṭṭharūpānaṃ sutasaddānaṃ dvādasahatthūpacārato bahi ṭhitānampi ārocetabbaṃ. Adiṭṭhāsutānampi anto dvādasahatthūpacāragatānaṃ ārocetabbanti daṭṭhabbaṃ. Sati karaṇīyeti idaṃ gantussa kāraṇadassanatthaṃ vuttaṃ. Asati karaṇīyepi gantuṃ vaṭṭati. Sopīti eko bhikkhupi. “Tassa santike ārocetvā”ti iminā anārocane vattabhedadukkaṭaṃ hotīti dasseti. Ekassa santike ārocetvā nikkhipiyamāne kiṃ ūne gaṇe caraṇadoso vā vippavāso vā na hotīti āha “ayañcā”tiādi. Tattha ayañcāti mānattacāriko pana. Yasmā kāraṇā vasi, tena kāraṇenāti yojanā. Bhikkhūnañca atthibhāvaṃ sallakkhetvāti pakatattāgatakāle tassa anārocetvāva gacchanti, tasmā bhikkhūnañca dvādasahatthūpacāre atthibhāvaṃ sallakkhetvāti attho. Ettha ca “gaṇassa ārocetvā”ti iminā ūne gaṇe caraṇadosābhāvaṃ dasseti. “Bhikkhūnañca atthibhāvaṃ sallakkhetvā”ti iminā vippavāsadosābhāvaṃ dasseti. Yanti pubbe anārocitaṃ yaṃ bhikkhuṃ[M 0.0426]. Ayanti paṭhamaṃ passitabbassa ārocetvā nikkhipanaṃ. “Nikkhittavattassa parihāro”ti iminā anikkhittavatte antoupacāragatānaṃ sabbesaṃ ārocetabbanti dasseti.

By 'having stepped within a twelve-cubit range,' it is shown that if one goes without stepping within and without knowing, there is no interruption of the night. Here, it should be announced even to seen forms and heard sounds situated outside the twelve-cubit range. And it should be understood that it must be announced even to unseen and unheard beings who are within the twelve-cubit range. 'When there is a need'—this is said to show the reason for going. Even when there is no need, it is permissible to go. 'Even he' means even a single monk. By 'having announced in his presence,' it is shown that if one does not announce, there is a dukkata offense for breaking the observance. When relinquishing after informing one person, lest there be a fault of conduct in an incomplete group or of separation, he says, 'And this,' etc. Here, 'and this' refers to the one undergoing mānatta. The construction is: 'For whatever reason he dwelt, for that reason.' 'And having taken note of the presence of the monks'—the meaning is: because at the time of their regular arrival they go without informing him, therefore one should take note of the presence of monks within the twelve-cubit range. Here, by 'having informed the group,' it shows the absence of the fault of conduct in an incomplete group. By 'and having taken note of the presence of the monks,' it shows the absence of the fault of separation. 'Yaṃ' refers to the monk who was not previously informed. 'Ayaṃ' refers to relinquishing after having announced to the one who is to be seen first. By 'the allowance for one who has relinquished the observance,' it is shown that for one who has not relinquished the observance, it must be announced to all who are within the range.

Ayanti mānattacāriko, ṭhitoti sambandho. Tenāpīti mānattacārikenapi, yācitabbanti yojanā. Soti anikkhittavatto bhikkhu. Tatrāti “so abbhetabbo”ti vacane. Ayaṃ abbhānavidhi vuttoti yojanā. Ayañcāti abbhānavidhi ca. Tāsanti āpattīnaṃ. Evantiādi nigamanaṃ. Paṭicchannamānattaṃ pana dātabbaṃ hotīti sambandho. “Paṭicchannāyā”tiādinā paṭicchannāya āpattiyā dātabbaṃ mānattaṃ paṭicchannamānattanti vacanatthaṃ dasseti. Nanti paṭicchannamānattaṃ.

'Ayaṃ' refers to one undergoing mānatta; the connection is with 'standing.' The explanation is: 'Even by one undergoing mānatta, it should be requested.' 'So' refers to a monk who has not relinquished his observance. 'Tatra' refers to the statement 'he should be reinstated.' The explanation is: 'This is the method of reinstatement stated.' 'Ayañca' refers to 'and the method of reinstatement.' 'Tāsaṃ' refers to 'of the offenses.' 'Evaṃ' and so forth is the conclusion. The connection is: 'However, concealed mānatta should be given.' By 'for a concealed [offense], etc.,' it shows that the mānatta to be given for a concealed offense is called concealed mānatta—this is the meaning of the statement. 'Naṃ' refers to concealed mānatta.

2. Parivāsakathā

2. The Discussion on Probation

102. Tassāti paṭicchannamānattassa. Samodhānetvāti idheva parivāsakathāyaṃ samodhānetvā. Idheva parivāsakathāyaṃ dassayissāmāti yojanā. Idhevasaddo hi pubbāparāpekkho.

102. "Tassa" refers to the concealed mānatta. "Samodhānetvā" means having combined it here in the discussion on probation. The connection is: "I will show it here in the discussion on probation." The word "idheva" indeed refers to both what precedes and follows.

Idha [V 2.0080] adhippetaṃ parivāsaṃ vitthāretvā dassento āha “ayaṃ hī”tiādi. Idha adhippeto parivāso nāma tividho hotīti yojanā. Tatthāti tividhesu parivāsesu. “Yathāpaṭicchannāya āpattiyā”ti vacanaṃ vitthārento āha “kassaci hī”tiādi. Yathā udāyittherassa ekāhapaṭicchannā ayaṃ āpatti hoti, tathā kassaci ekāhapaṭicchannā āpatti hotīti yojanā. Yathā ca parato āgatā udāyittherasseva āpatti hoti, tathā kassaci dvihādipaṭicchannā āpatti hotīti yojanā. Iminā vuttanayānusārena paratopi nayo netabbo. Tasmāti yasmā ekāhādipaṭicchannā ekādiāpatti hoti, tasmā jānitabboti yojanā.

Here, intending to elaborate on the intended probation, he says, "This indeed..." and so on. The connection is: the probation intended here is of three kinds. "Therein" refers to the three kinds of probation. Elaborating on the phrase "for an offense concealed as it was," he says, "For someone indeed..." and so on. The connection is: just as for the Elder Udāyi, this offense was concealed for one day, so too for someone there may be an offense concealed for one day. And just as for the Elder Udāyi, the offense was learned from another, so too for someone there may be an offense concealed for two days or more—this is the connection. According to the method stated here, the reasoning should also be applied to what follows. Therefore—because an offense concealed for one day, etc., is an offense of one day, etc., therefore it should be understood—this is the connection.

Paṭicchannabhāvaṃ vitthārento āha “ayaṃ hī”tiādi. Tatthāti “dasahākārehī”ti pāṭhe. Āpattiiti saññā etassāti āpattisaññī [M 0.0427] . Pahu cāti samattho ca. Papubbo hūdhātu samatthatthe hoti.

Explaining the state of being concealed, he says, "This indeed..." and so on. "Therein" refers to the reading "by ten modes." "Āpattisaññī" means one who has the perception "this is an offense." "Pahu" means capable. The root hū with the prefix pa- is in the sense of being capable.

Tatthāti tassaṃ mātikāyaṃ. Yanti āpattiṃ. Sopi cāti bhikkhupi ca. Tatthāti tassaṃ āpattiyaṃ. Ayanti bhikkhu. Tatthāti āpattiyaṃ. Alajjipakkhe tiṭṭhatīti “sañcicca āpattiṃ parigūhatī”ti (pari. 359) vuttapakkhe ṭhitattā alajjipakkhe tiṭṭhati.

"Therein" refers to that matrix. "Yanti" refers to an offense. "Sopi ca" means also that monk. "Therein" refers to that offense. "Ayaṃ" refers to this monk. "Therein" refers to the offense. "He stands on the side of the shameless" means he stands on the side of the shameless because he stands on the side spoken of as "intentionally concealing an offense" (Parivāra 359).

Pakatattoti ettha “pārājikaṃ anajjhāpanno”ti atthaṃ paṭikkhipanto āha “tividhaṃ ukkhepanīyakammaṃ akato”ti. Etanti appaṭicchannabhāvaṃ, “āpajjati…pe… kusalehi cintitā”ti vacanaṃ vā.

Here, for "pakatatto," rejecting the meaning "not having fallen into a pārājika offense," he says, "the threefold act of suspension has not been done." This refers to the state of not being concealed, or the statement, "he commits...pe... considered by the skillful."

Gāthāya “sāvasesa”nti iminā pārājikaṃ nivatteti. Garukanti ettha saṅghādisesameva adhippetanti dasseti. Anādariyanti sikkhāpade anādariyaṃ. Vajjanti dukkaṭaṃ. Ukkhittakena karaṇabhūtena.

By "sāvasesa" in the verse, he excludes the pārājika offense. "Garuka" here indicates that only the saṅghādisesa offense is intended. "Anādariya" refers to disrespect for the training rule. "Vajja" refers to the dukkaṭa offense. "Ukkhittakena" means by one who has been suspended, as the agent.

Yassāti bhikkhussa, natthīti sambandho. Bhīrukajātikatāyāti bhīrukasabhāvatāya. Pabbatavihāre vasantassa yassa bhikkhunoti yojanā. Pabbatavihāreti pabbatassa tale, antare vā kārite vihāre. Etasminti etādise. Antarāye satiyevāti yojanā. Tassa acchannāva hotīti yojanā. Anantarāyikasaññāya chādayato acchannāvāti anantarāyikasaññāya chādentassāpi ekantena antarāyikattā acchannāvāti adhippāyo.

"Yassa" refers to the monk, and the connection is "there is not." "Due to being of a fearful nature" means due to a naturally fearful disposition. The connection is: for which monk dwelling in a mountain monastery. "Mountain monastery" means a monastery built at the foot of a mountain or within it. "In such a case" means in such a situation. The connection is: only when there is an obstacle. The connection is: for him, it remains uncovered. "It remains uncovered for one who covers with the perception of no obstacle" means that the intention is: even for one who covers with the perception of no obstacle, because it is entirely an obstacle, it remains uncovered.

Assāti [V 2.0081] bhikkhussa. Hanukavātoti hanukassa gelaññakaro vāto. Vijjhatīti hanukaṃ vijjhati. Imināti bhikkhunā. Pahusaññino chāditāpi ekantena apahuttā acchāditāva hoti.

"Assa" refers to the monk. "Hanukavāta" means wind that causes illness of the jaw. "Vijjhati" means it pierces the jaw. "Iminā" refers to this monk. Even when covered by one who perceives himself as capable, it is utterly uncovered due to his actual incapability.

Chādetukāmo cāti ettha idaṃ catukkaṃ veditabbaṃ chādetukāmo chādeti, chādetukāmo nacchādeti, acchādetukāmo chādeti, nacchādetukāmo nacchādetīti. Tattha paṭhamapadaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ “idaṃ uttānatthamevā”ti. Evaṃ sesāsupi mātikāsu catukkaṃ veditabbaṃ[M 0.0428]. Catūsu catukkesu paṭhamapade eva channā hoti, na sesapadesu. Anuttānatthaṃ dassento āha “sace panā”tiādi. Purebhatte vāti purebhattaṃ vā, bhattato, bhattassa vā pureti purebhattaṃ. Abyayībhāvasamāse sattamīvibhattiyā amitikāriyassa aniccabhāvato vuttaṃ “purebhatte”ti. Eseva nayo “pacchābhatte”ti etthāpi. Dutiyapadassa atthaṃ dassetvā tatiyapadassa atthaṃ dassento āha “yassa panā”tiādi. Abhikkhuke ṭhāne vasantassa yassa bhikkhussāti yojanā. Āgamentassa gacchantassāti anādare cetāni sāmivacanāni.

Here, this fourfold classification should be understood regarding "chādetukāmo ca" (and one who wishes to conceal): one who wishes to conceal, conceals; one who wishes to conceal, does not conceal; one who does not wish to conceal, conceals; one who does not wish to conceal, does not conceal. In this regard, referring to the first term, it is said, "this is only of obvious meaning." Similarly, the fourfold classification should be understood in the remaining matrices as well. Among the four fourfold classifications, concealment occurs only in the first term, not in the remaining terms. To explain the non-obvious meaning, he says, "but if," etc. "Purebhatte" means either "purebhattaṃ" (before the meal), or "bhattato" (from the meal), or "bhattassa pure" (before the meal). In an indeclinable compound, due to the impermanent nature of the function of the seventh case ending, it is stated as "purebhatte." The same principle applies to "pacchābhatte" here as well. Having explained the meaning of the second term, he explains the meaning of the third term by stating, "but for whom," etc. The connection is: for which monk dwelling in a place without monks. "Āgamentassa" (of one who comes) and "gacchantassa" (of one who goes)—these are genitives indicating disrespect.

Catutthapadassa atthaṃ dassento āha “yo panā”tiādi. Tattha yo panāti bhikkhu pana, āvi karotīti sambandho. Sabhāganti averiṃ. Ayanti bhikkhu. Upajjhāyo iti vā ācariyo iti vāti yojanā. Lajjāyāti lajjanimittaṃ, lajjakāraṇā, lajjahetu vā. Hīti saccaṃ, yasmā vā, idhāti āpattiārocanaṭṭhāne. Averisabhāgassāti averī hutvā sabhāgassa.

To explain the meaning of the fourth term, he says, "yo pana," etc. Therein, "yo pana" means "a certain monk, moreover," and the connection is "he makes known." "Sabhāga" means without enmity. "Ayaṃ" refers to this monk. The connection is: "as a preceptor" or "as a teacher." "Lajjāya" means "as a cause of shame," "on account of shame," or "due to shame." "Hī" means "truly" or "since." "Idha" means "here"—referring to the place for declaring an offense. "Averisabhāgassa" means "being without enmity, of the same class."

Pakāsetukāmoti aññesaṃ pakāsetukāmo. Upajjhāyassāpīti pisaddena aññassa santike kā nāma kathāti dasseti. Tatthāti āpattiārocanaṭṭhāne. Sabhāgasaṅghādisesanti vatthusabhāgasaṅghādisesaṃ. Suddhassāti vatthusabhāgasaṅghādisesato suddhassa. Āvikaraṇākāraṃ dassento āha “āvikaronto cā”tiādi. Iti imānītiādi nigamanaṃ.

"Pakāsetukāmo" means one who wishes to make known to others. "Upajjhāyassāpi" (even to the preceptor)—with the particle pi, it shows what kind of talk there might be in the presence of another. "Therein" refers to the place for declaring the offense. "Sabhāgasaṅghādisesa" means a Saṅghādisesa offense of the same basis. "Suddhassa" refers to one who is pure from a Saṅghādisesa offense of the same basis. Showing the manner of disclosure, he says, "and while disclosing," etc. "Thus these," etc., is the conclusion.

Tatoti jānitabbato, paranti sambandho. Ekāhapaṭicchannāti ekāhena paṭicchannā. Yāva cuddasa divasāni, tāva divasavasena yojanā kātabbāti yojanā. Pakkhapaṭicchannanti pakkhena paṭicchannaṃ. Atirekapakkhapaṭicchannanti pakkhato atirekena paṭicchannaṃ.
