"Tato" means from what should be known; "paraṃ" is connected with it. "Ekāhapaṭicchannā" means concealed for one day. The connection is: up to fourteen days, the connection should be made according to the number of days. "Pakkhapaṭicchanna" means concealed for a fortnight. "Atirekapakkhapaṭicchanna" means concealed for a period exceeding a fortnight.

Saṃvaccharapaṭicchannanti [V 2.0082] saṃvaccharena paṭicchannaṃ. Tato vāti atirekasaṭṭhisaṃvaccha rato vā. Bhiyyopīti atirekampi.

"Saṃvaccharapaṭicchanna" means concealed for a year. "Tato vā" means or from beyond sixty years. "Bhiyyopi" means even more.

Tatoti [M 0.0429] tīhi āpattīhi. Paranti atirekaṃ. Gaṇanavasenāti āpattigaṇanavasena. Vatthukittanavasena vāti āpattīnaṃ vatthukittanavasena vā. Nāmamattavasena vāti “saṅghādisesāpattiyo”ti evaṃ nāmasseva vasena vā. Ettha hi mattasaddo avadhāraṇattho, tena vatthuṃ nivatteti.

"Tato" means from three offenses. "Para" means extra. "By way of counting" means by way of counting offenses. Or "by way of stating the basis" means by way of stating the basis of the offenses. Or "by mere name" means merely by the name, such as "Saṅghādisesa offenses." Here, the word "mere" indeed has the force of determination, thereby excluding the basis.

Tatthāti “nāmamattavasenā”ti pade. Sajātisādhāraṇanti sassa attano jāti sajāti, tāya sādhāraṇaṃ sajātisādhāraṇaṃ. Sabbesaṃ, sabbehi vā āpattīhi sādhāraṇaṃ sabbasādhāraṇaṃ. Tatthāti duvidhesu nāmesu. Sabbasādhāraṇanāmavasenāpīti ettha pisaddo “ahaṃ bhante sambahulā saṅghādisesā āpajjiṃ ekāhapaṭicchannāyo”ti evaṃ sajātisādhāraṇanāmavasenapi “ahaṃ bhante sambahulā saṅghādisesā āpattiyo āpajjiṃ ekāhapaṭicchannāyo”ti evaṃ ubhayasādhāraṇavasenapi vattuṃ vaṭṭatīti dasseti. Hīti saccaṃ. Sabbampi parivāsādikaṃ idaṃ vinayakammanti yojanā. Vasati āpatti ettha tadāyattavuttitāyāti vatthu. Go vuccati vacanaṃ vā ñāṇaṃ vā, taṃ tāyatīti gottaṃ.

"Therein" refers to the phrase "by mere name." "Common to the same type" means one's own type is the same type; what is common with that is "common to the same type." "Common to all" means common to all offenses or by all offenses. "Therein" refers to the two kinds of names. "Even by the name common to all"—here, the particle pi indicates that it is permissible to speak either by the name common to the same type, thus: "Venerable sir, I have incurred many Saṅghādisesas, concealed for one day," or by the name common to both, thus: "Venerable sir, I have incurred many Saṅghādisesa offenses, concealed for one day." "Hī" means truly. The connection is: all this, including probation, etc., is a disciplinary act. "Vatthu" means the offense resides here, because its occurrence is dependent on it. "Go" is called speech or knowledge; "gottaṃ" is what protects that.

Tatthāti vatthādīsu catubbidhesu. Tatthāti tesu vacanesu. Sukkavissaṭṭhiṃ kāyasaṃsaggantiādinā vacanenāpīti ettha ādisaddena duṭṭhullādivacanāni saṅgaṇhāti. Idha panāti imasmiṃ pana ṭhāne. Yo yoti tisso vā phusso vā āpanno hoti.

"Therein" refers to the four kinds of bases, etc. "Therein" refers to those words. "Even by speech such as 'emission of semen, bodily contact,' etc."—here, the word "etc." includes coarse speech, etc. "But here" means in this situation. "Whoever" means one who has incurred three or four offenses.

Evaṃ ārocetabbanti evaṃ vakkhamānanayena ārocetabbanti yojanā. Kiṃ ārocetabbaṃ? “Ahaṃ bhante…pe… saṅgho dhāretu” iti ārocetabbanti yojanā.

The connection is: "should be announced thus" means it should be announced in the manner to be stated thus. What should be announced? The connection is: "Venerable sir, ... may the Saṅgha remember me" should be announced.

Vedayāmahanti vedayāmi ahaṃ. Mama pārivāsikabhāvaṃ saṅghaṃ, saṅghassa vā jānāpemīti attho. Vedayatīti manti vedayati iti maṃ. Pārivāsikabhāvaṃ saṅghaṃ, saṅghassa vā jānāpetīti maṃ saṅgho dhāretūti attho. Ettha bahūsu aṭṭhakathāpotthakesu “tiṇṇaṃ vā atirekānaṃ vā ārocentena āyasmanto dhārentū”ti pāṭho atthi[M 0.0430]. Kesuci aṭṭhakathāpotthakesu “tiṇṇaṃ ārocentena āyasmanto dhārentū”ti ettakoyeva pāṭho atthi. Heṭṭhā mānattakathāyampi evameva atthi. Tattha “atirekāna”nti iminā tīhi atirekānaṃ ārocentena saṅghaṃ apekkhitvā sace ekavacanavasena [V 2.0083] vattukāmo hoti, “maṃ saṅgho dhāretū”ti vattabbaṃ. Atha sambahule bhikkhū apekkhitvā sace bahuvacanavasena vattukāmo hoti, yathā tiṇṇaṃ, evaṃ “maṃ āyasmanto dhārentū”ti vattabbanti dasseti. Idañca saddasatthavaseneva vuttaṃ, na vinayakammavipattivasenāti daṭṭhabbaṃ.

"Vedayāma" means "I declare." The meaning is: I make known my probationary state to the Saṅgha, or to the Saṅgha. "Vedayatīti maṃ" means "he declares me." The meaning is: "May the Saṅgha remember me" means he makes known my probationary state to the Saṅgha, or to the Saṅgha. Here, in many commentary texts, there is the reading: "By informing three or more, may the venerable ones remember." In some commentary texts, there is only this reading: "By informing three, may the venerable ones remember." Below, in the discussion on mānatta, it is similarly stated. There, by "atirekānaṃ" (of more), it indicates that if one wishes to speak in the singular, considering the Saṅgha, by informing more than three, one should say, "May the Saṅgha remember me." But if one wishes to speak in the plural, considering several monks, as with three, one should say, "May the venerable ones remember me." And this is stated based on grammatical usage, not due to a failure in Vinaya procedure—this should be understood.

“Vihāreyeva rattipariggaho”ti iminā antoupacārasīmāyampi parivasitabbabhāvaṃ dasseti. Upacārasīmanti parikkhittassa vihārassa parikkhepaṃ, aparikkhittassa parikkhepārahaṭṭhānaṃ. Esāti pārivāsiko bhikkhu. Assāti āgatassa bhikkhuno.

"Even taking shelter for the night in the monastery"—by this it shows that one must also undergo residence within the boundary of the inner precincts. "Boundary of the precincts" means the boundary of an enclosed monastery, or the area suitable as a boundary for an unenclosed one. "This" refers to the monk undergoing residence. "To him" refers to the monk who has come.

Tatoti āpattipaṭicchannadivasato. Kukkuccavinodanatthāyāti āpattipaṭicchannadivasena samaṃ parivasitabbaṃ nukho, na nukhoti kukkuccassa vinodanatthāya. Parivutthattāti parivasitattā. Soti parivuttho bhikkhu. Idanti dātabbamānattaṃ. Tanti paṭicchannamānattaṃ. Chārattanti charattiyo samāhaṭāti chārattaṃ, samāhāre digu. “Charatta”nti vattabbe sukhuccāraṇatthaṃ chakārassa dīghaṃ katvā evaṃ vuttaṃ, accantasaṃyoge cetaṃ upayogavacanaṃ.

"From that" means from the day the offense was concealed. "For the purpose of dispelling remorse" is for the purpose of dispelling remorse about whether residence should be observed equal to the number of days the offense was concealed, or not. "Because of having completed residence" means because of having observed residence. "He" means the monk who has completed residence. "This" refers to the mānatta to be given. "That" refers to concealed mānatta. "Six nights" means six nights gathered; hence "six nights," a collective compound. Though "charatta" should be said, for ease of pronunciation, the syllable "cha" is lengthened, and this is an expression of absolute connection.

Appaṭicchannāpattiṃ dātuṃ vaṭṭatīti sambandho. Iminā heṭṭhā vuttaṃ paṭicchannamānattaṃ imasmiṃ paṭicchannamānatte samodhānetvāpi dātuṃ vaṭṭatīti dasseti. Evaṃ santepi mūlamānattaṃ paṭicca paṭicchannamānattanti vuccati. Kathaṃ dātuṃ vaṭṭatīti yojanā.

"It is permissible to give mānatta for an unconcealed offense"—this is the connection. By this, it shows that it is permissible to give it even by combining the previously mentioned concealed mānatta with this concealed mānatta. Even so, because it relies on the original mānatta, it is called concealed mānatta. The construction is: how is it permissible to give mānatta?

Assāti mānattaṃ yācantassa. Tadanurūpanti tassa yācanassa anurūpaṃ. Sace paṭicchannā dveti ettha dveti nidassanamattaṃ tato atirekampi gahetabbattā. Sabbatthāti sabbesu ekabahūsu. Tadanurūpame vāti [M 0.0431] tassa mānattadānassa anurūpameva. Idha panāti paṭicchannamānatte pana. Itītiādi nigamanaṃ. Yaṃ mānattaṃ diyyatīti yojanā. Etthāti paṭicchannamānatte.

"To him" means to the one requesting mānatta. "That which is appropriate" means appropriate to that request. If concealed, "two" here is merely an indication, because more than that should also be taken. "In all cases" means in all instances, whether singular or plural. "Just that which is appropriate" means just that which is appropriate to the giving of mānatta. "But here" means in the case of concealed mānatta. "Thus, and so on" is the conclusion. The construction is: "The mānatta that is given." "Here" means in the case of concealed mānatta.

Avasesāti appaṭicchannaparivāsapaṭicchannaparivāsehi avasesā. Tatthāti avasesesu dvīsu parivāsesu. Adhammikamānattacārāvasāne anuññātaparivāsoti sambandho. Kismiṃ vatthusmiṃ anuññātoti āha “imasmiṃ vatthusmi”nti. Esāti suddhanto, dātabboti sambandho. Etanti jānanājānanaṃ.

"The remainder" means remaining from unconcealed residence and concealed residence. "There" means among the remaining two residences. "Authorized residence at the end of conduct under improper mānatta"—this is the connection. In what case is it authorized? He says: "In this case." "This" refers to the suddhanta; "should be given" is the connection. "This" refers to knowing or not knowing.

Tatthāti [V 2.0084] dvīsu suddhantesu, cūḷasuddhantoti vuccatīti sambandho. Yoti bhikkhu, vadatīti sambandho. Ārocitadivasatoti āpattiārocitadivasato.

"There" means among the two kinds of suddhanta; "it is called the minor suddhanta" is the connection. "Whoever" refers to the monk; "speaks" is the connection. "From the day of declaration" means from the day the offense was declared.

Tanti cūḷasuddhantaṃ, parivasantena parivasitabbanti sambandho. Aggahesīti parivāsaṃ aggahesi. Aññanti gahitamāsato aññaṃ. “Parivāsadānakiccaṃ natthī”ti iminā parivāsagahaṇakiccampi natthīti dasseti gaṇhantasseva dātabbattā, dentasseva gahetabbattā vā. Uddhampi ārohatīti parivāsagahaṇakālato aññampi kālaṃ parivasitabbattā uddhampi ārohati. Heṭṭhāpi orohatīti parivāsagahaṇakālato ūnampi kālaṃ parivasitabbattā heṭṭhāpi orohati. Idanti ārohanorohanaṃ. Tassāti suddhantaparivāsassa. Ekameva paṭicca dve, tisso, sambahulā vā bhavantīti āha “ekaṃ vinā sambahulānaṃ abhāvato”ti.

"That" refers to the minor suddhanta; "must be observed by one undergoing residence" is the connection. "He undertook" means he accepted residence. "Another" means different from the month already taken. "There is no duty of granting residence"—by this it shows that there is also no duty of undertaking residence, because it must be given to the one who takes it, or it must be taken by the one who gives it. "It also ascends upward" means it ascends upward because residence must be observed even for a time other than the time of acceptance of residence. "It also descends downward" means it descends downward because residence must be observed even for a time less than the time of acceptance of residence. "This" refers to the ascending and descending. "Of that" refers to the suddhanta residence. Depending on one, two, three, or many may arise—thus he says: "Without one, there is no existence of the many."

Evaṃ cūḷasuddhantaṃ dassetvā mahāsuddhantaṃ dassento āha “yo panā”tiādi. Tanti mahāsuddhantaṃ. Yāva yattako upasampadadivaso hoti, tāva tattakaṃ kālanti yojanā. Uddhaṃ nārohatīti uddhaṃ ārohanakālassa abhāvato uddhaṃ na ārohati. Etthāti suddhantaparivāse. Ayaṃ suddhantaparivāso nāmāti nigamanaṃ.

Having thus explained the minor suddhanta, in showing the major suddhanta, he said, "Now, whoever..." "That" refers to the major suddhanta. The construction is: "for as long as it is the day of ordination, for that long a period." "It does not ascend" means it does not ascend because there is no time for ascending beyond. "Here" refers to the suddhanta residence. "This is called the suddhanta residence" is the conclusion.

Tatthāti [V 2.0085] tividhesu samodhānaparivāsesu. “Odhunitvā samodahitvā dātabbaparivāso”ti iminā odhunitvā samodhānetvā dātabbo [M 0.0432] parivāso odhānasamodhānoti vacanatthaṃ dasseti, “parivāso”ti iminā taddhitaṇapaccayassa sarūpaṃ dasseti. Ettha ca avadhuniyate, avadhunitabbanti vā odhānaṃ, saṃ ekato odahīyate sampiṇḍīyate, udahiyati sampiṇḍiyatīti vā samodhānanti avayavavacanattho kātabbo. “Makkhetvā”ti iminā dhudhātuyā pappoṭanadhaṃsanadhovanāni dasseti. Soti odhānasamodhāno, āgatoti sambandho.

"There" means in the threefold kinds of combination residence. By "residence to be given having shaken off and gathered together," it shows the meaning of the word "odhāna-samodhāna" is "residence to be given having shaken off and gathered together." By "residence," it shows the nature of the taddhita suffix ṇa. And here, "odhāna" means it is shaken off or should be shaken off; "samodhāna" means it is gathered together into one, compacted, or it is heaped together, compacted—thus, the meaning of the components should be understood. By "Makkhetvā," it shows that striking, destroying, and washing are meanings of the root "dhu." "That" refers to the odhāna-samodhāna; "has come" is the connection.

Etthāti odhānasamodhāne. Yoti bhikkhu, paṭicchādetīti sambandho. Parivasanto vā mānattāraho vā mānattaṃ caranto vā abbhānāraho vā yo bhikkhūti yojanā. “Purimāya āpattiyā”ti padaṃ “samā vā”ti pade sahādiyogo. “Ūnatarā”tipade vibhattiapādānaṃ, anumeyyavisayaapādānaṃ vā. “Adivase katvā”ti iminā odhunitvāti ettha dhudhātuyā yathāvuttattheyeva dasseti. Ūnakapakkhapaṭicchannāti pakkhato ūnakena paṭicchannā. Etenupāyenāti pakkhe vuttena etena upāyena.

"Here" means in the odhāna-samodhāna. "Whoever" refers to the monk; "conceals" is the connection. The construction is: "that monk, whether undergoing residence, or deserving mānatta, or practicing mānatta, or deserving rehabilitation." The phrase "for the earlier offense" is a co-application with the word "similar." In the word "less than," it is either an ablative of separation or an ablative of inferential scope. By "having made it not a day," it shows the meaning of the root "dhu" in "having shaken off" is just as stated. "Concealed for less than a fortnight" means concealed by a period less than a fortnight. "By this means" refers to this means stated regarding the fortnight.

Tatthāti mūlāpattito atirekapaṭicchanne. Āvi kārāpetvāti mūlāpattito antarāpattiyā paṭicchannabhāvaṃ āvi kārāpetvā. Etthāti āpattipaṭicchanne. Pamāṇanti kāraṇaṃ. Yāti āpatti. Tatthāti mūlabhāvena kattabbāyaṃ mūliāpattiyaṃ. Itaranti mūlibhāvena kattabbaṃ mūlāpattiṃ. Samodhāyāti samodahitvā. Pakkhipitvāti attho.

"There" means in the case of a concealment exceeding that of the root offense. "Having made it openly known" means having made the concealed state of an intermediate offense from the root offense openly known. "Here" means in the concealment of an offense. "The measure" means the reason. "Which" refers to the offense. "There" refers to the secondary offense, which is to be made the basis. "The other" refers to the root offense, which is to be made the secondary one. "Having combined" means having gathered together. The meaning is "having included."

Ekā vā yā āpatti sabbacirapaṭicchannā hotīti yojanā. Sabbacirapaṭicchannāyoti sabbāsaṃ āpattīnaṃ cirena paṭicchannāyo. Tāsanti āpattīnaṃ. Agghenāti paricchedena. Agghasaddo hettha paricchedatthavācako. Abhidhāne (abhidhānappadīpikāyaṃ 1048 gāthāyaṃ) vuttaṃ “aggho mulye ca pūjane”ti. Ettha “mulye cā”ti padassa mūlaparicchedeti attho daṭṭhabbo. Tamevatthaṃ dassento āha “tāsaṃ rattiparicchedavasenā”ti. Imehi [M 0.0433] padehi agghena rattiparicchedena samodhānetvā dātabbo parivāso agghasamodhānoti vacanatthaṃ dasseti. Ettha ca “sabbacirapaṭicchannāyo”ti vuttattā kiñcāpi koṭiatthavācako tatiyakkharena pāṭho yutto viya dissati. Tathāpi so pāṭho na gahetabbo. Kasmā? Bahūsu pāḷipotthakesu, aṭṭhakathāpotthakesu ca alikhitattā. Bahūsu hi porāṇapotthakesu catutthakkharena pāṭhoyeva likhito, tasmā so pāṭhoyeva gahetabbo, na aññoti daṭṭhabbaṃ. Soti agghasamodhāno. Āgatoyevāti sambandho.

The construction is: 'one or any offense that is longest-concealed.' 'Longest-concealed' means, of all offenses, those concealed for a long time. 'Of those' refers to the offenses. 'By measure' means by limitation. Here, the term 'measure' conveys the meaning of limitation. In the Abhidhānappadīpikā (verse 1048), it is stated: 'Measure is in value and in honor.' Here, the meaning of the phrase 'and in value' should be understood as 'limitation by price.' To explain this very meaning, it is said: 'by way of the limitation of nights.' By these words, it shows the meaning of the word 'agghasamodhāna' as 'probation to be given by combining it with the measure of nights.' And here, because 'longest-concealed' is stated, even though the reading with the third letter seems appropriate as expressing a limit, that reading should not be adopted. Why? Because it is not written in many Pāli texts and commentary texts. For in many ancient texts, only the reading with the fourth letter is written; therefore, only that reading should be adopted, not another. 'That' refers to the agghasamodhāna; 'has indeed come' is the connection.

Yassa panāti bhikkhussa, paṭicchannāti sambandho. Sabbanti sakalaṃ. Āpattisahassagāthāya –

'But for whom' refers to a monk; 'concealed' is the connection. 'All' means complete. In the Āpattisahassagāthā—

Dasasataṃ āpattiyo rattisataṃ chādayitvānāti yojanā. Iminā nayenapi agghasamodhānoti ettha agghasaddassa catutthakkharena pāṭhassa yuttabhāvo veditabbo. Agghena dasarattiparicchedena samodhāya dātabbo agghasamodhāno.

The construction is: 'having concealed a thousand offenses for a hundred nights.' By this method also, the appropriateness of the reading with the fourth letter of the word 'aggha' in 'agghasamodhāna' should be understood. Agghasamodhāna is the probation to be given by combining it with the limitation of ten nights.

Yo parivāso nānāvatthukāyo āpattiyo ekato katvā diyyati, ayaṃ parivāso missakasamodhāno nāmāti yojanā. Ettha vatthuvasena missakā āpattiyo samodhānetvā dātabbo parivāso missakasamodhānoti vacanattho kātabbo. Tatrāti missakasamodhāne. Tadanurūpāyāti tassa yācanassa anurūpāya.

The construction is: 'The probation that is given by combining offenses of different natures into one, this probation is called missakasamodhāna.' Here, the meaning of the word 'missakasamodhāna' should be understood as 'probation to be given by combining mixed offenses based on their nature.' 'Therein' means in the missakasamodhāna. 'Suitable for that' means suitable for that petition.

Ettha cāti missakasamodhāne ca, kātuṃ vaṭṭatīti sambandho.

'And here' means in the missakasamodhāna; 'it is permissible to do' is the connection.

“Pakkhamānattañca [V 2.0086] …pe… kathayissāmā”ti yaṃ vacanaṃ vuttaṃ, tassa vacanassa okāsoti yojanā. Taṃ panāti pakkhamānattaṃ pana. “Aḍḍhamāsameva dātabba”nti iminā pakkhameva dātabbaṃ mānattaṃ pakkhamānattanti vacanatthaṃ dasseti. Hīti saccaṃ. Taṃ panāti pakkhamānattaṃ pana, dātabbanti sambandho. Attano sīmanti attano vihārasīmaṃ, mahāsīmanti attho. Sodhetvāti sabbāsaṃ hatthapāsanayanavasena, chandārahānaṃ chandanayanavasena, sīmato [M 0.0434] bahikaraṇavasena ca sodhetvā. Catuvaggagaṇanti catuvaggasaṅghaṃ. Gaṇoti cettha saṅghoyevādhippeto.

The construction is: 'the occasion for that statement which was said: “And the fortnight mānatta... we will explain.”' 'That, however,' means the fortnight mānatta. By 'it should be given for half a month,' it shows the meaning of the word 'pakkhamānatta' as 'mānatta that should be given for a fortnight.' 'Indeed' means it is true. 'That, however,' means the fortnight mānatta; 'should be given' is the connection. 'One's own boundary' means the boundary of one's own monastery; 'great boundary' is the meaning. 'Having purified' means having purified by way of bringing all within hand-reach, by way of bringing the consent of those worthy of consent, and by way of excluding those outside the boundary. 'A group of four' means a Saṅgha of four. Here, 'group' is intended to mean the Saṅgha.

Tatrāti “yojanā kātabbā”ti vacane. Mukhamattadassananti upāyamattadassanaṃ, ādimattadassanaṃ vā. “Āpannāya bhikkhuniyā”ti padaṃ “evamassa vacanīyo”ti pade kattā, “yācāpetvā”ti pade kāritakammaṃ. “Byattāya bhikkhuniyā”ti padaṃ “ñāpetabbo”ti pade kāritakattā, “saṅgho”ti padaṃ tattheva kāritakammaṃ. “Etaṃ kāraṇa”nti dhātukammaṃ ajjhāharitabbaṃ. Tabbapaccayena kāritakammameva vuttaṃ. Ñāpetabbākāraṃ dassento āha “suṇātu me”tiādi.

‘Therein’ refers to the statement ‘the construction should be made.’ ‘Seeing just the face’ means seeing merely the means, or seeing only the beginning. The phrase ‘by the bhikkhunī who has committed an offense’ is the agent in the phrase ‘thus she should be spoken to,’ and the causative object in the phrase ‘having had her request.’ The phrase ‘by a competent bhikkhunī’ is the causative agent in the phrase ‘should be announced,’ and the word ‘Saṅgha’ is the causative object in the same phrase. For ‘this reason,’ the object of the verb should be supplied. By the suffix -tabba, the causative object itself is stated. Showing the manner of announcement, he says, ‘Let the Saṅgha hear me,’ and so on.

Nikkhittavattanti karaṇatthe cetaṃ upayogavacanaṃ. Nikkhittavattenāti hi attho. Tatthevāti māḷakasīmāyameva. Hīti saccaṃ, yasmā vā. Assāti mānattacārikāya bhikkhuniyā. Tatrāti tasmā kattabbavinayakammabhāvatoti attho. Noti amhākaṃ, santikanti sambandho. Catūhi pakatattabhikkhunīhi nisīditabbanti sambandho. Gāmūpacārato dve leḍḍupāte atikkamitvāti idaṃ bhikkhunīvihārūpacārātikkamaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ. Vihārūpacāratopīti bhikkhuvihārūpacāratopi. Tatthāti bhikkhunīnaṃ nisinnaṭṭhānaṃ. Kurundimahāpaccarīsu pana vuttanti sambandho. Vihārassa cāti bhikkhuvihārassa ca. Gāmassa upacāraṃ muñcituṃ vaṭṭatīti na vuttanti yojanā. Tasmā gāmūpacārepi nisīdituṃ vaṭṭatīti adhippāyo.

'Nikkhittavatta' is a term used in the instrumental sense. Indeed, the meaning is 'by one who has given up the observance.' 'Right there' means within the boundary of the pavilion itself. 'Hi' means truly, or because. 'Of her' refers to the bhikkhunī undergoing the mānatta penance. 'Therein' means 'because it is a disciplinary action to be performed.' 'No' means 'of us'; the connection is to 'presence.' The connection is 'should be seated by four bhikkhunīs of normal standing.' 'Having gone beyond two stone-throws from the village precincts' is said with reference to exceeding the precincts of the bhikkhunīs' monastery. 'Even from the monastery precincts' means also from the bhikkhus' monastery precincts. 'There' refers to the place where the bhikkhunīs are seated. The connection is 'but it is stated in the Kurundī and Mahāpaccarī commentaries.' 'And of the monastery' refers to the bhikkhus' monastery. The construction is: 'it is not stated that it is proper to relinquish the village's precincts.' Therefore, the intention is that it is proper to sit also within the village's precincts.

Tāya bhikkhuniyā ārocetabbanti sambandho.

The connection is: 'it should be announced by that bhikkhunī'.

Tatthevāti bhikkhunīnaṃ nisīdanaṭṭhāneyeva. Ṭhānanti bhikkhūnaṃ ṭhānaṃ. Etīti āgacchati. Pagevāti pātoyeva. Tāyāti mānattacāriniyā.

'Right there' means at the bhikkhunīs' sitting place itself. 'The place' means the bhikkhus' place. 'She comes' means she arrives. 'Early in the morning' means at dawn itself. 'By her' means by the one undergoing the mānatta penance.

Anikkhittavattāya pana bhikkhuniyāti sambandho. Ajānanapaccayāti ajānanakāraṇā. Tanti vacanaṃ. Pārivāsikavattādīnanti ādisaddena āgantukavattapūraṇanissayapaṭippassaddhādayo saṅgaṇhāti[V 2.0087]. Yuttataraṃ dissatīti yuttataraṃ hutvā dissati. Iminā anikkhittavattabhikkhunā viya bhikkhuniyāpi antoupacārasīmagatānaṃyeva ārocetabbaṃ, na gāme ṭhitānampi [M 0.0435] gantvā ārocetabbanti dīpeti. Uposatheti uposathadivase. Eseva nayo pavāraṇāyapi. Devasikanti divase divase. Tasmiṃ gāmeti bhikkhunīnaṃ vasanagāme. Aññatrāti bhikkhunīnaṃ vasanagāmato aññasmiṃ gāme. Tatrāti bhikkhunīnaṃ vasanagāmaṃ. Dassetvāti bhikkhunīnaṃ dassetvā. Tāyāti mānattacāriniyā. Vihāranti bhikkhūnaṃ vihāraṃ. Upacārasīmāyāti upacārasīmato bahīti sambandho. Ayanti mānattacārinī.

The connection is 'but for a bhikkhunī who has not relinquished her observances.' 'Due to not knowing' means because of the cause of not knowing. 'That' refers to the word. 'Of the observances for one on probation, etc.'—by the word 'etc.' the observances for a newcomer, completion, dependence, temporary suspension, and so on are included. 'It appears more appropriate' means it appears as being more fitting. By this, it is shown that just as with a bhikkhu who has not relinquished his observances, a bhikkhunī too should announce only to those who are within the precincts-boundary; she should not go and announce even to those staying in the village. 'On the Uposatha' means on the Uposatha day. This same method applies to the Pavāraṇā as well. 'Daily' means day by day. 'In that village' means in the village where the bhikkhunīs reside. 'Elsewhere' means in a village other than the village where the bhikkhunīs reside. 'There' refers to the village where the bhikkhunīs reside. 'Having shown' means having shown to the bhikkhunīs. 'By her' means by the one undergoing the mānatta penance. 'The monastery' means the bhikkhus' monastery. 'From the precincts-boundary'—the connection is 'outside the precincts-boundary.' 'This one' refers to the one undergoing the mānatta penance.

Vīsati gaṇo imassāti vīsatigaṇo, saṅgho, tasmiṃ. Mānattaṃ caramānā bhikkhunīti yojanā. Idaṃ pakkhamānattaṃ nāmāti idaṃ pubbavacanassa nigamavasena paravacanassa kathanatthāya vuttanti daṭṭhabbaṃ.

'This one has a group of twenty' means the twenty-group, that is, the Saṅgha; 'in that' refers to it. The construction is: 'the bhikkhunī undergoing mānatta.' 'This is called the fortnight mānatta'—this should be understood as having been stated for the purpose of explaining the subsequent statement by way of concluding the previous statement.

Tatthāti tividhesu mānattesu. Yadetaṃ mānattaṃ anuññātanti sambandho. Paratoti parasmiṃ. Parivāsaṃ parivasantassa mūlāyapaṭikassitassa udāyittherassa anuññātanti sambandho. Āpajjitvāti āpajjanato. Idanti mānattaṃ vuccatīti sambandho. Hīti saccaṃ, yasmā vā. Odhānasamodhānanti ettha vacanattho heṭṭhā vuttoyeva. Tampīti kurundiyaṃ vuttavacanampi.

'Therein' refers to the three kinds of mānatta. The connection is 'that this mānatta is permitted.' 'From another' means to another. The connection is 'it is permitted to the Elder Udāyī, who is undergoing probation and has been sent back to the beginning.' 'Having committed an offense' means from the commission of an offense. The connection is 'this is called mānatta.' 'Hi' means truly, or because. 'Odhānasamodhāna'—here, the meaning of the word has already been stated above. 'That too' refers also to the statement made in the Kurundī commentary.

Tanti agghasamodhānamissakasamodhānaṃ, dātabbanti sambandho. Ettāvatāti etaparimāṇena vacanakkamena, “ayañhi idha adhippeto parivāso nāmā”ti (cūḷava. aṭṭha. 102) vacanato paṭṭhāya yāva “yojetvā dātabba”nti vacanaṃ, tāva vacanakkamenāti attho. “Tena hi bhikkhave…pe… dassessāmā”ti yaṃ vacanaṃ vuttanti yojanā. “Atthato”ti iminā saddopi gahetabbo avinābhāvato.

'That,' meaning the agghasamodhāna and the missakasamodhāna, 'should be given' is the connection. 'To this extent' means by this measure in the sequence of statements; the meaning is 'by the sequence of statements starting from the statement, “For this is the intended probation here,” (Cūḷavagga Aṭṭhakathā 102) up to the statement, “having arranged, it should be given.”' The construction is: 'that statement which was said: “Well then, bhikkhus... we will show.”' 'By meaning'—by this, the literal word should also be taken, because it is inseparable.

Paṭicchannaparivāsakathā

The Account of Concealed Probation

102. Yā pāḷi vuttāti sambandho.

102. The connection is 'that which is stated in the Pāli text'.

108. Tatoti pāḷito. Taṃ āpattinti taṃ antarāpattiṃ. Assāti bhikkhussa. Nikkhittavatto bhikkhūti sambandho, hutvāti vā. Soti [M 0.0436] bhikkhu, ṭhito hutvāti sambandho. Tassā āpattiyāti tassā antarāpattiyā. Paṭicchannā hotīti antarāpattipi paṭicchannā hoti[V 2.0088]. Tasmimpīti mūlāya paṭikassanepi. Makkhitāti pisitā, dhaṃsitā vā. Makkhiyanti pisiyanti, dhaṃsiyantīti vā makkhitā, parivutthadivasā. Tatoti pāḷito paranti sambandho. Paratopi eseva nayo. Evantiādi nigamanaṃ. Paṭicchannavāre dassitā hontīti sambandho.

108. 'From that' means from the Pāli. 'That offense' means that intermediate offense. 'To him' means of the bhikkhu. The connection is 'the bhikkhu who has laid down the observance,' or 'having been.' The connection is 'that bhikkhu, having stood.' 'For that offense' means for that intermediate offense. 'Is concealed' means the intermediate offense is also concealed. 'Even in that' means even in being sent back to the origin. 'Tainted' means smeared, or afflicted. 'Are tainted' means are smeared, or are afflicted; 'tainted' refers to the days that have been lived through. The connection is 'from that Pāli, beyond.' The same method applies to what is beyond as well. 'Thus' and so on is the conclusion. The connection is 'they are shown in the section on concealment'.

Samodhānaparivāsakathā

The Account of Combined Probation

125. Tatoti paṭicchannavārato, paraṃ dassitanti sambandho. Ettha cāti etasmiṃ vāre ca. Yasmāti yasmā kāraṇā, yena kāraṇena vā. Tenevāti teneva kāraṇena, tasmā kāraṇā vā, “mūlāya…pe… detū”ti vuttanti yojanā. Tasmā sabbe makkhitāva hontīti yojanā. Tatoti vārato paraṃ niṭṭhāpitanti sambandho.

125. ‘From that’ means from the section on concealment; the connection is ‘it is shown beyond’. ‘And here’ means ‘and in this section’. ‘Since’ means ‘for which reason’ or ‘by which cause’. ‘For that very reason’ means ‘by that very cause’ or ‘for that reason’; the construction is that ‘“…back to the origin… let him give”’ is said. The construction is ‘therefore, all are indeed tainted’. ‘From that’ means from the section; the connection is ‘it is completed beyond’.

Agghasamodhānaparivāsakathā

The Account of Combining Probation According to Value

134. Tatoti vārato paraṃ dassitoti sambandho. Tatoti vārato paraṃ pāḷi ṭhapitāti sambandho. Lajjidhamme vā uppanneti sambandho. Yanti kammaṃ. Tatoti vārato paraṃ tatheva pāḷi ṭhapitāti sambandho.

134. 'From that' means from the section; the connection is 'it is shown beyond'. 'From that' means from the section; the connection is 'the Pāli text is established beyond'. The connection is 'or arisen in a matter of conscientiousness'. 'They go' refers to the formal act. 'From that' means from the section; the connection is 'the Pāli text is established in the same way beyond'.

138. Tatoti vārato paraṃ purimanayeneva pāḷi ṭhapitāti sambandho.

138. 'From that' means from the section; the connection is 'the Pāli text is established beyond according to the previous method'.

Suddhantaparivāsādikathā

The Account of Pure-Interval Probation, and so on

156. Tatoti vārato paraṃ suddhantaparivāso dassitoti sambandho.

156. 'From that' means from the section; the connection is 'the Pure-Interval Probation is shown beyond'.

160. Tatoti pāḷito paraṃ pāḷi ṭhapitāti sambandho.

160. 'From that' means from the Pāli text; the connection is 'the Pāli text is established beyond'.

165. Tatthāti pāḷiyaṃ. Antarā…pe… appaṭicchannāyotiādīsu attho daṭṭhabboti sambandho.

165. 'There' means 'in the Pāli text'. The connection is that the meaning should be understood in '“in the interim… for an unconcealed (offense)”' and so forth.

166. Pacchimasmiṃ [M 0.0437] āpattikkhandheti ettha āpattikkhandhassa bhedabhāvato kiṃ “pacchimasmiṃ āpattikkhandhe”ti vuttanti āha “ekova so āpattikkhandho”ti. Atha kasmā “pacchimasmiṃ [V 2.0089] āpattikkhandhe”ti vuttanti āha “pacchā chāditattā panā”tiādi. Ettha panasaddo garahatthavācako, tathāpīti hi attho. Ekopi āpattikkhandho pacchā chāditattā pacchimasmiṃ āpattikkhandheti vuttanti adhippāyo.

166. Regarding 'in the last aggregate of offenses', here, since the aggregate of offenses is indivisible, why is it said 'in the last aggregate of offenses'? He says, 'It is just one aggregate of offenses'. Then why is it said 'in the last aggregate of offenses'? He says, 'But because it is concealed afterward,' and so forth. Here, the word 'pana' expresses censure, for the meaning is 'nevertheless'. The intention is that even though it is one aggregate of offenses, because it is concealed afterward, it is called 'the last aggregate of offenses'.

180. “Vavatthitā sambhinnā”ti etaṃ vacananti yojanā.

180. The construction is: 'determined, combined' is the statement.

8. Dvebhikkhuvāraekādasakādikathā

8. The Account of the Section of Two Bhikkhus, the Eleventh, and so on

181. Tatoti pāḷito paraṃ vuttanti sambandho. Tatthāti pāḷiyaṃ. Missakanti ettha kehi missakanti āha “thullaccayādīhi missaka”nti.

181. 'From that' means from the Pāli text; the connection is 'it is said beyond'. 'There' means 'in the Pāli text'. Here, regarding 'mixed', 'with what is it mixed?' he says, 'Mixed with grave offenses and so on'.

184. Tatoti pāḷito paraṃ vuttanti sambandho. Tatthāti “idha pana bhikkhave”tiādipāṭhe. Tañcāti “idha pana bhikkhave”tiādivacanañca ito pubbe avuttaṃ sabbaṃ vacanañcāti yojanā.

184. 'From that' means from the Pāli text; the connection is 'it is said beyond'. 'There' means 'in the passage beginning with “Now, bhikkhus, here…”'. The construction is: 'and that' means 'the statement beginning with “Now, bhikkhus, here…” and every statement not said before this'.

Iti samuccayakkhandhakavaṇṇanāya yojanā samattā.

Thus the syntactical analysis in the commentary on the Chapter of Summaries is concluded.

4. Samathakkhandhakaṃ

4. The Chapter on Settlements

1. Sammukhāvinayakathā

1. The Account of Sammukhāvinaya

186-7. Samathakkhandhake evamattho veditabboti yojanā. Cha mātikāpadānīti vākyampi samāsopi yuttoyeva. Tattha samāso pana asamāhāradiguyeva. “Nikkhipitvā”ti padaṃ “vutto”ti pade pubbakālakiriyāvisesanaṃ, tulyattho vā. Vitthāroti vibhaṅgo. Tatthāti vibhaṅge. Saññāpetīti ettha saññaṃ katvā jānāpetīti atthaṃ paṭikkhipanto āha “paritosetvā jānāpetī”ti. Iminā saṃpubbo ñādhātu paritosanatthaṃ antokatvā avabodhanattho hotīti dasseti. Kāraṇapatirūpakānīti kāraṇassa paṭibhāgāni. Nijjhāpetīti ettha jhedhātu olokanatthoti [V 2.0090] āha “oloketī”ti. Yathāti yenākārena, kariyamāneti [M 0.0438] sambandho. Soti dhammavādī. Paratopi eseva nayo. “Punappuna”nti iminā anupekkhatīti ettha anusaddo na upacchinnatthoti dasseti. Pekkhati anupekkhatīti ettha ikkhadhātu “dasseti anudassetī”ti ettha disadhātuyā sadisatthoti āha “dasseti…pe… pariyāyavacanānī”ti. Tesaññevāti “pekkhati anupekkhatī”ti padānaññeva. Pariyāyavacanānīti vevacanasaddā atthe paribyattiṃ ayanti gacchanti imehīti pariyāyāni, tāniyeva vacanāni pariyāyavacanāni. Soti adhammavādī. Mohetvāti dhammavādīpuggalādiṃ mohāpetvā.

186-7. In the Chapter on Settlements, the construction is 'the meaning should be understood thus'. The phrase 'six matrix-terms' is indeed appropriate both as a sentence and as a compound. Here, however, the compound is indeed a non-aggregative dvigu. The word 'having laid down' is an adverb of prior action to the word 'said', or it has an equivalent meaning. 'Elaboration' means 'analysis'. 'There' means 'in the analysis'. Here, regarding 'makes known', rejecting the meaning 'makes known after having made a sign', he says, 'makes known after having satisfied'. By this he shows that the root ñā preceded by saṃ, having included the meaning of satisfying, has the meaning of causing to understand. 'Things analogous to a reason' means 'counterparts of a reason'. Here, regarding 'makes clear', he says the root jhe has the meaning of observing, thus he says 'observes'. 'As' means 'in which manner'; the connection is with 'being done'. 'He' means 'a speaker of the Dhamma'. The same method applies beyond as well. By 'again and again', he shows that here in 'observes repeatedly', the prefix anu does not have the meaning of interruption. Here, regarding 'observes, observes repeatedly', he says that the root ikkh has a meaning similar to the root dis in 'shows, shows repeatedly', thus he says 'shows… etc.… synonyms'. 'Of these very ones' means of the very words 'observes, observes repeatedly'. 'Synonyms' means synonymous words; they are 'synonyms' (pariyāyāni) because by them they go (ayanti, gacchanti) to the expression (paribyattiṃ) of the meaning (atthe); those very words (vacanāni) are synonyms (pariyāyavacanāni). 'He' means 'a speaker of non-Dhamma'. 'Having deluded' means 'having caused a person who speaks the Dhamma, etc., to be deluded'.

188. Dhammavādī puggalo dassetīti sambandho. Amohetvāti adhammavādīpuggalādiṃ amohāpetvā, aviparītaṃ jānāpetvāti attho.

188. The connection is 'a person who speaks the Dhamma shows'. 'Without deluding' means 'without causing a person who speaks non-Dhamma, etc., to be deluded, making known without distortion'; this is the meaning.

2. Sativinayakathā

2. The Account of Sativinaya

195. Parammukhaṃ vineti vināsetīti vinayo, parammukhaṃ vineti vināseti anenāti vā vinayo, vinayakammaṃ. Saṅghadhammavinayapuggalasammukhānaṃ dātabbo vinayo sammukhāvinayo. Pañcimānīti ettha pañcannaṃ sarūpaṃ dassento āha “suddhassā”tiādi. Anuvaditassa dānanti sambandho. Etānīti pañca aṅgāni. “Ekekaaṅgavasena na labbhantī”ti iminā samudāyavākyanibbattibhāvato pañcaṅgavaseneva labbhantīti dasseti. Desanāmattamevetanti “pañcimānī”ti etaṃ vacanaṃ desanāmattameva, na avayavavākyanibbattivacananti adhippāyo. Dhammanti bhūtaṃ. Etthāti “pañcimāni bhikkhave”tiādivacane. Tattha cāti “pañcimāni bhikkhave”tiādivacane ca. Anuvadantīti ettha anuddhaṃsanena vadantīti dassento āha “codentī”ti. Ayaṃ pana sativinayo dātabboti sambandho. Anāgāminopīti pisaddo sambhāvane, sakadāgāmiādike pana kā nāma kathāti dasseti. So ca khoti sativinayo ca. Codiyamāneyevāti codiyamānasseva, ayameva vā pāṭho. Tasminti sativinayasmiṃ dinneti sambandho. Acoditattā [M 0.0439] kathā na rūhatīti āha “codentopī”tiādi. Āpajjatīti codako āpajjati. Codanādiasāruppe vineti vināsetīti vinayo, vineti vināseti anenāti vā vinayo, vinayakammaṃ. Sativepullapattassa dātabbo vinayo sativinayo.

195. It disciplines and destroys what is adverse, thus it is Vinaya. Or, it is Vinaya because by means of this one disciplines and destroys what is adverse; it is the act of discipline. The discipline to be given in the presence of the Sangha, the Dhamma, the Vinaya, and the individual is Sammukhāvinaya (Discipline in the Presence). Here, regarding 'these five', showing the nature of the five, he says, 'for the pure one,' and so on. The connection is 'the giving to one who has been accused'. 'These' refers to the five factors. By 'they are not obtained by way of each single factor', he shows that because they are produced by a collective statement, they are obtained only by way of the five factors. The intention is that 'these five' is merely a description, not a statement that produces a constituent phrase. 'Dhamma' means 'what is factual'. 'Here' means 'in the statement beginning with “these five, O bhikkhus…”'. And 'and there' means 'also in the statement beginning with “these five, O bhikkhus…”'. Here, regarding 'they accuse', showing that they speak by way of reproaching, he says, 'they charge'. The connection is 'but this Sativinaya (Discipline by Recollection) is to be given'. Regarding 'even a non-returner', the word 'pi' indicates possibility; he shows, 'but what is to be said of a once-returner and the like?' 'And that' refers to Sativinaya. 'While being accused' means 'of one being accused', or this itself is the reading. The connection is 'when that Sativinaya has been given'. Because of not being accused, the discussion does not proceed—thus he says, 'even the accuser,' and so on. 'He incurs' means 'the accuser incurs'. It disciplines and destroys what is improper regarding accusation, etc., thus it is Vinaya. Or, it is Vinaya because by means of this one disciplines and destroys; it is the act of discipline. The discipline to be given to one who has attained fullness of mindfulness is called Sativinaya (Discipline by Recollection).

3. Amūḷhavinayakathā

3. The Account of the Discipline for the Unbewildered

196. Bhāsitaparikantanti [V 2.0091] ettha bhāsitaparikantasaddānaṃ karaṇāpekkhattā visuṃ karaṇaṃ dassento āha “vācāya bhāsitaṃ, kāyena parikanta”nti. “Parikkametvā kata”nti iminā parikamatīti parikantaṃ, parikantaṃ hutvā kataṃ parikantanti vacanatthaṃ dasseti. Parikkametvāti atikkamitvā. Saratāyasmāti ettha ukāralopasandhiṃ dassento āha “saratu āyasmā”ti. “Evarūpiyā āpattiyā”ti iminā āpajjitāti ettha tupaccayayogabhāvato kammatthachaṭṭhiyāpi sambhavabhāvaṃ dasseti. Tupaccayayoge kammatthachaṭṭhī aniccaṃ hoti, tasmā pāḷiyaṃ “evarūpiyā āpattiyā”ti kammatthachaṭṭhībhāvena avatvā “evarūpiṃ āpatti”nti kammatthadutiyābhāvena vuttanti daṭṭhabbaṃ. Tassāti “āpajjitvā”ti pāṭhassa. “Paṭhamaṃ pacchā”ti padehi adhippāyatthaṃ dasseti. Codakassa kathaṃ vineti vināsetīti vinayo, codakassa kathaṃ vineti vināseti anenāti vā vinayo. Paṭhamaṃ mūḷhabhāvaṃ upagantvā pacchā amūḷhassa dātabbo vinayo amūḷhavinayo.

196. Regarding “bhāsitaparikantaṃ,” here, to show the separate instrument required by the words “bhāsitaṃ” and “parikantaṃ,” he says: “spoken by speech, transgressed by body.” By “done after transgressing,” he shows the word-meaning that “parikanta” is from “parikamati” (he transgresses), and “parikanta” means “done after having transgressed.” “Having transgressed” means “having gone beyond.” Regarding “saratāyasmā,” here, to show the elision of the vowel ‘u’ in sandhi, he says: “saratu āyasmā.” By “evarūpiyā āpattiyā,” he indicates that in the word “āpajjitā,” due to the connection with the ‘-tu’ suffix, the sixth case (genitive) in the sense of the object is also possible. When there is a connection with the ‘-tu’ suffix, the sixth case in the sense of the object is not invariable; therefore, it should be understood that in the Pāli, instead of stating it with the genitive of the object as “evarūpiyā āpattiyā,” it is stated with the accusative of the object as “evarūpiṃ āpatti.” “Of that” refers to the reading “āpajjitvā.” By the words “first, afterward,” he shows the intended meaning. Vinaya is that which trains or removes the accuser’s statement, or that by which one trains or removes the accuser’s statement. The amūḷhavinaya is the formal act to be given to one who is not bewildered, after he has first entered a state of bewilderment.

4. Paṭiññātakaraṇakathā

4. Account of the Procedure on Acknowledgment

200. Paṭijāniyate, paṭijānanaṃ vā paṭiññā, tāya kāretabbaṃ.

200. It is acknowledged; or, “paṭiññā” is acknowledgment; by that, the procedure is to be carried out.

5. Yebhuyyasikākathā

5. Account of the Procedure by Majority

202. Yebhuyyasikāti ettha yebhuyyena pavattā yebhuyyasikā, dhammavādīnaṃ yebhuyyatāsampādikā kiriyāti dassento āha “yassā kiriyāyā”tiādi. Tattha yassā kiriyāyāti yassā yebhuyyatāsampādikāya kiriyāya. Esāti yebhuyyatāsampādikā kiriyā.

202. Regarding “yebhuyyasikā,” here, showing that what proceeds by a majority is “yebhuyyasikā,” and that it is the action that brings about a majority for those who speak the Dhamma, he said: “by which action,” etc. Herein, “by which action” means “by which action that brings about a majority.” “This” refers to the action that brings about a majority.

204. Oramattakanti [M 0.0440] ettha orasaddo ca mattasaddo ca samūhaṃ katvā parittavācako appamattavācakoti āha “parittaṃ appamattaka”nti. “Bhaṇḍanamattamevā”ti iminā na mahantaṃ vivādādhikaraṇaṃ hotīti dasseti[V 2.0092]. Na ca gatigatanti ettha cirakālabhāvaṃ na ca gatanti dassento āha “dve tayo…pe… avinicchita”nti. Tattha tatthevāti tasmiṃ tasmiṃ vivādādhikaraṇajātaāvāse eva, na ca saritasāritapadānaṃ suddhakāritakiriyabhāvaṃ dassento āha “sayaṃ saritaṃ vā aññehi sāritaṃ vā na hotī”ti. Tehi bhikkhūhīti vivādakārakehi bhikkhūhi. “Salākaṃ gāhento”ti iminā “jānātī”ti padassa kattāraṃ dasseti. Iminā nīhārenāti iminā kāraṇena. Api nāmāti iminā appevanāmasaddo apināmapariyāyoti dasseti. Assūti bhaveyyuṃ. Iminā “pāḷiyaṃ adhammavādī bahutarā bhaveyyuṃ, appeva nāma sādhū”ti yojanānayaṃ dasseti. “Ayamassa ajjhāsayo hotī”ti iminā pāṭhasesaṃ dasseti. Assāti salākagāhassa. Dvīsupīti “jānāti saṅgho bhijjissatī”ti ca “appeva nāma saṅgho bhijjeyyā”ti ca dvīsupi padesu.

204. Regarding “oramattakaṃ,” here, the words “ora” and “matta” taken together denote “little” or “a small amount”; hence he says “little, a small amount.” By “merely a quarrel,” he shows that it is not a major legal dispute. Regarding “na ca gatigataṃ,” here, showing that it has not gone on for a long time, he says: “two or three… undecided.” “In that very place” means in that very residence where the legal dispute arose. And showing that the words “sarita” and “sārita” are not purely causative actions, he says: “it is neither remembered by oneself nor caused to be remembered by others.” “By those monks” means by the monks who cause the dispute. By “distributing the ticket,” he shows the agent of the word “knows.” “By this method” means “by this reason.” By “api nāma,” he shows that the word “appeva nāma” is a synonym for “api nāma.” “Assu” means “they would be.” By this, he shows the method of construction in the Pāli: “the speakers of non-Dhamma might be more numerous; perhaps the good ones…” “This is his intention” shows the remainder of the text. “Of him” refers to the ticket-taker. “In both cases” refers to the two phrases: “he knows the Saṅgha will be split” and “perhaps the Saṅgha might be split.”

“Adhammena gaṇhantī”ti ettha “gaṇhantī”ti kiriyāpadassa adhammavādino eva kattā nāmāti āha “adhammavādino”ti. “Dve dhammavādino”ti iminā “vaggā gaṇhantī”ti ettha “gaṇhantī”ti kiriyāpadassa dhammavādino eva kattā nāmāti dasseti. Na ca yathādiṭṭhiyā gaṇhantīti ettha dhammavādino hutvā dhammavādisalākaṃ aggahetvā adhammavādisalākassa gahaṇaṃ na ca yathādiṭṭhiyā gaṇhanti nāmāti dassento āha “dhammavādino hutvā”tiādi. Paṭivattetvāti imamevatthaṃ paṭisedhetvā. “Parivattetvā”tipi pāṭho, heṭṭhupariyāyaṃ katvāti attho. Teti dhammavādino. Etthāti samathakkhandhake.

Regarding “they take unrighteously,” here, he says “the speakers of non-Dhamma,” indicating that the speakers of non-Dhamma are indeed the agents of the verb “take.” By “two speakers of the Dhamma,” it is shown that the speakers of the Dhamma are indeed the agents of the verb “take” in “the factions take.” Regarding “they do not take according to their own view,” here, showing that being speakers of the Dhamma, they do not take the ballot of those who speak the Dhamma but take the ballot of those who speak non-Dhamma, and that this is indeed “not taking according to their own view,” he said: “being speakers of the Dhamma,” etc. “Having turned back” means having rejected this very meaning. “Having turned around” is also a reading, meaning having inverted it. “They” refers to the speakers of the Dhamma. “Here” refers to the Samathakkhandhaka.

6. Tassapāpiyasikākathā

6. Account of the Tassapāpiyasikā

207. Asucīti ettha natthi sucīni kāyavacīkammāni etassāti asucīti vacanatthaṃ dassento āha “asucīhi kāyavacīkammehi samannāgato”ti[M 0.0441]. Eseva nayo alajjīti etthāpi. Sānuvādoti ettha anuvādaupavādasaddānaṃ pariyāyattā vuttaṃ “saupavādo”ti. Iti pañcāti imāni pañca aṅgāni. Etthāti tassapāpiyasikakamme. Idanti kammaṃ vuccatīti sambandho. Hīti vitthāro. Yo puggalo pāpiyoti yojanā. Pāpussannatāyāti lāmakussannatāya. Iminā ayañca pāpo ayañca pāpo, ayamimesaṃ visesena pāpoti pāpiyoti ca pāpānaṃ atisayena pāpoti pāpiyoti ca vacanattho dassito. Tassāti puggalassa. Iminā tassa pāpiyassa kattabbaṃ tassapāpiyasikaṃ, tameva kammaṃ tassapāpiyasikakammanti vacanatthaṃ dasseti. Kesuci potthakesu yakāre dvebhāvo atthi, so ayuttoyeva. “Yebhuyyasikā”ti ettha yakāre dvebhāvassa dassanato etthāpi dvebhāvo yutto bhaveyyāti likhantīti daṭṭhabbaṃ.

207. Regarding “asucī” (unclean), here, showing the meaning of the word “asucī” as “one who has no pure bodily or verbal actions,” it is said: “endowed with unclean bodily and verbal actions.” The same method applies to “alajjī” (shameless) as well. Regarding “sānuvāda” (reproached), here, because the words “anuvāda” and “upavāda” are synonyms, it is said: “subject to censure.” “Thus five” refers to these five factors. “Here” refers to the “tassapāpiyasika” action. The connection is that “this” refers to the action. The particle “hī” indicates an elaboration. The construction is “the person who is worse.” “Due to an abundance of evil” means “due to an abundance of baseness.” By this, the meaning of “pāpiya” is shown as “this one is bad, and that one is bad, but this one is particularly bad among these,” and also as “exceedingly bad among the bad ones.” “Tassa” refers to that person. By this, it shows the meaning of the word “tassapāpiyasika” as “that which is to be done to that worse individual,” and that same action is called the “tassapāpiyasika action.” In some texts, there is a doubling of the letter ‘y,’ but that is indeed incorrect. It should be understood that because the doubling of the letter ‘y’ is seen in “Yebhuyyasikā,” some write that doubling might be appropriate here as well.

7. Tiṇavatthārakādikathā

7. Account of the Covering with Grass, etc.

212. Kakkhaḷatāya vāḷatāyāti ettha kakkhaḷassa bhāvo kakkhaḷatā, vāḷassa bhāvo vāḷatāti [V 2.0093] vacanatthaṃ dassento āha “kakkhaḷabhāvāya ceva vāḷabhāvāya cā”ti. Iminā tāpaccayassa samūhatthañca svatthañca paṭikkhipati. “Kakkhaḷatāya vāḷatāyā”ti byañjanatoyeva nānaṃ, na atthato. Bhedāyāti ettha aññassa bhedaṃ paṭikkhipanto āha “saṅghabhedāyā”ti. Gilānepīti pisaddo aññe pana kā kathāti dasseti. Tatthevāti adhikaraṇavūpasamaṭṭhāneyeva. “Ekato”ti iminā ekajjhanti padassa “ekato”ti padena samānataṃ dasseti, ekasaddato jjhapaccayo ca topaccayo ca viseso, “tiṇavatthārakasadisattā”ti iminā sadisūpacāraṃ dasseti. Tiṇehi avattharitabbanti tiṇavatthāraṃ, gūthamuttaṃ, tiṇavatthāramiva tiṇavatthārakaṃ. Ettha adhikaraṇameva mukhyato labbhati, samatho pana phalūpacārato, sadisatthe kapaccayo. Tamevatthaṃ pākaṭaṃ karonto āha “yathā hī”tiādi. Ghaṭṭiyamānaṃ gūthaṃ vā muttaṃ vāti yojanā. “Ghaṭṭiyamāna”nti padaṃ hetuantogadhavisesanaṃ, “bādhatī”ti iminā [M 0.0442] sambandhitabbaṃ. Suppaṭicchāditassa pana assa gūthamuttassāti yojanā. “Suppaṭicchāditassā”ti padampi hetuantogadhavisesanameva, “na bādhatī”ti iminā sambandhitabbaṃ. Yaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ saṃvattatīti sambandho. Mūlānumūlanti mūlañca anumūlañca mūlānumūlaṃ. Tanti adhikaraṇaṃ. Iminā kammenāti tiṇavatthārakakammena. Gūthaṃ tiṇehi paṭicchannaṃ suvūpasantaṃ hoti viya tiṇavatthārakena paṭicchannaṃ suvūpasantaṃ hotīti yojanā. Itīti tasmā.

212. Regarding 'kakkhaḷatāya vāḷatāya,' here the state of being harsh is kakkhaḷatā, and the state of being cruel is vāḷatā—thus explaining the meaning, it is said: 'for harshness and for cruelty.' By this, both the collective and inherent meanings of the suffix 'tā' are rejected. 'Kakkhaḷatāya vāḷatāya' shows a difference in wording only, not in meaning. Regarding 'bhedāya,' here rejecting that it refers to the division of another, it is said: 'for schism in the Saṅgha.' In 'gilānepi,' the particle 'pi' indicates, 'what then of others?' 'Tattheva' means right there, at the place where the abatement of the dispute occurs. 'Ekato' shows the equivalence of the word 'ekajjhaṃ' with 'ekato,' where the suffix 'jjha' and the suffix 'to' from the word 'eka' are distinct; 'like a covering of grass' illustrates the similarity in usage. That which is covered with grass is a grass-covering (tiṇavatthāraṃ), for instance, dung or urine; a grass-covering procedure (tiṇavatthārakaṃ) is like a grass-covering. Here, the dispute itself is primarily taken, but the settlement, however, is by way of a metaphorical result; the suffix 'ka' denotes similarity. Clarifying this meaning, it is said: 'just as,' etc. The construction is: 'dung or urine being stirred up.' The word 'ghaṭṭiyamānaṃ' is a qualifier implying a cause, to be connected with 'it troubles.' The construction is: 'of this well-covered dung or urine.' The word 'suppaṭicchāditassa' is also a qualifier implying a cause, to be connected with 'it does not trouble.' The connection is: 'which dispute arises.' 'Mūlānumūla' means root and secondary root. 'Taṃ' refers to that dispute. 'By this formal act' means by the formal act of covering with grass. The construction is: 'dung covered with grass is well-pacified, just as a dispute covered by the grass-covering procedure is well-pacified.' 'Iti' means therefore.

213. Thullavajjanti ettha thullaccayassāpi thullavajjattā idha pārājikasaṅghādisesamevādhippetanti āha “pārājikañceva saṅghādisesañcā”ti. Gihipaṭisaṃyuttanti ettha gihīnaṃ paṭisaṃyuttaṃ gihipaṭisaṃyuttanti vacanatthaṃ dassento āha “gihīna”ntiādi. “Hīnenā”ti padaṃ “khuṃsanavambhana” iti padeneva sambandhitabbaṃ. Dhammikapaṭissavesūti nimittatthe bhummavacanaṃ.

213. Regarding 'thullavajja,' here even a grave offense (thullaccaya) is called 'thullavajja,' so in this context, only pārājika and saṅghādisesa offenses are intended—thus it is said: 'pārājika and saṅghādisesa.' Regarding 'gihipaṭisaṃyutta,' here what is connected with laypeople is 'gihipaṭisaṃyutta'—explaining the meaning, it is said: 'with laypeople,' etc. The word 'hīnena' should be connected with the words 'khuṃsanavambhana.' 'Dhammikapaṭissavesu' is a locative case indicating the occasion.

214. Kammavācāpariyosāne vuṭṭhitā hontīti sambandho. Tatthāti adhikaraṇavūpasamaṭṭhāne. Aññāvihitāpīti adhikaraṇavinicchayato aññasmiṃ ṭhāne cittaṃ āvihitāpi ṭhapitāpi. Upasampadamaṇḍalatoti upasampadasīmabimbato, ye panāti bhikkhū pana, diṭṭhāvikammaṃ karontīti vā anāgatāti vā nisinnāti vā sambandho. Tehi vāti adhikaraṇaṃ vinicchinantehi bhikkhūhi vā. Tatthāti adhikaraṇavinicchitaṭṭhānaṃ. Chandaṃ datvāti chandaṃ saṅghassa datvā. Pariveṇādīsūtiādisaddena āvāsādayo saṅgaṇhāti. Teti bhikkhū.

214. At the conclusion of the Kammavācā, the connection is that they are settled. 'Therein' refers to the place of the settling of the case. 'Aññāvihitāpi' means even if the mind is directed or fixed on another matter than the adjudication of the case. 'Upasampadamaṇḍala' means from the boundary marker of the Upasampadā. 'But those'—the monks—the connection is: 'who perform the formal act of declaring a view' or 'who have not yet arrived' or 'who are seated.' 'Or by them' means by the monks who are adjudicating the case. 'Therein' refers to the place where the case is adjudicated. 'Having given consent' means having given consent to the Saṅgha. 'In the surrounding area, etc.' means the term 'etc.' includes residences and the like. 'They' refers to those monks.

8. Adhikaraṇakathā

8. Discussion of Disputes

215. Vipaccatāyāti [V 2.0094] ettha vikārabhāvena patati pavattatīti vipaccaṃ, cittadukkhaṃ, tadeva vipaccatā, tadatthāyāti dassento āha “cittadukkhattha”nti. “Pharusavacana”nti iminā vohāra saddo vacanapariyāyoti dasseti. Yo tatthāti ettha tasaddassa visayaṃ dassento āha “tesu anuvadantesū”ti. Yo upavādoti yojanā. “Anuvadanā”ti [M 0.0443] etaṃ padanti yojanā. Ākāradassananti anuvadanassa ākāradassanaṃ, dassanahetu vā. “Punappuna”nti iminā anusampavaṅkatāti ettha anusaddassa na upacchinnatthaṃ dasseti. Tatthevāti anuvadane eva. Sampavaṅkatāti sammā pakārena ninnaponapabbhāratā. Abbhussahanatāti ettha atirekaṃ ussāhanatāti dassento āha “kasmā”tiādi. Anubalappadānanti ettha punappunaṃ balassa padānanti dassento āha “purimavacanassā”tiādi.

215. 'Vipaccatāya'—here, 'vipacca' means that which falls or occurs by way of a state of alteration, namely mental suffering; that itself is vipaccatā. To explain its purpose, it is said: 'for the purpose of mental suffering.' 'Pharusavacana'—this indicates that the word 'vohāra' (utterance) is a synonym for 'vacana' (speech). 'Yo tatthāti'—here, to clarify the scope of the word 'that,' it is said: 'among those who repeat.' 'Yo upavādoti' is the connection. 'Anuvadanā' is the word. 'Ākāradassana' means showing the manner of repeating, or it is the reason for showing. 'Punappuna'—this indicates that the meaning of the prefix 'anu' in 'anusampavaṅkatā' is not 'uninterrupted' here. 'Tattheva' means in the repeating itself. 'Sampavaṅkatā' means thoroughly continuing with an inclination or tendency. 'Abbhussahanatā'—here, to explain 'excessive exertion,' it is said: 'why,' etc. 'Anubalappadāna'—here, to explain 'repeatedly giving strength,' it is said: 'to the prior statement,' etc.

Kiccayatāti ettha “mā paṇḍiccaya”ntiādīsu (jā. 2.22.1) viya byañjanavaḍḍhanavasena yakārāgamoti āha “kiccameva kiccaya”nti. “Ubhayaṃpetaṃ saṅghasseva adhivacana”nti iminā kiccakaraṇīyasaddo kattuvācakoti dasseti, saṅgho hi karotīti vacanatthena kiccoti ca karaṇīyoti ca vuccati. Tassa bhāvo, kiccayatā karaṇīyatāti vutte saṅghakammaṃyeva labbhati. Tena vuttaṃ “ubhayaṃpetaṃ saṅghakammasseva adhivacana”nti. Yadi kammavācako bhaveyya, “kattabbanti kiccaṃ, karaṇīya”nti vutteyeva saṅghakammassa labhanato tāpaccayo svattho bhaveyya. Evañhi sati kiccayassa bhāvo kiccayatā karaṇīyassa bhāvo karaṇīyatāti vacanattho na kattabbo bhaveyya, kato ca, tasmā na kammavācakoti daṭṭhabbaṃ. Tassevāti saṅghakammasseva. Tatthāti apalokanādīsu catūsu kammesu. Sīmaṭṭhakasaṅghanti “upacārasīmādīsu ṭhitaṃ saṅghaṃ. Sodhetvāti ettha sodhanaṃ nāma sīmaṭṭhakasaṅghassa hatthapāsanayanaṃ, chandārahānaṃ chandassa āharaṇaṃ, sīmato bahikaraṇaṃ. Tamevatthaṃ ekadesato dassetuṃ vuttaṃ “chandārahānaṃ chandaṃ āharitvā”ti. Apaloketi āpucchati anenāti apalokanaṃ, taṃyeva kammaṃ apalokanakammaṃ. Vuttanayenevāti “sīmaṭṭhakasaṅghaṃ sodhetvā”tiādinā vuttanayeneva. “Suṇātu me”tiādinā saṅghagaṇapuggale ñāpeti etāyāti ñatti, sāyeva kammaṃ ñattikammaṃ, ñattiyeva dutiyaṃ ñattidutiyaṃ, tameva kammaṃ ñattidutiyakammaṃ. Ettha kiñcāpi ñatti paṭhamaṃ ṭhapitā, kammavācāyeva dutiyā [M 0.0444] hoti, “phassapañcamā”tiādīsu (dhātu. 316) viya pana paṭilomavasena vohāraṃ katvā “ñattidutiyā”ti vuttaṃ. Phassapañcamāti ettha kiñcāpi dhammasaṅgaṇiyaṃ (dha. sa. 1 ādayo) “phasso hoti, vedanā hoti, saññā hoti, cetanā hoti[V 2.0095], cittaṃ hotī”ti phassaṃ paṭhamaṃ vuttaṃ, paṭilomavasena pana vohāraṃ katvā “phassapañcamā”ti dhātukathāyaṃ vuttanti daṭṭhabbaṃ. Eseva nayo ñatti catutthakammepi. Ekāya ca anusāvanāyāti ñattito anupacchā sāvetabbāti anusāvanā, tāya, tīhi ca anusāvanāhīti ñattitoanu pacchā, punappunaṃ vā tikkhattuṃ sāvetabbāti anusāvanā, tāhi. Tatthāti catūsu kammesu.

Here, the term 'kiccayatā' is explained as the addition of the letter 'ya' by way of phonetic lengthening, as seen in phrases like 'mā paṇḍiccaya' (Jā. 2.22.1). It is said, 'kiccameva kiccaya,' meaning 'it is indeed a duty.' The phrase 'ubhayaṃpetaṃ saṅghasseva adhivacana' indicates that the word 'kiccakaraṇīya' is an agentive term (kattuvācaka). For the Saṅgha is called 'kicca' and 'karaṇīya' by the meaning that it performs actions. Its state, when 'kiccayatā' or 'karaṇīyatā' is said, only the Saṅgha's formal act is taken. Hence, it is said, 'ubhayaṃpetaṃ saṅghakammasseva adhivacana'—both terms refer to the Saṅgha's formal acts. If it were a passive term (kammavācaka), then saying 'kattabbanti kiccaṃ, karaṇīya' would suffice to indicate the Saṅgha's formal acts, and the suffix 'tā' would have its own meaning. If this were the case, the meaning of 'kiccayatā' as the state of duty and 'karaṇīyatā' as the state of what should be done would not need to be made; but it is made, therefore it should not be considered a passive term. 'Tasseva' refers only to the Saṅgha's formal acts. 'Tatthāti' refers to the four types of formal acts, such as announcements (apalokana). 'Sīmaṭṭhakasaṅgha' means the Saṅgha residing within the boundary (upacārasīmā). 'Sodhetvā' here means purifying, which involves bringing the Saṅgha within reach, obtaining consent from those eligible, and excluding from the boundary. To illustrate this partially, it is said: 'obtaining consent from those eligible.' 'Apalokana' is that by which one announces or requests; that act itself is the apalokana formal act. 'Vuttanayenevāti' means 'in the manner already stated,' such as 'sīmaṭṭhakasaṅghaṃ sodhetvā.' 'Ñatti' is that by which one informs the Saṅgha, the group, or individuals, as in 'Suṇātu me.' That motion itself is the ñattikamma (a formal act consisting of a motion only). A formal act with a motion as the second part is a ñattidutiya; that very formal act is the ñattidutiyakamma. Here, although the motion (ñatti) is placed first, the proclamation (kammavācā) comes second. However, employing a reverse order of expression, as in 'phassapañcamā' (Dhātu. 316), it is called 'ñattidutiyā.' Regarding 'phassapañcamā,' in the Dhammasaṅgaṇī (Dha. Sa. 1 ff.), contact (phassa) is mentioned first, followed by feeling (vedanā), perception (saññā), volition (cetanā), and consciousness (citta). But employing a reverse order of expression, as in the Dhātukathā, it is called 'phassapañcamā.' The same principle applies to the fourth formal act (ñatti catuttha). 'Ekāya ca anusāvanāyāti' means anusāvanā is that which should be proclaimed immediately after the motion; by that. 'Tīhi ca anusāvanāhīti' means anusāvanā is that which should be proclaimed after the motion, or repeatedly three times; by those. 'Tatthāti' refers to the four types of formal acts.

Apaloketvāvāti ettha evaphalaṃ dassento āha “ñattikammādivasena na kātabba”nti. Ñattikammampīti pisaddena na kevalaṃ apalokanakammameva, atha kho ñattikammampīti dasseti. Ñattidutiyakammaṃ panāti ettha panasaddo visesatthajotako, pakkhantarajotako vā. Tatthāti dvīsu kammesu. Garukānīti alahukāni. Avasesānīti chahi kammehi avasesāni, evarūpāni lahukakammānīti sambandho. “Avasesā”tipi pāṭho, sammutiyoti sambandho. Apaloketvāpīti pisaddo ñattidutiyakammavācaṃ sāvetvāpīti sampiṇḍeti. Aññatthāpohanaṃ dassento āha “ñattikammañatticatutthakammavasena pana na kātabbamevā”ti. Ñatticatutthakammaṃ kātabbanti sambandho. Etthāti samathakkhandhake.

Regarding 'Apaloketvāva,' here, showing this very result, it is said: 'It should not be done by means of a motion, and so forth.' Regarding 'Ñattikammampi,' the particle 'pi' shows that it is not only an act by announcement, but also an act by motion. Regarding 'Ñattidutiyakammaṃ pana,' here, the word 'pana' serves to indicate a distinction or to highlight an alternative. 'Tattha' means in the two formal acts. 'Garukāni' means not light. 'Avasesāni' means the remaining from the six formal acts; the connection is that these are light formal acts. 'Avasesā' is also a reading; the connection is 'by agreement.' Regarding 'Apaloketvāpi,' the particle 'pi' combines this with 'also having announced the utterance of the act preceded by a motion.' To show the exclusion of other cases, it is said: 'But it should never be done by means of an act by motion or an act with a motion as the fourth part.' The connection is that the act with a motion as the fourth part should be done. 'Ettha' means in the Chapter on Settling.

Vitthārato pana āgatoyevāti sambandho. Etesanti catunnaṃ kammānaṃ. Yaṃ pana atthajātaṃ anuttānanti sambandho. Tatthāti catūsu kammesu. Tanti atthajātaṃ. Evanti evaṃ kammavaggeyeva vaṇṇayamāne. Hīti laddhaguṇajotako. Suviññeyyāti sukhena viññātabbā.

The connection is: 'However, it has already come in detail.' 'Etesaṃ' refers to the four formal acts. The connection is: 'But the matter that has arisen is not obscure.' 'Tattha' means in the four formal acts. 'Taṃ' means the matter that has arisen. 'Evaṃ' means 'even while describing in this very section on formal acts.' 'Hi' indicates an acquired excellence. 'Suviññeyyā' means easily knowable.

216. Pāḷivasenevāti na aṭṭhakathāvasenāti adhippāyo.

216. 'Pāḷivaseneva' means the intention is 'not in accordance with the commentary.'

220. Yenāti cittuppādena. Iminā vivadanti anenāti vivādoti vacanatthaṃ dasseti. Samathehi cāti casaddo sampiṇḍanattho. Tena [M 0.0445] na kevalaṃ vivādoyeva, atha kho adhikaraṇañcāti sampiṇḍeti, atha vā samathehi cāti samathehi eva. Iminā samathehi adhikarīyati vūpasamīyatīti adhikaraṇanti vacanatthaṃ dasseti. Vivādoyeva adhikaraṇaṃ vivādādhikaraṇaṃ. Evamādinā nayenāti ādisaddena anuddhaṃsanena vadanti anena cittuppādenāti anuvādotiādayo vacanatthe saṅgaṇhāti.

220. 'Yena' means by the arising of a thought. This shows the etymological meaning of the word 'vivādo': 'they dispute by means of this.' Regarding 'samathehi ca,' the word 'ca' has the meaning of combination. Thus, it combines not only a dispute but also a legal issue. Alternatively, 'samathehi ca' means 'only with settlements.' By this, it shows the etymological meaning of the word 'adhikaraṇaṃ': 'by means of these settlements, it is adjudicated or calmed.' A dispute itself is a legal issue: a dispute-legal-issue. Regarding 'by this method, and so forth,' the word 'ādi' includes the etymological meanings of words like 'anuvādo,' as in 'they speak with censure by means of this arising of a thought, therefore it is an accusation,' and so on.

222. Sandhāyabhāsitavasenāti lokavajjaṃ sandhāya bhāsitassa vacanassa vasena. Sandhāyabhāsitatthaṃ vitthārento āha “yasmiṃ hī”tiādi. Tattha pathavikhaṇanādike yasmiṃ āpattādhikaraṇeti [V 2.0096] yojanā. Tasminti kusalacittaṅge āpattādhikaraṇe. Tasmāti yasmā na sakkā vattuṃ, tasmā. Idanti “natthi āpattādhikaraṇaṃ kusala”nti vacanaṃ, vuttanti sambandho. Sandhāya avuttaṃ dassetvā sandhāya vuttaṃ dassento āha “idaṃ pana sandhāya vutta”nti. Tattha idaṃ panāti kāraṇaṃ pana sandhāyāti sambandho. Yaṃ āpattādhikaraṇanti yojanā. “Lokavajja”nti pade tulyādhikaraṇaṃ. Lokasmiṃ, lokehi vā vajjetabbanti lokavajjaṃ. Tanti āpattādhikaraṇaṃ. Tatthāti āpattādhikaraṇe. Vikappoti vividhā kappanaṃ, vividhatakko vā. Yaṃ panāti āpattādhikaraṇaṃ pana. “Paṇṇattivajja”nti pade tulyādhikaraṇaṃ. Bhagavato paññattiyā hetubhūtāya vajjetabbanti paṇṇattivajjaṃ. Tanti āpattādhikaraṇaṃ, akusalaṃ hotīti sambandho. Kiñcīti appamattakaṃ, āpattānāpattiṃ ajānantassa āpajjanatoti sambandho. Tasmāti yasmā abyākataṃ hoti, tasmā. Tatthāti paṇṇattivajjabhūte āpattādhikaraṇe. “Āpattādhikaraṇaṃ…pe… kusala”nti idaṃ vacanaṃ vuttanti yojanā.

222. Regarding 'sandhāyabhāsitavasena,' this means by way of a statement spoken with reference to worldly blame. Expanding on the meaning of what is spoken with reference, he says, 'In which,' and so on. Herein, the connection is: 'in which legal issue of an offense' refers to things like digging the earth. 'Tasmiṃ' means in that legal issue of an offense concerning a wholesome mental factor. 'Tasmā' means 'because it cannot be said, therefore.' 'Idaṃ' means the statement, 'There is no legal issue of an offense that is wholesome'; the connection is 'it is said.' Having shown what was not spoken with reference, showing what was spoken with reference, he says, 'But this was spoken with reference.' Herein, 'idaṃ pana' is connected to 'with reference to the reason.' The explanation is 'which legal issue of an offense.' In the term 'lokavajjaṃ,' the words are in apposition. 'Lokavajjaṃ' means what should be avoided in the world or by the world. 'Taṃ' refers to the legal issue of an offense. 'Tattha' means in the legal issue of an offense. 'Vikappo' means various conceptions, or diverse reasoning. 'Yaṃ pana' means 'but which legal issue of an offense.' In the term 'paṇṇattivajjaṃ,' the words are in apposition. 'Paṇṇattivajjaṃ' means what should be avoided because of the Blessed One’s rule, which is the cause. 'Taṃ' refers to the legal issue of an offense; the connection is that it is unwholesome. 'Kiñci' means a small amount; the connection is 'from one who does not know whether it is an offense or not-an-offense committing it.' 'Tasmā' means 'because it is indeterminate, therefore.' 'Tattha' means in the legal issue of an offense that is blameable by rule. The explanation is that this statement, 'A legal issue of an offense... is wholesome,' is said.

Yadi kusalacitto āpajjati, atha nanu āpattādhikaraṇaṃ kulalanti vattabbo bhaveyyāti āha “sace panā”tiādi. Yanti āpattādhikaraṇaṃ. “Idaṃ vuccati…pe… kusala”nti vadeyya saceti yojanā. Eḷakalomañca padasodhammañca eḷakalomapadasodhammāni, tāni ādīni yesaṃ tānīti eḷakalomapadasodhammādīni, tāni samuṭṭhānāni yāsanti [M 0.0446] eḷakalomapadasodhammādisamuṭṭhānā, tāsaṃ āpattīnampīti sambandho. Tatthāti eḷakalomapadasodhammādisamuṭṭhānāsu āpattīsu. Āpattiyā aṅganti āpattiyā kāraṇaṃ. Evaṃ āpattiyā anaṅgaṃ dassetvā tassāyeva aṅgaṃ dassento āha “kāyavacīviññattivasena panā”tiādi. Tattha calitappavattānanti calitena hetubhūtena pavattānaṃ. Atha vā calito ca kāyo, pavattā ca vācāti calitappavattā, tāsaṃ calitappavattānaṃ kāyavācānaṃ. Tañcāti kāyavācānaṃ aññatarañca. Abyākatanti ettha itisaddo parisamāpanattho.

If one with a wholesome mind commits an offense, then would not the question arise, 'Is the legal issue of an offense wholesome?' Thus, he says, 'But if...' and so on. 'Yaṃ' means the legal issue of an offense. The explanation is: 'If so, one might say, "This is called... wholesome".' 'Sheep's wool' and 'phrase-dhamma' are 'eḷakalomapadasodhammāni'; those of which these are the beginning are 'eḷakalomapadasodhammādīni'; those for which these are the origins are 'eḷakalomapadasodhammādisamuṭṭhānā'; the connection is 'of those offenses as well.' 'Tattha' means among offenses originating from sheep's wool, phrase-dhamma, and so on. 'Āpattiyā aṅgaṃ' means a cause of the offense. Having thus shown what is not a component of the offense, he then shows what is its component, saying, 'But by way of bodily and verbal intimation...' and so on. Here, 'calitappavattānaṃ' means 'of those that have occurred from movement as the cause.' Alternatively, 'the body has moved and speech has occurred,' thus 'calitappavattā'; 'of those moved bodies and occurred speeches.' 'Tañca' means either of the body or speech. Regarding 'abyākataṃ,' here the word 'iti' has the meaning of conclusion.

Ayamattho evaṃ veditabboti yojanā. Tenāti cittena. “Idaṃ…pe… saddhi”nti iminā sañjānantoti ettha saṃsaddassa sundaratthaṃ saha ākārena dasseti. “Vītikkama…pe… kappetvā”ti iminā ceccāti padassa atthaṃ saha visesanena dasseti. “Upakkamavasena…pe… pesetvā”ti iminā abhivitaritvāti padassa atthaṃ dasseti. Pāḷiyaṃ yaṃsaddovītikkamavisayoti āha “yaṃ āpattādhikaraṇaṃ vītikkama”nti. “Āpajjatī”ti iminā pāṭhasesaṃ dasseti. Evaṃ vītikkamato tassa bhikkhunoti yojanā.

The connection is: 'This meaning is to be understood in this way.' 'Tena' means by the mind. By 'this... along with,' regarding 'sañjānanto,' it shows the beautiful meaning of the word 'saṃ' together with its form. By 'transgression... having established,' it shows the meaning of the word 'cecca' together with its specific quality. By 'by way of approach... having dispatched,' it shows the meaning of the word 'abhivitaritvā.' In the Pāli, the word 'yaṃ' has transgression as its domain; thus he says, 'which legal issue of an offense is a transgression.' By 'āpajjati,' it indicates the remainder of the text. The connection is: 'Thus, from the transgression of that bhikkhu.'

Abyākatavārepīti [V 2.0097] pisaddo akusalavāraṃ apekkhati. Tassāti cittassa. Ajānantotiādīnaṃ padānamattho akusalavāre vuttapaṭipakkhavasena veditabbo. Yaṃ āpattādhikaraṇantiādīnaṃ padānamattho akusalavārena sadisoyeva.

Regarding 'abyākatavārepi,' the word 'pi' refers to the unwholesome section. 'Tassa' means of the mind. The meaning of terms like 'ajānanto' should be understood by way of the opposite of what is stated in the unwholesome section. The meaning of terms like 'yaṃ āpattādhikaraṇaṃ' is just the same as in the unwholesome section.

224. Ayaṃ vivādo no adhikaraṇantiādīsu evamattho veditabboti sambandho.

224. The connection is: 'In phrases like "This dispute is not a legal issue," the meaning should be understood in this way.'

9. Adhikaraṇavūpasamanasamathakathā

9. The Discourse on the Settling and Pacification of Legal Issues

228. Catuvaggakaraṇe kammeti sīmasammutiādikamme. Pañcavaggakaraṇeti paccantimesu janapadesu upasampadādikamme. Dasavaggakaraṇeti majjhimesu janapadesu upasampadakamme. Vīsativaggakaraṇeti abbhānakamme. Kammappattāti kammassa pattā yuttā anurūpā.

228. 'An act to be performed by a group of four' refers to acts such as the agreement on a boundary. 'An act to be performed by a group of five' refers to acts such as the higher ordination in outlying districts. 'An act to be performed by a group of ten' refers to the act of higher ordination in the central districts. 'An act to be performed by a group of twenty' refers to the act of rehabilitation. 'Kammappattā' means reached, fit, and suitable for the act.

230. Sampaṭicchitabbanti [M 0.0447] paṭiggaṇhitabbaṃ. Sampaṭicchitvā ca pana atikkāmetabbanti sambandho. Bhaṇḍakanti cīvarādibhaṇḍakaṃ. Mānaniggahatthāyāti bhaṇḍanajātānaṃ mānassa niggahatthāya. Katipāhanti katipayāhaṃ, dvīhatīhanti attho.

230. 'Sampaṭicchitabbaṃ' means it should be received. The connection is: 'And having accepted, it should then be allowed to pass.' 'Bhaṇḍakaṃ' refers to goods such as robes and so forth. 'Mānaniggahatthāya' means for subduing the pride of those who have become quarrelsome. 'Katipāhaṃ' means for some days; the meaning is for two or three days.

231. Anantāni ceva bhassānīti ettha anantasaddo aparimāṇasaddena atthato ekoti āha “aparimāṇānī”ti. “Vacanānī”ti iminā bhassasaddo vacanapariyāyoti dasseti. Ubbāhikāya sammanitabboti kena sammanitabboti āha “apaloketvā vā”tiādi. Iminā apalokanakammena vā ñattidutiyakammena vā sammanitabboti dasseti. Anantāni bhassāni dhammakathikaṃ uddharitvā bāhati paṭisedheti imāya sammutiyāti ubbāhikā, tāya. Evaṃ sammatehi pana bhikkhūhi vinicchitabbanti sambandho. Visuṃ nisīditvā tassāyeva parisāya nisīditvā vāti yojanā. Aññehīti sammatabhikkhūhi aññehi.

231. Regarding 'endless talk,' here the word 'endless' is one in meaning with 'immeasurable,' hence it says 'immeasurable.' By 'utterances,' it shows that the word 'talk' is a synonym for 'utterance.' Regarding 'should be sanctioned by an ubbāhikā,' by whom should it be sanctioned? It says, 'having consulted or...' etc. This shows that it should be sanctioned either by an apalokana act or by a ñattidutiya act. The ubbāhikā is that resolution by which endless talk is rejected or prevented, having singled out a Dhamma speaker. The connection is that it should be judged by the monks thus sanctioned. The construction is: 'sitting separately or sitting in that very assembly.' 'By others' means by others than the sanctioned monks.

233. Tatrassāti ettha tatra assāti padavibhāgaṃ katvā tasaddo parisavisayo pasiddhavisayo, assasaddo ākhyātikoti āha “tassaṃ parisati bhaveyyā”ti. “Neva suttaṃ āgata”nti sāmaññato vuttepi “no suttavibhaṅgo”ti vakkhamānattā mātikaṃ sandhāya vuttanti āha “na mātikā āgatā”ti. Vinayopīti khandhakavinayopi. Pisaddena suttavibhaṅgaṃ apekkhati. Byañjanacchāyāyāti ettha chāyāsaddo paṭibimbe ca pabhāya ca hotīti āha “byañjanamattamevā”ti, byañjanapaṭibimbikabyañjanapabhāvantabhūtaṃ atthaṃ aggahetvā byañjanapaṭibimbabyañjanapabhāmattameva [V 2.0098] gahetvāti adhippāyo. “Paṭisedhetī”ti iminā paṭibāhasaddo paṭisedhatthoyeva, na maddanatthoti dasseti. Paṭibāhanākāraṃ dassento āha “jātarūparajatakhettavatthupaṭiggahaṇādīsū”tiādi. Kinti kena kāraṇena, kasmā kāraṇā vā. Imeti jātarūpādipaṭiggāhake bhikkhū. Kārethāti tumhe [M 0.0448] kāreyyātha. Eyyāthassa hi ethādeso. Pucchāyaṃ sattamīvibhatti hoti. Sutteti suttantapiṭake. Aparo dhammakathiko vadatīti sambandho. Imesanti olambetvā nivāsentānaṃ. Etthāti olambetvā nivāsane.

233. Here, the word 'tatrassa' is divided as 'tatra assa.' The word 'ta' refers to the assembly and to a well-known matter, and the word 'assa' is a verb; thus, it says, 'he would be in that assembly.' Regarding 'Neva suttaṃ āgata' (it is not found in the Sutta), although stated generally, since it will be said 'no Suttavibhaṅgo' (nor in the Suttavibhaṅga), it is said with reference to the Mātikā; hence it says 'na mātikā āgatā' (nor is the Mātikā found). 'Vinayopi' means 'khandhakavinayopi.' The particle 'pi' implies the Suttavibhaṅga. Regarding 'byañjanacchāyāya' (by the shadow of the expression), here the word 'chāyā' can mean both reflection and radiance. Thus, it says, 'merely the expression.' The intention is that, without grasping the meaning that is the reflection or radiance of the expression, one grasps merely the reflection or radiance of the expression. By 'paṭisedheti' (prevents), it shows that the word 'paṭibāha' has the sense of prevention, not suppression. To illustrate the manner of hindrance, it says, 'such as in accepting gold, silver, fields, or property,' etc. 'Kinti' means 'for what reason?' or 'from what cause?' 'Ime' refers to the monks who accept gold, etc. 'Kāretha' means 'you should cause.' For 'eyyātha,' 'etha' is the substitute. In a question, the locative case is used. 'Sutte' means in the Suttanta Piṭaka. The connection is: 'another Dhamma speaker says.' 'Imesaṃ' means 'of those who wear their robes hanging down.' 'Ettha' means 'in the act of wearing robes hanging down.'

234. Bahutarā bhikkhūti ettha dviguṇatiguṇādinā adhikā eva bahutarā nāmāti āha “ekenapi adhikā bahutarāvā”ti. “Ko pana vādo”tiādinā “ekenapī”ti ettha pisaddassa garahatthaṃ dasseti.

234. Here, regarding 'the majority of bhikkhus,' while those who are more numerous by two or three times, etc., are called 'the majority,' it says, 'even one more is a majority.' By 'What need to say?' etc., it shows that the particle 'pi' in 'even one' has the sense of censure.

Tividhasalākaggāhakathā

The Discussion on the Three Ways of Taking Lots

235. Saññattiyāti ettha saññāpanaṃ saññatti, tadatthāyāti dassento āha “saññāpanatthāyā”ti. Gūhitabboti gūḷho, soyeva gūḷhako, salākaggāho kātabboti sambandho. Vivaritabboti vivaṭo, soyeva vivaṭako. Sassa attano kaṇṇasamīpe jappīyati kathīyatīti sakaṇṇajappo, soyeva sakaṇṇajappako. “Nimittasaññaṃ āropetvā”ti iminā vaṇṇāvaṇṇāyo katvāti ettha vaṇṇasaddo saṇṭhānavācakoti dasseti. Susaṇṭhānadusaṇṭhānā salākāyo katvāti attho. Tatoti visabhāgakaraṇato paraṃ gahetabboti sambandho. Sabbāpi tā salākāyoti yojanā. Katvāti pakkhipanaṃ katvā. Vuttanayenāti “alajjussannāyā”tiādinā vuttanayena. “Yāvatatiya”nti iminā paccukkaḍḍhitabbanti ettha punappunaṃ uddhaṃ kaḍḍhitabbanti atthaṃ dasseti. Atirekajāteti adhammavādīhi atirekato jāte satīti sambandho. Yāvatatiyampīti pisaddo tato ūne ekadvevāre pana kā nāma kathāti dasseti.

235. Here, regarding 'saññattiyā,' informing is 'saññatti'; to show that it is for this purpose, it says, 'for the purpose of informing.' 'Gūhitabbo' (to be concealed) means concealed, that very one is the concealed one; the connection is that the taking of lots should be done. 'Vivaritabbo' (to be opened) means opened, that very one is the opened one. 'Sakaṇṇajappo' is what is whispered or spoken near one's own ear, that very one is the whisperer. By 'nimittasaññaṃ āropetvā' (having imposed a sign), it is shown that here in 'vaṇṇāvaṇṇāyo katvā' (having made them of different colors), the word 'vaṇṇa' refers to a shape. The meaning is that the lots should be made with good or bad shapes. The connection is: 'Tato' means that after making them dissimilar, they should be taken. 'Sabbāpi tā salākāyo' (all those lots) is the construction. 'Katvā' means having placed them. 'Vuttanayena' (by the stated method) refers to the method stated, such as 'alajjussannāyā' (by the shameless majority), etc. By 'yāvatatiya' (up to the third time), it is shown that the meaning of 'paccukkaḍḍhitabbaṃ' (should be drawn up again) is that it should be repeatedly drawn upward. The connection is: 'Atirekajāte' (when an excess arises) means when an excess arises from those who speak against the Dhamma.
