The particle 'pi' in 'yāvatatiyampi' (even up to the third time) indicates that if it is less than that, for one or two times, what need is there to speak?

Sakaṇṇajappake pana evaṃ vinicchayo veditabboti yojanā. Sace saṅghatthero gaṇhātīti sambandho. Soti saṅghatthero. Vayoanuppattāti pacchimavayaṃ anuppattā. Etanti adhammavādisalākaṃ. Assāti [M 0.0449] saṅghattherassa. Itarā salākāti adhammavādisalākāhi aññā dhammavādisalākā. Soti saṅghatthero. Tanti dhammavādisalākaṃ. Tatoti neva avabujjhanakāraṇā. Vuttanayamevāti gūḷhake vuttanayameva. Vivaṭo attho imassāti vivaṭattho.

But in the case of the private whisper, the decision should be understood thus—this is the construction. The connection is: 'If the Sangha elder takes it.' 'So' (he) means the Sangha elder. 'Vayoanuppattā' (having attained age) means having attained the last stage of life. 'Etaṃ' (this) refers to the ballot of one speaking against the Dhamma. 'Assā' (of him) means of the Sangha elder. 'Itarā salākā' (the other ballot) means the ballot of one speaking for the Dhamma, other than the ballots of those speaking against the Dhamma. 'So' (he) means the Sangha elder. 'Taṃ' (that) means the ballot of one speaking for the Dhamma. 'Tato' (from that) means not because of a reason for not understanding. 'Vuttanayameva' (just the method stated) means just the method stated for the concealed ballot. 'Vivaṭo attho imassā' means 'its meaning is open,' hence 'vivaṭattho' (of open meaning).

Tassapāpiyasikāvinayakathā

The Discussion on the Tassapāpiyasikā Disciplinary Matter

238. Pārājikasāmantaṃ [V 2.0099] nāmāti pārājikassa āsannaṃ nāma. Adinnādānādīsūti ādisaddena manussaviggaha uttarimanussadhammapārājike saṅgaṇhāti. Nibbeṭhayamānanti veṭhanarahitaṃ, tamenaṃ bhikkhunti sambandho. Iminā nibbeṭhentanti ettha antasaddo mānasaddapariyāyoti dasseti. Ativeṭhetīti ettha kehi ativeṭhetīti āha “iṅghāyasmātiādivacanehī”ti. Tenāti codakena. Manti mamaṃ. Āhāti cuditako āha. Etassāti avajānanapaṭijānanādikārakassa pāpiyassa puggalassa. Sīlavā bhavissatīti pāpiyo puggalo sace sīlavā bhavissati. Paṭippassaddhinti pāpiyabhāvato paṭippassambhanaṃ. No ceti sīlavā no bhavissati ce. Tathā nāsitoti tena tassa pāpiyasikakammakaraṇena nāsaṃ gato bhavissati. Sabbatthāti sabbasmiṃ samathakkhandhake.

238. 'Pārājikasāmantaṃ nāma' means what is near to a pārājika offense. Regarding 'Adinnādānādīsu,' by the word 'ādi,' it includes the pārājika offenses of killing a human being and claiming superhuman states. 'Nibbeṭhayamānaṃ' means without concealment; the connection is 'that monk.' By this, it is shown that here in 'nibbeṭhenti,' the suffix '-anta' is a synonym for the suffix '-māna.' Regarding 'ativeṭheti' (excessively conceals), by what does he excessively conceal? It says, 'by sayings such as "Come, venerable one,"' etc. 'Tena' means by the accuser. 'Maṃ' means 'me.' 'Āha' means the accused said. 'Etassa' refers to that wicked person who acts with disrespect, denial, etc. 'Sīlavā bhavissati' means 'if that wicked person becomes virtuous.' 'Paṭippassaddhi' means the calming of the state of wickedness. 'No ce' means 'if he does not become virtuous.' 'Tathā nāsito' means 'by the performance of that Tassapāpiyasikā act for him, he will have gone to ruin.' 'Sabbattha' means in the entire Samathakkhandhaka.

Iti samathakkhandhakavaṇṇanāya yojanā samattā.

Thus the grammatical analysis of the Samathakkhandhaka commentary is concluded.

5. Khuddakavatthukkhandhakaṃ

5. The Chapter on Minor Matters

Khuddakavatthukathā

The Discussion on Minor Matters

243. Khuddakavatthukkhandhake muṭṭhikamallāti muṭṭhikena mathanti aññamaññaṃ hiṃsantīti muṭṭhikamallā. Iminā pāḷiyaṃ padassa heṭṭhupariyaṃ dasseti. Gāmamudavāti ettha chavirāgamaṇḍanānuyuttena mudo modanaṃ etesamatthīti mudavā, gāme vasantā mudavā gāmamudavāti dassento āha “chavirāgamaṇḍanānuyuttā nāgarikamanussā”ti. “Vaṇṇavā ahesu”ntiādīsu [M 0.0450] (pārā. 193; pāci. 67) viya vacanaṃ daṭṭhabbaṃ. Thambheti ettha na yattha katthaci thambho hoti, atha kho nhānatitthe nikhaṇitvā ṭhapitathambhoyevāti āha “nhānatitthe nikhaṇitvā ṭhapitatthambhe”ti.

243. In the Khuddakavatthukkhandhaka, 'muṭṭhikamallā' means those who strike each other with their fists, harming one another—hence, they are fist-fighters. By this, it shows the inversion of the words in the Pāli text. Here, regarding 'gāmamudavā,' 'mudavā' are those who find pleasure through being devoted to coloring and adorning the skin. 'Gāmamudavā' are 'mudavā' who live in a village. Showing this, it says, 'townsfolk devoted to coloring and adorning the skin.' The expression should be understood as in 'vaṇṇavā ahesu,' etc. (Pārā. 193; Pāci. 67). Here, regarding 'thambhe,' it is not just any post, but rather it is a post dug in and set up at a bathing place; thus it says 'on a post dug in and set up at a bathing place.'

Iṭṭhakāsilādārukuṭṭānanti iṭṭhakākuṭṭasilākuṭṭadārukuṭṭānaṃ. Aṭṭhapadākārenāti aṭṭhapadaphalakākārena. Rājiyoti lekhāyo. Tatthāti aṭṭāne, ākiritvāti sambandho. Gandhabbahatthakoti [V 2.0100] gandhabbānaṃ vīṇāhattho viyāti gandhabbahatthako. Dārūhi katattā vuttaṃ “dārumayahatthenā”ti. Tenāti gandhabbahatthena, gahetvāti sambandho. Kuruvindakapāsāṇacuṇṇānīti evaṃnāmakassa pāsāṇassa cuṇṇāni. Tanti kataguḷikakalāpakaṃ, gahetvāti sambandho. Viggayhāti aññamaññassa sarīre daḷhaṃ gahetvāti dassento āha “aññamaññaṃ sarīrena sarīra”nti. Makaradantaketi makaranāmakassa macchassa dantasadise dante. Mallakamūlasaṇṭhānenāti kheḷapaṭiggahapādasaṇṭhānena. Gilānassāpīti pisaddo agilānassa pagevāti dasseti.

"Iṭṭhakāsilādārukuṭṭāni" refers to brick walls, stone walls, and wooden walls. "Aṭṭhapadākārena" means in the shape of an eight-squared board. "Rājiyo" refers to lines. "Tattha" means in that place, on the board, and is connected with "ākiritvā". "Gandhabbahatthako" is like the hand of a celestial musician (gandhabba) holding a lute—hence, "gandhabba-hand." It is called "dārumayahatthena" because it is made of wood. "Tena" means by that gandhabba-hand, and is connected with "gahetvā". "Kuruvindakapāsāṇacuṇṇāni" refers to the powder of a stone named Kuruvindaka. "Tanti" refers to a bundle of prepared balls, and is connected with "gahetvā". "Viggayhā" means firmly grasping each other's bodies—hence, he says "body to body with each other's body," indicating a firm grip. "Makaradantake" refers to teeth resembling those of a fish called makara. "Mallakamūlasaṇṭhānena" means shaped like the base of a spittoon. Regarding "Gilānassāpi", the particle "pi" indicates 'even for the sick', and therefore, how much more so for one who is not sick.

244. Danteti makaradante. Akataṃ mallakaṃ akatamallakaṃ. Kapālakhaṇḍaṃ vāti vāsaddo samuccayattho. Kāsaphullavirahitattā vatthavaṭṭi ukkāsikā nāma. Natthi kāsaṃ phullametissāti ukkāsā, sā eva ukkāsikā. Yassa kassacīti gilānāgilānassa vā jarādubbalataruṇabalavassa vā. Piṭṭhinti piṭṭhiyaṃ, ayameva vā pāṭho. Pāṇitalassa puthuṭṭhānaṃ puthupāṇi, tena kataṃ puthupāṇikaṃ, hatthaparikammaṃ, tena vuttaṃ “hatthaparikammaṃ vuccatī”ti. Sabbesanti nhāyantānaṃ vā anhāyantānaṃ vā sabbesaṃ.

244. "Danteti" refers to a makara's tooth. "Akataṃ mallakaṃ" means an unfashioned bowl. In "Kapālakhaṇḍaṃ vā", the particle "vā" indicates conjunction. The cloth bandage is called "ukkāsikā" because it lacks kāsa grass flowers. That which has no kāsa grass flowers is "ukkāsā"; that itself is "ukkāsikā." "Yassa kassaci" means to anyone, whether sick or not sick, old and feeble, or young and strong. "Piṭṭhinti" means on the back; or this may be the reading itself. The broad part of the palm is a "puthupāṇi"; what is done with that is "puthupāṇikaṃ", a hand massage; therefore, it is said, "it is called a hand massage." "Sabbesanti" means for all, whether bathing or not bathing.

245. Kaṇṇatoti kaṇṇacchiddato. Muttolambakādivallisadisattā vallikā nāma. Palambakasuttanti parimuñcitvā lambiyati anenāti palambakaṃ, tameva suttaṃ palambakasuttaṃ. Valayanti niyuraṃ.

245. "Kaṇṇato" means from the ear hole. "Vallikā" is so called because it resembles a creeper, like a pearl necklace and so forth. Regarding "Palambakasutta", that by which something hangs down after being put on is a "palambakaṃ"; that very thread is the "palambakasutta". "Valayanti" means they wear an anklet or bracelet.

246. Dvīhi māsehi niyuttaṃ dumāsikaṃ. Dve aṅgulāni etassāti duvaṅgulaṃ, keso. Ubhayenapīti dumāsikaduvaṅgulasaṅkhātena ubhayenapi[M 0.0451]. Ayampi ukkaṭṭhaparicchedova vuttoti yojanā. Tatoti dumāsikaduvaṅgulato.

246. "Dumāsika" means appointed for two months. "Duvaṅgulaṃ" means that which is two finger-widths, referring to hair. "Ubhayenapi" means by both, that is, by both what is enumerated as two months and two finger-widths. This too is stated as the highest limit; this is the connection. "Tato" means from that, from the two-month and two-finger-width measure.

Osaṇṭhentīti ettha olikhitvā samaṃ patiṭṭhāpentīti dassento āha “olikhitvā sannisīdāpentī”ti. Dantamayādīsūti ādisaddena aṭṭhimayādayo saṅgaṇhāti. Hatthaphaṇenāti hatthasaṅkhātena phaṇena. Cikkhallenāti cikkhallasadisena niyyāsena. Udakatelenāti ettha udakañca telañcāti ca udakasaṅkhātena telenāti ca atthaṃ nivattento āha “udakamissakena telenā”ti. Iminā udakena missakaṃ telaṃ udakatelanti vacanatthaṃ dasseti. Uṭṭhalometi uṭṭhitalome. Hatthaṃ temetvāti hatthaṃ udakatelena temetvā. Uṇhābhitattarajokiṇṇasirānampīti uṇhena abhitatto ca rajehi okiṇṇasiro ca uṇhābhitattarajokiṇṇasirā, atha vā uṇhena abhitatto siro etesanti uṇhābhitattasirā, rajehi okiṇṇo siro etesanti rajokiṇṇasirā[V 2.0101], uṇhābhitattasirā ca rajokiṇṇasirā ca uṇhābhitattarajokiṇṇasirā, pubbapade uttarapadalopo, tesampi. Allahatthenāti addahatthena, ayameva vā pāṭho.

Regarding "Osaṇṭhentīti", here, showing that it means to smooth out and establish evenly by scraping, he says, "by scraping and settling evenly." In "Dantamayādīsu", the word "ādi" includes items made of bone, etc. "Hatthaphaṇena" means with the hand as a comb. "Cikkhallena" means with a sap-like substance resembling mud. Regarding "Udakatelena", here, rejecting the meanings 'water and oil' and 'oil designated as water', he says it means "with oil mixed with water." With this, he shows that the meaning of the word "udakatela" is oil mixed with water. "Uṭṭhalome" means on raised hair. "Hatthaṃ temetvā" means having moistened the hand with water-oil. Regarding "Uṇhābhitattarajokiṇṇasirānampi", it means of those whose heads are overheated by the heat and covered with dust; or alternatively, those whose heads are overheated by the heat are uṇhābhitattasirā; those whose heads are covered with dust are rajokiṇṇasirā; uṇhābhitattasirā and rajokiṇṇasirā become uṇhābhitattarajokiṇṇasirā, with the latter part of the first compound elided; even of those. "Allahatthenāti" means with a wet hand; or this itself may be the reading.

247. Yesu kaṃsapattādīsu mukhanimittaṃ paññāyati, sabbāni tāni kaṃsapattādīnipīti yojanā. Yattha katthacīti yasmiṃ kasmiṃci ādāse vā udakapatte vāti sambandho. Sañchavi nu khoti sañjātā chavi nu kho, ahaṃ jiṇṇo amhi nu kho, noti yojanā.

247. In whichever items such as bronze bowls a reflection of the face appears, all those items such as bronze bowls are also included; this is the connection. "Yattha katthaci" means in any mirror or water bowl; this is the connection. "Sañchavi nu kho" means "has my skin changed? Am I now old?"; this is the connection.

Mukhaṃ ālimpantīti ettha kehi ālimpantīti āha “vippasannachavirāgakarehi mukhalepanehī”ti. “Manosilāyā”ti iminā manosilā eva manosilikāti dasseti. Tānīti lañchanāni. Haritālādīhipīti pisaddena na kevalaṃ manosilikāya eva, atha kho haritālādīhipīti dasseti.

Regarding "Mukhaṃ ālimpanti", here, when asked with what they anoint, he said, "with facial ointments that make the complexion clear and radiant." By "Manosilāyā", he shows that "manosilā" itself is "manosilikā." "Tāni" refers to the marks. Regarding "Haritālādīhipi", by the particle "pi" he shows that it is not only with "manosilikā," but also with orpiment, etc.

248. Na [M 0.0452] bhikkhave naccaṃ vātiādīsu evaṃ vinicchayo veditabboti yojanā. Niccāpentassa vāti parehi naccāpentassa vā. Sādhugītanti sundaraṃ aniccatādipaṭisaṃyuttaṃ gītaṃ, sajjanānaṃ vā. Dantagītampi na vaṭṭatīti sambandho. Yanti gītaṃ. Pubbabhāgeti gāyanato pubbabhāge. Gāyāpentassāpīti parehi vā gāyāpentassāpi. Yaṃ panāti kiriyāparāmasanaṃ. Yaṃ paharati, tattha paharaṇe anāpattīti yojanā. Sabbanti akhilaṃ naccagītavāditaṃ. Passatoti passantassa ca suṇantassa ca. Savanampi hi ekasesena vā sāmaññaniddesena vā passaneneva saṅgahitaṃ. Vihāratoti anaccaagītaavāditaṭṭhānavihārato. Vihāranti naccagītavāditaṭṭhānavihāraṃ. Asanasālāyāti gāme ṭhitāya asanasālāya.

248. Regarding the passage beginning 'Monks, not dancing...', the decision should be understood in this way; this is the connection. "Niccāpentassa vā" means or of one who makes others dance. "Sādhugītaṃ" means beautiful singing connected with impermanence, etc., or the singing of virtuous people. "Even tooth-song is not allowed"—this is the connection. "Yaṃ" means singing. "Pubbabhāge" means in the earlier part, before the singing begins. "Gāyāpentassāpi" means even of one who is made to sing by others. "Yaṃ pana" is a reference to the action. "Whatever one strikes, there is no offense in that striking"; such is the explanation. "Sabbaṃ" means the entirety of dancing, singing, and instrumental music. "Passato" applies both to one who sees and one who hears, for hearing is also included under seeing, either by ellipsis or by general designation. "Vihārato" means from dwelling in a place free from dancing, singing, and instrumental music. "Vihāranti" means they dwell in a place of dancing, singing, and instrumental music. "Asanasālāyā" refers to an assembly hall situated in the village.

249. Sarakiriyanti sarassa kiriyaṃ. Iminā sarakuttinti ettha sarassa karaṇaṃ sarakuttīti vacanatthaṃ dasseti. Aladdhaṃ samādhinti sambandho. Pacchimā janatāti ettha samūhiṃ avayavaṃ vinā samūhassa avayavino abhāvā tāpaccayo svatthopi hotīti āha “pacchimo jano”ti. Taṃ taṃ vattanti suttantavattādiṃ taṃ taṃ vattaṃ. Akkharāni vināsetvāti aññathā vattabbāni akkharāni aññathā vadanena ca dīghādīni rassādivadanena ca vināsetvā. Dhamme panāti ettha saddo pana visesajotako. Gītato visesova veditabboti hi attho. Suttantavattanti suttantassa uccāraṇaṃ vattaṃ. Eseva nayo “jātakavattaṃ gāthāvatta”nti etthāpi. Tanti vattaṃ. Yadi pana taṃ vināsetvā atidīghaṃ kātuṃ na vaṭṭati, evaṃ sati yathā suttantavattādīni honti, tathā kathaṃ dassetabbānīti āha “caturassena vattenā”tiādi. Tattha caturassena [V 2.0102] vattenāti paripuṇṇena uccāraṇavattena. Parimaṇḍalānīti samantato maṇḍalāni bimbāni puṇṇānīti attho. “Sarena bhaṇita”nti iminā sarabhaññanti ettha sarena bhaṇitabbanti sarabhaññanti vacanatthaṃ dasseti. Sarabhaññe kira atthīti sambandho[M 0.0453]. Taraṅgavatthādīnaṃ uccāraṇavidhānāni (vajira. ṭī. cūḷavagga 249; sārattha. ṭī. cūḷavagga 3.249; vi. vi. ṭī. cūḷavagga 2.248-9) etarahi natthi. Dvattiṃsavattānīti ca saṅkhyāmattameva atthi, na saṅkhyeyyaṃ. Tasmā ṭīkāsu (sārattha. ṭī. cūḷavagga 3.249; vajira. ṭī. cūḷavagga. 249) “taraṅgavattādīnaṃ uccāraṇavidhānāni naṭṭhapayogānī”ti vuttaṃ. Atthīti saṃvijjanti. Ayañhi atthisaddo nipāto. Tesūti dvattiṃsavattesu. Yanti vattaṃ. Uccāraṇavidhānāni naṭṭhapayogānipi tesaṃ sabbesaṃ sāmaññalakkhaṇaṃ dassento āha “sabbesa”ntiādi. Tattha sabbesanti dvattiṃsavattānaṃ, lakkhaṇanti sambandho. “Avināsetvā”ti vatvā tamevatthaṃ pākaṭaṃ karonto āha “vikāraṃ akatvā”ti. Tattha vikārakaraṇaṃ nāma yattakāhi mattāhi akkharaṃ paripuṇṇaṃ hoti, tato adhikamattāyuttaṃ katvā kathanaṃ, tathā akatvā samaṇasāruppena caturassena nayena pavattanaṃyeva lakkhaṇanti attho.

249. 'Sarakiriyā' means the action of the voice. By this, it shows the verbal meaning of 'sarakutti' here as 'the production of the voice'. The connection is to 'aladdhaṃ samādhiṃ'. Regarding 'pacchimā janatā', because a collective whole does not exist without its collective members, the suffix '-tā' can also be used in its own sense; hence it is said 'pacchimo jano'. 'Taṃ taṃ vattaṃ' refers to each particular manner of recitation, such as the recitation of suttas. 'Akkharāni vināsetvā' means destroying the letters by pronouncing letters that should be said one way in another way, and by pronouncing long vowels as short, and so on. Regarding 'dhamme pana'—here the word 'pana' is a particle indicating a distinction. The meaning is that it should be understood as a distinction from chanting. 'Suttantavattaṃ' means the manner of reciting the sutta. The same method applies to 'jātakavattaṃ' and 'gāthāvattaṃ' here. 'Taṃ' refers to the manner of recitation. But if it is not proper to make it excessively long by destroying it, this being so, how should it be shown how the suttanta-recitations and so on are to be done? It is explained with 'caturassena vattenā', and so on. Here, 'caturassena vattenā' means with a complete and proper manner of recitation. 'Parimaṇḍalāni' means perfectly rounded, complete, and full, like orbs. By 'sarena bhaṇitaṃ', it shows that 'sarabhaññaṃ' here has the verbal meaning 'what is spoken with the voice'. The connection is 'sarabhaññe kira atthi'. The methods of recitation for 'taraṅgavatta' and so on are now lost. 'Dvattiṃsavattāni' is merely a number, not the things numbered. Therefore, in the subcommentaries, it is said, 'The recitation methods for taraṅgavatta and the like have fallen out of use.' 'Atthi' means they exist. This word 'atthi' is a particle. 'Tesu' refers to the thirty-two recitation styles. 'Yaṃ' refers to the manner of recitation. Even though the recitation methods have fallen out of use, their general characteristic is explained by saying 'sabbesaṃ' and so on. Here, 'sabbesaṃ' refers to all thirty-two recitation styles; 'lakkhaṇaṃ' is the connection. Having stated 'avināsetvā', the same meaning is clarified by saying 'vikāraṃ akatvā'. Here, 'vikārakaraṇaṃ' means pronouncing a letter with more morae than is required for it to be complete; whereas not doing so, and reciting in a manner befitting a recluse, with a complete and proper method, is the characteristic.

Bāhiralomiṃ uṇṇinti ettha “bāhiralomi”nti padaṃ bhāvanapuṃsakanti āha “uṇṇalomāni bahi katvā”ti. “Uṇṇapāvāra”nti iminā uṇṇīti ettha uttarapadalopaṃ dasseti. Atha vā pāvārapadena uṇṇā etassa atthīti uṇṇīti katvā taddhitapaccayassa sarūpaṃ dasseti. “Tathā dhārentassa dukkaṭa”nti vacanassa atthāpattinayaṃ dassento āha “lomāni anto katvā pārupituṃ vaṭṭatī”ti.

Regarding 'bāhiralomiṃ uṇṇiṃ', here it is said that the word 'bāhiralomiṃ' is neuter in the abstract sense, meaning 'having put the woolly hairs outside.' By 'uṇṇapāvāraṃ', it shows the elision of the latter word in 'uṇṇiṃ' here. Or alternatively, by the word 'pāvāra', it shows the form of the taddhita suffix, taking 'uṇṇī' as 'one who possesses wool'. Showing the method of implication in the statement 'Tathā dhārentassa dukkaṭaṃ', it says, 'It is allowable to wrap oneself having put the hairs inside.'

251. Aṅgajātaṃ chindantassevāti aṅgajātameva chindantassāti yojanā. Atha vā aṅgajātaṃ chindantassa thullaccayamevāti yojanā. Ahikīṭadaṭṭhādīsu nimittabhūtesu chindantassāti yojanā.

251. 'Aṅgajātaṃ chindantasseva'—the construction is 'aṅgajātameva chindantassa.' Or alternatively, the construction is: 'aṅgajātaṃ chindantassa, thullaccayameva.' The construction is 'chindantassa' when cutting due to indicative causes such as snake or insect bites.

252. Uppannā hotīti paṭilābhavasena uppannā hoti. Uppannabhāvaṃ pākaṭaṃ karonto āha “so”tiādi. Tattha soti rājagahako seṭṭhi, kīḷatīti sambandho. Tassāti seṭṭhissa. Idaṃ padaṃ “jāle”ti pade sāmyatthachaṭṭhī, “uppannā hotī”ti pade sampadānaṃ. Tanti candanagaṇṭhiṃ. Assāti seṭṭhissa. Idaṃ padaṃ “purisā”ti pade sāmyatthachaṭṭhī, “adaṃsū”ti pade sampadānaṃ. Vikubbaniddhīti vividhaṃ, vikāraṃ [M 0.0454] vā kubbanavasena pavattā iddhi (paṭi. ma. 3.12-16; visuddhi. 2.369-373). Adhiṭṭhāniddhīti [V 2.0103] adhiṭṭhānavasena pavattā iddhi (paṭi. ma. 3.12-16; visuddhi. 2.369-373).

252. 'Uppannā hoti' means it arose by way of gain. Making clear the state of having arisen, it is said, 'so', and so on. There, 'so' is the Rājagaha merchant; it is connected with 'kīḷati.' 'Tassa' means of the merchant. This word is a genitive in the sense of relation to the word 'jāle,' and a dative in relation to the phrase 'uppannā hoti.' 'Taṃ' means the sandalwood knot. 'Assa' means of the merchant. This word is a genitive in the sense of relation to the word 'purisā,' and a dative in relation to the phrase 'adaṃsu.' 'Vikubbaniddhi' is the power that proceeds by way of making various changes or transformations. 'Adhiṭṭhāniddhi' is the power that proceeds by way of determination.

Gihī upanāmentīti sambandho. Byañjanaṃ katvāti byañjanaṃ pakkhipanaṃ katvā. Tanti suvaṇṇataṭṭikādiṃ. Āmasitumpīti pisaddo pageva paṭiggaṇhitunti dasseti. Saṅghikaparibhogena vāti vāsaddo panasaddattho. Saṅghikaparibhogena panāti hi attho. Gihivikaṭāni vāti vāsaddo sampiṇḍanattho. Gihivikaṭāni bhājanānipi vaṭṭantīti hi attho. Kaṃsalohavaṭṭalohānaṃ sabhāgattā vuttaṃ “kaṃsa…pe… saṅgahito”ti.

'Gihī upanāmenti' is the connection. 'Byañjanaṃ katvā' means having put in the condiment. 'Taṃ' refers to a gold plate and so on. 'Āmasituṃ pi'—the word 'pi' here shows 'let alone to receive'. 'Saṅghikaparibhogena vā'—the word 'vā' here has the meaning of 'pana.' Indeed, the meaning is 'Saṅghikaparibhogena pana.' 'Gihivikaṭāni vā'—the word 'vā' here has the meaning of 'sampiṇḍana' (collection/inclusion). Indeed, the meaning is that even household utensils are allowable. Because bronze and lead are of the same nature as metal, it is said, 'bronze... and so on... is included.'

253. “Likhitu”nti etaṃ vuttanti yojanā. Pakatimaṇḍalanti ettha kiṃ makaradantamattampi acchinnamaṇḍalanti āha “makaradantacchinnakamaṇḍalamevā”ti.

253. The construction is that 'likhituṃ' is said. Regarding 'pakatimaṇḍalaṃ'—here, is it a circle that is not cut even to the extent of a makara-tooth? It is said, 'It is indeed a circle cut like a makara-tooth.'

254. Paharitvāti āvaṭṭanato aññamaññaṃ paharitvā. Tayo patte uparupari ṭhapetuṃ vaṭṭatīti sambandho. Bhūmiādhārako nāma bhūmiyā āsanno dantādīhi kato valayādhārako. Dāruādhārako nāma ekadārunā kato ādhārako. Daṇḍādhārako nāma catudaṇḍato paṭṭhāya bahūhi daṇḍehi kato ādhārako. Tatthāti bhamakoṭisadisadāru ādhārakatidaṇḍakādhāresu. Gahetvā evāti pattaṃ gahetvā eva, ekameva ṭhapetabbaṃ iti vuttanti yojanā.

254. 'Paharitvā' means having struck each other by turning round. The connection is that it is allowable to place three bowls one above the other. 'Bhūmiādhārako' is a ring stand made near the ground with ivory, etc. 'Dāruādhārako' means a stand made from a single piece of wood. 'Daṇḍādhārako' refers to a stand made with many sticks, starting from four sticks. 'Tattha' refers to a wooden stand resembling the rim of a wheel and to three-stick stands. 'Gahetvā eva' means having taken the bowl itself; the construction is that it is said only one should be placed.

Tatthevāti miḍḍhanteyeva. Vitthiṇṇāyāti vitthārāya. Bāhirapasseti kuṭṭassa bāhirapasse. Katāyāti kuṭṭassa thirabhāvatthaṃ katāya. Etthāti paribhaṇḍante.

'Tattheva' means just there, in the latrine. 'Vitthiṇṇāya' means for the spreading out. 'Bāhirapasse' refers to the outer side of the wall. 'Katāya' means made for the stability of the wall. 'Ettha' refers to while engaging in idle talk.

Yaṃ [M 0.0455] vatthaṃ pattharitvā patto ṭhapiyatīti vatthaṃ coḷakaṃ nāmāti yojanā. Tasmiṃ panāti coḷake pana. Yatthāti yassaṃ vālikāyaṃ. Na dussatīti patto na dussati. Pattamāḷakanti pattassa ṭhapanatthāya kataṃ aṭṭaṃ. Bhaṇḍakukkhaḷikāti pattādibhaṇḍakānaṃ pakkhipanā ukkhaḷikā. Yattha katthacīti bhittikhīlādike yasmiṃ kasmiṃci. Laggentassāti pattaṃ thavikāya laggentassa. Nisīdanasayanatthaṃ vā kataṃ hotūti yojanā. Aññenāti pattato aññena. Aṭṭakachannenāti aṭṭapatirūpena, aṭṭakasadisenāti attho. Tatthāti aṭṭakachannena ṭhapite mañcapīṭhe. Aṃse baddhiyati anenāti aṃsabaddho, soyeva aṃsabaddhako, tena laggetvāti sambandho. Chatte ṭhapetuṃ na vaṭṭatīti sambandho. Bhattena pūro bhattapūro, patto. Bandhitvā ṭhapite chatte vā aṭṭakaṃ katvā ṭhapite chatte vāti yojanā. Yo koci bhattapūropi tucchapattopīti sambandho.

The construction is that the cloth on which a bowl is spread out and placed is called 'coḷaka.' 'Tasmiṃ pana' means on that 'coḷaka.' 'Yattha' refers to on whichever sand. 'Na dussati' means the bowl does not get damaged. 'Pattamāḷaka' refers to a raised platform made for placing the bowl. 'Bhaṇḍakukkhaḷikā' means a bag-like container for putting bowls and other items in. 'Yattha katthaci' refers to any place, such as a wall peg and so on. 'Laggentassa' refers to hanging the bowl in a bag. The construction is 'nisīdanasayanatthaṃ vā kataṃ hotu' (or it may be made for sitting or lying down). 'Aññena' means by something other than the bowl. 'Aṭṭakachannena' means resembling a small roofed platform, that is, similar to a small roofed platform in appearance. 'Tattha' refers to a bed or bench on which something is placed with a small roofed platform. 'Aṃse baddhiyati anenāti aṃsabaddho'—that by which it is tied to the shoulder is 'aṃsabaddho,' and that is 'aṃsabaddhako'; the connection is 'tena laggetvā' (having hung it with that). The connection is that it is not proper to place it on an umbrella. 'Bhattena pūro' is 'bhattapūro,' a bowl filled with food. The construction is 'bandhitvā ṭhapite chatte vā' (on an umbrella placed by tying) or 'aṭṭakaṃ katvā ṭhapite chatte vā' (on an umbrella made into a small roofed platform and placed). The connection is 'yo koci bhattapūropi tucchapattopi' (any bowl, whether filled with food or empty).

255. Yassāti [V 2.0104] bhikkhuno. Hatthe patto atthi, so eva bhikkhu pattahattho na hoti, apica kho pana hatthe vā piṭṭhipāde vā yattha katthaci sarīrāvayave pattasmiṃ satīti yojanā. Eseva nayo anantaravākyepi. Imehi vākyehi “pattahattho”ti ca “kavāṭaṃ paṇāmetu”nti ca upalakkhaṇamattamevāti dasseti. Sūciṃ vā avāpuritunti sambandho. Kuñcikāya vāti vāsaddo “sarīrāvayavenā”ti padaṃ apekkhati.

255. 'Yassa' means 'of a bhikkhu.' A bhikkhu who has a bowl in his hand is not thereby 'one with bowl in hand' (pattahattho); rather, the construction is that the bowl is on any part of the body, whether on the hand, on the back of the foot, or anywhere else. This same principle also applies to the subsequent sentence. By these sentences, it is shown that 'pattahattho' and 'kavāṭaṃ paṇāmetu' are merely indicative. The connection is 'or to open the bolt' (sūciṃ vā avāpurituṃ). Regarding 'kuñcikāya vā,' the word 'vā' refers to the word 'sarīrāvayavena.'

Lābukaṭāhanti lambatīti lābu, lābuyā kaṭāhaṃ lābukaṭāhaṃ. “Tāvakālika”nti iminā ekavārameva tena āmisaṃ gahetvā paribhuñjitvā chaḍḍetabbanti dasseti. Ghaṭikapālanti bhājanakapālaṃ. Abhuṃ meti avaḍḍhi mayhaṃ, uppajjitthāti attho. “Abhu me”ti (ma. ni. aṭṭha. 2.149; ma. ni. ṭī. 2.149) vattabbe niggahitāgamavasena evaṃ vuttaṃ. Utrāsavacananti utrāsena vacanakāraṇaṃ padaṃ. Dinnakamevāti parehi dinnakameva āmisanti sambandho.

'Lābukaṭāhaṃ': 'lābu' is so called because it hangs; a 'lābukaṭāhaṃ' is a bowl made from a gourd. By 'tāvakālika,' it is shown that one should take food with it only once, consume it, and then discard it. 'Ghaṭikapālaṃ' means a pot-sherd. 'Abhuṃ me' means 'it did not increase for me,' the meaning of which is 'it arose.' When 'abhu me' should be said, it is expressed this way due to the insertion of a niggahīta. 'Utrāsavacanaṃ' is a word whose cause for being spoken is fear. 'Dinnakameva' is connected as 'only food given by others' (parehi dinnakameva āmisaṃ).

Cambetvāti [M 0.0456] mukhena cambetvā. Apaviddhāmisānīti chaḍḍitāni āmisāni. Etesūti calakādīsu. Anucchiṭṭhaṃ suddhapattanti natthi ucchiṭṭho etthāti anucchiṭṭho, suddhapatto, taṃ. Ucchiṭṭhahatthenāti ucchiṭṭho ettha atthīti ucchiṭṭho, soyeva hattho ucchiṭṭhahattho, tena. Vāmahatthena āsiñcitvāti sambandho. Etthāti suddhapatte. Ettāvatāpīti ettakena ekaudakageṇḍusagahaṇamattenāpi. Soti suddhapatto. Hatthaṃ panāti ucchiṭṭhahatthampi. Panasaddo hettha sampiṇḍanattho. Yaṃ aṭṭhiṃ vā yaṃ calakaṃ vāti yojanā. Tatthāti macchamaṃsaphalādīsu. Tanti aṭṭhicalakaṃ. Yaṃ panāti aṭṭhicalakādiṃ pana, paṭikhāditukāmoti sambandho, puna khāditukāmoti attho. Tatthevāti patte eva. Katvāti ṭhapanaṃ katvā. Yaṃ kiñci aṭṭhikaṇṭakādinti sambandho.

'Cambetvā' means having chewed with the mouth. 'Apaviddhāmisāni' means discarded food. 'Etesu' means among these, such as calaka and so on. 'Anucchiṭṭhaṃ suddhapattanti': 'anucchiṭṭho' means that in which there are no leftovers; a clean bowl; it refers to that. 'Ucchiṭṭhahatthenāti': 'ucchiṭṭho' is that which has leftovers; that very hand is the 'ucchiṭṭhahattho'; with that. The connection is 'having poured with the left hand.' 'Ettha' means in the clean bowl. 'Ettāvatāpi' means even by this much, even by the mere taking of a single scoop of water. 'So' means the clean bowl. 'Hatthaṃ pana' means also the hand with leftovers. Here, the word 'pana' has the meaning of inclusion. The construction is 'whatever bone or whatever calaka.' 'Tattha' means among fish, meat, fruits, and so on. 'Taṃ' means the bone or calaka. 'Yaṃ pana' refers to a bone, calaka, etc., and is connected with 'paṭikhāditukāmo,' which means 'wishing to eat again.' 'Tattheva' means in the bowl itself. 'Katvā' means having placed. The connection is 'whatever bone, fish-bone, etc.'

256. Satthakaveṭhanakanti satthakassa veṭhanakaraṇaṃ. Pipphalikaṃ vā daṇḍasatthakaṃ nāmāti yojanā. Pipphāleti etāyāti pipphali, sāyeva pipphalikaṃ. Aññampīti pipphalikato aññampi. Yaṃkiñci daṇḍaṃ yojetvā katasatthakaṃ vā daṇḍasatthakaṃ nāmāti yojanā. Iminā daṇḍena yojitaṃ satthakaṃ daṇḍasatthakanti vacanatthaṃ dasseti.

256. 'Satthakaveṭhanakaṃ' means the making of a wrapping for a knife. The construction is that a 'daṇḍasatthakaṃ' is also called a 'pipphalikaṃ.' 'Pipphali' is that by which one splits; that itself is a 'pipphalikaṃ.' 'Aññampi' means also something other than a pipphalika. The construction is that any knife made by attaching a handle is also called a 'daṇḍasatthakaṃ.' By this, it shows the verbal meaning of 'daṇḍasatthakaṃ' as 'a knife fitted with a handle.'

Malaggahitāti ayamalaggahitā. Kiṇṇenāti madirādibījena kiṇṇena. Tenāti pāsāṇacuṇṇasaṅkhātena saritakena. Makkhetunti sūciṃ makkhetuṃ. Makkhitamadhusitthakaṃ taṃ saritakaṃ paribhijjatīti [V 2.0105] yojanā. Madhusitthakapilotikanti madhusitthakena makkhitaṃ pilotikaṃ. Tatthāti nisseṇiyaṃ. Yāya rajjuyā kathine bandhanti, sā rajju kathinarajju nāmāti yojanā. Tatthāti dīghassa bhikkhuno pamāṇena kate kathine. Daṇḍaketi kathinadaṇḍakamhi. Tassāti dīghassa bhikkhuno pamāṇena katassa kathinassa. Itarassa bhikkhunoti dīghabhikkhuto itarassa rassabhikkhuno.

'Malaggahitā' means 'this is covered with rust.' 'Kiṇṇena' means with kiṇṇa, which is the fermenting agent for liquor and so on. 'Tena' means with saritaka, which is designated as stone powder. 'Makkhetuṃ' means to smear the needle. The construction is that that saritaka breaks the smeared beeswax. 'Madhusitthakapilotikaṃ' means a piece of cloth smeared with beeswax. 'Tattha' means on the ladder. The construction is that the rope with which they bind on the kathina frame is called the 'kathina rope.' 'Tattha' means on the kathina frame made to the measure of a tall bhikkhu. 'Daṇḍake' means on the kathina pole. 'Tassa' means of the kathina frame made to the measure of that tall bhikkhu. 'Itarassa bhikkhuno' means of the other bhikkhu, the short bhikkhu, as distinct from the tall bhikkhu.

Daṇḍakathinapamāṇena katassa kaṭasārakassāti yojanā. “Duguṇakaraṇa”nti iminā pidalakanti duguṇakaraṇasaṅkhātassa kiriyāvisesassa [M 0.0457] nāmanti dasseti. Vinandhanarajjunti visesena nahiyati bandhiyati etāyāti vinandhanā, sāyeva rajju vinandhanarajju, tamevatthaṃ dassetuṃ vuttaṃ “vinandhituṃ rajju”nti. Vinandhanasuttakanti etthāpi eseva nayo. Tena suttakenāti vinandhanasuttakena. Tatthāti khuddakanisseṇiyaṃ kāci suttantarikāyoti sambandho. Pamāṇasaññākaraṇanti suttantarikapamāṇassa saññākaraṇaṃ. Kāḷasuttena saññākaraṇaṃ viya haliddisuttena saññākaraṇanti yojanā. Aṅguliyā paṭiggaṇhantīti ettha “paṭiggaṇhantī”ti padassa “aṅguliyā”ti karaṇasseva vuttattā kammassa avuttattā tassa kammaṃ dassetuṃ vuttaṃ “sūcimukha”nti. Aṅgulikosakanti aṅgulikañcukaṃ.

The construction is 'of the mat made to the measure of the kathina pole.' By 'duguṇakaraṇa,' it shows that 'pidalaka' is the name of a specific action designated as 'doubling.' 'Vinandhanarajju': 'vinandhanā' is that by which one especially ties or binds; that very rope is the 'vinandhanarajju.' To show this same meaning, it is said, 'a rope for binding.' This same principle also applies to 'vinandhanasuttaka.' 'Tena suttakena' means with the binding thread. 'Tattha' means on the small ladder; the connection is 'by some thread-space.' 'Pamāṇasaññākaraṇaṃ' means the marking of the measure of the thread-space. The construction is 'the marking with a yellow thread, like the marking with a black thread.' Here, regarding 'aṅguliyā paṭiggaṇhanti,' since for the word 'paṭiggaṇhanti' only the instrument 'aṅguliyā' is stated, and the object is not stated, 'sūcimukhaṃ' is said to show that object. 'Aṅgulikosakaṃ' means a finger-sheath.

257. Pāticaṅkoṭakādinti ettha pāti nāma paṭiggahasaṇṭhānena kato sūciādibhaṇḍaṭṭhapano bhājanaviseso. Ākiritvāti pakkhipitvā. Odhunitvāti papphoṭetvā. Ghanadaṇḍakanti nirantaradaṇḍakaṃ. Antokatvāti kathinassa antokatvā.

257. Here, in 'pāticaṅkoṭakādi,' 'pāti' is a particular kind of vessel made in the shape of a receptacle, for placing needles and other items. 'Ākiritvā' means having put in. 'Odhunitvā' means having shaken off. 'Ghanadaṇḍakaṃ' means a solid, continuous pole. 'Antokatvā' means having made the border of the kathina frame.

258. Vinandhitvāti coḷakena vinandhitvā.

258. 'Vinandhitvā' means having bound with a piece of cloth.

259. Aparissāvanakasseva bhikkhunoti yojanā. Yo pana yācatīti sambandho. Majjhedaṇḍaketi daṇḍakassa majjhe. Udakanti akappiyaudakaṃ. Tanti udakaṃ. Yanti parissāvanaṃ. Udakaṃ parisuddhaṃ hutvā savati gacchati pavattati anenāti parissāvanaṃ. Yaṃ udake ottharitvā ghaṭena udakaṃ gaṇhanti, taṃ ottharakaṃ nāmāti yojanā. Tamevatthaṃ vitthārento āha “taṃ hī”tiādi. Tanti parissāvanaṃ, bandhitvāti sambandho. Tesūti catūsu khāṇukesu. Sabbapariyanteti sabbaparissāvanassa pariyante mocetvāti sambandho. Ottharitvāti ogāhetvā. Cīvarakuṭikāti cīvarena katā kuṭikā, sā makasānaṃ parittāṇatthaṃ katattā makasakuṭikāti vuccati.

259. The construction is 'of a bhikkhu who is without a strainer.' The connection is 'but who asks.' 'Majjhedaṇḍake' means in the middle of the pole. 'Udakaṃ' means unallowable water. 'Taṃ' means the water. 'Yaṃ' means the strainer. 'Parissāvanaṃ' is that by which water, having become pure, flows, goes, and proceeds. The construction is that that with which they take water with a pot, having submerged it in the water, is called an 'ottharakaṃ.' Elaborating on this same meaning, he said, 'for that...' and so on. 'Taṃ' means the strainer; the connection is 'having tied.' 'Tesu' means on the four posts. 'Sabbapariyante' means at the edge of the entire strainer; the connection is 'having untied.' 'Ottharitvā' means having submerged. 'Cīvarakuṭikā' is a hut made of cloth; since it is made for protection from mosquitoes, it is called a 'makasakuṭikā.'

260. Semhādidosussannakāyāti [V 2.0106] semhādidosehi ussannakāyā. Aggaḷatthambhoti kavāṭatthambho. Yatthāti aggaḷatthambhe. Tatthāti dvārabāhāya. Tatthāti aggaḷapāsake. Dhūmo nikkhamati etenāti dhūmanetto, chiddo. Tena vuttaṃ “dhūmanikkhamanachidda”nti[M 0.0458]. “Gandhehī”ti iminā “vāsetu”nti padassa karaṇaṃ dasseti. “Udakaṭṭhapanaṭṭhāna”nti iminā udakaṭṭhānanti ettha udakassa ṭhapanaṃ ṭhānaṃ udakaṭṭhānanti majjhepadalopasamāsaṃ dasseti. Tatthāti udakaṭṭhāne. Koṭṭhakoti ettha na yattha katthaci, yassa kassaci vā koṭṭhako hoti, api ca kho pana dvāre eva, dvārasseva vā koṭṭhakoti āha “dvārakoṭṭhako”ti.

260. 'Semhādidosussannakāyā' means having a body abounding in disorders such as phlegm. 'Aggaḷatthambho' means the bolt-post. 'Yattha' means on the bolt-post. 'Tattha' means on the door-jamb. 'Tattha' means in the bolt-hole. 'Dhūmanetto' is that by which smoke goes out, an opening. For that reason it is said, 'a smoke-exit-hole.' By 'gandhehī,' it shows the instrument for the word 'vāsetu.' By 'udakaṭṭhapanaṭṭhāna,' it shows that here 'udakaṭṭhāna' is a compound with an elided middle term, meaning 'a place for the setting down of water.' 'Tattha' means at the water-stand. Here, 'koṭṭhako' is not just any chamber, or anyone's chamber, but rather it is at the door, or it is the door's chamber; thus he says 'dvārakoṭṭhako.'

261. Parikammanti piṭṭhiādiparikammaṃ. Paṭicchādiyati imāyāti paṭicchādi, vatthameva paṭicchādi vatthapaṭicchādi. Udakaṃ na hotīti ettha pānodakaṃ nivattento āha “nhānodakaṃ na hotī”ti.

261. 'Parikammaṃ' means preparation, such as of the back. 'Paṭicchādi' is that by which one is covered; a cloth itself is a cover, hence 'vatthapaṭicchādi.' Here, regarding 'there is no water,' ruling out drinking water, he says, 'there is no bathing water.'

262. Paṇṇikānaṃ tulaṃ viya udakaubbāhanakatulanti yojanā. Dīghavarattādīhītiādisaddena rajju ādayo saṅgaṇhāti. Arahatthaghaṭiyantaṃ nāma cakkasaṇṭhānaṃ anekāraṃ are are ghaṭāni bandhitvā ekena vā dvīhi vā paribbhamiyamānaṃ yantaṃ. Arasaṅkhātesu hatthesu ghaṭā bandhitabbā etthāti arahatthaghaṭi, tameva yantaṃ arahatthaghaṭiyantaṃ. Cammabhājananti cammamayaṃ bhājanaṃ. Aparikkhittā hotīti candanikā apākārā hoti. Udakapuñjanaṃ vaṭṭatīti sambandho. Tasminti udakapuñjane. “Udakapuñjanī”tipi pāṭho. Evaṃ sati tāya udakapuñjaniyāti attho. Paccuddharitunti apanetuṃ.

262. The explanation is 'a water-lifting balance, like a balance for leaves'. By 'dīghavarattādīhi' (with long ropes, etc.), the word 'etc.' includes ropes and the like. An arahatthaghaṭiyanta is a wheel-shaped device with many spokes, where pots are fastened to each spoke, and the device is turned by one or two people. Pots must be fastened to the 'hands' (spokes) known as ara in this device; hence, it is an arahatthaghaṭi, and that very device is an arahatthaghaṭiyanta. 'Cammabhājanaṃ' means a leather vessel. 'Aparikkhittā hoti' means the candanikā (channel) is without a surrounding wall. The connection is 'a water-wiping cloth is permissible'. 'Tasmiṃ' refers to that water-wiping cloth. There is also a reading 'udakapuñjanī.' In that case, the meaning is 'by that water-wiping cloth'. 'Paccuddharituṃ' means to remove.

263. Ā samantato viddhaṃ pakkhapāsakametthāti āviddhapakkhapāsakaṃ. Maṇḍaleti kaṇṇikamaṇḍalamhi. Kataṃ kūṭañca chadanañca etthāti katakūṭacchadanaṃ, jantāgharaṃ, tassa. Etanti “nillekhajantāghara”nti etaṃ nāmaṃ. “Cattāro māse”ti iminā “catumāsa”nti digusamāsassa vākyaṃ dasseti.

263. That in which wing-shaped fastenings are fixed all around is an āviddhapakkhapāsaka. 'Maṇḍale' refers to the circular hub. That in which a peak and a roof are constructed is a katakūṭacchadana, that is, a hot room; of that. 'Etaṃ' refers to this name, 'nillekhajantāghara' (hot room without carvings). By 'cattāro māse,' it shows the phrase for the digusamāsa compound 'catumāsa' (four months).

264. Namatakanti ettha heṭṭhā vuttanamatakato (cūḷava. aṭṭha. 256) visesaṃ dassento āha “eḷakalomehī”tiādi. Avāyimanti vāyitvā na kataṃ. Cammakhaṇḍaparihārenāti cammakhaṇḍaṃ viya adhiṭṭhānavikappanaapanayanena, paribhuñjitabbanti attho. Peḷāyāti aṭṭhaṃsādiākārena katāya [M 0.0459] mañjūsāya. Etanti “āsittakūpadhāna”nti etaṃ nāmaṃ. Dārumayāpīti pisaddo na tambaloharajatamayā evāti dasseti. Etthevāti maḷorikāyameva. Ādhārakasaṅkhepagamanatoti [V 2.0107] ādhārake saṅkhepaṃ gamanato. Hīti saccaṃ, yasmā vā. Pubbe pattarakkhanatthaṃ ādhārako anuññāto, idāni bhuñjanatthanti daṭṭhabbaṃ. Eko bhikkhu gacchatīti sambandho. Sesakanti gahetabbaphalapūvehi sesakaṃ. Tasmiṃ khaṇeti tasmiṃ bhuñjanakkhaṇe.

264. Here, regarding 'namataka,' distinguishing it from the namataka mentioned previously (Cūḷavagga Aṭṭhakathā 256), he says, 'with goat hair,' etc. 'Avāyimaṃ' means not made by weaving. 'Cammakhaṇḍaparihārena' means in the manner of a piece of leather, that is, by determination, sharing, and removal; the meaning is that it should be used. 'Peḷāya' refers to a chest made in the shape of an octagon, etc. 'Etaṃ' refers to this name, 'āsittakūpadhāna'. By 'dārumayāpi' (made of wood also), the word 'pi' (also) shows that it is not only those made of copper, iron, or silver. 'Ettheva' means only in the maḷorikā (small water vessel) itself. 'Ādhārakasaṅkhepagamanato' means because of its inclusion under 'stand'. 'Hi' means truly, or because. Previously, a stand was allowed for protecting the bowl; now, it is for eating—this should be understood. The connection is 'one bhikkhu goes'. 'Sesakaṃ' means the remainder of fruits or cakes to be taken. 'Tasmiṃ khaṇe' means at that moment of eating.

265. Ekekenapi aṅgenāti pisaddo sambhāvanattho, tato pana adhikehi aṅgehi pagevāti hi attho. Samannāgatassa upāsakassa nikkujjitunti sambandho. Tassāti upāsakassa. Na gahetabboti saṅghena na gahetabbo. Asukassa upāsakassāti sambandho. Ukkujjanakāleti pattassa ukkujjanakāle. Yācāpetvāti pattanikujjitena upāsakena yācāpetvā. Hatthapāsanti saṅghassa hatthapāsaṃ.

265. 'Ekekenapi aṅgena' means that the word 'pi' indicates possibility, and therefore the meaning is 'how much more so with additional factors'. The connection is 'to overturn for a lay follower who is endowed'. 'Tassa' refers to the lay follower. 'Na gahetabbo' means it should not be accepted by the Saṅgha. The connection is 'for such-and-such lay follower'. 'Ukkujjanakāle' means at the time of righting the bowl. 'Yācāpetvā' means having caused the lay follower for whom the bowl was overturned to request. 'Hatthapāsaṃ' refers to the Saṅgha's arm's reach.

268. Purakkhatvāti ettha purasaddassa aggatthabhāvañca karasaddassa khādesabhāvañca dassento āha “aggato katvā”ti. Soti bodhirājakumāro, santharīti sambandho. Lacchāmīti labhissāmi, esa bodhirājakumāro puttalābhāya abhabboti yojanā. Akkamane dosaṃ dassento āha “yadī”tiādi. Pacchāti akkamanato pacchā. Ayanti bhagavā. Idanti kāraṇaṃ. Tāvāti sikkhāpadapaññattito, sikkhāpadapaññattiyā vā paṭhamaṃ. Paribhavatoti gihīnaṃ paribhavato.

268. Regarding 'purakkhatvā' (having placed in front), showing that the word 'pura' means 'foremost' and the root 'kar' has the sense of making, he says, 'aggato katvā' (having placed foremost). 'So' refers to Prince Bodhi; 'santhari' (spread) is the connection. 'Lacchāmi' means 'I will obtain'; the explanation is that this Prince Bodhi is incapable of obtaining a son. Showing the fault in stepping on it, he says, 'yadi' (if), and so on. 'Pacchā' means 'after stepping on it'. 'Ayaṃ' refers to the Blessed One. 'Idaṃ' means 'this reason'. 'Tāva' means 'before the laying down of the training rule'. 'Paribhavato' means 'due to disrespect from householders'.

Maṅgalatthāyāti arogādikassa maṅgalassa atthāya. Dhotapādakanti ettha dhotehi pādehi akkamanaṭṭhāne attharitaṃ dhotapādakanti vacanatthaṃ dassento āha “dhotapādakaṃ nāmā”tiādi. Tattha “paccattharaṇaṃ atthata”nti iminā “dhotapādaka”nti ettha ṇikapaccayassa attharitatthe pavattabhāvaṃ dasseti.

'Maṅgalatthāya' means for the purpose of a blessing such as good health and so on. Regarding 'dhotapādaka' (foot-wiping cloth), showing the meaning of the word 'dhotapādaka' as 'something spread out in a place where one steps with washed feet,' he says, 'dhotapādakaṃ nāma' (a foot-wiping cloth is), and so on. Therein, by 'paccattharaṇaṃ atthataṃ' (a covering is spread), he shows that the suffix '-ka' in 'dhotapādaka' has the sense of 'something spread out'.

269. Padumakaṇṇikākāranti padumakaṇṇikasaṇṭhānaṃ. Kataṃ pādaghaṃsanaṃ katakaṃ nāmāti yojanā. Tanti katakaṃ, paṭikkhittamevāti sambandho. Potthakesu taṃsaddo galitoti daṭṭhabbo. Bāhullikānuyogattāti [M 0.0460] paccayabahulabhāvāya anuyogattā. Pāsāṇapheṇakopīti pāsāṇaabbudampi. Bījanīti caturassabījanī. Tanti vidhūpanaṃ, kataṃ hotūti sambandho. Idhāpi taṃsaddo galito. Veḷudantavilīvehi vā morapiñchehi vā cammavikatīhi vā kataṃ hotūti yojanā. Sabbaṃ vidhūpananti sambandho. Pāḷiyaṃ tālavaṇṭanti saha vaṇṭena kataṃ tālaṃ tālavaṇṭaṃ, tālasaddena taṃmayā maṇḍalabījanī gahetabbā vikārīvikārabhāvena sambandhattā. Makasabījanīti [V 2.0108] makasānaṃ palāyanakabījanī, dantamayavisāṇamayadaṇḍakāpi makasabījanī vaṭṭatīti yojanā. “Vākamayabījaniyā”ti padaṃ “saṅgahitā”ti pade ādhāro, karaṇaṃ vā.

269. 'Padumakaṇṇikākāraṃ' means having the shape of a lotus pericarp. The explanation is that a 'kataka' is a foot-scraper that is made. 'Taṃ' refers to the kataka; the connection is that it is indeed rejected. It should be understood that the word 'taṃ' is elided in the texts. 'Bāhullikānuyogattā' means due to application for the sake of an abundance of requisites. 'Pāsāṇapheṇakopi' means even a stone protuberance. 'Bījanī' means a four-cornered fan. 'Taṃ' refers to a fan (vidhūpanaṃ); the connection is 'kataṃ hotu' (let it be made). Here too, the word 'taṃ' is elided. The explanation is: 'let it be made with strips of bamboo or ivory, or peacock feathers, or leather strips.' 'Sabbaṃ vidhūpanaṃ' (all fans) is the connection. In the Pāli, 'tālavaṇṭaṃ' means a palm leaf made together with its stem; by the word 'tāla,' a circular fan made of it should be understood, due to the connection of being the material and the product. 'Makasabījanī' means a whisk for driving away flies; the explanation is that a fly whisk with a handle made of ivory or horn is also permissible. The phrase 'vākamayabījaniyā' is the basis for the word 'saṅgahitā' (included), or it may be the means.

270. Yassāti bhikkhussa cakkhuṃ vā dubbalaṃ hotīti yojanā. Aññoti kāyaḍāhādīhi ābādhehi añño, koci ābādho vā uppajjatīti yojanā. “Vasse panā”ti padaṃ “cīvaraguttattha”nti pade eva sambandhitabbaṃ. Cīvaraguttatthanti cīvarassa vassatemanato guttatthaṃ, vāḷamigacorabhayesu santesūti sambandho. Tālapaṇṇādinā ekena paṇṇena kataṃ chattaṃ ekapaṇṇacchattaṃ. Sabbatthevāti sabbesu eva gāmāraññesu.

270. 'Yassa' means a bhikkhu whose eye is weak; this is the explanation. 'Añño' means another, apart from ailments such as a burning sensation in the body, or some other ailment arises; this is the explanation. The phrase 'Vasse pana' should be connected only to the phrase 'cīvaraguttatthaṃ'. 'Cīvaraguttatthaṃ' means for the purpose of protecting the robe from being soaked by rain; the connection is 'when there is danger from wild animals or thieves.' 'Ekapaṇṇacchattaṃ' means an umbrella made with a single leaf, such as a palm leaf. 'Sabbattheva' means in all places, in villages and forests.

“Asi assā”ti iminā asissāti padassa anavakāsavidhiṃ dasseti. Asīti khaggo. Assāti corassa, asīti sambandho. Vijjotalatīti ettha alapaccayo rūpasiddhimattovāti āha “vijjotatī”ti. “Catuhatthoyevā”ti iminā pamāṇayuttoti padassa atthaṃ dasseti. Tatoti catuhatthato. Sabbesanti gilānāgilānānaṃ. “Sakkā panā”ti padaṃ “na vaṭṭatī”ti pade kattā, “dātabbā”ti pade kammaṃ. Sammannitvāva dātabbā, na vinā sammutiyāti adhippāyo.

By 'Asi assa' (a sword of his), he shows the unconditional nature of the word 'asissa'. 'Asi' means a sword. 'Assa' means 'of a thief'; the connection is with 'asi' (sword). Regarding 'vijjotalati' (it flashes), since the suffix '-ala' is merely for establishing the form, he says 'vijjotati' (it flashes). By 'catuhatthoyeva' (only four hands), he shows the meaning of the word 'pamāṇayutto' (endowed with measure). 'Tato' means 'from that', i.e., from four hands. 'Sabbesaṃ' means for all, for both the sick and the non-sick. The phrase 'Sakkā pana' is the agent in relation to the phrase 'na vaṭṭati' and the object in relation to the phrase 'dātabbā'. The intention is: 'it should be given only after agreement, not without agreement'.

273. Āgatanti udariyato nikkhamitvā āgataṃ. Uggāranti galato uggāraṃ bhojananti sambandho. Sandhāretvāti patiṭṭhāpetvā. Asandhāritameva hutvāti sambandho.

273. 'Āgataṃ' means that which has come, having exited from the stomach. 'Uggāraṃ' means food belched from the throat; this is the connection. 'Sandhāretvā' means having retained. 'Asandhāritameva hutvā' (having been without retaining) is the connection.

Yanti [M 0.0461] khādanīyabhojanīyaṃ, patitanti sambandho. Tanti khādanīyabhojanīyaṃ, gahetvā paribhuñjitunti sambandho. Idanti vacanaṃ.

'Yaṃ' refers to hard and soft food; 'patitaṃ' (fallen) is the connection. 'Taṃ' refers to hard and soft food; 'gahetvā paribhuñjituṃ' (to take and consume) is the connection. 'Idaṃ' means this statement.

274. Kubbaṃ karissāmīti ettha kariyati uccāriyatīti kubbanti vutte saddoti āha “saddaṃ karissāmī”ti. Saddanti “ayaṃ maṃ bhikkhu vippakarotī”ti uccāsaddaṃ. Nakhādīhītiādisaddena mukhakuṭṭe saṅgaṇhāti. Anurakkhanatthanti anudayena pālanatthaṃ. Nakhacchedananti nakhaṃ chindati anenāti nakhacchedanaṃ, satthakādi. Vīsatimaṭṭhanti ettha vīsatiyā nakhānaṃ maṭṭhaṃ vīsatimaṭṭhanti dassento āha “vīsatipi nakhe”tiādi. Likhitamaṭṭheti likhite hutvā maṭṭhe. Kārāpentīti nahāpite kārāpenti. Nakhatoti nakhato vā nakhantarato vā. Apakaḍḍhitunti kaḍḍhitvā apanetuṃ.

274. Regarding 'kubbaṃ karissāmī' (I will make a sound), since 'kubba' means 'is made' or 'is uttered,' it is said 'saddaṃ karissāmī' (I will make a sound). 'Sadda' means a loud sound, as in 'This monk is offending me.' By the word 'nakhādīhi' (with nails, etc.), it includes striking the mouth and so on. 'Anurakkhanattha' means for the purpose of protecting with compassion. 'Nakhacchedana' means that with which the nail is cut, hence 'nakhacchedana' refers to a knife, and so on. Regarding 'vīsatimaṭṭha' (twenty-smoothed), showing that 'vīsatimaṭṭha' means 'smoothed by twenty nails,' it is said: 'even twenty nails,' and so on. 'Likhitamaṭṭha' means smoothed after being scraped. 'Kārāpenti' means they have a barber do it. 'Nakhato' means from the nail or from the space between the nails. 'Apakaḍḍhituṃ' means to pull out and remove.

275. Khurakosakanti [V 2.0109] khurassa ṭhapanakaṃ. Kattariyāti kantiyati chindiyati imāyāti kattari, ayomayo eko upakaraṇaviseso, tāya. “Chedāpentī”ti iminā kappāpentīti ettha kappasaddassa vidhyatthaṃ adhippāyena dasseti. Massuṃ vaḍḍhāpentīti ettha massuṃ vaḍḍhetvā ruhāpentīti atthaṃ paṭikkhipanto āha “massuṃ dīghaṃ kārāpentī”ti. Eḷakamassūti eḷakassa viya massūti eḷakamassu. “Golomika”nti vuccatīti sambandho. “Catukoṇa”nti iminā caturassanti ettha aṃsasaddo koṇatthoti dasseti. Caturassanti ettha hi “caturaṃsa”nti vattabbe niggahitassa lopaṃ katvā parassa sakārassa dvebhāvaṃ katvā “caturassa”nti vuttaṃ. Lomasaṃharaṇanti lomānaṃ apanayanaṃ. Lomarājiṭṭhapananti lomalekhāṭhapanaṃ. Sabbatthāti sabbesu, massukappanādīsūti sambandho. Gaṇḍavaṇarudhiābādhapaccayāti gaṇḍo ca vaṇo ca rudhi ca gaṇḍavaṇarudhayo, teyeva ābādhā gaṇḍavaṇarudhiābādhā, tesaṃ paccayā. Vaṇoti mahanto vaṇo. Rudhīti khuddako vaṇo. Sakkharādīhīti sakkharamadhusitthakehi. Saṇḍāsoti suṭṭhu lomaṃ ḍaṃsatīti saṇḍāso. Yanti lomaṃ, ṭhitanti sambandho. Kattha ṭhitanti āha “bhamukāya vā”tiādi. Kiṃ hutvā ṭhitanti [M 0.0462] āha – “uggantvā vibhacchaṃ ṭhita”nti, vibhacchaṃ hutvā ṭhitanti yojanā. Visesena sobhaṇaṃ bhakkhatīti vibhaccho, asobhaṇo. “Vigaccha”ntipi pāṭho, virūpaṃ gacchati, gamayatīti vā vigaccho. Tattha purimapāṭhoyeva mūlapāṭhoti daṭṭhabboti. Palitaṃ vā apalitaṃ vā tādisaṃ lomanti yojanā.

275. 'Khurakosaka' means a razor's sheath. 'Kattari' means that with which one cuts or severs; it is a specific iron tool; by that. By 'having it cut,' the meaning of 'kappāpenti' (having it trimmed) is shown with the intention of prescribing. Regarding 'massuṃ vaḍḍhāpenti' (making the beard grow), rejecting the meaning of 'making the beard grow out,' it is said: 'making the beard long.' 'Eḷakamassu' means a beard like a goat's. The connection is that it is called 'golomika' (like a cow's hair). By 'catukoṇa' (four-cornered), it is shown that the word 'aṃsa' in 'caturassa' (four-sided) means 'corner.' Indeed, regarding 'caturassa,' it is said 'caturassa' by dropping the nasal sound and doubling the following 'sa,' where it should have been 'caturaṃsa.' 'Lomasaṃharaṇa' means the removal of hair. 'Lomarājiṭṭhapanā' means arranging the hair in a line. 'In all cases' means in all instances; the connection is 'such as beard-trimming.' 'On account of an ailment such as a boil, wound, or sore' is explained: a boil, a wound, and a sore are 'gaṇḍavaṇarudhi'; these very ailments are 'gaṇḍavaṇarudhiābādhā'; 'paccayā' means on account of them. 'Vaṇa' means a large wound. 'Rudhi' means a small wound. 'With sugar, etc.' means with sugar, honey, and wax. 'Saṇḍāsa' means that which thoroughly plucks the hair. 'Yaṃ' refers to hair; 'standing' is the connection. Where does it stand? It is said: 'on the eyebrows, or so on.' How does it stand? It is said: 'having risen, it stands unnaturally'; the interpretation is 'having become unnaturally it stands.' 'Vibhaccha' means that which particularly devours beauty, hence 'unlovely.' There is also a reading 'vigaccha,' meaning it becomes misshapen, or causes to become misshapen. Here, the former reading should be understood as the root text. The interpretation is: 'such hair, whether gray or not gray'.

277. Kaṃsapattharikāti ettha kaṃsaāpaṇe pattharanti pasārentīti kaṃsapattharikāti vutte kaṃsabhaṇḍavāṇijā gahetabbāti āha “kaṃsabhaṇḍavāṇijā”ti. Vāsidaṇḍādīnaṃ apātanatthaṃ bandhati anena lohenāti bandhanaṃ, tameva mattaṃ appanti bandhanamattaṃ.

277. Regarding 'kaṃsapattharika' (brass-spreaders), since it is said 'they spread out wares in the brass market,' it is said that 'brassware merchants' should be understood. 'Bandhana' (a binding) is that metal with which one binds adze-handles and so on to prevent them from coming off; 'bandhanamatta' means just that small amount.

278. Nikkhamantenāti ārāmato nikkhamantena. Yatthāti yasmiṃ ṭhāne. “Saritvā”ti iminā asaritvā piṇḍāya caritabbanti dasseti. Bahurajjukanti bahū rajjuyo etassāti bahurajjukaṃ. Iminā kalāpena bahurajjūnaṃ samūhena kattabbanti kalāpukanti vacanatthaṃ dasseti, ikārassukāro. Deḍḍubhakanti ettha deḍḍubhasaddena tassa sīsaṃ gahetabbaṃ ekadesūpacārena, deḍḍubhaṃ viyāti deḍḍubhakaṃ, sadisatthe kapaccayo hoti. Tena vuttaṃ “udakasappasīsasadisa”nti. “Murajavaṭṭisaṇṭhāna”nti iminā murajasaddena murajavaṭṭi gahetabbā tassa vikārattā, tena sadisaṃ murajanti vacanatthaṃ dasseti. Veṭhetvāti bahurajjuke ekato veṭhetvā. Maddavīṇasaddo pāmaṅgapariyāyo. Maddavīṇaṃ viyāti maddavīṇaṃ. Tena vuttaṃ “pāmaṅgasaṇṭhāna”nti. “Pageva bahūnī”ti iminā “ekampī”ti ettha pisaddassa sambhāvanatthaṃ dasseti. Macchakaṇṭakavāyimāti macchakaṇṭakaṃ [V 2.0110] viya dassetvā vāyimā. Kuñjaracchikādibhedāti vāraṇaacchikādibhedā. Vāraṇo hi kuṃ bhūmiṃ jarāpetīti kuñjaroti (vi. va. aṭṭha. 31; a. ni. ṭī. 1.1.2) ca kuñje nikuñje ramatīti kuñjaroti ca vuccati. Tassa acchi viyāti kuñjaracchikaṃ, taṃ ādi yesaṃ tānīti kuñjaracchikādīni, tesaṃ bhedāti kuñjaracchikādibhedā. Ādisaddena goṇacchikādayo saṅgaṇhāti. “Kuñcikākosakasaṇṭhāna”nti iminā sūkarassa antaṃ viya [M 0.0463] sūkarantakanti atthaṃ dasseti. Sūkarassa hi antaṃ kuñcikākosakaṃ viya majjhe susiro hoti. Sūkarantakaṃ anulometīti sūkarantakena anulometi. Dasāsuyevāti kāyabandhanassa antesuyeva. Etthāti dasāsu. “Catunnaṃ upari na vaṭṭatī”ti iminā murajadasā tato upari vaṭṭatīti dasseti. Veṭhetvāti rajjuṃ vatthena veṭhetvā. Muddikasaṇṭhānenāti varakasīsasaṇṭhānena. Evaṃ sibbitāti evaṃ sibbiyamānā. Hīti phalajotako. Pāsantoti pāsakoṭi.

278. “Nikkhamantena” (by one leaving) means by one leaving the monastery. “Yattha” (where) means in which place. “Saritvā” (having remembered) indicates that one should wander for alms even without remembering. “Bahurajjuka” (having many ropes) means that which has many ropes. By this, it shows the meaning of the word 'kalāpuka' is 'that which is to be made with a bundle (kalāpa), a collection of many ropes'; the 'i' has become 'u'. “Deḍḍubhaka” (like a water snake) here, by the word `deḍḍubha`, its head should be taken by way of synecdoche, meaning `deḍḍubhaka` as ‘like a water snake’, the suffix `ka` being in the sense of similarity. Therefore, it is said, “resembling the head of a water snake.” “Murajavaṭṭisaṇṭhāna” (resembling a drumstick) indicates that by the word `muraja`, `murajavaṭṭi` (a drumstick) should be taken because it is a modification of it, thus showing the meaning of `muraja` as ‘similar to it’. “Veṭhetvā” (having wrapped) means having wrapped many ropes together. The word `maddavīṇā` is a synonym for `pāmaṅga` (a kind of musical instrument). “Maddavīṇa” (like a maddavīṇā) means like a maddavīṇā. Therefore, it is said, “resembling a pāmaṅga.” “Pageva bahūnī” (much more many) indicates the sense of possibility of the particle `pi` in “ekampi” (even one). “Macchakaṇṭakavāyimā” (woven like a fishbone) means woven so as to appear like a fishbone. “Kuñjaracchikādibhedā” (varieties like an elephant's eye) means varieties like an elephant's eye. For `vāraṇa` (elephant) is called `kuñjara` because it makes the earth tremble (`kuṃ bhūmiṃ jarāpetīti`) and because it delights in groves and thickets (`kuñje nikuñje ramatīti`). Like its eye is 'kuñjaracchika' (elephant's eye). `Kuñjaracchikādīni` are those that have that as their beginning, meaning varieties such as the elephant's eye. The word `ādi` includes the bull's eye and the like. By “resembling a key-case,” it indicates the meaning of `sūkarantaka` (pig’s intestine). For a pig’s intestine is hollow in the middle like a key-case. “Sūkarantakaṃ anulometi” (he makes the pig's intestine conform) means he makes it conform with a pig's intestine tool. “Dasāsuyeva” (only at the fringes) means only at the ends of the waist-band. “Ettha” (here) means at the fringes. “Catunnaṃ upari na vaṭṭatī” (it is not allowed beyond four) indicates that the drum-fringe is permissible beyond that. “Veṭhetvā” (having wrapped) means having wrapped the rope with a cloth. “Muddikasaṇṭhānena” (in the shape of a ring) means in the shape of the head of a varaka bean. “Evaṃ sibbitā” (sewn thus) means being sewn thus. “Hi” (indeed) is a particle indicating a consequence. “Pāsanta” (the end of the noose) means the tip of the noose.

280. Olambakaṃ katvā nivatthaṃ hatthisoṇḍakaṃ nāmāti yojanā. Coḷikaitthīnanti coḷaraṭṭhe nivāsīnaṃ itthīnaṃ. Hatthiyā soṇḍo viya hatthisoṇḍakaṃ nivatthaṃ. Macchavālaṃ viyāti macchavālakaṃ. Cattāro kaṇṇā etassa nivatthassāti catukaṇṇakaṃ. Tālavaṇṭaṃ viyāti tālavaṇṭakaṃ. Sataṃ valino etassa nivatthassāti satavalikaṃ. “Anekakkhattu”nti iminā “satavalika”nti ettha satasaddassa anekatthavācakataṃ dasseti. “Vāmadakkhiṇapassesu vā”ti iminā purimanivatthaṃ kaṭito paṭṭhāya heṭṭhā nivatthaṃ nāmāti dasseti.

280. The construction is that the garment worn, made to hang down, is called `hatthisoṇḍaka` (elephant’s trunk-like). “Coḷikaitthīnaṃ” (of Coḷa women) means of women residing in the Coḷa country. `Hatthisoṇḍakaṃ nivatthaṃ` is a garment like an elephant’s trunk. “Macchavālakaṃ” (fish-tail-like) means like a fish’s tail. “Catukaṇṇaka” (four-cornered) means a garment that has four corners. “Tālavaṇṭaka” (palm-leaf fan-like) means like a palm-leaf fan. “Satavalika” (hundred-folded) means a garment that has a hundred folds. “Anekakkhattuṃ” (many times) indicates that the word `sata` in “satavalika” conveys the meaning of ‘many’. “Vāmadakkhiṇapassesu vā” (or on the left and right sides) indicates that the previously mentioned garment is called a lower garment, starting from the waist downwards.

Saṃvallitvā nivatthaṃ saṃvalliyaṃ. Mallo ca kammakāro ca mallakammakārā, te ādayo yesaṃ teti mallakammakārādayo. Ādisaddena dhuttādayo saṅgaṇhāti. Yampi nivatthaṃ nivāsenti, sabbaṃ taṃ nivatthaṃ na vaṭṭatīti yojanā. Ekaṃ vā koṇanti sambandho. Koṇeti antaravāsakassa koṇe. “Tathā”ti iminā “ekaṃ vā dve vā koṇe ukkhipitvā antaravāsakassa upari laggentī”ti atthaṃ atidisati. Antokāsāvassa dassetvāti sambandho. Dve nivāsentena agilānenāti yojanā. Saguṇanti antokāsāvena bahikāsāvaṃ samānaguṇaṃ katvā. Itītiādi nigamanaṃ. Yañcāti yaṃ nivatthañca. Idhāti khuddakavatthukkhandhake. Yañca sekhiyavaṇṇanāyaṃ (pāci. aṭṭha. 576 ādayo) paṭikkhittanti sambandho. Sabbaṃ taṃ nivatthanti yojanā. Nibbikāraṃ katvāti sambandho. Ubho [M 0.0464] kaṇṇeti heṭṭhā ṭhite ubho kaṇṇe upari ca ṭhite ubho kaṇṇe. Tanti parimaṇḍalapārupanaṃ.

`Saṃvalliya` is a garment worn by wrapping. `Mallakammakārā` are wrestlers and laborers; `mallakammakārādayo` are those of whom they are the beginning. By the word `ādi`, it includes gamblers and the like. The construction is: whatever garment they wear, all of that garment is not proper. The connection is with `ekaṃ vā koṇaṃ` (one corner). `Koṇe` means at the corner of the under-robe. By 'Tathā' (thus), it extends the meaning to 'having lifted one or two corners and fastened them upon the under-robe.' The connection is with `antokāsāvassa dassetvā` (having shown the inner dyed robe). The construction is with `dve nivāsentena agilānena` (by one who is not ill wearing two). `Saguṇaṃ` means having made the outer dyed robe of equal quality with the inner dyed robe. `Iti`, and so on, is the conclusion. `Yañca` means 'and whatever garment.' `Idha` means here, in the Khuddakavatthukkhandhaka. The connection is with `yañca sekhiyavaṇṇanāyaṃ paṭikkhittaṃ` (and what is prohibited in the commentary on the Sekhiya rules). The construction is `sabbaṃ taṃ nivatthaṃ` (all that garment). The connection is with `nibbikāraṃ katvā` (having made it unaltered). `Ubho kaṇṇe` (both corners) means both corners situated below and both corners situated above. `Taṃ` refers to the circular manner of draping.

Tatthāti “gihipāruta”nti vacane yaṃkiñci aññathāpārutaṃ atthīti sambandho. Tasmāti yasmā [V 2.0111] gihipārutaṃ nāma, tasmā, parimaṇḍalaṃ pārupitabbanti sambandho. “Yathā pārupanti, yathā ca ṭhapentī”tiādinā yojanā kātabbā. Tassevāti dīghasāṭakasseva. Tassevāti sāṭakasseva. Pāḷikārakoti pāḷiṃ gaṇhantaṃ vā vācentaṃ vā kārako. Tathāti yathā pārupanti, tathā.

`Tattha` means: in the statement 'gihipāruta' (draped as by householders), there is something draped otherwise; this is the connection. `Tasmā` means: since it is called `gihipāruta`, therefore, it should be draped circularly; this is the connection. The construction should be made with 'yathā pārupanti, yathā ca ṭhapenti' (as they drape, and as they place) and so on. `Tasseva` means of that very long cloth. `Tasseva` means of that very cloth. `Pāḷikāraka` is one who takes up or recites the Pāli text. `Tathā` means: as they drape it, so.

281. Kuhiñci ṭhānaṃ gacchato raññoti yojanā. “Parikkhārabhaṇḍavahanamanussā”ti iminā te manussā muṇḍaṃ sīsaṃ coḷakena veṭhentīti muṇḍaveṭhino nāmāti dasseti. Adhippāyoti ujjhāyantānaṃ manussānamadhippāyo. Antarākājanti ettha antarāsaddo majjhatthavācakoti āha “majjhe”ti. “Laggetvā”tiādinā kājassa antare laggetvā vahitabbaṃ antarākājanti vacanatthaṃ dasseti.

281. The construction is with `rañño kuhiñci ṭhānaṃ gacchato` (of the king going to any place). By 'Parikkhārabhaṇḍavahanamanussā' (people carrying requisites and goods), it shows that those people wrap their shaven heads with a piece of cloth; hence, they are called `muṇḍaveṭhino` (head-wrappers). `Adhippāya` means the intention of the people who were complaining. Regarding `Antarākāja`, here the word `antara` denotes the middle, thus it says 'majjhe' (in the middle). By 'Laggetvā' (having attached) and so on, it shows the meaning of the word `antarākāja` as that which should be carried by attaching it in the middle of the carrying pole.

282. “Cakkhūnaṃ hita”nti iminā acakkhussanti ettha ssapaccayo cakkhusaddato hitatthe hotīti dasseti. Pamāṇaṅgulenāti vaḍḍhakīnaṃ pamāṇayuttena aṅgulena.

282. By 'Cakkhūnaṃ hitaṃ' (beneficial to the eyes), it shows that here, in `acakkhussa`, the suffix `-ssa` is from the word `cakkhu` in the sense of 'beneficial'. `Pamāṇaṅgulena` means with a carpenter's measuring finger-breadth.

283. “Tiṇavanādīsū”ti iminā dāyaṃ ālimpentīti ettha dāyasaddo vanavācakoti dasseti. “Aggiṃ dentī”ti iminā āpubbo lipidhātu upasaggavasena aggidānatthoti dasseti. Parittanti ettha samantato tāyati anenāti parittanti dassento āha “appaharitakaraṇena vā parikhākhaṇena vā parittāṇa”nti. Etthāti parittakaraṇe. Dātuṃ labbhatīti sayaṃ dātuṃ labbhati. Haritunti apanetuṃ. Pattaṃ vā apattaṃ vā agginti sambandho. Tathāti aggidānādinā ākārena. Udakena nibbāpentena bhikkhunāti sambandho.

283. By 'Tiṇavanādīsu' (in grass, forests, etc.), it shows that here, in 'dāyaṃ ālimpenti' (they set fire to the forest), the word `dāya` denotes 'forest'. By 'Aggiṃ denti' (they give fire), it shows that the root `lip` preceded by `ā`, by virtue of the prefix, has the meaning of 'giving fire'. Regarding `Paritta`, showing that here `paritta` means that by which one is protected on all sides, it says: 'protection by making it less green or by digging a trench.' `Ettha` means in the making of a protection. `Dātuṃ labbhati` means it is allowable to give it oneself. `Harituṃ` means to remove. The connection is with `pattaṃ vā apattaṃ vā aggiṃ` (fire, whether it has reached or not reached). `Tathā` means in the manner of giving fire and so on. The connection is with `udakena nibbāpentena bhikkhunā` (by the monk extinguishing with water).

284. Sati [M 0.0465] karaṇīyeti ettha karaṇīyasaddo kiccapariyāyoti āha “sukkhakaṭṭhādiggahaṇakicce”ti. “Sukkhakaṭṭhādiggahaṇa” iti padena kiccasarūpaṃ dasseti. “Purisappamāṇa”nti iminā porisiyanti ettha ṇiyapaccayo pamāṇatthe hotīti dasseti. Purisappamāṇaṃ nāma upari bāhudvayatatassa purisassa pamāṇaṃ. Disvā vā hutvā vā disvāti yojanā. Atiuccampīti pisaddo sambhāvanattho. Nīcaṃ pana rukkhaṃ pagevāti hi attho.

284. Regarding 'Sati karaṇīye' (when there is something to be done), here the word `karaṇīya` is a synonym for 'duty', thus it says 'in the duty of gathering dry wood, etc.'. By the term 'sukkhakaṭṭhādiggahaṇa' (gathering dry wood, etc.), it shows the nature of the duty. By 'Purisappamāṇa' (a man's measure), it shows that here, in `porisiya`, the suffix `-ṇiya` is in the sense of 'measure'. `Purisappamāṇa` is the measure of a man with his two arms stretched upwards. The construction is `disvā vā hutvā vā disvā` (having seen, or having been and then having seen). Regarding `Atiuccampi` (even very high), the particle `pi` is in the sense of possibility. The meaning is indeed: how much more so a low tree.

285. Kalyāṇavākkaraṇāti ettha kariyati uccāriyatīti karaṇo, saddo, vācāyeva karaṇo vākkaraṇo, kalyāṇo vākkaraṇo etesanti kalyāṇavākkaraṇāti dassento āha “madhurasaddā”ti. Vedaṃ viyāti sutiṃ viya. Vācanāmagganti vācanāya upāyaṃ. Sakāti sammāsambuddhasaṅkhātassa [V 2.0112] sassa attano esā sakā. Tena vuttaṃ “sammāsambuddhenā”ti. Sammāsambuddhena hi māgadhaniruttiyā eva dhammo bhāsito, tasmā sā māgadhanirutti sakā nāmāti vuccati. Niruttīti atthaṃ nīharitvā vuccate imāya saddapaññattiyāti nirutti, vacadhātussa vakārassa ukāro, sabbavohāro labbhati. Idha pana “sakāyā”ti vuttattā māgadhavohāro eva. Tena vuttaṃ “māgadhavohāro”ti. “Sabhāvaniruttī”tipi pāṭho. Evañhi sati sabbasattānaṃ sabhāvena pavattā mūlabhāsābhūtā māgadhaniruttiyeva.

285. Regarding `Kalyāṇavākkaraṇā`: here, `karaṇa` is that which is made or uttered, i.e., a sound; speech (`vācā`) itself is the `karaṇa`, hence `vākkaraṇa`; `kalyāṇavākkaraṇā` are those who have good (`kalyāṇa`) speech (`vākkaraṇa`). Showing this, it says `madhurasaddā` (sweet-sounding). `Vedaṃ viya` means like the sacred text (`suti`). `Vācanāmagga` means the method of recitation. `Sakā` means 'his own', that is, of him designated as the Perfectly Enlightened One. Therefore, it is said, 'by the Perfectly Enlightened One.' For the Dhamma was spoken by the Perfectly Enlightened One only in the Māgadhī dialect; therefore, that Māgadhī dialect is called `sakā` (one's own). `Nirutti` is that linguistic expression by which the meaning is extracted and spoken; the `va` of the root `vac` becomes `u`; all usage is included. Here, however, because 'sakāya' (in one's own) is stated, it is only the Māgadhī usage. Therefore, it is said, `māgadhavohāro` (Māgadhī usage). There is also the reading `sabhāvanirutti` (natural dialect). For if this is so, the Māgadhī dialect is indeed the fundamental language that proceeds naturally for all beings.

286. Lokāyataṃ nāma titthiyasatthanti sambandho. Imināva kāraṇenāti “seto kāko, kasmā? Aṭṭhīnaṃ setattā. Ratto bako, kasmā? Lohitassa rattattā” iti (ma. ni. aṭṭha. 2.223; saṃ. ni. aṭṭha. 3.5.1080; a. ni. 10.69-70) iminā eva kāraṇena.

286. The connection is: `Lokāyata` is the name of a teaching of the sectarians. `Imināva kāraṇena` (by this very reason) means by this very reason: 'A crow is white. Why? Because of the whiteness of its bones. A heron is red. Why? Because of the redness of its blood.'

288. Antarā [M 0.0466] ahosīti ettha antarasaddo byavadhānatthoti āha “antaritā ahosi paṭicchannā”ti. Tena saddena dhammakathā byavadhānā ahosīti attho.

288. Regarding 'Antarā ahosi' (it was in between), here the word `antara` has the meaning of 'interruption', thus it says 'it was interrupted, it was concealed.' The meaning is that the Dhamma talk was interrupted by that sound.

289. Ābādhappaccayāti ettha ābādhassa bhesajjasaṅkhāto paccayo ābādhapaccayoti dassento āha “yassā”tiādi. Iminā ābādhoyeva paccayo ābādhapaccayoti atthaṃ paṭikkhipati.

289. Regarding `Ābādhappaccayā`, showing that here `ābādhappaccaya` is the condition for an illness, designated as medicine, it says `yassā`, and so on. By this, it rejects the meaning that `ābādhappaccaya` is the illness itself as the condition.

293. Dukkaṭavatthu nāma akappiyavohārādinā mālāvaccharopanādi, pācittiyavatthu nāma mālāvaccharopanādiatthāya pathavīkhaṇanādi. Paharaṇīti paharati imāyāti paharaṇī. Etanti “paharaṇī”ti etaṃ nāmaṃ. Yassa kassaci āvudhasaṅkhātassa lohabhaṇḍassāti sambandho. Tanti āvudhasaṅkhātaṃ lohabhaṇḍaṃ. Vuttamevāti “katakaṃ nāma padumakaṇṇikākāra”ntiādinā (cūḷava. aṭṭha. 269) vuttameva. Dhaniyassevāti dhaniyassa eva. Aññesañhi katāya sabbamattikāmayakuṭiyā apākaṭattā vuttaṃ “dhaniyassevā”ti. Atha vā dhaniyassa sabbamattikāmayakuṭi ivāti yojanā. Sabbatthāti sabbasmiṃ khuddakavatthukkhandhake.

293. A `Dukkaṭa` offense means using improper speech, hanging garlands, and so on. A `Pācittiya` offense means digging the earth, and so on, for the purpose of hanging garlands. `Paharaṇī` is that with which one strikes, hence `paharaṇī`. `Etaṃ` refers to this name, `paharaṇī`. The connection is with any metal implement designated as a weapon. `Taṃ` refers to the metal implement designated as a weapon. `Vuttameva` means it has already been said, as in 'a `kataka` is in the shape of a lotus pericarp,' and so on. `Dhaniyasseva` means only Dhaniya's. For since an all-mud hut made by others is not well-known, it is said, 'only Dhaniya's.' Alternatively, the construction is: 'like Dhaniya's all-mud hut.' `Sabbattha` means in the entire Khuddakavatthukkhandhaka.

Iti khuddakavatthukkhandhakavaṇṇanāya yojanā samattā.

Thus the Yojanā on the commentary on the Khuddakavatthukkhandhaka is concluded.

6. Senāsanakkhandhakaṃ

6. The Section on Lodgings

Vihārānujānanakathā

The Discourse on the Permission for Monasteries

294. Senāsanakkhandhake [V 2.0113] apaññattaṃ hotīti ettha na ñapadhātu hoti, apica ñādhātuyeva, so ca kho anujānanatthoti āha “ananuññātaṃ hotī”ti. Iminā ñādhātussa avabodhanādayo atthe nivatteti, anujānanatthaṃyeva dasseti. Aḍḍhayogādīnaṃ visuṃ gahitattā vihārasaddena pārisesato avasesāvāsova gahetabboti āha “aḍḍhayogādimuttako avasesāvāso”ti. Suvaṇṇavaṅkagehanti suvaṇṇavaṅkachadanena chāditaṃ gehaṃ. Iṭṭhakāguhāti iṭṭhakāya [M 0.0467] katā guhā. Eseva nayo sesesupi. Āgatassa ca anāgatassa cāti ettha casaddena dvandavākyaṃ dasseti. Āgacchatīti āgato, na āgato anāgato, saṅgho. Āgato ca anāgato ca āgatānāgato, samāhāradvando puṃliṅgo, tassa. “Appaṭihatacārassā”ti iminā catūsu disāsu appaṭihatacāro cātuddisoti vacanatthaṃ dasseti.

294. In the Section on Lodgings, regarding "it is not prescribed," here there is not the root ñap, but rather only the root ñā, and that too for the purpose of permission. Thus he says, "it is not permitted." By this, he dismisses meanings such as understanding associated with the root ñā, and shows only the purpose of permission. Because the aḍḍhayoga and others are separately mentioned, the remaining dwellings should be understood by the term "vihāra" through the method of residues. Thus he says, "the remaining dwellings, excluding the aḍḍhayoga and others." "Suvaṇṇavaṅkageha" means a house covered with a golden bent roof. "Iṭṭhakāguhā" means a cave made of bricks. The same method applies to the rest as well. In "for those who have come and those who have not come," the word ca indicates a dvanda compound. One who comes is āgato; one who has not come is anāgato, referring to the Saṅgha. "Āgato ca anāgato ca" forms āgatānāgato, a collective compound in the masculine gender, referring to that. By "whose movement is unimpeded," he shows the meaning of the word cātuddisa as "one whose movement is unimpeded in the four directions."

295. Anumodanagāthāsu evaṃ vinicchayo veditabboti yojanā. Utuvisabhāgavasenāti sītauṇhānaṃ utūnaṃ visabhāgavasena. Saṃphusitakavātoti saha udakabindunā āgato vāto. Ettha hi saṃsaddo sahattho, phusitasaddo udakabinduvācako. Ujukameghavuṭṭhiyo evāti vātena apaharitattā ujukaṃ patitā meghavuṭṭhiyo eva. Pāḷiyaṃ tatoti ettha topaccayo paccattatthe vattati. So vihāroti hi attho. Vāḷamigāni cāti vāḷamige ca. Liṅgavipallāso hesa. Etāni sabbānīti “sīta”ntiādīni sabbāni satta padāni. Yojetabbānīti so vihāro sītaṃ paṭihanati…pe… vuṭṭhiyo paṭihanatīti yojetabbānīti attho.

295. In the verses of rejoicing, the interpretation should be understood thus. "Utuvisabhāgavasena" means due to the disparity of seasons, whether cold or hot. "Saṃphusitakavāta" means wind accompanied by raindrops. Here, the word saṃ means "together with," and the word phusita refers to raindrops. "Ujukameghavuṭṭhiyo eva" means the rain from the clouds falls straight down, not carried away by the wind. In the Pāli, regarding "tato," here the suffix -to is used in a specific sense. The meaning is "that dwelling." "Vāḷamigāni ca" means "and wild animals." This is a change of gender. "Etāni sabbānīti" means all seven terms beginning with "cold" (sīta). "Yojetabbāni" means that dwelling wards off the cold… wards off the rain, and so on—this is the meaning to be connected.

“Vihārenā”ti iminā pāḷiyaṃ tatoti ettha topaccayo kattutthe hotīti dasseti, tena vihārenāti attho. Paṭihaññatīti paṭihanīyati. Sukhatthanti ettha uttarapadalopoti āha “sukhavihārattha”nti. “Leṇatthañca sukhatthañcā”ti padadvayaṃ “hotī”ti pāṭhasesena yojetabbaṃ. Vihāradānaṃ leṇatthañca sukhatthañca hotīti hi attho. Idanti ayaṃ adhippāyo. Vuttanti vutto. Vihāradānaṃ sukhatthañca hotīti yojanā. Jhāyituṃ vipassituñca yaṃ sukhaṃ atthīti sambandho. Tadatthanti tassa sukhassa atthāya. Parapadenapīti “jhāyituñca vipassitu”nti padadvayato [V 2.0114] paraṃ ṭhitena “vihāradāna”nti padenapi. Idhāti imasmiṃ vihāre. Vihāradānanti vihārassa dānaṃ, dātabbavihāraṃ vā, vaṇṇitanti sambandho. Vuttanti saṃyuttanikāye vuttaṃ. Sādhakapāḷiyaṃ yo upassayaṃ dadāti, so ca sabbadado sabbesaṃ balādīnaṃ [M 0.0468] dado hotīti yojanā. So cāti ettha casaddo avadhāraṇattho. So evāti hi attho.

By "Vihārena," he shows that in the Pāli, regarding "tato," the suffix -to here has the sense of agency (kattuttha); therefore, the meaning is "by the monastery." "Paṭihaññati" means "is warded off." Regarding "sukhatthaṃ," he says that here there is an elision of the latter word, thus "for the purpose of a happy dwelling." The two phrases "for shelter and for happiness" should be connected with the remaining part of the reading, "is." The meaning is that the giving of a monastery is for shelter and for happiness. "Idaṃ" means this is the intended meaning. "Vuttaṃ" means "stated." The phrase "the giving of a monastery is for happiness" should be connected. The connection is: the happiness that exists for meditating and for insight. "Tadatthaṃ" means for the purpose of that happiness. "By another word" means by the word "vihāradāna" which comes after the two words "jhāyituñca vipassituṃ." "Idha" means in this monastery. "Vihāradāna" means the giving of a monastery, or a monastery to be given; the connection is with 'is praised.' "Vuttaṃ" means it is stated in the Saṃyutta Nikāya. In the Sādhaka Pāli passage, the connection is: whoever gives a dwelling, he is the giver of all, the giver of strength, and so forth, to all. Here, the word ca has a restrictive meaning. The meaning is "he alone."

“Vihāre”ti iminā vāsayetthāti ettha etasaddassa visayaṃ dasseti. Vāsayeti vāseyya. Tesaṃ annañcāti ettha “tesa”nti padaṃ “anucchaviya”nti pāṭhasesena yojetabbanti dassento āha “tesaṃ anucchaviya”nti. Tattha anucchaviyaṃ annañca anucchaviyāni vatthāni cāti yojanā. Atha vā tesanti bhummatthe sampadānavacananti dassento āha “tesū”ti, bhikkhūsūti attho. Ujubhūtesūti ettha sampadānatthe bhummavacanaṃ katvā ujubhūtānaṃ tesaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ dadeyyāti atthopi yujjateva. “Akuṭilacittesū”ti iminā “ujubhūtesū”ti ettha ujusaddassa akuṭilatthañca bhūtasaddena bāhiratthasamāsañca dasseti. Ujubhūtaṃ cittametesanti ujubhūtāti vacanattho kātabbo. Nidaheyyāti nikhaṇitvā ṭhapeyya. “Na cittapasādaṃ virādhetvā”ti iminā vippasannena cetasāti ettha evatthaphalaṃ vā aññatthāpohanaṃ vā dasseti. Hīti phalajotako. Evaṃ vippasannacittassa tassa vihāradāyakassa te bhikkhū dhammaṃ desentīti yojanā.

By "in the monastery," he shows the scope of the word eta in "vāsayettha." "Vāsayeti" means "he should cause to dwell." Regarding "for them, and food," he shows that the word tesaṃ should be connected with the remaining part of the reading, "suitable," thus he says, "suitable for them." There, the construction is: food that is suitable and clothing that is suitable. Alternatively, he shows that tesaṃ is a dative expression in the sense of the locative, thus he says "in them," meaning in the monks. In "among the upright," having made it a locative expression in the sense of the dative, the meaning "he should give to those upright monks" is also appropriate. By "with uncrooked minds," he shows that in "among the upright," the word uju means "uncrooked" and the word bhūta indicates a compound with an external meaning. The meaning of the word ujubhūta should be made: "those whose minds are upright." "Nidaheyya" means "having buried, he should keep." By "without ruining clarity of mind," he shows here either the fruit of a serene mind or the rejection of other aims, in "with a serene mind." "Hi" is a particle indicating result. Thus, the connection is: those monks teach the Dhamma to that giver of the monastery whose mind is so serene.

296. Āviñchanachiddanti aṅguliṃ ava pavesetvā añchati ākaḍḍhati ettha, etenāti vā āviñchanaṃ. Avapubbo achidhātu, upasaggaakārassa dīghaṃ katvā, dhātuakārassa ca ikāraṃ katvā “āviñchana”nti vuttaṃ, tameva chiddaṃ āviñchanachiddaṃ. Āviñchanarajjunti kavāṭacchidde ava pavesetvā añchati ākaḍḍhati imāyāti āviñchanā, sāyeva rajjūti āviñchanarajju. Kāci rajju na na vaṭṭatīti yojanā. Atha vā na vaṭṭati na hoti, vaṭṭatiyevāti yojanā. Tīṇi tālānīti ettha tālasaddo kuñcikāpariyāyoti āha “tisso kuñcikāyo”ti. Iminā tālasaddassa rukkhatūriyavisese nivatteti. Yaṃ yanti upakaraṇaṃ. Tassāti yantakassa. Vedikāvātapānanti vātaṃ pivati anenāti vātapānaṃ, vedikāya kataṃ vātapānaṃ vedikāvātapānaṃ. Cakkalikanti ettha cakkākārena alati pavattatīti cakkalaṃ, coḷakapādapuñjanaṃ. Tena bandhitabbanti cakkalikanti dassento āha [M 0.0469] “coḷakapādapuñjanaṃ bandhitu”nti. “Vātapānappamāṇena bhisiṃ katvā”ti iminā vātapānapamāṇena katā bhisi vātapānabhisīti vacanatthaṃ dasseti.

296. "Āviñchanachidda" means a hole where one inserts a finger and pulls or draws; or, "āviñchana" is that by which one pulls or draws.
