The root is añch prefixed with ava; having lengthened the vowel of the prefix and changed the vowel of the root to i, it is called "āviñchana." That very hole is "āviñchanachidda." "Āviñchanarajju" means the rope inserted into the door's hole to pull or draw; hence it is called "āviñchanā." That very rope is the "āviñchanarajju." The construction is: any rope is allowable. Or alternatively, 'it is not allowable' is not the case; it is indeed allowable—this is the interpretation. Regarding "tīṇi tālāni," here the word tāla is synonymous with kuñcikā (key); thus he says, "three keys." By this, he dismisses the meanings of the word tāla as a tree or a type of musical instrument. "Yaṃ yanti" refers to the implement. "Tassa" pertains to the mechanism. "Vedikāvātapāna" means a place through which wind passes, hence a vātapāna. A vātapāna made in a railing is a "vedikāvātapāna." Regarding "Cakkalikā," here cakkalaṃ means something that revolves in the shape of a wheel, a foot-wiper made of cloth. Indicating that it is for tying, he says, "to tie a foot-wiper made of cloth." By "having made a cushion to the size of the window," he shows the meaning of the word vātapānabhisī as a cushion made to the size of the window.

297. “Uccakampi āsandika”nti vacanato vaṭṭatīti veditabboti sambandho. Ekatobhāgena [V 2.0115] dīghapīṭhaṃ aṭṭhaṅgulapādakameva vaṭṭatīti yojanā. Tato adhikaṃ na vaṭṭatīti adhippāyo. Pamāṇātikkantopīti pisaddo pamāṇayutto pana pagevāti dasseti. Sattaṅgoti tīsu disāsu apassayo, cattāro pādāti satta aṅgāni etassāti sattaṅgo. Ayampīti pisaddo āsandikaṃ apekkhati. Eḷakapādapīṭhaṃ nāma vuccatīti sambandho. Eḷakassa pādo viya pādo etthāti eḷakapādaṃ, tameva pīṭhaṃ eḷakapādapīṭhaṃ. Āmalakavaṇṇikapīṭhanti āmalakāya vaṇṇo saṇṭhāno āmalakavaṇṇo, tena yojitaṃ āmalakavaṇṇikaṃ, tadeva pīṭhaṃ āmalakavaṇṇikapīṭhaṃ. “Ākārenā”ti iminā vaṇṇasaddassa saṇṭhānatthaṃ dasseti. Imānīti pīṭhāni. Etthāti pīṭhe. Muñcapabbajamayanti muñjena ca pabbajena ca kataṃ.

297. The connection is that, according to the saying "even a high seat," it is to be understood as allowable. The construction is that a long bench with one side and eight-finger-breadth legs is indeed allowable. The intention is that anything beyond that is not allowable. By "even exceeding the measure," the word pi shows that what is within the measure is certainly allowable. "Seven-limbed" refers to a seat with supports on three sides and four legs, making seven limbs in total. The word pi in "this too" refers back to the seat. The connection is that it is called "goat-footed seat." "Eḷakapāda" means a foot here is like a goat's foot, and that very seat is the "eḷakapādapīṭha." "Āmalakavaṇṇikapīṭha" means a shape like an embelic myrobalan is āmalakavaṇṇa, and that which is endowed with that shape is āmalakavaṇṇika; that very seat is the "āmalakavaṇṇikapīṭha." By "by appearance," he shows that the meaning of the word vaṇṇa is shape. "These" refers to the seats. "Here" means in the seat. "Made of muñja grass and pabbaja" means made from munja grass and pabbaja.

Manussānanti vaḍḍhakīmanussānaṃ. Chavisaṃrakkhanatthāyāti chaviyā vināsanato suṭṭhu rakkhanatthāya. Simbalirukkhādīnantiādisaddena tūlanibbattake sabbarukkhe saṅgaṇhāti. Khīravalliādīnantiādisaddena tūlanibbattakā sabbā latāyo saṅgaṇhāti. Poṭakītiṇādīnantiādisaddena tūlanibbattakā sabbā tiṇajātiyo saṅgaṇhāti. Tīhīti rukkhalatāpoṭakīhi. Nanu bhūtagāmānaṃ anekattā etehi tīhi mutto bhūtagāmo atthi, kasmā pana sabbabhūtagāmā saṅgahitā hontīti āha “rukkhavallitiṇajātiyo hī”tiādi. Tattha hi yasmā natthi, tasmā saṅgahitā hontīti yojanā. Tasmāti yasmā natthi, tasmā. Sabbampi etaṃ tūlanti yojanā. Bibbohane lomampi vaṭṭatīti sambandho. Lomampīti pisaddena tūlaṃ apekkhati. Yaṃkiñci pupphanti sabbaṃ pupphaṃ. Pattaṃ pāpuṇitvā suddhaṃ tamālapattameva na vaṭṭati, avasesaṃ [M 0.0470] sabbaṃ pattaṃ suddhampi vaṭṭatīti adhippāyo. Pañcavidhanti uṇṇacoḷavākatiṇapaṇṇavasena pañcapakāraṃ.

Here, 'manussānaṃ' refers to carpenters. Here, 'chavisaṃrakkhanatthāya' means for the purpose of thoroughly protecting the skin from destruction. By 'simbalirukkhādīnaṃ' are included all trees that produce cotton, such as the simbali tree and others. By 'khīravalliādīnaṃ' are included all creepers that produce cotton, such as the khīravalli and others. By 'poṭakītiṇādīnaṃ' are included all grass species that produce cotton, such as the poṭakī grass and others. Here, 'tīhi' refers to trees, creepers, and grasses. Now, one might ask: since beings in the plant kingdom are diverse, is there any plant not included in these three categories? Why then are all plants included? The answer is given: 'Because they are tree, creeper, and grass species,' and so on. Here, the interpretation is that because there is nothing outside these, they are all included. Here, 'tasmā' means 'because there is nothing outside these.' The interpretation is 'all this is cotton.' The connection is that 'even hair is allowable for a cushion.' The particle 'pi' in 'lomampi' is used with reference to cotton. Here, 'yaṃkiñci pupphaṃ' means 'any flower,' that is, all flowers. The meaning is that only the pure tamāla leaf, once obtained, is not suitable, but all other pure leaves are suitable. Here, 'pañcavidhaṃ' refers to the five kinds by way of wool, cloth, bark, grass, and leaves.

“Upaḍḍhakāyapamāṇānī”ti iminā addhakāyikānīti ettha addhassa kāyassa pamāṇena katāni addhakāyikānīti atthaṃ dasseti. Yesu bibbohanesu kaṭito paṭṭhāya yāva sīsaṃ upadahanti, tāni bibbohanāni addhakāyikāni nāmāti yojanā. Yassāti bibbohanassa. Vitthārato muṭṭhiratanaṃ hotīti sambandho. Iminā yattha saha gīvāya sakalaṃ sīsaṃ ṭhapetuṃ sakkā, tassa muṭṭhiratanaṃ vitthārapamāṇanti dasseti. “Tīsu kaṇṇesu dvinnaṃ kaṇṇāna”nti idaṃ bibbohanassa ubhosu antesu ṭhapetabbacoḷapamāṇaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ. Idaṃ pana bibbohanassa ubhosu antesu ṭhapitacoḷassa koṭiyā koṭiṃ āhacca dviguṇaṃ kataṃ tikaṇṇaṃ hoti, tesu tīsu kaṇṇesu dvinnaṃ kaṇṇānamantaraṃ vidatthi caturaṅgulaṃ hoti, majjhaṭṭhānaṃ koṭito koṭimāhacca muṭṭhiratanaṃ hoti, idaṃ pana bibbohanaṃ tikaṇṇaṃ hoti. Vaṭṭaṃ vā caturassādiṃ vā katvā sibbitaṃ [V 2.0116] yathā koṭito koṭi vitthārato puthulaṭṭhānaṃ muṭṭhiratanaṃ hoti, evaṃ sibbitabbaṃ. Ito adhikaṃ na vaṭṭati, ūnaṃ pana vaṭṭatiyeva. Sīsūpadhānanti sīsaṃ upadahanti ṭhapenti etthāti sīsūpadhānaṃ. Bibbohanānīti visesena, visesaṃ vā sukhaṃ vahantīti bibbohanāni. Uparīti bibbohanānaṃ upari. Yāni pana kappiyatūlāni santīti yojanā. Mahantampīti pisaddo khuddakaṃ pana pagevāti dasseti. Vinayadharaupatissatthero pana āhāti sambandho. “Vinayadhara” iti padena phussadevattherato visesaṃ dasseti. Akappiyatūlaṃ vāti bhisiyaṃ akappiyatūlaṃ vā. Bibbohane hi akappiyatūlaṃ nāma natthi.

Here, by 'upaḍḍhakāyapamāṇāni' is shown the meaning of 'addhakāyikāni' as 'made to the measure of half the body.' The interpretation is that those cushions on which one places the body from the waist up to the head are called 'half-body cushions.' Here, 'yassa' refers to the cushion. The connection is that 'its width is a fist-span.' By this, it is shown that the width is a fist-span where the entire head, including the neck, can be placed. The phrase 'of two corners among three corners' is stated with reference to the measure of the cloth to be placed at both ends of the cushion. This cushion, when the cloth placed at both ends is doubled by bringing edge to edge, becomes three-cornered. Among these three corners, the distance between two corners is a span and four fingers. The middle part, from edge to edge, is a fist-span. This cushion is three-cornered. It should be sewn either round or square, etc., so that the broad part, from edge to edge in width, is a fist-span. More than this is not allowed, but less is indeed allowed. Here, 'sīsūpadhāna' means 'that on which one places or supports the head,' hence a head-rest. Here, 'bibbohanāni' means 'cushions' because they especially, or in a special way, bear comfort. Here, 'upari' means 'above the cushions.' The interpretation is 'whatever permissible cotton there is.' Here, by 'mahantampi' (even if large), the particle 'pi' indicates that small is certainly allowed. The connection is that 'the Elder Upatissa, the Vinaya-holder, further says.' By the word 'Vinaya-holder,' it shows a distinction from the Elder Phussadeva. Here, 'akappiyatūlaṃ vā' means 'or impermissible cotton' in a mattress. For in cushions, there is no such thing as impermissible cotton.

Pañcabhisiyoti ettha vākyabhāvañca asamāhāradigubhāvañca paṭikkhipanto āha “pañcahi uṇṇādīhi pūritā bhisiyo”ti. Iminā pañcahi uṇṇādīhi pūritā bhisiyo pañcabhisiyoti vacanatthaṃ dasseti. Atthato pana vākyampi asamāhāradigupi yujjateva. Kasmā pañcagaṇanā hotīti [M 0.0471] āha “tūlagaṇanāya hī”tiādi. Hi yasmā tūlagaṇanāya etāsaṃ gaṇanā vuttā, tasmā pañcabhisiyo hontīti yojanā. Tatthāti uṇṇādīsu pañcasu. Uṇṇaggahaṇena gahitanti sambandho. Kambalamevāti uṇṇāmayaṃ kambalameva. Uṇṇāya, uṇṇaṃ vā pakkhipitvā katā bhisi uṇṇābhisi. Eseva nayo coḷabhisiādīsu.

Here, regarding 'pañcabhisiyo', rejecting both the possibility of a sentence-structure and a non-collective dvigu compound, he says, 'mattresses filled with five things beginning with wool.' By this, he shows the word-meaning of 'pañcabhisiyo' as 'mattresses filled with five things beginning with wool.' But in terms of the underlying meaning, both a sentence-structure and a non-collective dvigu compound are indeed fitting. Why is there a counting of five? He says, 'Because it is by the counting of cotton,' and so on. The construction is that because the counting of these is stated by the counting of cotton, therefore they are 'five mattresses.' Here, 'tatthā' refers to the five things beginning with wool. The connection is: 'taken by the inclusion of wool.' Here, 'kambalameva' means 'just a woolen blanket,' that is, a blanket made of wool. A mattress made with wool, or having wool put into it, is a woolen mattress (uṇṇābhisi). The same method applies in the case of a cloth mattress (coḷabhisi), etc.

Pamāṇaniyamoti ettakā pamāṇāti pamāṇassa niyamo. Mañce attharitabbā bhisi mañcabhisi. Etāsanti mañcabhisiādīnaṃ. Yaṃ etaṃ tūlanti yojanā. Sūrakepīti cammamayabhisiyampi. Etenāti kurundiyaṃ vuttavacanena siddhaṃ hotīti sambandho.

Here, 'pamāṇaniyamo' means 'the regulation of measure,' that is, the fixing of the measure as 'so much is the measure.' A mattress to be spread on a bed is a 'bed-mattress' (mañcabhisi). Here, 'etāsaṃ' refers to bed-mattresses and the like. The interpretation is 'that which is this cotton.' Here, 'sūrakepi' means 'even in a leather mattress.' The connection is that 'by this' (that is, by the statement in the Kurundī) it is established.

Mañcabhisinti mañce attharitabbaṃ bhisiṃ. “Attharaṇatthāya saṃharantīti yujjatī”ti iminā “attharantī”ti ettha kāriyūpacārena attho gahetabboti dasseti. Attharaṇāya hi saṃharaṇaṃ kāraṇaṃ nāma, attharaṇaṃ kāriyaṃ nāma. Uparīti bhisichaviyā upari. Phusitānīti bindūni. Bhittikammanti bhittiyaṃ nānāvaṇṇehi rājikaraṇaṃ viya kattabbaṃ kammaṃ.

Here, 'mañcabhisiṃ' means 'a mattress to be spread on a bed.' By the phrase 'it is fitting that they gather for the purpose of spreading,' he shows that the meaning of 'attharanti' here should be understood through the figurative use of the effect for the cause. For gathering is the cause of spreading, and spreading is the effect. Here, 'upari' means 'above the mattress cover.' Here, 'phusitāni' refers to drops. Here, 'bhittikamma' means 'work to be done on a wall, like painting with various colors.'

298. “Ikkāsa”nti nāmaṃ niyyāsasilesānaṃ nāmanti āha “rukkhaniyyāsaṃ vā silesaṃ vā”ti. “Kuṇḍakamissakamattika”nti iminā kuṇḍakena missakā mattikā kuṇḍakamattikāti vacanatthaṃ dasseti. Sāsapapiṭṭhanti sāsapacuṇṇaṃ. “Bindu bindu [V 2.0117] hutvā”ti iminā accussannaṃ hotīti ettha kāraṇūpacāraṃ dasseti. Accussannañhi kāraṇaṃ hoti, “bindu bindu hutvā”ti ṭhānaṃ kāriyaṃ hoti. “Puñjitu”nti sodhetuṃ. Gaṇḍuppādagūthamattikanti mahilatāya gūthamayaṃ mattikaṃ. Iminā laṇḍamattikanti ettha laṇḍasaddo gūthapariyāyoti dasseti.

298. Here, 'ikkāsa' is the name for resin and gum; thus, he says, 'tree resin or gum.' By 'kuṇḍakamissakamattika' is shown the word-meaning of 'kuṇḍakamattikā' as 'clay mixed with kuṇḍaka.' Here, 'sāsapapiṭṭha' means 'mustard powder.' By 'becoming drop by drop' is shown the figurative application of cause in the phrase 'becomes excessively saturated.' For excessive saturation is indeed the cause, and the state of 'becoming drop by drop' is the effect. Here, 'puñjituṃ' means 'to purify.' Here, 'gaṇḍuppādagūthamattika' means 'clay consisting of earthworm dung.' By this, it is shown that the word 'laṇḍa' in 'laṇḍamattika' is a synonym for dung.

299. Na bhikkhave paṭibhānacittanti ettha “itthirūpakaṃ purisarūpaka”nti pāḷiyaṃ vuttattā kiṃ itthipurisarūpameva na vaṭṭatīti āha “na kevala”ntiādi. Tiracchānarūpampi kātuṃ vā “karohī”ti vattuṃ vā na [M 0.0472] vaṭṭatīti sambandho. Dvārapālanti dvārapālarūpaṃ. Pasādanīyānīti pasādetabbāni, pasādetuṃ arahānīti attho.

299. Here, regarding 'Not, monks, a figurative painting,' since 'a female figure and a male figure' are mentioned in the Pāḷi, one might ask: 'Are only female and male figures not permissible?' Thus, he says, 'not only,' and so on. The connection is that it is not allowable to make even an animal figure or to say, 'Make one.' Here, 'dvārapāla' means 'a figure of a door-guardian.' Here, 'pasādanīyāni' means 'things which should inspire confidence,' or 'worthy of inspiring confidence'—this is the meaning.

300. Ekaṅgaṇāti avihāraṭṭhānena samānabhūmibhāgā. Muṇḍacchedanagabbhoti muṇḍena chādetabbo gabbho.

300. Here, 'ekaṅgaṇā' means 'having a ground-area on the same level as a non-monastic area.' Here, 'muṇḍacchedanagabbha' means 'a chamber to be covered with a flat roof.'

Tatthāti vijjhitabbarukkhe. “Kata”nti iminā kulaṅkapādakanti ettha ṇikapaccayassa atthaṃ dasseti. Taṃ āharimaṃ bhittipādaṃ patiṭṭhāpetunti sambandho. Vassaparittāṇatthanti vassodakaparittāṇatthaṃ. “Madditamattika”nti iminā uddasudhanti ettha sudhāsaddassa lepanasudhaṃ dasseti, bhojanasudhaṃ nivatteti.

Here, 'tatthā' refers to the tree to be pierced. By 'kata' (made) is shown the meaning of the suffix '-ṇika' in 'kulaṅkapādaka' (stump-footed). The connection is 'to establish that brought-in wall-foot.' Here, 'vassaparittāṇatthaṃ' means 'for protection from rain,' that is, for protection from rainwater. By 'madditamattika' (pounded clay) is shown that the word 'sudhā' in 'uddasudhā' refers to plastering lime, excluding edible lime.

Pamukhanti vihārassa pamukhaṃ. Yanti padesaṃ, hanantīti sambandho. Tassa katapadesassāti yojanā. “Paghāna”ntipi vuccatīti dīghavasena “paghāna”ntipi vuccati. Iminā purimapāṭhe rassabhāvaṃ dīpeti. “Pakuṭṭa”ntipi pāṭhoti sasaṃyogavasena “pakuṭṭa”ntipi pāṭho. Iminā purimapāṭhe nisaṃyogabhāvaṃ dasseti. Vaṃsanti veḷuṃ. Tatoti vaṃsato. “Osāretvā kata”nti iminā osāretvā kataṃ osārakanti vacanatthaṃ dasseti. “Chadanapamukha”nti iminā ṇikapaccayassa sarūpaṃ dasseti. Cakkalayuttoti cakkalena yutto.

'Pamukha' means the foremost part of the dwelling. The connection is: 'they go to a place, they strike.' The construction is: 'of that made place.' It is also called 'paghāna'; that is, with a long vowel, it is also called 'paghāna'. By this, he indicates the shortness of the vowel in the previous reading. There is also the reading 'pakuṭṭa'; that is, with a conjunct consonant, there is also the reading 'pakuṭṭa'. By this, he shows the non-conjunct nature in the previous reading. 'Vaṃsa' means bamboo. 'Tato' means from bamboo. By 'osāretvā kata' (having lowered and made), he shows the verbal meaning of 'osāraka' as 'made by lowering'. By 'chadanapamukha', he shows the nature of the suffix '-ṇika'. 'Cakkalayutto' means fitted with a wheel.

301. Pānīyadānabhājananti pānīyaṃ deti anenāti pānīyadānaṃ, tameva bhājanaṃ pānīyadānabhājanaṃ. “Uḷuṅko ca thālakañcā”ti iminā dve pānīyasaṅkhassa anulomānīti yojanā.

301. 'Pānīyadānabhājana' means a vessel for giving water; 'pānīyadāna' is that by which water is given, and that very vessel is a 'pānīyadānabhājana'. By 'a dipper and a bowl,' the construction is that these two are in conformity with the water-pot.

303. Dvārathakanakanti dvāraṃ thaketi anenāti dvārathakanakaṃ. Gāmadvāresu dvārathakanakaṃ viya cakkalayuttaṃ dvārathakanakanti yojanā.

303. 'Dvārathakanaka' is so called because the door is fastened by this. The construction is: a 'dvārathakanaka' fitted with a wheel, like a door-bolt at village gates.

305. Assatarirathāti [V 2.0118] assānaṃ visesena, atisayena vāti assataro, atha vā pakatiasse tarati atikkamatīti assataro, so etesu rathesu yujjitabboti assatarī, teyeva rathāti assatarirathāti dassento āha “assatarayuttā rathā assatarirathā”ti. Tattha “assatarayuttā”ti iminā “assatarī”ti padassa assatthitaddhitaṃ dasseti. Āmuttamaṇikuṇḍalāti padassa “sataṃ kaññā [M 0.0473] sahassānī”ti padena sambandhitabbattā vuttaṃ “āmuttamaṇikuṇḍalānī”ti. Iminā nikārassa ākāro hotīti dasseti. Kaṇṇesu āmuttaṃ maṇikuṇḍalaṃ etāsanti āmuttamaṇikuṇḍalā kaññāyo.

305. 'Assatarirathā': An 'assatara' (mule) is so called because it is special among horses, or exceedingly so; or alternatively, an 'assatara' because it surpasses ordinary horses. A chariot to which such a mule is to be yoked is an 'assatarī'; those very chariots are 'assatarirathā'. Showing this, it is said: 'chariots yoked with mules are assatarirathā'. Therein, by 'yoked with mules', the possessive suffix of the word 'assatarī' is shown. The word 'āmuttamaṇikuṇḍalā' is stated as 'āmuttamaṇikuṇḍalāni' because it must be connected with the words 'a hundred maidens, a thousand'. By this, it is shown that the letter 'ni' becomes the letter 'ā'. Maidens who have jeweled earrings fastened in their ears are 'āmuttamaṇikuṇḍalā'.

Khandhaparinibbānena parinibbutoti atthaṃ paṭikkhipanto āha “kilesaparinibbānena parinibbuto”ti. Sītibhūtoti ettha kilesātapānaṃ abhāveneva sītibhūto, na aññesanti āha “kilesātapābhāvenā”ti. “Kilesūpadhiabhāvenā”ti iminā nirupadhīti ettha khandhūpadhiabhisaṅkhārūpadhiabhāvenāti atthaṃ paṭikkhipati.

Rejecting the meaning 'fully extinguished by the parinibbāna of the aggregates,' he says: 'fully extinguished by the parinibbāna of the defilements.' Regarding 'become cooled,' here, one has become cooled by the absence of the heat of defilements alone, not by other things; thus it is said: 'by the absence of the heat of defilements.' By 'by the absence of the attachment of defilements,' he rejects the meaning of 'without attachment' here as 'by the absence of the attachment of the aggregates and the attachment of formations.'

Āsattiyoti ettha punappunaṃ visayesu, bhavesu vā sañjantīti āsattiyoti dassento āha “rūpādīsū”tiādi. Patthanāyoti taṇhāyo. Iminā āsattīnaṃ sarūpaṃ dasseti. “Chinditvā”ti iminā chetvāti ettha chedhātuyā chedanatthaṃ dasseti. Vineyyahadaye daranti ettha “vineyyā”ti padassa tvāpaccayantabhāvañca hadayasaddassa cittavācakabhāvañca darathasarūpañca dassento āha “citte kilesadarathaṃ vinetvā”ti. Tattha “citte”ti iminā hadayasaddassatthaṃ dasseti, “kilesa” iti padena darathasarūpaṃ, “vinetvā”ti iminā tvāpaccayantabhāvaṃ dasseti. Vayakaraṇanti paribbayamūlaṃ. Tañhi vayaṃ kariyati anenāti vayakaraṇanti vuccati. Iminā vayassa karaṇaṃ vayāyikaṃ, karaṇatthe āyikapaccayo, vayāyikameva veyyāyikanti atthaṃ dasseti.

Regarding 'āsatti' (attachment), showing that 'āsatti' means clinging repeatedly to sense objects or existences, he says: 'in forms, etc.' 'Longings' means cravings. By this, he shows the nature of attachments. By 'chinditvā' (having cut), he shows the meaning of cutting for 'chetvā' here, from the root 'chid'. Regarding 'vineyya hadaye daraṃ' (having removed the affliction in the heart), showing that the word 'vineyya' is a gerund equivalent to one ending with the suffix '-tvā', that the word 'hadaya' means 'mind', and the nature of 'dara' (affliction), he says: 'having removed the affliction of defilements in the mind'. Therein, by 'in the mind', he shows the meaning of the word 'hadaya'; by the word 'defilements', the nature of affliction; and by 'vinetvā' (having removed), he shows that it is a gerund. 'Vayakaraṇa' (cause of expense) is the root of decay. For it is called 'vayakaraṇa' because decay is caused by it. By this, he shows the meaning that 'vayāyikaṃ' is the causing of decay, that the suffix '-āyika' is in the sense of causing, and that 'vayāyika' itself is 'veyyāyika'.

307. Ādeyyavācoti ettha ādiyitabbāti ādeyyā, sā vācā etassāti ādeyyavācoti dassento āha “tassa vacana”ntiādi. Tattha tassāti anāthapiṇḍikassa. Sadhanāti saṃvijjamāna dhanā, attano vā dhanavanto. Mandadhanāti appadhanā. Adāsīti anāthapiṇḍiko adāsi. Itīti evaṃ, datvā katvāti sambandho. Soti anāthapiṇḍiko, agamāsīti sambandho.

307. Regarding 'ādeyyavāco' (whose word is worthy of acceptance), showing that 'ādeyyā' means 'worthy of being accepted' (ādiyitabbā), and that 'ādeyyavāco' means 'he whose word is that,' he says: 'his word,' etc. Therein, 'his' refers to Anāthapiṇḍika. 'Sadhanā' means possessing existing wealth, or wealthy in their own right. 'Mandadhanā' means having little wealth. 'Adāsi' means Anāthapiṇḍika gave. 'Iti' means 'thus'; the connection is 'having given, having done.' 'So' refers to Anāthapiṇḍika; the connection is with 'he went.'

Kahāpaṇe [M 0.0474] santharīti sambandho. Koṭiyā karaṇabhūtāya, ādhārabhūtāya vā. Paṭipātetvāti paṭihanāpetvā[V 2.0119]. Tattha tasmiṃ ṭhāne ye rukkhā vā yā pokkharaṇiyo vā tiṭṭhantīti yojanā. Tesanti tāsaṃ rukkhapokkharaṇīnaṃ. Sāmaññañhi apekkhitvā pulliṅgavasena vuttaṃ. Parikkhepapamāṇanti pariṇāhassa pamāṇaṃ. Assāti anāthapiṇḍikassa.

The connection is 'he spread out kahāpaṇas.' With a koṭi as the instrument or as the basis. 'Paṭipātetvā' (having made to fall) means 'having caused to be struck down.' The construction is: 'There, in that place, whatever trees or ponds stand.' 'Tesaṃ' (of those) means 'of those trees and ponds.' For it is spoken in the masculine gender with reference to the general term. 'Parikkhepapamāṇa' (measure of the circumference) means 'the measure of the girth.' 'Assa' (of him) means 'of Anāthapiṇḍika.'

Evaṃ bahudhanaṃ cajantassāpi gahapatinoti yojanā. Koṭṭhakaṃ māpesīti ettha aññe koṭṭhake paṭikkhipanto āha “dvārakoṭṭhakapāsāda”nti.

The construction is: 'Even for a householder who relinquishes so much wealth.' Regarding 'he had a koṭṭhaka built,' here, rejecting other types of koṭṭhakas, he says: 'a palace-like gatehouse.'

Vihārādayoti ettha ādisaddena pāḷiyaṃ āgate pariveṇādayo cuddasa upakaraṇe saṅgaṇhāti. Amhākaṃ bhagavato vihārakārāpanapasaṅgena sattannampi buddhānaṃ vihārakārāpanaṃ dassento āha “vipassissā”tiādi. Tattha vipassissa bhagavato vihāraṃ (dī. ni. aṭṭha. 2.12) kārāpesīti sambandho. Tigāvutappamāṇaṃ bhūmiṃ suvaṇṇayaṭṭhisantharena kiṇitvā vihāraṃ kārāpesīti yojanā. Eseva nayo paratopi. Aṭṭhakarīsappamāṇā bhūmi usabhena dasausabhappamāṇā yaṭṭhiyā dvisatayaṭṭhippamāṇā hotīti daṭṭhabbaṃ. “Evaṃ anupubbena parihāyantī”ti vatvā sabbajanaṃ saṃvejento āha “sampattiyo hī”tiādi. Tattha yasmā sampattiyo parihāyanti, tasmā alameva sabbasampattīsu virajjituṃ, alaṃ eva sabbasampattīhi vimuccitunti yojanā. “Sabbasampattīsū”ti padañhi “vimuccitu”nti padena vibhattipariṇāmaṃ katvā sambandhitabbaṃ.

Regarding 'vihārādayo' (monasteries, etc.), the word 'ādi' here includes the fourteen accessories, such as surrounding enclosures and so on, that are found in the Pāḷi. In connection with the causing to be built of a monastery for our Blessed One, showing the causing to be built of monasteries for all seven Buddhas, he says: 'for Vipassī,' etc. Therein, the connection is that he had a monastery built for the Blessed One Vipassī (Dī. Ni. Aṭṭha. 2.12). The construction is that he bought a plot of land measuring three gāvutas by covering it with golden rods, and had the monastery built. This same method applies hereafter. It should be understood that land measuring eight karīsas, with a rod ten usabhas in length, measures two hundred rods. Having stated, 'Thus, they gradually decline,' and stirring a sense of urgency in all people, he says: 'For attainments,' etc. Therein, the construction is: 'Since attainments decline, it is indeed enough to become dispassionate toward all attainments, and it is enough to be liberated from all attainments.' For the word 'sabbasampattīsu' must be connected with the word 'vimuccituṃ' by changing its case ending.

308. Khaṇḍaphullasaddānaṃ adhikaraṇabhāvaṃ dassento āha “khaṇḍanti chinnokāso. Phullanti phalitokāso”ti. Tattha “chinnokāso”ti iminā khaṇḍati chijjati etthāti khaṇḍanti vacanatthaṃ dasseti. “Phalitokāso”ti iminā phullati phalati etthāti phullanti vacanatthaṃ dasseti. Paṭisaṅkharissatīti ettha pāṭisaddassa pākatikatthabhāvaṃ, saṅkharissatisaddassa ca karadhātuyā nipphannabhāvaṃ dassetuṃ vuttaṃ “pākatikaṃ kariyatī”ti.

308. Showing the locative sense of the words 'khaṇḍa' and 'phulla,' he says: ''Khaṇḍa' means a broken place. 'Phulla' means a split-open place.' Therein, by 'a broken place,' he shows the verbal meaning of 'khaṇḍa' as 'it breaks, it is cut in this place, therefore it is khaṇḍa.' By 'a split-open place,' he shows the verbal meaning of 'phulla' as 'it blossoms, it bears fruit in this place, therefore it is phulla.' Regarding 'paṭisaṅkharissati' (will restore), to show that the prefix 'paṭi' has the meaning of 'original state,' and that the word 'saṅkharissati' is derived from the root 'kar,' it is said: 'It is made according to its original state.'

310. Theroti [M 0.0475] sāriputtatthero, āgacchatīti sambandho. Idanti gilānapaṭijagganādi. Assāti therassa. Aggāsanantiādīsu aggasaddo paṭhamatthopi uttamatthopi yujjati. Tena vuttaṃ “therāsana”ntiādi. Antarā satthīnanti ettha antarāti bhummatthe nissakkavacanaṃ. Satthisaddo ca ūrusaṅkhāto pādavācakoti āha “catunnaṃ pādānaṃ antare”ti.

310. 'Thera' refers to the Elder Sāriputta; the connection is with 'he comes.' 'Idaṃ' (this) refers to nursing the sick, etc. 'Assa' (for him) means 'for the elder.' In terms like 'aggāsana' (foremost seat), the word 'agga' can mean either 'first' or 'best.' Therefore, it is said: 'the elder's seat,' etc. Regarding 'antarā satthīnaṃ' (between the thighs), 'antarā' here is a word in the locative sense indicating separation. And the word 'satthi', known as 'thigh', also denotes 'leg'; thus he says: 'between the four legs.'

315. Patiṭṭhāpesīti [V 2.0120] ettha kaṃ vayaṃ katvā patiṭṭhāpesīti āha “aṭṭhārasakoṭipariccāgaṃ katvā”ti. Evantiādi nigamanaṃ.

315. Regarding 'patiṭṭhāpesī' (he established), in response to the question 'Having made what expenditure did he establish it?' he says: 'Having made a donation of eighteen crores.' 'Evaṃ' (thus), etc., is the conclusion.

Āsanappaṭibāhanādikathā

The Discourse on Refusing Seats and So Forth

316. Vippakatabhojanenāti ettha vippakatasaddo aniṭṭhitapariyāyoti āha “aniṭṭhite bhojane”ti. Pakiriyittha, pakiriyissate vā pakataṃ, na pakataṃ vippakatanti viggaho kātabbo, atthato pana “kariyamāno aniṭṭhito”ti vuttaṃ hoti. Etthāti ṭhāne. Atisamīpanti bhuñjamānassa bhikkhussa atiāsannaṃ. Tassāti bhuñjamānassa bhikkhussa. Pivitvā vāti yāguṃ pivitvā vā. Khāditvā vāti khajjakaṃ khāditvā vā. Rittahatthampīti tucchahatthampi. Pisaddena āmisahatthaṃ pana pagevāti dasseti. Hīti saccaṃ, yasmā vā. Soti rittahattho bhikkhu.

316. Regarding “with unfinished food” (vippakatabhojanena): here, the word “vippakata” is a synonym for “unfinished,” as stated: “with unfinished food.” The analysis should be made thus: that which was done or will be done is `pakataṃ`; that which is not `pakataṃ` is `vippakataṃ`. But in meaning, it is said to be “being done, unfinished.” “Here” (ettha) means “in this instance” (ṭhāne). “Too close” (atisamīpaṃ) means excessively near to the monk who is eating. “His” (tassa) refers to the monk who is eating. “Having drunk” (pivitvā vā) means having drunk rice gruel or the like. “Having eaten” (khāditvā vā) means having eaten hard food or the like. “Even with an empty hand” (rittahatthampi) means even with an empty hand (tucchahatthampi). The particle “pi” shows that a hand with food is all the more so. “Indeed” (hi) means “truly” (saccaṃ) or “because” (yasmā vā). “He” (so) refers to the monk with an empty hand.

Āpattinti dukkaṭāpattiṃ. Yanti vippakatabhojanaṃ bhikkhuṃ. Soti pacchā āgato bhikkhu. Ayañca bhikkhūti vippakatabhojano ayañca bhikkhu. Tenāti vippakatabhojanena navakena vā vuḍḍhatarena vā bhikkhunā. Kiṃ navakena vuḍḍhataraṃ āṇāpetuṃ vaṭṭatīti āha “vuḍḍhataraṃ hī”tiādi. Hīti saccaṃ, yasmā vā. Soti vuḍḍhataro bhikkhu. Tatoti udakaṃ āharāpetuṃ āṇattito. Yanti kammaṃ.

‘Offense’ (āpattiṃ) means an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭāpattiṃ). `Yaṃ` refers to the monk with unfinished food. `So` refers to the monk who came later. ‘And this monk’ (ayañca bhikkhu) means this monk who has unfinished food. ‘By that’ (tena) means by that monk with unfinished food, whether a junior or a senior. Is it proper for a junior to command a senior? He says, “Indeed, a senior,” and so on. ‘Indeed’ (hi) means ‘truly’ (saccaṃ) or ‘because’ (yasmā vā). `So` refers to the senior monk. ‘From that’ (tato) means from the command to bring water. `Yaṃ` refers to the act.

Yoti bhikkhu. “Evarūpassā”ti padena tassa niyamanaṃ veditabbaṃ. Kāsassa kheḷamallakaṃ ṭhapetabbaṃ. Bhagandaraatisārānaṃ vaccakapālaṃ ṭhapetabbaṃ[M 0.0476]. Aññesaṃ aññāni ṭhapetabbāni honti. Tena vuttaṃ “kheḷa…pe… hontī”ti. Yasmiṃti yasmiṃ gilāne. Yopi bhesajjaṃ karotīti sambandho. Lesakappenāti ettha lesakappasaddānaṃ atthato ekattā vuttaṃ “appakena sīsābādhādimattenā”ti. Bhikkhū gaṇetvāti ettha gaṇaṃ ñatvāti dassento āha “paricchedaṃ ñatvā”ti. Tattha “pariccheda”nti iminā gaṇasaddassa adhippāyatthaṃ dasseti. “Ñatvā”ti iminā idhātuyā atthaṃ dasseti.

`Yo` refers to the monk. By the word ‘of such a kind’ (evarūpassa), its restriction should be understood. A spittoon should be placed for one with a cough. A bedpan should be placed for those with fistula or dysentery. Other items should be placed for others. Hence it is said: “spittoon… and so on… they exist.” ‘In whichever’ (yasmiṃ) means in whichever sick person. The connection is with “who also prepares medicine.” Regarding ‘with a slight pretext’ (lesakappena): here, because the words `lesa` and `kappa` are one in meaning, it is said: “with a slight headache or the like.” Regarding ‘having counted the monks’ (bhikkhū gaṇetvā): here, showing it means ‘having known the group’ (gaṇaṃ ñatvā), it is said: ‘having known the limit’ (paricchedaṃ ñatvā). Therein, by ‘limit’ (paricchedaṃ), the intended meaning of the word ‘group’ (gaṇa) is shown. By ‘having known’ (ñatvā), the meaning of the root ‘to know’ is shown here.

Senāsanaggāhakathā

The Discussion on the Taking of Lodgings

318. Seyyāti kāyapasāraṇasaṅkhātaṃ sayanakiriyaṃ paṭikkhipitvā senāsanasaṅkhātaṃ seyyaṃ dassento [V 2.0121] āha “mañcaṭṭhānānī”ti. “Seyyāparicchedenā”ti iminā seyyagghenāti ettha agghasaddassa pūjanatthaṃ paṭikkhipitvā paricchedanatthaṃ dīpeti. Ettha ca agghasaddassa catutthakkharena yuttabhāvo heṭṭhā samuccayakkhandhakavaṇṇanā (cūḷava. aṭṭha. 102) yojanāya vuttoyeva. Kālanti seyyāpaṭiggahaṇassa kālaṃ. Gāhiyamānāti gāhāpiyamānā. “Atirekāni ahesu”nti iminā ussārayiṃsūti ettha uddhaṃ sārayiṃsu gacchiṃsu pavattiṃsūti atthaṃ dasseti. Atirekānīti ca bhikkhuparicchedato seyyāparicchedāni atirekāni. Anubhāganti ettha anu pacchā dātabbo bhāgo anubhāgoti dassento āha “puna aparampi bhāgaṃ dātu”nti. Atimandesūtiādivacanena kiñcimandesu bhikkhūsu ekekassa bhikkhuno dve tisso seyyā dātabbā. Yato kiñcimandesu bhikkhūsu dve tayo vihārā dātabbāti atthopi gahetabbo. Tatthāti “na akāmā dātabbo”ti vacane. Anubhāge gahiteti yojanā. Yena anubhāgo ca paṭhamabhāgo ca gahito, so bhikkhūti yojanā.

318. Regarding ‘seyyā’: rejecting the sense of ‘lying down’ (sayanakiriya), which is characterized by ‘stretching the body’ (kāyapasāraṇa), and showing ‘seyyā’ as characterized by ‘lodging’ (senāsana), it is said: ‘places for beds’ (mañcaṭṭhānāni). By ‘by the allocation of resting places’ (seyyāparicchedena), it is shown that ‘by the measure of the resting place’ (seyyagghena) here rejects the meaning of ‘aggha’ as ‘honor’ and indicates ‘measurement.’ And here, the connection of the word ‘aggha’ with the fourth syllable has already been stated in the explanation of the Samuccayakkhandhaka (Cūḷavagga Aṭṭhakathā 102) below, by way of construction. ‘Time’ (kālaṃ) refers to the time for receiving lodgings. ‘Being taken’ (gāhiyamānā) means being caused to be taken. By the phrase ‘there were extra’ (atirekāni ahesuṃ), the meaning of `ussārayiṃsu` here is shown as ‘they were raised up,’ ‘they went,’ or ‘they proceeded.’ And ‘extra’ (atirekāni) means the allocations of lodgings were extra compared to the allocations for monks. Regarding ‘additional portion’ (anubhāgaṃ): here, showing that `anubhāga` means a portion (`bhāga`) to be given (`dātabbo`) afterwards (`anu pacchā`), it is said: ‘to give another portion again.’ By the statement ‘even if the monks are somewhat slow’ (atimandesūtiādi), it means that two or three lodgings should be given to each monk when the monks are somewhat slow. From this, the meaning should also be taken that two or three dwellings should be given to monks who are somewhat slow. ‘Therein’ (tattha) refers to the statement ‘it should not be given unwillingly.’ The construction is ‘when the additional portion has been taken.’ The construction is ‘that monk by whom both the additional portion and the initial portion have been taken.’

“Upacārasīmato bahī”ti iminā nissīmeti ettha sīmato bahi nikkhantaṃ, nisinnaṃ vā nissīmanti atthaṃ dasseti. Upacārasīmāya āvāsavaḍḍhanavasena ativitthārattā vuttaṃ “dūre ṭhitassāpī”ti. Utukālepīti [M 0.0477] hemantagimhakālepi. Tasmiñhi kāle sītauṇhautu tikhiṇo hoti, tasmā tasseva visesena utukāloti nāmaṃ pākaṭaṃ hoti. Tena vuttaṃ “hemantagimhakālepī”ti. Pisaddena vassakālaṃ apekkhati. Purimavassūpanāyikadivase gāho purimako, pacchimavassūpanāyikadivase gāho pacchimako.

By “outside the boundary of the vicinity” (upacārasīmato bahī), it shows the meaning that “outside the boundary” (nissīma) here refers to that which has gone forth from the boundary or is seated outside it. Because the boundary of the vicinity is very extensive due to the expansion of the dwelling, it is said: “even for one standing far away.” ‘Even in the proper season’ (utukālepi) means even in the winter and summer seasons. For at that time, the cold and hot seasons are intense; therefore, the term ‘season’ (utukāla) is especially prominent for that very reason. Hence it is said: “even in winter and summer.” The particle “pi” implies the rainy season. The taking on the day of the earlier Rains-residence is the earlier taking; the taking on the day of the later Rains-residence is the later taking.

Antarā dvīhi vassūpanāyikadivasehi mutte kāle gāho antarāmuttako. Ekasmiṃ vihāreti ekissaṃ vihārasīmāyaṃ. Senāsanasāmikāti senāsanadāyakā, dentīti sambandho. Tanti senāsanaṃ. Āvāsikā na olokentīti sambandho. Etthāti senāsane. Palujjantampīti vinassantampi. Bhagavā āhāti sambandho. Tassāti senāsanassa. Aparajjūti aparasmiṃ ahani aparajju. Gatāyāti atikkamitāya. Pavāraṇāya gatāya pavāraṇadivase atikkamite sati aparajju antarāmuttako gāhetabboti yojanā.

The taking in the time freed between the two days for entering the Rains-residence is called `antarāmuttaka`. ‘In one monastery’ (ekasmiṃ vihāre) means within the boundary of one monastery (ekissaṃ vihārasīmāyaṃ). ‘Owners of the lodging’ (senāsanasāmikā) means donors of lodging (senāsanadāyakā); the connection is ‘they give.’ `Taṃ` refers to the lodging. The connection is ‘the residents do not look after.’ ‘Here’ (ettha) means in the lodging. ‘Even if it collapses’ (palujjantampi) means even if it is destroyed (vinassantampi). The connection is ‘the Blessed One said.’ ‘Of that’ (tassa) refers to the lodging. ‘The next day’ (aparajju) means on the next day, the day following. ‘When it has passed’ (gatāya) means when it has elapsed. The construction is: when the Invitation Day has passed, then on the following day, the interim taking should be undertaken.

Tanti antarāmuttakaṃ. Gāhentenāti gāhāpentena. Tenāti gaṇhantena. Aṭṭhamāseti cattāro hemantamāse, cattāro ca gimhamāseti aṭṭhamāse. Kadāci pañca gimhamāseti navamāse vā. Khaṇḍaṃ vāti chinnaṭṭhānaṃ vā. Phullaṃ vāti phalitaṭṭhānaṃ vā. Paṭisaṅkharitabbanti pākatikaṃ kātabbaṃ. Divasaṃ khepetvāti pariveṇe divasaṃ khepetvā. Tatthāti gahitasenāsane. Rattindivanti ratti [V 2.0122] ca divo ca rattindivaṃ, samāhāradvando, accantasaṃyoge cetaṃ upayogavacanaṃ. Na labbhatīti saṅghattherena na labbhati. Idanti senāsanaṃ.

`Taṃ` refers to the interim taking. ‘By the one who takes’ (gāhentena) means by the one who causes to be taken (gāhāpentena). ‘By him’ (tena) means by the one who takes (gaṇhantena). ‘Eight months’ (aṭṭhamāse) means four winter months and four summer months, making eight months; or sometimes five summer months, making nine months. ‘Or a piece’ (khaṇḍaṃ vā) means a broken part. ‘Or split open’ (phullaṃ vā) means a split part. ‘Should be repaired’ (paṭisaṅkharitabbaṃ) means it should be made normal. ‘Having spent the day’ (divasaṃ khepetvā) means having spent the day in the monastery precinct. ‘There’ (tattha) means in the lodging that has been taken. ‘Night and day’ (rattindivaṃ) means night and day; it is a collective copulative compound, and this is a usage for continuous duration. ‘Is not obtained’ (na labbhati) means it is not given by the senior monk of the Sangha. `Idaṃ` refers to the lodging.

Antarāmuttakagāhena agahetabbasenāsanaṃ dassento āha “yasmiṃ panā”tiādi. Temāsaccayena temāsaccayenāti tiṇṇaṃ māsānaṃ atikkamena tiṇṇaṃ māsānaṃ atikkamena. Hīti saccaṃ, yasmā vā. Yasmiṃ panāti senāsane pana. Sakidevāti ekavārameva. Ayanti esā kathā.

Showing the lodging that should not be taken by means of the interim taking, he says: “But in whatever…” and so on. ‘By after three months, after three months’ (temāsaccayena temāsaccayena) means by the lapse of three months, by the lapse of three months. ‘Indeed’ (hi) means ‘truly’ (saccaṃ) or ‘because’ (yasmā vā). ‘But in whatever’ (yasmiṃ pana) refers to the lodging. ‘Only once’ (sakideva) means just one time. `Ayaṃ` refers to this account.

Tatthāti duvidhesu senāsanaggāhesu. Utukālanti utukāle āgacchantīti sambandho. Tesaṃ tadāva dātabbanti sambandho. Akālo nāmāti [M 0.0478] uṭṭhāpanassa akālo nāma natthi. Ekaṃ vā mañcaṭṭhānaṃ vā ṭhapetabbanti yojanā. Eko vā thero āgacchatīti yojanā. Ubbhaṇḍikāti ukkhittabhaṇḍikā.

‘Therein’ (tattha) refers to the two kinds of lodging acquisitions. Regarding ‘seasonal time’ (utukālaṃ): the connection is “those arriving at the seasonal time.” The connection is “they should be given then and there.” ‘There is no such thing as an inappropriate time’ (akālo nāma) means there is no such thing as an inappropriate time for removal. The construction is: “one bed or a place for a bed should be set aside.” The construction is: “or one elder arrives.” `Ubbhaṇḍikā` means ‘a packed-up bundle.’

Bahūsūti tayo ādiṃ katvā bahūsu bhikkhūsu. Pahotīti ekekassa bhikkhussa pahoti. Tatthāti pariveṇe. Tassevāti pariveṇasāmikasseva. Evaṃ apahontesūti evaṃ pariveṇagghena apahontesu. Pāsādagghenāti vihārasaṅkhātassa pāsādassa paricchedena. Ovarakagghenāti gabbhassa paricchedena. Seyyagghenāti catupañcahatthappamāṇāya seyyāya paricchedena. Mañcaṭṭhānenāti dvihatthavitthārassa catuhatthaāyāmassa mañcassa ṭhānena. Ekamañcaṭṭhānassa dvinnaṃ pīṭhakānaṃ ṭhānattā vuttaṃ “ekapīṭhakaṭṭhānavasenā”ti. Idaṃ nisīdituṃ sakkuṇeyyavasena vuttaṃ. Sace na sakkā nisīdituṃ, na dātabbaṃ. Tena vuttaṃ “bhikkhuno pana ṭhitokāsamattaṃ na gāhetabba”nti. Etanti ṭhitokāsamattaṃ. Hīti saccaṃ, yasmā vā. Ekamañcaṭṭhānassa tiṇṇaṃ janānaṃ ekapīṭhakaṭṭhānabhāvena apahontattā vuttaṃ “ekaṃ mañcaṭṭhānaṃ vā tiṇṇaṃ janānaṃ dātabba”nti. Hīti saccaṃ. “Sītasamaye”ti iminā uṇhasamayepi sabbadivasaṃ ajjhokāse vasituṃ na sakkāti dīpeti. Pariḷāhasamaye pana sakkā sabbarattiṃ ajjhokāse vasituṃ. Kiñcāpi sakkā, sītuṇhakāle pana na dātabbattā pariḷāhasamayepi na dātabbanti veditabbaṃ. Ekamañcaṭṭhāne vā ekapīṭhakaṭṭhāne vā tiṇṇaṃ janānaṃ nisīdanākāraṃ dassento āha “mahātherenā”tiādi. Tattha mahātherena vattabbanti sambandho. Niddāgarukoti niddāya garukārako. Sītaṃ anudahatīti sītaṃ maṃ pīḷeti. Tenāti mahātherena. Dutiyattherenāpīti pisaddo mahātheraṃ apekkhati. Vuttanayenevāti “ukkāsitvā”tiādinā vuttanayeneva. Evantiādi nigamanaṃ. Jambudīpe pana ekacce bhikkhū gāhentīti sambandho. Kiñcideva mañcaṭṭhānaṃ [V 2.0123] vā pīṭhaṭṭhānaṃ vāti yojanā. Ayantiādi purimavacanassa nigamanavasena pacchimavacanassa kathanatthāya vuttavacanaṃ.

'Bahūsu' (among many) refers to many monks, beginning with three. 'Pahoti' (is sufficient) means it is sufficient for each monk. 'Tattha' (there) refers to the dwelling. 'Tasseva' (his own) means only for the owner of that dwelling. 'Evaṃ apahontesu' (thus being insufficient) means when it is insufficient according to the value of the dwelling. 'Pāsādagghena' (by the measure of the mansion) means by the measure of the mansion, which is designated as a monastery. 'Ovarakagghena' (by the measure of the inner chamber) means by the measure of the inner room. 'Seyyagghena' (by the measure of the bed) means by the measure of a bed four or five cubits in size. 'Mañcaṭṭhānena' (by the space of a bed) means by the space of a bed two cubits wide and four cubits long. Since the space for one bed is the space for two stools, it is said, 'by the space for one stool.' This is said with reference to the ability to sit. If one cannot sit, it should not be given. Therefore, it is said, 'But for a monk, even standing space should not be taken.' 'Etaṃ' (this) refers to even standing space. 'Hi' (indeed) means truly, or because. Since the space for one bed is insufficient for three people in terms of providing space for one stool each, it is said, 'Or one bed space should be given for three people.' 'Hi' (indeed) means truly. By 'in the cold season,' it is indicated that it is not possible to stay outdoors all day even in the hot season. However, in the season of great heat, one can stay outdoors all night. Although it is possible, since it should not be given in the cold and hot seasons, it should be understood that it should not be given even in the season of great heat. Showing the manner of sitting for three people in the space of one bed or one stool, it is said, 'by the great elder,' etc. Here, the connection is 'should be spoken by the great elder.' 'Niddāgaruko' (heavy with sleep) means one who is heavy with sleep. 'Sītaṃ anudahati' (the cold oppresses) means the cold afflicts me. 'Tena' (by him) refers to that great elder. 'Dutiyattherenāpi' (by the second elder also)—the particle 'pi' refers back to the great elder. 'Vuttanayeneva' (in the manner stated) means in the manner stated, 'having coughed,' etc. 'Evaṃ' and so on is the conclusion. The connection is: 'But in Jambudīpa, some monks take.' The construction is: 'some bed space or stool space.' 'Ayaṃ' and so on is a statement made to explain the subsequent statement by way of concluding the previous statement.

Vassāvāse [M 0.0479] senāsanaggāho evaṃ veditabboti yojanā. Āgantukavattanti āgantukassa vattaṃ. Aññatthāti aññasmiṃ ṭhāne. Gantvā vasitukāmena āgantukenāti yojanā. Vassūpanāyikadivasamevāti vassaṃ upagamanadivaseyeva. Tatthāti aññaṃ ṭhānaṃ. Nagantabbakāraṇaṃ dassento āha “vasanaṭṭhānaṃ vā hī”tiādi. Hīti yasmā. Tatrāti aññasmiṃ ṭhāne. Tenāti sambādhaasampajjanakāraṇā. Tasmāti yasmā na phāsuṃ vihareyya, tasmā. Taṃ vihāranti yasmiṃ vasitukāmo, taṃ vihāraṃ. Tatthāti vihāre, vasanto sukhaṃ vasissatīti sambandho. Uddesatthikoti uddesaṃ atthiko, uddesena vā. Kammaṭṭhānasappāyatanti kammaṭṭhānena, kammaṭṭhānassa vā sappāyabhāvaṃ.

The construction is: the assignment of lodgings for the rains residence should be understood in this way. 'Āgantukavattaṃ' (the duties for a guest) refers to the duty of a guest. 'Aññattha' (elsewhere) means in another place. The construction is: by a guest who wishes to go and stay. 'Vassūpanāyikadivasameva' (on the very day of entering the rains) means on the very day of undertaking the rains. 'Tattha' (there) refers to another place. Explaining the reason for not going, it is said: 'Or the place of dwelling,' etc. 'Hi' (because) means since. 'Tatra' (there) refers to another place. 'Tena' (because of that) means due to the reason of crowding and unsuitability. 'Tasmā' (therefore) means since one would not dwell comfortably, therefore. 'Taṃ vihāraṃ' (that dwelling) refers to the monastery where one wishes to stay. 'Tattha' (there) refers to in the monastery; the connection is: dwelling there, one will dwell happily. 'Uddesatthiko' (desiring instruction) means desirous of instruction, or through instruction. 'Kammaṭṭhānasappāyataṃ' (suitability for a meditation subject) means by means of a meditation subject, or the suitability of a meditation subject.

Tatthāti aññavihāraṃ. Gacchantena ghaṭṭetabboti sambandho. Ghaṭṭetabbākāraṃ dassento āha “na tatthā”tiādi. Tattha tatthāti sakaṭṭhāne. Kiṃ na vattabbāti āha “tumhe”tiādi. Salākabhattādīni vā yāgukhajjakādīni vā natthi na vijjantīti yojanā. Uposathāgārassa parikkhāroti sambandho. Tumhākaṃ vihārassa idaṃ tāḷañceva imaṃ sūciñca sampaṭicchathāti yojanā. Gamiyavattanti gamikānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ vattaṃ. “Daharehī”ti padaṃ “ukkhipāpetvā”ti ca “gāhāpetvā”ti ca padadvaye kāritakammaṃ, “pattacīvarabhaṇḍikāyo”ti padaṃ “ukkhipāpetvā”ti pade dhātukammaṃ, “telanāḷikattaradaṇḍādīnī”ti padaṃ “gāhāpetvā”ti pade dhātukammameva. Attānaṃ dassentenāti attānaṃ manussānaṃ pakāsentena. Vitakkanti paccayabāhullikavitakkaṃ. “Saparivāra”nti padaṃ “gacchantañcā”ti pade kiriyāvisesanaṃ. Evañhi sati saparivāraṃ gacchantañcāti sambandho. “Na”nti pade pana kārakavisesanaṃ. Evañhi sati saparivāraṃ naṃ bhikkhunti sambandho. “Disvā”ti pade ca kiriyāvisesanameva. Evañhi sati gacchantañca naṃ bhikkhuṃ saparivāraṃ disvāti sambandho. Manussā vadantīti sambandho. Tesūti manussesu. Eko paṇḍitamanussoti sambandho. Ayaṃ kālo vassūpanāyikakālo nāmāti yojanā. Yatthāti ṭhāne. Tassāti ekassa paṇḍitamanussassa, vacananti sambandho. Te manussā yācantīti sambandho[M 0.0480]. Aññatthāti aññaṃ ṭhānaṃ. Mejjanti aññamaññaṃ sinehantīti mittā. Sukhadukkhesu amā saha vattantīti amaccā. Mittāyeva amaccāti mittāmaccā, te. Sammantayitvāti samaṃ, sammā vā mantayitvā. Idhevāti gāme eva, vihāre eva vā. Kasmā sādituṃ vaṭṭati, nanu sabbametaṃ akappiyañca sāvajjañcāti āha [V 2.0124] “sabbañhetaṃ kappiyañceva anavajjañcā”ti. Hi yasmā etaṃ sabbaṃ kappiyañca anavajjañca, tasmā sabbaṃ sādituṃ vaṭṭatīti yojanā. Kurundiyaṃ pana vuttanti sambandho. Ubhayampīti mahāaṭṭhakathākurundīsu vuttavacanavasena ubhayampi etaṃ vacananti sambandho.

'Tattha' (therein) refers to another dwelling place. The connection is: 'an attempt should be made by one who is going.' Showing how the attempt should be made, it says: 'Na tattha' (not there), etc. 'Tattha tattha' (there, there) means in one's own place. 'Kiṃ na vattabbaṃ' (What should not be said?) is explained by: 'Tumhe' (you), etc. The construction is: 'Salākabhatta' (meal tickets) and so on, or 'yāgu-khajjaka' (gruel and snacks) and so on, are not present or do not exist. The connection is: 'the requisites of the Uposatha hall.' The construction is: 'You should accept this key and this bolt for your dwelling.' 'Gamiyavattaṃ' (the duty of those who travel) refers to the duties of traveling monks. The word 'daharehi' (by the younger monks) is the agent of the causative action in the two phrases 'ukkhipāpetvā' (having had lifted) and 'gāhāpetvā' (having had taken). The phrase 'pattacīvarabhaṇḍikāyo' (bowls, robes, and other belongings) is the object of the verb in 'ukkhipāpetvā.' The phrase 'telanāḷikattaradaṇḍādīni' (oil tubes, staffs, etc.) is the object of the verb in 'gāhāpetvā.' 'Attānaṃ dassentena' (showing oneself) means revealing oneself to people. 'Vitakkaṃ' (thought) refers to thought about an abundance of requisites. The word 'saparivāraṃ' (with an entourage) is an adverb modifying the word 'gacchantañca' (while going). Thus, the connection is: 'while going with an entourage.' As for the word 'naṃ' (him), it is a modifier of the noun. Thus, the connection is: 'him, the monk with an entourage.' And in the word 'disvā' (having seen), it is also an adverb. Thus, the connection is: 'having seen that monk going with an entourage.' The connection is: 'People speak.' 'Tesu' (among them) refers to among the people. The connection is: 'one wise person.' The construction is: 'This is the time called the beginning of the rains residence.' 'Yattha' (where) means in a place. 'Tassa' (his) refers to that one wise person; the connection is 'speech.' The connection is: 'Those people request.' 'Aññattha' (elsewhere) means another place. 'Mejjanti' means they are affectionate to one another, hence 'mittā' (friends). 'Amaccā' (ministers) means those who exist together in happiness and suffering. 'Mittāmaccā' (friends and ministers) are friends who are also ministers. 'Sammantayitvā' (having consulted together) means having deliberated equally or properly. 'Idheva' (here itself) means in the village itself or in the monastery itself. 'Why is it proper to approve? Is not all this improper and blameworthy?' To this, it is said: 'For all this is proper and blameless.' The construction is: 'Because all this is proper and blameless, therefore it is proper to approve of it all.' The connection is: 'But in the Kurundī, it is said.' 'Ubhayampi' (both) refers to this statement being found in both the Great Commentary and the Kurundī—this is the connection.

Āvāsikavattaṃ vitthārento āha “paṭikacceva hī”tiādi. Tattha paṭikaccevāti āgantukānaṃ āgatato paṭhamameva. Padhānagharavihāramaggoti padhānagharamaggo ca vihāramaggo ca. Muddavedikāyāti cetiyassa hammiyavedikāya. Kasmā idampi sabbaṃ kātabbanti āha “vassaṃ vasitukāmā hī”tiādi. Hīti saccaṃ, yasmā vā. Vassaṃ vasitukāmā sukhaṃ vasissantīti sambandho. Kataparikammehi āvāsikehīti sambandho. Yato kulato pakatiyā labbhati, tasmiṃ kule vassāvāsikaṃ pucchitabbanti yojanā. Na dinnapubbanti pubbe na dinnaṃ. Hīti yasmā. Upaddutāti upagantvā, bhusaṃ vā pīḷitā. Tatthāti manussesu. Yeti manussā. Vassāvāsike gāhiteti vassāvāsike senāsane gāhāpiyamāne. Gāhitabhikkhūnanti gāhāpitabhikkhūnaṃ. Vassāvāsikanti vassaṃ āvasantānaṃ dātabbaṃ cīvaraṃ. Gāhaṇakāloti gāhāpanakālo. Upakaṭṭhoti āsanno. Chātakādīhīti ādisaddena rogādayo saṅgaṇhāti. Yanti cīvaraṃ. Tatoti cīvarato. Tanti vacanaṃ. Tadanurūpenāti tesaṃ manussānaṃ vacanassānurūpena. Tesaṃ tesanti manussānaṃ, vassāvāsikaṃ cīvaranti sambandho.

Explaining the duties of a resident monk, he says, ‘paṭikacceva hi,’ and so on. Here, ‘paṭikacceva’ means even before the arrival of visiting monks. ‘Padhānagharavihāramaggo’ means the path to the main hall and the path to the monastery. ‘Muddavedikāya’ means at the railing of the shrine’s upper terrace. As to why all this must be done, it is stated: ‘Vassaṃ vasitukāmā hi,’ and so on. ‘Hi’ means truly, or because. The connection is: ‘They who wish to spend the rains will dwell comfortably.’ The connection is with ‘by resident monks who have prepared.’ The construction is: from whichever family it is customarily received, in that family, one should ask about the rains-residence. ‘Na dinnapubbaṃ’ means not previously given. ‘Hi’ means because. ‘Upaddutā’ means having approached or being severely afflicted. ‘Tattha’ means among people. ‘Ye’ refers to people. ‘Vassāvāsike gāhite’ means when the rains-residence lodging is being assigned. ‘Gāhitabhikkhūnaṃ’ means of the monks who have been assigned. ‘Vassāvāsikaṃ’ means the robe to be given to those spending the rains. ‘Gāhaṇakālo’ means the time of assignment. ‘Upakaṭṭho’ means close at hand. Regarding ‘chātakādīhi,’ the word ‘ādi’ (and so on) includes illnesses and other such things. ‘Yaṃ’ refers to the robe. ‘Tato’ means from that robe. ‘Taṃ’ refers to that statement. ‘Tadanurūpena’ means in accordance with the statement of those people. ‘Tesaṃ tesaṃ’ refers to the people; the connection is with ‘the rains-residence robe.’

Yassāti bhikkhuno. Soti bhikkhu. Iti vadantīti yojanā. Tanti cīvaraṃ. Paṭikkammāti paṭikkamitvā. Vihārato apasakkitvāti attho. Tatrāti gāme. Upanikkhepaṃ ṭhapetvāti kappiyavatthuṃ vā akappiyavatthuṃ vā ārāmikādīnaṃ hatthe upanikkhepaṃ ṭhapetvā. Vihāreti vihārassa, vihāre vassaṃ vasantassa vā. Apucchitvāpīti pisaddena [M 0.0481] “pucchitvāpī”ti atthaṃ dasseti. Tesantikulānaṃ. Vattanti jagganādivattaṃ. Tesanti kulānaṃ. Āgatañca tanti taṃ paṃsukūlikaṃ āgatañca vadantīti sambandho. Tenāti paṃsukūlikena. Dātuṃ na icchantīti saṅghassa ācikkhantepi saṅghassa dātuṃ na icchanti. Sabhāgo bhikkhūti attanā sabhāgo bhikkhu. Etanti vassāvāsikaṃ. Paṃsukūlikassa na vaṭṭati, kasmā? Gahapaticīvarattā. Itītiādi nigamanaṃ. Saddhādeyyeti saddhāya dātabbe vassāvāsikalābhavisaye.

‘Yassa’ refers to the monk. ‘So’ refers to the monk. The construction is: thus they say. ‘Taṃ’ refers to the robe. ‘Paṭikkamma’ means having retreated. The meaning is: having withdrawn from the dwelling. ‘Tatra’ means in the village. ‘Upanikkhepaṃ ṭhapetvā’ means having set aside either allowable or unallowable items in the hands of monastery workers and so on, as a deposit. ‘Vihāre’ refers to the dwelling, or to one dwelling in the dwelling during the rains retreat. Regarding ‘apucchitvāpi’ (even without asking), the particle ‘pi’ also indicates the meaning of ‘even having asked.’ ‘Tesaṃ’ means of those families. ‘Vattaṃ’ means duties such as being watchful. ‘Tesaṃ’ means of the families. The connection is with ‘Āgatañca taṃ,’ meaning they say, ‘That rag-robe has come.’ ‘Tena’ refers to the rag-robe wearer. ‘Dātuṃ na icchanti’ means they do not wish to give to the Saṅgha, even when he informs the Saṅgha. ‘Sabhāgo bhikkhu’ means a monk who is a co-sharer with oneself. ‘Etaṃ’ refers to the rains-residence robe. It is not allowable for the rag-robe wearer—why? Because it is cloth given by a householder. ‘Iti,’ and so on, is the conclusion. ‘Saddhādeyya’ refers to what is to be given out of faith, in the context of gains from the rains-residence.

Tatruppādeti tasmiṃ vihāre uppajjanakalābhavisaye. Bhaṇḍapaṭicchādananti paṭicchādanacīvarabhaṇḍaṃ. Cīvarabhaṇḍameva hi yasmā anena sarīraṃ paṭicchādiyati, tasmā bhaṇḍapaṭicchādananti [V 2.0125] vuccati. Gāhethāti bhikkhūhi gāhāpetha. Gāhetabbanti bhikkhūhi gāhāpetabbaṃ. Vatthu panāti sāṭakato aññaṃ kappiyaṃ vā akappiyaṃ vā vatthu pana. Kasmā vaṭṭatiyeva, nanu akappiyavatthu na vaṭṭatīti āha “kappiyakārakānañhi”tiādi. Tattha hi yasmā anuññātaṃ, tasmā vaṭṭatiyevāti yojanā. Dinnavatthuto uppannanti sambandho.

‘Tatruppādeti’ refers to the matter of a gain arising in that monastery. ‘Bhaṇḍapaṭicchādana’ means robe-material for covering. Indeed, because the body is covered by this robe-material, it is called ‘bhaṇḍapaṭicchādana.’ ‘Gāhetha’ means ‘you should cause it to be taken by the monks.’ ‘Gāhetabbaṃ’ means ‘it should be caused to be taken by the monks.’ ‘Vatthu pana’ means another item, whether allowable or unallowable, apart from the sāṭaka-cloth. Why is it indeed allowable? Is not an unallowable item unallowable? He says, ‘kappiyakārakānañhi,’ and so on. Here, because it is permitted, therefore it is indeed allowable—this is the connection. The connection is with ‘arisen from the given item.’

Yanti vatthu dinnanti sambandho. Etthāti kappiyakārakānaṃ hatthe dinnavatthūsu. Tanti vatthu upanāmentehīti sambandho. Garubhaṇḍaṃ hoti, garubhaṇḍattā aññesu paccayesu na upanāmetabbanti adhippāyo. Puggalavasenevāti “bhikkhū cīvarena kilamanti, ettakaṃ nāma taṇḍulabhāgaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ cīvaraṃ kātuṃ ruccati saṅghassā”tiādinā puggalaṃ parāmasitvā puggalavaseneva. Saṅghavasenāti “saṅgho cīvarena kilamatī”tiādinā saṅghavasena na kātabbanti sambandho. Evaṃ puggalavasena apalokanakammassa akattabbataṃ dassetvā idāni vatthuvasena tasseva akattabbataṃ dassento āha “jātarūparajatavasenāpī”tiādi. Kappiyabhaṇḍavasenāti cīvarataṇḍulehi avasesassa kappiyabhaṇḍassa vasena. Cīvarataṇḍulānañhi visuṃ gahitattā “kappiyabhaṇḍavasenā”ti ettha tehi avaseso kappiyabhaṇḍova gahetabbo. Taṃ panāti apalokanakammaṃ pana. Kattabbākāraṃ dassento āha “idānī”tiādi. Subhikkhanti samiddhabhikkhaṃ. Sulabhapiṇḍanti [M 0.0482] sukhena labhapiṇḍaṃ. Dvīhi padehi aññamaññassa kāraṇaṃ dasseti, subhikkhattā sulabhapiṇḍaṃ, sulabhapiṇḍattā subhikkhanti vuttaṃ hoti.

The connection is with ‘the item that was given.’ ‘Ettha’ refers to the items given into the hands of those who make them allowable. The connection is with ‘by those presenting that item.’ It is heavy goods, and because it is heavy goods, it should not be presented with other requisites—this is the intention. ‘By personal consideration’ means, considering the individual, such as, ‘The monks are troubled for robes; this much of a portion of rice is suitable for the Saṅgha to make a robe,’ and so forth, by personal consideration only. ‘By Saṅgha consideration’ means, it should not be done by considering the Saṅgha, such as, ‘The Saṅgha is troubled for robes,’ and so forth—this is the connection. Having thus shown that the act of seeking consent should not be performed by personal consideration, now showing that the same should not be performed by means of the item, he says, ‘even by means of gold and silver,’ and so forth. ‘By means of allowable goods’ refers to the remaining allowable goods apart from robe-cloth and rice. Since robe-cloth and rice are mentioned separately, here, by ‘by means of allowable goods,’ only the remaining allowable goods should be taken. ‘Taṃ pana’ refers to the act of seeking consent. Showing the manner in which it should be performed, he says, ‘idāni,’ and so forth. ‘Subhikkha’ means abundant alms-food. ‘Sulabhapiṇḍa’ means alms-food obtained with ease. By these two phrases, the mutual cause is shown: because alms-food is abundant, it is easy to obtain; because alms-food is easy to obtain, it is abundant—this is what is said.

Evaṃ cīvarapaccayaṃ sallakkhetvā senāsanaṃ sallakkhetabbanti sambandho. Kāleti gāhāpanassa kāle. Vuttanti mahāaṭṭhakathāya vuttaṃ. Kasmā dve sammannitabbā, nanu ekampi sammannituṃ vaṭṭatīti āha “evañhī”tiādi. Tattha hi yasmā gāhessati, tasmā dve sammannitabbāti yojanā. Ekena hi sammutiladdhena sakkā paraṃ gāhāpetuṃ, attanā pana attano pāpetuṃ na sakkā, tasmā dvīsu sammatesu navako vuḍḍhassa, vuḍḍho ca navakassāti ubho aññamaññaṃ gāhessantīti adhippāyo. Sammannitabbāti ekato sammannitabbā. Aṭṭhapi soḷasapīti ettha pisaddena tato adhikampi ekato sammannituṃ vaṭṭatīti dīpeti. Sattasatikakkhandhake ubbāhikasammutiyaṃ (cūḷava. 456) aṭṭhapi janā ekatova sammatāti vacanañcettha sādhakaṃ. Niggahakammameva hi saṅgho saṅghassa na karotīti daṭṭhabbaṃ. Tesanti aṭṭhasoḷasajanānaṃ, sammuti vaṭṭatiyevāti sambandho. Kinti sallakkhetabbanti āha “cetiyaghara”ntiādi.

The connection is: having thus considered the robe-requisite, the lodging should be considered. ‘At the time’ means at the time of assignment. ‘Stated’ refers to what was said in the Great Commentary. Why should two be appointed? Is it not permissible to appoint even one? To this, he says, ‘evañhi,’ and so on. Here, since one will cause another to take, therefore two should be appointed—this is the construction. For by one who has received the appointment, it is possible to have another assigned, but one cannot cause oneself to receive it. Therefore, when two are appointed, the junior will have the senior assigned, and the senior the junior—thus both will have each other assigned; this is the intention. ‘Should be appointed’ means they should be appointed together. Regarding ‘eight or sixteen,’ here the particle ‘pi’ indicates that even more than that may be appointed together. In the Chapter of the Seven Hundred, regarding the appointment for an investigation (ubbahikasammutiyaṃ) (Cūḷavagga 456), the statement that eight people were appointed together is a support for this. For it should be understood that the Saṅgha does not perform a censure action (niggahakamma) against the Saṅgha itself. ‘Tesaṃ’ refers to the eight or sixteen people; the connection is that the appointment is indeed permissible. How should it be considered? To this, he says: ‘cetiyaghara,’ and so on.

Āsanagharanti [V 2.0126] paṭimāgharaṃ. Maggapokkharaṇīnaṃ samīpe katā sālāyo upacāravasena vuccanti “maggo”ti ca “pokkharaṇī”ti ca. Tā hi sālāyo upacārasīmabbhantaragate gāmābhimukhamagge ca antoupacārasīmāyaṃ khaṇitā yattha katthaci pokkharaṇiyo ca karīyanti, iti sallakkhetabbanti yojanā. Asenāsanaṃ dassetvā senāsanaṃ dassento āha “vihāro”tiādi. Rukkhamūlanti channakavāṭabaddharukkhamūlaṃ. Eseva nayo veḷugumbepi. Gāhentena ca gāhetabbānīti sambandho. Saṅghikoti tatruppādo. Tesūti dvīsu cīvarapaccayesu. Yanti cīvarapaccayaṃ. Tassāti cīvarapaccayassa. Ṭhitikatoti pabandhavasena ṭhitaṭṭhānato. Itaroti paṭhamaṃ gahitacīvarapaccayato itaro.

‘Āsanaghara’ means an image house. Halls made near a path and lotus ponds are called ‘path’ and ‘pond’ by figurative expression. For those halls are made near a path facing the village that is within the precinct boundary, and near lotus ponds dug somewhere within the inner precinct boundary; this is how it should be understood. Having shown what is not a lodging, he then shows what is a lodging, saying, ‘vihāro,’ and so on. ‘The foot of a tree’ means the foot of a tree that is roofed and fitted with a door. This same method applies to a bamboo grove. The connection is: by one who is taking, the things to be taken should be taken. ‘Saṅghiko’ means that which arises there. ‘Tesū’ refers to the two robe-requisites. ‘Yaṃ’ refers to the robe-requisite. ‘Tassa’ refers to that robe-requisite. ‘Ṭhitikato’ means from a fixed place established by arrangement. ‘Itaro’ means the other from the robe-requisite taken first.

Appatāyāti [M 0.0483] appabhāvato, gāhiyamāneti sambandho. Pariveṇagghenāti pariveṇaparicchedena. Labhantīti pariveṇasāmikā bhikkhū labhanti. Tanti pariveṇaṃ. Vijaṭetvāti vijaṭaṃ katvā, dve vā tayo vā koṭṭhāse katvāti attho. Pakkhipitvāti bhāgakoṭṭhāsaṃ pakkhipitvā. Na evaṃ kātabbanti yathā mahāsumatthero āha, tathā na kātabbanti attho. Akātabbakāraṇaṃ dassento āha “manussā hī”tiādi. Tatthāti pariveṇe, pavisitabbaṃ iti āhāti yojanā. Etthāti etasmiṃ gāhaṇaṭṭhāne. Paṭikkosatīti paṭisedheti. Paṭikkosanākāraṃ dassento āha “mā āvuso”tiādi. Iti vuttaṃ, iti paṭikkosatīti yojanā. Eko hi itisaddo luttaniddiṭṭho. Tassāti mahātherassa. Saṅgahanti bhikkhūnaṃ saṅgahaṃ. Tanti mahātheraṃ.

'Appatāyāti' means 'due to lack of power'; 'gāhiyamāneti' is the connection. 'Pariveṇagghenāti' means 'by the enclosure limit of the dwelling'. 'Labhantīti' means 'the monks who own the dwelling receive'. 'Tanti' refers to the dwelling. 'Vijaṭetvāti' means 'having divided it, making two or three sections'—that is the meaning. 'Pakkhipitvāti' means 'placing a portion into'. 'Na evaṃ kātabbanti' means 'it should not be done as the elder Mahāsuma said'—that is the meaning. Showing the reason why it should not be done, he says, 'For people,' and so forth. 'Tatthāti' refers to the dwelling; the connection is 'he says it should be entered'. 'Etthāti' means 'in this place of taking'. 'Paṭikkosatīti' means 'rejects'. Showing the manner of rejection, he says, 'Do not, friend,' and so forth. The connection is 'it is said thus, he rejects thus'. Indeed, one 'iti' word is understood as elided. 'Tassāti' refers to the great elder. 'Saṅgahanti' means 'the monks' support'. 'Tanti' refers to the great elder.

Evaṃ vattabbanti evaṃ vakkhamānanayena vattabbaṃ. Paccayaṃ dhāretha, iti vattabbanti yojanā. Pāpuṇāti āvuso iti vutteti yojanā. “Gahitaṃ hotī”ti iminā “gaṇhatha, gaṇhāmī”ti paccuppannakālavasena vuttattā gahitaṃ hotīti dasseti. Atītaanāgatakālavasena agahitabhāvaṃ dassento āha “sace panā”tiādi. Satuppādamattanti gahaṇe satiyā uppādanamattaṃ. Etthāti senāsanapaccayagahaṇaṭṭhāne.

'Evaṃ vattabbanti' means 'it should be spoken in this way, in the manner to be stated'. The connection is 'Hold the requisite, it should be spoken thus'. The connection is 'It is obtained, friend,' it is said thus. By 'it is taken' he shows that it is taken because it is spoken in the present tense as 'take' and 'I take'. Showing the state of not being taken in the past or future tense, he says, 'But if,' and so forth. 'Satuppādamatta' means 'merely the arising of mindfulness upon taking'. 'Etthāti' refers to the place of taking lodging or requisites.

Yopīti yampi. Upayogatthe cetaṃ paccattavacanaṃ, yampi paccayaṃ vissajjetīti yojanā. Paccayanti ca cīvarapaccayaṃ. Ayampīti ayampi paccayo. Pisaddo mahālābhapariveṇe paccayaṃ sampiṇḍeti. Tasmiṃyeva pariveṇeti tasmiṃ paṃsukūlikena gahitapariveṇe eva. Aññassāti paṃsukūlikato aññassa bhikkhussa. Paṃsukūliko “ahaṃ vasāmī”ti senāsanaṃ jaggissati. Itaro “ahaṃ paccayaṃ gaṇhāmī”ti senāsanaṃ jaggissatīti yojanā. Dvīhi kāraṇehīti vasanagahaṇavasena dvīhi kāraṇehi. Paṃsukūlike gaṇhanteti sambandho. Idhāti senāsane. Tenāti [V 2.0127] paṃsukūlikena. Heṭṭhāti senāsanassa heṭṭhā, ṭhitaṃ aññaṃ bhikkhunti sambandho. Tenāti paṃsukūlikena[M 0.0484], kiñci vacananti sambandho. Vutthavassassa paṃsukūlikassāti yojanā. Vaṭṭatīti paṃsukūlikassa vaṭṭati. Tasmiṃ senāsaneti paṃsukūlikena gahitasenāsane. Yesaṃ panāti manussānaṃ pana. Tesanti manussānaṃ.

'Yopīti' means 'whatever also'. This is a word in the accusative case in the sense of use; the connection is 'whatever requisite he also gives up'. 'Paccayanti' refers to the robe requisite. 'Ayampīti' means 'even this requisite'. The particle 'pi' combines the requisites in the great-gain dwelling. 'Tasmiṃyeva pariveṇeti' means 'in that very dwelling taken by the rag-robe wearer'. 'Aññassāti' means 'another monk apart from the rag-robe wearer'. The rag-robe wearer will guard the lodging thinking, 'I will stay here'; the other will guard the lodging thinking, 'I will take the requisite'—that is the connection. 'Dvīhi kāraṇehīti' means 'by two reasons: staying and taking'. The connection is 'when the rag-robe wearer takes'. 'Idhāti' refers to the lodging. 'Tenāti' means 'by the rag-robe wearer'. 'Heṭṭhāti' means 'below the lodging'; the connection is 'another monk standing there'. 'Tenāti' means 'by the rag-robe wearer'; the connection is 'some word'. The connection is 'of the rag-robe wearer who has spent the rains'. 'Vaṭṭatīti' means 'it is suitable for the rag-robe wearer'. 'Tasmiṃ senāsaneti' means 'in the lodging taken by the rag-robe wearer'. 'Yesaṃ panāti' means 'but of the people'. 'Tesanti' means 'of the people'.

Thūpaṃ katvāti cetiyaṃ katvā. Tassāti thūpassa. Tena bhikkhunāti vassāvāsikaṃ gāhakabhikkhunā. Tanti bhojanasālaṃ. Gāhetuṃ vaṭṭatīti sambandho. Sabbamidanti sabbaṃ idaṃ vacanaṃ.

'Having made a stupa' means 'having made a shrine'. 'Of that' refers to the stupa. 'By that monk' means 'by the monk who dwells for the rains and is the receiver'. 'That' refers to the dining hall. The connection is 'it is proper to receive'. 'All this' means 'this entire statement'.

Pāṭipadaaruṇatoti vassūpanāyikadivasasaṅkhātassa pāṭipadassa aruṇuggamanato. Vitakkacārikoti “kattha nu kho vasissāmī”tiādinā vitakkena caraṇe anuyutto. Senāsanaṃ yācatīti senāsanaggāhāpakaṃ senāsanaṃ yācati. Gahitanti saṅghena gahitaṃ. Yatthāti ṭhāne. Vassūpagatehi vattabbāti sambandho. Punappunaṃ, samaṃ vā cetiyaṅgaṇādiṃ muñcanti sodhenti imāhīti sammuñcaniyo. Mucidhātu sodhanatthe yupaccayo karaṇatthe hoti. Tālujo paṭhamakkharo. Sulabhā ce daṇḍakā, ekekena dve tisso yaṭṭhisammuñcaniyo bandhitabbā. Sulabhā ce salākā, chapañcamuṭṭhisammuñcaniyo bandhitabbāti attho. Pañca pañca ukkāti araññavihāresu parissayavijānanatthaṃ pañca pañca aggiukkā koṭṭetabbā chinditabbāti attho.

'Pāṭipadaaruṇatoti' means 'from the dawn of the first day', which is counted as the day of entering the rains retreat. 'Vitakkacārikoti' refers to one who is engaged in wandering with thoughts like, 'Where indeed shall I stay?' and so forth. 'Senāsanaṃ yācatīti' means 'he asks for a lodging from the lodging allocator'. 'Gahitanti' means 'accepted by the Saṅgha'. 'Yatthāti' refers to the place. The connection is 'to be spoken by those who have entered the rains retreat'. 'Sammuñcaniyo' means 'brooms', because again and again, they clean or level the courtyard or shrine grounds with these. The root 'muc' has the meaning of cleaning, and the suffix 'yu' is in the instrumental sense. 'Tālujo' is the first syllable. If sticks are easily available, two or three sweeping sticks should be tied by each one. If twigs are easily available, five or six handfuls of sweeping twigs should be tied—this is the meaning. 'Pañca pañca ukkāti'—in forest dwellings, for the purpose of recognizing dangers, five by five firebrands should be struck or cut—this is the meaning.

“Nibaddhavattaṃ ṭhapetvā”ti ettha akattabbavattaṃ dassento āha “vattaṃ karontehi cā”tiādi. Tattha vattaṃ karontehi ca evarūpaṃ adhammikavattaṃ na kātabbanti sambandho. Hi saccaṃ, sabbeva ete uddesādayo papañcāti yojanā. Papañcenti saṃsāre ciraṃ ṭhapentīti papañcā. Mūgabbatanti mūgānaṃ vataṃ, mūgehi kattabbaṃ vā, mūgena viya vā amūgehi kattabbaṃ vataṃ. Evaṃ akātabbavattaṃ dassetvā idāni kātabbavattaṃ dassento āha “pariyattidhammo nāmā”tiādi. Tividhampīti pariyattipaṭipattipaṭivedhavasena tippakārampi. Avayavapariyattidhammopi avayavipariyattidhammaṃ, avayavipariyattidhammo [M 0.0485] vā avayavapariyattidhammaṃ patiṭṭhāpeti, tasmā pariyattidhammo attanāpi attānaṃ patiṭṭhāpesīti veditabbaṃ. Uddisathāti pariyattiṃ uddisatha. Sodhetvā…pe… upasampādethāti ettha sodhanaṃ nāma sabbesaṃ ācārakulaputtānaṃ upaparikkhanaṃ. Sodhetvā nissayaṃ dethāti ettha sodhanaṃ nāma bhikkhusabhāgataṃ upaparikkhanaṃ. Hīti saccaṃ. Kulaputtoti ācārakulaputto. Yattakāni dhutaṅgāni samādiyituṃ sakkothāti yojanā. Antovassaṃ nāmetanti bhummatthe upayogavacanametaṃ. Etasmiṃ antovasseti hi attho, bhavitabbantiādīsu [V 2.0128] sambandhitabbaṃ. Sakaladivasanti sakaladivasamhi, appamattehīti sambandho. Ekacārikavattanti ekakena caritabbaṃ vattaṃ. Bhasseti vacane. Dasavatthukakathanti appicchatādidasavatthuka kathaṃ.

"Except for established duties," here, to show what should not be done, it is said: "and by those who perform duties," etc. In that context, the connection is that such improper duties should not be performed by those who perform duties. For it is true, all these recitations and so on are proliferations. They proliferate, prolonging existence in the cycle of rebirth—hence they are called proliferations. "The vow of silence" means the vow of mutes, or what should be done by mutes, or a vow that should be performed by non-mutes as if by a mute. Having thus shown what should not be done, now showing what should be done, it is said: "The Dhamma of learning is called," etc. "Threefold too"—by way of learning, practice, and realization, it is threefold. The Dhamma of partial learning also establishes the Dhamma of complete learning, or the Dhamma of complete learning establishes the Dhamma of partial learning. Therefore, it should be understood that the Dhamma of learning establishes itself by itself. "Recite"—recite the learning. "Purify... and ordain"—here, purification means the examination of all sons of good families who adhere to good conduct. "Having purified, give dependence"—here, purification means examination by the assembly of monks. "For"—it is true. "Son of a good family"—a son of a good family who adheres to good conduct. "As many ascetic practices as you are able to undertake"—this is the connection. "During the rains residence"—this is a term of location. Here, the meaning is "during this rains residence," and it should be connected with "should be," etc. 'Sakaladivasanti' means 'throughout the entire day'; the connection is with 'by the diligent'. "The duty of a solitary wanderer"—the duty to be practiced alone. "Speak"—regarding speech. "Talk on the ten topics"—talk on the ten topics beginning with fewness of wants.

Viggāhikapisuṇapharusavacanānīti viggahaṃ kalahaṃ janetīti viggāhikaṃ, viggāhikavacanañca pisuṇavacanañca pharusavacanañca viggāhikapisuṇapharusavacanāni. Manasikārabahulā viharatha iti ovaditabbāti yojanā. Dantakaṭṭhakhādanavattanti heṭṭhā adinnādānavaṇṇanāyaṃ vuttaṃ dantakaṭṭhakhādane, dantakaṭṭhakhādanassa vā vattaṃ. “Pattaṃ thavikāya pakkhipantena na kathetabba”nti iminā kathente pamādena patto bhijjeyyāti pattassa guttatthāya kathanaṃ nivāreti. Ācikkhitabbāti itisaddo parisamāpanattho.

Contentious, backbiting, and harsh speech—that which generates quarrels and disputes is contentious; and contentious speech, backbiting speech, and harsh speech are the contentious, backbiting, and harsh speeches. The connection is that one should exhort thus: "You should live cultivating mindfulness." The practice of chewing tooth-wood—as mentioned earlier in the section on taking what is not given, regarding chewing tooth-wood, or the proper conduct for chewing tooth-wood. "One should not speak while placing the bowl into the bowl-bag"—this prohibits speaking so that, through carelessness, the bowl might break; this is to protect the bowl. "It should be announced"—the word "iti" here serves to conclude the discourse.

Koci dāyakoti sambandho. Āgantuko bhikkhūti cīvaraggāhitato pacchā āgato āgantuko bhikkhu. Saṅghattheroti āvāsikasaṅghatthero. Paṭhamabhāganti pubbe gāhitaṃ paṭhamabhāgaṃ, parivattetvāti pubbe gāhitabhāgena pacchā dātabbaṃ vassāvāsikaṃ parivattetvā. Āgantukassa vassaggena pattaṭṭhāne āgantukassa dātabbanti yojanā. “Āgantukassā”ti padaṃ pubbāparaṃ apekkhati. Tasmā dvinnaṃ padānaṃ majjhe vuttaṃ. Paṭhamavassūpagatāti paṭhamavassūpanāyikadivase vassūpagatā. “Dve tīṇi cattārī”ti vacanassa vā bahūnaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ vā byāpanatthāya “laddhaṃ laddha”nti vicchāvasena vuttaṃ. Tena panāti āgantukena [M 0.0486] pana. Paṭhamavassūpagatehi appake laddhe pacchimavassūpanāyikadivase dātabbānaṃ vassāvāsikānaṃ bahukepi ayaṃ nayo ñātabboti katvā na vutto.

The connection is with 'some donor'. 'A visiting monk' is one who arrives after the acceptance of robes. 'The senior monk of the Sangha' refers to the resident senior monk of the Sangha. 'The first portion' means the first portion taken previously; 'after exchanging' means exchanging the previously taken portion with the rains-residence robe to be given later. The construction is: it should be given to the visiting monk at the place where the bowl is received, by seniority of rains-residence. The phrase 'to the visiting monk' relates to both what precedes and what follows. Therefore, it is stated between the two phrases. 'Those who entered the first rains' refers to those who entered the rains on the day of the commencement of the first rains-residence. The words 'two, three, four' are spoken to indicate distribution to many monks, hence the phrase 'received, received' is spoken by way of scattering. 'But by that' means by the visiting monk. This principle is not stated because it should be understood that it applies even when few are received by those who entered the first rains, and even when many rains-residence robes are to be given on the day of the last rains-residence.

Dvīsupīti paṭhama dutiyavasena dvīsupi. Vassūpagatā bhikkhū bhikkhāya kilamantā vadantīti sambandho. Idhāti ṭhāne. Vasantāti ekato vasantā. Dve bhāgā homa sādhu vatāti yojanā. Sādhu vatāti ekaṃsena sundarā bhaveyyunti attho. Yesanti bhikkhūnaṃ. Tatthāti ñātipavāritaṭṭhānesu. Pavāraṇāyāti pavāraṇādivase. Tesūti bhikkhūsu. Yeti bhikkhū. Tatthāti ñātipavāritaṭṭhānesu. Kasmā apaloketvā dātabbaṃ, nanu te sādiyantīti āha “sādi yantāpi hī”tiādi. Tattha hīti yasmā. “Neva vassāvāsikassa sāmino”ti iminā tesaṃ vassacchinnataṃ dīpeti. Neva adātuṃ labhantīti paṭhamameva katikavattassa katattā adātuṃ neva labhanti, sabbesaṃ no amhākanti yojanā. Idhāti ṭhāne. Tanti katikavattaṃ. Eko bhikkhūti sambandho. Tesanti bhikkhūnaṃ. Tatthāti sabhāgaṭṭhāne. Vasitvā āgatānaṃ tesaṃ bhikkhūnanti [V 2.0129] yojanā. Na labbhati iti vuttanti yojanā. Imesanti vassāvāsiappattakānaṃ ekaccānaṃ. Gāhitasadisamevāti vassāvāsikassa gāhitena sadisameva. Tesamevāti ekaccānameva.

'In both' means in both, by way of first and second. The connection is: the monks who have entered the rains-residence, being weary with alms-seeking, speak. 'Here' means in this place. 'Dwelling' means dwelling together. The construction is: 'Let us become two parts, good indeed'. 'Good indeed' means it would be entirely beautiful. 'Of whom' means of the monks. 'There' means in the places where they are invited by relatives. 'On Pavāraṇā' means on the day of Pavāraṇā. 'Among them' means among the monks. 'Who' means the monks. 'There' means in the places where they are invited by relatives. Why should it be given after seeking agreement? Do they not consent? To this, it is said: 'Even if they consent, because...'. There, 'because' means since. By 'not even for the master of the rains-residence', it shows that their rains-residence is broken. The construction is: 'They are not able not to give' means because the agreement was made at the very beginning, they are not able not to give; 'it is for all of us'. 'Here' means in this place. 'That' means the agreement. The connection is with 'one monk'. 'Of them' means of the monks. 'There' means in the common place. The construction is: 'of those monks who have come after dwelling'. The construction is: it is said, 'It is not obtained'. 'Of these' means of some of those who have not completed the rains-residence. 'Just like what has been taken' means just like what has been taken by one who has observed the rains-residence. 'Of them only' means of some only.

Pakkantopīti aññaṃ ṭhānaṃ pakkamantopi. Hīti saccaṃ, yasmā vā. Tena bhikkhunā kataṃ pānīyaupaṭṭhapanādikammaṃ bhatiniviṭṭhaṃ bhatiyā ṭhitanti yojanā. Apalokanakammaṃ katvā gāhitaṃ saṅghikanti sambandho. Saṅghikanti tatruppādaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ. Vibbhantopīti pisaddo pageva chinnavassoti dasseti. Paccayavasenevāti saddhādeyyapaccayavasena. Vadantīti keci vadanti.

'Even when departing' means even when departing to another place. 'Hi' means truly, or because. The construction is: the work of providing drinking water, etc., done by that monk, is included in the wage; it stands as a wage. The connection is: having performed the act of announcing, what is taken belongs to the Sangha. 'Belonging to the Sangha' is said with reference to what has arisen there. 'Even if he has wandered away'—the word 'pi' shows that his rains-residence is already broken. 'By way of requisites only' means by way of requisites that are gifts of faith. 'They say' means some say.

Disaṃgamiko bhikkhu vibbhamatīti sambandho. Manusseti vassāvāsikadāyakamanusse. Sammukhāti āvāsikassa sammukhā. Sampaṭicchāpetvāti “suṭṭhu dassāmā”ti paṭicchāpetvā. Yassa gāhitanti yassa bhikkhuno senāsanaṃ gāhitaṃ. Senāsanasāmikassāti senāsanadāyakassa puttadhītādayoti [M 0.0487] sambandho. Senāsane demāti senāsanassa dema. Tatthāti senāsane. Ekameva vatthaṃ dātabbaṃ. Kasmā? Puggalassa adatvā senāsanasseva dātabbattā. Vassāvāsikaṭṭhitikāyāti vassāvāsikagāhitassa ṭhitikāya. Eseva nayoti senāsanasseva dinnattā eseva nayo. Tasseva hontīti puggalasseva dinnattā tasseva honti.

The connection is: a monk going to another region wanders. 'People' means the people who are donors of the rains-residence robe. 'In the presence' means in the presence of the resident monk. 'Having had it accepted' means having had it accepted by saying, 'We will give it well'. 'For whom it was taken' means for which monk the lodging was taken. The connection is: 'of the owner of the lodging' refers to the donor of the lodging, such as sons, daughters, etc. 'We give to the lodging' means we give for the lodging. 'There' means in the lodging. Only one cloth should be given. Why? Because it is to be given to the lodging itself, not to the individual. 'For the duration of the rains-residence' means for the duration of what was accepted as the rains-residence robe. 'This is the same principle' means because it is given to the lodging itself, this is the same principle.
