'They belong to him alone' means because they are given to the individual, they belong to him alone.

Dutiyo therāsane gāhito hotīti sambandho. Paṭhamabhāgassa sāmaṇerassa gāhitattā vuttaṃ “varabhāgaṃ sāmaṇerassa datvā”ti. Ubhopīti dve therasāmaṇerepi. Sayamevāti dāyako sayameva. Yanti vassāvāsikaṃ. Yassāti therassa vā sāmaṇerassa vā.

The connection is: the second is taken in the elder's seat. It is said, 'having given the best portion to the novice,' because the first portion was taken for the novice. 'Both' refers to both the elder and the novice. 'By himself' means the donor himself. 'Which' means the rains-residence robe. 'Of whom' refers to either the elder or the novice.

Itoti vuttanayato. Daharasāmaṇerassāti taruṇassa sāmaṇerassa. Soti gharasāmiko. Nanti pattajanaṃ. Yassāti bhikkhuno. Tesanti manussānaṃ. Yathābhūtaṃ ācikkhitabbanti vibbhamakālaṅkatakāraṇaṃ yathābhūtaṃ ācikkhitabbaṃ. Suddhapaṃsukūlikāyevāti aññehi amissā suddhā paṃsukūlikāyevāti. Idaṃ nevāsikavattanti nigamanaṃ.

'From this' means by the method stated. 'Of the young novice' means of the youthful novice. 'He' means the householder. 'Them' means the people who have arrived. 'Of whom' refers to the monk. 'Of them' refers to the people. 'The truth should be told as it is' means the reason for wandering away or for dying should be explained as it really is. 'Only pure rag-robe wearers' means only pure rag-robe wearers, unmixed with others. The conclusion is: 'This is the duty of a resident'.

Upanandavatthukathā

The Story of Upananda

319. Ayamatthoti ayaṃ vakkhamāno attho, evaṃ veditabboti sambandho. Tatthāti gāmake[V 2.0130]. Tanti senāsanaṃ, gaṇhantenevāti sambandho. Idhāti sāvatthiyaṃ. Muttanti te senāsanaṃ muñcitaṃ hoti. Tatrāpīti gāmakepi. Ubhayatthāti sāvatthiyaṃ, gāmake cāti ubhayattha.

319. The connection is: 'This is the meaning' means this is the meaning that will be spoken; 'it should be understood thus'. 'There' refers to the small village. The connection is: 'that' refers to the lodging; with 'by the one who takes it'. 'Here' refers to Sāvatthī. 'Released' means that lodging of yours is relinquished. 'Even there' means also in the small village. 'In both places' means both in Sāvatthī and in the small village—thus, in both places.

Etthāti upanandavatthusmiṃ. Kathanti kena pakārena paṭippassambhati. Idhāti sāsane. Ekacco gaṇhātīti sambandho. Tatrāpīti sāmantavihārepi[M 0.0488]. Tassāti bhikkhussa. Idhāti senāsane. Ālayamattanti cittuppādamattaṃ. Iccassāti iti assa, evaṃ assa bhikkhussāti attho. Sabbatthāti sabbasmiṃ “gahaṇena gahaṇa”ntiādike catukke. Yo pana gacchatīti sambandho. Upacārasīmātikkameti nimittatthe cetaṃ bhummavacanaṃ, bhāvena bhāvalakkhaṇe vā. Tatthāti aññasmiṃ vihāre paccāgacchati, vaṭṭati, senāsanaggāho na paṭippassambhatīti adhippāyo.

'Here' means in the story of Upananda. 'How' means in what way does it subside. 'Here' means in the Dispensation. The connection is with 'a certain one takes'. 'Even there' means even in a nearby monastery. 'Of him' refers to the monk. 'Here' refers to the lodging. 'Merely an attachment' means merely the arising of a thought. 'Thus for him' means 'thus it is for him,' that is, the meaning is 'thus it is for that monk'. 'In all cases' refers to the entire fourfold group beginning with 'taking by taking'. The connection is with 'but one who goes'. 'When the boundary of the precincts is exceeded'—this is a locative expression in the sense of a sign, or it is a locative absolute. The intention is: 'there' means he returns to another monastery; it is allowable; the taking of the lodging does not subside.

320. Yoti bhikkhu. Mahantataro vā daharataro vāti attano mahantataro vā daharataro vā hoti. So bhikkhu tivassantaro nāmāti yojanā. Ekassa bhikkhuno tiṇṇaṃ vassānamantare ṭhito tivassantaro añño bhikkhu. Tatthāti bhikkhūsu. Ime sabbeti tivassantaradvivassantarasamānavassike ime bhikkhū, labhantīti sambandho. Yaṃ tiṇṇaṃ pahotīti mañcapīṭhavinimuttaṃ yaṃ āsanaṃ tiṇṇaṃ sukhaṃ nisīdituṃ pahoti, tathārūpe āsanepi dve dve hutvā nisīdituṃ labhantīti yojanā. Apisaddena mañcapīṭhāni apekkhati. Idaṃ pacchimadīghāsanaṃ. Anupasampannenāpīti pisaddo pageva upasampannenāti dasseti.

320. 'Who' means a monk. 'Older or younger' means one who is either older or younger than oneself. The construction is: that monk is called 'one with a three-year interval'. Another monk standing within an interval of three years from one monk is 'one with a three-year interval'. 'There' refers to among the monks. The connection is: 'all these' refers to these monks—those with three-year intervals, two-year intervals, or an equal number of rains-residences—'they obtain'. The construction is: 'which suffices for three' means a seat, other than a bed or a bench, on which three can sit comfortably; even on such a seat, they are permitted to sit two by two. By the word 'api' (even), beds and benches are referred to. This is the last long seat. 'Even by one not fully ordained'—the word 'pi' (even) shows that it is all the more so by one who is fully ordained.

Hatthikumbheti hatthisiropiṇḍe. Iminā hatthisaddena hatthikumbho gahito avayavūpacārena vā uttarapadalopena vāti dasseti. Hatthī viyāti hatthī, bhūmibhāgo, hatthimhi patiṭṭhito pādasaṅkhāto nakho imassāti hatthinakhako, pāsādo. Etaṃ “hatthinakhako”ti nāmaṃ evaṃkatassa pāsādassa nāmanti yojanā. “Suvaṇṇarajatādivicitrānī”ti padaṃ “kavāṭāni mañcapīṭhāni tālavaṇṭānī”ti sabbapadesu yojetabbaṃ. Yaṃkiñci cittakammakataṃ atthi, sabbaṃ vaṭṭatīti yojanā. Pāsādassa demāti sambandho. Pāṭekkanti pāsādato visuṃ. Paṭiggahitamevāti sabbaṃ paṭiggahitameva hoti. Gonakādīni aṭṭhārasa attharaṇāni paribhuñjitunti sambandho. Gihivikaṭanīhārenāti gihīhi visesena yathākāmaṃ kariyatīti gihivikaṭaṃ, gihisantakaṃ. “Gihivikaṭa”nti nīhāro abhinīhāro gihivikaṭanīhāro, tena. Labbhantīti nisīditumeva labbhanti. Tatrāpīti dhammāsanepi.

‘Elephant’s dome’ refers to the protuberance on an elephant’s head. By this word ‘hatthi’ (elephant), ‘hatthikumbha’ (elephant’s dome) is taken, either by synecdoche (part for the whole) or by ellipsis of the latter part of the compound; this is what is shown. ‘Like an elephant’ means an elephant, a portion of ground; ‘hatthinakhaka’ (elephant-nail) is a palace, so called because it has a nail, understood as a foot, established on an elephant. The construction is that this name ‘hatthinakhaka’ is the name of a palace constructed in this way. The phrase ‘adorned with gold, silver, etc.’ should be applied to all items: ‘doors, beds, benches, palm-leaf fans,’ etc. The construction is that whatever artistic work there is, all that is allowable. The connection is ‘we give of the palace’. ‘Separately’ means separate from the palace. ‘Everything is accepted’ means everything is indeed accepted. The connection is ‘the eighteen kinds of spreads, beginning with those made of goat hair, are to be used’. ‘By the householder’s vikata’ means that which is done especially by householders as they wish; hence, ‘gihivikaṭa’ is that which belongs to householders. ‘Gihivikaṭa’ is the handling, the special handling, the ‘gihivikaṭa-handling’; by that. ‘They are obtained’ means they are obtained just for sitting. ‘Even there’ refers even to the Dhamma seat.

Avissajjiyavatthukathā

The Account of Non-transferable Property

321. Etānīti [V 2.0131][M 0.0489] garubhaṇḍāni. Tatthāti rāsivasena pañcasu sarūpavasena pañcavīsatiyā garubhaṇḍesu. Āgantvā, ābhuso vā ramanti etthāti ārāmo. Tesaṃyevāti pupphārāmaphalārāmānameva. “Ṭhapitokāso”ti iminā vatthusaddassa bhūmibhedatthaṃ dasseti. Vasati ārāmo patiṭṭhahati etthāti ārāmavatthu. Tesu vāti ettha vāsaddena navabhūmibhāgato aññassa porāṇabhūmibhāgassapi ārāmavatthubhāvaṃ vikappeti. Visesena catuiriyāpathe harati pavatteti etthāti vihāro. Tassāti vihārassa. Catunnaṃ mañcānanti niddhāraṇatthe sāmivacanaṃ. Aññataro mañco nāmāti yojanā. Eseva nayo sesesupi. “Lohena katā kumbhī”ti iminā lohakumbhīti ettha majjhelopasamāsaṃ dasseti. Lohamayā kumbhī lohakumbhīti vacanatthopi yujjateva. “Eseva nayo”ti iminā lohena kataṃ bhāṇakaṃ, lohena kato vārako, lohena kataṃ kaṭāhanti atthaṃ atidisati. Etthāti bhāṇakavārakakaṭāhesu. Arañjaroti atimahantattā araṃ khippaṃ jarati vināsetīti arañjaro. Atha vā jalaṃ gaṇhituṃ alanti arañjaro lakārānaṃ rakāre katvā.

321. ‘These’ refers to heavy goods. ‘Therein’ means among the heavy goods, which are five by way of category and twenty-five by way of individual items. ‘Having come, they delight exceedingly here’—thus, a park (ārāma). ‘Theirs alone’ refers specifically to flower parks and fruit parks. By ‘space designated,’ the meaning of ‘vatthu’ (site) as a division of ground is shown. ‘A park dwells, is established here’—thus, a park site (ārāmavatthu). ‘Or among them’—here, by the word ‘vā’ (or), even an older portion of land is considered a park site, in addition to the nine divisions of land. ‘Especially conducts the four postures’—thus, a monastery (vihāra). ‘Its’ refers to the monastery. ‘Of four beds’ is a genitive term used in the sense of specification. The construction is: ‘A certain bed’. The same principle applies to the rest. By ‘a pot made of metal,’ the middle-term elision compound in ‘lohakumbhī’ (metal pot) is shown. The meaning ‘a pot made of metal is a metal pot’ is also valid. By ‘the same applies,’ the meaning is extended to ‘a vessel made of metal,’ ‘a bucket made of metal,’ and ‘a pan made of metal’. ‘Here’ refers to the vessel, bucket, and pan. ‘Arañjara’ (large water jar) is so called because, due to its very large size, it quickly deteriorates, quickly destroys, hence ‘arañjara’ (quick destroyer). Alternatively, it is called ‘arañjara’ because it is sufficient to hold water, with the ‘l’ sounds changed to ‘r’.

Gāthāvasena nigamanaṃ dassento āha “eva”ntiādi. Tattha evaṃ pakāsayīti sambandho. Dve garubhaṇḍāni dvisaṅgahāni honti, tatiyaṃ garubhaṇḍaṃ catusaṅgahaṃ hoti, catutthaṃ garubhaṇḍaṃ navakoṭṭhāsaṃ hoti, pañcamaṃ garubhaṇḍaṃ aṭṭhabhedanaṃ hoti, iti iminā pakārena pañcanimmalalocano nātho pañcahi rāsīhi pañcavīsavidhaṃ garubhaṇḍaṃ pakāsayīti yojanā.

Showing the conclusion by way of a verse, he said, ‘Thus,’ etc. Here, the connection is ‘thus he explained’. The construction is: Two heavy goods form two collections; the third heavy good forms four collections; the fourth heavy good forms nine sections; the fifth heavy good forms eight divisions. Thus, in this manner, the Protector with five stainless eyes explained the twenty-five kinds of heavy goods by means of five categories.

Tatrāti garubhaṇḍe. Hīti vitthāro. Sabbampi idaṃ garubhaṇḍaṃ avissajjiyanti vuttanti yojanā. Idhāti imasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ. Parivāre pana āgatanti sambandho.

‘Therein’ refers to heavy goods. ‘Hī’ (indeed) is for elaboration. The construction is: ‘All these heavy goods are said to be non-transferable’. ‘Here’ refers to this matter. The connection is: ‘but it is included in the Parivāra’.

Pañca rāsayo mahesinā vuttāti yojanā. Etthāti parivāre.

The construction is: ‘The five categories were stated by the Great Sage’. ‘Here’ refers to the Parivāra.

Tatrāti [M 0.0490] “parivattanavasenā”ti vacane. Idaṃ garubhaṇḍaṃ upanetunti sambandho. Niccaṃ tiṭṭhantīti thāvarā, ṭhādhātu varapaccayo, ṭhākārassa thākāro. Iminā ārāmaārāmavatthuvihāravihāravatthūni gahetabbāni. Avissajjiyaavebhaṅgīyattā garu alahukaṃ bhaṇḍaṃ garubhaṇḍaṃ. Iminā mañcādīni ekavīsati garubhaṇḍāni gahetabbāni. Thāvareti ādhāre bhummaṃ, pariyāpannanti sambandho. Atha vā niddhāraṇe bhummaṃ, thāvaresūti hi attho, khettantiādīsu sambandhitabbaṃ. Khipati [V 2.0132] pubbaṇṇabījametthāti khettaṃ. Vasati aparaṇṇabījaṃ patiṭṭhāti etthāti vatthu, tale bhūmibhāge ekato vā dvīhi vā tīhi vā ṭhānehi āvaraṇaṃ karīyati etthāti taḷāko, saro. Kassakānaṃ matena kattabbāti mātikā. Ārāmena parivattetunti sambandho. Kāni parivattetunti āha “imāni cattāripī”ti. Pisaddo avayavasampiṇḍano.

‘Therein’ refers to the phrase ‘by means of exchange’. The connection is: ‘This heavy article is to be brought forward’. ‘Always remaining’—thus, ‘thāvara’ (stable); the root is ‘ṭhā’ with the suffix ‘vara,’ and the ‘ṭhā’ sound becomes ‘tha’. By this, parks, park sites, monasteries, and monastery sites should be understood. Because it is not to be given away and not to be divided, it is weighty, a non-light article, hence a ‘heavy article’ (garubhaṇḍa). By this, twenty-one heavy articles such as beds and so forth should be understood. ‘On the stable ground’ is a locative case in the sense of location; the connection is ‘it is included’. Alternatively, it is a locative case in the sense of determination; indeed, the meaning is ‘among stable things’; it should be connected to terms like ‘field’ and so forth. ‘A field’ (khetta) is where the first crop seed is sown. ‘A site’ (vatthu) is where the later crop seed dwells and is established; ‘a pond’ (taḷāka) or ‘lake’ (sara) is where an enclosure is made in one, two, or three places on the surface of the ground. ‘Mātikā’ (water-course) is that which is to be made according to the judgment of the farmers. The connection is: ‘It is to be exchanged by the park’. ‘What is to be exchanged?’ He says, ‘These four also’. The particle ‘pi’ is for including components.

Tatrāti “parivattetuṃ vaṭṭatī”ti vacane. Dūreti saṅghārāmato dūraṭṭhāne. Yampīti nāḷikeraphalampi. Harantīti saṅghassa haranti. Aññesanti saṅghato aññesaṃ manussānanti sambandho. Teti manussā. Saṅghena sampaṭicchitabboti sambandho. Ruccatīti saṅghassārāmena manussānamārāmaṃ, manussānamārāmena vā saṅghassārāmaṃ parivattetuṃ rucīyati icchīyati. Bhikkhūnaṃ ārāmoti sambandho. Ayanti manussānamārāmo. Khuddakoti saṅghārāmato khuddako. Āyanti ayati āyasāmiko dhanena vaḍḍhiṃ gacchati anenāti āyo, taṃ. Samakamevāti samappamāṇameva, āyaṃ sace detīti sambandho. Pamāṇatthe kapaccayo. Manussānaṃ rukkhāti sambandho. Atirekaṃ saṅghassa demāti sambandho. Jānāpetvāti “saṅghe dinnaṃ mahapphala”nti (ma. ni. 3.376) saṅghassa dinnadānassa ānisaṃsaṃ manussānaṃ jānāpetvā. Phaladhārino honti nanūti yojanā. Evantiādi nigamanaṃ. Eteneva nayenāti yena nayena ārāmo ārāmena parivattetabbo, eteneva nayena. Mahantena vā khuddakena vā ārāmavatthunā cāti yojanā. Ārāma ārāmavatthuvihāravihāravatthūni parivattetabbānīti sambandho.

‘Therein’ refers to the phrase ‘it is allowable to exchange’. ‘Far away’ means in a distant place from the Sangha’s park. ‘Even what’ refers to even a coconut fruit. ‘They carry’ means they carry it for the Sangha. ‘To others’—the connection is ‘to people other than the Sangha’. ‘They’ refers to those people. The connection is: ‘It should be accepted by the Sangha’. ‘It is agreeable’ means it is pleasing or desired to exchange the Sangha’s park for the people’s park, or the people’s park for the Sangha’s park. The connection is: ‘the monks’ park’. ‘This’ refers to the people’s park. ‘Small’ means smaller than the Sangha’s park. ‘Profit’ (āya) is that through which an increase in wealth is attained. ‘Exactly equal’ means of the same measure; the connection is ‘if profit is given’. The suffix ‘-ka’ is in the sense of measure. The connection is: ‘the people’s tree’. The connection is: ‘we will give the excess to the Sangha’. ‘Having informed’ means having informed the people of the benefit of a gift given to the Sangha, saying, ‘A gift given to the Sangha is of great fruit’ (M.iii.376). The construction is: ‘They will surely be fruit-bearers’. ‘Thus’ and so on is the conclusion. ‘In the same way’ means by the same method by which a park should be exchanged for a park, by this same method. The construction is: ‘whether with a large or small park site’. The connection is: ‘A park, park site, monastery, or monastery site should be exchanged’.

Ubhopīti [M 0.0491] gehapāsādavasena ubhopi. Tatthāti gehe. Idaṃ panāti pāsādasaṅkhātaṃ gehaṃ, manussānaṃ gehanti sambandho. Mahagghena vā appagghena vā vihāravatthunā cāti yojanā. Vihāravihāravatthuārāmaārāmavatthūni parivattetabbānīti sambandho. Evantiādi nigamanaṃ.

‘Both’ refers to both a house and a palace, by way of house and palace. ‘Therein’ refers to the house. ‘This, however’ refers to a house designated as a palace; the connection is ‘the house of humans’. The construction is: ‘whether with a valuable or inexpensive monastery site’. The connection is: ‘A monastery, monastery site, park, or park site should be exchanged’. ‘Thus’ and so on is the conclusion.

Garubhaṇḍena garubhaṇḍaparivattane evaṃ vinicchayo veditabboti yojanā. Paṃsvāgārakesūti paṃsukīḷanatthāya katesu agārakesu. Kappiyamañcāti saṅghagaṇapuggalānaṃ kappiyā suvaṇṇarajatādīhi akatā mañcā. Vihārassa pana suvaṇṇarajatamayādikāpi kappiyā mañcā dātabbāti sambandho. Bahisīmāyāti upacārasīmato bahi. Tatthāti saṅghattherassa vasanaṭṭhāne. Tatthāti tassa bhikkhuno vasanaṭṭhāne. “Mahagghenā”ti vuttavacanaṃ niyamento āha “satagghanakena vā sahassagghanakena vā”ti. Mañcasatanti mañcabahuṃ. Etesupīti pīṭhabhisibibbohanesupi. Tatthāti pīṭhabhisibibbohanesu. Kappiyaṃ pīṭhādīti sambandho. Akappiyaṃ vā mahagghaṃ kappiyaṃ vāti kappiyena vā mahagghakappiyena vā parivattetvāti sambandho. “Vuttavatthūnī”ti [V 2.0133] padaṃ “parivattetvā”ti pade avuttakammaṃ, “gahetabbānī”ti pade vuttakammaṃ, pubbāparāpekkhapadaṃ.

Regarding the exchange of heavy goods with heavy goods, the decision should be understood in this way—this is the interpretation. 'Paṃsvāgārakesū' means in houses made for playing in the dust. 'Kappiyamañcā' means beds allowable for the Sangha, for groups, or for individuals, not made of gold, silver, and so on. However, for a monastery, beds made even of gold, silver, and so on, may be given—this is the connection. 'Bahisīmāya' means outside the boundary of the precinct. 'Tattha' refers to the dwelling place of the Sangha's elder. 'Tattha' refers to the dwelling place of that monk. The phrase 'Mahagghena' is qualified by saying, 'with something worth a hundred or a thousand.' 'Mañcasata' means many beds. 'Etesupi' means even in these: stools, cushions, and pillows. 'Tattha' refers to stools, cushions, and pillows. The connection is 'Kappiyaṃ pīṭhādī' (allowable stools, etc.). The connection is with 'Akappiyaṃ vā mahagghaṃ kappiyaṃ vā' (an impermissible item, or a valuable permissible item), meaning having exchanged it for something permissible or for something permissible of great value. The word 'Vuttavatthūni' is an unstated object of the word 'parivattetvā,' while it is a stated object of the word 'gahetabbāni'; it is a word that refers to both the preceding and succeeding context.

Pasatamattaudakagaṇhakānipīti ettha pasato nāma kuñcitapāṇi. Sīhaḷadīpeti sīhaṃ lāti gaṇhātīti sīhaḷo lakārassa ḷakāraṃ katvā, sīhabāhunāmako rājā, tassa puttattā vijayakumāropi sīhaḷo nāma, tena ādimhi nivāsabhāvena gahitattā dīpo sīhaḷadīpo nāma, tasmiṃ. Pādaṃ gaṇhātīti pādagaṇhano, soyeva pādagaṇhanako. Pādo nāmāti “pādagaṇhanako”ti ettha pādo nāma. Yo lohavārako magadhanāḷiyā pañcanāḷimattaṃ gaṇhāti, so lohavārako pādo nāmāti yojanā. Iminā pamāṇassa nāmaṃ pamāṇavante upacārato vohāranayaṃ dasseti. Tatoti pañcanāḷimattagaṇhanakavārakato. Imānīti lohakumbhīādīni.

'Pasatamattaudakagaṇhakānipi': here, 'pasata' means a cupped hand. 'Sīhaḷadīpe': Sīhaḷa is one who seizes a lion (sīhaṃ lāti), with 'la' changed to 'ḷa'; the king was named Sīhabāhu, and because he was his son, Prince Vijaya was also named Sīhaḷa, and because the island was first taken by him as a dwelling place, the island is named Sīhaḷadīpa; 'tasmiṃ' means therein. 'Pādaṃ gaṇhāti' means one who takes a quarter, hence 'pādagaṇhano'; this itself is 'pādagaṇhanako'. 'Pādo nāma': here, in the word 'pādagaṇhanako,' 'pādo' means this: the iron measure that holds five nāḷis by the Magadhan nāḷi measure, that iron measure is called a 'pādo'—this is the interpretation. By this is shown the principle of conventional usage, whereby the name of a measure is applied metaphorically to that which has the measure. 'Tato' means from that measure which holds five nāḷis. 'Imāni' means iron pots and so on.

Bhiṅgāra [M 0.0492] …pe… kaṭacchuādīnīti bhiṅgāro ca paṭiggaho ca uḷuṅko ca dabbi ca kaṭacchu ca pāti ca taṭṭako ca sarako ca samuggo ca aṅgārakapallo ca dhūmakaṭacchu ca bhiṅgāra…pe… dhūmakaṭacchuyo, tā ādi yesaṃ tānīti bhiṅgāra…pe… kaṭacchuādīni. Ādisaddena aññāni upakaraṇāni gahetabbāni. Bhājanīyānīti bhājetabbāni. Kaṃsalohādītiādisaddena vaṭṭalohaṃ saṅgaṇhāti. Vaṭṭalohaṃ nāma pītalohaṃ. Hīti saccaṃ, yasmā vā. Pārihāriyanti saṅghikaparibhogaṃ pariharitvā apanetvā puggalikaparibhogena paribhuñjanaṃ, “attasantaka”nti vā pariggahena haritvā bhuñjanaṃ na vaṭṭati. Gihivikaṭanīhārenevāti “gihivikaṭa”nti abhinīhāreneva.

'Bhiṅgāra…pe… kaṭacchuādīni': this means the ewer, the receptacle, the cup, the spoon, the ladle, the bowl, the plate, the saucer, the casket, the coal pan, and the incense ladle—these are the ewers…up to…the incense ladles. Those things of which these are the beginning are 'bhiṅgāra…pe… kaṭacchuādīni'. By the word 'ādi' (etc.), other implements should be understood. 'Bhājanīyāni' means they are to be divided. 'Kaṃsalohādi': by the word 'ādi' (etc.), brass is included. Brass is known as yellow metal. 'Hī' means truly, or because. 'Pārihāriyaṃ' means, having set aside and removed an item from the Sangha's use, to use it for personal enjoyment; or it is not allowable to take it with the claim that it is one's own property and use it. 'Gihivikaṭanīhāreneva' means simply with the intention of 'gihivikaṭa' (improper disposal as if by a householder).

Aññasmimpi kappiyalohabhaṇḍe pariyāpannā añjanīti yojanā. Atha vā kappiyalohabhaṇḍeti niddhāraṇe bhummaṃ, “añjanī”tiādinā sambandhitabbaṃ. Sūcīti cīvarādisibbanakā sūci. Paṇṇasūcīti paṇṇe likhanā sūci. Aññampīti añjaniādito aññampi. Dhūmanettañca phālañca dīparukkho ca dīpakapallako ca olambakadīpo ca dhūmanetta…pe… olambakadīpā. Itthipurisatiracchānagatasaṅkhātāni rūpāni etesu atthīti itthipurisatiracchānagatarūpakāni. Dhūmanetta…pe… olambakadīpā ca te itthipurisatiracchānagatarūpakāni ceti dhūmanetta…pe… rūpakāni, visesanaparanipāto. Tāni vā aññāni vā bhitticchadanakavāṭādīsu upanetabbāni lohabhaṇḍānīti sambandho. Lohakhilakanti lohamayaṃ āṇiṃ. Pariharitvāti “attano santaka”nti pariggahena haritvā, saṅghikaparibhogagihivikaṭāni vā apanetvā. Khīrapāsāṇamayānīti khīravaṇṇena pāsāṇena katāni.

The interpretation is that an ointment pot is included even among other allowable metal items. Alternatively, 'kappiyalohabhaṇḍe' is a locative of specification, to be connected with 'añjanī,' etc. 'Sūcī' means a needle for sewing robes and so on. 'Paṇṇasūcī' means a stylus for writing on leaves. 'Aññampi' means other items besides the ointment pot and so on. A fumigation tube, a ploughshare, a lamp-tree, a small lamp-stand, and a hanging lamp—these are the fumigation tube…up to…the hanging lamps. Because forms designated as female, male, or animal exist in these, they are called 'itthipurisatiracchānagatarūpakāni' (having forms of females, males, or animals). 'Dhūmanetta…pe… olambakadīpā ca te itthipurisatiracchānagatarūpakāni ca' becomes 'dhūmanetta…pe… rūpakāni'; this is a case of the adjective being placed after the noun. The connection is that those or other metal items are to be applied to walls, roofs, doors, and so on. 'Lohakhilakaṃ' means a metal pin. 'Pariharitvā' means having taken it with the claim that it is one's own property, or having removed it from the Sangha's use or from improper disposal by householders. 'Khīrapāsāṇamayāni' means made of stone the color of milk.

Suvaṇṇañca [V 2.0134] rajatañca hārakūṭañca jātiphalikañca suvaṇṇa…pe… jātiphalikāni, tehi katāni bhājanāni suvaṇṇa…pe… bhājanāni. Sabbanti suvaṇṇarajatādisabbaṃ. Vaṭṭatīti saṅghagaṇapuggalānaṃ vaṭṭati.

Gold, silver, hārakūṭa gold, and genuine crystal—these are gold…up to…genuine crystals. Vessels made from them are 'suvaṇṇa…pe… bhājanāni' (vessels of gold, etc.). 'Sabbaṃ' means all such things as gold, silver, and so on. 'Vaṭṭati' means it is allowable for the Sangha, for a group, and for an individual.

Vāsiādīsu [M 0.0493] evaṃ vinicchayo veditabboti yojanā, niddhāraṇe vā bhummaṃ. Yāya vāsiyā na sakkāti sambandho. Tatoti vāsito. Mahattarīsaddo mahantapariyāyo anipphannapāṭipadiko. Mahattarī vāsīti sambandho. Vejjānanti bhisakkānaṃ. Sirāvedhanapharasupīti pisaddena tato mahantaṃ pana pagevāti dasseti. Yā pana kuṭhārī āvudhasaṅkhepena katāti sambandho. Atha vā āvudhasaṅkhepena katā yā pana kuṭhārī atthīti yojanā. Anāmāsāti anāmasitabbā, anāmāsārahāti attho. Caturaṅgulamattopīti pisaddo tato adhiko pana pagevāti dasseti. Nikhaṇitvā khādatīti nikhādanaṃ. Caturassaṃ mukhametassāti caturassamukhaṃ. Doṇisadisaṃ mukhametassāti doṇimukhaṃ. Sammuñcanidaṇḍavedhanampi nikhādanaṃ daṇḍabaddhaṃ hoti ceti yojanā. Daṇḍena bandhitabbanti daṇḍabaddhaṃ, daṇḍaṃ baddhametassāti vā daṇḍabaddhaṃ. “Adaṇḍaka”nti vatvā tassevatthaṃ dassetuṃ vuttaṃ “phalamattamevā”ti. Natthi daṇḍametassāti adaṇḍakaṃ. Yanti nikhādanaṃ. Pariharitunti puggalikabhāvena pariggahetvā harituṃ, saṅghikabhāvaṃ apanetuṃ vā. Sikharampi nikhādaneneva saṅgahitaṃ lakkhaṇahāranayena samānakiccabhāvato. Sikharanti yena paribbhamitvā chindanti, yehi manussehi dinnānīti sambandho. Teti manussā, vadantīti sambandho. Noti amhākaṃ. Pākatiketi pakatiyā ṭhite, yathā paṭhamaṃ ṭhitā honti, tathā karissāmāti attho. Sace āharantīti sace āyācanaṃ akatvā haranti. Anāharantāpīti puna anāharantāpi.

Regarding axes and so on, the decision should be understood in this way—this is the interpretation; or this is a locative of specification. The connection is: with which axe it is not possible. 'Tato' means from the axe. The word 'mahattarī' is a synonym for 'mahanta' (large), and it is an underived nominal stem. The connection is 'mahattarī vāsī' (a large axe). 'Vejjānaṃ' means of physicians. 'Sirāvedhanapharasupi': by the word 'pi' (even), it is shown that something larger than that is certainly meant. The connection is: the axe that is made in the form of a weapon. Alternatively, the interpretation is: there is an axe that is made in the form of a weapon. 'Anāmāsā' means not to be touched; the meaning is, not fit to be touched. 'Caturaṅgulamattopi': by the word 'pi' (even), it is shown that something larger than that is certainly meant. 'Nikhādanaṃ' is that which digs and bites. 'Caturassamukhaṃ' is that which has a four-cornered mouth. 'Doṇimukhaṃ' is that which has a mouth like a trough. The interpretation is: even a tool for boring a hole in a broomstick is a 'nikhādana' if it is attached to a handle. 'Daṇḍabaddhaṃ' means it is to be bound with a handle, or it has a handle bound to it. Having said 'adaṇḍakaṃ' (without a handle), to explain its meaning, it is said: 'merely the blade.' 'Adaṇḍakaṃ' means it has no handle. 'Yaṃ' refers to the digging tool. 'Pariharituṃ' means to take away by claiming it as personal property, or to remove it from the Sangha's ownership. 'Sikhara' is also included under 'nikhādana' by the interpretive method based on characteristics, because it has the same function. 'Sikhara' is that with which one cuts by swinging it around. The connection is: which were given by people. 'Te' means those people; the connection is with 'vadanti' (they say). 'No' means of us. 'Pākatike' means in their natural state; the meaning is: we will make them as they were at first. 'Sace āharanti' means if they take them without asking. 'Anāharantāpi' means even if they do not bring them back.

Kammāro ca taṭṭakāro ca cundakāro ca naḷakāro ca maṇikāro ca pattabandhako ca kammāra…pe… pattabandhakā, tesaṃ. Adhikaraṇī ca muṭṭhiko ca saṇḍāso ca tulā ca adhikaraṇi…pe… tulā. Saṅghe dinnakālatoti saṅghassa dinnakālato. Tipuṃ chindati anenāti tipucchedanaṃ, tameva satthakaṃ tipucchedanasatthakaṃ. Mahākattariñca mahāsaṇḍāsañca [M 0.0494] mahāpipphilikañca ṭhapetvāti yojanā. Kasmā ṭhapitānīti āha “mahākattariādīni garubhaṇḍānī”ti. Tattha yasmā mahākattariādīni garubhaṇḍāni, tasmā “ṭhapetvā mahākattari”nti ādi mayā vuttanti yojanā.

The blacksmith, the coppersmith, the turner, the reed-worker, the jeweler, and the bowl-mender—these are the blacksmith…up to…the bowl-menders; of them. The anvil, the hammer, the tongs, and the balance—these are the anvil…up to…the balance. 'Saṅghe dinnakālato' means from the time they were given to the Sangha. 'Tipucchedanaṃ' is that by which one cuts tin; that very knife is a 'tipucchedanasatthakaṃ' (tin-cutting knife). The interpretation is: excluding the large scissors, the large tongs, and the large pincers. Why are these excluded? It is said: 'The large scissors, etc., are heavy goods.' The interpretation is: therein, because the large scissors, etc., are heavy goods, therefore 'excluding the large scissors,' etc., was said by me.

Valliādīsu [V 2.0135] evaṃ vinicchayo veditabboti yojanā. Vettavalliādikāti vettasaṅkhātavalliādikā. Aḍḍhabahuppamāṇāti ettha –

Regarding creepers and so on, the decision should be understood in this way—this is the interpretation. 'Vettavalliādikā' means creepers known as cane, and so on. 'Aḍḍhabāhuppamāṇā' (of half an arm's length in measure): here—

“Byāmo sahakarā bāhu, dvepassadvayavitthatā”ti. –

A fathom is the arms with the hands, extended on both sides.

Abhidhāne (abhidhānappadīpikāyaṃ 269 gāthāyaṃ) vuttattā bāhu nāma idha byāmova adhippeto. Tasmā dvīsu passesu vitthatānaṃ byāmasaṅkhātānaṃ sahakarānaṃ dvinnaṃ bāhūnaṃ aḍḍhoti aḍḍhabāhu, tassa pamāṇametassāti aḍḍhabāhuppamāṇāti vacanattho kātabbo, dīghato dvihatthā vallīti vuttaṃ hoti. Tatthajātakāti tissaṃ saṅghassa bhūmiyaṃ jātakā. Rakkhitagopitāti saṅghena sayaṃ rakkhitā, parehi gopitā. Iminā arakkhitaagopitā garubhaṇḍaṃ na hotīti dasseti. Sāti valli. Atirekā hotīti sambandho. Upanetunti taṃ valliṃ upanetuṃ. Suttañca makacivākañca nāḷikerahīrañca cammañca sutta…pe… cammāni, tehi katā sutta…pe… cammamayā. Rajjukā vā yottāni vā garubhaṇḍaṃ hotīti sambandho. Ekavaṭṭā vā dvivaṭṭā vāti ettha vāsaddena tivaṭṭādiṃ saṅgaṇhāti. Avaṭṭetvā dinnaṃ suttañca avaṭṭetvā dinnā makacivākanāḷikerahīrā cāti yojanā.

Since it is stated in the lexicon (in the Abhidhānappadīpikā, verse 269), the term 'bāhu' (arm) here is intended to mean 'byāma' (fathom). Therefore, 'aḍḍhabāhu' (half-arm) is half of the two arms with hands, known as a fathom, extended on two sides. The meaning of the word 'aḍḍhabāhuppamāṇā' (of half-arm measure) should be understood as 'having that as its measure.' This means that the creeper is two cubits long. 'Tatthajātakā' (growing there) means growing on the Sangha's ground. 'Rakkhitagopitā' (protected and guarded) means protected by the Sangha itself and guarded by others. By this, it shows that what is unprotected and unguarded is not a heavy article. 'Sā' (that) refers to the creeper. The connection is: it is in excess. 'Upanetuṃ' (to bring) means to bring that creeper. Thread, makacivāka, coconut fiber, and leather—these are thread… up to… leather items. Those made from them are thread-made… up to… leather-made. The connection is that cords or straps are heavy articles. 'Ekavaṭṭā vā dvivaṭṭā vā' (one-twisted or two-twisted): here, by the word 'vā' (or), three-twists, etc., are included. The interpretation is: thread given without twisting, and makacivāka and coconut fiber given without twisting.

Yo koci veḷūti sambandho. Sopīti veḷupi vaṭṭatīti sambandho. Pisaddena valliṃ apekkhati. Idametthāti idaṃ sabbaṃ ettha veḷumhi, veḷūsu vā idanti sambandho. Samakaṃ vāti gahitaveḷunā samappamāṇaṃ vā. Atirekaṃ vāti tato atirekaṃ vā. Taṃagghanakanti tassa veḷuno agghanārahaṃ. Phātikammanti vaḍḍhikammaṃ. Tatthevāti gaṇhanaṭṭhāneva. Gamanakāleti gaṇhanaṭṭhānato aññattha gamanakāle. “Pahiṇitvā dātabbo”ti iminā sayaṃ vā āgantvā dātabboti atthopi lakkhaṇahāranayena gahetabbo samānakiccattā.

The connection is with 'Yo koci veḷu' (Whatever bamboo). The connection is: 'so pi' (that too) means 'bamboo is also permissible.' By the word 'pi' (also), it refers to the creeper. The connection is: 'idam ettha' (this here) means 'all this is here in this bamboo, or in these bamboos.' 'Samakaṃ vā' (or equal) means 'or of equal measure to the bamboo taken.' 'Atirekaṃ vā' (or more) means 'or more than that.' 'Taṃagghanakaṃ' (worth that much) means 'worth the price of that bamboo.' 'Phātikammaṃ' means 'work of increase.' 'Tattheva' (right there) means 'right at the place of taking.' 'Gamanakāle' (at the time of going) means 'at the time of going elsewhere from the place of taking.' By 'it should be given after sending,' the meaning 'it should be given by coming oneself' is also to be understood by the method of implication, due to the similarity of function.

Muñjapabbajasaddena [M 0.0495] muñjapabbajatiṇānaṃ pāḷiyaṃ visuṃ gahitattā tiṇasaddena tāni ṭhapetvā pārisesañāyena avasesatiṇameva gahetabbanti dassento āha “muñjaṃ pabbajañca ṭhapetvā”tiādi. Samānaphalattā lakkhaṇahāranayena paṇṇampi tiṇeneva saṅgahitanti dassento āha “yatthā”tiādi. Tattha yatthāti yasmiṃ ṭhāne, itīti evaṃ. Tiṇañca garubhaṇḍaṃ hotīti sambandho. Tatthajātakaṃ vāti tasmiṃ saṅghārāme jātakaṃ vā. Bahārāmeti saṅghārāmato bahi. Tampīti tiṇampi. Pisaddena valliveḷū apekkhati. Aṭṭhaṅgulappamāṇopīti dīghato aṭṭhaṅgulapamāṇopi[V 2.0136]. Rittapotthakoti alikhitattā tuccho makacivatthādikopi paṇṇamayopi potthako. Idañca paṇṇapasaṅgena vuttaṃ.

Since the muñja and pabbaja grasses are taken separately in the Pāli by the term 'muñjapabbaja,' he shows by stating 'excluding muñja and pabbaja,' etc., that by the term 'grass,' only the remaining grass should be taken, by the principle of residue. He shows by stating 'yatthā,' etc., that because they have the same result, leaves are also included under grass by the method of implication. Therein, 'yatthā' means 'in which place,' and 'iti' means 'thus.' The connection is that grass is also a heavy article. 'Tatthajātakaṃ vā' (or grown there) means 'or grown in that monastery.' 'Bahārāme' (outside the monastery) means 'outside the monastery.' 'Tampi' (that too) means 'grass too.' By the word 'pi,' it refers to creepers and bamboo. 'Aṭṭhaṅgulappamāṇopi' (even of eight finger-breadths' measure) means 'even if it measures eight finger-breadths in length.' 'Rittapotthako' (an empty book) means a blank book, such as one of unwritten cloth etc. or one made of leaves, because it is unwritten. And this is stated in connection with leaves.

Pañcavaṇṇā vāti nīlapītalohitodātamañjiṭṭhavasena pañcavaṇṇanā vā. Tampīti mattikampi. Pisaddena valliveḷutiṇāni apekkhati.

'Pañcavaṇṇā vā' (or of five colors) means 'or of five colors, namely blue, yellow, red, white, and madder.' 'Tampi' (that too) means 'clay too.' By the word 'pi,' it refers to creepers, bamboo, and grass.

Dārubhaṇḍe evaṃ vinicchayo veditabboti yojanā. Rakkhitagopito yo koci dārubhaṇḍako atthīti yojanā. Mahāaṭṭhakathāyaṃ pana vuttoti sambandho.

The construction is that the decision regarding wooden articles should be understood thus. The construction is that 'whatever wooden article there is that is protected and guarded...'. The connection is that it is stated in the Great Commentary.

Tatrāti mahāaṭṭhakathāyaṃ, “tena kho pana samayenā”ti pāḷiyaṃ vā. Imesūti āsandikādīsu. Etthāti pīṭhesu, palālapīṭhenāti sambandho. Byagghacammaonaddhanti byagghacammena avanaddhaṃ. Vāḷarūpaparikkhittanti vāḷarūpehi parivāritaṃ. Ratanaparisibbitanti ratanasuttena samantato sibbitaṃ.

'Tatra' (there) means 'in the Great Commentary,' or in the Pāli at 'tena kho pana samayena...' (at that time...). 'Imesu' (among these) means 'among chairs, etc.' 'Ettha' (here) means 'among seats'; the connection is with 'palālapīṭhena' (with a straw seat). 'Byagghacammaonaddhaṃ' (covered with tiger skin) means 'covered with tiger skin.' 'Vāḷarūpaparikkhittaṃ' (surrounded by beast-figures) means 'surrounded by beast-figures.' 'Ratanaparisibbitaṃ' (stitched around with jewels) means 'stitched all around with jewel-thread.'

Etesupīti vaṅkaphalakādīsupi. “Saṅkhathālakaṃ pana bhājanīya”nti pāṭhassānantaraṃ “tathā”ti pāṭho atthi, so ettha na yujjati, parato pana “yena kenaci kataṃ garubhaṇḍamevā”ti pāṭhassānantaraṃ yujjati. Tattha hi yathā yena kenaci kataṃ garubhaṇḍameva hoti, tathā thambhatulāsopānaphalakādīsu dārumayaṃ vā pāsāṇamayaṃ vā yaṃkiñci gehasambhārarūpaṃ garubhaṇḍamevāti attho.

'Etesupi' (among these too) means 'among curved planks, etc., too.' After the reading 'Saṅkhathālakaṃ pana bhājanīyaṃ' (But a conch-shell vessel is a distributable item), there is the reading 'tathā' (thus), but it is not appropriate here. However, it is appropriate later on, after the reading 'yena kenaci kataṃ garubhaṇḍamevā' (made by anyone whatsoever, it is indeed a heavy article). For there the meaning is: just as whatever is made by anyone whatsoever is a heavy article, so too, in the case of pillars, beams, stairs, planks, etc., any kind of household requisite, whether made of wood or stone, is indeed a heavy article.

Sabbanti sakalaṃ udakatumbapādakathalikamaṇḍalaṃ. Etesupīti ādhārakādīsupi. Tathā thambhatalāti ettha tathāsaddena ‘garubhaṇḍamevā”ti [M 0.0496] padaṃ atidisati. Saṅghe dinnanti saṅghassa dinnaṃ. Bhūmattharaṇanti bhūmiyaṃ attharitabbaṃ. Tampīti eḷakacammampi.

'Sabbaṃ' (all) means 'the entire set of water-gourd, foot-stool, and circular mat.' 'Etesupi' (among these too) means 'among supports, etc., too.' In 'tathā thambhatalā' (likewise, pillar bases), the word 'tathā' (likewise) applies by extension the phrase 'garubhaṇḍamevā' (is indeed a heavy article). 'Saṅghe dinnaṃ' (given to the Saṅgha) means 'given for the Saṅgha.' 'Bhūmattharaṇaṃ' (ground-covering) means 'what is to be spread on the ground.' 'Tampi' (that too) means 'ram's skin too.'

Udukkhalaṃ garubhaṇḍamevāti sambandho. Eseva nayo musalantiādīsupi. Etesūti mañcapādādīsu. Anuññātavāsiyāti bhājanatthāya anuññātavāsiyā. Dhamakaraṇoti ettha “saṅkhaṃ dhamati, saṅkhadhamako”tiādīsu viya nissaṃyogapāṭhoyeva yujjati. Tasmā dhamati vātena pavattatīti dhamo, vātahetuko saddo, dhamaṃ karotīti dhamakaraṇoti vacanattho kātabbo. Sabbametanti anuññātavāsidaṇḍādikaṃ etaṃ sabbaṃ. Tatoti anuññātavāsidaṇḍādikato, mahantataraṃ vāsidaṇḍādikaṃ garubhaṇḍanti yojanā.

The connection is: 'A mortar is indeed a heavy article.' This same principle applies to 'pestle,' etc., too. 'Etesu' (among these) means 'among bed-legs, etc.' 'Anuññātavāsiyā' (with a permitted adze) means 'with an adze permitted for the purpose of bowls.' Here, in 'dhamakaraṇa' (bellows), the reading as a compound is appropriate, as in phrases like 'saṅkhaṃ dhamati, saṅkhadhamako' (he blows the conch, a conch-blower), etc. Therefore, the meaning of the word should be constructed thus: 'dhamo' is that which proceeds by wind, a sound caused by wind; 'dhamakaraṇa' is that which makes that 'dhama.' 'Sabbametaṃ' (all this) means 'all this, such as the handle of a permitted adze, etc.' 'Tato' (than that) means 'than the handle of a permitted adze, etc.'; the construction is that a larger adze handle, etc., is a heavy article.

Yathājātamevāti [V 2.0137] yathāpavattameva. Tehīti hatthidantādīhi, “kata”iti padena sambandhitabbaṃ. Tacchitaniṭṭhitopīti tacchitakammena niṭṭhitopi.

'Yathājātameva' (just as it has come to be) means 'in its natural state.' 'Tehi' (by these) means 'by ivory, etc.'; it should be connected with the word 'kata' (made). 'Tacchitaniṭṭhitopi' (even if finished by shaping) means 'even if finished by the work of shaping.'

Mattikābhaṇḍe evaṃ vinicchayo veditabboti yojanā, upabhogo ca paribhogo ca upabhogaparibhogaṃ, samāhāradvando. Idaṃ padaṃ “ghaṭapidhānādikulālabhājana”nti padeneva sambandhitabbaṃ. Thupikātīti ettha itisaddo imasaddattho. Idaṃ sabbaṃ saṅghassa dinnakālato paṭṭhāya garubhaṇḍanti yojanā. “Anatirittapamāṇo”ti visesanapadaṃ “ghaṭako”ti visesyapadeneva sambandhitabbaṃ. Etthāti mattikābhaṇḍe, ādhāre vā niddhāraṇe vā ttha paccayo. Mattikābhaṇḍe kuṇḍikā bhājanīyakoṭṭhāsaṃ bhajati, evaṃ lohabhaṇḍepīti yojanā. Etthāti garubhaṇḍavinicchaye.

The construction is: 'Regarding earthenware, the decision should be understood thus.' 'Upabhogaparibhogaṃ' is a collective compound (samāhāradvanda) of 'upabhogo ca paribhogo ca' (use and enjoyment). This word should be connected with the phrase 'ghaṭapidhānādikulālabhājanaṃ' (potter's vessels such as pots, lids, etc.). Here, in 'thupikāti,' the word 'iti' has the meaning of the word 'ima' (this). The construction is: 'All this is a heavy article from the time it is given to the Saṅgha.' The adjective 'anatirittapamāṇo' (not exceeding the measure) should be connected with the noun 'ghaṭako' (a small pot). 'Ettha' (here) means 'in earthenware'; the suffix '-ttha' is used for location or for specification. The construction is: 'Among earthenware, a water pot falls into the category of distributable items; the same applies to metalware too.' 'Ettha' (here) means 'in the decision regarding heavy articles.'

Navakammadānakathā

The Discourse on Giving for New Works

323. Bhaṇḍikāṭṭhapanamattenāti ettha bhaṇḍikāṭṭhapanaṃ nāma bhaṇḍikayojananti āha “kapotabhaṇḍikayojanamattenā”ti. Assāti bhikkhussa. Citakadhūmoti citake uṭṭhito dhūmo. Etassevāti bhikkhussa [M 0.0497] eva vihāroti sambandho. Dhūmakāleti dhūmassa uṭṭhitakāle. “Apaloketvā”ti iminā dhūmakāle apalokitaṃ dhūmakālikaṃ. Dhūmakālikaṃ hutvāti atthayojanaṃ katvā pāḷiyaṃ “pariyositavihāra”nti padena sambandhitabbabhāvaṃ dasseti. Katapariyositavihāranti katapariyosito vihāro imassa navakammassāti katapariyositavihāraṃ. Idaṃ navakammaṃ dentīti sambandho. Yāva gopānasiyo na ārohanti, tāva vippakato nāmāti yojanā. Tatoti gopānasiārohanato. Kañcideva samādapetvā kāressatīti vihārasāmikoyeva kañci bhikkhuṃsamādapetvā kāressati. Pañcahatthe vihāreti sambandho. Chavassikaṃ navakammanti sambandho. Etthāti aḍḍhayoge. Soti aḍḍhayogo. Mahallakaṃ niyāmetvā dassento āha “dasahatthe ekādasahatthe”ti. Dasavassikaṃ vā ekādasavassikaṃ vā navakammanti sambandho. Tatoti dvādasahatthato. Lohapāsādasadisepi pāsādeti sambandho. Tatoti dvādasavassikanavakammato.

323. Regarding 'merely by placing a shelf': here, 'placing a shelf' means assembling a shelf; thus, it is said, 'by merely assembling a pigeon-hole shelf.' 'Of him' (assāti) means of a monk. 'Smoke from a pyre' (citakadhūmoti) is smoke that has risen from a pyre. 'Of this very one' (etassevāti) is connected thus: 'the dwelling of this very monk.' 'At the time of smoke' (dhūmakāleti) means at the time of the smoke's rising. By this 'after informing' (apaloketvāti), what is informed at the time of smoke becomes valid for the time of smoke (dhūmakālikaṃ). Having become valid for the time of smoke, by explaining the meaning, it shows that in the Pāli text it should be connected with the word pariyositavihāra (a completed dwelling). 'A dwelling whose completion is done' (katapariyositavihāranti) means a dwelling whose completion is done for this new work; thus, katapariyositavihāraṃ. 'They give this new work'—this is the connection. 'As long as the rafters are not raised, it is called unfinished'—this is the construction. 'From that' (tatoti) means from the raising of the rafters. 'Having encouraged someone, he will have it done' means the owner of the dwelling himself, having encouraged some monk, will have it done. 'In a five-cubit dwelling'—this is the connection. 'New work for six years'—this is the connection. 'Here' (etthāti) means in the case of a half-hipped roof. 'That' (soti) refers to the half-hipped roof. Indicating what is larger, he says: 'ten cubits, eleven cubits.' 'New work for ten years or eleven years'—this is the connection. 'From that' (tatoti) means from twelve cubits. 'Even in a palace like the Lohapāsāda'—this is the connection. 'From that' (tatoti) means from new work of twelve years.

Navakammikoti navakamme yuttapayutto. Utukāleti hemantagimhakāle. Paṭibāhitunti aññesaṃ sampattabhikkhūnaṃ paṭisedhetuṃ. Āvāsasāmikassāti āvāsadāyakassa. Tassāti āvāsasāmikassa. Vaṃseti anvaye. Teti tava. Soti āvāsasāmiādiko. Bhikkhūhi jaggitabboti [V 2.0138] sambandho. Tepīti ñātiupaṭṭhākāpi. Tasmimpīti saṅghikapaccayepi. Bahū āvāseti sambandho. Ekaṃ āvāsanti yojanā.

'One undertaking new construction' (navakammikoti) means one engaged and employed in new construction. 'At the proper season' (utukāleti) means during the winter and summer seasons. 'To obstruct' (paṭibāhitunti) means to prevent other monks who have arrived. 'Of the owner of the residence' (āvāsasāmikassāti) means of the donor of the residence. 'Of him' (tassāti) means of the owner of the residence. 'In the lineage' (vaṃseti) means in the lineage. 'Te'ti means 'your'. 'So'ti means the owner of the residence, and so on. 'Should be looked after by the monks'—this is the connection. 'They too' (tepīti) means relatives and attendants too. 'In that too' (tasmimpīti) means even in requisites belonging to the Saṅgha. 'Many residences'—this is the connection. 'One residence'—this is the construction.

Ekaṃ vā āvāsanti sambandho. Tatoti visajjitāvāsehi, uppannānīti sambandho. Kurundiyaṃ pana vuttaṃ, kinti vuttanti yojanā. Ekaṃ mañcaṭṭhānaṃ gahetvāti ekaṃ mañcaṭṭhānaṃ puggalikabhāvena gahetvā. Tibhāganti tatiyabhāgaṃ. Ayameva vā pāṭho. Etthāti naṭṭhavihāre. Puggalikamevāti puggalikaṃ eva, puggalikaṃ iva vā. Jaggāti jaggāhi. Hīti [M 0.0498] phalajotako. Evaṃ jaggito panāti evaṃ jaggito vihāro pana. Tasminti jaggante. Saddhivihārikādīnaṃ dātukāmo hotīti saṅghassa bhaṇḍaṭṭhapanaṃ vā navakānaṃ vasanaṭṭhānaṃ vā adatvā attanoyeva saddhivihārikādīnaṃ dātukāmo hoti. Saddhivihārikādīnaṃ dātuṃ labbhatīti sabbavihāraṃ puggalikabhāvena aggahetvā ekadesasseva gahitattā saddhivihārikādīnaṃ dātuṃ labbhatīti attho. Jaggāpetabbo iti vuttanti yojanā. Ettha “vutta”nti pāṭho atthi, so apāṭhoyeva “kurundiyaṃ pana vutta”nti padassa ākārattā.

'Or one residence' (ekaṃ vā āvāsanti)—this is the connection. 'From that' (tatoti) means from abandoned residences; 'arisen' is the connection. 'But in the Kurundī it is said'—how is it said?—this is the construction. 'Having taken one bed-place' means having taken one bed-place as personal property. 'A third part' (tibhāganti) means the third part. Or this is the reading itself. 'Here' (etthāti) means in a ruined dwelling. 'As personal' (puggalikamevāti) means 'personal indeed' or 'like personal'. 'Jaggā'ti means 'you should guard'. 'Hi'ti is an indicator of the result. 'But thus guarded' (evaṃ jaggito panāti) means 'but the dwelling thus guarded'. 'In that' (tasminti) means 'while guarding'. 'He wishes to give to his co-residents, etc.' means that without giving a storage place for the Saṅgha's goods or a dwelling place for new monks, he wishes to give only to his own co-residents and so on. 'It is permissible to give to one's co-residents, etc.'—the meaning is that because he has not taken the entire dwelling as personal property but has taken only a part of it, it is permissible to give to his co-residents and so on. 'It should be caused to be guarded, thus it is said'—this is the construction. Here, there is the reading 'vuttaṃ', but it is not a correct reading because of the form of the phrase 'kurundiyaṃ pana vuttaṃ'.

Aññaṃ idampi ca vakkhamānavacanaṃ tattheva kurundiyaṃ vuttanti yojanā. Kinti vuttanti āha “dve bhikkhū”tiādi. Dve bhikkhū karontīti sambandho. Yenāti bhikkhunā. Soyeva sāmīti yena sā bhūmi paṭhamaṃ gahitā, soyeva sāmīti attho. Patirūpe ṭhāneti patirūpe senāsanaṭṭhāne. Tanti puggalikakaraṇaṃ. Yaṃ pana vayakammanti yojanā. Ettha ca vayakammanti tasmiṃ vihāre katassa kammassa mūlaṃ. Vihārassa mūlaṃ dātabbanti vuttaṃ hoti. Tassāti saṅghikaṃ karontassa. Tatthevāti katavihāre eva. Katāvāseti samīpatthe bhummavacanaṃ, katāvāsasamīpeti vuttaṃ hoti. Chāyūpagaphalūpagāti chāyaṃ upagacchantā ca phalaṃ upagacchantā ca, chāyāphalāni upaharantāti attho. Apaloketvāti saṅghaṃ apaloketvā. Sāmikāti rukkhasāmikā. Hāretabbāti apanetabbā.

This other statement that will be spoken is also said in that very Kurundī—this is the construction. How is it said? He says, 'two monks,' and so on. 'Two monks are making'—this is the connection. 'By whom' (yenāti) means by the monk. 'He himself is the owner' (soyeva sāmīti)—the meaning is that he by whom that land was first taken, he himself is the owner. 'In a suitable place' (patirūpe ṭhāneti) means in a suitable lodging place. 'That' (tanti) means the making of it as personal property. 'But whatever is the work of expenditure'—this is the construction. And here, 'work of expenditure' means the capital for the work done in that dwelling. It is said that the capital for the dwelling should be given. 'Of him' (tassāti) means of the one who is making it belong to the Saṅgha. 'In that very place' (tatthevāti) means in the dwelling that has been made. 'In the made residence' (katāvāseti) is a locative expressing proximity; it means 'near the made residence'. 'Approaching for shade, approaching for fruit' (chāyūpagaphalūpagāti) means those who approach the shade and those who approach the fruit; the meaning is they bring shade and fruit. 'Having informed' (apaloketvāti) means having informed the Saṅgha. 'Owners' (sāmikāti) means the owners of the trees. 'Should be removed' (hāretabbāti) means should be taken away.

“Saṅghikavallimattampi aggahetvā”ti iminā saṅghikaṃ gahetvā saṅghikāya bhūmiyā sace vihāraṃ karoti, saṅghikamevāti dasseti. Dvibhūmakatibhūmakādīsu pāsādesu upaḍḍhabhāgaṃ dassento āha “pāsādo ceva hotī”tiādi. Upari pāsādoti sambandho. Soti vihārakārako bhikkhu, tassa heṭṭhāpāsādoti sambandho. Vihāreti saṅghikavihāre, vihārasamīpeti attho. Akataṭṭhāneti cayapamukhānaṃ akatapubbaṭṭhāne. Cayaṃ vā pamukhaṃ vāti saṅghikavihārassa cayaṃ vā pamukhaṃ vā. Bahikuṭṭeti kuṭṭassa, kuṭṭato vā bahi. Tassāti cayapamukhakārakassa bhikkhussa hotīti [V 2.0139] sambandho[M 0.0499]. Visamaṃ pabbatakandarādinti sambandho. Apadeti sukarassa akāraṇe. Kataṃ hotīti cayaṃ vā pamukhaṃ vā kataṃ hoti. Tatthāti cayapamukhesu, saṅgho anissaro iti vuttanti yojanā.

By this 'not taking even the measure of a creeper belonging to the Saṅgha', it shows that if one builds a dwelling on land belonging to the Saṅgha after taking what belongs to the Saṅgha, it becomes the Saṅgha's property indeed. In the case of palaces with two stories, three stories, and so on, showing the half-share, he says: 'it is a palace,' and so on. 'The upper palace'—this is the connection. 'He' (soti) is the monk who is the maker of the dwelling; 'the lower palace is his'—this is the connection. 'In the dwelling' (vihāreti) means in the Saṅgha's dwelling; the meaning is 'near the dwelling'. 'In a place not made' (akataṭṭhāneti) means in a place where a caya or pamukha has not been made before. 'A caya or a pamukha' means a caya or a pamukha of the Saṅgha's dwelling. 'Outside the wall' (bahikuṭṭeti) means outside of the wall, or outside from the wall. 'It is his' (tassāti) means it belongs to the monk who made the caya or pamukha—this is the connection. 'Uneven, like a mountain cave, etc.'—this is the connection. 'Apade'ti means when there is no reason for it to be easy. 'It is made' means the caya or the pamukha is made. 'There' (tatthāti) means in the cayas and pamukhas; 'the Saṅgha is not the owner, thus it is said'—this is the construction.

Varaseyyaṃ gahetunti sambandho.

To take the best lodging—this is the connection.

Puna āgantvāti pakkamitvā puna āgantvā. Tassāti navakammagāhakassa bhikkhussa. Etanti senāsanaṃ.

'Having come again' (puna āgantvāti) means having departed and having come again. 'Of him' (tassāti) means of the monk who has taken up the new work. 'This' (etanti) means the lodging.

Aññatraparibhogapaṭikkhepādikathā

The Discussion on the Prohibition of Use Elsewhere, and so forth

324. Nātiharantīti ettha atisaddo haraṇattho, harasaddo paribhuñjanatthoti āha “aññatra haritvā na paribhuñjantī”ti. Yaṃ mañcapīṭhādīti yojanā. Tatthāti undriyamahāvihāre. Tanti mañcapīṭhādiṃ. Tasmāti yasmā anujānāti, tasmā. Tanti mañcapīṭhādiṃ. Aññatrāti aññaṃ vihāraṃ. Aroganti anaṭṭhājiṇṇattā arogaṃ. Tasmiṃ vihāreti undriyavihāre. Tasminti undriyavihāre. Tatoti undriyavihārato. Suyojitānīti suṭṭhu yojitāni. Mūladānaṃ vā paṭipākatikaṃ vā natthīti adhippāyo. Chaḍḍitavihāratoti bhikkhūhi anapekkhena chaḍḍitasaṅghikavihārato ca puggalena sāpekkhena chaḍḍitapuggalikavihārato ca. Āvāsikakāleti āvāsikānaṃ ṭhitakāle. Tatoti chaḍḍitavihārato.

324. Regarding 'they do not carry away' (nātiharantīti): here, the prefix ati- has the meaning of 'carrying away', and the root har- has the meaning of 'using'; thus, it is said, 'having carried elsewhere, they do not use.' 'Whatever beds, chairs, etc.'—this is the construction. 'There' (tatthāti) means in the Undriya Mahāvihāra. 'That' (tanti) means beds, chairs, etc. 'Therefore' (tasmāti) means 'because he permits, therefore'. 'That' (tanti) means beds, chairs, etc. 'Elsewhere' (aññatrāti) means another dwelling. 'Sound' (aroganti) means sound because of not being ruined or worn out. 'In that dwelling' (tasmiṃ vihāreti) means in the Undriya dwelling. 'In that' (tasminti) means in the Undriya dwelling. 'From that' (tatoti) means from the Undriya dwelling. 'Well-fitted' (suyojitānīti) means properly fitted. The intention is that there is no original donation or subsequent restoration. 'From an abandoned dwelling' (chaḍḍitavihāratoti) means from a Saṅgha dwelling abandoned by monks without attachment, and from a personal dwelling abandoned by an individual with attachment. 'At the time of residents' (āvāsikakāleti) means at the time when residents are staying. 'From that' (tatoti) means from the abandoned dwelling.

Phātikammatthāyāti ettha phātisaddo vaḍḍhanatthoti āha “vaḍḍhikammatthāyā”ti. Etthāti “phātikammatthāyā”ti pāṭhe.

Regarding 'for the purpose of growth' (phātikammatthāyāti): here, the word phāti has the meaning of 'increase'; thus, it is said, 'for the purpose of increasing' (vaḍḍhikammatthāyāti). 'Here' (etthāti) means in the reading 'phātikammatthāya'.

Cakkalikanti cakkākārena lāti pavattati, cakkākāraṃ vā lāti gaṇhātīti cakkalaṃ, tadeva cakkalikaṃ, pādapuñjanaṃ, “kambalādīhi veṭhetvā kata”nti iminā tassa karaṇākāraṃ dasseti. Yehīti pādehi[M 0.0500]. Udakanti senāsanassa tintakaṃ udakaṃ. Udakaṃ na paññāyatīti yojanā. Saupāhanena akkamituṃ na vaṭṭatīti yojanā.

Regarding cakkalikaṃ: it proceeds taking the shape of a wheel, or it takes the shape of a wheel, thus it is cakkalaṃ; that very thing is cakkalikaṃ, a foot-wiper. By this 'made by wrapping with blankets, etc.', he shows the manner of its making. 'By which' (yehīti) means by the feet. 'Water' (udakanti) means water that wets the lodging. 'Water is not perceived'—this is the construction. 'It is not proper to tread on it with sandals'—this is the construction.

Sudhābhūmiyanti sudhāya littāyaṃ bhūmiyaṃ. Paribhaṇḍabhūmiyanti gomayakasāvaparibhaṇḍabhūmiyaṃ. Pādāti mañcapādā. Tasminti coḷake. Ṭhapentassāti mañcapāde ṭhapentassa. Tatthāti tesu bhikkhūsu[V 2.0140]. Nevāsikāti nibaddhaṃ vasantīti nevāsikā. Ṭhapentīti mañcapāde ṭhapenti. Tathevāti yathā nevāsikā vaḷañjanti, tatheva āgantukehi vaḷañjituṃ vaṭṭatīti attho.

'On a ground smeared with plaster' (sudhābhūmiyaṃ) means on a ground smeared with plaster. 'On a ground covered with refuse' (paribhaṇḍabhūmiyaṃ) means on a ground covered with cow dung and chaff. 'Feet' (pādā) means the legs of a bed. 'In that' (tasmiṃ) means in that rag. 'For one placing' (ṭhapentassa) means for one placing the legs of the bed. 'There' (tatthā) means among those monks. 'Resident monks' (nevāsikā) means those who dwell permanently, thus resident monks. 'They place' (ṭhapenti) means they place the legs of the bed. 'Similarly' (tatheva) means that just as resident monks use it, so too is it proper for visiting monks to use it—this is the meaning.

Setabhitti vāti ettha vāsaddena nīlabhittiādayo sampiṇḍeti. “Dvārampi vātapānampī”tiādinā sāmaññato vuttattā dvāravātapānādayo aparikammakatāpi na apassayitabbā. Kenaci vā vatthādināti sambandho.

'Or a white wall' (setabhitti vā): here, by the word 'or' (vā), blue walls and so forth are included. Since it is stated generally by 'a door or a window, etc.' (dvārampi vātapānampītiādinā), doors, windows, and the like, even if unfinished, should not be leaned against. The connection is 'or by any cloth, etc.' (kenaci vā vatthādinā).

“Hutvā”ti iminā “dhotapādakā”ti padassa “nipajjitu”nti pade kiriyāvisesanabhāvaṃ dasseti, “bhikkhū”ti pade kārakavisesanabhāvaṃ nivatteti. Kasmiṃ ṭhāne nipajjituṃ kukkuccāyantīti āha “dhotehi pādehi akkamitabbaṭṭhāne”ti. “Akkamitabbaṭṭhānassetaṃ adhivacana”nti iminā “dhotapādake”ti pāṭhassa dhoto pādo tiṭṭhati ettha ṭhāneti dhotapādakaṃ, tasmiṃ dhotapādaketi atthaṃ dasseti. Etanti “dhotapādake”ti nāmaṃ. “Paccattharitvā”ti ettha kena paccattharitvāti āha “paccattharaṇenā”ti. “Attano santakenā”ti iminā saṅghikena paccattharaṇena paccattharaṇaṃ paṭikkhipati. Niddāyatopīti niddāyakāraṇāpi, saṃkuṭiteti sambandho. Atha vā niddāyatopīti niddāyantassapi. “Sarīrāvayavo”ti pade sāmyatthachaṭṭhī, “āpattiyevā”ti pade sampadānaṃ. Lomesu phusantesūti sambandho. “Paribhogasīsenā”ti iminā paribhogaṃ akatvā kenaci kammena sarīrāvayavena phusantassa anāpattīti dasseti. Hatthatalena phusituṃ pādatalena phusituṃ vā akkamituṃ vāti yathālābhayojanā daṭṭhabbā. “Paribhogasīsenā”ti padassa atthaṃ dassento āha “mañcapīṭhaṃ nīharantassā”tiādi.

By 'having been' (hutvā), he shows that the word 'with washed feet' (dhotapādakā) is an adverbial qualifier for the verb 'to lie down' (nipajjituṃ), and he negates its being an agentive qualifier for the word 'monks' (bhikkhū). 'In what place do they hesitate to lie down?'—he says: 'on the place that should be stepped on with washed feet'. By 'this is a term for the place to be stepped on' (akkamitabbaṭṭhānassetaṃ adhivacanaṃ), he shows the meaning of the reading 'dhotapādake' as 'dhotapādakaṃ' (a place where a washed foot stands), and 'in that dhotapādaka' (tasmiṃ dhotapādake). 'This' (etaṃ) is the name 'dhotapādake'. 'Having spread' (paccattharitvā): Here, he explains 'with what is it spread?' by saying 'with a spread' (paccattharaṇena). By 'with one’s own belongings' (attano santakena), he prohibits spreading with a communal spread. 'Even while sleeping' (niddāyatopi): The connection is 'even due to the cause of sleeping, one tosses about'. Alternatively, 'even while sleeping' means even for one who is sleeping. In the word 'a limb of the body' (sarīrāvayavo), the sixth case is for possession; in the word 'only an offense' (āpattiyevā), it is the dative case. The connection is 'when touching the hairs'. By 'by way of use' (paribhogasīsena), he shows that there is no offense for one touching a limb of the body by some action without making use of it. 'To touch with the palm of the hand, to touch with the sole of the foot, or to step'—these constructions should be understood as appropriate. Explaining the meaning of the word 'by way of use' (paribhogasīsena), he says 'for one removing a bed or bench,' etc.

Saṅghabhattādianujānanakathā

Discussion on the Permitting of Sangha Meals and so forth

325. “Saṅghassa [M 0.0501] bhatta”nti iminā saṅghabhattanti padassa chaṭṭhīsamāsaṃ dasseti. Saṅghassa atthāya ābhataṃ bhattaṃ kātuṃ na sakkontīti yojanā. Uddesabhattantiādīsu evamattho veditabboti yojanā. “Uddesena laddhabhikkhūnaṃ bhattaṃ kātu”nti iminā uddesena laddhabhikkhūnaṃ kātabbaṃ bhattaṃ uddesabhattanti vacanatthaṃ dasseti. Tathevāti yathā saṅghato uddisitvā laddhabhikkhū, tatheva. Paricchinditvāti “ekaṃ vā”tiādinā paricchinditvā. Tesanti laddhabhikkhūnaṃ. Iminā nimantetvā laddhabhikkhūnaṃ kātabbaṃ bhattaṃ nimantanabhattanti vacanatthaṃ dasseti. “Salākāyo chinditvā”ti iminā salākāyo chinditvā kātabbaṃ bhattaṃ salākabhattanti vacanatthaṃ [V 2.0141] dasseti. Pakkhikanti uposathikanti pāṭipadikanti evaṃ niyāmetvāti yojanā. Pañcamīādīsu pakkhesu kātabbaṃ pakkhikaṃ. Uposathe kātabbaṃ uposathikaṃ. Pāṭipade kātabbaṃ pāṭipadikaṃ, tameva bhattaṃ pāṭipadikabhattaṃ. Uddesabhattaṃ nimantananti ettha itisaddo ādyattho, uddesabhattaṃ nimantanantiādiṃ imaṃ vohāraṃ pattānīti hi attho. Uddesabhattādīniyeva anujānanamakatvā kasmā saṅghabhattampi anujānātīti āha “yasmā panā”tiādi. Tattha yasmā sakkhissantīti sambandho. Teti manussā. Tampīti saṅghabhattampi. Pisaddena uddesabhattādīni apekkhati.

325. By 'meal for the Sangha' (saṅghassa bhattaṃ), he shows that 'saṅghabhatta' is a sixth-case compound. The construction is that they are unable to prepare a meal brought for the benefit of the Sangha. The construction is that the meaning should be understood thus in 'uddesabhatta,' etc. By 'to prepare a meal for monks obtained by designation' (uddesena laddhabhikkhūnaṃ bhattaṃ kātuṃ), he shows the meaning of the word 'uddesabhatta' as a meal to be prepared for monks obtained by designation. 'Just as' (tatheva) means just as monks are obtained by designation from the Sangha, so too. 'Having specified' (paricchinditvā) means having specified by 'one or,' etc. 'For them' (tesaṃ) means for the designated monks. By this, he shows the meaning of the word 'nimantanabhatta' as a meal to be prepared for monks obtained by invitation. By 'having drawn lots' (salākāyo chinditvā), he shows the meaning of the word 'salākabhatta' as a meal to be prepared after drawing lots. The construction is 'having determined thus: fortnightly, Uposatha, Pāṭipada'. What is to be prepared on the fortnights, such as on the fifth day and so on, is 'fortnightly' (pakkhikaṃ). What is to be prepared on the Uposatha is 'an Uposatha meal' (uposathikaṃ). What is to be prepared on the Pāṭipada is 'a Pāṭipada meal' (pāṭipadikaṃ); that very meal is 'pāṭipadikabhatta'. In 'uddesabhattaṃ nimantanaṃ', the word iti has the meaning of 'and so forth'. Indeed, the meaning is that this usage, beginning with 'uddesabhatta, nimantanabhatta,' etc., is attained. Why does he permit Sangha meals as well, without having permitted only uddesabhatta, etc.? He says: 'But because,' etc. Here, the connection is 'because they will be able'. 'They' (te) means the people. 'That too' (tampi) means Sangha meals as well. The particle pi refers back to uddesabhatta, etc.

Saṅghabhattādīnaṃ vitthāraṃ dassento āha “tatthā”tiādi. Tattha tatthāti “saṅghabhattaṃ uddesabhatta”ntiādipāṭhe, evaṃ vinicchayo veditabboti yojanā, saṅghabhattādīsu vā niddhāraṇe bhummaṃ, bhuñjantānaṃ amhākaṃ ajja dasa dvādasa divasā ahesunti yojanā. Aññatoti aññasmā ṭhānā. Tatthāti saṅghabhatte. Vattabbāti manussā vattabbā. Tanti saṅghabhattaṃ, dhātukammaṃ, “amhāka”nti kāritakammaṃ. Tanti saṅghabhattaṃ.

Explaining the details of Sangha meals, etc., he says: 'There,' etc. 'There, there' (tattha tattha): The construction is that the determination should be understood thus in the reading 'Sangha meal, uddesabhatta,' etc. Or, the locative case is for specification among Sangha meals, etc. The construction is that those eating thought: 'For us today, it has been ten or twelve days'. 'From elsewhere' (aññato) means from another place. 'There' (tattha) means in the Sangha meal. 'To be spoken' (vattabbā) means people are to be spoken to. 'That' (taṃ) means the Sangha meal, the relic ceremony, and 'for us' (amhākaṃ) is the causative object. 'That' (taṃ) means the Sangha meal.

Uddesabhattakathā

The Account of the Meal by Designation

Ayaṃ nayo evaṃ veditabboti yojanā. Raññā vā pahiteti sambandho. Sace atthīti sace ṭhitikā atthi. Uddesakenāti bhattuddesakena[M 0.0502]. Na atikkāmetabbanti uddesabhattaṃ na atikkāmetabbaṃ. Te panāti piṇḍapātikā pana. Ṭhitikaṃ ṭhapetvāti ṭhitikaṃ ṭhitaṭṭhāne ṭhapetvā muñcitvāti attho. Tesanti mahātherānaṃ. Yojanantarikavihāratopīti yojanena byavadhāne ṭhitavihāratopi. Ṭhitaṭṭhānatoti ṭhitikāya ṭhitaṭṭhānato. Asampattānampīti bhattuddesaṭṭhānaṃ asampattānampi. Vaḍḍhitā nāma sīmāti upacārasīmā vaḍḍhitā nāma. Saṅghanavakassa dinnepīti yāva dutiyabhāgo na dātabbo, tāva saṅghanavakassa dinnepi. Vassaggenāti gaṇiyatīti gaṃ, vassameva gaṃ vassaggaṃ, tena vassaggena, vassagaṇanāyāti vuttaṃ hoti. Yadi “vassagghenā”ti catutthakkharena pāṭho bhaveyya, evaṃ sati vassaparicchedenāti attho daṭṭhabbo, ayameva yuttataro.

This is the method to be understood thus—this is the explanation. 'Sent by the king'—this is the connection. 'If there is'—means if a fixed arrangement exists. 'By the one who assigns'—means by the meal assigner. 'Should not be exceeded'—means the meal by designation should not be exceeded. 'But those'—means the alms-goers. 'Having established the fixed arrangement'—means having established the fixed arrangement in its place, having released it. 'To them'—means to the senior monks. 'Even from a dwelling a yojana distant'—means even from a dwelling situated at a distance of a yojana. 'From the established place'—means from the established place of the fixed arrangement. 'Even for those who have not arrived'—means even for those who have not arrived at the meal-assigning place. 'An extended boundary is called'—means the proximity boundary is called extended. 'Even if given to the newest monk of the Sangha'—means until the second portion is given, even if given to the newest monk of the Sangha. 'By the rains-reckoning': 'gaṃ' means 'is counted'; 'vassaggaṃ' is 'rains-reckoning' itself; by that rains-reckoning, it is said to be by the counting of rains. If the reading were 'vassagghena' with the fourth syllable, then the meaning should be understood as 'by the limit of the rains'; this is more appropriate.

Ekasmiṃ vihāreti ekissaṃ vihārasīmāyaṃ. Tasmiṃyeva bhattuddesaṭṭhāneti ettha evasaddena aññasmiṃ ṭhāne gāhaṇaṃ paṭikkhipati. Ekoti eko dāyako. Tenāti pahitabhikkhunā. So atthoti so hetu. Taṃdivasanti tasmiṃ pahitadivase. Pamussatīti satipavāsena mussati. Bhojanasālāyāti bhattuddesaṭṭhānasaṅkhātāya bhojanasālāya. Yā pakatiṭṭhitikāti yojanā. “Ekābaddhā [V 2.0142] hontī”ti vuttavacanassa atthaṃ dassento āha “aññamaññaṃ dvādasahatthantaraṃ avijahitvā”ti. Navaṃ ṭhitikanti bhattuddesaṭṭhāne ṭhapitapakatiṭṭhitikato aññaṃ navaṃ ṭhitikaṃ. Hīti saccaṃ, yasmā vā. Etanti uddesabhattaṃ. “Sve”ti niyāmetvā vuttattā dutiyadivase na labbhati.

'In one monastery'—means within the boundary of one monastery. 'In that very meal-assigning place'—here, by the word 'very,' the taking in another place is rejected. 'One'—means one donor. 'By him'—means by the sent monk. 'That reason'—means that cause. 'On that day'—means on the day he was sent. 'Forgets'—means forgets due to loss of mindfulness. 'In the dining hall'—means in the dining hall, known as the meal-assigning place. 'Which is the customary arrangement'—this is the explanation. 'They are bound together'—explaining the meaning of this statement, he says, 'without being more than twelve hands apart from each other.' 'A new arrangement'—means a new arrangement other than the customary arrangement established at the meal-assigning place. 'Indeed'—means truly, or because. 'This'—means the meal by designation. 'Tomorrow'—since it is said with a specification, it is not obtainable on the second day.

Kocīti dāyako. Sakavihāre ṭhītikāvaseneva gāhetabbanti yaṃ vihāraṃ gacchanti, tattha apaviṭṭhattā sakavihāre ṭhitikāvaseneva gāhetabbaṃ. Dinnaṃ pana bhattaṃ gāhetabbanti sambandho. Sampattānanti dinnaṭṭhānaṃ sampattānaṃ. Tatthāti dinnaṭṭhānaṃ, sampattānaṃyevāti sambandho. Tassa vihārassāti paviṭṭhavihārassa. Tasmiṃ tasmiṃ ṭhāneti gāmadvāravīthicatukkasaṅkhāte tasmiṃ tasmiṃ ṭhāne. Antoupacāragatānanti ettha antoupacāro nāma dvādasahatthabbhantaraṃ.

'Koci' means the donor. 'It should be taken only by the established custom of one's own monastery' means: because they go to a certain monastery but have not entered it, it should be taken only by the established custom of their own monastery. 'But the given meal should be taken'—this is the connection. 'For those who have arrived' means for those who have arrived at the place where it is given. 'There' means at the place where it is given; 'only for those who have arrived'—this is the connection. 'Of that monastery' means of the monastery that has been entered. 'In such and such a place' means in such and such a place, reckoned as the village gate, street, or crossroads. 'Having gone within the inner proximity' means: here, 'inner proximity' is the name for the area within twelve cubits.

Gāmadvārūpacāra [M 0.0503] vīthicatukkūpacāra gharūpacāresu tīsu gharūpacārassa visesaṃ dassento āha “gharūpacāro cetthā”tiādi. Etthāti tīsu upacāresu. Gharūpacāro veditabboti sambandho. Eko upacāro etthāti ekūpacāraṃ gharaṃ. Imesanti catunnaṃ gharānaṃ. Tatthāti catūsu gharesu. Ekakulassa yaṃ gharanti sambandho. Ekavaḷañjanti ekadvārena samānaparibhogaṃ. Tatthāti ekūpacāre.

Showing the distinction of the house proximity among the three proximities—the village gate proximity, the street crossroads proximity, and the house proximity—he says, 'Here, the house proximity,' and so on. 'Here' means among the three proximities. 'The house proximity should be understood'—this is the connection. 'A house with one proximity here' means a single-proximity house. 'Of these' means of the four houses. 'There' means in the four houses. 'The house of a single family'—this is the connection. 'Of single use' means having shared use through one door. 'There' means in a single proximity.

Yaṃ pana ekaṃ gharaṃ katanti sambandho. Sukhavihāratthāyāti kalahaṃ vicchinditvā sukhavihāratthāya. Tasmiṃ tasmiṃ ṭhāneti bhittiyā paricchinne tasmiṃ tasmiṃ ṭhāne.

But 'which one house was made'—this is the connection. 'For the purpose of dwelling comfortably' means for the purpose of dwelling comfortably, having cut off strife. 'In each and every place' means in each and every place demarcated by a wall.

Yasmiṃ pana ghare nisīdāpentīti sambandho. Yampi nivesananti yojanā.

Moreover, 'in whichever house they seat them'—this is the connection. And 'which dwelling'—this is the explanation.

Yo pana uddesalābho uppajjati, so pāpuṇātīti yojanā. Kiñcāpi dissanti, tathāpīti yojanā.

Whatever stipulated gain arises, one obtains it—this is the explanation. 'Even if they are seen, still'—this is the explanation.

Yo panāti bhikkhu pana, labhatīti sambandho. Aññasminti attanā aññasmiṃ. Tenāti uddesabhattaṃ labhantena bhikkhunā.

'Now, whoever' means the monk; 'obtains'—this is the connection. 'In another' means by oneself in another place. 'By that' means by a monk obtaining a stipulated meal.

Kālaṃ paṭimānentesūti bhojanakālaṃ paṭimānentesu bhikkhūsu, nisinnesūti sambandho. Koci [V 2.0143] manusso vadatīti sambandho. Saṅghuddesapattaṃ detha iti vāti yojanā. “Eseva nayo”ti iminā pattassa ṭhāne bhikkhuṃ pakkhipitvā vutte atidisati.

'When they are waiting for the time' means while monks are seated, waiting for mealtime—this is the connection. 'A certain person says'—this is the connection. 'Or, “Give the bowl designated for the Sangha”'—this is the explanation. 'This is the same method'—by this, he applies the rule by extension when it is stated with a monk substituted in place of the bowl.

Etthāti uddesabhatte, evaṃvacane vā. Pesaloti piyasīlo. Tenāti uddesakena. Kinti jānātīti āha “dasavassena laddha”nti. Tassāti uddesakassa, vacananti sambandho. Appasaddāti saṇikasaddā. “Apasaddā”tipi pāṭho, nissaddāti attho. Sabbanavakassāti sabbesaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ navakassa. Chāyāyapi pucchiyamānāyāti anādare bhummavacanaṃ, sāmivacanaṃ vā. Na labhatīti pāpuṇāpitattā na labhati. Nisinnassāpi niddāyantassāpīti anādare sāmivacanaṃ, bhikkhussa nisinnassāpi niddāyantassāpīti attho. Hīti saccaṃ. Etaṃ bhājanīyabhaṇḍaṃ [M 0.0504] nāmāti yojanā. Tatthāti “sampattasseva pāpuṇātī”ti vacane. Upacārenāti dvādasahatthūpacārena. Tasminti antoparikkhepe.

'Here' means in the stipulated meal, or in such a statement. 'Amiable' means of pleasant conduct. 'By that' means by the assigner. 'How does he know?'—he says, 'obtained after ten years.' 'His' means of the assigner; 'statement'—this is the connection. 'Of faint sound' means a quiet sound. 'Apasaddā' is also a reading, meaning 'soundless.' 'To the most junior of all' means to the most junior of all the monks. 'Even when the shadow is being asked about' is a locative of disregard, or a genitive. 'He does not obtain' means because it has not been delivered to him, he does not obtain. 'Even of one seated and dozing' is a genitive of disregard, meaning 'even of a monk who is seated and dozing.' 'Hi' means truly. 'This is called an item for distribution'—this is the explanation. 'There' means in the statement, 'it reaches only one who has arrived.' 'By proximity' means by a twelve-cubit proximity. 'In that' means within the inner enclosure.

Koci upāsako pahiṇātīti sambandho. Paṇītabhojanānanti paṇītabhojanehi. Udakassāti udakena, pūretvāti sambandho. Āgatā manussāti sambandho. Yenāti bhikkhunā. Yanti vatthu. Ticīvaraparivāranti ticīvarena parivāritaṃ, ticīvaraparivāravantaṃ vā uddesabhattanti attho. Hi saccaṃ assa bhikkhussa puññaviseso īdisoti yojanā. Nanu udakaṃpissa puññavisesaṃ, kasmā aññaṃ uddesabhattaṃ labhatīti āha “udakaṃ panā”tiādi.

'A certain lay follower sends'—this is the connection. 'Of excellent foods' means with excellent foods. 'Of water' means with water; 'having filled'—this is the connection. 'The people who have come'—this is the connection. 'By whom' means by the monk. 'What' means the object. 'Accompanied by the three robes' means surrounded by the three robes, or the stipulated meal possessing the accompaniment of the three robes—this is the meaning. 'Indeed, this monk's special merit is of such a kind'—this is the explanation. 'Is not the water also his special merit? Why does he receive another stipulated meal?'—thus he says, 'But water...' and so on.

Gahetvā āgatā te manussāti yojanā. Tesanti mahātherādīnaṃ. Daharasāmaṇerehīti daharehi sāmaṇerehi, laddhesūti sambandho.

'Those people came, having taken it'—this is the explanation. 'Of them' means of the great elders and so on. 'By the young novices' means by young novices; 'when it was obtained'—this is the connection.

Tatthāti uddesabhatte. Puratoti mahātherānaṃ purato. Patteti saṅghuddesapatte, agāhiteyevāti sambandho. Āhaṭampi uddesabhattanti sambandho.

'There' means in the stipulated meal. 'In front' means in front of the senior monks. 'In the bowl' means in the Sangha's designated bowl; 'while it is still untaken'—this is the connection. 'Even what is brought is a stipulated meal'—this is the connection.

Eko vadatīti sambandho. Soti manusso, bhaṇatīti sambandho. Yathā te ruccati, tathā vatvā āharāti yojanā. Vissaṭṭhadūto nāmāti attano ruciṃ vissajjitvā tassa ruciyā vissaṭṭho dūto nāma. Paṭipāṭipattaṃ vāti saṅghato paṭipāṭiyā laddhaṃ pattaṃ vā, idaṃ nimantanabhattaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ. Yaṃ icchatīti vissaṭṭhadūto yaṃ icchati. Soti bālo, na vattabboti sambandho. Pucchāsabhāgena vadeyyāti sambandho. Tatoti vadanakāraṇā.

'One speaks'—this is the connection. 'He' means that person; 'says'—this is the connection. 'Having spoken as it pleases you, bring it'—this is the explanation. An 'authorized messenger' is the name for a messenger who is dispatched according to that person's preference, having set aside his own preference. Or 'a bowl received in turn' means a bowl received in sequence from the Sangha; this is said with reference to an invitation meal. 'Whatever he desires' means whatever the authorized messenger desires. 'He' means a fool; 'should not be spoken to'—this is the connection. 'He should speak in a way that is partly a question'—this is the connection. 'From that' means for the reason of speaking.

Kūṭaṭṭhitikā [V 2.0144] nāmāti aññehi uddesabhattehi missetvā ujukaṭṭhitikāya pavattitvā kūṭena pavattā ṭhitikā nāma hoti. Tamevatthaṃ vitthārento āha “rañño vā hī”tiādi. Ekacārikabhattānīti pati ekaṃ katvā caritabbāni bhakkhitabbānīti ekacārikāni, aññehi uddesabhattehi amissetvā pati ekaṃ katvā bhakkhitabbānīti vuttaṃ [M 0.0505] hoti, tāniyeva bhattāni ekacārikabhattāni. Ekacce bhikkhū gatāti sambandho. Tesūti ekaccesu bhikkhūsu. Taṅkhaṇaṃyevāti tasmiṃ nisinnakkhaṇeyeva. Puna taṅkhaṇaṃyevāti tasmiṃ gāhaṇakkhaṇeyeva. “Paṇītabhatta”nti vutte “kativassato paṭṭhāyā”ti vadanti, “ettakavassato nāmā”ti vutteti yojanā. Gāhiteti ṭhitikaṃ ajānantehi āgantukehi patte gāhite. Āgatehipi ṭhitikaṃ jānanakabhikkhūhīti sambandho. Eseva nayo paratopi. Bhikkhūyeva āgacchantūti pattaṃ aggahetvā bhikkhūyeva āgacchantūti adhippāyo.

A 'deceitful arrangement' is the name for an arrangement that, having been mixed with other stipulated meals and having proceeded as a straightforward arrangement, then proceeds deceitfully. Elaborating on this very meaning, he says, 'For the king, indeed...' and so on. 'Meals for a single wanderer' means they are for a single wanderer because they are to be partaken of and eaten one by one; it is said that they are to be eaten one by one without being mixed with other stipulated meals; those very meals are meals for a single wanderer. 'Some monks went'—this is the connection. 'Among them' means among some monks. 'At that very moment' means at the very moment of sitting down. 'Again, at that very moment' means at the very moment of taking. When 'excellent meal' is said, they ask, 'Starting from how many years?'; when it is said, 'From so-and-so many years'—this is the explanation. 'When it is taken' means when the bowl is taken by visiting monks who do not know the arrangement. 'Even by those who have arrived, by the monks who know the arrangement'—this is the connection. This is the same method hereafter as well. 'Let the monks themselves come' means the intention is that the monks themselves should come, without taking the bowl.

Neti ṭhitikaṃ ajānante āgantuke. Rājā bhojetvāti rājā attano gehe bhojetvā. Nesanti āgantukānaṃ, pattepīti sambandho. Yaṃ āhaṭanti yaṃ bhattaṃ abhuñjitvā āhaṭaṃ. Taṃ na gāhetabbanti taṃ bhattaṃ ṭhitikāya na gāhetabbaṃ thokattā. Nesanti āgantukānaṃ. Gīvā hotīti iṇaṃ hoti. Iṇaṃ nāma paṭidātabbasabhāvo hoti, tasmā paṭidātabbanti adhippāyo. Etthāti ṭhitikaṃ ajānitvā bhuttaṭṭhāne. Tāva nisīditabbanti tāva āgametvā nisīditabbaṃ. Pattaṭṭhānena gāhaṇampi gīvāsadisoti purimatherassa mati bhaveyya. Evañhi sati dvinnaṃ therānaṃ vādo sadisoyeva.

'Not them' means the visiting monks who do not know the arrangement. 'The king, having fed them' means the king, having fed them in his own house. 'Of them' means of the visiting monks; 'even in the bowls'—this is the connection. 'What is brought' means the food that was brought without being eaten. 'That should not be taken' means that food should not be taken for the arrangement, because it is a small amount. 'Of them' means of the visiting monks. 'It becomes a debt' means it becomes an obligation. An obligation is by nature something that must be repaid; therefore, the intention is that it must be repaid. 'Here' means at the place where one has eaten without knowing the arrangement. 'One should sit for that long' means one should sit, waiting for that long. 'Taking in place of the bowl is also like a debt'—this might be the opinion of the first elder. This being so, the view of the two elders is indeed similar.

Eko piṇḍapātoti sambandho. Tathārūpoti ticīvaraparivāro satagghanako. Ayanti piṇḍapāto. Iti vuttaṃ aṭṭhakathāsu.

'A single portion of alms-food'—this is the connection. 'Of such a kind' means accompanied by the three robes and worth a hundred. 'This' means the alms-food. Thus it is said in the commentaries.

Eko bhikkhūti sambandho. Antarābhaṭṭhakoti uddesabhattassa antare vemajjhe bhassati galatīti antarābhaṭṭhako. Paripuṇṇavasso yo pana sāmaṇeroti yojanā. Tassa upasampajjitasāmaṇerassa ṭhitikā atikkantāti sambandho. Soti uddesabhattapatto bhikkhu. Samīpeti attano samīpe. Tañce theyyāya harantīti taṃ pattaṃ pattahārakā theyyāya haranti ce. Gīvā hotīti pattadāpakassa gīvā hoti. So bhikkhūti samīpe nisinno so bhikkhu. Assāti pattadāpakassa. “Aya”nti potthakesu pāṭho atthi, so na sundaro. Tatoti uddesabhattagharato. “Suhaṭo”ti vacanassa atthaṃ dassento āha “bhattassa dinnattā gīvā na hotī”ti.

‘A single monk’ is the connection. ‘Antarābhaṭṭhako’ means in the middle, in the interval of the designated meal, it spills or slips; thus it is ‘antarābhaṭṭhako’. The construction is: ‘one who has completed the rains, but is a novice’.
