The connection is that the standing invitation of that novice who has received higher ordination has passed. ‘He’ means the monk who receives the designated meal. ‘Nearby’ means near himself. ‘If they steal it for theft’ means if bowl-bearers steal that bowl for theft. ‘There is a debt’ means the bowl-giver incurs a debt. ‘That monk’ means that monk seated nearby. ‘His’ refers to the bowl-giver. The reading ‘this’ is found in some books, but it is not elegant. ‘From there’ means from the designated meal house. Explaining the meaning of the phrase ‘suhaṭo’, he says, ‘because the meal was given, there is no debt’.

Sādiyanakoti [V 2.0145][M 0.0506] uddesabhattasādiyanako, hotīti sambandho. Dasahipi pattehi bhattaṃ āharāpetvāti yojanā. Bhikkhudattiyaṃ nāmāti bhikkhunā dattiyaṃ nāma. So bhikkhūti sādiyanako so bhikkhu. Te bhikkhūti piṇḍapātike te bhikkhū. Etha bhante mayhaṃ sahāyā hotha iti vatvāti sambandho. Tassāti upāsakassa. Tatthāti upāsakassa ghare. Tassevāti sādiyanakasseva. Itareti navapiṇḍapātikā. Nesanti dasannaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ. Tassa bhikkhunoti sādiyanakassa bhikkhuno. Bhuttāvīnanti bhuttavantānaṃ.

‘The one who accepts’ means the one who accepts the designated meal; the connection is that he is an acceptor. ‘Having had the meal brought even with ten bowls’ is the construction. ‘Given by a monk’ is the name, meaning it is called ‘given by a monk’. ‘That monk’ means that accepting monk. ‘Those monks’ means those alms-round monks. The connection is: ‘Come, venerable sirs, be my companions,’ having said this. ‘His’ refers to the lay follower. ‘There’ means in the lay follower’s house. ‘His alone’ means only the accepting monk’s. ‘The others’ means the nine alms-round monks. ‘Their’ refers to the ten monks. ‘That monk’ refers to the accepting monk. ‘Bhuttāvīnaṃ’ means those who have eaten.

Teti navapiṇḍapātikā, vuttā gacchantīti sambandho. Tatthāti upāsakassa ghare. Tatrāti dasasu bhikkhūsu. Madhurena sarena anumodanaṃ karontassa ekassa dhammakathaṃ sutvāti yojanā. Akatabhāgo nāmāti pubbe na kariyitthāti akato, soyeva bhāgo koṭṭhāsoti akatabhāgo, āgantukabhāgo nāmāti attho.

‘They’ refers to the nine alms-round monks; the connection is with the phrase, 'they, having been told, go'. ‘There’ means in the lay follower’s house. ‘There’ refers to among the ten monks. The construction is: having heard the Dhamma talk of one who, with a sweet voice, was giving thanks. ‘Akatabhāgo’ means ‘unmade’ because it was not made formerly; that very share is a portion, therefore ‘akatabhāgo’, meaning the share for a newcomer.

Eko upāsako detīti sambandho. Imanti khādanīyabhojanīyaṃ. Pattasāmikassa dātabbanti yojanā. Ṭhapetvāti pakatiyā ṭhapetvā. “Sabbo saṅgho bhuñjatū”ti vatvā ca kiñci avatvā ca gatepi paṭhamameva “sabbaṃ saṅghikaṃ pattaṃ dethā”ti vuttattā bhājetvā paribhuñjitabbaṃ.

‘A lay follower gives’ is the connection. ‘This’ refers to food and drink. ‘It should be given to the owner of the bowl’ is the construction. ‘Setting aside’ means setting aside according to the original state. Even if one says, ‘May the entire Saṅgha partake,’ or says nothing at all after having left, still, because it was first said, ‘Give all the bowls belonging to the Saṅgha,’ it should be distributed and then enjoyed.

Pātiyā āharitvāti sambandho. Ekekaṃ ālopanti ekekassa bhikkhussa ekekaṃ ālopaṃ. Acchatīti vasati. Kassa teti kassa atthāya tayā, ānītanti yojanā. “Ekena bhikkhunā”ti padaṃ “gāhetabba”nti pade kāritakammaṃ, “bhatta”nti dhātukammaṃ tabbapaccayo vadati.

‘Having brought the bowl’ is the connection. ‘One mouthful each’ means one mouthful for each monk. ‘He stays’ means he dwells. ‘For whose sake?’ is the construction: ‘for whose benefit was it brought by you?’ The word ‘by one monk’ is the causative object (kāritakamma) with the word ‘should be taken’; and the suffix ‘tabba’ expresses the root-object (dhātukamma) of ‘meal’.

Kiṃ āharīyatīti avatvāti kiṃ vatthu tayā āharītīti upāsakaṃ apucchitvā. “Kiṃ āharissasī”tipi pāṭho, kiṃ vatthuṃ tvaṃ āharissasīti attho. Saparivārāya yāguyā ca mahagghānaṃ phalānañca paṇītānaṃ khajjakānañca tathā āveṇikā ṭhitikā kātabbāti yojanā[M 0.0507]. Ekā eva ṭhitikāti samānā eva ṭhitikā. Tathā phāṇitassāti ettha tathāsaddena “ekā eva ṭhitikā vaṭṭatī”ti padaṃ atidisati.

‘Without saying, “What is being brought?”’ means without asking the lay follower, ‘What object did you bring?’ The reading ‘What will you bring?’ is also found, meaning, ‘What object will you bring?’ The construction is: a unique permanent allocation should be established for rice gruel with accompaniments, as well as expensive fruits and exquisite sweets. ‘Only one permanent allocation’ means the same permanent allocation applies. Similarly, regarding molasses—here, the word ‘tathā’ extends the phrase ‘only one permanent allocation is suitable’.

Iti uddesabhattakathāya yojanā samattā.

Thus, the explanation of the section on the designated meal is completed.

Nimantanabhattakathā

The Section on the Invited Meal

Nimantanaṃ [V 2.0146] puggalikaṃ saṅghikañcāti duvidhaṃ. Tattha puggalikaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ “puggalikaṃ ce sayameva issaro”ti. “Ettake bhikkhū saṅghato uddisathā”tiādīni avatvā “ettakānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ bhattaṃ gaṇhathā”ti nimantetvā dinnaṃ saṅghikaṃ nimantanaṃ nāma. Etthāti nimantane. Piṇḍapātikānampi vaṭṭatīti “bhikkha”nti kappiyavohārena vuttattā piṇḍapātikānampi vaṭṭati. Paṭipāṭiyāti saṅghato laddhapaṭipāṭiyā. Āgatamanusso vadatīti sambandho. Vicchinditvāti “tumhe ca gacchathā”ti vacanaṃ vicchinditvā.

Invitation is of two kinds: personal and pertaining to the Saṅgha. Herein, with reference to the personal, it is said, ‘If it is a personal invitation, he is the master himself’. Without saying, ‘Assign so many monks from the Saṅgha,’ etc., but inviting with the words, ‘Accept a meal for so many monks,’ what is given is called an invitation pertaining to the Saṅgha. ‘Herein’ means in the invitation. ‘It applies even to those who live on alms’ means it applies even to those who live on alms, because it is spoken of in permissible usage as ‘alms’. ‘In order’ means according to the order received from the Saṅgha. ‘The person who has come speaks’ is the connection. ‘Having interrupted’ means having interrupted the speech by saying, ‘You also go’.

Nimantanabhattagharatoti nimantanabhattassa dinnagharato. Eko āharatīti sambandho. Pūretvāti bhattassa pūretvā. Tanti bhattaṃ. Idhāpīti nimantanepi.

‘From the house for the invitational meal’ means from the house where the invitational meal was given. ‘One brings’ is the connection. ‘Having filled’ means having filled with the meal. ‘That’ refers to the meal. ‘Here too’ means even in the case of an invitation.

Tatoti vadanakāraṇā. “So bhikkhū”ti padaṃ “assā”ti pade pakatikattā, “jigucchanīyo”ti padaṃ tattheva vikatikattā. Assāti bhaveyya, hoti vā. “Pattatthāya āgatomhī”ti vadantassa tassa patto dātabboti yojanā. Bhattāharaṇakapattanti bhattaṃ āharati anenāti bhattāharaṇako, soyeva patto bhattāharaṇakapatto, taṃ. Paṭipāṭibhattanti paṭipāṭiyā laddhaṃ bhattaṃ.

‘Therefore’ means for the reason of that statement. The word ‘so bhikkhū’ is the subject (pakatikattā) of the word ‘assa’, and the word ‘jigucchanīyo’ is the subject complement (vikatikattā) in the same context. ‘Assa’ means ‘he might be,’ or ‘he is’. The construction is that the bowl should be given to one who says, ‘I have come for the sake of a bowl’. ‘Bhattāharaṇakapattaṃ’ means ‘a bowl for bringing food’; because food is brought with it, it is called a ‘bhattāharaṇaka’, and that very bowl is a ‘bhattāharaṇakapatta’. ‘Paṭipāṭibhattaṃ’ means food obtained in order.

Ālopabhattaṭṭhitikatoti ekekaālopena laddhassa bhattassa ṭhitikato. Ālopasaṅkhepenāti ekekasmiṃ ālope taṃsaṃkhipanena. Ayaṃ nayo uddesabhattato viseso. Kassa te ābhatanti kassa atthāya tayā ābhatanti yojanā. Saṅghassa me bhattanti saṅghassa atthāya mayā bhattaṃ ābhataṃ. Therānaṃ me bhattanti therānaṃ mayā bhattaṃ ābhataṃ.

‘Ālopabhattaṭṭhitikato’ means because of the standing custom of the meal obtained with each morsel. ‘Ālopasaṅkhepena’ means by abridging it to each morsel. This method is a distinction from the designated meal. ‘For whom is this brought?’ is the construction: ‘for whose benefit was it brought by you?’ ‘The meal is for the Saṅgha’ means the meal has been brought by me for the sake of the Saṅgha. ‘The meal is for the elders’ means the meal has been brought by me for the elders.

Upāsako [M 0.0508] pahiṇātīti sambandho. Ime tayo janāti saṅghatthero ca ganthadhutaṅgavasena abhiññāto ca bhattuddesako cāti ime tayo janā. Pucchitunti “kiṃ saṅghato gaṇhāmi, udāhu ye jānāmi, tehi saddhiṃ āgacchāmī”ti pucchituṃ. Āruhiyitthāti ārūḷhā. Attanavamehīti attā navamo etesanti attanavamā, tehi bhikkhūhīti sambandho. Hīti yasmā. Ete bhikkhūti saṅghattherādayo tayo ete bhikkhū. Tenāti ganthadhutaṅgādīhi anabhiññātena bhikkhunā paṭipajjitabbanti sambandho. Nissitake vā, ye bhikkhū jānātha, te bhikkhū vā gahetvāti [V 2.0147] yojanā. Attanā añño gāmo gantabboti sambandho. Soyeva gāmoti nimantanagāmoyeva.

‘The lay follower sends’ is the connection. ‘These three people’ means these three people: the Saṅgha elder, one known for the ascetic practice of book learning, and the meal distributor. ‘To ask’ means to ask, ‘Shall I take monks from the Saṅgha, or shall I go with those I know?’ ‘Āruhiyittha’ means ‘climbed’. ‘With oneself as the ninth’ means ‘oneself is the ninth of these,’ thus ‘attanavamā’; the connection is ‘with those monks’. ‘Hī’ means ‘because’. ‘These monks’ refers to these three monks, the Saṅgha elder and the others. The connection is: ‘Therefore,’ one should associate with a monk who is not known for the ascetic practice of book learning, etc. The construction is: ‘Or dependents,’ or taking those monks whom you know. ‘One should go to another village oneself’ is the connection. ‘That very village’ means the very village of the invitation.

Tatrāti asanasālāyaṃ. Ussavādīsūti chaṇādīsu. Ādisaddena aññena kenaci kāraṇena manussānaṃ bahusannipātaṃ saṅgaṇhāti. Tadāti tasmiṃ nimantanakāle. Sannipātaṭṭhānatoti bhikkhūnaṃ sannipātaṭṭhānato. Yathāsattīti sattiyā anurūpaṃ, sattiṃ anatikkamitvāti attho. Ettha ca sattisaddassa kuntasaṅkhātassa satthassapi vācakattā taṃ paṭikkhipanto āha “yathābala”nti.

‘There’ means in the assembly hall. ‘Ussavādīsu’ means in festivals and the like. By the word ‘ādi,’ it includes any other reason for a large gathering of people. ‘At that time’ refers to the time of the invitation. ‘From the gathering place’ means from the place of the monks’ gathering. ‘According to capacity’ means in proportion to one’s capacity, without exceeding one’s capacity—this is the meaning. Here, since the word ‘satti’ can also refer to a spear (kunta), rejecting that interpretation, he says, ‘according to strength’.

Saṅghatthero vā āgacchantīti sambandho. Bahukattāramapekkhitvā “āgacchantī”ti bahuvacanavasena vuttaṃ. Ekavāranti ekasmiṃ divase, āgamanadivaseti attho. Paṭibaddhakālatoti tattheva sakaṭṭhāne vāsassa nibaddhakālato. Dutiyavāreti dutiyadivase. Abhinavaāgantukāvāti anāgamanapubbā abhinavā āgantukāva. Tatrāti tasmiṃ pattaṭṭhāne. Tesanti abhinavaāgantukānaṃ. Etthāti anāgatapubbaṭṭhāne.

‘The Saṅgha elder or those coming’ is the connection. With respect to the many agents, it is said in the plural as ‘āgacchanti’ (they come). ‘Once’ means on one day, meaning the day of arrival. ‘Bound by time’ refers to the time fixed for dwelling in that very place. ‘A second time’ means on the second day. ‘Newly arrived guests’ means newly arrived guests who have not come before. ‘There’ means in that alms-bowl stand. ‘Them’ refers to the newly arrived guests. ‘Here’ means in a place not previously visited.

Sabbatthāti sabbesu sakaṭṭhānaāgantukaṭṭhānesu. Tenāti atilābhinā bhikkhunā. Avisesetvāti visesamakatvā.

‘Everywhere’ means in all one’s own locations and visiting locations. ‘By him’ means by a monk who has obtained an excess. ‘Without distinction’ means without making a distinction.

Salākabhattakathā

The Explanation of the Lot-Meal

Salākabhattaṃ [M 0.0509] pana evaṃ veditabbanti yojanā. “Vacanato”ti padaṃ “dātabbā”ti pade ñāpakahetu. Salākāya vāti kusadaṇḍe vā. Asukassa nāmāti asukassa nāma upāsakassa. Upanibandhitvāti likhitvā, chinditvāti attho. “Opuñjitvā”ti padassa atthaṃ dassento āha “punappunaṃ heṭṭhupariyavasena āloḷetvā”ti. Bhattuddesakena dātabbāti sambandho.

The lot-meal, however, should be understood thus—this is the interpretation. The word 'by speech' is the indicative cause for the word 'should be given.' 'By a lot' means by a kusa-grass stick. 'For so-and-so by name' means for a lay follower named so-and-so. 'Having recorded' means having written, that is, having cut. Explaining the meaning of the word 'having piled them up,' he said: 'having repeatedly stirred up and down.' It should be given by the meal-allocator—this is the connection.

Na bahukāti appakā. Gāmavasenapīti yebhuyyena samānalābhagāmavasenapi. Pisaddena kulaṃ apekkhati. Gāhentena gāhitānevāti sambandho. Saṭṭhisalākabhattāni hontīti yojanā. Tesanti dvinnaṃ tiṇṇaṃ salākabhattānaṃ.

‘Not many’ means few. ‘Even by way of a village’ means mostly by way of villages with similar gains. By the word ‘pi’ (also), family is intended. ‘By one who takes, they are indeed taken’—this is the connection. ‘There are sixty lot-meals’—this is the interpretation. ‘Of them’ means of two or three lot-meals.

Tanti bahusalākabhattagāmaṃ. Taṃ panāti ekasalākabhattaṃ pana. Etesūti bhikkhūsu. Niggahenāti [V 2.0148] dūrattā anicchantassapi ekassa niggahena. Tanti salākabhattaṃ. Orimagāmeti orabhāge ṭhite gāme. Gāhitasaññāyāti gāhitā iti saññāya. Puna vihāraṃ āgantvāti puna vihāraṃ anāgantvā orimagāme salākabhattāni paṭhamaṃ gahetvā pacchā vihāraṃ āgantvā attano pāpetvā bhuñjitumpi vaṭṭati. Kasmā puna vihāro āgantabbo, nanu agāhitopi attano pattattā gahetvā bhuñjituṃ vaṭṭatīti āha “na hī”tiādi. Hi yasmā bahisīmāya saṅghalābho gāhetuṃ na labbhati, tasmā vihāro āgantabboti yojanā. Ekabāhavasena vāti ekāya gharapāḷisaṅkhātāya bāhāyavasena vā. Vīthiādīsu cāti vīthibāhakulesu ca, niddhāraṇe bhummaṃ. Yatthāti yasmiṃ ṭhāne. Salākāsu asati asantāsūti yojanā. Uddisitvāpīti “asukagāmassa salākabhattāni tuyhaṃ pāpuṇantī”ti gāmādīni uddisitvāpi.

‘That’ means the village with many lot-meals. ‘But that’ means a single lot-meal. ‘Among these’ means among the monks. ‘By compulsion’ means by the compulsion of even one who is distant and unwilling. ‘That’ means the lot-meal. ‘In a nearby village’ means in a village located in the near part. ‘With the perception of having been taken’ means with the perception that ‘it has been taken.’ ‘Having returned to the monastery again’ means: it is permissible to first take the lot-meals in the nearby village without returning to the monastery again, and then later, having returned to the monastery and having made them one's own, to eat them. Why must one return to the monastery? Is it not permissible to take and eat even if unassigned, since it is one’s own portion? He said: ‘No, because,’ and so on. For since a gain of the Saṅgha cannot be taken outside the boundary, therefore one must return to the monastery—this is the interpretation. ‘Or by way of one branch’ means or by way of one branch, which is reckoned as a row of houses. ‘And in streets, etc.’ means in households of the street-branches, etc.; the locative is in the sense of determination. ‘Where’ means in which place. ‘When lots are not present’—this is the interpretation. ‘Even after assigning’ means even after assigning villages, etc., saying, ‘The lot-meals of such-and-such village reach you.’

Tamevatthaṃ [M 0.0510] vitthārento āha “tena hī”tiādi. Tattha tenāti salākadāyakena bhikkhunā. Gāhetabbanti sambandho. Vāragāmeti atidūrattā vārena gantabbe gāme. Tatrāti taṃ gāmaṃ.

Explaining that very meaning in detail, he said: ‘Therefore,’ and so on. Therein, ‘by him’ means by the monk who gives the lots. ‘Should be taken’ is the connection. ‘A turn-village’ means a village to be gone to by turns because of being very far away. ‘There’ means that village.

Atirekagāvuteti gāvutato atireke ṭhāne. Taṃdivasanti tasmiṃ salākabhattagahaṇadivase. Yo na gacchati, tassa na dātabbāti yojanā. Hīti yasmā. Tīṇi pana divasānīti accantasaṃyoge cetaṃ upayogavacanaṃ. Tanti orimavāragāmasalākaṃ. Daṇḍakammaṃ pana kinti gāḷhaṃ kātabbanti āha “saṭṭhito vā paṇṇāsato vā na parihāpetabba”nti. Vihāravāroti vihārassa rakkhanatthāya vāro. Vihāravārikassāti vihāraṃ vārena, vāraṃ gahetvā vā rakkhatīti vihāravāriko, tassa dātabbāti sambandho. Vihāragopakāti vihāraṃ gopentīti vihāragopakā. Aññathattanti pasādaññathattaṃ. Aññesu kulesu dātabbāti aññesaṃ kulānaṃ yāguādayo dātabbā.

‘Beyond a gāvuta’ means in a place beyond a gāvuta. ‘On that day’ means on that day of taking the lot-meal. ‘It should not be given to one who does not go’—this is the interpretation. ‘Hi’ means ‘because.’ ‘For three days’—this is a usage in the sense of continuous connection. ‘That’ means the lot of the turn-village on this side. But regarding the punishment, how strictly should it be done? He said: ‘It should not be reduced from sixty or fifty.’ ‘Monastery-turn’ means the turn for guarding the monastery. ‘For the one on monastery-duty’ means: he is a vihāravārika because he guards the monastery by turn or having taken a turn; it should be given to him—this is the connection. ‘Monastery-guards’ means those who guard the monastery. ‘Otherness’ means a change in faith. ‘Should be given to other families’ means that gruel and other things should be given to other families.

Vāraṃ gāhetvāti aññehi vāraṃ gāhāpetvā. Nesanti vihāravārikānaṃ. Salākāti pakatikattāraṃ apekkhitvā “bhavantī”ti bahuvacanavasena vuttaṃ. Phātikammamevāti vihārarakkhanatthāya saṅghena dātabbaphātikammameva. Aññampīti pisaddena na kevalaṃ phātikammameva, aññampīti dasseti. Atirekauttaribhaṅgassāti atirekaṃ uttaribhaṅgametassāti atirekauttaribhaṅgaṃ, tassa.

‘Having caused the turn to be taken’ means having caused the turn to be taken by others. ‘Of them’ means of the monastery guards. ‘The lot’ (salākā): with reference to the regular agent, it is spoken in the plural as ‘bhavanti’ (they are). ‘It is merely a transaction’ means it is merely the transaction to be given by the Saṅgha for the sake of the monastery's protection. ‘And also another’—by the word ‘pi’ (also), it shows that it is not only the transaction, but also another. ‘Of the extra upper robe’ is explained as: he has an extra upper robe; of that.

Salākā laddhāti salākā eva laddhā. Taṃdivasanti tasmiṃ salākaladdhadivase. Ekassevāti [V 2.0149] ekekasseva. Vijaṭetvāti tāni dve tīṇi ekacārikabhattāni vijaṭaṃ nigumbaṃ katvā.

‘A lot is obtained’ means a lot is indeed obtained. ‘On that day’ means on that day the lot was obtained. ‘For one only’ means for each and every one. ‘Having disentangled’ means having made those two or three meals for a solitary wanderer disentangled and un-clumped.

Ekasambhogāti ekato sambhogā. Gāhentena dātunti sambandho. Sammukhībhūtassāti upacārasīmāyaṃ ṭhitassa yassa kassaci, pāpetvāti yojanā. Rasasalākanti ucchusalākaṃ. “Rasālasalāka”ntipi pāṭho, ayamevattho. Khuddakavihāre gāhetabbavidhānaṃ dassetvā mahāāvāse taṃ dassento āha “mahāāvāse”tiādi.

‘Of one partaking’ means partaking together. ‘Should be given by the one taking’—this is the connection. ‘For one who is present’ means for anyone standing within the boundary of proximity; ‘having caused to reach’ is the interpretation. ‘Juice-lot’ means a sugarcane lot. There is also a variant reading, ‘Rasālasalāka,’ and it has the same meaning. Having shown the method of taking in a small monastery, in order to show that in a large residence, he says, ‘in a large residence,’ and so on.

“Takkasalākampi [M 0.0511] …pe… dātuṃ vaṭṭatī”ti idaṃ khuddakavihāraṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ, tena vuttaṃ “mahāāvāse”tiādi. Bhesajjādisalākāyoti ettha ādisaddena gandhamālāsalākāyo saṅgaṇhāti. Etthāti salākāsu. Aggabhikkhamattanti aggato dātabbaṃ bhikkhāmattaṃ. Tādisāni bhattānīti aggabhikkhāmattasabhāvāni bhattāni. No ceti tādisāni bhattāni bahūni no ce honti. Laddhā vā aladdhā vāti labhitvā vā alabhitvā vā.

‘It is permissible to give even a buttermilk-lot… and so on’ – this was said referring to a small monastery; therefore it was said ‘in a large residence,’ and so on. ‘In the medicine-lot, etc.’: here, by the word ‘etc.’, it includes lots for perfumes and garlands. ‘Here’ means among the lots. ‘The foremost amount of alms’ means the amount of alms to be given foremost. ‘Such meals’ means meals of the nature of the foremost amount of alms. ‘If not’ means if such meals are not many. ‘Whether obtained or not obtained’ means having obtained them or not having obtained them.

Salākāsu gāhitāsūti aññāsu salākāsu gāhitāsu. Samīpe ṭhitassāti hatthaṃ apasāretvā samīpe ṭhitassa. Assāti bhikkhussa. Ayaṃ salākāti “ayaṃ tassa salākā”ti ṭhapetuṃ vaṭṭati. Adhammikāti katikā adhammayuttā. Anāgatassa dethāti anāgatassa bhikkhussa salākaṃ detha.

‘When lots have been taken’ means when other lots have been taken. ‘For one standing nearby’ means for one standing nearby, having withdrawn his hand. ‘For him’ means for the monk. ‘This lot’ means it is suitable to set it aside saying, ‘This is his lot.’ ‘Unrighteous’ means an agreement that is not in accordance with the Dhamma. ‘Give to the one who has not come’ means give the lot to a monk who has not yet arrived.

Soti bhattuddesako, vadeyyāti sambandho. Mayā mayhaṃ pāpitanti sambandho. Tatthāti gāme. Bhuñjeyyātha iti vadeyya, vaṭṭatīti yojanā. Tatthevāti asanasālāyameva. Tatrāti tasmiṃ gāme. Vihāraṃ ānetvāti vihāraṃ salākabhattaṃ ānetvā. Salākaggāhaṇakāleti salākāya bhikkhūhi gāhāpanakāle.

‘He’ means the meal-allocator; ‘he should speak’ is the connection. ‘By me, it is caused to reach me’—this is the connection. ‘There’ means in the village. He should say, ‘You should eat’; ‘it is permissible’ is the interpretation. ‘Right there’ means in the dining hall itself. ‘There’ means in that village. ‘Having brought to the monastery’ means having brought the lot-meal to the monastery. ‘At the time of the taking of the lot’ means at the time of having the monks take the lot.

Tatthāti tasmiṃ disābhāge. Aññenāti attanā aññena, laddhā hotīti sambandho. Tena panāti gamikato itarena. Tasminti gamike. Upacārasīmaṃ anatikkanteyevāti yojanā.

‘There’ means in that region. ‘By another’ means by one other than oneself; ‘it is obtained’ is the connection. ‘But by that one’ means by one other than the traveler. ‘In that one’ means in the traveler. ‘Without having transgressed the vicinity-boundary itself’—this is the interpretation.

Tatthāti chaḍḍitavihāre. Tesūti āvāsikesu bhikkhūsu, gatesūti sambandho. Sovāti āgantuko eva. Yo pana gacchatīti sambandho. Tanti salākabhattaṃ, na pāpuṇātīti sambandho.

‘There’ means in the abandoned monastery. ‘Among them’ means among the resident monks; ‘when they have gone’ is the connection. ‘He’ means the visiting monk indeed. ‘But whoever goes’—this is the connection. ‘That’ means the lot-meal; ‘does not obtain’ is the connection.

Puññenāti [V 2.0150] puññasmā. Tā ca kho panāti salākāyo pana. Pacchiṃ panāti salākapacchiṃ pana. Tatthāti pacchiyaṃ. Ettovāti ākiraṇaṭṭhānatova. Ekanti ekaṃ salākaṃ. Vattabbanti salākadāyakena vattabbaṃ.

‘By merit’ means from merit. ‘But those indeed’ means but the lots. ‘But the basket’ means but the lot-basket. ‘There’ means in the basket. ‘From here only’ means from the scattering place only. ‘One’ means one lot. ‘Should be said’ means should be said by the lot-giver.

Bhikkhū gatāti sambandho. Tatthāti aññasmiṃ vihāre. Mahātheropi gacchatīti sambandho. Gatavihāre abhuñjitvāva gocaragāmaṃ anuppattehi [M 0.0512] bhikkhūhi pattā na dātabbāti yojanā. Vihāraṭṭhakaṃ bhattanti vihāre ṭhitaṃ bhattaṃ.

‘The monks have gone’—this is the connection. ‘There’ means in another monastery. ‘The great elder also goes’—this is the connection. The interpretation is that bowls should not be given to monks who, without having eaten in the monastery to which they have gone, have arrived at the alms village. ‘The monastery-meal’ means the meal that is in the monastery.

Pakkhikabhattādikathā

Explanation of Fortnightly Meals and So On

Yanti bhattaṃ diyyatīti sambandho. Cātuddasīpañcaddasīpañcamīaṭṭhamīti abhilakkhitesūti yojanā. Kammappasutehīti kammūpacayehi. Imehi pāṭhehi pakkhesu dātabbaṃ pakkhikanti vacanatthaṃ dasseti. Tanti pakkhikabhattaṃ. “Hotī”ti pade vuttakattā, “gāhetvā”ti pade dhātukammaṃ, “bhuñjitabba”nti pade vuttakammaṃ. Sabbesanti bhikkhūnaṃ. Yesanti bhikkhūnaṃ. Mandāti appā. Tanti salākabhattaṃ. Paṇītaṃ dentīti paṇītaṃ katvā denti. Lūkhabhattanti asiniddhabhattaṃ.

The connection is 'food is given'. The application is to the days designated as the fourteenth, fifteenth, fifth, and eighth. By 'kammappasutehi' is meant 'by the accumulation of kamma'. Through these readings, it shows the meaning of the word 'pakkhika' as 'to be given on the fortnightly days'. That is the pakkhikabhatta. In the word 'hoti', the agent is expressed; in the word 'gāhetvā', the object of the root is indicated; in the word 'bhuñjitabba', the object is expressed. 'Sabbesaṃ' means 'of all monks'. 'Yesaṃ' means 'of those monks'. 'Mandā' means 'few'. That is the salākabhatta. 'Paṇītaṃ denti' means 'they give after making it excellent'. 'Lūkhabhattaṃ' means 'coarse food'.

Yaṃ bhattaṃ attanā bhuñjati, tadeva diyyatīti yojanā. Iminā uposathe dātabbaṃ uposathikanti vacanatthaṃ dasseti. Uposatheti uposathadivase. Ettha ca pañcaddasiyaṃ sace dāyakā “pakkhika”nti vatvā denti, pakkhikaṃ nāma. Atha “uposathika”nti vatvā denti, uposathikaṃ nāmāti viseso. Pāṭipadeti pāṭipadadivase. Uposathakammenāti uposathakammena hetubhūtena. “Pāṭipade diyyanakadāna”nti iminā pāṭipade dātabbaṃ pāṭipadikanti vacanatthaṃ dasseti. Tampi ubhayanti uposathikapāṭipadikavasena ubhayampi taṃ bhattaṃ. Iti imānīti ettha imasaddena itisaddassa imasaddatthabhāvo dassito hoti. Sattapi bhattānīti imasmiṃ senāsanakkhandhake āgatāni saṅghabhattādīni sattapi bhattāni.

The application is that the food one eats oneself, that very food is to be given. By this, it shows the meaning of the word 'uposathika' as 'to be given on the Uposatha day'. 'Uposathe' means 'on the Uposatha day'. And here, on the fifteenth day, if donors say 'it is for the pakkhika' and give it, it is called pakkhika. But if they say 'it is for the uposathika' and give it, it is called uposathika—this is the distinction. 'Pāṭipade' means 'on the first day'. 'Uposathakammena' means 'caused by the Uposatha act'. By 'the donation given on the first day', it shows the meaning of the word 'pāṭipadika' as 'to be given on the first day'. That food, too, is both, in the sense of being uposathika and pāṭipadika. In 'iti imāni', by the word 'ima', it is shown that the word 'iti' has the meaning of 'ima'. 'Sattapi bhattāni' refers to the seven meals, such as the Sangha meal, that are mentioned in this Section on Lodgings.

Aparānipi cattāri bhattānīti sambandho. Tatthāti catūsu bhattesu. “Āgantukānaṃ dinna”ntiādinā āgantukabhattanti padassa catutthīmajjhelopasamāsaṃ dasseti. Aññattha pana “āgantukassa atthāya ābhata”ntiādinā chaṭṭhīmajjhelopasamāsaṃ dasseti. Etthāti catūsu [M 0.0513] bhattesu. Sabbesanti bhikkhūnaṃ. Eko āgantuko nisīdatīti sambandho. Tenāti paṭhamaāgantukena.

The connection is 'also four other meals'. 'Tattha' means 'among the four meals'. By 'given to the newcomers', etc., it shows the fourth-case middle-term elision compound of the word 'āgantukabhatta'. Elsewhere, however, by 'brought for the sake of a newcomer', etc., it shows the sixth-case middle-term elision compound. 'Ettha' means 'among the four meals'. 'Sabbesaṃ' means 'of all monks'. The connection is 'one newcomer sits down'. 'Tena' means 'by the first newcomer'.

Yoti [V 2.0151] āgantuko. Āgantvāpīti pisaddo garahattho, pacchā pana pagevāti attho. Tena gaṇhitabbanti yojanā. “Āgatadivaseyevā”ti iminā na dutiyadivasādīsu bhuñjitabbanti dasseti.

'Yo' means 'the newcomer'. In 'āgantvāpi', the particle 'pi' has the sense of censure, but afterwards it has the meaning 'at once'. The application is 'it should be taken by him'. By 'on the very day of arrival', it shows that one should not eat on the second day or subsequent days.

Katthacīti kiñci ṭhānaṃ. Tanti āgantukabhattaṃ. Nibandhāpitanti niccaṃ ṭhapitaṃ. Asanasālāyanti antogāme asanasālāyaṃ. Asatīti asantesu.

'Katthaci' means 'some place'. That is the āgantukabhatta. 'Nibandhāpitaṃ' means 'established permanently'. 'Asanasālāyaṃ' means 'in the dining hall inside the village'. 'Asati' means 'among those who are not present'.

Āvāsikopīti pisaddo na gamikoyevāti dasseti. Yathā āgantukabhattaṃ dve vā tīṇi vā satta vā divasāni labbhati, evaṃ idaṃ gamiyabhattaṃ na labbhatīti yojanā. Panthanti maggaṃ. Rundhantīti pidahanti. Udakaṃ vā rundhatīti sambandho. Ete upaddaveti corādayo ete upaddave. Oḍḍetvāti ṭhapetvā.

The particle 'pi' in 'āvāsikopi' shows that it is not only for a traveler. The application is that just as the āgantukabhatta is obtained for two, three, or seven days, this gamiyabhatta is not obtained in the same way. 'Panthaṃ' means 'the road'. 'Rundhanti' means 'they block'. The connection is 'or they block water'. 'Ete upaddave' means 'these disturbances, such as thieves'. 'Oḍḍetvā' means 'having set aside'.

Etassāti mahāgilānassa. Puna etassāti anāgatassa mahāgilānassa. Sappāyabhojananti gilānānaṃ sappāyabhojanaṃ. Missakayāgunti nānātaṇḍule missetvā pacitaṃ yāguṃ. Na kuppatīti na vikāraṃ karoti.

'Etassa' means 'of this seriously ill person'. 'Puna etassa' means 'of a future seriously ill person'. 'Sappāyabhojanaṃ' means 'suitable food for the sick'. 'Missakayāgu' means 'gruel cooked by mixing various types of rice'. 'Na kuppati' means 'it does not cause disturbance'.

Idampīti gilānupaṭṭhākabhattampi. Tatthāti tasmiṃ kule. Assāti gilānassa. Evaṃ dinnānīti evaṃ vakkhamānanayena dinnāni honti. Piṇḍapātikānampi vaṭṭatīti “bhikkha”nti kappiyavohārena vuttattā piṇḍapātikānampi vaṭṭati. Na vaṭṭatīti “bhatta”nti akappiyavohārena vuttattā na vaṭṭati.

'Idampi' means 'also the meal for nursing the sick'. 'Tattha' means 'in that family'. 'Assa' means 'for the sick person'. 'Evaṃ dinnāni' means 'given in this manner, as will be described'. 'Piṇḍapātikānampi vaṭṭati'—since it is spoken of as 'alms' (bhikkhā) with an allowable term, it is allowable even for alms-gatherers. 'Na vaṭṭati'—since it is spoken of as 'meal' (bhatta) with an unallowable term, it is not allowable.

Aparānipi tīṇi bhattānīti sambandho. Tatthāti tīsu bhattesu. Dhurabhattanti ettha dhurasaddassa dhuvasaddena atthato sadisattā niccatthoti āha “niccabhattaṃ vuccatī”ti. Tanti dhurabhattaṃ. Tatthāti duvidhesu. “Saṅghike”ti pāṭhaseso yojetabbo. Puggalikepīti pisaddo “saṅghike”ti padaṃ apekkhati. Pacchāti paṭhamaṃ “bhikkhaṃ gaṇhathā”ti vuttavacanato, vuttavacanassa vā paraṃ.

The connection is 'also three other meals'. 'Tattha' means 'among the three meals'. In 'dhurabhattaṃ', because the word 'dhura' is similar in meaning to the word 'dhuva', it means 'permanent'; thus, it says, 'it is called a permanent meal'. That is the dhurabhatta. 'Tattha' means 'among the two types'. The remaining reading 'saṅghike' should be connected. The particle 'pi' in 'puggalikepi' refers back to the word 'saṅghike'. 'Pacchā' means 'after the first statement "take alms", or after the spoken words'.

Kuṭiṃ [M 0.0514] katvā dātabbaṃ bhattaṃ kuṭibhattanti dassento āha “kuṭibhattaṃ nāmā”tiādi. Yanti bhattaṃ, nibandhāpitanti sambandho, senāsanavāsino bhikkhūti sambandho. Yaṃ panāti bhattaṃ pana, dinnanti sambandho. Tassevāti puggalasseva. Tasminti puggale.

Showing that the meal to be given after making a hut is kuṭibhatta, he says, 'what is called kuṭibhatta', etc. The connection is 'yaṃ' with 'bhattaṃ' and 'nibandhāpitaṃ'; there is also a connection with 'senāsanavāsino bhikkhū'. The connection is 'yaṃ pana' with 'bhattaṃ pana' and 'dinnaṃ'. 'Tasseva' means 'of that very individual'. 'Tasmiṃ' means 'in that person'.

Vārena[V 2.0152], vāraṃ gahetvā vā dinnaṃ bhattaṃ vārabhattanti dassento āha “vārabhattaṃ nāmā”tiādi. Tampīti vārabhattampi. Nigamanavasena sampiṇḍetvā dassento āha “iti imāni cā”tiādi.

Showing that the meal given by turns, or having taken turns, is vārabhatta, he says, 'what is called vārabhatta', etc. 'Tampi' means 'even this vārabhatta'. Concluding by way of summary, he states, 'thus these', etc.

Aṭṭhakathāyanti mahāaṭṭhakathāyaṃ, vuttānīti sambandho. Tatthāti catūsu bhattesu. Vihāre uppannaṃ bhattaṃ vihārabhattanti dassento āha “vihārabhattaṃ nāmā”tiādi. Tatruppādabhattanti tasmiṃ vihāre dinnakhettavatthuādīhi uppādabhattaṃ. Tanti vihārabhattaṃ. Yathāti yenākārena, paṭiggahiyamāneti sambandho. Aṭṭhannaṃ samūho, aṭṭha parimāṇāni yassāti vā aṭṭhako, tassa dinnaṃ bhattaṃ aṭṭhakabhattaṃ. Evaṃ catukkabhattanti etthāpi. Tamevatthaṃ dassento āha “aṭṭhannaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ demā”tiādi. Mahābhisaṅkhārikenāti sabbinonītādīhi mahanto abhisaṅkhāro mahābhisaṅkhāro, so etassa atthīti mahābhisaṅkhāriko, tena atirasakapūvena patte pakkhipitvāti sambandho. “Thaketvā dinna”nti iminā gūhitvā dātabbaṃ guḷhakaṃ, tameva bhattaṃ guḷhakabhattanti vacanatthaṃ dasseti.

'Aṭṭhakathāyaṃ' means 'in the Great Commentary'; the connection is with 'vuttāni' (what is said). 'Tattha' means 'among the four meals'. Showing that the meal arising in the monastery is vihārabhatta, he says, 'what is called vihārabhatta', etc. 'Tatruppādabhattaṃ' means 'the meal produced in that monastery through fields, land, etc., given to it'. That is the vihārabhatta. 'Yathā' means 'in whatever manner'; the connection is with 'paṭiggahiyamāne' (it is being received). A group of eight, or that which has eight as its measure, is an aṭṭhaka; the meal given to it is an aṭṭhakabhatta. The same applies to 'catukkabhatta'. Showing just that meaning, he says, 'Let us give to eight monks', etc. 'Mahābhisaṅkhārikena' means 'by one who has great preparation' (a great preparation is a mahābhisaṅkhāra, with all kinds of ghee, etc., and he is one who has that); the connection is 'having placed a very delicious cake in the bowl by him'. By 'given concealed', it shows the meaning of the word 'guḷhakabhatta', that the meal to be given secretly is a guḷhaka, and that very meal is guḷhakabhatta.

Idhāti imasmiṃ loke. Ekacce manussā dentīti sambandho. “Bhikkhuparicchedajānanatthaṃ guḷake dentī”ti iminā guḷakena bhikkhū gaṇetvā dātabbaṃ bhattaṃ guḷakabhattanti vacanatthaṃ dasseti. Ettha ca purimanaye ḷakāre hakārasaṃyogo atthi, pacchimanaye natthīti daṭṭhabbaṃ. Guḷapiṇḍagaṇanāya bhikkhugaṇanaṃ jānāti. Itītiādi nigamanaṃ. Cīvarabhājanīyaṃ vuttanti sambandho.

'Idha' means 'in this world'. The connection is 'some people give'. By 'they give lumps to know the number of monks', it shows the meaning of the word 'guḷakabhatta', that the meal to be given after counting the monks with a lump is guḷakabhatta. And here, in the former method, there is a combination of the letter 'ḷ' with 'h', but not in the latter—this should be noted. One knows the count of monks by counting the lumps of food. 'Iti', etc., is the conclusion. The connection is 'the distribution of robes is spoken of'.

Sabbiādīsu bhesajjesūti niddhāraṇe bhummaṃ, “sabbissā”ti padaṃ “kumbhasatampī”ti pade nissitasambandho.

In 'sabbiādīsu bhesajjesu', the locative case is used for specification; the word 'sabbissa' is dependently connected to the phrase 'kumbhasatampi'.

Pacchā [M 0.0515] āgatānaṃ dātabbamevāti dutiyabhāge adātabbeyeva pacchā āgatānaṃ dātabbameva. Sabbasannipātaṭṭhāneyevāti sabbesaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ sannipātaṭṭhāneva. Bhājanīyabhaṇḍaṃ nāma bhājanaṭṭhānaṃ sampattasseva pāpuṇāti, na asampattassa. Sabbasannipātaṭṭhāne ca yebhuyyena sampatto hoti, tena vuttaṃ “sabbasannipātaṭṭhāneyevā”ti.

'Pacchā āgatānaṃ dātabbameva' means 'even in the second part, where it should not be given, it should indeed be given to those who come later'. 'Sabbasannipātaṭṭhāneyeva' means 'only in the place of a gathering of all monks'. An article suitable for distribution reaches only the one who is present at the place of distribution, not the one who is absent. And in the place of a full gathering, one is mostly present; therefore it is said: 'sabbasannipātaṭṭhāneyeva'.

Yathāṭhitaṃyevāti kiñci abhājetvā yathāṭhitaṃyeva. “Duggahita”nti vatvā tadatthaṃ dassento āha “taṃ gatagataṭṭhāne saṅghikameva hotī”ti. Āvajjetvāti pariṇāmetvā. Tampīti thālake [V 2.0153] pakkhittaṃ sabbimpi. Thinanti ghanabhāvena tiṭṭhatīti thinaṃ, ghananti vuttaṃ hoti. Vuttaparicchedatoti “dasa bhikkhū, daseva ca sabbikumbhā”ti vuttaparicchedato.

Yathāṭhitaṃyeva means 'just as it is', without dividing anything. Having said 'duggahita', while explaining its meaning, he says, 'that, in every place it goes, remains the property of the Saṅgha'. Āvajjetvā means 'having designated'. Tampi means 'all of it, even that placed in the bowl'. Thinaṃ means 'it stands in a dense state', thus it is called thinaṃ, meaning 'dense'. Vuttaparicchedato means 'according to the stated limit', that is, 'ten monks, and just ten pots of ghee'.

Gāthāyaṃ pāḷinti vinayapāḷiṃ. Aṭṭhakathañcevāti tassā aṭṭhakathañceva. Vicakkhaṇoti vividhaṃ atthaṃ cakkhati passatīti vicakkhaṇo. Evanti yathāvuttanayena. Tatrāyaṃ yojanā – evaṃ vicakkhaṇo bhikkhu pāḷiṃ, aṭṭhakathañceva oloketvā appamattova hutvā saṅghike paccaye bhājayeti.

In the verse, 'the Pāḷi' means the Vinaya Pāḷi. 'And the commentary' means 'and its commentary'. Vicakkhaṇa means 'one who sees various meanings', thus 'discerning'. Evaṃ means 'in the manner stated'. Herein, this is the application: 'Thus, a discerning monk, having examined the Pāḷi and its commentary, and being heedful, should distribute the requisites belonging to the Saṅgha'.

Iti paccayabhājanīyakathāya yojanā samattā.

Thus concludes the explanation of the construction for the discourse on the distribution of requisites.

Upaḍḍhabhāgoti bhikkhūnaṃ laddhabhāgato upaḍḍho bhāgo. Sesaṃ suviññeyyameva.

Upaḍḍhabhāgo means 'a half share from the portion received by the monks'. The rest is indeed easily understood.

Iti senāsanakkhandhakavaṇṇanāya yojanā samattā.

Thus concludes the explanation of the construction for the commentary on the chapter concerning lodgings.

7. Saṅghabhedakakkhandhakaṃ

7. The Chapter on Schism in the Saṅgha

Chasakyapabbajjākathā

The Story of the Going Forth of the Six Sakyans

330. Saṅghabhedakakkhandhake abhiññātā abhiññātāti ettha abhipubbo ñātasaddo pākaṭatthoti āha “pākaṭā pākaṭā”ti. Kāḷudāyippabhūtayoti kāḷudāyiādayo. Parivārehi saddhiṃ dasa dūtā ca aññe ca bahū janā sakyakumārā nāmāti yojanā. Amhesūti [M 0.0516] sakyakulasaṅkhātesu amhesu, niddhāraṇe bhummaṃ. Iminā pāṭhasesaṃ dasseti. “Kulato”ti iminā “kulā”ti ettha nissakkatthe nissakkavacananti dasseti. Gharāvāsatthanti ettha ghare āvasantānaṃ manussānaṃ kiccanti dassento āha “gharāvāse ya”ntiādi. Tattha yanti yaṃkiñci. Udakaṃ ninnetabbanti ettha udakaṃ nīharitvā netabbaṃ apanetabbanti dassento āha “yathā udakaṃ sabbaṭṭhānesu susaṃ hotī”ti. Susanti sukkhaṃ. Tiṇānīti sassadūsakāni tiṇāni. “Uddharitabbānī”ti iminā niddhāpetabbanti ettha dhudhātuyā papphoṭanadhaṃsanatthe dasseti[V 2.0154]. Bhusāti sassanāḷadaṇḍā, tehi missā palālā bhusikā. Ophuṇāpetabbanti ettha phuṇadhātuyā avakiraṇatthaṃ dassento āha “apanetabba”nti. Tvaññeva gharāvāsatthena upajānāti ettha gharāvāsatthenāti upayogatthe karaṇavacanaṃ. Upajānāti upatyūpasaggo dhātvatthānuvattako, hivibhatti ca lopo hoti, tena vuttaṃ “tvaññeva gharāvāsatthaṃ jānāhī”ti. Ahanti bhaddiyakumāranāmako ahaṃ. Tayāti anuruddhakumāranāmakena tayā. “Saddhiṃ pabbajissāmī”ti iminā pāṭhasesaṃ dasseti. Sesanti “saddhiṃ pabbajissāmī”ti vacanaṃ.

330. In the chapter on schism in the Saṅgha, regarding 'abhiññātā abhiññātā', here the word 'ñāta' preceded by 'abhi' has the meaning of 'evident'; thus he says, 'pākaṭā pākaṭā' (evident, evident). 'Kāḷudāyippabhūtayo' means Kāḷudāyi and others. The construction is: 'Ten messengers, along with their retinues, and many other people, namely the Sakyan princes'. 'Amhesu' means 'among us', who are counted as the Sakya clan; this is the locative case used for determination. By this, he indicates the remainder of the text. By 'kulato', he shows that 'kulā' here is an ablative form in the sense of separation. Regarding 'gharāvāsatthanti', while showing this means 'the duty of people dwelling in a house', he says 'gharāvāse yaṃ', etc. Therein, 'yaṃ' means 'whatever'. Regarding 'udakaṃ ninnetabbaṃ', while showing that water should be drawn out and removed, he says, 'so that the water may be thoroughly dry in all places'. 'Susaṃ' means 'dry'. 'Tiṇāni' means weeds that spoil the crops. By 'uddharitabbāni', while indicating 'niddhāpetabbaṃ', he shows that the root 'dhu' has the meaning of shaking off and destroying. 'Bhusā' means the stalks and stems of grain; straw mixed with these is 'bhusikā'. Regarding 'ophuṇāpetabbaṃ', while showing that the root 'phuṇa' has the meaning of scattering, he says 'apanetabbaṃ' (should be removed). In 'tvaññeva gharāvāsatthena upajānāti', 'gharāvāsatthena' is the instrumental case in the sense of purpose. In 'upajānāti', the prefix 'upa' follows the meaning of the root, and the 'hi' ending is elided; therefore it is said, 'tvaññeva gharāvāsatthaṃ jānāhi' (you yourself know the purpose of household life). 'Ahaṃ' means 'I, the prince named Bhaddiya'. 'Tayā' means 'by you, the prince named Anuruddha'. By 'saddhiṃ pabbajissāmī', he indicates the remainder of the text. 'Sesaṃ' means the statement 'saddhiṃ pabbajissāmī' (I will go forth with you).

331. Nippātitāti ettha nikkhamitvā gamāpitāti dassento āha “nikkhāmitā”ti. Mānassinoti ettha mānaṃ sayanti nissayantīti mānassinoti dassento āha “mānassayino”ti.

331. Regarding 'nippātitā', showing that it means 'having gone out, they were made to go', he says 'nikkhāmitā' (caused to go out). Regarding 'mānassino', showing that it means 'they lie on, they depend on, pride', he says 'mānassayino' (those who depend on pride).

332. Yassantarato na santi kopāti ettha antarasaddo cittavācako, topaccayo ca sattamyatthavācakoti dassento āha “yassa citte”ti. Kasmā kopā na santīti āha “tatiyamaggena samūhatattā”ti. Anāgāmimaggena dosassa samūhatattā yassa khīṇāsavassa citte kopā na santīti adhippāyo. Iti bhavābhavatañca vītivattoti ettha atthaṃ dassento āha “yasmā panā”tiādi. Tattha yasmā pana vuccati, tasmā evamattho daṭṭhabboti yojanā[M 0.0517]. Vibhavoti pāpaṃ vuccatīti sambandho. Nanu pāḷiyaṃ “vibhavo”ti natthi, “abhavo”ti eva atthi, atha kasmā “vibhavoti abhavo”ti vuttanti āha “vibhavoti ca abhavoti ca atthato ekamevā”ti. Iminā saddatoyeva nānanti dasseti. Yā esā bhavābhavatā vuccatīti sambandho. “Anekappakārā”ti iminā itisaddassa pakāratthaṃ dasseti. Catūhipi maggehi vītivattoti sambandho. Tassāti khīṇāsavassa.

332. Regarding 'yassantarato na santi kopā' (in whose interior there are no angers), here the word 'antara' denotes the mind, and the suffix '-to' denotes the locative sense; thus he says, 'yassa citte' (in whose mind). Why are there no angers? He says, 'because they have been eradicated by the third path'. The intention is that, because aversion has been eradicated by the path of non-returning, there are no angers in the mind of that one whose taints are destroyed. Regarding 'iti bhavābhavatañca vītivatto' (thus having transcended the state of existence and non-existence), while explaining the meaning, he says 'yasmā pana', etc. The construction there is: since it is said..., therefore the meaning should be understood thus. The connection is: 'vibhava' is called 'evil'. But is it not so that in the Pāḷi the term 'vibhava' does not exist, only 'abhava' exists? So why is it said, 'vibhava means abhava'? He says, 'because vibhava and abhava are one and the same in meaning'. By this, he shows that they differ only in the word. The connection is: 'that which is called the state of existence and non-existence'. By 'of various kinds', he shows that the word 'iti' has the sense of 'type'. The connection is: 'transcended by the four paths'. 'Tassa' means 'of him', the one whose taints are destroyed.

333. Ahimekhalikāti mekhalā viya mekhalikā, ahimeva mekhalikā ahimekhalikā. Tamevatthaṃ dassento āha “ahiṃ kaṭiyaṃ bandhitvā”ti.

333. 'Ahimekhalikā': a 'mekhalikā' is like a 'mekhalā' (girdle); the snake ('ahi') itself is the girdle, hence 'ahimekhalikā'. Explaining this very meaning, he says, 'having bound a snake around the waist'.

334. Sammannatīti ettha “sammānetī”ti curādigaṇikadhātuvasena vattabbe divādigaṇikadhātuvasena vuttanti dassento āha “sammānetī”ti. Acinteyyo hi pāḷinayo. Sammānetīti sammānaṃ karoti. Yanti kammaṃ. Soti satthā. Iminā yaṃ tumoti ettha tumoti ruḷhīsaddo idha “so”ti sabbanāmasaddena sadisatthoti dasseti.

334. Regarding 'sammannati', showing that although 'sammāneti' from the curādi group of verbal roots should be said, it is stated as from the divādi group, he says 'sammāneti'. For the way of the Pāḷi is indeed inconceivable. 'Sammāneti' means 'he pays honor'. 'Yaṃ' is the object. 'So' is the Teacher. By this he shows that in 'yaṃ tumo', the word 'tumo' is a conventional term that here has the same meaning as the pronoun 'so'.

Pakāsanīyakammādikathā

The Discourse on the Act of Proclamation and so forth.

336. “Kheḷasadisā”ti [V 2.0155] iminā micchājīvena uppannapaccayānaṃ sadisūpacārena kheḷabhāvaṃ dasseti. Tasmā kheḷā viyāti kheḷo, micchājīvapaccayā, kheḷe asati bhakkhati ajjhoharatīti kheḷāsakoti vacanattho kātabbo. Etarahi pāḷiyaṃ, aṭṭhakathāyañca “kheḷāpakassā”ti oṭṭhajena paṭhamakkharena pāṭho atthi.

336. By 'like spittle', he shows, by way of simile, that requisites obtained through wrong livelihood are like spittle. Therefore, the meaning of the word 'kheḷāsaka' should be constructed thus: 'like spittle' are the requisites of wrong livelihood; he who eats and consumes that spittle is a 'kheḷāsaka'. Nowadays, in the Pāḷi and the commentary, there is the reading 'kheḷāpakassa', with the first letter being a labial.

340. Patthaddhenāti ettha bhūso thaddho patthaddho, bāḷhathaddhoti attho. Tena vuttaṃ “niccalenā”ti. Potthakarūpasadisenāti ettha potthakarūpaṃ nāma vatthadantādimayaṃ, tena sadiso potthakarūpasadiso, tena.

340. Regarding 'patthaddhena', here 'patthaddha' means 'bhūso thaddho' (very stiff); the meaning is 'extremely stiff'. Therefore it is said, 'niccalena' (unwavering). Regarding 'potthakarūpasadisena' (like a sculpted figure), here a 'potthakarūpa' is something made of cloth, ivory, or the like; one similar to that is 'potthakarūpasadiso'; 'tena' means by that.

342. Rājañātakā [M 0.0518] nāmāti ettha raññā jāniyanti “amhākaṃ garū”ti rājañātā, teyeva rājañātakāti attho daṭṭhabbo. Tadatthaṃ adhippāyena dassento āha “rājā amhe jānātī”tiādi. Pahaṭṭhakaṇṇavāloti pahaṭṭho kaṇṇo ca vālo ca etassāti pahaṭṭhakaṇṇavālo. Bandhaniccaleti rajjuvallīhi bandho viya niccale, pahaṭṭhakaṇṇavāleti sambandho. “Katvā”ti iminā “abhidhāvī”ti pade kiriyāvisesanabhāvaṃ dasseti.

342. Regarding 'rājañātakā nāma', here 'rājañātā' are those who are known by the king as 'our revered ones'; the meaning should be understood as just 'rājañātakā'. Explaining that intended meaning, he says, 'rājā amhe jānāti' (the king knows us), etc. 'Pahaṭṭhakaṇṇavālo' means 'one whose ears and hair are thrilled'. In 'bandhaniccale' (unmoving as if bound), it means unmoving as if bound by ropes and creepers; this is connected with 'pahaṭṭhakaṇṇavālo'. By 'katvā', he shows that the word 'abhidhāvī' functions as an adverb.

Dukkhañhi kuñjara nāgamāsadoti ettha kuñjarasaddassa āmantanapadabhāvaṃ āvikaronto āha “bho kuñjarā”ti. Nāgasaddassa ahināgahatthināgesu pavattanato vuttaṃ “buddhanāga”nti. Āsadoti padassa ākodhena sadanaṃ upagamanaṃ āsadoti dassento āha “vadhakacittena upagamanaṃ nāmā”ti. Dukkhanti etarahi ca āyatiñca dukkhakāraṇaṃ. Dukkhaṃ hīti hisaddo padapūraṇamattaṃ, atha vā dukkhamevāti attho. “Buddhanāgaṃ ghātakassā”ti iminā nāgaṃ hanatīti nāgahatoti vacanatthaṃ dasseti.

Regarding 'dukkhañhi kuñjara nāgamāsado' (Indeed, O elephant, attacking a nāga is suffering), here, making clear that the word 'kuñjara' is a term of address, he says, 'bho kuñjara' (O elephant). Since the word 'nāga' is used for serpent-nāgas and elephant-nāgas, it is said, 'Buddha-nāga'. Regarding the word 'āsado', showing that 'āsado' means approaching and assailing with anger, he says, 'it means approaching with a mind bent on killing'. 'Dukkhaṃ' is the cause of suffering both now and in the future. Regarding 'dukkhaṃ hi', the word 'hi' is merely a particle to fill out the meter, or else it has the emphatic meaning 'suffering itself'. By 'to the killer of the Buddha-nāga', he shows the verbal meaning of 'nāgahato' as 'one who kills a nāga'.

Paṭikuṭiyova osakkīti ettha tathāgatassa paṭimukhaṃ kuṭena gamanametassāti paṭikuṭiyo, paṭikuṭiyo eva hutvā osakkīti dassento āha “tathāgatābhimukhoyeva piṭṭhimehi pādehi osakkī”ti. “Na jānātī”ti iminā lakkha dassanaṅkesūti dhātupāṭhesu (pāṇinī 1539 saddanītidhātumālāyaṃ 18 dakārantadhātu) vuttesu atthesu idha dassanatthoti dasseti. Na lakkhitabboti aññehi sappurisehi na lakkhitabboti attho. Ettha ṇyapaccayo kattukammesu hoti, yakārassa kakāraṃ katvā alakkhikoti vuttaṃ.

Regarding 'He retreated crookedly': here, paṭikuṭiyo means 'his going crookedly towards the Tathāgata'. Showing that he retreated while being crooked, it is said: 'While facing the Tathāgata, he retreated backwards.' By the phrase 'He does not know', it is shown that here the meaning of the root lakkha is 'seeing', from among the meanings such as 'seeing' and 'marking' stated in the Dhātupāṭha (Pāṇinī 1539; Saddanīti Dhātumālā 18, dakāra-ending roots). 'Not to be marked' means not to be marked by other virtuous people. Here, the ṇya-suffix occurs in the active and passive senses. Having changed the 'ya' to 'ka', the word alakkhiko is formed.

343. “Bhuñjitabbabhojana”nti [V 2.0156] iminā tikabhojananti ettha yupaccayassa kammatthabhāvaṃ dasseti. Tanti tikabhojanaṃ. Yathādhammoti “gaṇabhojane pācittiya”nti (pāci. 209) vuttāya mātikāvibhaṅgapāḷiyā anurūpaṃ[M 0.0519]. Pañcavatthuyācanakathāti pañca vatthūni yācanassa kathā. Āyukappanti avīcimahāniraye āyukappaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ. Avīcimahāniraye āyukappo nāma eko antarakappoti jinālaṅkāraṭīkādīsu (mi. pa. 4.1.3; kathā. aṭṭha. 654-657; itivu. aṭṭha. 18; sārattha. ṭī. cūḷavagga 3.343; a. ni. ṭī. 3.662) vutto. “Eko asaṅkhyeyyakappo”ti sammohavinodanādīsu (vibha. aṭṭha. 809; ma. ni. aṭṭha. 3.128; vi. vi. ṭī. 1.410; vajira. ṭī. pārājikaṇḍa 410) vutto. Seṭṭhaṃ puññanti mahantaṃ puññaṃ. Iminā brahaṃ puññanti brahasaddo mahantatthoti dasseti. Braha vuddhiyanti dhātupāṭhesu (pāṇinī 735; saddanītidhātumālāyaṃ 16 hakārantadhātu) vuttattā brahasaddo mahantavācako hoti. Brahadhātuto apaccayaṃ katvā “brahā”tipi, mapaccayaṃ katvā “brahmā”tipi pāṭho atthi. Āyukappamevāti saggesu āyukappameva.

343. By 'food to be eaten', it is shown that in the word tikabhojana (threefold food), the yu-suffix has a passive sense. Taṃ refers to the threefold food. 'According to the Dhamma' means in conformity with the Pāḷi of the Mātikāvibhaṅga, where it is said, 'In group-eating, there is a pācittiya offense' (Pāc. 209). 'A talk on the request for five items' means a talk on the request of five items. 'A life-span of an eon' is said with reference to a life-span of an eon in the great Avīci hell. A life-span of an eon in the great Avīci hell is said to be one intermediate eon (antarakappa) in the Jinālaṅkāraṭīkā and other texts (Mi. Pa. 4.1.3; Kathā. Aṭṭha. 654–657; Itivu. Aṭṭha. 18; Sārattha. Ṭī. Cūḷavagga 3.343; A. Ni. Ṭī. 3.662). It is said to be 'one incalculable eon' (asaṅkhyeyyakappa) in the Sammohavinodanī and other texts (Vibha. Aṭṭha. 809; Ma. Ni. Aṭṭha. 3.128; Vi. Vi. Ṭī. 1.410; Vajira. Ṭī. Pārājikaṇḍa 410). 'Highest merit' means great merit. By this, it is shown that in the phrase brahaṃ puññaṃ, the word braha means 'great'. Because it is said in the Dhātupāṭha, 'Braha in the sense of growth' (Pāṇinī 735; Saddanītidhātumālā 16, hakāra-ending roots), the word braha is a term for 'great'. From the root braha, by adding the a-suffix, there is also the reading 'brahā'; and by adding the ma-suffix, there is also the reading 'brahmā'. 'Only the life-span of an eon' means only the life-span of an eon in the heavens.

Saṅghabhedakathā

A Discourse on Schism in the Saṅgha

344. Soti devadatto, gato kirāti sambandho. Tatthevāti vihārasīmāyameva. Āveṇikanti bhikkhusaṅghato āveṇikaṃ.

344. 'So' refers to Devadatta; the connection is with 'gato kirā' (he has gone, it is said). 'There itself' means precisely within the monastery boundary. 'Āveṇikaṃ' means separate from the community of bhikkhus.

345. Āgilāyatīti ettha ātyūpasaggo abhibhavanattho, giledhātu bādhanatthoti āha “vedanābhibhūtā bādhatī”ti. Tanti piṭṭhiṃ. Parassa cittaṃ ādisitvā desayati etāyāti ādesanā, sā eva pāṭihāriyaṃ ādesanāpāṭihāriyaṃ. Anusāsati etāyāti anusāsanī, imamevatthaṃ dassento āha “evampi te”tiādi.

345. Regarding 'āgilāyati': here, the prefix ā has the meaning of overpowering, and the root gil has the meaning of afflicting; thus it is said, 'being overpowered by feeling, it afflicts.' Taṃ refers to the back. 'Having discerned another's mind, one teaches by means of this', thus it is ādesanā (instruction by mind-reading); that itself as a marvel is ādesanāpāṭihāriyaṃ (the marvel of instruction by mind-reading). 'One instructs by means of this', thus it is anusāsanī (instruction). To show this very meaning, it is said, 'even so for you,' and so forth.

346. Mamānukrubbanti ettha anutyūpasaggo anukiriyattho karadhātu antapaccayo gacchantādigaṇoti dassento āha “mamānukiriyaṃ kurumāno”ti. “Dukkhito”ti iminā kapaṇoti ettha kapadhātu hiṃsanatthoti dasseti. Mahāvarāhassāti varāhasaddassa sūkaratthaṃ paṭikkhipanto āha “mahānāgassā”ti. “Pathavi”nti iminā mahiṃ vikubbatoti ettha mahīsaddassa evaṃnāmakaṃ mahānadiṃ [M 0.0520] paṭikkhipati. “Padālentassā”ti iminā karadhātuyā vityūpasaggavasena padālanatthaṃ dasseti. Bhisaṃ [V 2.0157] ghasamānassāti ettha mānasaddo katvatthoti āha “bhisaṃ ghasantassā”ti. Ghasantassāti bhakkhantassa. Nadīnāmakaṃ taṃ pokkharaṇinti yojanā. Iminā nadīsu jaggatoti ettha nadī nāma pokkharaṇīti dasseti. Jaggatoti hatthiyūthaṃ pālentassa.

346. Regarding 'mamānukrubbaṃ': to show that here the prefix anu has the meaning of imitation, that the root is kar with the suffix anta, and that it belongs to the gacchantādi group, it is said, 'imitating me.' By 'afflicted' (dukkhito), it shows that in the word 'wretched' (kapaṇo), the root kap has the meaning of harming. Regarding 'of the great varāha': rejecting the meaning 'boar' for the word varāha, it is said, 'of the great elephant (nāga)'. By 'earth' (pathavi), it rejects that the word mahī in the phrase 'disturbing the mahī' refers to the great river of that name. By 'of one who is splitting' (padālentassa), it shows the meaning of splitting by means of the prefix vi with the root kar. Regarding 'of one eating lotus roots' (bhisaṃ ghasamānassa): here, the suffix -māna has the sense of an action, thus it is said, 'eating lotus roots' (bhisaṃ ghasantassa). 'Of one eating' (ghasantassa) means of one consuming. The connection is: 'that lotus pond named after a river'. By this, it shows that in the phrase 'he guards in the rivers', 'river' means a lotus pond. 'Of one who guards' (jaggato) means of one protecting a herd of elephants.

347. “Sutāti sotā”ti iminā pāḷiyā dvidhābhāvaṃ dasseti. “Nissandeho”ti iminā asandiddhoti ettha dihadhātuṃ dasseti, disadhātuṃ nivatteti.

347. By 'sutā ti sotā', it shows the twofold nature of the Pāḷi text. By 'without doubt' (nissandeho), it shows that in the word asandiddho, the root is dih, and it excludes the root dis.

350. Buddhasahassenapīti pisaddo garahattho, pageva ekena buddhenāti dasseti.

350. Regarding 'even with a thousand Buddhas' (buddhasahassenapi): the particle pi is used in the sense of censure, showing: how much more so with a single Buddha.

“Satto”ti iminā kocisaddassa padhānapadaṃ dasseti. Aṭṭhāti ākhyātapadassa atthaṃ dassento āha “ṭhito”ti. Devadattoti me sutanti ettha “me”ti padaṃ bhagavantaṃ sandhāya vuttanti āha “bhagavatā”ti. Tadevāti sutameva. Idanti “devadattoti me suta”nti vacanaṃ. Anucinātīti anuvaḍḍheti. “Patvā”ti iminā āsajjananti ettha sadadhātuyā gatyatthaṃ, kiriyāvisesanañca dasseti. Avīcinirayaṃ pattoti ettha idāni na devadatto avīcinirayaṃ patto hoti, āyatiṃ pana avīciniraye avassambhāviyattā “avīcinirayaṃ patto”ti vuttanti āha “āsaṃsāyaṃ atītavacana”nti. Āsaṃsāyanti avassambhāviyatthe. Bhesmā hi udadhī mahāti ettha bhesmāsaddo bhayānakapariyāyoti āha “bhayānako”ti.

By 'a being' (satto), it indicates the principal word for 'someone' (koci). Regarding 'aṭṭhā': showing the meaning of the verb, it says 'stood' (ṭhito). In 'I have heard this about Devadatta', the word 'me' is said with reference to the Blessed One; thus it says 'by the Blessed One'. 'That very thing' (tadeva) means 'just what was heard'. 'This' (idaṃ) refers to the statement 'I have heard this about Devadatta'. 'Anucināti' means 'he increases'. By 'having reached' (patvā), it shows that in the word āsajjana, the root sad has the meaning of motion, and it also indicates an adverbial modifier. Regarding 'he has reached the Avīci hell': here, Devadatta has not yet reached the Avīci hell, but because it is inevitable that he will be in the Avīci hell in the future, it is said 'he has reached the Avīci hell'. Thus it is called 'a past tense statement in the sense of expectation'. 'In the sense of expectation' means in the sense of inevitability. In 'For the great ocean is awesome', the word bhesmā is a synonym for 'terrifying'; thus it says 'fearful'.

Upālipañhākathā

A Discourse on Upāli's Question

351. Ekatoti ettha topaccayassa sattamyatthe pavattabhāvaṃ dassento āha “dhammavādīpakkhe”ti. “Anunayanto”ti iminā anussāvetīti [M 0.0521] ettha anusaddassa atthaṃ dasseti. Anunayantoti punappunaṃ nayanto. Sāvanākāraṃ dassento āha “na tumhākaṃyevā”tiādi. Ayaṃ adhammo vā ayaṃ avinayo vā idaṃ asatthusāsanaṃ vā yadi bhaveyyāti yojanā. “Bodhetī”ti iminā sāvetīti ettha sudhātuyā atthaṃ dasseti. “Anussāvetvā”ti iminā “anussāveti, salākaṃ gāhetī”ti ettha anussāvanakiriyā pubbabhāge pavattā, salākaggāhakiriyā pacchābhāgeti dasseti.

351. Regarding 'ekato': to show that the suffix -to occurs in the sense of the locative case, it says 'on the side of the Dhamma-speaker.' By 'persuading' (anunayanto), it shows the meaning of the prefix anu in the word anussāveti. 'Persuading' means leading again and again. Showing the manner of the announcement, it says, 'It is not only yours,' and so forth. The connection is: 'If this were non-Dhamma, or this were non-Discipline, or this were not the Teacher's teaching.' By 'he makes known' (bodheti), it shows the meaning of the root su in sāveti. By 'having announced', it shows that in the phrase 'he announces, he has the voting-tickets taken', the action of announcing occurs in the first part, and the action of taking the voting-tickets occurs in the latter part.

Ettāvatāti ettakena anussāvanasalākaggāhamattena. Na pana saṅgho bhinno hoti, anussāvetvā [V 2.0158] salākaṃ gāhetvā āveṇikaṃ saṅghakamme kateyeva saṅgho bhinno hotīti adhippāyo.

'By this much' means by merely this much: the announcement and the taking of voting-tickets. But the Saṅgha is not yet divided. The intention is that the Saṅgha is divided only when, after announcing and having the voting-tickets taken, a separate community act is performed.

Ettha ṭhatvā kassaci codakassa anuyogo siyāti yojanā. Kinti siyāti āha “evaṃ devadatto”tiādi. Tattha evanti pakatatte saṅghe bhinde satīti attho. Kathanti kenākārena. Puna kathanti kasmā kāraṇā. Raññoti ajātasatturañño, kāritakammaṃ. “Ghātāpitattā”ti bimbisārarājānaṃ ghātāpitattā. Tatthāti “bhikkhu kho upālī”tiādivacane, ṭhatvā parihāraṃ vadāmāti yojanā. Viraddhattāti virādhitattā. Tamatthaṃ vitthārento āha “tena hī”tiādi. Tattha tena hīti uyyojanatthe nipāto. Evañhīti evameva. Tassāti devadattassa. Kumāro panāti ajātasattukumāro pana, katamatteyeva na vuttāti sambandho. Tassāti devadattassa. Tasmāti yasmā saṅghabhedato pubbe ruhituppādakammaṃ karontassāpi pacchā abhabbabhāvo ropito, tasmā.

The connection is: 'Standing on this point, there might be an accusation from some accuser.' How might it be? It says, 'Thus, Devadatta,' and so forth. There, 'thus' means 'when the Saṅgha, being as it was, was split'. 'How?' means 'in what manner?'. 'Again, how?' means 'for what reason?'. 'Of the king' refers to King Ajātasattu's instigated act. 'Because he had him killed' means because he had King Bimbisāra killed. Regarding 'tatthā': the connection is 'in that statement beginning "Indeed, bhikkhu Upāli," standing there, I will give a refutation'. 'Because of failure' (viraddhattā) means 'because of having failed' (virādhitattā). Elaborating on that meaning, it says, 'Well then,' and so forth. There, 'tena hi' is a particle in the sense of prompting. 'Evañhi' means 'just so'. 'But the prince' refers to Prince Ajātasattu; the connection is 'it was not said at the very point of the deed'. 'His' refers to Devadatta. 'Therefore' means: because, even for one who performed an act that produces a wound before the schism of the Saṅgha, the state of being incapable was later established, therefore...

Bhedakaravatthūsu evaṃ vinicchayo veditabboti yojanā. Dhammādhammādīnaṃ suttantavinayapariyāyena visesaṃ dassento āha “suttantapariyāyenā”tiādi. Tattha suttantapariyāyenāti suttantadesanāya, suttantadesanānayatoti vuttaṃ hoti. Tathāti tato aññathā.

In cases of schism, the judgment should be understood to be thus—this is the connection. To show the distinction between Dhamma and non-Dhamma, and so forth, through the method of the Suttanta and Vinaya, he says: 'by the method of the Suttanta,' and so forth. There, 'suttantapariyāyena' means 'by the teaching of the Suttanta,' or 'by the method of the Suttanta teaching'—this is said. 'Tathā' means 'differently.'

Tatthāti [M 0.0522] dvīsu dhammādhammesu. Evaṃ amhākanti evaṃ kariyamāne amhākaṃ. Evaṃ suttantapariyāyena dhammādhammānaṃ visesaṃ dassetvā idāni vinayapariyāyena tesaṃ taṃ dassento āha “vinayapariyāyena panā”tiādi. Bhūtena vatthunā kātabbanti sambandho. Evaṃ “abhūtena vatthunā”ti etthāpi.

There, that is, in the two things: Dhamma and non-Dhamma. 'Evaṃ amhākaṃ' means 'thus, when it is being done for us.' Having thus shown the distinction between Dhamma and non-Dhamma by the method of the Suttanta, now showing that same distinction by the method of the Vinaya, he says: 'but by the method of the Vinaya,' and so forth. The connection is: 'to be done with a true ground.' Thus also in 'with an untrue ground.'

Evaṃ dvinnaṃ pariyāyānaṃ vasena dhammādhammadukassa visesaṃ dassetvā idāni vinayāvinayadukassa visesaṃ dassento āha “suttantapariyāyenā”tiādi[V 2.0159]. Tattha suttantanayena rāgādayo vinetīti vinayo, vinayanayena kāyaṃ vācaṃ vinetīti vinayoti vacanattho kātabbo.

Having thus shown the distinction of the Dhamma-non-Dhamma pair by means of the two methods, now, showing the distinction of the Vinaya-non-Vinaya pair, he says: 'By the method of the Suttanta,' and so forth. Here, by the Suttanta method, it is called Vinaya because it removes lust and so forth; by the Vinaya method, it is called Vinaya because it restrains body and speech—this is the meaning of the word to be understood.

Evaṃ dvinnaṃ pariyāyānaṃ vasena vinayāvinayadukassa visesaṃ dassetvā idāni bhāsitābhāsitadukassa visesaṃ dassento āha “suttantapariyāyena cattāro satipaṭṭhānā”tiādi. Tattha “aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo”ti idaṃ vacanaṃ tathāgatena bhāsitaṃ lapitanti yojanā.

Having thus shown the distinction of the Vinaya-non-Vinaya pair by means of the two methods, now, showing the distinction of the spoken-unspoken pair, he says: 'By the Suttanta method, the four foundations of mindfulness,' and so forth. Here, the statement 'the eightfold path' is spoken and uttered by the Tathāgata—this is the connection.

Evaṃ dvinnaṃ pariyāyānaṃ vasena bhāsitābhāsitadukassa visesaṃ dassetvā idāni āciṇṇānāciṇṇadukassa visesaṃ dassento āha “suttantapariyāyena devasika”ntiādi. Tattha “devasika”nti padaṃ “samāpajjanaṃ, volokana”nti tīsuyeva padesu yojetabbaṃ. Aṭṭhuppattivasenāti kāraṇuppattivasena. Kāraṇañhi arati phalaṃ etasmāti atthoti vuccati, atthassa uppatti atthuppatti, sāyeva aṭṭhuppatti tthakārassa ṭṭhakāraṃ katvā, aṭṭhuppattiyā vaso aṭṭhuppattivaso, tena. Idaṃ padaṃ “suttantadesanā jātakakathā”ti dvīhipi padehi yojetabbaṃ. Idanti phalasamāpattisamāpajjanādi. Āciṇṇanti ā bandhitaṃ, punappunaṃ vā upacitaṃ vaḍḍhitaṃ, paguṇaṃ vā. Cāriyapakkamananti cāriyatthaṃ pakkamanaṃ.

Having thus shown the distinction of the spoken-unspoken pair by means of the two methods, now, showing the distinction of the practiced-unpracticed pair, he says: 'By the Suttanta method, daily,' and so forth. Herein, the word 'daily' should be applied to three terms only, which include 'attaining' and 'observing.' 'By way of the arising of the occasion' means by way of the arising of the cause. For the cause is called 'attha' because the result arises from it; the arising of the 'attha' is 'atthuppatti'. That very thing is 'aṭṭhuppatti', having changed the 'tth' to 'ṭṭh'; the state of 'aṭṭhuppatti' is 'aṭṭhuppattivasa,' by that. This term should be applied to both phrases: 'the teaching of the Suttanta' and 'the Jātaka stories.' 'This' refers to the attainment of fruition, entering into attainment, and so forth. 'Practiced' means bound, or repeatedly accumulated, increased, or proficient. 'Going forth for walking practice' means going out for the purpose of walking practice.

Evaṃ [M 0.0523] dvinnaṃ pariyāyānaṃ vasena āciṇṇānāciṇṇadukassa visesaṃ dassetvā idāni paññattadukassa visesaṃ dassento āha “suttantapariyāyena cattāro satipaṭṭhānā”tiādi. Taṃ bhāsitābhāsitadukasadisameva. Evaṃ dvinnaṃ suttantavinayapariyāyānaṃ vasena pañcannaṃ dukānaṃ viseso dassito.

Having thus shown the distinction of the practiced-unpracticed pair by means of the two methods, now, showing the distinction of the laid-down pair, he says: 'By the Suttanta method, the four foundations of mindfulness,' and so forth. This is similar to the spoken-unspoken pair. Thus, by means of the two methods of Suttanta and Vinaya, the distinction of the five pairs has been shown.

Āpattānāpattiduke “na mocanādhippāyassā”ti pāṭhassa anantare pacchimavākye ṭhito ādisaddo ānetabbo. Iti ādinā nayenāti hi attho. Tattha tatthāti tasmiṃ tasmiṃ sikkhāpade. Idaṃ padaṃ pacchimavākyepi anuvattetabbaṃ.

In the offense-non-offense pair, the word 'ādi' that is located in the final clause following the passage 'na mocanādhippāyassa' should be supplied. For the meaning is, 'by this method and so forth.' 'Therein, therein' refers to each training rule. This term should also be carried forward into the final clause.

Lahukagarukaduke pañcāpattikkhandhāti thullaccayapācittiyapāṭidesanīyadukkaṭadubbhāsitavasena pañca āpattirāsayo. Dve āpattikkhandhāti pārājikasaṅghādisesavasena dve āpattirāsayo.

In the light-heavy pair, 'the five groups of offenses' means the five aggregates of offenses: thullaccaya, pācittiya, pāṭidesanīya, dukkaṭa, and dubbhāsita. 'The two groups of offenses' means the two aggregates of offenses: pārājika and saṅghādisesa.

Sāvasesānāvasesaduke cha āpattikkhandhāti pārājikāpattito avasesā cha āpattirāsayo.

In the pair of offenses with and without a remainder, 'the six groups of offenses' means the six groups of offenses remaining apart from the pārājika offense.

Duṭṭhullāduṭṭhulladuke lahukagarukadukasadisameva. Ayaṃ pana viseso – garukāpatti duṭṭhullā nāma[V 2.0160], lahukāpatti aduṭṭhullā nāmāti evaṃ vinayapariyāyavaseneva catunnaṃ dukānaṃ viseso dassito.

The gross-non-gross pair is similar to the light-heavy pair. However, this is the distinction: a heavy offense is called a gross offense, while a light offense is called a non-gross offense. Thus, the distinction among the four pairs is shown by means of the Vinaya method only.

Etthāti “adhammaṃ dhammoti dīpentī”tiādivacane. Catunnaṃ saṅghakammānanti apalokanādivasena catunnaṃ saṅghakammānaṃ. Karontehi hetubhūtehi, hetvatthe cetaṃ karaṇavacanaṃ.

Here, it refers to statements such as, 'declaring what is not Dhamma as Dhamma.' Regarding the four Saṅgha acts, it refers to the four Saṅgha acts by way of proclamation and the like. By those performing them, being the cause; this is an instrumental term in the sense of cause.

Tatthāti “te imehī”tiādivacane. Apakassantīti ettha kasadhātussa gatyatthaṃ dassento āha “parisaṃ ākaḍḍhantī”ti. Vijaṭentīti vijaṭaṃ karonti, visuṃ karontīti attho. Ekamantaṃ ussādentīti ekasmiṃ ante ussadaṃ karonti. Avapakassantīti ettha dvinnaṃ upasaggānaṃ vasena ativiyattho daṭṭhabboti āha “ati viya ākaḍḍhantī”ti. Ativiyatthaṃ āvikaronto āha “yathā visaṃsaṭṭhāva [M 0.0524] honti, evaṃ karontī”ti. Yathāti yenākārena kariyamāneti sambandho. “Visu”nti iminā āveṇisaddo “visu”ntiatthavācako anipphannapāṭipadikoti dasseti. Vatthūsūti bhedakaravatthūsu. Imaṃ gaṇhathāti imaṃ vādaṃ gaṇhatha. Visunti āveṇiṃ. Imasmiṃ khandhake vuttavacanaṃ parivārapāḷiyā saṃsandento āha “parivāre panā”tiādi. Tattha pañcahi ākārehīti “kammena uddesena voharanto anussāvanena salākaggāhenā”ti (pari. 458) evaṃ pañcahi kāraṇehi. Tassāti parivāre vuttavacanassa. Idhāti imasmiṃ saṅghabhedakakkhandhake, vuttena iminā saṅghabhedalakkhaṇenāti yojanā. “Atthato nānākaraṇaṃ natthī”ti iminā saddato nānākaraṇaṃ atthīti dīpeti. Assāti saṅghabhedalakkhaṇassa. Taṃ pana nānākaraṇābhāvanti yojanā. Tatthevāti parivāre eva. Sabbatthāti sabbasmiṃ saṅghabhedakakkhandhake.

Here, 'tatthāti' refers to 'te imehī' and similar expressions. Regarding 'apakassanti,' here, showing the meaning of movement in the root 'kas,' he says: 'they drag the assembly away.' 'Vijaṭentīti' means they disentangle, they make things distinct—this is the meaning. 'Ekamantaṃ ussādentīti' means they create a prominence on one side. Regarding 'avapakassanti,' here, due to the force of two prefixes, the meaning of 'excessively' should be understood, as he says: 'they pull away excessively.' Explaining the meaning of 'excessively,' he says: 'they act so that they are completely unmingled.' 'Yathāti' is connected to 'in which manner it is done.' By 'visuṃ,' he shows that the word 'āveṇi' is an underived nominal stem meaning 'visuṃ' (separately). 'Vatthūsūti' means in matters causing schism. 'Imaṃ gaṇhathāti' means 'accept this doctrine.' 'Visunti' means 'āveṇiṃ' (separately). Correlating what is said in this chapter with the Parivāra text, he states: 'but in the Parivāra...' etc. There, 'by five modes' means by five reasons: 'by an act, by recitation, by a transaction, by an announcement, by taking of voting-tickets' (Pari. 458). 'Tassāti' refers to the statement made in the Parivāra. 'Idhāti' means in this chapter on schism in the Saṅgha; the connection is with this characteristic of schism that has been stated. By 'Atthato nānākaraṇaṃ natthī' (there is no difference in meaning), he indicates that there is a difference in wording. 'Assāti' refers to the characteristic of schism. But that is the absence of difference—this is the connection. 'Tatthevāti' means precisely in the Parivāra. 'Sabbatthāti' means throughout this entire chapter on schism in the Saṅgha.

Iti saṅghabhedakakkhandhakavaṇṇanāya yojanā samattā.

Thus the syntactical explanation in the commentary on the chapter on schism in the Saṅgha is concluded.

8. Vattakkhandhakaṃ

8. The Chapter on Duties

1. Āgantukavattakathā

1. The Discourse on the Duties for Incoming Monks

357. Vattakkhandhake [V 2.0161] ārāmanti upacārasīmaṃ sandhāya vuttanti āha “upacārasīmasamīpa”nti. “Gahetvā”ti padassa “upāhanā”ti kammaṃ pākaṭaṃ, karaṇaṃ pana apākaṭaṃ. Tasmā karaṇaṃ dassento āha “upāhanadaṇḍakena gahetvā”ti. Iminā “hatthenā”ti karaṇaṃ nivatteti. Paṭikkamantīti ettha pavisantīti ca apakkamantīti ca atthaṃ paṭikkhipanto āha “sannipatantī”ti. Upāhanā…pe… pucchitabbāti ettha “pucchitabbā”ti padassa saha kammena pucchitabbākāraṃ dassento āha “katarasmiṃ ṭhāne”tiādi. Tattha “katarasmiṃ…pe… coḷaka”nti iminā pucchitabbākāraṃ dasseti. “Āvāsikā bhikkhū”ti iminā kammaṃ dasseti. “Pattharitabba”nti iminā vissajjetabbanti ettha sajadhātuyā cajanatthaṃ [M 0.0525] paṭikkhipati. Gocaro pucchitabboti ettha gocarasaddo bhikkhācārasaddena atthato ekanti dassento āha “bhikkhācāro pucchitabbo”ti. Bhikkhāya caranti etthāti bhikkhācāro, gocaragāmo. Yatthāti yasmiṃ gāme. “Ki”ntiādinā pānīyaṃ pucchitabbantiādīsu pucchitabbākāraṃ dasseti. Kaṃ kālanti kasmiṃ kāle.

357. In the chapter on duties, regarding 'monastery', it is said with reference to the boundary of the monastery: 'near the boundary of the monastery.' For the word 'gahetvā' (taking), the object 'upāhanā' (footwear) is clear, but the instrument is not clear. Therefore, showing the instrument, it is said: 'taking with a shoe-stick.' By this, he excludes the instrument 'by hand.' Regarding 'paṭikkamantīti,' here, rejecting the meanings of both 'entering' and 'leaving,' it is said: 'assembling.' Regarding 'Upāhanā...pe... pucchitabbā' (footwear... should be asked)—here, showing the manner of asking along with the object of the question, it is said: 'in which place,' etc. There, by 'katarasmiṃ...pe... coḷaka' he shows the manner of asking. By 'āvāsikā bhikkhū' (resident monks) he shows the object. By 'pattharitabba' (should be spread out), he rejects the meaning of abandoning for the root saj in the word 'vissajjetabba' (should be released). Regarding 'gocaro pucchitabbo' (the alms-range should be asked)—here, showing that the word 'gocara' is one in meaning with the word 'bhikkhācāra,' it is said: 'the alms-round should be asked.' 'Bhikkhācāro' is where they wander for alms, the village for alms. 'Yatthāti' means in which village. By 'kiṃ' and so forth, in 'drinking water should be asked,' etc., he shows the manner of asking. 'Kaṃ kālaṃ' means at which time.

Bahi nikkhamantassāti vihārato bahi nikkhamantassa. Nilloketabboti oloketabbo. “Yadi sakkotī”ti iminā sace ussahatīti ettha sacesaddo yadipariyāyo, ussahatisaddo sakkoti pariyāyoti dasseti. Sakkontassa vihārasodhanavatteti sambandho.

'Bahi nikkhamantassa' means of one who is going out from the monastery. 'Nilloketabbo' means one should look around. By 'yadi sakkoti,' it is shown that in 'sace ussahati,' the word 'sace' is a synonym for 'yadi,' and the word 'ussahati' is a synonym for 'sakkoti.' The connection is with 'the duty of cleaning the monastery for one who is able.'

2. Āvāsikavattakathā

2. The Discourse on the Duties of Resident Monks

359. Āvāsikavatte evaṃ vinicchayo veditabboti yojanā. Sabbaṃ kātabbanti sambandho. Tassāti vuḍḍhatarassa āgantukassa. “Paṇḍito”tiādinā sace bālo “sammajjāhi tāva cetiyaṅgaṇa”nti na vadati, sammajjaniṃ nikkhipitvā tassa vattameva kātabbanti dasseti. Bhesajjameva kātabbanti sahāvadhāraṇena vuttattā bālo “karohi tāva bhesajja”nti avadantopi bhesajjameva kātabbaṃ. “Paṇḍito hī”tiādinā pana āgantukassa vattabbabhāvamattameva [V 2.0162] dasseti. Pāḷimuttakavattaṃ dassento āha “apicā”tiādi. Bījanenāti bījaniyā. “Bījana”nti hi napuṃsakaliṅgo, “bījanī”ti itthiliṅgo. “Bījitabbo”ti ca “bījitabba”nti ca iminā aṭṭhakathāvacanena bījiyati anenāti bījanaṃ, bījiyati etāyāti bījanīti vacanattho kātabbo. Assāti vuḍḍhataraāgantukassa. Makkhetabbāti añjetabbā. Hīti saccaṃ. Etthāti upāhanapuñchane. Katthāti kasmiṃ vihāre. Pucchitena āvāsikenāti sambandho.

359. In the duties of residents, the decision should be understood thus—this is the construction. The connection is: 'Everything must be done.' 'Tassāti' refers to the more senior incoming guest. With 'paṇḍito' (if he is wise), etc., it is shown that if a foolish one does not say, 'First, sweep the courtyard of the shrine,' then having set aside the broom, only the duty towards him should be performed. Because 'bhesajjameva kātabbaṃ' (only the medicine should be prepared) is said with emphasis, even if a foolish one does not say, 'Prepare the medicine first,' the medicine alone should be prepared. But with 'paṇḍito hi' (for he is wise), etc., it merely shows that this is something that should be said to the incoming guest. Explaining a duty not mentioned in the Pāli Canon, he says, 'apicā' (moreover), etc. 'Bījanenāti' means with a fan (bījaniyā). For 'bījana' is of neuter gender, while 'bījanī' is of feminine gender. And by this statement of the commentary, 'bījitabbo' and 'bījitabba', the meaning of the words should be understood as: 'bījanaṃ' is that by which one fans, and 'bījanī' is that with which one fans. 'Assāti' refers to the more senior incoming guest. 'Makkhetabbāti' means they should be anointed. 'Hīti' means truly. 'Etthāti' refers to in the wiping of sandals. 'Katthāti' means in which monastery. The connection is: by the resident who was asked.

“Attano santikaṃ…pe… na labhatī”ti iminā attānaṃ sandhāya anāgacchantopi attano santikaṃ sampattassa āgantukassa vattaṃ akātuṃ na labhatīti dasseti.

By 'Attano santikaṃ…pe… na labhatī' (To one's own presence... one is not permitted), it is shown that even if a guest does not come specifically for oneself, one is not permitted to fail to perform the duties for a guest who has arrived in one's presence.

3. Gamikavattakathā

3. The Discourse on the Observances for a Traveler

360. Gamikavatte [M 0.0526] evaṃ vinicchayo veditabboti yojanā. Tatthāti senāsanakkhandhake. Taṃ sabbaṃ paṭisāmetvāti sambandho. Yattha yesu pāsāṇapiṭṭhipāsāṇatthambhesu upacikā nārohanti, tassaṃ pāsāṇapiṭṭhiyaṃ vā tesu pāsāṇatthambhesu vā yaṃ katasenāsanaṃ atthi, taṃ anāpucchantassāpi anāpattīti yojanā. Catūsu pāsāṇesūtiādi vuttanti sambandho, upacikānaṃ uppattiṭṭhāne kateti sambandho. Ayanti ānisaṃso. Ovassakagehe pana ṭhapitānaṃ mañcapīṭhānanti sambandho.

360. In the observance for a traveler, the decision should be understood thus—this is the construction. ‘There’ refers to the chapter on lodgings. The connection is: ‘Having put away all that.’ Where termites do not climb on stone platforms or stone pillars, on that stone platform or on those stone pillars, whatever lodging has been made, there is no offense even for one who does not ask—this is the construction. The connection is: 'it is said, "Among the four stones," etc.'; the connection is: 'made in the place where termites originate.' This is the benefit. But the connection is with 'couches and chairs placed in a rain-shelter.'

4. Anumodanavattakathā

4. The Discourse on the Observance of Anumodanā

362. Iddhaṃ ahosīti ettha idhadhātuyā vaḍḍhanatthaṃ paṭikkhipanto āha “sampannaṃ ahosī”ti. Saṅghatthere nisinneti sambandho. Anuthere anumodanatthāya nisinneti yojanā. Saṅghattherena ajjhiṭṭhepīti sambandho. Anumodako vadatīti sambandho. Anu punappunaṃ, pacchā vā dāyake dhammakathāya modetīti anumodako. “Gacchathā”ti sace vadati anumodakoti yojanā. Tassāti anumodakassa. Manussā kārentīti sambandho. “Ekenā”ti padaṃ “kārentī”ti pade kāritakammaṃ. Tassāti kāritabhikkhussa. Anumodanatoti anumodanakāraṇā. Upanisinnakathāti upasamīpe nisinnānaṃ kathiyati etāyāti upanisinnakathā. Anumodanāyāti anumodanatthāya. Ajjhiṭṭhovāti sayaṃ ajjhiṭṭho eva. Etthāti anumodanavatthusmiṃ. “Sañjātavacco”ti iminā vacco sañjāto imassāti vaccitoti katvā sañjātatthe ita paccayoti dasseti.

362. Regarding ‘iddhaṃ ahosi’ (it was prosperous): here, rejecting the meaning of growth for the root idh, he says, ‘sampannaṃ ahosi’ (it was well-provided). The connection is: ‘seated with the elder of the Sangha.’ The construction is: ‘seated for the purpose of giving anumodanā to the next senior monk.’ The connection is: ‘even when requested by the elder of the Sangha.’ The connection is: ‘The one who performs anumodanā speaks.’ ‘Anu’ means repeatedly or later; he delights the donors with a Dhamma talk—thus, he is an ‘anumodako’ (one who performs anumodanā). If he says, ‘Go,’ the construction is: he is the one who performs anumodanā. ‘Tassāti’ refers to the one who performs anumodanā.
