The connection is: ‘People have it done.’ The word ‘ekena’ (by one) is the causative object in the word ‘kārenti’ (they have it done). ‘Tassāti’ refers to the monk who is made to do it. ‘Anumodanatoti’ means because of the anumodanā. ‘Upanisinnakathā’ (a talk for those seated nearby) is so called because by it, it is spoken to those seated nearby. ‘Anumodanāyāti’ means for the purpose of anumodanā. ‘Ajjhiṭṭho vāti’ (or requested) means being requested oneself. ‘Etthāti’ refers to this matter of anumodanā. By ‘sañjātavacco’ (one for whom the need to relieve oneself has arisen), he shows that the suffix ita is in the sense of ‘arisen’, by making the derivation ‘vacco sañjāto imassā’ti vaccito’ (the need has arisen for him, thus he is vaccito).

5. Bhattaggavattakathā

5. The Discourse on the Observance of the Meal Hall

364. Bhattaggavatteti [V 2.0163] bhattaṃ gaṇhanti etthāti bhattaggaṃ, parivisanaṭṭhānaṃ. Tasmiṃ kattabbaṃ vattaṃ bhattaggavattaṃ, tasmiṃ bhattaggavatte evaṃ vinicchayo veditabboti [M 0.0527] yojanā. Manussānaṃ parivisanaṭṭhānaṃ nāma yattha manussā saputtadārā āvasitvā bhikkhūbhojenti. “Atiallīyitvā”ti iminā anupakhajjāti ettha khadadhātussa hiṃsanaṃ nāma atiallīyananti dasseti. Āsanesu satīti āsanesu santesu. Nisīdantassa navakassāti sambandho. Āpajjatīti āpattiṃ āpajjati. Āpucchite ananujānanto thero āpajjatīti yojanā. Saṅghāṭinti pārutasaṅghāṭiṃ.

364. Regarding ‘bhattaggavatta’ (meal hall observance): ‘bhattagga’ (meal hall) is where food is received, that is, the serving place. The observance to be performed there is the meal hall observance. In that meal hall observance, the decision should be understood thus—this is the construction. The serving place for people is where people, along with their children and wives, reside and feed the monks. By ‘atiallīyitvā’ (by being too familiar), he shows that for the root khad in ‘anupakhajja’ (intruding), 'harming' means 'excessive familiarity.' ‘Āsanesu satīti’ means when seats exist. The connection is: ‘for the newly ordained one who is sitting.’ ‘Āpajjatīti’ means he incurs an offense. The construction is: ‘The elder who does not grant permission when asked incurs an offense.’ ‘Saṅghāṭinti’ means the worn outer robe.

Pattadhovanaudakanti bhuñjanatthāya pattānaṃ dhovanaudakaṃ. Gahetabbanti hatthena gahetabbaṃ.

‘Pattadhovanaudakaṃ’ (bowl-washing water) means the water for washing bowls for the purpose of eating. ‘Gahetabbanti’ means it should be taken with the hand.

Yathā gaṇhiyamāneti yojanā. Mattāyāti pamāṇāya. Sabbiādīsu evāti evasaddo ajjhāharitabbo. Sabbiādīsūti sabbitelauttaribhaṅgesu, niddhāraṇe bhummaṃ. Yanti sabbiādikaṃ. Appahotīti sabbesaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ nappahoti. Tanti sabbiādikaṃ, sampādehīti sambandho. Tādisaṃ sabbiādikanti sambandho.

The construction is: ‘As it is being taken.’ ‘Mattāyāti’ means in proportion. Regarding ‘sabbiādīsu eva’ (in ghee, etc., only), the word ‘eva’ should be supplied. ‘Sabbiādīsūti’ refers to ghee, oil, extra delicacies, etc.; the locative case is used for specification. ‘Yaṃti’ (which) refers to ghee, etc. ‘Appahotīti’ means it is not enough for all the monks. ‘Tanti’ refers to that ghee, etc.; the connection is with ‘sampādehi’ (provide). The connection is: ‘such ghee, etc.’

Yaṃ bhattagganti yojanā. Hatthadhovanaudakanti bhuttāvīnaṃ hatthassa dhovanaudakaṃ. Antarāti bhojanassa majjhe. Pipāsitenāti pivituṃ icchantena. Galeti kaṇṭhe.

The construction is: ‘Whatever meal hall.’ ‘Hatthadhovanaudakaṃ’ (water for washing hands) means water for washing the hands of those who have eaten. ‘Antarāti’ means in the middle of the meal. ‘Pipāsitenāti’ means by one desiring to drink. ‘Galeti’ means in the throat.

Nivattantenāti ettha kasmā ṭhānā nivattantenāti āha “bhattaggato”ti. Kathaṃ kenākārena nivattitabbanti yojanā. Kasmā navakehi bhikkhūhi paṭhamataraṃ nivattitabbanti āha “sambādhesu hī”tiādi. Nikkhamanokāsoti paṭhamataraṃ nikkhantokāso. Paṭipāṭiyāti vuḍḍhapaṭipāṭiyā. Dhureti gehadvārassa samīpe. Dhurasaddo hi idha samīpavācako. Navakā antogehe ce nisinnā hontīti yojanā. Antarenāti bhikkhūnaṃ vivarena, majjhena vā. Viraḷāyāti tanukāya.

Regarding ‘nivattantena’ (by one turning back): as to the question ‘from what place turning back?’, he says, ‘from the meal hall’. The construction is: How, in what manner, should they turn back? As to why the newer monks should turn back earlier, he says, ‘sambādhesu hī’ (because in crowded places), etc. ‘Nikkhamanokāsoti’ means the first opportunity to depart. ‘Paṭipāṭiyāti’ means according to the order of seniority. ‘Dhureti’ means near the house door. Indeed, the word ‘dhura’ here signifies proximity. The construction is: If the newer monks are seated inside the house. ‘Antarenāti’ means through the gap between the monks, or through the middle. ‘Viraḷāyāti’ means sparse or thin.

6. Piṇḍacārikavattakathā

6. The Explanation of the Alms-Round Observance

366. Piṇḍacārikavatte [M 0.0528] evaṃ vinicchayo veditabboti yojanā. Kappāsaṃ vā gahetvāti [V 2.0164] sambandho. Yañcāti yañca kiñci vatthuṃ, gahetvāti sambandho. Karontī ṭhitā vāti karontī hutvā ṭhitā vā. Tanti kammaṃ. Na ca bhikkhādāyikāyāti itthiliṅgavasena vuttattā itthiyā eva mukhaṃ na ulloketabbanti atthaṃ paṭikkhipanto āha “itthī vā hotū”tiādi. “Bhikkhādānasamaye”ti iminā aññasmiṃ samaye olokentopi natthi dosoti dasseti. Ekasmiṃ kāle bhikkhāya dadamānāya sabbakālampi na oloketabbanti anicchitatthaṃ paṭikkhipati.

366. In the observance of the alms-round, the decision should be understood thus—this is the application. ‘Having taken cotton, or’ is the connection. ‘And whatever’ means whatever thing; ‘having taken’ is the connection. ‘While doing or standing’ means having been doing or standing. That is the task. Regarding ‘and not of the female alms-giver’: since it is stated in the feminine gender, rejecting the meaning that one should not look only at a woman’s face, he says, ‘whether it be a woman or,’ and so forth. By ‘at the time of giving alms,’ he shows that there is no fault in looking at another time. He rejects the unintended meaning that because she is giving alms on one occasion, one should never look at her at any time.

7. Āraññikavattakathā

7. The Explanation of the Forest-Dweller's Observance

368. Āraññikavatte evaṃ vinicchayo veditabboti yojanā. Senāsanā otaritabbanti ettha araññe rukkhamūlādīsu nisinnassa vihārābhāvato senāsanaṃ nāma vasanaṭṭhānaṃ sandhāya vuttanti āha “vasanaṭṭhānato nikkhamitabba”nti.

368. In the observance of a forest-dweller, the decision should be understood thus—this is the application. Regarding the phrase, “one should descend from a dwelling,” here, in the forest, since there is no monastery for one seated at the foot of a tree and so on, the term “dwelling” is said with reference to a place of residence. Thus, it is said, “one should depart from the place of residence.”

Pattaṃ thavikāya pakkhipitvāti ettha kathaṃ patto thavikāya pakkhipitabboti āha “sace bahī”tiādi. Tattha patto pakkhipitabboti sambandho. Dhovitvā katvāti padesu “pattaṃ vodaka”nti vibhattipariṇāmaṃ katvā sambandhitabbaṃ. Tampīti veḷunāḷikampi. Samīpeti āraññakassa senāsanassa samīpe. Yathā ca āraññakassa araṇisahitaṃ icchitabbaṃ, evaṃ kantāraṃ paṭipannassāpi araṇisahitaṃ icchitabbanti yojanā. Gaṇavāsinoti gaṇena saha vāsino, āraññakassāti sambandho. Tenāti araṇisahitena. “Nakkhattāneva nakkhattapadānī”ti iminā assayujādinakkhattāneva (abhidhānappadīpikāyaṃ 58-60 gāthāsu) disābhāgajānanassa, ca samayajānanassa ca kāraṇattā nakkhattapadāni nāmāti dasseti.

Regarding the phrase, “having placed the bowl in the bag,” here, how should the bowl be placed in the bag? He says, “If outside,” and so on. There, “the bowl should be placed” is the connection. In the passages, “having washed and done,” it should be connected by making a case-ending modification of “the bowl with water.” That too refers to even the bamboo tube. “Near” means near the forest-dweller’s dwelling. And just as an araṇi is desirable for the forest-dweller, so too for one traveling through the wilderness, an araṇi is desirable—this is the application. “One dwelling with the group” means those dwelling with a group; this is related to the forest-dweller. “With that” means with the araṇi. By the phrase, “the constellations are merely constellation-terms,” he shows that the constellations such as the Assayuja constellations (in the Abhidhānappadīpikā, verses 58-60) are called constellation-terms because they are the cause for knowing the divisions of the directions and also for knowing the time.

8. Senāsanavattakathā

8. The Explanation of the Observance for Dwellings

369. Senāsanavatte [M 0.0529] evaṃ vinicchayo veditabboti yojanā. Dvāraṃ nāmāti mahādvāraṃ. Mahāvaḷañjanti mahantehi janehi paribhuñjitabbaṃ. Tatthāti dvāre. Āpucchitvāvāti vuḍḍhaṃ āpucchitvāva, sabhāgassa vuḍḍhatarassāti sambandho. Vaṭṭatiyevāti yathāsukhaṃ viharituṃ vaṭṭatiyeva. Parivattitabbanti parimukhaṃ vattitabbaṃ.

369. In the observance for dwellings, the decision should be understood thus—this is the application. The term “door” means the main door. “Mahāvaḷañja” means it is to be used by many people. “There” means at the door. “Having asked leave” means having asked leave of the elder; this is connected with ‘of a senior co-resident.’ “It is indeed allowable” means it is indeed allowable to dwell at ease. “Should be turned around” means it should be turned to face the front.

9. Jantāgharavattādikathā

9. The Explanation of the Observance of the Hot Bath House and So Forth

371. Jantāgharavatte [V 2.0165] evaṃ vinicchayo veditabboti yojanā. Bahijagatīti bahiālindo.

371. In the observance of the hot bath house, the decision should be understood thus—this is the application. “Bahijagatī” means the outer verandah.

373. Ācamanavatthusmiṃ evamattho veditabboti yojanā. Nīharitvāti udakaṃ nīharitvā. Ācamitabbanti dhovitabbaṃ. “Āpubbo camu dhovane”ti hi dhātupāṭhesu vuttaṃ. Idaṃ ativivaṭanti idaṃ ṭhānaṃ ativivaṭaṃ, na kenaci paṭicchannanti attho. Udakaṃ alabhantassevāti udakaṃ alabhanteyeva.

373. In the matter of the water for rinsing, the meaning should be understood thus—this is the application. “Having removed” means having removed the water. “Should rinse” means should wash. For in the Dhātupāṭha it is said: “The root camu preceded by ā is in the sense of washing.” “This is too open” means this place is too exposed, not covered by anything—this is the meaning. “Only for one not getting water” means only when water is not available.

374. Vaccakuṭivatte evaṃ vinicchayo veditabboti yojanā. Ayanti dantakaṭṭhaṃ khādato vaccakaraṇaṃ. Sabbatthevāti sabbasmiṃ eva ṭhāne. “Na pharusena kaṭṭhenā”ti ettha na kevalaṃ kharakaṭṭhameva, phālitakaṭṭhādayopi chaviavalekhanakaṭṭhā pharusāyeva nāmāti dassento āha “phālitakaṭṭhena vā”tiādi. Paviṭṭhassāti vaccakuṭiṃ paviṭṭhassa.

374. In the observance of the latrine, the decision should be understood thus—this is the application. “This” means the act of defecating while chewing a toothstick. “In all cases” means in every place. Regarding the phrase, “not with a harsh stick,” here, showing that not only rough sticks but also split sticks and other sticks that scrape the skin are indeed called harsh, he says, “or with a split stick,” and so on. “For one who has entered” means for one who has entered the latrine.

Sabbasādhāraṇaṭṭhānanti sabbesaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ, sabbehi vā sādhāraṇaṃ vaccakuṭisaṅkhātaṃ ṭhānaṃ. Tatrāti tasmiṃ sabbasādhāraṇe ṭhāne. Nibaddhagamanatthāyāti attano nibaddhagamanatthāya kataṃ yaṃ ṭhānaṃ vā yaṃ puggalikaṭṭhānaṃ vā hotīti yojanā.

“A place common to all” means a place, known as a latrine, common to all bhikkhus, or shared by all. “There” means in that common place. “For the purpose of regular use” means whatever place is made for the purpose of one’s own regular use, or which is a personal place—this is the application.

Uhatāti ettha upubbo hadadhātūti dassento āha “uhaditā”ti. “Hada karīsossagge”ti dhātupāṭhesu (pāṇinī 977 dhātupāṭhe; saddanītidhātumālāyaṃ 15 dakārantadhātu) vuttattā vaccakūpato bahi [M 0.0530] karīsassa ossajjananti āha “bahi vaccamakkhitā”ti. Dhovitabbāti udakena dhovitabbā. Etampīti udakassa avijjamānampi. Sabbatthāti sabbasmiṃ vattakkhandhake.

Regarding “uhatā,” here, showing that it is the root hada preceded by upa, he says “uhaditā.” Because in the Dhātupāṭha it is stated “Hada in the casting away of excrement” (Pāṇini 977, Dhātupāṭha; Saddanīti Dhātumālā, 15, root ending in da), he says “defecated outside,” meaning the casting away of excrement outside the toilet pit. “To be washed” means to be washed with water. “Even this” refers to even the non-existence of water. “In all cases” means in the entire Section on Observances.

Iti vattakkhandhakavaṇṇanāya yojanā samattā.

Thus, the application in the commentary on the Section on Observances is concluded.

9. Pātimokkhaṭṭhapanakkhandhakaṃ

9. The Section on the Suspension of the Pātimokkha

1. Pātimokkhuddesayācanakathā

1. The Explanation of the Request for the Pātimokkha Recitation

383. Pātimokkhaṭṭhapanakkhandhake [V 2.0166] nandimukhiyā rattiyāti ettha nandiyati tusiyatīti nandi, ikārantoyaṃ napuṃsakaliṅgo. “Nandiseno (jā. aṭṭha. 3.4.1) nandivisālo”tiādīsu ikārantoyaṃ pulliṅgo hoti, idha pana mukhaṃ apekkhitvā ikāranto napuṃsakaliṅgo hoti. Aruṇuṭṭhitakāle odātadisāmukhatāya nandi mukhaṃ etissaṃ rattiyanti nandimukhī, ratti, tāya nandimukhiyā rattiyā, tena vuttaṃ “aruṇuṭṭhitakālepi hi nandīmukhā viya ratti khāyatī”ti. Antopūtinti ettha kāyassa anto kuṇapapūtinti atthaṃ paṭipakkhipanto āha “attacittasantāne”tiādi. “Kilesavassanavasenā”ti iminā udakavassanavasenāti atthaṃ paṭikkhipati. Avassutanti tintaṃ, kilinnanti attho. Kasambujātanti ettha kasambūti saṅkāro. So hi sammuñcaniyā kasiyamāne vilekhiyamāne sambati saddaṃ karotīti kasambu, taṃ viya jātanti kasambujātanti attho daṭṭhabbo. Aṭṭhakathāyaṃ pana adhippāyavasena “ākiliṭṭhajāta”nti vuttaṃ, ativiya kiliṭṭhajātanti attho. “Ākiṇṇadosatāya kiliṭṭhajāta”ntipi pāṭho. “Yāva bāhāgahaṇāpi nāmā”ti iminā pāṭhena dassetīti sambandho. Hīti padapūraṇamattaṃ. Tenāti moghapurisena. “Yāvā”ti nipātapayogattā “bāhāgahaṇāpī”ti ettha pañcamīvibhatti avadhiatthe hoti. Nāma-saddo garahatthajotako, tassa payogattā “āgamessatī”ti ettha atītatthe anāgatavacanaṃ (saddanītisuttamālāya 893 sutte). Āgamessati [M 0.0531] nāmāti yojanā. Āgamessatīti īsaṃ adhivāsessati. “Āto gamuīsamadhivāsane”ti hi dhātupāṭhesu (saddanītidhātumālāyaṃ 18 makārantadhātu) vuttaṃ.

383. In the Section on the Suspension of the Pātimokkha, regarding the phrase ‘on the Nandimukhī night’: here, ‘nandi’ means delight or satisfaction; this is a neuter-gender term ending in ‘i.’ In instances like ‘Nandiseno’ (Jātaka Aṭṭhakathā 3.4.1) and ‘Nandivisālo,’ the term ending in ‘i’ is masculine, but here, with reference to ‘face,’ it is a neuter. At the time of dawn, due to the bright appearance of the direction, the face (mukha) of the night is delightful (nandi), hence it is a ‘Nandimukhī’ night. Thus, it is said, “For even at dawn, the night appears like a delightful face.” Regarding ‘rotten within,’ rejecting the meaning that the inside of the body is a rotting corpse, he says ‘within the continuum of one’s own mind,’ and so forth. By the phrase ‘by means of the rain of defilements,’ he refutes the idea that it is by means of actual rainfall. ‘Avassuta’ means soaked, that is, defiled. Regarding ‘kasambujāta,’ ‘kasambu’ here means refuse. For when being swept or scraped with a broom, it makes a sound (sambati), thus it is ‘kasambu.’ ‘Born like that’ is ‘kasambujāta’—this is the meaning to be understood. In the commentary, however, according to the intended meaning, it is explained as ‘born defiled,’ meaning extremely defiled. Another reading is ‘born defiled due to being filled with faults.’ By the reading, ‘even up to the seizing of the arm, indeed,’ he shows—this is the connection. ‘Hī’ is merely a particle filling the meter. ‘By him’ refers to the foolish man. The word ‘yāva’ is a particle indicating extent, and here the fifth case (ablative) is used in the sense of a limit. The term ‘nāma’ serves to indicate censure. Due to its usage, ‘āgamessati’ here is a future tense used in a past sense (as explained in Saddanīti Suttamālā 893). The construction is ‘āgamessati nāma.’ ‘Āgamessati’ means ‘he will slightly endure.’ For as stated in the Dhātupāṭha, the root ‘gam’ with ‘ā’ is in the sense of slight endurance (Saddanīti Dhātumālā, 18, root ending in ma).

384. Na āyatakeneva papātoti ettha dīgheneva papātoti dassento āha “na paṭhamameva gambhīro”ti. Āyatasaddo hi dīghapariyāyo. “Na āyatakena gītassarena dhammo gāyitabbo”tiādīsu (cūḷava. 249) viya papāto dīghena tīrassa ādimhi na hotīti vuttaṃ hoti. Paṭhamamevāti tīrassa ādimhiyeva. “Anupubbena gambhīro”ti iminā “na paṭhamameva gambhīro”ti vacanassa adhippāyatthaṃ dasseti. Ṭhitadhammoti tīrassa antoyeva ṭhitasabhāvo[V 2.0167]. Velaṃ nātivattatīti ettha velāsaddassa tīramariyādatthesu pavattabhāvaṃ dassento āha “osakkanakandaraṃ mariyādavela”nti. Tattha “osakkanakandara”iti padena tīratthaṃ dasseti, “mariyāda” iti padena mariyādatthaṃ. Kena udakena daritabboti kandaro, udakena osakkano kandaro etthāti osakkanakandaraṃ, tīraṃ. Osakkanakandarabhūtañca mariyādabhūtañca velaṃ tīraṃ nātikkamatīti attho. Tīraṃ vāhetīti ettha vahadhātuyā pāpuṇanatthaṃ dassento āha “tīraṃ appetī”ti. Tattha appetīti pāpuṇāpeti. “Ussāretī”ti iminā pāḷiyaṃ “thalaṃ ussāretī”ti padena “tīraṃ vāhetī”ti padassa atthaṃ dassetīti attho dassito. Ussāretīti uddharitvā gamāpeti. Aññāpaṭivedhoti ettha ājānāti, ājānitthāti vā aññaṃ arahattamaggo vā arahattaphalaṃ vā, tassa paṭivijjhanaṃ aññāpaṭivedho, sukhuccāraṇatthaṃ majjhe dīgho, aññāpaṭivedho nāma arahattuppattiyeva hoti. Tena vuttaṃ “arahattuppattī”ti.

384. Here, regarding the phrase 'it is not a long, sheer drop,' showing that it is a long slope, he says, 'it is not deep right at the beginning.' For the word 'āyata' is a synonym for 'long.' Just as in passages such as, 'the Dhamma should not be chanted with a drawn-out vocal tone' (Cūḷavagga 249), so it is said that the slope is not long at the beginning of the shore. 'Right at the beginning' means at the very start of the shore. By 'gradually deep,' he shows the intended meaning of the statement 'it is not deep right at the beginning.' 'Of a stable nature' means having a stable nature right within the shore. Here, regarding 'it does not transgress the boundary (velā),' showing that the word 'velā' is used in the senses of 'shore' and 'limit,' he says, 'a sloping ravine, a limiting boundary.' There, by the word 'osakkanakandara,' he indicates the meaning 'shore,' and by the word 'mariyāda,' he indicates the meaning 'limit.' A ravine (kandara) is so-called because 'by what water is it to be split (daritabba)?' A sloping ravine (osakkanakandara) is a place where there is a ravine sloping with water; it means the shore. The meaning is that it does not transgress the shore, which is a sloping ravine and a boundary. Here, regarding 'it carries to the shore,' showing the meaning of 'to reach' for the root 'vah,' he says, 'it makes it reach the shore.' There, 'appeti' means 'causes to reach.' By 'ussāretī,' it is shown that in the Pāli, the word 'thalaṃ ussāretī' (it raises to the land) indicates the meaning of the phrase 'tīraṃ vāhetī.' 'Ussāretī' means 'having lifted up, it causes to go.' Here, regarding 'aññāpaṭivedho' (penetration of final knowledge), 'aññā' is 'one knows' or 'one has known,' which is either the path to arahantship or the fruit of arahantship. The penetration (paṭivedho) of that is 'aññāpaṭivedho.' For ease of pronunciation, the middle vowel is lengthened. 'Aññāpaṭivedho' is the arising of arahantship itself. Therefore, it is said, 'the arising of arahantship.'

385. Channamativassatīti udānapāḷiyā sandhāyabhāsitapāḷibhāvaṃ dassento āha “āpatti”ntiādi. Tattha idanti “channamativassatī”ti vacanaṃ vuttanti sambandho. Etanti navāpattiāpajjanaṃ sandhāyāti sambandho.

385. Regarding 'it rains on the roofed,' showing that this is a Pāli passage spoken with reference to the Udāna Pāli, he says, 'an offense,' and so on. There, the connection is that 'this' refers to the statement 'it rains on the roofed.' The connection is that 'this' is with reference to incurring a new offense.

4. Pātimokkhasavanārahakathā

4. The Discussion on Eligibility for Hearing the Pātimokkha

386. Pure [M 0.0532] vā pacchā vāti ñattito pure vā pacchā vā. Khetteti pātimokkhaṭṭhapanassa khette. Khettaṃ dassento āha “tasmā”tiādi. Rekāraṃ bhaṇatīti chattiṃsatyakkharesu re-kāraṃ ñattiṭṭhapanako bhaṇati. Idanti pañcatiṃsatyakkharānaṃ uccāraṇaṭṭhānaṃ. Vutteti ñattiṭṭhapanakena vutte. “Suṇātu me”ti vacane anāraddheyevāti yojanā.

386. 'Before or after' means before or after the motion. 'In the field' means in the field for the suspension of the Pātimokkha. Showing the field, he said, 'therefore,' and so on. 'He utters the sound "re"' means that among the thirty-six letters, the one who proposes the motion for suspension utters the sound 're.' 'This' is the place for the utterance of the thirty-five letters. 'When said' means when it is said by the one who proposes the motion for suspension. The connection is with the words 'Let them hear me' not yet having been started.

5. Dhammikādhammikapātimokkhaṭṭhapanakathā

5. The Discussion on Lawful and Unlawful Suspension of the Pātimokkha

387. Tena puggalenāti tena cuditakena puggalena. Sā vipattīti sīlavipattiādisaṅkhātā sā vipatti. Saññāamūlikavasenāti “katā” iti saññāya amūlikavasena. Katañcāti ekantena katañca. Akatañcāti ekantena akatañca.

387. 'By that person' means by that person who has been accused. 'That downfall' means that downfall designated as moral failure and so on. 'By way of the perception being groundless' means by way of the perception 'done' being groundless. 'And done' means absolutely done. 'And not done' means absolutely not done.

Kopetukāmatāya neva āgacchatīti sambandho. Tenāti anāgamanādikāraṇena. Āpajjatīti pātimokkhaṭṭhapanako āpajjati. Iccassāpīti iti evaṃ assa pātimokkhaṭṭhapanakassāpi[V 2.0168]. Paccādiyatīti pati ādiyati, “akataṃ kammaṃ, puna kātabbaṃ kamma”ntiādinā puna ādīyati, puna ārabhatīti attho.

'He does not come out of a desire to provoke anger'—this is the connection. 'By that' means by the reason of not coming, and so on. 'He incurs' means the one who proposes the suspension of the Pātimokkha incurs an offense. 'Thus, even for him' means thus, even for that one who proposes the suspension of the Pātimokkha. 'He takes it up again' means he takes it up again (paṭi-ādiyati); he takes it up again by saying, 'The act was not done; the act must be done again,' and so on. The meaning is that he begins again.

6. Dhammikapātimokkhaṭṭhapanakathā

6. The Discussion on the Lawful Suspension of the Pātimokkha

388. Maggapaṭipādanādīsūti maggasmiṃ paṭipādanādīsu. Ādisaddena theyyacittena avahārādayo saṅgaṇhāti. Ākārādisaññāti ākārasaññā liṅgasaññā nimittasaññā. Tanti parisaṅkaṃ sandhāyāti sambandho.

388. 'In guiding on the path, and so on' means in guiding on the path, and so on. By the word 'and so on,' he includes misappropriation with intent to steal, and so on. 'Perception of features, and so on' means perception of features, perception of signs, and perception of indications. The connection is that 'that' refers to suspicion.

7. Attādānaaṅgakathā

7. The Discussion on the Factors of Taking Up a Case Oneself

398. Attādānaṃ ādātukāmenāti ettha kiṃ attādānanti āha “sāsanaṃ sodhetukāmo”tiādi. Iminā paraṃ codetuṃ attanā ādātabbaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ attādānanti vuccatīti dasseti. Akālo [M 0.0533] imaṃ attādānaṃ ādātunti ettha akālaṃ dassento āha “rājabhaya”ntiādi. Tattha vassārattoti vassakālo. So hi vasso ativiya rañjati ettha kāleti vassārattoti vuccati. Vassārattopi adhikaraṇavūpasamatthaṃ lajjiparisāya dūrato ānayanassa dukkarattā akālo nāma. Itīti ayaṃ rājabhayādikāloti attho. Viparītoti rājabhayādīnaṃ abhāvakālo.

398. Regarding 'wishing to take up a case oneself': here, what is 'taking up a case oneself'? He says, 'wishing to purify the Teaching,' and so on. By this, he shows that 'taking up a case oneself' refers to a legal case to be taken up by oneself in order to accuse another. Regarding 'it is the wrong time to take up this case oneself,' here, indicating the wrong time, he says, 'fear of the king,' and so on. There, 'vassāratta' means the rainy season. For at this time, the rain is especially delightful, hence it is called 'vassāratta.' Even the rainy season is called the wrong time because of the difficulty of bringing someone from afar to an assembly of the scrupulous for the purpose of settling a legal case. 'Thus' means this is the time of fear of the king, and so on. 'The opposite' means the time when there is no fear of the king, and so on.

Abhūtaṃ idaṃ attādānanti ettha abhūtasaddo avijjamānapariyāyoti āha “asantamida”nti, idaṃ attādānaṃ avijjamānanti attho. Mayā gahitoti sambandho. Sīlavā puggaloti yojanā. Yanti attādānaṃ saṃvattatīti sambandho. Idanti attādānaṃ.

Regarding 'this taking up of a case is untrue': here, the word 'untrue' is a synonym for 'non-existent,' as he says, 'this is non-existent'—the meaning is that this taking up of a case is non-existent. The connection is 'taken by me.' The construction is 'a virtuous person.' The connection is 'that to which the taking up of a case leads.' 'This' means the taking up of a case.

Na labhissāmi sandiṭṭhe, labhissāmi sandiṭṭheti ettha “na labhissāmi, labhissāmī”ti idaṃ kiṃ sandhāya vuttanti āha “appekadā hī”tiādi. Tattha appekadāti api ekadā. Hisaddo vitthārajotako. Evarūpāti sandiṭṭhasambhattasabhāvā. Tanti upatthambhakabhikkhulabhanaṃ sandhāyāti sambandho. “Na labhissāmī”ti idaṃ vacanaṃ vuttanti sambandho.

Regarding 'I will not obtain allies, I will obtain allies': here, with reference to what is 'I will not obtain, I will obtain' said? He says, 'for sometimes,' and so on. There, 'appekadā' means 'sometimes.' The particle 'hi' is an indicator of amplification. 'Of such a nature' means having the nature of being allies and companions. The connection is that 'that' refers to obtaining supporting monks. The connection is that this statement 'I will not obtain' is said.

Kosambakānaṃ bhaṇḍanādi bhavati viya bhaṇḍanādi bhavissatīti yojanā. Pacchāpi avippaṭisārakaraṃ bhavissatīti ettha kesaṃ avippaṭisārakaraṃ bhavati viya pañcaṅgasampannāgataṃ attādānaṃ [V 2.0169] ādiyato pacchāpi avippaṭisārakaraṃ bhavatīti āha “subhaddaṃ vuḍḍhapabbajita”ntiādi. Tattha pañcasatikasaṅgītinti pañcasatehi mahākassapādīhi kattabbaṃ saṅgītiṃ. Mahākassapattherassa pacchā samanussaraṇakaraṃ hoti iva hotīti yojanā. Eseva nayo sesesupi. Samanussaraṇakaranti sammodavasena punappunaṃ anussaraṇassa karaṃ. Iminā “avippaṭisārakara”nti padassa atthaṃ dasseti. Pacchāpīti ettha pisaddassa avuttasampiṇḍanatthaṃ dassento āha “sāsanassa cā”tiādi. Tattha sāsanassa ca sassirikatāyāti sambandho. Vigataupakkilesacandimasūriyānaṃ viya sāsanassa ca sassirikatāya saṃvattatīti adhippāyo.

The construction is: just as the quarrel of the Kosambakas, and so on, occurs, so a quarrel, and so on, will occur. Regarding 'afterwards, it will be a cause for no remorse,' here, just as for whom does it become a cause for no remorse? For one who takes up a case oneself, endowed with five factors, it becomes a cause for no remorse afterwards. Thus he said, 'Subhadda, the aged renunciate,' and so on. There, 'the council of five hundred' means the council to be held by the five hundred headed by Mahākassapa. The construction is: it is as if it becomes a cause for Mahākassapa Thera's later remembrance. This same method applies in the remaining instances. 'Causing remembrance' means causing repeated remembrance by way of mutual appreciation. By this, he shows the meaning of the word 'avippaṭisārakara' (a cause for no remorse). Here, in 'afterwards too,' showing that the particle 'pi' (too) serves to include what is not stated, he says, 'and for the Teaching,' and so on. There, the connection is 'and for the glory of the Teaching.' The intention is that it leads to the glory of the Teaching, just like the moon and sun that are free from defilements.

8. Codakena paccavekkhitabbadhammakathā

8. The Discussion on the Principles to be Reflected Upon by the Accuser

399. “Acchiddena [M 0.0534] appaṭimaṃsenā”tiādīsu evamattho veditabboti yojanā. Chiddasappaṭimaṃsaṃ paṭhamaṃ dassetvā viparītavasena acchiddaappaṭimaṃsaṃ dassento āha “yenā”tiādi. Tattha yena katānīti sambandho. Chijjatīti chiddo, paṭi punappunaṃ masiyati āmasiyatīti paṭimaṃso, niggahitāgamo, bhāvappadhānoyaṃ kammaniddeso. Saha paṭimaṃsenāti sappaṭimaṃso, kāyasamācāro. Viparītoti viparivattavasena ito pavatto, kāyasamācāroti attho. Amūlakānuddhaṃsanādīhīti ādisaddena duṭṭhullavācādayo saṅgaṇhāti.

399. The construction is that in passages such as 'without fault, without blemish,' the meaning should be understood in this way. First showing what is faulty and blemished, and then by way of the opposite showing what is without fault and without blemish, he says, 'by which,' and so on. There, the connection is 'by which they are done.' 'Chidda' (fault) is so-called because it is broken. 'Paṭimaṃsa' is so-called because it is repeatedly smeared or touched; this is a designation of action with the state being primary. 'With blemish' means blemished—bodily conduct. 'Opposite' means proceeding from this in reverse; the meaning is bodily conduct. Regarding 'by groundless accusation, and so on,' by the word 'and so on,' he includes gross speech and the like.

Mettaṃ nu kho me cittanti ettha appanābhāvappattaṃ mettacittamevādhippetanti dassento āha “palibodhe chinditvā”tiādi. Tattha palibodheti āvāsapalibodhādike palibodhe. “Vikkhambhanavasena vihatāghāta”nti iminā appanābhāvappattaṃ mettacittameva dasseti. Idaṃ panāvuso kattha vuttaṃ bhagavatāti ettha idaṃsaddakiṃsaddānaṃ visayaṃ dassento āha “idaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ katarasmiṃ nagare”ti.

"Is my mind indeed endowed with loving-kindness?" Here, showing that what is meant is the mind of loving-kindness that has attained absorption, he says, "having cut off the obstacles," etc. There, 'obstacles' means obstacles such as the obstacle of a dwelling, etc. By 'hatred is eliminated by way of suppression,' he shows the mind of loving-kindness itself that has attained absorption. "But, friend, where was this spoken by the Blessed One?" Here, showing the scope of the words "this" and "which," he says, "This training rule—in which city?"

9. Codakena upaṭṭhāpetabbakathā

9. The Account of What Should Be Raised by the Accuser

400. “Kālena vakkhāmī”tiādīsu codanāya kālaakālādiṃ dassento āha “eko eka”ntiādi. Tattha ekoti ekako codako. Ekanti ekakaṃ cuditakaṃ. Saṅghamajjha…pe… asanasālādīsu vā parivāritakkhaṇe vāti yojanā. Tattha “saṅghamajjha…pe… asanasālādīsū”ti iminā ṭhānābhāvaṃ dasseti, “upaṭṭhākehi parivāritakkhaṇe”ti iminā kālābhāvaṃ dasseti. Imehi padehi ṭhānampi kālena saṅgahetvā “kālena [V 2.0170] vakkhāmī”ti vuttanti dasseti. Tacchenāti saccena. Hambhoti nipāto pacchimapadesu paccekaṃ yojetabbo. Hambho mahallaka, hambho parisāvacara, hambho paṃsukūlika, hambho dhammakathikāti hi attho. Idanti kammaṃ. Kāraṇanissitanti mahallakabhāvakāraṇādīsu [M 0.0535] nissitaṃ. “Bhante”ti nipātopi paccekaṃ yojetabbo. Ettha ca “hambho”ti nipātena lokavohāravasena anādarassa pakāsakattā pharusena vadati nāma, “bhante”ti nipātena sādarassa pakāsakattā saṇhena vadati nāma. Kāraṇanissitaṃ katvāti imasmiṃ vītikkame ayaṃ nāma dosoti kāraṇanissitaṃ katvā. “Mettacittaṃ upaṭṭhapetvā”ti iminā mettacittoti padassa “vakkhāmī”ti pade kiriyāvisesanabhāvaṃ dasseti. No dosantaroti ettha antarasaddassa cittavācakabhāvaṃ dassento āha “na duṭṭhacitto”ti. “Hutvā”ti iminā kiriyāvisesanabhāvaṃ dasseti.

400. In the phrase "I will speak at the proper time," etc., showing the proper and improper time for an admonishment, he says, "one to one," etc. Here, 'one' refers to a single admonisher. 'One' refers to a single person being admonished. In the midst of the Saṅgha...or in places like assembly halls, or at a time when surrounded by attendants—this is the connection. Here, "in the midst of the Saṅgha...or in places like assembly halls" indicates the absence of a suitable place, while "at a time when surrounded by attendants" indicates the absence of a suitable time. By these words, it shows that 'place' is also included under the term 'time', which is why it is said, "I will speak at the proper time." "Truthfully" means with truth. "Hambho" is a particle to be construed individually with each of the subsequent terms. For example, "Hambho, elder," "Hambho, one who frequents assemblies," "Hambho, rag-robe wearer," "Hambho, Dhamma speaker"—this is the meaning. "This" refers to the action. "Dependent on a reason" means dependent on reasons such as being an elder, etc. The particle "bhante" should also be construed individually with each term. Here, the particle "hambho" conveys harsh speech because it reveals disrespect according to worldly convention, while the particle "bhante" conveys gentle speech because it reveals respect. "Having made it dependent on a reason" means having made it dependent on a reason such as, 'this is the fault in this transgression.' By "having established a mind of loving-kindness," he shows that the word "mettacitto" has the function of an adverb modifying the verb "I will speak." Regarding "not with another mind": here, showing that the word "antara" means "mind," he says, "not with a hostile mind." By the implied "hutvā" (having been), he shows its adverbial function.

10. Codakacuditakapaṭisaṃyuttakathā

10. Discussion Related to the Admonisher and the Admonished

401. Ajjhattanti ettha attasaddassa cittavācakabhāvañca sattamīvibhattiyāpi amādesabhāvañca dassento āha “attano citte”ti. Uppādetvāti iminā “manasikaritvā”ti padassa adhippāyatthaṃ dasseti. Kāruññatāti ettha dvīsu ṇyapaccayatāpaccayesu ekasseva bhāvavācakattā eko svatthoti dassento āha “karuṇabhāvo”ti. Tattha karuṇassa puggalassa bhāvo kāruññaṃ, tadeva kāruññatā. Atha vā karuṇo eva puggalo kāruññaṃ, tassa bhāvo kāruññatāti vacanattho kātabbo. Imināti “kāruññatā”ti padena. Karuṇañcāti appanāpattaṃ karuṇañca. Karuṇāpubbabhāgañcāti appanāpattāya karuṇāya pubbabhāge parikammūpacāravasena pavattaṃ kāmāvacarakaruṇañca. Dvīhipīti “hitesitā, anukampitā”ti dvīhipi padehi. Mettañcāti appanāpattamettañca. Mettāpubbabhāgañcāti appanāpattāya mettāya pubbabhāge parikammūpacāravasena pavattaṃ kāmāvacaramettañca. Suddhanteti suddhe koṭṭhāse. Paṭiññaṃ āropetvāti cuditakaṃ paṭiññaṃ āropetvā. Ye eteti “kāruññatā”tiādinā nayena ye ete pañca dhammā vuttāti yojanā. Iminā ime pañca dhammeti ettha imasaddassa aniyamaniddesabhāvaṃ dasseti.

401. Regarding 'internally' (ajjhattaṃ): here, showing that the word 'atta' (self) means 'mind' and that the ending '-aṃ' is a substitute for the seventh case ending, he says, 'in one's own mind' (attano citte). By 'having aroused' (uppādetvā), he shows the intended meaning of the word 'having attended to' (manasikaritvā). Regarding 'compassionateness' (kāruññatā): here, of the two suffixes, '-ṇya' and '-tā', since both express an abstract state, one is redundant. Showing this, he says it means 'the state of compassion' (karuṇabhāvo). Here, the state of a compassionate person is compassion (kāruññaṃ); that itself is compassionateness (kāruññatā). Alternatively, the meaning should be understood thus: a compassionate person is himself compassion (kāruññaṃ), and his state is compassionateness (kāruññatā). By 'this' (iminā) is meant by the word 'kāruññatā'. 'And compassion' means compassion that has attained absorption. 'And the preliminary part of compassion' means the sense-sphere compassion that occurs by way of the preliminary and access stages, prior to the compassion that has attained absorption. 'By both' means by the two words 'wishing for welfare' (hitesitā) and 'having compassion' (anukampitā). 'And loving-kindness' means loving-kindness that has attained absorption. 'And the preliminary part of loving-kindness' means the sense-sphere loving-kindness that occurs by way of the preliminary and access stages, prior to the loving-kindness that has attained absorption. 'In the pure section' means in the pure division. 'Having made (him) admit the charge' means having made the accused admit the charge. The connection for 'which these' (ye ete) is: 'which these five qualities are spoken of' according to the method beginning with 'compassionateness,' etc. By this, it shows that in the phrase 'these five qualities' (ime pañca dhammā), the word 'these' (ime) is an unspecified reference.

Sacce [M 0.0536] ca akuppe cāti ettha saccasaddassa viratisaccaparamatthasaccāni paṭikkhipanto āha “vacīsacce cā”ti. “Akuppanatāyā”ti iminā nakupassa bhāvo akuppanti katvā ṇyapaccayassa [V 2.0171] bhāvatthaṃ dasseti. Hīti saccaṃ, vitthāro vā. Na paro ghaṭṭetabboti na paro kujjhāpetabbo. Sabbatthāti sabbasmiṃ pātimokkhaṭṭhapanakkhandhake.

Regarding 'in truth and in the unshakable': here, rejecting the meanings of truth as abstinence-truth and ultimate truth, it is said, 'and in verbal truth.' By 'unshakableness' (akuppanatāyā), he shows that the suffix '-ṇya' has the meaning of an abstract state by explaining 'akuppaṃ' as 'the state of not being shaken.' 'Hi' means truth, or an elaboration. 'One should not provoke another' means one should not make another angry. 'In all cases' means in the entire Chapter on the Establishment of the Pātimokkha.

Iti pātimokkhaṭṭhapanakkhandhakavaṇṇanāya yojanā samattā.

Thus concludes the grammatical explanation of the commentary on the Chapter on the Establishment of the Pātimokkha.

10. Bhikkhunikkhandhakaṃ

10. The Chapter on Nuns

Mahāpajāpatigotamīvatthukathā

The Story of Mahāpajāpatī Gotamī

402. Bhikkhunikkhandhake kasmā paṭikkhipatīti codanaṃ dassetvā tassā ābhogaṃ dassento āha “nanū”tiādi. “Kāma”ntiādinā abhyūpagamaparihāravasena vissajjeti. Tattha kāmaṃsaddo anuggahattho, pana saddo garahattho, pana tathāpi paṭikkhipatīti sambandho. Tanti mahāpajāpatiṃ gotamiṃ. Yācitena hutvā anuññātanti yojanā. Ayanti pabbajjā. Bhaddakaṃ katvāti laddhakaṃ katvā, manāpaṃ katvāti attho.

402. In the Chapter on Nuns, having presented the accusation, "Why does he reject?" and then showing his consideration, he says, "nanu," and so on. With the words, "kāmaṃ," and so on, he replies by way of acceptance and avoidance. Here, the word "kāmaṃ" is in the sense of acceptance, while the word "pana" is in the sense of censure; the connection is, "pana" (nevertheless), he rejects. "That" refers to Mahāpajāpatī Gotamī. The connection is: having been requested, it was permitted. "This" refers to the going forth. "Having made it good" means having made it obtainable, having made it pleasing—this is the meaning.

403. Kumbhathenakehīti ettha kumbhe dīpaṃ jāletvā tenālokena thenentīti kumbhathenakāti dassento āha “kumbhe dīpaṃ jāletvā”tiādi.

403. Regarding "by pot-thieves": here, showing that a 'pot-thief' is one who steals by the light of a lamp they have lit inside a pot, he says, "having lit a lamp in a pot," etc.

Nāḷimajjhagatanti sassanāḷassa majjhe gataṃ. Gaṇṭhinti phaḷuṃ. “Kaṇḍa”ntipi pāṭho, daṇḍanti attho. Yenāti pāṇakena. Ayañhi yaṃsaddo taṃsaddānapekkhoti daṭṭhabbo.

"Gone into the middle of a reed" means gone into the middle of a stalk of grain. "Knot" means a joint. There is also the reading "kaṇḍa," meaning a staff. "By which" refers to a creature. Here, the word "yaṃ" should be understood as not requiring the word "taṃ."

Antorattabhāvoti antolohitabhāvo. Etamatthanti etaṃ vakkhamānaṃ atthaṃ. Āḷiyāti āvaraṇāya. Abaddhāyapīti pisaddo anuggahattho, baddhāya pana pagevāti attho. Kiñcīti appamattakaṃ. Yanti udakaṃ. Tampīti udakampi. Pisaddo abaddhāya ṭhitaṃ kiñci udakaṃ apekkhati. Ye ime garudhammā paññattāti yojanā. Paṭikaccevāti pageva[M 0.0537], paṭhamamevāti attho. Tesūti garudhammesu. Apaññattesu santesupīti yojanā. Paṭhamaṃ vuttantiādi vuttaṃ, vassasahassameva ṭhassati iti imamatthaṃ dassetīti yojanā. “Vassasahassa”nti ca etaṃ vacanaṃ vuttanti [V 2.0172] sambandho. Tatoti vassasahassato. Pariyattidhammopīti pisaddo paṭivedhasaddhammaṃ apekkhati. Dvīsu saddhammesu ṭhitesu paṭipattisaddhammo ṭhitoyevāti katvā na vuttaṃ. Tāniyevāti pañcavassasahassāniyeva. Pariyattiyā sati paṭivedho na hotīti nāpi vattabboti yojanā. Liṅganti samaṇavesaṃ, samaṇākāranti attho.

"The state of being internally red" means the state of having internal blood. "This meaning" refers to the meaning about to be explained. "For a dike" means for protection. "Even if not bound": the particle 'pi' is concessive; the meaning is, how much more so if it is bound. "A little" means a small amount. "Which" refers to water. "That too" means that water too. The particle 'pi' refers to any small amount of water that remains unbound. The connection is: "which these grave rules are laid down." "Beforehand" means precisely, the very first—this is the meaning. "In these" refers to the grave rules. The connection is: "even while they were unpromulgated." The connection is: what was said previously, beginning with "what was said first," was said to show this meaning: "it will last for only a thousand years." And the statement "a thousand years" is connected. "From that" means from that thousand years. "The teaching of the true Dhamma too": the particle 'pi' refers to the true Dhamma of realization. It is not stated because when these two true Dhammas remain, the true Dhamma of practice remains also. "Only those" means only those five thousand years. The connection is: nor should it be said that when the teaching exists, realization does not exist. "Sign" means the appearance of a renunciate, the guise of a renunciate—this is the meaning.

Bhikkhunīupasampadānujānanakathā

Discussion on the Authorization of the Higher Ordination of Nuns

404. Imāya anupaññattiyāti mahāpajāpatiyā aṭṭhagarudhammapaṭiggahaṇūpasampadaṃ upanidhāya ayaṃ paññatti anupaññatti nāma, tāya anupaññattiyā upasampādetunti attho. Mahāpajāpatiyā saddhivihāriniyo katvāti mahāpajāpatiṃ upajjhaṃ katvā pañcasatā sākiyāniyo tassā saddhivihāriniyo katvāti attho. Itīti tasmā ahesunti sambandho. Iminā ovādenāti bhagavato iminā ovādena.

404. "By this supplementary rule" means that, in dependence on Mahāpajāpatī's acceptance of the eight grave rules as her higher ordination, this rule is called a supplementary rule; the meaning is, "to ordain by that supplementary rule." "Making them pupils of Mahāpajāpatī" means making Mahāpajāpatī the preceptor and making the five hundred Sakyan women her pupils—this is the meaning. The word "iti" (thus) is connected to "tasmā ahesuṃ" (therefore they were). "By this advice" means by this advice of the Blessed One.

410. Etissāti etissā bhikkhuniyā. Tanti kammaṃ. Aññasminti aññasmiṃ kamme. Aññanti ropitabbakammato aññaṃ kammaṃ.

410. 'For her' means for this bhikkhunī. 'That' refers to the act. 'In another' means in another act. 'Another' means an act other than the act to be established.

411. Kaddamodakenāti kaddamena āluḷitena udakeneva. Kaddamādīsupīti pīsaddo “yena kenacī”ti ettha yojetabbo. Yena kenacipīti hi attho. Sannipatitvāti bhikkhunisaṅghena sannipatitvā. Apasādanīyanti apasādetabbaṃ kammaṃ. Ettāvatāti ettakena sāvanamattena. Avandiyoti na vandetabbo, vandituṃ na arahoti attho. Tatoti tikkhattuṃ sāvetabbato. Na vandantīti bhikkhuniyo na vandanti. Disvāpīti taṃ bhikkhuṃ disvāpi. Tena bhikkhunāti apasādanīyaṃ dassentena bhikkhunā, khamāpetabbanti sambandho. Vihāreyevāti bhikkhūnaṃ vihāreyeva. Tena bhikkhunāti upasaṅkamitabbena [M 0.0538] bhikkhunā, vattabbanti sambandho. Tatoti vattabbakālato. Soti apasādanīyaṃ dassento bhikkhu. Etthāti bhikkhunikkhandhake. Kammavibhaṅgeti parivārāvasāne kammānaṃ vibhaṅgaṭṭhāne (pari. aṭṭha. 495-496).

411. 'With muddy water' means with water that has been mixed with mud. 'Even with mud, etc.'—the word 'even' should be applied here to 'by any means.' The meaning is 'by whatever means.' 'Having assembled' means having gathered together as a community of bhikkhunīs. 'Apasādanīya' refers to an act that should be disparaged. 'To this extent' means merely by this much announcement. 'Not to be paid respect' means one should not pay respect; the meaning is that they are not worthy of respect. 'From that' means from the fact that it must be announced three times. 'They do not pay respect' means the bhikkhunīs do not pay respect. 'Even having seen' means even after seeing that bhikkhu. 'By that bhikkhu' refers to the bhikkhu showing the disparaging act; 'should be asked for forgiveness' is the connection. 'In the monastery itself' means right in the bhikkhus' monastery. 'By that bhikkhu' refers to the bhikkhu who should be approached; 'should be spoken to' is the connection. 'From that' means from the time when it should be spoken. 'He' refers to the bhikkhu showing the disparaging act. 'Here' refers to the section on bhikkhunīs. 'In the analysis of the act' refers to the place where the analysis of acts is given at the end of the Parivāra (Parivāra-aṭṭhakathā 495-496).

Obhāsantīti ava hīnena bhāsantīti dassento āha “asaddhammena obhāsantī”ti. “Bhikkhunīhi saddhiṃ sampayojentī”ti ettha kammakaraṇe dassento āha “purise asaddhammenā”ti. Ettha “purise”ti iminā kammaṃ dasseti, “asaddhammenā”ti iminā karaṇaṃ. Vihārappavesaneti bhikkhūnaṃ vihārappavesane. Ovādaṃ ṭhapetunti ettha ovādaṭṭhapanākāraṃ dassento [V 2.0173] āha “na bhikkhunupassaya”ntiādi. Ovādatthāyāti ovādapaṭiggahaṇatthāya. Mā karitthāti mā kareyyātha.

Regarding 'obhāsanti,' showing that it means 'they speak in a low or inferior way,' he says, 'they disparage with the untrue Dhamma.' Regarding 'associating with bhikkhunīs,' showing the object and the instrument, he says, 'men with the untrue Dhamma.' Here, 'men' indicates the object, and 'with the untrue Dhamma' indicates the instrument. 'Entering the monastery' means the entering of bhikkhus into the monastery. Regarding 'stopping the exhortation,' showing the manner of stopping the exhortation, he says, 'not to the bhikkhunī residence,' and so on. 'For the purpose of exhortation' means for the purpose of receiving exhortation. 'Do not do it' means you should not do it.

416. Gihidārikāyoti gihibhūtā dārikāyo bandhanti viyāti yojanā. Ghanapaṭṭakenāti ghanabhūtena paṭṭena niyuttena. Ekapariyakanti ettha ekavāraṃ kaṭiyaṃ parikkhipitvā kataṃ kāyabandhanaṃ ekapariyakanti dassento āha “ekavāraṃ parikkhipanaka”nti. Tattha parikkhipanakanti kaṭiyaṃ parikkhipanārahaṃ.

416. 'Like lay girls' means the connection is 'as girls who are laypeople bind themselves.' 'With a thick belt' means with a belt that is thick and well-secured. Regarding 'a single wrapping,' showing that a body-binding made by wrapping it once around the waist is called 'a single wrapping,' he says, 'a single wrapping.' There, 'a wrapping' means fit to be wrapped around the waist.

Vilīvenāti ettha bahutthe ekavacananti āha “saṇhehi vilīvehī”ti. “Katapaṭṭenā”ti iminā pāḷiyaṃ “katenā”ti pāṭhasesaṃ dasseti. Setavatthapaṭṭenāti setavatthena katena paṭṭena. Kataveṇiyāti katāya veṇiyā. Iminā dussena katā veṇi dussaveṇīti vacanatthaṃ dasseti. Eseva nayo purimapacchimapadesupi. Coḷakāsāvanti coḷameva kasāvena rattattā coḷakāsāvaṃ.

'With a strip of bamboo'—here, it is a singular for a plural, as he says, 'with fine strips of bamboo.' By 'with a made belt,' he shows that 'made' is the remainder of the reading in the Pāli. 'With a white cloth belt' means with a belt made of white cloth. 'With a made braid' means with a braid that has been made. By this, he shows the meaning of the word 'cloth-braid' is a braid made of cloth. This same method applies to the preceding and following terms as well. 'An ochre cloth' means a piece of cloth that is an ochre cloth because it has been dyed with ochre.

Aṭṭhillenāti addena aṭṭhinā. “Gojaṅghaṭṭhike”ti iminā aṭṭhino sambandhaṃ dasseti. Hatthaṃ koṭṭāpentīti ettha hatthaṃ nāma aggabāhamevādhippetaṃ, na kapparato paṭṭhāyāti dassento āha “aggabāha”nti. Piṭṭhihatthanti hatthapiṭṭhiṃ. Piṭṭhipādanti pādapiṭṭhiṃ.

'With a piece of bone' means with a fresh bone. By 'a bone from a cow's leg,' he shows the context of the bone. Regarding 'they cause the arm to be struck,' here 'arm' is specifically intended to mean the forearm, not from the elbow onwards; showing this, he says, 'forearm.' 'Back of the hand' means the back of the hand. 'Back of the foot' means the back of the foot.

417. Vuttanayānevāti [M 0.0539] chabbaggiyānaṃ mukhalimpanādīsu (cūḷava. aṭṭha. 247) vuttanayāneva. Aṅgadeseti sarīrappadese. Gaṇḍappadeseti kapolappadese. Sāloke tiṭṭhantīti ettha saṃvijjati āloko etthāti sālokanti katvā dvāraṃ gahetabbaṃ. Tena vuttaṃ “dvāraṃ vivaritvā”ti. Vuṭṭhāpentīti upasampādenti. Sūnaṃ ṭhapentīti ettha sūnāsaddo maṃsapariyāyoti āha “maṃsaṃ vikkiṇantī”ti. Tenāti dāsena. Idaṃ padaṃ “kārentī”ti pade kāritakammaṃ. “Haritakañceva pakkañcā”ti iminā haritakapakkikanti padassa dvandavākyaṃ dasseti. Tattha haritakanti haritameva paṇṇaṃ. Pakkanti seditaṃ paṇṇaṃ.

417. 'In the very way that was stated' refers to the manner described in the case of the group-of-six bhikkhus regarding facial ointments, etc. (Cūḷavagga-aṭṭhakathā 247). 'A part of the limb' means a part of the body. 'A part of the cheek' means the cheek area. Regarding 'they stand in a place with light,' here, 'a place with light' should be understood as a door, because it is a place where light is present. Therefore, it is said, 'having opened the door.' 'They cause to stand up' means they ordain. Regarding 'they set up a butcher's shop,' here the word 'sūnā' is a synonym for meat, as he says, 'they sell meat.' 'By him' means by the slave. This word is the causative object of the word 'they cause to do.' By 'fresh and cooked,' he shows the dvandva phrase for the word 'haritakapakkika.' There, 'haritaka' means a fresh leaf. 'Pakka' means a steamed leaf.

418. Kathitāyevāti cīvarakkhandhake kathitāyeva.

418. 'Just as was stated' means just as was stated in the section on robes.

419. Pāḷimuttakavinicchayoti pāḷiyaṃ vuttavinicchayato mutto vinicchayo. Pāḷimuttakavinicchayaṃ vitthārento āha “sace hī”tiādi. Yo koci kālaṃ karonto vadatīti sambandho. Mamaccayenāti mama atikkamena. Aññassāti vuttehi upajjhāyādīhi aññassa[V 2.0174]. Tesanti upajjhāyādīnaṃ. Na hotīti parikkhāro na hoti. Hīti saccaṃ, yasmā vā. Accayadānanti accayena hotūti dānaṃ. Na ruhatīti pañcannaṃ sahadhammikānaṃ pabbajitassa vā gahaṭṭhassa vā yassa kassaci accayadānaṃ tesaṃ na ruhati, saṅghasseva ruhatīti adhippāyo. Gihīnaṃ pana accayadānanti sambandho. Ruhatīti gihīnaṃ pabbajitassa vā gahaṭṭhassa vā yassa kassaci accayadānaṃ tesaṃ ruhati, tesaṃyeva santako hotīti adhippāyo.

419. 'A judgment independent of the Pāli' means a judgment that is independent of the judgment stated in the Pāli. Elaborating on 'a judgment independent of the Pāli,' he says, 'if indeed,' and so on. The connection is, 'Whoever, while dying, says...' 'After my passing' means after I have passed away. 'To another' means to another, other than the aforementioned preceptor and so on. 'Of them' refers to the preceptor and so on. 'It is not' means the requisite is not. 'Hi' means truly, or because. 'A bequest' means a gift given with the words, 'Let this be after my passing.' 'It does not accrue' means a bequest made to any of the five co-religionists, whether ordained or a householder, does not accrue to them; the intention is that it accrues only to the Saṅgha. For laypeople, however, 'a bequest' is connected. 'It accrues' means for laypeople, a bequest made to anyone, whether ordained or a householder, accrues to them; the intention is that it becomes their own property.

420. Purāṇamallīti ettha mallassa bhariyā mallī, purāṇe mallī purāṇamallīti dassento āha “purāṇe”tiādi. “Gihikāle”ti iminā “purāṇe”ti ettha ṇapaccayassa sarūpaṃ dasseti. Mallassāti muṭṭhimallassa. Purisabyañjananti ettha byañjanasaddo nimittapariyāyoti āha “purisanimitta”nti. Cittanti rāgacittaṃ.

420. Regarding 'Purāṇamallī,' here, Mallī is the wife of Malla; showing that 'the former Mallī is Purāṇamallī,' he says, 'purāṇe,' and so on. By 'in his time as a householder,' he shows the nature of the suffix '-ṇa' in 'purāṇe.' 'Of Malla' means of the wrestler Muṭṭhimalla. Regarding 'the male characteristic,' here the word 'byañjana' is a synonym for 'sign,' as he says, 'purisanimitta' (male sign). 'Mind' means a mind of lust.

421. Yanti [M 0.0540] yaṃ vatthu, agganti paṭhamabhāgaṃ. Asappāyanti attano asappāyaṃ.

421. 'Which' means which thing. 'The best' means the first part. 'Unsuitable' means unsuitable for oneself.

Hiyyoti atītānantarāhani. Aññasminti bhikkhunīhi aññasmiṃ. “Bhikkhunīhī”ti padaṃ “paṭiggāhāpetvā”ti pade kāritakammaṃ. Hīti saccaṃ, yasmā vā.

'Yesterday' means on the day immediately past. 'In another' means in another than the bhikkhunīs. The word 'by the bhikkhunīs' is the causative object in the phrase 'having had it received.' 'Hi' means truly, or because.

426. “Bhojanakāla”nti iminā “kālaṃ vītināmesu”nti ettha kālavisesaṃ dasseti.

426. By 'mealtime,' he indicates a specific time within the phrase 'let us pass the time.'

Pureti ādimhi. Tāsanti aṭṭhannaṃ bhikkhunīnaṃ. Abbhantarimāti abbhantare pariyāpannā. Aññāti aṭṭhahi bhikkhunīhi aññā. Navakatarā hotīti sambandho. “Ṭhapetvā bhattagga”nti iminā aññattha sabbattha yathāvuḍḍhaṃ na paṭibāhitabbanti ettha aññasaddassa apādānaṃ dasseti. Aññasminti ettha smiṃvacanena tthapaccayassa atthaṃ dasseti. “Catupaccayabhājanīyaṭṭhāne”ti iminā sarūpaṃ dasseti.

'Before' means at the beginning. 'Of them' means of the eight bhikkhunīs. 'Included within' means comprised within. 'Another' means another, other than the eight bhikkhunīs. The connection is, 'she is more junior.' By 'except for the meal hall,' it is shown that elsewhere seniority should not be obstructed; here, this shows the ablative sense of the word 'añña.' Regarding 'aññasmiṃ,' here the locative ending '-smiṃ' shows the meaning of the suffix '-ttha.' By 'in the place suitable for the distribution of the four requisites,' he shows its form.

430. Dūtenapi upasampādetunti ettha kiṃ sabbathā dūtena upasampadā vaṭṭatīti āha “dūtena…pe… vaṭṭatī”ti. Yena kenaci antarāyenāti sambandho, asati antarāye na vaṭṭatīti adhippāyo. Kammavācāpariyosāne upasampannāva hotīti sambandho. Tāvadevāti upasampannakkhaṇeyeva.

430. Regarding 'she may be ordained even by a messenger,' here, he asks, 'Is ordination by a messenger valid in every case?' and answers, 'By a messenger... it is valid.' The connection is, 'due to some obstacle or other'; the intention is that without an obstacle, it is not valid. The connection is, 'At the conclusion of the formal act, she is indeed ordained.' 'At that very moment' means at the very moment of ordination.

431. Navakammampīti [V 2.0175] pisaddo udositaupassaye apekkhati.

431. 'Even new work'—the word 'pi' refers to an abandoned dwelling.

432. Tassāti tassā itthiyā. Yāva so dārako viññutaṃ pāpuṇātīti ettha kathaṃ viññubhāvo gahetabboti āha “yāva khāditu”ntiādi.

432. 'Of her' means of that woman. Regarding 'Until that boy reaches understanding,' here, he asks, 'how should the state of understanding be understood?' and answers, 'until he can eat,' and so on.

Ṭhapetvā sāgāranti ettha sakāro sahasaddakāriyo, agāranti ca seyyāgāranti dassento āha “sahāgāraseyyamattaṃ ṭhapetvā”ti. Yathā aññasmiṃ purise paṭipajjitabbaṃ, evaṃ tathāti yojanā. “Aññasmi”nti iminā pāḷiyaṃ aññe puriseti ettha smiṃvacanassa sabbanāmato ekārādeso [M 0.0541] dassito, taṃdassanena ca kaccāyane (kaccāyane 110 sutte) sabbanāmato smiṃvacanassa ekārādesanisedhanaṃ aniccanti dasseti.

Regarding 'Except for the dwelling' (sāgāran): here, the 'sa' has the meaning of 'saha' (together), and showing that 'agāra' means 'seyyāgāra' (sleeping-quarters), he says: 'except for sharing the same lodging.' 'As one should act towards another man, so in that case'—this is the connection. By 'In another' (aññasmiṃ), it is shown that in the Pāli 'another man' (aññe purise), the locative ending '-smiṃ' has been replaced by '-e' from the pronoun. And by showing this, it indicates that in the Kaccāyana grammar (Kaccāyana 110 sutta), the prohibition of the replacement of '-smiṃ' with '-e' from pronouns is not invariable.

434. “Yadeva sā vibbhantā”ti iminā dassetīti sambandho. “Yasmā”ti iminā yadevāti ettha yaṃsaddassa kāraṇatthaṃ dasseti. Odātāni vatthāni nivatthāti sambandho. “Tasmāyevā”ti iminā tadevāti padassa kāraṇatthameva dasseti. “Na sikkhāpaccakkhānenā”ti iminā evatthaphalaṃ dasseti. Sā puna upasampadaṃ na labhatīti sā vibbhantā bhikkhunī puna upasampadaṃ na labhati.

434. The connection is with what is shown by 'Because she has gone astray.' By 'Because' (yasmā), he shows the causal meaning of the word 'yaṃ' in 'yadeva'. The connection is with 'she is clothed in white garments.' By 'Therefore' (tasmāyeva), he shows the causal meaning of the word 'tadeva'. By 'not by rejection of the training,' he shows the result of the emphatic particle 'eva'. 'She does not obtain higher ordination again' means that the nun who has gone astray does not obtain higher ordination again.

Pabbajjampi na labhatīti titthāyatanasaṅkantā bhikkhunī pabbajjampi na labhati, pageva upasampadaṃ.

‘She does not even obtain monastic ordination’ means that a nun who has gone over to a sectarian group does not obtain monastic ordination, let alone higher ordination.

Pāde sambāhantāti bhikkhunīnaṃ pāde sambāhantā. Keseti bhikkhunīnaṃ kese. Tatrāti “kukkuccayantā na sādiyantī”ti vacane. Eke ācariyā vadantīti sambandho. Sārattā hontīti yojanā. Etthāti purisānaṃ abhivādanādīsu. Idanti purisānaṃ abhivādanādi, “anuññāta”nti pade vuttakammaṃ “vaṭṭatī”ti pade vuttakattā. Atha vā odissa anuññātaṃ idaṃ purisānaṃ abhivādanādi vaṭṭatīti yojanā. Evañhi sati “odissa anuññāta”nti padaṃ hetuantogadhavisesanaṃ, odissa anuññātattā vaṭṭatīti adhippāyo. Tanti aṭṭhakathāsu vuttavacanaṃ. Hīti saccaṃ, yasmā vā.

‘Massaging the feet’ means massaging the feet of the nuns. ‘Hair’ means the hair of the nuns. ‘There’ means in the statement, ‘being scrupulous, they do not consent.’ The connection is ‘some teachers say.’ The interpretation is ‘they become impassioned.’ ‘Here’ means in regard to bowing down to men, etc. ‘This’ means bowing down to men, etc., which is the object stated in the word ‘allowed’ and the agent stated in the word ‘is permissible.’ Alternatively, the interpretation is: ‘This bowing down to men, etc., is permissible because it is specifically allowed.’ For if this is so, the phrase ‘specifically allowed’ is a qualifier included as a reason; the intention is that it is permissible because it has been specifically allowed. ‘That’ refers to the statement made in the commentaries. ‘Hi’ means truly, or because.

435. Pallaṅkena nisīdantīti ettha āsanapallaṅkaṃ paṭikkhipanto āha “pallaṅkaṃ ābhujitvā nisīdantī”ti. Tattha ābhujitvāti ābandhitvā. Kūpoti vaccakūpo. Uparīti kūpato [V 2.0176] upari. “Sabbadisāsu paññāyatī”ti iminā paṭicchannameva atthi, na upari channanti dasseti.

435. Regarding 'Sitting cross-legged': here, rejecting a couch-seat, he says, 'sitting having folded the legs crosswise.' There, 'having folded' means 'having bound.' 'A pit' means a cesspit. 'Above' means above the pit. By 'it is visible in all directions,' he shows that it is only screened at the sides, not covered above.

436. Kuṇḍakanti kaṇaṃ. Etthāti bhikkhunikkhandhake.

436. ‘Kuṇḍaka’ means rice-bran. ‘Here’ means in the Bhikkhunīkhandhaka.

Iti bhikkhunikkhandhakavaṇṇanāya yojanā samattā.

Thus ends the interpretation in the commentary on the Bhikkhunīkhandhaka.

11. Pañcasatikakkhandhakaṃ

11. The Chapter of the Five Hundred

1. Khuddānukhuddakasikkhāpadakathā

1. The Discussion on the Minor and Lesser Training Rules

441. Pañcasatikakkhandhake [M 0.0542] “cattāri…pe… khuddakānī”ti evamādi vuttanti sambandho. Pariyāyenāti kāraṇena. Dhūmakālikanti ettha dhūmassa kālo dhūmakālo, dhūmassa uṭṭhitakāloti attho. So etassatthīti dhūmakālikaṃ, sikkhāpadapaññattaṃ. Iti imamatthaṃ dassento āha “yāvā”tiādi.

441. In the Pañcasatikakkhandhaka, the connection is with what was said beginning with ‘four… minor,’ and so forth. ‘By way’ means ‘by reason.’ Regarding ‘smoke-time’: here, ‘the time of smoke’ is ‘smoke-time,’ meaning the time when smoke has arisen. That which has this is ‘dhūmakālikaṃ,’ a laid-down training rule. Thus, showing this meaning, he says, ‘as long as…’ etc.

443. Idanti “katamāni pana bhante khuddānukhuddakāni sikkhāpadānī”ti apucchanaṃ. “Tayā”ti iminā idaṃ teti ettha tesaddassa “tuyhaṃ, tavā”ti atthe paṭikkhipati. Āpattinti dukkaṭāpattiṃ. Hīti saccaṃ, yasmā vā. Teti therā. “Saṅgho…pe… na samucchindatī”ti etaṃ vacanaṃ anussāvitanti yojanā. “Desehi taṃ āvuso dukkaṭa”nti idampi ca vuttanti sambandho. Thero panāti ānandatthero pana āhāti sambandho. Tatthāti apucchane. Yathāti yenākārena. Catūsu ṭhānesūti “bhagavato vassikasāṭikaṃ akkamitvā sibbesī”tiādīsu catūsu ṭhānesu. Etthāti pañcasatikakkhandhake.

443. ‘This’ refers to the failure to ask, ‘But, venerable sir, what are the minor and lesser training rules?’ By ‘by you,’ he rejects the meaning ‘of you’ or ‘yours’ for the word ‘te’ here in ‘idaṃ te.’ ‘An offense’ means an offense of wrong conduct. ‘Hi’ means truly, or because. ‘Te’ means the elders. The interpretation is that this statement, ‘The Saṅgha… does not abolish,’ was announced. The connection is that this too was said: ‘Friend, confess that offense of wrong conduct.’ ‘But the elder’: the connection is ‘but the elder Ānanda said.’ ‘There’ means in the failure to ask. ‘As’ means in what manner. ‘In four instances’ means in the four instances beginning with ‘he sewed the Blessed One’s rains-cloth after stepping on it.’ ‘Here’ means in the Pañcasatikakkhandhaka.

Iti pañcasatikakkhandhakavaṇṇanāya yojanā samattā.

Thus ends the interpretation in the commentary on the Pañcasatikakkhandhaka.

12. Sattasatikakkhandhakaṃ

12. The Chapter of the Seven Hundred

Dasavatthukathā

The Discussion on the Ten Points

447. Sattasatikakkhandhake [V 2.0177] vaḍḍhenti kaṭasinti ettha kaṭasīsaddo susānabhūmivācakoti dassento āha “punappunaṃ kaḷevaraṃ nikkhipamānā bhūmiṃ vaḍḍhentī”ti. Tattha kaḷevaranti dehaṃ. Tañhi kaḷe aṅgapaccaṅgānaṃ avayave sampiṇḍetvā variyati icchiyatīti kaḷevaranti vuccati. Evaṃ ghoraṃ kaṭasiṃ vaḍḍhentāva punabbhavaṃ ādiyantīti yojanā.

447. In the Sattasatikakkhandhaka, regarding ‘they increase the charnel ground,’ to show that the word ‘kaṭasī’ here is a term for a cemetery ground, he says: ‘Repeatedly depositing corpses, they expand the ground.’ There, ‘kaḷevara’ means the body. For it is called ‘kaḷevara’ because, having been gathered together in the limbs (kaḷe), the collection of major and minor members is enclosed (variyati) or desired (icchiyati). The interpretation is: Thus, while expanding such a dreadful charnel ground, they take up renewed existence.

454. Pāpakaṃ [M 0.0543] no āvuso katanti ettha nosaddo amhasaddakāriyo, chaṭṭhīkattā ca hotīti dassento āha “āvuso amhehi pāpakaṃ kata”nti.

454. Regarding ‘Friend, wrong has been done by us,’ here, showing that the word ‘no’ has the function of ‘amha’ (we/us) and is an agent in the genitive case, he says: ‘Friend, wrong has been done by us.’

455. “Piyavacana”nti iminā katamena tvaṃ bhūmi-vihārenāti ettha bhūmisaddo piyavācako ruḷhīsaddoti dasseti. “Āmantetī”ti iminā ālapanapadanti dasseti. Āvuso bhūmīti attho. Kullavihāro nāma mettāvihāro, so ca heṭṭhimajhānattaye yuttattā uttānavihāroti āha “uttānavihārenā”ti.

455. By ‘endearing speech,’ he shows that the word ‘bhūmi’ here, in ‘With what bhūmi-abiding, friend?,’ is a conventional term expressive of endearment. By ‘he addresses,’ he shows that it is a term of address. The meaning is ‘friend, bhūmi.’ The raft-abiding is the abiding in loving-kindness, and since that is connected with the lower three jhānas, it is a ‘manifest abiding’; thus he says ‘with a manifest abiding.’

457. Sāvatthiyāti sāvatthinagare. Suttavibhaṅgeti padabhājanīye. Paṭikkhittabhāvaṃ vitthārento āha “tatra hī”tiādi. Tatrāti suttavibhaṅge, paṭikkhittaṃ hotīti sambandho. Tatrāti “sannidhikārake asannidhikārakasaññī”tiādivacane. Eke ācariyā evaṃ maññantīti yojanā. Kinti maññantīti āha “yo pana bhikkhū”tiādi. Aloṇakaṃ yampi āmisanti yojanā. Tenāti purepariggahitaloṇena. Tanti āmisaṃ. Tadahupaṭiggahitamevāti tasmiṃ ahani paṭiggahitameva. Tasmāti yasmā tadahupaṭiggahitameva, tasmā. Vadatoti vadantassa, bhagavato vacanenāti sambandho. Etthāti aloṇakāmisaparibhuñjane, dukkaṭena bhavitabbaṃ iti maññantīti yojanā. Teti eke ācariyā. Dukkaṭenapīti pisaddena pageva pācittiyenāti dasseti. Hīti saccaṃ, yasmā vā. Etthāti yāvajīvikayāvakālikesu. Yāvajīvikaṃ na tadahupaṭiggahitaṃ, yāvakālikameva tadahupaṭiggahitanti yojanā. Tadahupaṭiggahitañca yāvakālikanti sambandho. Taṃ dukkaṭaṃ tumhe yadi [V 2.0178] maññathāti yojanā. Yāvajīvikamissanti loṇasaṅkhātena yāvajīvikena saṃsaṭṭhaṃ. Byañjanamattanti vikāle na kappatīti byañjanamattaṃ.

457. ‘At Sāvatthī’ means in the city of Sāvatthī. ‘In the Suttavibhaṅga’ means in the Padabhājanīya. Elaborating on its being prohibited, he says: ‘For there…’ etc. ‘There’ means in the Suttavibhaṅga; the connection is ‘it is prohibited.’ ‘There’ means in the statement beginning with ‘perceiving what is stored as not stored,’ etc. The interpretation is that some teachers think thus. How do they think? He says: ‘But if a monk…’ etc. The interpretation is ‘even relish without salt.’ ‘With that’ means with salt accepted previously. ‘That’ refers to the relish. ‘Accepted that very day’ means accepted on that same day. ‘Therefore’ means because it was accepted that very day, therefore. ‘Of the one who speaks’—the connection is ‘by the word of the Blessed One.’ ‘Here’ refers to consuming relish without salt; the interpretation is that they think it must be an offense of wrong conduct. ‘They’ refers to some teachers. By ‘even an offense of wrong conduct,’ with the word ‘even,’ he shows ‘let alone a pācittiya offense.’ ‘Hi’ means truly, or because. ‘Here’ means regarding lifelong and temporary items. The interpretation is that a lifelong item is not one accepted on that same day; only a temporary item is one accepted on that same day. The connection is ‘and a temporary item is one accepted on that same day.’ The interpretation is ‘if you think that is an offense of wrong conduct.’ ‘Mixed with a lifelong item’ means mixed with the lifelong item designated as salt. ‘Merely a condiment’ means it is not allowable at the wrong time, hence ‘merely a condiment.’

Etthāti “yāvakālikena bhikkhave”tiādivacane (mahāva. 305) tadahupaṭiggahitaṃ yāvajīvikanti yojanā. Yāvakālikassa gati viya gati etassāti [M 0.0544] yāvakālikagatikaṃ. Tasmā dukkaṭaṃ na hotīti sambandho. Etthāti purepaṭiggahitaloṇena āmisaparibhuñjane. Tadahupaṭiggahitaṃ yāvakālikena sambhinnarasaṃ yāvajīvikanti yojanā. Tanti yathāvuttaṃ yāvajīvikaṃ, vikālabhojanapācittiyā eva kāraṇaṃ hotīti yojanā. Evanti tathā, ajja paṭiggahitampi yāvajīvikanti sambandho. Aparajju paṭiggahitena yāvakālikenāti yojanā. Tanti yāvajīvikena sammissaṃ yāvakālikaṃ, ajānantopīti sambandho. Idanti yathāvuttaṃ yāvakālikaṃ. Tatoti sannidhibhojanapācittiyato. Hīti saccaṃ. “Sāvatthiyā suttavibhaṅge”ti idaṃ byākaraṇaṃ parisuddhanti yojanā.

‘Here,’ in the statement beginning with ‘for a limited time, monks,’ etc. (Mahāvagga 305), the interpretation is that what was received on that day is lifelong. Something whose nature is like the duration of something temporary is ‘temporary in nature.’ Therefore, no dukkaṭa offense occurs—this is the connection. ‘Here’ means in consuming food with salt received previously. The interpretation is that a lifelong item received on that day, having its flavor mixed with a temporary item, is lifelong. The interpretation is that that, the aforementioned lifelong item, is the very reason for the pācittiya offense of eating at the wrong time. ‘Thus’ means in that way; the connection is that even a lifelong item received today is lifelong. The interpretation is: with a temporary item received on the next day. ‘That’ refers to a temporary item mixed with a lifelong item; the connection is ‘even if one does not know.’ ‘This’ refers to the aforementioned temporary item. ‘From that’ means from the pācittiya offense of consuming stored food. ‘Indeed’ means truly. The interpretation is that this explanation, ‘In the Suttavibhaṅga at Sāvatthī,’ is pure.

“Rājagahe uposathasaṃyutte”ti idaṃ vacanaṃ vuttanti sambandho. Uposathasaṃyutteti uposathena sambandhe uposathakkhandhake. Kiṃ sandhāya vuttanti āha “na bhikkhave…pe… dukkaṭassāti (mahāva. 141) etaṃ sandhāyā”ti. Atisāreti atikkamitvā saraṇe gamane pavattaneti attho. Nimittatthe cetaṃ bhummaṃ. “Campeyyake vinayavatthusmi”nti idaṃ vuttanti sambandho. “Campeyyakkhandhake āgata”nti iminā campeyye āgataṃ campeyyakanti vacanatthaṃ dasseti.

The connection is that this statement, ‘In Rājagaha, in the Uposathasaṃyutta,’ was stated. ‘In the Uposathasaṃyutta’ means in connection with the Uposatha, in the Uposatha Khandhaka. Regarding what was intended by this, he says, ‘This was intended: “Monks, not… up to… of a dukkaṭa offense” (Mahāvagga 141).’ ‘Atisāreti’ means having transgressed, in going to refuge, in proceeding; this is the meaning. And this is a locative case indicating purpose. The connection is that this was stated: ‘In the Vinaya matter at Campeyya.’ With the phrase ‘what has come in the Campeyya Khandhaka,’ he shows the meaning of the word ‘Campeyyaka’ to be ‘what has come in Campeyya.’

Dhammikanti bhūtena pavattaṃ. Suttavibhaṅge hi yasmā āgatanti sambandho. Dasāyevāti dasāyameva, ādhāre cetaṃ bhummaṃ. Vidatthimattāti vidatthipamāṇā. Dasāya vināti dasaṃ vajjetvā. Taṃ pamāṇanti vidatthittayasaṅkhātaṃ taṃ pamāṇaṃ karontassa vuttapācittiyaṃ āpajjatīti sambandho. “Taṃ atikkāmayato chedanakaṃ pācittiya”nti (pāci. 533) idaṃ vacanaṃ āgatameva hotīti yojanā. Sabbatthāti sabbasmiṃ sattasatikakkhandhake.

‘Dhammika’ means what has occurred in truth. Indeed, in the Suttavibhaṅga, the connection is because it has come. ‘Dasāyeva’ means only on the fringe, and this is a locative case indicating basis. ‘Vidatthimatta’ means of the measure of a span. ‘Dasāya vinā’ means excluding the fringe. ‘That measurement’: the connection is that one who makes that measurement, reckoned as three spans, incurs the stated pācittiya offense. The interpretation is that this statement, ‘For one who exceeds that, it is a pācittiya offense requiring cutting’ (Pāci. 533), has indeed come. ‘Sabbatthā’ means everywhere, in the entire Sattasatikakkhandhaka.

Iti samantapāsādikāya vinayasaṃvaṇṇanāya

Thus, in the Samantapāsādikā, the Exposition of the Vinaya,

Sattasatikakkhandhakavaṇṇanāya

in the commentary on the Khandhaka of the Seven Hundred,

Yojanā samattā.

the interpretation is complete.

Dvivaggasaṅgahāti [M 0.0545] mahāvaggacūḷavaggavasena dvīhi vaggehi saṅgahitā. Dvāvīsatipabhedanāti mahāvagge [V 2.0179] dasa, cūḷavagge dvādasāti evaṃ dvāvīsatipakārā. Pañcakkhandhadukkhappahāyinoti pañcakkhandhasaṅkhātaṃ dukkhaṃ pajahanasīlassa, bhagavatoti sambandho. Āsāpīti icchāpi. Ayaṃ panettha yojanā-pañcakkhandhadukkhappahāyino bhagavato sāsane dvivaggasaṅgahā dvāvīsatipabhedanā ye khandhakā bhagavatā vuttā, tesaṃ khandhakānaṃ esā vaṇṇanā antarāyaṃ vinā yathā siddhā, evaṃ tathā pāṇīnaṃ kalyāṇā āsāpi sijjhantūti.

‘Dvivaggasaṅgahā’ (collected into two sections) means collected into two sections, namely the Mahāvagga and the Cūḷavagga. ‘Dvāvīsatipabhedanā’ (divided into twenty-two distinctions) means ten in the Mahāvagga and twelve in the Cūḷavagga, thus twenty-two types. ‘Pañcakkhandhadukkhappahāyino’ (of one who abandons the suffering of the five aggregates) is connected to ‘Bhagavato’ (of the Blessed One), meaning of one whose nature is to abandon the suffering designated as the five aggregates. ‘Āsāpi’ means also ‘icchā’ (desire). Herein, the construction is as follows: In the Dispensation of the Blessed One, who abandons the suffering of the five aggregates, the Khandhakas that were spoken by the Blessed One are collected into two sections and divided into twenty-two distinctions—just as this commentary on those Khandhakas has been accomplished without obstruction, so too may the wholesome aspirations of beings be fulfilled.

Iti samantapāsādikāya vinayasaṃvaṇṇanāya

Thus ends the Samantapāsādikā, the commentary on the Vinaya.

Cūḷavaggasaṃvaṇṇanāya

Commentary on the Cūḷavagga.

Yojanā samattā.

The explanation is complete.

Jādilañchitanāmena, nekānaṃ vācito mayā;

Cūḷavaggakhandhakassa, samatto yojanānayoti.

By the name Jādilañchita, I was requested by many; the method of explanation for the Cūḷavagga Khandhaka is complete.

Namo tassa bhagavato arahato sammāsambuddhassa

Homage to that Blessed One, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One.

Pācityādiyojanā

Explanation of the Pācittiya, etc.

Parivāravaggayojanā

Explanation of the Parivāra Chapter.

Cūḷavaggakhandhakassevaṃ[V 2.0181][M 0.0547], katvāna yojanānayaṃ;

Adhunā parivārassa, karissaṃ yojanānayaṃ.

Having thus made the method of explanation for the Cūḷavagga Khandhaka, now I shall make the method of explanation for the Parivāra.

Soḷasamahāvāro

The Sixteen Great Chapters.

Paññattivārayojanā

Explanation of the Paññatti Chapter.

Evaṃ dvāvīsatikhandhakānaṃ saṃvaṇṇanaṃ katvā idāni “parivāro”ti saṅgahamārūḷhassa vinayassa saṃvaṇṇanaṃ karonto ayamācariyo paṭhamaṃ tāva anusandhidassanamukhena paṭiññaṃ kātukāmo [V 2.0182] āha “visuddhaparivārassā”tiādi. Tattha visuddhaparivārassāti visuddhāya catuparisāya parivāritassa, athavā visuddhena catuparisasaṅkhātena parivārena samannāgatassa bhagavatoti sambandho. Parivāre hi visuddhe tena parivārito, taṃparivārito vā bhagavāpi visuddhoyeva nāma hoti. Iminā saṃvaṇṇiyamānassa “parivāro”ti saṅgahamārūḷhassa desetabbadhammassa anurūpena desakabhūtassa bhagavato thomanaṃ kataṃ hoti. Dhammakkhandhasarīrassāti sīlādidhammakkhandhasaṅkhātena sarīrena samannāgatassa, iminā saṃvaṇṇitānaṃ khandhakānamanurūpena bhagavato thomanaṃ kataṃ hoti. Pakati hesācariyānaṃ yadidaṃ desetabbadhammānurūpena desakassa thomanā (sārattha. ṭī. 1.ganthārambhakathā; visuddhi. mahāṭī. 1.1). Anantarāti anantare kāle.

Having thus made an exposition of the twenty-two Khandhakas, now this teacher, wishing first to make a declaration by way of showing the connection, begins the exposition of the Vinaya, which has come to be compiled as ‘Parivāra,’ saying ‘visuddhaparivārassā’tiādi (of one with a pure retinue, etc.). Therein, ‘of one with a pure retinue’ is connected to ‘of the Blessed One,’ meaning of one who is surrounded by the pure fourfold assembly, or endowed with a pure retinue consisting of the fourfold assembly. For when the retinue is pure, the Blessed One, being surrounded by it or having it as his retinue, is indeed called pure. By this, praise is given to the Blessed One, who is the speaker, in a manner befitting the Dhamma to be taught, which is being expounded and has come to be compiled as ‘Parivāra’. ‘Of one with a body of Dhamma aggregates’ means of one endowed with a body consisting of the aggregates of Dhamma, such as virtue and so forth. By this, praise is given to the Blessed One in a manner befitting the Khandhakas that have been expounded. For this is the custom of teachers: praise of the speaker in accordance with the Dhamma to be taught (Sāratthadīpanī-ṭīkā 1, Ganthārambhakathā; Visuddhimahāṭīkā 1.1). ‘Anantarā’ means in the immediately following time.

Yoti [M 0.0548] vinayo. Pubbāgatanti pubbe vuttesu vibhaṅgakhandhakesu āgataṃ. Nayanti saddaatthavinicchayanayasaṅkhātaṃ sabbaṃ nayaṃ. Hitvāti cajitvā. Anuttānatthavaṇṇananti anuttānānaṃ padānamatthavaṇṇanaṃ. Ayaṃ panettha yojanā – visuddhaparivārassa dhammakkhandhasarīrassa bhagavato sāsane khandhakānamanantarā “parivāro”ti yo vinayo saṅgahaṃ samārūḷho, tassa vinayassa pubbāgataṃ nayaṃ hitvā idāni anuttānatthavaṇṇanaṃ karissāmīti.

‘Yo’ means the Vinaya. ‘Pubbāgataṃ’ means that which has come in the previously spoken Vibhaṅga and Khandhaka sections. ‘Nayaṃ’ means the entire method, reckoned as the method of determining word and meaning. ‘Hitvā’ means ‘cajitvā’ (having given up). ‘Anuttānatthavaṇṇanaṃ’ is the explanation of the meaning of unclear terms. Herein, the construction is as follows: In the Dispensation of the Blessed One, who has a pure retinue and a body of Dhamma aggregates, regarding that Vinaya which follows the Khandhakas and has come to be compiled as ‘Parivāra’—having set aside its previously established method, I shall now make an explanation of its unclear meanings.

1. Tattha tatthāti “tassa anuttānatthavaṇṇanaṃ karissāmī”ti yo parivārasaṅkhāto vinayo saṃvaṇṇetabbabhāvena vutto, tattha. Saṅkhepatthoti samāsattho. Yaṃ tenāti ettha tasaddassa aniyamaniddesabhāvaṃ dassento āha “yo so”ti. Tattha yoti aniyama niddeso, tassa “tenā”ti niyamanaṃ daṭṭhabbaṃ. Soti padālaṅkāro. Dvīsu hi sabbanāmesu yebhuyyena pubbameva padhānaṃ, pacchimaṃ pana vacanālaṅkāraṃ. Yo so bhagavā paññapesīti sambandho. Ciraṭṭhitikatthanti ciraṃ pañcavassasahassakālaṃ ṭhitikatthāya, “yācito”ti ca “paññapesī”ti ca sambandho. Dhammasenāpatinā yācitoti sambandho. Yācito hutvā paññapesīti yojanā. Tena bhagavatā paññattanti sambandho. “Jānatā passatā”ti dvinnaṃ padānaṃ kammameva dassento āha “tassa tassā”tiādi. Tattha “paññattikāla”nti iminā “jānatā”ti padassa kammaṃ dasseti, “dasa atthavase”ti iminā “passatā”ti padassa kammaṃ.

1. ‘Tattha tattha’ means therein, in that Vinaya known as the Parivāra, which was mentioned as needing to be commented on, when it was said: ‘tassa anuttānatthavaṇṇanaṃ karissāmī’ti (I shall make an explanation of its unclear meanings). ‘Saṅkhepattho’ means ‘samāsattho’ (brief meaning). Regarding ‘yaṃ tena,’ here, to show the indefinite nature of the word ‘ta,’ he says ‘yo so.’ Here, ‘yo’ is an indefinite reference, and its definite form ‘tena’ should be understood. ‘So’ is a particle of embellishment. For in two pronouns, the former is usually primary, while the latter is a verbal embellishment. The connection is ‘yo so bhagavā paññapesī’ (that Blessed One promulgated). ‘Ciraṭṭhitikatthaṃ’ means for the purpose of lasting for a long time, for a period of five thousand years; it is connected to both ‘yācito’ (having been requested) and ‘paññapesī’ (he promulgated). The connection is ‘Dhammasenāpatinā yācito’ (requested by the General of the Dhamma). The construction is: ‘Having been requested, he promulgated.’ The connection is ‘tena bhagavatā paññattaṃ’ (promulgated by that Blessed One). To show the object of the two words ‘jānatā’ (knowing) and ‘passatā’ (seeing), he says ‘tassa tassā,’ etc. Here, with ‘paññattikālaṃ’ he indicates the object of the word ‘jānatā,’ and with ‘dasa atthavase’ he indicates the object of the word ‘passatā.’

Evaṃ kammadassanena yojanānayaṃ dassetvā idāni karaṇadassanena aparampi yojanānayaṃ dassento āha “apicā”tiādi. “Pubbenivāsādīhī”tiādisaddena dibbacakkhussa visuṃ gahetabbattā iddhividhadibbasotaparacittavijānanāni gahetabbāni. Imehi padehi “jānatā, passatā”ti [V 2.0183] dvinnaṃ padānaṃ pañcannaṃ lokiyaabhiññānameva karaṇabhāvaṃ dasseti. Tīhi vijjāhīti pubbenivāsadibbacakkhuāsavakkhayañāṇasaṅkhātāhi tīhi vijjāhi. Chahi vā pana abhiññāhīti saha āsavakkhayañāṇena pañcalokiyābhiññāsaṅkhātāhi chahi abhiññāhi. Sabbatthāti [M 0.0549] sabbesu tīsu kālesu, pañcasupi ñeyyadhammesu. Samantacakkhunāti anāvaraṇasabbaññutaññāṇasaṅkhātena samantacakkhunā. Paññāyāti sabbaññutapaññāya. Tirokuṭṭādīti ādisaddena tiropabbatādayo saṅgaṇhāti. Maṃsacakkhunāti pasādacakkhunā. Paṭivedhapaññāyāti maggapaññāya. Desanāpaññāyāti sabbaññutapaññāya. Sabbaññutapaññāyeva hi atthato desanāpaññā nāma. Tena vuttaṃ “tassā paññāya tejasā. Abhidhammakathāmaggaṃ, devānaṃ sampavattayīti (dha. sa. aṭṭha. ganthārambhakathā 5). Imehi padehi avatthāvasena visuṃ visuṃ dvinnaṃ padānaṃ karaṇasambhavaṃ dasseti. Arahatāti arīnaṃ arānañca hatattā, paccayādīnañca arahattā arahatā. Sammāsambuddhenāti sammā sāmañca sabbadhammānaṃ buddhattā sammāsambuddhena, tena bhagavatāti sambandho.
