Aṅgulimattampīti pisaddena kesaggamattampīti atthaṃ sampiṇḍeti. Tanti mañcapīṭhaṃ. Gamiyo āpajjati nāmāti sambandho.

In aṅgulimattampi (even a finger's breadth), the word pi includes the meaning 'even a hair's tip.' Taṃ refers to a bed or bench. The connection is: 'a traveler commits an offense.'

“Ādiyanto āpajjati nāmā”tiādinā atthāpatti ādiyanto āpajjatīti pāḷiyaṃ ādiyanto hutvā āpajjati āpatti atthīti yojanānayaṃ dasseti. Evañhi sati “āpajjatī”ti ākhyātapadaṃ “atthī”ti kiriyantaraṃ apekkhitvā kattā hotīti daṭṭhabbaṃ. Atha vā ādiyanto puggalo yaṃ āpattiṃ āpajjati, sā āpatti atthīti yojanā. Eseva nayo aññesupi. Mūgabbatādīnīti ādisaddena govatakukkuravatādīni saṅgaṇhāti. Pārivāsikādayo āpajjantīti sambandho. Tajjanīyādikammakatā vā puggalāti yojanā. Asamādiyantā [M 0.0568] āpajjantīti asamādiyantā hutvā āpajjanti. Teti puggale. Karonto āpajjati nāmāti karonto hutvā āpajjati nāmāti yojanā. Evaṃ dento āpajjati nāmātiādīsupi.

By the phrase 'Ādiyanto āpajjati nāma' and so forth, it shows the method of construction that in the Pāli phrase 'ādiyanto āpajjati', the meaning is 'having taken, one incurs; an offense exists.' Thus, this being the case, it should be understood that the finite verb āpajjati becomes the agent by depending on another verb, atthi. Alternatively, the construction is: 'whatever offense a person who takes incurs, that offense exists.' The same method applies in other cases as well. By the word ādi in mūgabbatādīni, vows such as the cow-vow and the dog-vow are included. The connection is: 'those undergoing probation and so forth incur.' Or the construction is: 'persons who are subject to a formal act of censure and so forth.' Asamādiyantā āpajjanti means 'having not undertaken, they incur.' Te refers to those persons. The construction of Karonto āpajjati nāma is 'having done, one incurs an offense.' Similarly in dento āpajjati nāma and so forth.

Ekarattachārattasattāhadasāhamāsātikkamesūti “ekarattampi ticīvarena vippavaseyyā”ti (pārā. 475-476) ca “chārattaparamaṃ tena bhikkhunā tena cīvarena vippavasitabba”nti (pārā. 653) ca “sattāhaparamaṃ sannidhikārakaṃ paribhuñjitabba”nti [V 2.0200] (pārā. 622-623) ca “dasāhaparamaṃ atirekacīvaraṃ dhāretabba”nti (pārā. 462-463) ca “māsaparamaṃ nikkhipitabba”nti (pārā. 499-500) ca vuttakālātikkamesu.

The phrase Ekarattachārattasattāhadasāhamāsātikkamesu refers to the exceeding of the stated time limits, namely: 'even if one should remain apart from the three robes for a single night' (Pārā. 475-476); 'that bhikkhu should remain apart from that robe for a maximum of six nights' (Pārā. 653); 'what has been stored is to be used within a maximum of seven days' (Pārā. 622-623); 'an extra robe may be kept for a maximum of ten days' (Pārā. 462-463); and 'it may be set aside for a maximum of one month' (Pārā. 499-500).

Imaṃ pana āpattiṃ āpajjati nāmāti sambandho.

The connection is: 'But he incurs this offense.'

Yasmiṃ pakkhe nisinnoti yasmiṃ pakkhe sayaṃ nisinno. Tesanti attano pakkhe nisinnānaṃ, nānāsaṃvāsakanti sambandho. Yesanti sakapakkhe nisinnānaṃ. Kammaṃ kopetīti nānāsaṃvāsakattā kammaṃ kopeti. Itaresanti parapakkhe nisinnānaṃ. Hatthapāsaṃ anāgatattā kammaṃ kopetīti yojanā. “Eseva nayo”ti vuttavacanaṃ vitthārento āha “yesaṃ hī”tiādi. Yesanti sakapakkhe vā parapakkhe vā nisinnānaṃ yesaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ. Soti bhikkhu. Āpajjitabbatoti āpajjitabbabhāvato. Iminā puggalena chahi samuṭṭhānehi āpajjitabbāti āpattiyoti vacanatthaṃ dasseti. Kammena vā salākaggāhena vāti ettha uddeso kamme lakkhaṇahāranayena saṅgahaṃ gacchati, vohārānussāvanā salākaggāheti dassento āha “uddeso ceva…pe… eka”nti. Pubbabhāgāti saṅghabhedassa pubbabhāge pavattā. Pamāṇanti saṅghabhedassa kāraṇaṃ.

Yasmiṃ pakkhe nisinno means 'on which side he himself sits.' Tesaṃ refers to those sitting on his own side; the connection is nānāsaṃvāsaka. Yesaṃ refers to those sitting on his own side. Kammaṃ kopeti means 'he disrupts the formal act because he is in non-communion.' Itaresaṃ refers to those sitting on the opposite side. The construction is that 'he disrupts the formal act because they have not come within arm's reach.' Expanding on the statement 'Eseva nayo' (This is the method), he says, 'Yesaṃ hi' and so forth. Yesaṃ refers to those bhikkhus sitting on his own side or on the opposite side. So refers to the bhikkhu. Āpajjitabbato means 'from the state of being liable to incur.' By this, he shows the meaning of the word āpatti (offense) as 'it should be incurred by this person through the six origins.' In 'by a formal act or by taking a voting slip,' here the recitation is included under 'formal act' by the method of applying the characteristic, while showing that the announcement is the taking of a voting slip, he says: 'the recitation indeed... up to one.' Pubbabhāga refers to what occurs in the preliminary stage of schism. Pamāṇa refers to the cause of schism.

Addhānahīno nāmāti ettha addhānasaddo kālapariyāyoti āha “ūnavīsativasso”ti. Theyyasaṃvāsakādayotiādisaddena titthiyapakkantakabhikkhunīdūsakapañcānantariyā saṅgahetabbā. Aṭṭha abhabbapuggalā [M 0.0569] karaṇadukkaṭakā nāma hontīti yojanā. Ettha kattabbanti karaṇaṃ, kammaṃ, duṭṭhu kattabbanti dukkaṭaṃ, kammameva. Karaṇaṃ dukkaṭametassāti karaṇadukkaṭako. Visesanaparanipāto “agyāhito”tiādīsu viya. Tadevatthaṃ dassento āha “dukkaṭakiriyā”tiādi. No ca yācatīti ettha yācadhātuyā padhānakammaṃ dassento āha “upasampada”nti, “saṅgha”nti apadhānakammamānetabbaṃ. Tepiṭakoti tipiṭakaṃ vācuggatavasena dhārako. Āṇāyapīti pisaddo “matenapī”ti atthaṃ sampiṇḍeti. Yācantassevāti nissayaṃ ācariyaṃ yācantasseva. Yaṃ vatthuṃ ajjhācaranto āpattiṃ āpajjati, taṃ vatthu sātisāraṃ nāmāti yojanā.

In 'addhānahīno nāma' (one who is deficient in time), the word 'addhāna' here is a synonym for time, thus he says, 'less than twenty years old'. By the word 'ādi' in 'theyyasaṃvāsakādayo', those who have defected to other sects, those who have defiled bhikkhunīs, and those who have committed the five heinous offenses are to be included along with those who live in communion with thieves. The connection is that the eight incapable individuals are called 'karaṇadukkaṭakā'. Here, 'what is to be done' (kattabbaṃ) is an action (karaṇaṃ), a deed (kammaṃ); 'what is wrongly to be done' (duṭṭhu kattabbaṃ) is a wrongdoing (dukkaṭaṃ), the deed itself. 'Karaṇaṃ dukkaṭam etassa' means 'his action is a wrongdoing,' hence 'karaṇadukkaṭako'. The postposing of the adjective is like in 'agyāhito' and so forth. Showing that very meaning, he says, 'dukkaṭakiriyā' and so forth. In 'no ca yācati' (but he does not ask), showing the primary object of the root 'yāc', he says 'upasampadaṃ'; 'saṅghaṃ' should be understood as the secondary object. 'Tepiṭaka' is one who bears the Tipiṭaka by way of oral mastery. The particle 'pi' in 'āṇāyapi' combines the meaning of 'matenapi' (even by death). 'Yācantasseva' means 'of one who asks the teacher for dependence'. The connection is that the matter regarding which one, by transgressing, incurs an offense is called 'sātisāra'.

Upaghātikāti ettha upahanantīti upaghātā, teyeva upaghātikāti dassento āha “upaghātā”ti. Tatthāti dvīsu upaghātikesu. Dve venayikāti ettha vinayena siddhā venayikāti dassento āha “vinayasiddhā”ti. “Dve atthā”ti iminā ṇikasaddassa sarūpaṃ dasseti[V 2.0201]. Paññattānulomaṃ nāma daṭṭhabbanti sambandho. Paccayaghātoti paccayassa ghāto. Iminā setughātoti ettha setusaddo paccayavācakoti dasseti. Cittassāpīti pisaddo pageva kāyavācānanti dasseti. Itipīti pisaddo dutiyatthasampiṇḍano. “Pamāṇenā”ti iminā mattakāritāti ettha mattasaddo pamāṇatthoti dasseti. “Karaṇa”nti iminā kāritāti taddhitabhāvaṃ kitabhāvena dasseti sabhāgattā. Kāyadvārikanti kāyadvāre pavattaṃ āpattiṃ. Iminā āpajjatīti padassa kammaṃ dasseti. Kāyeneva vuṭṭhātīti kāyasāmaggiyā dānattā kāyeneva vuṭṭhāti. Sīsamakkhanādīti ādisaddena pādamakkhanādiṃ saṅgaṇhāti.

Here, 'upaghātikā' means 'those who harm,' thus 'upaghātā'; showing that these are 'upaghātikā,' he says 'upaghātā'. 'Tattha' refers to the two types of 'upaghātika'. In 'dve venayikā' (two who are skilled in the Vinaya), showing that 'venayikā' means 'accomplished in the Vinaya,' he says 'vinayasiddhā'. By 'dve atthā' (two meanings), he shows the form of a word with the suffix '-ika'. The connection is that 'it should be understood as conforming to the promulgation'. 'Paccayaghāto' means 'destruction of a condition'. By this, he shows that the word 'setu' in 'setughāto' refers to a condition. The word 'pi' in 'cittassāpi' indicates that it applies to body and speech even more so. The word 'pi' in 'itipi' consolidates the second meaning. By 'pamāṇena' (by measure), he shows that the word 'matta' in 'mattakāritā' means 'measure'. By 'karaṇa', he shows the derived state (taddhita) of 'kāritā' through its primary derivative (kṛt) form, due to their similarity. 'Kāyadvārika' refers to an offense that occurs through the bodily door. By this, he shows the object of the word 'āpajjati'. 'Kāyeneva vuṭṭhāti' means 'it emerges through the body itself' because it is given by means of bodily effort. By the word 'ādi' in 'sīsamakkhanādi', foot-anointing and so forth are included.

Tanti bhāraṃ. “Nittharituṃ vīriyaṃ ārabhatī”ti iminā vahanākāraṃ dasseti. Thero samānoti yojanā. Navahanākāraṃ dassento āha “anujānāmī”tiādi. “Kukkuccāyitvā karotī”ti iminā kukkuccasaddassa [M 0.0570] nāmadhātuṃ dasseti. “Divā ca ratto cā”ti iminā abhiṇhaṃ āsavavaḍḍhanaṃ dasseti. Tattha tatthāti tesu tesu vibhaṅgakkhandhakesu.

'Taṃ' refers to the burden. By 'nittharituṃ vīriyaṃ ārabhati' (he begins effort to accomplish), he shows the manner of carrying. The connection is that 'the elder is in agreement'. Showing a new manner of carrying, he says, 'I allow,' and so forth. By 'kukkuccāyitvā karoti' (he acts with scruples), he shows the denominative verb from the word 'kukkucca'. By 'divā ca ratto ca' (by day and by night), he shows the frequent increase of taints. 'Tattha tattha' refers to those various Vibhaṅgas and Khandhakas.

Iti dukavāravaṇṇanāya yojanā samattā.

Thus, the structural explanation of the section on pairs is completed.

Ekuttarikanayo tikavāravaṇṇanā

The Numerical Method: Commentary on the Section of Triplets.

323. Tikesu bhagavati tiṭṭhante yaṃ āpattiṃ āpajjati, sā āpatti atthīti yojanā. Sabbatthāti sabbesu padesu. Vitthāraṃ dassento āha “tatthā”tiādi. Tattha tatthāti tikesu, vitthāro evaṃ veditabboti yojanā. Lohituppādāpattīti anulomapārājikāpatti. “Āvusovādenā”ti “āvuso”ti vohārena. Voti tumhehi.

323. The connection is: In the triplets, while the Blessed One is present, whatever offense one commits, that offense exists. 'Sabbattha' means in all places. Showing the detail, he says, 'tattha,' etc. The connection is: 'Tattha tattha' means 'in the triplets', and the detailed explanation should be understood thus. 'The offense of causing blood to flow' is an offense analogous to a pārājika. 'By addressing as "āvuso"' means by the expression 'āvuso'. 'Vo' means 'by you'.

Kāleti purebhattakāle. Vikāleti pacchābhattakāle. Avasesaṃ āpattinti sambandho. Dasavassomhīti ahaṃ dasavasso amhi. Navoti pañcavassaaparipuṇṇo. Majjhimoti pañcavassato paṭṭhāya yāva dasavassaaparipuṇṇo. Kusalacitto āpajjatīti kusalacitto hutvā āpajjati. Abyākatacittoti supantassa bhavaṅgacittaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ. Yanti āpattiṃ. Sabbanti āpattiṃ, āpajjatīti sambandho. Dukkhavedanāsamaṅgī hutvā āpajjatīti yojanā. Yanti āpattiṃ.

'At the proper time' means before mealtime. 'At the improper time' means after mealtime. The connection is 'the remaining offense'. 'I am ten years old' means 'I am ten years old'. 'New' means not having completed five years. 'Middle' means from five years up to not having completed ten years. 'Commits with a wholesome mind' means having a wholesome mind, one commits. 'With an indeterminate mind' is said in reference to the life-continuum consciousness of one who is asleep. 'Which' refers to the offense. 'All' refers to the offense; the connection is 'commits'. The connection is: 'one commits while endowed with painful feeling'. 'Which' refers to the offense.

Tayo paṭikkhepāti ettha paṭikkhepassa sāmikaṃ dassento āha “buddhassa bhagavato”ti. Kilesasallekhanakapaṭipattiyāti [V 2.0202] kilesaṃ sallikhati tanuṃ karotīti kilesasallekhanakā, sāyeva paṭipatti kilesasallekhanakapaṭipatti, tāya.

Here, in 'the three rejections', showing the owner of the rejection, he says, 'of the Buddha, the Blessed One'. 'By the practice of scouring defilements': one who scours defilements, that is, makes them thin, is a 'scourer of defilements'; that very practice is the 'practice of scouring defilements'; by that practice.

Parisaṃ upaṭṭhāpento bāloti sambandho. Parisaṃ upaṭṭhāpento paṇḍito cāti sambandho. Avasesaṃ āpattinti yojanā. Kāḷeti kāḷapakkhe. Juṇheti juṇhapakkhe.

The connection is: 'a fool attending upon an assembly'. The connection is: 'and a wise one attending upon an assembly'. The connection is: 'the remaining offense'. 'Kāḷe' means in the dark fortnight. 'Juṇhe' means in the bright fortnight.

Kattikapuṇṇamāsiyāti [M 0.0571] pacchimakattikapuṇṇamāsiyā. Kurundiyaṃ vuttanti sambandho. Suvuttakāraṇaṃ dassento āha “cātumāsa”ntiādi. Hīti yasmā, pariyesanto ca nivāsento ca bhikkhūti yojanā.

'On the full-moon day of Kattika' means on the last full-moon day of Kattika. The connection is: 'as stated in the Kurundī'. Showing the well-stated reason, he says, 'the four months,' etc. 'Hi' means 'because'; the connection is: 'bhikkhus both seeking and residing'.

Vatthunti methunadhammādivatthuṃ.

'The object' means the matter of sexual intercourse and so on.

Paṭicchādeti etāyāti paṭicchādīti karaṇatthopi yujjati. Vitthāraṃ dassento āha “dvāraṃ pidahitvā”tiādi. Etadevāti parikammameva. Ubhayatthāti ubhayesu jantāgharapaṭicchādiudakapaṭicchādīsu. Sabbanti akhilaṃ parikammādiṃ. Niyyantīti nilīyitvā yanti. Iminā vahantīti ettha vahadhātu gatyatthoti dasseti. Abbhamahikādhūmarajarāhuvimuttanti abbhena ca mahikāya ca dhūmena ca rajena ca rāhunā ca vimuttaṃ. Tesūti abbhādīsu. Tathāti yathā candamaṇḍalaṃ virocati, tathā sūriyamaṇḍalaṃ.

'One conceals with this, thus it is a concealer'; the instrumental sense is also suitable. To explain in detail, he says, 'having closed the door,' etc. 'This very' means the preliminary work only. 'For both' means for both the bathhouse covering and the water covering. 'All' means the entire preliminary work, etc. 'They go forth' means they go, having hidden themselves. By this, he shows that here in 'vahanti' (they carry), the root 'vah' has the meaning of 'to go'. 'Free from clouds, mist, smoke, dust, and Rāhu' means freed from clouds and from mist and from smoke and from dust and from Rāhu. 'Among these' means among clouds, etc. 'Likewise' means just as the moon's disc shines, so does the sun's disc.

Karaṇīyena hutvāti sambandho.

The connection is: 'having a duty to perform'.

Kappentoti karonto. Āgantuko āpajjatīti sambandho. Anajjhiṭṭhoti anajjhesito hutvāti sambandho. Tiṇavatthārakasamathe kāyena vuṭṭhāti kāyasāmaggiyā dānattā.

'Kappento' means 'making'. The connection is: 'a newcomer incurs an offense'. The connection is: 'anajjhiṭṭho' means 'having been unrequested'. In the settlement by covering with grass, one settles it by bodily presence, because it is a granting of unanimity by the body of monks.

Āgāḷhāya ceteyyāti āgāḷhasaddo daḷhapariyāyoti āha “daḷhabhāvāyā”ti. Ā bhuso gāhiyate āgāḷho, gāḷho bāḷho daḷhoti atthato ekaṃ. Ceteyyāti pakappeyya. Na pūrayatoti na pūrayantassa. Alajjī ca hoti bālo ca apakatatto cāti ettha bālamattaapakatattamattena kammaṃ na kātabbaṃ, āpattivaseneva pana kātabbanti dassento āha “bālo”tiādi. Tattha bālo na jānātīti sambandho. Ayanti bālo. Ettāvatāti ettakena ajānanamattena. Bālabhāvamūlakaṃ āpattinti sambandho. Dve āpattikkhandheti pārājikasaṅghādisesavasena [V 2.0203] dve āpattirāsayo. Tesanti tiṇṇaṃ puggalānaṃ, kātabbanti sambandho.

Regarding 'āgāḷhāya ceteyya' (he should intend strongly), he says that the word 'āgāḷha' is a synonym for 'firm', thus 'for the sake of firmness'. 'Āgāḷha' means being grasped intensely; 'gāḷha', 'bāḷha', and 'daḷha' are one in meaning. 'Ceteyya' means he should form an intention. 'Na pūrayato' means of one who does not fulfill. In 'he is shameless, foolish, and unrestrained', showing that an act should not be done merely because of foolishness and unrestraint, but should be done only on the basis of the offense, he says 'foolish,' etc. Here, the connection is: a fool does not know. 'Ayaṃ' means this fool. 'Ettāvatā' means merely by this much not knowing. The connection is: an offense rooted in foolishness. 'Dve āpattikkhandhe' means two aggregates of offenses, namely pārājika and saṅghādisesa. 'Tesaṃ' means of the three individuals; the connection is 'should be done'.

Kāyiko davo nāmāti kāyiko parihāso nāma. Mukhālambarakaraṇādibhedoti mukhena ālambaranāmakatūriyakiccassa karaṇādibhedo[M 0.0572]. Dvīhipi dvārehīti kāyavacīvasena dvīhipi dvārehi. Kāyadvāre paññattasikkhāpadavītikkamoti kāyadvāre paññattassa kāyasaṃsaggādisikkhāpadassa vītikkamo. Vacīdvāre paññattasikkhāpadavītikkamoti vacīdvāre paññattassa duṭṭhullavācādisikkhāpadassa vītikkamo. Kāyikena upaghātikenāti ettha upaghātikaṃ nāma asikkhananti āha “asikkhanenā”ti. Kasmā asikkhanaṃ upaghātaṃ nāmāti āha “yo hī”tiādi. Tattha yoti puggalo. Tanti kāyadvāre paññattasikkhāpadaṃ. Nanti evameva. Hi yasmā upaghātetīti sambandho. Vejjakammena samannāgatoti sambandho. Sāsanauggahaṇaārocanādinā vācasikena micchājīvenāti yojanā.

'Bodily frivolity' means bodily jesting. 'Such as making mouth-noises, etc.' means the various ways of performing with the mouth the function of a musical instrument called ālambara, and so on. 'Through both doors' means through both the bodily and verbal doors. 'Transgression of a training rule laid down for the body-door' means the transgression of a training rule laid down for the body-door, such as that concerning physical contact, etc. 'Transgression of a training rule laid down for the speech-door' means the transgression of a training rule laid down for the speech-door, such as that concerning coarse speech, etc. 'With bodily harm'—here, 'harm' means lack of training, as it is said, 'due to lack of training.' Why is lack of training called harm? It is said, 'For one who...' etc. Here, 'one' refers to a person. 'That' refers to the training rule laid down for the body-door. 'Naṃ' means 'just so'. The connection is: 'because he harms.' 'Endowed with medical practice'—this is the connection. 'With wrong livelihood involving speech, such as learning the Teaching, making announcements, etc.'—this is the construction.

“Mā bhaṇḍanaṃ karī”ti iminā “mā”ti paṭisedhassa “karī”ti pāṭhasesena sambandhitabbabhāvaṃ dasseti. Na voharitabbanti ettha vipubbaavapubba-haradhātu kathanatthoti āha “na kiñci vattabba”nti. Hīti saccaṃ. Bījanaggāhādiketi ādisaddena dhammajjhesanādiṃ saṅgaṇhāti. Okāsakammaṃ kārentassāti ettha “okāsa”nti ca “okāsakamma”nti ca sadisanti āha “okāsaṃ kārentassā”ti. Na ādātabbanti na gaṇhitabbaṃ. Tamevatthaṃ dassento āha “yattha gahetvā”tiādi.

'Do not quarrel'—by this it shows that the prohibition 'mā' should be connected with the remainder of the reading, 'karī.' 'It should not be spoken of'—here, the root 'har,' preceded by 'vi' and 'ava,' is in the sense of speaking; thus it is said, 'nothing should be said.' 'Hi' means truly. 'Such as taking hold of seeds, etc.'—by the word 'etc.' it includes requesting the Dhamma, and so on. 'For one who is causing the okāsa-kamma to be performed'—here, since 'okāsa' and 'okāsa-kamma' are similar, it is said, 'for one who is causing an opportunity to be made.' 'Should not be taken' means should not be accepted. Explaining that very meaning, it is said, 'where, having taken...' etc.

Yanti vinayaṃ. Soti bhikkhu. Soti vinayo. Tassāti bhikkhussa. Idanti kammaṃ. Aññaṃ pucchāti mayā aññaṃ bhikkhuṃ pucchāhīti yojanā. Itīti evaṃ. Soti tīhaṅgehi samannāgato bhikkhu. Assāti tīhaṅgehi samannāgatassa. Na sākacchitabboti na saha kathetabbo.

'They adhere to the discipline.' 'He' means a monk. 'That' means the discipline. 'His' means the monk's. 'This' means the formal act. 'He asks another'—the construction is: 'Ask another monk instead of me.' 'Thus' means in this way. 'He' means a monk possessed of three factors. 'His' means of one possessed of three factors. 'Should not be conversed with' means should not be spoken with.

“Laddhi”nti iminā idamappahāyāti ettha idaṃsaddassa visayaṃ dasseti. “Avijahitvā”ti iminā hādhātu tvāpaccayoti dasseti. Suddhaṃ brahmacārinti ettha sabbathā kilesasuddho khīṇāsavova gahetabboti āha “khīṇāsavaṃ bhikkhu”nti. “Pātabyabhāva”nti iminā pātabyatanti ettha tāpaccayo bhāvatthe hotīti dasseti. “Paṭisevana”nti iminā pātabyasaddo yathākāmaparibhuñjanatthoti dasseti[M 0.0573]. Gativisodhananti duggatito sugatiyā visujjhanaṃ[V 2.0204]. “Akusalāni ceva mūlāni cā”ti iminā akusalasaddassa ca mūlasaddassa ca tulyādhikaraṇabhāvaṃ dasseti. Tasmā akusalasaṅkhātāni mūlāni akusalamūlānīti tulyādhikaraṇasamāso kātabbo. Duccaritānīti ettha dusaddassa duṭṭhuvirūpatthabhāvaṃ dassento āha “duṭṭhu caritāni, virūpāni vā caritānī”ti. Virūpānīti vikārasabhāvāni. “Karaṇabhūtenā”ti iminā “kattubhūtenā”ti atthaṃ paṭikkhipati. Tattha tatthāti tasmiṃ tasmiṃ khandhake.

'A view'—by this, in the phrase 'without abandoning this,' it indicates the object of the word 'this.' 'Without having abandoned'—by this, it indicates that the root is 'hā' with the suffix 'tvā.' 'A pure practitioner of the holy life'—here, one who is entirely pure of defilements, an Arahant, should be understood; thus it is said, 'an Arahant monk.' 'The state of being drinkable'—by this, in the word 'pātabyatā,' it indicates that the suffix 'tā' is in the sense of 'state.' 'Consuming'—by this, it indicates that the word 'pātabya' is in the sense of consuming as one pleases. 'Purification of destination' means purification from a bad destination to a good one. 'Unwholesome and roots'—by this, it indicates the appositional relationship between the words 'unwholesome' and 'roots.' Therefore, 'unwholesome roots' (akusalamūlāni) should be taken as an appositional compound, meaning 'the roots which are unwholesome.' 'Misconduct'—here, indicating that the prefix 'du' has the meaning of 'bad' or 'deformed,' it says, 'badly conducted, or deformed conduct.' 'Deformed' means having a nature of corruption. 'By that which is the instrument'—by this, it rejects the meaning 'by that which is the agent.' 'In each case' means in each and every section.

Iti tikavāravaṇṇanāya yojanā samattā.

Thus, the explanation of the construction in the commentary on the Section of Triplets is complete.

Ekuttarikanayo catukkavāravaṇṇanā

The Method of Gradual Increase by One: The Commentary on the Section of Fours.

324. Catukkesu evaṃ vinicchayo veditabboti yojanā. Tiṇavatthārakasamathaṭṭhānanti tiṇavatthārakasamathena adhikaraṇavūpasamitaṭṭhānaṃ. Parassa kammavācāyāti parassa karaṇabhūtāya kammavācāya. Tatoti catukkato. Paresūti aññesu catukkesu evamattho veditabboti yojanā. Tamevāti kāyadvārikameva. Puna tamevāti vacīdvārikameva. Āpajjitabbāpattiñca sahāgāraseyyāpattiñcāti yojanā. Jaggantoti jāgaranto.

324. 'In the sections of fours, the determination should be understood thus'—this is the construction. 'The ground for settlement by covering with grass' means the place where a legal issue has been settled by the procedure of covering with grass. 'By another’s formal act' means by the formal act of another which serves as the instrument. 'From that' means from the section of four. 'In others' means in other sections of four, the meaning should be understood thus—this is the construction. 'That very one' means only that related to the body-door. 'Again, that very one' means only that related to the speech-door. 'And the offense to be incurred and the offense of sharing a dwelling'—this is the construction. 'Being vigilant' means being awake.

Acittako āpajjati nāmāti “acittako bhikkhu āpajjati nāmā”ti vā “acittako hutvā āpajjati nāmā”ti vā yojanā kātabbā. Sabhāganti vatthusabhāgaṃ. Tañcāti aññataraṃ tañca āpattiṃ. Itīti evaṃ.

'One without intention incurs an offense'—the construction should be made either as 'a monk without intention incurs an offense' or as 'having become one without intention, he incurs an offense.' 'Of the same kind' means of the same kind with respect to the object. 'And that' means and that one particular offense. 'Thus' means in this way.

Kammenāti samanubhāsanakammena. Kammena vuṭṭhātīti kammena eva vuṭṭhāti.

'By a formal act' means by the formal act of admonishment. 'He is rehabilitated by a formal act' means he is rehabilitated by a formal act alone.

Soti gihiparikkhāro, āhaṭo hotīti sambandho. Avāpuraṇanti kuñcikaṃ. Antoti bhaṇḍāgārassa anto.

'It' means a householder's requisite; the connection is 'is brought.' 'An opener' means a key. 'Inside' means the interior of the storeroom.

Sammukhā [M 0.0574] vuṭṭhātīti sammukhā eva vuṭṭhāti.

'He is rehabilitated in the presence' means he is rehabilitated in the very presence.

Sayitāya eva bhikkhuniyāti yojanā. Idanti sahāgāraseyyāpattiṃ, paṭiccāti sambandho. Etanti “liṅgapātubhāvenā”ti vacanaṃ, vuttanti sambandho. Ubhinnampīti bhikkhubhikkhunīnampi[V 2.0205]. Liṅgapaṭilābhenāti itthiliṅgapaṭilābhena. Paṭhamanti ādikappakāle. “Paṭhamaṃ uppannavasenā”ti iminā pure uppannaṃ purimanti vacanatthaṃ dasseti. “Seṭṭhabhāvenā”ti iminā purabhāvena seṭṭhabhāvena uppannaṃ purimanti vacanatthaṃ dasseti. “Purisaliṅga”nti iminā imapaccayassa sarūpaṃ dasseti. Purisakuttapurisākārādīti ādisaddena purisanimittādayo saṅgaṇhāti. Yāni chacattālīsa sikkhāpadānīti yojanā. Iminā vuttanayānusārena dutiyacatukkepi attho veditabbo. Tehīti tiṃsādhikehi satasikkhāpadehi.

'With a nun who is indeed sleeping'—this is the construction. 'This' refers to the offense of sharing a dwelling; the connection is with 'on account of.' 'This' refers to the statement 'by the manifestation of gender'; the connection is with 'is said.' 'Of both' means of both monks and nuns. 'By the acquisition of gender' means by the acquisition of the female gender. 'First' means at the time of the beginning of the aeon. 'By virtue of having arisen first'—by this phrase, it shows the meaning of the word 'purima' is 'what arose before.' 'By virtue of being superior'—by this phrase, it shows the meaning of the word 'purima' is 'what arose first by virtue of being foremost and superior.' 'Male gender'—by this, it shows the nature of the suffix '-ima.' 'Male conduct, male appearance, etc.'—by the word 'etc.' it includes male signs and so forth. 'Which are the forty-six training rules'—this is the construction. In accordance with the method stated here, the meaning should be understood in the second section of four also. 'By these' means by the one hundred and thirty-odd training rules.

Mahāpadesāti vinaye (mahāva. 305) āgatā mahāpadesā. Kasmā mahāpadesā “sāmukkaṃsā”ti vuccantīti āha “te hī”tiādi. Tattha teti cattāro mahāpadesā, vuccantīti sambandho. “Saya”nti iminā sāmukkaṃsāti ettha saṃsaddassa sayamatthaṃ dasseti. “Ukkhipitvā”ti iminā ukkaṃsasaddo ukkhipanatthoti dasseti. “Ṭhapitattā”ti iminā sayaṃ ukkaṃsitvā ṭhapitā sāmukkaṃsāti vacanatthaṃ dasseti. “Ajjhoharaṇīyaparibhogā”ti iminā bāhiraparibhogaṃ nivatteti. Udakaṃ panāti kenaci asaṃsaggaṃ pasannodakaṃ pana. Kāleti sappadaṭṭhakāle. “Pañca vā dasa vā sīlānī”ti iminā pañca vā dasa vā sīlāni upāsakasīlanti dasseti.

'Great References' refers to the great references found in the Vinaya (Mahāvagga, paragraph 305). Why are the great references called 'sāmukkaṃsā'? It is said, 'For they...' etc. Here, 'they' refers to the four great references; the connection is with 'are called.' By the word 'sayaṃ' (oneself), it shows that in 'sāmukkaṃsā,' the word 'saṃ' has the meaning of 'self.' By the word 'ukkhipitvā' (having lifted up), it shows that the word 'ukkaṃsa' has the meaning of 'lifting up.' By the word 'ṭhapitattā' (because of being established), it shows the meaning of the word 'sāmukkaṃsā' is 'what is established by oneself after having been lifted up.' By the phrase 'use of what is to be consumed,' it excludes external use. 'But water' means clear water that is not mixed with anything. 'At the time' means at the time of being bitten by a snake. By the phrase 'five or ten precepts,' it shows that the five or ten precepts are the precepts for a lay follower.

Tattha cāti vihāre ca. Ubhopīti āgantukāvāsikavasena ubhopi. Asādhāraṇanti dvīhi asādhāraṇaṃ. Āpattinti bhikkhunīhiyeva sādhāraṇaṃ āpattiṃ. Gamiyacatukkepīti pisaddo āgantukacatukkaṃ apekkhati. Vatthunānattatāvāti methunādivatthunānattatā eva. Hīti saccaṃ, yasmā vā. Sāti āpatti. Tathāti yathā kāyasaṃsagge, tathā lasuṇakhādaneti yojanā. Etthāti vatthunānattatādicatukke[M 0.0575]. Cattāri pārājikānīti bhikkhupātimokkhe āgatāni. Visuṃ āpajjantesupi eseva nayoti sambandho.

'And there' means and in the monastery. 'Both' means both in the sense of visiting and resident monks. 'Not shared' means not shared by the two. 'An offense' means an offense shared only with nuns. 'In the section of four concerning travel also'—the word 'pi' (also) has reference to the section of four concerning visiting monks. 'Just the diversity of objects' means precisely the diversity of objects such as sexual intercourse and so on. 'Hi' means truly, or because. 'That' means the offense. 'So'—the construction is: 'as in the case of bodily contact, so too in the case of eating garlic.' 'Here' means in the section of four beginning with 'diversity of objects.' 'The four offenses of defeat' are those that appear in the Monks' Pātimokkha. 'Even for those who incur them separately, this is the same method'—this is the connection.

Purimacatukketi vatthunānattatādicatukke. Yo paṭhamo pañhoti yojanā. Idhāti vatthusabhāgatādicatukke. Yo cāti yo ca pañho. Tatthāti vatthunānattatādicatukke. Tatiyacatutthesu pañhesūti sambandho.

‘In the former fourfold section’ means in the fourfold section beginning with the diversity of grounds. ‘Which is the first question’—this is the construction. ‘Here’ means in the fourfold section beginning with the similarity of grounds. ‘And which’ means ‘and which question.’ ‘There’ means in the fourfold section beginning with the diversity of grounds. ‘In the third and fourth questions’—this is the connection.

“Saddhivihārikassā”ti padaṃ “kattabba”iti pade sampadānaṃ.

The word ‘saddhivihārikassa’ is in the dative case in relation to the word ‘kattabba’.

Garukanti pārājikaṃ. Lahukanti thullaccayaṃ vā dukkaṭaṃ vā.

‘Grave’ means a pārājika offense. ‘Light’ means either a thullaccaya or a dukkaṭa offense.

Aṭṭhannaṃ [V 2.0206] bhikkhunīnaṃ paṭipāṭiyā nisīditabbato vuttaṃ “navamabhikkhunito”ti. Paccuṭṭhānārahāti paṭimukhaṃ upaṭṭhātuṃ arahā. Avisesena cāti “bhikkhū”ti vā “bhikkhunī”ti vā visesa, makatvā sāmaññena ca. “Āsanārahacatukkassā”ti padaṃ “paṭhamapada”nti pade avayavisambandho.

Because one should sit in sequence after eight bhikkhunīs, it is said ‘from the ninth bhikkhunī.’ ‘Worthy of rising’ means worthy of attending in front. ‘And without distinction’ means without making a distinction between ‘bhikkhu’ or ‘bhikkhunī,’ but generally. The word ‘āsanārahacatukkassa’ has a part-whole relationship with the word ‘paṭhamapada’.

Asādhāraṇanti bhikkhūhi asādhāraṇaṃ. Vikāle kappatīti tadahuvikāle kappati. Kālātītanti kālayāmasattahātītaṃ. Yāvakālikādittayañca akappiyamaṃsañca uggahitakañca apaṭiggahitakañcāti yojanā.

‘Not shared’ means not shared with bhikkhus. ‘Permissible at the wrong time’ means permissible on that very day outside the proper time. ‘Beyond the time’ means beyond the time-period of a watch or seven days. ‘The triad beginning with what is permissible until noon, and non-permissible meat, and what has been taken up, and what has not been received’—this is the construction.

Guṇaṅguṇūpāhanañca dhuvanhānañca cammattharaṇañca guṇaṅguṇūpāhanadhuvanhānacammattharaṇāni. Imāni cattārīti pañcavaggena gaṇena upasampadadānādīni. Idhāti paccantimesu janapadesu. Idhāti majjhimesu. Idanti catubbidhaṃ vatthu. Dīpetumpīti dīpanampi. Tuṃpaccayo hi katvatthajotako. Eseva nayo dīpetuṃ panāti etthāpi. Sesaṃ anuññātakanti sambandho. Ubhayatthapīti paccantimamajjhimavasena ubhayatthāpi.

‘Footwear with straps, permanent bathing, and leather mats’—these are footwear with straps, permanent bathing, and leather mats. ‘These four’ refers to things such as the giving of ordination by a group of five. ‘Here’ refers to the border regions. ‘Here’ refers to the middle regions. ‘This’ refers to the fourfold basis. ‘Even to illuminate’ means also the illuminating. Indeed, the tuṃ suffix indicates the sense of the gerund. The same principle applies also here in ‘dīpetuṃ pana’ (but to illuminate). ‘The remainder is permitted’—this is the connection. ‘In both places’ means in both places, namely the border and middle regions.

Chandapārisuddhiakkhānaṃ ekaṃ katvā “cattāro”ti vuttaṃ. Cattāro pubbakiccāti liṅgavipallāso, “cattāri pubbakiccānī”ti hi attho. Evaṃ vuttāni imāni cattārīti sambandho. Evaṃ āgatā sammutiyoti sambandho. Sabbatthāti sabbesu catukkesu.

Taking the declaration of consent and purity as one, it is said ‘four.’ ‘Four preliminary duties’ is a change of gender; indeed, the meaning is ‘four preliminary duties’ (cattāri pubbakiccāni). ‘These four are stated thus’—this is the connection. ‘The agreements come about thus’—this is the connection. ‘In all places’ means in all fourfold sections.

Iti catukkavāravaṇṇanāya yojanā samattā.

Thus the explanation for the exposition of the fourfold section is concluded.

Ekuttarikanayo pañcakavāravaṇṇanā

The Method of Increment by One: An Exposition of the Fivefold Section

325. Pañcakesu [M 0.0576] “pañca puggalā niyatā”ti etaṃ ānantariyānameva gahaṇanti yojanā. Pañca chedana kā āpattiyo nāma veditabbāti sambandho. Yā vikappanā vuttāti yojanā. Ussaṅkitoti uṭṭhahitvā saṅkito. Parisaṅkitoti punappunaṃ saṅkito. Akuppo arahattaphalasaṅkhāto dhammo imassāti akuppadhammo, khīṇāsavo. Khīṇāsavo samānopi ussaṅkito ceva parisaṅkito cāti yojanā. Pariharitabbāti apanetabbā. Hīti saccaṃ, yasmā vā. Etesūti agocaresu. Thūpacīvaranti ettha thūpaṃ parikkhipitvā kataṃ cīvaraṃ thūpacīvaranti dassento āha “vammika”ntiādi. Vammiko hi thūpayati uddhaṃ ārohatīti thūpoti vuccati[V 2.0207]. Nhānaṭṭhāneti sabbesaṃ nhānaṭṭhāne. Tañhi udakena kāyaṃ abhisiñcati etthāti abhisekanti vuccati. Abhiseke chaḍḍitaṃ ābhisekikaṃ, cīvaraṃ. Tena vuttaṃ “chaḍḍitacīvara”nti. Bhatapaṭiyābhatanti ettha bharadhātuyā posanatthaṃ paṭikkhipitvā dhāraṇatthaṃ dassento āha “susānaṃ netvā puna ānītaka”nti. Tattha “susāna”nti iminā kammaṃ dasseti, “punā”ti iminā paṭisaddassa atthaṃ dasseti. Imehi padehi susānaṃ bhataṃ hutvā gehaṃ paṭiābharitabbanti bhatapaṭiyābhatanti vacanatthaṃ dasseti, yakāro padasandhikaro. Pāḷiyaṃ, aṭṭhakathāyañca potthakesu “gatapaṭiyāgata”nti kaṇṭhajatatiyakkharena pāṭho atthi, so asundaro.

325. In the fivefold sections, the phrase 'five individuals are certain' is to be understood as referring only to those who have committed immediately consequential actions—this is the explanation. ‘What are the five offenses that entail cutting off?’—this is the connection to be understood. ‘The allowance that was stated’—this is the explanation. 'Ussaṅkito' means being suspicious after rising up. 'Parisaṅkito' means being repeatedly suspicious. 'Akuppadhammo' refers to one whose state is unshakable, which is designated as the fruit of arahantship; a khīṇāsava. Even a khīṇāsava, though in that state, may be suspicious after rising up and repeatedly suspicious—this is the explanation. 'Pariharitabbā' means it should be removed. 'Hī' means truly, or because. 'Etesu' refers to improper resorts. Regarding 'thūpacīvara,' here, showing that a robe made by encircling a thūpa is called 'thūpacīvara,' it is said, 'like an anthill,' and so on. For an anthill rises upwards, therefore it is called a 'thūpa.' 'Nhānaṭṭhāne' refers to a bathing place for all. There, one sprinkles water on the body—hence it is called 'abhiseka' (sprinkling). The robe discarded during the sprinkling is called the 'ābhisekika' robe. Therefore, it is said, 'the discarded robe.' Regarding 'bhatapaṭiyābhata,' here, rejecting the meaning of 'nourishing' from the root 'bhar' and showing the meaning of 'carrying,' it is said, 'taken to the charnel ground and brought back again.' In this, 'susāna' indicates the action, and 'puna' indicates the meaning of the word 'paṭi.' By these words, it shows the meaning of the word 'bhatapaṭiyābhata' as 'having been carried to the charnel ground, it should be brought back to the house'; the letter 'ya' serves to connect the words. In the Pāli texts and commentaries, in the books, there is a reading 'gatapaṭiyāgata' with the third guttural letter, but this is unattractive.

Kāyo paṭhamaṃ, vācā dutiyaṃ, kāyavācā tatiyaṃ, idaṃ sandhāya “tatiyenā”ti vuttaṃ. Tatthevāti antarapeyyāle eva.

The body is first, speech is second, body and speech together are third; 'with the third' is said referring to this. 'Therein' means precisely in the intermediate repetition passage.

Adinnanti ettha akārassa nakāriyabhāvañca tapaccayassa kammavācakabhāvañca dassento āha “aññena na dinna”nti. Tattha “aññenā”ti iminā tapaccayassa kammavācakabhāvaṃ dasseti, nakārena akārassa kāriyaṃ dasseti. Kena kāraṇena aviditanti āha “paṭiggaṇhāmīti cetanāya abhāvenā”ti. Aviditanti apākaṭaṃ. Naṭasamajjādidānanti naṭasamajjādīnaṃ [M 0.0577] sabbesaṃ dānaṃ. Usabhavissajjananti usabhassa vissajjanaṃ. Idaṃ upalakkhaṇavasena vuttaṃ. Sabbāsampi pana manussāmanussānaṃ itthīnaṃ methunarativasena purisānaṃ dānampi gahetabbaṃ. Itthidānanti etthāpi yāsaṃ kāsañci itthīnaṃ yesaṃ kesañci purisānaṃ dānaṃ gahetabbaṃ. Paṭibhānacittakammadānanti methunasevanapaṭibhānacittakammadānaṃ. Lokassāti lokena. Kathetukamyatāti kathetukāmatā. “Na suppaṭivinodayā”ti iminā dukkhena paṭivinodetabbāti duppaṭivinodayā, paṭivinodetuṃ na sukarāti dasseti. Upāyenāti yuttiyā.

Regarding 'adinna,' here, showing both the negative function of the 'a' prefix and the passive function of the 'ta' suffix, it is said, 'not given by another.' Here, 'by another' indicates the passive function of the 'ta' suffix, and the negative particle 'na' shows the function of the 'a' prefix. For what reason is it 'not known' (avidita)? It is said, 'due to the absence of the intention to accept.' 'Avidita' means not evident. 'Gifts to actors and assemblies' refers to all gifts given to actors, assemblies, and the like. 'Releasing a bull' means the releasing of a bull. This is said by way of illustration. However, the giving of women to men for the purpose of sexual pleasure by all humans and non-humans should also be taken into account. 'Gifts of women' here also refers to the giving of any women whatsoever to any men whatsoever. 'The gift of a work of art inspiring a ready response' means the gift of a work of art inspiring a ready response for the purpose of sexual intercourse. 'Of the world' means by the world. 'Desire to speak' means the wish to speak. 'Not easily removed' indicates that it is to be removed with difficulty, thus 'duppaṭivinodayā' (difficult to remove), showing that it is not easy to dispel. 'By means' refers to by a suitable method.

Phussadevatthero aṭṭhāsi kirāti sambandho. Ekaṃsanti bhummatthe cetaṃ upayogavacanaṃ. Ekasmiṃ aṃseti hi attho. Buddhārammaṇanti buddhaguṇārammaṇaṃ. Māroti devaputtamāro, gatoti sambandho. Gomayanti gomīḷhaṃ. Jaraggavoti jaragoṇo. Tādisamevāti gomayavippakiraṇasabhāvameva. Vippakāranti visesapakārena karaṇaṃ. Vaṅkapādanti kuṭilapādaṃ. Parikasantoti paricchedaṃ katvā vilekhanto. Vigacchapurisoti vikāraṃ, virūpaṃ vā gatapuriso. “Vibhacchapuriso”tipi pāṭho, visesena sobhaṇaṃ bhakkhapurisoti attho. Ayameva pāṭho abhidhānādīsu (abhidhānappadīpikāyaṃ 102 gāthāyaṃ) dissati. Samantāti kaṭaandhakāravihārassa [V 2.0208] samantato. Māro siyā nu khoti yojanā. Na asakkhiṃ iti āhāti yojanā. Diṭṭhapubboti pubbe diṭṭho. Mahānubhāvoti deviddhiyā mahānubhāvo. Iṅghāti uyyojanatthe nipāto, uyyojemīti attho. Attabhāvanti tava attabhāvaṃ. Tādisaṃ rūpanti buddhassa bhagavato attabhāvasadisaṃ rūpaṃ. Taṃsarikkhakanti tena rūpena sadisaṃ. Patirūpameva sadisaṭṭhena patirūpakaṃ, na ekaṃsasadisaṃ rūpaṃ kiñci sadisarūpanti attho. Sakattabhāvanti sassa eso sako, soyeva attabhāvo sakattabhāvo, taṃ. Ayanti māro. Kathanti [M 0.0578] kena kāraṇena bhagavā na sobhati nu kho, sobhatiyevāti attho. Tadeva samatthetuṃ vuttaṃ “sabbaso vītarāgadosamoho”ti. Vañcitomhīti ahaṃ vañcito amhi. Kiṃ atthīti kiṃ nāma atthi, mama vañcanacittaṃ natthīti adhippāyo. Daharabhikkhu paṭilabhatītiādinā sambandhitabbaṃ.

The connection is that Phussadevatthera stood, it is said. 'Ekaṃsaṃ' is a term used in the locative sense, for its meaning is 'on one side.' 'Buddhārammaṇa' means having the qualities of the Buddha as its object. 'Māra' refers to Devaputta Māra; 'gato' denotes the connection. 'Gomaya' means cow dung. 'Jaraggava' means an old bull. 'Tādisameva' means just like the nature of scattered cow dung. 'Vippakāra' means acting in a special manner. 'Vaṅkapāda' means a crooked foot. 'Parikasanto' means delineating and carving out. 'Vigacchapuriso' means a deformed or disfigured person. 'Vibhacchapuriso' is another reading, meaning a particularly loathsome person, or one who eats repulsive things. This very reading is found in lexicons (as in Abhidhānappadīpikā, verse 102). 'Samantā' means all around the Kaṭaandhakāra residence. 'Māra might be, might he not?'—this is the construction. 'I was unable'—thus he said; this is the construction. 'Diṭṭhapubba' means seen before. 'Mahānubhāva' means possessing great power through divine might. 'Iṅgha' is a particle indicating incitement, meaning 'let me urge on.' 'Attabhāva' means your own being. 'Tādisaṃ rūpaṃ' means a form similar to the Blessed One’s being. 'Taṃsarikkhaka' means resembling that form. 'Patirūpameva' means a likeness, in the sense of being similar; it is not entirely identical—the meaning is that no form is completely similar. 'Sakattabhāva' means 'his own being'; that is, that very being is his own. 'Ayaṃ' refers to Māra. 'Kathaṃ' means 'for what reason does the Blessed One not shine? Indeed, he does shine'—this is the meaning. To confirm that, it is said, 'completely free from lust, hatred, and delusion.' 'Vañcitomhi' means 'I have been deceived.' 'Kiṃ atthi?' means 'what is there?' The intention is, 'there is no deceitful thought in my mind.' This should be connected with 'Daharabhikkhu paṭilabhati,' etc.

Daharabhikkhu aṭṭhāsīti sambandho. Saṅkārachaḍḍaniṃ pacchinti sambandho. Saṅkāraṃ chaḍḍeti imāyāti saṅkārachaḍḍanī. Tissadattatthero nāma pucchīti sambandho. Nāvātoti potato. Pañhāsahassanti samathavipassanākammaṭṭhānesu pucchāsahassaṃ. Pucchīti daharaṃ pucchi. Paricchindīti tasmiṃ divase kātabbavattaṃ niṭṭhapesīti attho. Yonakavisayatoti yonakalokato. Aṭṭha kappe anussarīti cetiyaṅgaṇaṃ disvā cittassa pasīdanato pubbenivāsañāṇena aṭṭha kappe anussari.

The connection is that the young monk stood. The connection is with 'a basket for throwing away rubbish.' 'Saṅkārachaḍḍanī' means 'that by which rubbish is thrown away.' The connection is that the elder named Tissadatta asked. 'Nāvāto' means a ship. 'Pañhāsahassa' means a thousand questions on the subjects of serenity and insight meditation. 'Pucchi' means he asked the young one. 'Paricchindī' means he completed the duties to be done on that day—this is the meaning. 'Yonakavisayato' means from the Yonaka region. 'Aṭṭha kappe anussarī' means, upon seeing the cetiya courtyard and the consequent serenity of his mind, he recollected eight eons through the knowledge of past lives.

Eko bhikkhu gatoti sambandho. Devatā pupphahatthā aṭṭhaṃsūti manussavesaṃ gahetvā aṭṭhaṃsu. Tena vuttaṃ “kataragāmavāsikātthā”ti. Tumhe katarasmiṃ gāme vasanasīlā attha bhavathāti yojanā. Idhevāti imasmiṃyeva ṭhāne. Ṭhitāmhāti mayaṃ ṭhitā amhāti yojanā.

The connection is that one monk went away. Deities holding flowers stood there, having taken human form. Therefore, it was said, 'Which village dwellers are you?' The meaning is: 'In which village are you accustomed to dwell?' 'Idheva' means 'in this very place.' 'Ṭhitāmha' means 'we are standing'—this is the explanation.

Ayaṃ kathāti ayaṃ vakkhamānakathā. Kiṃ amaccaputto pāsādiko nu khoti yojanā. Neti amaccaputtaabhayatthere. Ñātakā agamaṃsūti sambandho. Theramātāpi pahiṇīti sambandho. Pisaddena ñātake apekkhati. Pahiṇākāraṃ dassento āha “putto me”tiādi. Amaccaputto ārūḷhoti sambandho. Abhayatthero āhāti sambandho. Tenāti amaccaputtena. Yugaggāhanti yugassa gāhaṃ. “Mahallakattherassa sammaṭṭhaṭṭhāne kacavaraṃ chaḍḍetvā”ti vacanaṃ āvi karonto āha “atītattabhāve kirā”tiādi. Amaccaputto chaḍḍesīti sambandho.

'Ayaṃ kathā' means 'this is the discussion to follow.' 'Is the minister's son pleasant?'—this is the explanation. 'Na' (No) refers to the elder Abhaya, the minister's son. The connection is that relatives came. The connection is that the elder's mother also sent. The word 'pi' (also) refers to the relatives. Showing the reason for sending, he said, 'My son,' etc. The connection is that the minister's son ascended. The connection is that the elder Abhaya said. 'Tena' (by him) refers to the minister's son. 'Yugaggāha' means grasping the end of the yoke. Revealing the statement, 'Having thrown rubbish in the swept place of the elder Mahallaka,' he said, 'In a past existence, it seems,' etc. The connection is that the minister's son threw.

Tanti sammajjanavattaṃ. Tatrāti “satthusāsanaṃ kataṃ hotī”tivacane. Āyasmā sāriputto nisīdi kirāti sambandho. Bhagavā paccāgañchīti [M 0.0579] sambandho. Pādānīti pādassa akkamanaṭṭhānāni, pādacetiyānīti attho. Thero nisīdīti sambandho. Jaṇṇukehi patiṭṭhāya “pādacetiyaṃ [V 2.0209] vanditvā”ti pāṭhaseso ajjhāharitabbo. Me nisinnabhāvaṃ me satthā aññāsi vatāti yojanā. Mesaddo hi pubbaparāpekkho. Codananti dosāropanaṃ. Kāressāmīti dasabalaṃ kāressāmi. Bhagavā āhāti sambandho. Gatosīti tvaṃ gato asi, vicarantassa tuyhaṃ na patirūpanti yojanā. Tatoti codanakālato.

'That' refers to the rule for sweeping. 'Tatra' (therein) refers to the statement, 'The Teacher’s instruction is done.' The connection is that Venerable Sāriputta sat down, it is said. The connection is that the Blessed One returned. 'Pādāni' (feet) refers to the places where the feet stepped, meaning the foot-shrines. The connection is that the elder sat down. Resting on his knees, the remainder of the passage 'having worshipped the foot-shrine' should be supplied. 'My Teacher knew my seated posture, indeed'—this is the explanation. The word 'me' indeed refers to both what precedes and what follows. 'Codana' means accusation. 'Kāressāmi' means 'I will cause the Ten-Powered One to do.' The connection is that the Blessed One said. 'Gatosī' means 'you have gone'; 'it is not fitting for you while wandering'—this is the explanation. 'Tato' (thence) refers to from the time of the rebuke.

Ettako vinicchayo upalabbhatīti sambandho. Bhāsapariyantanti vacanaparicchedaṃ. Ayanti kathā. Ettakaṃ vacananti sambandho. Gayhūpaganti gahetabbabhāvaṃ upagamanaṃ, gaṇhituṃ khamanīyanti attho. Tānīti dve mūlāni. Puna tānīti samudayabhūtāni cha āpattisamuṭṭhānāni. Vatthunti methunādivatthuṃ. Itipīti pisaddo paṭhamanayaṃ apekkhati. Ettha paṭhamanaye mūlena samudayassa pāyato abhedo hoti, pacchimanaye pana sabbathā bhedo hoti. Tasmā pacchimanayoyeva yuttataroti daṭṭhabbo. “Vūpasammatī”ti iminā “nirujjhatī”ti padassa samucchedanirodhaṃ dasseti. Vuṭṭhānenāti parivāsādivinayakammena.

The connection is that such a decision is found. 'Bhāsapariyanta' means the demarcation of words. 'Ayaṃ' refers to the discourse. The connection is 'so much speech.' 'Gayhūpaga' means approaching the state of being taken, meaning suitable to be grasped. 'Tāni' refers to the two roots. Again, 'tāni' refers to the six arisings which are the source of offenses. 'Vatthu' refers to the basis of sexual intercourse and the like. 'Itipi' (thus also) means the word 'pi' refers to the first method. Here, in the first method, there is mostly no difference between the root and the arising; however, in the latter method, there is a complete difference in every way. Therefore, the latter method alone should be seen as more appropriate. 'It subsides'—by this, he shows that the word 'ceases' means cessation by cutting off completely. 'By rising up' refers to by the disciplinary procedure of probation, etc.

Tettiṃsamūlānaṃ sarūpaṃ dassento āha “vivādādhikaraṇassa dvādasa mūlānī”tiādi. Ekaṃ mūlanti sambandho. Tānīti tettiṃsa mūlāni. Paratoti parasmiṃ. “Aṭṭhārasa bhedakaravatthūnī”tiādinā adhikaraṇānaṃ samuṭṭhānaṃ dasseti. Cattāri saṅghakiccāni nissāya uppajjatīti yojanā. Idanti vatthu. Sattannaṃ nidānanti sattannaṃ āpattikkhandhānaṃ paññattiṭṭhānasaṅkhātaṃ nidānaṃ. Etthāti ṭhāne. Paññattiṃ na jānātīti ettha “anupaññattiṃ na jānātī”ti vakkhamānattā paṭhamapaññatti gahetabbāti āha “paṭhamapaññattiṃ na jānātī”ti. Anupaññattīti ettha anusaddo naupacchinnatthoti āha “punappunaṃ paññattiṃ na jānātī”ti. Pacchātthopi yujjateva paṭhamapaññattito pacchā paññattattā. Anusandhivacanapathanti ettha anusandhīnaṃ vasena vacanapathanti dassento āha “kathānusandhivinicchayānusandhivasena vatthu”nti. Ñattikiccanti ñattiyā kiccaṃ[M 0.0580]. Iminā ñattiyāti ettha sāmyatthe sāmivacanaṃ. Karadhātusambandhe karaṇavacanampi yujjateva. Karaṇanti ettha ca yupaccayassa kammatthabhāvañca dasseti. Na kevalaṃ ñattikamme eva ñattikiccaṃ na jānāti, atha kho ñattidutiyañatticatutthakammesupi na jānātīti dassento āha “ñattidutiyañatticatutthakammesū”tiādi. Pubbe ṭhapetabbāti ñatti nāma kammavācāya pubbe ṭhapetabbāti na jānāti. Iminā napubbakusalabhāvaṃ dasseti. “Pacchā”ti iminā naaparakusalabhāvaṃ dasseti. Pisaddena paṭhamanayaṃ apekkhati. “Kālaṃ na jānātī”ti iminā akālaññūti padassa viggahavākyaṃ dasseti. Kālaṃ dassento āha “anajjhiṭṭho”tiādi.

To show the nature of the thirty-three roots, he says, 'The twelve roots of a legal issue concerning a dispute,' and so on. 'One root' is the connection. 'Those' refers to the thirty-three roots. 'From another' means in another person. By 'eighteen grounds for creating a schism,' and so on, he shows the arising of legal issues. The construction is: it arises dependent on the four acts of the Sangha. 'This' means the matter. 'The seven sources' means the source designated as the basis for the formulation of the seven classes of offenses. 'Here' means in this place. Regarding 'does not know the formulation,' since 'does not know the subsequent formulation' will be stated, the first formulation should be understood; thus he says, 'does not know the first formulation.' Regarding 'subsequent formulation,' the prefix 'anu' here has the sense of 'not cut off'; thus he says, 'does not know the formulation again and again.' The meaning of 'after' is also suitable, because it was formulated after the first formulation. Regarding 'the way of speaking in sequence,' showing that this means the way of speaking by means of sequences, he says: 'the matter by way of the sequence of discussion and the sequence of decision.' 'The duty of the motion' means the function of the motion. In 'by this motion,' the word is in the genitive case with the sense of relation. In connection with the verbal root 'kar,' the instrumental case is also suitable. And in 'instrument,' he also shows that the suffix 'yu' has the sense of the object. Showing that one not only does not know the duty of the motion in a formal act with a motion, but also does not know it in formal acts with a motion and one proclamation or a motion and three proclamations, he says, 'in formal acts with a motion and one proclamation or a motion and three proclamations,' and so on. 'Should be placed before' means one does not know that what is called a motion should be placed before the formal proclamation. By this, he shows the state of not being skilled in what comes first. By 'after,' he shows the state of not being skilled in what comes later. The word 'pi' refers to the first method. By 'does not know the time,' he shows the analytical phrase for the word 'akālaññū' (one who does not know the time). Showing the time, he says, 'uninvited,' and so on.

“Dhutaṅge [V 2.0210] ānisaṃsaṃ ajānitvā”ti iminā mandamomūhānaṃ phalaṃ dasseti. Pāpicchoti ettha pāpiccho nāma paccayalābhassa patthanāti āha “paccayalābhaṃ patthayamāno”ti. Kāyaviveko ca cittaviveko ca upadhiviveko ca kāyacittaupadhivivekaṃ, samāhāradvando, pubbapadesu uttarapadalopo. Etassāti āraññikassa. Iminā imāya attho idamattho, so etassatthīti idamatthīti vacanatthaṃ dasseti. Appicchaññevātiādīsu evasaddānaṃ chaḍḍetabbatthaṃ dassento āha “na aññaṃ kiñci lokāmisa”nti.

By 'not knowing the benefits of the ascetic practices,' he shows the result for the dull and deluded. Regarding 'of evil desires,' one of evil desires is one who wishes for the gain of requisites; thus he says, 'wishing for the gain of requisites.' 'Seclusion of body, seclusion of mind, and seclusion from the substrates of existence' becomes 'seclusion of body-mind-substrates'; it is a copulative compound of the collective type, with the elision of the latter member in the preceding members. 'Of this' means of the forest-dweller. By this, he shows the meaning of the word 'idamattha' (having this purpose) as: 'this is its purpose,' or 'it exists for this purpose.' In 'only of few wishes,' and so on, showing that the word 'eva' (only) has the meaning of exclusion, he says, 'no other worldly bait.'

Navavidhanti divasavasena tividhaṃ, tathā kattabbākāravasena, tathā kārakavasenāti navavidhaṃ uposathaṃ.

The Uposatha is ninefold: threefold by way of the division of days, likewise threefold by way of the manner in which it should be done, and likewise threefold by way of the doer; thus, the Uposatha is ninefold.

Kāyaduccaritādi yasmā na pasādaṃ saṃvatteti, na pasādāya vā saṃvattati, tasmā apāsādikanti vuccati. Tena vuttaṃ “apāsādikanti kāyaduccaritādi akusala”nti. Velaṃ atikkammāti bhojanādikālaṃ atikkamitvā. Iminā ativelanti ettha atisaddassa atikkamanatthañca “ativela”nti padassa “viharato”ti pade kiriyavisesanabhāvañca dasseti. Appaṃ kālanti yojanā. Avataraṇaṃ otāroti dassento āha “otaraṇa”nti. Sabbatthāti sabbesu pañcakesu.

Because bodily misconduct and the like do not conduce to confidence, nor do they lead to confidence, they are called 'uninspiring.' For that reason it is said, 'Uninspiring means bodily misconduct and other unwholesome things.' 'Having transgressed the time' means having transgressed the time for meals and so on. By this, regarding 'too long,' he shows that the word 'ati' has the meaning of transgression, and that the word 'ativela' is an adverb modifying the word 'viharato' (dwelling). 'A short time' is the construction. Showing that 'avataraṇa' is 'otāra,' he says 'descending.' 'In all' means in all the groups of five.

Iti pañcakavāravaṇṇanāya yojanā samattā.

Thus the explanation of the commentary on the section of fives is completed.

Ekuttarikanayo chakkavāravaṇṇanā

The method of increasing by one: The commentary on the section of sixes.

326. Chakkesu [M 0.0581] evamattho veditabboti yojanā. Itīti evaṃ. Imā cha sāmīciyoti yojanā. Tatthāti chasu ākāresu. Satisammosenāti satiyā vippavāsena.

326. The construction is: 'In the groups of six, the meaning should be understood thus.' 'Iti' means 'thus.' The construction is: 'These are the six proper practices.' 'Therein' means 'in the six aspects.' 'Through confusion of mindfulness' means 'through the absence of mindfulness.'

Tatthāti cuddasasu paramesu. Tatoti chakkato. Ekaṃ apanetvāti yaṃkiñci ekaṃ apanetvā. Sesesūti chahi paramehi sesesu aṭṭhasu paramesu. Aññānipi chakkānīti paṭhamachakkato aññānipi aṭṭha chakkāni.

'Therein' means in the fourteen supreme things. 'From that' means from the group of six. 'Having removed one' means having removed any one. 'In the remaining' means in the eight supreme things remaining from the six supreme things. 'Other groups of six too' means the other eight groups of six apart from the first group of six.

Cha āpattiyoti tīṇi chakkānīti “cha āpattiyo”ti vuttāni tīṇi chakkānīti yojanā[V 2.0211]. Vuttadvayaṃ ekaṃ katvā. Nhāneti nhānasikkhāpade. Chakkadvayanti ādāyasamādāyavasena chakkadvayaṃ. Sabbatthāti sabbesu chakkesu.

The construction is: 'Six offenses' means three groups of six; thus, 'six offenses' refers to the three groups of six that were stated. The two statements are made into one. 'In bathing' means in the training rule on bathing. 'Two groups of six' means two groups of six by way of taking and undertaking. 'In all' means in all the groups of six.

Iti chakkavāravaṇṇanāya yojanā samattā.

Thus the explanation of the commentary on the section of sixes is completed.

Ekuttarikanayo sattakavāravaṇṇanā

The method of increasing by one: The commentary on the section of sevens.

327. Sattakesu chasu sāmīcīsu pakkhipitvāti sambandho. Tatthevāti samathakkhandhake eva.

327. The connection is: 'having inserted it into the six proper practices among the groups of seven.' 'Therein' means in the Samathakkhandhaka itself.

Campeyyaketi campeyyakkhandhake. “Asaddhammā”ti padassa bhedanissitatulyanissitasamāsaṃ dassento āha “asataṃ dhammā”tiādi. Tattha “asataṃ dhammā”ti iminā bhedanissitasamāsaṃ dasseti, “asanto vā dhammā”ti iminā tulyanissitasamāsaṃ dasseti. Sabbatthāti sabbesu sattakesu. Sesaṃ suviññeyyameva.

'In the Campeyyaka' means in the Campeyyakkhandhaka. Showing the compound of the word 'asaddhammā' as one dependent on difference and one dependent on equivalence, he says, 'qualities of the bad,' and so on. Therein, by 'qualities of the bad,' he shows the compound dependent on difference; by 'or, bad qualities,' he shows the compound dependent on equivalence. 'In all' means in all the groups of seven. The rest is indeed easy to understand.

Iti sattakavāravaṇṇanāya yojanā samattā.

Thus the explanation of the commentary on the section of sevens is completed.

Ekuttarikanayo aṭṭhakavāravaṇṇanā

The method of increasing by one: The commentary on the section of eights.

328. Aṭṭhakesu [M 0.0582] aṭṭhānisaṃsādīnaṃ desanākāradesanaṭṭhānāni dassento āha “na maya”ntiādi. Tattha “na mayaṃ…pe… karissāmā”ti iminā desanākāraṃ dasseti, “kosambakakkhandhake”ti iminā desanaṭṭhānaṃ dasseti. Tampīti dutiyaaṭṭhakampi.

328. Showing the manner of teaching and the place of teaching of the eight benefits and so on among the groups of eight, he says, 'We will not,' and so on. Therein, by 'We will not...pe...do,' he shows the manner of teaching; by 'in the Kosambakakkhandhaka,' he shows the place of teaching. 'That too' means the second group of eight too.

Terasake vuttāti sambandho. Kulāni dūsetīti ettha “dūsetī”ti kiriyāpadassa karaṇaṃ dassento āha “pupphena vā”tiādi. Imehi aṭṭhahi dūsetīti yojanā. “Lābhenā”tiādinā “aṭṭhahi asaddhammehī”ti ettha asaddhammasarūpaṃ dasseti. Sārāgoti saṃrāgo, bhusaṃ rajjananti attho. Paṭivirodhoti doso. So hi yasmā alābhādīsu paṭivirujjhati, tasmā paṭivirodhoti vuccati. Pāḷiyanti vinayapāḷiyaṃ.

The connection is: 'it is stated in the section of thirteen.' Here, in 'corrupts families,' showing the instrument of the verb 'corrupts,' he says, 'with flowers or,' and so on. The construction is: 'he corrupts with these eight.' By 'by gain,' and so on, he shows the nature of the 'bad qualities' in 'by the eight bad qualities.' 'Sārāgo' is 'saṃrāgo'; the meaning is 'strong passion.' 'Paṭivirodha' is aversion. Since it is indeed opposed to non-gain and so on, it is called 'paṭivirodha.' 'In the Pāḷi' means in the Vinaya Pāḷi.

Pāṇantiādikā dve gāthāyo dvādasakkharena bandhitā. Paṭhamagāthāya tatiyapāde cariyasaddena [V 2.0212] yuttattā ekakkharo adhiko. Ayaṃ panettha yojanā – pāṇaṃ na hane na ghāteyya, ādinnañca na ādiye na gaṇheyya, musā vitathavacanaṃ na bhāse na katheyya, majjapo majjapānaṃ na ca siyā, abrahmacariyā methunā virameyya, rattiṃ vikālabhojanaṃ na bhuñjeyya.

The two verses beginning with 'pāṇaṃ' are composed with twelve syllables. In the third line of the first verse, because it is joined with the word 'cariya,' there is one extra syllable. This is the construction here: One should not kill or strike a living being; and one should not take what is not given; one should not speak a false, untrue word; and one should not be a drinker of intoxicants; one should abstain from unchastity, from sexual intercourse; one should not eat food at night, at the wrong time.

Mālaṃ na dhāre na dhāreyya, gandhañca na ācare, santhate mañce ca chamāyañca sayetha. Etañhi uposathaṃ aṭṭhaṅgikaṃ uposathaṃ iti dukkhantagunā buddhena pakāsitanti āhu paṇḍitāti.

One should not wear a garland, and one should not use perfume; one should sleep on a couch or on the ground. Indeed, this Uposatha, this eight-factored Uposatha, proclaimed by the Buddha as having the quality of ending suffering—so say the wise.

Saṅghabhedaketi saṅghabhedakakkhandhake. Tāsaṃyevāti bhikkhunīnameva. “Upāsikā aṭṭha varāni yācatī”ti evaṃ sāmaññavacanassāpi atthapakaraṇādinā visesavisayo hotīti āha “visākhā”ti. Sā hi vividhā puttanattusaṅkhātā sākhā etissātthīti visākhāti vuccati. Sabbatthāti sabbesu aṭṭhakesu. Sesaṃ suviññeyyameva.

'Saṅghabhedake' is to be understood in the Saṅghabhedakakkhandhaka. 'Tāsaṃyeva' means of the bhikkhunīs themselves. Thus, even a general statement like 'The laywoman requests eight boons' becomes specific by means of the topic of the meaning and so on; therefore he says 'Visākhā'. For she is called Visākhā because she has various branches, designated as sons and grandsons. 'Sabbatthāti' means in all the eights. The rest is easily understood.

Iti aṭṭhakavāravaṇṇanāya yojanā samattā.

Thus is concluded the construing of the explanation of the chapter on eights.

Ekuttarikanayo navakavāravaṇṇanā

The Method of Increasing by One: The Explanation of the Chapter on Nines.

329. Navakesu [M 0.0583] acarītiādīnīti ādisaddena “carati, carissatī”tiādīni (dī. ni. 3.340; aṭṭha. ni. 9.29-30) saṅgaṇhāti. Taṃ kutettha labbhāti ettha tanti anatthacaraṇaṃ, kopakaraṇaṃ vā. Kutoti kena kāraṇena. Etthāti etasmiṃ anatthacarakapuggale. Labbhāti laddhā, sakkā laddhuṃ na labbhā evāti attho. Navannaṃ vā bhikkhūnaṃ kāraṇāti yojanā. Taṇhanti dvīsu esanataṇhāesitataṇhāsu esanataṇhaṃ. Paṭiccāti ārabbha. Pariyesanāti punappunaṃ esanā. Lābhoti rūpādiārammaṇalābho. Vinicchayoti ñāṇataṇhādiṭṭhivitakkavasena catubbidho vinicchayo. Catubbidho hi dhammo “ettakaṃ mayhaṃ bhavissatī”tiādinā vinicchinati anenāti vinicchayoti vuccati. Chandarāgoti balavarāgo. Ajjhosānanti “ahaṃ mama”nti balavasanniṭṭhānaṃ, pariggahoti taṇhādiṭṭhivasena paricchinditvā gahaṇaṃ. Macchariyanti paresaṃ sādhāraṇabhāvassa asahanatā. Ārakkhāti dvārapidahanamañjūsagopanādivasena ābhuso rakkhanaṃ. Ārakkhādhikaraṇanti ārakkhakāraṇā, hetvatthe cetaṃ paccattavacanaṃ. Daṇḍādānādīsu paranisedhanatthaṃ daṇḍassa ādānaṃ daṇḍādānaṃ. Tathā ekatodhārādino satthassa ādānaṃ satthādānaṃ. Kalahoti kāyakalahopi vācākalahopi. Viggahoti [V 2.0213] viruddhavasena gahaṇaṃ. Vivādoti viruddhavasena vadanaṃ. “Tuvaṃ tuva”nti anādaravasena vadanaṃ tuvaṃtuvaṃ vādo, pesuññavasena vadanaṃ pesuññavādo, musāvasena vadanaṃ musāvādo, daṇḍādānañca satthādānañca kalaho ca viggaho ca vivādo ca tuvaṃtuvaṃvādo ca pesuññavādo ca musāvādo ca daṇḍādāna…pe… musāvādā. Musāvādāti ettha vādasaddo “tuvaṃ tuva”nti ca “pesuñña”nti ca etthāpi yojetabbo. “Ahaṃ seyyohamasmī”ti pavattamānādayoti yojanā. Adhiṭṭhitakālato paṭṭhāya na vikappetabbānīti adhiṭṭhānavikappanaṃ ekato na kātabbaṃ, adhiṭṭhite na vikappetabbanti adhippāyo. Pariṇataṃ lābhaṃ pariṇāmetīti sambandho.

329. 'Navakesu acarītiādīni' means that by the word 'ādi', it includes such phrases as 'carati, carissatī' (Dī. Ni. 3.340; Aṭṭha. Ni. 9.29-30). Regarding 'Taṃ kutettha labbhāti' (How is this obtainable here?): here, 'taṃ' refers to unbeneficial conduct or the causing of anger. 'Kutoti' means 'for what reason'. 'Etthāti' means in this person who engages in unbeneficial conduct. 'Labbhāti' means 'is obtained' or 'can be obtained'; the meaning here is 'it cannot be obtained at all'. Or, the construing is: 'because of nine monks'. 'Taṇhā' (craving) refers to the craving for seeking (esanataṇhā) among the two: craving for seeking and craving for what has been sought (esitataṇhā). 'Paṭicca' means 'in relation to'. 'Pariyesana' means 'repeated seeking'. 'Lābho' means 'the gain of objects such as forms'. 'Vinicchayo' means 'deliberation', which is fourfold by way of craving for knowledge, views, and thoughts. Indeed, the fourfold phenomenon is called 'vinicchayo' (deliberation) because one deliberates by means of it, thinking, 'This much will be mine,' and so on. 'Chandarāgo' means 'strong lust'. 'Ajjhosānaṃ' means 'strong conviction' as in 'I' and 'mine'. 'Pariggaho' means 'grasping after having demarcated by way of craving and views'. 'Macchariyaṃ' means 'the inability to tolerate something being common to others'. 'Ārakkhā' means 'thorough protection' by way of locking doors, safeguarding chests, and so on. 'Ārakkhādhikaraṇaṃ' means 'the cause of guarding'; this is a dative expression in the sense of a reason. In 'Daṇḍādāna' (taking up the rod) and so on, 'daṇḍādānaṃ' means taking up the rod for the purpose of restraining others. Similarly, taking a knife with a single edge, etc., is called 'satthādāna' (taking up the knife). 'Kalaho' (quarreling) means both physical quarreling and verbal quarreling. 'Viggaho' (dispute) means grasping in opposition. 'Vivādo' (conflict) means speaking in opposition. 'Tuvaṃ tuvaṃ' (you, you) is speaking disrespectfully, and is called 'tuvaṃtuvaṃ vādo' (you-you speech). Speaking divisively is called 'pesuññavādo' (slanderous speech). Speaking falsely is called 'musāvādo' (false speech). Taking the rod, taking the knife, quarreling, dispute, conflict, you-you speech, slanderous speech, and false speech—these are 'daṇḍādāna...pe...musāvādā'. Here, in 'musāvādā', the word 'vāda' (speech) should also be connected with 'tuvaṃ tuvaṃ' and 'pesuñña'. The construing is: 'those which are occurring, such as 'I am better, I am superior', etc.' 'From the time of determination, they should not be disposed of' means that determination and disposal should not be done together; the intention is that one should not dispose of what has been determined. The connection is: 'He diverts the acquired gain'.

Etesaṃyeva [M 0.0584] dānānanti etesaṃyeva adhammikānaṃ dānānaṃ. Saṅghassa ninnanti saṅghassa nataṃ, nāmitaṃ vā lābhanti sambandho. Saṅghassa namati, nāmiyatīti vā ninnaṃ. Tesaṃyevāti tesaṃyeva tiṇṇaṃ dhammikadānānaṃ. Tayo tayo dānapaṭiggahaparibhoge sampiṇḍetvā navako gahetabbo. Tatthevāti samathakkhandhake eva. Ovādavaggassāti bhikkhunovādavaggassa. Tatthevāti ovādavaggassa paṭhamasikkhāpade eva. Sabbatthāti sabbesu navakesu.

'Etesaṃyeva dānānaṃ' means of these very unrighteous gifts. 'Saṅghassa ninnaṃ' means gain that is bent or inclined towards the Saṅgha—this is the connection. Or 'ninnaṃ' means that which bends or is bent towards the Saṅgha. 'Tesaṃyeva' means of those very three righteous gifts. Combining three each of giving, receiving, and using, the group of nine should be understood. 'Tattheva' means in the Samathakkhandhaka itself. 'Ovādavaggassa' means of the Bhikkhunovādavagga. 'Tattheva' means in the first training rule of the Ovādavagga itself. 'Sabbatthāti' means in all the nines.

Iti navakavāravaṇṇanāya yojanā samattā.

Thus is concluded the construing of the explanation of the chapter on nines.

Ekuttarikanayo dasakavāravaṇṇanā

The Method of Increasing by One: Explanation of the Chapter on Tens.

330. Dasakesu aṭṭhāne vā panāti akāraṇe vā pana. Tatthāti navakesu. “Natthi dinnantiādivasenā”ti ādisaddena “natthi yiṭṭhaṃ natthi huta”ntiādayo (dha. sa. 1221; ma. ni. 94.225; 3.91, 116; saṃ. ni. 3.210; a. ni. 10.176) nava natthikā saṅgahetabbā. “Sassato lokoti ādivasenā”tiādisaddena (dī. ni. 1.31; ma. ni. 1.269) “asassato loko”tiādayo (ma. ni. 1.269) nava antaggāhike saṅgaṇhāti. Viparītā sammattāti dasahi micchattehi viparītā dasa sammattā sammādiṭṭhi sammāsaṅkappo sammāvācā sammākammanto sammāājīvo sammāvāyāmo sammāsati sammāsamādhi sammāñāṇaṃ sammāvimuttīti.

330. In the chapter on tens, 'aṭṭhāne vā pana' means 'or in an impossible case, or without a cause'. 'Tattha' means in the chapter on nines. By the word ‘etc.’ in ‘by way of “There is no giving,” etc.’, the nine nihilistic views, such as ‘there is no sacrifice, there is no offering,’ etc., should be included. By the word ‘etc.’ in ‘by way of “The world is eternal,” etc.’, it includes the nine extremist views, such as ‘the world is not eternal,’ etc. 'Viparītā sammattā' means the ten rightnesses which are the opposite of the ten wrongnesses: right view, right intention, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, right concentration, right knowledge, and right liberation.

Dasa ādīnavā niddiṭṭhāti sambandho. Undūrakkhāyitanti mūsikena khāditaṃ. Ettha hi khedhātu khādanattho hoti. Aggidaḍḍhanti agginā daḍḍhaṃ. Etesūti etesu dasasu paṃsukūlesu. Udakasāṭikaṃ vā saṃkaccikaṃ vāti bhikkhunīnaṃ udakasāṭikaṃ [V 2.0214] vā saṃkaccikaṃ vā. Ettha vāsaddo aniyamavikappattho.

The ten drawbacks have been pointed out—this is the connection. ‘Gnawed by a rat’ means eaten by a mouse. Here, the root 'khe' is in the sense of eating. ‘Burnt by fire’ means burnt by fire. ‘Among these’ means among these ten kinds of rag robes. ‘A bathing cloth or a breast-band’ means for the bhikkhunīs, a bathing cloth or a breast-band. Here, the word ‘or’ indicates an unrestricted alternative.

Paṇṇasanthāro tiṇasanthārena saṅgahito. Sabbatthāti sabbesu dasakesu.

A leaf mat is included in a grass mat. ‘Sabbatthā’ means in all the tens.

Iti dasakavāravaṇṇanāya yojanā samattā.

Thus is concluded the construing of the explanation of the chapter on tens.

Ekuttarikanayo ekādasakavāravaṇṇanā

The Method of Increasing by One: Explanation of the Chapter on Elevens.

331. Ekādasakesu [M 0.0585] tiṇapādukāti muñjapabbajehi avasesā tiṇamayapādukā. Kaṭṭhapādukasaṅgahamevāti kaṭṭhapāduke saṅgahaṃ eva. Tambalohamayena vā dārumayena vāti vāsaddo aniyamavikappattho. “Nasi animittā”tiādayo bhikkhunikkhandhake (cūḷava. 423) niddiṭṭhā. Te sabbeti sabbe te gaṇṭhikavidhā. Naggenāti acelakena. Te sabbeti sabbe te avandiyapuggalā. Pubbeti dasake. Kammavaggeti avasāne kammavagge.

331. In the chapter on elevens, ‘grass sandals’ means the remaining grass sandals apart from those made of muñja grass and pabbaja grass. ‘Kaṭṭhapādukasaṅgaham eva’ means ‘the inclusion of wooden sandals only’. ‘Made of copper or wood’: here, the word ‘or’ indicates an unrestricted alternative. ‘Nasi animittā,’ etc., are pointed out in the Bhikkhunikkhandhaka (Cūḷavagga 423). ‘All those’ means all those kinds of knots. ‘Naked’ means by a naked ascetic. ‘All those’ means all those persons not to be venerated. ‘Previously’ means in the chapter on tens. ‘In the Kammavagga’ means at the end, in the Kammavagga.

So bhikkhu yaṃ na nigaccheyya, etaṃ na nigataṃ aṭṭhānaṃ anavakāsoti yojanā. Evañhi sati yaṃsaddo kiriyāparāmasano hoti, atha vā yaṃ yena kāraṇena na nigaccheyya, etaṃ kāraṇaṃ aṭṭhānanti yojanā. Anadhigataṃ samādhinti yojanā. Saddhammāssāti saddhammā assa. Assa akkosakaparibhāsakassa bhikkhussa saddhammā na vodāyanti na pariyodapentīti attho. Rogātaṅkanti rogasaṅkhātaṃ ātaṅkaṃ. Nirayaṃ upapajjatīti nirayamhi upapajjati. “Upapajjatī”ti ettha upaiti kammappavacanīyaupasaggena yuttattā “niraya”nti ettha bhummatthe upayogavacanaṃ daṭṭhabbaṃ. Ettha etasmiṃ aṅguttarapāḷiyaṃ (a. ni. 11.6).

The construing of 'impossible, without opportunity' is: 'That which a monk should not attain, that is not attained'. When this is so, the word 'yaṃ' refers to an action; or alternatively, the construing is: 'The reason by which one should not attain something, that reason is impossible'. The construing is 'unattained concentration'. ‘Saddhammāssa’ means ‘saddhammā assa’ (the true Dhamma would be his). The meaning is that for that abusive and insulting monk, the true Dhamma does not become pure, does not become cleansed. ‘Rogātaṅkaṃ’ means the affliction designated as disease. ‘He is reborn in hell’ means he is reborn in hell. Here, in ‘upapajjati’ (is reborn), because it is connected with the prepositional prefix 'upa', the accusative expression ‘nirayaṃ’ should be understood as being in the locative sense. ‘Ettha’ means in this Aṅguttara Pāli text (A. Ni. 11.6).

Āsevitāyāti ettha ātyūpasaggo ādikammatthoti āha “ādito paṭṭhāya sevitāyā”ti. “Nipphāditāyā”tiiminā bhāvitāyāti ettha bhūsaddo sattatthoti dasseti, “vaḍḍhitāyā”ti iminā vaḍḍhanatthoti dasseti. Bahulīkatāyāti ettha bahulaṃ nāma atthato punappunanti āha “punappunaṃ katāyā”ti. Suyuttayānasadisāyāti suṭṭhu yuttena yānena sadisāya. Iminā yānīkatāyāti ettha na yaṃkiñci yānaṃ viya kataṃ hoti, atha kho icchiticchitakkhaṇe ārohanīyattā suyuttayānaṃ viya kataṃ hotīti dasseti. Yathā kariyamāne patiṭṭhā hotīti yojanā. Vatthukatāyāti ettha vatthusaddo patiṭṭhatthoti dasseti. Vasati [M 0.0586] patiṭṭhahati [V 2.0215] etthāti vatthūti vacanattho kātabbo. Anuṭṭhitāyāti ettha anusaddo naupacchinnattho, ṭhādhātu uppajjanatthoti dassento āha “anu anu pavattitāyā”ti. “Samantato”ti iminā paricitāyāti ettha parisaddo samantatthoti dasseti. “Abhivaḍḍhitāyā”ti iminā cidhātu vaḍḍhanatthoti dasseti. Samāraddhāyāti paripuṇṇaṃ ārādhitāya. Rādhadhātu hi sādhanattho hoti. “Vasībhāvaṃ upanītāyā”ti iminā tadatthaṃ adhippāyena dasseti. “Na pāpakaṃ supinaṃ passatī”ti vacanassa atthāpattinayaṃ dassento āha “bhadrakaṃ panā”tiādi. Vuddhikāraṇabhūtanti vuddhiyā kāraṇabhūtaṃ supinanti sambandho. Devatā rakkhantīti ettha sāmaññato vuttepi ārakkhadevatāyeva gahetabbāti āha “ārakkhadevatā”ti. Ārakkhadevatā nāma bhummadevādayo. Khippanti bhāvanapuṃsakaṃ. Iminā tuvaṭaṃ cittanti ettha tuvaṭasaddo khippapariyāyoti dasseti. Uttarimappaṭivijjhantoti ettha “uttari”nti padassa avadhipekkhattā tassa avadhi ca uttarisaddassa idha arahattavācakabhāvañca vidhadhātuyā sacchikaraṇatthañca dassento āha “mettājhānato”tiādi. Tattha “mettājhānato”ti iminā avadhiṃ dasseti, “arahatta”nti iminā “uttari”nti padassa sarūpatthaṃ dasseti, “asacchikaronto”ti iminā vidhadhātuyā sacchikaraṇatthaṃ dasseti. Sabbatthāti sabbesu ekādasakesu.

Regarding ‘āsevitāya’, here the prefix ‘ā’ has the meaning of beginning an action; thus, it is said, ‘practiced from the very start’. By ‘nipphāditāya’, it shows that in ‘bhāvitāya’ the word ‘bhū’ has the meaning of existence; by ‘vaḍḍhitāya’, it shows that it has the meaning of growth. Regarding ‘bahulīkatāya’, here ‘bahula’ in essence means ‘repeatedly’; thus, it is said, ‘done again and again’. ‘Like a well-yoked chariot’ means like a chariot that is well-yoked. By this, it shows that in ‘yānīkatāya’ it is not made like just any vehicle, but rather, because it can be mounted at any desired moment, it is made like a well-yoked chariot. The construing is: ‘It is a foundation when being done’. Regarding ‘vatthukatāya’, here it shows that the word ‘vatthu’ has the meaning of a foundation. The verbal meaning of ‘vatthu’ should be understood as ‘that wherein one dwells and is established’. Regarding ‘anuṭṭhitāya’, here it shows that the prefix ‘anu’ has the meaning of ‘uninterrupted’, and the root ‘ṭhā’ has the meaning of ‘arising’; thus, it is said, ‘continuously occurring’. By ‘samantato’ (all around), it shows that in ‘paricitāya’ the prefix ‘pari’ has the meaning of ‘all around’. By ‘abhivaḍḍhitāya’, it shows that the root ‘ci’ has the meaning of growth. ‘Samāraddhāya’ means fully accomplished, for the root ‘rādh’ has the meaning of accomplishment. By ‘vasībhāvaṃ upanītāya’ (brought to a state of mastery), it indicates the meaning by way of intention. Showing the implication of the statement ‘one does not see a bad dream’, it says, ‘but an auspicious one,’ etc. The connection is: ‘that which has become a cause of growth’ means a dream that is the cause of growth. Regarding ‘the deities protect’, here, although stated generally, it should be understood as guardian deities; thus, it is said, ‘guardian deities’. Guardian deities are earth deities and so forth. ‘Khippaṃ’ is a neuter noun expressing a state. By this, it shows that in ‘tuvaṭaṃ cittaṃ’ the word ‘tuvaṭa’ is a synonym for ‘khippa’ (quick). Regarding ‘uttarimappaṭivijjhanto’, here, showing that the word ‘uttari’ implies a limit, and its limit, and the fact that the word ‘uttari’ here denotes arahantship, and the meaning of realization for the root ‘vidh’, it says, ‘from the jhāna of loving-kindness,’ etc. Therein, by ‘from the jhāna of loving-kindness’ it indicates the limit; by ‘arahantship’ it indicates the essential meaning of the word ‘uttari’; by ‘asacchikaronto’ (not realizing) it indicates the meaning of realization for the root ‘vidh’. ‘Sabbattha’ (everywhere) means in all the eleven sections.

Iti ekādasakavāravaṇṇanāpariyosānāya

Thus ends the explanation of the Elevenfold Section.

Ekuttarikavaṇṇanāya

In the Commentary on the Method of Increasing by One,

Yojanā samattā.

The construing is complete.

Uposathādipucchāvissajjanā

The Questions and Answers on the Uposatha and so forth

332. Vissajjane evamattho veditabboti yojanā. Kāyasāmaggī ādi nāmāti yojanā. Osāraṇakiriyāti kathanakiriyā. Chandapavāraṇaṃ [M 0.0587] āharitvāti chandañca pavāraṇañca āharitvā. Pavāraṇākathāti “saṅghaṃ bhante pavāremī”tiādikā (mahāva. 210) pavāraṇākathā. Tajjanīyakammādīsu vatthu nāma kiṃ? Puggalo nāma koti āha “vatthu nāmā”tiādi. Tattha yena vatthunāti bhaṇḍanakārakādinā yena vatthunā karaṇabhūtena, hetubhūtena vā[V 2.0216]. Yenāti puggalena kattubhūtena, katanti sambandho. “Tassā tassā kammavācāyā”ti padaṃ “avasānavacana”nti pade avayavisambandho. Sabbatthāti sabbesu vissajjanesu.

332. In the explanation, the meaning should be understood thus—this is the construing. ‘Bodily harmony, etc., is the name’—this is the construing. The act of reinstatement (osāraṇa) is the act of speaking. ‘Having brought forth the consent and the invitation’ means having brought forth both the consent (chanda) and the invitation (pavāraṇā). The speech of invitation (pavāraṇākathā) is the speech of invitation beginning, ‘Venerable sirs, I invite the Saṅgha,’ etc. (Mahāvagga 210). In the acts of censure (tajjanīyakamma), etc., what is the basis (vatthu)? Who is the person (puggala)? Thus, it is said, ‘the basis is,’ etc. Therein, ‘by which basis’ (yena vatthunā) means by which basis, which is the instrument or the cause, such as a quarrel-maker. ‘By whom’ (yena) means by the person who is the agent; the connection is with ‘done’ (kataṃ). The phrase ‘of that particular formal act’ (tassā tassā kammavācāyā) has a part-whole relationship with the phrase ‘the concluding word’ (avasānavacana). ‘Sabbattha’ (in all cases) means in all explanations (vissajjanesu).

Iti uposathādipucchāvissajjanavaṇṇanāya yojanā

Thus, the construing of the commentary on the questions and answers concerning the Uposatha and so forth.

Samattā.

Completed.

Atthavasapakaraṇavaṇṇanā

Commentary on the Treatise on the Grounds for Enactment

334. Atthavasapakaraṇeti avayaviādhāro. Dasa atthavasetiādīsūti avayavādhāro. Yanti vacanaṃ. Uparimaṃ uparimaṃ padanti “saṅghaphāsutāyā”tiādikaṃ uttaruttari vuttaṃ padaṃ. Heṭṭhimassa heṭṭhimassa padassāti “saṅghasuṭṭhutāyā”tiādikassa adho adho vuttassa padassa.

334. ‘Atthavasapakaraṇe’ (in the Treatise on the Grounds for Enactment) is a locative of the whole (avayaviādhāro). ‘Dasa atthavase’ (in the ten grounds for enactment), etc., is a locative of the part (avayavādhāro). ‘Yanti’ is the word. ‘Uparimaṃ uparimaṃ padaṃ’ (the higher and higher phrase) refers to the successively stated phrase, such as ‘for the comfort of the Saṅgha’ (saṅghaphāsutāya), etc. ‘Heṭṭhimassa heṭṭhimassa padassa’ (of the lower and lower phrase) refers to the phrase stated below and below, such as ‘for the well-being of the Saṅgha’ (saṅghasuṭṭhutāya), etc.

Yadetaṃ padasataṃ vuttanti yojanā. Tatthāti tasmiṃ padasate, niddhāraṇe bhummaṃ, atthasatanti abhidheyyasataṃ.
