Dhammasatantiabhidhānasataṃ, pāḷisatanti attho. “Atthasataṃ dhammasata”nti padānaṃ atthantaravikappaṃ dassento āha “atha vā”tiādi. Tattha ye dasa atthavase paṭicca paññattaṃ, tesaṃ dasaatthavasānanti yojanā, ye dasa atthavase pubbe vaṇṇitā, tesaṃ dasaatthavasānanti yojanā. Paṭhamapārājikavaṇṇanāyaṃ (pārā. aṭṭha. 1.39) vaṇṇitāti sambandho. Tatthāti “saṅghasuṭṭhutāyā”tiādipāṭhe. Suṭṭhu devāti suṭṭhu mahārāja. Hi yasmā āṇābalabhogabalaissariyabalehi dibbati, tasmā devoti vuccati. Yo cāti gahaṭṭho vā pabbajito vā, sampaṭicchatīti sambandho. Tasmāti yasmā hitāya sukhāya hoti, tasmā. Ānisaṃsaṃ dassetvā paññapessāmīti [M 0.0588] sambandho. Abhibhavitvā na paññapessāmīti yojanā. Idhāti atthavasapakaraṇe. Tadatthajotakānanti soyeva attho tadattho, tassa jotakā tadatthajotakā, tesaṃ. Idāni veditabbānīti sambandho. Atthaṃ jotentīti atthajotakā, saddā. Nīharitvā, niyametvā vā attho vuccate imāhi saddapaññattīhīti niruttiyo.

The construing is of ‘that which is this hundredfold phrase that was spoken’. ‘Tattha’ (therein) means in that hundredfold phrase; it is a locative of determination. ‘Atthasataṃ’ (a hundred meanings) means a hundred things to be denoted. ‘Dhammasataṃ’ (a hundred principles) means a hundred denotations, that is, a hundred canonical texts. Showing an alternative interpretation of the phrase ‘a hundred meanings, a hundred principles,’ it says, ‘or else,’ etc. Therein, the construing is: ‘of those ten grounds for enactment’ refers to that which was laid down in dependence on the ten grounds for enactment. The construing is also: ‘of those ten grounds for enactment’ refers to the ten grounds for enactment previously explained. The connection is with ‘explained in the commentary on the first Pārājika’ (Pārā. Aṭṭha. 1.39). ‘Tattha’ (therein) means in the text beginning ‘for the well-being of the Saṅgha’. ‘Suṭṭhu deva’ (it is well, Your Majesty) means ‘it is well, great king’. For, because one sports (dibbati) with the power of command, the power of wealth, and the power of sovereignty, one is therefore called a ‘deva’. ‘Yo ca’ (and whoever) refers to a householder or one gone forth; the connection is with ‘accepts’ (sampaṭicchati). ‘Tasmā’ (therefore) means because it is for one’s welfare and happiness, therefore. The connection is with ‘having shown the benefit, I will lay it down’ (paññapessāmi). The construing is: ‘I will not lay it down after overpowering them’. ‘Idha’ (here) means in the Treatise on the Grounds for Enactment. ‘Tadatthajotakānaṃ’ (of those that illuminate that meaning) is explained as: that very meaning is ‘that meaning’ (tadattho); those that illuminate it are ‘illuminators of that meaning’; ‘of them’ (tesaṃ). The connection is with ‘are now to be understood’. Those that illuminate the meaning (atthaṃ jotenti) are illuminators of meaning (atthajotakā), that is, words. ‘Niruttiyo’ (etymologies) are those verbal conventions by which a meaning is expressed, having been extracted or determined.

Atthasatanti gāthāyaṃ atthavase pakaraṇe atthasataṃ veditabbantiādinā yojanā kātabbā. Iti hīti iti eva. Hisaddo hi evasaddattho. Idanti “atthasata”ntiādivacanaṃ, vuttanti sambandho. Etanti yathāvuttaṃ atthaṃ paṭiccāti sambandho.

In the verse ‘Atthasataṃ’ (a hundred meanings), the construing should be made by way of ‘a hundred meanings in the Treatise on the Grounds for Enactment should be understood,’ etc. ‘Iti hi’ means ‘iti eva’ (thus indeed). The word ‘hi’ has the meaning of the word ‘eva’. ‘Idaṃ’ (this) refers to the expression beginning with ‘a hundred meanings’; the connection is with ‘spoken’ (vuttaṃ). ‘Etaṃ’ (this) is connected to ‘in dependence on the meaning as stated’ (yathāvuttaṃ atthaṃ paṭicca).

Iti samantapāsādikāya vinayasaṃvaṇṇanāya

Thus in the Samantapāsādikā, the Commentary on the Vinaya,

Mahāvaggavaṇṇanāya

in the Commentary on the Mahāvagga,

Yojanā samattā.

the construing is completed.

Paṭhamagāthāsaṅgaṇikaṃ

The Compilation of the First Verses.

Sattanagaresu paññattasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

The Commentary on the Training Rules Enacted in the Seven Cities.

335. Ekaṃsanti [V 2.0217] ettha bhummatthe upayogavacananti āha “ekasmiṃ aṃse”ti. Dasanakhasamodhānasamujjalanti dasannaṃ nakhānaṃ samūhena suṭṭhu ujjalaṃ. Ettha “samujjala”nti iminā añjalinti padassa ādarena, abhimukhaṃ vā jalati dibbatīti añjalīti atthaṃ dasseti. Āsīsamānarūpovāti ettha āsīsamānarūpo evāti atthaṃ paṭikkhipanto āha “paccāsīsamānarūpo viyā”ti. Ettha “viyā”ti iminā “āsīsamāno ivā”ti padavibhāgaṃ katvā ivasaddo upamatthajotakoti dasseti. Kissāti ettha karaṇatthe chaṭṭhīvibhatti hotīti āha “kena kāraṇenā”ti. Idhāti mama nisinnaṭṭhānaṃ. “Āgato”ti iminā idhamāgatoti ettha makāro padasandhikaramattoti dasseti. Assāti upālissa vissajjesīti sambandho. Sabbatthāti sabbesu pañhesu. Itīti evaṃ.

335. Regarding ‘ekaṃsaṃ’, here it is a term of reference in the locative sense; thus, it is said, ‘on one shoulder’. ‘Dasanakhasamodhānasamujjalaṃ’ (shining brightly with the joining of the ten nails) means shining very brightly with the collection of the ten nails. Here, by means of ‘samujjalaṃ,’ it shows the meaning of the word ‘añjali’ as ‘it shines (jalati) or is radiant (dibbati) with reverence or towards someone’. Regarding ‘āsīsamānarūpo’, here, rejecting the meaning ‘appearing as if wishing indeed,’ it says, ‘appearing as if anticipating’ (paccāsīsamānarūpo viya). Here, by means of ‘viya,’ having made the word division ‘āsīsamāno iva’ (as if wishing), it shows that the word ‘iva’ illuminates the meaning of simile. Regarding ‘kissa’, here the sixth case (genitive) is in the instrumental sense; thus, it is said, ‘for what reason?’ (kena kāraṇena). ‘Idha’ (here) means my seated place. By means of ‘āgato’ (has come), it shows that the letter ‘m’ in ‘idhamāgato’ (has come here) is merely for euphonic conjunction. ‘Assa’ (to him) is connected to ‘he replied to Upāli’. ‘Sabbattha’ (in all cases) means in all questions. ‘Iti’ means ‘evaṃ’ (thus).

Tatthāti vissajjane. Bhaddako te ummaṅgoti ettha ummaṅgasaddo pañhavācakoti āha “bhaddakā te pañhā”ti. Tattha teti tava. Kasmā [M 0.0589] pañhā “ummaṅgo”ti vuccatīti āha “pañcā hī”tiādi. Hi yasmā ummaṅgoti vuccati, tasmā pañhā ummaṅgo nāmāti yojanā. “Ummujjitvā ṭhitattā”ti iminā ummujjatīti ummaṅgoti vacanatthaṃ dasseti. Mujadhātu ukārassa akāro, avijjandhakārasaṅkhātā udakato ummujjatīti attho. “Tagghā”ti nipātassa tasmā kāraṇāti atthaṃ dassento āha “yasmā”tiādi. “Sampaṭicchanatthe”ti iminā tagghasaddo sādhuatthoti dasseti, taggha sādhūti attho. Tīṇiyevāti “samādahitvā visibbentī”ti ekaṃ, “sāmisenā”ti ekaṃ, “sasitthaka”nti ekanti imāni tīṇiyeva.

'Therein' (tattha) means in the explanation (vissajana). 'Good is your ummaṅga' (bhaddako te ummaṅgo)—here, he says that the word 'ummaṅga' is a word for 'question,' hence 'good are your questions' (bhaddakā te pañhā). There, 'te' means 'tava' (your). Why is a question called 'ummaṅga'? He says, 'Because it has five aspects' (pañcā hi), etc. For because it is called 'ummaṅga,' therefore a question is named 'ummaṅga'—this is the construction (yojanā). By means of 'because it has emerged and stands' (ummujjitvā ṭhitattā), he shows the meaning of the word 'ummaṅga' as 'that which emerges' (ummujjati). The root 'muj,' where the vowel 'u' becomes 'a,' has the meaning 'emerging from the water, which is regarded as the darkness of ignorance'. Showing that the particle 'tagghā' has the meaning 'therefore, for that reason,' he says 'because' (yasmā), etc. By means of 'in the sense of acceptance' (sampaṭicchanatthe), he shows that the word 'taggha' means 'good,' i.e., 'indeed, it is good' (taggha sādhu). 'Only three' (tīṇiyeva)—these are: 'settling down and scattering' (samādahitvā visibbentī) is one, 'with the bait' (sāmisena) is one, 'with wax' (sasitthakaṃ) is one—thus, only these three.

Catuvipattivaṇṇanā

The Explanation of the Four Kinds of Loss

336. Yaṃ taṃ pucchimhāti ettha niggahitato paraṃ akāralopoti āha “yaṃ taṃ apucchimhā”ti[V 2.0218]. Tattha yanti pañhaṃ. Tanti tuvaṃ. “Tva”ntipi pāṭho, ayamevattho. Taṃ tadevāti taṃ taṃ eva pañhaṃ. Aññathāti aññaṃ ākāraṃ.

336. In 'Yaṃ taṃ pucchimhāti', he says that after the niggahīta there is an elision of the letter 'a', and the full form is 'yaṃ taṃ apucchimhā'. Therein, 'yaṃ' refers to the question. 'Taṃ' refers to 'you'. There is also a variant reading as 'tvaṃ', but the meaning is the same. 'Taṃ tadeva' means that very question. 'Aññathā' means in another manner.

Ye duṭṭhullā sā sīlavipattīti ettha nanu sīlavipattiṃ pucchanto pañho natthi, kasmā pana “sā sīlavipattī”ti vissajjanaṃ vuttanti āha “kiñcāpī”tiādi. Etanti “ye duṭṭhullā sā sīlavipattī”ti vacanaṃ. Tamevatthaṃ vitthārento āha “catūsu hī”tiādi. Vatvāti saṃkhepena vatvā.

'Those that are coarse, that is a breach of morality.' Here, although there is no question asking about the breach of morality, why then is the answer given as 'that is a breach of morality'? He said, 'kiñcāpī' and so on. 'This' (etaṃ) refers to the statement 'ye duṭṭhullā sā sīlavipattī'. Expanding on that meaning, he said, 'catūsu hī' and so on. 'Vatvā' means having stated it concisely.

Tissannaṃ vipattīnanti sīlavipattito avasesānaṃ tissannaṃ vipattīnaṃ. Tatthāti “thullaccaya”ntiādivacane.

'Of the three failures' refers to the three failures remaining from the breach of morality. 'Therein' means in the statement beginning with 'thullaccaya' and so on.

“Abbhācikkhantī”ti padassa kattāraṃ dassento āha “vadantā”ti. “Tathāha”ntiādinā vadanākāraṃ dasseti.

Showing the agent of the word 'Abbhācikkhantī', he says 'vadantā'. With 'tathāha' and so on, he shows the manner of speaking.

“Ayaṃ chahī”ti iminā ayaṃ sāti ettha sāsaddo padālaṅkāroti dasseti. Ettāvatāti ettakena “thullaccaya”ntiādivacanamattena. Vissajjitaṃ hotīti sambandho.

By 'Ayaṃ chahī', he shows that in 'ayaṃ sā', the word 'sā' is a verbal embellishment. 'To this extent' means by this much, merely by the statement 'thullaccaya' and so forth. 'It is answered'—this is the connection.

Chedanakādivaṇṇanā

Explanation of Offenses Requiring Cutting Off, etc.

337. Kati [M 0.0590] chedanakānītiādipucchānaṃ anusandhipucchābhāvaṃ dassento āha “yasmā panā”tiādi. Pucchā hi anusandhiananusandhivasena duvidhā. Tattha vissajjanena anusandhivasena pucchā anusandhipucchā nāma, vissajjanamanapekkhitvā yathākāmapucchā ananusandhipucchā nāma. Tāsaṃ vitthāro nettiaṭṭhakathādīsu gahetabbo. Idhāpi “ekādasa yāvatatiyakā”ti vissajjanena anusandhānattā anusandhipucchā nāma. Yasmā pana vissajjitoti sambandho. Saṅkhāvasenāti ekādasā”ti saṅkhāya sattiyā, āyattena vā. Saṅkhānusandhivasenevāti “katī”ti saṅkhāya anusandhivasena eva. Tesanti pañhānaṃ. Tatthāti “cha chedanakānī”tiādipāṭhe. Idamevāti idaṃ eva vacanaṃ. Apubbanti pubbe na vuttaṃ, aporāṇaṃ navanti attho. Yaṃ panetanti yaṃ pana etaṃ vacanaṃ. “Soḷasā”ti iminā sodasāti ettha dakārassa ḷakāraṃ katvā “soḷasā”ti pāṭhopi yujjatīti dasseti. Jānanti paññattāti ettha “evaṃ vatvā”ti pāṭhasesaṃ ajjhāharitvā yojetabbabhāvaṃ dassento āha “jāna”nti [V 2.0219] evaṃ vatvā paññattā”ti. Teti “jāna”nti paññattā sikkhāpadāti attho. Evanti vakkhamānanayena. Paviseyyātīti ettha itisaddo parisamānattho. Iti veditabboti yojanā.

337. 'How many are the offenses requiring cutting off?' and so on—to show the absence of a follow-up question in these inquiries, he says, 'yasmā pana' and so on. For questions are of two kinds: those with a follow-up and those without a follow-up. Among them, a question that, in the answering, has a follow-up is called a follow-up question; while a question asked arbitrarily, without regard for the answer, is called a non-follow-up question. Their details should be understood from commentaries such as the Nettipakaraṇa commentary. Here too, 'ekādasa yāvatatiyakā' is called a follow-up question because it follows up in the answering. 'Since, however, it is answered'—this is the connection. 'By way of number' means by the power of the number eleven, or by reckoning. 'By way of numerical follow-up' means precisely by way of the follow-up of the number 'katī'. 'Of these' means of the questions. 'Therein' means in the passage 'cha chedanakānī' and so on. 'This very' means this very statement. 'Not previously' means not stated before, that is, new. 'But this' means but this statement. By 'Soḷasā', he shows that in 'sodasā' (sixteen), the reading 'soḷasā', where the letter 'd' is changed to 'ḷ', is also suitable. In 'Jānanti paññattā', to show that the remainder of the passage, 'evaṃ vatvā' (having said thus), should be supplied and connected, he says, 'jānaṃ... evaṃ vatvā paññattā' (knowing... having said thus, they are laid down). 'Those' (te) means: the training rules are laid down for one who knows. 'Thus' means in the manner to be explained. In 'Paviseyyātī', the word 'iti' has the sense of conclusion. 'It should be understood thus'—this is the construction.

Asādhāraṇādivaṇṇanā

Explanation of the Uncommon, etc.

338. Purima pañhanti “kati chedanakānī”tiādipañhānaṃ pure vuttaṃ pañhaṃ. Tatthāti “vīsaṃ dve satānī”tiādipāṭhe. “Dveaniyatehī”ti padassa asamāhāradiguvākyaṃ dassento āha “dvīhi aniyatehī”ti. “Saddhi”nti iminā sahādiyoge karaṇavacananti dasseti.

338. 'The first question' means the question stated before among the questions beginning with 'How many cutting-off offenses?'. 'Therein' means in the passage 'vīsaṃ dve satānī' and so on. Regarding the word 'Dveaniyatehī', showing it is a non-collective dvigu compound, he says 'dvīhi aniyatehī' (by the two undetermined cases). By 'Saddhiṃ', he shows that it is an instrumental expression used in conjunction with 'saha' and so on.

Gāthāyaṃ “dhovanañca sikkhāpada”ntiādinā yojanā kātabbā. Dve lomāti dve eḷakalomasikkhāpadāni.

In the verse, the construction should be made beginning with 'dhovanañca sikkhāpada' and so on. 'Dve lomā' refers to the two training rules concerning goat's wool.

“Sakalo”tiādikāya aḍḍhateyyagāthāya yojanā suviññeyyāva.

The construction of the two and a half verses beginning 'Sakalo' and so on is easily understood.

Saṅghamhā [M 0.0591] dasa nissareti ettha “saṅghamhā nissārīyatī”ti (pāci. 680, 730) evaṃ vuttā dasāti yojanānayaṃ dassento āha “saṅghamhā nissārīyatī”tiādi. Tatthāti bhikkhunivibhaṅge. Tathāti yathā khuddakā, tathāti attho. Itīti evaṃ.

In 'Ten expelled from the Saṅgha', showing the method of construction, he says 'saṅghamhā nissārīyatī' and so on, meaning the ten who are spoken of thus. 'Therein' means in the Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga. 'Similarly' means as in the Khuddaka; that is the meaning. 'Thus' means in this manner.

Tesanti pārājikānaṃ. Kaṇhasappādayo durāsadā viya durāsadā hontīti yojanā. “Durūpagamanāti iminā sadadhātuyā gatyatthaṃ dasseti. Durāsajjanāti dukkhena āsajjitabbā, āsajjituṃ na sukarāti attho. Samūpamāti samaupamā. Samūpamākāraṃ dassento āha “yathā”tiādi.

'Of these' means of the pārājikas. The construction is: 'Like black snakes, etc., they are hard to approach.' By 'Durūpagamanā', he shows that the root 'sad' is used in the sense of movement. 'Durāsajjanā' means difficult to approach, not easy to approach; this is the meaning. 'Samūpamā' means a similar comparison. Showing the manner of the similar comparison, he says, 'yathā' and so on.

Sādhāraṇanti aṭṭhahi pārājikehi sādhāraṇaṃ. Ekekassa pārājikassāti sambandho. Avirūḷhī bhavanti teti ettha upamānopameyyānaṃ pākaṭabhāvaṃ katvā yojanānayaṃ dassento āha “yathā ete”tiādi. Avirūḷhidhammāti avirūḷhīsabhāvā. Pakatisīlabhāvenāti pakatiyā sīlavantabhāvena, “pakatisīlābhāvenā”tipi pāṭho, pakatisīlassa abhāvena, abhāvahetūti attho. Ettāvatāti ettakena “aṭṭheva pārājikā”tiādivacanamattena, dassitaṃ hotīti sambandho. Vibhattiyoti pārājikādivasena vibhajitabbāti vibhattiyoti. Tatthāti “tevīsati saṅghādisesā”tiādipāṭhe[V 2.0220]. Sabbasaṅgāhikavacananti sabbesaṃ tiṇṇaṃ samathānaṃ, sabbāsaṃ vā āpattīnaṃ samathānaṃ saṅgāhikavacanaṃ. “Dvīhi samathehī”ti sammukhāvinayena ca paṭiññātakaraṇena cāti dvīhi samathehi.

'Common' means shared by the eight pārājikas. The connection is 'for each pārājika.' In 'They do not grow', showing the method of construction by making clear the relationship between the simile and the subject of comparison, he says, 'just as these,' etc. 'Of a non-growing nature' means having a nature of not growing. 'By natural virtuous conduct' means by having a naturally virtuous nature; alternatively, the reading may be 'by the absence of natural virtue,' meaning due to the lack of innate virtue, the cause being absence. 'Up to this point' means by just this much, merely by the statement 'aṭṭheva pārājikā' and so on, it is shown—this is the connection. 'By classification' means to be classified according to pārājikas, etc., hence 'classification'. 'Therein' means in the passage 'tevīsati saṅghādisesā' and so on. 'An inclusive term for all' means a term encompassing all three settlements, or a settlement encompassing all offenses. 'By two settlements' means by face-to-face procedure and by acting on admission—these are the two settlements.

Etanti “dve uposathā dve pavāraṇā”ti vacanaṃ. Vibhajanānīti vibhajitabbānaṃ vibhajanakiriyāya avinābhāvato bhāvavasena vuttaṃ, tasmā vibhajitabbāti vibhattiyoti vacanattho kātabbo. Aparāpi imā vibhattiyo hontīti yojanā. Heṭṭhā vuttassa “vibhattimattadassaneneva cetaṃ vuttaṃ, na samathehi vūpasamanavasenā”ti vacanassa atthanayato aññaṃ atthanayaṃ dassento āha “athavā”tiādi, “imāpi vibhattiyo”ti padaṃ “nissāyā”ti pade avuttakammaṃ[M 0.0592]. Nissāya āpajjantīti sambandho. Tāti āpattiyo. Vuttappakārehevāti tīhi samathehīti vuttapakāreheva. Taṃmūlikānanti te eva uposathādayo mūlametāsanti taṃmūlikā, tāsaṃ. Iminā kāriyūpacārena vuttanayaṃ dasseti. Tā vibhattiyoti uposathādivibhattiyo.

'This' means the statement 'two uposathas, two pavāraṇās'. The term 'Vibhajanānī' (classifications) is spoken in the sense of an action because the things to be classified are inseparable from the act of classifying. Therefore, the meaning of the word should be taken as 'what is to be classified' or 'classifications' (vibhattiyo). The construction is: 'These other classifications also exist'. Showing another method of meaning than that of the statement mentioned below, 'This is stated merely by seeing the classification, not by way of pacification through settlements,' he says, 'athavā' and so on. The phrase 'imāpi vibhattiyo' is the unexpressed object of the word 'nissāyā'. The connection is: 'Having depended on, they are incurred' (Nissāya āpajjanti). 'Those' (tā) refers to the offenses (āpattiyo). 'In the manner already stated' means in the manner stated as 'by the three settlements'. 'Of those rooted in them' (taṃmūlikānaṃ) means: those very uposathas, etc., are their root, hence 'rooted in them'; 'of them'. By this, he shows the stated method by way of a functional metaphor. 'Those classifications' refers to the classifications such as uposatha, etc.

Pārājikādiāpattivaṇṇanā

The Explanation of Offenses Beginning with Pārājika

339. Evaṃ vissajjetvāti sambandho. Yadidaṃ āpattipārājikaṃ nāmāti yojanā. Āpattipārājikanti āpattisaṅkhātaṃ pārājikaṃ. “Parājayamāpanno”ti iminā sāsanato puggalaṃ parājetīti pārājikanti vacanatthaṃ dasseti. Ṇyapaccayo hetukatvatthavācako, yakārassa kakāro. Cutoti cavako. Paraddhoti viraddho. Bhaṭṭhoti patito. Niraṅkatoti saṅghamhā apasārito. Anīhate tasmiṃ puggaleti tasmiṃ puggale saṅghamhā nīharitvā na harite, anapanīteti attho. “Uposathapavāraṇādibhedo”ti iminā saṃvāsasarūpaṃ dasseti. Byañjane ādaramakatvā “etaṃ āpattī”ti vuttaṃ. Ayaṃ hīti ayaṃ evaṃ vakkhamāno. Etthāti gāthāyaṃ. Tena tasmāti ettha “tasmā”ti padena “tenā”ti padassa kāraṇatthaṃ dasseti.

339. Having thus explained, this is the connection. The construction is: ‘This is what is called a pārājika offence.’ ‘Pārājika offence’ means the pārājika designated as an offence. By ‘one who has incurred defeat,’ it shows the etymological meaning of ‘pārājika’ as that which defeats a person from the Dispensation. The suffix ‘ṇya’ has a causal meaning, and the letter ‘y’ becomes ‘k’. ‘Fallen’ means ‘fallen away’. ‘Failed’ means ‘gone wrong’. ‘Lost’ means ‘fallen down’. ‘Made null’ means ‘removed from the Saṅgha’. ‘When that person is not removed’ means: that person, having been led out from the Saṅgha, is not taken away; the meaning is ‘not expelled’. By ‘the distinctions such as Uposatha and Pavāraṇā,’ it shows the nature of communion. Without regard for the literal expression, it is said, ‘This is an offence.’ ‘This indeed’ means ‘this which will be spoken of thus’. ‘Here’ means ‘in the verse’. In the phrase ‘By that, therefore,’ the word ‘therefore’ shows the causal meaning of the word ‘by that’.

Etthāti dutiyagāthāyaṃ. Ādimhi ceva icchitabboti sambandho. Hīti saccaṃ. Etthāti parivāsadānādīsu catūsu kammesu. “Saṅgho”tiādivacanattho tipadabhinnādhikaraṇabāhiratthasamāso hoti, cevasaddacasaddehi ādisesapadānaṃ ubhayapadatthapadhānabhāvaṃ dasseti, “icchitabbo”ti padaṃ kārakānaṃ kiriyāpekkhattā kiriyatthāya pakkhittaṃ. Assāti āpattiyā, iminā aññapadaṃ dasseti. Icchitabbatthe apaccayaṃ katvā taddhitantipi vadanti. Lahukanayo panesa. Ayaṃ panettha [V 2.0221] garukanayo – ādi ca seso ca ādisesā, saṅgho ādisesesu assā icchitabboti saṅghādisesoti.

‘Here’ means ‘in the second verse’. The connection is: ‘in the beginning, and also what should be desired’. ‘Indeed’ means ‘truly’. ‘Here’ refers to the four legal procedures, beginning with the granting of probation. The meaning of the phrase beginning with ‘Saṅgha’ is a bahubbīhi compound with an external referent, composed of three words in different grammatical cases. By the words ‘ceva’ and ‘ca’, it shows that the meanings of both constituent words, ‘ādi’ (beginning) and ‘sesa’ (remainder), are primary. The word ‘should be desired’ is inserted to supply the meaning of an action, as the grammatical agents require an action. ‘Of it’ refers to the offence; by this, it indicates the external referent. Some also say it is a secondary derivative (taddhita) formed without a suffix in the sense of ‘what should be desired’. However, this is the simpler method. Here is the more complex method: ‘beginning’ (ādi) and ‘remainder’ (sesa) are ‘ādisesā’; the Saṅgha should be desired for it (the offence) in the beginning and in the remainder (ādisesesu), hence ‘Saṅghādisesa’.

Anekaṃsikataṃ [M 0.0593] padanti ettha padanti sikkhāpadaṃ. Anekaṃsena kataṃ anekaṃsikatanti dassento āha “yasmā idaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ anekaṃsena kata”nti. Yasmā kataṃ, tasmā aniyatoti pavuccatīti yojanā. Tatthāti aniyate. Yatthāti sikkhāpade. Sopīti sikkhāpadadhammopi.

In the phrase ‘anekaṃsikataṃ padaṃ’ (a matter made uncertain), the word ‘padaṃ’ means ‘training rule’. Showing that ‘done with uncertainty’ is ‘anekaṃsikataṃ’, he says, ‘because this training rule is made with uncertainty’. The construction is: ‘Because it is so made, therefore it is called “Aniyata” (undetermined)’. ‘Therein’ means ‘in the Aniyata’. ‘Wherein’ means ‘in the training rule’. ‘That also’ means ‘the principle of the training rule also’.

Accayesūti dosesu. Te hi niddosaṃ atikkamma ayanti gacchanti pavattantīti accayāti vuccanti. Tenāti accayena. Thūloti oḷāriko. “Thūlattā”ti iminā “teneta”nti ettha tenasaddassa kāraṇatthaṃ dasseti. Accayassa thūlattāti sambandho. Etanti āpattidhammaṃ. Imāya gāthāya aññesaṃ lahukāpattīnaṃ thūlo accayo thullaccayoti vacanatthaṃ dasseti. Dvebhāve sati saṃyogaparattā rasso hotīti daṭṭhabbaṃ.

‘In transgressions’ means ‘in faults’. For they go beyond what is faultless and proceed, thus they are called ‘transgressions’ (accayā). ‘By that’ means ‘by that transgression’. ‘Gross’ means ‘coarse’. By ‘because of grossness,’ it shows the causal meaning of the word ‘tena’ (by that) in the phrase ‘tenetaṃ’. The connection is ‘because of the grossness of the transgression’. ‘This’ refers to the principle of the offence. By this verse, it shows the etymological meaning of ‘Thullaccaya’ (gross transgression) to be a gross transgression in relation to other minor offences. It should be understood that when there is a doubling of a consonant, the preceding vowel becomes short because it is followed by a conjunct consonant.

“Nissajjitvā desetabbato”ti iminā nissajjanaṃ nissaggo, āpattidesanato pubbabhāge kattabbassa vinayakammassetamadhivacanaṃ, so etassatthīti nissaggiyanti vacanatthaṃ dasseti.

By the phrase ‘because it must be confessed after having relinquished it,’ it shows the etymological meaning of ‘nissaggiya’ as follows: ‘nissagga’ is the act of relinquishing; this is a designation for the disciplinary act that must be performed in the preliminary stage, before the confession of the offence. That which involves this (nissagga) is called ‘nissaggiya’.

Kusaladhammasaddena kusalacittameva gahetabbanti āha “kusaladhammasaṅkhātaṃ kusalacitta”nti. “Kusalacittaṃ pātetī”ti iminā cittaṃ pātetīti pācittiyanti vacanatthaṃ dasseti. Ettha “cittapātiya”nti vattabbe padavipariyāyaṃ katvā, takārassa ca lopaṃ katvā “pācittiya”nti vuttaṃ. Acinteyyo hi pāḷinayo. Ṇyapaccayo hetukatvatthavācako. Nanu “pāteti kusalaṃ dhamma”nti imināva “pācittiya”nti padassa nibbacanaṃ siddhaṃ, kasmā pana “aparajjhati cittasammohanaṭṭhāna”nti vuttanti āha “yaṃ panā”tiādi. Yasmā hotīti sambandho.

By the term ‘wholesome states,’ only the wholesome mind is to be understood; thus it is said, ‘the wholesome mind, designated as wholesome states’. By ‘it causes the wholesome mind to fall,’ it shows the etymological meaning of ‘pācittiya’ as ‘it causes the mind to fall’. Here, when ‘cittapātiya’ should have been said, ‘pācittiya’ is said by reversing the order of the components and eliding the letter ‘t’. Indeed, Pāḷi usage is inconceivable. The suffix ‘ṇya’ has a causal meaning. Is it not so that with the phrase ‘it causes the wholesome state to fall,’ the derivation of the word ‘pācittiya’ is already established? Why then is it said, ‘it is an offence, a basis for mental confusion’? He says, ‘But that which…,’ and so on. The connection is: ‘because it is’.

Pāṭidesanīyāsu nibbacanameva adassetvā kasmā “bhikkhu aññātako santo”tiādi vuttanti āha “vuttagārayhabhāvakāraṇadassanatthamevā”ti. “Paṭidesetabbato”ti iminā aññāpattidesanānayato “gārayha”ntiādinā paṭi visuṃ vatvā desetabbāti pāṭidesanīyāti nibbacanaṃ dasseti.

Regarding the Pāṭidesanīya offences, without showing the mere derivation, why is it said, ‘a monk, not being a relative…,’ and so on? He says, ‘It is only to show the reason for the state of being blameworthy as stated.’ By the phrase ‘because it must be confessed in a particular way,’ it shows the derivation of ‘pāṭidesanīya’ as follows: it must be confessed by stating separately with the prefix ‘paṭi’ the blameworthy act, etc., which is a method different from the confession of other offences.

Dukkaṭanti [V 2.0222][M 0.0594] ettha dusaddo duṭṭhuattho ca virūpattho ca hotīti dassento āha “duṭṭhu kataṃ, virūpaṃ vā kata”nti. Tanti kammaṃ. Taṃ panetanti dukkaṭaṃ, khalitanti sambandho. Assāti dukkaṭassa. Tassattho evaṃ veditabboti yojanā. Hīti vitthāro. Yaṃ pāpanti yojanā. Yadīti atha. Yadisaddo hi athapariyāyo. Idampīti idampi kammaṃ, pāpanti sambandho.

Regarding ‘dukkaṭa’, showing that here the prefix ‘du’ has the meaning of both ‘badly’ and ‘improperly’, he says, ‘badly done, or improperly done’. ‘That’ refers to the action. The connection is: ‘But that dukkaṭa is a failure’. ‘Of it’ means ‘of the dukkaṭa’. The construction is: ‘Its meaning should be understood thus’. ‘Hi’ means ‘in detail’. The construction is: ‘What is evil’. ‘Yadi’ means ‘atha’ (then). For the word ‘yadi’ is a synonym for ‘atha’. ‘This also’ means ‘this action also’; the connection is with ‘evil’.

“Lapita”nti iminā durābhaṭṭhanti ettha bhāsadhātuyā kathanatthaṃ dasseti. Yanti vacanaṃ. Kiñca bhiyyoti tato atirekaṃ kathetabbavacanaṃ kiñcāti attho. Saṃkiliṭṭhañca yaṃ padanti ettha cakāro pisaddattho “pada”nti ettha yojetabbo, yaṃsaddo kāraṇatthoti āha “saṃkiliṭṭhaṃ yasmā tampi pada”nti. Tampi padanti tampi vacanaṃ. Padasaddo hi vacanavācako. Tampi vacanaṃ yasmā saṃkiliṭṭhaṃ hotīti yojanā. Kathaṃ saṃkiliṭṭhaṃ hotīti yojanā. “Yasmā”ti padena yaṃsaddo kāraṇatthoti dasseti. Nanti padaṃ. “Etaṃ iti vuccatī”ti saṃvaṇṇetabbapadaṃ. “Dubbhāsitanti etaṃ vuccatī”ti saṃvaṇṇanāpadaṃ. Etanti etaṃ padaṃ, etaṃ vacananti attho.

By ‘lapitaṃ’ (spoken), it shows that in the word ‘durābhaṭṭhaṃ’ (badly spoken), the meaning of speaking comes from the root ‘bhās’. ‘Yaṃ’ means ‘speech’. ‘Kiñca bhiyyo’ means ‘what further speech is there to be said beyond that?’ In the phrase ‘saṃkiliṭṭhañca yaṃ padaṃ’ (and which word is defiled), the particle ‘ca’ has the meaning of ‘pi’ (also) and should be construed with ‘padaṃ’. The word ‘yaṃ’ has a causal meaning, thus he says, ‘because that word also is defiled’. ‘That word also’ means ‘that speech also’. For the word ‘pada’ is a term for speech. The construction is: ‘Because that speech also is defiled’. How is it defiled? By the word ‘yasmā’ (because), it shows that the word ‘yaṃ’ has a causal meaning. ‘Naṃ’ is the word in question. ‘Etaṃ iti vuccati’ (it is called this) is the phrase to be explained. ‘Dubbhāsitanti etaṃ vuccati’ (it is called dubbhāsita) is the explanatory phrase. ‘Etaṃ’ means ‘this word,’ that is, ‘this speech’.

Etthāti sekhiyagāthāya. Idanti āpattīnaṃ nibbacanadīpakaṃ vacanaṃ, vuttanti sambandho. Kassa dīpanatthaṃ vuttanti āha “saṅgahitassa atthassa dīpanattha”nti.

‘Here’ means ‘in the Sekhiya verse’. ‘This’ refers to the statement that illuminates the derivation of the offences; the connection is with ‘was spoken’. For the purpose of illuminating what was it spoken? He says, ‘for the purpose of illuminating the meaning that has been summarized’.

Tatthāti “channamativassatī”tiādivacane. Gehanti pakatigehaṃ. Idaṃ pana gehanti yojanā. Vitthārento āha “mūlāpattiñhī”tiādi. “Avivaṭa”nti vatvā tassatthaṃ dassetuṃ vuttaṃ “succhanna”nti. Vivaṭanti acchannaṃ. Nātivassanabhāvaṃ vitthārento āha “mūlāpattiñhī”tiādi. Vivaranto bhikkhu nāpajjatīti sambandho. Suddhanteti suddhakoṭṭhāse. “Tasmā”ti ca “tenā”ti ca yebhuyyena atthato ekaṃ, tasmā vuttaṃ “tena kāraṇenā”ti. Evañcetaṃ vivaṭanti evaṃ etaṃ channaṃ ce vivaṭanti yojanā.

‘Therein’ means ‘in the statement beginning with “channaṃ ativassati” (it rains on what is covered)’. ‘Gehaṃ’ (house) means ‘an ordinary house’. The construction is: ‘But this is a house’. Elaborating, he says, ‘For the root offence…,’ and so on. Having said ‘avivaṭaṃ’ (uncovered), ‘succhannaṃ’ (well-covered) is stated to show its meaning by contrast. ‘Vivaṭaṃ’ means ‘not covered’. Explaining the state of not being rained on, he says, ‘For the root offence…,’ and so on. The connection is: ‘a monk who uncovers does not incur an offence’. ‘Suddhante’ means ‘in a clean part’. ‘Tasmā’ (therefore) and ‘tena’ (by that) are for the most part one in meaning; therefore, it is said, ‘for that reason’. The construction is: ‘And thus this is uncovered,’ and ‘thus this, though covered, is uncovered’.

Paripātiyamānānanti abhibhūyamānānaṃ. “Rukkhādigahanaṃ arañña”nti iminā pavananti padassa araññapariyāyataṃ dasseti. Gatisaddassa bhavabhedādiatthaṃ paṭikkhipitvā paṭissaraṇatthe hotīti dassento āha [M 0.0595] “paṭissaraṇaṃ hotī”ti. Tanti pavanaṃ. Teti migā. “Assasantī”ti padena “passasantī”ti atthopi gahetabbo avinābhāvato, ānāpānaṃ karontīti attho. Ākāsoti ajaṭākāso. Pakkhīnanti vihaṅgamānaṃ. “Sabbesaṃ saṅkhatadhammāna”nti iminā dhammānanti ettha saṅkhatadhammoyeva gahetabboti dasseti. “Vināsovā”ti [V 2.0223] iminā vibhavasaddo vināsavācakoti dasseti. Tesanti sabbesampi saṅkhatadhammānaṃ. Gatīti patiṭṭhā. Kasmā vibhavo dhammānaṃ gati hotīti āha “na hī”tiādi. Hīti yasmā. Teti sabbepi saṅkhatadhammā. Vināsanti vibhavaṃ. Sucirampīti asītivassādikālampi. Nibbānaṃ arahato gatīti saṃvaṇṇetabbapadaṃ. “Khīṇāsavassā”ti iminā arahatoti padassa atthaṃ dasseti. “Anupādisesanibbānadhātū”ti iminā “nibbāna”nti padassa idha adhippetanibbānaṃ dasseti. Gāthāya te te atthā saṃgahetvā gaṇiyanti etthāti gāthāsaṅgaṇikaṃ.

'Paripātiyamānānaṃ' means 'being overwhelmed'. By 'a dense forest of trees, the wilderness,' it shows that the word 'pavana' is a synonym for 'arañña'. Rejecting such meanings of the word 'gati' as difference in states of being, he shows that it is in the sense of refuge, thus he says, 'it becomes a refuge'. 'That' refers to the forest. 'They' refers to the deer. By the word 'assasanti' (breathing in), the meaning 'passasanti' (breathing out) should also be taken due to their inseparability; the meaning is 'they are breathing'. 'Ākāsa' means 'unobstructed space'. 'Pakkhīnaṃ' means 'of the flying creatures'. By 'of all conditioned phenomena,' it shows that by 'dhammānaṃ' (of phenomena) here, only conditioned phenomena should be understood. By 'vināso vā' (or destruction), it shows that the word 'vibhava' is indicative of destruction. 'Of them' means 'of all conditioned phenomena'. 'Gati' means 'a foundation'. As to why cessation is the destination of phenomena, he says, 'for indeed, not...' etc. 'Indeed' means 'because'. 'They' refers to all conditioned phenomena. 'Vināsaṃ' (destruction) means 'vibhavaṃ' (cessation). 'Even for a long time' means 'even for a period of eighty years or more'. 'Nibbāna is the destination of the Arahant' is the phrase to be explained. By 'of the one whose taints are destroyed,' it shows the meaning of the word 'Arahant'. By 'the Nibbāna element without residue remaining,' it shows the Nibbāna intended here by the word 'Nibbāna'. The various meanings of the verse are collected and enumerated herein; thus, it is a 'Gāthāsaṅgaṇika' (summary of the verse).

Iti paṭhamagāthāsaṅgaṇikavaṇṇanāya yojanā samattā.

Thus ends the explanation of the commentary on the summary of the first verse.

Adhikaraṇabhedaṃ

The Division of Disputes

Ukkoṭanabhedādivaṇṇanā

Explanation of Subversion, its Kinds, and so on

340. Adhikaraṇabhede evamattho veditabboti yojanā. Dassetuṃ āhāti sambandho. Dve samatheti ettha dvinnaṃ samathānaṃ sarūpaṃ dassento āha “sammukhāvinayañca yebhuyyasikañcā”ti. “Paṭisedhetī”ti iminā ukkoṭetīti ettha kuṭadhātuyā chedanatthaṃ atthato dasseti. Chedanaṃ nāma atthato samathapaṭisedhananti attho.

340. In the division of disputes, the meaning should be understood thus—this is the construction. The connection is, he says this to show. Regarding “the two settlements,” here, showing the nature of the two settlements, he states: “the settlement in the presence and the settlement by majority decision.” By “he rejects,” he shows that here, in “he subverts,” the root ‘kuṭa’ has the meaning of cutting. Cutting, in meaning, is the rejection of a settlement—this is the meaning.

341. Dvādasasu ukkoṭesūti niddhāraṇe bhummaṃ. Akataṃ kammantiādayoti ettha ādisaddena “dukkaṭaṃ kammaṃ, puna kātabbaṃ kamma”nti dve ukkoṭā saṅgahetabbā. Anihataṃ kammantiādayoti ettha ādisaddena “dunnihataṃ, puna nihanitabba”nti dve ukkoṭā saṅgahetabbā. Avinicchitantiādayoti ettha ādisaddena “duvinicchitaṃ, puna vinicchitabba”nti dve [M 0.0596] ukkoṭā saṅgahetabbā. Avūpasantantiādayoti ettha ādisaddena “duvūpasantaṃ, puna vūpasametabba”nti dve ukkoṭā saṅgahetabbā. Apicāti sāmaññato pana.

341. In 'in the twelve subversions,' the locative case is for determination. By “an undone act,” etc., here, the word “etc.” should include two subversions: “a wrongly done act” and “an act to be done again.” By “an unsettled act,” etc., here, the word “etc.” should include two subversions: “a badly settled act” and “an act to be settled again.” By “an undecided act,” etc., here, the word “etc.” should include two subversions: “a badly decided act” and “an act to be decided again.” By “an unappeased act,” etc., here, the word “etc.” should include two subversions: “a badly appeased act” and “an act to be appeased again.” Moreover, this is generally understood.

Tattha jātakanti ettha tasaddassa visayaṃ dassento āha “yasmiṃvihāre”ti. Yasmiṃvihāre uppannaṃ [V 2.0224] hotīti sambandho. Aññamaññassa attesu, attānaṃ vā paṭipakkhaṃ atthayanti icchantīti attapaccatthikā. Pāḷimuttakavinicchayenevāti pāḷiyaṃ āgatehi samathehi muttakena dhammadesanāmattavinicchayeneva. Idanti adhikaraṇaṃ. Yenāpi vinicchayenāti pāḷimuttakena yenāpi vinicchayena.

Here, in 'arisen there,' showing the scope of the word 'that,' he says, 'in which dwelling.' The connection is, 'it arises in which dwelling.' 'Attapaccatthikā' means those who desire to be hostile to each other, or who are hostile to themselves. 'Pāḷimuttakavinicchayeneva' means solely by a judgment that is merely a teaching of the Dhamma, separate from the settlements found in the Pāli canon. 'This' refers to the dispute. 'Yenāpi vinicchayena' means by whatever judgment that is outside the Pāli canon.

Aññoti nevāsikehi añño vinayadharo pucchatīti sambandho. Tehi cāti nevāsikehi ca.

“Other” means that another Vinaya-holder is questioned by the residents—this is the connection. “And by them” means and by the residents.

Etassāti vinayadharassa. Ayanti vinayadharo. Tatthāti taṃ gāmaṃ. Aññamaññaṃ vā saññāpentīti attapaccatthikā aññamaññaṃ vā saññāpenti. Te bhikkhūti te attapaccatthikā bhikkhū. Nijjhāpentīti saññāpenti. Ukkoṭeti yoti yo ukkoṭeti. Eteti attapaccatthike bhikkhū, disvāti sambandho. Tatthāti gāmaṃ. Tatthevāti antarāmagge eva.

'Of this' refers to the Vinaya-holder. 'This' refers to the Vinaya-holder. 'There' refers to that village. 'Or they convince each other' means the hostile ones convince each other. 'Those monks' refers to those hostile monks. 'Nijjhāpenti' (they make reflect) means 'saññāpenti' (they convince). 'He who subverts' means 'whoever subverts'. 'These' refers to the hostile monks; the connection is with 'having seen'. 'There' refers to the village. 'Right there' means right on the road in between.

Tatthevāti gāmameva. Tatthevāti tasmiṃyeva ṭhāne. Tattha gatanti taṃ gāmaṃ gataṃ.

“Right there” means that very village. “Right there” means in that very place. “Gone there” means gone to that village.

“Eseva nayo”ti iminā pācittiyameva atidisati.

By “this is the same rule,” he applies by analogy only this pācittiya.

Saṅghena…pe… adhikaraṇe vadantopīti sambandho. Yaṃ panetaṃ āpattivuṭṭhānaṃ nāma hotīti yojanā. Etanti āpattivuṭṭhānaṃ. Vadantopīti pisaddo na kevalaṃ tiṇavatthārakaṃ ukkoṭentoyeva ukkoṭeti nāma, atha kho vadantopīti dasseti.

The connection is with “even while speaking in the dispute” (with the Sangha…etc.). The construction is: “That which is called the emergence from an offense.” “This” refers to the emergence from an offense. The word 'pi' in “even while speaking” shows that not only is one who subverts the grass-covering called a subverter, but indeed also one who is “even while speaking.”

Chandāgatiṃ gacchantotiādīsu agatigamanākāraṃ dassento āha “vinayadharo hutvā”tiādi. Atthāya ukkoṭentoti sambandho. Tassāti anatthaṃ carantassa. Mando pana ukkoṭeti nāmāti sambandho. Eko balavanissito ca hotīti sambandho. Gahanamicchādiṭṭhinti [M 0.0597] gahanasadisaṃ micchādiṭṭhiṃ pavanasadisaṃ micchādiṭṭhinti attho. Balavante cāti ettha casaddo sabbakammesu yojetabbo. Nissitattāti ekassa nissitattā. Balavanissito cāti etthāpi ca saddo sabbakattūsu yojetabbo. Tassāti visamādinissitassa.

In 'going by favor,' etc., showing the manner of going by wrong courses, he says, 'having become a Vinaya-holder,' etc. The connection is with 'subverting for a purpose.' 'Of him' refers to one acting unbeneficially. The connection is with 'but a fool subverts.' The connection is with 'and one is reliant on a powerful person.' 'Wrong view like a thicket' means wrong view like a dense thicket, wrong view like a forest. In 'and the powerful,' here the word 'ca' should be joined with all actions. 'Due to reliance' means due to reliance on one. In 'and reliant on the powerful,' here too the word 'ca' should be joined with all agents. 'Of him' refers to one who relies on injustice, etc.

Soti sāmaṇero. Maṅkubhūtātthāti maṅkū hutvā bhūtā, maṅkuṃ vā pattā attha bhavathāti attho. Teti parājayabhikkhū. Tassāti sāmaṇerassa. Soti sāmaṇero. Teti parājayabhikkhū. Tanti [V 2.0225] sāmaṇeraṃ. Soti daharo. Tatoti sannipātakāraṇā. Hiyyoti anantarātītāhe. Itīti evaṃ vadeti. Soti daharo. Idaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ paññattanti yojanā. Gacchāti gacchāhi. Itīti evaṃ vattabboti yojanā.

“He” refers to the novice. “Maṅkubhūtāttha” means 'you have become dejected,' or 'you have attained a dejected state.' “They” refers to the defeated monks. “Of him” refers to the novice. “He” refers to the novice. “They” refers to the defeated monks. “Him” refers to the novice. “He” refers to the young monk. “From that” refers to the reason for the assembly. “Yesterday” refers to the immediately preceding day. “Thus” means 'he speaks thus.' “He” refers to the young monk. The construction is: “This training rule is laid down.” “Go” means “go!” The construction is: “It should be said thus.”

Saṅghena saddhiṃ adhikaraṇaṃ vinicchinitvā pariveṇagataṃ ekaṃ bhikkhunti yojanā. Kissāti kena kāraṇena. Evaṃ iminākārena vinicchitabbaṃ nanūti yojanā. Soti vinicchayakārako bhikkhu. Chandadāyako suviññeyyoyeva.

The construction is with: 'a certain monk who, having decided the dispute together with the Sangha, has gone to his cell.' “Why?” means for what reason? The construction is: “Should it not be decided thus, in this manner?” “He” refers to the monk who decides the case. The giver of consent is indeed easily understood.

Adhikaraṇanidānādivaṇṇanā

Explanation of the Origins of Disputes, and so on

342. Kiṃnidānantiādīsu chasu padesu samāsabhāvaṃ dassento āha “kiṃnidānamassā”tiādi. Assāti vivādādhikaraṇassa. “Kiṃnidāna”nti padānaṃ satipi samāsabhāve byañjanantapakatikattā “ki”nti niggahitantabhāvena uccāraṇaṃ kātabbaṃ. Sabbānetānīti sabbāni nidānantiādīni etāni padāni. Vevacanānīti ekasmiṃyeva “kāraṇa”nti atthe vividhāni vacanāni vivacanāni, tāniyeva vevacanāni. Atha vā vividhaṃ vacanametassatthassāti vivacanaṃ, kāraṇasaṅkhāto attho, abhidheyyaabhidhānabhāvena sambandhattā vivacanassa etāni vevacanāni, padāni.

342. In the six phrases beginning with 'What is the origin?' he shows the state of being a compound by saying, 'What is its origin?' etc. 'Its' refers to the dispute-adhikaraṇa. Although the word 'Kiṃnidāna' is a compound, because its nature is to end in a consonant, the pronunciation should be made as 'kiṃ', ending with a niggahita. 'All these' means all these words, such as 'origin,' etc. 'Synonyms' are diverse expressions for the single meaning of 'cause,' which are vivacanāni; these are indeed vevacanāni. Alternatively, 'vivacana' is a diverse expression for this meaning, the meaning termed 'cause'; and because of the relationship of being the expressed and the expression, these words are synonyms of 'vivacana'.

“Aṭṭhārasabhedakaravatthusaṅkhāto”ti iminā vivādasarūpaṃ dasseti. Vivādanti aṭṭhārasabhedakaravatthusaṅkhātaṃ vivādaṃ. Etanti “vivādanidāna”nti [M 0.0598] etaṃ vacanaṃ. Assāti anuvādādhikaraṇassa. Idampīti “anuvādanidāna”nti vacanampi. Assāti āpattādhikaraṇassa. Etanti “āpattinidāna”nti vacanaṃ. Kiccameva byañjanavaḍḍhanavasena kiccayanti vuttaṃ. Assāti kiccādhikaraṇassa. Samanubhāsanādīnaṃ uppajjanakakiccānanti sambandho. Etanti “kiccayanidāna”nti vacanaṃ. Ekapadayojanāti ekena “nidāna”nti padena yojanā. Sabbapadānīti sabbāni samudayādīni padāni.

'Comprising the eighteen bases for causing schism'—by this, it shows the nature of a dispute. 'They dispute' means they dispute a dispute comprising the eighteen bases for causing schism. 'This' means this expression, 'the cause of dispute.' 'Its' refers to the legal case of accusation. 'This too' means the expression 'the cause of accusation' as well. 'Its' refers to the legal case of an offense. 'This' means the expression 'the cause of an offense.' Mere function is called 'function' by way of adding a syllable. 'Its' refers to the legal case of proceedings. The connection is with the functions that give rise to interrogation and so forth. 'This' means the expression 'the cause of proceedings.' 'Connection with a single word' means connection by the single word 'cause.' 'All the words' means all the words, such as 'origin,' etc.

Navannanti jātivasena channaṃ hetūnaṃ navasu antogadhattā tikavasenetaṃ vuttaṃ. Byañjanamattanti hetupaccayavasena byañjanameva. Hīti saccaṃ, yasmā vā. Etthāti tatiyapucchāvissajjane.

'Of the nine'—because six causes are included within the nine by way of their category, this is stated in terms of the triad. 'Mere expression' means merely the expression in terms of cause and condition. 'Hi' means truly, or because. 'Here' means in the answer to the third question.

343. Dvādasa mūlānīti ettha dvādasannaṃ mūlānaṃ sarūpaṃ dassento āha “kodhaupanāhayugaḷakādīnī”tiādi[V 2.0226]. Ettha (vibha. 833, 944) ādisaddena makkhapaḷāsayugaḷa issāmacchariyayugaḷa māyāsāṭheyyayugaḷa pāpicchamicchādiṭṭhiyugaḷa sandiṭṭhiparāmāsiādhānaggāhiduppaṭinissaggiyugaḷavasena pañca yugaḷāni saṅgaṇhāti. Ajjhattasantānappavattānīti niyakajjhattasantāne pavattāni.

343. 'Twelve roots'—here, showing the nature of the twelve roots, he says, 'the pair of anger and hostility,' etc. Here (Vibhanga 833, 944), by the word 'etc.' he includes five pairs: the pair of contempt and domineering, the pair of envy and stinginess, the pair of deceit and craftiness, the pair of evil wishes and wrong view, and the pair of adherence to one's own views and obstinate grasping. 'Arising in one’s own continuum' means occurring in one's own personal continuum.

Aṭṭhārasabhedakaravatthūnaṃ samuṭṭhānabhāvaṃ nibbacanena pakāsento āha “taṃ hī”tiādi. Tanti anuvādādhikaraṇaṃ, samuṭṭhātīti sambandho. Ettha ca “etesū”ti iminā adhikaraṇabhāvaṃ dasseti. “Etehī”ti iminā karaṇabhāvaṃ dasseti. Tenāti kāraṇena. Assāti vivādādhikaraṇassa. Etānīti aṭṭhārasabhedakaravatthūni. Sabbatthāti sabbesaṃ adhikaraṇānaṃ sabbesu samuṭṭhānesu.

Explaining by way of analysis that the eighteen bases for causing schism are the origin, he said, 'For that,' etc. 'That' means the legal case of accusation; the connection is with 'arises.' And here, by 'in these,' it shows the locative sense. By 'by these,' it shows the instrumental sense. 'By that' means for that reason. 'Its' refers to the legal case of dispute. 'These' means the eighteen bases for causing schism. 'Everywhere' means in all the origins of all the legal cases.

344. Ekena adhikaraṇena kiccādhikaraṇenāti idaṃ vuttanti sambandho. Etānīti adhikaraṇāni. Ekaṃsatoti ekaṃsena, ekakoṭṭhāsenāti attho. Hīti saccaṃ, yasmā vā.

344. The connection is with what is said: 'by one legal case, by the legal case of proceedings.' 'These' means the legal cases. 'Definitely' means certainly, in one part—this is the meaning. 'Hi' means truly, or because.

Sāvasesāpatti sammati viya anavasesāpatti na sammatīti yojanā. Kasmā na sammatīti āha “na hī”tiādi. Hīti yasmā. Sāti anavasesā āpatti. Tatoti anavasesāpattito. Ettha [M 0.0599] ca “na sakkā desetu”nti iminā desanāgāminiyā abhāvaṃ dīpeti. “Na sakkā…pe… patiṭṭhātu”nti iminā vuṭṭhānagāminiyā abhāvaṃ dīpeti.

The connection is: just as an offense with a remainder is settled, an offense without a remainder is not settled. Why is it not settled? He says, 'For not...,' etc. 'Hi' means because. 'That' is the offense without a remainder. 'From that' means from the offense without a remainder. And here, by 'it is not possible to confess,' it indicates the absence of a procedure leading to confession. By 'it is not possible... to be reinstated,' it indicates the absence of a procedure leading to rehabilitation.

349. Tatoti nayato. Yattha sativinayotiādikā cha yamakapucchāti sambandho. Tāsanti pucchānaṃ. Pakāsitoti pākaṭo.

349. 'From that' means by the method. The connection is with 'where there are the six paired questions beginning with “verdict of mindfulness.”' 'Of those' means of the questions. 'Explained' means apparent.

351. Dvinnampi samathānanti sammukhāvinayasativinayavasena dvinnampi samathānaṃ. Yasmāti yena kāraṇena na sakkāti sambandho. Pattavaṭṭīnaṃ nānākaraṇanti sambandho. Tesanti sammukhāvinayasativinayānaṃ nānākaraṇanti sambandho. Ayaṃ panettha yojanā – yasmā kadalikkhandhe pattavaṭṭīnaṃ nānākaraṇaṃ vinibbhujjitvā dassetuṃ na sakkā viya tesaṃ nānākaraṇaṃ vinibbhujjitvā dassetuṃ na sakkāti. Tenāti kāraṇena. Sabbatthāti sabbesu vissajjanesu.

351. 'Of both settlements' means of both settlements, namely, the verdict in the presence and the verdict of mindfulness. 'Because' means for which reason; the connection is with 'it is not possible.' The connection is with 'the differentiation of the sheaths of a banana stalk.' 'Of those' refers to the differentiation of the verdict in the presence and the verdict of mindfulness; this is the connection. This is the connection here: just as it is not possible to separate and show the differentiation of the sheaths in a banana stalk, so it is not possible to separate and show their differentiation. 'By that' means for that reason. 'Everywhere' means in all the answers.

Sattasamathanidānavaṇṇanā

The Explanation of the Cause of the Seven Settlements

352. Assāti [V 2.0227] sammukhāvinayassa. Tatthāti “nidānanidāno”ti pāṭhe. Idanti sammukhācatukkaṃ. Laddhupavādoti laddho paresaṃ upavādo yenāti laddhupavādo, khīṇāsavo. Yassa cāti yassa ca santiketi sambandho. Ubhinnanti desakapaṭiggāhakānaṃ dvinnaṃ.

352. 'Its' refers to the verdict in the presence. 'There' means in the reading 'the cause of the cause.' 'This' refers to the fourfold presence. 'One who has received reproach' means one by whom the reproach of others has been received; that is, one whose cankers are destroyed. 'And of whom' is connected with 'and in whose presence.' 'Of both' means of the two, the one confessing and the one receiving the confession.

353. Nanu pucchāyaṃ “sattannaṃ samathāna”nti vuttaṃ, kasmā pana vissajjanāyaṃ sammukhāvinayassa samuṭṭhānaṃ na vuttanti āha “kiñcāpī”tiādi. Tattha kiñcāpi vuttanti yojanā. Ettha kiñcāpisaddo sambhāvanattho, panasaddo garahattho. Tathā vuttampīti yojanā. Kammasaṅgahābhāvenāti kamme saṅgahassa abhāvena. Tatthāti tasmiṃ “kammassa kiriyā”tiādipāṭhe. Kammaṃ karīyati imāyāti kiriyā, ñatti. Tena vuttaṃ “kammassa kiriyāti ñatti veditabbā”ti. Kariyate ṭhapiyate karaṇaṃ. Sayaṃ upagamiyate upagamanaṃ. Ajjhesanena paraṃ upagamāpiyate ajjhupagamanaṃ. Adhivāsiyate adhivāsanā. Appaṭikkosiyate apaṭikkosanā. Iti imamatthaṃ dassento āha “karaṇanti tassāyevā”tiādi. Etanti kammaṃ. Meti mayhaṃ. Khamudhātupayoge sampadānatthe [M 0.0600] sampadānavacanaṃ. Atha vā meti mayā. Katvatthe karaṇavacanaṃ, sāmivacanaṃ vā. Khamatīti katturūpasadisaṃ kammarūpaṃ. Rūpañhi katturūpasadisaṃ kammarūpaṃ “khamati saṅghassā”tiādīsu (mahāva. 127) viya. Kammarūpasadisaṃ katturūpaṃ “upāsako sīlaṃ samādiyatī”tiādīsu (paṭṭhā. 1.1.423) viya. Ettha kammatthe pavatto yapaccayo lopoti daṭṭhabbaṃ.

353. Surely in the question it is said, 'of the seven settlements'; why then in the answer is the origin of the verdict in the presence not stated? He says, 'Although...,' etc. Therein, the connection is with 'although it is said.' Here, the word `kiñcāpi` has the sense of possibility, and the word `pana` has the sense of censure. The connection is with 'although it was said thus.' 'Due to the non-inclusion in the act' means due to the absence of inclusion in the act. 'There' means in that passage beginning 'the performance of the act.' 'Performance' (`kiriyā`) is that by which an act is performed; it is a motion (`ñatti`). Therefore it is said, '“the performance of the act” should be known as the motion.' It is done, it is established—that is the doing (`karaṇa`). One approaches by oneself—that is approaching (`upagamana`). Another is caused to approach by request—that is consenting (`ajjhupagamana`). It is accepted—that is acceptance (`adhivāsanā`). It is not objected to—that is non-objection (`apaṭikkosanā`). Thus, showing this meaning, he says, '“the doing” is of that very thing,' etc. 'This' means the act. 'Me' means `mayhaṃ` (to me). In the use of the root `kham`, the dative word is in the sense of the dative. Or, 'me' means `mayā` (by me). The instrumental word is in the sense of the agent, or it is a genitive word. 'Khamati' is a passive form similar to an active form. Indeed, a passive form is similar to an active form, as in 'it is approved by the Sangha,' etc. An active form is similar to a passive form, as in 'a lay follower undertakes the precepts,' etc. Here, it should be understood that the `ya` suffix, which occurs in the sense of the passive, is elided.

Sattasamathanānātthādivaṇṇanā

The Explanation of the Various Meanings, etc., of the Seven Settlements

354. Mātāputtādīnaṃ ayaṃ vivādoti yojanā. “Viruddhavādattā”ti iminā vadanaṃ vādo, viruddho vādo vivādoti nibbacanaṃ dasseti. Adhikaraṇīyatāyāti vūpasamitatāya. Iminā adhikariyati samathehi vūpasamiyatīti adhikaraṇanti vacanatthaṃ dasseti. Sabbatthāti sabbesu adhikaraṇabhedesu.

354. The connection is: 'This is the dispute of mother and son, etc.' By 'because of contradictory speech,' it shows the etymology: speaking is `vāda`, contradictory speech is `vivāda` (dispute). 'Because it is to be settled' means because of being pacified. By this, it shows the meaning of the word `adhikaraṇa` as: it is adjudicated, it is pacified by the settlements. 'Everywhere' means in all the kinds of legal cases.

Iti adhikaraṇabhedavaṇṇanāya yojanā samattā.

Thus, the exposition in the Explanation of the Kinds of Legal Cases is concluded.

Dutiyagāthāsaṅgaṇikaṃ

The Second Verse Section

Codanādipucchāvissajjanāvaṇṇanā

The Explanation of the Questions and Answers beginning with Accusation

359. Dutiyagāthāsaṅgaṇiyaṃ [V 2.0228] codanā nāma kiṃ dassetvā codanāti āha “vatthuñca āpattiñca dassetvā codanā”ti. Dosaṃ sarāpetīti dosasāraṇā. Saṅghasannipātoti saṅghassa sannipatanaṃ. Iminā saṅghoti ettha uttarapadalopaṃ dasseti. Matikammanti ettha matisaddo icchatthoti āha “vuccati mantaggahaṇa”nti. Tanti matikammaṃ.

359. In the Second Verse Section, having shown what is meant by accusation, he says: 'Having shown the matter and the offense, this is accusation.' 'Causing one to remember the fault' is reminding of the fault. 'The assembly of the Sangha' means the gathering of the Sangha. By this, it shows the elision of the latter word here in `saṅgho`. Regarding 'an act of resolution,' here the word `mati` has the sense of desire, so he says, 'it is called taking counsel.' 'That' means the act of resolution.

“Tena cuditakapuggalenā”ti padaṃ “sāraṇatthāyā”ti pade kāritakammaṃ. Tassa puggalassāti tassa cuditakassa puggalassa, iminā “niggahatthāyā”ti padassa kammaṃ dasseti. Tatthāti tasmiṃ adhikaraṇavinicchayaṭṭhāne. Pariggahaṇatthāyāti pari vīmaṃsitvā gahaṇatthāya. Dhammā-dhammanti [M 0.0601] bhūtābhūtaṃ. “Vinicchayasanniṭṭhāpanattha”nti iminā pāḷiyaṃ pāṭhasesaṃ dasseti.

The phrase 'by that accused person' is the causative object of the word 'for the purpose of reminding.' 'Of that person' means of that accused person; by this, it shows the object of the word 'for the purpose of censuring.' 'There' means in that place for judging a legal case. 'For the purpose of grasping' means for the purpose of grasping after having thoroughly investigated. 'Doctrine and non-doctrine' means what is true and what is not true. By 'for the purpose of establishing the judgment,' it indicates the remainder of the text in the Pāli.

Mā kho paṭighanti ettha paṭighasaddo kopapariyāyoti āha “kopaṃ mā janayī”ti. “Cuditake vā codake vā”ti iminā “saṅghe”ti ādhāraṃ paṭikkhipati. Sace anuvijjako tuvanti ettha anuvijjakasaddo vinayadharapariyāyoti āha “vinayadharo”ti. Vinayadharo hi yasmā codakacuditakānaṃ vacanaṃ anuminitvā vatthuāpattādivasena vidati, tasmā anuvijjakoti vuccati.

Do not resent": here, the word paṭigha is a synonym for anger; hence, it says "do not generate anger." By "whether in the accused or the accuser," he rejects "in the Sangha" as the basis. "If you are an investigator": here, the word anuvijjaka is a synonym for one versed in the Vinaya; hence, it says "a Vinaya-holder." For since a Vinaya-holder, having inferred the words of the accuser and the accused in terms of the matter, offense, etc., knows, therefore he is called an investigator.

Viruddhaṃ gāhaṃ saṃvattetīti viggāhikaṃ. “Na tva”ntiādinā ṇikapaccayassa sarūpaṃ dasseti. Yāyāti kathāya. Suttādīnaṃ sarūpaṃ dassento āha “suttaṃ nāmā”tiādi.

Because it promotes a conflicting view, it is contentious (viggāhikaṃ). By 'not you,' etc., it shows the form of the ṇika suffix. Yāya means 'by which speech.' Showing the nature of sutta, etc., it says, 'sutta is so-called,' etc.

Anuyuñjanavattanti anuyuñjanassa, anuyuñjane vā vattaṃ. Kusalena buddhimatāti ettha kusalasaddo chekapariyāyo, buddhimantusaddo paṇḍitapariyāyoti āha “chekena paṇḍitenā”ti. “Ñāṇapāramippattenā”ti iminā buddhimatāti ettha na kevalaṃ ñāṇasāmaññaṃ, atha kho sabbaññutaññāṇanti dasseti. Ayanti eso yathāvutto attho. Ayaṃ panāti eso vakkhamāno pana. Etthāti imāsu gāthāsu. Sace tvaṃ anuvijjako hosīti yojanā. Yaṃ pana anuyogavattaṃ kataṃ supaññattaṃ sabbasikkhāpadānaṃ anulomanti yojanā. Tanti anuyogavattaṃ. Itīti ayaṃ sādhippāyasaṅkhepavaṇṇanā. Attanoti anuvijjakassa. Samparāyeti paraloke. Yoti anuvijjako. Tanti anuyogavattaṃ[V 2.0229]. Gatinti sugatiṃ. Hitanti codakacuditakānaṃ hitaṃ. Gavesantoti ñāṇena esanto. Iminā hitaṃ esantoti hitesīti vacanatthaṃ dasseti. Mettañcāti appanāpattaṃ mettañca. Mettāpubbabhāgañcāti appanāmettāya pubbabhāge pavattaṃ parikammaupacāramettañca. Tava bhāre saṅghena kate evāti yojanā.

Anuyuñjanavatta means "the practice of interrogation," or "the conduct in interrogation." "By a wise and intelligent one": here, the word kusala is a synonym for "skilled," and the word buddhimantu is a synonym for "learned"; hence it says "by a skilled and learned one." By "one who has attained the perfection of knowledge," it indicates that buddhimat here means not merely general knowledge, but indeed omniscient knowledge. Ayaṃ means "this is the meaning as stated." Ayaṃ pana means "this, however, is what is being explained." Ettha means "in these verses." The connection is: "If you are an investigator." The connection is: "That the practice of interrogation is well-established and conforms to all training rules." Tanti anuyogavattaṃ means "that is the practice of interrogation." Iti means "this is a brief explanation with the intended meaning." Attano means "of the investigator." Samparāye means "in the next world." Yo means "the investigator." Tanti anuyogavattaṃ means "that is the practice of interrogation." Gati means "to a good destination." Hitaṃ means "the welfare of the accuser and the accused." Gavesanto means "searching with knowledge." By this, it shows the meaning of the word hitesī as "one who seeks welfare." Mettañca means "and loving-kindness that has attained absorption." Mettāpubbabhāgañca means "and the preliminary and access loving-kindness practiced before absorption-loving-kindness." The connection is: "When the Sangha has placed the burden on you, thus."

Yoti anuvijjako. Etesanti codakacuditakānaṃ. “Bhāsita”nti iminā vohārasaddo bhāsitapariyāyoti dasseti. Tanti sahasā vohāraṃ.

Yo means "the investigator." Etesaṃ means "of the accuser and the accused." By "spoken," it shows that the word vohāra (usage) is synonymous with "spoken." Tanti sahasā vohāraṃ means "that is hasty usage."

Anusandhitanti [M 0.0602] ettha vinicchayānusandhiṃ paṭikkhipanto āha “kathānusandhi vuccatī”ti. Kathāya anurūpaṃ sandahanaṃ kathānusandhi. Paṭiññānusandhitenāti ettha paṭiññāsaddaanusandhisaddānaṃ tulyādhikaraṇato aññaṃ bhinnādhikaraṇaṃ dassento āha “athavā”tiādi. Lajjiṃ puggalanti sambandho. Tatthāti gāthāyaṃ. Vattānusandhināti ācārasaṅkhātena vattena anusandhinā assa alajjīssa vattena saddhiṃ yā paṭiññā sandhiyatīti yojanā.

Anusandhitaṃ: here, rejecting the connection of ascertainment, it is said: "It is called the connection of discussion." The connection of discussion is the appropriate joining according to the discussion. Paṭiññānusandhitena (by the connection of avowal): here, showing that the words paṭiññā (avowal) and anusandhi (connection) have different referents, unlike having the same referent, it is said: "Or else," etc. The connection is: "a person who is ashamed." Tattha means "in the verse." Vattānusandhinā (by the connection of conduct) means: "the connection through conduct, which is behavior; the avowal that is connected with the conduct of that shameless one"—this is the construction.

Jānanto āpajjatīti jānanto hutvā āpajjati. Iminā sañciccāti padassa sañcetetvāti atthaṃ dasseti. Vītikkamacetanāya saddhiṃ cetetvāti attho. “Na deseti na vuṭṭhātī”ti iminā parigūhatīti ettha parigūhanaṃ nāma atthato na desanaṃ na vuṭṭhānanti dasseti.

Jānanto āpajjati means "knowing, he commits an offense." By this, it shows that the meaning of the word sañcicca is "having intended." The meaning is: "having intended together with the intention to transgress." By "he does not declare, he does not rise from it," it is shown that concealing (parigūhanaṃ) here means, in essence, neither declaring nor rising from it.

Yanti “sañcicca āpattiṃ āpajjatī”ti vacanaṃ. Tumhehīti parihārakārakehi. Saccanti tathaṃ avitathaṃ. Ahampīti codakopi. Pisaddena parihārakaṃ sampiṇḍeti. Nanti “sañciccā”tiādivacanaṃ. Tanti tuvaṃ, tvaṃ vā.

Yaṃ refers to the saying "intentionally commits an offense." Tumhehi means "by those undergoing probation." Saccaṃ means "factual, not false." Ahaṃpi means "I too," referring to the accuser. The particle pi also includes the one undergoing probation. Naṃ refers to the saying "intentionally," etc. Taṃ means "you," or "you."

Pubbāparanti ettha pubbe kathetabbaṃ pubbaṃ, aparamhi kathetabbaṃ aparaṃ, pubbañca aparañca pubbāparanti dassento āha “pure”tiādi. “Tasmiṃ pubbāpare”ti iminā pāḷiyaṃ pubbaparassāti ettha bhummatthe sāmivacananti dasseti.

Pubbāparaṃ: here, showing that what should be spoken first is pubbaṃ (first), what should be spoken later is aparaṃ (later), and both first and later are pubbāparaṃ (before and after), it says: "formerly," etc. By "in that before and after," it indicates that in the Pāli, pubbaparassa here is a genitive case in the locative sense (bhummatthe).

Dvīhīti [V 2.0230] pārājikasaṅghādisesavasena dvīhi. Pañcahīti thullaccayādivasena pañcahi. Micchādiṭṭhiyāti “natthi dinna”ntiādinā (dha. sa. 1221) dasavatthukāya micchādiṭṭhiyā. Antaggāhikadiṭṭhiyāti “sassato loko”tiādinā (dī. ni. 1.31; ma. ni. 1.269) dasavatthukāya antaggāhikadiṭṭhiyā. Sabbatthāti sabbesu dutiyagāthāsaṅgaṇikesu.

Dvīhi means "by two," in terms of pārājika and saṅghādisesa. Pañcahi means "by five," in terms of thullaccaya, etc. Micchādiṭṭhiyā (by wrong view) means "by the ten-factored wrong view beginning with 'There is no gift'" (Dhs. 1221). Antaggāhikadiṭṭhiyā (by an extremist view) means "by the ten-factored extremist view beginning with 'The world is eternal'" (DN 1.31; MN 1.269). Sabbattha means "in all the second verse sections."

Iti dutiyagāthāsaṅgaṇikavaṇṇanāya yojanā samattā.

Thus, the construction in the explanation of the second verse section is complete.

Codanākaṇḍaṃ

The Chapter on Censure

Anuvijjakakiccavaṇṇanā

Explanation of the Duties of an Investigator

360-1. Idāni [M 0.0603] āraddhanti sambandho. Eko bhikkhu ekena mātugāmenāti yojanā. Soti passanto bhikkhu. Tanti nikkhamantaṃ pavisantaṃ vā bhikkhuṃ. Itaroti cuditako. Tassāti codakassa. Na upetīti na upagacchati. Na paṭijānātīti na paṭissavaṃ karoti. Etthāti mātugāmena nikkhamantapavisantaṭṭhāne. Yanti kammaṃ. Tenāti codakena. Tassāti codakassa vacanenāti sambandho. Itaroti cuditako. Asuddhaparisaṅkitoti asuddhāya aṭṭhāne uppannāya parisaṅkāya parisaṅkito. Tadatthaṃ dasseti “amūlakaparisaṅkito”ti iminā. Tassa puggalassāti cuditakassa paṭiññāyāti sambandho. Sabbatthāti sabbesu anuvijjakakiccesu.

The connection is 'now begins.' 'One monk with one woman'—this is the construction. 'He' refers to the monk who sees. 'That' refers to the monk entering or leaving. 'The other' means the accused. 'Of that' refers to the accuser. 'Does not approach' means does not go near. 'Does not admit' means does not make an acknowledgement. 'Here' refers to the place of entering or leaving with the woman. 'Which' refers to the action. 'By that' refers to the accuser. 'Of that' is connected with 'by the words of the accuser.' 'The other' means the accused. 'Suspected of impurity' means suspected with a suspicion that is impure, arisen in an improper place. Its meaning is shown by 'suspected without basis.' 'Of that person' is connected with 'by the acknowledgement of the accused.' 'In all cases' means in all the duties of an investigator.

Iti anuvijjakakiccavaṇṇanāya yojanā samattā.

Thus, the construction of the explanation of the duties of an investigator is complete.

Codakapucchāvissajjanā

Questioning and Answering of an Accuser

362-3. Sacce ca akuppe cāti padhānaṃ sambandhaṭṭhānaṃ dassento āha “patiṭṭhātabba”nti. “Ya”ntiādinā sacce patiṭṭhātabbabhāvaṃ dasseti. Yanti kammaṃ. “Na cā”tiādinā akuppe patiṭṭhātabbabhāvaṃ dasseti. Otiṇṇañcāti vinicchayaṃ otiṇṇañca. “Vacana”nti iminā otiṇṇānotiṇṇasarūpaṃ dasseti. Tatrāti purimavacanāpekkhaṃ. “Otiṇṇānotiṇṇaṃ [V 2.0231] jānitabba”nti vacaneti hi attho. Codakassa pamāṇanti “dhammo”ti vā “adhammo”ti vā “bālo”ti vā “paṇḍito”ti vā codakassa pamāṇaṃ. Cuditakassa pamāṇanti dhammacuditako nu kho, noti cuditakassa pamāṇaṃ. Anuvijjakassa pamāṇanti sakkā nu kho vinicchituṃ, noti anuvijjakassa pamāṇaṃ. Anuvijjako vattabboti sambandho. Yena dhammenātiādīsu dhammādīnaṃ sarūpaṃ dassento āha “dhammoti bhūtaṃ vatthū”tiādi. Etena dhammena ca etena vinayena ca etena satthusāsanena cāti yojanā. Tasmā anuvijjakena vūpasametabbanti sambandho. Etthāti anuvijjakassa paṭipajjitabbaṭṭhāne.

Showing the main place of connection, 'in truth and in the unshakable,' he says, 'one should be established.' By 'which,' etc., the state of being established on truth is shown. 'Which' refers to the action. By 'and not,' etc., the state of being established on the unshakable is shown. 'Entered into' means entered into the investigation. By 'statement,' the nature of what is entered into and not entered into is shown. 'There' refers to the previous statement. Indeed, the meaning of the statement is: 'what is entered into and not entered into should be known.' The accuser's measure is whether it is 'Dhamma' or 'non-Dhamma,' 'a fool' or 'a wise one.' The accused's measure is whether he is accused according to the Dhamma or not. The investigator's measure is whether it can be investigated or not. 'The investigator should be spoken to'—this is the connection. In 'by which Dhamma,' etc., showing the nature of Dhamma, etc., he says, 'Dhamma means a true matter,' etc. 'By this Dhamma, by this Vinaya, and by this Teacher's instruction'—this is the construction. Therefore, 'it should be settled by the investigator'—this is the connection. 'Here' refers to the place where the investigator should proceed.

Avaññanti [M 0.0604] avajānanaṃ. Imeti therā. “Khatattā”ti iminā attanāva attā khaññatīti khatoti vacanatthaṃ dasseti. Upahaniyantīti upahatāni, upahatāni indriyāni anenāti upahatindriyo. “Paññāya abhāvato”ti iminā dummedhoti ettha dusaddo abhāvattho, medhāsaddo paññāpariyāyoti dasseti. Natthi medhā etassāti dummedhoti nibbacanaṃ kātabbaṃ. Khato…pe… dummedho so anuvijjako upagacchatīti yojanā. Tasmāti yasmā upagacchati, tasmā vuttanti sambandho. Tassāti pāṭhassa, gāthāya vā. Vitthāraṃ dassento āha “cuditakacodakesu hī”tiādi. Ubhopeteti ubhopi ete āmisapuggalanissaye. Dhammoti sāsanadhammo. Itīti ayamattho.

'Disrespect' means looking down upon. 'These' refers to the elders. By 'because of being broken', the meaning of the word 'broken' is shown to be: the self is broken by itself. 'Being destroyed' means the faculties are destroyed; one whose faculties are destroyed by this is called 'one with destroyed faculties'. By 'due to the absence of wisdom', it is shown that here, in 'foolish' (dummedho), the prefix 'du-' conveys the meaning of absence, and the word 'medhā' is a synonym for wisdom. The derivation should be made as 'one who lacks wisdom', hence 'foolish'. 'Broken... foolish, that investigator approaches'—this is the construction. 'Therefore'—because he approaches, therefore it is said—this is the connection. 'Of that' refers to the text or the verse. Explaining in detail, he says: 'indeed, among the accused and accusers', etc. 'Both these'—both of these are dependent on persons concerned with material gain. 'Dhamma' refers to the Dhamma of the Dispensation. 'Thus'—this is the meaning.

Upakaṇṇakaṃ jappatīti ettha kaṇṇassa samīpaṃ upakaṇṇaṃ, tadeva upakaṇṇakanti dassento āha “evaṃ kathehī”tiādi. “Kaṇṇamūle”ti iminā upakaṇṇakanti ettha upasaddassa samīpatthaṃ dasseti. Mantetīti katheti. Iminā jappadhātuyā kathanatthaṃ dasseti. Jimhaṃ pekkhatīti ettha jimhasaddo kuṭilavācako, kuṭilaṃ nāma atthato idha dosoti āha “dosamevā”ti.

'Whispers in the ear'—here, showing that 'near the ear' is upakaṇṇa, and that upakaṇṇaka is the same, he says, 'speak thus', etc. By 'at the root of the ear', he shows that the prefix 'upa-' in 'upakaṇṇaka' indicates proximity. 'Consults' means speaks. By this, he shows that the root 'japp' means speaking. 'Looks askance'—here, the word 'jimha' means crooked; crookedness here, in meaning, is a fault, as he says: 'only a fault'.

Kathānusandhīti cuditakaanuvijjakānaṃ kathāya anusandhi. Vinicchayānusandhīti anuvijjakena katassa āpattānāpattivinicchayassa anusandhi. Sabbatthāti codanākaṇḍe.

'The connection of the discussion'—this is the connection in the discussion of the accused and investigators. 'The connection of the judgment'—this is the connection in the judgment of offenses and non-offenses made by the investigator. 'Everywhere' means in the chapter on censure.

Iti codanākaṇḍavaṇṇanāya yojanā samattā.

Thus, the construction of the explanation of the chapter on censure is complete.

Cūḷasaṅgāmaṃ

The Lesser Battle

Anuvijjakassa paṭipattivaṇṇanā

The Explanation of the Practice of the Investigator

365. Cūḷasaṅgāme [V 2.0232] samāgamanaṃ saṅgāmo, samāgamenti sannipatanti etthāti vā saṅgāmoti vacanatthaṃ dassento āha “saṅgāmo vuccati…pe… saṅghasannipāto”ti. Sannipatanaṃ sannipāto, sannipatanti [M 0.0605] ettha deseti vā sannipāto, saṅghassa sannipāto saṅghasannipāto. Saṅgāma yuddheti dhātupāṭhesu (saddanītidhātumālāyaṃ 18 makārantadhātu) vuttaṃ. Tattha yuddhaṃ nāma atthato adhikaraṇavinicchayoti gahetabbaṃ. Tadatthaṃ vitthārento āha “tatra hī”tiādi. Tattha tatrāti tasmiṃ saṅgāme, samosarantīti sambandho. Attapaccatthikāti attano paṭipakkhaṃ atthayanti. Uddhammanti dhammato viyogaṃ. Dīpentā hutvāti yojanā. Ke viyāti āha “vajjiputtakā viyā”ti. So bhikkhu pavattetīti sambandho. Laddhinti uddhammādivādaṃ. Tatthāti saṅgāme. Avacaratīti ogāhetvā cāreti pavatteti. Tamevatthaṃ dassento āha “ajjhogāhetvā vinicchayaṃ pavattetī”ti. Ettha “ajjhogāhetvā”ti iminā avatyūpasaggassa ogāhatthaṃ dasseti. “Vinicchayaṃ pavattetī”ti iminā caradhātussa kāritantogadhattā sahakāritakammena pavattanatthaṃ dasseti. Iminā saṅgāme avacaratīti saṅgāmāvacaroti nibbacanaṃ dasseti. Ko viyāti āha “yasatthero viyā”ti. Mānaddhajanti ketukamyatāpaccupaṭṭhānamānasaṅkhātaṃ dhajaṃ. Rajoharaṇasamenāti ettha rajaṃ harati apaneti anenāti rajoharaṇaṃ, pādapuñjanaṃ, tena samenāti dassento āha “pādapuñjanasamenā”ti. Pādaṃ puñjati sodheti anenāti pādapuñjanaṃ, tena samo pādapuñjanasamo, tena. Samākāraṃ dassento āha “yathā”tiādi. Rajoharaṇassa neva rāgo hotīti sambandho. Yathāpatirūpanti patirūpassa anulomaṃ, patirūpānatikkantanti attho. Akathentena nisīditabbanti sambandho. Sāmaṃ vā dhammoti ettha dhammo nāma koti āha “kappiyākappiyanissitā vā”tiādi. Rūpārūpaparicchedo ca samathācāro ca vipassānācāro ca ṭhānavattañca nisajjavattañca, ādisaddena caṅkamavattādīni saṅgaṇhāti. Cuddasamahāvattādīnaṃ “kappiyākappiyanissitā”ti padena gahitattā vattasaddena ṭhānavattādīni eva gahetabbāni, ādisaddena caṅkamavattādīni gahetabbāni. Paro vā ajjhesitabboti yovā so vā koci ajjhesitabboti āha “yo”tiādi. Iminā [M 0.0606] na yo vā so vā koci ajjhesitabbo, samatthoyeva pana ajjhesitabboti vā dasseti. “Āvuso”tiādinā vattabbākāraṃ dasseti. Ariyo [V 2.0233] vā tuṇhībhāvoti ettha na kevalaṃ kathetuṃ asamatthavasena tuṇhībhāvo, kammaṭṭhānamanasikāravasena panāti āha “kammaṭṭhānamanasikāravasena tuṇhībhāvo”ti. Ariyānaṃ eso ariyo, tuṇhībhāvo. “Nāvajānitabbo”ti iminā nātimaññitabboti padassa atikkamma na maññitabboti dasseti.

365. In the Cūḷasaṅgāma, 'coming together' is a saṅgāma; or 'saṅgāma' because they come together, they assemble here—thus explaining the meaning of the word, he says: 'Saṅgāma is called... the assembly of the Sangha'. Gathering is 'sannipāta'; or 'sannipāta' because they gather and teach here. The gathering of the Sangha is 'saṅghasannipāta'. In the Dhātupāṭhas (Saddanītidhātumālā, 18th root ending in 'ma'), it is said: 'Saṅgāma means battle'. There, 'battle' should be understood in meaning as the settling of a legal case. Elaborating on that meaning, he says: 'for there', etc. 'Therein' (tatra tatra) means in that saṅgāma; 'they come together'—this is the connection. 'Attapaccatthika' means they desire the harm of their own opponents. 'Uddhamma' means separation from the Dhamma. 'Having illuminated'—this is the construction. 'Like whom?' It is said: 'Like the Vajjiputtakas'. That monk propagates—this is the connection. 'Laddhi' refers to the view of deviation from Dhamma, etc. 'Tattha' means in the saṅgāma. 'Avacarati' means having plunged into, he moves, he propagates. Showing that very meaning, he says: 'having plunged into, he propagates the investigation'. Here, by 'ajjhogāhetvā', he shows that the prefix 'ava-' has the meaning of plunging into. By 'vinicchayaṃ pavatteti', he shows that because the root 'car' has entered into the causative, it has the meaning of propagating through cooperative action. By this, he shows the derivation of 'saṅgāmāvacara' as 'one who moves in the saṅgāma'. 'Like whom?' It is said: 'Like the Elder Yasa'. 'Mānaddhaja' means a banner consisting of pride, characterized by the arising of the desire for a banner. 'Like a dust-remover'—here, 'rajoharaṇa' means 'that by which dust is removed or swept away', i.e., a foot-wiper; showing that it is similar to that, he says: 'like a foot-wiper'. 'Pādapuñjana' means 'that by which the feet are wiped or cleaned'; 'pādapuñjanasama' means similar to that, by that. Explaining the similarity, he says: 'Just as...'. For a dust-remover, there is no attachment—this is the connection. 'Yathāpatirūpa' means in conformity with what is fitting, not transgressing what is fitting—this is the meaning. 'One should sit without speaking'—this is the connection. 'Or Dhamma by oneself'—here, what is 'Dhamma'? He says: 'or dependent on what is allowable or unallowable', etc. The distinction of form and formlessness, the practice of serenity, the practice of insight, standing observance and sitting observance—and by the word 'etc.', walking observance etc. are included. Since the fourteen great observances, etc., are included by the phrase 'dependent on what is allowable or unallowable', by the word 'observance' only standing observance, etc., should be taken, and by the word 'etc.', walking observance, etc., should be taken. 'Or another should be requested'—he says 'whoever, anyone, should be requested', etc. By this, he shows that not just anyone should be requested, but only one who is competent should be requested. By 'Friend', etc., he shows the manner of speaking. 'Or noble silence'—here, silence is not merely due to inability to speak, but due to attention to the meditation subject, he says: 'silence due to attention to the meditation subject'. This silence is noble for the noble ones. By 'it should not be despised', he shows that the word 'nātimaññitabbo' means 'it should not be thought of with contempt'.

Upajjhāyoti codakacuditakānaṃ upajjhāyo. Sabbatthāti sabbesu “na ācariyo pucchitabbo”tiādipadesu. Kulameva jātināmagottavasena ayanti apadisiyatīti kulapadeso. Atrassāti ettha atra assāti padacchedaṃ katvā atrasaddo puggalavisayo, assasaddo ākhyātikoti āha “atra puggale”tiādi. Tattha “bhaveyyā”ti iminā assasaddassa sabbanāmattañca “bhavatī”ti vattamānikabhāvañca paṭikkhipati. Parisānuvidhāyakenāti parisāya anumataṃ karontena. Iminā no parisakappikenāti ettha kappasaddo vijhatthoti dasseti. Yanti vacanaṃ. Na hatthamuddāti mudanti etāyāti muddā, sakkharamaṅguliyaṃ hatthassa muddā avayaviavayavavasena sambandhattāti hatthamuddā. Tassā vikāro “hatthamuddā”ti gahetabboti āha “hatthavikāro”ti.

'Preceptor' means the preceptor of the accuser and the accused. 'In all cases' means in all passages beginning with 'the teacher should not be questioned', etc. 'Family designation' means that this is designated by way of birth, name, and clan, as 'family itself'. 'Atrassa'—here, having made a word division as 'atra assa', he says that the word 'atra' pertains to a person, and the word 'assa' is a verb, as in 'in this person', etc. There, by 'bhaveyyā', he rejects both the pronominal nature of 'assa' and its present tense nature as 'bhavati'. 'One who complies with the assembly' means one who does what is approved by the assembly. By this, he shows that the word 'kappa' in 'not according to the assembly's liking' means prohibition. 'Which' is a word. 'Not by hand gestures'—'muddā' means that by which one signifies; 'hatthamuddā' means a gesture of the hand, such as snapping fingers, because it is related by way of part and whole. Its modification should be taken as 'hatthamuddā', therefore he says 'a modification of the hand'.

“Atthaṃ anuvidhiyantenā”ti ettha atthanti vinicchayatthaṃ. Anuvidhiyantenāti sallakkhentena. Iti imamatthaṃ dassento āha “vinicchayapaṭivedhameva sallakkhentenā”ti. Sannipātamaṇḍaleti sannipātāya parisāya samūhe, sannipātamaṇḍalassa majjheti attho. Na vītihātabbanti ettha vītiharaṇaṃ nāma atthato hāpananti āha “na vinicchayo hāpetabbo”ti. Duruttavācanti codakacuditakānaṃ duruttavācaṃ. Hitaparisakināti ettha hitaṃ pari esatīti hitaparisako, karuṇā ca karuṇāpubbabhāgo ca, so etassatthīti hitaparisakī, puggalo, tena hitaparisakinā. Tamevatthaṃ dassento āha “hitesinā hitagavesinā”ti[M 0.0607]. Karuṇāti appanāpattā karuṇā. Karuṇāpubbabhāgoti appanāpattāya karuṇāya pubbabhāge pavattā parikammaupacārakaruṇā. Padadvayepīti “hitānukampinā kāruṇikena bhavitabbaṃ. Hitaparisakinā asamphappalāpinā bhavitabba”nti padadvayepi. Ayaṃ adhippāyo veditabboti yojanā. “Asundaravacana”nti iminā asuruttanti ettha sundaraṃ uttaṃ suruttaṃ, na suruttaṃ asuruttanti vacanatthaṃ dasseti. Pariggahetabboti parivīmaṃsitvā gahetabbo.

In 'Atthaṃ anuvidhiyantenā,' 'attha' here means the matter for decision. 'Anuvidhiyantena' means by one who considers. Thus, explaining this meaning, it is said, 'by one who considers only the penetration of the decision.' 'Sannipātamaṇḍale' means in the group of the assembled community; the meaning is in the midst of the assembly circle. In 'Na vītihātabbaṃ,' 'vītiharaṇa' means to cause the matter to be lost; hence it is said, 'the decision should not be abandoned.' 'Duruttavācaṃ' refers to the harsh words of the accuser and the accused. In 'Hitaparisakinā,' a `hitaparisako` is one who seeks welfare. A `hitaparisakī` is a person who possesses compassion and the preliminary part of compassion; by such a one is meant `hitaparisakinā`. Explaining that very meaning, it is said, 'by one who desires welfare, by one who seeks welfare.' 'Karuṇā' is compassion that has reached absorption. 'Karuṇāpubbabhāgo' is the preparatory and access compassion that occurs in the preliminary stage of compassion that has reached absorption. In both phrases—'one should be sympathetic and compassionate' and 'one should be a welfare-seeker, not speaking frivolously'—this is how the connection should be understood. By 'improper speech,' it shows the meaning of the word 'asurutta' here: 'surutta' is what is well-spoken; what is not well-spoken is 'asurutta.' 'Pariggahetabbaṃ' means it should be taken up after having been investigated.

Tassāti adhammacodakassa. Anosaṭaṃ vatthunti ettha “codakacuditakehi vutta”nti padaṃ adhikāravasena veditabbaṃ. Ettha ca anosaṭanti vinicchayaṃ anosaṭanti attho.
