Kiṃ paggaṇhitabboti [V 2.0234] āha “nanu tva”ntiādi. Anuyogavattanti “kālena vakkhāmī”tiādinā (cūḷava. 399; pari. 362, 437) vuttaṃ, “sacce ca akuppe cā”ti (cūḷava. 401) ca vuttaṃ anuyuñjanavattaṃ. Tañhi yasmā anena vattena codako cuditakaṃ, cuditako vā codakaṃ anuyuñjati, codakena cuditako, cuditakena vā codako anuyuñjiyati, tasmā anuyogavattanti vuccati. Kathāpetvāti codakacuditakeheva kathāpetvā. Tassāti codakassa vā cuditakassa vā, sārajjanti bhayaṃ. Teti tava. Vatvāpīti mukhena vatvāpi. Pisaddena kāyavikāraṃ dassetvāpīti sampiṇḍeti. “Anuyogavatta”nti dhātukammaṃ, “so bhikkhū”ti kāritakammaṃ ajjhāharitabbaṃ, taṃ kammaṃ tabbapaccayo vadati. Asuci vibhāvetabboti ettha natthi suci sīlametassāti asucīti vutte alajjīti āha “alajji”nti. Uju sīlavā kāyavaṅkādirahito hotīti yojanā. Ettha ca kāyavaṅkādirahito hotīti iminā ujuno kāraṇaṃ dasseti. Kāyavaṅkādirahitattā uju hotīti adhippāyo. Soti bhikkhu. Maddavenevāti mudubhāveneva. Upacaritabboti kathetabbo. Iminā ujumaddavenāti padassa sambandhaṭṭhānaṃ pāṭhasesaṃ dasseti. Yoti bhikkhu. Ayamevāti evasaddena na dhammagaruko, puggalagaruko, dhammesu ca puggalesu ca na majjhattoti veditabboti dasseti.

‘Tassa’ refers to the unrighteous accuser. In ‘Anosaṭaṃ vatthuṃ,’ the phrase ‘spoken by the accuser and the accused’ should be understood according to the context. And here, ‘anosaṭaṃ’ means not settled; the meaning is that the decision has not been settled. What should be taken up? It is said, ‘Is it not that you…?’ and so forth. ‘Anuyogavattaṃ’ refers to the procedure of questioning spoken of in such passages as ‘I will speak at the proper time’ (Cūḷavagga 399; Parivāra 362, 437) and ‘in truth and in what is unshakeable’ (Cūḷavagga 401). For, since by this procedure the accuser interrogates the accused, or the accused interrogates the accuser—the accused is interrogated by the accuser, or the accuser is interrogated by the accused—it is therefore called ‘the procedure of interrogation.’ ‘Kathāpetvā’ means having made the accuser and the accused themselves speak. ‘Tassa’ refers to either the accuser or the accused. ‘Sārajjaṃ’ means fear. ‘Te’ means yours. ‘Vatvāpi’ means even having spoken with the mouth. By the word ‘pi,’ it includes ‘even having shown a bodily distortion.’ ‘Anuyogavattaṃ’ is the object of the verb root; ‘so bhikkhu’ is the object of the causative verb, which is to be supplied; the `-tabba` suffix expresses that object. In ‘Asuci vibhāvetabbaṃ,’ when ‘asuci’ (impure) is said because ‘for him there is no pure virtue,’ it means ‘shameless’; thus it says ‘shameless.’ The connection is: one who is upright in virtue is free from bodily crookedness and so on. And here, by ‘he is free from bodily crookedness and so on,’ it shows the reason for being upright. The intention is that because he is free from bodily crookedness and so on, he is upright. ‘So’ means the monk. ‘Maddaveneva’ means only with gentleness. ‘Upacaritabbo’ means he should be addressed. By this, it shows the remaining part of the text as the place of connection for the phrase ‘ujumaddavena.’ ‘Yo’ means the monk. By ‘ayameva,’ the word ‘eva’ shows that it should be understood that he is not one who respects the Dhamma but one who respects persons, and is not impartial towards the Dhamma and persons.

366. Tena [M 0.0608] ca pana anuvijjakenāti yojanā. Suttādīsūti ādisaddena vinayaanuloma paññattaanulomikāni saṅgahetabbāni. Suttaṃ saṃsandanatthāya hotīti yojanā. Kesaṃ saṃsandanatthāyāti āha “āpattānāpattīnaṃ saṃsandanattha”nti. Opammaṃ atthadassanatthāya hotīti yojanā. Eseva nayo sesesupi. Paccekaṭṭhāyino avisaṃvādakaṭṭhāyinoti ettha paccekasmiṃ tiṭṭhanti sīlenāti paccekaṭṭhāyino, avisaṃvādake tiṭṭhanti sīlenāti avisaṃvādakaṭṭhāyinoti dassento āha “issa…pe… ṭhitā”ti. “Issariyādhipaccajeṭṭhakaṭṭhāne”ti iminā paccekasarūpaṃ dasseti. Teti saṅghena anumatā puggalā.

366. The connection should be made with the phrase, 'And by that investigator...' In 'Suttas, etc.,' by the word 'etc.,' what is in conformity with the Vinaya and in conformity with what has been laid down should be included. The connection is that the Sutta is for the purpose of comparison. For the comparison of what? It is said, 'For the comparison of offenses and non-offenses.' The connection is that the simile is for the purpose of showing the meaning. This same method applies to the rest as well. Regarding 'Paccekaṭṭhāyino avisaṃvādakaṭṭhāyino': showing that 'those who are established individually by virtue are `paccekaṭṭhāyino`' and 'those who are established in non-contradiction by virtue are `avisaṃvādakaṭṭhāyino`,' it says, 'dominion... and so on... established.' By 'in a position of sovereignty, authority, and seniority,' it shows the nature of individuality. 'Te' refers to the persons authorized by the Saṅgha.

Kimatthaṃ “vinayo saṃvaratthāyā”tiādi vuttanti āha “idānī”tiādi. Idāni dassetuṃ āhāti sambandho. Ye mandā mandabuddhino hutvā evaṃ vadeyyunti yojanā. Atha vā mandā mandabuddhino ye puggalā evaṃ vadeyyunti yojanā. Sakalāpi vinayapaññatti upanissayo hotīti sambandho. Iminā “saṃvaratthāyā”tiādīsu “anupādāparinibbānatthāyā”tipariyosānesu terasavākyesu “upanissayo hotī”ti pāṭhaseso ajjhāharitabboti dasseti. “Paccayo”ti iminā “upanissayo”ti padassa upanissayapaccayoti [V 2.0235] atthaṃ dasseti. Sabbatthāti sabbesu dvādasavākyesu. Visesaṃ dassento āha “apicetthā”tiādi. Tattha apica visesaṃ vakkhāmīti yojanā. Etthāti “avippaṭisāratthāyā”tiādīsu. Tanti sukhaṃ. Taruṇavipassanā nāma kassa adhivacananti āha “udayabbayañāṇassetamadhivacana”nti. Nanu “virāgo”ti ettha catubbidhassa ariyamaggassa gahitattā “vimuttī”ti etthāpi catubbidhaṃ phalaṃ gahetabbaṃ, kasmā pana “vimuttīti arahattaphala”nti vuttanti āha “catubbidhopi hī”tiādi. Hīti saccaṃ, yasmā vā. Apaccayaparinibbānatthāyāti asaṅkhataparinibbānatthāya. Natthettha hi parinibbāne koci paccayo, tasmā apaccayaparinibbānanti vuccati. Tanti vimuttiñāṇadassanaṃ. Tasmiṃanuppatteti tasmiṃ vimuttiñāṇadassane [M 0.0609] anukkamena patte. Avassanti dhuvaṃ ekantenāti attho. Etadatthāti eso anupādā parinibbānasaṅkhāto attho payojanaṃ imissā kathāyāti etadatthā. Kathāti atthassa kathā. Mantanāti dhammassa mantanā. Etadatthā upanisāti ettha upanisāsaddo paccayavācakoti āha “paraṃparapaccayatāpī”ti. Paraṃparapaccayo hi yasmā ettha paraṃparaphalaṃ upagantvā nisīdati, tasmā upanisāti vuccati. “Vinayo saṃvaratthāyā”tiādikā ayaṃ paraṃparapaccayatāpīti yojanā. Sotāvadhānanti ogāhetvā dhiyate ṭhapiyate avadhānaṃ, sotassa avadhānaṃ sotāvadhānaṃ. Imaṃ kathanti “vinayo saṃvaratthāyā”tiādiṃ imaṃ kathaṃ. Yaṃ ñāṇaṃ uppajjati, tampi etadatthanti yojanā. Yadidaṃ anupādā cittassāti ettha “yadida”nti nipāto “vimokkho”ti padamapekkhitvā yo ayanti atthaṃ vadati. Anupādāti ettha “sayaṃ abhiññā”tiādīsu (mahāva. 11) viya yakāralopo hoti, tassa padassa karaṇaṃ pana “catūhi upādānehī”ti veditabbaṃ. Iti ima matthaṃ dassento āha “yo ayaṃ catūhi upādānehi anupādiyitvā”ti. Ettha catūhi upādānehi anupādiyitvā cittassa arahattaphalasaṅkhāto yo ayaṃ vimokkho atthi, sopi etadatthāya hotīti yojanā. “Arahattaphalasaṅkhāto”ti iminā “vimokkho”ti padassa atthaṃ dasseti. Arahattaphalañhi yasmā viruddhehi, visesena vā sabbakilesehi muccittha, tasmā vimokkhoti vuccati. “Apaccayaparinibbānatthāya evā”ti iminā etadatthāyāti padassa atthaṃ dasseti.

Why is it said, “The discipline is for the sake of restraint,” and so forth? He says, “Now,” and so on. The connection is: Now, to show, it is said. The application is: Those who are dull and of weak understanding might speak thus. Or, the application is: Those individuals who are dull and of weak understanding might speak thus. The connection is: The entire disciplinary code is a supporting condition. By this, it shows that in the thirteen statements beginning with “for the sake of restraint” and ending with “for the sake of final nibbāna without clinging,” the remaining part of the text, “it is a supporting condition,” should be supplied. By “condition,” it shows the meaning of the word “supporting condition” as a supporting-condition cause. “In all” means in all twelve statements. Showing the distinction, he says, “Moreover here,” and so on. The application is: There, moreover, I will speak of the distinction. “Here” means in the statements beginning with “for the sake of non-remorse.” That is happiness. The term “young insight”—whose designation is it? He says, “It is the designation for the knowledge of rise and fall.” Now, if in “dispassion,” because the fourfold noble path is included, and in “liberation,” the fourfold fruit should also be included, why then is it said, “Liberation is the fruit of arahantship”? He says, “Though fourfold,” and so on. “Hī” means truly, or because. “For the sake of final nibbāna without a cause” means for the sake of unconditioned final nibbāna. For here, in final nibbāna, there is no cause; therefore it is called “final nibbāna without a cause.” That is the knowledge and vision of liberation. “Attained in that” means gradually attained in that knowledge and vision of liberation. “Certainly” means definitely, absolutely—this is the meaning. “For this purpose” means this purpose, designated as final nibbāna without clinging, is the aim of this discussion—thus, “for this purpose.” “Kathā” means the discussion of the meaning. “Mantanā” means the deliberation on the Dhamma. In “For this purpose is the proximate cause,” the word “proximate cause” is a term for condition—he says, “also as a successive condition.” For here, because the successive fruit approaches and settles, therefore it is called a “proximate cause.” The application is: “The discipline is for the sake of restraint,” and so forth—this is also a successive condition. “Sotāvadhānaṃ” means attention is fixed, established, having entered; the attention of the ear is “listening attentively.” “This discussion” means this discussion beginning with “the discipline is for the sake of restraint.” The application is: The knowledge that arises—that too is for this purpose. In “Yadidaṃ anupādā cittassa,” the particle “yadidaṃ” refers to the word “vimokkho,” meaning “which is this.” In “Anupādā,” as in “by oneself directly knowing,” and so forth (Mahāvagga 11), the letter ‘ya’ is elided, but the function of that word should be understood as “by not clinging to the four kinds of clinging.” Thus, showing this meaning, he says, “which is this, not clinging to the four kinds of clinging.” Here, the application is: The liberation of the mind designated as the fruit of arahantship, which is this, by not clinging to the four kinds of clinging, is also for this purpose. By “designated as the fruit of arahantship,” it shows the meaning of the word “liberation.” For the fruit of arahantship, because it is freed from its opposing states, or especially from all defilements, therefore it is called “liberation.” By 'for the sake of final nibbāna without a cause alone,' it shows the meaning of the phrase 'for this purpose.'

367. Vatthuṃ…pe… na jānātīti etthāti yojanā kātabbā. Tasmāti yasmā sambandho, tasmā. Etthāti imāsu gāthāsu. Samena cāti ettha “samenā”ti padaṃ “aññāṇenā”ti atthassa vācakaṃ rūḷhīpadanti dassento āha “teneva pubbāparaṃ ajānanassa samena aññāṇenā”ti. Pāḷiyaṃ kena kāraṇena katākataṃ na jānātīti āha “samenā”ti. Samena pubbāparassa aññāṇena katākataṃ na [M 0.0610] jānātīti attho. Evantiādi nigamanaṃ[V 2.0236]. Yaṃ panetaṃ vacanaṃ vuttanti yojanā. “Tatthā”ti ca “ākāraakovido”ti ca ādhārādheyyānamabhedo hoti, tasmā avayavī ādhāro, avayavo ādheyyoti daṭṭhabbaṃ. Ākārasaddo iṅgitatthoti āha “kāraṇākāraṇe”ti. Kāraṇaakāraṇasaṅkhāte iṅgiteti attho. Ākārassāti bhummatthe sāmivacanaṃ. Ākārasminti hi attho.

367. The interpretation should be made here, in 'he does not know the subject matter...'. Regarding 'tasmā' (therefore): the connection is with 'yasmā' (because), hence 'tasmā'. 'Here' means 'in these verses.' Here, regarding 'and with evenness,' showing that the word 'with evenness' is a conventional term expressing the meaning of 'with ignorance,' he says: 'Therefore, due to not knowing the sequence of prior and subsequent, with evenness, with ignorance.' In the Pāli, to the question, 'For what reason does he not know what has been done and what has not been done?,' the answer is given: 'with evenness.' The meaning is: 'He does not know what has been done and what has not been done due to evenness, through ignorance of the sequence of prior and subsequent.' 'Thus,' etc., is the conclusion. The interpretation is: 'As for this statement that was said...' Regarding 'there' and 'unskilled in modes,' there is no distinction between the container and the contained. Therefore, it should be understood that the whole is the container and the part is the contained. He says that the word 'mode' has the meaning of 'indication,' as in 'cause and non-cause.' The meaning is 'an indication designated as cause and non-cause.' 'Of the mode' is the genitive case in the sense of the locative. Indeed, the meaning is 'in the mode.'

Tathevāti yathā vatthuādīni na jānāti, tatheva. Itīti evaṃ. Yvāyanti yo ayaṃ bhikkhu. “Bhayenā”ti iminā bhayāti ettha kāraṇatthe nissakkavacananti dasseti. Bhayā bhayena gacchatīti yojanā. Eseva nayo sammohena mohā gacchatīti etthāpi. Chandāti chandena. Dosāti dosena. Attanā ñātuṃ asamatthatāya na saññattiyā kusaloti āha “paraṃ saññāpetuṃ asamatthatāyā”ti. Kasmā nijjhattiyā ca akovidoti āha “kāraṇā…pe… tāyā”ti. “Parisāya laddhattā”ti iminā laddho parisasaṅkhāto pakkho yenāti laddhapakkhoti vacanatthaṃ dasseti. Sace tādisako bhikkhu hoti, so bhikkhu “apaṭikkho”ti vuccatīti yojanā. Eseva nayo heṭṭhāpi. “Na paṭikkhitabbo”ti iminā paṭimukhaṃ na ikkhitabboti apaṭikkhoti vacanatthaṃ dasseti. “Na oloketabbo”ti iminā ikkhadhātuyā dassanatthaṃ dasseti.

'Just so' means just as he does not know the facts of the case, etc., just so. 'Thus' means in this way. 'Whoever' means 'this monk.' By 'because of fear,' he shows that 'from fear' here is the ablative case in the sense of cause. The interpretation is 'he goes because of fear.' The same method applies here too, in 'he goes by delusion, from delusion.' 'By desire' means by desire. 'By hatred' means by hatred. Because he is incapable of knowing for himself, he is not skilled in communication; he says: 'due to being incapable of communicating to others.' Why is he unskilled in reasoning? He says: 'due to reasons... etc.' By 'because of being obtained by the assembly,' he shows the meaning of the word 'one who has obtained a faction,' which is 'one by whom a faction reckoned as the assembly has been obtained.' If such a monk exists, that monk is called 'uncontested'—this is the interpretation. The same method applies below too. By 'not to be contested,' he shows the meaning of the word 'uncontested,' which is 'not to be looked at face to face.' By 'not to be looked at,' he shows that the root 'ikkh' has the meaning of 'to see.'

Iti cūḷasaṅgāmavaṇṇanāya yojanā samattā.

Thus the explanation in the commentary on the Minor Conflict is concluded.

Mahāsaṅgāmaṃ

The Great Conflict

Voharantena jānitabbādivaṇṇanā

The Explanation of What Is to Be Known, and so forth, by One Engaged in Legal Discourse

368-74. Mahāsaṅgāme eteneva nayena veditabbanti sambandho. Vatthusaṅkamanākāraṃ dassetvā avajānanapaṭijānanākāraṃ dassento āha [M 0.0611] “yo panā”tiādi. Yo pana vadatīti sambandho. Esevāti eso eva, avajānanapaṭijānanabhikkhūti attho.

368-74. In the Great Conflict, the connection is that it should be understood in this same manner. Having shown the mode of introducing the subject matter, he shows the mode of disavowal and admission by saying: 'Now whoever,' etc. The connection is 'now whoever speaks.' 'Just this' means 'this very one,' that is, the monk who disavows or admits.

375. Nīlādivaṇṇāvaṇṇavasenāti nīlādivaṇṇavasena ca ārogyatthādiavaṇṇavasena ca. Sañcarittaṃ [V 2.0237] yasmā anena sikkhāpadena dhanaṃ anupadīyati, tasmā dhanamanuppadānanti vuccati. Pubbapayogoti pubbe payujjitabbo.

375. 'By means of praise and dispraise, such as color' means both by means of colors such as blue, etc., and by means of dispraise concerning matters such as health. Regarding sañcaritta: since wealth is not given by this training rule, it is called 'non-giving of wealth.' 'Prior application' means 'it should be applied beforehand'.

Agatiagantabbavaṇṇanā

The Explanation of Wrong Courses Not to Be Taken

379. Bahujanaahitāya paṭipanno hotīti pāḷiṃ vitthārento āha “vinayadharena hī”tiādi. Tattha vinayadharenāti anuvijjakena, vinicchiteti sambandho. Ovādūpajīviniyoti bhikkhūnaṃ ovādaṃ upanissāya jīviniyo. Upāsakāpīti ratanattayaṃ paṭissaraṇanti upāsakāpi. Dāyakāpīti bhikkhūnaṃ paccayadāyakāpi. Tesanti upāsakādīnaṃ. Tathevāti yathā upāsakādayo dvidhā bhijjanti, tatheva. Tatoti ārakkhadevatāhi paranti sambandho. Tenāti dvidhākāraṇena.

379. Expanding on the Pāli passage 'he is acting for the harm of many people,' he says: 'Indeed, by the Vinaya-holder,' etc. Herein, 'by the Vinaya-holder' means 'by the investigator,' and the connection is with 'should be judged.' 'Living by advice' means those who live relying on the advice of the monks. 'Also lay devotees' means lay devotees who take refuge in the Triple Gem. 'Also donors' means donors of requisites to monks. 'Of them' means of the lay devotees, etc. 'Just so' means just as the lay devotees, etc., are divided into two, just so. 'Thence' is connected with 'beyond the guardian deities.' 'By that' means 'by the twofold reason.'

382. Gahananissitoti ettha gahanasaddo diṭṭhipariyāyoti āha “micchādiṭṭhiantaggāhikadiṭṭhisaṅkhātaṃ gahana”nti.

382. 'Dependent on a thicket'—here, he says the word 'thicket' is a synonym for view, that is, 'the thicket reckoned as wrong view, as the view that grasps at extremes'.

393. Tassa avajānantoti ettha “tassā”ti padaṃ “vacana”nti pāṭhasesena sambandhitabbanti āha “tassa vacana”nti. Tassāti navakassa. Tanti navakaṃ.

393. 'Disregarding him'—here, he says that the word 'his' should be connected with 'words' as a textual remainder, thus 'his words.' 'His' means 'of the novice.' 'Him' means 'the novice'.

394. “Yaṃatthāyā”ti eso saddo samāsoti āha “yadatthāyā”ti. “Taṃ attha”nti eso saddo liṅgavipallāsoti āha “so attho”ti. Atthasaddo hi pulliṅgo, pāḷiyaṃ na parihāpetabbanti etthāpi liṅgavipallāso veditabbo. Sabbatthāti sabbasmiṃ mahāsaṅgāme.

394. He says that the word 'for what purpose' is a compound, thus 'for what purpose.' He says that the word 'that meaning' is a gender inversion, thus 'that meaning.' Indeed, the word 'meaning' is masculine, and in the Pali, 'it should not be abandoned'—here too, a gender inversion should be understood. 'Everywhere' means 'in every great battle'.

Iti mahāsaṅgāmavaṇṇanāya yojanā samattā.

Thus ends the interpretation of the commentary on the Great Battle.

Kathinabhedaṃ

The Dissolution of the Kathina

Kathinaatthatādivaṇṇanā

Explanation of the Spreading of the Kathina, etc.

403. Kathine [M 0.0612][V 2.0238] khandhaketi kathinakkhandhake. Pubbeti kathinakkhandhake.

403. 'In the Kathina section' means in the Kathina Khandhaka. 'Previously' means in the Kathina Khandhaka.

404. Payogassāti ettha payogo nāma koti āha “cīvaradhovanādino”tiādi. Ettha ādisaddena vicāraṇachedanabaddhanasibbanarajanakappabinduādiyanāni cha pubbakaraṇāni saṅgaṇhāti. Udakāharaṇādiko yo payogo karīyatīti yojanā. Anantaro nāma atītānantaraanāgatānantaravasena duvidho, idha anāgatānantaroyeva adhippetoti āha “anāgatavasenā”ti. Udakāharaṇādipayoge hi uppanne pacchā dhovanādipubbakaraṇassa uppattito tappayogassa anāgatavaseneva paccayo. Samanantarapaccayenāti ettha saṃsaddo suṭṭhuatthoti āha “suṭṭhu anantarapaccayenā”ti. “Āsannatara”nti iminā suṭṭhubhāvaṃ dasseti. “Payogassā”ti padaṃ “ādhārabhāva”nti pade sāmī, “paccayā hontī”ti pade sampadānaṃ. “Nissaya”nti padaṃ “ādhārabhāva”nti padena saṃvaṇṇeti. “Upetenā”ti iminā upasaddassa upagamanatthaṃ dasseti, balavatthaṃ paṭikkhipati. Paṭhamanti payogato, payogassa vā tāva. Iminā purejātapaccayenāti ettha puresaddo paṭhamatthoti dasseti. Pacchāti payogato, payogassa vā paraṃ. Apubbaṃ acarimanti ekapahārena. Iminā sahajātasaddassa atthaṃ dasseti.

404. 'Of the application'—here, he asks what is meant by 'application,' and says: 'such as the washing of robes,' etc. Here, by the word 'etc.,' he includes the six preliminary actions: examining, cutting, binding, sewing, dyeing, and applying the marking-dot. The interpretation is that 'whatever application, such as fetching water, etc., is made.' 'Immediate' is twofold: by way of past immediate and future immediate. Here, only future immediate is intended, so he says: 'by way of the future.' Indeed, when an application such as fetching water arises, it is a condition for the arising of the subsequent preliminary actions such as washing, etc., only by way of the future for that application. 'By the immediately contiguous condition'—here, he says that the prefix 'sam' has the meaning of 'thoroughly,' thus 'by a thoroughly immediate condition.' By 'more proximate,' he shows the thoroughness. The word 'of the application' is the genitive case in relation to the word 'state of being a support,' and the dative case in relation to the word 'they become conditions.' He explains the word 'dependence' by the word 'state of being a support.' By 'by approaching,' he shows the meaning of the prefix 'upa' as 'approaching,' and rejects the meaning of 'strength.' 'First' means from the application, or indeed, of the application. By this, he shows that the word 'pure' in 'by the pre-nascence condition' has the meaning of 'first.' 'After' means from the application, or after the application. 'Neither prior nor subsequent' means 'at a single stroke.' By this, he shows the meaning of the word 'simultaneously arisen'.

Evaṃ pucchitvāti sambandho. Yanti dhammajātaṃ. Idāni āhāti sambandho. Yassāti payogādikassa. Tadevāti dhammajātameva. Tassāti “pubbakaraṇaṃ payogassā”tiādivacanassa attho evaṃ veditabboti yojanā. “Payogassa katame dhammā”tiādi yaṃ vacanaṃ vuttaṃ, tattha vissajjanaṃ mayā vuccateti yojanā. Iminā pāḷiyaṃ ajjhāharitvā yojetabbabhāvaṃ dasseti. Catūhi paccayehi paccayākāraṃ vitthārento āha “payogassa hī”tiādi. Payogassa pubbakaraṇaṃ paccayo hotīti sambandho. Uddiṭṭhadhammesūti “anantarapaccayena [M 0.0613] paccayo”tiādinā uddiṭṭhesu dhammesu purejātapaccayo panesāti sambandho. Atha vā uddiṭṭhadhammesūti pubbakaraṇavasena uddiṭṭhesu dhovanādidhammesu ekadhammampīti sambandho. Na labhatīti udakāharaṇādipayogassa pubbe na labhati. Ayanti udakāharaṇādipayogo. Pacchājātapaccayaṃ pana labhatīti udakāharaṇādipayogo [V 2.0239] pacchājātapaccayaṃ labhati. Kasmā labhatīti āha “pacchā uppajjanakassa hī”tiādi. Pacchāti payogassa, payogato vā paraṃ. Hi yasmā kayirati, tasmā labhatīti yojanā. Sahajātapaccayaṃ pana na labhatīti sambandho. Mātikāpalibodhānisaṃsasaṅkhāteti aṭṭhamātikādvepalibodhapañcānisaṃsasaṅkhāte. Aññoti pannarasahi dhammehi añño. Payogādīsūtiādisaddena pubbakaraṇapaccuddhāraadhiṭṭhānāni saṅgaṇhāti. Etenupāyenāti etena yathāvuttaupāyena.

The connection is 'having asked thus.' 'Which' refers to the collection of phenomena. The connection is 'now he speaks.' 'Of which' refers to the application, etc. 'That very thing' means 'the collection of phenomena itself.' The interpretation is that the meaning of the statement 'the preliminary action is for the application,' etc., should be understood thus. The interpretation is that 'the answer to the statement "What phenomena are for the application?" etc., will be stated by me.' By this, he shows that it should be interpreted by supplying words in the Pali. Elaborating on the mode of conditionality by means of four conditions, he says: 'Indeed, for the application,' etc. The connection is that 'the preliminary action is a condition for the application.' 'Among the phenomena specified'—the connection is that 'among the phenomena specified by "a condition by immediately contiguous condition," etc., the pre-nascence condition, however...?' Or, 'among the phenomena specified'—the connection is that 'among the phenomena specified in terms of preliminary action, such as washing, etc., even a single phenomenon...?' 'Does not obtain' means 'the application of fetching water, etc., does not obtain beforehand.' 'This' refers to the application of fetching water, etc. 'But it obtains the post-nascence condition' means 'the application of fetching water, etc., obtains the post-nascence condition.' Why does it obtain? He says: 'Indeed, because for that which arises afterwards,' etc. 'Afterwards' means 'of the application,' or 'after the application.' The interpretation is: 'Indeed, because it is done, therefore it obtains.' The connection is: 'However, it does not obtain the co-nascence condition.' 'Reckoned as the benefits and obstructions of the matrices' refers to what is reckoned as the eight matrices, the two obstructions, and the five benefits. 'Other' means 'other than these fifteen phenomena.' By the word 'etc.' in 'in the application, etc.,' he includes preliminary action, rejection, and determination. 'By this method' means 'by this method as stated'.

Pubbakaraṇanidānādivibhāgavaṇṇanā

Explanation of the Division of Preliminary Actions, Introduction, and so forth

406-7. Dvikkhattuṃ pucchitattā “pucchādvaya”nti vuttaṃ. Hetupaccayānaṃ sarūpaṃ dassento āha “cha cīvarānī”ti. Kasmā veditabbānīti āha “pubbapayogādīnañhī”tiādi. Hīti yasmā. Tāniyevāti cha cīvarāni eva. Evasaddo pacchāpi yojetabbo, tāni evāti attho. Hīti saccaṃ, pubbakaraṇādīni na atthīti yojanā.

406-7. Because it was asked twice, it is called 'the double question.' Showing the nature of the causal conditions, he said, 'six robes.' Why should they be known? He said, 'because of prior use, etc.' 'Hi' means 'because.' 'Those very things' means 'just those six robes.' The word 'eva' should also be connected afterward, meaning 'just those things.' 'Hi' means 'truly'; the explanation is that preliminary acts, etc., do not exist.

408. “Imāya saṅghāṭiyā”tiādinā vacībhedākāraṃ dasseti. Kathinatthārakena yasmā paccuddhāro ca adhiṭṭhānañca karīyati, tasmā kiriyāti vuccati. Tena vuttaṃ “paccuddhāro ceva adhiṭṭhānañcā”ti.

408. By 'with this outer robe,' and so on, he shows the manner of verbal expression. Since relinquishment and determination are done by the one who spreads the Kathina, it is called an action. Therefore, it is said, 'both relinquishment and determination.'

411. Vatthuvipannādīnaṃ sarūpaṃ dassento āha “akappiyadussaṃ hotī”tiādi. Vināsaṃ, vikāraṃ vā pajjatīti vipannaṃ, vatthumeva vipannaṃ vatthuvipannaṃ.

411. To show the nature of spoiled material, etc., he says, 'It becomes unsuitable cloth,' etc. 'Spoiled' means what undergoes destruction or change; 'material-spoiled' means the material itself is spoiled.

Kathinādijānitabbavibhāgavaṇṇanā

Explanation of the Classification of What Should Be Known Regarding the Kathina and so forth

412. Tesaññeva dhammānanti ettha dhammānaṃ sarūpaṃ dassento āha “yesu rūpādidhammesū”ti. Tattha rūpādidhammesūti vaṇṇagandhādīsu suddhaṭṭhakarūpakalāpadhammesu. [M 0.0614] Satīti santesu. Tesanti rūpādīnaṃ dhammānaṃ. “Samodhāna”nti iminā saṅgahoti padassa atthaṃ dasseti. “Missībhāvo”ti iminā samavāyoti padassa atthaṃ dasseti. Avayavadhammānaṃ saṃ ekabhāvassa gahaṇaṃ saṅgaho. Avayavadhammānaṃ samaṃ ayanaṃ pavattanaṃ samavāyo. Bahūsu dhammesūti bahūsu paramatthapaññattidhammesu. Nāmamattanti nāmapaññattimattaṃ. Pubbeti kathinakkhandhake.

412. 'Of those very dhammas'—here, showing the nature of the dhammas, he says: 'in which rūpa and other dhammas.' Herein, 'in rūpa and other dhammas' means in color, smell, etc., in the phenomena of the pure octad of material kalāpas. 'Existing' means being present. 'Those' refers to the dhammas of rūpa, etc. By 'combination,' he shows the meaning of the word 'collection.' By 'mixing,' he shows the meaning of the word 'integration.' The grasping of the oneness of component dhammas is collection. The equal occurrence of component dhammas is integration. 'In many dhammas' means in many ultimate reality and conceptual dhammas. 'Mere name' means a mere name designation. 'Formerly' means in the Kathina Khandhaka.

“Kāraṇehī”ti [V 2.0240] iminā ākārasaddo kāraṇatthoti dasseti. Yanti vacanaṃ.

By 'by means of causes,' he shows that the word 'ākāra' means 'reason.' 'Yaṃ' is the word.

416. Uppajjantīti kathinuddhārā uppajjanti. Kinti kiṃ atthajātaṃ. Sabbepi kathinuddhārāti sambandho. Hīti saccaṃ, yasmā vā. Etthāti kathinuddhāresu. Purimā dveti antarubbhārasahubbhāravasena purimā dve. Etesañcāti purimānaṃ dvinnañca. Itareti avasesā kathinuddhārā. Tesupīti itaresu kathinuddhāresu. Sabbatthāti sabbasmiṃ kathinavinicchaye.

416. 'Arising'—the withdrawals of the Kathina arise. 'Kiṃ' means 'what kind of meaning?' 'All withdrawals of the Kathina'—this is the connection. 'Hi' means 'truly,' or 'because.' 'Here' means in these withdrawals of the Kathina. 'The first two' means the first two in terms of withdrawal during the interval and withdrawal together with. 'And of these' means and of these first two. 'The others' means the remaining withdrawals of the Kathina. 'Even in these' means even in these other withdrawals of the Kathina. 'In all cases' means in every decision regarding the Kathina.

Iti samantapāsādikāya vinayasaṃvaṇṇanāya

Thus in the Samantapāsādikā, the Commentary on the Vinaya,

Paññattivaggavaṇṇanāya

of the Explanation of the Paññatti Chapter,

Yojanā samattā.

the Interpretation is complete.

Upālipañcakaṃ

The Upāli Pentad

Anissitavaggavaṇṇanā

Explanation of the Independent Chapter

417. Upālipañhesu “kati hi nu kho bhante”ti pucchāya sambandho natthīti kassaci maññanaṃ nivārento āha “aya sambandho”ti. Theroti upālitthero, pucchīti sambandho. Imesanti pañcakānaṃ tantinti sambandho. Kesaṃ atthāya tantiṃ ṭhapessāmīti āha “nissāya vasanakārīnaṃ atthāyā”ti. Vasanakārīnaṃ bhikkhūnanti sambandho. Tesanti pañhānaṃ.

417. In the Upāli Pentad, preventing anyone from thinking there is no connection in the question 'how many indeed, venerable sir?', he says, 'this is the connection.' 'The Elder' means the Elder Upāli; 'asked' is the connection. 'Of these' is the connection to 'of the five texts.' To the question, 'For whose benefit shall I establish the text?', he says, 'for the benefit of those who make their dwelling dependent.' 'Of those who make their dwelling' is connected to 'of the monks.' 'Of those' refers to 'of the questions.'

Āpanno [M 0.0615] kammakatoti ettha “āpanno”ti padaṃ “kammakato”ti padassa kāraṇadassananti āha “āpattiṃ āpanno, tappaccayāva saṅghena kammaṃ kataṃ hotī”ti. Tappaccayāvāti taṃāpattiāpannasaṅkhātā kāraṇā eva.

Regarding 'āpanno kammakatoti,' he says that the word 'āpanno' shows the reason for the word 'kammakato': 'He has incurred an offense, and precisely because of that, a formal act has been performed by the Sangha.' 'Tappaccayāva' (precisely because of that) means precisely because of that reason designated as having incurred an offense.

Nappaṭippassambhanavaggavaṇṇanā

Exposition of the Nappaṭippassambhana Chapter.

420. Ayanti [V 2.0241] kammakato bhikkhu, na vattatīti sambandho. Anulomavatteti katakammassa anulome vatte. Assāti bhikkhussa. Sarajjukoti saha kammasaṅkhātāya rajjuyāti sarajjuko.

420. 'Ayaṃ' means the monk upon whom a formal act has been performed; the connection is with 'na vattati.' 'Anulomavatte' means in conduct that is in accordance with the formal act performed. 'Assa' means 'of the monk.' 'Sarajjuko' means 'together with the cord designated as the formal act'; hence, 'sarajjuko'.

421. Samaggehi bhikkhūhīti sambandho. Hīti saccaṃ. Accayaṃ desāpetvāti aññamaññaṃ dosaṃ desāpetvā. Tiṇavatthārakasamathaṃ vāti vāsaddo atthantaravikappo. Tatra ceti ettha tasaddo kammavisayo, cesaddo sacepariyāyoti āha “sace tādise kamme”ti. Diṭṭhāvikammampi katvāti diṭṭhāvikammaṃ katvāpīti yojanā. Pisaddena akatvāpīti sampiṇḍeti. Yatra panāti kamme pana. Tatthāti kamme. Pakkamitabbanti saṅgāmāvacarena pakkamitabbaṃ.

421. The connection is with 'samaggehi bhikkhūhi' (by harmonious monks). 'Hi' means 'truly.' 'Accayaṃ desāpetvā' means having caused the fault to be confessed to one another. In 'tiṇavatthārakasamathaṃ vā,' the word 'vā' indicates an alternative meaning. Here, in 'tatra ca,' the word 'ta' refers to the formal act, and the word 'ca' is a synonym for 'if,' as in 'if in such a formal act.' The construction of 'diṭṭhāvikammampi katvā' is 'diṭṭhāvikammaṃ katvāpi' (even having performed the formal act of making things clear). By the word 'pi,' it also includes 'even without having done it.' 'Yatra pana' means 'but in which formal act.' 'Tattha' means 'in that formal act.' 'Pakkamitabbaṃ' means one should depart as one departs from a battlefield.

422. Ussitamantīti ettha ussitaṃ mantī ussitamantīti dassento āha “lobha…pe… bhāsitā”ti. Tattha “lobhadosa mohamānussannaṃ vāca”nti iminā ussitapadassa atthaṃ dasseti. “Bhāsitā”ti iminā “mantī”ti padassa atthaṃ dasseti. Nissitajappīti ettha aññanissitaṃ jappametassāti nissitajappīti dassento āha “attano”tiādi. Ettha jappanti vacanaṃ. Jappa vacaneti hi dhātupāṭhesu vuttaṃ. Ussadayuttanti lobhādiussadayuttaṃ, vacananti sambandho. Evamaññanti evaṃ attanā aññaṃ. Kathānusandhivacaneti codakacuditakānaṃ kathāya anusandhivacane. Ettha “vacane”ti iminā “bhāsānusandhī”ti ettha bhāsasaddo vacanapariyāyoti dasseti.

422. Regarding 'ussitamantī,' showing that it means 'ussitaṃ mantī' (arrogant speech), he says, 'greed... etc. ...spoken.' There, by 'speech abounding in greed, hatred, delusion, and conceit,' he shows the meaning of the word 'ussita.' By 'spoken,' he shows the meaning of the word 'mantī.' Regarding 'nissitajappī,' showing that it means 'one whose speech depends on another,' he says, 'one's own,' etc. Here, 'jappa' means speech, for in the Dhātupāṭha it is said that the root 'jappa' is in the sense of speaking. 'Ussadayuttaṃ' means connected with the arising of greed, etc.; the connection is with 'speech.' 'Evamaññaṃ' means 'thus another by oneself.' 'Kathānusandhivacane' means in the connecting speech of the conversation between the accuser and the accused. Here, by 'vacane,' he shows that in 'bhāsānusandhī,' the word 'bhāsa' is a synonym for speech.

Ussāretīti uddhaṃ gamāpeti. Iminā ussādeti upari gamāpetīti ussādetāti vacanatthaṃ dasseti. Ettha hi dakārarakārā sadisatthā[M 0.0616]. Te hi dve akkharā kadāci katthaci sadisatthā honti. Avasāretīti hīnabhāvaṃ gamāpeti. Iminā avasādeti adhobhāvaṃ gamāpetīti avasādetāti vacanatthaṃ dasseti. “Apasādetā”tipi pāṭho, upasaggamattameva nānaṃ. Samphañca bahuṃ bhāsatīti ettha samphasaddo niratthakakathāvacanoti āha “niratthakakatha”nti. Niratthakakathā hi yasmā saṃ hitasukhaṃ phalati vināseti, tasmā samphanti vuccati. Phā dhātūti ca phaladhātūti ca dhātupāṭhesu (saddanītidhātumālāyaṃ 16 lakārantadhātu) vuttaṃ.

'Ussāreti' means to cause to go upwards. By this, he shows the meaning of the word 'ussādeti' as 'to make go upward.' Here, indeed, the letters 'da' and 'ra' have similar meanings, for these two letters sometimes have the same meaning in some places. 'Avasāreti' means to cause to go to a lower state. By this, he shows the meaning of the word 'avasādeti' as 'to make go downwards.' 'Apasādetā' is also a reading; only the prefix is different. With regard to 'samphañca bahuṃ bhāsati,' the word 'sampha' means 'pointless talk,' thus he says, 'niratthakakatha.' For because pointless talk destroys the fruit that is welfare and happiness, it is called 'sampha.' The root 'phā' and the root 'phala' are mentioned in the Dhātupāṭha (Saddanītidhātumālā, 16th lakārantadhātu).

Bhāre anāropiteti “tava bhāro”ti saṅghena bhāre anāropite. Ajjhottharitvāti abhibhavitvā[V 2.0242]. Iminā pasayha pavattāti ettha pasayhasaddassa abhibhavanatthaṃ dasseti. Anadhikāreti anadhipaccaṭṭhāne. “Kathetā”ti iminā vatudhātuyā kathanatthaṃ dasseti. Anokāsakammaṃ kāretvāti ettha nakārassa ayuttayogabhāvato yuttaṭṭhānaṃ dassento āha “okāsakammaṃ akāretvā”ti. Yassāti yā assa. Assa bhikkhuno attano yā diṭṭhi atthīti yojanā, athavā attano yā diṭṭhi bhaveyyāti yojanā. Tanti diṭṭhiṃ. “Kathetā”ti iminā byākatāti ettha vi ā pubbakaradhātuyā kathanatthaṃ dasseti.

'Bhāre anāropite' means when the burden has not been placed by the Sangha with the words, 'This is your burden.' 'Ajjhottharitvā' means having overpowered. By this, he shows that in 'pasayha pavatta,' the word 'pasayha' has the meaning of 'overpowering.' 'Anadhikāre' means in a place without authority. By 'kathetā,' he shows the meaning of speaking for the root 'vad.' Regarding 'anokāsakammaṃ kāretvā,' here, because the particle 'na' is in an unsuitable position, showing the suitable position, he says 'okāsakammaṃ akāretvā' (having not caused a permission act to be done). 'Yassa' means 'yā assa' (which is his). The construction is: 'whatever view that monk himself has'; or the construction is: 'whatever view he himself might have.' 'Taṃ' means 'that view.' By 'kathetā,' he shows that in 'byākatā,' the root 'kar' preceded by 'vi' and 'ā' has the meaning of speaking.

Vohāravaggavaṇṇanā

Exposition of the Chapter on Judicial Procedure.

424. “Neva desanāya na vuṭṭhānenā”ti idaṃ pārājikāpattiṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ. Dosānurūpanti vatthusaṅkhātassa dosassa anurūpaṃ.

424. 'Neither by confession nor by rehabilitation'—this was said with reference to a pārājika offense. 'Corresponding to the offense' means corresponding to the offense designated as the basis.

Payogaṃ na jānātīti ettha sace payogo mūlena visadiso hutvā bhinno hoti, evaṃ sati mūlapayoganti na vattabbanti āha “adhikaraṇānaṃ hī”tiādi. Hīti saccaṃ, yasmā vā. Mūlameva payogā nāma honti, na aññanti adhippāyo.

Regarding 'does not know the application,' here, if the application, being dissimilar to the root, becomes distinct, in that case it should not be called 'the root application'; thus he says, 'adhikaraṇānaṃ hi' (for of disputes), and so forth. 'Hi' means 'truly' or 'because.' The intention is that only the roots are called applications, not anything else.

Kātabbanti na jānātīti kātabbaṃ iti kammassa karaṇaṃ na jānātīti yojanā. Vatthūti bhaṇḍanakalahādivatthu, niyassādīnaṃ vatthūti sambandho[M 0.0617]. Catunnanti tajjanīyaniyassapabbājanīyapaṭisāraṇīyavasena catunnaṃ. Yācatīti saṅghaṃ kammassa vūpasamaṃ yācati.

'Does not know what should be done'—the construction is that he does not know the performance of the formal act that should be done. 'The basis' refers to the basis for quarrels, disputes, and so forth; the connection is to the basis for `niyassa` and so forth. 'Of the four' refers to the four kinds: `tajjanīya` (censure), `niyassa` (subordination), `pabbājanīya` (banishment), and `paṭisāraṇīya` (reconciliation). 'Requests' means he requests the Sangha for the cessation of the formal act.

Vatthunti ettha āpattikkhandhānameva vatthunti āha “sattannaṃ āpattikkhandhāna”nti. Padesapaññattisabbatthapaññattisādhāraṇapaññattiasādhāraṇapaññattiekatopañña- ttiubhatopaññattivasena channaṃ paññattīnaṃ paññattiyaṃ paviṭṭhattā vuttaṃ “tividhaṃ paññatti”nti. “Heṭṭhupariyaṃ katvā padaṃ yojetī”ti iminā padapaccābhaṭṭhanti ettha padānaṃ heṭṭhupariyavasena paṭinivattitvā ābhassanaṃ gaḷanaṃ cutaṃ padapaccābhaṭṭhanti atthaṃ dasseti.

'The basis'—here, he says that the basis is 'of the seven aggregates of offenses.' Because the six kinds of designation—namely, partial designation (`padesapaññatti`), universal designation (`sabbatthapaññatti`), common designation (`sādhāraṇapaññatti`), uncommon designation (`asādhāraṇapaññatti`), one-sided designation (`ekatopaññatti`), and two-sided designation (`ubhatopaññatti`)—are included in 'designation,' it is said, 'threefold designation.' By the phrase 'having inverted the words, he joins the word,' he shows the meaning of `padapaccābhaṭṭha` here as the falling away, dropping, or deviation of words that have been turned back by way of inversion.

Vinayeti ettha na kevalaṃ pāḷiyaṃyeva, atha kho aṭṭhakathāyampīti āha “vinayapāḷiyañceva aṭṭhakathāyañcā”ti.

Regarding 'Vinaya,' here he says that it refers not only to the Pāli but also to the commentary: 'both in the Vinaya Pāli and in the commentary.'

Ñattiṃ [V 2.0243] na jānātīti ettha ñattibhedaṃ dassento āha “saṅkhepato”tiādi. Tatthāti duvidhāsu ñattīsu. Kammañattīti anussāvanakammassa ṭhāne ṭhitā ñatti. Anussāvanakammaṃ natthi, sayameva anussāvanakammaṭṭhāne ṭhitāti attho. Kammapādañattīti anussāvanakammassa pādabhūtā mūlabhūtā ñatti. Navasu ṭhānesūti osāraṇādīsu navasu ṭhānesū. Dvīsu ṭhānesūti ñattidutiyañatticatutthavasena dvīsu ṭhānesu, kammapādañattiyā karaṇaṃ na jānātīti sambandho. Yvāyaṃ catubbidho samathoti yojanā. Tanti catubbidhaṃ samathaṃ. Ñattiyāti sāmyatthe sāmivacanaṃ. Yaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ vūpasamatīti sambandho. Tassāti adhikaraṇassa. Taṃ vūpasamaṃ na jānātīti sambandho.

'Does not know the motion'—here, explaining the types of motions, he says, 'In brief,' and so forth. 'Here' refers to the two kinds of motions. 'Motion as the formal act' is a motion that stands in place of the formal act of proclamation. The meaning is that there is no formal act of proclamation; it stands by itself in place of the formal act of proclamation. 'Motion as a basis for the formal act' is a motion that is the basis or root of the formal act of proclamation. 'In nine instances' refers to the nine instances beginning with reinstatement (`osāraṇa`), and so forth. 'In two instances' refers to the two instances, namely, a motion with one proclamation (`ñattidutiya`) and a motion with three proclamations (`ñatticatuttha`); the connection is that he does not know how to perform the motion as a basis for the formal act. 'This fourfold settlement'—this is the construction. 'That' refers to the fourfold settlement. 'By the motion' (`ñattiyā`)—the genitive case has the sense of association. The connection is: 'which settles the dispute.' 'Of that' refers to the dispute. The connection is: 'he does not know that settlement.'

Suttaṃ na jānātīti ettha suttasaddassa kadāci katthaci mātikāyañca suttantapiṭake ca pavattanato idha ubhatovibhaṅgeti āha “ubhatovibhaṅga”nti. Vinayaṃ na jānātīti ettha vinayasaddassa sakale vinayapiṭake vattamānassāpi suttanti ettha ubhatovibhaṅgassa gahitattā idha khandhakaparivārāva gahetabbāti āha “khandhakaparivāraṃ na jānātī”ti.

Regarding 'does not know the Sutta,' here, because the word 'sutta' sometimes refers to the Mātikā and sometimes to the Suttanta Piṭaka, in this context it means the two Vibhaṅgas; thus he says, 'the two Vibhaṅgas.' Regarding 'does not know the Vinaya,' here, although the word 'vinaya' applies to the entire Vinaya Piṭaka, since 'the two Vibhaṅgas' has been taken for 'sutta,' here only the Khandhaka and Parivāra are to be taken; thus he says, 'he does not know the Khandhaka and Parivāra.'

Vinayaṃ na jānātīti ettha vinayapiṭakassa gahetabbattā vuttaṃ “ṭhapetvā vinayapiṭaka”nti. Suttantike cattāro mahāpadeseti (dī. ni. 2.187 ādayo; a. ni. 4.180) buddhāpadesasaṅghāpadesasambahulattherāpadesaekattherā [M 0.0618] padesavasena cattāro mahāpadese. Etthāti pañcake. Yanti vacanaṃ. Sabbatthāti sabbesu pañcakesu.

"Does not know the Vinaya"—here, since the Vinaya Piṭaka is to be taken, it is said: "Excepting the Vinaya Piṭaka." In the Suttanta, the four great authorities (Dī. Ni. 2.187 ff.; A. Ni. 4.180) are the authority of the Buddha, the authority of the Saṅgha, the authority of many elders, and the authority of a single elder. "Here" refers to the group of five. "Goes" is the word. "Everywhere" refers to all the groups of five.

Iti

Thus,

Anissitavagga-nappaṭippassambhanavagga-vohāravaggavaṇṇanāya

Of the Commentary on the Anissita Chapter, the Nappaṭippassambhana Chapter, and the Vohāra Chapter,

Yojanā samattā.

The explanation is concluded.

Diṭṭhāvikammavaggavaṇṇanā

Commentary on the Chapter on Manifestation of Views

425. Diṭṭhāvikammavagge diṭṭhāvikammāti ettha āvi karīyate āvikammaṃ, diṭṭhīnaṃ āvikammaṃ diṭṭhāvikammanti dassento āha “diṭṭhīnaṃ āvikammānī”ti. “Laddhipakāsanāna”nti iminā diṭṭhisaddo laddhipariyāyo, āvikammasaddo pakāsanapariyāyoti dasseti. Etanti “diṭṭhāvikammā”ti nāmaṃ. Adesanāgāminī nāma atthato garukanti āha “garukāpattiyā”ti. Lahukāyapīti pisaddo garahattho. Lahukāyapi desitāya diṭṭhāvikammaṃ adhammikaṃ hoti, pageva garukāyāti attho.

425. In the Chapter on Manifestation of Views, concerning `diṭṭhāvikamma`—here, showing that 'what is made manifest is `āvikamma`,' and 'the manifestation of views is `diṭṭhāvikamma`,' he says: "The manifestations of views." By the phrase "of the declarations of doctrines," he shows that the word `diṭṭhi` is a synonym for `laddhi` (doctrine), and the word `āvikamma` is a synonym for `pakāsana` (declaration). This is the name `diṭṭhāvikamma`. The name `adesanāgāminī` is, in meaning, weighty; thus, he says: "for a weighty offense." "Even a light one"—the particle `pi` has the sense of reproach. The meaning is that even if a light `diṭṭhāvikamma` is declared, it is unlawful, how much more so a weighty one.

Yathā [V 2.0244] …pe… hotīti yathā āvikate catūhi pañcahi ekībhūtehi āvikatā hotīti yojanā. Catūhi pañcahīti antimaparicchedadassanaṃ. Tato atirekehipi ekato desetuṃ na vaṭṭati, desitā ca āpatti na vuṭṭhāti, desanāpaccayā dukkaṭañca hoti. “Catūhi pañcahī”ti antimaparicchedassa dassitattā dvīhi tīhi pana ekato desetuṃ vaṭṭatīti daṭṭhabbaṃ. Manomānasenāti ettha manosaddena mānasasaddassa rāgaarahattesupi pavattanato tadatthe paṭikkhipitvā citte eva vattatīti dasseti. Tena vuttaṃ “manasaṅkhātena mānasenā”ti. Iminā manabhūtaṃ mānasaṃ manomānasanti vacanatthaṃ dasseti.

As... and so forth... it is: The explanation is that as it is declared by four or five united, it is declared. "By four or five" shows the final limit. Beyond that, it is not permissible to declare together, and an offense thus declared is not cleared, and there is also a `dukkaṭa` offense due to the declaration. Since the phrase "by four or five" indicates the final limit, it should be understood that it is permissible to declare together by two or three. "By mind-mental"—here, because the word `manas`, in relation to the word `mānasa`, also occurs in the sense of `rāga` (lust) and `arahatta` (arahantship), he rejects those meanings and shows that it refers only to `citta` (thought). Therefore, it is said, "by the mental reckoned as mind." By this, he shows the meaning of the expression `manomānasa` as `mānasa` that has become `mana`.

Samānasaṃvāsakassāpīti pisaddo samānasaṃvāsakassapi nānāsīmāya ṭhitassa santike āvikammaṃ adhammikaṃ hoti, pageva nānāsaṃvāsakassāti dasseti. Māḷakasīmāyāti khaṇḍasīmāya aṅgaṇe. Avippavāsasīmāyāti [M 0.0619] mahāsīmāya, ṭhitassāpi santiketi sambandho. Pisaddena “khaṇḍasīmāya ṭhitassapī”ti atthaṃ sampiṇḍeti.

"Even for one living in communion"—the particle `pi` shows that even for one living in communion, if a declaration is made in the presence of one standing in a different boundary, it is unlawful, how much more so for one not living in communion. "Within the `māḷaka` boundary" refers to the courtyard of a partial boundary. "Within the non-separation boundary" refers to the great boundary; the connection is "even in the presence of one standing." By the particle `pi`, the meaning "even for one standing within a partial boundary" is condensed.

430. Na pariyattanti na samatthaṃ. Iminā nālanti ettha alaṃsaddo pariyattatthova, nārahabhūsanavāraṇatthoti dasseti. Idhāpīti pañcakepi. Pisaddena purimapañcakaṃ apekkhati. “Sāsanato”ti iminā cudhātuyā apādānaṃ dasseti. “Kāmo”ti iminā adhippāyasaddo kāmapariyāyoti dasseti.

430. "They do not suffice" means they are not capable. By this, he shows that in `nālaṃ`, the word `alaṃ` has only the meaning of sufficiency, not of suitability, adornment, or prevention. "Here too" refers to the group of five. The particle `pi` refers to the previous group of five. By "from the Teaching," he shows the ablative case in relation to the root `cu`. By "desire," he shows that the word `adhippāya` (intention) is a synonym for `kāma` (desire).

432. Mandattā momūhattāti ettha ttapaccayassa bhāvatthe, pañcamīvibhattiyā ca kāraṇatthe pavattabhāvaṃ dassento āha “mandabhāvena momūhabhāvenā”ti. Paribhavāti ettha paribhavakāmāti atthaṃ dassento āha “paribhavaṃ āropetukāmo hutvā”ti. Aññabyākaraṇesupīti arahattabyākaraṇesupi. Sabbatthāti diṭṭhāvikammavagge. Yanti vacanaṃ.

432. "Due to foolishness and delusion"—here, showing that the suffix `tta` has the sense of state and the ablative case (`pañcamīvibhatti`) has the sense of cause, he says: "due to the state of foolishness and the state of delusion." "To despise"—here, showing the meaning is `paribhavakāma` (desiring to despise), he says: "having the desire to inflict contempt." "Even in other declarations" refers to declarations of arahantship. "Everywhere" refers to the Chapter on Manifestation of Views. "Goes" is the word.

Iti diṭṭhāvikammavaggavaṇṇanāya yojanā samattā.

Thus, the explanation of the Commentary on the Chapter on Manifestation of Views is concluded.

Musāvādavaggavaṇṇanā

Commentary on the Chapter on False Speech

444. Dhammapadhānaṃ dhammādhiṭṭhānaṃ sandhāya “pārājikaṃ gacchatīti pārājikagāmī”ti suddhakattuvasena vuttaṃ, puggalapadhānaṃ puggalādhiṭṭhānaṃ sandhāya “pārājikaṃ gacchati anena, gamāpetīti vā pārājikagāmī”ti karaṇahetukattuvasenapi vattabbaṃ. Vitthāraṃ dassanto āha “tatthā”tiādi[V 2.0245]. Tattha tatthāti “musāvādo pārājikagāmī”tiādipāṭhe, evaṃ vitthāro veditabboti sambandho. Tesu “musāvādo pārājikagāmī”tiādīsu vā, niddhāraṇe bhummaṃ.

444. With reference to the primacy of the Dhamma and the foundation of the Dhamma, it is stated in terms of the simple agent: 'He goes to defeat, therefore he is a defeat-goer.' With reference to the primacy of the person and the foundation of the person, it should also be stated in terms of the instrument, cause, and agent: 'By this he goes to defeat, or he causes another to go to defeat, therefore he is a defeat-goer.' Showing the detailed explanation, he said, 'There,' etc. 'There, there' refers to the text beginning with 'False speech is a defeat-goer'; the connection is that the detailed explanation should be understood in this way. Or, in these, such as 'False speech is a defeat-goer,' it is a locative of specification.

Adassanenāti ettha kassa adassanenāti āha “vinayadharassā”ti. Vitthāraṃ dassento āha “kappiyākappiyesu hī”tiādi. Tanti vinayadharaṃ. Assavanenāti ettha kesaṃ vacanaṃ assavanenāti āha “ekavihārepī”tiādi. Ekavihārepīti vinayadharena ekavihārepi. Pisaddena nānāvihāre pana pagevāti dasseti. Upaṭṭhānanti [M 0.0620] upaṭṭhānatthaṃ, upaṭṭhānaṭṭhānaṃ vā. Vuccamānaṃ aññesaṃ vacanaṃ asuṇanto hutvā vāti yojanā. Pasuttakatāti ettha yakāralopoti āha “pasuttakatāyā”ti. Pasuttakabhāvenapīti pisaddo aññampi adassanādikāraṇaṃ sampiṇḍeti. Tathāsaññīti ettha tathāsaddo kovisayoti āha “akappiye…pe… āpajjanto”ti. Ekarattātikkamādivasenāti ādisaddena chārattātikkamādiṃ saṅgaṇhāti. Sabbatthāti musāvādavagge.

Regarding 'by not seeing,' here, whose not seeing? He says, 'of the Vinaya-holder.' Explaining in detail, he says, 'in allowable and unallowable matters,' etc. That refers to the Vinaya-holder. Regarding 'by not hearing,' here, whose words are not heard? He says, 'even in a single monastery,' etc. 'Even in a single monastery' means even in a single monastery with the Vinaya-holder. The particle 'pi' indicates that it is even more so in various other monasteries. 'Attendance' means for the purpose of attendance, or the place of attendance. The construction is: or being one who does not hear the words being spoken by others. Regarding 'being addicted' (`pasuttakatā`), here he says that there is elision of the letter 'ya' in `pasuttakatāya`. The particle 'pi' in 'pasuttakabhāvenapi' (also by being addicted) includes other reasons like not seeing, etc. Regarding 'thus perceiving,' here, what is the scope of the word 'thus'? He says, 'in what is unallowable... committing an offense,' etc. By 'exceeding a single night, etc.,' the word 'etc.' includes exceeding six nights, etc. "Everywhere" refers to the chapter on false speech.

Iti musāvādavaggavaṇṇanāya yojanā samattā.

Thus, the explanation of the Commentary on the Chapter on False Speech is concluded.

Bhikkhunovādavaggavaṇṇanā

Commentary on the Chapter on Advice to Bhikkhunīs

450. Bhikkhunivagge alābhāyāti ettha labhadhātuyā kammaṃ, sampadānavacanassa ca tadatthaṃ dassento āha “catunnaṃ paccayānaṃ alābhatthāyā”ti. “Vāyamatī”ti iminā parisakkatīti ettha sakkadhātuyā samatthatthaṃ paṭikkhipitvā vāyamatthaṃ dasseti. Kalisāsananti pāpaparājayaāṇaṃ. Nīharaṇatthāyāti niddharitvā apanayanatthāya.

450. In the Bhikkhunī-vagga, regarding 'alābhāya' (for the sake of not gaining), here, showing the object of the root `labh` and that this is the meaning of the dative case, he says: 'for the sake of not gaining the four requisites.' By 'vāyamati' (strives), he rejects the meaning of capability from the root 'sakk' (to be able) in 'parisakkati' (exerts), and shows the meaning of exertion. 'Kalisāsana' means the command for the defeat of evil. 'For the sake of removing' means for the purpose of removing and eliminating.

451. “Kamma”nti sāmaññato vuttattā “sattannaṃ kammānaṃ aññatara”nti.

451. Because 'kamma' is stated in a general sense, it means 'one of the seven kinds of kamma.'

454. Na [V 2.0246] sākacchātabboti ettha ko nāma kathāmaggo na sākacchātabbo, nanu vinayoyevāti āha “kappiyā…pe… kathāmaggo”ti. “Na kathetabbo”ti iminā kacchasaddassa kathadhātuyā nipphannabhāvaṃ dīpeti. Kasmā pana paṭhamapañcake “na asekkhenā”ti paṭikkhipitvā dutiyapañcake “asekkhenā”tiādi vuttanti āha “yasmā panā”tiādi. Itaro puthujjano na kathetīti yojanā.

454. Regarding 'not to be discussed,' here, what path of talk is it that should not be discussed? Is it not precisely the Vinaya? Thus he says, 'permissible... path of talk.' By 'na kathetabbo' (not to be spoken), he indicates that the word `kaccha` is derived from the root `kath`. But why, having rejected 'not by a non-learner' in the first group of five, is 'by a non-learner,' etc., stated in the second group of five? He says, 'Because,' etc. The connection is that the other, the ordinary person, does not speak.

Na atthapaṭisambhidāpattoti ettha attho nāma aṭṭhakathāyevādhippetāti āha “aṭṭhakathāyā”ti. “Pabhedagatañāṇappatto”ti iminā atthādīsu pati visuṃ sambhijjatīti paṭisambhidā, paññā, taṃ pattoti paṭisambhidāpatto[M 0.0621]. Atthe paṭisambhidāpatto atthapaṭisambhidāpattoti dasseti. “Pāḷidhamme”ti iminā dhammapaṭisambhidāpattoti ettha dhammasarūpaṃ dasseti. Vohāraniruttiyanti paññattiniruttiyaṃ. Iminā niruttipaṭisambhidāpattoti ettha niruttisarūpaṃ dasseti. Paṭibhānapaṭisambhidāpattoti ettha paṭibhānaṃ nāma heṭṭhimañāṇattayamevāti āha “atthapaṭisambhidādīni ñāṇānī”ti, tesūti ñāṇesu, yaṃ yaṃ vimuttaṃ yathāvimuttaṃ, cittaṃ. Paccavekkhitāti punappunaṃ olokitā. Sabbatthāti bhikkhunivagge.

Regarding 'not having attained the analytical knowledge of meaning,' here, 'meaning' (attha) is intended to be the commentary itself, as he says, 'in the commentary.' By 'one who has attained the knowledge of distinctions,' he shows that 'paṭisambhidā' (analytical knowledge) is wisdom (paññā) because it discerns separately in meaning and other aspects; one who has attained that is 'paṭisambhidāpatto' (one who has attained analytical knowledge). He shows that 'atthapaṭisambhidāpatto' means 'one who has attained analytical knowledge of meaning.' By 'in the Pāḷi Dhamma,' he shows the nature of phenomena (dhammasarūpa) here, in 'dhammapaṭisambhidāpatto' (one who has attained analytical knowledge of phenomena). 'In conventional terminology' means in the language of designations. By this, he shows the nature of language (niruttisarūpa) here, in 'niruttipaṭisambhidāpatto' (one who has attained analytical knowledge of language). Regarding 'paṭibhānapaṭisambhidāpatto' (one who has attained analytical knowledge of ready wit), here, 'ready wit' (paṭibhāna) is precisely the three preceding knowledges, as he says, 'the knowledges of analytical knowledge of meaning, etc.' 'Among these' (tesu) means among these knowledges; whatever mind is liberated, as it is liberated, is reflected upon (paccavekkhitā), meaning repeatedly observed. 'In all respects' means in the Bhikkhunī-vagga.

Iti bhikkhunovādavaggavaṇṇanāya yojanā samattā.

Thus ends the explanation of the Commentary on the Chapter on Advice to Bhikkhunīs.

Ubbāhikavaggavaṇṇanā

The Commentary on the Chapter on Suspension.

455. Ubbāhikavagge atthakusalotiādipadānaṃ bhedanissitasamāsaṃ dassento āha “aṭṭhakathākusalo”tiādi. Ācariyamukhatoti ācariyavadanato, ācariyasammukhe vā, sithiladhanitādīti ādisaddena dīgharassādīni (pari. aṭṭha. 485; vi. saṅga. aṭṭha. 252) saṅgaṇhāti. Akkharaparicchedeti ettako sithilo, ettako dhanitotiādinā akkharaparicchede. Iminā byañjanakusaloti ettha byañjanasaddo akkharapariyāyoti dasseti. Na pubbāparakusaloti ettha pubbāparo nāma purimānaṃ catunnañceva kathāya ca pubbāparoti āha “atthapubbāpare”tiādi.

455. In the Ubbāhikavagga, showing the compound based on the division of words like 'atthakusala,' etc., he says, 'skilled in the commentary,' etc. 'From the teacher's mouth' means from the teacher's utterance, or in the teacher's presence. By the word 'etc.' in 'sithiladhanitādi' (unaspirated, aspirated, etc.), he includes long and short vowels, etc. (as in the Parivāra Aṭṭhakathā 485; Vinaya Saṅgaha Aṭṭhakathā 252). 'In the division of syllables' means in the division of syllables, determining 'this much is unaspirated, this much is aspirated,' etc. By this, he shows that in 'skilled in letters,' the word 'byañjana' is a synonym for 'akkhara' (syllable/letter). Regarding 'not skilled in sequence,' here, 'sequence' (pubbāpara) refers to the sequence of the first four and the discourse, and he says, 'the sequence of meaning,' etc.

Kodhanotiādīni vuttānīti sambandho. Yasmā na sakkotīti yojanā. Pasāretāti ettha saradhātu upasaggavasena vecittavācakoti āha “mohetā”ti.

The connection is that 'angry,' etc., were stated. The explanation is: 'because one is not able.' Regarding 'pasāreti,' here he says that the root 'sar' with a prefix conveys a distinctive meaning, hence 'mohetā' (deluder).

Iti ubbāhikavaggavaṇṇanāya yojanā samattā.

Thus ends the explanation of the Commentary on the Chapter on Suspension.

Adhikaraṇavūpasamavaggavaṇṇanā

Commentary on the Chapter on the Settlement of Disputes

457. Adhikaraṇavūpasamavagge saṅghagaru nāma koti āha “dhammañca…pe… saṅghagaru nāma hotī”ti. Tānīti cīvarādīni.

457. In the Chapter on the Settlement of Disputes, he says what is called 'saṅghagaru': 'Respect for the Dhamma...and so forth...is called "saṅghagaru."' 'These' refer to robes and so forth.

458. Pañcahupāli [V 2.0247][M 0.0622] ākārehīti ettha ākārasaddo kāraṇatthoti āha “pañcahi kāraṇehī”ti. Kammenātiādīsu kammādīnaṃ sarūpaṃ dassento āha “apalokanādīsū”tiādi. Upapattīhīti yuttīhi. Mayhaṃ uccākulā pabbajitabhāvañca bahussutabhāvañca tumhe jānāthāti yojanā. Mādiso nāma…pe… tumhākaṃ yuttaṃ nanūti yojanā. Kaṇṇamūleti kaṇṇasamīpe. Anussāvanenāti anusamīpe sāvāpanena. Tesanti bhikkhūnaṃ. Anivattidhammeti anivattanasabhāve. Salākaggāhenāti attano salākāya gāhāpanena.

458. Regarding 'in five ways, Upāli' (pañcahupāli ākārehi), here the word 'ākāra' means 'reason'; thus he says, 'by five reasons.' In 'by action' and so forth (kammenātiādīsu), showing the nature of actions and the like, he says, 'by announcement and so forth.' 'By reasons' (upapattīhi) means 'by appropriate justifications.' 'You know that I have gone forth from a high family and that I am learned'—this is the connection. 'One like me...is it not fitting for you?'—this is the connection. 'At the root of the ear' (kaṇṇamūle) means 'near the ear.' 'By announcing' (anussāvanena) means 'by having it announced nearby.' 'To them' (tesaṃ) means 'to the bhikkhus.' 'Of an irreversible Dhamma' (anivattidhamme) means 'having the characteristic of not turning back.' 'By taking the voting slip' (salākaggāhena) means 'by having one's own voting slip taken.'

Etthāti kammādīsu. Pamāṇanti saṅghabhedassa kāraṇaṃ. Pubbabhāgāti saṅghabhedato pubbabhāge pavattā. Pubbabhāgabhāvaṃ āvikaronto āha “aṭṭhārasavatthudīpanavasena hī”tiādi. Voharantepīti yojanā. Tatthāti vohāre. Kadā pana saṅgho bhinnoti āha “yadā panā”tiādi. Yadā pana karotīti sambandho. Kammanti uposathakammato aññaṃ kammaṃ gahetabbaṃ. Uddesanti uposathakammaṃ. Itīti evaṃ. Saṅghabhedakakkhandhakavaṇṇanāyaṃ “evaṃ…pe… pakāsayissāmā”ti (cūḷava. aṭṭha. 351) yaṃ vacanaṃ avocumhāti yojanā. Tassa vacanassāti pāṭhaṃ ajjhāharitvā “svāyaṃ attho”ti padena sambandhitabbo.

'Here' (ettha) means 'in actions and so forth.' 'The measure' (pamāṇa) is the cause of schism in the Saṅgha. 'The preliminary stage' (pubbabhāga) refers to what occurs as a preliminary to the schism. Revealing the nature of the preliminary stage, he says, 'indeed, by way of elucidating the eighteen grounds and so forth.' 'Even when speaking' (voharantepi)—this is the connection. 'There' (tattha) means 'in that speaking.' But when is the Saṅgha split? He says, 'But when...and so forth.' 'But when it does' (yadā pana karoti)—this is the connection. 'Action' (kamma) should be taken to mean an action other than the Uposatha action. 'Recitation' (uddesa) refers to the Uposatha action. 'Thus' (iti) means 'in this way.' In the commentary on the Saṅghabhedaka Khandhaka, the connection is, 'which statement we made: "Thus...we will explain..." (Cūḷavagga, Aṭṭha. 351).' Having supplied the reading 'regarding that statement' (tassa vacanassa), it should be connected with the phrase 'this is the meaning.'

Paññattetanti ettha niggahitalopasandhīti āha “paññattaṃ eta”nti. Kvāti kismiṃ khandhake. Tatrāti vattakkhandhake. Ettāvatāti ettakena āgantukavattādiakaraṇamattena. Anupubbenāti anukkamena. Yathārattanti ettha yathāsaddo anurūpatthavācako, rattisaddena rattippamāṇaṃ gahetabbanti dassento āha “rattiparimāṇānurūpa”nti. Iminā rattiyā anurūpaṃ yathārattanti nibbacanaṃ dasseti. “Rattiparimāṇānurūpa”nti vutte rattiparimāṇassa atikkantattā atthato theroti āha “yathātheranti attho”ti. Vavatthānanti paricchedo. So hi visuṃ avahito hutvā tiṭṭhatīti vavatthānanti vuccati. Kammākammānīti ettha kammaṃ akammānīti padavibhāgaṃ katvā akāro vuddhatthoti āha “khuddakāni ceva mahantāni ca kammānī”ti. Sati ca akammassa mahantabhāve [M 0.0623] kammaṃ nāma khuddakanti atthato siddhaṃ hoti. Tena vuttaṃ “khuddakāni cevā”ti. Akārassa appatthaṃ gahetvā “mahantāni ceva khuddakāni ca kammānī”ti atthopi yujjateva. So pana idha na gahito, aññattha pana dissati. “Uccāvacāni kammānī”ti hi vākyavasena vuttaṭṭhāne uccasaddena mahantatthaṃ dasseti, avacasaddena khuddakatthaṃ dasseti. Tasmā mahantakhuddakāni kammānīti attho veditabbo. Sati ca akammassa khuddakabhāve kammaṃ nāma mahantanti atthatopi siddhanti daṭṭhabbaṃ.

Regarding 'paññattetaṃ' (paññattetanti), here he says 'paññattaṃ etaṃ' because of the elision and sandhi of the niggahita. 'Where?' (kva) means 'in which section?' 'There' (tatra) means 'in the Vatta section.' 'By this much' (ettāvatā) means 'merely by this much, namely, by not performing the duties for incoming bhikkhus and so forth.' 'Gradually' (anupubbena) means 'sequentially.' Regarding 'according to the night' (yathārattaṃ), here the word 'yathā' expresses suitability, and showing that the word 'ratti' is to be taken as the measure of the night, he says, 'appropriate to the measure of the night.' By this, he shows the etymology of 'yathārattaṃ' as 'suitable to the night.' Having said 'appropriate to the measure of the night,' because the measure of the night has passed, the meaning is, in effect, that of a Thera; so he says, 'the meaning is "according to seniority".' 'Vavatthāna' means 'delimitation.' For it stands separately, distinctly; thus it is called 'vavatthāna.' Regarding 'kammākammāni,' here, having divided the words as 'kammaṃ akammāni,' he says that the 'a' is for augmentation; therefore he says, 'both minor and major actions.' And since `akamma` has the state of being great, it is established in meaning that `kamma` is minor. Therefore it is said, 'both minor...' And taking 'a' as having the meaning of 'small,' the meaning 'both major and minor actions' is also fitting. But that is not taken here; however, it is seen elsewhere. For in places where it is said in a sentence like 'actions of various kinds' (uccāvacāni kammāni), the word 'ucca' shows the meaning of 'great,' and the word 'avaca' shows the meaning of 'small.' Therefore, the meaning should be understood as 'great and small actions.' And it should be seen that, since `akamma` has the state of being small, it is also established in meaning that `kamma` is great.

Saṅghabhedavaggadvayavaṇṇanā

Commentary on the Two Chapters on the Schism of the Saṅgha.

459. Saṅghabhedavaggadvaye [V 2.0248] eteti sabhāvā. Teti adhammādayo. Itīti evaṃ. Yaṃ kammanti yojanā. Diṭṭhiṃ vinidhāyāti sambandho. Ekasmiṃ pañcake ayaṃ atthayojanā kātabbāti sambandho. Etthāpīti imasmiṃ pañcakepi. Pisaddena heṭṭhā vuttaṃ pañcakaṃ apekkhati. Sabbatthāti sabbesu pañcakesu. Hīti saccaṃ. Pubbe avuttanayaṃ yaṃ vacanamatthi, taṃ vacanaṃ ettha pañcakesu na atthīti yojanā.

459. In the two chapters on the schism of the Saṅgha, 'ete' means inherent natures. 'Te' means unrighteousness and so forth. 'Iti' means 'in this way.' 'Which action' (yaṃ kammaṃ)—this is the connection. 'Having laid aside one's view' (diṭṭhiṃ vinidhāya)—this is the connection. In one group of five, this explanation of the meaning should be made—this is the connection. 'Here too' (etthāpi) means 'in this group of five as well.' The word 'pi' refers back to the group of five mentioned previously. 'Everywhere' (sabbattha) means 'in all groups of five.' 'Indeed' (hi) means 'truly.' The explanation is: whatever statement of a method not previously mentioned there is, that statement does not exist here in these groups of five.

Āvāsikavaggavaṇṇanā

Commentary on the Chapter on Resident Bhikkhus.

461. Āvāsikavagge “haritvā”ti iminā yathābhatanti ettha bharadhātuyā haraṇatthañca kiriyāvisesanabhāvañca dasseti. “Ṭhapito”ti iminā nikkhittoti ettha khipadhātuyā ṭhapanatthaṃ dasseti.

461. In the Chapter on Resident Bhikkhus, by 'having carried' (haritvā), he shows both the meaning of 'carrying' from the root 'bhara' in 'as it was brought' (yathābhataṃ), and its state as an adverb of action. By 'placed' (ṭhapito), he shows the meaning of 'placing' from the root 'khipa' in 'deposited' (nikkhitto).

462. Pariṇāmetīti pariṇataṃpāpeti. “Niyāmeti kathetī”ti iminā adhippāyatthaṃ dasseti, etthāti āvāsikavagge.

462. 'Pariṇāmeti' means 'he brings to maturity.' By 'he directs, he speaks' (niyāmeti katheti), he shows the intended meaning; 'here' (ettha) means 'in the Chapter on Resident Bhikkhus.'

Kathinatthāravaggavaṇṇanā

Explanation of the Kathina Chapter

467. Kathinatthāravagge otamasikoti ettha avatamaṃ gato otamasikoti dassento āha “andhakāragato”ti. Andhakārasaddena tamasaddo andhakārapariyāyoti dasseti. Tanti otamasikaṃ[M 0.0624]. Asamannāharantoti taṃ asamannāharanto, kasmā asamannāharantoti āha “kiccayapasutattā vandana”nti. Ekatoti kopena saddhiṃ. Verī visabhāgapuggalo ekato ākodhena vattanaṭṭhena ekāvattoti vuccati. Pahareyyāti vandantaṃ pahareyya. “Aññaṃ cintayamāno”ti iminā aññasmiṃ ārammaṇe cittaṃ vidahati ṭhapetīti aññavihitoti dasseti.

467. In the Kathinatthāravagga, regarding 'otamasiko' here, showing that it means 'avatamaṃ gato' (one who has entered the dark), he says: 'andhakāragato' (gone into darkness). By the word 'andhakāra,' he shows that the word 'tamas' is a synonym for darkness. That is 'otamasikaṃ.' 'Asamannāharanto' means not paying attention to it. Explaining why he does not pay attention, he says: 'because of being intent on the duty of veneration.' 'Ekato' means together with anger. 'Verī' is a disagreeable person. He is called 'ekāvatto' in the sense of acting together with anger. 'Pahareyya' means he would strike one who is paying respects. By 'aññaṃ cintayamāno' (thinking of something else), it is shown that he places and fixes his mind on another object—thus, he is 'aññavihito' (one whose mind is otherwise directed).

Saṅghato uddharitvā khipitabbo apanetabboti ukkhitto, soyeva ukkhittako. Tehīti catūhi. Avandiyesu pannarasapuggalesūti sambandho. Antarā vuttakāraṇena cāti antare vuttena “tañhi vandantassa mañcapādādīsupi nalāṭaṃ paṭihaññeyyā”tiādinā kāraṇena ca. Itoti pannarasapuggalamhā[V 2.0249]. Itīti evaṃ. Sace uddesācariyo ca ovādācariyo ca navako hoti, na vandanīyo. Sabbatthāti kathinatthāravagge.

Having been lifted up from the Saṅgha, he should be thrown out and removed; thus he is 'expelled' (ukkhitto). That very one is the 'expelled person' (ukkhittako). 'By them' (tehi) means by the four. The connection is with 'the fifteen persons who should not be venerated' (avandiyesu pannarasapuggalesu). And by the reason stated in between (antarā vuttakāraṇena ca), that is, by the reason stated in between, such as, 'For if he were venerating, his forehead might strike against the bed leg, etc.' 'Ito' means from the fifteen persons. 'Iti' means in this way. If both the preceptor who gives the recitation (uddesācariyo) and the preceptor who gives the instruction (ovādācariyo) are newly ordained (navako), they should not be venerated. 'Sabbatthā' (in all instances) means in the Kathinatthāravagga.

Iti kathinatthāravaggavaṇṇanāya yojanā samattā.

Thus the exposition of the commentary on the Kathinatthāravagga is completed.

Niṭṭhitā ca upālipañcakavaṇṇanāya yojanā.

And the exposition of the commentary on the Upāli-pañcaka is completed.

Āpattisamuṭṭhānavaṇṇanā

The Commentary on the Arising of Offenses

470. “Acittako āpajjatī”tiādīsu evamattho veditabboti yojanā. Acittako āpajjatīti acittako hutvā āpajjati. Eseva nayo acittako vuṭṭhātīti etthāpi. Yaṃkiñci āpattinti sambandho. Itaraṃ āpattinti yojanā. Dhammadānaṃ karomīti “sabbadānaṃ dhammadānaṃ jinātī”ti (dha. pa. 354) ca “amataṃdado ca so hoti, yo dhammamanusāsatī”ti (saṃ. ni. 1.42) ca bhagavatā vuttavacanaṃ sutvā dhammadānaṃ karomi. Domanassikoti domanassena yutto, domanassavanto vā. Etthāti abyākatamūle.

470. In phrases such as 'Acittako āpajjati' (He incurs an offense without intention), the meaning should be understood thus. 'Acittako āpajjati' means he incurs it while being without intention. The same principle applies in 'Acittako vuṭṭhāti' (He arises without intention). 'Yaṃkiñci āpattiṃ' (whatever offense) is the connection. 'Itaraṃ āpattiṃ' (the other offense) is the explanation. 'Dhammadānaṃ karomi' (I give the gift of the Dhamma)—having heard the Blessed One’s words, such as 'The gift of Dhamma excels all gifts' (Dhp. 354) and 'He is a giver of the Deathless, who instructs in the Dhamma' (SN 1.42), I give the gift of the Dhamma. 'Domanassiko' (one with displeasure) means one who is joined with displeasure, or one who possesses displeasure. 'Ettha' (here) refers to the indeterminate root.

473. Yassa yassāti sikkhāpadassa. Taṃ sabbanti sabbaṃ taṃtaṃsamuṭṭhānasikkhāpadaṃ.

473. 'Yassa yassa' refers to the training rule. 'Taṃ sabbaṃ' (all that) refers to every training rule of this or that origin.

Aparadutiyagāthāsaṅgaṇikaṃ

The Collection of Verses With and Without a Second Element

(1) Kāyikādiāpattivaṇṇanā

(1) The Commentary on Offenses Relating to the Body, etc.

474. Cha [M 0.0625] āpattiyo kāyikāti ettha cha āpattiyo nāma kāti āha “antarapeyyāle”tiādi. Antarapeyyāle vuttāti sambandho. “Kāyadvāre samuṭṭhitattā”ti iminā kāye samuṭṭhantīti kāyikāti vacanatthaṃ dasseti. Tasmiṃyeva antarapeyyāle vuttāti sambandho. “Vajjapaṭicchādikāyā”tiādinā chādentassa tissoti ettha tiṇṇaṃ sarūpaṃ dasseti. “Bhikkhuniyā”tiādinā pañca saṃsaggapaccayāti ettha pañcannaṃ sarūpaṃ dasseti.

474. Regarding 'Six offenses are bodily,' when asked what the six offenses are, he says, 'in the `antarapeyyāla`,' and so on. The connection is 'stated in the `antarapeyyāla`.' By 'Because they arise through the body-door,' he shows the meaning of the word 'kāyika,' that is, 'they arise in the body.' The connection is 'stated in that same `antarapeyyāla`.' By 'Vajjapaṭicchādikāya,' and so on, he shows the nature of the three offenses for one who conceals. By 'With a bhikkhunī,' and so on, he shows the nature of the five offenses that are conditioned by association.

“Ekaratta”itiādinā [V 2.0250] aruṇugge tissoti ettha tiṇṇaṃ sarūpaṃ dasseti. Dve yāvatatiyakāti saṃvaṇṇetabbena “ekādasa yāvatatiyakā nāmā”ti saṃvaṇṇanāya viruddhabhāvaṃ paṭikkhipanto āha “paññattivasena panā”tiādi. “Imasmiṃ sāsane”ti iminā etthasaddassa visayaṃ dasseti. Ekena sabbasaṅgahoti ettha eko nāma ko, sabbāni nāma kānīti āha “yassa siyā”tiādi. “Nidānuddesenā”ti iminā ekassa sarūpaṃ dasseti. “Sikkhāpadānañca pātimokkhuddesānañcā”ti imehi padehi sabbasarūpaṃ dasseti. Saṅgaha saddena kammachaṭṭhīsamāso.

By 'Ekaratta' (one night), and so on, he shows the nature of the three here in 'three at the rising of dawn.' Regarding 'two `yāvatatiyakā` offenses,' rejecting the contradiction with the description 'eleven are called `yāvatatiyakā`,' he says, 'but by way of designation,' and so on. By 'in this dispensation,' he shows the scope of the word 'ettha' (here). Regarding 'by one, all are included,' when asked 'what is the one, and what is the all?', he says 'yassa siyā' (whatever there may be), and so on. By 'Nidānuddesena' (by the recitation of the introduction), he shows the nature of the one. By the words 'of the training rules and of the Pātimokkha recitations,' he shows the nature of 'all.' With the word 'saṅgaha' (inclusion), there is an objective genitive compound.

“Vajjapaṭicchādikāyā”tiādinā dve duṭṭhullacchādanāti ettha dvinnaṃ sarūpaṃ dasseti.

By 'Vajjapaṭicchādikāya' (by concealing an offense), and so on, he shows the nature of the two concealments of a grave offense here.

“Bhikkhu bhikkhuniyā”tiādinā gāmantare catassoti ettha catassannaṃ sarūpaṃ dasseti. Puna “bhikkhu bhikkhuniyā”tiādinā cetassā nadipārapaccayāti ettha catassannameva sarūpaṃ dasseti. “Cīvaradāne pācittiya”nti iminā pācittiyabhāvena sadisattā saṅkhyāviseso na kātabboti dasseti.

By 'a bhikkhu with a bhikkhunī,' and so on, he shows the nature of the four here in 'four in another village.' Again, by 'a bhikkhu with a bhikkhunī,' and so on, he shows the nature of those same four here in 'conditioned by crossing to the other side of a river.' By 'a pācittiya offense for giving a robe,' he shows that because of the similarity of being a pācittiya, no numerical distinction should be made.

(2) Desanāgāminiyādivaṇṇanā

(2) The Commentary on Offenses Leading to Confession, etc.

475. Eketthāti [M 0.0626] etthasaddo sāsanavisayo.

475. In 'Ekettha' (in one here), the word 'ettha' (here) refers to the dispensation.

Ekasikkhāpadampi natthīti pisaddo bahusikkhāpadāni pana pagevāti ca āpatti pana pagevāti ca āpattīpi natthīti ca atthaṃ dasseti.

The particle 'pi' in 'Ekasikkhāpadampi natthi' (not even one training rule exists) shows the following meanings: let alone many training rules; let alone an offense; and that there is not even an offense.

“Sakalepi vinaye”ti iminā dvetthāti pāṭhe etthasaddassa visayaṃ dasseti. Ubhinnanti bhikkhubhikkhunīnaṃ. Aññathā pana kittakā paṭhamāpattikāti āha “itarathā panā”tiādi. Tattha itarathāti paññattito aññena pakārena. Kammañcāti kammañatti ca. Kammapādikā cāti kammapādañatti ca. Navasu ṭhānesūti osāraṇādīsu navasu ṭhānesu. Dvīsūti ñattidutiya, ñatticatutthakammesu.

By 'Sakalepi vinaye' (in the entire Vinaya), he shows the scope of the word 'ettha' (here) in the reading 'dvettha' (in two instances). 'Ubhinnanti' (of both) means of bhikkhus and bhikkhunīs. Otherwise, how many are first-offenders? He says, 'itarathā pana' (but otherwise), and so on. Here, 'itarathā' (otherwise) means in a manner different from the enactment. 'Kammañca' (and the formal act) means also the motion for a formal act. 'Kammapādikā ca' (and the basis of a formal act) means also the enactment that is the basis of a formal act. 'Navasu ṭhānesu' (in nine instances) means in the nine instances beginning with reinstatement. 'Dvīsu' (in two) means in formal acts requiring a motion and one announcement (ñattidutiya), and a motion and three announcements (ñatticatuttha).

Vajjapaṭicchādikāya pārājikaṃ, ukkhittānuvattikāya pārājikaṃ, aṭṭhavatthukāya pārājikanti [V 2.0251] iti ime tayoti yojanā. Kāraṇabhūtenāti hetubhūtena, “karaṇabhūtenā”tipi pāṭho, sādhakatamasattibhūtenāti attho.

A pārājika for concealing an offense, a pārājika for following one who has been suspended, a pārājika for the eight-factored case—thus, these are the three; this is the connection. 'Kāraṇabhūtena' (by being a cause) means by being a reason (hetubhūtena). There is also a reading 'karaṇabhūtena,' meaning being the most effective instrument (sādhakatamasattibhūtena).

Tesanti addhānahīnādīnaṃ. Etthāti “tayo puggalā na upasampādetabbā”ti pāṭhe, etesu aṅgahīnādīsu vā. Yoti puggalo. Aparipūro na yācatīti sambandho. Mātughātakādayo karaṇadukkaṭakā cāti yojanā. Tatthāti tesu ñattikappanādīsu. Ñattikappanāti ñattividhi. Vippakatapaccattanti vippakataṃ paccattaṃ. Atītakaraṇanti atītassa karaṇaṃ. Vitthārento āha “vatthusampannaṃ hī”tiādi. Tayo kammāna saṅgahāti ettha chandabhedarakkhanatthāya nakāre niggahitalopo. Nāsitakāti nāsetabbā puggalā, nāsitabbāti nāsitā, nāsitā eva nāsitakā. Tiṇṇaṃ janānanti tiṇṇaṃ upasampadāpekkhajanānaṃ ekūpajjhāyena nānācariyena hutvāti yojanā. Ekānussāvanāti ekato anussāvanā.

'Tesanti' refers to those deficient in age, and so on. 'Ettha' (here) refers to the passage 'three persons are not to be ordained,' or to these persons deficient in limbs, and so on. 'Yo' refers to a person. The connection is 'one who is incomplete does not request.' Matricides, and so on, and those who commit a dukkaṭa by the act—this is the connection. 'Tatthāti' (therein) refers to those, such as the proposing of a motion. 'Ñattikappanā' means the procedure of the motion. 'Vippakatapaccattaṃ' means an incomplete personal matter. 'Atītakaraṇaṃ' means the doing of something past. Explaining in detail, he says: 'vatthusampannaṃ hi' (for it is complete as to the object), and so on. In 'Tayo kammāna saṅgahā' (three inclusions of formal acts), the niggahita on the 'na' is elided to prevent a splitting of the vote. 'Nāsitakā' (those to be banished) means persons who are to be banished; 'nāsitā' means banished; the banished are 'nāsitakā.' 'Tiṇṇaṃ janānaṃ' (of three persons) means of three persons aspiring for ordination, having one preceptor but different teachers—this is the connection. 'Ekānussāvanā' (one proclamation) means a proclamation made together.

Pādo [M 0.0627] nāma kahāpaṇassa catutthabhāgo. Māsako nāma pādassa pañcamabhāgo. Pārājikanti vanappatiṃ chindantassa dutiyapārājikaṃ (pārā. 110). Anodissāti “manusso maratū”tiādinā na uddisitvā. Tenāti visena.

A 'pāda' is a fourth part of a kahāpaṇa. A 'māsaka' is a fifth part of a pāda. 'Pārājika' refers to the second pārājika offense for one who cuts down a tree (Pārā. 110). 'Anodissā' (without specifying) means not specifying with 'may a person die,' and so on. 'Tena' (by that) means by poison.

Bhikkhunovādakavaggasminti sāmaññādhāro. Dasasu sikkhāpadesūti visesādhāro. Paṭhamasikkhāpadamhiyevāti dasasu sikkhāpadesu paṭhamasikkhāpadamhiyeva. Upasampannāya bhikkhuniyāti sambandho. “Āpatti hotī”ti iminā “cīvarenā”ti padassa sambandhaṭṭhānaṃ dasseti.

'Bhikkhunovādakavaggasmiṃ' (in the Bhikkhunovādakavagga)—this is a general locative. 'Dasasu sikkhāpadesu' (in the ten training rules)—this is a specific locative. 'Paṭhamasikkhāpadamhiyeva' (in the very first training rule) means in the first training rule among the ten training rules. 'Upasampannāya bhikkhuniyā' (for an ordained bhikkhunī) is the connection. By 'Āpatti hoti' (there is an offense), he indicates the point of connection for the word 'cīvarena' (with a robe).

“Catasso evā”ti iminā tattikāti ettha tasaddassa visayaṃ dasseti. Tā catasso parimāṇā yāsaṃ āpattīnanti tattikā. Nipannassāpi tattikāti etthāpi eseva nayo. Sāti bhikkhunī.
