By 'Catasso evā' (just four), he shows the scope of the pronoun 'ta' in the word 'tattikā' here. 'Tattikā' means those offenses that have those four as their measure. In 'Nipannassāpi tattikā' (even for one lying down, they are tattikā), the same principle applies. 'Sā' (she) means a bhikkhunī.

(3) Pācittiyavaṇṇanā

(3) The Commentary on the Pācittiyas

476. Pañca bhesajjānīti sabbiādīni pañca bhesajjāni. Imaṃ āpattinti sambandho. Pacchā āpannoti yojanā.

476. 'Five medicines' means the five medicines beginning with ghee. 'This offense' is the connection. 'Subsequently incurred' is the construction.

Ekaṃ [V 2.0252] kabaḷanti ekaṃ ālopaṃ, tumhamūleti tumhaṃ santike.

'One mouthful' means one morsel. 'At your root' means in your presence.

Yathāvatthukanti vatthuanulomaṃ, āpattiyo desitāva hontīti yojanā.

'According to the case' means in accordance with the case. 'The offenses are indeed confessed' is the construction.

Kokālikādīnantiādisaddena kaṭamodakatissakādayo (pārā. 417) saṅgaṇhāti. Pāpikāya diṭṭhiyā appaṭinissagge pācittiyañca caṇḍakāḷikāya bhikkhuniyā pācittiyañcāti yojanā. Payuttavācāpaccayāti viññattinimittādīhi pakārena yuttāya vācāya paccayā. Āpatti pārājikassāti pārājikassa āpajjanaṃ. Athavā pārājikassāti assa bhikkhussa pārājikā āpatti hotīti vā pārājikā āpatti assa bhavatīti vā yojanā kātabbā. Itīti imā cha āpattiyo āpajjatīti yojanā.

'Kokālikādīnaṃ' includes Kaṭamodakatissaka and others (Pārā. 417) by the word 'ādi'. The construction is that for not abandoning a wicked view, it is a pācittiya offense, and for the nun Caṇḍakāḷikā, it is a pācittiya offense. 'Payuttavācāpaccayā' means because of speech connected by way of hints, signs, etc. 'Āpatti pārājikassa' means the incurring of a pārājika offense. Alternatively, 'pārājikassa' should be construed as 'that monk incurs a pārājika offense' or 'a pārājika offense occurs for him'. 'Iti' is the construction that he incurs these six offenses.

Bhojanaṃ [M 0.0628] gahetvā ajjhoharamānāti sambandho. Tathevāti yathā khādane, tatheva maṃsaṃ lasuṇaṃ ajjhoharamānāti yojanā. “Paṇītabhojanānī”ti ca “akappiyamaṃsa”nti ca padāni “ajjhoharamānā”ti padena sambandhitabbāni.

'Having taken food and consuming it' is the connection. 'Just so' means just as in eating, so too consuming meat or garlic—this is the construction. The words 'choice foods' and 'unallowable meat' should be connected with the word 'consuming'.

Pañca ṭhānānīti pañca āpattisaṅkhātāni ṭhānāni. Tatthāti pañcasu sahadhammikesu. Dvinnanti bhikkhubhikkhunīnaṃ. Tesanti sikkhamānādīnaṃ. Pañcannamevāti sahadhammikānaṃyeva. Vinicchayavohāroti vinicchayavacanaṃ. Iminā cattāri adhikaraṇāni paṭikkhipati. Aḍḍakammaṃ nāmāti abhiyuñjantānaṃ kammaṃ nāma.

'Five instances' means five instances reckoned as offenses. 'There' means among the five co-religionists. 'Of two' means of monks and nuns. 'Of them' means of female probationers and the like. 'Of five only' means only of co-religionists. 'Discourse on the judgment' means a word of judgment. With this, he rejects the four kinds of legal disputes. 'Aḍḍakamma' means the act of those making an accusation.

“Sahadhammikāna”nti iminā pañjannaṃ vinicchayoti ettha pañcasarūpaṃ dasseti. Sobhaṇabhāvaṃ vitthārento āha “katavītikkamo hī”tiādi. Abbhuṇhasīloti abhinavuppannasīlo. Abbhuṇhasīlo nāma atthato pākatikasīloti āha “pākatiko”ti, pakatisīlena niyuttoti attho.

With 'of co-religionists,' he shows by this the nature of the five here, in 'the judgment of five'. Elaborating on the state of beauty, he says, 'for indeed, one who has transgressed,' and so on. 'Abbhuṇhasīla' means one whose virtue has newly arisen. 'Abbhuṇhasīla' means, in essence, one with natural virtue—thus he says 'natural,' meaning endowed with natural virtue.

“Kāyadvārasambhavā”ti iminā kāyikāti padassa taddhitabhāvaṃ dasseti. Mukhaṃ oloketabbanti ettha vuttāti sambandho.

With 'arising from the bodily door,' he shows by this the derivative nature of the word 'kāyikā'. 'The face should be looked at' is connected to what was said here.

Catunnaṃ desanāya cāti ettha “desanāyā”ti padaṃ ādipadalopanti āha “accayadesanāyā”ti. Sāti accayadesanā. Abhinilīyitvā dhanunā mārentīti abhimārā.

Here, in 'and for the confession of four,' he says that the word 'desanāyā' has an elision of the initial part of the word, hence 'accayadesanāyā'. 'That' refers to the confession of a transgression. 'Abhimārā' means those who kill with a bow, having hidden themselves.

Chejjaṃ [V 2.0253] hotīti ettha chejjaṃ nāma pārājikāpajjanamevāti āha “devadatto viya pārājikaṃ āpajjatī”ti. Imā pana āpattiyoti pārājikathullaccayāpattiyo.

Here, in 'it is a cutting off,' he says that 'cutting off' means only incurring a pārājika offense—thus, 'like Devadatta, he incurs a pārājika'. 'But these offenses' means pārājika and thullaccaya offenses.

(4) Avandanīyapuggalādivaṇṇanā

(4) Explanation of Persons Not Deserving of Veneration, etc.

477. Tesanti dasannaṃ puggalānaṃ. “Saddhi”nti iminā sāmīcenāti ettha sahatthe karaṇavacananti dasseti. Sāmīcenāti ca sāmīcinā kattabbaṃ sāmīcaṃ kammaṃ, tena sāmīcena. Dasa cīvaradhāraṇāti padassa samāsabhāvaṃ [M 0.0629] paṭikkhipanto āha “dasa divasāni atirekacīvarassa dhāraṇā”ti.

477. 'Of them' means of the ten persons. With 'together,' he shows by this that 'with propriety' here is an instrumental word in the sense of 'together with'. And 'with propriety' means: a proper act is an act to be done properly; by that propriety. Rejecting the compounded nature of the word 'dasa cīvaradhāraṇā,' he says, 'the wearing of an extra robe for ten days'.

Katisatantiādīsu dvīsu gāthāpādesu catūsu vibhatyantapadesu purimaṃ purimena, pacchimañca pacchimena yathākkamaṃ yojetabbanti dassento āha “katisataṃ āpattiyo rattisataṃ chādayitvānā”ti. Pacchimagāthāya pubbaḍḍhepi eseva nayo. Ayaṃ hīti ayaṃ eva vakkhamāno. Etthāti gāthāyaṃ. Yoti bhikkhu, paṭicchādetīti sambandho. Itīti ayaṃ saṅkhepattho.

Showing that in the two verse-quarters beginning with 'how many hundreds,' among the four words with case endings, the former should be connected with the former, and the latter with the latter, in order, he says, 'how many hundreds of offenses, having covered up for a hundred nights'. The same method applies also in the first half of the latter verse. 'For this' means this very one about to be spoken. 'Here' means in this verse. 'Whoever' refers to the monk, and is connected with 'covers up'. 'Thus' is this concise meaning.

Heṭṭhā vuttesu catūsu catukkesu dhammena samaggaṃ apanetvā dvādasa kammadosā vuttāti daṭṭhabbaṃ. Adhammena vaggakammaṃ, adhammena samaggakammanti yojetabbaṃ.

It should be understood that in the four sets of four mentioned below, twelve faults of formal acts are stated, excluding that which is harmonious with the Dhamma. 'An unlawful act by a faction' and 'an unlawful act by a complete assembly' should be construed.

Etthāti chasu kammesu. Etadevāti dhammena samaggakammameva.

'Here' means in the six formal acts. 'This alone' means only the formal act that is harmonious with the Dhamma.

Yaṃ desitāti ettha yaṃsaddo vacanavipallāsoti āha “yāni desitānī”ti. “Desitānī”ti iminā desitāti ettha nikārassa ākārādesabhāvaṃ dasseti. “Pariyantaparicchedabhāvarahitattā”ti iminā natthi antaṃ pariyantametassāti anantanti vacanatthaṃ dasseti. Tanti nibbānaṃ, jitanti sambandho. Kena kaṃ kinti katvā jitanti āha “bhagavatā kilesagaṇaṃ abhimadditvā”ti. Kena kaṃ kinti katvā kiṃ jitaṃ viyāti āha “raññā sapattagaṇaṃ abhimadditvā rajjaṃ viyā”ti. Tattha “raññā”ti iminā “kenā”ti pucchaṃ vissajjesi. “Sapattagaṇa”nti iminā “ka”nti pucchaṃ vissajjesi. “Abhimadditvā”ti iminā “kinti katvā”ti pucchaṃ vissajjesi. “Rajja”nti iminā “ki”nti pucchaṃ vissajjesi. Sapattagaṇanti verigaṇaṃ. Ayaṃ panettha yojanā – raññā sapattagaṇaṃ abhimadditvā rajjaṃ rājabhāvaṃ jitaṃ viya, bhagavatā kilesagaṇaṃ abhimadditvā nibbānaṃ [V 2.0254] jitanti. Svevāti bhagavā eva. “Nibbikāratāyā”ti iminā tādisaddo nibbikāratthavācako anipphannapāṭipadikoti dasseti. “Vivekapañcaka”nti iminā kāyacittaupadhivasena vivekattayampi gahetabbaṃ vivekabhāvena samānattā. Tena bhagavatāti sambandho. “Yāni satta āpattikkhandhānī”ti [M 0.0630] iminā eketthāti ettha ekasaddassa visayaṃ dasseti. Tatthāti sattasu āpattikkhandhesu. Ettha panāti samathesu pana. Hīti saccaṃ. Tassāti sammukhāvinayassa. Aṭṭhakathāsūti sabbaaṭṭhakathāsu. Mayaṃ panāti saṅgahakārakā amhe pana, buddhaghosanāmakā mayaṃ panāti attho, rocayāmāti sambandho. Kassa kimatthaṃ gahetvā rocesīti āha “vināti nipātassa paṭisedhanamatthamatta”nti. “Vināti nipātassā”ti padaṃ “atthamatta”nti pade vācakasambandho. Attano sādhyavacanaṃ buddhavacanasaṅkhātena sādhakavacanena sādhento āha “vuttampi ceta”ntiādi.

Here, in 'what is taught,' he says that the word 'yaṃ' is an interchange of number, hence 'yāni desitāni'. With 'desitāni,' he shows by this that here, in 'desitā,' there is a substitution of 'ā' for 'ni'. With 'because it lacks limitation or boundary,' he shows the meaning of the word 'ananta' (endless), as in, 'there is no end or limit to it'. 'That' refers to Nibbāna, and 'conquered' is the connection. By whom, what, and how was it conquered? He says, 'by the Blessed One, having crushed the multitude of defilements'. By whom, what, and how was something conquered, like what conquest? He says, 'like a king, having crushed the host of enemies, conquers the kingdom'. There, with 'by the king,' he answers the question 'by whom'. With 'the host of enemies,' he answers the question 'what'. With 'having crushed,' he answers the question 'how'. With 'the kingdom,' he answers the question 'what'. 'The host of enemies' means the group of foes. Here is the construction: just as a king, having crushed the host of enemies, conquers the kingdom, that is, kingship, so too the Blessed One, having crushed the multitude of defilements, conquered Nibbāna. 'He himself' means the Blessed One himself. With 'because of being without alteration,' he shows by this that the word 'tādi' conveys the meaning of being unaltered and is an underived stem. With 'the fivefold seclusion,' the threefold seclusion (of body, mind, and attachments) should also be included, due to their shared nature of seclusion. The connection is with 'by that Blessed One'. With 'the seven classes of offenses,' he shows by this the scope of the word 'one' here, in 'one here'. 'There' means in the seven classes of offenses. 'Here, however' means among those who are competent, however. 'Indeed' means truly. 'Of that' refers to the settlement in the presence of the parties. 'In the commentaries' means in all the commentaries. 'We, however' means we, the compilers; that is, we who are named Buddhaghosa. 'We approve' is the connection. For whom and for what purpose did he approve it? He says, 'for the mere purpose of negating the particle 'vinā'. The word 'of the particle vinā' is semantically connected to the word 'for the mere purpose'. Proving his own statement with the authoritative words reckoned as the words of the Buddha, he says, 'and this has also been said,' and so on.

Aṭṭhārasa aṭṭhakānīti adhammadiṭṭhibheda, dhammadiṭṭhibheda, vematikabhedesu tīsu ekamekaṃ mūlaṃ katvā tayo tayo mūliṃ katvā nava honti, tesu dhammadiṭṭhibhedesu dhammadiṭṭhibhedaṃ apanetvā aṭṭha honti, tāni aṭṭhārasa bhedakaravatthūsu yojetvā aṭṭhārasa aṭṭhakāni hontīti daṭṭhabbaṃ. Chaūnadiyaḍḍhasatanti catucattālīsādhikaṃ satanti vuttaṃ hoti.

It should be understood that 'eighteen sets of eight' means that among the three kinds of splits—splits of wrong view, splits of right view, and splits of doubt—making each one a root and making three branches from each, they become nine. Among these, removing the split of right view, they become eight. These, when combined with the eighteen bases for causing a schism, become eighteen sets of eight. 'One hundred and forty-four' means 'one hundred plus forty-four,' as it is said.

Ekekavatthusminti aṭṭhārasasu bhedakaravatthūsu ekekasmiṃ vatthusmiṃ.

'In each single case' means in each single case among the eighteen bases for causing a schism.

Iti gāthāsaṅgaṇikavaṇṇanāya yojanā samattā.

Thus the explanation of the commentary on the Compilation of Verses is concluded.

Sedamocikagāthā

The Sweat-Inducing Verses

(1) Avippavāsapañhāvaṇṇanā

(1) Explanation of the Questions on Non-Separation

479. Sedamocikagāthāsūti adhippāyatthassa gambhīrattā taṃ cintentānaṃ vinayadharānaṃ kāye sedaṃ mocetīti sedamocikā, sāyeva gāthā sedamocikagāthā, tāsu. “Akappiyasambhogo na labbhatī”ti iminā kappiyasambhogo labbhatīti dasseti. Kappiyasambhogaṃ [M 0.0631] dassetuṃ “nahāpanabhojanādī”ti [V 2.0255] vuttaṃ. Anāpattīti mātubhikkhuniyā anāpatti. Esā pañhāti ettha pañhasaddo sabhāvatiliṅgoti saddasatthesu (saddanītidhātumālāyaṃ 16 hakārantadhātu; abhidhānappadīpikāyaṃ 115 gāthāyaṃ) vutto, idha itthiliṅgavasena vutto. “Paṇḍitehī”ti iminā kusalassa kāraṇaṃ dasseti, paṇḍitattā kusaloti adhippāyo. Assāti pañhāya. Etanti vissajjanaṃ. Assāti gāthāya.

479. The verses are called 'Sedamocikā' because they cause sweat to flow from the bodies of those Vinaya experts who ponder their profound meaning; these very verses are the Sedamocikā verses. In reference to them, the statement 'Unsuitable association is not obtained' (akappiyasambhogo na labbhati) indicates that suitable association is obtained. To show suitable association, 'bathing, eating, etc.' is stated. 'No offense' means there is no offense for the mother-bhikkhunī. Here, the word 'question' (pañhā) is said to be of natural gender in treatises on grammar (Saddanīti Dhātumālā, 16th root ending in 'ha'; Abhidhānappadīpikā, verse 115), but here it is stated in the feminine gender. 'By the wise' (paṇḍitehi) indicates the cause of what is wholesome; the intention is that it is wholesome because of wisdom. 'Assa' refers to the question. 'Etaṃ' is the explanation. 'Assa' refers to the verse.

Ekādasa vivajjiyāti avibhattikaniddeso, ekādasa vivajjiyeti attho. Tena vuttaṃ “ye”tiādi. Tepīti pisaddo gāthāyaṃ luttaniddiṭṭhagamyamānabhāvaṃ dasseti.

'Ekādasa vivajjiya' is an indeclinable expression; the meaning is 'eleven should be avoided.' Therefore, it is said, 'those,' and so on. The particle 'pi' in 'tepi' indicates a state of being understood through an elided expression in the verse.

Ayanti nhāpitapubbako bhikkhu. Nimmitabuddhanti buddhena nimmitaṃ buddharūpaṃ.

'Ayaṃ' refers to the monk who was formerly a barber. 'Nimmita-buddha' means a Buddha-form created by the Buddha.

Vivajjiyāti ettha yakāro tvāpaccayassa kāriyoti āha “vivajjetvā”ti. Asīsakaṃ yaṃ taṃ kabandhaṃ atthīti yojanā. Asīsakattā kena sarīrena jīvitaṃ bandhatīti kabandho. Yassāti kabandhassa.

Here, in 'vivajjiya,' the letter 'ya' is the result of the 'tvā' suffix, thus it is said 'vivajjetvā.' The construction is: 'That which is headless, that kabandha, exists.' Because it is headless, with what body does it bind to life? Therefore, it is called kabandha. 'Yassa' refers to the kabandha.

Hīti saccaṃ. Teti abhabbapuggalā.

'Hī' means truly. 'Te' refers to the incapable persons.

Vācāti ettha yakāralopoti āha “vācāyā”ti. Iti meti evaṃ mama. Evaṃ vadamāne mama vacananti yojanā. Athavā itimeti evaṃ ime, evaṃ vadamāne ime janāti yojanā. Saddampīti iminā girasaddo saddapariyāyoti dasseti. Hīti saccaṃ. Tuṇhībhūtassa nisinnassa tassa bhikkhunoti yojanā. Yadi manodvāre āpatti nāma natthi, evaṃ sati kasmā āpajjeyya vācasikanti vuttanti āha “yasmā panā”tiādi. Tenāti tasmā. Assāti bhikkhussa.

Here, the elision of the letter 'ya' in 'vācā' is indicated by 'vācāya.' 'Iti me' means 'thus my.' The construction is: 'Thus speaking, my word.' Alternatively, 'iti me' means 'thus these,' and the construction is: 'Thus speaking, these people.' By 'saddampi,' it is shown that the word 'gira' is a synonym for 'sadda' (sound). 'Hī' means truly. The construction is: 'of that monk sitting silent.' If there is no offense at the mind-door, then in that case, why is a verbal offense spoken of? This is stated as: 'Because, however...' and so on. 'Tena' means 'therefore.' 'Assa' refers to the monk.

Sāti bhikkhunī, āpajjatīti sambandho. Vuttappakāranti “gāmantarapariyāpanna”nti vuttappakāraṃ.

'Sā' refers to the bhikkhunī; the connection is 'commits an offense.' 'Vuttappakāraṃ' refers to the manner stated as 'included within another village.'

Tāsūti dvīsu bhikkhunīsu.

'Tāsu' refers to the two bhikkhunīs.

Caturo janāti ettha catunnaṃ janānaṃ sarūpaṃ dassento āha “ācariyo ca tayo ca antevāsikā”ti[V 2.0256]. Sāhatthikāti sahatthā avaharitā. [M 0.0632] Āṇattiyāpīti āṇattena avaharitāpi. Itaresanti antevāsikānaṃ, ekeko māsakoti sambandho. Etthāti parivāre sedamocikagāthāyaṃ.

Here, showing the nature of 'four persons,' it is said: 'the teacher and the three pupils.' 'Sāhatthikā' means taken away by one's own hand. 'Āṇattiyāpi' means even taken away by command. 'Itarānaṃ' refers to the pupils; the connection is 'one māsaka each.' 'Ettha' refers to the Sedamocikā verse in the Parivāra.

(2) Pārājikādipañhāvaṇṇanā

(2) Explanation of the Questions beginning with the Pārājikas

480. Santhatapeyyālañcāti paṭhamapārājikavibhaṅge (pārā. 65) vuttaṃ santhatapeyyālañca.

480. 'Santhatapeyyālañca' refers to the section on bedding and so on, as stated in the analysis of the first Pārājika (Pārā. 65).

Liṅgaparivattaṃ sandhāyāti sati liṅge parivatte paṭiggahaṇassa vijahanaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ.

'Liṅgaparivattaṃ sandhāya' means with reference to the rejection of acceptance when there is a change of gender.

Yoti bhikkhu, pariṇāmetīti sambandho. Attano atthāyāti yojanā.

'Yo' refers to the bhikkhu; the connection is 'he diverts.' 'Attano atthāya' is the construction.

Assāti gāthāya. Kākauhadanti kākehi karīsussaggaṃ. Kaddamamakkhitanti kaddamena makkhitaṃ. Kāyagatāneva hutvāti sambandho.

'Assa' refers to the verse. 'Kākauhadanti' means the crows discharge excrement. 'Kaddamamakkhitaṃ' means smeared with mud. The connection is 'having become inherent in the body itself.'

Hīti vitthāro. Anariyaṃ taṃ itthiṃ vā taṃ purisaṃ vā haneyyāti yojanā. Liṅgaparivattena hetubhūtena itthibhūtaṃ, purisabhūtañcāti sambandho. Itthibhūtanti ca itthī hutvā bhūtaṃ, itthibhāvaṃ vā pattaṃ.

'Hī' means expansion. The construction is: 'that ignoble woman or that ignoble man should be killed.' The connection is: 'having become a woman and having become a man' due to the change of gender as the cause. 'Itthibhūtaṃ' means having become a woman, or having attained the state of womanhood.

Migasiṅgatāpasasīhakumārādīnaṃ tiracchānagatamātāpitaro viyāti yojanā. Migasiṅgatāpasoti migasiṅganāmako (jā. aṭṭha. 5.17.96 ādayo) tāpaso. Sīhakumāroti sīhabāhukumāro. Ādisaddena bhūridattādayo saṅgaṇhāti.

The construction is: 'like the parents of Migasiṅgatāpasa, Sīhakumāra, and others, who were reborn in the animal realm.' 'Migasiṅgatāpasa' refers to the ascetic named Migasiṅga (as in Jātaka Aṭṭhakathā 5.17.96 and others). 'Sīhakumāra' refers to Sīhabāhukumāra. The term 'and others' includes Bhūridatta and so on.

Kurundiyaṃ āgatanti sambandho.

The connection is with 'it is stated in the Kurundi'.

“Saccaṃ bhaṇantoti gāthāyā”ti padaṃ “saccaṃ bhāsato lahukāpatti hotī”ti ettha itisaddena sambandhitabbaṃ. “Saccaṃ bhaṇanto”ti gāthāya iti atthoti yojanā.

The phrase 'of the verse "Speaking the truth..."' is to be connected with the word 'iti' in the passage 'for one speaking the truth, there is a light offense'. The construction is: 'such is the meaning of the verse "Speaking the truth..."'.

(3) Pācittiyādipañhāvaṇṇanā

(3) Explanation of the Questions on the Pācittiya and Similar Rules

481. Salākaṃ [V 2.0257][M 0.0633] dentassa assa bhikkhussa chejjaṃ hotīti yojanā. “Pārājikaṃ hotī”ti iminā hotichejjanti padassa atthaṃ dasseti.

481. The construction is: 'for that monk who gives a voting ticket, there is severance.' By 'it is a pārājika,' it indicates the meaning of the word 'entailing severance.'

Suppatiṭṭhitanigrodhasadisaṃ rukkhamūlaṃ, tameva vā gahetabbaṃ.

One should take a tree root similar to that of a well-established banyan tree, or the root of that very banyan tree itself.

Tissitthiyoti ettha bhummatthe upayogavacanaṃ, paccattavacanaṃ vāti āha “tāsupī”ti. “Yaṃ taṃ methunaṃ nāma ta”nti iminā “methunaṃ yaṃ ta”nti padānaṃ samānādhikaraṇabhāvaṃ dasseti. “Na sevatī”ti iminā na seveti ettha tikārassa ekārādesabhāvaṃ (jā. aṭṭha. 4.11.76 putto vā pitaraṃ yāce viya) dasseti. Tayo puriseti ettha “upagantvā”ti padaṃ ajjhāharitvā sambandhitabbanti dassento āha“tayo purisepi upagantvā”ti. Iminā tayo puriseti ettha upayogatthe upayogavacananti dasseti. Purimanayaṃ gahetvā etthāpi “tīsu purisesū”ti bhummatthe upayogavacananti atthopi yujjateva. Imaṃ nayaṃ gahetvā purimapadepi tissitthiyo upagantvāti upayogatthe upayogavacananti atthopi yujjateva. Tasmā te dve nayā aññamaññopadesadāyakanayā nāmāti daṭṭhabbaṃ. “Ubhatobyañjanasaṅkhāte”ti iminā anariyasaddena ubhatobyañjanova idha gahetabboti dasseti. “Nācaratī”ti iminā na cācareti etthāpi tisaddassa ekārādesabhāvameva dasseti. Methunadhammassa pubbabhāgaṃ kāyasaṃsaggaṃ āpajjituṃ vāyamantiyā tassā bhikkhuniyāti yojanā.

Here, regarding 'tissitthiyo,' it is said 'tāsupi' to indicate that it is a locative case or an accusative case. The phrase 'yaṃ taṃ methunaṃ nāma taṃ' indicates that the words 'methunaṃ yaṃ taṃ' are in apposition. 'Na sevatī' shows that 'na seveti' here implies the transformation of the 'ti' ending into 'e' (as in Jātaka Aṭṭhakathā 4.11.76: 'putto vā pitaraṃ yāce viya'). Regarding 'tayo purise,' it is said 'tayo purisepi upagantvā' to show that the word 'upagantvā' should be supplied and connected. This indicates that in 'tayo purise,' the term is used in the sense of the locative. Following the previous method, here too, the meaning 'tīsu purisesu' as a locative case is also valid. Applying this method, even in the earlier phrase 'tissitthiyo upagantvā,' the meaning as a locative case is also valid. Therefore, these two methods should be seen as mutually instructive. 'Ubhatobyañjanasaṅkhāte' indicates that here, only the term 'ubhatobyañjana' should be taken in the sense of 'anariya' (ignoble). 'Nācaratī' shows that 'na cācareti' here also implies the transformation of the 'ti' ending into 'e.' The construction is: 'of that bhikkhunī who attempts to engage in physical contact, which is the preliminary part of sexual intercourse.'

Assāti gāthāya, titthiyo ārādhako hotīti yojanā. Tatthevāti titthiyavatte eva. Assāti titthiyassa. Tamevāti titthiyavattameva.

'Assa' refers to the verse; the construction is: 'the sectarian becomes one who wins favour.' 'Tattheva' means in that very sectarian practice. 'Assa' refers to the sectarian. 'Tameva' means that very sectarian practice.

Saṅghādisesantiādigāthā vuttāti sambandho. Tanti ajjhoharaṇaṃ.

The connection is: 'the verses beginning with Saṅghādisesa are stated.' 'Taṃ' means supplying.

Ākāsagataṃ [M 0.0634] sāmaṇeranti sambandho. Saṅghenapīti pisaddo na kammārahenevāti dasseti. “Na kātabba”nti iminā saṅghopi kammārahopi bhūmigatova vaṭṭatīti dasseti.

The connection is: 'the novice who has gone into the sky.' The particle 'pi' in 'saṅghenapi' indicates that it is not only by one worthy of the act. By 'it should not be done,' it shows that even the Sangha and the one worthy of the act are properly situated on the ground.

Assāti gāthāya vinicchayoti sambandho.

The connection is with 'the determination of this verse'.

“Na [V 2.0258] deti, na paṭiggaṇhātī”ti kiriyāpadānaṃ kattāraṃ dassento āha “nāpi uyyojikā”tiādi. Tassāti avassutapurisassa. “Kāraṇenā”ti iminā tenāti padassa kāraṇatthaṃ dasseti. Evasaddo pana sambhavavasena yojito, na aññena kāraṇenāti attho, avassutassa purisassāti sambandho. Gahaṇeti uyyojitāya gahaṇe. Tañca paribhogapaccayāti ettha tasaddassa visayaṃ, paribhogassa ca sambandhaṃ dassento āha “tañca panā”tiādi. Tattha “āpatti”nti iminā tasaddassa visayaṃ dasseti. “Tassā uyyojitāyā”ti iminā paribhogassa sambandhaṃ dasseti. Tassāti uyyojitāya.

Showing the agent of the verbs 'does not give' and 'does not receive,' it is said 'nor is she the instigator,' etc. 'Tassa' refers to the incontinent man. By 'kāraṇena,' it indicates the meaning of 'reason' for the word 'tena.' The word 'eva,' however, is connected in the sense of possibility; the meaning is 'not by any other reason'; the connection is 'of the incontinent man.' 'Gahaṇe' refers to the seizing by the one who is instigated. Here, showing the scope of the word 'taṃ' and its connection to 'paribhoga' (use), it is said 'tañca pana,' etc. There, by 'āpatti,' it indicates the scope of the word 'taṃ.' By 'tassā uyyojitāya,' it indicates the connection to 'paribhoga.' 'Tassā' refers to the one who was instigated.

Sattarasakesu saṅghādisesesūti sambandho. Vajjaṃ na phusatīti padassa atthaṃ dassento āha “aññaṃ navaṃ āpatti”nti.

The connection is: 'in the seventeen Saṅghādisesa offenses.' Explaining the meaning of the phrase 'does not incur an offense,' he says, 'another new offense.'

Iti sedamocikagāthāvaṇṇanāya yojanā samattā.

Thus ends the explanation of the commentary on the Sedamocikā verses.

Pañcavaggo

The Fifth Section

Kammavaggavaṇṇanā

Commentary on the Section on Formal Acts

482. Kammavagge “gaṇanaparicchedavacana”nti iminā na pamāṇavacananti dasseti. Iminā kammānaṃ tato ūnātirekabhāvaṃ nivāreti. Gaṇiyate gaṇanaṃ, paricchijjati anenāti paricchedo, gaṇanassa paricchedo gaṇanaparicchedo. Atha vā gaṇiyati anenāti gaṇanaṃ, tameva paricchedo gaṇanaparicchedo, soyeva vacanaṃ gaṇanaparicchedavacanaṃ. Apalokanakammaṃ nāmāti kattabbaṃ kammanti sambandho. Vuttanayenevāti “sīmaṭṭhakasaṅghaṃ [M 0.0635] sodhetvā chandārahānaṃ chandaṃ āharitvā”ti vuttena eva nayena.

482. In the Section on Formal Acts, by the phrase “a statement of numerical delimitation,” it is shown that this is not a statement of quantity. By this, he prevents the formal acts from being fewer or more than the required number. That which is counted is a 'counting' (gaṇana); that by which something is delimited is a 'delimitation' (pariccheda); the delimitation of the counting is 'numerical delimitation' (gaṇanapariccheda). Alternatively, that by which one counts is a 'counting'; that itself is the 'delimitation'; that very thing is the 'statement'; hence, 'a statement of numerical delimitation.' The connection is: 'an act of seeking permission by name' is 'a formal act that is to be done.' 'In the manner stated' means in the very manner that was stated: “having purified the Saṅgha within the boundary and having brought the consent of those eligible to give consent.”

Tatthāti catūsu kammesu, ñattidutiyakammaṃ pana atthīti sambandho.

`Tattha` means 'among the four formal acts'; the connection is that the formal act consisting of a motion and one proclamation, however, exists.

Tatthāti dvīsu kammesu. Avasesāti chahi kammehi avasesā. Yadi parivattetvā kataṃ daḷhīkammaṃ [V 2.0259] na hoti, evaṃ sati daḷhīkammatthāya kinti kātabbanti āha “sace panā”tiādi. Tattha “akkharaparihīnaṃ vā padaparihīnaṃ vā”ti idaṃ akkharapadānaṃ gaḷitaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ. “Duruttapadaṃ vā”ti idaṃ sithiladhanitādiaparipuṇṇaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ. Ettha “duruttakkharaṃ vā”ti ajjhāharitabbaṃ. Idanti punappunaṃ vacanaṃ. Kammaṃ hutvāti sukammaṃ hutvā.

`Tattha` means 'among the two formal acts.' `Avasesā` means 'the remaining' from the six formal acts. If a confirmatory act, having been altered, is not valid, this being the case, what should be done for the purpose of a confirmatory act? He says, “But if…” and so on. Therein, the phrase “deficient in a syllable or a word” is said with reference to the elision of syllables and words. The phrase “a badly uttered word” is said with reference to what is incomplete, such as lax or aspirated sounds. Here, “or a badly uttered syllable” should be supplied. `Idaṃ` means 'this repetition of the words.' `Kammaṃ hutvā` means 'having become a well-done formal act.'

483. Sammukhākaraṇīyaasammukhākaraṇīyesu asammukhākaraṇīyāni appakattā paṭhamaṃ dassetvā sesānaṃ sammukhākaraṇīyabhāvaṃ dassento āha “tatthā”tiādi. Tattha tatthāti tesu dvīsu, asammukhākaraṇīyaṃ nāma aṭṭhavidhaṃ hotīti sambandho. Tattha tatthāti tesu tesu khandhakesu. “Sukataṃ hotī”ti vacanasāmatthiyato sammukhākatampi sukataṃ hotīti atthopi gahetabbo.

483. Among the acts to be done in the presence of the Saṅgha and those not to be done in the presence of the Saṅgha, having first shown those not to be done in the presence of the Saṅgha, as they are fewer, he then shows that the remainder are to be done in the presence of the Saṅgha, saying, “Therein…” and so on. Therein, `tattha` refers to those two kinds; the connection is that the act not to be done in the presence of the Saṅgha is of eight kinds. Therein, `tattha` refers to those respective sections. By the force of the statement “it is well done,” the meaning should also be taken that what is done in the presence of the Saṅgha is also well done.

Sesānīti aṭṭhakammehi sesāni. Etānīti kammāni. Vatthuvipannānīti vatthunā vipannāni.

`Sesāni` means 'the rest,' remaining from the eight formal acts. `Etāni` means 'these' formal acts. `Vatthuvipannāni` means 'defective in basis,' that is, defective by way of the basis.

Tesampīti paṭipucchākaraṇīyānampi. Etthāti “paṭipucchākaraṇīya”nti pade. “Pucchitvā”ti iminā paṭipucchāti padassa tvāpaccayantabhāvaṃ dasseti. “Kātabba”nti iminā karaṇīyanti ettha anīyasaddassa kammatthabhāvaṃ dasseti. Yathādinnāyāhi cuditakena yathādinnāya. Vippalapantassāti vikārena yaṃ vā taṃ vā vacanaṃ palapantassa cuditakassāti sambandho. Sabbatthāti sabbesu “tajjanīyakammārahassā”tiādīsu.

`Tesampi` means 'even for those' who are subject to questioning. `Ettha` means 'here' in the word `paṭipucchākaraṇīya`. By `pucchitvā`, 'having questioned,' he shows that the word `paṭipucchā` is a gerund ending in `-tvā`. By `kātabbaṃ`, 'to be done,' he shows that here in `karaṇīya`, the suffix `-anīya` has the sense of the passive. `Yathādinnāya` means 'according to what was given' by the accuser. `Vippalapantassa` means 'of one who babbles'; the connection is with the accuser who babbles, uttering this or that statement incoherently. `Sabbatthāti` means 'in all instances,' such as in “for one worthy of the act of censure” and so on.

Anuposathadivaseti uposathadivasato aññasmiṃ divase. Tamevatthaṃ dassento āha “uposathadivaso nāmā”tiādi. Kattikamāsanti pacchimakattikamāsaṃ. Tassa pavāraṇamāsattā “ṭhapetvā”ti vuttaṃ. Sāmaggidivaso ca yathāvuttā cātuddasapannarasā ca uposathadivaso [M 0.0636] nāmāti yojanā. Yatrahīti yasmiṃ pana vihāre, ṭhapentīti sambandho. Antarāti cātuddasīpannarasīnaṃ majjhe.

`Anuposathadivase` means 'on a day other than the Uposatha day.' Explaining this very meaning, he says, “The Uposatha day is called…” and so on. `Kattikamāsaṃ` means 'the month of Kattika,' that is, the latter month of Kattika. Because it is the month of the Pavāraṇā ceremony, “except for” is stated. The construction is: the day of harmony and the aforementioned fourteenth and fifteenth days are called the Uposatha day. `Yatra hi` means 'in whichever monastery'; the connection is with `ṭhapenti`, 'they set aside.' `Antarā` means 'in between' the fourteenth and fifteenth days.

Paccukkaḍḍhitvā ṭhapitadivasoti pacchā upari kaḍḍhitvā ṭhapitaṃ kattikakāḷapakkhacātuddasiṃ vā pañcadasiṃ vā sandhāya vuttaṃ. Idhāpīti apavāraṇāya pavāraṇaṭṭhānepi. Pāḷiyamāgatanayato aññampi nayaṃ dassento āha “apicā”tiādi. Antimavatthunti pārājikavatthuṃ. Yassāti puggalassa. Iminā kammāraho puggalo vatthu nāmāti dasseti.

`Paccukkaḍḍhitvā ṭhapitadivaso`, 'the day postponed and set aside,' is said with reference to the fourteenth or fifteenth day of the dark fortnight of the month of Kattika, which was subsequently pulled back and set aside. `Idhāpi`, 'here too,' means even in the place of the Pavāraṇā ceremony for one who does not participate in it. Showing another method apart from the one found in the Pāḷi canon, he says, “Furthermore…” and so on. `Antimavatthuṃ`, 'the final basis,' means the basis for a Pārājika offense. `Yassa` means 'of which' person. By this, it is shown that a person fit for a formal act is called a 'basis.'

484. Dabbassa [V 2.0260] aggaṇhanaṃ vatthuaparāmasanaṃ nāma na hoti, atha kho nāmassa aggaṇhanamevāti āha “tassa nāmaṃ na gaṇhātī”ti. Aparāmasanākāraṃ dassento āha “suṇātu me”tiādi.

484. Not taking the substance is not what is called 'not referring to the basis'; rather, it is only not taking the name. Thus he says, 'He does not take its name.' Showing the manner of not referring, he says, 'Let the venerable Saṅgha listen to me…' and so on.

Puggalaṃ na parāmasatīti ettha puggalo nāma upajjhāyoti āha “yo upasampadāpekkhassa upajjhāyo”ti. Tanti upajjhāyaṃ.

In the phrase 'he does not refer to the person,' 'person' here means the preceptor; thus he says, “who is the preceptor of one seeking higher ordination.” `Taṃ` refers to 'that' preceptor.

Sabbena sabbanti sabbathā sabbaṃ, nipātasamudāyoyaṃ, sabbena vā ākārena sabbaṃ ñattinti yojanā.

`Sabbena sabbaṃ` means 'in every way, completely'; this is a collection of particles. Or, the construction is: 'the entire motion in every way.'

Ñattikamme paṭhamaṃ kammaṃ katvā pacchā ñattiṭṭhapanampi pacchā ñattiṃ ṭhapetiyeva nāma. Iti imehītiādi nigamanaṃ.

In a formal act initiated by a motion, even if one performs the act first and establishes the motion afterwards, this is indeed called 'establishing the motion afterwards.' The conclusion is: “Thus, by these…” and so on.

485. “Vuttanayenevā”ti atidisitvāpi ñattikammavācānaṃ asadisattā aparāmasanākāraṃ dassento āha “evaṃ panā”tiādi. Tattha nesanti vatthusaṅghapuggalānaṃ, paṭhamānussāvane vā dutiyatatiyānussāvanāsu vā vattabbe vadantoti sambandho.

485. Even after applying the principle 'in the manner stated,' because of the dissimilarity of the motion and the proclamations, showing the manner of not referring to them, he says, 'But thus…' and so on. Here, the connection is: `nesanti` means they say what ought to be said regarding the basis, the Saṅgha, and the person, either in the first proclamation or in the second and third proclamations.

Sāvanaṃ hāpetīti ettha anusaddo lopoti āha “anussāvanaṃ na karotī”ti. “Sāvanaṃ hāpetī”ti ettha na kevalaṃ sabbena sabbaṃ anussāvanaṃ akarontoyeva sāvanaṃ hāpeti nāma, atha kho anussāvanāya duruttachaḍḍanampi hāpetiyeva nāmāti dassento āha “yopī”tiādi. “Sakimeva vā dvikkhattuṃ vā”ti iminā tikkhattuṃ aparipūrentoyeva sāvanaṃ hāpeti nāmāti dasseti. Imassa vacanassa sāmatthiyato ñattidutiyakamme ekakkhattuto, ñatticatutthakamme [M 0.0637] tikkhattuto atirekaṃ kammavācaṃ karonto na hāpetīti ñāyati.

In the phrase 'he omits the proclamation,' he says that the prefix `anu-` is elided, meaning 'he does not perform the proclamation.' In the phrase 'he omits the proclamation,' it is not only one who entirely fails to perform the proclamation who is said to 'omit the proclamation,' but also, showing that even discarding a poorly uttered part of the proclamation is indeed called 'omitting,' he says, “Whoever also…” and so on. By the phrase “only once or twice,” he shows that one who does not complete it three times is said to 'omit the proclamation.' From the force of this statement, it is understood that in a formal act with a motion and one proclamation, one who recites the formal proclamation more than once does not 'omit' it; and in a formal act with a motion and three proclamations, one who recites it more than three times does not 'omit' it.

“Chaḍḍetī”ti ettha chaḍḍanassa padakkharānaṃ gaḷitabhāvena pākaṭattā taṃ adassetvā “duruttaṃ karotī”ti ettha duruttameva dassento āha “duruttaṃ karotīti ettha panā”tiādi. Karontena bhikkhunā upalakkhetabboti sambandho.

In the phrase 'he discards,' because the act of discarding is evident through the elision of words and syllables, he does not show it. Instead, pointing out only the 'badly uttered' part in 'he utters it badly,' he says, “But here, in ‘he utters it badly’…” and so on. The connection is: this should be noted by the monk performing the act.

“Sithila…pe… pabhedo”ti yvāyaṃ byañjanappabhedo vutto, ayaṃ byañjanappabhedoti yojanā[V 2.0261]. Gāthāyaṃ dasadhāti dasappakārena. Byañjanabuddhiyāti vaddhetīti buddhi, byañjanameva akkharameva sithilādivasena dasadhā buddhi byañjanabuddhi, tāya. Ettha “dasadhā”ti padena “byañjanabuddhī”ti samāsapadassa antare dasadhāsaddassa lopaṃ dasseti “kammajaṃ evā”tiādīsu (visuddhi. 2.450; visuddhi. mahāṭi. 2.450) viya. Ettha hi evasaddena kammena eva jātaṃ kammajanti samāsaṃ katvā samāsamajjhe evasaddalopaṃ dasseti. Pabhedoti viseso. Ayaṃ panettha yojanā – sithilañca dhanitañca dīghañca rassañca garukañca lahukañca niggahitañca sambandhañca vavatthitañca vimuttañcāti dasadhā byañjanabuddhiyāva pabhedo viseso ñātabboti. “Sithila”nti ādīni dasa padāni “akkharaṃ padaṃ byañjana”nti napuṃsakaliṅgavasena vuttapāṭhaṃnissāya vuttānīti daṭṭhabbaṃ.

The construction for “Lax… etc. …distinction” is: that which was stated as the differentiation of consonants is this very differentiation of consonants. In the verse, `dasadhā` means 'in ten ways.' `Byañjanabuddhiyā`, 'by the understanding of consonants,' means: `buddhi` is 'understanding,' from `vaddheti`, 'it increases'; `byañjanabuddhi` is the tenfold understanding of the consonants or letters themselves, such as lax, etc.; `tāya` means 'by that.' Here, by the word `dasadhā`, he indicates the elision of the word `dasadhā` from the middle of the compound word `byañjanabuddhi`, just as in examples like `kammajaṃ eva` (Visuddhimagga II 450). For here, by the word `eva`, it is shown that the compound `kammaja` is formed from `kammena eva jātaṃ`, with the elision of the word `eva` from the middle of the compound. `Pabhedo`, 'distinction,' means a particular characteristic. The interpretation here is this: the distinction, the particular characteristic, should be known as tenfold through the understanding of consonants—lax, aspirated, long, short, heavy, light, nasalized, connected, fixed, and released. It should be understood that the ten terms starting with `sithila` are stated in the neuter gender, following the reading `akkharaṃ padaṃ byañjanaṃ`, 'letter, word, consonant.'

Gāthāya vitthāraṃ dassento āha “ettha hī”tiādi. Agāḷhena vacīpayogena vattabbaṃ akkharaṃ sithilaṃ. Gāḷhena vacīpayogena vattabbaṃ akkharaṃ dhanitaṃ. Tesvevāti pañcasu eva vaggesu. Na kevalaṃ dīghameva garukaṃ nāma, atha kho saṃyogaparampīti āha “yaṃ vā”tiādi. Yaṃ akkharaṃ saṃyogaparaṃ katvā vuccati, tampi garukaṃ nāmāti yojanā. Saṃyogo paro yassa akkharassāti saṃyogaparaṃ. “Saṃyogapada”ntipi pāṭho. Yaṃ asaṃyogaparaṃ katvā vuccati, tampi lahukaṃ nāmāti yojanā. Yaṃ sānunāsikaṃ katvā vattabbaṃ, taṃ niggahitaṃ nāmāti yojanā. Niggahetvāti niggahitaṃ nāma atthato ṭhānakaraṇānaṃ [M 0.0638] avissajjanaṃ amuñcananti āha “avissajjetvā”ti. Yaṃ sambandhitvā vuccati, taṃ sambandhaṃ nāmāti yojanā. Yaṃ asambandhaṃ katvā vuccati, taṃ vavatthitaṃ nāmāti yojanā. Yaṃ aniggahetvā vuccati, taṃ vimuttaṃ nāmāti yojanā. Aniggahetvāti aniggahaṃ nāma atthato vissajjananti āha “vissajjetvā”ti.

To elaborate on the verse, he said, ‘Here indeed’ (ettha hi), and so on. A letter to be pronounced with a relaxed vocal effort is called loose (sithila). A letter to be pronounced with a strong vocal effort is called firm (dhanita). ‘In these very’ (tesveva) refers to the five groups. Not only is a long vowel called heavy (garuka), but also one followed by a conjunct consonant, as stated, ‘Or whatever’ (yaṃ vā), and so on. The explanation is: a letter that is pronounced with a conjunct consonant following it is also called heavy (garuka). ‘Followed by a conjunct’ (saṃyogapara) means a letter after which there is a conjunct consonant. ‘Conjunct-word’ (saṃyogapada) is also a reading. The explanation is: a letter that is pronounced without a conjunct consonant following it is also called light (lahuka). The explanation is: what is to be pronounced with a nasal sound is called a niggahita. ‘Having held back’ (niggahetvā)—a niggahita, in essence, is the non-release, the not letting go, of the place and instrument of articulation, as stated, ‘without releasing’ (avissajjetvā). The explanation is: what is pronounced connectedly is called ‘connected’ (sambandha). The explanation is: what is pronounced without connection is called ‘fixed’ (vavatthita). The explanation is: what is pronounced without holding back is called ‘released’ (vimutta). ‘Without holding back’ (aniggahetvā)—non-holding back (aniggaha), in essence, is release, as stated, ‘having released’ (vissajjetvā).

Evaṃ byañjanabuddhivisesaṃ dassetvā idāni kammavācāya uccāraṇavisesaṃ vitthārena dassento āha “tatthā”tiādi. Tattha tatthāti tāsu dasasu byañjanabuddhīsu. Tathāsaddena takārassa thakārakaraṇañca sithilassa dhanitakaraṇañca atidisati, tathā “pattakallaṃ esā ñattī”tiādivacanañca sithilassa dhanitakaraṇaṃ nāmāti yojanā.

Having thus shown the distinctions in the cognition of consonants, now, elaborating in detail on the distinctions in the recitation of the formal act, he says, 'Therein' and so forth. The phrase 'therein, therein' refers to those ten cognitions of consonants. The word 'tathā' indicates by analogy both the changing of 'ta' into 'tha' and the making of a loose sound into a firm one. Similarly, the statement 'this motion is timely' (pattakallaṃ esā ñattī) is an instance of making a loose sound firm—this is the explanation.

Itīti evaṃ. Sithile kattabbe dhanitaṃ karotīti sambandho. Cattāri byañjanānīti cattāri akkharāni. Byañjanasaddo hi idha akkharavācako. Catassannaṃ byañjanabuddhīnaṃ kammadūsanaṃ dassetvā itarāsaṃ adūsanaṃ dassento āha “itaresu panā”tiādi. Anukkamāgatanti [V 2.0262] ariyehi otaritvā anukkamena āgataṃ. Paveṇinti santatiṃ. Vināsetvā vutte kiṃ kammavācākopo hotīti āha “sace panā”tiādi. Na kuppatīti na nassati. Kasmā pana kammavācā na kuppati, nanu kammaṃ kopentī kammavācā kuppatīti āha “imāni hī”tiādi. Hi yasmā na kopenti, tasmā kammavācā na kuppatīti yojanā.

'Thus' means in this manner. The connection is: one makes a firm sound when a loose one should be made. 'Four consonants' means four letters. Indeed, here the word 'byañjana' refers to letters. Having shown the corruption of the act by the four cognitions of consonants and then showing the non-corruption by the others, he says, 'But in the others,' and so forth. 'Arrived in sequence' means descended from the Noble Ones and arrived in due order. 'Continuity' means a lineage. If it is said, 'having destroyed,' what disruption of the formal act occurs? He says, 'But if,' and so forth. 'Does not become ruined' means it is not destroyed. But why does the formal act not become ruined? Does not the formal act become ruined when it ruins the act? He says, 'For these indeed,' and so forth. The explanation is: because they do not ruin, therefore the formal act does not become ruined.

Yaṃ pana vacanaṃ suttantikattherā vadantīti sambandho. Kaccāyanādisuttantaṃ karontīti suttantikā, kaccāyanādayo, suttantikā ca te therā ceti suttantikattherā. Na vaṭṭatīti akkharavikāro na vaṭṭati. Vinayadharena kammavācā kātabbāti sambandho. Yathāpāḷiyāti bhagavatā yathāvuttāya pāḷiyā. Byañjananiruttiyāti byañjananiruttiyaṃ. Itarathāti vuttadosapariharaṇato aññena pakārena.

The connection is: 'whatever statement the Suttantika Elders say.' Those who compose the suttas of Kaccāyana and others are 'suttantikas', that is, Kaccāyana and others; 'Suttantikattherā' means 'those who are suttantikas and also elders.' 'Na vaṭṭati' means the alteration of letters is not allowable. The connection is: 'the formal act should be performed by a Vinaya-holder.' 'Yathāpāḷiyā' means according to the Pāḷi as spoken by the Blessed One. 'Byañjananiruttiyā' means in the expression of consonants. 'Itarathā' means in another way, other than avoiding the faults mentioned.

Akāle [M 0.0639] vā sāvetīti ettha akālo nāma anokāsoti āha “anokāse”ti. Anokāso nāma ñattianussāvanānaṃ pubbāparavitathanti āha “ñattiṃ aṭṭhapetvā”tiādi. Paṭhamaṃyeva ñattiṃ aṭṭhapetvā paṭhamaṃyeva anussāvanakammaṃ katvāti yojanā. “Paṭhamaṃyevā”ti hi padaṃ pubbāparāpekkhaṃ. Itītiādi nigamanaṃ.

Regarding 'or announces at an inappropriate time,' here 'inappropriate time' means 'lack of opportunity,' as he says, 'at an inopportune time.' 'Lack of opportunity' means the proposal and announcement are out of proper sequence, as he says, 'without having established the proposal,' and so forth. The explanation is: without having established the proposal first, having performed the announcement procedure first. Indeed, the word 'first' is relative to what precedes and what succeeds. 'Thus' and so forth is the conclusion.

486. Yā ekavīsati bhikkhū na gaṇhāti, ayaṃ atikhuddakasīmā nāmāti yojanā. Ekavīsati bhikkhūti abbhānakamme kammārahena saddhiṃ ekavīsati bhikkhū. Yattha sīmāyaṃ nisīdituṃ na sakkonti, ayaṃ atikhuddakasīmā nāmāti yojanā. Nisīditunti aññamaññassa hatthapāsaṃ avijahitvā parimaṇḍalākārena nisīdituṃ. Tatthāti atikhuddake. Etthāti sesasīmāsu. Yā sammatā hoti, ayaṃ atimahatī nāmāti yojanā. Kesaggamattenāpīti pisaddo tato atirekena pana pagevāti dasseti. Aghaṭitaṃ asambandhaṃ nimittaṃ imissāti aghaṭitanimittā. Khaṇḍanimittabhāvaṃ akhaṇḍanimittadassanena pākaṭaṃ karonto āha “puratthimāyā”tiādi. Pubbakittitanti paṭhamakittitaṃ. Tatthevāti uttarāya eva disāya. Aparāpīti pisaddo dutiyatthasampiṇḍanattho. Yā sammatā hoti, khaṇḍanimittā nāmāti yojanā. Animittupaganti yathābhūtakathanavisesanameva, na byavacchedavisesanaṃ tacasārādiggahaṇena animittupagabhāvassa pākaṭattā. Antarāti majjhe. Yā sammatā hoti, sā chāyānimittā nāma, animittā nāmāti yojanā.

486. The explanation is: the boundary that does not hold twenty-one bhikkhus is called an excessively small boundary. 'Twenty-one bhikkhus' means twenty-one bhikkhus including the one worthy of the formal act in the act of rehabilitation. The explanation is: the boundary where they are unable to sit is called an excessively small boundary. 'To sit' means to sit in a circular formation without abandoning one another's arm's reach. 'There' refers to the excessively small one. 'Here' refers to the other boundaries. The explanation is: the boundary that is designated is called an excessively large boundary. 'Even by a hair's breadth'—the particle 'pi' shows that if it is more than that, it is all the more so. The boundary that has an unconnected, unrelated marker is an 'unconnected marker boundary.' Making the state of a fragmented marker clear by showing an unbroken marker, he says, 'from the eastern direction,' and so forth. 'Previously declared' means first declared. 'Right there' means in the northern direction itself. 'And the other'—the particle 'pi' has the meaning of compounding the second sense. The explanation is: the boundary that is designated is called a 'fragmented marker boundary.' 'Reaching a state without a marker' is merely a qualification that describes the true nature, not a defining qualification, since the state of having no marker is evident by the taking of bark, sapwood, and so forth. 'In between' means in the middle. The explanation is: the boundary that is designated is called a 'shadow marker boundary' or a 'markerless boundary.'

Bahi ṭhito hutvā sammannatīti yojanā. Nimittāni pana bahi ṭhatvāpi kittetuṃ vaṭṭati[V 2.0263]. Evaṃ sammatāpīti pisaddo asammatā pana pagevāti dasseti. Sīmāya sīmanti padānaṃ sambandhāpekkhattā, tassa ca asamānabhāvato tesaṃ visuṃ visuṃ sambandhaṃ dassento āha “attano sīmāya paresaṃ sīma”nti. Sambhindatīti sambandhaṃ karoti. Ettha hi bhididhātu dvidhākaraṇatthavācako, dhātvatthabādhakena saṃtyūpasaggena sambandhavācako [M 0.0640] hotīti daṭṭhabbaṃ. Tatthāti tāsu dvīsu sīmāsu. Itīti evaṃ. Tāsūti sīmāsu.

The explanation is: having stood outside, he designates. However, it is allowable to declare the markers even while standing outside. 'Even when designated'—the particle 'pi' shows that if not designated, it is all the more so. Because the words 'a boundary for a boundary' require a connection, and because that connection is not of a single kind, showing their respective connections, he says, 'one's own boundary' and 'the boundary of others.' 'Connects' means he makes a connection. Indeed, here the root 'bhid' expresses the meaning of dividing into two, but it should be understood that with the prefix 'saṃ,' which obstructs the meaning of the root, it expresses connection. 'There' means in those two boundaries. 'Thus' means in this manner. 'In those' means in the boundaries.

487-8. Yampi kammappattachandārahalakkhaṇanti yojanā. Tatthāti tassaṃ parisato kammavipattiyaṃ. Tampīti kammappattachandārahalakkhaṇampi, vuttamevāti sambandho. Tatthāti “cattāro bhikkhū pakatattā kammappattā”ti pāṭhe. Anukkhittāti saṅghena ukkhepanīyakammassa akatattā anukkhittā. Parisuddhasīlāti pārājikaṃ anajjhāpannattā parisuddhasīlā. Imehi padehi pakati attā sabhāvo etesanti pakatattāti atthaṃ dasseti. “Kammassa arahā”ti iminā “kammappattā”ti padassa chaṭṭhīsamāsañca pattasaddassa arahaanucchavikatthabhāvañca dasseti. Tehīti catūhi pakatattehi. Etīti āgacchati. Avasesāti catūhi pakatattehi avasesā. Yassa panāti puggalassa pana. Kammārahoti kammassa araho.

487-8. The explanation is: 'the characteristic of having attained the act and being worthy of consent.' 'Therein' refers to the failure of the act in that assembly. 'That too' means the characteristic of having attained the act and being worthy of consent, has already been stated—this is the connection. 'Therein' refers to the reading: 'four bhikkhus who are in their natural state and have attained the act.' 'Not suspended' means not suspended because the Sangha has not performed the act of suspension upon them. 'Pure in virtue' means pure in virtue because they have not committed a pārājika offense. By these words, he shows the meaning of 'pakatattā' as: 'those for whom their own nature is their state.' By 'worthy of the act,' he shows both that the word 'kammappattā' is a genitive compound and that the word 'patta' has the meaning of 'worthy' or 'suitable.' 'By them' means by these four in their natural state. 'Comes' means arrives. 'The rest' means those remaining apart from the four in their natural state. 'But of which' means of which person. 'Worthy of the act' means worthy of the act.

489. Etthāti paṇḍakādīnaṃ avatthubhāvadassanaṭṭhāne.

489. 'Here' refers to the place where the state of being an unsuitable basis for those such as eunuchs is shown.

Apalokanakammakathā

The Discourse on the Act of Announcement

495-6. Tatthāti catūsu kammesu. Etthāti osāraṇādipāṭhe. Padasiliṭṭhatāyāti loke padānaṃ siliṭṭhabhāvato. Tatthāti osāraṇādīsu pañcasu. Kaṇṭakasāmaṇerassa yā sā daṇḍakammanāsanā atthi, sā nissāraṇāti yojanā. “Micchādiṭṭhiko hotī”ti vatvā tamevatthaṃ dassetuṃ “antaggāhikāya diṭṭhiyā samannāgato”ti vuttaṃ. Micchādiṭṭhi hi liṅganāsanāya kāraṇaṃ hoti. Soti sāmaṇero, “nissajjāpetabbo”ti pade kāritakammaṃ, vuttakammaṃ vā. Taṃ laddhinti dhātukammaṃ, avuttakammaṃ vā. Kinti kātabbanti āha “evañca pana kammaṃ kātabba”nti.

495–6. “Therein” refers to the four kinds of actions (kamma). “Herein” refers to the reading beginning with osāraṇā (summoning). “Due to the agglutinative nature of words” means due to the agglutinative nature of words in the world. “Therein” refers to the five beginning with osāraṇā (summoning). That destruction of status by disciplinary action which was for the novice Kaṇṭaka is to be construed as nissāraṇa (expulsion). Having stated, “He is one who holds wrong view,” to show that same meaning, it is said, “He is endowed with a view that grasps at extremes.” For wrong view is the cause for the loss of monastic status. “He” refers to the novice. In the phrase “should be made to give up,” it is either a causative passive (kāritakamma) or a passive participle (vuttakamma). “That which is obtained” is either a direct object (dhātukamma) or an unexpressed object (avuttakamma). “How then is this to be done?” He says, “And the action should be done thus.”

Kātabbākāraṃ dassento āha “saṅghaṃ bhante”tiādi. Yaṃ sahaseyyaṃ labhantīti yojanā. Tassāti sahaseyyassa. Alābhāyāti [M 0.0641] alābhatthāya. “Cara pire vinassā”ti iminā nissāraṇākāraṃ dasseti. Attho panassa heṭṭhā vuttoyeva.

Showing the manner of what should be done, he says, “Venerable Sir, the Saṅgha,” and so on. The construction is: “they obtain the shared dwelling.” “Tassa” (of that) refers to the shared dwelling. Alābhāyāti means for the purpose of non-gain. With the phrase, “Go, wretch, perish!” he shows the manner of expulsion. But its meaning has already been stated below.

Soti [V 2.0264] samaṇero, osāretabboti sambandho.

Soti refers to the novice; the connection is: 'he should be reinstated'.

Svāyanti so ayaṃ sāmaṇero, accayaṃ desetīti sambandho. Soratoti sundaraladdhiyaṃ rato, duladdhito vā suṭṭhu orato. Yathā pureti yathā pubbe ruccati, tathāti yojanā. Kāyasambhogasāmaggidānanti kāyena ca sambhogena ca sāmaggiyā dānaṃ.

Svāyanti means 'this novice'; the connection is: 'he confesses an offense'. Sorato means delighting in an excellent doctrine, or well-restrained from a bad doctrine. Yathā pureti means 'as before'; the construction is: 'as it was previously agreeable'. Kāyasambhogasāmaggidānanti means the giving of bodily communion and concord.

Evantiādi nigamanaṃ. Yasmā pana brahmadaṇḍo pañcasatikakkhandhake (cūḷava. 445) channasseva paññatto, tasmā tasseva dātabboti āha “na kevala”ntiādi. Esāti brahmadaṇḍo, aññopi yo bhikkhu viharati, tassapi dātabboti sambandho. Kinti dātabboti āha “evañca pana dātabbo”ti. Dātabbākāraṃ dassento āha “saṅghamajjhe”tiādi.

“Thus” and so on is the conclusion. But because the brahmadaṇḍa was prescribed in the Pañcasatikakkhandhaka (Cūḷavagga 445) only for Channa, therefore it is said, “not only,” and so on, to indicate that it is to be given to others as well. Esāti refers to the brahmadaṇḍa; the connection is that it is to be given also to any other monk who may be living there. “How is it to be given?” It is said, “and thus it should be given.” Showing the manner of giving, it is said, “in the midst of the Saṅgha,” and so on.

Yaṃ vacanaṃ iccheyya, taṃ vacananti yojanā. Khamāpentassāti saṅghaṃ khamāpentassa tassa bhikkhussāti yojanā.

The construction is with the words: 'Whatever speech he might wish, that speech...'. Khamāpentassāti means 'of that monk asking the Saṅgha for forgiveness'; that is the construction.

Paṭisaṅkhāti paṭisaṅkhāya, ñāṇena paccavekkhitvāti attho.

Paṭisaṅkhāti means paṭisaṅkhāya, that is, having reflected with wisdom.

Yanti avandiyakammaṃ, anuññātanti sambandho. Kena anuññātanti āha “bhagavatā”ti. Kismiṃ khandhake anuññātanti āha “bhikkhunikkhandhake”ti. Kesu vatthūsu anuññātanti āha “tena kho pana…pe… imesu vatthūsū”ti (cūḷava. 411). Kiṃ katvā anuññātanti āha “dukkaṭaṃ paññapetvā”ti. Kinti anuññātanti āha “anujānāmi…pe… kātabbo”ti. Tassāti avandiyassa. “Na osāraṇādīnī”ti iminā evasaddassa chaḍḍetabbatthaṃ dasseti. Tassāti kammalakkhaṇabhūtassa avandiyassa. Tatthevāti bhikkhunikkhandhakeyeva. Nanti kammalakkhaṇaṃ. Idhāpīti parivāre kammavaggepi.

Yanti means the formal act of not paying respects; the connection is: 'is permitted'. “By whom was it permitted?” He says, “by the Blessed One.” “In which Khandhaka was it permitted?” He says, “in the Bhikkhunikkhandhaka.” “In what circumstances was it permitted?” He says, “then indeed… in these circumstances” (Cūḷavagga 411). “Having done what was it permitted?” He says, “having laid down a dukkaṭa offense.” “How was it permitted?” He says, “I allow… it should be done.” Tassāti refers to that which is not to be respected. By “Not reinstatement, etc.” he shows that the word eva is to be discarded. Tassāti refers to that which is not to be respected, which has the characteristic of a formal act. Tatthevāti means in the Bhikkhunikkhandhaka itself. Nanti refers to the characteristic of the formal act. Idhāpīti means also here in the Parivāra, in the Kammavagga.

Apāsādikanti apasādāvahaṃ, apasādajanakaṃ vā.

Apāsādikanti means causing displeasure or generating displeasure.

Tatoti [M 0.0642] avandiyakaraṇato. Imanti bhikkhuṃ. Vandiyanti vanditabbaṃ, vandanaṃ vā.

Tatoti means because of making someone not worthy of respect. Imanti means 'this monk'. Vandiyanti means 'worthy of obeisance,' or 'the act of paying obeisance'.

Etthāti apalokanakamme, bhikkhunisaṅghamūlakaṃ katvā paññattanti yojanā. Bhikkhusaṅghassāpīti pisaddo na bhikkhunisaṅghassevāti dasseti. Panasaddo sambhāvanattho, tathā bhikkhunisaṅghamūlakaṃ [V 2.0265] paññattampīti attho, labhitabbabhāvaṃ vitthārena dassento āha “yaṃ hī”tiādi. Yaṃ apalokanakammaṃ karotīti yojanā. Appamattakavissajjakena pana dātabbānīti sambandho. Tesanti sūciādīnaṃ. Soyevāti appamattakavissajjakoyeva. Tatoti appamattakato. Tatthāti senāsanakkhandhakavaṇṇanāyaṃ (cūḷava. aṭṭha. 321). Vuttappakāraṃ gilānabhesajjampīti sambandho. Yopi cāti bhikkhupi ca hotīti sambandho. Tassa dātabbāti sambandho. Tatruppādatoti tasmiṃ mahāvāse uppādapaccayato, gahetvāti sambandho. “Pesalassā”tiādinā dussīlādīnaṃ dātuṃ na vaṭṭatīti dasseti.

Etthāti means in the formal act of announcement; the construction is: 'it is laid down based on the community of bhikkhunīs'. Bhikkhusaṅghassāpīti means the word pi indicates that it is not exclusively for the bhikkhunī saṅgha. The word pana is used in the sense of possibility; the meaning is that even a rule laid down based on the bhikkhunī saṅgha is possible. Explaining in detail the state of what is obtainable, he says, 'Because whatever...' and so on. The construction is: 'Whatever formal act of announcement he performs...'. The connection is: 'but they are to be given by the distributor of small items'. Tesanti refers to needles, etc. Soyevāti means only the distributor of small items. Tatoti means from the distributor of small items. Tatthāti means in the commentary on the chapter on monastic dwellings (Cūḷavagga Aṭṭhakathā 321). The connection is with 'and medicine for the sick of the aforesaid kind'. Yopi cāti is connected with 'and a bhikkhu exists'. Tassa dātabbāti is the connection. Tatruppādatoti means from the requisites arising in that great monastery; the connection is: 'having taken'. By 'to the well-behaved,' and so on, it is shown that it is not proper to give to the immoral, etc.

Jaggāpetuṃ vaṭṭatīti ettha apucchitvā jaggāpetuṃ vaṭṭatīti āha “ayaṃ bhikkhū”tiādi. Odissāti uddisitvā.

Regarding 'it is proper to have him guarded', here, he says, 'this monk,' and so on, meaning it is proper to have him guarded without asking. Odissāti means uddisitvā, that is, having pointed out.

Āsanagharaṃ vāti paṭimāgharaṃ vā, kārako manussoti sambandho. Upanikkhepato gahetvāti sambandho. Saṅghikenapīti pisaddo na kevalaṃ cetiyassa upanikkhepeneva, atha kho saṅghikenapīti dasseti.

Āsanagharaṃ vā means 'or an image house'; the connection is: 'the doer is a person'. The connection is: 'having taken from the deposit'. Saṅghikenapīti means the word pi indicates that it is not only by a deposit for the shrine, but also by that which belongs to the Saṅgha.

Yāpanamattaṃ alabhantehi karontehīti yojanā, paribhuñjantehi hutvāti sambandho. “Vattaṃ karomā”tiādinā “yāpanamatta”nti padassa atthaṃ dasseti. Vihāre ropitā ye phalarukkhāti yojanā. Yesanti rukkhānaṃ. Tesūti rukkhesu. Ye panāti rukkhā pana, apariggahitā hontīti sambandho. Taṃ panāti apalokanakammaṃ pana. Salākaṃ gaṇhanti etthāti salākaggaṃ, ṭhānaṃ. “Yāgaggabhattagga”iti etthāpi [M 0.0643] eseva nayo. Uposathaggeti uposathassa gahaṇaṭṭhāne, uposathageheti attho. Tatthāti uposathagge. Tanti apalokanakammaṃ.

The construction is: 'by those doing it while not obtaining more than just enough for subsistence'; the connection is: 'having become those who use it'. By 'We perform the duty,' and so on, he shows the meaning of the word yāpanamattaṃ. The construction is: 'those fruit trees planted in the monastery'. Yesanti refers to the trees. Tesūti means in the trees. Ye panāti means 'but those trees'; the connection is: 'they are unclaimed'. Taṃ panāti refers to the formal act of announcement. 'They take a ticket here', thus it is a ticket-hall, a place. The same method applies also here to yāgagga-bhattagga. Uposathaggeti means in the place for undertaking the Uposatha, that is, in the Uposatha hall. Tatthāti means in the Uposatha hall. Tanti refers to the formal act of announcement.

Yaṃ mūlatacapattaaṅkurapupphaphalakhādanīyādīti yojanā. Antosīmāyāti anto upacārasīmāya.

The construction is with the words: 'Whatever root, bark, leaf, sprout, flower, fruit, edible things, and so on...'. Antosīmāyāti means within the precincts.

Sukatamevāti saṅghena katameva. Uposathadivaseti nidassanamattaṃ yasmiṃ kasmiṃci divasepi katattā.

Sukatamevāti means 'well done by the Saṅgha'. Uposathadivaseti is just an indication, because it can be done on any day.

Phalavārenāti rukkhānaṃ phalagahaṇavārena. Rukkhā dharantīti rukkhā tiṭṭhanti, saṃvijjanti vā[V 2.0266]. Yehīti bhikkhūhi ropitā, hontīti sambandho. Sā eva katikāti pubbe katā sā eva katikā, aññā katikā na kātabbāti adhippāyo.

Phalavārenāti means 'by the turn for gathering the fruits of the trees'. Rukkhā dharantīti means 'the trees remain or exist'. Yehīti means 'planted by the monks'; the connection is: 'they exist'. Sā eva katikāti means 'that very agreement previously made'; the intention is that no other agreement should be made.

Aññasmiṃ vihāreti rukkhānaṃ ṭhitavihārato aññasmiṃ vihāre. Tesanti rukkhānaṃ, sāmīti sambandho. Yepīti rukkhāpi, ropitāti sambandho. Aññato ṭhānatoti yojanā. Tesūti rukkhesu. Etthāti vihāre. Tehi panāti pariveṇasāmikehi bhikkhūhi pana. Dasabhāganti dasamabhāgaṃ. “Eseva nayo”ti iminā dasabhāgaṃ datvāti atthaṃ atidisati.

Aññasmiṃ vihāreti means 'in another monastery, apart from the monastery where the trees stand'. Tesanti refers to the trees; the connection is: 'the owner'. Yepīti means 'even these trees'; the connection is: 'planted'. The construction is: 'from another place'. Tesūti means in the trees. Etthāti means in the monastery. Tehi panāti means 'but by the monks who are the owners of the cell'. Dasabhāganti means 'a tenth part'. By 'This is the method,' he extends the meaning 'having given a tenth part'.

Sambhāvanīyabhikkhunoti sīlasutādīhi sambhāvanīyassa bhikkhuno. Tatthāti porāṇavihāre. Mūleti pubbe, ādikāleti attho. Nikkukkuccenāti “abhājitamida”nti kukkuccavirahena. Khiyyanamattameva tanti taṃ khiyyanaṃ khiyyanamattameva, na sāmaṇerānaṃ khiyyanaṃ ruhatīti attho.

Sambhāvanīyabhikkhunoti means 'of a monk worthy of respect due to virtue, learning, etc.'. Tatthāti means in the ancient monastery. Mūleti means 'in the beginning,' that is, 'at the initial time' is the meaning. Nikkukkuccenāti means 'without scruple,' that is, 'without the worry, “this is undivided.”' Khiyyanamattameva tanti means 'that blame is merely blame, it does not grow into blame of the novices'; this is the meaning.

Panasarukkhanti kaṇṭakīphalarukkhaṃ. Ayaṃ sāmīcīti ayaṃ bhājetvā khādanaṃ anudhammatā. Khāyitanti khāditaṃ. Dvinnaṃ tiṇṇaṃ katikapaṭippassambhanaṃ nayena ñātuṃ sakkuṇeyyattā taṃ adassetvā ekasseva katikapaṭippassambhanaṃ dassento āha “ekabhikkhuke panā”tiādi. Purimakatikāti “yathāsukhaṃ paribhuñjituṃ ruccatī”ti (pari. aṭṭha. 495-496) pure katā katikā. Tesanti [M 0.0644] sāmaṇerānaṃ, phātikammanti sambandho. Bhājetvāti sāmaṇerānaṃ bhājetvā. Iminā sāmaṇerānaṃ phātikammaṃ na dātabbampi bhāgaṃ bhājetabbanti dasseti.

Panasarukkhaṃ means 'a jackfruit tree,' that is, 'a tree with thorny fruit'. Ayaṃ sāmīcīti means 'this is proper,' that is, 'dividing and eating it is in accordance with the Dhamma'. Khāyitanti means 'eaten,' that is, 'consumed'. Since the resolution of an agreement for two or three could be understood by analogy, without presenting that, he shows the resolution of an agreement for just one, saying, 'but in the case of one monk,' and so on. Purimakatikāti means 'the earlier agreement,' that is, 'the agreement made earlier: 'It is agreeable to use as one pleases' (Pari. Aṭṭh. 495–496)'. Tesanti refers to the novices; phātikammanti is the connection. Bhājetvāti means 'having divided,' that is, 'having distributed to the novices'. By this, it is shown that a share should be divided, even if it is not to be given to the novices as a transaction.

Sāmantagāmehīti āsannagāmehi, āgantvāti sambandho. Ekaṃ ambaṃ ekaṃ labujanti yojanā. Adiyyamāne dose dassite diyyamāne ānisaṃsampi atthato ñātabbanti dassento āha “adiyyamāne hī”tiādi.

Sāmantagāmehīti means 'from nearby villages'; the connection is with 'having come'. Ekaṃ ambaṃ ekaṃ labujanti is the construction. To show that since the fault in not giving is shown, the benefit in giving should also be understood in its meaning, he says, 'when not being given,' and so on.

Gaṇhantānaṃ manussānanti sambandho. Tatoti katikavattaṭṭhapanato. Na vattabbāti phaladānakuladūsakattā na vattabbā. Kinti ācikkhitabbanti āha “nāḷikerādīnī”tiādi. Anuvicaritvāti padānamanukkamena vicaritvā. Upaḍḍhabhāgoti bhikkhūnaṃ laddhabhāgato upaḍḍho bhāgo. Apaloketvāti saṅghaṃ āpucchitvā.

Gaṇhantānaṃ manussānanti is the connection. Tatoti means 'from the establishment of the agreed procedure'. Na vattabbāti means 'they should not be spoken to because they are corrupters of families that give fruit'. To the question, 'How should it be explained?' he says, 'coconuts, etc.,' and so on. Anuvicaritvāti means 'having gone about in sequence of the offerings'. Upaḍḍhabhāgoti means 'half the share from the share received by the monks'. Apaloketvāti means 'having asked the Saṅgha'.

Maggagamiyasatthavāhoti maggaṃ gamiko satthavāho. Soti balakkārena gahetvā khādanto. Chāyādīnantiādisaddena [V 2.0267] ārāmavanāni saṅgahetabbāni. Sace atthīti sace attho atthi. Phalabharitāti phalena paripuṇṇā. “Phalabhāritā”tipi pāṭho. Phalasaṅkhātena bhārena samannāgatāti attho. Apaccāsīsantenāti tesaṃ santikā dānapaṭidānaṃ apaccāsīsantena. Pubbe vuttamevāti pubbe saṅghikaṭṭhāne “kuddho hi so”tiādinā vuttameva. Etthāti puggalikaṭṭhāne.

Maggagamiyasatthavāhoti means a caravan leader who travels the road. Soti means 'he who takes and eats by force'. Chāyādīnanti—by the word 'etc.', parks and groves should be included. Sace atthīti means 'if there is a need'. Phalabharitāti means 'full of fruit'. 'Phalabhāritā' is also a reading. The meaning is 'endowed with the weight consisting of fruit'. Apaccāsīsantenāti means 'without expecting a gift in return from them'. Pubbe vuttamevāti means 'as previously stated in the context of what belongs to the Saṅgha: "For he is angry," etc.' Etthāti means 'here, in the context of what is personal'.

Tanti phalārāmaṃ. Soti paṭibalo bhikkhu. Bhāriyaṃ kammanti jagganakammaṃ bhāriyaṃ. Ettakenāti tatiyabhāgaupaḍḍhabhāgamattena. Sabbaṃ phalārāmanti sambandho. Mūlabhāganti paṭhamabhāgaṃ. “Dasabhāgamatta”nti iminā tadatthaṃ dasseti. Datvāti saṅghassa datvā. Soti bhikkhu. Akatāvāsanti pubbe akataṃ navaṃ senāsanaṃ. Ārāmanti saṅghassa ārāmaṃ. Tehipīti nissitakehipi. Pisaddo ācariyaṃ apekkhati. Tesanti nissitakānaṃ. Jaggitakāleti jaggitānaṃ rukkhānaṃ pupphaphalabharitakāle. Jagganakāleti jagganamattakāle, jagganamattameva, na jagganakāraṇā [M 0.0645] kiñci pupphaṃ vā phalaṃ vā hoti, tasmiṃ kāleti attho. “Bahu”ntiādinā vāretabbākāraṃ dasseti.

Tanti means 'that fruit park'. Soti means 'a capable monk'. Bhāriyaṃ kammanti means 'the duty of tending is weighty'. Ettakenāti means 'by just a third part or a half part'. Sabbaṃ phalārāmanti is the connection. Mūlabhāganti means 'the first portion'. By 'a tenth part', it shows the meaning of that. Datvāti means 'having given to the Saṅgha'. Soti means 'the monk'. Akatāvāsanti means 'a new dwelling, not made before'. Ārāmanti means 'the Saṅgha's park'. Tehipīti means 'even by the dependents'. The word 'pi' refers to the teacher. Tesanti means 'of the dependents'. Jaggitakāleti means 'at the time when the tended trees are laden with flowers and fruit'. Jagganakāleti means 'at the time of merely tending'; the meaning is 'at the time when there is only the act of tending, and there is no flower or fruit on account of that tending'. By 'much,' etc., he shows the manner of what should be prevented.

Phātikammena jagganto na atthīti yojanā. Anāpucchitvāvāti saṅghaṃ anapaloketvāva. Itīti evaṃ.

The construction is: 'There is no one tending it as a transaction'. Anāpucchitvāvāti means 'without having asked the Saṅgha, that is, without having sought permission'. Itīti means 'thus'.

Ñattikammaṭṭhānabhede pana evaṃ vinicchayo veditabboti yojanā. Osāreti saṅghamajjhaṃ paveseti imāya ñattiyāti osāraṇā.

The construction is: 'However, in the classification of the grounds for a formal act with a motion, the decision should be understood thus'. One introduces (`osāreti`), that is, makes enter (`paveseti`) into the midst of the Saṅgha by this motion (`imāya ñattiyā`); thus, it is `osāraṇā` (introduction).

Nissāriyati saṅghato bahi kariyati imāyāti nissāraṇā. Ñatti uposatho nāmāti idaṃ kāraṇūpacāravasena vuttaṃ. Tenāha “uposathakammavasena ṭhapitā”ti. Eseva nayo ñattipavāraṇā nāmāti etthāpi.

One is expelled (`nissāriyati`), that is, one is put outside (`bahi kariyati`) of the Saṅgha by this (`imāya`); thus, it is `nissāraṇā` (expulsion). 'A motion is called the Uposatha'—this is said by way of a figurative expression based on the cause. Therefore, he said, 'established by way of the Uposatha act'. This same principle also applies here in 'a motion is called the Pavāraṇā'.

Anusāseyyātiādinā paṭhamapurisaeyyavibhattivasena ṭhapitā ñatti attanā paraṃ sammanituṃ ṭhapitā ñatti nāma. Anusāseyyantiādinā uttamapurisaeyyaṃvibhattivasena ṭhapitā ñatti attanāva attānaṃ sammanituṃ ṭhapitā ñatti nāma. Attanāva attā vā paro vā sammaniyati imāya ñattiyāti sammuti. Nissaṭṭhapattacīvarādīni dīyanti anenāti dānaṃ, ñatti. Vaccaṃ anapekkhitvā vācakassa niyatanapuṃsakaliṅgattā napuṃsakaliṅgavasena vuttaṃ.

By 'should instruct,' etc., a motion established with the third-person optative ending is called a motion established to appoint another by oneself. By 'I should instruct,' etc., a motion established with the first-person optative ending is called a motion established to appoint oneself by oneself. One appoints oneself or another by oneself with this motion; thus, it is `sammuti` (appointment). Forfeited bowls, robes, etc., are given by this (`anena`); thus, it is a `dāna` (giving) motion. Without regard to the gender of the thing spoken of, it is stated in the neuter gender due to the fixed neuter gender of the word expressing it.

Āpatti [V 2.0268] paṭiggaṇhiyati anenāti paṭiggaho.

An offense is accepted by this; thus, it is `paṭiggaho` (acceptance).

Paṭimukhaṃ upari kaḍḍhiyati imāyāti paccukkaḍḍhanā.

It is drawn up (`kaḍḍhiyati`) again (`paṭi`) in front (`mukhaṃ`) by this (`imāya`); thus, it is `paccukkaḍḍhanā` (rejection).

Kammamevāti lakkhiyati anenāti kammalakkhaṇaṃ.

An act itself is marked by this; thus, it is `kammalakkhaṇa` (the characteristic of an act).

“Tathā”ti padena “kammalakkhaṇaṃ nāmā”ti padaṃ atidisati. Tatoti sabbasaṅgāhikañattito. Parā dve ñattiyo kammalakkhaṇaṃ nāmāti yojanā. Itītiādi nigamanaṃ.

By the word 'tathā', the phrase 'is called the characteristic of an act' is applied by extension. Tatoti means 'from the all-inclusive motion'. The construction is that the other two motions are called 'the characteristic of an act'. 'Iti,' etc., is the conclusion.

Ñattidutiyakammaṭṭhānabhede osāraṇādīnaṃ visesaṃ dassento āha “vaḍḍhassa licchavino”tiādi. Sīmāsammuti cātiādinā yojanā kātabbā.

In the classification of the grounds for a formal act with a motion and one announcement, showing the distinction of 'introduction' and so on, he says, 'of the Licchavi Vaḍḍha,' and so on. The construction should be made with 'agreement on a boundary,' etc.

Yā [M 0.0646] pana dve ñattidutiyakammavācā vuttāti yojanā. Itītiādi nigamanaṃ.

The construction is: 'As for the two proclamations for a formal act with a motion and one announcement that were spoken of...' 'Iti,' etc., is the conclusion.

Ñatticatutthakammaṭṭhānabhede yojanānayo pākaṭoyeva.

In the classification of the grounds for a formal act with a motion and three announcements, the method of construction is indeed obvious.

497. Catuvaggakaraṇe kammetiādikāya desanāya sambandhaṃ dassento āha “iti kammāni cā”tiādi. Tattha itīti evaṃ dassetvāti sambandho. Tassatthoti tassa “catuvaggakaraṇe kamme”tiādivacanassa attho veditabboti sambandho.

497. Showing the connection with the teaching beginning 'the act in making a fourfold group,' he says, 'thus the acts,' and so on. There, the connection is: 'iti' means 'having shown thus'. Tassatthoti means 'the meaning of that statement beginning "the act in making a fourfold group" should be understood'—this is the connection.

Iti kammavaggavaṇṇanāya yojanā samattā.

Thus ends the explanation of the construction of the commentary on the Chapter on Acts.

Atthavasavaggādivaṇṇanā

The Commentary on the Chapter on the Grounds for Benefit and so on.

498. Evaṃ kammavaggavaṇṇanaṃ dassetvā tassānantare vuttāya “dve atthavase paṭiccā”tiādikāya desanāya anusandhiṃ dassento āha “idānī”tiādi, idāni āraddhanti sambandho. Yāni tāni sikkhāpadānīti yojanā. Diṭṭhadhammikaverānanti diṭṭhadhamme pavattattā ca viramitabbattā ca diṭṭhadhammikānaṃ verānaṃ. Saṃvarāyāti ettha saṃpubbo varadhātu pidahanattho, āyasaddo ca tadatthoti āha “pidahanatthāyā”ti. Vipākadukkhasaṅkhātānanti pāṇātipātādīnaṃ [V 2.0269] vipākabhūtānaṃ dukkhasaṅkhātānaṃ. Samparāyikānanti samparāye pavattānaṃ. Idhāti imasmiṃ sikkhāpadapaññattānisaṃsaṭṭhāne. “Vajjanīyabhāvato”ti iminā vajjetabbānīti vajjānīti vacanatthaṃ dasseti. Bhāyanti etehīti bhayāni. Akkhamaṭṭhenāti asahaṇīyaṭṭhena. “Akusalānīti vuccantī”ti iminā vipākadukkhāni phalūpacārena akusalāni nāmāti dasseti. Gaṇabandhabhedanatthāya sikkhāpadaṃ paññattanti evameva pāṭho. Potthakesu pana “gaṇabhojanasikkhāpadaṃ paññatta”nti pāṭho likhito. Sabbatthāti sabbasmiṃ atthavasavagge. Yanti vacanaṃ. Etthāti imasmiṃ vagge.

498. Having thus shown the commentary on the Chapter on Acts, showing the connection with the teaching spoken immediately after it, beginning 'depending on two grounds for benefit,' he says, 'now,' etc. The connection is: 'now begun'. The construction is: 'those training rules'. Diṭṭhadhammikaverānanti means 'of enmities pertaining to the present life', because they occur in the present life and should be refrained from. Saṃvarāyāti—here, the root 'var' preceded by 'saṃ' has the meaning of covering, and the word 'āya' also has that meaning; therefore, he says, 'for the purpose of covering'. Vipākadukkhasaṅkhātānanti means 'of what is designated as the suffering of results', which are the results of killing and so on. Samparāyikānanti means 'of those that occur in the future life'. Idhāti means 'here, in this context of the benefit of laying down the training rule'. By 'because of the state of being something to be avoided,' it shows the meaning of the word 'vajja' is 'what should be avoided'. One is afraid on account of these; thus, they are `bhayāni` (fears). Akkhamaṭṭhenāti means 'in the sense of being unbearable'. By 'they are called unwholesome,' it is shown that the suffering of results is called 'unwholesome' by a figurative expression based on the fruit. 'The training rule was laid down for the purpose of breaking the group-bond'—this is indeed the reading. In the books, however, the reading is written as 'the training rule on group meals was laid down'. Sabbatthāti means 'in every instance in the Chapter on the Grounds for Benefit'. Yanti is the word. Etthāti means 'in this chapter'.

Iti atthavasavaggavaṇṇanāya yojanā samattā.

Thus ends the explanation of the construction of the commentary on the Chapter on the Grounds for Benefit.

499. Vattesu vattamāno puggalo osārīyati anenāti osāraṇīyaṃ, kammaṃ. Tena vuttaṃ “yena kammena osārīyati, taṃ kammaṃ [M 0.0647] paññatta”nti. “Yena kammenā”tiādinā bhaṇḍanakārakādayo nissārīyanti anena kammenāti nissāraṇīyanti vacanatthaṃ dasseti.

499. A person engaged in duties is introduced by this; thus, it is `osāraṇīyaṃ` (introduction), an act. Therefore, it is said: 'The act by which one is introduced, that act is prescribed'. By 'by which act,' etc., it shows the meaning of the word `nissāraṇīya` as 'those who cause quarrels and the like are expelled by this act'.

500. Sattāpattikkhandhā paññattaṃ nāmāti sambandho. Antarāti kakusandhādīnaṃ tiṇṇaṃ buddhānañca amhākaṃ bhagavato ca antare. “Sikkhāpade”ti iminā “apaññatte”ti padassa atthaṃ dasseti. Makkaṭīvatthuādivinītakathā anupaññattaṃ nāmāti sambandho. “Sikkhāpade”ti iminā “paññatte”ti padassa atthaṃ dasseti. Sabbatthāti sabbasmiṃ ānisaṃsavagge.

500. The connection is: the seven aggregates of offenses are called 'established' (paññattaṃ). 'Antara' means in the interval between the three Buddhas, Kakusandha and others, and our Blessed One. By 'in the training rule' (sikkhāpade), it shows the meaning of the word 'unestablished' (apaññatte). The connection is: the decided cases, beginning with the story of the monkey, are called 'subsequently established' (anupaññattaṃ). By 'in the training rule' (sikkhāpade), it shows the meaning of the word 'established' (paññatte). 'Sabbattha' means in every instance in the Ānisaṃsavagga.

Iti ānisaṃsavaggavaṇṇanāya yojanā samattā.

Thus, the explanation of the syntax for the commentary on the Ānisaṃsavagga is completed.

501. Sabbasikkhāpadānaṃ saṅgahanti sambandho. Tatthāti “nava saṅgahā”tiādipāṭhe evamattho veditabboti yojanā. “Vatthunā saṅgaho”ti iminā “vatthusmiṃ, vatthūnaṃ saṅgaho”ti atthaṃ nivāreti. Etthāti “vatthusaṅgaho”tiādipāṭhe. Hīti vitthāro. Yasmā natthīti sambandho. Sabbānīti sikkhāpadāni. “Saṅgahitānī”ti iminā saṅgahitabboti saṅgahoti nibbacanaṃ dasseti. Evaṃ tāvātiādi nigamanaṃ.

501. The connection is: 'the collection of all the training rules'. 'Tattha' means: in the reading beginning 'nine collections,' the meaning should be understood thus—this is the explanation of the syntax. By 'collection by subject matter,' it precludes the meaning 'a collection in the subject matter' or 'a collection of subject matters'. 'Ettha' means in the reading beginning 'collection of subject matters'. 'Hi' means 'explanation'. The connection is: 'because there is not'. 'Sabbāni' means 'all the training rules'. By 'saṅgahitāni' (collected), it shows the etymology that 'saṅgaha' (collection) is that which is to be collected. 'Evaṃ tāva' and so on is the conclusion.

Yasmā pana saṅgahitāti sambandho.

However, the connection is: 'because it is collected'.

Evametthātiādinā [V 2.0270] khandhasamuṭṭhānaadhikaraṇasamathe sampiṇḍetvā nigamanaṃ dasseti. Etthāti saṅgahavagge.

By 'Thus, here...' and so on, it shows the conclusion by summarizing the aggregates, origins, legal questions, and settlements. 'Ettha' means in the Saṅgahavagga.

Iti samantapāsādikāya vinayasaṃvaṇṇanāya

Thus, in the Samantapāsādikā, the commentary on the Vinaya,

Navasaṅgahitavaṇṇanāya yojanā samattā.

The explanation of the syntax for the commentary on the Nine Collections is completed.

Niṭṭhitāti niṭṭhaṃ nipphattiṃ itā gatāti niṭṭhitā, atha vā niṭṭhe nipphattiyaṃ itā ṭhitāti niṭṭhitā. Casaddo avadhāraṇattho, niṭṭhitā evāti hi attho. Anuttānatthapadavaṇṇanāti anuttānānaṃ atthavantapadānaṃ, atthānañca padānañca vaṇṇanā.

'Niṭṭhitā' means: having gone to completion or accomplishment; thus, 'niṭṭhitā'. Or else, standing in completion or accomplishment; thus, 'niṭṭhitā'. The word 'ca' has the meaning of emphasis; for indeed, the meaning is 'it is truly finished'. 'Anuttānatthapadavaṇṇanā' is the explanation of meaningful words that are not obvious, and of meanings and words.

Iti parivāravaṇṇanāya yojanā samattā.

Thus, the explanation of the syntax for the commentary on the Parivāra is completed.

Niṭṭhitā ca pācityādivaṇṇanāya yojanāti.

And the explanation of the syntax for the commentary on the Pācittiya and so on is completed.

Jādilañchitanāmenanekānaṃ [M 0.0648] vācito mayā;

Parivāravinayassa, samatto yojanānayo.

By me, who has taught many and whose name is marked with 'Jādila', the method of explaining the syntax for the Parivāra Vinaya has been completed.
