Nigamanakathāvaṇṇanā

The Explanation of the Discourse on the Conclusion

Evaṃ vinayasaṃvaṇṇanaṃ katvā idāni taṃ nigamento āha “ettāvatā”tiādi. Tattha ettāvatāti ettakena “yo kappakoṭīhipi appameyya”ntiādivacanato (pārā. aṭṭha. 1.ganthārambhakathā) paṭṭhāya “navasaṅgahitavaggavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā”ti vacanapariyosānānaṃ akkharapadabyañjanānaṃ samudāyabhūtena vacanakkamena, samattāti sambandho.

Having thus composed the commentary on the Vinaya, now, concluding it, he says, 'to this extent,' and so on. Therein, 'to this extent' means by this much: by that sequence of speech which is the aggregate of letters, words, and syllables, from the statement beginning 'one who is immeasurable even by crores of aeons' (Pārā. Aṭṭha. 1. Ganthārambhakathā) up to the final words, 'the commentary on the chapter of the nine collections is finished'—'is complete' is the connection.

Ubhatovibhaṅgakhandhakaparivāravibhattidesananti ubhatovibhaṅgena ca khandhakena ca parivārena ca vibhajitabbadesanaṃ vinayapiṭakanti sambandho. Nāthoti bhikkhubhikkhunīnaṃ hitapaṭipattiṃ yācanaṭṭhena ca kilesānaṃ upatāpanaṭṭhena ca veneyyānaṃ hitasukhaṃ āsīsanaṭṭhena ca cittissariyaṭṭhena ca nātho. Veneyyanti vinetabbaṭṭhena veneyyaṃ. Jinoti pañcamārānaṃ jitaṭṭhena jino. Ayaṃ panettha yojanā – nātho veneyyaṃ vinento jino ubhatovibhaṅgakhandhakaparivāravibhattidesanaṃ yaṃ vinayapiṭakaṃ āhāti.

'The teaching divided into the Ubhatovibhaṅga, the Khandhaka, and the Parivāra' means the teaching to be divided by the Ubhatovibhaṅga, the Khandhaka, and the Parivāra, which is the Vinaya Piṭaka—this is the connection. The Protector (Nātha) is so called because he is besought for the beneficial practice of monks and nuns, because of tormenting the defilements, because of wishing for the benefit and happiness of those to be trained, and because of lordship over the mind. 'Those to be trained' (Veneyya) are so called because they are to be trained. 'The Victor' (Jina) is so called because he has conquered the five Māras. This is the explanation of the syntax here: The Protector, the Victor, while training those to be trained, spoke the Vinaya Piṭaka, which is the teaching divided into the Ubhatovibhaṅga, the Khandhaka, and the Parivāra.

Samadhikasattavīsatisahassamattenāti saha adhikena sattasahassappamāṇena ca vīsatisahassappamāṇena [V 2.0271] ca ganthenāti sambandho. Tassāti vinayapiṭakassa. Samantapāsādikāti samantato pasādaṃ vahikā, janikā vā. Tatrāyaṃ yojanā – tassa samadhikasattavīsatisahassamattena ganthena samantapāsādikā nāma saṃvaṇṇanā samattāti.

'By the measure of twenty-seven thousand with an excess' means by a text of twenty-seven thousand and more—this is the connection. 'Tassa' means of that Vinaya Piṭaka. 'Samantapāsādikā' means that which brings or generates faith all around. This is the explanation of the syntax there: of that Vinaya Piṭaka, the commentary named Samantapāsādikā, with a text of twenty-seven thousand and more, is completed.

Tatridanti tatra idaṃ. “Tatrā”ti padaṃ purimavacanāpekkhaṃ. Tatra “samantapāsādikā nāmā”ti vacaneti hi attho. Samantapāsādikattasminti paccattatthe cetaṃ bhummavacanaṃ hoti “idampi sīlasmi”ntiādīsu (dī. ni. 1.194 ādayo) viya, samantapāsādikattanti attho. Ayaṃ panettha yojanātatra “samantapāsādikā nāmā”ti vacane samantapāsādikāya idaṃ samantapāsādikattaṃ [M 0.0649] hotīti ayaṃ samantapāsādikabhāvoti attho.

'Tatridan'ti means 'tatra idaṃ' (there, this). The word 'tatrā' refers to the preceding statement. Indeed, the meaning is in the statement 'Samantapāsādikā by name.' 'Samantapāsādikattasmiṃ' is a locative case used in the sense of individuality, as in 'idampi sīlasmiṃ' (Dī. Ni. 1.194, etc.), meaning 'this too is in virtue,' and it means 'the state of being Samantapāsādikā.' This is the explanation of the syntax here: in the statement 'Samantapāsādikā by name,' this state of being Samantapāsādikā exists for the Samantapāsādikā; that is, this is the nature of being Samantapāsādikā.

Ācariyaparaṃparatotiādīsu gāthāsu vuttaṃ navavidhaṃ visesanapadaṃ “na dissatī”ti padena sambandhitabbaṃ. Sampassatanti sammā passantānaṃ viññūnanti sambandho. Yatoti yasmā, na dissatīti sambandho. Etthāti saṃvaṇṇanāyaṃ. Samantapāsādikātvevāti samantapāsādikā iti eva nāma. Vinayassāti vinayapiṭakassa. Vineyyadamanakusalenāti vineyyānaṃ damane chekena. Lokanāthenāti lokānaṃ nāthena. Lokamanukampamānenāti lokaṃ anukampamānena. Ayañhettha yojanā – ācariyaparaṃparato…pe… vibhaṅganayabhedadassanato sampassataṃ viññūnaṃ ettha kiñci apāsādikaṃ yato na dissati, tasmā vineyyadamanakusalena lokanāthena lokamanukampamānena bhagavatā vuttassa vinayassa ayaṃ samantapāsādikātveva saṃvaṇṇanā pavattāti.

In the verses beginning with ‘Ācariyaparaṃparato,’ the ninefold qualifying phrase mentioned should be connected with the phrase ‘na dissatī.’ ‘Sampassataṃ’ is connected with ‘of the wise’ (viññūnaṃ), meaning ‘of those who rightly see.’ ‘Yato’ means ‘because’ and is connected with ‘na dissatī’ (‘is not seen’). ‘Ettha’ means ‘in this commentary.’ ‘Samantapāsādikātveva’ means ‘it is indeed named Samantapāsādikā.’ ‘Vinayassa’ means ‘of the Vinaya Piṭaka.’ ‘Vineyyadamanakusalena’ means ‘by one skilled in taming those who are to be tamed.’ ‘Lokanāthena’ means ‘by the Lord of the World.’ ‘Lokamanukampamānena’ means ‘by one who has compassion for the world.’ This is the explanation of the syntax here: Because nothing unpleasing is seen here by the wise who rightly see—from the lineage of teachers... up to the discernment of the distinctions in the method of analysis—therefore, this commentary on the Vinaya spoken by the Blessed One—who is skilled in taming those to be tamed, the Lord of the World, compassionate towards the world—proceeds as indeed the ‘Samantapāsādikā’.

Tissopi imā sīhaḷaṭṭhakathāyo sutvāti sambandho. Kassa santike sutanti āha “buddhamitto…pe… santike”ti. “Buddhamitto”ti nāmena vissutassa yasassino vinayaññussa dhīrassa therassa santike sutvāti yojanā. “Sutvā”ti padaṃ “āraddhā”ti pade pubbakālakiriyāvisesanaṃ.

'Tissa also, having heard these Sinhalese commentaries'—this is the connection. In whose presence were they heard? He says, 'in the presence of Buddhamitta… and so on'. The explanation of the syntax is: having heard in the presence of the elder renowned by the name 'Buddhamitta', who was glorious, wise, and a knower of the Vinaya. The word 'sutvā' is an adverb of prior action modifying the word 'āraddhā'.

Mahāmeghavanuyyāne bhūmibhāge patiṭṭhito satthu mahābodhivibhūsito yo mahāvihāro atthīti yojanā.

The explanation of the syntax is: there is that great monastery which is established on a plot of land in the Mahāmeghavana park, adorned with the Teacher’s great Bodhi tree.

Tassa mahāvihārassa dakkhiṇe disābhāge padhānagharaṃ padhānagharanāmakaṃ uttamaṃ sucicārittasīlena bhikkhusaṅghena sevitaṃ yaṃ pariveṇaṃ atthi, tattha kārayīti yojanā.

The explanation of the syntax is: he had it constructed there, in that excellent residence named Padhānaghara, a meditation hall in the southern quarter of that great monastery, which is frequented by the community of monks of pure virtue and conduct.

Konāmo [V 2.0272] kārayīti āha “uḷārakulasambhūto…pe… vissuto”ti. Tattha uḷārakulasambhūto saṅghupaṭṭhāyako sadā anākulāya saddhāya ratanattaye pasanno “mahānigamasāmī”ti vissuto upāsako kārayīti sambandho.

Who had it constructed? He says, ‘born of a distinguished family… and so on… well-known’. Here, the connection is: a lay follower, born of a distinguished family, a supporter of the Sangha, always with unwavering faith, devoted to the Triple Gem, well-known as ‘Mahānigamasāmī,’ had it constructed.

Kaṃ [M 0.0650] kārayīti āha “cāru…pe… sampannasalilāsaya”nti. Tattha cārupākārasaṃcitaṃ sobhena pākārena suṭṭhu citaṃ cinitaṃ manoramaṃ sītacchāyatarūpetaṃ sītacchāyena rukkhena upetaṃ sampannasalilāsayaṃ madhurajalādhāraṃ yaṃ pāsādaṃ kārayīti yojanā. Mahānigamasāmino tatra pāsāde vasatāmayāti sambandho.

What was constructed? He says, ‘charming… and so on… endowed with an excellent water reservoir’. Here, the explanation of the syntax is: he had constructed that mansion which was charming and well-enclosed by a wall—meaning, well-built with a beautiful wall—delightful, endowed with cool, shady trees, and having a reservoir of sweet water. The connection is: by me, residing in that mansion of Mahānigamasāmī.

Kaṃ uddisitvā kīdisā kā āraddhāti āha “sucisīlasamācāraṃ…pe… vinayavaṇṇanā”ti. Tattha sucisīlasamācāraṃ buddhasirivhayaṃ theraṃ uddisitvā iddhā atthavinicchayādīhi paripuṇṇā yā vinayavaṇṇanā āraddhāti yojanā.

For whom was it intended, and what kind of work was begun? He says, ‘of pure virtue and conduct… and so on… the commentary on the Vinaya’. Here, the explanation of the syntax is: having intended it for the elder named Buddhasiri, who is of pure virtue and conduct, that commentary on the Vinaya was begun which is prosperous and complete with determinations of meaning and so on.

Kiṃnāmassa rañño katame saṃvacchare āraddhā, kismiṃ kāle pariniṭṭhitāti āha “pālayantassa…pe… pariniṭṭhitā”ti. Tattha sakalaṃ laṅkādīpaṃ nirabbudaṃ katvāti sambandho. Pālayantassa sirinivāsassa siripālayasassino rañño jayasaṃvacchareti sambandho. Samavīsatime kheme jayasaṃvacchare ayaṃ vinayasaṃvaṇṇanā āraddhā, ekavīsamhi rañño ekavīsatime saṃvacchare sampatte sati pariniṭṭhitāti yojanā.

In which year of which king was it begun, and at what time was it completed? He says, ‘while ruling… and so on… it was completed’. Here, the connection is: ‘having made the entire island of Lanka free from disturbance’. The connection is: in the year of victory of the illustrious King Sirinivāsa, possessor of glorious protection, while he was ruling. The interpretation is: this Vinaya commentary was begun in the twentieth auspicious year of victory, and it was completed when the twenty-first year of the king’s reign arrived.

Yathā attano saṃvaṇṇanā nirupaddavā sīghaṃ niṭṭhaṃ upagatā, evaṃ lokassa dhammūpasaṃhitā sīghaṃ gacchantūti āsīsaṃ dassento āha “upaddavākule”tiādi. Tattha upaddavākule upaddavehi ākule loke sattaloke nirupaddavato upaddavavirahato yathā ayaṃ vinayasaṃvaṇṇanā ekasaṃvacchareneva niṭṭhaṃ upāgatā, evaṃ sabbassa lokassa āraddhā sabbepi dhammūpasaṃhitā atthā nirupaddavā sīghaṃ niṭṭhaṃ gacchantūti yojanā.

Just as his own commentary, being free from obstacles, quickly reached completion, so too may all undertakings connected with the Dhamma swiftly progress for the world—thus, expressing this wish, he says, ‘upaddavākule’ and so on. Here, ‘upaddavākule’ means in a world afflicted with calamities, the world of beings, free from obstacles, devoid of obstacles. The interpretation is: just as this Vinaya commentary, being free from obstacles, was completed in a single year, so too may all Dhamma-related matters undertaken for the entire world, being free from obstacles, swiftly reach completion.

Attanā samācitassa puññassa icchitatthe pariṇāmanaṃ dassento āha “ciraṭṭhitatthaṃ dhammassā”tiādi. Tattha dhammassa ciraṭṭhitatthaṃ imaṃ vinayasaṃvaṇṇanaṃ karontena saddhammabahumānena mayā yañca puññaṃ samācitaṃ, sabbassa tassa puññassa ānubhāvena sabbepi pāṇino dhammarājassa bhagavato saddhammarasasevino bhavantu.

Showing the dedication of the merit he himself has accumulated for the desired purpose, he says, ‘ciraṭṭhitatthaṃ dhammassā’ and so on. Here, by composing this Vinaya commentary for the long endurance of the Dhamma, out of reverence for the true Dhamma, whatever merit I have accumulated, may all beings, through the power of all that merit, become partakers of the nectar of the true Dhamma of the Blessed One, the King of Dhamma.

Saddhammo [M 0.0651][V 2.0273] ciraṃ tiṭṭhatu, devo kāle vassaṃ vassanto ciraṃ pajaṃ sattasamūhaṃ tappetu. Rājā dhammena medaniṃ rakkhatūti yojanā. Itisaddo parisamāpanattho. Iti pariniṭṭhaṃ suṭṭhu āpanaṃ daṭṭhabbantīti attho.

The interpretation is: may the true Dhamma long endure. May the deva rain in due season, and may he long delight the masses, the multitude of beings. May the king protect the earth righteously. The word ‘iti’ serves to conclude. The meaning is: thus, it is completely finished and should be seen as a very good acquisition.

Saddhā ca buddhi ca vīriyañca saddhābuddhivīriyāni, visuddhāni ca tāni saddhābuddhivīriyāni ceti visuddhasaddhābuddhivīriyāni, paramāni ca tāni visuddhasaddhābuddhivīriyāni ceti paramavisuddhasaddhābuddhivīriyāni, tehi parimaṇḍito paramavisuddhasaddhābuddhivīriyapaṭimaṇḍito, tena, therenāti sambandho. Sīlañca ācāro ca ajjavañca maddavañca sīlācārajjavamaddavāni, tāni ādīni yesaṃ teti sīlācārajjavamaddavādayo, ādisaddena khantisoraccādayo saṅgaṇhāti, teyeva guṇāti sīlācārajjavamaddavādiguṇā, tesaṃ samudayoti sīlācārajjavamaddavādiguṇasamudayo, tena samudito suṭṭhu pākaṭoti sīlācārajjavamaddavādiguṇasamudayasamudito, tena therenāti sambandho.

Faith, wisdom, and energy—these are ‘saddhābuddhivīriyāni.’ And those faith, wisdom, and energy are pure, thus ‘visuddhasaddhābuddhivīriyāni.’ And those purified faith, wisdom, and energy are supreme, thus ‘paramavisuddhasaddhābuddhivīriyāni.’ Endowed with these, he is ‘paramavisuddhasaddhābuddhivīriyapaṭimaṇḍito’—this is the connection with the elder. Virtue, conduct, honesty, and gentleness—these are ‘sīlācārajjavamaddavāni.’ Those and others beginning with them are ‘sīlācārajjavamaddavādayo.’ By the term ‘ādi’ are included patience, meekness, and so forth. These very qualities are ‘sīlācārajjavamaddavādiguṇā.’ Their collection is ‘sīlācārajjavamaddavādiguṇasamudayo.’ Endowed with that collection, and thus clearly manifest, is ‘sīlācārajjavamaddavādiguṇasamudayasamudito’—this is the connection with the elder.

Sakasamayo ca samayantaro ca sakasamayasamayantarā, teyeva pana gahanasadisattā gahananti sakasamayasamayantaragahanaṃ, tassa ajjhogāhaṇaṃ sakasamayasamayantaragahanajjhogāhaṇaṃ, tasmiṃ samattho sakasamayasamayantaragahanajjhogāhaṇasamattho. Tena therenāti sambandho. Visesena añjati pākaṭaṃ karotīti viyatto, puggalo, viyattassa idaṃ veyyattiyaṃ, sati. Paññā ca veyyattiyañca paññāveyyattiyaṃ, tena samannāgatenāti sambandho. Samannāgatena therenāti yojanā.

One’s own system and another system are ‘sakasamayasamayantarā.’ These themselves, being like a thicket due to their difficulty, are a thicket, ‘sakasamayasamayantaragahanaṃ.’ The plunging into that is ‘sakasamayasamayantaragahanajjhogāhaṇaṃ.’ Capable in that is ‘sakasamayasamayantaragahanajjhogāhaṇasamattho.’ This is the connection with the elder. One who makes especially clear, makes manifest, is ‘viyatto,’ a person. This ‘veyyattiyaṃ’ is the perspicuity of the skilled one, which is mindfulness. Wisdom and skill is ‘paññāveyyattiyaṃ.’ The connection is with one endowed with that. The interpretation is: with the elder endowed with that.

Tīṇi piṭakānīti tipiṭakaṃ, tameva pariyāpuṇitabbattā pariyattīti tipiṭakapariyatti, tassa pabhedo ettha satthusāsaneti tipiṭakapariyattipabhedaṃ, tasmiṃ. Saha aṭṭhakathāyāti sāṭṭhakathaṃ, satthu sāsanaṃ, tasmiṃ satthusāsaneti sambandho. Satthuno pariyattipaṭipattipaṭivedhavasena tividhaṃ sāsanaṃ satthusāsanaṃ, byāsopi yujjateva, tasmiṃ satthusāsane “appaṭihata”iti padena sambandhitabbaṃ. Appaṭihataṃ ñāṇaṃ appaṭihatañāṇaṃ, idaṃ tasmiṃ vinayasaṃvaṇṇanākāle therassa paṭivedhañāṇābhāvato [M 0.0652] sutamayacintāmayañāṇaṃ sandhāya vuttanti daṭṭhabbaṃ. Appaṭihatañāṇassa pabhāvo etassāti appaṭihatañāṇapabhāvo, tena therenāti sambandho. Mahantaṃ veyyākaraṇametassāti mahāveyyākaraṇo, iminā sikkhāniruttiādīhi chaḷaṅge mahantaveyyākaraṇe therassa appaṭihatañāṇapabhāvataṃ dasseti, tena mahāveyyākaraṇena therenāti sambandho.

The three baskets are the Tipiṭaka. Because it is to be learned, it is called the Tipiṭaka as the Teaching (pariyatti). Its division here in the Teacher’s Dispensation is the division of the Tipiṭaka as the Teaching. ‘Saha aṭṭhakathāya’ means ‘sāṭṭhakathaṃ’, together with the commentaries. The Teacher’s Dispensation; the connection is with that, in the Teacher’s Dispensation. The Teacher’s Dispensation is threefold by way of learning, practice, and penetration; this analysis also fits. In that Teacher’s Dispensation, the word 'unobstructed' should be connected. Unobstructed knowledge is 'unobstructed knowledge.' This should be understood as referring to knowledge born of hearing and reflection, because at the time of composing the Vinaya commentary, the Elder lacked the knowledge of penetration. The power of unobstructed knowledge belongs to him, thus he is 'one with the power of unobstructed knowledge'; the connection is with that Elder. He is a great grammarian, thus 'the great grammarian.' By this, it shows the Elder’s power of unobstructed knowledge in the great grammar of the six limbs, beginning with phonetics and etymology. Thus, the connection is with that Elder, the great grammarian.

Karaṇaṃ vuccati ṭhānaṃ kariyati uccāriyati ettha, etenāti vā vacanatthena, karaṇassa sampatti [V 2.0274] karaṇasampatti, tāya janitaṃ karaṇasampattijanitaṃ. Sukhena theramukhato viniggataṃ sukhaviniggataṃ, karaṇasampattijanitena hetubhūtena sukhaviniggataṃ karaṇasampattijanitasukhaviniggataṃ. Madhuravacanañca udāravacanañca madhurodāravacanaṃ, pubbapade uttarapadalopo, iminā keṭubhapakaraṇe (subodhālaṃkāre 127-142 gāthāsu) vuttesu dasasu saddaguṇesu madhuratāguṇena ca udāratāguṇena ca samannāgatabhāvaṃ dasseti. Karaṇasampattijanitasukhaviniggatañca taṃ madhurodāravacanañceti karaṇasampattijanitasukhaviniggatamadhurodāravacanaṃ. Atha vā karaṇasampattijanitañca taṃ sukhaviniggatamadhurodāravacanañceti karaṇasampattijanitasukhaviniggatamadhurodāravacanaṃ. Elaṃ vuccati duruttadoso, natthi elametassāti nelā, soyeva vaṇṇo nelavaṇṇo, tena yuttaṃ nelavaṇṇayuttaṃ, karaṇasampattijanitasukhaviniggatamadhurodāravacanaṃ nelavaṇṇayuttametassāti karaṇasampattijanitasukhaviniggatamadhurodāravacananelavaṇṇayutto, thero. Visesanaparapadasamāso, nelavaṇṇayuttakaraṇasampatti janitasukhaviniggatamadhurodāravacanoti hi attho, tena therenāti sambandho. Yuttañca parisāya sotena anurūpattā, muttañca parisāya visāradattāti yuttamuttaṃ, vacanaṃ, taṃ vadati sīlenāti yuttamuttavādī, tena therenāti sambandho.

The organ of speech (`karaṇa`) is said to be the place of articulation, because something is done or uttered here, or by this, according to the meaning of the word; the accomplishment of this organ of speech is `karaṇasampatti`. What is produced by that is `karaṇasampattijanita`. What flows pleasantly from the Elder’s mouth is `sukhaviniggata`. What flows pleasantly, caused by the accomplishment of the organ of speech, is `karaṇasampattijanitasukhaviniggata`. Sweet speech and noble speech together are `madhurodāravacana`, with elision of the final part of the first word. By this, it shows the presence of the qualities of sweetness and nobility among the ten qualities of good speech mentioned in the Keṭubha treatise (Subodhālaṃkāra, verses 127–142). That sweet and noble speech which flows pleasantly, born of the accomplishment of the organ of speech, is `karaṇasampattijanitasukhaviniggatamadhurodāravacana`. Or alternatively, that pleasantly flowing, sweet, and noble speech which is born of the accomplishment of the organ of speech, is `karaṇasampattijanitasukhaviniggatamadhurodāravacana`. `Ela` is said to be the fault of harsh speech. Where there is no `ela`, it is `nelā`. That very quality is `nelavaṇṇa`. What is endowed with that is `nelavaṇṇayutta`. Thus, the Elder is `karaṇasampattijanitasukhaviniggatamadhurodāravacananelavaṇṇayutto`, meaning he has speech, born of the accomplishment of the organ of speech, pleasantly flowing, sweet, and noble, endowed with the quality of being faultless. This is a compound with the qualifying term at the end. Indeed, the meaning is: 'one endowed with faultless quality, with speech born of the accomplishment of the organ of speech, pleasantly flowing, sweet, and noble.' This connects with that Elder. The speech is `yutta` because it is fitting for the assembly, suiting their hearing, and it is `mutta` (clear) because of the assembly's confidence. Thus, `yuttamuttaṃ` is the speech. He speaks this habitually, therefore he is a `yuttamuttavādī`. This connects with that Elder.

Kammasassataucchedaissaranimmānādivasena [M 0.0653] nānā vādā etesanti vādino, nānāvādā janā, vādīnaṃ, vādīsu vā varo kammakiriyavādattāti vādivaro, tena therenāti sambandho. Pāḷiyā atthaṃ vaṇṇetuṃ samatthattā mahanto kavi mahākavi, tena therenāti sambandho.

Various doctrines, such as those based on karma, eternalism, annihilationism, creation by a Lord (Īśvara), and so on, belong to them, thus they are called disputants (vādino). These are people of diverse views. The best among the disputants, or among those holding views, is the one who teaches the doctrine of action and its result (kammakiriyavāda), thus he is the supreme disputant (vādivaro). This connects with that Elder. Because he is capable of explaining the meaning of the Pāli, he is a great poet, thus 'the great poet' (mahākavi). This connects with that Elder.

Atthadhammaniruttipaṭibhānavasena pabhinnāya paṭisambhidāya parivāritoti pabhinnapaṭisambhidāparivāro, tasmiṃ uttarimanussadhammeti sambandho. Cha abhiññā ca paṭisambhidā ca chaḷabhiññāpaṭisambhidā, tā ādayo yesaṃ teti chaḷabhiññāpaṭisambhidādayo, ādisaddena tevijjādayo saṅgaṇhāti. Chaḷabhiññāpaṭisambhidādayo pabhedā etassāti chaḷabhiññāpaṭisambhidādippabhedo, soyeva guṇo chaḷabhiññāpaṭisambhidādippabhedaguṇo, tena paṭimaṇḍito chaḷabhiññāpaṭisambhidādippabhedaguṇapaṭimaṇḍito, tasmiṃ uttarimanussadhammeti sambandho. Uttarimanussānaṃ jhānalābhiādīnaṃ dhammo uttarimanussadhammo, atha vā manussānaṃ kusalakammapathasaṅkhātadhammato uttarīti uttarimanussadhammo, jhānādidhammo, tasmiṃ, “suppatiṭṭhita” iti padena sambandhitabbaṃ. Suppatiṭṭhitā buddhi etesanti suppatiṭṭhitabuddhino, tesaṃ therānanti sambandho. Therānaṃ vaṃse pakārena dippanti, padīpo viyāti vā theravaṃsappadīpā, tesaṃ. Thiro sīlasamādhipaññāsaṅkhāto guṇo etesamatthīti therā, tesaṃ, vaṃsālaṅkārabhūtenāti sambandho. Mahāvihāre vasanasīlā vasanadhammā, vasane sādhukārīti vā mahāvihāravāsino, tesaṃ, therānanti sambandho[V 2.0275]. Vaṃse alaṅkāro, vaṃsassa vāti vaṃsālaṅkāro, so hutvā bhūto, vaṃsālaṅkārabhāvaṃ vā pattoti vaṃsālaṅkārabhūto, tena therenāti sambandho.

Surrounded by the analytical knowledges, which are distinguished by way of meaning, Dhamma, etymology, and inspiration—thus he is 'surrounded by the distinguished analytical knowledges.' The connection is with 'the superior human Dhamma' in this. The six direct knowledges and the analytical knowledges are the 'six direct knowledges and analytical knowledges.' Those who possess these and others like them are the 'possessors of the six direct knowledges and analytical knowledges and so on'; the term 'and so on' includes the threefold knowledge and others. The distinctions of these are the 'distinctions of the six direct knowledges and analytical knowledges and so on.' That very quality is the 'quality of the distinctions of the six direct knowledges and analytical knowledges and so on.' Adorned by this, he is 'adorned with the quality of the distinctions of the six direct knowledges and analytical knowledges and so on.' The connection is with 'the superior human Dhamma' in this. The Dhamma of superior humans—attainers of jhāna and so on—is the 'superior human Dhamma.' Alternatively, it is 'superior human Dhamma' because it surpasses the Dhamma of humans, which is reckoned as the wholesome courses of action. It is the Dhamma of jhāna and so on. In this, the word 'well-established' should be connected. Those whose wisdom is well-established are 'those with well-established wisdom.' The connection is with 'of those Elders.' They shine in a special way in the lineage of the Elders, or like a lamp—thus, they are the 'lamps of the Elders' lineage.' The connection is with 'of those.' Those who possess the steadfast quality reckoned as virtue, concentration, and wisdom are Elders. The connection is with 'by the one who has become the adornment of the lineage' among them. Those whose nature it is to dwell in the Great Monastery, or who are skilled in dwelling there—these are the 'dwellers of the Great Monastery.' The connection is with 'of those Elders.' The adornment in the lineage, or of the lineage—this is the 'adornment of the lineage.' Having become that, or having attained the state of being an adornment of the lineage—this is the 'one who has become the adornment of the lineage.' The connection is with that Elder.

Vipulā ca sā visuddhā ceti vipulavisuddhā, visesanobhayapado, vipulavisuddhā buddhi etassāti vipulavisuddhabuddhi, tena therenāti sambandho. Nāmameva nāmadheyyaṃ, gahitaṃ nāmadheyyametassāti gahitanāmadheyyo[M 0.0654], tena therena katā samantapāsādikā nāma ayaṃ vinayasaṃvaṇṇanā tiṭṭhatūti sambandho.

And it is vast and pure, thus 'vast and pure'—a compound of two qualifying terms. One who has vast and pure wisdom is 'one with vast and pure wisdom.' The connection is with that Elder. Name itself is designation. One whose designation has been taken is 'one with a taken designation.' The connection is: 'May this Vinaya commentary called Samantapāsādikā, made by that Elder, endure.'

Suddhacittassa tādino lokajeṭṭhassa mahesino “buddho”ti nāmampi yāva lokamhi pavattati, tāva lokanittharaṇesīnaṃ kulaputtānaṃ sīlavisuddhāya nayaṃ dassentī lokasmiṃ tiṭṭhatūti yojanā.

The construction is: As long as the name 'Buddha'—of the pure-hearted, the Stable One, the World's Foremost, the Great Seer—prevails in the world, so long may this work remain in the world, showing the method for the purification of virtue to sons of good family who seek deliverance from the world.

Iti nigamanassa atthayojanā samattā.

Thus the explanation of the meaning of the conclusion is finished.

Nigamanakathā

The Concluding Verses

Ettāvatā ca –

And thus far:

Ratanapuṇṇanāmassa, purassa rājadhāniyā;

Dakkhiṇe munirūpassa, īsaṃpācīnanissite.

To the south of the capital city named Ratanapuṇṇa, situated slightly to the east of the sage's image,

Yo vihāro sapāsādo, kārito rājadeviyā;

Yā vasatā mayā tatra, katā pācityādiyojanā.

is the monastery with its palace, caused to be built by the queen; while dwelling there, this exposition of the Pācittiya and so on was made by me.

Māpitaratnapuṇṇassa, sattaraseva rājino;

Jayavasseṭṭhārasamhi, sampatteyaṃ suniṭṭhitā.

This was well completed in the eighteenth year of the Victory, which was the seventeenth year of King Māpitaratnapuṇṇa.

“Ratanapuṇṇā”tivhayassa rājadhānīnagarassa dakkhiṇasmiṃ disābhāge pañcayojanappamāṇe ṭhāne dvīhi mahātaḷākehi susobhitassa midhilanāmanagarassa puratthimasmiṃ disābhāge diyaḍḍhagāvutappamāṇe ṭhāne anekatālapantīhi susobhito catunnaṃ kulānaṃ ramaṇīyabhūto “kaphrū” iti [V 2.0276] voharito yo so mahāgāmo patiṭṭhito, tattha paṭisandhiyā jātena sīlādiguṇehi pasaṃsitena “jāgaro”ti garūhi gahitanāmadheyyena tikkhattuṃ rājūhi rājamuddinā lañchitena me katāyaṃ pācityādivaṇṇanāya yojanā sampatte jinacakke terasādhikacatuvassasatādhikaṃ dvisahassaṃ, sakkarāje pana ekatiṃsādhikadvivassasatādhikaṃ sahassaṃ gimhāne jeṭṭhamāse juṇhapakkhassa pañcame sukkavāre niṭṭhaṃ pattā anāyāsenāti.

In the southern direction of the royal capital city called 'Ratanapuṇṇa,' at a distance of five yojanas, is the town named Midhila, beautifully adorned with two great lakes. In the eastern direction of that town, at a distance of one and a half gāvutas, is established the great village called 'Kaphrū,' beautifully adorned with numerous rows of palm trees and delightful to the four families. There, I was reborn, praised for qualities such as virtue, and given the name 'Jāgaro' by my teachers. Thrice honored by kings with the royal seal, this exposition of the commentary on the Pācittiya and so on, made by me, was completed without difficulty in the summer, in the month of Jeṭṭha, on the fifth day of the waxing moon, a Friday, when the Jina cycle had reached two thousand, four hundred and thirteen years, and the Sakkarāja era had reached one thousand, two hundred and thirty-one years.

Yojanāya [M 0.0655] imissāhaṃ, racanassānubhāvato;

Bhaveyyānekajātīsu, piṭakattayadhārako.

By the power of composing this exposition, may I, in many births, become a bearer of the Three Piṭakas.

Kusalo cubhayatthesu, parisāsu visārado;

Samijjhantu susaṅkappā, mayhañca sabbapāṇinaṃ.

May I be skilled in both aims and confident in assemblies; may the good aspirations of myself and of all beings be fulfilled.

Vappādimanatikkamma, sammā devo pavassatu;

Attajamiva rakkhantu, rājāno cāpi medininti.

Without failing the season for sowing and so on, may the deva rain properly; and may kings also protect the earth as if it were their own offspring.

Iti bhadantajāgarattherena katā

Thus was it made by the Venerable Elder Jāgara.

Pācityādivaṇṇanāya yojanā samattā.

The exposition of the commentary on the Pācittiya and so on is complete.
